english: Planting seeds too close together forces individual plants to fight one another for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, preventing any single plant from reaching its full strength.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso atswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ koni tsei komɛi akakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my maize when the rains start coming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi ebaa lɛ?

english: Do not plant after the very first rain because it might be a false start. Wait until the rains become steady and the soil stays moist for a few consecutive days so your seeds do not dry up underground.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ejaakɛ ekolɛ ebaafee amale shishijee. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow so much faster than my crops right after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are hardy wild plants with aggressive root systems that absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than domesticated crops, which is why early clearing is necessary to prevent them from taking over.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe shia tsei. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni atsĩ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye nɔyeli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and falling off during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during long dry periods to reduce water loss and protect its roots. Once regular rains return, the plant will sprout healthy green leaves again.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ebu eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ daa Tso lɛ baawo baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil lacks adequate moisture, which stops successful pollination and prevents the fruit from setting.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa pollination lɛ kpaa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are holes appearing on the leaves of my cabbage crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji miije kpo yɛ mi-cabbage tsei lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by hungry caterpillars or beetles feeding on the green leaves, which reduces the plant's ability to make food and grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ loo ladybugs ni yeɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bulɛ baa kaabeji baai lɛ amli. Enɛ haaa tsei afee niyenii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it better to buy certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahere dumɔwui ni jɛ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Certified seeds are specially selected and treated to resist common diseases and yield more food, whereas seeds saved from hybrid harvests lose their strength and produce fewer crops.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni atsaa amɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni amɛha niyenii babaoo aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ amli lɛ he waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: What will happen to my crops if I apply fertilizer when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires water to dissolve so plant roots can safely soak up the nutrients; putting chemical fertilizer on dry soil can burn your crop's roots and waste your money.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ nu ni ekɛshwie shi bɔni afee ni tsei ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite shika.

english: Can I plant cassava and cowpea together on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, cowpea fix nitrogen into the soil which enriches the land for cassava, while providing ground cover that prevents weed growth while the cassava is still young.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmeii saa nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni haa ŋmeii ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa be mli ni ŋmei lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ.

english: How can I protect my harvested maize from insects while storing it in my barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ahe be mli ni mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Ensure your maize is dried completely until the grains are hard, then store it in sealed, airtight bags (like PICS bags) to suffocate any insects and protect your harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni o-corn lɛ agbi kwraa kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛwo kotoku ko ni vacuum tsiɔ mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku) mli koni ekɛmu ŋmeii lɛ ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: How do I decide which crop to grow to make a good profit at the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni esa akɛ makwɛ koni maná sɛɛnamɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Choose crops that suit your local soil and rain patterns, check which produce is in high demand near market days, and calculate input costs beforehand to ensure good returns.
ga: Halamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi. Kwɛmɔ nibii ni ataoɔ waa lɛ ateŋ nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ jarayeli gbi lɛ. ni abu nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo he akɔntaa kɛtsɔ hiɛ koni ana sɛɛnamɔi kpakpai.

english: Can I plant my farm crops right next to the edge of the river?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu okwaayeli nibii yɛ faa lɛ naa?

english: While planting near water gives crops easy moisture, planting too close to the riverbank can cause your crops to drown or get washed away during heavy floods. It is best to plant a short distance away where the soil stays moist but does not collect standing water.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kɛ́ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ moŋ. Shi kɛ́ adu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ faa ko naa tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ nu mli loo ekɛ amɛ aya yɛ nu afua ni naa wa mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu yɛ he ko ni kɛ jɛmɛ jɛkɛɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo shi ehiɛɛɛ nu ni damɔ shi.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need plenty of sunlight to manufacture food for the tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground into the sun, which boosts tuber growth and prevents leaves from rotting due to soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la mli. Enɛ haa tuber lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ helai ahewɔ.

english: How can I tell when my yams are fully ready to be dug out of the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yams are usually ready for harvesting when the leaves and vines above the ground dry up and turn yellow or brown. This sign shows that the plant has stopped growing and has stored all its energy inside the tuber.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Okadi nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested yams start growing green shoots even inside my dry storage shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ mi ŋmɔ mli ni egbi lɛ po mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living seeds that naturally break their rest period when warm weather comes, preparing to grow into new plants. Keeping your storage shed cool, well-ventilated, and shaded helps slow down this early sprouting.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji dumɔwui ni hiɛ ka ni fiteɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ba. Koni esaa ehe koni eda ni etsɔ tso henɔ hee. Oshĩa lɛ mli ni oooha efee fɛ̃i Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ. Ni kɛ́ oná hulutsoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ mra be mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Plantain leaves turn yellow and drop off in dry weather because the plant is trying to conserve water to stay alive. Giving your plantain trees water or mulching around their roots during dry months helps keep the leaves green and growing.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ nu ato koni ehi shi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-plantains lɛ anɔ loo okɛ sũ wo amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara.

english: Why do some of my plantain trees fall over easily before the fruits are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi oya dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that cannot support heavy bunches during strong winds or in soft, wet soil. Propping up the stems with bamboo or wooden poles and trimming extra shoot suckers helps keep the main tree standing.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ aye abua ŋmɔlɔ ni tsii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmei loo tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ Ni akɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni edamɔɔ shi.

english: How do I choose the right plantain shoot from my old farm to start a new one?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantains kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛje tso hee shishi?

english: Look for young shoots called 'sword suckers' that have thick bases and narrow, spear-like leaves. These grow faster and produce stronger plantain trees than suckers that already have broad, wide leaves.
ga: Taomɔ tsei bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘sword shoots’ ni yɔɔ shishi ni mli tse kɛ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi. Enɛɛmɛi daa oya ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni he wa fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ momo lɛ.

english: Is it good practice to plant yams and plantains together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ekome yɛ he kome?

english: Yes, planting yams and plantains together works well because yams produce tubers underground while plantains grow tall and offer light shade. Proper spacing is necessary so their roots do not fight each other for water and manure.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii kɛ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmeii woɔ ŋmeii. yɛ be mli ni plantains lɛ daa ni amɛhaa hulutsoo be mli lɛ Ehe miihia ni aŋmɛ gbɛ ni sa bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ akatswa akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I know if my soil is too weak to support a healthy crop of plantains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ makwɛ plantains ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: If your soil stays very hard, dry, or only grows thin weeds, it likely lacks nutrients. Plantains require rich, dark, loose soil mixed with compost or animal manure to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa waa, egbi, loo jwɛi fioo pɛ yɔɔ nɔ. Efɔɔ niyenii ni esaaa he. Plantains he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni tsuɔ, ni mli edɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii efutu mli koni ekɛwo ŋmɔji wuji ni tsii.

english: What causes black spots on my plantain leaves, and will it ruin my harvest?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi plantain baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa? Ni ani ebaafite bɔ ni mitsuɔ nii ehaa lɛ?

english: Black spots on plantain leaves are caused by a leaf disease that spreads quickly in damp, shaded farms. It reduces the plant's strength, leading to smaller fruit bunches, but clearing weeds and cutting off heavy dark leaves helps control it.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni yɔɔ plantain baa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa ji baa hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa aduawai akuu bibioo ko baa. Shi jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa lɛ ni afoɔ waa Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because full sunlight burns their young leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Keeping taller plants or shade trees nearby protects cocoa from harsh sun and keeps soil moisture in place.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ Ebaabu kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. When soil nitrogen is low, maize moves whatever nutrients it has left to new top leaves, leaving the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Abele lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies. Treating insect infestations early stops leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Nibii ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ ahe tsamɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wood poles or stakes to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso loo tso ni akɛkwɔɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high up toward the sun to make food for growing underground tubers. Staking keeps leaves off the damp ground, improving air movement and preventing rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ he koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ni etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni atsĩ fitemɔ naa

english: Why do I get smaller maize ears when I plant my seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa toi bibii anɔ be mli ni adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe kpaakpa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, plants compete for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space ensures it gets enough food to build large, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaha ená niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too high or water is irregular. Heat stress prevents successful pollination, so the plant drops the unpollinated flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ mli haomɔ tsiɔ pollination ni yeɔ omanye lɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shĩɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal nutrients and water away from the main mother tree. Keeping only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main plant produces bigger bunches of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ahiɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ baawo tsei babaoo babaoo.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt during the hot afternoon even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛgbi moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: On hot afternoons, leaves lose water faster through heat evaporation than roots can suck up from the soil. This temporary wilting protects the plant, and leaves usually revive when heat cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni dɔlɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɔ ni fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ tso lɛ ni shwieɔ shi be kukuoo nɛɛ buɔ tso lɛ he. Ni bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ baa wala mli ekoŋŋ kɛ́ latsaa lɛ ba shi.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants well adapted to local soils. Their seeds germinate fast to capture rainwater and soil nutrients before soft farm crops have a chance to grow strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni wa ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔji lɛ anɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya koni amɛkɛ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dani ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ baaná hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ shishifãi ni wa

english: Why do my cassava roots go soft and spoil quickly if I leave them in the ground after the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni hulutsoo be lɛ eje shishi lɛ?

english: When rain stops and soil bakes hard, cassava roots lose water back to the soil or suffer damage from soil pests, leading to internal rot before you get a chance to dig them up.
ga: Beni nugbɔ lɛ kpa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ waa lɛ. Cassava shishifãi lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ loo sũ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa mligbɛ fiteɔ dani onáa hegbɛ ni okɛfoɔ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees grow much better when I leave big leguminous trees standing on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ mishi cacao tsei wuji ni damɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Big trees act as natural shields for cocoa. They filter harsh sunlight to protect fragile cocoa leaves from burning, and their roots draw up nutrients from deep underground while their falling leaves decay to naturally fertilize the soil.
ga: Tsei wuji lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ni akɛbuɔ kookoo lɛ he. Amɛ shwieɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ mli koni amɛ bu kookoo baai ni waaa lɛ ahe koni aka shã amɛ. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aba.

english: Why do my young crop shoots wither and die quickly when I clear all the tall trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie tsei kakadaji fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Without shade trees to block intense sun and hot winds, young plant shoots lose moisture faster than their roots can draw water from the soil. Shade trees create a cooler climate that keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kɛji tsei bɛ ni baatsi hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ naa lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Can planting specific trees next to my main crops help reduce how much chemical fertilizer I need to buy?
ga: Tsei pɔtɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eba tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni ehe hiaa ni mahe lɛ shi?

english: Yes, leguminous trees like Gliricidia take nitrogen directly from the air and store it. When you prune their leaves and drop them on the soil around your crops, they break down and release free nitrogen fertilizer into the ground.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii tamɔ Gliricidia lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ ebaai lɛ ni okɛwo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ mli lɛ, amɛgbalaa ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How far apart should I plant shade trees so they help my farm instead of stealing water from my main crops?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu tsei ni haa ŋmɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji tɛŋŋ koni eye ebua ŋmɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni maju nu kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ amli?

english: Shade trees should generally be spaced about 12 to 15 meters apart. This gap allows filtered sunlight to reach your main crops while preventing the shade tree roots from competing heavily for water.
ga: Esa akɛ bei pii lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ shade lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 12 kɛyashi 15. Nɛkɛ he nɛɛ haa hulu la ni ajieɔ lɛ shɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatswa akaŋ waa yɛ nu he.

english: What does it mean when my plantain plant starts 'shooting', and how should I care for it when that happens?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ mi-plantains lɛ je shishi ‘fɔlɔ’? Ni mɛni esa akɛ makwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ enɛ ba?

english: Shooting' means the plantain has stopped making leaves and is now pushing out its flowering stalk to form a bunch. At this stage, the plant needs plenty of water and clear space around it so all its energy goes into filling out the fruit.
ga: Tutswaa’ tsɔɔ akɛ plantain lɛ ekpa baai feemɔ. Amrɔ nɛɛ, ashɛreɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe tsei lɛ kɛyaa mli yɛ kui amli. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, tso lɛ he miihia nu babaoo kɛ he ko ni ebɔle ehe. Bɔni afee ni hewalɛ fɛɛ aya koni ekɛwo aduawai lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava plants shooting out a lot of thick green leaves, but the tubers under the ground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or gets too much deep shade, the cassava puts all its energy into growing top stems and leaves instead of sending starch down to expand the underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo hulutsoo be lɛ mli kwɔ tsɔ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ etsitsi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ starch kɛ yaa si konɛ e ha nɛ a ngmɛɛ ngmami ɔmɛ a he ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why does my plantain crop produce so many small shoots around the main stem, and should I cut them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ, ni ani esa akɛ mafolɔ amɛ?

english: Those extra shoots are suckers competing with the main plant for food and water. You should cut away most of them, leaving only one strong shoot to replace the main stem after you harvest the current bunch.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Esa akɛ ofo mli babaoo. Tso kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ eshwɛ ni baaye tso titri lɛ najiaŋ beni okpa tso ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants shoot up very tall and skinny without making full corn cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Maize stretches tall and thin when planted too close together or under heavy shade because it is fighting for sunlight. Good spacing allows sunshine to hit every plant so the cobs can develop fully.
ga: Abɛi baanyɛ afee kakadaŋŋ ni efee mlɛo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli waa ejaakɛ ekɛ hulu la miitswa akaŋ. He ni ato jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ tso fɛɛ tso he. No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ adara kwraa.

english: How do planting trees around the border of my farm protect my crops during rainstorms?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ buɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Border trees act as windbreaks. They slow down heavy gusts of wind during storms so your tall crops, like maize, cassava, or plantain, do not bend, break, or get uprooted.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ husu lɛ naa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsimɔ. Amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ baa shi yɛ ahum be mli. No hewɔ lɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛlɛ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo plantains lɛ efoŋ, efoŋ loo efoŋ.

english: Why do my fruit trees shoot out fresh flowers right after a short dry period followed by rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ be kukuoo ko ni nugbɔ enɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fruit trees interpret a short dry rest period followed by rain as a signal that good growing conditions have arrived. This trigger causes the tree to shoot out new flowers and leaves all at once.
ga: Tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ tsɔɔ be kuku ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ shishi akɛ eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ shihilɛ kpakpa ni haa mɔ daa lɛ eba. Nɛkɛ nɔ ni tsiɔ tso lɛ naa nɛɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ baai heei shikome.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants turn yellow at the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. The plant starves and moves nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the fresh leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tso lɛ dalɛ Tso lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ ni ejieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaf rolling is the crop's natural way of protecting itself from losing too much water during hot hours. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to direct heat and sunshine.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu babaoo ni efiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Tsei baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does the top flower on my maize plant bloom before the silk threads show up on the cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii fɔɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ dani siliki jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The top flower (tassel) produces male pollen, while the silks are female parts that need pollen to form seeds. The plant naturally releases pollen slightly earlier or at the exact time silks appear so wind can drop pollen onto the silks to form grain.
ga: Fɔfɔ lɛ yiteŋ (tassel) lɛ jieɔ pollen. Yɛ be mli ni siliki ŋmeii ji yei lɛ, amɛdamɔɔ pollen nɔ koni amɛwo dumɔwui. Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, tsei jieɔ pollen lɛ mra fioo loo yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ni siliki lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ anyɛ ajie pollen awo siliki lɛ nɔ koni ekɛfee dumɔwui.

english: Why does my farm produce fewer bags of maize every year even when I use the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ miiwo ŋmãa kotokui fioo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ.

english: Maize is a heavy feeder that quickly pulls nutrients out of the soil. Planting maize in the exact same spot season after season drains the land unless you rotate crops with beans or groundnuts to rebuild soil health.
ga: Abɛi ji niyenii ni tsii ni gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu atsɔ jɛmɛ. Ja okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake ŋmɔshi nibii koni okɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is planting maize in the major rainy season better than planting during the minor season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ hi fe ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The major rainy season provides cooler soil temperatures and consistent moisture over many weeks, giving maize roots a steady supply of water and food needed to fill out heavy cobs.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa baa yɛ otsii babaoo mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ náa nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmãa ni tsii lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are there small ragged holes in my maize leaves and soft green waste in the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ tsɔne lɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. The caterpillars hide inside the center growing point of the plant and eat the leaves before they open up, which can destroy the yield if untreated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni edaa lɛ, ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite yibiiwoo lɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: What is the main difference between yellow maize and white maize, and can I feed both to chickens?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmãa yɛŋ teŋ? Ni ani manyɛ makwɛ kooloi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Both supply good energy, but yellow maize contains natural compounds that give chicken skin and egg yolks a rich yellow color. Poultry farmers often prefer yellow maize for egg production, but both types nourish birds well.
ga: Hei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ haa hewalɛ kpakpa. Shi adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa tsina hewolo kɛ tsina ŋmɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli kwɔ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ mli. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi akwɛlɔi sumɔɔ abele ŋmɔŋ kɛha wɔji feemɔ. Shi henɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ haa okpoi niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some maize seeds produce big, full cobs while seed kept from my last harvest produces smaller cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii komɛi woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Specially bred hybrid seeds carry strong genetics designed for high yield and disease resistance. Replanting seeds saved from previous harvests loses that strength, resulting in weaker plants and smaller cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ wala yibii ni mli wa ni afee koni ewo yibii babaoo ni ekɛ helai akaye. Dumɔwui ni adu ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ hewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ hu feɔ bibii.

english: Why does my stored maize turn into white powder and get full of small insects after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ powda yɛŋ ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Ani ebaafee nɔ ni yeɔ emuu yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: Insects like grain weevils lay eggs inside maize kernels, especially if the maize was not dried completely before storage. Moist grains allow these insects to hatch, feed, and multiply quickly, destroying the grain.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii amli. Titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto. Dumɔwui ni mli efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kooloi nɛɛ ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ, amɛnaa niyenii, ni amɛfɔɔ oya. kpata dumɔwui ahiɛ

english: How can I tell if my harvested maize is dry enough to put in bags for long-term storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛwo kotoku mli koni akɛto be kakadaŋŋ?

english: You can test grain dryness by biting a kernel or pressing it with your thumbnail. Dry maize is glass-hard and breaks with a sharp crack, whereas wet maize feels soft and dents easily.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ egbi ha lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni oooŋmɔ loo okɛ oshishifã lɛ anyɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni egbi lɛ wa tamɔ glase, ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa ni efɔ lɛ baanu he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni egbɔjɔ oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants need plantain trees planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ aná dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: When cassava stems are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients. This competition causes the plants to put energy into growing tall stalks instead of expanding their underground roots, leading to a smaller harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛhe. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afee lɛ fioo.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the maize plant lacks essential nutrients, especially nitrogen, or that the roots are sitting in waterlogged soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or improving field drainage helps the leaves regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen loo shishifãi ni ta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafata he loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni ooofee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do flowers drop off my pepper plants before producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ dani ewoɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers often fall off due to extreme heat stress, lack of water, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weather helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can develop into peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Seeds fail to sprout if the soil is too dry, if they are buried too deep for sunlight to reach them, or if insect pests damaged the seeds before planting. Planting good-quality seeds at the proper depth in moist soil ensures proper sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni hulu la lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he loo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kpata dumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ dani adu Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This naturally enriches the soil, helping nearby maize grow stronger without relying entirely on expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ daa waa ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔɔɔ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my plants with dry leaves or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Tso ni baai egbi loo jwɛi?

english: Covering soil with dry organic matter creates mulch. Mulch protects the soil from direct heat, traps moisture so the ground stays wet longer, and prevents weeds from taking root.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni egbi ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Mulch buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i be kakadaŋŋ, ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ akawo shishifãi.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow slower and yield less?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ miida blɛoo ni ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds act as aggressive competitors that absorb water, fertilizer, and sunlight faster than your main crops. When weeds take over, your crops receive fewer nutrients, leading to weak growth and lower yields.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei, ni amɛmɔɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ ohe lɛ. Beni jwɛi lɛ ye nɔ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes in the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes in the same soil continuously allows soil-borne pests and fungal diseases that feed on tomatoes to multiply. Rotating tomatoes with crops like corn or cassava starves those specific pests and restores soil balance.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tomato lɛ yaa nɔ amɛshwereɔ. Tomato ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ. Ebaaha hɔmɔ aye kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ekomɛi, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to prune branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ aniji lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to allow sunlight and fresh air to pass through the branches. This reduces moisture buildup, which prevents humid conditions that encourage diseases like black pod rot.
ga: Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ni abua naa lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ helai tamɔ black rot ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa lɛ naa.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants turn yellow and fall off when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is a natural survival trick cassava uses to save water. By dropping its leaves, the plant loses less moisture through evaporation and stores its energy safely in the underground roots until the rains return.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa ni ŋmei kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛbu nu he. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ mli nu fioo pɛ baa kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. ni akɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli shweshweeshwe kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, usually caused by extremely high heat, poor pollination, or irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiihao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. pollination ni ehiii loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually a sign of stress caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites, or an infection from a leaf curl virus. Controlling pests early and shading young plants helps prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ ji haomɔ ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites kɛbaa lɛ he okadi. loo hela ni jɛɔ leaf curl virus mli Mra Be mli Kojolɔi Akwɛmɔ Ni tsei bibii ni akɛwoɔ shade mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need sunlight to build energy for growing tubers. Staking lifts the leaves into the air for better light and air flow, while keeping them off damp ground where diseases spread easily.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulbs ni miida lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves start turning light green or yellow after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ fioo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away nitrogen—the main plant nutrient—deep into the soil where roots cannot reach it. Adding a quick-acting nitrogen fertilizer after excessive heavy rain helps the corn regain its dark green color.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen, ni ji tso mli niyenii titri ko lɛ, kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsuɔ nii oya wo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛ babaoo sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts before planting my maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii dani madu ŋmãa yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, which naturally enriches your soil with free fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko awo oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: This practice, called mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps soil cool under the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, stops weeds from growing, and rots into food for your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho oya Ha jwɛi akakwɛ̃ ni egbo ni etsɔ niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do I need to trim off branches from my cocoa trees when they seem to be growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo kookoo tso nine lɛ? Etamɔ nɔ ni kookoo tso lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lolo?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches so sunlight and fresh air can reach the inner branches. This cuts down humidity inside the farm, preventing black pod disease while helping the tree produce larger pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa anyɛ ashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Etsiɔ black pod hela naa yɛ be mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ pods wuji baa.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce smaller bunches if I leave all the young shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛji mishi ŋmeii bibii ni bɔle tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: The main plantain stem shares its food and water with all the young shoots growing around it. If you cut off extra shoots and leave only one or two strong ones, the main plant receives enough energy to grow a large bunch.
ga: Plantain tso titri lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ jaa niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛji ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, tso titri lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii agbo.

english: Why does my cassava root become hard and woody to cook if I leave it in the ground for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots reach peak harvest quality at maturity, but if left in the ground too long, the plant converts soft starch into tough fiber to stay alive, making the tubers hard and woody to eat.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ su ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ kɛji amɛdara kwraa. Shi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Tsei lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa koni amɛhi shi. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni ayeɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops turn yellow before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting from the tips down the middle, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛyashi amɛteŋgbɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops when I plant the same crop on the same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with different crops, like beans or groundnuts, restores soil health.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni tsakeɔ amɛhe, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my plants even when the crops are already big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi yɛ mitsei lɛ ahe eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eda momo moŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for groundwater, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil regardless of crop size. Clearing weeds ensures your crops get all the food and water they need to yield heavy harvests.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ekɔɔɔ he eko bɔ ni tso lɛ da ha Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa onibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ agbo.

english: Why is it better for me to water my garden vegetables early in the morning rather than in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ anɔ nu leebi moŋ fe shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the plant roots to absorb moisture before the hot afternoon sun evaporates it. It also lets leaf surfaces dry during the day, which prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa baa lɛ hu ni egbiɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa

english: Why do my cassava plants stay alive during the dry season while my other crops dry up and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi hiɔ shi lɛ? Mi nɔ lɛ gĩɔ ni egboɔ?

english: Cassava has deep, thick roots that store water and food far beneath the soil surface. During dry periods, cassava drops its leaves to save water and rests until the rains return.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ, ni mli tse ni toɔ nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Cassava shwieɔ baai koni ekɛto nu ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa trees exposed to excessive sun will develop burnt, yellow, or brown leaf edges, and their growth will slow down. Young cocoa needs shade from taller crops like plantains to shield tender leaves from scorching heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii ni hulu la shɛɔ amɛnɔ babaoo lɛ baashã baai lɛ ashishigbɛ. Amɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ loo asarasu. ni dalɛ baafee mlɛo Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ, koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Plantain roots grow close to the soil surface rather than deep underground. When heavy bunches form at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for rain-soaked soil and strong winds to pull the roots loose.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ daa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ fe shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Kɛji kuu ko ni tsii fee yɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baaná muji babaoo yɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ gbalaa shishifãi lɛ oya.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and fall off without growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when insects fail to pollinate the blossoms. Keeping soil moisture steady with mulch helps prevent flower drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ amli fɔfɔii lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ mulch tsuɔ nii be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Yam rot happens when water sits around the tubers due to poor soil drainage, creating wet conditions where fungal diseases thrive. Building higher mounds helps excess water drain away from the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato rot baa kɛji nu ebɔle ŋmeii lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni aaafee lɛ baaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Curled or twisted pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. Spraying with neem oil or soapy water helps clear these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa ni ebɔle ehe loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni mli ewo samla shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi bibii nɛɛ kɛjɛ ohe.

english: Leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to grow strong green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer like urea near the roots will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ni yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I place fertilizer directly touching the stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem causes 'fertilizer burn', which damages the delicate skin and roots of the plant. Fertilizer should be placed in a small ring or line a few inches away from the stem so the roots can stretch out and safely drink the nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa ‘ŋmɔshi nibii shãa’ ni efiteɔ tso lɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. Aloo okɛto he ko ni kɛ tsɔne lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛnuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cassava tubers rot when water collects and stays around the roots for too long due to heavy rain and poor soil drainage. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil dries out suddenly, which stresses the plant. Watering your tomatoes regularly at the base early in the morning keeps the soil moist and protects the flowers so they can form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi trukaa. ni kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tomato nɔ yɛ shishigbɛ daa leebi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaabu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni ekpa shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap and spreading plant sicknesses. Spraying your pepper crop with neem leaf water or recommended safe pesticides gets rid of these pests and allows new leaves to grow flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Amɛmuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ shwie pepper tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaaha baai heei lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why are tiny young cocoa pods turning black and drying up on my trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cocoa pods bibii No hewɔ lɛ etsɔɔ ediŋŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ mi tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa pods dry up either because the tree naturally sheds extra pods it cannot feed, or due to black pod disease caused by too much shade and dampness. Trimming extra tree branches to let in sunlight and fresh air reduces moisture and keeps pods healthy.
ga: Kokoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ejaakɛ tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ, ni anyɛɛɛ aye niyenii. Aloo black pod hela ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aba lɛ haa hulutsoo baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cowpeas and beans take natural air and turn it into plant food stored in tiny nodules on their roots. When the bean roots decompose after harvest, they leave this nitrogen food in the soil, which feeds the next crop like maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii lɛ heɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ beni ŋmeii lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Amɛshiɔ niyenii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii kɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal the nutrients, sunlight, and water from the soil that your main crop needs. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to soil food so they can grow thick and produce good yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛkɛ ekãa juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, hulu la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ taoɔ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during strong winds when they carry heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli, be mli ni eyɛ yitsɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that cannot easily balance the weight of a heavy bunch during strong winds. Supporting the stalk with a sturdy wooden prop or bamboo pole prevents the plant from bending or snapping before the fruits ripen.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ amli tsiimɔ lɛ nɔ mlɛo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ loo ekakumɔ dani eyibii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start sprouting shoots in the barn before I am ready to plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mifee klalo akɛ madu amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally wake up from dormancy after a few months when they feel warmth and humidity in storage. Storing yams on raised racks in a cool, shaded, and well-ventilated barn slows down shoot growth and keeps the tubers fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ baate shi kɛjɛ wɔɔhe yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni amɛnuɔ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ. Kɛ atomo ni mli ŋɔɔ ato adeka ni awó nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni yɔɔ shade, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ aba shi, ni eye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build green leaves and grow tall. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores this nutrient so the plant can grow healthy again.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ koni tsei lɛ anyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of big leaves, but the roots underneath stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daraaa lolo.

english: When soil has plenty of nitrogen but lacks potassium, cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storing food in its underground tubers. Balanced soil nutrients encourage the plant to send its energy downward into making large, heavy roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei baato niyenii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ebaa lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsɔɔ hewalɛ gbɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ shishifãi wuji ni tsii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans in the same field make my maize grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa ŋmãa waa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. As those roots break down, they release natural food that nearby maize plants can easily drink up.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ nakai shishifãi lɛ gbee shi lɛ Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baanyɛ anu mlɛo lɛ kpo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their leaves as soon as the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ baai babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi pɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during severe heat to save water and keep their trunks alive. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains near young cocoa keeps the air cool and preserves soil moisture so the cocoa keeps its leaves.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni eha tso lɛ yitso lɛ ahi shi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, kookoo hiɛɔ ebaa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves curl up and look wilted in the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: Vegetable leaves curl during intense heat to shrink their surface area and slow down water loss. Putting dry grass or leaves on top of the soil around the plant stem keeps the roots cool and stops water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Aduawai baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ dɔlɛ be mli koni amɛha amɛhiɛ afee bibioo ni amɛha nu lɛ aya hiɛ blɛoo. Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that do not go deep into the earth, making them top-heavy when carrying big bunches of fruit. Propping up heavy stalks with strong wooden poles or bamboo gives them the extra support needed during storms.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛ́ ootere aduawai akui wuji. Shishijee ni tsii Tso loo ŋmei tsei ni wa baaha yelikɛbuamɔ ni he hiaa yɛ ahum be mli.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience sudden temperature changes, dry soil, or lack of soil food. Keeping the soil evenly moist and protected with shade or mulch helps the flowers stay attached long enough to turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tsake trukaa, shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ hulutsoo loo ŋmɔtɔ bu he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my tomatoes get black, rotten bottoms while they are still growing on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishi lɛ yɛ ediŋŋ ni egbo yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes happen when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil into the growing fruit, usually caused by irregular watering. Watering crops on a steady schedule helps calcium move smoothly through the stem to the fruit.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo otsei lɛ amli yɛ be naa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni calcium lɛ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛya aduawai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out small and bent instead of straight and long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee tɛ̃ɛ ni kɛlɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are soft roots that push deep into the earth, and hard or rocky soil stops them from spreading smoothly. Making high, soft soil mounds creates loose earth that allows the tubers to expand straight and wide.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii ji shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. ni shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Gɔŋ kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afee lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ daa tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally tougher than food crops and are designed to grab available water and plant food instantly. Clearing weeds early in the season stops them from stealing the water and sunlight your young crops need to establish themselves.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli jwɛi lɛ wa fe niyenii tsei, ni afee amɛ koni amɛmɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkaju nu kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa ni otsei bibii lɛ afee lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants full of holes and look like something is eating them from the inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ eyi kɛ bu ni etamɔ nɔ ko miiye amɛ kɛmiijɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central shoot of the maize plant during the day and eat the tender growing leaves, leaving ragged holes and waste that looks like sawdust.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai ni miida ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Eshiɔ buji ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ sũ ni tamɔ tsei ahe sũ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up into tight little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi bibii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips. As they suck the juice from young leaves, they spread viruses that cause the leaves to wrinkle and deform.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. be mli ni amɛmuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ Amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn turning yellow in a V-shape starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the tip of older maize leaves is a classic sign that the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is essential food for plant growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the plant turn green again.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa baai momoi lɛ anaa lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ miiho. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants have huge leafy bushes above ground, but very small tubers when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ beni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen or unbalanced nutrients. The plant uses all its energy to grow big green leaves and stems instead of storing food underground in the tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai agboi kɛ tsei ashishifãi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ niyenii ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ oyitsoŋ lɛ najiaŋ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in direct sunlight and dry out fast. Plantains grow very quickly and produce large leaves that provide living shade, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist during its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Plantain lɛ daa oya waa, ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves to catch sunlight to make food for big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot soil, prevents diseases from splashing soil, and gives leaves maximum light.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbele amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi helai ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. ni ehaa baai lɛ náa la babaoo

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when they start carrying big bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ebɔi ŋmeii wuji shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the ground. When a heavy fruit bunch grows, the plant becomes top-heavy, so strong winds can easily pull the roots out of the soil unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu agbo ko da Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli oya. ja akɛ tso nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsu nii

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, extreme dry soil, or sudden heavy rains. When the plant feels too stressed, it sheds flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ amɛmiifee basaa tsɔ Ebaajie fɔfɔi koni ekɛto hewalɛ he koni ekɛha ehe ahi wala mli.

english: The first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell before the main rains start. If your seeds sprout during this false start, the young seedlings will dry up and die from heat before the continuous rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji odumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ amale shishijee mli Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ mli dani nugbɔ lɛ aya nɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable roots turn black and rot when water sits on my field for two days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni nu ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii enyɔ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe just like people do. When water completely covers the ground, air cannot reach the roots, causing them to suffocate, die, and rot from soil bacteria.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu, tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Beni nu lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ, gbele kɛ fitemɔ ni jɛɔ bacteria ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ mli baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the big shade trees from the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni edara lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly in harsh sunlight. Leaving or planting shade trees creates a cool, humid canopy that protects the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ ni ashiɔ loo aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: I am starting a farm on a new piece of land, how can I know if the soil is good for growing cocoa?
ga: Mijeɔ ŋmɔ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ hee ko nɔ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha kookoo dumɔ?

english: Good cocoa soil should be dark and rich in plant matter, soft enough to dig deep, and able to hold moisture without turning into a muddy swamp where water stands still for days.
ga: Esa akɛ kookoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ afee diŋŋ ni tsei babaoo ahi mli. Eyɛ bɔdɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ efo mli kɛya shɔŋŋ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni etsɔko ŋmɔtɔ ni nu lɛ damɔɔ shi gbii babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa seedlings very close to each other so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni manyɛ mikɛwo he ko ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi babaoo lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees are planted too close together, their roots and branches fight for the same water, soil food, and sunlight, resulting in tall, weak trees that produce very few pods.
ga: Kɛ́ adu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛniji lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná nu, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ baa.

english: Yellow and falling leaves are a cocoa tree's way of surviving drought; the tree sheds its leaves to conserve water so its trunk and roots can stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni kookoo tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai koni amɛkɛto nu koni amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many small flowers, but very few of them turn into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo, shi amɛteŋ fioo pɛ tsɔɔ fɔfɔi diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny beneficial insects called midges to carry pollen between them. If the farm is too dry, lacks natural leaf cover on the ground, or is sprayed heavily with pesticides, those insects disappear and the flowers drop off without forming pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midges lɛ woɔ pollen yɛ amɛteŋ. Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Adebɔɔ mli baa ko bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. aloo akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ waa Kooloi lɛ laajeɔ ni fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii.

english: Why do people tell me to cut off some branches from my cocoa tree when it looks healthy and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ mafolɔ mi-kookoo niji lɛ ekomɛi amli be mli ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ ni amɛji eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-producing or overlapping branches, allowing fresh air and sunlight into the center of the tree. This prevents fungal diseases and forces the tree to direct its energy into growing big, healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii loo ni tsɔɔ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la boteɔ tso lɛ teŋ. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ anaa, ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmɔji wuji ni mli wa.

english: What causes the pods on my cocoa tree to turn dark black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: That rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and shady conditions when rain water stays on the surface of the pods for too long.
ga: Blackpod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my young cocoa seedlings, and how does it hurt my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe mi-kookoo dumɔwui lɛ? Ni te eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants designed to grab water and nutrients quickly. If left unchecked, they steal all the food from the soil and block sunlight from reaching your young cocoa seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni afee amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Ebaju niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ebaatsi hulu la naa koni ekashɛ o-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees giving me smaller pods and far less harvest than they did ten years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei momo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kwraa ni amɛkpaaa nii babaoo fe afii nyɔŋma ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their internal transport system weakens and soil nutrients become depleted, making it harder for the tree to feed large pods efficiently.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tsei lɛ ye afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, amɛmli gbɛfaa gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ baa shi, ni niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hu faaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ewa waa kɛha tso lɛ akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some cocoa trees look bushy with lots of leaves but never bear any pods at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei komɛi tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai babaoo shi amɛbɛ ŋmeii kwraa lɛ?

english: Trees offshoot wild branches called 'water suckers' from their base. These branches consume all the water and nutrients the tree absorbs without ever producing any flowers or pods.
ga: Tsei kwɛ̃ɔ niji yɛ koo lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘nu ni shwieɔ nu’ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishi. Nɛkɛ tsei niji nɛɛ holeɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni tso lɛ shwieɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛ fɔfɔi loo ŋmɔtɔ ko baaa.

english: How do my crops actually take in food and water from the soil through their roots?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛjieɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Crop roots work like tiny drinking straws. They soak up water and essential minerals dissolved in the soil, carrying them up through the stem to nourish the leaves, flowers, and fruits.
ga: Tsei shishifãi tsuɔ nii tamɔ jwɛi bibii ni anuɔ. Ekɛ nu kɛ shika tsuru ni he hiaa ni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Akɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi koni akɛha baai, fɔfɔi, kɛ aduawai lɛ niyenii.

english: Does a crop get all of its food directly from the ground through its roots?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii naa amɛ niyenii fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ?

english: Roots only pull water and mineral nutrients from the soil. The plant actually manufactures its main food in its green leaves by using sunlight, water, and air.
ga: Shishifãi gbalaa nu kɛ shika tsuru pɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei kɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ feɔ amɛ niyenii titri kɛjɛɔ amɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ amli.

english: Are there natural things in the soil that help bring food to my plant roots?
ga: Ani adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii baa mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli?

english: Yes, beneficial soil microbes, earthworms, and fungi break down dead leaves and manure into small, natural nutrients that your plant's roots can easily feed on.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbálaa baai ni egboi kɛ ŋmeii amli amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii bibii. Otsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni ayeɔ oya.

english: Can my crops grow healthy and give good yield without using chemical fertilizers?
ga: Ani mitsei lɛ baanyɛ adara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Crops can thrive naturally if your soil is rich in organic matter like compost, animal manure, and decomposed leaves, which naturally feed the soil micro-organisms and roots.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi ashishifãi, kɛ baai ni fiteɔ. ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha nibii bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ

english: How can I tell if my crop's root system is healthy and free from diseases?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli?

english: A healthy root system is usually firm, light-colored or white at the growing tips, and spreads out well without any dark rotting, foul smell, or swollen knots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifã ni mli wa lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ. Amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo eyɛŋ yɛ amɛdalɛ naagbeehei lɛ. ni egbɛɔ eshwaa jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ duŋ, ŋmeii gbohii, loo ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ bɛ mli

english: Will relying only on natural soil nutrients be enough for heavy crops like maize or cassava?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni fa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Natural soil nutrients can be enough if you regularly replenish the ground with decomposed compost, crop rotation, and manure, though worn-out soils may need extra boost to yield heavily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni fa kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo fata he. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa Shikpɔji ni efite po baanyɛ abi ni akɛ nibii krokomɛi afata he koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aba.

english: Why do some of my crops have deep roots while others have roots near the top of the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ?

english: Deep roots reach down to find hidden water during dry seasons, while shallow roots spread out near the surface to quickly catch rainfall and nutrients from decaying surface leaf litter.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛyana nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. yɛ be mli ni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ koni ekɛbua nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ baai ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli oya.

english: Why are the roots of my crops turning dark and soft instead of staying clean and firm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi yɛ hetsemɔ kɛ shiŋŋfeemɔ mli lɛ?

english: Dark, soft roots are a sign of root rot, usually caused by poor drainage, overly wet soil, or fungal infection, which prevents the crop from absorbing food properly.
ga: Shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni tsuɔ ediŋŋ lɛ ji shishifãi ni egbo lɛ he okadi. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. loo fungal infection Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What main nutrients do my crop roots need to draw from the soil for good growth?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii titrii esa akɛ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Roots mainly look for nitrogen for green leaves, phosphorus for strong root development, and potassium to build thick stems and fight off crop diseases.
ga: Shishifãi titri taoɔ nitrogen kɛha baai eŋɔli. Phosphorus kɛha shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ potassium ni akɛfeɔ tsei ashishifãi ni mli tse ni akɛwuɔ ashiɔ tsei ahelai.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop under the hot afternoon sun even when the plant looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ? Kɛji tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ po

english: Plants droop in extreme heat to save water from escaping through their leaves. Once the sun goes down, the roots drink up soil moisture to make the plant stand firm again.
ga: Tso lɛ baashwie baai lɛ shi yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni nu akatsɔ ebaa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha tso lɛ adamɔ shi ekoŋŋ.

english: What does it mean when an officer tells me that cassava is a 'heavy feeder' crop?
ga: Beni onukpa lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ ŋmei ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni ‘yeɔ nii waa’ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ?

english: A heavy feeder is a plant that takes a massive amount of nutrients and water from the soil to grow. Cassava puts a lot of energy into producing thick root tubers, which means it pulls out essential food like potassium and nitrogen from the earth faster than many other crops.
