ga: Niyenii wuji ji tsei ni biɔ niyenii kɛ nu babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Cassava kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni shishifãi lɛ mli tse. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ nitrogen tsuɔ nii. kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi

english: How can I tell if growing cassava has drained all the nutrients out of my farm's soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei ni miduɔ lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: You will notice that crops planted after the cassava look weak, grow slowly, or have pale yellow leaves. The soil itself may also become hard, dusty, and produce lower yields than it used to.
ga: Obaayɔse akɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa, amɛdaraa blɛoo loo amɛyɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni wa, ni sũ yɔɔ mli, ni ebaaha yibiiwoo aba shi.

english: Does cassava take away too much water and nutrients from other plants growing near it on my farm?
ga: Ani ŋmei heɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli?

english: Yes, cassava has wide and deep roots that aggressively absorb soil moisture and plant food. Any delicate crops planted too close to cassava will often get starved of nutrients and remain small.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu babaoo kɛ tsei aniyenii. Etamɔ nɔ ni tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo fɛɛ ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmei tsɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaaya nɔ amɛfee bibii.

english: Why do my maize crops grow so poorly when I plant them right after harvesting cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu lɛ beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves the ground tired and empty of basic nutrients after its long growing cycle. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to thrive, so planting it immediately after cassava without feeding the soil causes the maize to struggle.
ga: Yucca shĩɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etɔ lɛ ni niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni edara lɛ sɛɛ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃, no hewɔ lɛ, dumɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ niyenii haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. baaha ŋmãa lɛ abɔi ŋmɔlɔ

english: Why should I clear cassava completely out of my field before planting a new set of crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmei kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii heei?

english: Clearing cassava stops its aggressive root system from continuing to exhaust the soil. It gives your new, delicate crops a fresh space where they do not have to compete with cassava for light, water, and plant nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmei lɛ, ebaatsi eshishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ anaa koni ekafite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ naa he ko hee ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ŋmei aka akaŋ kɛha la, nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii.

english: What is the best crop for me to plant on my field right after I harvest cassava?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji mikpa ŋmei amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is best to plant legumes like cowpeas, groundnuts, or soybeans after cassava. These plants pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, helping to rebuild the field's strength.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo soybeans yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ. Tsei nɛɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ ŋmɔ nɛɛ.

english: How can I rebuild my soil's strength after growing cassava on my land for a long time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ beni midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: You can restore tired soil by adding well-rotted chicken or cow manure, planting nitrogen-fixing leguminous crops like beans, or letting the land rest without crops for a season.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsina loo tsina ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen-fixing legumes, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni aduɔ, loo ni ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli yɛ be ko mli.

english: Can I plant cassava together with groundnuts or beans on my piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava with groundnuts or beans works well. While cassava feeds heavily on the soil, groundnuts and beans add fresh nitrogen back into the earth, helping balance out the soil's nutrient supply.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛduɔ ŋmei lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei yeɔ niyenii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ, shi Peanuts kɛ Nuts Ekɛ nitrogen hee baaku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Do I need to put extra fertilizer on my cassava plants to get a good harvest?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe koni maná yibii kpakpai?

english: While cassava can survive in poor soil, giving it a balanced fertilizer rich in potassium helps it yield bigger tubers while keeping your soil from becoming completely worn out.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ moŋ, shi kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei ni sa ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ ha lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ bulbs wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ kwraa.

english: If I leave harvested cassava leaves and stems to rot on my field, will it return nutrients to my soil?
ga: Kɛji oshi ŋmei baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni akpa lɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani ebaaku sɛɛ ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, leaving healthy cassava leaves and green stems on the soil to decompose puts organic matter and nutrients back into the topsoil. Just make sure not to leave stems that show signs of disease.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi ŋmei baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛfite lɛ, ebaaha nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ yiteŋ. Kwɛmɔ pɛ akɛ okashi tso lɛ yibii ni tsɔɔ hela he okadii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea will help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Covering the soil with organic matter, called mulching, keeps the ground cool under the hot Ghanaian sun, holds moisture in the soil longer, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli woɔ mli lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ yɛ Ghana hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes in the exact same spot where I harvested tomatoes last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ he ni mifo yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot allows crop-specific pests and soil diseases to build up. Rotating with a different crop, like beans or maize, breaks disease cycles and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ tso pɔtɛɛ ko mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai aba. Nibii ni aduɔ ni tsakeɔ amɛhe, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. Enɛ haa helai lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo.

english: My tomato plants are flowering well, but why are the flowers falling off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ miikwɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shi mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers often drop off during extreme heat or when plants experience sudden dry spells. Ensuring regular watering at the base of the plant during hot weather helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo be trukaa. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ shishi daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why does a plantain stem die after giving me only one bunch of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tso lɛ gbo beni ekɛ aduawai akuu kome pɛ ha mi lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is naturally designed to flower and bear fruit only once in its lifetime. After harvest, that stem dies, but it passes its nutrients to the new shoots (suckers) growing at its base to produce the next crop.
ga: Afee plantain tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli. kpamɔ sɛɛ Nakai tso lɛ baagbo. Mohu ɔ, e ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ yaa tso ehehi (tso) nɛ ngɛ wae ngɛ sisi ɔ mi konɛ e ya nɔ nɛ e wo ngmɔ ɔ.

english: How come my cassava roots are rotting underground before I even dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mifolɔ amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long, usually during heavy rains in poorly drained land. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds helps water drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Bei pii lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ hei ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ Dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough resources to form big, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmei agbo ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and give sticks to my yam plants for them to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni maha mi sweet potato tsei lɛ aniji koni amɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for the growing tuber under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves into the sunlight and away from damp soil pests, while clearing weeds removes competition for food.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ ashɛ hulu la he ni ekɛ ehe akabɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii he akaŋshii kɛyaa lɛ,.

english: Why do my small cocoa trees die when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii ni Mine lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain beside young cocoa protects them from heat until they grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he ni amɛdara waa.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the plant's juices and spreading leaf viruses. Spraying early with neem water or recommended pest control keeps these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Neem nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Aloo, tsofa ni akɛbuɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe ŋaa lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akabote mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I clear all the large forest trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie koo mli tsei wuji kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants naturally thrive under a forest canopy. Without shade trees, strong direct sunlight scorches their delicate leaves and dries out the topsoil, causing the young cocoa to suffer severe heat stress, turn yellow, and wither.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ koo lɛ shishi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ Hewalɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kookoo bibii lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbo

english: Why does crop yield drop so quickly after just two years of farming on newly cleared forest soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ ba shi oya yɛ afii enyɔ pɛ ni akɛtsu nii yɛ koo mli shikpɔŋ hee ni agbele naa lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Forest soil is rich initially because falling leaves constantly decay into natural fertilizer. Once all trees are removed, heavy rains wash away the topsoil nutrients and hot sunshine breaks down organic matter, causing soil fertility to drop rapidly without added compost or fertilizer.
ga: Koo mli shikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shishijee mli ejaakɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ be fɛɛ be ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Beni ajie tsei lɛ fɛɛ lɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baafite nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ baa shi oya ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like drinking straws during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi ni anuɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves on hot afternoons as a defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, trapping air and moisture inside to prevent excessive water loss during dry heat.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Tsɔɔmɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli koni nu akafite fe nine yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do the roots on my cassava plants start rotting in the ground if heavy rain falls right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require oxygen in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the land, water fills all the soil air pockets, suffocating the roots and creating perfect conditions for soil fungi to attack and rot the crop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atutua ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why does my main plantain stem produce smaller bunches of fruit if I leave too many suckers growing around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso titri lɛ woɔ aduawai bibii kɛji miŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: All plantain suckers attached to the main plant share the same root system. Leaving too many suckers forces them to compete for available water and soil nutrients, stealing food away from the main stem and reducing fruit bunch size.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ fɛɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ tso titri lɛ he lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shishifã kome. Kɛ́ amɛshwie ŋmeii babaoo amɛshwie shi lɛ, ebaanyɛ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛtsɔ niyenii ni ajuɔ kɛjɛɔ tsɔne wulu lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ aduawai akuu lɛ dalɛ aba shi

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce a lot of green leaves but very few pods when I apply excess fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli fe nine lɛ?

english: High-nitrogen fertilizers encourage plants to focus entirely on leaf and stem growth. When cowpeas receive too much nitrogen, the plant stays in a vegetative state instead of shifting its energy into flowering and forming seed pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ fɛɛ maa baa kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ cowpea nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baakã he ahi e-vegetative shihilɛ lɛ mli. Mohu ɔ, a jeɔ he wami ɔ kɛ yaa fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwuhi nɛ a peeɔ ɔ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when air temperatures become too high, which prevents proper pollination. When heat damages the pollen, the flower cannot form a fruit and drops off naturally.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa lɛ naa. Beni latsaa fiteɔ pollen lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do groundnut flowers bend down and push small stalks into the dirt after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ? kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Groundnuts have a unique way of growing where flowers are pollinated above ground, but the developing seed pods—called 'pegs'—must push themselves into the soil to safely grow into mature peanuts underground.
ga: Peanuts yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko ni etsɔɔ nɔ edaa kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Shi esa akɛ dumɔwui akutsei ni miiya hiɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ lɛ ashɛre amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara shweshweeshwe ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni eda yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my yam vines yield much smaller tubers if I do not supply tall wooden stakes for them to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ bulbs bibii kwraa kɛji akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni amɛkɛkwɔ lɛ haaa amɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight so their leaves can manufacture food efficiently. Without stakes, the leaves bunch up on the ground and shade each other, drastically cutting down the energy sent underground to grow big tubers.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ tso bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ baabua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛbaafee amɛhe shade. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni akɛmajeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni akɛkwɛ bulb agboi lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why do the leaves on my hot pepper plants curl upward and look wrinkled like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi chili tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni efee tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Upward leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites feeding on leaf juices under the leaf, or by a viral infection spread by whiteflies that messes with normal leaf development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa lɛ mli.

english: How do legumes like beans and cowpeas actually help improve the soil on my farm?
ga: Te ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes have microscopic organisms on their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into food for the plant. When the crop season ends, those roots decay and leave nitrogen rich organic matter behind, naturally fertilizing the ground for your next crop.
ga: Legumes yɛ nibii bibii ni anaa yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa efeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tsei Kɛ́ dumɔ be lɛ ba naagbee Nakai shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛshiɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Koni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants are starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Heavy rains can wash nutrients down deep into the earth where plant roots cannot reach them, so you may need to add organic manure or compost to feed the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ekolɛ ehe baahia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Are locally grown seed varieties better for planting in Ghana than imported seeds?
ga: Ani dumɔwui srɔtoi ni aduɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ hi kɛha dumɔwui yɛ Ghana fe dumɔwui ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ baa lɛ?

english: Local seeds are naturally adapted to Ghana's high heat, native pests, and rainfall patterns over many generations. Imported seeds might promise high yields under perfect conditions, but local seeds usually perform more reliably under unpredictable weather.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ Ghana adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ gbɛjianɔtoi kɛha yinɔi babaoo. Dumɔwui ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo yɛ shihilɛi ni yeɔ emuu shishi. Shi maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ fɔɔ yibiiwoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ babaoo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni bɛ faŋŋ shishi.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme hot days, dry soil, or heavy pest attacks. Keeping the roots moist with grass mulch and watering regularly helps the plant retain its blossoms and produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ haomɔ mli, tamɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni naa wa waa lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ha shishifãi lɛ mli fũu, ni akɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do people recommend planting cowpeas in between my rows of cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina ŋmeii yɛ mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas grow quickly along the ground, acting as a green carpet that shades the earth. This blocks weeds from taking over and keeps the moisture in the soil, while the cowpeas feed nitrogen to the cassava roots.
ga: Cowpeas kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kapɛti eŋɔli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ baatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni cowpea kɛ nitrogen haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge bushy leaves but thin, woody roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen or are planted too close together, they spend all their energy growing leaves upward to reach sunlight instead of sending energy down into the roots to build thick tubers.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛdaraa amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛná hulu la. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ he wami kɛ yaa sisi ɔ mi konɛ e pee bulb nɛ mi wa.

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water sits too long around the roots without draining away properly. Building raised mounds or ridges lets water drain freely and keeps the soil loose so tubers can grow healthy and dry.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni enyɛɛɛ efo mli jogbaŋŋ. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ agbɔjɔ Koni ŋmeii lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛgbi.

english: How does heavy rainfall right after flowering affect my vegetable crops?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa beni fɔfɔi ewo lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ saa mitsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rain can physically knock delicate blossoms off the branches and wash away the pollen needed to form fruits. It can also swamp the roots with excess water, causing young vegetables to split or drop off.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbee shi kɛjɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ ni ekɛ pollen ni he hiaa koni efee aduawai lɛ aya. Ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ hu atsɔ nu babaoo nɔ. Ehaa aduawai bibii lɛ fãa loo amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why are my nursery seeds taking so many weeks to sprout out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ otsii babaoo dani amɛjeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need warm temperature and constant moisture to wake up. If they are buried too deep in hard soil or if the nursery bed dries out under the sun, the seed shell remains locked and germination slows down.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be koni amɛte shi. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa mli tsɔ loo ŋmɔ mli saatso lɛ gĩ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Dumɔwui lɛ ahe tsɔne lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni amɛkwɛ̃mɔ baafee blɛoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my bean crop curling up and feeling sticky to the touch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni minuɔ he akɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ he kɛji mita he lɛ?

english: Curled, sticky leaves are caused by tiny insects called aphids that suck the sweet sap from under the leaves. They leave behind a sticky liquid that attracts mold, which can be stopped by spraying a mild soapy water solution or neem oil.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ aphids ni nuɔ wuo nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baa. Amɛshiɔ nu ni mli tse ni gbalaa ŋmeii kɛbaa amɛsɛɛ. Abaanyɛ akpa enɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni mli ejɔ loo neem fɔ ni akɛbaashwie nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better for me to start planting on a small piece of land first before expanding to many acres?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaaje shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ dani agbɛ ashwã kɛyashɛ acre babaoo nɔ?

english: Starting on a small plot allows you to learn how the crop behaves, manage weeds and pests easily, and protect your money. Once you see good results on a small scale, you can expand safely using the knowledge you gained.
ga: Shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ shishijee Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okaseɔ bɔ ni tsei feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa. Kwɛmɔ jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ mlɛo ni obu oshika he Kɛji ona yibii kpakpai yɛ gbɛ bibioo nɔ Obaanyɛ okɛ nilee ni oná lɛ atsu nii ni okɛgbala onilee mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings dying when I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily in direct sunshine. Leaving big trees or planting shade crops like plantains creates a cool umbrella over them until they grow strong enough to handle full heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ aba amɛnɔ kɛyashi tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulutsoo be lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch sunlight, which feeds the growing yam underground. Climbing also keeps the leaves dry and away from soil diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe. ni ji ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii Tsei ni kwɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ agbiɔ ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ akashɛ amɛhe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build green leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help them turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves in hot sun to hide from the heat and keep water from escaping. If they bounce back when the sun goes down or after watering, the plant is just protecting itself.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛtee amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ he ni nu akaje mli. Kɛji amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi loo beni afɔ amɛ nu sɛɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibu ehe.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall with thick green leaves but produce very few flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen food or shade, they spend all their energy growing tall leaves instead of making fruits. Sunlight and balanced soil food encourage the plant to produce flowers and fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aha tsei niyenii loo akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo amɛhe shade mli lɛ Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ baai kakadaji moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii. Hulu la ni ja kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: How can I tell if my soil is rich enough for planting without buying test equipment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse bɔ ni sa kɛha okwaayeli ni miheee nibii ni akɛkaa nii lɛ?

english: Good, fertile soil is usually dark brown or black, soft to dig, holds moisture well after rain, and has earthworms crawling inside it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni hi ni baa nii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ, ni efomɔ waaa, ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii miiho yɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than the crop seeds I planted in the same soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe dumɔwui ni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are natural to the area, so they are stronger at fighting for food, water, and sunlight. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing food from your farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe wa yɛ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la he tawuu mli, ni ejieɔ amɛ mra. Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: Why should I remove some of the young suckers growing around my main plantain shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi plantain tsei titri lɛ.

english: If too many suckers grow around one stem, they all fight for the same water and soil food. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures your main stem produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii hu. Kɛ́ oshi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha otso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are ready to harvest since they grow under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava shows it is mature when its lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack open from the tubers swelling beneath.
ga: Yucca jieɔ dalɛ kpo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ bulb ni efuu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout if I plant them in dry soil before the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need moisture to awaken from dormancy. When planted in dry soil, seeds sit helpless and dry out, or insects and birds eat them before rain falls to start germination.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛte shi kɛjɛ wɔɔhe. Kɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ taraa shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee nɔ ko ni amɛgbi. Aloo kooloi bibii kɛ okpoi baaye lɛ dani nugbɔ anɛ koni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How should I store my harvested corn seeds so they do not spoil before the next planting season?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato koni ekafite dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ aba?

english: Seeds must be dried until they are very hard and stored in sealed, dry containers or airtight bags, often mixed with clean wood ash, to keep mold and weevils from destroying them.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ aahu kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa ni akɛto tsɛnsi ni egbi loo kotoku ko ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ mli lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, akɛ tso sũ ni he tse futuɔ enɛ. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akafite amɛ.

english: A nursery bed acts like a protected shelter, allowing delicate young seedlings to grow strong roots safely away from harsh direct sun, pests, and heavy rains before facing the open farm.
ga: Gbekɛbii akwɛmɔ saatso lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ko ni abuɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui bibii ni amɛdaraa shishifãi ni wa shweshweeshwe. Ekɛ hulu ni naa wa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ dani ekɛ ŋmɔ ko ni agbele naa lɛ kpeɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings look weak and droopy right after I move them into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo saatso wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Moving plants causes transplant shock because tiny root hairs get damaged. Transplanting late in the afternoon and watering immediately helps them recover until roots settle into the new soil.
ga: Tso lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ahewɔ lɛ haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli. damaged Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shwane mli ni awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhe waa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants turn yellow and die when water sits on my farm after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu shwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Too much standing water drowns crop roots by blocking air. Without oxygen, roots rot and cannot absorb nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ haa tsei shishifãi shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ hewɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why does water sit on top of my clay soil like a small pond instead of sinking down to the roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu kpɛtɛɔ mi shikpɔŋ lɛ he tamɔ ŋshɔ bibioo ko lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefo kɛyashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Clay soil has extremely tiny particles packed tightly together that block water movement. Adding organic compost breaks up clay so water can sink down to where roots need it.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nibii bibii waa ni akɛwo amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛtsi nu lɛ gbɛfaa naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, egbaa shikpɔŋ sũ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni nu lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he ni ehe hiaa ni eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Why does rice grow well in flooded lowlands while other crops rot underwater?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu afua hei yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fiteɔ yɛ nu shishi lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air tubes that carry oxygen from their leaves down to their underwater roots, allowing them to survive submerged while competing weeds drown.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ nu shishi yɛ be mli ni jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa trees burn and turn brown during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under strong heat and dry winds because dry soil prevents roots from supplying enough water to cool the leaves down.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaha nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha baai lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow huge leafy tops but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ baai shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer causes them to spend all their energy growing tall green leaves instead of storing food in the underground roots.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛ baai ni kɛlɛ ni eŋɔli lɛ akwɛ̃. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: When planted too close, crops compete fiercely for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, forcing them to stretch upward for light instead of growing thick stems and large fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Nibii ni adu lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwereɔ koni amɛná la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why are my crops drying up even during months when it usually rains in my district?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ nyɔji ni bei pii lɛ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ po mli lɛ?

english: Rainfall patterns across districts have shifted due to environmental changes, causing rains to come late or stop early. When crops do not get steady water during critical growth stages, their roots cannot absorb soil nutrients, causing them to wither.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ miitsake yɛ shihilɛ mli tsakemɔi ahewɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ blɛoo loo ekpaa oya. Kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso lɛ ni egboɔ.

english: What will happen to my maize seeds if it rains just once and then stays dry for weeks?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ shikome pɛ ni ehi shi otsii babaoo?

english: A single rain can trigger seeds to germinate, but without follow-up water, the delicate young roots dry out and die under the soil. It is safer to wait until the rain becomes regular before planting.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃. Shi kɛji nu ko bɛ ni nyiɛɔ Young sɛɛ lɛ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baanɛ dani odu.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out much faster nowadays than it used to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho oya fe bɔ ni eji yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Loss of trees and vegetative cover leaves soil bare and directly exposed to sunlight and wind, causing water to evaporate rapidly. Without natural cover or organic matter, soil loses its natural ability to hold water.
ga: Tsei kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni elaaje lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya Kɛji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko bɛ ni haa nɔ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu lɛ.

english: How can I keep my farm soil moist when nearby streams and water sources are drying up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni faai kɛ nu jɛɛhei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ miiho lɛ?

english: Covering your soil with dry grass, leaves, or crop residue (mulching) acts like a protective blanket. It shields the ground from direct sun, keeping the soil cool and trapping moisture around your crop roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: How does keeping trees around rivers and streams near my farm help my crops?
ga: Tsei ni ebɔle mihe lɛ akwɛmɔ Te faai kɛ faai ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Trees protect water bodies from drying out under the sun and help keep the underground water table high. This maintains moisture in nearby soil, ensuring your crops have water access during dry spells.
ga: Tsei buɔ nu jɛɛhei ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Kwɛmɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Should I start planting my crops immediately if it rains unexpectedly during the dry season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ trukaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: No, sudden off-season rains are usually temporary and do not mark the real start of the rainy season. Planting right away risks losing your seeds when dry weather returns high temperatures.
ga: Dabi, bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ ji be kukuoo mli nɔ, ni jeee nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee diɛŋtsɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni baafite lɛ woɔ oshara mli kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ha hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops look stressed or diseased when rain falls at unusual times of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhao loo hela emɔ amɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli bei ni jeee nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Unusual rain brings sudden humidity and temperature changes that can promote fungal growth and disrupt a crop's natural flowering or fruiting schedule, causing stress to the plant.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ kɛ hulutsoo kɛ dɔlɛ tsakemɔi baa trukaa. ni baanyɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ ada ni efite tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔfɔii loo yibiiwoo be lɛ. Ekɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ

english: What kind of crops should I choose to plant if the rainy season in my area is getting shorter?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ mahala kɛji akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba shi yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: You should plant fast-maturing or drought-tolerant crop varieties. These crops are bred to complete their growth cycle quickly so you can harvest a good yield before the rains stop early.
ga: Esa akɛ odu tsei ni daa oya loo ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. Afɔ tsei nɛɛ koni amɛgbe amɛdalɛ be lɛ naa oya. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oná kpamɔ kpakpa dani nugbɔ lɛ akpa mra.

english: How does planting shade trees alongside my main crops protect them from harsh weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ ahe?

english: Trees act as windbreaks and living umbrellas, lowering temperatures around your crops, reducing water evaporation from their leaves, and preventing soil erosion during heavy storms.
ga: Tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsimɔ kɛ hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa nu ni jɛɔ baai amli lɛ baa shi. ni etsi shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ahum ni naa wa be mli lɛ naa.

english: Why are extension officers asking us to adopt new farming methods instead of continuing our traditional practices?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ biɔ ni wɔya nɔ wɔkɛ okwaayeli gbɛi heei atsu nii yɛ wɔtsutsu nifeemɔi lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Because weather conditions, rainfall timing, and water resources have changed significantly, old planting calendars often fail. New techniques are designed to protect soil moisture and help your crops survive current climate challenges.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, nugbɔnɛmɔ bei, kɛ nu nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ etsake kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, kusum naa dumɔwui akalandai lɛ tsuuu nii. Afee ŋaai heei ni baabu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he ni eye ebua onibii ni oduɔ nii lɛ koni amɛye ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe naagbai lɛ anɔ kunim.

english: Why do I need to break up the hard dirt and make the soil soft before putting my new seedlings into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa mli ni mifeɔ lɛ blɛoo dani mikɛ dumɔwui heei woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soft soil allows young, fragile roots to spread easily, breathe, and drink water. If the soil is too hard, the new roots cannot grow deep into the ground, and the plant will dry out or remain small.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ lɛ haa shishifãi bibii ni waaa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa, amɛmuɔ, ni amɛnuɔ nu. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ Shishifãi heei nyɛŋ ada kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. kɛji tso lɛ egbi loo eji bibioo lolo

english: Why does placing dry grass around the bottom of my young crops keep them healthier during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, works like a blanket. It stops the sun from drying out the soil too fast, keeps the roots cool, and turns into plant food as it rots.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Ehaa hulu lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ebafeɔ tso niyenii kɛji egbo

english: Why should I remove extra suckers from my plantain plant instead of letting all of them grow together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie plantain tso ko mli ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛ fɛɛ amɛfee ekome kɛkwɛ̃?

english: When too many suckers grow from one plantain stem, they fight over the same water and nutrients in the soil. Removing the extra shoots allows the remaining plant to produce a bigger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu kome mli. Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: How do I choose the best sucker from a healthy plant to move and replant in a new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala suckers ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli koni mikɛfã ni mikɛwo saatso hee nɔ ekoŋŋ?

english: Look for a sucker that has a strong, thick base shaped like a sword leaf, with firm roots already starting to show. Avoid soft, pale, or leafy shoots because they take longer to adjust and are prone to dying after being moved.
ga: Taomɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shishitoo ni mli wa ni mli wa. Ehe tamɔ klante ŋmei ni ebɔi shishifãi ni wa namɔ Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii bibii, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ahe ejaakɛ amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ he kroko.

english: Why is it good practice to cut off old or yellow leaves from the bottom of my vegetable plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni egbɔ loo ni miifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ kɛjɛ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Removing weak or dying leaves stops the plant from wasting energy on parts that no longer help it grow. It also allows fresh air to blow through the crop, preventing moisture build-up that causes diseases.
ga: Kɛtsɔ baai ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni miigboi lɛ ni ejieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ efiteee hewalɛ yɛ hei ni eyeee ebuaaa tso lɛ ni edara dɔŋŋ lɛ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu tsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni buaa ehe naa ni kɛ hela baa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my young crop shoots look droopy and tired right after I move them into a new field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi ni etɔ amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ hee mli lɛ?

english: This is called transplant shock. Moving a plant disturbs its small roots, so it temporarily loses water faster than it can take it in. Giving it shade and water right away helps it recover within a few days.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Tso lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ gbaa eshishifãi bibii lɛ anaa, no hewɔ lɛ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ nu lɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Kɛ́ aná hulutsoo kɛ nu oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die if I plant them in a field without any shade plants around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo bɛ amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot survive strong, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains beside them shields the leaves from burning and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings sprout better when I insert them slanting into the soft ground instead of flat on top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛwo nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pushing the cassava cutting into soft soil holds it firmly so roots can grow straight down into the earth for food, while the buds stay above ground to sprout strong shoots.
ga: Kɛ́ ashɛɔ ŋmei shishifã lɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ shi shiŋŋ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ adara tɛ̃ɛ kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛye nii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii ni he wa akwɛ̃ kɛje kpo.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin with tiny stems when I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe tse ni amɛshishifãi bibii yɔɔ lɛ? Akɛni midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ hewɔ lɛ

english: When plants are crowded, they stretch upward to steal sunlight from one another. Giving each plant enough space ensures they get plenty of sun and grow thick, sturdy stems that can carry heavy yields.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la ni jɛ amɛhe lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa enáa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa, ni eyɛ tso ni mli tse ni mli wa ni baanyɛ awo ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves of my crop turn towards the sun during the early morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ?

english: Leaves act like tiny solar panels that catch sunlight to make food for the plant. Turning toward the light helps the plant gather maximum energy to grow healthy and strong.
ga: Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo be mli tsɔnei bibii. ni nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha tsei La lɛ ni akɛtsɔɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni eda ni ená hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains beside them creates a cool canopy that protects the young leaves from burning and keeps moisture in the soil until the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa.

english: How does spreading dry grass on the ground around my crop stems help them during hot periods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass, or mulching, acts like a blanket over the dirt. It blocks the scorching sun from evaporating soil water, keeps the roots cool, and slowly decays to feed the soil.
ga: Hay loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baatsu nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsĩɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my green maize plants start turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize plant are usually a sign that the crop has run out of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food maize needs to stay green and build big ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ efo. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ toi wuji aba.

english: Why do my vegetable crops stay thin and produce tiny harvests when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and plant food in the dirt. Giving crops proper space ensures every single plant gets enough energy to grow strong and fruit well.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni eda ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden poles in the dirt for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves up into the air and sunshine. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, allowing the plant to catch maximum light to feed the tubers growing under the soil.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ewo ebaa lɛ nɔ kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la mli. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ naa la babaoo ni ekɛhaa bulb ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii.

english: How can I tell which end of a cassava stick should face upwards when I am planting it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei naagbee ni esa akɛ ekwɛ hiɛ beni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Look closely at the tiny bumps or 'eyes' where old leaves used to grow on the stem stick. Those small buds must always point upwards toward the sky so the leaves can sprout easily out of the soil.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii, loo ‘ŋmei’, he ni be ko ni eho lɛ baai momoi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ehe miihia ni akɛ nakai ŋmeii bibii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi koni baai lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: Why should I wait to plant my seeds instead of sowing right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimɛɔ koni madu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a hot, dry spell before the real rainy season sets in. If you plant too early, the hot soil will dry out and kill your newly sprouted seeds before the next rain falls.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbeɔ dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa.

english: What is eating small holes in the middle whorl of my young maize leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day and chews tender new leaves before the crop can produce ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni amɛyeɔ baai heei dani tso lɛ baanyɛ afee toi.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants without turning into any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the air gets too hot or when the plant experiences sudden water stress. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ trukaa. Kɛji haomɔ ba lɛ Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why do wild weeds seem to grow so much faster and healthier than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally wild and tough plants with deep roots that steal water and nutrients out of the ground much faster than farm crops. Clearing them early gives your crops a fair chance to feed and grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛye niyenii ni amɛdara.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide essential shade and moisture to keep cocoa saplings alive during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa koni kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves toward sunlight to make energy for growing heavy tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, which prevents leaf diseases and helps the tubers grow bigger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɛya hulu la lɛ he koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha bulbs ni tsii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ baa helai anaa ni eye ebua ni eha bulb lɛ afee wuji.

english: Cassava plants naturally shed their leaves during dry spells to save water and protect themselves from heat. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eda bɔ ni sa.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when the weather gets too hot or when the soil dries out completely. Keeping the soil constantly moist around the base helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni aaafee Kɛ́ shishigbɛ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi ni tsɔɔ tomato lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize leaves have small holes and look chewed from the inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni okwɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed inside the center of young maize plants. Treating the crop early with recommended neem extracts or bio-pesticides protects the growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsei akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Kɛtsɔ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebuɔ baai ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are often caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking the plant juices. Spraying the leaves early with gentle pest treatments keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ blɛoo lɛ, baai lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches when too many shoots grow around the main trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni ŋmeii ni miida yɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ fa babaoo lɛ

english: When too many suckers grow at the base, they steal water and nutrients from the main tree. Removing extra suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures the main tree produces a large bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are ready to harvest since they grow under the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ be mli ni adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves yellow and drop, and small cracks appear in the soil near the base where the roots are expanding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ edara kwraa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ fee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ Ejeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ miigbɛ amɛshwã lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to burn weeds and old stems on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mashã jwɛi kɛ tsei momo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable natural nutrients and beneficial soil insects that help crops grow. Leaving cleared grass to decompose naturally builds up the soil and helps it hold onto rainwater longer.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni jara wa kɛ sũ mli kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Jwɛi ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni efiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni etswaa shikpɔŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why should I wait for the soil to become wet before planting my maize seeds instead of sowing in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting in hot, dry soil can damage or dry out seeds before they get a chance to sprout. Waiting for the initial heavy rains ensures the soil stays damp enough for all seeds to sprout evenly.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ baanyɛ afite loo egbi dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni ooomɛ yɛ shishijee mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ akwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why should I leave dry leaves and clear weeds around the base of my crops instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi baai ni egboi ni majie jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ he moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ?

english: Covering the soil around plants with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool and traps water in the soil during hot days. It also stops weeds from taking over and breaks down into natural plant food over time.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi haa tsei lɛ ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni jwɛi lɛ akaye nɔ ni amɛgbala amɛfee adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do I know if the soil has enough water to start planting my maize when the rain begins?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: You can dig down a few inches into your field and squeeze a handful of soil. If it forms a loose ball that holds its shape without dripping excess water, the soil is moist enough for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli inchi fioo komɛi atsu nii ni okɛ sũ ko awo mli. Kɛji akɛ efee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni hiɛɔ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni ekɛ nu shwieee shi fe nine lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa creates living umbrellas that protect them from harsh sun and keep the soil humid.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ Cocoa tso lɛ masɛi lɛ haa shade ni buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or too much leafy growth from excessive nitrogen. Keeping the soil consistently moist and balanced helps flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo baa ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ nitrogen babaoo mli baa lɛ yɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for leafy green growth. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai eŋɔli lɛ daa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ amɛshishifãi ni wa.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer to my crop after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli beni midu nii sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer is best applied a few weeks after seeds sprout and roots have formed, while the soil is moist from recent rain. Applying it to dry soil or too close to young stems can burn the roots and waste the fertilizer.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli otsii 2-3 sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni shishifãi lɛ etsɔ hiɛ lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ loo ni bɛŋkɛ tso bibioo lɛ he tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What is eating small holes inside the top leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are often caused by fall armyworm caterpillars hiding in the plant stem. Inspecting plants early and applying safe insecticides or recommended natural traps into the central shoot can protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbee shi ni amɛtee amɛhe amɛwo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo adebɔɔ mli tsɔnei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: How can I prevent my cassava roots from rotting underground before harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water builds up around them in heavy clay soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu ni ekã shi ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ Shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Is it good to plant beans on the same farm alongside my maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize helps the soil because leguminous crops like beans draw nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow better without competing heavily.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni akaŋshii ni mli wa bɛ mli.

english: Should I remove some of the young suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ. Ani ajie plantain tsei titrii lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving too many suckers causes them to fight for food and water with the main plant, resulting in small bunches. Pruning extra suckers to leave only two or three strong stems ensures larger and healthier plantain bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo ni agbele mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Kɛ́ atsake tsei lɛ ahe koni ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why are small green worms eating the inside of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a major pest in Ghana that attacks young corn. They crawl into the center funnel of the plant to feed on tender leaves, which can severely ruin your yield if not treated early with recommended organic or chemical insecticides.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ Ghana ni tutuaa ŋmãa bibii lɛ. Amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii. Enɛ baanyɛ afite onibii lɛ waa kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra. kɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ he ŋaa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to leave some big shade trees on my cocoa farm instead of clearing them all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ moŋ fe ni mafo amɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally grow under larger forest trees. Keeping some tall shade trees protects young cocoa from harsh sunlight and drying winds, keeps the soil moist, and drops leaves that decay into natural manure for your crops.
ga: Cocoa tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ashishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo be ha kookoo tso lɛ, ebaabu ehe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa baai ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava turning yellow and falling off before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, or the plant is suffering from dry weather. Nitrogen helps leaves stay green and produce food, so adding well-rotted animal manure or compost can strengthen your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ tso lɛ miina shihilɛi ni mli egbi. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ ewaje oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak stalks with small or missing cobs instead of strong, healthy plants.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ni elaaje, yɛ tsei ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, while leguminous crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth. Rotating your crops this way keeps the soil fertile naturally without relying only on expensive fertilizers.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ nɛkɛ gbɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa pɛ anɔ.

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny whitefly insects. The best cure is prevention: always obtain disease-free stems from certified agricultural officers for your new farm.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ woɔ amɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni atsĩ naa: be fɛɛ be lɛ, ná tsei ni hela bɛ mli lɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ dɛŋ kɛha oŋmɔ hee lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to water my tomato plants early in the morning or late in the evening?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ?

english: Early morning is best because the soil absorbs the moisture before the sun gets too hot, allowing roots to drink throughout the day. Watering late at night leaves wet moisture on the leaves, which can attract harmful fungal diseases.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ mli dɔɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ nɔ ni anuɔ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli gbɛkɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi baai lɛ anɔ. ni baanyɛ agbala tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ kɛba.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my main crops after a fresh rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ hee sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, aggressive plants that are naturally adapted to grab water and nutrients faster than farm crops. Removing weeds within the first few weeks after planting gives your main crops a head start so they do not get choked out.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ basabasa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii amli oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha otso titri lɛ aná yitso bɔni afee ni ekɛ ehe akawo mli.

english: Why is my stored maize developing dark mold and turning black inside the bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikɛto lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ diŋ ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grains develop mold when they are bagged before they are completely dry. Moisture trapped inside the bag allows fungi to grow, which ruins the grain and makes it unsafe to eat; always dry your corn thoroughly on clean tarpaulins before bagging.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmaa baaná ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli dani amɛgbi kwraa. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ aya hiɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni ehaaa efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ ayeɔ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ha o-corn lɛ agbi kwraa yɛ tarp ni he tse nɔ dani okɛwo kotoku mli.

english: Why should I trim off the lowest branches of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishi fe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Removing the lowest leaves prevents heavy rain from splashing soil and fungal spores onto the leaves. It also improves air circulation around the base of the plant, helping it direct more energy into growing larger, healthier fruit.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmeii amli tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ yɛ baa lɛ nɔ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ hu yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa anyɛɔ atsuɔ hewalɛ babaoo he nii koni akɛwo aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why can't I just plant vegetable seeds like broccoli directly in my main farm field instead of starting them in a nursery first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu aduawai dumɔwui tamɔ brokoli yɛ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ.

english: Vegetable seeds are very small and fragile. Starting them in a nursery bed protects them from heavy rains, hot sun, and insect pests while they are young, giving them a much higher chance of surviving before you move them to the farm.
ga: Aduawai dumɔwui lɛ daraaa kwraa ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛ́ oje amɛ shishi yɛ gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe lɛ, ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛnáa hegbɛ babaoo ni amɛhiɔ shi dani okɛ amɛ yaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some farmers prefer buying pre-raised seedlings from specialized nursery operators instead of raising their own?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi sumɔɔ ni amɛhe dumɔwui ni akwɛ̃ momo lɛ kɛjɛ mɛi ni he esa waa ni kwɛɔ amɛ lɛ adɛŋ moŋ fe ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛaatsɔse amɛ lɛ?

english: Raising delicate seedlings takes special care, proper shading, and constant watering. Buying ready-to-plant seedlings saves you time and reduces the risk of losing young plants to disease or poor germination before field planting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akwɛmɔ biɔ hiɛdɔɔ krɛdɛɛ ko. shading ni sa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa daa Dumɔwui ni asaa he ni abaadu lɛ ahemɔ haa be baa shi, ni ehaa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ helai loo amɛkwɛ̃mɔ ni ehiii baaha tsei bibii lɛ baafite dani adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do officers advise us to expose our nursery seedlings to direct sunlight a few days before transplanting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔshi dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ hulu la mli gbii fioo komɛi dani wɔdu wɔ yɛ he kroko lɛ?

english: This process is called 'hardening off.' Gradually giving seedlings more sunlight and less water toughens their stems so they don't get scorched or weak when moved to the open field.
ga: Atsɛɔ gbɛ nɛɛ akɛ ‘Harding off’ Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ hulu la babaoo kɛ nu fioo lɛ, ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni ekashã loo egbɔjɔ kɛ́ adu kɛtee ŋmɔ mli.

english: How do I uproot young seedlings from my nursery bed without destroying their roots when I am ready to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie tsei bibii kɛjɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ ni mifiteee amɛshishifãi lɛ beni mifee klalo akɛ madu amɛ lɛ?

english: Water the nursery bed thoroughly a few hours before uprooting so the soil becomes soft. Gently lift the plant together with a small ball of wet soil around its roots instead of pulling it out forcefully by the stem.
ga: Okɛ nu awo ŋmɔ mli saatso lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi dani ojie koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo. Okɛ tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ bibioo ko ni efɔ lɛ nɔ blɛoo. shishifãi lɛ ahe moŋ fe ni okɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ baagbala amɛ waa

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt and look almost dead immediately after I transplant them into the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshwɛ fioo ni amɛbaagboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: This is known as transplant shock, which happens when roots are disturbed and cannot pull in water quickly under hot sun. Transplanting late in the evening and watering immediately helps young plants recover overnight.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ gbala ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbala nu oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ gbɛkɛ ni awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhe waa nyɔɔŋ kome mli.

english: What is the best soil preparation I should do before moving my nursery crops into the main field?
ga: Mɛni ji shikpɔŋ he saamɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafee dani mikɛ tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ aya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Clear all weeds, loosen the soil deeply so roots can push through easily, and mix in decomposed manure or compost to feed the young roots as soon as they are planted.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ ohe. Gbalamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ abote mli mlɛo. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo lɛ afutu mli koni shishifãi lɛ afee blɛoo kɛji adu amɛ pɛ.

english: Why is it important to spread out my seedlings with proper spacing instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni magbɛ midumɔwui lɛ ashwã he ko ni sa lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ

english: Spreading out your plants ensures each crop gets enough space, sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Planting too close forces crops to fight each other, resulting in thin stems and small harvests.
ga: Tsei ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa, hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe awuu. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni akpaaa nii babaoo.

english: What will happen if I scatter my seeds across the bed and do not thin them out when they sprout?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji migbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã saatso lɛ nɔ ni mikɛfeee amɛ mlɛo tsɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: If you leave crowded seedlings without thinning or spreading them, they will grow tall and weak because of competition, making them weak and prone to falling over or carrying diseases.
ga: Kɛji oshi dumɔwui lɛ ni adu shi shiŋŋ ni okɛ amɛ shwieee shi loo ogbɛɛɛ amɛshwãaa lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baafee mɛi ni kwɔlɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ akaŋshii hewɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji bɔjɔmɔ kɛ oshara ni ji shigbeemɔ loo hela.

english: I want to grow broccoli on my farm in Ghana, but how does this crop react to hot weather?
ga: Miisumɔ ni madu brokoli yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli. Shi te tso nɛɛ feɔ enii ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ mli edɔ waa?
