english: Broccoli prefers cooler temperatures. In very high heat, it can flower too early or form small, loose heads that taste bitter, so it grows best during cooler months or under light shade with plenty of moisture.
ga: Broccoli sumɔɔ he ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli Ebaanyɛ efɔ oya tsɔ loo ehiɛ yitso bibioo, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni mli edɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, edaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nyɔji ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli loo yɛ hulutsoo be ni hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ shishi.

english: How can I tell if an exotic vegetable crop like broccoli is suitable for the climate and soil in my region?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofa ko ni yɔɔ srɔto, tamɔ broccoli lɛ sa kɛha mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Exotic vegetables need well-draining soil, reliable water, and heat-tolerant seed varieties. You can check with your agricultural extension officer or test a small bed before planting a large field.
ga: Aduawai ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ dɔlɛ mli Obaanyɛ okɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ akwɛ loo oka saatsoi bibii okwɛ dani odu yɛ shikpɔji wuji anɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate full, harsh sunlight and can easily dry out or burn. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that create a natural protective umbrella, giving the young cocoa the shade and humidity it needs to establish its roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. ni ebaanyɛ egbi loo eshã oya Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ mɔ he. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni ená shishifãi.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away nitrogen—the main nutrient plants need for green growth—from the top layer of soil. Without enough nitrogen, maize plants cannot produce green chlorophyll, causing their leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara lɛ, kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, Abɛi tsei nyɛŋ afee klorofil ni ji eŋɔli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay tiny even when the plants grow very tall and full of leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ miida ni eyi obɔ kɛ baai moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, cassava plants spend all their energy growing thick stems and lush leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei ni mli ewo muji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my farm help other crops grow better afterwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ? Oda jogbaŋŋ sɛɛ mli

english: Cowpeas are leguminous crops that pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the ground through their roots. When the plant dies, this nitrogen remains in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow tall and thin with very few fruits when planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are planted too close to each other, their leaves block sunlight from reaching one another. They waste their energy stretching upwards to reach light instead of branching out wide and producing pepper fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Amɛfiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkpãa kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛshɛ la he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofee niji babaoo lɛ, no lɛ feemɔ pepper

english: Extreme afternoon heat or inconsistent watering stresses tomato plants. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself from drying out, which stops fruits from forming.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Kɛji haomɔ ba lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Enɛ haa aduawai feemɔ kpaa.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tightly during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon is a natural defense mechanism. The plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun, preventing excessive water loss through evaporation.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ aba shi. Etsiɔ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ naa kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting right while hanging on the trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite beni amɛkpɛtɛ tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a water-loving fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy periods when humidity is high and air cannot flow freely through crowded tree branches.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo lɛ. ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ tsei niji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli oya.

english: Why do my planted yam seed pieces rot in the ground before they even shoot up leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛwoɔ baai po lɛ?

english: If yam seed setts are planted in waterlogged soil without proper drainage, small soil organisms and fungi attack the seed in the excess water, causing it to rot before root system development occurs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu sweet potato dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Microscopic soil organisms kɛ fungi tutuaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani shishifãi lɛ feɔ.

english: Why does my field give me fewer bags of maize each year even when I use the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ haaa mi ŋmãa kotokui fioo ko pɛ daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop season after season continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover, while allowing crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the dirt.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsofai fɔji kɛ helai ni yeɔ tsei anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it better to plant my crops in straight rows with measured space instead of scattering seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni gbɛ kã amɛteŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ dumɔwui ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ

english: Planting in straight rows gives each crop enough space to get sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with neighboring plants. It also makes weeding, clearing, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ni ajieɔ, kɛ nikpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Does it matter how deep I push seed grains into the dirt when planting?
ga: Ani bɔ ni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ mihaa beni miduɔ nii lɛ he hiaa mi?

english: Yes, planting seeds too deep prevents them from reaching the surface before running out of energy, while planting too shallow exposes them to birds or causes them to dry out in the sun. A good rule is to plant a seed twice as deep as its size.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkashɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ dani amɛhewalɛ lɛ afite. yɛ be mli ni dumɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baajie okpoi akpo loo ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Mla kpakpa ji ni adu dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ fe bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shii enyɔ.

english: My maize leaves are turning yellow from the bottom of the stalk upward. What is happening to my crop?
ga: Mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi. Mɛni ba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is lacking nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to stay green and grow. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop and curl during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miigbee shi ni ekɛmiibɔle ehe yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl and droop to reduce water loss during intense heat. If the leaves bounce back in the cool evening, the crop is simply protecting itself, but if they remain limp, the plants need watering.
ga: Ehaa curling ni ehaa nu ni laajeɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baa shi. Kɛji baai lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibu amɛhe kɛkɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔlɔ nyiɛ lolo lɛ, ehe miihia ni awo tsei lɛ hu nu.

english: My pepper plants are dropping all their blossoms before growing peppers. What causes this?
ga: Mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ miiwo fɔfɔi dani midu amɛ. Mɛni kɛ enɛ ba?

english: Pepper plants drop blossoms when stressed by extreme sun heat, lack of soil moisture, or attacks from small insects like thrips. Keeping the soil moist and protecting flowers from pests allows them to turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ fɔfɔi ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings die when I clear away all the big trees from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn under full direct sunlight. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains provides a canopy that shields the young cocoa until it is strong enough for full light.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe la babaoo.

english: Why do weeds cause my main crops to stay small and yield very little harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ miifee bibioo ni ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital nutrients, soil water, and root space away from your crops. When weeds grow closely around your crop rows, your main plants become starved and cannot grow healthy produce.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, sũ mli nu, kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otsei titrii lɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: If I cut off the extra side branches from my tomato plants, won't that harm the crop?
ga: Kɛ mifo niji ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ tomato tso lɛ mli lɛ, Ani no eyeŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Removing small side shoots and low leaves actually helps tomatoes by directing the plant's energy away from unwanted leaf growth and straight into growing larger, healthier fruit.
ga: Nibii bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ He lɛ afãi kɛ baai lɛ baa shi diɛŋtsɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tomato kɛtsɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ baa ni ataooo lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. ni eyaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa aduawai ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I leave dried weeds and leaves around the stems of my crops instead of sweeping the soil bare?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi jwɛi kɛ tsei ni egboi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifã lɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground, keeps root zones cool under strong sun, and stops new weed seeds from sprouting.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩ jwɛi dumɔwui heei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts on a plot after harvesting maize instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ moŋ fe ni madu ŋmãa lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of food from the dirt, but beans and groundnuts naturally put nutrients back into the soil through their roots, restoring soil fertility and breaking pest cycles for the next season.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ. ni ofo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Is it better for my crops if I manually channel water to my farm instead of waiting for the rain?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji mi diɛŋtsɛ mikɛ nu lɛ tee ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mamɛ nugbɔ?

english: Crops perform much better when they have a consistent, intentional water supply. Relying only on seasonal rain leaves your crops vulnerable to dry spells, while actively supplying water keeps their growth steady and increases your final harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kwraa kɛji amɛyɛ nu jɛɛhe ni yaa nɔ ni amɛsusuɔ he. Kɛ́ okɛ ohe fɔ̃ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be mli lɛ pɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni ooofee kɛ ekãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa be fɛɛ be ni ehaa onaagbee yibiiwoo lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow so much faster when I plant them close to a stream or river?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya waa kɛ́ midu yɛ faa loo faa ko masɛi lɛ?

english: Crops near natural water sources benefit from constantly moist soil. This moisture allows the roots to easily absorb nutrients from the soil, preventing wilt and promoting lush green growth.
ga: Tsei ni bɛŋkɛ adebɔɔ mli nu jɛɛhei lɛ náa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ he sɛɛ. Nɛkɛ fɛ̃i nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ daa.

english: What will happen to my crops if the rains stop unexpectedly during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa yɛ be mli ni amɛduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Without a secured water source, sudden dry spells cause crops to stop growing, drop their flowers, and produce small or poor-quality fruits as they enter survival mode.
ga: Kɛji nu jɛɛhe ko bɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe Hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kpaa shweremɔ. fɔfɔi ni gbeeɔ shi ni ewoɔ yibii bibii loo nɔ ni baa shi beni eboteɔ wala shihilɛ mli lɛ.

english: If I only rely on short seasonal rains to farm, will my yields be lower?
ga: Kɛ wɔkɛ wɔhe fɔ̃ nugbɔ nɔ be kukuoo ko lɛ, ani ŋmãa ni anáa lɛ baa shi?

english: Yes, relying solely on unpredictable seasonal rains often leads to smaller yields because the crops may not get enough moisture at critical stages like flowering and fruiting.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ he fɔ̃ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be mli ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ pɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ekolɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ bei ni he hiaa waa tamɔ fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo mli.

english: Can I continue to plant crops on the same garden beds I used last year if I use fertilizer?
ga: Ani manyɛ maya nɔ madu tsei yɛ abɔɔ mli saatso ni mikɛtsu nii nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii?

english: Yes, you can reuse the same beds successfully if you add fertilizer. The fertilizer replaces the nutrients that the previous crop removed, allowing the new plants to thrive on the same land.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ saatso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii ekoŋŋ yɛ omanyeyeli mli kɛji okɛ fɔ wo mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ jie lɛ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei heei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why does adding fertilizer to old farm land make my crops grow like new land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ momo ni mikɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa tamɔ shikpɔŋ hee lɛ?

english: Over time, soil loses its natural food as crops grow. Fertilizer acts like a nutrient boost, providing essential elements like nitrogen and phosphorus that give crops the strength to grow vigorously again.
ga: Beni be hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa lɛ. Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni haa niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa hiɛ. Ehaa nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer on structured nursery beds or on unprepared open ground?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ mli loo he ko ni asaaa he?

english: Applying fertilizer on prepared raised beds is better because the enclosed shape keeps the fertilizer and water right where the crop roots are, preventing rain from washing the plant food away.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo saatsoi ni awó nɔ ni asaa he lɛ anɔ. Akɛni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ hewɔ lɛ, akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu woɔ he ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Etsiɔ nugbɔ naa koni ekafɔ tsei aniyenii.

english: What is the most important thing I should check for when choosing a new plot of land for farming?
ga: Mɛni ji nibii ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ makwɛ mli beni mihalaa shikpɔŋ hee kɛha okwaayeli?

english: While soil quality is important, access to a reliable water source is critical. Land where you can easily bring water to your crops will always give better and more consistent yields.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he hiaa moŋ Shi nu jɛɛhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni anáa lɛ he miihia. Shikpɔŋ ni obaanyɛ okɛ nu awo onibii amli yɛ nɔ mlɛo lɛ baaha yibii kpakpai, ni yaa nɔ daa be fɛɛ be.

english: How do fertilizer and water work together to make my crops grow big and strong?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer provides the essential food for the crop, but water is necessary to dissolve that food so the roots can drink it in. Without enough water, crops cannot take full advantage of the fertilizer you apply.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa. Shi nu he miihia koni niyenii lɛ atsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu. Kɛji nu faaa lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aná ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do crops on well-watered land stay green even when the surrounding bushes turn brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu yɔɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ eŋɔli eyɛ mli akɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When land receives regular water, the plants keep making food through their leaves without losing moisture, allowing them to stay healthy, green, and productive while unwatered plants dry up.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nine shɛ nu nɔ daa lɛ Tso lɛ baaya nɔ etsɔ ebaa lɛ nɔ efee niyenii ni ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ efooo. Ehaa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni tsei ni náaa nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ.

english: How do I choose the right crop variety or seed brand to buy for my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tso henɔ loo dumɔwu henɔ ni sa ni mikɛbaahe kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: You should choose certified seed varieties approved for your region that resist local pests and drought. Picking a reliable, well-known brand recommended by agricultural officers ensures healthy crop growth and gives you a product buyers will recognize and want to purchase.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala dumɔwui srɔtoi ni yɔɔ he odaseyeli ni awo he odaseyeli kɛha okpokpaa lɛ nɔ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ. Kɛ́ ohala nɔ ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ jieɔ yi lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa onáa nɔ ko ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baakai ni amɛbaasumɔ ni amɛhe.

english: Why do high-yielding crop varieties need more care than my traditional local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ fe mi maŋbii akusum dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are bred to grow faster and produce much larger yields, which means they feed and drink more aggressively. Giving them adequate water, protection, and soil nutrients allows them to perform at their best.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyeɔ nii ni amɛnuɔ nii babaoo. Nu, hebuu, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the shade trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily in direct sunlight. Leaving some large trees or planting fast-growing plantains alongside them creates a living shelter that keeps the young trees cool and holds moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei wuji komɛi ni ashiɔ loo tsei bibii ni shwereɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa shihilɛhe ko ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my maize seeds closer together in the field?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: Planting too close causes crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin plants with small cobs. Giving plants the correct spacing ensures each one gets enough resources to yield a full harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Kɛ́ akɛ he ni sa ha tsei lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekpa nii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and grow tall. Applying organic manure or NPK fertilizer early in the growing season restores the nutrients your crops need.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ okɛ organic loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli mra yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How does planting groundnuts on my field help my maize crop grow better next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally traps nitrogen from the air and leaves it in the soil. Rotating your maize with groundnuts enriches the land naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛshiɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled cassava leaves are often caused by mosaic disease spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant stems prevents the virus and lets the tubers grow thick and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mosaic hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ yucca baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ ahe odaseyeli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu he kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ahe, ni ebaaye ebua bulb lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe awa.

english: Early morning watering is best because the soil absorbs the moisture before the hot sun can evaporate it. Watering in the heat of the afternoon wastes water and can burn or stress hot plant leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaŋɔ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha etsɔ la. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ fiteɔ nu, ni ebaanyɛ eshã loo eha tso lɛ baai lɛ afee nɔ ni haoɔ mɔ.

english: Why should I trim off extra branches and side shoots from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji kɛ amɛsɛɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Trimming extra shoots directs the plant's energy away from growing leaves and into producing larger, healthier tomatoes. It also improves airflow around the plant, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ejieɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ adalɛ mli. ni oha tomatoi lɛ afee wuji ni amɛná hewalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ naa.

english: How can I stop insects from destroying my maize after I harvest and store it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi ni fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ naa beni akpa ni akɛtoɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Insects need moisture to thrive, so sun-drying your grain until it is completely hard is essential. Storing clean, dry grain in airtight bags stops insects from multiplying and keeps your crop safe until market day.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia kooloi koni amɛdara. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe hia ni agbi dumɔwui lɛ kɛyashi amɛbaa wa kwraa. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui ni he tse ni egbi lɛ wo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafɔ, ni ebaaye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe kɛyashi jarayeli gbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and burn after I spray them with pest medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ helai lɛ efɔ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow or burnt leaves often mean the chemical spray was mixed too strong, applied during the hottest part of the day, or was unsuitable for that specific crop. Crops experience chemical stress when exposed to incorrect chemical dosages.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni shãa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛtsu nii yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. loo esaaa nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Tsei naa tsofai ahe haomɔ kɛji akɛ tsofai ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ wo amɛmli.

english: How long must I wait to harvest my maize after spraying it against fall armyworm?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani makpa ŋmãa yɛ be mli ni mikɛ tsofa efɔse ŋmãa ni akɛfoɔ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Every agricultural chemical has a mandatory waiting period, known as the pre-harvest interval, usually between 7 to 14 days. Harvesting too soon leaves dangerous chemical residues on the grains that can make consumers sick.
ga: Okwaayeli tsofai fɛɛ yɛ be ni esa akɛ amɛmɛ. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ be ni tsɔ nikpamɔ hiɛ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ yaa nɔ yɛ gbii 7 kɛyashi 14 teŋ. Kɛ́ akpa dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui shwɛɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ ni baanyɛ aha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ hela mɔ amɛ.

english: Why are insects still destroying my cabbage even after I sprayed the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-cabbage lɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa shwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Pests can build resistance if the same chemical is used repeatedly, or the chemical might have been fake, expired, or washed away by rain. Rotating different approved chemicals prevents pests from becoming immune.
ga: Tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛhe shi kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii shii abɔ. Aloo tsofai lɛ baanyɛ afee amalei, amɛbe eho, loo nugbɔ baashwie amɛ. Tsofai srɔtoi ni tsɔɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli ni awo he odase lɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akaná hewalɛ ni tsiɔ hela naa.

english: Is it safe to buy and use unlabelled chemical liquid sold in clear water bottles at the market?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooohe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ nu mli ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni mli tse mli yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ni okɛtsu nii?

english: Unlabelled chemicals are dangerous because you cannot know their correct mixing strength, safety waiting times, or toxicity. Using unknown liquids can ruin your soil, leave harmful residues in crops, and destroy your harvest.
ga: Tsofai ni aŋmalako nɔ ko lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ onyɛɛɛ ole bɔ ni amɛfutuɔ nii amɛhaa. be ni akɛmɛɛɔ shweshweeshwe loo tsofa fɔŋ ni ja Nu ni aleee ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ afite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eshiɔ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni efiteɔ nibii ni ofeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and drop leaves after my neighbor sprays his nearby farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gbo ni ebaai lɛ sɛɛ fo beni akutsoŋnyo ko shwie nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Strong winds can carry chemical sprays from a neighboring field onto your farm, a process called chemical drift. Sensitive crops like peppers can suffer severe damage or toxicity when hit by chemicals meant for other crops.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ aŋɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli kɛba oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ kemikal drift. Tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ afite loo amɛná poison ni naa wa waa kɛji akɛ tsofai ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha tsei krokomɛi lɛ wo mli.

english: What happens to my cassava tubers if I apply too much pesticide to the farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi babaoo tsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Excessive pesticide use does not make crops grow faster; instead, it damages the plant's roots and leaves toxic chemical residues trapped inside the edible cassava roots.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haaa tsei adara oya. Mohu ɔ, e kpataɔ tso ɔ sisifã ɔmɛ a hɛ mi, nɛ e haa nɛ tsopa nɛ gbeɔ mɛ ɔ hiɔ si fɔfɔɛ nɛ a yeɔ ɔ mi.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot so quickly in the baskets even when they looked good on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ mli lɛ? Ani tomato lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ lolo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Applying non-approved chemicals or spraying too close to harvest weakens the skin of the tomato and leaves chemical residues that accelerate spoilage during transport and storage.
ga: Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tomato lɛ hewolo lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni eshiɔ tsofai ni eshwɛ ni haa efiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko kɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Can I completely wash away chemical sprays from my vegetables using ordinary water after harvesting?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ nu ni sa tsuɔ nii kɛfɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ aduawai anɔ lɛ he yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Washing removes dirt and some surface sprays, but systemic chemicals travel inside the plant's veins and tissues. Once inside the crop, chemicals cannot be washed off with water, which is why observing safety waiting periods before harvest is crucial.
ga: He ni ooofɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ejie muji ni ekɛshwie hei komɛi anɔ. Shi tsofai ni yɔɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ yaa lá fãji kɛ tsei amli fãji amli. Kɛji akɛ eshɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli pɛ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ akɛ nu afɔ Tsofai lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni akwɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ mli mɛmɔ bei dani akpa ŋmaa lɛ.

english: Rain creates wet conditions where black pod fungus thrives on cocoa trees. If protective sprays are washed away by heavy rains or applied incorrectly, the fungus quickly infects and destroys the pods.
ga: Nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ baa. Pod diŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tsei anɔ. Kɛji akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa loo akɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ hewɔ lɛ, nu ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ ho. Fuji lɛ tsɛŋeɔ ŋmeii lɛ oya ni efiteɔ amɛ.

english: How do I know if a chemical spray is safe to use on food crops like spinach and kontomire?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ niyenii nɔ tamɔ spinach kɛ contomir lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: Safe crop chemicals have official registration labels that explicitly list approved food crops, mixing proportions, and harvest waiting times. Chemicals intended for non-food crops or weed control should never be sprayed on leafy greens.
ga: Tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ tsei ahe woji ni tsɔɔ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ. Nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii kɛ be ni akɛmɛɔ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ mli ka shi faŋŋ Esaaa akɛ akɛ Tsofai ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni jeee niyenii loo jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam plants grow best when their leaves get plenty of sunlight to manufacture energy for the growing tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light and preventing soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ amɛbaai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ. Staking baaye abua ni awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ha ená la ni etsi helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks essential nutrients, especially nitrogen, or when the ground is waterlogged. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore healthy green foliage.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa. titri lɛ nitrogen loo be mli ni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, or viruses spread by these pests. Controlling these insects early prevents leaf damage and keeps the plant growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Mra be mli ni akwɛɔ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ Ebaatsi baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigboi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, overly shaded environments. Pruning excess tree branches to improve airflow and sunlight helps protect the pods from infection.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni hulu la lɛ aba lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ helai ahe.

english: Cassava roots need soil that drains water well. When excessive rain stays trapped in dense soil, it starves the roots of oxygen and promotes fungal decay, causing the tubers to rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo lɛ, ekpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ he. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yeɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii fiteɔ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures are extremely high or when the soil moisture fluctuates too drastically. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake fe nine. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes the specific soil nutrients that plant relies on and allows pests and diseases tailored to that crop to build up in the soil over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaha sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni ŋmɔ lɛ damɔ nɔ lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni etsɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Sowing should begin after the first few consistent heavy rains have thoroughly soaked the topsoil, ensuring seeds receive steady moisture to germinate without drying out.
ga: Esa akɛ aje dumɔ shishi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa klɛŋklɛŋ bei fioo lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa nu be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not anchor deeply into the soil. As heavy fruit bunches develop, the plant becomes top-heavy and needs support from sturdy wooden poles to stay upright.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli shwereɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baafee tsiimɔ ni ehe baahia ni tso ni wa aye abua lɛ koni ehi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and stop growing when I irrigate them with dirty water from the local river?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ mikɛ nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli faa lɛ mli lɛ wo amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Water contaminated by mud or illegal mining contains heavy metals and high acid levels that block plant roots from taking in nutrients, causing leaves to turn yellow and growth to stop.
ga: Nu ni sũ loo shika tsuru ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ efite lɛ yɛ dade ni tsii kɛ acid ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ.

english: Can I safely plant cassava on farmland where mud and mining waste washed over the soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei shweshweeshwe yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni sũ kɛ mi-mi sũ lɛ hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Mining waste strips away fertile topsoil and introduces toxic chemicals. Before planting cassava, the soil needs time to recover, and heavy organic compost must be added to make it safe and fertile again.
ga: Sũ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shika tsuru mli lɛ jieɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ ni ekɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei baa. Dani abaadu ŋmei Shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia be koni ekɛ ehe awo mli ekoŋŋ. Ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii awo mli koni ekɛku esɛɛ kɛba ehewalɛ fɛɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my vegetable leaves burning at the edges even though I water them regularly from the stream?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ shãa lɛ? Namɔ ahaa lɛ nu kɛjɛɔ faa ko mli daa?

english: If the stream water contains chemicals or heavy mineral salts from upstream activities, it pulls moisture out of the plant roots instead of feeding them, making leaf edges look scorched.
ga: Kɛji tsofai ni tsii loo shika tsuru ni jɛ faa lɛ ŋwɛi nitsumɔi amli lɛ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ faa lɛ mli lɛ mli. Egbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ asɛɛ shãa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and die so easily during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow roots and tender leaves that lose water fast in direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains keeps the soil cool and moist so young cocoa survives.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaa bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Maintaining steady moisture and light shade stops flower drop.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into small cups instead of growing big and flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle kɔɔpoi bibii ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee agbo ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on leaf sap. Neem leaf extract or targeted insecticides can keep these pests away.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni akɛ hiɛ fɔɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu he kɛjɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantains fall over when their shallow root system is weak or damaged by root pests. Adding wood ash or potassium fertilizer strengthens roots and stems against wind.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo shishifãi lɛ amli tsɛŋemɔ helai efite. Kɛ́ akɛ tso mli sũ loo potassium ŋmɔtɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi kɛ tsei lɛ ahe awa koni amɛte shi amɛwo kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: Why does my rice crop have plenty of long green leaves but very few grain heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei yɛ baai kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji babaoo shi ŋmãa ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer causes rice plants to put all their energy into leafy growth instead of seeds. Balanced fertilizers containing phosphorus and potassium are needed for full grains.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai yɛ dumɔwui najiaŋ. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni phosphorus kɛ potassium yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia kɛha ŋmaa muu fɛɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field help my maize yield more in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni mi-ŋmãa yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When maize is planted next, it uses this natural nitrogen to grow faster and produce larger cobs.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni abaadu ŋmãa yɛ sɛɛ mli Ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekwɛ̃ oya ni ekɛ ŋmãa wuji aba.

english: Why do my yams grow short and twisted instead of big and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ kuku ni ebɔle ehe yɛ agbo ni etse lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose, deep soil to stretch easily. Hard or stony soil blocks the growing tuber, forcing it to bend and become misshapen.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ koni amɛgbala mli mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi tsiɔ bulbs ni miida lɛ anaa. ni nyɛɔ enɔ koni ebɔle ehe ni efite

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing many flowers but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need to be pollinated by tiny insects or by hand to turn into pods. If there aren't enough pollinating insects on your farm, many flowers drop off without growing into cocoa pods.
ga: Esa akɛ kooloi bibii awo kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli. loo kɛtsɔ nine nɔ kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmei Kɛji oŋmɔ lɛ bɛ pollinators ni fa bɔ ni sa Fɔfɔi babaoo baagbee shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Hand pollination is when you manually move pollen from one cocoa flower to another using a small pin or brush. Doing this guarantees that more flowers get pollinated, which can significantly increase the number of pods your trees produce.
ga: Nine nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji be mli ni okɛ onine jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ pin loo brɔsh bibioo ko nɔ. Nakai feemɔ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ fɔfɔi babaoo baawo ŋmɔtɔ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii ni otso lɛ woɔ lɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: How long does it take for a cocoa flower to grow into a mature pod after it gets pollinated?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eda yɛ be mli ni amɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Once a flower is successfully pollinated, it takes about 5 to 6 months to grow into a full, ripe cocoa pod ready for harvesting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ye omanye yɛ pollination mli lɛ Eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 5 kɛyashi 6 dani kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni asaa he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy seasons when humidity is high. Removing sick pods quickly and keeping the farm clear of weeds helps stop the spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ oya ni ahaa jwɛi bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: What causes the stems of my young cocoa trees to look swollen?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ shishitso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efuu?

english: Swollen stems are a clear sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. Sick trees must be completely cut down because there is no chemical cure for the virus.
ga: Tsoi ni efuu lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Ehe bahia ni afo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ kwraa ejaakɛ tsofai ni akɛtsaa hela lɛ bɛ.

english: How can I tell early on if a disease is spreading on my cocoa farm?
ga: Kulɛ mana mra. Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela ko miigbɛ eshwa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Check your farm regularly for early signs such as yellowing leaves, unusual spots on pods, wilting branches, or sudden flower drops, so you can treat or remove affected trees before the problem spreads.
ga: Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa kɛha mra be mli okadii tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ hei ni yɔɔ srɔto yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Niji loo fɔfɔi ni egbo lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa Enɛ ji koni onyɛ otsa loo ojie tsei ni ena naagba lɛ dani naagba lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do I need to prune my mature cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overgrown branches so sunlight and fresh air can reach all parts of the tree. This keeps the tree healthy, reduces disease risks, and directs energy into pod growth.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni eda fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa anyɛ ayashɛ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewaa. Ha helai ni baanyɛ aba lɛ aba shi ni oha hewalɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ

english: Can I grow my cocoa trees in full sunlight without any shade trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo tsei yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade trees like plantains or timber to protect them from harsh heat and moisture loss. Mature trees can take more sun, but complete lack of shade can stress them and shorten their lifespan.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo tsei, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi lɛ he. Tsei ni eda lɛ baanyɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Shi hulutsoo ni bɛ kwraa lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ aná haomɔ ni eha ewala be lɛ afee kuku.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees need fertilizer to grow better?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your trees have pale yellow leaves, slow growth, or stop bringing out new pods despite proper watering and pest control, it means the soil lacks essential nutrients and requires fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eedara blɛoo, loo ekpa ŋmeii heei ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. kɛ nu ni sa kɛ kooloi akudɔmɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: What should I do when small insects start eating the leaves and young pods of my cocoa?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ kooloi bibii bɔi mi-kokoo lɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeli?

english: These insects are likely pests like mirids or capsids that suck sap from the tree, causing young pods to dry up. You can manage them by spraying approved crop protection products during their peak seasons.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ mirids loo capsids ni nuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ. dry the young pods Obaanyɛ okwɛ amɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni buɔ tsei ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni oookɛshwie nɔ yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ fa babaoo lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and short roots that cannot absorb enough water under harsh, direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade plants like plantains creates a protective canopy that keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa roots grow deeper.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Be kukuoo mli tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ.

english: Can I grow cassava on the same plot with my young cocoa plants without affecting them?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ ni ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ ni enaaa enɔ hewalɛ?

english: Cassava grows very fast and has greedy root systems that steal water and nutrients away from young cocoa plants. It is better to use plantains or cocoyams as nurse crops because they provide shade without competing as aggressively for underground nutrients.
ga: Cassava daa oya waa ni eyɛ shishifãi ni yeɔ nii waa ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei bibii amli. Esa akɛ akɛ plantains loo cocoa tsei atsu nii akɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ ejaakɛ amɛhaa hulutsoo ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ shishi niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ akaŋ waa.

english: Why do the fresh new leaves on my cocoa trees look red or purple before turning green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ tsuru loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani amɛfeɔ eŋɔli lɛ?

english: The red or purple color comes from natural protective pigments in young leaves that shield them from sun scorch while they are soft. As the leaf thickens and matures, it builds green chlorophyll to start producing food for the tree.
ga: Su tsuru loo purple lɛ jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ mɔ he ni yɔɔ baai bibii amli ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he beni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ amli. Kɛji baai lɛ mli edɔ ni amɛdara kwraa Efeɔ klorofil eŋɔli koni ebɔi niyenii feemɔ kɛha tso lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees burst into flower right after the first rains follow a long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The dry season causes the tree to conserve energy, and the sudden arrival of moisture acts as a natural signal, waking up the tree and triggering it to bloom heavily so it can produce pods.
ga: Hɔmɔ be lɛ haa tsei lɛ buɔ hewalɛ he. Ni hulutsoo ni baa trukaa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli okadi. Teemɔ tso lɛ ni owo lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi waa bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔi aba.

english: Why does cutting off healthy-looking extra branches help my cocoa tree produce more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-cacao tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes crowded, non-essential branches so that sunlight and air can reach the lower trunk where flowers grow. It also stops the tree from wasting food on excess leaves, directing energy straight into growing big, heavy pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ shishigbɛ tsei lɛ ahe he ni fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Etsiɔ tso lɛ hu naa koni ekafite niyenii kɛjɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ mli. Ekɛ hewalɛ haa ŋmeii wuji ni tsii ni miida lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their small young green pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii bibii lɛ? babaoo dani etsɔ agbo

english: This is called cherelle wilt, which happens when the tree is overwhelmed by water stress, nutrient shortages, or shade competition. The tree naturally sheds extra small pods so it can focus its limited energy on nourishing the remaining ones.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu he haomɔ ye tsei anɔ kunim. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa loo ŋmɔlɔ akaŋshii Tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii. go out naturally Koni amɛnyɛ amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ fioo ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ atsu nii yɛ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives and spreads rapidly in wet, cold, and dark conditions. Pruning overhead branches to let in sunlight and clearing wet leaves from around the tree trunk helps prevent the fungi from taking over.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ duŋ mli. Niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni aaafolɔ koni hulu la aba mli kɛ baai ni efɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua. Tso lɛ shishitso lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akaye nɔ.

english: What causes tiny dark burn marks on my young cocoa stems and pods?
ga: Mɛni kɛ shãa he okadii bibii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ kɛ mi-pods lɛ anɔ

english: Those marks are caused by tiny sap-sucking insects called capsids or mirids that pierce the plant tissue to feed. Spraying approved treatments at the right time of year keeps these insects from damaging the shoots and ruining your harvest.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ okadii nɛɛ baa. Atsɛɔ amɛ capsids loo myrids ni tsɔɔ tsei amli fãji amli koni amɛna niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do I know if the soil in my farm has lost its strength to feed my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiho ni ekɛbaakwɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: When soil nutrients are low, cocoa leaves turn pale or yellow, flowering decreases, and pods remain small or turn brittle. Adding recommended cocoa fertilizer or organic compost restores vital nutrients to the soil.
ga: Kɛji niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi, ni ŋmeii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does COCOBOD pay better prices when cocoa beans are properly fermented and dried?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ COCOBOD woɔ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ afee cocoa ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni egbi lɛ?

english: Proper fermentation develops the rich chocolate flavor and removes moisture to prevent mold growth during shipping. Premium quality beans protect Ghana's reputation on the world market, allowing officers to pay higher rates for well-cured beans.
ga: Kɛ́ afee tsokolate lɛ ŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔ waa, ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ koni ekɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa hiɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ naa. Beans ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ Ghana gbɛi kpakpa he yɛ jeŋ jarayeli mli. Enɛ haa onukpai lɛ woɔ nyɔmɔ babaoo kɛha ŋmeii ni atsa amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is short on nitrogen. Maize needs this nutrient to grow strong, and when soil lacks it, the plant moves its remaining nitrogen to the newer, upper leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse Tso lɛ baajie nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many tiny young pods before they get the chance to grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? shika babaoo dani amɛná hegbɛ ni amɛdara

english: This is a natural process called cherelle wilt. The tree drops extra young pods it cannot feed due to a shortage of water, nutrients, or light, allowing it to save energy for the healthiest pods.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherry wilting. Tso lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aye yɛ nu, niyenii loo la ni bɛ hewɔ lɛ, ni no haa amɛbuɔ hewalɛ amɛhaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: On very hot days, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil. They temporarily wilt to conserve moisture and usually bounce back once the afternoon heat cools down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa nɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaagboi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Ni bei pii lɛ, amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa kɛji shwane mli latsaa lɛ ba shi pɛ.

english: How do I know that my cassava roots are ready for harvesting without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually ready around 8 to 12 months after planting. Look for cracks appearing in the soil around the base of the stem and the bottom leaves naturally turning yellow and falling off.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha dumɔ aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Taomɔ ŋmeii ni jeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ mli. Tso lɛ shishi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Removing all but 1 or 2 healthy suckers ensures your main plantain tree yields big, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ojie tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa o-plantain titri lɛ náa tsei niji wuji ni tsii.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stems and very small or missing corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. ni ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ faaa kwraa loo amɛbɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to prune unnecessary branches off my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to let in sunlight and fresh air. This reduces dampness where black pod disease thrives and helps the tree put more energy into producing cocoa pods.
ga: Kpojiemɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo aba shi yɛ hei ni black pod hela lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ lɛ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: If I cut plant stems using sharp metal tools during harvest, will it make the main plant decay or die?
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ dade nibii ni mli wa tsu nii kɛfo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli lɛ Ani ebaaha tso titri lɛ agbo loo egbo?

english: Sharp tools make clean cuts that heal quickly without damaging the crop. Blunt tools tear the plant skin, leaving open wounds where diseases, mold, and insects can easily enter and rot the plant.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ haa pilamɔi ahe tseɔ ni etsaa oya ni efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii. Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ gbalaa tsei lɛ ahiɛ. Enɛ haa pilamɔi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ he ni helai, ŋmeii, kɛ kooloi bibii baanyɛ abote mli oya ni amɛfite tso lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Exposure to sunlight helps the plant manufacture food, which travels down to make the underground tubers grow large.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni eha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ adara

english: Why do the stems of my pepper plants start rotting at ground level during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei akutsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rains keep the soil constantly waterlogged, fungi multiply near the root zone and attack the stem. Creating raised soil beds helps rainwater drain away from the plant stems.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Fuŋ lɛ fɔɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifã lɛ ni etutuaa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ saatsoi ni awo nɔ lɛ ni afee lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it so important for me to plant my crops as soon as the rains start in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ yɛ Ghana pɛ?

english: Planting at the very start of the rains ensures your crops get enough water during their crucial growth stage. If you plant late, the rains might end before your crops are mature, leading to small yields or crop failure.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa onibii lɛ naa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ. Kɛji odu nii yɛ sɛɛ mli Nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpa dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi.

english: What is the benefit of buying commercial seed varieties instead of using old seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni akɛheɔ jarayeli lɛ ahe moŋ fe ni akɛ dumɔwui momoi ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Commercial seed varieties are specially developed to yield more food, resist local diseases, and grow faster. Saved seeds often lose their strength over time and give lower yields.
ga: Afee dumɔwui srɔtoi ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni ekɛ yibii babaoo aba. helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahewalɛ ni amɛdaraa oya Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ fɔɔ hewalɛ ni baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni baa shi.

english: What does it mean when someone recommends a 'short-duration' crop variety for my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛji mɔ ko jie ‘be kukuoo mli’ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi ahe ŋaa kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: A short-duration crop variety is one that grows and is ready for harvest in a shorter amount of time—usually a few months—allowing you to produce food quickly before the dry season begins.
ga: Be kukuoo mli henɔi lɛ ji nɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji fioo komɛi. Enɛ haa onáa niyenii oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: What happens to my mature crops if I delay harvesting them from the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii ni edara lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ sɛɛ fo?

english: Leaving mature crops in the field too long exposes them to insect attacks, mold, wild animals, and dry season bushfires that can destroy your entire harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii, ŋmeii, koo mli kooloi kɛ koo mli la ni baanyɛ afite oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ lɛ baatutua amɛ.

english: How can I tell if my maize is fully ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves turn yellow and brown, the husks covering the cob dry out completely, and the grains feel hard when pressed with your fingernail.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ. Hewolo ni ha ŋmei lɛ he lɛ egbi kwraa. Ni dumɔwui lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛ́ okɛ onineshi tsɔne lɛ miimɔ nɔ.

english: Why is quick harvesting so important when growing fast-maturing crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nikpamɔ oya he hiaa kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ?

english: Fast-maturing crops dry out quickly once they reach maturity. Harvesting them promptly secures your yield before the plants become brittle or vulnerable to field hazards.
ga: Tsei ni daa oya lɛ baagbi oya be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Nikpamɔ haa onáa nikpamɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛhe baawo oshara mli kɛjɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why are my farm crops in Ghana at such high risk of catching fire during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okwaayeli nibii ni miduɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ yɛ la he oshara waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the dry Harmattan season, the hot sun and dry winds remove all moisture from grass and dry crops, making them catch fire very easily from even a small spark.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shãa oya waa kɛ la bibioo ko po.

english: How can I create a firebelt to protect my farm from bushfires?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee la hose ni mikɛbu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ koo mli la he?

english: A firebelt is a wide strip of cleared, bare land around your farm boundary. By clearing all weeds and dry leaves from this strip, you create a barrier that stops bushfires from jumping onto your land.
ga: La line lɛ ji he ko ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ husui Jiemɔ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ nɛkɛ he nɛɛ. Obaafee gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ koo mli la naa koni ekatu kɛba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does dry, dead plant material on my farm cause fires to spread so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni egboi kɛ tsei ni egboi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa la gbɛɔ eshwaa oya nɛkɛ?

english: Dry stems and dead leaves act like fuel for fire. When left lying on the field during hot weather, they burn intensely and carry fire rapidly across the entire farm.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei ni egbi kɛ baai ni egboi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofa kɛha la. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ Amɛshãa waa ni amɛgbɛɔ la amɛshwãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: How does the dry Harmattan weather affect crops that are left unharvested in the field?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi yɛ Harmattan lɛ ená ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaaa lɛ anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: The Harmattan wind sucks moisture out of standing crops very fast, making them dry, brittle, and extremely flammable, which increases the danger of losing everything to a sudden wildfire.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ amli oya, ni ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ, amɛhe shwieɔ shi, ni amɛshãa waa. Enɛ haa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ baafite yɛ koo mli la ni tsoɔ trukaa lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: If I plant maize seeds saved from my last harvest, will they yield as well as the seeds I bought from the shop?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, Ani ebaawo yibii tamɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Not always. Hybrid seeds bought from agro-dealers are specially bred for high yields, but seeds saved from those harvested crops lose their vigor in the next generation, producing smaller cobs and uneven growth.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa baa.

english: Is it a good idea to plant many different crops very close together in one small field to make more profit?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ ooodu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli? He kome ni abaaná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo yɛ

english: Planting too many crops close together causes them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. When crowded, none of the crops get enough care or food, leading to poor growth and smaller harvests overall.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Beni gbɔmɛi babaoo yɔɔ lɛ Dumɔwui bɛ kwɛmɔ loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haaa shweremɔ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni nibii fɛɛ ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my crops look pale yellow and weak even when I give them enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil is exhausted of basic nutrients like nitrogen. Plants need soil food (fertilizers, manure, or compost) just as much as water to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei he miihia shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii (ŋmei, ŋmei, loo ŋmei) tamɔ nu koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my vegetables are getting enough water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-vegetables lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Check the soil about two inches deep; if it feels dry and powdery, your plants need water. Also, if leaves look dull or begin wilting early in the morning before the sun gets hot, your crops are thirsty.
ga: Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aaafee inchi enyɔ. Kɛji enu he akɛ egbi ni efee powder Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia otso lɛ. Kɛfata he lɛ, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ loo amɛjeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi leebi dani hulu lɛ edɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye onibii lɛ.

english: What signs should I look for to know if my young cassava plants are growing healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii esa akɛ matao koni mana kɛji mi yucca tso lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ?

english: Healthy cassava plants should sprout firm green leaves within a few weeks, produce sturdy stems, and show no signs of leaf curling, yellow patches, or stem rot.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli. Eyɛ tso ni mli wa. ni ejieee okadi ko ni tsɔɔ akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle Yellow patches loo tsei ni egbo lɛ ahe okadi ko kwraa

english: What happens to my maize if I focus on my other business and neglect weeding for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-abele lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ma jarayeli nitsumɔi krokomɛi anɔ ni miku mihiɛ mishwie jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ otsii fioo komɛi?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and will quickly steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your maize, leaving your crop stunted and severely reducing your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebaaju nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-ŋmãa lɛ oya. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ehaa okpamɔ lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Can planting beans together with my maize help my soil stay rich?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baaye abua ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii?

english: Yes. Legumes like beans trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, acting like a natural fertilizer that helps feed the neighboring maize plants.
ga: Hɛɛ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant the exact same crop every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi moŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes the exact same soil nutrients year after year without giving the land time to recover, causing the soil to become exhausted.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite afi fɛɛ afi ni ehaaa sũ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and dropping off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbee shi oya nɛkɛ?

english: Leaf curling usually signals plant distress, often caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap, or extreme heat coupled with irregular watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa fataa he

english: If I give my corn fields full attention, can I be sure to harvest good cobs at the end of the season?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ fɛɛ wo ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ Ani manyɛ maná ŋmãa kpakpa yɛ ŋmãa be lɛ naagbee?

english: Good management greatly increases your chances, but crop performance also depends on weather, good spacing, timely weeding, and protecting plants from pests throughout their lifecycle.
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa baaha ohegbɛi lɛ aya hiɛ waa. Shi bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ hu damɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anɔ. good distance Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be naa kɛ tsei ahebuu kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe yɛ amɛwala be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my maize seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants are forced to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and weak, resulting in small ears of corn or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, anyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa toi bibii baa loo ŋmãa ko bɛ kwraa.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing large tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the vines off the hot soil, preventing leaves from rotting and allowing them to catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni oha amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni ooonyɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that easily burn under strong sunshine. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that provide natural shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen is a vital nutrient that helps plants stay green, and when the soil lacks it, the plant pulls nitrogen from older leaves to support new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni eye ebua dalɛ hee.

english: Why does my land produce smaller cassava tubers when I plant cassava on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ be mli ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting cassava continuously on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating cassava with legumes like cowpeas helps restore fertility to the soil.
ga: Kasava ni yaa nɔ akwɛɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Cassava ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ cowpea tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: How does spreading dry grass or dry leaves around the base of my tomato plants help them?
ga: Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi afɔ he. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tomato tso shishitoo baanyɛ aye abua?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil moist by preventing water from evaporating quickly in the sun. It also stops weeds from growing and keeps the plant roots cool.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni ehaaa efo oya yɛ hulu la mli lɛ nɔ. Ehaa jwɛi hu shwereɔ ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes through the heart of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Koni maye bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on the central growing leaves of corn plants. Applying approved insecticides or neem leaf extracts early in the morning or late evening helps control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ wo mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni akudɔɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ dani efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain trees growing very small, yellow, and bunched up at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji bibii, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: This bunching is caused by the Banana Bunchy Top Virus, which is spread by tiny insects called aphids. Infected plants cannot produce good fruits and must be dug up and destroyed so the disease does not spread to healthy trees.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ kuu nɛɛ baa ji Banana Bunchy Top hela, ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ aphids Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii ni esa akɛ atsa amɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before any peppers start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as sudden hot spells, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Consistent watering during flowering helps the plant keep its blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ hulutsoo ni baa trukaa lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why does clearing weeds late reduce my crop yield even if I weed the farm eventually?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ naagbee lɛ mijie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ.

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and light during the critical early weeks when your crop is establishing its root system. Even if you clear them later, the crop has already suffered early growth damage that reduces the final yield.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la yɛ shishijee otsii ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli beni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitswa amɛshishifãi lɛ ama shi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ojie mli yɛ sɛɛ mli po. Nibii ni aduɔ hu fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ mra be mli dalɛ mli. ni haa naagbee nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the ground where roots cannot reach it, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.
