No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants make many flowers but produce very few pods when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewoɔ fɔfɔi fioo pɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall can wash away pollen from cowpea blossoms before insects can pollinate them, or cause fungal rot that makes the delicate flowers fall off before pods can form.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ tsina fɔfɔi lɛ amli muji lɛ ahe dani kooloi bibii lɛ baanyɛ afee amɛ muji. aloo ekɛ fungal rot ni haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shwieɔ shi dani pods baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots spoil and turn watery if I leave them in the soil after the major rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ nu kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Mature cassava tubers stop growing and begin absorbing excessive water when heavy rains arrive. Waterlogged soil cuts off air to the roots, causing them to rot and lose their starchy quality quickly.
ga: Kasava shishifãi ni eda lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni amɛjeɔ nu babaoo shishi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni starch lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya.

english: Why does my yam crop grow thick green leaves above ground but only small tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli edɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or manure, the yam plant spends all its energy growing leaves and vines above ground instead of storing food in the tuber below. A balanced soil food mix encourages larger tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmeii babaoo yɔɔ Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai kɛ wain tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato tuber ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli Niyenii nibii ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa bulbs lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees dropping their flowers before setting any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛfee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from heat stress, dry soil, or a lack of tiny insects called midges that pollinate them. Plantain shade trees keep the farm cool and provide a moist home for these helpful insects.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ dɔlɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii hao amɛ. Atsɛɔ nakai tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akɛ hemorrhoids ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Dumɔwui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ náa shĩa ni mli ejɔ.

english: Why is my oil palm farm yielding much fewer fruit bunches this season after a very dry year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa yɛ be nɛɛ mli yɛ afi ni hulu enyɔ shi waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Oil palms decide how many fruit bunches to form up to two years in advance. When a severe drought occurs, the tree cancels young flower buds to save water and energy for its own survival, leading to lower yields later on.
ga: Mu tso lɛ tsɔɔ aduawai akui ni baafee lɛ ayibɔ kɛyashi afii enyɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ. Kɛji hɔmɔ ni naa wa ba lɛ Tsei shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward like cups during hot dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up to reduce water loss under intense sunshine or because tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips are hiding underneath. Light shade and pest control help the leaves lay flat and stay healthy.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni nu ni fiteɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ aba shi. Aloo akɛni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ thrips, ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ yɛ hewɔ. Shade kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do black spots appear at the bottom of my tomatoes just as they start to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ tomato shishi beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Black spots on the bottom of tomatoes are caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium due to irregular watering or drying out in hot sun.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be loo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to sprout new leaves when planted in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani midumɔwui lɛ baawo baai heei kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers need high moisture and rich soil to build new roots. In dry soil, the sucker sleeps to conserve water and will not sprout until steady rains arrive or manual watering begins.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ koni amɛfee shishifãi heei. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii maleɔ koni amɛbua nu naa. Ni ebaakwɛɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ daa loo obaabɔi bo diɛŋtsɛ ohe nu shwiemɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster in my farm than the crop seeds I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants native to the soil that have evolved to sprout instantly with the smallest amount of rain, while crop seeds need carefully prepared soil and constant moisture to establish.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni etsake ni amɛje kpo amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ ni nu yɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ he miihia dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛma shi.

english: Is June a good time for me to start planting my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani June ji be kpakpa ni esa akɛ mabɔi kookoo tsei bibii akwɛmɔ?

english: June is usually the height of the major rainy season in Ghana. Planting cocoa during this wet month ensures the young seedlings get plenty of water to establish deep root systems before the dry season begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, June ji be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ Ghana. Cocoa ni aduɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ waa nɛɛ amli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ nu babaoo koni amɛkɛma shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani hulutsoo be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why is it important for me to wait until the rains start before transplanting seedlings into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ abɔi nɛmɔ dani mikɛ dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Transplanting causes shock to young plants. Rainwater softens the soil and provides consistent moisture, helping the seedlings recover quickly and start growing roots instead of drying out under the heat.
ga: Tsei bibii ni aduɔ awoɔ he kroko lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ amɛ yaa. Nugbɔ nu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ po baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhe wa oya ni amɛjeɔ shishifãi lɛ akwɛmɔ shishi moŋ fe ni amɛaagbi yɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do I need to clear all the bush and weeds on my land before I plant cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛ jwɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani madu kookoo lɛ?

english: Clearing the land removes weeds that steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients from your young plants. A clean field gives your cocoa seedlings a fair chance to grow without being choked by wild plants.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ooosaa lɛ baaye abua ni ejie jwɛi ni juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ. Gbɛ ni mli tse haa o-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ hegbɛ ni amɛdara ni koo mli tsei etsĩii amɛ gbɛ.

english: Should I apply weed-killing chemicals to my land before putting my new crops into the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mikɛ tsei heei awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Applying herbicides before planting helps destroy stubborn weed roots and overgrown bush. This creates a clean seedbed so your young crops do not have to fight fast-growing weeds during their first critical weeks.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛbaatsu nii dani adu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni efiteɔ jwɛi shishifãi ni wa kɛ tsei bibii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ahe tseɔ bɔni afee ni ehe ehiaaa ni odumɔwui lɛ kɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ akpee yɛ nakai klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli.

english: Can I plant my cocoa trees right next to a river or stream on my land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo tsei yɛ faa loo faa ko naa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too close to water can cause roots to sit in flooded soil, which rots them. Cocoa plants need moist soil, but sitting directly in stagnant water or riverbanks that overflow will kill the young roots.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ nu tsɔ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ afu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli, ni baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ he miihia koko tsei. Shi kɛ́ ota nu ni damɔ shi loo faa ni hoɔ babaoo lɛ naa lɛ, ebaagbe shishifãi bibii lɛ.

english: What will happen to my crop if the soil on my farm is too muddy and waterlogged?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ewo muji tsɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When land stays too muddy or waterlogged, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing them to drown, turn soft, and stop taking up plant food.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo muji loo nu babaoo yɛ nɔ lɛ. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛfeɔ blɛoo, ni amɛkpaa tsei aniyenii yeli.

english: How can I prepare swampy or muddy land so that my crops can survive on it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi?

english: You can dig drainage ditches across swampy land to channel standing water away from your field. Draining excess water lowers the water table and creates drier topsoil where crop roots can breathe.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu tsɔnei yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ koni nu ajie kɛjɛ oŋmɔji amli. Nu ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ amu yɛ nɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow in low-lying areas of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves in low-lying spots often mean the roots are drowning in trapped water. Excessive moisture prevents the roots from taking up nitrogen, an essential food plant leaves need to stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ miiho nu ni emɔ mli lɛ mli. Fɛ̃i babaoo haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei ni esa akɛ amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: Is it safe for me to spray weedkillers on soil that is wet and muddy?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ kɛ muji nɔ?

english: Spraying chemicals on waterlogged ground reduces their effectiveness because the rainwater washes the chemical away before weeds can absorb it. It is best to spray when the soil is moist but not covered in standing water.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha amɛhewalɛ aba shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ tsofai kɛyaa dani jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu ni damɔ shi lɛ ehiɛɛɛ nɔ.

english: Will spraying chemicals to kill weeds near a water body contaminate the water?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛshwieɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhei lɛ baafite nu lɛ?

english: Yes, farm chemicals sprayed near streams or rivers easily wash into the water with rainfall. This pollutes drinking sources for the community and harms fish, so a safe distance must always be kept when spraying.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ faai loo faai ahe lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ nu lɛ mli oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ nu ni anuɔ kɛhaa akutsei lɛ, ni eyeɔ loo awui. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akwɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe be fɛɛ be kɛ́ ashɛreɔ tsofa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight dries up their leaves and burns them. Taller trees act as living umbrellas that protect young cocoa until they grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbi ni eshã baai lɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa ni ewaa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ naa.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with bushy leaves but produces small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or rain, the plant focuses all its energy into growing stems and green leaves instead of pushing nutrients down into the root tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei loo nugbɔ babaoo nɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ baai ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsi niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛya shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop during hot afternoons even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: In intense heat, pepper leaves lose moisture faster through evaporation than the roots can pump it up from the soil. Drooping is the plant's natural way to reduce sunlight exposure and conserve water until the air cools down.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Pepper baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ fe be mli ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Drooping ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa hulu la lɛ baa shi ni ekɛtoɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Yellow maize leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build green leaves. Applying organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shi waa.

english: Maize uses up a lot of soil nutrients, but legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, naturally restoring fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni okɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small and produce weak yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water, soil food, and sunlight away from your crops, leaving your plants starved and unable to grow properly.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni boteɔ mli ni juɔ nu, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otsei lɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: When plantains are crowded, their large leaves block sunlight from each other and their roots fight over the same soil nutrients, which slows down their growth and fruiting time.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ, baai wuji lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaha dalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off before setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high, when watering is uneven, or when small pests attack the flower stems, causing the plant to drop flowers to protect itself from stress.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii tutuaa fɔfɔii ahe tsei. Gbalamɔ tomato tsei lɛ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ haomɔ he.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start rotting quickly inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ oya yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot easily if they are bruised during harvest, stored in a hot room without airflow, or exposed to moisture, which allows fungal mold to enter the cuts and decay the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Okɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli. loo ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli Enɛ haa ŋmeii boteɔ pilamɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why does the crop buyer offer me a lower farm gate price when my harvested maize is still damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko ni heɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaha mi ŋmɔ shinaa lɛ naa jara ni baa shi yɛ be mli ni mi-ŋma ni mikpaa lɛ mli edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Buyers pay less for damp maize because wet grain quickly develops mold and spoils during transport, meaning the buyer takes on the cost and risk of drying it before selling.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ ŋmãa ni mli efɔ lɛ he nyɔmɔ fioo Akɛni dumɔwui lɛ mli efɔ hewɔ lɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋmãa oya ni amɛfiteɔ kɛ́ akɛ amɛ tee. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ awo shika kɛ oshara ni yɔɔ he akɛ ebaagbi lɛ dani ekɛhɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do most farmers in my area start land preparation and planting around April?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ ateŋ mɛi babaoo jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kɛ dumɔ shishi yɛ April afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: April usually marks the onset of the major rainy season in southern and central Ghana. Planting at this time ensures your seeds get reliable rainfall to germinate and build strong roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, April ji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee yɛ Ghana wuoyigbɛ kɛ teŋgbɛ. Dumɔwui ni ooodu yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ náa nugbɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Can I still plant food crops around August or September, or is it too late in the year?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii lolo yɛ August loo September mli loo afi lɛ mli eshɛ sɛɛ tsɔ?

english: You can still plant during August and September because this is the start of the minor rainy season. It is a good time to plant fast-growing crops like short-duration maize, cowpeas, or vegetables before the dry weather sets in.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu hu yɛ August kɛ September teŋ ejaakɛ enɛ ji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ shishijee. Eji be kpakpa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa ni yeɔ be kukuoo, tsina ŋmãa loo aduawai dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them close to November without an extra water source?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ November ni nu jɛɛhei krokomɛi fataaa he?

english: By November, the rainy season ends and dry weather begins. Without an artificial water supply, rain-fed crops will dry up, stop growing, and produce very little or fail entirely.
ga: Beni shɛɔ November Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa naagbee ni kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji akɛ nu ni akɛfee pɔmpi mli bɛ Dumɔwui ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ baagbi. ekpaa dalɛ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ loo efiteɔ kwraa.

english: How do I know which months of the year are suitable for rain-fed farming?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole afi lɛ mli nyɔji ni sa kɛha okwaayeli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ mli lɛ?

english: In Ghana, traditional farming depends on two main rain periods: the major season starting around April and the minor season starting around August. Matching your crops to these rainy periods ensures they get enough water.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, blema okwaayeli damɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be titrii enyɔ nɔ: be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ April aaafee. ni be ni ji enyɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ August aaafee. Okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato nugbɔ bei nɛɛ ahe koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ amɛná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why am I only able to harvest crops twice a year while some neighboring farmers harvest three times?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ manyɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ pɛ yɛ afi mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni okwaafoi komɛi ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ kpaɔ nii shii etɛ lɛ?

english: Farmers relying only on rainfall can usually only plant during the two wet seasons. Farmers who harvest three times a year use irrigation systems to supply water, allowing them to plant even when there is no rain.
ga: Okwaafoi ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ nu pɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ adu nii yɛ nugbɔ bei enyɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Okwaafoi ni kpaa nii shii etɛ yɛ afi mli lɛ kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha nu. Bɔni afee ni anyɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: How does having an irrigation system on my farm change my planting plan?
ga: Te nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ midumɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Irrigation frees you from relying only on natural rainfall. Instead of waiting for the April or August rains, you can control water application yourself and plant crops continuously throughout the entire year.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haaa okɛ ohe afɔ̃ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ pɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ yɛ April loo August mli lɛ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ bɔ ni okɛ nu tsuɔ nii ohaa lɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ ni okwɛ tsei anɔ daa afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Is it really possible for me to grow and harvest crops three times in a single year on the same land?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ madu ni makpa ŋmɔshi nibii etɛ yɛ afi kome mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, it is possible if you plant quick-maturing crops like vegetables or legumes and use irrigation to keep the soil moist during the dry months between natural rainy seasons.
ga: Hɛɛ, ebaanyɛ eba mli kɛji odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii. ni okɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ atsu nii koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ amli.

english: Why are vegetables good crops to plant if I have access to irrigation?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai hi kɛji akɛ miyɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Vegetables grow quickly and yield harvests in a short time, but they require continuous moisture. Irrigation gives them the regular water they need, allowing you to complete multiple harvest cycles every year.
ga: Aduawai daa oya ni amɛkpaa nii yɛ be kukuoo mli. Shi ehe miihia ni hulutsoo be fɛɛ be. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa amɛnáa nu ni he hiaa amɛ daa. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ofeɔ kpamɔɔ shii abɔ daa afi.

english: Why do my crops stop growing well between the August rains and November?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekpaa shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ August kɛyashi November nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During this transition period, rainfall becomes less frequent as the dry season approaches. As soil moisture drops, crop growth slows down unless additional water is provided.
ga: Yɛ tsakemɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ falɛ baa shi be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ boteɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ba shi lɛ Tsei lɛ adalɛ baafee mlɛo ja akɛ nu kroko fata he.

english: Is there an advantage to growing crops towards November when the dry season starts?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ ko yɛ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ November mli beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ he?

english: Growing crops into November using irrigation allows you to sell fresh produce when rain-fed farms cannot produce. Because supply on the market is low during dry periods, you can often sell your harvest for higher prices.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ November mli kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ nibii heei beni ŋmɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo nibii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jarayeli nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ faaa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and drying up in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive under harsh, direct sunlight without shade. Plantains or shade trees planted nearby shield young cocoa plants from intense sun and hold moisture in the soil so the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Koni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Why is my maize growing short and pale yellow instead of tall and dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ kuku ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow maize leaves mean the soil is hungry and lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plants. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer feeds the soil so the leaves turn dark green and produce strong stalks.
ga: Abɛi baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye shikpɔŋ lɛ ni nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi ashishifãi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha sũ lɛ aya hiɛ. Kɛkɛ lɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni wa.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains the same plant nutrients from the soil every year and lets maize pests build up. Switching to legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, abaajie tso lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni eha ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa nɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the soil before I even get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛná hegbɛ po ni amɛkpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water collects around them in heavy, poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to run off, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Cassava shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ Cassava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ baaha nugbɔ nu ni mli wa lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my crops after the long dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ eho lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting immediately after the very first rain is risky because the weather can stay dry for weeks after. It is best to wait until the rains become regular and wet the soil deeply so your seeds have continuous water to sprout and survive.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shihilɛi baanyɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ otsii babaoo yɛ no sɛɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ anɛ daa ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni eha odumɔwui lɛ aná nu be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do I see small holes in my corn leaves and tiny caterpillars inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest, which eats the growing leaves at the heart of young corn. Catching them early and applying recommended pest treatments or soapy neem water directly into the central leaves protects the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ baai ni miida yɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem samla ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds cause my crop yields to drop so low even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kwraa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm by taking away water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds early gives your crops all the space and nutrients they need to grow large and produce a full harvest.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmaa ni fa babaoo.

english: Too many extra shoots compete directly with the main plantain tree for nutrients and water. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong stems, allowing the main tree to direct all its energy into producing large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Tsobii babaoo ni fata he lɛ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no haa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ yibii ni tsii ni dara.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight for the leaves to make food. Staking spreads out the vines into the sunlight, directing energy down into growing larger, healthier yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ anyɛ ahoo. Staking gbɛɔ wain tso lɛ eshwaa kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli. Kɛ hewalɛ awo shi kɛyashi sweet potato tubers ni dara, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baafee shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like calcium in the soil. Mulching the soil and keeping it regularly watered helps flowers stay on the plant to form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Mulching kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛto tomatoi lɛ ama shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil, or that water is settling around their roots for too long. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or improving soil drainage helps them turn green and grow strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu ko ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Burning destroys valuable natural nutrients in the topsoil and kills earthworms and good microbes. Leaving cleared leaves and grass to rot naturally on the soil creates mulch that feeds your crops and keeps moisture in the ground during hot weather.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni jara wa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii bibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni baai kɛ jwɛi ni ajie lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and how do I fix it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the growing point of the plant. Spraying an approved, targeted insecticide early in the morning directly into the central leaf funnel kills the pests before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fall armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ hei ni edara yɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni ekumɔ yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni akɛ hiɛ fɔɔ nɔ lɛ shwie tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding on the plant's sap under the leaves. Applying an appropriate neem-based or recommended insecticidal spray stops these pests and allows new leaves to uncurl and grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni neem yɔɔ mli loo bɔ ni atsɔɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akpa kooloi nɛɛ ni ebaaha baai heei ajie amɛhe kpo ni amɛdara.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Keeping the soil evenly watered and mulched helps the plant hold its blossoms and set healthy fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔii amli ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do I need to cut away extra suckers growing at the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they compete for food, light, and water, resulting in small bunches. Keeping only one main stem and one or two young suckers ensures maximum nutrients go into producing large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ plantain kome he lɛ Amɛyeɔ niyenii, la kɛ nu he akaŋ, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohiɛ tso titri kome kɛ tso bibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ. Enɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ ni baaha aná niji wuji ni tsii.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is fully ripe and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when the bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to swell and crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the hot ground into the air so they can catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food, which flows down to build bigger and heavier yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potatoes kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. Enɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why is pruning dead or crowded branches important for my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ afolɔ he hiaa mi-kokoo tso lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to let in sunlight and air, which dries up dampness that causes black pod disease while encouraging the tree to produce more flowers and pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ agbi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekanyaa tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do hybrid seeds bought from agro-dealers produce more than seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred in laboratories for high yield and strong disease resistance in their first generation. Saved seeds from hybrid harvests lose these special traits, leading to uneven growth and lower yields in the next season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ yɛ laboratori lɛ mli koni eha yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ helai ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli lɛ baafite sui nɛɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli baa.

english: Why does my harvested rice break into small pieces when I take it to the milling machine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akumɔ mikpamɔ lɛ mli bibii bibii lɛ? Beni okɛ penti tsɔnei baa maŋsɛɛ?

english: Rice usually breaks during milling because it dried too fast in harsh sun or was left in the field too long before harvesting. Drying the grains slowly and evenly prevents internal stress cracks, keeping the grains whole during milling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa fãa yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ ŋmãa lɛ ejaakɛ egbiɔ oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli loo ashiɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani akpaa. Dumɔwui ni agbiɔ blɛoo Ni daa lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ mligbɛ haomɔ mli lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some extension officers advise us to parboil our paddy rice before milling it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi komɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔkɛ ŋmãa awo la mli dani wɔshã lɛ?

english: Parboiling involves soaking and steaming the raw rice in its husk before drying. This process hardens the grain so it breaks much less during milling, and it also drives vitamins from the husk into the grain.
ga: Nɔ ni fata steaming he ji ni akɛ ŋmãa ni ahoko lɛ awo ŋmãa ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ashã lɛ dani agbi. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ mli waɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ mli fãa fioo kwraa yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ekɛ vitamini ni jɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ yaa ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: Why do I see cracks inside my rice grains while they are still drying on the drying floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli be mli ni amɛmiigbi lolo yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cracks occur when rice loses moisture too quickly due to extreme heat from direct sunlight. To prevent this, spread the rice in thin layers and turn it frequently, or dry it under shade during the hottest parts of the day.
ga: Kpãa baa kɛji ŋmãa mli nu lɛ fite oya tsɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Bɔni afee ni enɛ akafee lɛ Gbalamɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ ŋmãa bibioo mli. Ni otsɔ mli shii abɔ. Aloo egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Is it really necessary for me to dry my rice before selling or milling it?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ ni magbi ŋmãa lɛ dani mahɔ̃ɔ loo mafolɔ mli?

english: Yes, drying reduces the moisture inside the grain. Proper drying prevents mold growth, stops insect infestations, prevents bad smells during storage, and allows the milling machine to remove husks cleanly.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ egbi lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Kɛ́ egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa. Kpaa ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Etsiɔ ŋmeii gbohii anaa yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋtayaa lɛ ni ejieɔ ŋtayaa lɛ kwraa.

english: Will drying my crops too much make me lose money when I sell them by weight?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛgbiɔ fe nine lɛ baaha mishika afite beni mikɛ amɛ hɔ̃ɔ yɛ shwiili mli lɛ?

english: Over-drying reduces grain weight slightly, but it protects your crop from rotting completely. Buyers pay higher prices for clean, dry, unbroken grain compared to heavy, wet grain that will spoil quickly.
ga: Kɛ́ agbi fe nine lɛ, ehaa ŋmaa lɛ tsiimɔ baa shi fioo. Shi ebuɔ onibii ahe kwraa koni amɛkafite. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ ŋmaa ni he tse, ni egbi, ni efiteee lɛ jara babaoo fe ŋmaa ni efɔ, ni tsii ni fiteɔ oya lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my harvested grains are dry enough to store safely in bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mawo kotoku mli shweshweeshwe?

english: A simple way is to test a grain by biting or pressing it with your thumbnail. If it snaps cleanly with a crisp sound without bending or mashing, it is dry enough for long-term storage.
ga: Gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ji ni oka dumɔwui lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ o-thumbnail lɛ ni oookɛmɔ loo onyɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ehiɛ ehe tse ni eyɛ gbee ni mli wa ni efooo loo efooo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What causes my bagged grain to get warm and moldy inside the storehouse?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi dumɔwui ni awo kotoku mli lɛ mli edɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsũ lɛ mli?

english: Heat and mold occur when grain is bagged before it is fully dry, or when bags are stacked directly on concrete floors without wooden pallets for airflow. Trapped moisture causes the grains to sweat and spoil.
ga: Dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo kotoku mli dani amɛgbi kwraa. Aloo kɛ́ akɛ kotokui eto shikpɔŋ ni akɛ tsei fee lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ latsaa ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my crops spoil much faster after harvest compared to when they were still growing on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto be mli ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ he?

english: Once harvested, the plant stops supplying moisture and natural defenses to the grain. Cut grains become vulnerable to heat, trapped moisture, insects, and fungi if they are not dried and stored properly.
ga: Kɛji akpa tso lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni ekɛhaa dumɔwui lɛ. Dumɔwui ni afolɔ lɛ nyɛɔ dɔlɛ, fɛ̃i, kooloi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ amɛ waa. Kɛji akɛ agbiko lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ

english: Is it better for me to sell my raw paddy rice right after harvest or process it first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa ni ahoo yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ loo matsu he nii klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Selling raw paddy saves you time and labor, but processing it (drying, parboiling, and milling) adds value, allowing you to sell clean white rice directly to consumers at a much higher profit.
ga: Abele ni ahoo lɛ ni ooohɔ̃ɔ lɛ haaa okɛ be kɛ nitsumɔ akafite, shi nitsumɔ (ni egbiɔ, ni ekɛshãa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii) kɛ sɛɛnamɔ baa. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa yɛŋ ni he tse tɛ̃ɛ ohaa mɛi ni heɔ lɛ ni onáa sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kwraa.

english: Why does rain during the harvest season spoil the quality of my rice crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Rain soaking ripe rice in the field forces the grains to reabsorb water, which makes them sprout early, yellow in color, and shatter easily into small fragments when processed.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ nɔ koni emɔ nu ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbalaa bibii bibii. Ehe nitsumɔ waaa

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for green leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost around the base will help the plant recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ atsu nii yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he. Konii lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant peppers in the exact same spot where I harvested tomatoes last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-peppers lɛ yɛ he ni mifo mi-tomato lɛ yɛ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Peppers and tomatoes belong to the same plant family and suffer from the same soil diseases and pests. Planting them in the same spot year after year builds up harmful pests in the soil and drains the ground of specific nutrients.
ga: Pepper kɛ tomato yɛ tsei akuu kome mli ni helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛbaa lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ekɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui baa sũ lɛ mli, ni ehaa niyenii mli nibii komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after light rain, but not right before a heavy downpour. Burying or covering the fertilizer lightly with soil near the root zone prevents running water from sweeping it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi esaaa akɛ ofeɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ ni shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ fu loo okɛ sũ ha he fioo yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nu naa koni ekafo lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When the ground remains waterlogged for too long, water replaces air in the soil, causing the roots to suffocate and decay.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu eshwɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Nu baaye kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Rolling leaves is a survival mechanism maize uses to protect itself from water loss. By curling up, less leaf surface is exposed to the hot sun and wind, helping the plant hold onto its internal moisture.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ko ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛbu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Curling haa baa lɛ hiɛ shɛɛɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: What is eating ragged holes inside the young leaves of my corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni bɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant. Early detection and applying recommended sprays or neem liquid directly into the plant funnel helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Mra namɔ kɛ neem spray loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he ŋaawoo. Kɛya dumɔwu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ lɛ.

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered by irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant move calcium from the ground into the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need direct sunshine to manufacture food for growing large underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground toward the light and keeps them dry, reducing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ ateshi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya la lɛ he ni amɛgbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa baa helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ shi.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow creates competition for water, light, and soil nutrients. Pruning down to one main stem and one or two replacement shoots concentrates energy into producing larger plantain bunches.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo shwereɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni ashi tso lɛ yitso titri kome kɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ ni akɛto najiaŋ lɛ baaha hewalɛ aba koni ekɛfee plantain jwɛi wulu ko.

english: Why is it better for me to get crop seedlings raised in a nursery instead of planting seeds directly into my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Seedlings raised in a nursery receive special care during their weakest stage, protecting them from pests, diseases, and harsh weather. This gives them strong roots so they survive much better when moved to your main farm.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ naa kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ yɛ amɛbe ni amɛhe yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ lɛ mli. Ebuɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa ahe. Enɛ haa amɛnáa shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kwraa kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛtee oŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why do my seedlings droop and look like they are dying right after I transplant them from the nursery into my main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiigboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is called transplant shock, caused by roots being disturbed during the move. Moving seedlings in the late afternoon or on cloudy days helps them recover in cool weather without losing too much water to the hot sun.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji shishifãi ni agbalaa mli yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ he kroko yɛ shwane mli loo yɛ atatu gbi nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ mli ni nu babaoo ni jɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli baa lɛ fiteee amɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees scorch and turn dry when I clear all the big trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to strong direct sunlight and heat. They need shade from surrounding trees or plantains to shield their leaves and keep the soil moist while their roots grow.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ adɛŋ. loo plantains ni akɛbuɔ baai lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen nutrients or when there is too much standing water around the roots, preventing the plant from absorbing the food it needs to grow green and healthy.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛ́ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haaa tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before any peppers grow on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or sudden changes in water. The plant discards the flowers to save energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu tsakemɔi trukaa hao amɛ. Tsei baajie fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my tomato crop grow thick leaves and branches but produces very little fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ baai kɛ niji ni mli tse shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen or aren't pruned, they focus all their energy on growing tall stems and leaves instead of forming flowers and fruits. Trimming side shoots helps direct energy to fruit production.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo loo afolɔɔɔ amɛhe lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ maa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni kɛlɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii. Afolɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ aduawai afeemɔ mli.

english: What will happen to my cassava crop if I plant the stems too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin plants and very small tuber yields compared to properly spaced plants.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tsei lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ bulb bibioo kwraa baa kɛ akɛto tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: How does spreading dried grass around the base of my crops help them grow during hot weather?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te mi tso shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, acts like a protective cover. It locks moisture into the soil, keeps the plant roots cool, and stops weeds from taking over your land.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni ekaye oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I wait until after a heavy rain to plant my crop seeds instead of planting in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ dani madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ moŋ?

english: Seeds require consistent soil moisture to break open and sprout roots. Planting in dry soil leaves seeds vulnerable to heat, ants, and birds before the rain comes to start their growth.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ daa koni amɛ gbá shishifãi ni amɛ kwɛ̃. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo, ŋmeii kɛ okpoi nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe oya dani nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi enáa.

english: Why should I avoid putting raw fertilizer directly onto my seeds when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ midu lɛ he?

english: Raw chemical fertilizer is too strong for young seeds and can burn their delicate roots as soon as they emerge, killing the seedling before it breaks through the soil surface.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ kɛha dumɔwui bibii, ni ebaanyɛ eshã amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛji amɛje kpo pɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ dani amɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my cassava take up to nine months or more to mature, and are there varieties I can harvest sooner?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ heɔ nyɔji nɛɛhu loo nɔ ni fe nakai dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ? Ni ani srɔtoi komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ makpa mra?

english: Traditional cassava varieties usually take 9 to 12 months to mature, but improved early-maturing varieties developed for Ghanaian soils can be harvested in 6 to 8 months with proper care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani amɛshwereɔ. Shi abaanyɛ akpa mra be mli ŋmei henɔi ni afee aha Ghana shikpɔŋ lɛ ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 8 mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if the early major season rains are enough for me to start planting my crop seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ he hiaa mi bɔ ni sa koni mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because the soil underneath is still hot and dry. Wait until the soil remains moist at finger-depth for a few consecutive rainy days so your seeds do not dry out after sprouting.
ga: Kaadu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli edɔ lolo ni egbi. Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashɛ inchi he kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ gbii 2-3 ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni odumɔwui lɛ akagbi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Why do farmers plant plantains together with young cocoa seedlings on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ dumɔwui ni kookoo tsei bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun, so fast-growing plantain plants act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil moist during the cocoa trees' first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ ni akɛduɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli.

english: Is it good practice to plant cassava and maize together on the same field at the same time?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava is a smart practice because maize grows quickly and is harvested within three months, leaving the cassava room to spread out and mature over the remaining months.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa dumɔ ji nilee nifeemɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli. Ha ni ŋmei tsu lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni eda yɛ nyɔji ni eshwɛ lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen or that the soil is waterlogged, which suffocates the roots and prevents the crop from absorbing food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa tso lɛ aŋɔ niyenii.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience heat stress from lack of water or when tiny insect pests like thrips attack the flowers, stopping the fruit from forming.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji amɛna dɔlɛ he haomɔ yɛ nu ni bɛ hewɔ. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips tutua fɔfɔi, ni no haa aduawai lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly even after I have cleared and prepped my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jɛmɛ ni misaa he lɛ dani midu lɛ?

english: Clearing land exposes weed seeds buried in the dirt to sunshine and rain, triggering them to sprout; covering bare soil with organic mulch helps block sunlight and stops weeds from rising.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa hulu la kɛ nugbɔ. stimulate seeds to germinate Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli lɛ baaye abua ni etsĩ hulu lɛ naa ni eha jwɛi akakwɛ̃.

english: Why is it not advisable for me to save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds lose their special vigor and high yield capacity after the first harvest, so planting saved hybrid seeds will result in uneven plants and much lower yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ ni fa kɛ nyɛmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ni amɛkɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ adumɔ baaha tsei ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ aba, ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi kwraa.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my crops so the heavy rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli? Koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akafɔ̃ tsei lɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not flooded, and bury it a few inches into the dirt near the plant roots rather than leaving it open on top where rainwater can sweep it off.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu ehiɛɛɛ nɔ. ni okɛfu lɛ aaafee inchi 2-3 yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, mo ngmɛɛ e nɔ konɛ hiɔmi nyu nɛ nyɛ nɛ e ngɔ lɛ kɛ ya.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start sprouting and getting soft before I can take them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ bɔi shweremɔ ni amɛfee blɛoo dani mikɛtee jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams sprout when stored in warm, dark, or unventilated places because heat triggers their growth cycle. Storing them in a cool, elevated, well-ventilated yam barn keeps them firm longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ, duŋ, loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ yaa hiɛ. Okɛto sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni awo nɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if the maize seeds I buy from the local market are safe and will grow well on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni ebaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Always look for official government certification tags or buy directly from registered agro-dealers. Certified seeds are tested for high germination rates and purity, whereas uncertified market seeds may be diseased, damaged, or fail to yield proper crops.
ga: Taomɔ nɔyeli lɛ wolo ni tsɔɔ akɛ eji nɔ ko ni tsɔɔ akɛ oyɛ hegbɛ loo hemɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko ni aŋma egbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ dɛŋ. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ akwɛɔ koni ana bɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ bɔ ni amɛhe tse ha. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jara nɔ ni bɛ he odaseyeli lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ, amɛfite loo amɛwooo yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just save seeds from my harvested crops to plant again during the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If you plant saved seeds from hybrid crop varieties, the new plants will grow weaker and yield much less harvest than the original parent plants. Buying fresh, registered seeds every season guarantees strong crop growth and high yields.
ga: Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ tsei srɔtoi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ Tso hee lɛ baakwɛ̃ fioo ni ebaawo yibii fioo kwraa fe shishijee fɔlɔ tso lɛ. Dumɔwui heei ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ ni aheɔ daa be lɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do some of the seeds I planted fail to sprout out of the soil completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kwraa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are bad quality, planted too deep, or if the soil lacks moisture. Using certified seeds ensures that the seeds are viable and healthy enough to germinate when properly watered.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛŋ kɛji amɛhiii. adu yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ mli Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛnáa hewalɛ bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings suddenly fall over and rot at the soil level?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛmiifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal condition called damping-off, which happens when the soil stays too wet or when uncertified, infected seeds are used. Proper drainage and quality seeds keep young seedlings upright and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dampening off, ni baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lolo loo akɛ dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ ni asaaa amɛhe lɛ tsu nii. Nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei bibii lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: How do I know the best time to put my seeds into the ground after the rainy season starts?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the soil receives steady, deep rainfall rather than planting right after the very first rain. Planting in shallow moisture causes seeds to dry out and die underground if the rain pauses.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nugbɔ ni mli kwɔ ni baa daa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that the soil is waterlogged and drowning the roots, or that the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen. Improving soil drainage and applying balanced fertilizer helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ ni abaafee jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛfata he lɛ baaye abua ni eha ehiɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off before turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants experience extreme heat stress, dry soil, or pest attack, which prevents the flower from successfully pollinating and forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tsei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are my maize plants growing thin and tall without developing big ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛnáaa abele toi wuji lɛ?

english: Maize plants grow tall and weak when planted too close together or flooded with too much nitrogen without enough sunlight, forcing them to compete for resources instead of forming thick ears.
ga: Abɛi daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ loo akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Enɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye nibii ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ ahe akaŋ moŋ fe ni amɛaama toi ni mli tse.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly whenever weeds start spreading around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo be fɛɛ be ni jwɛi baaje shishi amɛgbɛ amɛshwã amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. When weeds surround a plant, they effectively starve it and stunt its overall growth.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ jwɛi bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ Hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ni amɛha amɛdalɛ fɛɛ afee mlɛo.

english: Will applying a double portion of fertilizer all at once make my crops grow twice as fast?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli shii enyɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara oya shii enyɔ?

english: No, putting too much fertilizer at once can burn the plant's root system and kill the crop. Crops need small, measured amounts of fertilizer given at key growth stages to feed safely.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Tsei biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni asusuɔ he yɛ amɛdalɛ bei titrii amli koni amɛye niyenii shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn under direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or bananas next to young cocoa provides a living umbrella that shields the cocoa trees and keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa canopy matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo banana yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba koni ebu kookoo tsei lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: How should I position cassava stem cuttings in the soil so they don't rot?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ koni amɛkafite?

english: Cassava cuttings should be planted at a 45-degree angle or vertically with the leaf buds pointing upward into well-drained soil. Avoid planting them upside down or flat in waterlogged areas, as sitting water will cause the stem to rot before it can sprout roots.
ga: Esa akɛ adu Yucca niji lɛ yɛ 45-degree angle loo yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni okɛ ohiɛ fɔ̃ɔ nɔ loo ni oookã shi yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nu wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbo dani shishifãi lɛ adara.

english: Yellowing starting at the tips of lower maize leaves is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize requires nitrogen to stay green and produce full ears, which can be corrected by applying nitrogen-rich fertilizers or well-rotted animal manure early in the growing season.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ toi ni eyi obɔ aba. Abaanyɛ asaa enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ nɔ.

english: What is eating holes into the central leaves of my young corn crops and leaving sawdust-like waste?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni eshiɔ ŋmeii yɛ sɛɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a major pest for maize in Ghana. They hide inside the central funnel of the plant, and applying approved insecticides or dropping neem leaf extract or clean wood ash into the funnel early in the infestation can kill them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei titri ni fiteɔ ŋmei yɛ Ghana lɛ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli. Ni kɛ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii loo akɛ neem baa mli nu ni he tse loo tso mli sũ awo tsɔne lɛ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko je shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbe amɛ.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often brought on by irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist through regular watering and mulching helps the plant take up calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium ni sa.

english: How do I choose the best plantain suckers to transplant to a new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo shikpɔŋ hee nɔ?

english: Look for 'sword suckers,' which have narrow, blade-like leaves and a large bulbous base at the bottom. Avoid 'water suckers' that have broad leaves early on, as sword suckers grow faster, establish stronger roots, and produce heavier bunches.
ga: Taomɔ ‘sword shoot’ ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ ŋmei kɛ shishitoo agbo ko ni tamɔ bulbous yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ‘nu tso’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ he mra. Ejaakɛ klante lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ baadara oya. Tsɔɔmɔ shishifãi ni wa ni ofee tsei ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ

english: Why do I need to clear bushes and weeds away from the base of my crops regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi kɛjɛ mitsei lɛ ashishi daa lɛ?

english: Weeds and tall wild bushes compete with your crops for light, soil nutrients, and water. Keeping the field clear prevents weeds from choking your plants and reduces hideouts for snakes, rodents, and destructive insects.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ koo mli tsei bibii ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni okɛ nu awo onibii amli Kɛ́ oha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaatsi jwɛi anaa koni amɛkafite onibii lɛ. ni ajie hei ni onufui, ŋmeii, kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ shi.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun, improves air flow, and prevents fungal diseases from spreading across the leaves.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulb agboi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa baa lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, drought stress, or an excess of nitrogen fertilizer. Ensuring the soil stays moist during hot spells and avoiding over-fertilization helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. hɔmɔ he haomɔ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa Ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni okɛbaafata he koni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii lɛ he.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot during the wet rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Black Pod disease is caused by a water-loving fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and heavy shade. Pruning overhead tree branches to let in sunlight, removing infected pods immediately, and applying recommended copper fungicides help protect your yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni afoɔ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ni akɔɔble tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct heat and heavy sunlight. Their leaves lose water much faster than their young roots can drink, so keeping shade trees or planting plantains protects them from burning and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ anu. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen nutrient. When the plant is hungry, it moves the little nitrogen it has from its old bottom leaves up to its new growing leaves at the top to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ hɔmɔ ye tso ko lɛ, ejieɔ nitrogen fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ ebaai momo lɛ amli kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni ehi shi.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my field make my maize crop grow better in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have friendly tiny organisms in their roots that grab nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a natural fertilizer for crops you plant afterwards.
ga: Nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii amli. Naanyobɔɔ damɔ eshishijee nɔ. Etsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the soil stays full of water for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nu yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like human beings do. When heavy rain leaves standing water in the soil, air cannot reach the cassava roots, causing them to drown, die, and rot.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu kpɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni haa amɛshwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboiɔ

english: Why do my yam plants need tall sticks to climb up before they can produce big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa niji ni kwɔlɔ koni enyɛ ekwɔ dani ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb high so their leaves can spread out to swallow maximum sunlight. Sunlight is what the leaves use to manufacture the food that goes down into the ground to build large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni amɛŋɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la ji nɔ ni baai lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii ni yaa shikpɔŋ ni efeɔ bulb agboi.

english: Why do small armyworms always hide deep inside the funnel of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: The central funnel of a young maize plant is the softest and most nutritious part for the worm to eat, and hiding deep inside also protects it from hot sun rays and predators.
ga: Abɛi tso bibioo ko teŋgbɛ nu lɛ ji he ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ ni niyenii yɔɔ mli fe fɛɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ. Ni kɛ́ akɛtee emli shɔŋŋ lɛ hu buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming any tomatoes when the weather becomes extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato plants go into survival mode to save water and energy. They drop their flowers because they cannot support forming heavy fruits under severe heat stress.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ yaa wala shihilɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Amɛshwie fɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwie shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii ni anáa lɛ. yɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ ni naa wa shishi

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when the fruit bunch becomes big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains do not have deep timber roots; they have shallow surface roots. When the heavy bunch forms, the top part becomes very heavy, making wind easily pull the shallow roots out of wet, soft soil.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Beni ŋmeii lɛ amli shwereɔ lɛ, ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ feɔ mlɛo waa, ni no haa ewaa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baagbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I pinch off extra side branches from my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Removing extra unwanted branches forces the plant to send all its food and water directly to growing bigger and healthier pepper fruits instead of feeding useless stems.
ga: Niji ni ataooo lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ eniyenii kɛ nu lɛ fɛɛ aya pepper tso ko ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha lɛ ŋmeii ni he ehiaaa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and yield very small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the plant food, water, and sunlight that your main crops need to grow strong. When weeds overcrowd your farm, your crops end up starving and underperforming.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ tsei aniyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ he hiaa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ jwɛi ha oŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo muji tsɔ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye hɔmɔ ni amɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains soak the soil and fill up the air spaces around roots. Without air, roots cannot breathe and easily get infected by soil fungi and bacteria that cause tuber rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũuɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ eyiɔ obɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli kɛ helai ni haa ŋmeii fiteɔ lɛ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up toward the sun, allowing the plant to catch more light and turn it into food, which leads to much larger tubers underground.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ akwɛ hulu la lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa tsei naa la babaoo ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ niyenii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji babaoo baa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong, direct sunlight because heat causes them to lose water faster than their roots can take it up, burning the leaves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ haa nu lɛ laajeɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baa shãa

english: Why should I cut off extra suckers growing around my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra suckers steal food, water, and sunlight from the main stem. Keeping only two or three strong suckers ensures the main plant produces large, heavy bunches.
ga: Suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ahiɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why should I avoid cutting too many green leaves when harvesting oil palm bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo ni mifoɔ lɛ he beni mikpaa mu tsei akui lɛ?
