english: Green leaves produce the plant's food using sunlight. Removing too many healthy fronds weakens the palm and reduces the number of palm bunches it will produce next season.
ga: Baai eŋɔli lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la nɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ehaa panicles ni baajɛ mli aba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ baa shi.

english: Yellowing starting from the tip of lower maize leaves is a sign of nitrogen deficiency; the plant is pulling nitrogen from older leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Abɛi baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tso lɛ miigbala nitrogen kɛmiijɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cowpea plants make the soil healthier for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have friendly bacteria living on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ naanyobɔɔ helai ni hiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my young maize plants develop pale yellow stripes along their leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn plant lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow stripes are a common sign of Maize Streak Virus, which is spread by tiny insects called leafhoppers that suck sap from plant to plant.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ Maize Streak Virus, ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he. Atsɛɔ amɛ leafhoppers ni nuɔ tso kome mli nu lɛ kɛyaa ekroko mli.

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during extreme heat and dryness as a natural response to protect themselves and reduce water loss through the leaf surface.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hetoo ni amɛkɛbuɔ amɛhe he ni amɛhaa nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep falling off without forming any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which prevents the flowers from forming fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. ni tsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkawo yibii

english: Why is it good for me to plant plantains next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide gentle shade and keep moisture in the soil, protecting your young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo blɛoo ni amɛhiɛɔ sũ lɛ mli nu. Buu o-cocoa bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and fall off when the dry Harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry weather to save water stored inside their stems and roots. The plant is not dead; as soon as the rains return, it will grow new leaves and continue growing its tubers underground.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu ni buaa ehe naa yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ he. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ kɛkɛ Ebaakwɛ baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will restore their green color and increase your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I harvest more corn from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani minyɛŋ makpa ŋmãa babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close together makes the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak stalks and tiny cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough food to produce big, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: What is causing small green caterpillars to eat the center leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which feed on the tender young leaves inside the shoot. Checking your farm early and applying neem leaf extract or recommended sprays to the center of the plants will protect them before they are destroyed.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ awo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu ŋmɔ lɛ he dani efite.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my pepper plants with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out the dirt, keeps the root area cool, and prevents weeds from sprouting around your crops.
ga: Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight in and removing the infected black pods from the farm helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Nibii krokomɛi ni abaakpa koni hulu la babaoo abote mli kɛ ŋmeii diji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ akpa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeee amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil lacks steady water. Water your plants regularly at the roots and avoid letting the soil dry out completely while they are flowering.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu faaa be fɛɛ be. Ha tso lɛ nu yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe daa ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha egbi kwraa beni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ he.

english: How do I know that my yams are fully mature and ready to dig up from the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni sweet potatoes lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When the yam vines and leaves start turning yellow and drying up naturally at the end of the season, it means the plant has finished growing and has stored all its energy into the tuber underground.
ga: Beni sweet potato wain tsei kɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ edara ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than the cassava and maize I intentionally planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni mito gbɛjianɔ akɛ madu lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants that naturally adapt to survive in local soil, so they quickly drink up water and fertilizer intended for your crops. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks gives your crops the advantage they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji maŋ lɛ mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ jɛmɛ shikpɔji lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ onibii amli lɛ oya. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and curling up into strange shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellow and twisted leaves on cassava are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems provided by the agricultural office helps keep your farm healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ baa. Kooloi bibii eyɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ kɛhaa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni oŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot right on the tree during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Black pod is a disease caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, damp, and overly shaded conditions. Pruning excess shade tree branches and picking off infected pods keeps the air dry and stops the rot from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ fe nine. Niji ni yɔɔ shade ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli agbi ni ebaaha ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: I see small caterpillars hiding inside the leaves of my young maize and eating holes through them; what are they doing?
ga: Mina ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-babi corn baai lɛ amli ni amɛmiitsɔ mli amɛmiiye bu. Mɛni amɛfeɔ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms that feed on the soft, young leaf shoots inside the central funnel of the plant. Applying recommended treatments or neem water directly into the center of the leaves early in the morning destroys them before they kill the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii loo neem nu lɛ wo tsei lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaagbe tsei lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why is my maize growing very tall with broad green leaves, but producing tiny cobs with few grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ? Shi ŋmei bibioo ko yɛ. No ji dumɔwui fioo pɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer without enough phosphorus and potassium, the plant puts all its energy into growing tall leaves instead of making fruits. Using a balanced fertilizer mix ensures the plant puts energy into forming large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ ni phosphorus kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai kakadaji moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni ja tsu nii lɛ, ehaa tsei kɛ hewalɛ woɔ mli koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before any fruit begins to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or sudden changes from dry to wet soil. Watering your crops regularly at the roots and providing light shade during extremely hot afternoons keeps the flowers on the stem so fruits can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa loo tsakemɔ trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ oofɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe daa, ni oooha amɛ hulutsoo yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ koni anyɛ awo yibii.

english: Why do my hot pepper leaves look burnt and dry after I water them in the middle of a sunny day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã ni egbi beni mikɛ nu wo amɛmli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Watering under bright sunlight leaves water droplets on the leaves that act like small magnifying glasses, burning the leaves. It is best to water early in the morning or late in the evening so the plant absorbs the water without damaging its leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ glase bibii ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo, ni shãa baai lɛ. Okɛ nu awo mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ ni efiteee baai lɛ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger yield from my small land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Ani minɔ ni?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water, resulting in weak plants and tiny ears. Proper spacing gives every single plant enough food and light to produce big, healthy ears.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli, ni no haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ toi bibii. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ baaha tsei fɛɛ aná niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛfee toi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do farmers plant plantain suckers right beside young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn and die easily under harsh afternoon sunshine. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, sheltering the young cocoa with shade and moisture until it grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Okɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aha kookoo tso lɛ nɔ kɛyashi ebaada waa bɔ ni sa.

english: How can I tell if my farmland has lost its strength and needs fertilizer or a rest period?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔi lɛ ahewalɛ miiho ni ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo hejɔɔmɔ awo mli?

english: When soil becomes weak, crop leaves turn pale yellow, plants grow slowly, and tough weeds like spear grass begin to take over. Planting cover crops like cowpeas or groundnuts helps restore natural food and strength back into the soil.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ Tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Tso lɛ daa blɛoo. ni jwɛi ni wa tamɔ akpɔlɔ jwɛi jeɔ shishi eyeɔ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ hewalɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Does planting a very large seed yam guarantee that I will harvest a giant yam tuber?
ga: Ani sweet potato dumɔwui wuji waa ni aduɔ lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ abaakpa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji?

english: Harvest size depends more on loose, deep soil mounds and adequate rain than the size of the seed. A medium-sized healthy seed yam planted in rich, soft soil will yield a large tuber because the roots can easily expand.
ga: Nikpamɔ dalɛ damɔ sũ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni fa fe dumɔwui lɛ dalɛ nɔ. Atomɔ mli dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɔ lɛ baawo ŋmeii wuji ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo.

english: What is the best type of oil palm tree to plant if I want to start a commercial farm in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ mu tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ madu kɛji miisumɔ ni mabɔi jarayeli ŋmɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: For commercial palm oil production, the Tenera hybrid variety is the best choice. It is a specially bred cross between two palm types designed to produce much more oil per bunch than traditional local varieties.
ga: Kɛha tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ, Tenera hybrid lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Eji tso krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛfee ŋmei tsei henɔi enyɔ ni afee koni ekɛ mu babaoo aba yɛ kuu kome mli fe blema tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: What is the main difference between the wild palm trees in my bush and the hybrid ones sold at agriculture centers?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ mi ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ kɛ tsei ni akɛfee tsofai krokomɛi ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ okwaayeli hei lɛ ateŋ?

english: Wild local palm trees usually have thick shells with thin fruit flesh and take up to 7 years to produce. Hybrid palm trees like Tenera have thin shells, very thick oil-rich flesh, and begin producing fruit much faster, usually in about 3 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse kɛ aduawai ni mli edɔ ni amɛheɔ afii 7 dani amɛwoɔ. Tso ni ji hybrid tamɔ Tenera lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tseee. Fɔ babaoo yɛ loo lɛ mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ waa. Ni ebɔi yibiiwoo oya kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee afii 3.

english: What makes the Tenera palm variety so popular for palm oil production?
ga: Mɛni haa Tenera tso lɛ he gbɛi waa kɛha tso lɛ mli fɔ feemɔ?

english: Tenera is popular because of its fruit structure. It has a thin shell around the nut and a very thick layer of outer pulp, which gives a much higher yield of palm oil compared to other palm types.
ga: Tenera ji nɔ ko ni ehe gbɛi waa yɛ bɔ ni amɛyibii lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ hewɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmei bibioo ko ni bɔleɔ ŋmei lɛ he, ni eyɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni mli tse waa. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmei fɔ babaoo fe ŋmei henɔi krokomɛi.

english: Can I just pick seeds from my neighbor's high-yielding palm tree and plant them on my land?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafolɔ dumɔwui yɛ mikutsoŋnyo tɛŋ tso ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting seeds saved directly from a hybrid tree will not produce the same high quality. The offspring will split into mixed varieties, many of which will yield thick shells or low oil. You should always buy certified hybrid seedlings from licensed nurseries.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haŋ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ tamɔ nɛkɛ aba. Abaajara seshibii lɛ amli afee hybrids. Henɔi babaoo baaha ŋmeii ni mli wa loo fɔ fioo aba. Esa akɛ ohe hybrid dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do some oil palm trees produce thick hard nuts with very little oil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmeii ni mu fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: That depends on the palm variety. The traditional 'Dura' variety naturally grows a thick shell around a small nut with thin pulp, meaning most of the fruit's energy goes into making a hard shell instead of producing palm oil.
ga: Kɛjɛ tso lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, blema ‘Dura’ tso lɛ feɔ ŋmei ni mli tse ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ he. Nut bibioo lɛ yɛ loo ni mli tse yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni tsɔɔ akɛ aduawai lɛ ahewalɛ babaoo yaa ŋmei ni wa lɛ feemɔ mli moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmei fɔ.

english: Why is it better to pay for certified palm seedlings instead of transplanting young wild palms from the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaawo ŋmei dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ he nyɔmɔ moŋ fe ni abaadu tsei bibii ni jɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Wild seedlings taken from the bush have unknown genetics and usually yield low amounts of oil after waiting many years. Certified hybrid seedlings guarantee fast growth and maximum oil production for market sale.
ga: Koo mli dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ bɛ fɔmɔ nii ni aleee, ni bei pii lɛ, amɛwoɔ mu fioo ko yɛ afii babaoo ni amɛmɛ sɛɛ. Hybrid dumɔwui ni aŋmala he odaseyeli lɛ haa amɛdaraa oya ni amɛnáa mu babaoo ni akɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ.

english: How many years do I have to wait after planting a hybrid palm tree before I can harvest fruits?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko du ŋmei tso ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ emɛ dani enyɛ ekpa enɔ yibii lɛ?

english: With good farm management and proper soil care, hybrid palm trees like Tenera start bearing fruits within 2.5 to 3 years after field planting, compared to local wild palms which can take 5 to 7 years.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akwɛ ŋmɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Hybrid palm tsei tamɔ Tenera lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2.5 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ. Enɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli koo mli tsei ni baanyɛ ahé afii 5 kɛyashi 7 lɛ toɔ he.

english: Does a hybrid palm tree produce both palm oil for cooking and kernel oil from the nut?
ga: Ani ŋmei tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jieɔ ŋmei fɔ ni akɛhooɔ nii kɛ ŋmei ŋmei mli fɔ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, hybrid palms produce both. The thick outer reddish flesh provides palm oil for cooking, while the small nut inside contains the kernel used to extract palm kernel oil.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ woɔ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Loo ni mli tse ni tsuɔ yɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ ji ŋmei fɔ ni akɛhooɔ nii. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei bibioo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli dumɔwui ni ajieɔ ŋmei mli fɔ lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: How long will a hybrid oil palm tree continue to give me fruit after I plant it?
ga: Be enyiɛ mi hybrid oil palm tso lɛ baawo yibii beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: A properly cared for Tenera hybrid oil palm tree will remain commercially productive for 25 to 30 years, providing consistent harvests every few weeks throughout its lifetime.
ga: Tenera hybrid oil palm tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaya nɔ awo yibii yɛ jarayeli mli afii 25 kɛyashi 30, ni ebaaha ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa nɔ daa afi lɛ aba. otsii fioo komɛi yɛ ewala be fɛɛ mli

english: Can I grow commercial hybrid palm trees anywhere in Ghana, or do they need specific regions?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsei ni akɛfee jarayeli nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yɛ Ghana he fɛɛ he? loo kpokpaa pɔtɛɛ ko he miihia

english: Commercial oil palms need consistent rainfall and warmth, so they grow best in the forest and transition zones of southern and central Ghana, such as the Western, Central, Eastern, and Ashanti regions.
ga: Palm oil ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ biɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo. No hewɔ lɛ, ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooi kɛ tsakemɔ hei ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ kɛ teŋgbɛ tamɔ Anaigbɛ, Teŋgbɛ, Bokagbɛ kɛ Ashanti kpokpai lɛ amli.

english: Is it safe for me to mix two different farm chemicals together in one tank to save time when spraying?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai enyɔ baafutu yɛ tanki kome mli koni mikɛ be akafite yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he?

english: Mixing chemicals without proper guidance can cause dangerous reactions that burn your crop leaves or destroy the effectiveness of the chemicals entirely.
ga: Tsofai ni okɛfutuɔ ni gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ni sa bɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aha nɔ ko ni yɔɔ oshara aba ni baashã otso lɛ baai loo efite tsofa lɛ nitsumɔ kwraa.

english: What should I do with leftover chemical spray in my tank after I finish treating my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni eshwɛ yɛ tanki lɛ mli beni mikɛtsa ŋmɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should never store mixed chemicals for another day because they lose their strength quickly and can damage your sprayer or poison the soil if dumped in one spot.
ga: Esaaa akɛ okɛ tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ toɔ gbi kroko ejaakɛ amɛhewalɛ baaje mli oya. ni ebaanyɛ efite tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ loo ekɛ poison awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ yɛ he kome.

english: Can spraying my fruit trees during the hot afternoon sun damage the crops?
ga: Ani mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ni mikɛshwieɔ amɛnɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, high afternoon heat causes the liquid to evaporate quickly, leaving concentrated chemical residue that can scorch leaves and flowers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shwane mli la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu shwieɔ oya. Eshiɔ tsofai ni eshwɛ ni baanyɛ ashã baai kɛ fɔfɔii lɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds and fallen rotting fruits from under my fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛ aduawai ni egboi kɛjɛ aduawai tsei ashishi lɛ?

english: Cleaning under your trees removes hiding places for pests and harmful fungi that can easily climb back up to infect healthy leaves and fruit.
ga: Tsei ashishi ni asaa he lɛ jieɔ hei ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni baanyɛ akwɔ kɛku amɛsɛɛ oya koni amɛyawo baai kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why does trimming dead or overcrowded branches help my tree produce bigger fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baaye abua mitso lɛ ni ewo yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Trimming allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the inner parts of the tree while directing energy away from dead wood into producing larger fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ mlifomɔ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni egboi amli koni ewo yibii wuji.

english: Why do my mango flowers drop off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers often fall because tiny pests or fungal infections attack them at early flowering, which can be prevented with properly timed crop protection sprays.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ahewɔ. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ tutuaa fɔfɔii yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ jeɔ shishi mra lɛ. Abaanyɛ atsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do dark spots appear on the skin of my fruit while it is still growing on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi yibii lɛ anɔ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Dark spots are usually caused by fungal diseases that spread during rainy conditions, requiring protective spraying early in the fruit's development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji baa. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ tsofa abu he mra. yɛ aduawai ahe nitsumɔ mli

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are changing color because of disease or because of poor soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii hewɔ ni mitso lɛ baai lɛ etsake lɛ?

english: Pest or disease damage usually appears as spots, holes, or patches, while nutrient problems from soil usually cause even yellowing across whole leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai fiteɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ ŋmeii, bu, loo ŋmeii, yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii he naagbai haa baai muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How long do I need to wait to harvest my fruits after spraying them with chemicals?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai wo mihe lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani makpa aduawai lɛ?

english: Every chemical has a specific waiting period, usually 7 to 14 days, allowing the medicine time to break down so the food is safe to eat.
ga: Tsofai fɛɛ yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛmɛɔ, bei pii lɛ gbii 7 kɛyashi 14, dani tsofa lɛ fiteɔ koni efee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ayeɔ.

english: Why do I need to spray my mango trees even when they look healthy and show no sickness?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afɔ mango tsei anɔ tsofa yɛ be mli ni mango lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ ni hela he okadi ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Preventive spraying protects healthy crops before invisible pests and diseases strike, saving your yield before damage actually happens.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe dani tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni anaaa lɛ baatutua amɛ. Ye obua ni okwɛ onibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ dani nɔ ko ni fiteɔ diɛŋtsɛ aba.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when I cut down all the large trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need shade, especially when they are young, because strong direct sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the soil. Keeping shade trees protects the cocoa plants from excessive heat and helps keep the ground moist.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ hia hulutsoo. Titri lɛ, beni tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo ha kookoo tso lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means your soil lacks nitrogen. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help the maize regain a healthy dark green color and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa, ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔji ni mli wa.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water sits around them for too long without draining. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to run off, protecting the roots from waterlogging.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ efooo Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ atsɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he.

english: Is it really necessary for me to tie my yam vines onto tall wooden poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ akpɛtɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko he moŋ fe ni mahã egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ?

english: Lifting yam vines onto tall stakes keeps the leaves spread out so they can catch more sunlight. More sunlight allows the plant to produce more energy, leading to much larger yam tubers at harvest time.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni hulu la babaoo aba amɛnɔ. Hulu la babaoo yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ wuji babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather becomes too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Giving your plants consistent moisture and placing dry grass around the roots keeps the soil cool and stops blossom drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Ni aaaha tso lɛ mli ajɔ daa ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo ehe Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Black pod is a disease caused by a tiny fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and dark conditions. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight reach the trunk and removing black pods quickly stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pods ji hela ko ni ŋmei bibioo ko kɛbaa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni afeɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ tso lɛ shishi, ni ajie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ lɛ oya lɛ baaha hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ akpa.

english: Spreading dry grass, called mulching, prevents weeds from growing by blocking sunlight from weed seeds. It also acts like a blanket, trapping moisture in the soil so you don't need to water as often.
ga: Hay ni aduɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ ni tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii hu tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu afɔ nɔ shii abɔ.

english: Why is it a bad idea for me to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ makwɛ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific nutrients from the soil and lets maize-loving pests build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni oha kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ.

english: Why do I see small chewed holes in my young corn leaves and tiny caterpillars hiding inside the center shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Abɛi bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni ayeɔ. Akɛtee teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which target young corn leaves. Spraying recommended bio-pesticides or applying neem leaf extract early in the morning when plants are cool will destroy the pests before they kill the plant.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ shwie nɔ loo okɛ neem baa mli nu tsu nii leebi be mli ni tso lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ, ebaakpata kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛgbe tso lɛ.

english: Leaving too many small shoots forces them to steal nutrients and water from the main plantain tree. Pruning them so only one or two strong shoots remain allows the main plant to yield a larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: ŋmeii bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ Kɛ́ afee babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛ ŋmeii titrii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ dara ni tsii yɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ.

english: When the lower leaves turn yellow in a V-pattern starting from the tip, your soil is usually running low on nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to build green leaves and grow tall, so adding decomposed manure or a nitrogen-based fertilizer will restore their bright green color.
ga: Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, nitrogen ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba ni ekwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni egbo loo ŋmeii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans on my plot help other crops grow better afterwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua tsei krokomɛi ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to a plant family that pulls nitrogen gas out of the air and stores it in their roots. When the plant harvest is done and the roots decompose, that captured nitrogen stays in the soil as free, natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas fata tsei aweku ko ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ he. Kɛji akpa tso lɛ ni eshishifãi lɛ fite Nitrogen ni aŋɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko, ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the small pods on my cocoa trees turn black and dry up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives when the farm stays too cool, dark, and wet. Clearing weeds around the tree bases and cutting away overcrowded branches lets sunlight and air dry out the pods and reduce the disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ ŋmɔji amli ejɔ tsɔ, eyɛ duŋ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ajiemɔ Tso lɛ shishi kɛ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ. Enɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni helai aba shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling upwards and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Wrinkled or upward-curling pepper leaves are usually a sign that tiny invisible pests like thrips or mites are sucking sap from the leaf undersides. Spraying the leaves with clean water mixed with wood ash or neem leaf extract can help deter these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baa ni egbɔjɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ahe okadi. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ thrips loo mites Nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ nuɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli tse ni akɛ tso sũ loo neem tso mli nu efutu mli lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ekɛtsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rainfall fills up all the space in flat land, the roots drown and rot, so planting your cassava stems on top of raised earth mounds or ridges allows extra water to run off safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi. No hewɔ lɛ, aduɔ ŋmeii tsei yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ koni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do seeds take so much longer to sprout when planted in hard, dry ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need to absorb water to break open their tough outer skin and start growing. If the soil is dry and packed hard, water cannot get inside the seed easily, and the soft young shoot struggles to push up through the crust.
ga: Ehe miihia ni dumɔwui lɛ aŋɔ nu koni amɛgbala amɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ni wa lɛ mli ni amɛbɔi dalɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ Nu nyɛŋ abote dumɔwui lɛ amli mlɛo. Ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do flowers drop off my tomato plants without turning into tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛtsakeee amɛhe amɛfeɔ tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme afternoon heat stresses tomato plants and dries out the pollen inside the blossoms, preventing fruit from forming. Mulching around the plants with dry grass keeps the soil cool and helps retain ground moisture.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ egbiɔ. Etsiɔ aduawai anaa koni amɛkafee Mulching tsei ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi woɔ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do groundnut plants flower above the ground but form their nuts underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shi ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: After a groundnut flower is pollinated, it grows a long stem called a peg that bends downward and burrows directly into the soil. The nut then swells and matures underground where it is protected from sun and pests.
ga: Beni afee ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ sɛɛ lɛ Eyɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ peg ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishi ni efoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fũuɔ ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi he ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Yam tubers are ready for harvesting when the leafy vines above ground stop growing green and naturally dry up to a brownish color. This shows the plant has moved all its energy into feeding the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni wain tsei ni baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛyashɛɔ adebɔɔ mli su ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ eshi ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛtee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when strong winds blow during the rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that spread outwards rather than deep down, making them top-heavy when carrying a heavy bunch. Supporting the main stem with a sturdy wooden prop pole prevents wind from tipping the tree over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kponɔgbɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeya shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛhe feɔ tsiimɔ kɛ́ amɛmiitere tsɔne ni tsii. Tso lɛ mli tsei ni wa ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers and stop fruiting during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need steady moisture to keep flowers and young pods growing. During dry spells, the tree sheds them to save water and keep itself alive, which is why artificial watering or irrigation helps keep cocoa producing continuously.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃ fɔfɔii kɛ amɛbii bibii. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛhetsɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛha amɛhi wala mli. Enɛ hewɔ ni nu ni akɛfee loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa koni aná kookoo ni yaa nɔ lɛ.

english: Can I irrigate my cocoa farm, or does cocoa only rely on rain to grow well?
ga: Ani manyɛ mawo mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu? Aloo ani kookoo damɔ nugbɔ pɛ nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: While cocoa has traditionally relied on rainfall, using irrigation during dry months keeps the soil moist, prevents leaf drying, and allows trees to produce more pods throughout the year.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kookoo damɔ nugbɔshiimɔ nɔ moŋ, Shi nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How will getting electricity in my village help me become a better crop farmer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ sarawa hewalɛ ni akɛhaa mi akrowa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni matsɔ okwaafonyo kpakpa?

english: Electricity allows you to power water pumps for farm irrigation, operate processing machines like cocoa pod breakers or drying equipment, and keep produce safe after harvest.
ga: La haa onyɛɔ okɛ nu pɔmpii tsuɔ nii kɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ mli nu. Kɛ tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ kookoo podi ajiemɔ loo nibii ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ atsu nii. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ

english: What kind of machine support can extension services or Cocobod help me get for my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ tsɔne he yelikɛbuamɔ manyɛ maha koni eye ebua ni mikɛ Cocobod nitsumɔi lɛ aya miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Agricultural extension services and Cocobod provide access to motorized spraying machines, motorized weed cutters, and irrigation pumping units that reduce heavy manual labor and speed up farm maintenance.
ga: Okwaayeli He Nitsumɔhei kɛ Cocobod haa anyɛɔ ashɛɔ tsɔnei ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ ahe. Motor ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi kɛ nu shwiemɔ pɔmp ni haa nitsumɔ ni tsii baa shi ni ehaa ŋmɔ mli saamɔ yaa oya.

english: Why shouldn't I wait until my cocoa trees look sick before buying chemicals to spray them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mimɛɔ ni cacao tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ dani mihe tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pests like capsids and fungal diseases like black pod attack quietly before you see severe damage. Regular preventive spraying protects the farm early, saving you money compared to trying to cure a destroyed crop.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids kɛ fungal helai tamɔ black pods lɛ tutuaa amɛ dioo. Dani obaana nɔ ni efite waa lɛ Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni tsiɔ hela naa daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔji ahe mra. Enɛ haa okɛ shika baa shi kɛ akɛto bɔ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite lɛ ato he lɛ he.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in excess shade and wet conditions. Pruning overhanging branches, clearing weeds, and applying protective sprays keep the pods healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nine kɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni etse amɛhe lɛ, ojie jwɛi lɛ, ni okɛ tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I afford expensive farm inputs like fertilizer if I cannot pay all the money at once?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahe nibii ni jara wa tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni kɛji akɛ minyɛɛɛ mawo fɛɛ shikome hu?

english: Many agricultural support initiatives and cooperatives allow farmers to acquire inputs early and pay in small installments over time or after selling their harvest, so you don't have to wait to care for your farm.
ga: Okwaayeli he yelikɛbuamɔ gbɛjianɔtoi kɛ nitsumɔhe nine babaoo yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛnáa nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mra. ni owo nyɔmɔ bibii yɛ be mli loo yɛ nibii ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni omɛ dani okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I reach out to government extension services to get help for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matswa nɔyeli lɛ extension service lɛ adafi koni maná yelikɛbuamɔ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: You can connect with your local district agricultural officer or join a local farmers' cooperative, as extension officers visit organized groups to offer advice, seedlings, and government support projects.
ga: Obaanyɛ oya okpokpaa nɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ loo okɛ ohe awo okwaafoi akuu ko mli. Enɛ ji akɛ, sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ nitsulɔi lɛ baasara kui ni ato amɛ shishi lɛ koni amɛha ŋaawoo, dumɔwui kɛ nɔyeli yelikɛbuamɔ nitsumɔi.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is starving and needs fertilizer for my cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni akɛdu kookoo?

english: When soil lacks nutrients, cocoa leaves turn yellow, tree growth slows down, and pods remain small or fall off early. Applying the right cocoa fertilizer restores the soil balance so the trees produce heavy pods.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ, Cocoa baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Tsei lɛ daa blɛoo fe tsutsu lɛ. ni ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo loo amɛgbeeɔ shi oya Kookoo ŋmeii ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ naa ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why do young cocoa plants need shade trees, but mature cocoa trees seem to need more sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ? Shi etamɔ nɔ ni hulu la babaoo he miihia kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under harsh sunlight. As the tree grows older and stronger, it needs more light to manufacture food and produce cocoa pods.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Beni tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ lɛ Ehe miihia la babaoo hu koni ekɛ niyenii aba ni ekɛ kookoo ŋmeii aba.

english: Which direction should I face cassava cuttings when putting them in the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ekwɛ?

english: Always plant cassava stems with the small growth buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the shoots struggle to grow upwards, resulting in weak plants and tiny tuber yield.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji okɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ shwie shi lɛ Ebaafee nɔ ni wa akɛ oookwɛ tsei lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off because of extreme heat or lack of water in the soil. When the weather gets too hot, the flower cannot produce pollen properly, so the plant sheds the flower to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee pollen jogbaŋŋ. Kɛkɛ lɛ tsei jieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: What is making holes in my maize leaves and leaving dark dirt inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmãa baa lɛ mli ewo bu ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ baa lɛ mli?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide deep inside the growing center of the maize plant to eat young leaves, and the dark dirt you see is their waste.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Ni muji ni tsuɔ waa ni onaa lɛ ji amɛ jwɛi.

english: Leaf curl is caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies that sit under the leaves and suck the sap. As they feed, they weaken the leaves and can spread tiny plant sicknesses that cause the leaves to wrinkle.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni taraa baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii Amɛhaa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ tsei bibii ahe helai amɛshwã. No baanyɛ aha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellow leaves mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food for green leaf growth. It can also happen when heavy rain washes plant food away or leaves roots drowning in excess water.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji tsei aniyenii titri kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ jieɔ tsei lɛ amli niyenii loo ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine mli.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or straw, known as mulching, acts like a blanket. It protects the soil from hot sun, keeps water from drying out quickly, and blocks weeds from growing.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ akagbi oya. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Cereal crops like maize pull food out of the soil, but legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, naturally replacing lost plant food for your next crop.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa mli, tamɔ ŋmãa, gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii, tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ekɛ tso niyenii ni elaaje lɛ yeɔ najiaŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my harvested yams soft and rotting in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ efee blɛoo ni egbo yɛ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are cut or bruised during harvest, or if they are stored in a hot room without fresh air. Wounds let germs enter, while heat and moisture cause fungi to grow fast.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ loo atswa yɛ kpamɔ be mli. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛwo tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli Pilamɔi haa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ boteɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dɔlɛ kɛ latsaa haa ŋmɔtɔ daa oya.

english: Why do my maize grains get small holes and powdery dust when stored in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ni ani sũ yɛ mli kɛ́ akɛto kotoku lɛ mli?

english: The holes and dust are caused by tiny insects called grain weevils. They eat into the dried seeds from the inside out, especially if the maize was not dried completely before being stored in bags.
ga: Kplukai bibii kɛ bu kɛ sũ baa. Atsɛɔ nakai dumɔwui lɛ. Amɛyeɔ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛwo kotoku lɛ mli.

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during dry spells to save water and stay alive. As long as the stem remains healthy, the plant is resting and will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi wala mli. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ yitso lɛ baahi shi shiŋŋ lɛ Tsei lɛ baajɔɔ amɛhe ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during extreme heat to reduce water loss from their leaf surfaces. It is the plant's natural way of protecting itself from drying out in direct sun.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ latsaa be mli koni nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed so many of their flowers before small pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo dani ŋmeii bibii baa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop extra flowers when they face stress from lack of water, poor soil nutrients, or insect pests. Maintaining proper shade and soil moisture helps the tree hold onto its flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi titri lɛ kɛ́ amɛkɛ nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ he haomɔ kpe. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant my yams on raised soil mounds instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil so their tuber roots can expand deep and wide. Raised mounds improve water drainage to prevent rot and make harvesting the mature tubers much easier.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia sweet potato koni tuber lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛmli alɛɛ. Gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ koni akafite ni ehaa ŋmeii ni eda lɛ akpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and release it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds the nearby maize plants and keeps the soil rich for future seasons.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do my young maize plants turn light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow maize leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient needed for green leaf growth. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will turn the leaves dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but produce no fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ebɛ yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants focus on making leaves instead of flowers when they get too much nitrogen fertilizer or lack full sunlight. Reducing heavy nitrogen and ensuring full sun encourages flowering and fruiting.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ yɛ baai ni amɛbaafee yɛ fɔfɔii najiaŋ lɛ he kɛ́ amɛná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo hulu la ni fa babaoo bɛ amɛhe. Nitrogen ni tsii lɛ ni abaaba shi ni akwɛ koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni eha fɔfɔi kɛ yibii aba.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and do not grow deep into the earth to hold the heavy trunk. Propping the stems up with wooden poles and protecting the roots from tiny soil pests keeps the trees standing.
ga: Plantain tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛkwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛkɛfi tso ni tsii lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ma shi, ni abu shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ sũ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔɔ shi.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot while still hanging on the trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads quickly in damp, shaded environments. Pruning excess branches to allow sunlight and airflow through the farm prevents the moisture that fungus needs to grow.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ naa.

english: Why are ragged holes showing up in the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by fall armyworm caterpillars eating the tender leaves. Checking the central funnel of the plant early and applying safe remedies prevents the pests from destroying the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbee shi ni amɛye baa bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa bibii amli lɛ baa. Tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe baatsu nii lɛ baatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops grow differently if I move my farm from a forest area to a dry transition zone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ kɛji mijie miŋmɔ lɛ kɛjɛ kooi amli kɛtee he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Forest areas have richer organic soil, higher humidity, and more shade, while transition zones have stronger sunlight, lower rainfall, and drier soils. Plants react to these differences in temperature and moisture, which changes how fast they grow and how much yield they give.
ga: Kooi amli hei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɔɔ mli babaoo. eyɛ hulutsoo be babaoo ni eyɛ hulutsoo be babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsakemɔ he lɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi Tsei lɛ hereɔ srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni haa shweremɔ lɛ yaa oya kɛ yibiiwoo enyiɛ?

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow and dry up faster during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When the sun is very intense and rainfall drops, plants lose water faster through their leaves than their roots can absorb from the dry soil. To survive the heat stress, the plant sheds older leaves to conserve moisture for its stem and roots.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ tso waa ni nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahi shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli lɛ, amɛshwieɔ baai momoi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛha amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops start producing flowers earlier than usual when there is a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi mra fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ kɛ́ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ eba lɛ?

english: When crops experience severe stress from lack of water or extreme heat, their natural instinct is to produce flowers and seeds quickly so they can reproduce before the plant potentially dies.
ga: Beni nu ni bɛ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa haa tsei haoɔ waa lɛ Amɛ adebɔɔ mli su ji ni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui oya koni amɛfɔ dani tso lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my maize plants stay small and yellowish even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall can wash away essential soil nutrients like nitrogen below the root level, or waterlogged soil can stop roots from breathing. Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is starving for nutrients despite having enough water.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ashishi lɛ. Aloo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha niyenii kpakpai eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ jɛmɛ moŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I burn the bush on my field before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani miduɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter and kills helpful soil organisms that break down nutrients for your crops. It also leaves the topsoil bare, making it easy for rain to wash away the good soil.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni fiteɔ niyenii ni haa oŋmɔshi nii lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ nugbɔ baafɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ.

english: Why do my crops perform poorly when I plant them on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the land time to recover, while allowing crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa jɛmɛ be ni ekɛtsa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it helpful to plant groundnuts or beans together with my cassava or maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei baafata ŋmei loo ŋmei he lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which naturally fertilizes neighboring crops like maize or cassava without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he.

english: Why do seeds I buy from certified dealers produce better yields than seeds I save from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred and selected for strong growth, high yield, and disease resistance, whereas saved seeds gradually lose those strong traits and become weaker over generations.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni ahalaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa, amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛnyɛŋ helai ana amɛ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baafee fiofio Efiteɔ nakai sui ni mli wa lɛ ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry stretch before the rainy season fully establishes. If the soil dries out after the seed absorbs the initial water, the seedling dies and rots inside the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi kwraa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi beni dumɔwui lɛ eŋɔ shishijee nu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do young tree crops need tall leafy plants around them during their first year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni tsei bibii ni yɔɔ baai kakadaji abɔle amɛhe yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young saplings have tender leaves and fragile root systems that burn easily under direct sunlight. Taller companion plants act as living umbrellas, giving them the needed shade and moisture to survive their early stage.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni waaa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Hefatalɔi tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa amɛnáa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee bei amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which acts as essential food for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the plants turn green and stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni no haa niyenii ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ adara. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool soil moisture it needs during its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them in the soil for too long during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away so the tubers stay dry enough to grow well.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the heat becomes too intense or when the plant suffers from inconsistent watering. Weather stress prevents the flower from setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi haaa fɔfɔi awo yibii.

english: No, planting too closely forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and resources to produce larger, healthier ears.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee toi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the center of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer to hide and feed on the tender young leaves inside the center whorl of corn plants. Treating them early with appropriate organic or chemical sprays protects the growing point of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ loo tsofa ni sa tsu amɛhe mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu he ni tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ he.

english: Why should I wait until the ground is moist before applying fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the roots can drink it up. Applying fertilizer on dry soil under hot sun can scorch the plant roots and waste your fertilizer.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: How do weeds harm my crops even if they are not touching each other?
ga: Te jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛtaaa amɛhe po?

english: Weed roots spread quickly underground and steal water and soil nutrients before your crop roots can reach them. This leaves your main crops weak and hungry even if they appear separate above ground.
ga: Jwɛi shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ kɛji akɛ amɛtse amɛhe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he po.

english: Why do my crops look pale and weak even though rains are falling heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash key nutrients deep down into the soil where roots cannot reach, or make the soil too soggy for roots to breathe. Adding organic compost helps hold nutrients in the topsoil.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Aloo ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Organic compost ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunshine to make food for the tubers underneath. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground toward the sun, which leads to bigger and healthier yam yields.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking kɛ baai lɛ baa ŋwɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants keep dying when the weather gets very sunny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under direct sunlight. Providing shade crops like plantain shields them from heat and keeps the soil moist until their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that plants need to build strong stems and healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly exhausts the specific nutrients that crop uses most and allows crop-specific pests and soil diseases to multiply in your field.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii fe fɛɛ lɛ afite. ni eye ebua tsei pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa lɛ babaoo yɛ oŋmɔji amli.

english: When heavy rain leaves standing water in the field, oxygen cannot reach the soil. Without air, root tissues suffocate and harmful fungal rot sets in.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifã lɛ mli fãji lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ boteɔ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants dry up and die even when I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gĩɔ ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much water causes root rot, a disease that destroys the roots so they can no longer suck up moisture, making the plant look dry and wilted.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ fe nine lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Eji hela ko ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe ŋmɔtɔ dɔŋŋ. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi ni egbo.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots near the surface and heavy fruit at the top, which makes them unstable during strong winds unless supported with wooden poles.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛ aduawai ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. ja tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves toward sunlight; more leaves catching light means the plant can produce larger, heavier tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Baai babaoo ni la tsɔɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I leave weeds in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ mishi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, fertilizer, and water away from your crops, leaving your plants weak and unable to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why are the leaves of my young corn plants covered in small holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ehà mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Holes in young corn leaves are typically caused by caterpillars like fall armyworms feeding on the tender foliage inside the plant's funnel.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ cutworms, ni egbee shi ni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu baa.

english: Extreme heat or sudden dry spells stress the tomato plant, causing it to drop flowers to save water and energy for its own survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Ha egbee shi koni ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why should I spray medicine on my farm trees even if I don't see any pests yet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ nu afɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ minako tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi lolo moŋ?

english: Spraying medicine creates a protective shield on your trees. It prevents hidden pests from entering the bark and stops diseases before they can infect and damage your crop.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni buɔ otsei lɛ ahe. Tsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote tso lɛ mli ni okpa helai dani amɛba oŋmɔshi nibii amli ni amɛfite.

english: How does chemical medicine actually help a sick tree recover from pest damage?
ga: Bɔ ni tsofai ni akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ amli

english: The medicine stops pests from continuing to attack the tree, allowing the tree to rest, heal its internal wounds, and direct its energy back into healthy growth.
ga: Tsofa lɛ baatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ anaa koni amɛkaya nɔ amɛtutua tso lɛ. Ye obua tso lɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe. Tsamɔ mligbɛ pilamɔi ni okɛ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ awo dalɛ kpakpa mli

english: How long should I wait to harvest my crop after spraying medicine on the trees?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You must wait a specific number of days according to the chemical instructions so the medicine has time to protect the crop and safely break down before you pick the produce.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ gbii babaoo taakɛ tsofa lɛ he gbɛtsɔɔmɔi lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsofa lɛ aha be ni ekɛbu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ni efite shweshweeshwe dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsu nii.

english: How can I tell if my trees are starting to recover after I treat them for pests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitsei lɛ miibɔi tsamɔ beni mikɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai etsa amɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Look closely at the branches for fresh green shoots sprouting, new clean leaves unfolding, and overall healthier bark without new insect holes.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ona tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni miikwɛ̃. baai heei ni he tse ni ŋshɔŋloo lɛ fɛɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni kooloi bibii heei bɛ mli.

english: Why do my tree leaves turn green and fresh again after I eliminate a pest infestation?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe feɔ ehee ekoŋŋ beni atsa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once pests stop sucking out nutrients, the tree can finally send water and plant food straight up from the roots to the leaves, giving them back their vibrant color and life.
ga: Kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kpa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ numɔ Tsei baanyɛ ajie nu ni amɛdu niyenii kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛya baai lɛ anɔ. Ha amɛfee fɛo ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is young, new growth on trees usually the first part to get damaged by insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, tso hee ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ji nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ lɛ?

english: New shoots and tender leaves are soft and full of fresh water and nutrients, making them the easiest and most appealing food source for pests.
ga: Tsofɔi heei kɛ baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni nu kpakpa kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ ni ŋɔɔ fe fɛɛ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why do insects try to bore inside the trunk and branches of my trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miitao ni amɛbote mitsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛniji amli lɛ?

english: Insects burrow into bark to lay their eggs and feed on the sap inside the wood, which blocks the tree from transporting food to its fruits.
ga: Kplukai shwieɔ tsei ahewolo mli koni amɛwo amɛwui ni amɛye nu ni anaa yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ kɛ niyenii aya eyibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crop trees stop producing good pods or fruits after insects attack them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii loo aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ feemɔ beni kooloi bibii etutua amɛ lɛ?

english: Pest attacks drain the tree of vital nutrients, leaving it too weak to form healthy flowers and support growing fruit.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ tsei anɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ jeɔ tsei amli. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni ekɛ fɔfɔi ni mli wa baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Will protecting my tree stems from pests give me a bigger harvest at the end of the season?
ga: Ani mitsei lɛ ahe ni mibuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ baaha maná ŋmaa babaoo yɛ be lɛ naagbee?

english: Yes, when trees do not waste energy fighting off pests, they can use all their food and water to grow more leaves and bigger, heavier fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, be mli ni tsei efiteee hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ amɛ niyenii kɛ nu lɛ fɛɛ atsu nii koni amɛkwɛ baai babaoo ni amɛdara ni amɛwo muji.

english: How frequently should I walk through my farm to check on the condition of my trees?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ bɔ ni tsei lɛ yɔɔ ha?

english: It is best to inspect your crops every week so you can spot early signs of pest damage or sickness before it spreads to the rest of your farm.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii amli daa otsi. Enɛ ji koni onyɛ ona okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ nɔ ko efite loo hela ni jɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ mra dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã hei krokomɛi. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct sunlight because their tender leaves lose water very quickly. Planting shade crops like plantains or cassava nearby creates a cool canopy that protects young cocoa from burning in the heat.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kookoo tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo be ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe koni amɛkashã yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Will planting my crops very close together give me a bigger harvest from my small plot of land?
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ he bibioo ko. mi nɔ loo daabi

english: No, planting seeds too close together forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong roots and produce larger yields.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa baakwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plants regain their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛ su ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to take quick advantage of soil moisture and nutrients before cultivated crops can. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing water and plant food away from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni afee amɛ bɔ ni sa koni amɛná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya dani tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nakai. Eliminating weeds early It will prevent them from stealing water and growing food from your crops.

english: It is best not to plant after the very first rain, as the ground underneath remains dry and hot. Wait until you have two or three steady rains so the soil holds enough deep moisture to keep germinating seeds alive.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ lolo. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔshiimɔi fioo komɛi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃.
