english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and look weak during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl in intense afternoon heat to reduce their surface area and prevent water loss. If they recover in the evening when temperatures cool down, it is a normal defense mechanism, though watering at the root helps reduce stress.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu ni elaaje lɛ naa. Kɛji akɛ ehiɛ ba ehe nɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ, abuɔ lɛ akɛ eji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shishitoo lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nɔnyɛɛ baa shi moŋ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, uneven watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Consistent watering and keeping the soil covered with dry leaves helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and stays around them for too long in heavy, poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa ni ebɔle amɛhe. Etsɛ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Which crops can I plant on a small piece of land to harvest and earn income within three months?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ madu yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ? koni akpa ni ana shika yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli

english: Short-cycle crops like vegetables (okra, garden eggs, pepper, tomatoes) and legumes (cowpeas) mature within two to three months, allowing you to harvest and sell quickly compared to long-term tree crops.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ aduawai (okra, abɔɔ mli ŋmei, ŋmei, tomato) kɛ ŋmei (cowpea) baakwɛ̃ yɛ nyɔji enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ni ohɔ̃ɔ oya kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: How can I store my harvested maize at home so insects do not destroy the grains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ ato shia? Bɔni afee ni kooloi akafite dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Insects thrive on moist grain, so drying your maize under the sun until the kernels are completely hard is the first key step. Storing the dry grain in airtight bags or clean, dry storage structures keeps pests out.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye yɛ dumɔwui ni mli efɔ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ ni oooha egbi kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ mli baawa kwraa lɛ ji klɛŋklɛŋ gbɛ ni he hiaa waa. Dumɔwui ni egbi ni akɛtoɔ vacuum kotokui amli loo he ko ni egbi ni he tse lɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli.

english: How can I store my harvested maize so it stays good for months without getting destroyed by insects?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato nyɔji babaoo ni ŋmeii efiteee lɛ?

english: Make sure your maize is completely dried under the sun until the grains are hard and crack when bitten. Storing them in airtight bags, like PICS bags, or sealed drums keeps oxygen out, which suffocates insects and prevents mold from spoiling your harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni oŋmãa lɛ agbi kwraa yɛ hulu lɛ shishi kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaatse kɛji akɛ okɛ amɛ ŋmɔ. Kɛ́ okɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli, tamɔ PICS kotoku mli, loo baagi ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni oxygen akabote mli. Enɛ baaha kooloo lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni otsi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ onibii lɛ anaa.

english: What can I do to keep my harvested yams from rotting in my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mi-sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ akafite yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli?

english: Yams rot quickly when exposed to moisture and heat. Keep them off the bare ground by storing them on raised wooden slatted shelves in a well-ventilated, shaded barn, and handle them carefully during harvest to avoid cuts where rot can enter.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ kɛ latsaa mli. Ha amɛkafee he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni oookɛto shɛlɛf ni awo nɔ ni akɛ tsei ewula nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. ni okɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli koni akafee pilamɔi ni baanyɛ afite.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by whiteflies, or it can be a reaction to extreme heat and dry soil. Shielding young plants with insect-proof nets and watering consistently at the roots helps reduce this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Aloo ebaanyɛ efee nɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli baa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ahe ŋmeii bu tsei bibii ahe, ni afɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ nu daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni naagba nɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my cocoa trees without forming into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei anɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by drought, lack of nutrients in the soil, or damage from mirid insects. Maintaining proper shade trees, applying recommended fertilizers, and controlling mirids will help the flowers stay on and set pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni fiteɔ nii Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ akwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli Ni akudɔ mirids lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain trees turning brown and dying prematurely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Premature leaf death in plantains is often caused by leaf spot diseases like Black Sigatoka, or a lack of potassium in the soil. Cutting off infected brown leaves cleanly and leaving them on the ground away from the plant stem helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni gboɔ oya yɛ plantains mli lɛ jɛɔ baa mli ŋmɔtɔ helai tamɔ Black Sigatoka loo potassium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ afo baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni kɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and develop broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity needed for young cocoa trees to survive their first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni amɛnáa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant leguminous crops like cowpeas on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa, tamɔ tsina ŋmãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nitrogen from the soil, leaving it weak. Legumes like cowpeas naturally fix nitrogen from the air into the soil, restoring fertility naturally for the next crop season without relying entirely on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ ŋmɛɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ehe afɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ anɔ kwraa.

english: Why is my maize crop growing very tall but producing small, empty cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa shi ewoɔ toi bibii lɛ? He ko ni nɔ ko bɛ?

english: Maize grows tall with small cobs when it receives too much nitrogen early on but lacks phosphorus or water when forming ears. Planting seeds too close together also causes overcrowding, making plants compete for light and nutrients.
ga: Abele daa kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Beni nitrogen babaoo nine shɛɔ nɔ mra Shi fɔsfɔs loo nu baafee nɔ ni bɛ beni toi lɛ feɔ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ hu kɛ mɛi babaoo baa. Enɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots turn hard and woody instead of cooking soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfee tso yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaahoo koni efee blɛoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become tough and woody if left in the ground too long past their maturity date, or if the soil experiences prolonged dry spells during root growth. Harvesting your cassava variety at its recommended age keeps the roots starchy and tender.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa ni ebaafee tsei kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni amɛho amɛhe. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ na hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miida lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa cassava henɔi lɛ yɛ afii ni atsɔɔ akɛ aye lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee bɔdɔɔ.

english: How can I prevent my harvested garden eggs and peppers from softening and going bad right after harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee blɛoo ni amɛfite kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Harvest peppers and garden eggs early in the morning while it is cool, keep them out of direct sunlight, and store them in ventilated plastic crates rather than sealed sacks to prevent heat build-up that causes rapid rotting.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli leebi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Ha hulu la akashɛ ohe tɛ̃ɛ. Ni okɛto plastic adekai ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli moŋ fe kotokui ni atsĩ naa koni hulutsoo akafee nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa oya.

english: How can I know if my tomato farm is producing a good harvest amount?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato ŋmɔ lɛ miiwo yibii kpakpai?

english: A good harvest depends on crop variety and proper spacing, but under good management, a standard tomato plot should produce around 100 to 120 crates per acre over its harvest cycle.
ga: Nikpamɔ kpakpa damɔ tsei srɔtoi lɛ kɛ gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ nɔ. Shi yɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa shishi lɛ, esa akɛ tomato ŋmɔ ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ awo aaafee 100 kɛyashi 120 yɛ acre kome mli yɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: I want to start crop farming, but what does it actually entail beyond planting seeds?
ga: Miisumɔ ni mabɔi tsei adumɔ, shi ani nɔ ko yɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni fe dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Crop farming involves land preparation, choosing high-quality seed varieties, managing soil fertility, weeding, pest control, timely watering, and finding a market before harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni fata ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ he ji shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ. Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahalamɔ Shikpɔŋ nɔ shweremɔ he nitsumɔ Jwɛi ni gbeɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ Nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be ni ato lɛ mli kɛ jarayeli hei ataomɔ dani akpa

english: Where can I get modern farming knowledge if I live in a rural area far from the city?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli he nilee yɛ kɛji mihi maŋ lɛ sɛɛgbɛ?

english: You can learn modern techniques by contacting your district agricultural extension officer, joining local farmer groups, attending demonstration farms, or listening to community agricultural radio programs.
ga: Obaanyɛ okase ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai kɛtsɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ okwaayeli nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ ohe awo akutsoŋ okwaafoi akuu mli Kɛ ohe awo okwaayeli he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ mli loo bo akutsoŋ okwaayeli redio nifeemɔi atoi

english: Why do flowers fall off my tomato plants without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flower drop usually happens because of high temperatures, irregular watering, excess nitrogen fertilizer, or a lack of bees and wind to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli Aloo ŋmeii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I test if my land has good soil for growing vegetable crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛduɔ aduawai?

english: Good vegetable soil should feel dark and rich, drain water easily after heavy rain without waterlogging, and be free of hard underground rock layers.
ga: Esa akɛ tsei ahe shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ afee ediŋŋ ni eyɛ shweremɔ. Ekɛ nu hoɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ ni nu ehiɛɛɛ mli. Ni tɛ ni wa ko bɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are often caused by sap-sucking insects like whiteflies, plant viruses, or a lack of nitrogen in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi tamɔ whiteflies, tsei amli helai, loo nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa.

english: Why is it important to space out my plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mitsei lɛ abɔ he kroko moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures plants do not fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, and it keeps air moving to prevent fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe wooo hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋshii mli. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ mli koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How often should I water my vegetable crops during the dry season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Vegetables generally need light watering early in the morning or late in the afternoon every 1 to 2 days so the roots stay moist without drowning.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehe hiaa ni afɔ aduawai anɔ nu fioo leebi loo shwane daa gbi 1 kɛyashi 2 koni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛkabote nu mli.

english: When is the correct time to apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Apply root-building fertilizer at planting or early growth, and apply growth-boosting top-dress fertilizer 3 to 4 weeks later when the plants start branching and flowering.
ga: Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ama shishifãi kɛji oodu loo ookwɛ oya. Ni okɛ tsofa ni haa tsei lɛ daraa lɛ atsu nii yɛ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ beni tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ niji ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to plant tomatoes on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ aaadu tomato yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that attack that specific crop to build up in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa nakai tso lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What does it mean when people say a crop seed is a 'hybrid'?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛɛ tso ko dumɔwu ji ‘hybrid’ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: A hybrid seed is created by carefully crossing two different strong plant parents—a male and a female—to produce a seed that inherits the best traits of both, such as higher yield, better taste, or resistance to diseases.
ga: Akɛ tso fɔlɔi sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni wa ni akɛfoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid: nuu kɛ yoo. Koni afee dumɔwui ni gboshinii ji sui ni hi fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ amɛyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli, tamɔ yibiiwoo ni fa, ŋmɔlɔ ni hi loo helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ.

english: Why am I advised not to save seeds from my harvested hybrid crops to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛɛɛ akɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ ato koni akɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from a hybrid harvest will not produce plants like the original parent crop. They lose their high yields and uniform growth, so you must buy fresh certified hybrid seeds from the supplier every season to get the best results.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli lɛ wooo tsei tamɔ shishijee fɔlɔ tso lɛ. Amɛfiteɔ amɛ yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ mɛi ni kɛ nibii lɛ baa lɛ adɛŋ daa be mli koni nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ aba.

english: Why do high-grade hybrid seeds cost more money to buy than regular seeds from the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ jara wa fe dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa ni jɛɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Producing hybrid seeds requires careful laboratory and field work by experts who manually control the breeding between male and female plant lines. This specialized work makes the seeds cost more, but the higher yield usually pays back the cost.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ afeemɔ biɔ ni ŋaalɔi ni kɛ amɛdɛŋ kudɔɔ tsei hii kɛ yei ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ ekome lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ laboratori kɛ ŋmɔ mli. Nitsumɔ kroko ni fata he nɛɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ ahe jara waa. Shi bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo lɛ woɔ shika ni afiteɔ lɛ he nyɔmɔ.

english: Where do seed suppliers get the high-grade hybrid seeds that they sell to us?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni mɛi ni kɛ dumɔwui haa lɛ naa dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ amɛhaa wɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ?

english: Agricultural research institutions and certified seed companies produce them under strict conditions by growing pure male and female parent plant lines together and harvesting only the controlled cross-bred seeds.
ga: Okwaayeli he niiamlitaomɔ nitsumɔhei kɛ dumɔwui ahe nitsumɔhei ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ feɔ dumɔwui nɛɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa amli kɛtsɔ tsei ni ji purebred kɛ tsei ni ji fɔlɔi ni amɛduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nɔ. ni dumɔwui ni akɛfee nɔ ko ni akudɔɔ lɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni akpaa.

english: Do crops also have male and female parts that need to come together to make fruit?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nuu kɛ yoo fãi ni esa akɛ amɛfee ekome dani amɛwo yibii?

english: Yes, crops have male parts that produce pollen and female parts that produce eggs. When pollen moves from the male part to the female part through wind or insects, the plant becomes fertilized and develops fruits or seeds.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hii ahe nibii ni feɔ pollen. ni yoo lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii Beni pollen lɛ jɛɔ stamen lɛ mli kɛyaa pistil lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi amli lɛ. Akɛ fɔ woɔ tso lɛ mli ni ewoɔ aduawai loo dumɔwui.

english: Why did my crops look so mixed and uneven when I planted seeds I collected from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni efutu ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds from a hybrid harvest are replanted, their genetic traits split apart in the next generation. Some plants grow tall, others short, and yields drop because the strong hybrid combination has broken down.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid kpamɔ mli lɛ Amɛfɔmɔ sui lɛ baajara mli yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Tsei komɛi kwɔlɔ. Tsei komɛi yɛ kuku. ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi be mli ni hardy hybrids lɛ gbee shi lɛ.

english: Why do some improved bean varieties produce so many more pods per plant than our local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tso kome mli fe wɔ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Improved varieties are bred to use sunlight, water, and soil nutrients much more efficiently. This allows a single plant to support over a hundred healthy pods without dropping its flowers.
ga: Henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso kome pɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii ohai abɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fɔfɔi lɛ fiteee.

english: What happens when two different varieties of the same crop are planted close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ adu tsei enyɔ ni ji henɔ kome yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: Wind and bees can carry pollen from one variety to another, causing them to cross-pollinate. The resulting seeds inside the fruit will contain a mix of features from both parent varieties.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ aŋɔ pollen kɛjɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ cross-pollinate. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ ji sui ni jɛ fɔlɔi srɔtoi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli ni efutu.

english: Can I produce my own hybrid seeds on my own farm to save money?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee mi diɛŋtsɛ mi hybrid dumɔwui yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ mli koni mikɛ shika ato?

english: It is very difficult because you must completely isolate your crops from outside pollen and carefully hand-pollinate the specific male and female parent plants. It is usually easier and safer to buy tested seeds from certified dealers.
ga: Enɛ wa waa ejaakɛ esa akɛ otsi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kwraa. ni okɛ onine afee fɔlɔ tsei hii kɛ yei lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, ewaaa ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni aka amɛ akwɛ kɛjɛ jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ.

english: How can I tell if a crop variety is high-grade before I buy the seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso henɔ ko hi jogbaŋŋ dani mahe dumɔwui?

english: Look for certified seed tags from government agricultural agencies on the package. Certified high-grade seeds guarantee fast germination, strong growth, and consistent high production when cared for properly.
ga: Taomɔ maŋ okwaayeli nitsumɔhe lɛ dumɔwui akadi ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ana he odaseyeli haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya. shweremɔ ni mli wa kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo be fɛɛ be kɛji akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it needs to build green leaves and grow strong. Adding manure, compost, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer can help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni afee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do small caterpillars keep eating the inside of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛye mibii bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are often Fall Armyworms, which prefer to hide and feed inside the tender center of young corn plants. Keeping your farm free of weeds and applying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening when the worms come out to feed will protect your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛye nii yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ eje kpo kɛmiitao niyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: What will happen if I plant my cassava cuttings very close together on the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow thin and produce very small tubers instead of large, healthy ones.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ daa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the tall trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot tolerate strong, direct sunlight, which burns their leaves and dries out the soil around their roots. Keeping tall shade trees or planting plantains nearby provides them with the cooling shade they need to survive.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛŋmɛɛɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Enɛ baa shã baai lɛ ni eha sũ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ agbi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aná hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the branches without growing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, severe dry spells, or sudden over-watering. Watering your plants regularly at the base and keeping the soil moist helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa trukaa fe nine Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa yɛ eshishigbɛ ni ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũuɔ lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I work animal manure into my soil before planting my vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ kooloo ŋmei awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani madu aduawai?

english: Animal manure improves the soil so it can hold water longer during hot days and slowly releases essential food that helps vegetable plants grow faster and resist common diseases.
ga: Manure haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa aduawai ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ fiofio.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops as soon as the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshinii lɛ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ?

english: Weeds naturally have deep, hardy roots designed to capture water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds while they are still small prevents them from stealing food and water away from your young crops.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni afee koni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lolo lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my harvested yams begin to rot quickly after I store them in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ oya beni mikɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot quickly if they are bruised during harvest or if they are stored in a hot, damp place without good airflow. Storing unbruised yams on raised wooden racks in a shade-covered, well-ventilated barn keeps them dry and prevents rot.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. Kɛ atomo ni etseko lɛ ato tso adekai ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ shade, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ehi shi ni eha ehiɛ akafite.

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves inward during hot afternoons to reduce the amount of water escaping from their leaves into the air. Covering the soil around the plant base with dry grass mulch keeps the roots cool and conserves soil moisture.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ aba shi. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Planting maize in the same spot year after year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows corn pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas returns nutrients naturally to the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade and moisture, helping the cocoa survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How do I know which direction to insert cassava stems into the ground when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: You need to look at the small buds on the stem cutting and make sure they are pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant the stem upside down, the shoots and roots will struggle to grow properly.
ga: Obaasumɔ ni okwɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso ni afo lɛ nɔ lɛ ni okwɛ akɛ amɛmiitsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu tso lɛ shishi lɛ, Tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ baaná naagba yɛ amɛdalɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can capture direct sunlight. The more sunlight the leaves get, the more energy the plant sends underground to grow larger yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ baa lɛ naa lɛ, babaoo ni tsei tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkwɛ̃ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to stay healthy and green. Adding animal manure or a nitrogen-based fertilizer like urea helps restore their green color and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni ŋmãa ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ nitrogen fee tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji kɛ amɛdalɛ.

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, stops heat from drying out the ground too fast, keeps weeds from growing, and adds natural food back into the soil as the dry leaves decay.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa hulutsoo lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni baai ni egboi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas naturally capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which feeds your maize plants and improves the fertility of your farm.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ náa niyenii, ni ehaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why does clearing weeds around my crops make them grow much faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya kwraa.

english: Weeds steal water, light, and nutrients from your crops. Removing the weeds leaves all the water and plant food exclusively for your crops to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ shĩɔ nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛtee ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ amli

english: This damage is typically caused by pests like the fall armyworm, which feed on young leaves. Catching them early and applying recommended treatments keeps them from destroying the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ cutworms ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely hot weather or lack of water in the soil. Consistent watering helps the plant keep its flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔ ko ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why must I make sure my harvested maize is completely dry before putting it in sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mana nɔmimaa akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbi kwraa dani mikɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: If maize is stored while still damp, mold will grow and insects will quickly attack it, spoiling the grain and making it unsafe to eat or sell.
ga: Kɛji okɛ ŋmãa lɛ to be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo lɛ, Fungus baakwɛ̃ ni kooloi bibii baatutua bo oya. efiteɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ni ehaa ebɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aye loo ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Can I use water from a river near a galamsey site to water my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ faa ni bɛŋkɛ Galamsey kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli nu?

english: Water near illegal mining (galamsey) often contains invisible chemicals like mercury and heavy mud that poison the soil, stunt plant growth, and make crops unsafe for people to eat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni anaaa tamɔ mercury kɛ sũ ni tsii ni yeɔ awui kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni bɛŋkɛɔ shika tsuru ni mla eŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ (galamsey) lɛ mli. dwarf tsei lɛ adalɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha gbɔmɛi ni amɛyeɔ.

english: If river water looks clear, does that automatically mean it is safe for my farm?
ga: Kɛji nu ni yɔɔ faa lɛ mli lɛ mli tse Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Clear water is not always safe water. It can still carry hidden chemicals, excess salt, or invisible pollutants that ruin soil fertility and harm plant roots.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be nu ni mli tse ji nu ni hi. Eyɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lolo. ŋoo ni fa fe nine loo mujiwoo ni anaaa ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɔmɔ nii ni eyeɔ tsei shishifãi awui

english: What happens to my crops if mud from a nearby mining site washes onto my farmland?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji muji ni jɛ shika tsuru ŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ tswa kɛba miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Mining mud hardens into a crust on top of the farm, blocking air and rain from reaching the roots and leaving harmful heavy metals that prevent seeds from sprouting.
ga: Muji ni jɛɔ shika tsuru tsaa mli lɛ mli waa ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ yiteŋ. Blocks air and rain from reaching the roots. ni eshiɔ dade ni tsii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni haaa dumɔwui akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize turn yellow and roll up during hot dry days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's natural defense to conserve water, while yellowing usually signals that the plant is stressed and lacking nitrogen or soil moisture.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe koni ekɛbu nu he. Shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao ni nitrogen loo ŋmɔtɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but give me small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai bibii shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen or shade, they spend all their energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing nutrients in the roots.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nitrogen loo shade babaoo Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients, saving their energy to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni akɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha wala.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Shade trees act as blankets that protect them from sun heat and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do the roots of my tomato plants turn soft and rot when I give them too much water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ fe nine lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air just like water. Flooding the soil drowns the roots by cutting off oxygen, allowing root-rot fungi to thrive and kill the plant.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu hu he miihia tsei shishifãi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ daa ni amɛfiteɔ tsei.

english: Yes, because maize grows quickly and feeds from the top soil, while cassava grows slower and feeds deeper underground, allowing them to share the space well if planted with good spacing.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni enaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei daa blɛoo ni eyeɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Ehaa anyɛɔ ajaa he jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ adu kɛ he ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does resting my land for a year make my crops yield better when I plant again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hejɔɔmɔ afi kome lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yaa hiɛ kɛ́ midu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaving land fallow gives natural weeds and plants time to grow, die, and decompose, which naturally reloads organic matter and essential nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi he ko ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛdaraa, amɛgboiɔ, ni amɛfiteɔ, ni no yeɔ ebuaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛ nibii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep turning yellow and dying when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the soil moisture. Keeping large shade trees or planting plantains around them creates a natural umbrella that protects the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi. Tsei wuji akwɛmɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ Ehaa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get dark brown spots and dry up when I pour water on top of the whole plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbi kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Wetting tomato leaves directly creates a damp environment where fungal diseases like leaf blight easily spread. Watering only at the base of the stem keeps the leaves dry and prevents dark fungus spots from ruining your harvest.
ga: Tomato baai ni afɔɔ nu tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ baa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo Nu ni oooha yɛ tso lɛ shishi pɛ lɛ baaha baa lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai diji lɛ anaa koni ekafite oŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling upward and twisting like little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices out of the leaves and spreading viruses. Spraying neem oil or an approved pesticide gets rid of these tiny insects so new leaves can grow flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi bibii nɛɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi bibii nɛɛ koni baai heei lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: This is a clear sign that your soil is running low on nitrogen, which maize needs to stay green and grow tall. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK at the right time feeds the plant and stops the leaves from yellowing.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tso lɛ niyenii ni ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on my field after harvesting corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ?

english: Corn takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, but leguminous crops like groundnuts and beans naturally fix nitrogen back into the soil through their roots. Rotating them restores soil fertility without relying entirely on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Abele jieɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛsaa nitrogen lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ he afɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ anɔ kwraa.

english: Cassava tubers rot when excess water stays around the roots for too long without draining away, suffocating the plant. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain off quickly so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ta shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is eating small holes in the center leaves of my young corn plants and leaving dark dust behind?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ sũ diŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest that hides deep inside the growing tip of the corn plant. Spraying approved insecticides or applying neem leaf extract directly into the central leaf funnel will kill the worms before they destroy your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie shi loo okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu wo baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ dani amɛfite onibii lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away most of the small shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Midumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe lɛ ateŋ babaoo.

english: Small shoots (suckers) steal water and plant food away from the main mother plant, making the fruit bunches small. Leaving only one or two strong shoots alongside the main stem ensures all the soil nutrients go into producing big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso bibii (tso lɛ) lɛ juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Ha aduawai lɛ afee bibii Kɛ́ oshi tso yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yaa ni amɛwoɔ tso yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do crops grow better and bigger when I do not plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei daa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdaraa lɛ? Akɛni miduuu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ hewɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving them weak and thin. Giving each plant proper spacing lets its roots spread wide and leaves catch enough light to grow strong.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa, ni ebaa lɛ hu naa la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food that grows big tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil, exposing them to full sunshine while preventing ground rot and diseases.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii beni akwɛɔ bulb agboi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha ni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ nɔ. Kɛ agbɛnɛ hu, etsiɔ fitemɔ kɛ helai srɔtoi anaa.

english: Officer, why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and dying before the corn is ready?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong. When the soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant steals it from its oldest leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ba naagbee Tso lɛ juɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my crops still growing poorly even after I spent money to apply chemical fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ lolo yɛ be mli ni mifite shika yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If your soil is too acidic, the plant roots become 'locked' and cannot absorb the fertilizer you applied. Adding agricultural lime to the soil neutralizes the acid so the crop roots can freely drink up the nutrients.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ acid tsɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ‘baatsi amɛhe’ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ okwaayeli mli lime fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa acid lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the big trees off my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and fragile root systems that burn under direct sunlight. Retaining larger shade trees or planting plantains beside them shields the young cocoa from harsh sun and keeps the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni waaa ni shãa yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with many green leaves, but the tubers underground remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni eyɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients like potassium, the plant spends all its energy producing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nine kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ potassium he lɛ, tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ feɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to manufacture the food that feeds the growing tuber under the ground. Lifting the vines up on stakes exposes all leaves to the sun and keeps them away from rot-causing diseases on the damp ground.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ awó wain tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fɛɛ shɛɔ hulu la nɔ, ni ehaa hela ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do experienced farmers tell me to plant cowpea or groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ baakɛɛ mi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have special microbes in their roots that grab nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the dirt, naturally fertilizing the soil for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ nibii bibii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are the yellow flowers on my tomato plants falling off onto the ground instead of turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shikpɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air becomes too hot and dry or when the soil lacks moisture. Extreme heat prevents the flowers from pollinating themselves, causing the plant to shed them to conserve water.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. or when the soil lacks moisture Extreme heat will prevent flowers from being pollinated. This causes trees to secrete water to store water.

english: Every sucker growing at the base acts like an extra mouth drinking water and feeding on soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest plant to focus its energy on producing big, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: All suckers growing at the base act as additional drinking water and consume nutrients in the soil. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, tsei ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ plantains wuji ni tsii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ he nii.

english: Why am I finding small chewed holes and brown, sawdust-like powder inside the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Ashɛreɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ko ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ ateŋ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the growing tip of the plant during the day to feed on soft leaf tissue. Early spot treatments with organic or chemical controls are required to stop them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Mra mli lɛ, tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he lɛ he miihia. kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛkpa amɛ dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the roots of my vegetables rot and turn soft whenever heavy rain falls on my flat farm plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shishifãi fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ mi shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Standing water fills up all the air spaces in flat soil, suffocating the roots because they cannot breathe. Building raised soil beds or mounds allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping root zones oxygen-rich.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔlɔ hewɔ. Saji ni awó nɔ loo gɔji ni afee lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ náa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii babaoo

english: Can I feed the leftover dry corn stalks on my farm to my cattle after harvesting?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni egbi ni eshwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha mitsinai lɛ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, dry corn stalks are a great feed source for cattle, especially during the dry season when fresh grass is scarce. They give animals energy and fiber, though chopping them up first makes them easier for animals to eat and digest.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ ji niyenii kpakpa kɛha tsinai. Titri lɛ, yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni jwɛi heei faaa lɛ. Amɛ haa kooloi hewalɛ kɛ fiber. Eyɛ mli akɛ kɛ́ afolɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ehaa kooloi yeɔ amɛ ni amɛyeɔ amɛhe mlɛo moŋ.

english: How can I store crop stalks and dry grass so they do not rot before the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ tsei ashishifãi kɛ jwɛi ato koni amɛkafite dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba?

english: You need to dry the crop stalks completely in the sun, tie them into tight bundles, and store them off the ground under a raised shed or cover. Keeping them dry prevents mold and keeps them fresh for your animals.
ga: Esa akɛ ogbi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kpɛtɛɔ he yɛ tsɔne ni mli wa mli. ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ shĩa ko loo shĩa ko ni awo nɔ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ oogbi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ehaa okooloi lɛ feɔ ehee.

english: Can I feed fresh cassava peels and leaves directly to my sheep and goats right after harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha mitooi kɛ mitooi lɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai heei tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to dry fresh cassava peels in the sun for a day or two before feeding them to animals. Fresh peels contain natural compounds that can cause stomach distress, but drying removes these harmful substances.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooogbi ŋmei hee yɛ hulu mli gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ dani okɛha kooloi. Adebɔɔ mli nibii ni baanyɛ aha musu lɛ mli ajɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii heei amli. Shi kɛ́ egbi lɛ, ejieɔ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ.

english: Yellow bottom leaves mean the plant lacks enough food in the soil, usually nitrogen. The crop automatically moves the remaining food from its older lower leaves to feed the young upper leaves, causing the bottom ones to yellow and dry up.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni bei pii lɛ eji nitrogen Tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants dry up so quickly when the rain stops for just a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ lɛ?

english: Maize plants have shallow roots that stay near the top of the soil. When the topsoil loses water during a short dry spell, the roots cannot reach deeper soil moisture, causing the leaves to dry out fast to save water.
ga: Abele tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nu fiteɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli ni hɔmɔ baa lɛ. Shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni mli kwɔ fe bɔ ni sa. Ha baai lɛ agbi oya koni nu akafite.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with weak stems when weeds grow high around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ be mli ni jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to grow strong. When tall weeds block the sun, the crops stretch rapidly upward to reach light, which makes their stems thin, tall, and easily broken by wind.
ga: Hulu la he miihia tsei koni amɛdara waa. Kɛ jwɛi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ tsi hulu la lɛ naa lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baagbala amɛhe oya kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛha la lɛ abote mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ekwɛɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ fiteɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why does wild grass grow much faster on my land than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Wild grasses are naturally suited to the local climate and have deep root systems that grab water and plant food faster than farmed crops. Clearing grass early gives your crops a fair chance to take up those nutrients.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ ji nɔ ni sa kɛha he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ ajie nu kɛ niyenii oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Jwɛi lɛ ni ooofo mra Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná hegbɛ ni sa ni amɛná nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ.

english: Is it good to burn dry grass and leftover stems on my farm before the planting season?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ashã jwɛi kɛ tsei ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ aba?

english: Burning clears the land quickly, but it burns away useful organic matter and nutrients that make soil rich. Leaving crop residues to decompose or using them as animal feed keeps your farmland much healthier over time.
ga: Shãa baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ oya. Shi ebaashã nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite lɛ fite loo akɛtsu nii akɛ kooloi aniyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ni efee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Can I intentionally plant useful grass on my land to feed my animals, or will it ruin my soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu jwɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni majɛ yiŋtoo mli mahã kooloi niyenii? Aloo ebaafite mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Planting specific high-quality fodder grasses like elephant grass on dedicated plots is good practice. It provides continuous feed for your animals and protects the soil from being washed away by heavy rains.
ga: Niyenii jwɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ shwuɔ jwɛi, ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔji pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Ehaa kooloi yeɔ niyenii be fɛɛ be, ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akahole lɛ.

english: Why do crops grow much bigger and greener on land where cows were kept previously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii miidara ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔji yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ akɛkwɛɔ tsinai lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cow dung and urine contain high amounts of natural plant food, especially nitrogen. When dropped on the soil, it acts as a rich natural fertilizer that feeds your crops and improves the soil's ability to hold water.
ga: Tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei mli tsei aniyenii ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo. titri lɛ nitrogen Kɛji akɛ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ Ebaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa oŋmɔshi nii lɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ nɔ kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the whorl (funnel) of the maize plant during the day, chewing on fresh leaves and leaving behind waste that looks like fine sawdust.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ a-whorls (cones) lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Okɛ baai heei lɛ atsu nii ni oshi jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the plant's juices, or by a viral infection spread by these insects while they feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young leafy vegetables wilt in the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, be mli ni mi lɛ shwieee lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During peak heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up from the soil. As long as they recover in the cool evening, it is just temporary heat defense.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ. Eji nɔ ko kɛkɛ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Yellowing that starts at the tip of lower leaves and moves down the center midrib indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which the plant needs to build green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni eyaa shishi kɛyaa shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my yams grow short, bent, and hairy instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ kuku, ebɔleɔ, ni eyɛ yitsɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers become bent and deformed when they hit hard, compacted soil or rocks underground. Building high, loose soil mounds allows the tubers to grow downward easily.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfiteɔ kɛji amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa mlɛo.

english: Why do I need to cut away the small suckers growing around the bottom of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: Extra suckers steal water and food from the main mother plant. Removing all but one or two strong shoots ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ja ekome loo enyɔ pɛ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee niji agboi ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit when temperatures get too high or when plants experience dry spells, as heat stress prevents proper flower pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei naa hulutsoo bei. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, latsaa tsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ ni sa lɛ naa.

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves yellow and drop off, the lower stem turns woody, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack from expanding roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ, kɛ́ eshishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ bafeɔ tso. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ beni shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do small cocoa pods on my tree turn black and dry up while they are still tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbi beni amɛji gbekɛbii lolo lɛ?

english: This is often 'cherelle wilt,' a natural mechanism where the tree sheds excess pods it cannot feed, though it can also be caused by fungal diseases like Black Pod during heavy rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji ‘cherel wilt’, ni ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aha lɛ niyenii lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ekolɛ ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛbaa moŋ.

english: Yellow leaves during heavy rain usually mean the soil is waterlogged. Drowning roots cannot breathe or absorb nitrogen from the soil. Improving field drainage helps the roots recover and feed the plant again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu loo amɛŋɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni ehaa tsei lɛ niyenii ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpea alongside my maize help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpea pull nitrogen out of the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. This acts as a natural, free fertilizer that feeds the nearby maize crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by sudden heat, dry soil, or a lack of plant nutrients like calcium. Keeping the moisture in the soil steady with mulch often stops this.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni baa trukaa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tso lɛ mli niyenii tamɔ calcium ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ haa naagba nɛɛ kpaa.

english: Why does my cassava produce large leaves and stems but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii wuji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer, it spends all its energy growing big leaves and tall stems above ground instead of sending food down to swell the tubers below.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ lɛ Ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai wuji kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu niyenii kɛba shi kɛya shishigbɛ yitso lɛ koni efuu.

english: Why do my cabbage heads split open right before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ mli gbalaa dani mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads split open when heavy rain or sudden watering comes after a dry spell. The inside of the cabbage expands faster than the outer leaves can stretch, causing it to burst.
ga: Kaabeji yitsei lɛ tswaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa loo nu ho trukaa yɛ hɔmɔ be sɛɛ. Kaaba lɛ mligbɛ lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Enɛ haa kaabe lɛ fãa.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, overly shaded conditions. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight in and lowers the humidity that the fungus needs to spread.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ fe nine lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa hulu la boteɔ mli ni ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ŋmei lɛ agbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Underground yam rot is caused by soil fungi and tiny worms called nematodes, which enter the tuber when water collects around the roots without draining away properly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes. Enɛ boteɔ bulb lɛ mli kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni enyɛɛɛ efo mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Armyworms leave ragged, torn holes in the maize leaves and deposit small piles of yellowish, sawdust-like droppings inside the central funnel (whorl) of the growing plant.
ga: Cutworms shĩɔ bu ni etsilɛ, ni egbɛ eshwa yɛ ŋmãa baai amli ni ebuaa ŋmãa ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa lɛ anaa yɛ tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi (rings) lɛ amli.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for a single strong generation. If you plant seeds saved from that harvest, the new plants will be weak, grow unevenly, and produce much less grain.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha yinɔ kome ni he wa. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tso hee lɛ baagbɔjɔ. shweremɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni ehaa dumɔwui fioo kwraa.

english: Why do my stored dried grains get ruined by small insects even when kept indoors?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii fiteɔ miŋmaa ni egbi lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ shĩa mli moŋ?

english: Insects like weevils often lay invisible eggs on the grain while it is still in the field. Once stored in a warm space, the eggs hatch into larvae that eat the grain from the inside out unless treated or sealed airtight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ ŋmaa nɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. ja atsu he nii loo akɛ vacuum ewo mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the nutrient that gives crops their healthy green color and strength. Adding organic manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer gives the plants the nutrients they need to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛhe wa Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do people say that planting groundnuts on my land will make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and other legumes have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When you harvest the groundnuts and leave the roots and leaves to rot, they release free natural fertilizer into the soil for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ legumes krokomɛi Amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Kɛji okpa ŋmeii ni oha shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ fite lɛ, Amɛbaajie adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni aheee nɔ ko awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha odumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. This competition leaves all the plants weak and small, resulting in a smaller total harvest than if you had spaced them properly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii. As a result, the total yield is less than with proper spacing.

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my crops with grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he? ŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi loo baai yɔɔ mli

english: Covering the ground with grass or leaves—a method called mulching—acts like a blanket. It traps moisture in the dirt so water doesn't evaporate quickly in the heat, keeps the roots cool, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai baaha nɔ - gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching - tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nu shɛ latsaa he lɛ, efooo oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why is it smart for me to try a new crop or planting method on just one small plot first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nilee akɛ maka tso hee loo gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ nii yɛ he ko bibioo lɛ makwɛ lɛ? Tsakemɔ kome pɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Testing a new technique or crop variety on a small plot lets you observe how it behaves in your specific soil without risking your whole farm's yield or your family's investment if something goes wrong.
ga: Kaa ŋaa heei loo tsei srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔji bibii anɔ Ehaa okwɛɔ esubaŋ yɛ oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ lɛ nɔ. ni ekɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ loo weku lɛ shika ni ekɛwoɔ mli lɛ wooo oshara mli kɛji nɔ ko ba.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when the dry Harmattan wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind pulls moisture out of plant leaves much faster than the roots can pull water from the dry ground. Planting temporary shade trees like plantains protects the young cocoa by blocking the hot wind and trapping moisture around the leaves.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ni etsiɔ naa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔleɔ baai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi ni mikɛ tsei awo mli koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to generate energy to grow big tubers under the ground. Staking holds the leaves up into the light and keeps them off the wet ground where diseases and rot can easily attack them.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba ni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ la mli ni ehaaa amɛhe afee ŋmɔtɔ, he ni helai kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ atutua amɛ oya lɛ.

english: How do I know if cassava stems are good enough to cut and plant for my next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ afolɔ ni adu kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Good cassava stems should come from healthy, mature plants with no insect holes or visible spots. The stem should feel firm, be about as thick as a finger, and show clear, healthy bud nodes along its length.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei kpakpai ajɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Kɔɔyɔɔ mli ŋmeii loo hei ni anaa lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ. Esa akɛ tso lɛ anu he akɛ eyɛ shiŋŋ. Aaafee inchi kome ni ona ŋmeii ni mli tse ni mli wa yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why am I finding ragged holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hidden in the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu ni etse ehe yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ? ni akɛtee baai lɛ amli

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on young crop leaves from the inside out. Checking your farm early and applying recommended biological control or approved sprays early prevents them from destroying the crop before the cobs grow.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ tsei bibii ahe baai kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kpo lɛ he okadi. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ nibii ahe loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii mra. Ebaatsi ŋmɔji anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii dani ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant tomatoes in the exact same spot where I harvested peppers last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu tomato yɛ he ni mifo mi-pepper lɛ yɛ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Tomatoes and peppers belong to the same plant family and suffer from the same soil diseases and pests. Planting them back-to-back in the same spot allows hidden soil pests from the pepper crop to immediately attack the new tomato plants.
ga: Tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei akuu kome mli, ni helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa sũ mli kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtee ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ he lɛ tutuaa tomato tso hee lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and the ground around the main stem starts to crack. You can dig up one root to check if it is thick and firm before harvesting the whole field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ be mli ni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso titri lɛ miije shishi egbɛ eshwa. Obaanyɛ otsa shishifã kome ni okwɛ kɛji eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehi shi shiŋŋ dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my maize is dry enough on the stalk to harvest for storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa koni akɛto?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the outer husks turn dry and brown, and the kernels feel very hard. If you press your fingernail into a kernel and it leaves no mark, it means moisture is low enough for long-term storage.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa waa. Kɛji okɛ otsitsi mii ŋmaa lɛ mli ni eshiii okadi ko. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting and shrinking while resting in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ beni mijɔɔ mihe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living plant roots that wake up and try to grow new vines when kept in warm, damp places. The growing sprout consumes the food and water stored inside the yam, which causes the tuber to shrink and soften.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii ji tso shishifãi ni hiɛ ka. ni baate shi ni ebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɛ wain tsei heei kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ ni edɔ ni edɔ. Dumɔwui ni miida lɛ yeɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni buaa ehe naa yɛ sweet potato lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ blɛoo.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil goes too dry. The plant gets stressed by high heat and drops flowers to save its energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Tsei kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kpeɔ ni amɛjieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni amɛdaraa yɛ mli lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing very tall and thin instead of producing large cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa waa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: When maize plants are planted too close to each other, they compete for sunlight and soil nutrients. The plants put all their energy into growing taller to reach light rather than building thick stalks and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara koni amɛshɛ la he. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ tsohi agbohi.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl tightly upward during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl upward as a natural defense to protect themselves from losing too much water when it is hot and dry. Providing shade or regular watering helps lower heat stress so the leaves stay open.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite kɛji edɔ ni edɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo loo nu ha lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi. No hewɔ lɛ, baai lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛgbeleɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young cocoa plants turning yellow and falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually indicate that the young cocoa plant is missing nitrogen in the soil or that the soil is holding too much water around its roots. Adding compost or fertilizer helps the leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo tsɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my plantain bunches coming out much smaller than my neighbor's bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ ji bibioo kwraa fe mikutsoŋnyo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain bunches remain small when the soil lacks essential nutrients like potassium, or when too many suckers grow around one stem. Removing extra suckers leaves more food and water for the main plant to produce large fruit.
ga: Plantains ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi bibioo kɛ́ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo kɛ́ ŋmeii kwɛ̃ yɛ amɛhe. Tso kome fa tsɔ Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa niyenii kɛ nu babaoo baa tso titri lɛ nɔ koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why does my cassava root start turning dark and brown inside just two days after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ feemɔ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni akpa lɛ?

english: Once cassava is pulled out of the soil, air reacts with enzymes inside the root, causing it to spoil within two to three days. Peeling and processing the cassava quickly into gari or flour stops this reaction and preserves it.
