ga: Kɛji akɛ ajieɔ ŋmei kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ enzymes ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ feɔ ekome. Enɛ haa efiteɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmei lɛ oya ni afee lɛ gari loo ashikishaŋ lɛ, ehaa nɛkɛ nifeemɔ nɛɛ kpaa ni ehaa ehiɔ shi.

english: Heavy rainfall causes high moisture around the cocoa tree, allowing fungal spores known as black pod disease to spread quickly. Pruning extra shade tree branches lets sunlight dry the farm and reduces fungus growth.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa kookoo tsei lɛ ahe, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ale lɛ akɛ black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha hulu lɛ akagbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ aba shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a vital nutrient for leafy growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps the plant recover and produce healthy corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same land where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ he ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches your land, feeding your maize plants and keeping the soil fertile for future seasons.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why does lowland rice need standing water in the field while other crops rot in wet soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ he hiaa ŋmãa folo yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi hu he hiaa lɛ lɛ? Ani egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels that allow their roots to breathe underwater, while most weeds cannot survive submerged. The water acts as a natural weed suppressor while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi ni haa amɛshishifãi lɛ muɔ yɛ nu shishi. Yɛ be mli ni jwɛi babaoo nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ nu shishi lɛ, Nu tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni tsiɔ jwɛi anaa yɛ be mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off before turning into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani ebatsɔ anɔkwa yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers often drop when the plant faces heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulched helps the plant hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: If I plant my corn seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Ani minɔ ni?

english: No, planting seeds too close forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leads to thin, weak stalks and tiny corn ears, whereas proper spacing yields bigger, healthier harvests.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. This leads to thin, weak stalks and small ears of corn. Meanwhile, proper spacing will result in a bigger, healthier crop.

english: Why is it necessary to clear weeds while my crops are still very small seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji dumɔwu bibioo kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crop seedlings and quickly steal the sunlight, water, and fertilizer meant for your crop. Cleaning weeds early ensures your young plants get all the nourishment needed to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe dumɔwui bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ oya. Jwɛi lɛ ahe saamɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei bibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I find holes and small worms hidden inside the center funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those are Fall Armyworms, which feed on the delicate central leaves where new growth happens. Applying recommended treatments or wood ash into the leaf funnels early prevents them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Amɛji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ yɛ he ni shweremɔ heei miiba lɛ. Tsamɔ tsofa loo tso ashwishwɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ baa lɛ nɔ mra. Ebaatsi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ afitemɔ naa.

english: Tomatoes curl their leaves in intense heat to reduce surface area and prevent water from evaporating too quickly. If they uncurl by evening, the plant is managing, but covering the soil with mulch keeps the roots cooler.
ga: Akɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi ni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya tsɔ. Kɛji amɛkpɛ amɛyiŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's high-yield hybrid corn harvest produce weaker plants than the original seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli lɛ wo tsei ni baanyɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to show high yields only in their first generation. Seeds collected from that harvest lose those superior traits, leading to uneven growth and lower yields in the next planting.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi yɛ dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cassava tubers tiny and woody even though the leafy tops look huge and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji tsei lɛ? Ani baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to spend all its energy growing heavy leaves above ground instead of swelling its tubers below. Loose soil with balanced nutrients encourages energy to go into the roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, moŋ fe ni eeeha ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni niyenii mli nibii ni ja yɔɔ mli lɛ woɔ hewalɛ hewalɛ koni ebote shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct hot sunlight burns their tender leaves and quickly dries up moisture in the soil. Planting plantains alongside them or keeping bigger shade trees acts as a living shield to protect them until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni akwɛɔ koni amɛdara lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ amɛhe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛbaadara.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make leaves green and grow big. Adding poultry manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea restores their health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil if I leave them in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water during heavy rainfall fills up the air pockets in the soil, which suffocates the roots and creates a wet environment for fungal diseases to break down and rot the cassava tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ baa koni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ akpãtã ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ ni amɛfite.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars inside the central stem?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. The moth lays eggs on the plant, and the hatched caterpillars eat the fresh center of the leaves, which can be controlled by applying recommended treatments early in the morning.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ. Ni ŋmeii ni baa lɛ baaye baai heei lɛ ateŋ. Abaanyɛ akudɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni ajieɔ yi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii leebi lɛ nɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas on the same land help my maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that catch natural nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. This enriches the soil with natural fertilizer that nearby crops like maize can feed on.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmli ni amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa baanyɛ aye nii.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off before turning into actual pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛmiitsɔ pepper aduawai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they suffer heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli, ni no haa ebafeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do weeds growing near my crops cause my farm yield to drop so low?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa yibiiwoo ni baa shi waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm; they aggressively drink up the water and suck up the soil fertilizers that your crops need to produce food, while also blocking sunlight.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛmuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni amɛná niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ hulu la lɛ hu naa.

english: Why do I get smaller harvests when I plant my seeds very close together in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for root space, water, and light. Proper spacing lets every individual plant spread its leaves and roots to produce larger fruits or ears.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shishifãi ahe he, nu, kɛ la he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso gbɛɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa koni ewo yibii loo toi wuji.

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass is called mulching. It keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating too fast, and stops weeds from sprouting around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi haa lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight to manufacture energy, which is sent underground to expand the size of the yam tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. ni abaamaje shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ amli alɛɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up during the sunny months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle full, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted around them to block direct sun and keep the soil cool until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Amɛmiisumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛhe. Enɛ ji koni ekɛtsi hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Can I plant cassava inside my fresh cocoa farm without hurting the cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cassava yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ hee mli ni miyeee kookoo tsei lɛ awui?

english: Yes, you can plant cassava alongside young cocoa because the cassava plants provide helpful shade for the cocoa. However, keep enough space between them so the cassava roots do not steal all the water and food from the young cocoa plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmei yɛ kookoo bibii ahe. Shi kɛlɛ, akɛni ŋmei tsei haa ŋmei tsei lɛ náa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ hewɔ lɛ, shimɔ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ bɔni afee ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ akaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛjɛɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, damp weather. Rain splashes the fungus onto the pods, so clearing weeds and pruning branches to let sun and wind in helps keep the pods dry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli. Nugbɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, shwiemɔ jwɛi ni ofolɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: What causes the branches on my cocoa trees to swell up like big fingers?
ga: Mɛni miiha niji ni yɔɔ mikoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miifu tamɔ niji wuji?

english: This swelling is a sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, which is spread by tiny bugs called mealybugs. Once a tree gets this virus, it cannot produce properly, so the infected tree must be cut down to stop it from spreading to healthy trees.
ga: Nɛkɛ fuumɔ nɛɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Kɛji tsei lɛ ná nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ afo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are tiny insects causing brown spots on my green cocoa pods and killing them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiha mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbe amɛ lɛ?

english: These tiny insects are likely mirids (akate). They suck the juice out of young pods and stems, killing the plant tissue; spraying recommended protective sprays at the right time of year prevents them from damaging your harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ji mirids (akate). Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ. efiteɔ tsei ahe fãji Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to trim off extra branches and unwanted shoots from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ niji ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmeii ni ataooo kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Trimming off unnecessary branches allows sunlight and air to move through the tree, which prevents fungal diseases. It also makes sure the tree sends its food and energy to making big pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa. Ehaa tso lɛ tsuɔ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ hu koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers fall off the tree before turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by drought, poor soil food, or a lack of beneficial insects to pollinate the blossoms. Keeping moisture in the soil and protecting good insects helps the flowers stay on the tree.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. niyenii ni ehiii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kooloi ahebuu kpakpa haa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops drop their leaves and stop growing during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ baai ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During Harmattan, dry air and hot winds pull water out of plant leaves very quickly. Crops naturally drop their leaves to conserve moisture so the root and stem stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi kɛ tso lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its strength and needs food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni aha lɛ niyenii?

english: If your crops have light green or yellowish leaves, grow very slowly, or produce small fruits even when rain falls, your soil is exhausted and needs manure or compost to rebuild its strength.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ, edaa blɛoo waa, loo ewoɔ aduawai bibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, no lɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni ekɛha ehewalɛ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with aggressive roots that steal water and nutrients much faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early stops them from choking your crops and taking away their sunlight.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɔjɔ ni hulu la akashɛ amɛnɔ.

english: Why should I plant plantains in the same field with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or beans in my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of food from the soil as it grows. Legumes like cowpeas put good food, especially nitrogen, back into the soil naturally, which makes the land fertile again for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni edaa lɛ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas feɔ niyenii kpakpa. titri lɛ nitrogen Ku osɛɛ kɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or compost helps the leaves turn healthy green so the plant can grow strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Tsei lɛ baaná ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cover the ground around my vegetable crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, called mulching, keeps the blazing sun from drying out the soil. It traps moisture in the ground longer, stops weeds from growing, and keeps the soil cool for plant roots.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Tsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛha tsei shishifãi

english: Does it matter which direction I point cassava stem cuttings when I plant them in the dirt?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni atsɔɔ ŋmei niji lɛ gbɛ nɔ beni aduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, cassava stems must be planted with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the roots and leaves will struggle to grow, leading to weak plants and small harvests.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei tso lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋwɛi shishi lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ baaná naagba akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko baa.

english: Yams need soft, loose earth to grow long and thick tubers easily. Soil mounds give yam tubers space to expand underground and protect them from rotting when heavy rains flood the farm.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potatoes bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya. Gɔŋ lɛ haa sweet potato tsei lɛ hegbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni ehaaa amɛfite kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa ba ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunshine, groundwater, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to feed and grow large cobs.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni adu lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: This rot is caused by a fungal infection called black pod disease, which spreads quickly in wet, shaded farms. Pruning thick tree branches lets in sunlight and breeze to dry the pods and stop the sickness.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. niji ni mli tse ni afoɔ Ha hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ agbi ŋmeii lɛ ni ekpa hela lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants getting dark spots and dying during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rainwater splashes fungal spores from the soil onto the lower tomato leaves, causing a disease called blight. Trimming the bottom leaves and placing dry grass underneath prevents dirty water from splashing onto the plant.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ kɛyaa tomato baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ kɛ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ leaf blight baa. Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shishi lɛ, no tsiɔ nu fɔŋ naa koni ekashwie tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes twisting and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsi amɛhe ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Twisted leaves are a sign of cassava mosaic disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties protects your farm from this problem.
ga: Baai ni etsilɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ naagba nɛɛ he.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting from the tip down the center, it usually means the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build strong, green leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛtee teŋgbɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically a reaction to stress caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaf undersides, or a virus transmitted by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni jɛɔ haomɔ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baa lɛ shishi nu lɛ kɛbaa lɛ mli baa. loo helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them out in the open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct hot sun. They need shade crops like plantain trees around them to block harsh sunlight and retain soil moisture while their roots grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ koni amɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when heavy rains flood the field for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔji lɛ amli otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rainwater floods the field and stays for too long, it pushes all the air out of the soil, causing the roots to suffocate and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyi ŋmɔji amli ni ehiɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants before any fruit can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani aduawai baa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers as a survival trick when they face extreme heat, irregular watering, or prolonged dry spells, which prevents the plant from spending energy on fruit it cannot support.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi akɛ teemɔŋ sane ni baaha amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ aduawai ni enyɛŋ eŋmɛ etsui shi yɛ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up while they are still growing on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo be mli ni amɛmiida lolo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Blackening pods are caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads rapidly in cool, wet weather when raindrops splash fungal spores from wet soil onto low-hanging pods.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pods ji nɔ ni kɛ pods ni efee ediŋŋ lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛji nugbɔshiimɔi shwie fungal spores kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛtee pods ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ,

english: Why are my maize leaves covered in ragged holes when the crop is just a few weeks old?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ buji ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ? Ni tso lɛ hiɔ shi otsii fioo pɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize plants are caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that crawl into the dark center leaf funnel during the day and feed on the tender leaf tissue.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei bibii amli lɛ baa.

english: Why do groundnut plants push thin stalks into the dirt after their flowers fall off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ tsiɔ amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni fɔfɔi lɛ egbee shi lɛ?

english: Groundnut pods grow underground. After the yellow flower on top is pollinated, the plant sends down a peg stalk into the soil so the nut can safely develop underground away from heat and open air.
ga: Peanut ŋmɔtɔi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni afee fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pollination sɛɛ. Tso lɛ tsuɔ peg ŋmeii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he.

english: Why do my seed yams start sprouting in the storage barn before the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato dumɔwui jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break their rest period when air temperatures inside the barn rise, signaling to the tuber that it is time to start growing shoots even if it has not been planted in soil yet.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafo amɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa bulb lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ ebɔi ŋmeii akwɛ̃mɔ, kɛji akɛ aduko amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo po.

english: Why does my rice crop fall flat to the ground right before it is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Rice falls over, or lodges, when the stems grow too tall and weak to support heavy grain heads, often because too much nitrogen fertilizer was applied or heavy winds hit wet soil.
ga: Omɔ gbeeɔ shi loo efoɔ kɛji eshishifãi lɛ dara tsɔ ni egbɔjɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni tswaa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the maize seeds I planted a week ago not coming up out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni midu yɛ otsi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ejeee kpo kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds need moisture to wake up and start growing. If rain does not fall after planting, the seeds simply stay dormant in the dry ground waiting for water, or heat and soil insects can destroy them before they sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia amɛ koni amɛte shi ni amɛbɔi dalɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ No lɛ dumɔwui lɛ baajɔɔ amɛhe yɛ hei ni egbi, ni amɛbaamɛ nu. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, dɔlɛ kɛ sũ mli kooloi baanyɛ afite dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How can I check if seeds lying in dry ground are still alive or if they have rotted?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji dumɔwui ni akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo loo amɛgboi?

english: Gently dig up a few spots in your planted row. If the seed is firm and looks the same as when you planted it, it is alive and waiting for rain; if it is soft, mushy, smells bad, or eaten by pests, it has rotted and you will need to replant.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ he bibioo ko yɛ ŋtayaa ni adu lɛ mli blɛoo. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ wa lolo ni amɛhiɛ tamɔ be ni adu lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛmiimɛ nugbɔ. Kɛji amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛhe ŋmɔlɔ, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui eye amɛ lɛ, Ebaafite ni ehe baahia ni okɛwo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has enough water in it before I start planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil from a few inches below the surface into a ball. If it holds together without crumbling and leaves your palm damp, there is enough water for seeds to sprout; if it crumbles into dry dust, you should wait for more rain.
ga: Okɛ shikpɔŋ fioo ko ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shishi lɛ afee bɔɔlu. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ he ni egbeeee shi ni ehaaa oniji afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Etsɔɔ akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji egbɛ eshwa ni etsɔ sũ ni egbi lɛ, esa akɛ omɛ nugbɔ babaoo.

english: If rain falls heavily for just one day and then stops for two weeks, will my newly planted seeds survive?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa gbi kome ni no sɛɛ lɛ ekpa otsii enyɔ Ani dumɔwui heei ni adu lɛ baahi shi?

english: A single day of rain often only wets the top layer of dirt, which dries out fast under hot sun. If the ground dries completely before the seedling establishes strong roots, the sprout will dry up and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ gbi kome lɛ haa muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ shwieɔ shi. ni gĩɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ kwraa dani dumɔwui lɛ ná shishifãi ni wa lɛ, Tso bibioo lɛ baagbi ni ebaagbo.

english: Why do the leaves on my crop plants droop and curl up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miigbo ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants curl and droop their leaves to protect themselves from losing water through heat. It is a survival mechanism where the plant rolls up its leaves to shield them from the burning sun when there is little moisture in the soil.
ga: Tsei lɛ baabɔle amɛhe ni amɛbaajie amɛbai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni hulutsoo be lɛ fiteɔ lɛ he. Eji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahiɔ shi ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛfoɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Why do my crops stop growing tall when rain does not fall for two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko otsii enyɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Water works like a carrier that takes plant food from the soil up into the stems and leaves. Without rain, the plant cannot absorb these nutrients, so it pauses its growth to conserve energy until moisture returns.
ga: Nu tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni hiɛɔ tsei amli niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ kpaɔ amɛdalɛ be kukuoo ko koni amɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni nu lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants without producing any fruits during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When a plant experiences heat and lack of water, it gets stressed and drops its flowers to save its own life, because making fruits requires a lot of water that the plant currently lacks.
ga: Kɛ tsei na dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baaná haomɔ ni ekɛ fɔfɔii baashwie shi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, aduawai akwɛ̃mɔ biɔ nu babaoo, ni tsei bɛ amrɔ nɛɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass or leaves around my crops help them when there is no rain?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ tɛŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Covering the ground around crops with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like an umbrella for the soil. It blocks the hot sun from drying out the ground, keeping the soil cool and moist for a longer time.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha he ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ lɛ he lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does the top layer of my soil turn into a hard crust that young crop shoots cannot push through?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ ebatsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ŋmeii bibii nyɛɛɛ abote mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain followed immediately by strong sun bakes bare soil into a hard crust. Adding organic matter like decomposed animal manure or compost helps keep the soil loose and soft so young shoots can push up easily.
ga: Amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa nyiɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ, ni eha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee blɛoo bɔni afee ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli mlɛo.

english: What is the best thing for me to do on my farm immediately after rain falls after a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafee yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ enɛ yɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ sɛɛ?

english: Clear out weeds right away because they grow fast after rain and will steal the fresh water from your crops, and hold off on applying strong dry chemical fertilizers until the soil is thoroughly soaked.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛdaraa oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. ni ebaaju nu kpakpa kɛjɛ onibii amli Ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni egbi ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there is too much direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to survive because direct sunlight dries them out and burns their young leaves. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shade and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating under the hot sun. It keeps the soil moist for longer, suppresses weed growth, and eventually breaks down to enrich the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ la yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, efoɔ koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yellow leaves on growing maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, a vital nutrient plants need to stay green and produce big ears. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or farm manure early in the plant's life prevents this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni tsei ni niyenii ni he hiaa yɔɔ mli lɛ ahi shi akɛ eŋɔli ni amɛná toi wuji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Will planting cowpeas or beans in the same field with my maize harm my crop?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni mikɛduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Planting legumes like beans or cowpeas alongside maize actually helps the soil. Legumes take nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which feeds the maize and improves your total harvest.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa woɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Legumes gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. ni haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa onibii fɛɛ ni onáa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why is it bad to apply chemical fertilizer when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baawo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. Putting dry fertilizer on dry soil can burn plant roots and cause the fertilizer to wash away or waste without helping the crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ loo eyafite ni ehaaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in the middle leaf funnels of my young maize?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni ji niyenii ni ayeɔ yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli?

english: Small holes inside the funnel of maize plants are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. Spraying targeted controls early when the caterpillars are small prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the maize.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ amli lɛ baa. Mra be mli, nibii ni akɛyeɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lɛ, enɛ haaa amɛfite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants twisting up and turning yellowish?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf twisting in tomatoes is often caused by a plant virus spread by tiny whiteflies, or by extreme heat and uneven watering. Controlling whitefly insects and watering regularly helps keep tomato leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa mli Whitefly nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tomato baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I leave all the young shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi tsei bibii lɛ fɛɛ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ashishi?

english: Leaving too many suckers starves the main plantain tree of food and water, leading to tiny bunches. Pruning the extra shoots so that you keep only one main tree, one medium shoot, and one small shoot yields larger plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tsei lɛ ashishifãi babaoo lɛ, ebaaha niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ faaa. ni kɛ jwɛi bibii baa Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oookpa bɔni afee ni okɛ tso titri kome pɛ, tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tso kome, kɛ tso bibioo kome pɛ ahi shi lɛ baaha dumɔwui wuji aba.

english: Yam plants produce tubers underground by using sunlight collected by their leaves. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so leaves get maximum sunlight, which results in larger, heavier yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii ni dara ni tsii.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water cuts off air to the soil and encourages fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ be mli ni nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die if I clear all the shade trees from my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji mijie cacao tsei fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani midu lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or forest trees to protect them from heat stress and retain soil moisture until they are mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a short dry spell, which can dry out and kill newly sprouted seeds before the main rainy season fully established.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ, ni baanyɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baa naagbee.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in wet, humid conditions when trees are pruned too dense or weed cover is too high.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Beni afo tsei lɛ babaoo tsɔ Aloo jwɛi lɛ nɔ kwɔ tsɔ.

english: This damage is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies that feed on the sap of young plants.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly, ni yeɔ tsei bibii amli nu lɛ.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient the plant needs to grow strong leaves and healthy grains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛná baai ni wa kɛ ŋmaa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yam tubers become misshapen when the soil is too hard or stony, preventing the tuber from pushing downward easily as it grows.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ tɛi. Enɛ haaa yitso lɛ ashɛ shi mlɛo beni edaa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their blossoms before any tomatoes actually form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani tomato lɛ eba diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when there are not enough insects to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ bɛ

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants shrinking and twisting into tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiitsɔ kɔɔpoi bibii amli lɛ?

english: Twisted or cupped pepper leaves are usually caused by microscopic pests like mites or thrips sucking nutrients from the underside of the leaf.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni shwieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa ni etsɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same plot of land without killing both crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mifiteee ŋmãa enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, planting them together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in three months, leaving space and light for the slower-growing cassava.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli. Enɛ haa gbɛ kɛ la haa ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous maize harvest produce smaller yields than certified seed bags from agro-dealers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui kotoku ni okwaayeli mlijalɔ lɛ kpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Many modern seeds are hybrids engineered for one strong harvest; saving seeds from those plants causes the next generation to lose their strength and disease resistance.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui babaoo ji dumɔwui ni afee amɛ ekome kɛha kpamɔ ni mli wa shikome. Nakai tsei lɛ amli dumɔwui ni abuɔ he lɛ haa wɔsɛɛ yinɔi lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ helai ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Where can I get good quality maize seeds to plant so that my farm yields a plenty harvest?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana ŋmãa dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni madu koni eha miŋmɔ lɛ aná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: You can buy certified improved seeds from registered agricultural dealers or through your local Ministry of Agriculture office. Certified seeds are specially selected to withstand local heat, resist diseases, and yield much more grain than seeds saved from your last harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ ohe dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ loo kɛtsɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ nɔ. Ahala dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli dɔlɛ naa, amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai, ni amɛwo dumɔwui babaoo fe dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ okpamɔ ni okpa nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure early in the plant's life will turn the leaves green and help them feed the growing crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni baai lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni eda.

english: How does a sudden dry spell after planting affect my young maize crop?
ga: Te hulutsoo be ni baa trukaa yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ saa mibi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Young maize plants need moisture during their first few weeks to build deep roots. A dry spell right after sprout can stunt the roots, making the plant weak and unable to absorb nutrients properly when rains return.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛ́ hulu lɛ enyɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii kpakpa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are there small holes in my young maize leaves with tiny caterpillars hiding inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni ani ŋmeii bibii Ehi mli?

english: This is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which eat the young tender leaves of maize. Spraying recommended treatments into the center funnel of the plant early in the morning or late evening stops them before they ruin the entire cob.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkpa dani amɛbaafite ŋmei muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: When is the exact right time for me to plant maize during the rainy season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔ be mli yɛ Ghana?

english: The best time to plant is immediately after two or three strong, steady rains have wet the soil deeply. Planting in dry soil risks seed rot, while waiting too late misses the full rainfall needed for the ears to fill up with grain.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite. Kɛ́ omɛ sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo ni he hiaa koni akɛwo ŋmaa lɛ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to apply fertilizer twice instead of putting all of it in the soil at once when planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii shii enyɔ moŋ fe ni makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikome beni miduɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Maize uses different nutrients at different times. Putting NPK fertilizer at planting builds strong roots, while adding Nitrogen four weeks later feeds the fast-growing stalk and developing ear, preventing heavy rains from washing all the food away too soon.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii srɔtoi tsuɔ nii yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Kɛ́ okɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii fata odumɔ he lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi ni mli wa aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nitrogen ni akɛfataa he yɛ otsii ejwɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni eha tsei ni daraa oya kɛ toi ni daraa lɛ niyenii. Tsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ oya tsɔ.

english: How can I tell that my maize is completely mature and ready to be harvested from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Maize is ready when the green outer husks dry up and turn brown, and the grains feel hard when pressed with a thumbnail. You will also see a small black spot at the tip of individual grains where they attach to the cob.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ji ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ nuɔ he waa kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne bibioo ko nyɛ nɔ. Obaana ŋmeii diji bibii. Yɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa

english: Why does my stored harvested maize turn into powder and get eaten by small insects in my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mifo lɛ etsɔ powda ni kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ eye lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils attack maize if it is stored while still slightly damp. Drying your maize thoroughly in the sun until the grains crack cleanly when bitten, and using airtight storage bags, starves insects of moisture and air so your grain stays safe.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii baatutua ŋmãa kɛji akɛ akɛto be mli ni edɔ fioo lolo. Okɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ fɛɛ baanyɛ atswa kɛji akɛ amɔ lɛ. ni okɛ vacuum storage bag atsu nii Eshwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi amli. Koni odumɔwui lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: How can the local Ministry of Agriculture help me if my maize crop fails because of difficult climate conditions?
ga: Te maŋ lɛ mli Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi aha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa hewɔ lɛ?

english: Local extension officers can visit your farm to assess damage, connect you with government input assistance or subsidized seed programs, and guide you on planting drought-tolerant varieties suited for bad weather seasons.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ayasara oŋmɔ lɛ koni amɛyakwɛ nɔ ni efite lɛ. Ekɛ bo tsa maŋ nɔyeli yelikɛbuamɔ loo dumɔwui ahe gbɛjianɔtoi ni akɛ shika yeɔ ebuaa lɛ nɔ. ni etsɔɔ bo gbɛ yɛ tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ hɔmɔ naa ni sa kɛha bei ni kɔɔyɔŋ ehiii lɛ adumɔ mli.

english: Why should I keep proper distance between my maize plants instead of planting them very close to get more crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee gbɛ ni sa yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: If maize plants are too close, they fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water, resulting in thin stalks and small or empty cobs. Giving them proper spacing allows each plant to get full sunlight and produce big, healthy ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ekɛ hulu la, shikpɔŋ niyenii kɛ nu yeɔ akaŋ, ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmãa bibii kɛ ŋmãa bibii loo nɔ ko ni bɛ nɔ ko. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ, enáa hulu la ni fa babaoo, ni ehaa etoi lɛ feɔ agbo ni ehe wa.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to plant plantains on the same land with young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔdu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wɔduɔ cocoa tsei bibii lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings die easily when exposed to direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that create living shade umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting the cocoa while giving you food and income in the early years.
ga: Young cacao trees easily die when exposed to direct sunlight. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa. It keeps the soil moist and protects the cocoa while providing food and income in the early years.

english: How do I choose the best plantain sucker to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain sucker ni hi fe fɛɛ ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Always select 'sword suckers' which have narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a thick base near the soil. They grow faster, produce stronger plants, and yield larger bunches compared to 'water suckers' which have broad leaves early on and weak stems.
ga: Always select 'Sword Bud' which has narrow, lance-shaped leaves and a thick base close to the soil. Amɛ daa oya. Produce stronger plants and gives larger clusters of fruits compared to 'water-sucking shoots' which have broad leaves early and weak stems.

english: Plant them about 3 meters (around 10 feet) apart in a grid. Proper spacing ensures that every plant gets enough sunlight, rain, and soil nutrients without competing with neighboring plants.
ga: Dumɔ amɛ aaafee mitai 3 (aaafee ninetalɔi 10) yɛ grid mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu, nugbɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: This is usually caused by stem or root borers (weevils) and tiny root worms underground that eat through the plant's base. This destroys the root system so the heavy plant can no longer hold itself upright.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso loo shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi (ŋmeii) kɛ shishifãi bibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. shikpɔŋ shishi ni yeɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi Enɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ, ni ehaa tso ni tsii lɛ nyɛɛɛ adamɔ shi shiŋŋ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain plants turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tso lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: As plantains grow, older bottom leaves naturally dry up and die. However, if many leaves turn yellow at once, it usually means the soil lacks water or nutrients like nitrogen, or the plant is affected by a fungal leaf disease.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ dara lɛ Baai ni edara lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgboiɔ. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai babaoo batsɔ ŋmɔŋ shikome lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ nu loo niyenii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ fungal leaf hela ko emɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do plantain leaves split into ribbons when the weather gets windy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain baai lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves are designed by nature to tear along their veins during high winds. This allows the wind to pass through harmlessly so the whole main stem doesn't snap or get uprooted.
ga: Plantain leaves are naturally designed to tear along their veins during high winds. Eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efeee lɛ. The entire main stem was therefore not broken or uprooted.

english: How many suckers should I allow to grow around one parent plantain tree?
ga: Esa akɛ maŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii enyiɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu kome he?

english: Keep only 2 or 3 healthy suckers at different ages (one main fruiting plant, one medium sucker, and one small shoot). Allowing too many suckers starves the main plant of food, resulting in very small plantain bunches.
ga: Ha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 2 loo 3 pɛ ahi shi yɛ afii fɛɛ mli. (1 main fruiting plant, 1 medium-sized shoot, and 1 small fruiting plant) Leaving too many shoots to develop will starve the main food plant. Enɛ haa anáa plantains bibii bibii waa.

english: Is it better to clear weeds around plantain trees using a cutlass or weedkiller spray?
ga: Ani ebafeŋ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaajie jwɛi kɛjɛ he ni ebɔle he lɛ? Dumɔwui ni akɛ tsɔne kuku loo tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Manual clearing with a cutlass or using mulch is generally safer because plantain roots grow very close to the top of the soil. Heavy chemical spraying or digging deep into the soil can damage these surface roots and stunt crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nine ni akɛ cutlass loo mulch tsuɔ he nii lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ejaakɛ plantain shishifãi lɛ daa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Tsofai ni tsii ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ afite nɛkɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi nɛɛ ni etsĩ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer or manure to my plantain crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo midumɔwui lɛ amli?

english: Apply fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure early in the rainy season when the soil is moist. This allows the root system to easily absorb nutrients without burning the plant.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ afata he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛshãaa tso lɛ.

english: How can I tell when a plantain bunch is fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni plantains lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A plantain bunch is mature when the individual fruits lose their sharp, angular edges and become full and rounded, and the dry flower tips at the ends easily drop off when touched.
ga: Plantains kuu ko shɛɔ dalɛ he beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni eyi obɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Ni fɔfɔii ni egbi ni yɔɔ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baagbee shi oya kɛji akɛ ata he.

english: Can I plant my corn in that low area of my farm where rainwater usually gathers and settles?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ? ni ji ŋmɔ ko ni bei pii lɛ nugbɔ nu buaa ehe naa ni ehaa shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: No, corn roots dislike sitting in standing water. When water settles on the land, it drowns the roots, rots them, and causes the crop to turn yellow and die.
ga: Dabi, ŋmãa shishifãi sumɔɔɔ ni amɛtaraa nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli. Kɛ́ nu gbee shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgboɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Does maize need heavy, continuous rainfall throughout the season to grow well?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni naa wa ni yaa nɔ yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: No, maize actually prefers moderate moisture. Too much water harms the plant far more than a short dry period, especially if the ground stays soaked.
ga: Dabi, ŋmãa sumɔɔ hulutsoo ni mli wa. Nu babaoo yeɔ tsei awui fe be kuku ni nu bɛ. Titri lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo.

english: Is it a good idea to plant maize on a path where rainwater flows down during heavy storms?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔ nu line nɔ yɛ ahum ni naa wa ko mli?

english: It is best to avoid areas where water flows over the ground. Moving water washes away the topsoil around maize roots and can expose or uproot young plants.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ hei ni nu hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe. Nu ni hoɔ lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ kɛbɔleɔ he. ajieɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ni ebaanyɛ eha tsei bibii aba loo ajie amɛ kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi amli.

english: How do I know if a piece of land is good enough for planting corn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ko hi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa?

english: Look for land where water drains away naturally after a downpour. Corn requires well-drained land and will fail in places where water gathers or leaves muddy pools.
ga: Taomɔ hei ni nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ. He ko ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa he miihia. ni ebaafite yɛ hei ni nu buaa ehe naa loo ejɛɔ sũ mli ŋmeii amli lɛ.

english: Why do my corn plants turn yellow and stop growing whenever we get heavy rain for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: When water collects underground around the roots, it blocks the air the plant needs to breathe. The yellow leaves are a sign that the roots are suffocating from too much water.
ga: Kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛmu lɛ naa. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nu babaoo bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tsɔ.

english: I have a swampy patch on my farmland. Can I clear it and plant corn there?
ga: Miyɛ ŋshɔ ko yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ani obaanyɛ otsi mli ni odu ŋmãa yɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Corn is not suitable for swampy or marshy ground because its roots decay quickly in wet soil. That type of land is better suited for crops that love water, like rice.
ga: Abɛi esaaa kɛha hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ejaakɛ eshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɛɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei ni sumɔɔ nu, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: What will happen to my corn seeds if I plant them in soil that stays wet long after the rain stops?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If the soil remains soaked for too long, the corn seeds will rot under the ground before they even have the chance to sprout.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewo nu be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Abɛi dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi dani amɛnáa hegbɛ po ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: If rainwater collects under my plants after every downpour, will I still get a good harvest?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi be fɛɛ be beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ Ani maná yibiiwoo kpakpa lolo?

english: Water collecting around the root zone weakens the whole plant, which leads to poor cob development, stunted growth, and a low harvest.
ga: Nu ni akɛtoɔ he ni ebɔle Shishifã lɛ he lɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haaa cob lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. ŋmɔji ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli ni ŋmaa lɛ faaa

english: Should I plant my maize on higher ground or down in the flat valley where the soil stays wet?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ loo yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: It is safer to plant maize on higher or gently sloping ground. Valley floors often collect standing water, which prevents maize roots from growing deep and strong.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu abele yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ loo yɛ he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ fioo. Bei pii lɛ, jɔɔ lɛ shishi buaa nu ni damɔ shi lɛ naa. Enɛ haaa ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why does water pooling around my young corn stalks cause them to fall over easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu buaa ehe naa Mɛni hewɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ miigbee shi mlɛo lɛ?

english: Standing water softens the earth around the base of the plant and weakens the roots, leaving the corn with no firm grip to stay upright against the wind.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ hu gbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa lɛ nyɛɛɛ adamɔ ehe shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops refuse to grow well even when I clear the land and remove all weeds regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jɛmɛ ni mijieɔ jwɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ daa moŋ?

english: Crops require healthy soil filled with nutrients and proper moisture to grow, not just a clean field. Poor soil quality, high soil acidity, or a lack of organic matter can prevent crops from thriving regardless of how clean the land is kept.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa eyi mli obɔ lɛ he miihia tsei koni amɛshwere. Jeee ŋmɔ ni mli tse kɛkɛ ni. shikpɔŋ ni ehiii shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ acid ni fa babaoo Aloo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse ha

english: Why did my neighbor get a huge harvest while my farm right next to theirs failed on the same type of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ miiwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Farm success relies heavily on specific management techniques—such as correct planting distances, timely application of fertilizer, pest management, and using certified seeds—rather than land location alone.
ga: Okwaayeli omanyeyeli damɔ gbɛi pɔtɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ nɔ, tamɔ gbɛ ni ja ni akɛduɔ nii. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii Yɛ shikpɔŋ pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland is exhausted and needs rest or treatment before I plant again?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔ nii lɛ efo ni ehe miihia ni mafo mli loo atsa lɛ dani madu ekoŋŋ?

english: Exhausted soil often shows signs like crop leaves turning pale yellow, stunted crop growth, thin plant stems, water washing away soil easily, and low crop yields even when rainfall is good.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ jieɔ okadii tamɔ tsei ahe baai ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tseee lɛ akpo. dwarf tso dalɛ tso shishifã bibioo Nu hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ oya. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does it take up to two or three years for new cocoa trees to start giving good harvest after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii enyɔ loo etɛ dani kookoo tsei heei jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Perennial crops like cocoa focus their early years on building deep root systems and sturdy stems to support future pods; they need time to mature fully before they can produce heavy yields.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ kookoo kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni wa ni baaye abua wɔsɛɛ pods lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná be dani amɛdara dani amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Is weeding my cassava farm once every few months enough to keep the tubers growing big?
ga: Ani nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ adara?

english: No, early and frequent weeding is critical during the first few months because weeds aggressively steal soil nutrients and water, leaving the cassava roots weak and small.
ga: Dabi, jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ni bei pii lɛ, enɛ he hiaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ kɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and drop during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense mechanism crops use to reduce water loss during intense heat. If the soil lacks adequate moisture, the plant sheds leaves to keep its main stem alive.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he.

english: Can adding animal manure or compost really bring life back to poor farm land?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha wala aku sɛɛ aba hei ni okwaayeli bɛ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, organic matter like manure adds essential plant nutrients, helps the soil hold onto water longer, and encourages healthy soil organisms that break down minerals for crops to feed on.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmei kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa fataa tsei ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni ewo shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni gbálaa sũ mli nibii amli lɛ ahe hewalɛ koni efee nɔ ni tsei yeɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I just plant the leftover seeds saved from my previous maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni eshwɛ ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from past harvests lose their vigor and disease resistance over time, while certified seeds are specifically bred to produce uniform, high-yielding crops resistant to local pests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni akɛwo tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why are yellow spots appearing on my tomato leaves before they turn brown and fall off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi jeɔ kpo yɛ tomato baai anɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yellow and brown spots are usually caused by fungal or bacterial diseases spreading in damp soil or high humidity, which deprives the plant of leaves needed to make food for flowers and fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo helatsɛmɛi ahelai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ bɛ baai, ni he hiaa koni ewo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: If my crop failed on a piece of land this year, can I make that same land productive again next year?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fite yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi nɛɛ Ani manyɛ maha nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ awo yibii ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Yes, poor land can be restored over time by rotating crops, applying organic fertilizer, practicing proper tillage, and using recommended planting techniques to rebuild soil health.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ organic fertilizers ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ aduɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛtswa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to grow strong. It can also happen if the field is flooded with too much water, which prevents roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha shweremɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu eyi ŋmɔji amli babaoo. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ anine shɛɛɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the central funnel leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that burrows into the leaf funnel of maize. Applying recommended biopesticides or neem leaf extract early in the morning or evening can help control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ wo mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ lɛ dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before growing fully?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii So minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo dani ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, wet conditions. Pruning extra shade branches to let sunlight in and clearing weeds around the tree base helps prevent it.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni duŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ amli koni hulu la babaoo abote mli, ni ajie jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before they can form pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress from dry weather or extreme heat. Maintaining adequate shade trees helps keep the farm cool and retains moisture so flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei lɛ ni oooha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii.

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. You can manage this by planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties provided by agricultural officers.
ga: Enɛ ji cassava mosaic hela, ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛhaa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: Early drying of yam vines is often caused by Yam Anthracnose, a fungal disease spread by rain splashing on the leaves. Planting clean seed yams and clearing infected vines prevents it from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni ji anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Sweet potatoes ni he tse ni aduɔ ni ajieɔ wain tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow tall with lots of green leaves but produce very few flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo shi ewoɔ fɔfɔi fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: This happens when plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces them to produce stems and leaves instead of fruit. Using fertilizers with higher phosphorus content encourages flowering.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛwo tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are my chili pepper leaves rolling up into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ mi chili baai lɛ ebɔle kɔɔpoi ahe shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a leaf curl virus. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaves from curling and keeps the plant productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo leaf curl virus Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baatsi baa lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua ni tso lɛ aya nɔ ewo yibii.

english: Why is my plantain stem falling over at the roots before the fruit cluster is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ miiho kɛmiiya shishifãi lɛ anɔ dani aduawai akui lɛ efee klalo lɛ?

english: Tiny underground worms called nematodes or stem borer insects weaken the roots and base of the plantain stem. Planting clean, treated suckers helps anchor the plant firmly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ haa plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni he tse ni atsa amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: Drooping is a natural mechanism plants use to protect themselves from hot weather. They reduce their leaf surface area exposed to the sun to hold onto moisture until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Drooping ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Tsɔɔmɔ baai ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning yellow at the bottom instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK helps the leaves make food again.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ fãi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo NPK tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛwo niyenii ekoŋŋ.

english: If I put a lot of fertilizer on my crops at once, will it make them yield twice as fast?
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ be kome too mli lɛ, ani ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abɔ he toi enyɔ?

english: No, putting too much chemical fertilizer at once can burn the crop's roots and dry out the leaves. Crops can only absorb a certain amount of food at a time, so it is better to give smaller amounts at the right growth stages.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ tsofai babaoo wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni eha baai lɛ agbi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii fioo ko pɛ yɛ be kome mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ aha amɛ niyenii bibii yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or if there is too much nitrogen in the soil making the plant grow leaves instead of fruit. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ha tsei lɛ aná baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.
