english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall and thin with few leaves when planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ebɛ baai fioo pɛ kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs full sunlight to produce energy and grow big roots under the ground. When planted in heavy shade, the plant wastes its energy stretching upward to reach the light instead of feeding the underground tubers.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia cassava koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba ni ekwɛ̃ shishifãi wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli Tsei lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ni amɛkpãa koni amɛná la nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaaha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Rolling leaves is a pepper plant's natural shield against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant shrinks the area exposed to the sun to prevent water from evaporating too quickly from its body.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji pepper tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ he tsɔne. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la lɛ mli koni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my okra stems turn soft and rot at the bottom during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tsei lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water collects around the roots for too long, the soil runs out of air and bad fungi grow easily. Planting on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away so the stem base stays healthy.
ga: Kɛ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli ni ewaaa akɛ ŋmeii gbohii baakwɛ̃. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛyaa. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ mli wa.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over easily when I plant three or four seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ midu dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds grow in one spot, the stems compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves them with thin, weak stems and shallow roots that cannot hold the plant up against strong winds.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa.

english: How do weeds growing close to my yam heaps prevent the yam tubers from expanding?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ he lɛ atsĩ sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã?

english: Weeds steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight that your yam plant needs to make food. Without enough food reaching the leaves, the plant cannot send energy down to swell the underground tuber.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa sweet potato tsei koni amɛfee niyenii lɛ. Kɛji niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baashɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ bɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ atsu hewalɛ kɛba shi ni eha tuber lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cowpea plants covered in a sticky liquid and turning black?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni shãa mɔ he ehà mi-cowpea tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ? ni etsake efee ediŋŋ

english: Tiny insects called aphids suck the sweet juice from cowpea leaves and leave behind a sugary liquid. Black mold then grows on this sweet liquid, which blocks sunlight and stops the leaves from working properly.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ aphids lɛ nuɔ tsina ŋmeii ahe nu ni amɛshiɔ nu ni mli edɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ diŋ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni ŋɔɔ nɛɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa ni ehaaa baai lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Groundnut plants show maturity when their outer leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off. Pulling up one test plant and checking inside the shell will confirm it: if the inside lining has turned dark brown or black, the nuts are ready.
ga: Peanut tsei lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ko ni akaa lɛ akwɛɔ lɛ wo ŋwɛi ni okwɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaama enɛ nɔ mi: Kɛji akɛ mligbɛ tsɔne lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen gives leaves their dark green color and energy to grow, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps bring back their health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Nitrogen haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛdaraa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow so tall with many leaves but produce very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ pepper fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Giving your pepper plants too much nitrogen fertilizer makes them focus all their energy on growing foliage instead of fruit. Switching to fertilizers richer in phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to form flowers and yield peppers.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen babaoo ha o-pepper tso lɛ, ebaaha ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe aduawai. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do small caterpillars manage to destroy my entire maize farm in just a few days?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei bibioo ko akpata mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli?

english: These pests, commonly called fall armyworms, hide deep inside the central funnel of the plant during the day and eat rapidly at night. Because a single moth lays hundreds of eggs at once, a small attack can multiply into full farm damage very quickly if not caught early.
ga: Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ Ale amɛ hu akɛ fall cutworm. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ shwane mli, ni eyeɔ nii oya gbɛkɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei kome baanyɛ awo wuji ohai abɔ shikome. Tutuamɔi bibii baanyɛ aya hiɛ oya ni efite ŋmɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛji akɛ amɔmɔɔɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why do the yam tubers in my field turn soft and rot underground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Soft underground rot is caused by microscopic pests like nematodes or fungi that live in waterlogged or poorly drained soil. They enter the yam through tiny cracks or insect wounds and break down the flesh before the yam fully matures.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi fitemɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ nematodes loo fungi ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii loo pilamɔi ni jɛ kooloi amli lɛ amli amɛboteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛfoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: What will happen if I accidentally plant my cassava stem cuttings upside down in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ oshara du ŋmei nine ko ni mikɛ mihe wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stem nodes have small buds that need to point upward to sprout leaves quickly. Planting them upside down forces the new stems to curve around underground to find the light, which weakens the plant and leads to a much smaller yield of root tubers.
ga: Kasava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Esa akɛ no atsɔɔ ŋwɛi koni baai lɛ adara oya. Dumɔ ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ haa tso hee lɛ shwieɔ shi. shikpɔŋ shishi koni ana la ni haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa shishifãi ni baa lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants die during the dry season if I do not plant plantains near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli kɛji miduuu plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate direct sunlight and harsh dry winds like the Harmattan. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist during the cocoa plant's first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa tamɔ Harmattan lɛ naa. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ cacao tso lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I buy fresh hybrid maize seeds each season instead of saving seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa heei ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ daa afi moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields and disease resistance, but those strong qualities only last for the first generation. If you plant saved seeds, the crop will grow unevenly, attract more diseases, and produce much smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye helai anɔ. Shi nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ato lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ edaŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Egbalaa helai babaoo ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bibioo kwraa lɛ baa

english: How does growing groundnuts or cowpeas on my field make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas work with beneficial organisms in the soil to grab nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop finishes growing and decomposes, that stored nitrogen stays behind as natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei lɛ dara ni amɛfite Nitrogen ni ato lɛ baakã he ahi shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without growing any fruits when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat destroys the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing them from forming fruit. To save water and survive the heat stress, the plant naturally drops its unpollinated flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. ha efee nɔ ni wooo yibii Koni ekɛ nu akafite ni ehi shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shĩɔ fɔfɔi ni jeee adebɔɔ mli fɔfɔi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: How can I easily tell that my cassava roots are fully matured and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving leaves mostly at the very top of the stem. You can also dig up one sample plant in the field to confirm the roots are thick and firm before harvesting the rest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ashiɔ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Obaanyɛ otsa tso kome hu he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ ni ehi shi shiŋŋ dani okpa nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: How can I quickly get a lot of cassava planting materials if I only have a few stems?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná ŋmei dumɔ nibii babaoo oya kɛji tsei fioo pɛ miyɔɔ?

english: You can cut the healthy cassava stems into very small pieces called minisetts, each having just one or two nodes. When planted in a nursery bed, almost every small cut sprouts into a full new plant, allowing you to multiply your starting stock very quickly.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofolɔ ŋmei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli bibii bibii. Atsɛɔ lɛ minisɛt. Tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko yɛ node kome loo enyɔ pɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ, nɔ ni miihe ashɛ tso niji bibii fɛɛ baakwɛ̃ ni etsɔ tso hee. Ehaa okɛ tsei lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ oya.

english: Why do some farmers get dozens of plantain shoots from a single stump while mine only produces one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi naa plantain dumɔwui srɔtoi srɔtoi kɛjɛɔ shishifã kome mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni minɔ lɛ wo nine kome pɛ lɛ?

english: They use a technique called macropropagation where they cut the growing tip of a clean plantain corm. Destroying this main tip forces the corm to sprout many dormant buds, producing multiple young suckers in a short time.
ga: Akɛ ŋaa ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ makropropagation tsuɔ nii. Bɔni afee ni ofee enɛ lɛ, gbee dumɔwui ni miida lɛ ashishifãi ni he tse lɛ. Kɛ́ ofite nɛkɛ tip titri nɛɛ, ebaaha corm lɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii babaoo ni egboi. Ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Is it possible for me to increase my yam yield without spending a lot of money to buy heavy seed yams?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ mafee mi-sweet potato lɛ yibii babaoo ni mikɛ shika babaoo tsuuu nii yɛ sweet potato ni dumɔwui babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ he?

english: Yes, you can cut one tuber into many small seed pieces known as yam minisetts, treat them with ash or fungicide to prevent rotting, and plant them. This turns one seed yam into dozens of new tubers for the next season.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ ofolɔ ŋmei kome mli bibii babaoo ni atsɛɔ lɛ yam minisett lɛ, ni okɛ sũ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii atsu he nii koni ekafite, ni okɛdu. Enɛ baaha sweet potato kome afee tubers heei srɔtoi srɔtoi kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do my nursery seeds take so long to sprout compared to my neighbor's seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋbii lɛ dumɔwui ahe lɛ?

english: Seeds sprout fastest when kept at the right soil depth, given gentle watering, and kept warm. Planting seeds too deep or letting the soil dry out delays their growth or causes them to rot.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe fɛɛ kɛji akɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ ni sa mli. nu mli blɛoo ni eha edɔ Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ tsɔ loo aŋmɛ gbɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aya hiɛ fioo loo ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo.

english: Can I grow new pepper or tomato plants using cuttings from old branches instead of buying seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo tomato tso hee nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ momo nɔ moŋ fe ni mahe dumɔwui?

english: While some crops like sweet potatoes and cassava easily grow from stem cuttings, tomatoes and peppers grow much stronger and yield better fruits when raised directly from healthy seeds.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei komɛi, tamɔ sweet potatoes kɛ cassava, ji nɔ ni anyɛɔ akwɛɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ mli lɛ amli moŋ, shi tomato kɛ pepper lɛ daa waa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo kɛji akɛ adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak when I put four or five seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni mikɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young plants compete with each other for space, light, and soil nutrients. Giving each seed its own space allows roots to spread and grow thick, healthy stalks with big cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛdaraa kɛ ŋmei agbo ni mli wa.

english: Why do my young vegetable plants wilt quickly in the afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi shwane mli mra eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu wo amɛmli leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: Hot sunshine makes water evaporate quickly from both the soil and leaves. Covering the soil surface with dry leaves or straw (mulching) keeps the soil cool and traps water so roots stay hydrated all day.
ga: Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulching) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning yellow, and how does it stop them from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ ekpa dalɛ hu?

english: Leaf curling is caused by a virus usually spread by small insects like whiteflies. The damaged leaves cannot process sunlight properly to feed the plant, which slows down growth and leads to very small tubers.
ga: Virus ko ni bei pii lɛ koolooi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Baai ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa edalɛ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: What is the benefit of buying certified clean planting seeds instead of using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni he tse ni awo he odaseyeli he lɛ hemɔ he yɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Saved seeds often carry hidden diseases and pests from the previous season. Certified seeds are bred to be disease-free and vigorous, which means they sprout uniformly and grow much faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ yɛ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ koni hela akafee amɛ ni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: How do crop roots turn fertilizer into faster plant growth?
ga: Te tsei shishifãi tsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii koni tsei lɛ adara oya lɛ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Roots absorb dissolved nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus from moist soil. The plant uses sunlight to turn these nutrients into plant food, which powers rapid leafy growth and strong root development.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni mli edɔ tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Tsei kɛ hulu la tsakeɔ niyenii nɛɛ amɛfeɔ tsei niyenii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient plants need to grow green and strong, or that heavy rain has washed the nutrient too deep into the soil away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Niyenii nibii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ, ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with thick green leaves, but the tubers under the soil are very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa tsɔ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are crowded, cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground rather than storing starch in the roots to grow tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baawo baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ sisi a mi konɛ bulb nɛ wa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves tear into narrow strips when there is heavy wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gbálaa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves naturally split along their veins during strong winds to let air pass through easily, preventing the heavy wind from snapping the entire plant stem.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli mlɛo. Tsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ ni efite tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are my watermelons bursting open in the field right before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Watermelons crack open when they absorb a sudden, large amount of water after a dry spell, causing the inside of the fruit to expand faster than the outer skin can stretch.
ga: Watermelon lɛ tswaa kɛ́ eŋɔ nu babaoo trukaa beni egbi sɛɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ amli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Cocoa flowers drop off if the tree lacks moisture or nutrients, or if tiny insects called midges are not present to pollinate the blossoms so they can develop into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo niyenii kpakpai. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii bɛ Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture more food to send down to build larger underground tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo ni ekɛbaa shi koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does swamp rice grow well submerged in standing water while my maize crop rots and dies in wet soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ swamp rice lɛ shwereɔ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mi-corn lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels in their stems that carry oxygen down to their roots even underwater, whereas maize roots drown without oxygen in waterlogged soil.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii tsuɔ nii kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi po. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ baagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap underneath the leaves, or by a virus carried by insects that slows down growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi bibii ni haa amɛdalɛ baa shi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turning dark brown and soft before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the fruit, which often happens when watering is inconsistent during hot dry days.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ amli.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans in my field make the soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have natural nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and leave it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni eshiɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Is it a good idea for me to build a plastic greenhouse if I am farming in a very hot area like Tamale?
ga: Eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ matswa plastic greenhouse kɛji miitsu okwaayeli yɛ he ko ni hulu tsoɔ waa tamɔ Tamale.

english: Plastic greenhouses trap heat inside. In extremely hot places like Tamale, the temperature inside a standard greenhouse can get so high that it burns crops and stops them from producing fruit, unless you use expensive modern cooling equipment.
ga: Plastic tsũi ni haa jeŋ dɔɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ yɛ mli. Yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ waa, tamɔ Tamale lɛ, hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ waa aahu akɛ eshã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni eha ekpa yibiiwoo. Ja okɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ friji ni jara wa tsu nii.

english: How does using a shade net help my crops differently than a plastic greenhouse?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shade netting ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni esoroɔ amɛ yɛ plastic ŋmɔ mli?

english: A plastic greenhouse seals heat and moisture inside, which can overheat your plants. A shade net shields your crops from harsh, burning sunlight while still allowing cool breezes to flow through freely.
ga: Plastic tsũ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baamɔmɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ mli adɔ fe nine. Shade netting buɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, aŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ gbɛ ni etswaa oya.

english: What can I do if the inside of my plant shelter feels too hot and stuffy during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ mi tsei lɛ ashihilɛhe lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shwane mli?

english: You need to increase ventilation by opening or rolling up the side vents and curtains. This allows warm air to escape and fresh air to circulate, lowering both the temperature and the risk of crop disease.
ga: Esa akɛ oha kɔɔyɔɔ ni boteɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ sɛɛgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai kɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ ni ooogbele loo okɛwo nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo kɛ tso helai ahe oshara fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my crops seem to catch diseases more easily when the air around them feels hot and trapped?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aná hela oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli edɔ ni emɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Stuffy, unventilated environments trap humidity around plant leaves. Fungi and bacteria thrive in high heat and damp, stagnant air, making it very easy for diseases to attack your plants.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ ahe lɛ. Fungus kɛ bacteria yeɔ omanye yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni damɔ shi, ni mli edɔ mli. Ehaa helai yeɔ tsei oya waa.

english: Proper spacing allows air to flow freely between the plants. Good airflow dries excess moisture on leaves quickly, which prevents humidity build-up and reduces the spread of fungal diseases.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jogbaŋŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ agbi oya. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa shi, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why shouldn't I spray water directly on my crop leaves during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ nu shwieɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Water droplets on leaves during intense sunshine can cause heat damage to the leaf tissue. Additionally, wet leaves combined with hot air create an ideal environment for plant diseases to start.
ga: Nu ni shwieɔ baai anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha dɔlɛ afite baai lɛ ahe fãji. Kɛfata he lɛ, baai ni efɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei ahe helai shishijee.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them during hot periods?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tso shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ tɛŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Spreading dry grass or straw on the ground, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket over the soil. It shields the soil from direct sunlight, keeps the root zone cool, and stops soil moisture from evaporating quickly.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi fɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekaho oya

english: Are there specific seeds I should buy if I am farming in a hot, dry region of Ghana?
ga: Ani dumɔwui pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ ni esa akɛ mahe kɛji mifee okwaayeli yɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ ni jɛmɛ egbi yɛ Ghana?

english: Yes, seed varieties labeled as heat-tolerant or drought-resistant are bred specifically to handle high temperatures and limited rainfall, allowing them to produce good yields where normal seeds might fail.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔse dumɔwui srɔtoi ni aŋmala nɔ akɛ amɛnyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ naa lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛtsu hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ he nii. Enɛ haa amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ hei ni dumɔwui ni sa lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni bɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves wilt in the afternoon heat even when the ground is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: On extremely hot days, water evaporates from the leaves faster than the roots can suck it up from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to protect itself and will usually bounce back in the evening when temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa nɔ lɛ Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ehe he. Ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ esɛɛ gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without turning into fruit during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get excessively high, pollen becomes weak or sterile, preventing the flowers from getting fertilized. As a defense against heat stress, the plant naturally drops its unfertilized flowers.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pollen lɛ baagbɔjɔ loo ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. Etsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkawo fɔmɔ nii Koni hulutsoo haomɔ akafee lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni fɔfɔi bɛ mli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Officer, why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and burning when the sun is very bright?
ga: Agent Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa beni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and small roots that cannot handle direct harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing food crops like plantain next to them provides shade and retains soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii. ni nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ waa tɛ̃ɛ Niyenii nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Sir, why do I need to cut away some of the small shoot suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ hu ajie?

english: If too many suckers grow around the mother plantain, they will fight with it for water and soil nutrients, resulting in tiny plantain bunches. Pruning extra suckers ensures the main tree gets enough food to produce big bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ he lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tsei niji wuji.

english: Sir, why do my maize plants turn yellow and stop growing whenever rain does not fall for two weeks?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko otsii enyɔ?

english: Maize needs regular water to absorb food from the soil. When the soil dries out during a dry spell, the plant cannot feed itself, which causes the leaves to turn yellow and stunts its growth.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmãa daa koni enyɛ ejie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ ana niyenii amɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa amɛdaraaa.

english: Officer, why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before turning into fruits?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, usually caused by lack of water, extreme heat, or poor nutrients. Giving them steady moisture helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna haomɔ. This is usually caused by dehydration, extreme heat, or poor nutrition. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Sir, why are my cassava stems growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but the roots under the ground stay small?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or the soil is too hard, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Officer, why do my crops dry up and die when I put fertilizer right next to their stems?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii miigbi ni amɛmiigboi lɛ? Fɛɛnamɔ ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ he?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated chemical salts. Touching the main stem directly draws water out of the plant tissue, burning it. Fertilizer should always be placed a small distance away from the plant stem.
ga: Tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛ́ mɔ ko ta tso lɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ fãji lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ ni eshãa. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo.

english: Officer, what is causing small holes in the middle of my maize leaves with green dirt left inside?
ga: Official Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? ŋmãa baa teŋgbɛ Ni muji eŋɔli ni ekpɛtɛ mli?

english: This is typical damage caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide deep inside the center of the maize leaves to feed and leave behind their waste.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ fe fɛɛ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ koni amɛye niyenii ni amɛshi jwɛi yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Sir, why do my green cocoa pods turn black and rot when the heavy rainy season starts?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains and high humidity create the perfect environment for Black Pod fungal disease to spread quickly across cocoa pods. Clearing surrounding bushes helps airflow dry out the farm.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha black pod fungus hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ni afoɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebɔleɔ ŋmɔji ni egbi lɛ amli

english: Officer, why do my corn plants grow thin and tall without making big ears when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛkwɔ shi amɛwooo toi wuji kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ hei srɔtoi? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight. Instead of growing strong stems and fruit, they stretch upwards to try to get light before their neighbors.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ tsei kɛ aduawai ni mli wa. Mohu ɔ, a ngmɛɛ a he konɛ a bɔ mɔde nɛ a ha nɛ la nɛ ba a kpɔ mi bi ɔmɛ a hɛ mi.

english: Sir, why do my crops become weak and small if I leave weeds to grow in the farm?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛji mishi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the soil's water, sunlight, and nutrients. Removing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow healthily.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: Planting too closely causes overcrowding. Crops need space for air to circulate and roots to spread; otherwise, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stalks and smaller yields.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ gbɔmɛi babaoo baa. He ko he miihia tsei koni kɔɔyɔɔ abɔle amɛhe kɛ shishifãi ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, amɛbaatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I plant them in an open field without any trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooko tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the surrounding air moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why is it necessary to cut away some of the extra leaves from my pepper and tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai ni fa fe nine lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Trimming dense leaf growth allows fresh air to circulate through the middle of the plant. This reduces trapped moisture on leaves, which prevents fungal diseases and allows more sunlight to reach the fruit.
ga: Baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ amɛ, ni ebaaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ aduawai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so quickly when I pack them tightly into deep wooden crates for transport?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛwo tso adekai ni mli kwɔ amli jogbaŋŋ koni mikɛmaje lɛ?

english: Harvested tomatoes continue to breathe and produce heat. When packed tightly without room for air movement, heat and moisture get trapped inside the crate, causing the fruit to crush, sweat, and rot rapidly.
ga: Tomato ni akpa lɛ yaa nɔ emuɔ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ awo mli jogbaŋŋ ni gbɛ ko bɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli lɛ, Dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baatsi adeka lɛ mli. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ fãa, amɛshwieɔ latsaa ni amɛfiteɔ oya.

english: How should I load sacks of harvested cassava onto a truck for a long journey to market so they stay fresh?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mawo ŋmei ni akpa lɛ kotokui awo lɔle mli yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ ni mikɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi ehee?

english: You should arrange the sacks to leave small channels for air to pass through rather than stacking them tightly. Proper ventilation prevents heat from building up inside the load, which stops the cassava from fermenting and turning soft.
ga: Esa akɛ ato kotoku lɛ he gbɛjianɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii bibii pɛ ahi mli. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ amɛ ato shi shiŋŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa baatsi dɔlɛ naa koni ekabua jatsu lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee blɛoo.

english: Is it a good idea to cover my truckload of freshly picked cabbages tightly with a heavy plastic tarp while driving to the city?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mikɛ plastic tarp ni mli wa baaha kaaba ni ajie ehee ni yɔɔ mitsɔne lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ? Beni miikudɔ tsɔne kɛbote maŋ lɛ mli lɛ

english: No, covering fresh vegetables tightly with plastic tarps traps heat and moisture inside. This creates a hot environment that makes the cabbages sweat, wilt, and rot before you reach the market.
ga: Dabi, okɛ tarp aha aduawai heei lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ koni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli dɔɔ waa aahu akɛ, kaaba lɛ shwieɔ latsaa, egbɔjɔɔ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ jara nɔ.

english: Why should I leave spaces between the bags of dried maize stored inside my storeroom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmãa ni egbi ni akɛto mi nitoohe lɛ kotokui lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Leaving gaps between bags allows air to circulate constantly around them. Good airflow keeps the stored grain cool and dry, preventing mold growth and damp conditions that attract insects.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi gbɛ yɛ kotokui lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ yaa nɔ ebɔleɔ kotokui lɛ ahe. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmaa ni ato lɛ mli jɔɔ ni egbiɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ dalɛ kɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni gbalaa koolooi.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly when I stack them in a heap in the corner of my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto koŋ lɛ?

english: Harvested yams give off heat and moisture naturally. Piling them together traps this heat, so storing them on elevated, slotted shelves or yam barns allows cool air to blow around each tuber and keep them firm.
ga: Atomɔ ni akpaa lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i baa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ to he kome lɛ, ebaamɔ la ni tsoɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo shwɛmɔhe ni nɔ kwɔ loo sweet potato ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ abɔle ŋmeii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he ni eha amɛhi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do black spots appear on my vegetable leaves during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai lɛ feɔ diji yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: During heavy rains, high humidity and lack of air circulation keep leaf surfaces wet for long periods. Damp leaves create an ideal environment for fungal spores to settle and spread disease.
ga: yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ baaha baa lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i be kakadaŋŋ. Baai ni mli efɔ lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha fungal spores lɛ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛgbɛ helai amɛshwã.

english: Why is cocoa failing to grow properly on farmland that was previously cleared for galamsey mining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ni tsutsu lɛ ajie kɛha galamsey shika tsuru lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Mining strips away the fertile topsoil where plants get their food, leaving behind hard subsoil and chemicals that prevent cocoa roots from breathing, taking in nutrients, or finding clear water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atsaa lɛ jieɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni tsei naa amɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ. Nɔ pɛ ni eshwɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ tsofai ni haaa kookoo shishifãi lɛ amu, amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ, loo amɛkaná nu ni mli tse.

english: Why do my crops dry up and refuse to produce fruit when I water them with river water near mining sites?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛkpooɔ yibiiwoo beni mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa ni bɛŋkɛ he ni atsuɔ nii yɛ lɛ shwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: River water polluted by mining contains heavy mud and toxic chemicals that clog plant roots and prevent them from absorbing the clean water and soil nutrients needed for growth.
ga: Faa mli nu ni shika tsuru ŋmɔji efite lɛ yɛ muji ni tsii kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni tsiɔ tsei shishifãi anaa ni ehaaa amɛŋɔ nu ni mli tse kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛdara lɛ.

english: Why do leaves that rot on the ground under my trees help my cocoa farm produce better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni egboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Fallen leaves decompose into organic matter that acts like natural food for the soil, holding moisture near the roots and slowly feeding the trees.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oooha ebɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni okɛ niyenii aha tsei lɛ fiofio lɛ nɔ

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn brown and yellow when there are no shade trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni tsei ni haa ŋmɔtɔ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are soft and sensitive to strong sunlight; without shade crops like plantain to cover them, direct heat burns their leaves and dries out their roots.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ darako ni amɛnuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ekãa ni baaha nɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ, Direct heat baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: Can I plant cassava together with my young cocoa trees, or will it hurt the cocoa growth?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kookoo tsei bibii adu ŋmei? Aloo ebaafite bɔ ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots grow very large and aggressively take water and nutrients out of the soil, which can starve young cocoa trees before they are strong enough to compete.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ daa waa ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha cacao tsei bibii lɛ aye hɔmɔ dani amɛhe awa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛ amɛhe awo akaŋshii mli.

english: Why do the small flowers on my cocoa trees drop off before turning into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ cocoa ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from lack of nutrients, severe heat stress, or when sap-sucking insects damage the delicate stalks.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafite amɛ fɔfɔii kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ amɛmli. heat stress ni naa wa Aloo be mli ni kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ fiteɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why does trimming away extra branches from my cocoa tree help it make bigger pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cacao tso lɛ niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Pruning removes useless foliage, allowing the tree to send its energy and water directly into making healthy pods rather than feeding empty leaves.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛ nu tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛma ŋmeii ni wa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ baai ni bɛ nɔ ko baaha lɛ

english: When trees are overcrowded, their roots fight over soil food and their leaves block sunlight from one another, causing them to grow weak and bear less fruit.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ewooo yibii babaoo.

english: What will happen to my cocoa trees if tall weeds are left to grow around them for months?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔle mihe? cacao nyɔji babaoo

english: Tall weeds steal sunlight and soil food from cocoa trees while trapping humidity that causes black pod fungal disease to spread quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ juɔ hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ kookoo tsei amli lɛ, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa black pod fungus hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing smaller and fewer pods now compared to ten years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii bibii fe bɔ ni amɛji afii 10 ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees pass 20 to 30 years of age, their internal food transport weakens and the surrounding soil becomes exhausted, causing lower production unless renewed.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso ko eye afii 20 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, tso lɛ mli niyenii ni ekɛyaa lɛ baa shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ hu baa shi. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi ja afee ehee.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and turn yellow when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ beni mifolɔ tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct, intense sunlight and harsh winds. Big shade trees or temporary plants like plantains act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting the cocoa leaves from sun damage.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he.

english: What causes tiny caterpillars to eat holes inside the funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on the soft center leaves of young maize. Early detection and applying recommended treatments directly into the plant center help stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nibii ni anaa mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsuɔ he nii lɛ baatsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baaye abua ni akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or whiteflies that transmit viruses. Managing these small insects early prevents leaf damage and allows the plant to set healthy fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, thrips, loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ŋmeii bibii akwɛmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaatsi baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I get smaller yields when I plant cassava on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Cassava takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts the soil strength, so rotating crops or giving the soil a rest helps restore nutrients for better future harvests.
ga: Cassava gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni kɛ́ adu lɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ewajeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ loo ni ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he jɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it good for me to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize on the same field?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ ooodu tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa ewo mli lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting leguminous crops like cowpeas alongside maize is very beneficial. Cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that helps the maize grow better.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops right on the day I put the seeds in the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ gbi ni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: It is usually better to wait until seeds sprout and develop healthy roots—typically two to three weeks after germination—so the young plants are actually capable of taking up the fertilizer nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa—bei pii lɛ, otsii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ—koni tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do we raise large soil mounds to plant yam tubers instead of planting them in flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔwoɔ shikpɔŋ wulu ko nɔ koni wɔkɛdu sweet potato ŋmeii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni wɔbaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep soil so they can expand downward without resistance. Tall mounds also prevent heavy rainwater from pooling around the roots and causing the yams to rot.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse bɔni afee ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shi ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akatsi amɛnaa. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ hu tsiɔ nugbɔ nu babaoo naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, soil nutrients, and root space. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crop gets all the food and light it needs to grow fast and strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ aná niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda oya ni ená hewalɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting seeds after the long dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ maje dumɔwui ashishi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ eho lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground receives two or three heavy rains that thoroughly wet the deep soil, rather than planting after the very first shower, which can quickly dry up and spoil the seeds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ nɔ ewo nu. Mohu ɔ, mo du lɛ ngɛ kekleekle nu ɔ se. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbiɔ oya ni ehaa amɛfiteɔ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off during periods of extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist and healthy helps the flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build healthy green leaves. Heavy rains can also wash this nutrient deeper into the ground where short crop roots cannot reach it.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi kukuji nyɛŋ ashɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing very tall with thick green leaves, but no peppers are coming out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi chili ko ejeee kpo?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer makes them focus all their energy on growing leaves and stems instead of flowers. Without flowers, the plant cannot produce any peppers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha amɛjwɛŋmɔ ahi baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Kɛji fɔfɔii bɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee chili ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Yam tubers grow large deep under the ground, so they need soft and loose soil to expand easily. Soil mounds also keep rain from collecting around the seed yam and causing it to rot.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ waa. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ekɛ ehe afɔ̃ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ koni enyɛ egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Gɔŋ lɛ hu tsiɔ nugbɔ naa koni ekabua ehe naa. Seed yam lɛ ni oha egbo.

english: How does covering my crop beds with dry grass help my vegetables during the dry season?
ga: Te jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-aduawai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a shade cover for the soil. It stops the hot sun from evaporating soil water quickly, keeping the roots moist for a longer time.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why will planting my maize seeds very close together lower my total yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa mi ŋmãa fɛɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This leaves all the plants thin and weak, resulting in smaller cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ bafeɔ bibioo.

english: Why should I cut off some of the bottom branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ekomɛi kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing extra side branches stops the plant from wasting food on unnecessary leaves. It directs the plant's energy into growing larger tomatoes and lets air flow through to prevent damp rot.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ akafite baai niyenii ni he ehiaaa. Ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ tomatoi wuji. ni oha kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli koni ŋmɔtɔ akafite.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when weather temperatures become too hot or when the plant doesn't get enough water. Heat stress stops the flowers from pollinating properly to form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Hedɔlɛ haomɔ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are small green insects crowding on the underside of my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miibua amɛhe naa yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: These insects are aphids that suck juice from the plant. They stay on the undersides of leaves to protect themselves from direct sunlight, heavy rain, and birds while they feed.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ji aphids ni nuɔ tsei amli nu. Amɛhiɔ baai ashishi koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ okpoi ahe be mli ni amɛtaoɔ niyenii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when water sits on my farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ? Ani nu edamɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Crop roots need to breathe air that is trapped in soil spaces. When standing water fills all those air gaps for days, the roots drown, die, and rot underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni tsei shishifãi lɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ ni emɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ nu ni ekã shi lɛ eyi nakai kɔɔyɔɔ hei lɛ amli gbii babaoo lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgboiɔ, ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do young cocoa trees dry up and die when planted in an open field with no shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli tse ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants naturally grow best under forest canopies. Full sun scorches their tender leaves and dries out their shallow roots before the plant is strong enough to handle strong heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ kooi lɛ ashishi. Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shãa ebaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Egbiɔ dani tso lɛ he wa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he nii.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive and burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to young cocoa creates a living umbrella that provides necessary shade and retains soil moisture during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Cocoa tso lɛ masɛi lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying off from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to make food and grow green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-decomposed manure will restore leaf color and help the maize thrive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Cassava tubers rot when excess water stays around the roots due to poor drainage or waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain freely away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ hewɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli oya.

english: If I apply fertilizer to my crops during heavy rain, why does it fail to make them grow?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Mɛni hewɔ tso lɛ ekwɛɛɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away fertilizer from the topsoil before the roots can absorb it. Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is damp but not during heavy downpours, and covered lightly with soil near the plant base.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi ajie nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ. ni okɛ shikpɔŋ fioo ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ aha nɔ

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants drop off instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or extreme dry conditions. Consistent watering at the roots and providing light shade during scorching weather helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi. Nu ni oooha shishifãi lɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field as my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, this naturally feeds the nearby maize crops and enriches the soil for future seasons.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ebaaha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ bei.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the center of the young maize plant. Checking crops early and applying organic treatments or targeted sprays inside the leaf funnel controls the pest before it ruins the yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baaye tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I harvest more cobs from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani makpa ŋmãa babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close forces plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and tiny cobs. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to produce large, full cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa nitsumɔhe fɛɛ nitsumɔhe náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and reducing fruit growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiiha aduawai lɛ adalɛ miiba shi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or a virus transmitted by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early using natural neem oil sprays or recommended treatments keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids. loo helai ni ŋmeii tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Staking spreads out yam leaves so they can catch maximum sunlight, which the plant turns into energy to grow large underground tubers. Vines left on the ground rot easily from hot soil and yield smaller yams.
ga: Staking gbɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ eshwaa koni ená hulu la babaoo. ni tsei lɛ baatsake amɛfee hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni akwɛɔ lɛ Wein tsei ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient, or that excessive rainfall has waterlogged the soil and prevented the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ amu.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips sucking juice from the underside of leaves, or by a virus transmitted by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and dry up when I clear all the big trees from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate root systems and sensitive leaves that burn under full, direct sunlight; they need shade trees or plantains nearby to protect them and keep the air cool.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do I get small maize cobs when I plant my seeds very close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛ ŋmãa bibioo ko nɔ lɛ? Beni adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops must fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leading to thin stalks and small, poorly filled cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Esa akɛ Dumɔwui lɛ atswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ dumɔwui bibii ni anyɛɛɛ akɛwo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge stems and leaves above ground but very small tubers inside the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of tubers when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or when the ground is too hard and compact for tubers to expand.
ga: Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ mli yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ beni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni bulb lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã.

english: What makes my yam tubers rot in the soil before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifeɔ klalo akɛ makpa?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water sits in the soil for too long due to poor drainage, or when soil pests like nematodes create small wounds that allow fungal diseases to enter.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Aloo beni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes lɛ feɔ pilamɔi bibii. ni baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures become too hot, when water supply is irregular, or when the plant lacks enough calcium during the flowering stage.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ

english: Why are my garden eggs cracking open while they are still growing on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miihoso yɛ be mli ni amɛmiida lolo yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Garden eggs crack when soil moisture changes suddenly from very dry to very wet, causing the fruit inside to expand faster than its outer skin can stretch.
ga: Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ fãa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ he ni egbi waa kɛtee he ni edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa aduawai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: How do I know if the soil is ready for me to plant my seeds after the first rains fall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ eshɛ kɛha dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Soil is ready for planting when moisture has penetrated deeply enough that a handful of soil formed into a ball stays moist but does not drip water or crumble instantly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ beni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ebote mli shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ ni feɔ bɔɔlu lɛ falɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lolo shi nu ni hoɔ loo efoŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why does my land yield less food each year even though I plant the exact same crop every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi moŋ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific crop pests to build up in the ground.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water is scarce and temperatures rise, plants drop leaves to reduce water loss and protect their roots. Adding mulch around the base of your crops helps retain moisture in the soil and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Mulching around Tso lɛ shishi yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil needs fertilizer before I plant my next crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If your previous crop grew slowly, had pale or light green leaves, or produced small harvests, your soil is likely low in nutrients. Adding compost, manure, or the right chemical fertilizer restores those missing nutrients for healthy growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ dara blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ewoɔ yibii fioo Ekolɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ hu faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting too closely forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing allows every plant to get enough sunlight and food, resulting in stronger stems and larger yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why does my plantain plant produce smaller bunches when many suckers grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young suckers draw food and water away from the main mother plant. Pruning extra suckers and keeping only two or three strong ones allows the mother plant to direct its energy into producing large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso bibii lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli ni ahiɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ fɔfɔii wuji ni tsii.

english: These are fall armyworms, a common pest that targets the soft growing leaves inside the maize funnel. Identifying them early and applying approved organic or chemical controls prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall asraafoi. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ekɛ ehiɛ fɔ̃ɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii amli lɛ anɔ. Ni oooyɔse amɛ mra Ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids that carry plant viruses. Managing these pests early with neem oil or targeted spraying keeps the leaves healthy so the plant can set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni hiɛ hela ko yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo shwiemɔ ni akɛtoɔ hiɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaawo baai lɛ ahe hewalɛ koni tso lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why do my mature cassava tubers become soft and watery if I leave them in the ground after heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni eda lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When heavy rains start, mature cassava plants use the starch stored in their tubers to grow new leaves and stems. Harvesting cassava before the heavy rains resume ensures the roots remain firm and starch-filled.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ Cassava tsei ni eda lɛ kɛ starch ni ato yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai kɛ ŋmeii heei. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmei dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ŋmei eyi mli obɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when watering is irregular, or when there is a lack of key nutrients like phosphorus. Consistent watering and proper fertilizer help flowers set into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa daa kɛ fɔmɔ nii ni sa yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive quickly by taking up available soil moisture and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing sunlight and nourishment from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi oya kɛtsɔ sũ mli nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds around my yam mounds regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Ehe miihia ni mibua sweet potatoes anaa daa.

english: Yam vines need full sunlight on their leaves to produce energy for growing big tubers under the ground. Weeds shade the vines and steal nutrients from the soil mound, resulting in smaller yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Jwɛi haa wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ gɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. When the soil lacks nutrients or when heavy rain washes fertilizer away, the plant cannot make enough green color (chlorophyll) to grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ laajeɔ. Tsei nyɛŋ afee nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli (chlorophyll) ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells as a natural way to save water. By shedding leaves, the plant stops losing moisture through evaporation and rests until the rains return to sprout fresh foliage.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli, ni eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he. Kɛji baai lɛ gbee shi lɛ Tsei lɛ baakpa ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfiteɔ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba koni eha baai heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why do cocoa pods grow directly on the main trunk instead of on the outer branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe niji ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa naturally produces flowers and pods on its thick, strong trunk and main branches because cocoa pods are heavy. The main trunk provides the solid support needed to carry heavy pods without breaking under their weight.
ga: Cocoa fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii yɛ tsei ni mli tse ni wa kɛ niji wuji anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ejaakɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ tsii. Gbɔmɔtso titri lɛ haa yelikɛbuamɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni he hiaa koni anyɛ atere pod ni tsii ni etsiii lɛ akumɔɔɔ.

english: Yam vines need stakes so their leaves can reach sunlight above the ground. When the leaves get plenty of sun and air, they create food that flows down into the ground to produce bigger and healthier yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ashɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Efeɔ niyenii ni hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and rotten before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused mainly by irregular watering and a lack of calcium in the plant. When water supply goes up and down, the plant cannot transport calcium to the fruit tip, causing the bottom to collapse and turn black.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ titri ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium ni faaa yɛ tsei amli lɛ. Kɛ nu ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ tee ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ amɛkɛ calcium aya aduawai lɛ ashishi. Ehaa aduawai lɛ ashishi shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas together with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that trap natural nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. Planting them with maize acts like natural manure, making the soil richer for your maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha o-ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown and rot when the weather is cold and wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egboɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shady conditions. Pruning excess shade tree branches lets sunlight and fresh air into the farm, which helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.
