english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive shade. The plant drops flowers to save energy so it can survive until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo hulutsoo babaoo mli. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut away small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Too many young shoots (suckers) steal food, water, and sunlight from the main stem. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, allowing the main plant to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo (tso lɛ) juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ dumɔwui wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why is it beneficial to cover the ground around my vegetables with dry grass or cocoa husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔ baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil (mulching) keeps the ground cool and traps moisture so you water less often. It also prevents weeds from growing and turns into rich natural compost as the grass breaks down.
ga: Mulching (mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. koni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo Etsiɔ jwɛi hu naa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛji jwɛi lɛ fite.

english: Why are my tomato leaves turning yellow even though I gave the plants plenty of nitrogen fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nitrogen babaoo ewo tsei lɛ amli moŋ?

english: Plants need a balanced mix of nutrients to stay healthy. Giving crops only nitrogen without other essentials like calcium or magnesium is like feeding a child only rice; the plant becomes unhealthy, leaves turn yellow, and it struggles to produce good fruit.
ga: Niyenii ni ja he miihia tsei koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nitrogen ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa krokomɛi tamɔ calcium loo magnesium bɛ mli. Etamɔ niyenii pɛ ni akɛhaa gbekɛ. Tso lɛ miigbɔjɔ. baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná yibii kpakpai

english: Can I use only urea fertilizer on my maize field to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ urea pɛ atsu nii yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: Relying on urea alone gives your maize quick leaf growth, but misses phosphorus for strong roots and potassium for grain filling. Without a balanced nutrient diet, your maize stalks will grow tall but end up weak with small, light ears.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ urea pɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ adara oya. Shi ebɛ fɔsfɔs kɛha shishifãi ni wa kɛ potassium kɛha dumɔwui ni woɔ mli ekoŋŋ. Kɛji niyenii ni ja bɛ O-ŋmãa lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ shi yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaagbɔjɔ be mli ni toi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ.

english: What causes the bottom of my hot peppers to turn black and rot before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-peppers lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egbo dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ?

english: This is blossom-end rot, usually caused by a lack of calcium and improper watering. Just like an incomplete diet makes humans weak, missing key minerals weakens the cell walls of your peppers, causing the fruit flesh to break down.
ga: Enɛ ji fɔfɔii lɛ anaagbee fitemɔ he okadi. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni faaa kɛ nu ni esaaa. Taakɛ niyenii ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ haa adesai gbɔjɔɔ lɛ. Minerals titrii ni bɛ lɛ haa chili lɛ mli wala yibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji aduawai lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mligbalamɔ.

english: If I dump a large amount of chicken manure on my cassava farm at once, will it produce bigger tubers?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ babaoo wo ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ be kome mli lɛ, Ani ebaaha yitso lɛ agbo?

english: Too much rich manure at once creates a nutrient imbalance. Your cassava will spend all its energy growing heavy leaves above ground while developing tiny, watery roots underneath because the soil feeding was not balanced.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ni sa. O yucca lɛ baafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ekɛ shishifãi bibii hu baa. No ji nu ni yɔɔ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ niyenii ni ejaaa hewɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over easily whenever a light wind blows through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ gbeeɔ shi mlɛo be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ baatswa miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Over-feeding plants with single high-nitrogen fertilizers makes them grow very fast and soft, but leaves their stems weak. Crops need potassium to build tough, sturdy stalks that can withstand wind and hold heavy ears.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo ha tsei fe nine lɛ, ebaaha amɛdara oya waa ni amɛfee blɛoo. Shi ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Tsei hia potassium koni amɛfee tsei ni wa ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Ebaanyɛ edamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ toi ni tsii naa.

english: Will giving my vegetables extra chemical fertilizer make them stay fresh longer after I harvest them?
ga: Ani tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ aduawai amli lɛ ni akɛaawo mli lɛ baaha amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Over-fertilizing actually spoils crop quality. Too much of one fertilizer makes fruits and vegetables soft and watery, causing them to rot quickly in the market instead of staying firm and healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli lɛ, ebaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ baaha aduawai kɛ aduawai afee bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai kɛ aduawai fiteɔ oya yɛ jara nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my cabbage leaves curling and showing spots even though the crop looks well-fed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔɔ ŋmeii eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: When plants get an uneven feed, they develop nutrient disorders that look like diseases. Without balanced soil nutrients, cabbages lose their resistance, making their leaves twist and become easy targets for infections.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aha tsei niyenii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ Niyenii baafee tamɔ nɔ ni ejaaa, tamɔ hela. Kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Cabbage lɛ baafee mɔ ni nyɛŋ ekɛ ehe awo mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ he ni helai baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe oya.

english: Is chemical fertilizer alone enough to keep my soil fertile every farming season?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ be fɛɛ mli?

english: Chemical fertilizer supplies quick food for plants, but it does not feed the soil structure. Over time, relying on just one input makes the soil tired and acidic, leading to sick crops unless you also add organic compost.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii oya. Shi ekɛ niyenii haaa sũ lɛ mli nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Saji nɛɛ pɛ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbɔjɔ ni etsɔ acidic. Ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ baa Ja okɛ organic compost hu fata he.

english: Why do my watermelons crack open on the vine right before they are ready for picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miitswa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Fruit cracking happens when plants receive sudden, uneven spikes of water and nutrients. The inside of the watermelon grows faster than the outer skin can handle, causing the flesh to burst open.
ga: Yibii amli fãmɔ baa kɛji tsei lɛ ná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ trukaa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Watermelon lɛ mli lɛ baada oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsu he nii. ha loo lɛ mli agbala

english: Why do my young cocoa pods shrivel up and turn black while still small on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods shrivel when the tree lacks balanced nutrients to support all its fruits. When the tree cannot supply a complete diet to every pod, it discards the extra pods to keep itself alive.
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa ni baaye abua tso lɛ yibii lɛ fɛɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ niyenii ni yeɔ emuu Ebaashɛrɛ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ ashwie koni ehi wala mli.

english: Why do my corn plants turn pale yellow and stop growing tall even after I clean all the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ moŋ?

english: Corn leaves turn yellow when the plant is starving for nitrogen, a key food in the ground. Even if weeds are gone, worn-out soil lacks the nutrients needed for green leaves, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps them green up.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Eyɛ mli akɛ jwɛi lɛ etee moŋ Shi shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni jwɛi lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: Why do some of my harvested corn cobs have missing seeds and empty spaces on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi bɛ ŋmeii ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii lolo lɛ?

english: Corn cobs lack full seeds when pollination fails during flowering time, usually caused by extreme heat or dry dry weather when the silks first come out. Without enough moisture, pollen cannot travel properly to form every grain.
ga: Abɛi ŋmeii lɛ bɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ kɛji pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shihilɛ ni mli egbi beni siliki lɛ jeɔ kpo klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛji hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, Pollen ŋmaa lɛ nyɛɛɛ aya gbɛ jogbaŋŋ koni efee dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu.

english: Can I plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my corn on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cowpeas loo peanuts kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans or groundnuts with corn is very good because legumes take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, acting like natural food for your corn while giving your family another crop to eat.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa o-corn lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi haa oweku lɛ koni amɛye.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year when I plant corn in the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of the exact nutrients that plant relies on. Rotating your field with crops like beans or leaving the land to rest brings life and richness back to the soil.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei lɛ damɔɔ nɔ lɛ daa. Oŋmɔji ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii baatsake loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha akɛfee hiɛtserɛjiemɔ Ebaaha wala kɛ emuuyeli aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do little worms eat the soft centers of my young corn plants before they even flower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli fãi bibii lɛ dani amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Those worms are called Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the leaves to eat the softest parts of young plants. Checking your farm early and using ash, neem leaves, or recommended sprays kills them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye tsei bibii lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ sũ, neem baai, loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwie nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baagbe amɛ dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are tiny insects destroying my dried corn inside the barn after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: These insects are grain weevils that lay eggs inside corn kernels. If the corn is not dried completely under the sun or stored in sealed airtight bags, the eggs hatch and the pests eat your stored grain from the inside.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ji dumɔwui amli kooloi ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii amli. Kɛji akɛ agbiko ŋmãa lɛ kwraa yɛ hulu lɛ mli loo akɛtoko vacuum bag ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli.

english: How can I tell that my cassava under the ground is mature enough to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem, and the earth right around the stem begins to crack open as the underground tubers swell up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Eshwɛ tso ko ni nɔ ko bɛ mli. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishitso lɛ baabɔi mligbalamɔ be mli ni tuber lɛ mli fũuɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during rainy windstorms before the fruit bunches get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli dani aduawai wuji lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are close to the surface and can get weakened by soil pests or heavy water. Propping up your fruiting plantain trees with strong bamboo poles gives them extra support against strong winds.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ, ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi loo nu afua baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei ni wa wo tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ahe fɛo lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ anyɛ atsu nii babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato plant blossoms fall off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ tomato ko kwraa wooo lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly soaked with water, which stresses the plant and stops it from turning flowers into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni edɔ trukaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my crops curl their leaves and droop during hot afternoons even if it rained two days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ gbii enyɔ ni eho nɛ moŋ?

english: Plants curl their leaves in strong afternoon heat to trap moisture and protect themselves from losing water too fast; as long as they recover in the cool evening, it is just their way of surviving the hot sun.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu lɛ akafite oya tsɔ. Shii abɔ ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Eji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa foi kɛkɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for healthy leaf growth. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the crop regain its rich green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ baai ni he wa lɛ adalɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa su ni mli kwɔ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my cassava yield getting smaller every year even though I keep planting on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mifeɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi lɛ? Ani adu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Planting the same crop on the exact same soil every year drains all the specific nutrients that crop needs to grow well. Rotating cassava with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores essential nutrients to the soil and improves future yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ ajɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsake ŋmeii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmeii lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing tall and full of leaves, but not producing many peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miida ni ekɛ baai eyi mli obɔ lɛ? Shi ani afeee chili ŋmɔtɔi babaoo?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients like phosphorus, they focus all their energy on leaf growth rather than flowering. Balancing the soil nutrients encourages the plant to shift energy from leaves into producing peppers.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nitrogen babaoo fe niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ phosphorus lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai lɛ adalɛ he moŋ fe fɔfɔi. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛjieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa chili ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong, direct sunlight and lose moisture quickly. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shade that keeps the plants cool and retains soil moisture until the cocoa matures.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛmli shwieɔ oya. Kɛ́ oshi tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo odu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha hulutsoo aba. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds closer together, won't I get a much bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani maná ŋmãa babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and small or empty cobs. Giving each plant proper space allows them to produce full, healthy yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni eyi obɔ.

english: Curled leaves with yellow patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is carried and spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava varieties and removing infected plants early stops the disease from spreading across your field.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ amɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã okpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there is enough rainfall for everything growing on the farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal the nutrients and root space in the soil, as well as sunlight from above. Even with plenty of rain, unchecked weeds will choke the crop and lower your overall harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Hulu la ni jɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ fata he. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ Shi jwɛi ni ashi ni asaaa lɛ baafite oŋmɔshi nibii ni ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off the plant during hot periods without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Extremely high heat stresses tomato plants, causing them to drop their flowers to save water and survival energy. Providing regular watering early in the morning helps the plant stay cool enough to hold its flowers and form fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: Why should I pinch off the small extra branches growing on the sides of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei niji bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ nɔ ni fata he ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tsei lɛ afã lɛ.

english: Removing those extra side branches, known as suckers, directs the plant's energy and nutrients into growing bigger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on unnecessary stems and leaves.
ga: Nakai niji krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ lɛ shoo lɛ ni ajieɔ Eheɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ tsei kɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know when my underground yam tubers are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Yams indicate maturity when the upper green leaves and vines naturally yellow and dry up. This change shows that the plant has finished sending stored energy down into the underground tuber, meaning it is ready to dig up.
ga: Sweet potatoes tsɔɔ akɛ eshɛ kɛji ŋwɛi baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbiɔ. Tsakemɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe ehewalɛ ni ekɛto lɛ majemɔ naa kɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly if I plant the same maize on the same field every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil every season. When you plant it repeatedly on the same land, those nutrients get completely exhausted, causing the soil to lose its strength until you rotate with another crop like beans.
ga: Abɛi yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ odu ekoŋŋ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ Nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ baaho kwraa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ he waaa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni okɛ tsei krokomɛi, tamɔ ŋmeii baatsake lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put fertilizer on my farm again this year when I already applied it last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ afi nɛɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli?

english: Crops consume most of the fertilizer food during their growth, and heavy rains wash away the rest deep into the earth. Once the plant finishes using it, the soil returns to its low-nutrient state and needs a fresh supply for the next harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ babaoo yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ amli kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɔ̃ɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ kɛtsu nii egbe naa lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shihilɛ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ mli ni ebiɔ niyenii hee kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very tiny cobs when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are packed too tightly together, their roots fight over the limited food and water in the ground while their leaves block each other from getting sunlight. Spacing them out gives each plant enough free room to grow big cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa amɛ. Gbɛ ni kã tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the crops growing near the big shade tree on my farm growing much slower than the ones in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo kwraa fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ?

english: The big tree's large roots suck up most of the water and food in the soil around it, while its thick branches block the sun. The crops underneath are left starving for sunlight and soil nutrients.
ga: Tsei wuji lɛ ashishifãi wuji lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ babaoo. yɛ be mli ni tsei niji ni mli tse lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa Ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni hɔmɔ ye hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop down in the hot afternoon sun but stand up straight again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi shidaamɔ tɛ̃ɛ ekoŋŋ leebi?

english: Plants lose water quickly through their leaves during intense heat. Drooping is the plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce sunlight exposure and save water until the cool night and morning allow it to drink and recover.
ga: Tsei laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Drooping ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he koni ekɛba hulu la ni ekɛkpeɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛto nu he kɛyashi leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ, ni ehaa enyɛɔ enuɔ nu ni enáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my cassava plants turn yellow and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water becomes scarce, cassava plants drop their older leaves on purpose to reduce water loss. This helps the plant survive the dry spell by directing all remaining energy underground to keep the tubers alive.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa lɛ Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai momoi koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli kɛtsɔ ehewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does sickness spread so fast from one infected crop row to the rest of my healthy farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hela ko gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ateŋ ekome nɔ kɛyaa miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plant diseases travel through wind, rain splashes, and insects jumping from leaf to leaf. When plants are touching along a row, the sickness moves continuously down the line just like people moving down a open path.
ga: Tsei ahe helai tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, ni kooloi bibii shwieɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ baa kome nɔ kɛyaa baa kroko nɔ. Kɛ tsei ta amɛhe yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ Hela yaa nɔ etsɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ shishi. Tamɔ mɔ ko ni nyiɛ gbɛ ni agbele nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants start rotting at the bottom if I let the branches rest directly on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shishigbɛ kɛji mishi niji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Soil naturally carries tiny germs and fungus spores. When wet leaves or fruits rest directly on the ground, dirt and moisture move straight onto the plant, creating an easy pathway for decay and rot to take hold.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ helai bibii kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii kɛji baai loo aduawai ni efɔ lɛ gbee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Muji kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yaa tso lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa gbɛ ko ni fiteɔ oya ni efiteɔ baa.

english: Why does my land produce a much bigger harvest after I leave it resting without planting for a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wo ŋmaa babaoo kwraa fe tsutsu lɛ beni mishi nɔ afi ni miduko nɔ ko lɛ?

english: Leaving land unplanted gives nature time to break down old weeds and leaves, rebuilding the soil's natural energy. This rest period restores missing nutrients so the land is refreshed and fertile when you return to plant.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi he ko ni aduuu nii yɛ lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ naa be ni ekɛfiteɔ jwɛi kɛ tsei ahe tsei momo. ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ Hejɔɔmɔ be nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaawo yibii beni oku osɛɛ obaduɔ tsei ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why does animal manure take longer to make my crops green compared to chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ashishifãi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ eŋɔli be kakadaŋŋ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers release their food instantly, whereas animal manure must first be broken down by tiny organisms in the living soil. The manure releases its food slowly and gradually over time, giving long-term strength to the land.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ jieɔ niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, esa akɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ akpata kooloi ashishifãi lɛ ahiɛ. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hiɛ ka nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ Manure jieɔ niyenii fiofio kɛ fiofio yɛ be ni sa mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli

english: Why do my crops need so much water right after I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve completely so that your crop roots can actually drink it in. Without water, the fertilizer just sits dry in the dirt, and your plants cannot perform the work of growing.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli kwraa bɔni afee ni otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu mli diɛŋtsɛ.Kɛ́ nu bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baata shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Ni otsei lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃.

english: What is a soluble fertilizer, and how does it help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni nu mli shwieɔ shi? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Soluble fertilizer is a type of crop food that easily dissolves in water. When mixed with water, it breaks down so that plants can quickly absorb the nutrients through their roots or leaves.
ga: Nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii ji tso niyenii henɔ ko ni shwieɔ nu mli oya. Kɛ́ akɛ nu futu mli lɛ, efiteɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ atsɔ amɛshishifãi loo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya.

english: What happens if I apply dry fertilizer to my crops during a long heatwave without rain?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi tsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: Without water to dissolve the fertilizer, your crops cannot feed on it, and the concentrated chemical strength can actually burn the plant roots instead of helping them.
ga: Kɛji nu bɛ ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii kɛkɛ. Ni tsofai lɛ ni fa babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua amɛ.

english: Why do my crops stop growing properly even when I have put plenty of fertilizer in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekpa shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ewo ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Plants use water as a transport system to move nutrients from the soil up into their stems and leaves. Even with plenty of fertilizer, a lack of water prevents the crop from doing the internal work needed to build new leaves and fruit.
ga: Tsei kɛ nu tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ moŋ Shi nu ni bɛ lɛ hu tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkatsu mligbɛ nitsumɔ ni he hiaa koni amɛfee baai kɛ aduawai heei.

english: How does water actually help a plant use the food present in the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii?

english: Water acts like a vehicle that carries dissolved nutrients into the root hairs, allowing the crop to pump food to every branch so it can perform its growth processes.
ga: Nu tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni kɛ niyenii ni mli ewo muji lɛ yaa shishifãi ahe yitsɔi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yaa tso lɛ nine fɛɛ nine mli koni enyɛ eya nɔ eda.

english: Why must some crop inputs be diluted heavily in water instead of put directly on the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ekomɛi awo nu mli waa moŋ fe ni akɛbaawo tsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Diluting inputs in water spreads the chemicals safely and evenly, preventing damage to leaves while ensuring every crop gets just the right amount to grow strong.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ wo nu mli lɛ, tsofai lɛ jaa shweshweeshwe ni amɛfeɔ ekome. Tsi baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaná nɔ ni sa kɛha dalɛ ni mli wa.

english: Can I mix fertilizer directly into water and spray it on my crops using a machine?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afutu nu mli tɛ̃ɛ ni mikɛ tsɔne afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Yes, mixing soluble fertilizer into water allows you to use spraying equipment to feed and water your crops at the same time, making the application faster and more uniform.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni nu mli shwieɔ shi lɛ ni okɛfutuɔ nu mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ onibii ni okɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni okɛhaa onibii lɛ niyenii kɛ nu yɛ be kome mli, ni no haa onyɛɔ okɛtsu nii oya, ni okɛtsu nii be fɛɛ be.

english: Why should I use a spraying machine to apply liquid fertilizer instead of applying it by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baatsu nii moŋ fe ni okɛ oniji baatsu nii?

english: A spraying machine pushes the liquid solution evenly across all your crops under pressure, ensuring every plant gets equal access to water and food without wasting inputs.
ga: Sprayer lɛ tsiɔ nu mli tsofa lɛ kɛyaa onibii fɛɛ nɔ yɛ nɔnyɛɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nitsumɔhe fɛɛ nitsumɔhe náa nu kɛ niyenii ni sa ni efiteee nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ.

english: Why is it important to completely dissolve chemical fertilizers before putting them into my sprayer machine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kwraa dani akɛwo tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If fertilizer is not completely dissolved in water, dry grains can block the machine's nozzles and prevent the liquid from spreading evenly over your farm.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛɛɛ nu mli kwraa lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsɔne lɛ naa ni eha nu lɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How does using specialized watering equipment help my crops during dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nibii krɛdɛɛi ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Watering machinery delivers water and liquid nutrients right to the root zone under consistent pressure, giving the crop the exact moisture service it needs to keep working and growing during dry weather.
ga: Nu tsɔnei kɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ yaa shishifã lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ shishi. Ehaa tsei lɛ náa nu pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsu nii ni amɛdara yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning light green and yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to grow strong leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi he miihia lɛ babaoo koni baai lɛ adara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does growing beans or groundnuts help improve my farmland for other crops?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii adumɔ aha miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules. When these roots decay, they leave rich food in the soil for crops like maize planted next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛji shishifãi nɛɛ fite Ebaashi niyenii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni abaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away down the slopes or deep into the soil before crop roots can drink it, wasting your money and starving your plants.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa gɔŋji lɛ anɔ loo kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Efiteɔ shika ni ehaa tsei yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there is full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and easily burn in harsh sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa protects them until they grow old enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa shɛ amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Does lifting yam vines onto wooden stakes really help make the yam roots bigger?
ga: Ani sweet potato wain tsei ni awoɔ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potato shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, lifting yam vines off the ground lets leaves catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food, which flows down to build much bigger yam tubers underground.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ owó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la ni fa babaoo ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe koni ekɛ niyenii aba. Enɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I cut off extra small plantain shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ.

english: Leaving too many small shoots forces them to steal water and food from the main mother plant, resulting in small, light plantain bunches.
ga: ŋmeii bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ Kɛ́ efee babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, plantains lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off without turning into pepper fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers as a defence mechanism when stressed by severe heat or dry soil, preventing the plant from producing fruits until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shi akɛ hebuu gbɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi hao amɛ. Tsi tso lɛ naa koni ekawo yibii kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa tso lɛ daa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is causing small green caterpillars to eat holes into the funnel leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ bu yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai ni tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ amli?

english: These are Fall Armyworms that hatch from eggs laid by moths. They hide inside the central leaves of maize to eat tender plant tissue before the leaves open.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms ni fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛye tso bibii lɛ ahe fãji dani baai lɛ agbele.

english: Why do dark black patches appear on my tomato stems and leaves during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mi tomato tsei kɛ baai anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The damp, wet air encourages a fungal disease called blight to spread rapidly across leaves, causing rot if foliage stays wet for long periods.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ late blight lɛ hewalɛ koni egbɛ eshwa baai lɛ amli oya. Enɛ haa egboɔ kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tee nɔ ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft, dark, and smelly underground during heavy rain periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ duŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when trapped in waterlogged soil that lacks air passage, essentially suffocating the tubers under standing water.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ boteɔ nu ni mli ejɔ mli.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plants are short on nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leaf growth. This usually happens after heavy rains wash nutrients deeper into the soil or when the soil lacks organic matter.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ewo sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ loo be mli ni sũ lɛ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge, healthy leaves above ground but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baa agbo ni mli wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, cassava plants put all their energy into growing leaves and stems instead of roots. Excess foliage without tuber growth often occurs when high-nitrogen chemical fertilizer is applied incorrectly.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ shishifãi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe shishifãi. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni fa fe nine ni tuber dalɛ bɛ mli lɛ baa kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off before producing any fruit during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when heat is too high or when plants experience water stress. Excessive temperatures prevent proper pollination, causing the plant to shed unpollinated blossoms to save water and energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Ha tsei afee fɔfɔi ni pollination bɛ mli koni ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why does my maize crop start flowering early when the rains stop unexpectedly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa lɛ?

english: When crops face extreme water stress, they activate a survival mechanism to reproduce before dying. Premature flowering is the plant's attempt to produce seeds quickly while it still has enough moisture to survive.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu he haomɔ ni naa wa kpe Amɛhaa wala yibiiwoo gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ jeɔ shishi koni amɛfɔ bii dani amɛgboi. Fɔfɔi ni baa oya ji mɔdɛŋ ni tso lɛ bɔɔ koni ewo dumɔwui oya yɛ be mli ni eyɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lolo ni ekɛhi shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during storms when they start bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli beni ejeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and do not grow deep taproots. As the heavy bunch of fruit develops at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for strong winds to pull the shallow roots out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni amɛkwɛɛɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ shwereɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Tso lɛ baaná muji babaoo yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ aaajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die if I clear away all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot withstand direct sunlight and harsh winds because their roots and leaves are delicate. Leaving canopy trees or planting plantains provides shade and retains soil moisture needed for cocoa seedlings to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ waaa. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai amli loo adu dumɔwui lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni he hiaa koni kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi.

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground helps the leaves catch more sunlight to feed the tuber beneath. Staking also keeps the leaves dry and off hot soil, preventing fungal diseases that ruin the harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la babaoo ni ekɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ ni amɛjeɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the underside of young leaves. Their feeding damages the leaf tissue and can spread plant viruses that distort growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Amɛ niyenii lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ tso mli helai ni fiteɔ dalɛ lɛ eshwa.

english: The tiny bumps on cowpea roots are called nodules and are actually beneficial. They contain helpful soil bacteria that capture nitrogen from the air and convert it into natural food for the plant and soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ cowpea shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ akɛ nodules ni amɛhe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ diɛŋtsɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa tsei kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ mli.

english: Why do my vegetable seeds fail to sprout when I plant them in hard, dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds require air, moisture, and soft soil to break open and push roots downward. Hard, compacted soil stops water from reaching the seed and mechanically blocks the tender sprout from breaking through to the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa kɔɔyɔɔ, nu mli nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛtsi shishifãi lɛ kɛba shi. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ haaa nu ayashɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe. ni etsĩ tsei bibii anaa koni amɛkatsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ tsɔne nɔ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nutrients, particularly nitrogen, or that the roots are drowning in too much trapped water. Adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green so the plant can make food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ kɛha niyenii kpakpai. titri lɛ nitrogen loo shishifãi lɛ ebote nu ni emɔ mli lɛ mli tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ organic fertilizer loo nitrogen fertilizer fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli koni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests that feed on that specific crop to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans restores nitrogen to the soil and starves out pests.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ nakai tso lɛ koni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli.

english: Why shouldn't I apply my fertilizer right before a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa?

english: Heavy rainfall causes water to run rapidly over the soil, which washes the expensive fertilizer away into streams or deep into the ground where your plant's roots cannot reach it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but heavy downpours are not expected.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu hoɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa lɛ kɛyaa faai amli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni otsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi akpaaa nugbɔ ni naa wa gbɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain or shade trees next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantain loo shade tso yɛ mi-kokoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide broad leaf umbrellas that shield the cocoa from intense heat and keep the surrounding soil moist until the cocoa roots grow deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know which way to put cassava stem cuttings into the ground when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni esa akɛ odu kɛ bɔ ni ooofee okɛ ŋmei ni afo lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small buds or leaf scars along the cassava stem. These buds should point upwards toward the sky like arrows, ensuring that roots grow down into the soil easily and branches shoot up to catch sunlight.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. loo baai bibii ahe okadii Nyiɛmɔ ŋmei lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi tamɔ akpɔlɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya ni niji lɛ shɛɔ ŋwɛi koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee.

english: Why do my yam plants grow bigger tubers when I give the vines sticks to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji beni mihaa wain tso lɛ kwɔɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants use their leaves to catch sunlight and turn it into food that gets stored in the root tuber underground. Lifting the vines off the ground on wooden stakes exposes maximum leaf space to the sun and prevents leaves from rotting on damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛheɔ hulu la ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la ni tsoɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ aná tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ. ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and produce smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee mlɛo ni amɛmiiwo yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal sunlight, water, and soil food directly away from your crops. Removing weeds early ensures your main plants get all the resources they need to grow strong and fruit well.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ, ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otso titri lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii.

english: How can I keep my vegetable garden from drying out and dying during the harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ naa koni ekagbi ni egbo yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the bare earth around your crops with dry grass, leaves, or cocoa husks—a method called mulching—acts like a blanket. It blocks harsh dry winds, keeps the soil cool, and traps water underground for a much longer time.
ga: Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo kookoo ŋmeii awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni ebɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ekɛ nu toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi be kakadaŋŋ

english: Flowers drop off when the plant gets severe stress, usually caused by sudden heat, irregular watering, or a lack of food in the soil. Keeping moisture levels steady in the root zone helps the flowers stay attached and swell into healthy peppers.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao waa. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni baa trukaa lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is causing holes in the leaves and centers of my young maize plants, and why is it bad?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli kɛ amɛteŋ lɛ baa? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehiii lɛ?

english: Small caterpillars, like the Fall Armyworm, burrow into the center of young maize plants to eat the soft tender leaves. Damaging these growing leaves stops the plant from growing properly and can destroy your entire harvest if not caught early.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ, shwieɔ bu yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Kɛ́ ofite baai ni miida nɛɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, ni ebaanyɛ efite onibii fɛɛ kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii oya.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build strong stems and green leaves. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted animal manure will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing huge green stems and leaves but hardly producing any flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi eshwɛ fioo ni fɔfɔi ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Giving tomato plants too much nitrogen causes them to spend all their energy building leaves instead of fruits. To get fruits, tomatoes need more phosphorus and potassium, which encourage flower formation and help the tomatoes grow big.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tomato tso lɛ, ehaa ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai moŋ fe aduawai. koni ená aduawai Tomato he miihia fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium babaoo. Enɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ahe hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tomatoi lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my vegetables with dried grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ? Aduawai ni jwɛi yɔɔ mli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Covering soil with dried grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the dirt so it does not dry out quickly under the hot sun. It also keeps the roots cool and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli, ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, egbiɛɛ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ hu feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by too much direct sunlight, lack of water, or attacks from tiny insects like mirids. Keeping enough shade trees on your farm and controlling pests around flowering time helps the flowers stay on the tree and develop into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ atatu ni tswaa lɛ tutua amɛ. Kɛ́ oha tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be ni sa mli yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni oye tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up into small cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ kɔɔpoi bibii? ni okpa dalɛ

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the juices from under the leaves. Spraying early with appropriate organic or recommended pest treatments keeps the leaves flat so the plant can make food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Akɛ tsofai ni sa loo ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuɔ nii mra. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ afee niyenii.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over when strong winds blow through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa kɛfo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots stay very shallow in the ground, so when heavy bunches grow at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy. Propping up the stem with a strong bamboo pole or wooden fork gives the plant extra support to hold the weight of the heavy bunch.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ sũ lɛ mli waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ tsei niji ni mli tse lɛ dara yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ baaná muji babaoo. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso loo tso ni akɛfee ŋmei ni wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni enyɛ eye ŋmei ni tsii fe nine lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food that travels down to build large underground tubers. Lifting the vines on tall stakes ensures maximum sunlight hits the leaves and protects them from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni fãa kɛyaa shi koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ awó wain tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo lɛ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe, ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ baa.

english: How does planting cowpeas inside the same field as my maize help both crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it directly into the soil to feed the nearby maize. Planting them together feeds your soil naturally while giving you two different food harvests from the same piece of land.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ lɛ fee ekome lɛ, ebaaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, anáa niyenii srɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kuku kome nɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready to harvest so they do not rot in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, which you can tell when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off. Leaving mature cassava in very wet soil causes the roots to absorb excess water and rot.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo shɛɔ shweremɔ he yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ole be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei ni eda lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ waa nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ni amɛbaagboi.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by several hot, dry weeks before the real rains begin. If you plant too early, the seeds will sprout after the first rain and then dry up and die in the heat before the next rain falls.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, otsii babaoo ni mli edɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, egbiɔ ni egboɔ yɛ latsaa be mli dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ nɛɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp conditions. When rainy weather stays long, the fungus attacks the pods, making them black and unfit for sale unless you manage the farm conditions and protect your trees.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ Kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ŋmei lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ ediŋŋ ni esaaa akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ. Ja okwɛ oŋmɔ mli shihilɛ lɛ nɔ ni obu otsei lɛ ahe.

english: How does spraying insect medicine on my farm help my crops produce more harvest?
ga: Te tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Insects eat leaves and stems that plants use to feed themselves. Spraying controls these pests so your crops can keep their leaves green and healthy, allowing all their energy to go into producing larger fruits and seeds.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ baai kɛ tsei ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ. Enɛ ji koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ. Ha hewalɛ fɛɛ aya ni okɛfee aduawai kɛ dumɔwui wuji.

english: Is it safe for me to harvest and eat my vegetables right after spraying them with pest medicine?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makpa mi-vegetables lɛ ni maye amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ?

english: No, pest medicines stay poisonous on the plants for several days. You must wait out the required waiting period after spraying so the chemical breaks down safely before you pick food for consumption or sale.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ baafee awui kɛha tsei gbii babaoo. Esa akɛ omɛ shika ni he hiaa lɛ beni okɛ tsofai lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni tsofai lɛ akumɔ shweshweeshwe dani okɛ niyenii ni obaaye loo ohɔ̃ɔ lɛ aba.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before the peppers start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant suffers stress from insect attacks, extreme heat, or lack of water. Keeping pests away and ensuring steady water helps the flowers stay on the plant and develop into peppers.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi tutua tso lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nu ni bɛ. Kɛ́ atsĩ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa ni akwɛɔ nu ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my maize leaves get dark spots and turn yellow during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Continuous moisture creates a perfect home for leaf fungus to grow. The fungus destroys the leaf tissue, which weakens the plant because it cannot catch sunlight properly to make food.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa shia ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Fung lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ejaakɛ enyɛɛɛ emɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛfee niyenii.

english: If I spray medicine to kill insects on my farm, will the chemical burn or hurt my crops?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ Ani tsofai lɛ baashã loo ebaaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: When mixed correctly at the right dosage, the medicine targets only pests without hurting the plant. However, putting too much chemical in your spray machine can burn the leaves and weaken the crop.
ga: Kɛ akɛfutu mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ bɔ ni sa mli lɛ Tsofa lɛ tsɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ pɛ nɔ ni eyeee tso lɛ awui. Shi kɛlɛ, tsofa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why are insects attacking my young crops much faster during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa midumɔwui lɛ mra kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the dry season arrives, wild plants dry up and insects run out of food. They flock to your irrigated or fresh farm crops because your plants are the only rich source of moisture and nutrients nearby.
ga: Kɛ́ fɛ̃i be lɛ shɛ lɛ, Koo mli tsei lɛ egbi ni kooloi bibii lɛ aniyenii miiho. Amɛbuaa amɛhe naa kɛyaa okwaayeli mli nibii ni okɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ loo nibii heei ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni oyɔɔ lɛ pɛ ji hei ni hulutsoo kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɔɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black rotten bottoms while ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɔɔ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This issue, called Blossom End Rot, happens when the plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil into the fruit, often caused by irregular watering or damage to the plant's roots.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Blossom End Rot lɛ baa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbala calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛya aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ be fɛɛ be loo tso lɛ shishifãi ni efiteɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and yellow when left growing together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Because weeds grow aggressively, they steal these vital resources away from your crops, leaving them malnourished.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya. No sɛɛ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. ni haa amɛnáaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa

english: Why do caterpillars prefer eating the new soft leaves of my cabbage instead of the outer leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛye mi-cabbage lɛ baai bibii lɛ moŋ fe kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ?

english: New leaves are softer and filled with high amounts of water and easy-to-digest nutrients. Caterpillars target these parts first because it gives them the energy to grow rapidly.
ga: Baai heei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni nu babaoo kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ eyi mli obɔ. Kpluka lɛ baakwɛ nɛkɛ fãi nɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Ejaakɛ ehãa amɛnáa hewalɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Why do the maize seeds I bought from the shop have a pink powder on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mihe yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ powda ni ji pinki lɛ?

english: That powder is a seed dressing chemical that coats the seed to protect it from soil insects and fungal sicknesses so it can germinate safely.
ga: Powda lɛ ji tsofa ko ni akɛhaa dumɔwui anɔ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe koni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: If one of my cassava plants gets a disease, why should I dig it up and burn it?
ga: Kɛji mi-cassava tsei lɛ eko mli hela lɛ emɔ lɛ Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ otsa ni oshã?

english: Crop diseases easily spread from plant to plant through rain splash, wind, or insects, so removing and burning a sick plant stops the sickness from catching the rest of your farm.
ga: Tse helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi anɔ, no hewɔ lɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie ni oshã lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akashɛ oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: How can I stop my cassava roots from rotting underground when it rains heavily?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha shishifãi lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water settles around them, so planting on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni damɔ shi ebɔle amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli ni eye ebua ni ewaje shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do you advise me to apply fertilizer in small amounts around the plant instead of dumping a whole bowl at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo komɛi afata tso lɛ he moŋ fe ni aaashwie tsɛnsi muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much fertilizer at one time can burn their roots and spoil the crop, but feeding them little by little allows them to absorb nutrients safely as they grow.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa wo tso lɛ mli babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Shi niyenii ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ fioo fioo lɛ baaye abua ni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key food crops need to build strong green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves roll up and look weak during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants temporarily curl their leaves during extreme heat to reduce water loss, and they normally bounce back once the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafo amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my pepper crops grow thin and yield small fruit when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ yibii bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots and leaves fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food, leaving no plant with enough energy to produce big fruits.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náaa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when the soil gets too dry or when the sun is too scorching, as the plant tries to save water to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɛ́ hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Can I mix crushed wood ash with my stored cowpea seeds to protect them from insects?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tso mli sũ ni atswa lɛ afutu tsina ŋmeii ni ato lɛ koni mikɛbu he kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe?

english: Yes, fine wood ash coats the stored seeds and blocks small insects like weevils from breathing and laying eggs, keeping your stored harvest safe without liquid chemicals.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei amli sũ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ dumɔwui toɔ ni etsĩɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkamu ni amɛkawo ŋmeii. Ha okpamɔ nibii ni okɛto lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe ni okɛ tsofai ni ji nu tsuuu nii.

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred to yield heavily only in their first planting, so seeds saved from that crop will grow into weak plants with small ears.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni baahi shi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baatsɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni toi bibii yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my crops seem weak and grow slowly after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa fiofio beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops need essential nutrients like nitrogen from the soil to build strong stems and leaves. If the soil lacks these nutrients, the plants struggle to grow and will appear weak until you feed them.
ga: Tsei hia niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛma tsei kɛ baai ni wa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii nɛɛ Tsei lɛ baaná naagba yɛ amɛdalɛ mli ni amɛbaafee gbɔjɔmɔ ja oha amɛ niyenii.

english: What does it mean to nurture my crops after planting them?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ be mli ni midu nii sɛɛ?

english: Nurturing crops means giving them proper care during their growth stage—such as clearing weeds, watering them, and applying fertilizers—so they have the energy to flourish and produce high yields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ tsɔɔ akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, koni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛdara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: When is the right stage in a plant's life to start feeding it fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa yɛ tso ko shihilɛ mli ni esa akɛ aje ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: The best time to feed your crops is during their early growth stage after planting, while you are actively nurturing them, so they get the necessary strength to build roots and foliage.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ okɛha onibii lɛ niyenii ji be mli ni amɛdalɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Be mli ni okɛ ekãa miikwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛfee shishifãi kɛ baai.

english: How does chicken manure help my crops grow better than unfertilized soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Chicken manure is rich in organic matter and vital nutrients that improve soil fertility, help soil hold water longer, and give plants the food they need to grow strong.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ fa babaoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa.

english: What is the benefit of using organic manure instead of just relying on rain and normal soil?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ nugbɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa nɔ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ najiaŋ lɛ he?

english: Normal soil loses its food over time from repeated farming. Organic manure restores vital nutrients to the soil naturally, helping your plants flourish without damaging the soil structure over long periods.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ daa lɛ laajeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni jɛɔ okwaayeli nitsumɔi ni afeɔ shii abɔ lɛ mli. Organic fertilizers yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua otsei lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛfiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Will applying organic fertilizer help my young plants yield more crops at harvest time?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua midumɔwui lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Yes, organic fertilizer strengthens the roots and stems of young plants, allowing them to absorb more water and food, which directly leads to larger and healthier harvests.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ wajeɔ tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni da ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees losing their strength and struggling to grow fresh leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ hewalɛ miiho ni eebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɛ baai heei lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees take a lot of food from the soil to produce foliage and pods. Over time, exhausted soil makes the trees weak unless you give them extra nourishment through fertilizers.
ga: Cacao tsei yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛwo baai kɛ ŋmeii. Beni be hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Ja okɛ niyenii kroko fata he kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: If your cocoa trees have pale yellow leaves, thin trunks, or slow pod development, it is a sign that the soil is out of nutrients and the trees need fertilizer to regain their strength.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cacao tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eshishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ, loo eshishifãi lɛ shwereɔ blɛoo Ebaanyɛ efee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni akɛ tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛku esɛɛ eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does fertilizer help a cocoa tree survive harsh weather and dry conditions?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ hɔmɔ mli?

english: Fertilizer gives cocoa trees the nutrients needed to build deep roots and thick trunks, giving them the natural strength to thrive even when conditions are tough.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli tse lɛ akwɛ̃. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni ekɛdaa yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli po.

english: Can organic manure be used on cocoa trees, or is it only for small vegetables?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo kookoo tsei anɔ? Aloo okɛ aduawai bibii pɛ atsu nii

english: Organic manure works very well on tree crops like cocoa because it releases nutrients steadily into the soil, giving the cocoa trees ongoing strength to flourish year after year.
ga: Organic fertilizers tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ tsei tamɔ kookoo nɔ ejaakɛ amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ daa afi daa afi.

english: If I spray chemical weedkiller on my farm, will it poison the vegetables growing nearby?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ Ani ebaafee nɔ ni gbeɔ aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, if chemical sprays drift onto your vegetables, they can burn the leaves, destroy the crop, or leave harmful residue on food plants. Always spray on windless days, use a shield on your nozzle, and keep chemicals away from edible crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ hoɔ yɛ o-vegetables lɛ anɔ. Amɛ baanyɛ amɛ ha baai lɛ ashã, amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii, loo amɛ shi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛshwie gbii ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ shield abu nozzle lɛ he. Ni ha tsofai akatse tsei ni ayeɔ lɛ ahe.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the tree?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called black pod, which spreads quickly during cool, wet weather. Pruning extra shade tree branches to let in sunlight and harvesting ripe pods quickly stops the moisture that helps this disease grow.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod kɛ enɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be babaoo lɛ aniji ni afolɔ koni hulu la aba mli, ni akpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ baaye abua ni akpa ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ daa oya lɛ.

english: Twisted or curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking liquid from under the leaves. Inspecting under the leaves early and using safe insect sprays or soapy water solutions helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etsilɛ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Ni oookwɛ baai lɛ ashishi mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo nu ni akɛ samla tsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for leaf growth. Adding animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea restores green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ adara Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaha efee ŋmɔŋ ni efee hewalɛ.

english: Is it good to put fertilizer on my crops right before a heavy rain falls?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: No, heavy rain washes away fertilizer before the roots can swallow it, wasting your money and polluting nearby streams. Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a light rain instead.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Efiteɔ shika ni efiteɔ faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ moŋ.

english: Yes, cowpeas and maize grow very well together. Cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which naturally feeds the maize and keeps your soil healthy for longer.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei feɔ ekome kɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. Cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because excess water prevents the roots from breathing. Planting cassava on raised soil ridges or mounds helps rain water drain away safely from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli shweshweeshwe.
