english: My tomato plants are producing plenty of yellow flowers, but why are no fruits growing from them?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo. Shi mɛni hewɔ etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off without setting fruit if the weather gets too hot, if the soil dries out, or if there are no bees to move pollen around. Regular watering at root level keeps the blossoms healthy enough to turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi, loo kɛji ŋmeii bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii. Kɛ́ afɔ nu daa yɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛtsɔ tomato.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and cannot naturally hold up heavy fruit during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with a bamboo pole or strong wooden stick acts as a crutch to keep the tree upright until harvest.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkpa aduawai ni tsii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tso loo tso ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ nɔ ni fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ koni ehi shi shiŋŋ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: What happens if I plant my crops very close to each other so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni maná gbɛ babaoo?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin, weak plants with smaller yields. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed and produce full harvests.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ shi yibiiwoo faaa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni ewoɔ eyibii fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when they are exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense heat because their roots and leaves are delicate. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary canopy shade and retains soil moisture during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ waaa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo ewo mli lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba be kukuoo mli, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it risky to plant my maize seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry hot spell that can dry out and kill newly germinated seeds. Waiting until the rains become consistent ensures your seedlings get continuous moisture to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ odumɔwui lɛ baaná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ koni amɛdara.

english: Why should I leave space between my cassava stalks instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishiɔ gbɛ yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for water, light, and soil nutrients. Giving them adequate space allows each plant to expand its roots fully and produce larger tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso shwereɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli kwraa ni efeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or over-watering. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-decomposed manure will help the maize regain its green color and growth energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu ewo mli fe nine. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni ená hewalɛ ni ekɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl upward and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miihoso ni ekpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking nutrients from the leaves, or by a virus they spread. Spraying organic solutions like neem oil helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even though the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by soil-borne fungal or bacterial diseases that block the plant's internal stem pipes. Rotating crops annually prevents these soil diseases from accumulating.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ sũ mli loo bacteria ni tsiɔ tso lɛ mli shishifãi lɛ anaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ shwiemɔ trukaa nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ daa afi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nɛkɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa nɛɛ akabua amɛhe naa.

english: Why do my plants grow tall and thin with very few leaves when planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni eyɛ baai fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Plants stretch upward when they are starved of direct sunlight, spending energy to search for light instead of developing thick stems, roots, or fruit.
ga: Tsei lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ bɛ amɛnɔ. Amɛkɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛtao la moŋ fe ni amɛaawo tsei bibii, shishifãi, loo aduawai.

english: Why does removing weeds early in the season help my crops yield more food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and steal essential nutrients, water, and sunlight. Clearing weeds early ensures all the soil food goes directly to your crops during their critical growth period.
ga: Jwɛi daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hia, nu kɛ hulu la. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli.

english: Why should I trim off extra side shoots from my tomato branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni yɔɔ tomato niji amli lɛ?

english: Trimming unnecessary side shoots, known as suckers, directs the plant's energy into producing larger, healthier tomatoes rather than growing excess leaves.
ga: Afoɔ sɛɛ tsei ni he ehiaaa, ni atsɛɔ amɛ hu akɛ tsei. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwo tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe baai krokomɛi ni ebaakwɛ̃.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant starts to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: If my crops are failing in one part of my farmland, should I move my farm to a new piece of land?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fite yɛ miŋmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ fã lɛ nɔ Ani Esa akɛ majie miŋmɔ lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ hee nɔ?

english: Moving to a new site can help if the old land has lost its richness or is infested with disease, but you can often restore your current soil right where it is by adding animal manure or compost without the high cost of buying new land.
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko fã kɛtee he hee lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ momo lɛ nɔ hewalɛ efite loo hela emɔ nɔ. Shi bei pii lɛ obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ mli amrɔ nɛɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ ni shika babaoo ni okɛheɔ shikpɔŋ hee lɛ fataaa he.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land I want to buy will be good for growing crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni misumɔɔ ni mahe lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Good farmland usually has dark, soft topsoil that crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well after rainfall without getting flooded, and naturally grows healthy, green wild plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni fiteɔ oya yɛ oniji amli. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ ni nu shwieee nɔ. ni amɛdara amɛtsɔmɔ koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why do some soils require animal manure or compost before crops can grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔji komɛi biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔji awo mli dani tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Soil needs nutrients just like people need food; animal manure acts as slow-releasing food that enriches tired dirt, improves water retention, and gives young roots the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Shikpɔŋ he miihia niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ bɔ ni niyenii he hiaa adesai lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Manure tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni ajieɔ lɛ blɛoo ni haa muji ni etɔ lɛ eyiɔ obɔ ekoŋŋ. Eha nu ni ahiɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ni eha shishifãi bibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: What can I do if the soil on my farm has become too hard and dry for my plants?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbi tsɔ kɛha mitsei lɛ?

english: Adding organic matter like dried leaves, poultry dung, or cow manure breaks up hard soil, allowing plant roots to breathe easily and helping the earth hold onto rainwater longer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egbi, kooloi ashishifã, loo tsina ashishifã fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ akumɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi ni amɛmuɔ mlɛo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ

english: What simple methods can I use to protect my young crops from harsh sun and roaming animals?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mabu miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni nyiɛɔ kɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ ahe?

english: You can build simple shade covers using palm leaves to shield young seedlings from intense sun heat, and place stick or bamboo fencing around your plot to keep animals out.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei tsei afee he ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni okɛbuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ni okɛ tsei niji loo ŋmeii abɔle oshikpɔŋ lɛ he koni kooloi akabote mli.

english: How can I tell if my plant leaves are turning yellow because of insect attacks or because the soil is poor?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ ahewɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ?

english: Yellow leaves spread evenly across the plant usually mean the soil lacks nutrients like nitrogen, while yellowing accompanied by spots, holes, or curled leaf edges usually points to insects or plant disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni gbɛ eshwa tso lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, yɛ be mli ni baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni fata he kɛ ŋmeii, bu, loo baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, kooloi loo tso helai miimɔ amɛ.

english: Is it better to burn cleared bushes on my land or leave them to clear the field for planting?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã brɔshi ni ajie lɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo mashi lɛ ni ajie lɛ koni akɛdu nii?

english: Burning cleared bush might seem quick, but it destroys beneficial soil life and burns away good organic nutrients; letting the cleared plants decay naturally into the ground makes the soil much richer for your crops.
ga: Ekolɛ jwɛi ni ajie lɛ ni ashãa lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni yaa oya. Shi efiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ wala ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ni eshãa niyenii kpakpai ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Ha tsei ni ajie lɛ lɛ afite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops stop growing halfway through the season even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ yɛ be lɛ fã mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Crops often stop growing because the nutrients in the soil have been completely used up, the soil around the roots is packed too tightly, or hidden pests in the ground are damaging the root system.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kpaa kwɛ̃mɔ ejaakɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ efo. Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Aloo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ miifite shishifãi lɛ?

english: Is it safe to plant two different types of food crops together in the same farm plot?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaadu niyenii henɔi enyɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting complementary crops together—like maize with beans—can protect your soil, keep weeds down, and allow legumes like beans to add natural nitrogen food into the dirt for the maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa. Ebaanyɛ ebu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he, egbe jwɛi, ni eye ebua ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni amɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen niyenii afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛha ŋmeii.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow much faster than the food crops I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe niyenii tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to the local environment, making them faster at grabbing available moisture, sunlight, and soil nutrients than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛ mɔɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: What is the difference between the tall coconut trees and the short ones when deciding what to plant on my farm in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei ni kwɔlɔ kɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ kuku lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ mikpɛ miyiŋ yɛ nɔ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ Ghana lɛ he?

english: Tall coconut trees live longer and are very hardy for oil production, while dwarf (short) coconut varieties produce fruit much faster, are easier to harvest without climbing high, and are preferred for selling fresh coconut water.
ga: Kokoo tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee mu. Yɛ be mli ni dwarf (kuku) ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ woɔ yibii oya kwraa lɛ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ abaakpa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. kɛ ŋmei nu hee ni ehe gbɛi ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ

english: How can I tell when a coconut on my tree is ready for drinking fresh water versus ready for making oil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaanu nu kpakpa ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaafee fɔ?

english: Young coconuts harvested at around 6 to 7 months are bright green and full of sweet water, while coconuts left on the tree for 11 to 12 months turn brown and dry, forming a thick white meat inside that is ideal for processing into coconut oil.
ga: Kokooi bibii ni akpaa beni amɛye aaafee nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 7 lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛyiɔ obɔ kɛ ŋmeii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni ashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 12 lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii ni amɛbaagbi. Efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ futafuta yɛ emli ni sa kɛha nitsumɔ ni akɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ fɔ.

english: Why do tiny young coconuts keep falling off my trees before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ? Ni magbee shi kɛjɛ mitso lɛ nɔ dani eda?

english: Premature button shed happens naturally when a tree produces more flowers than it can support, but severe fruit drop is usually triggered by dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or insect pests feeding on the young flowers.
ga: Button ni shwieɔ shi oya lɛ baa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ tso ko wo fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ nɔ. Shi bei pii lɛ, aduawai ni fiteɔ waa lɛ baa kɛ hulutsoo be. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ fɔfɔi bibii

english: Why are the leaves on my coconut palm turning yellow and dying from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves can be caused by a lack of nutrients like potassium in the soil, but in Ghana, it can also be a sign of Cape Saint Paul Wilt Disease, a serious infection spread by small insects that requires removing infected trees early.
ga: Niyenii nibii, tamɔ potassium, ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha baai ŋmɔŋ aba. Shi yɛ Ghana lɛ Ebaanyɛ efee Cape Saint Paul Wilt hela lɛ hu he okadi, ni ji hela ko ni naa wa ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa ni biɔ ni ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ mra.

english: What is making V-shaped cuts in the leaves of my young coconut trees, and how do I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-kokoo baa bibioo lɛ nɔ fã ni tamɔ V lɛ ba? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he?

english: This damage is caused by the Rhinoceros Beetle, which burrows into the top growing cluster of the tree to feed; you can control it by clearing nearby rotting logs where the beetles lay eggs and keeping the farm clear of decaying organic matter.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ ji nɔ ni rhinoceros ŋmeii lɛ kɛbaa. Amɛfoɔ bu yɛ tsei akui ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli koni amɛtao niyenii. Obaanyɛ okudɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ tsei ni egboi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ fɛɛ ni oootsi lɛ nɔ. He ni ladybugs fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ ni amɛhaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli tseɔ kɛjɛɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or maize between my coconut trees without harming them?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei ateŋ ni miyeee amɛ awui?

english: Yes, intercropping works very well during the first few years after planting coconut seedlings because light still reaches the ground, giving you extra income and food while keeping weeds managed around your palms.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni adu yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ sɛɛ. Ejaakɛ la lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lolo. Ehaa onáa shika kɛ niyenii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ jwɛi ni bɔle onine lɛ he lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do coconut palms grow so well in sandy soil near the coast compared to heavy clay soils inland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ nɔ kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Coconut palms have deep, fibrous roots that need loose, well-draining soil to absorb air and water easily; heavy clay soil traps water around the root zone, which can cause root rot and stunt the tree's growth.
ga: Kokoo tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni enyɛ eŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu oya. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu kɛbɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni etsĩ tso lɛ shweremɔ naa.

english: How can I protect my young coconut trees from drying out during the long harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmeii bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ harmatta be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli?

english: Mulching—placing a thick layer of dry grass, palm fronds, or cocoa husks around the base of the tree—helps retain moisture in the soil, suppresses weeds, and keeps root temperatures cool during dry months.
ga: Mulching—ni ji jwɛi ni egbi, ŋmei tsei, loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ—haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. tsiɔ jwɛi anaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Does cutting fresh green coconuts directly off the tree damage the tree's ability to produce flowers later?
ga: Ani ŋmeii heei ni afolɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baafite nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛwoɔ fɔfɔi yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, harvesting fresh coconuts by cutting the bunch stalk cleanly does not harm the tree, as long as you do not damage the growing crown or bruise the nearby flower clusters where future fruits develop.
ga: Dabi, akokooi heei ni akpaa kɛtsɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeee tso lɛ awui. Shii abɔ ni ofiteee yitso ni miida lɛ loo ofiteee fɔfɔi akui ni bɛŋkɛ he ni wɔsɛɛ aduawai baakwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ,

english: How do I know if my coconut trees need fertilizer, and what type should I use?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji ŋmei tso he miihia ŋmei loo ehe ehiaaa? Ni mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ akɛtsu nii?

english: If your palms grow slowly, produce small nuts, or have pale leaves, they likely lack nutrients; applying a balanced fertilizer or organic manure around the base, along with a bit of salt for sodium, helps palms yield bigger fruits and stay green.
ga: Kɛji otsitsi lɛ miida blɛoo Ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii loo eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ otsitsi lɛ mli. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli abɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he kɛfata sodium ŋmei fioo he. Ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo yibii wuji ni eha efee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crop leaves need to stay green and healthy. It can also happen when the soil is waterlogged or too dry for roots to take up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei ahe koni amɛya nɔ amɛfee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo egbi tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves, but the tubers underground stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or is planted too close together, the plant spends all its energy growing branches and leaves above ground instead of sending energy down into the roots to build big tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei niji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ he wami kɛ yaa sisi ɔ mi konɛ e pee bulb nguahi.

english: Why do my plantain leaves fold up and droop during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves roll or droop in high heat to protect themselves from losing too much water. It is the plant's natural way of saving moisture until the hot sun goes down.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɛɔ nu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gboɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die if I don't plant plantains next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji miduuu amɛ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and broad, providing living shade umbrellas that protect young cocoa until it gets older.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa. Ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my pepper plants when they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Pepper tso lɛ beni eji bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that steal water, sunlight, and soil food much faster than young pepper plants. Clearing them early ensures your peppers get all the food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔtɔ tsei bibii. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha o-peppers lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why didn't my maize seeds sprout after I buried them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni afu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds need air and mild moisture close to the surface to wake up. If planted too deep, the young shoot runs out of energy before it can push through the heavy soil to reach sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ fioo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ koni amɛte shi. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahewalɛ baaho dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too hot, when the soil alternates between very dry and very wet, or when tiny insects attack the blossoms before the fruit can start forming.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ nɔ ni efɔ waa teŋ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii tutuaa fɔfɔi dani aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop producing fruits during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ekpaa yibiiwoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash key nutrients out of the soil, flood the plant roots so they cannot breathe, and knock off flowers before they turn into peppers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii titrii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ekɛ nu shwieɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Ni fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my groundnuts rot inside the soil before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ nɔ ni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut pods rot underground if left in wet, waterlogged soil for too long after maturity, or if soil fungi attack the pods when harvest is delayed.
ga: Peanut pods lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutua ŋmeii lɛ beni kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso afɔ sweet potato wain tso nɔ koni makwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce food that grows the tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where they can get sun and stay free from leaf rot.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii beni aduɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Amɛ baanyɛ amɛ na hulu la ni baa fitemɔ bɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my crops grow very well in one part of my field but stay small and yellowish in another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fã ko mli shi eyɛ bibioo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ fã kroko lɛ?

english: Soil quality is rarely uniform across a farm. Variations in topsoil depth, water drainage, and natural nutrient levels cause crops to grow unevenly across different spots on the same land.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su lɛ jeee nɔ kome yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mlibotemɔ, nu ni hoɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ srɔtoi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daaa yɛ hei srɔtoi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ

english: Why is it better for me to start farming a small portion of my land before expanding to the whole farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mabɔi okwaayeli yɛ he bibioo ko lɛ? Dani ebaagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: Starting small allows you to properly manage weeds, labor, and fertilizer costs without getting overwhelmed. As you gain yields and income, you can expand gradually without risking crop failure on a huge cleared area.
ga: shishijee bibioo Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ jwɛi, nitsumɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nyɔmɔwoo tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni haomɔ ko bɛ he. Kɛji onine shɛ nibii ni anáa kɛ shika ni yaa hiɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ Obaanyɛ Ogbɛ oshwa fiofio ni oshara ko bɛ he akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafite yɛ hei wuji ni agbele naa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up and droop when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the weather gets very hot and dry, pepper plants curl their leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant trap moisture inside so it does not dry out completely.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛmli koni amɛkagbi kwraa.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms keep falling off without forming any fruits during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ? Ni nɔ ko jɛɛɛ mli baa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and prevents proper pollination. When temperature spikes, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy and water until conditions improve.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my old cassava plants drop most of their leaves during the Harmattan dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso momo lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fite yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a survival technique. Cassava sheds leaves during dry spells to stop water from evaporating into the dry air, storing water and energy safety inside its underground roots instead.
ga: Baai ni ashwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala. Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni nu akaho kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli. ni moŋ lɛ, ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear away all the big shade trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong, direct sunlight. Shade trees act as living canopy shields that keep the temperature cool and preserve soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enáa hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to compete for light, water, and soil food. The plants stretch upward to catch light, leaving them weak and unable to nourish full maize cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tso lɛ shwieɔ ehe koni emɔ kane lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛha ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cowpea or beans alongside my maize make the maize grow better later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni midu yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpea take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. This leaves natural fertilizer in the ground that feeds neighboring or subequent crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii eshwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if fall armyworms have started attacking my young maize plants before my leaves get destroyed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji fall cutworms lɛ ebɔi mi-baby corn tsei lɛ tutuamɔ dani mibaai lɛ efite?

english: Check the central funnel (whorl) of young maize plants for small pinholes in leaves and powdery, saw-dust-like waste (frass). Catching these signs early means the caterpillars are hiding inside feeding.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmãa bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ (ring) lɛ mli kɛji buji bibii yɛ mli. yɛ baai kɛ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmeii amli? Okadii nɛɛ ni ooomɔ mra Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo niyenii lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the ground before harvest time when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpa be mli ni nugbɔ miinɛ waa lɛ?

english: Excess rain on poorly drained soil starves plant roots of oxygen and creates wet conditions where fungal and bacterial rots thrive, causing tubers to decay in flooded earth.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha tsei shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ shwereɔ yɛ mli lɛ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I stop heavy rain from washing away the good soil and crops on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashwie shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rain hits bare farm land, rushing water strips away topsoil and uproots young plants. Digging drainage trenches, building raised ridges across slopes, and planting cover crops like groundnuts help slow down rainwater and keep your soil in place.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tswa okwaayeli hei ni egbi lɛ Nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ jieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni ejieɔ tsei bibii lɛ. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni oootsi, ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni oootswa yɛ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ baa shi ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground after heavy rains sit on my land for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When water collects on your farm without draining, it starves plant roots of air, causing cassava tubers to rot. Planting on high mounds and creating simple water channels around your plot allows excess rainwater to flow away safely.
ga: Beni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli. Ebaaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ baagboi. Dumɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ kɛ nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni afee yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he Enɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: How do vetiver grass or trees planted at the edge of my land protect my farm during big storms?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo tsei ni adu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ naa lɛ abu miŋmɔ lɛ he yɛ ahum wulu ko mli?

english: Deep-rooted grass and trees act as living barriers. Their roots hold the soil tightly together like a network, while their thick stems slow down rushing floodwater before it can wash away your crops.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ wala he. Amɛshishifãi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ waa tamɔ ŋshɔŋloo. yɛ be mli ni amɛ tsei ni mli tse lɛ haa nu afua lɛ hoɔ fioo dani amɛshwieɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: What simple land preparation can I do before the rainy season so my farm isn't ruined?
ga: Saamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlɛo Te ooofee tɛŋŋ atsĩ ŋmɔ lɛ naa koni ekagbee shi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi?

english: Before heavy rains arrive, clear choked gutters, build stable ridges across slopes, and plant border hedges. Setting up proper drainage pathways ensures heavy rainwater escapes your farm without destroying your raised beds.
ga: Dani nugbɔ baanɛ waa lɛ, jiemɔ nu ŋshɔi ni atsĩ naa lɛ. Bɔɔ ŋshɔkpɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tsɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni odu gbogbo Nu ni hoɔ lɛ gbɛ ni sa lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ joɔ foi kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni efiteee otsui ni awó nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my raised soil mounds and ridges break down and flatten after a month of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi gɔji kɛ ŋshɔkei ni awó nɔ lɛ miifite ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa nyɔŋ kome sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous falling raindrops and surface water runoff slowly beat down loose soil structure. Compacted mound walls and planting cover crops along ridge edges help keep the soil firm and resistant to rain damage.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hoɔ fiofio kɛboteɔ mli.Enaa shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Gbogboi ni akɛma shi ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ekɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fiteɔ nii.

english: Why does my farm soil get as hard as concrete after heavy rain floods dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ kɔnkrit yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa kɛ nu afua ni egbi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain breaks down natural soil clumps, causing fine particles to seal together smoothly as they dry. Spreading mulch, such as dry leaves or grass, cushions the impact of falling raindrops and keeps the soil soft.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli sũ lɛ mli fãa. Ehaa nibii bibii lɛ feɔ ekome jogbaŋŋ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Mulch tamɔ baai ni egboi loo jwɛi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nugbɔshiimɔi ni baa shi lɛ he hewalɛ baa shi. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ

english: Why is it bad to apply fertilizer right before a big downpour falls on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa anɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain quickly washes loose fertilizer off the surface into streams before roots can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when soil is moist and cover it lightly with dirt so rainwater does not sweep it away.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ faai ni hoɔ oya mli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fioo koni nugbɔ nu akashwie nɔ.

english: What should I do to save my maize field after a heavy storm knocks down my plants and floods the ground?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mahere mi-ŋma ŋmɔ lɛ yiwala beni ahum ni naa wa ko kpata tsei lɛ ahiɛ ni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: First, clear drainage paths immediately to let trapped water out of the field. Once standing water is gone, gently scoop soil around stem bases to support fallen plants and apply a light boost of nitrogen fertilizer to help them recover.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, jiemɔ nu lɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni nu ni emɔ mli lɛ ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tee lɛ, shwiemɔ sũ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he blɛoo koni ekɛfi tsei ni egbee shi lɛ asɛɛ. Ni okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko aye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: If heavy rain destroys my young vegetable seedbed, how long should I wait before planting again?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kpata aduawai tsei bibii lɛ ahiɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu eheei?

english: Wait a few days until the topsoil has dried enough that it no longer sticks heavily to your hoes or hands. Replanting too quickly in soggy, oxygen-deprived soil causes new seeds to rot before they sprout.
ga: Mɛɛ gbii fioo komɛi kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baagbi bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ehe akakpɛtɛ shɔvel lɛ loo oniji ahe waa dɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu tsei heei mra tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui heei lɛ agbo dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do some of my crops survive heavy downpours easily while others die off quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi yeɔ wala yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi gboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Crops with deep taproots and strong flexible stems withstand floodwaters better than soft, shallow-rooted plants. Planting sensitive crops on raised mounds protects their roots from drowning during sudden heavy rains.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa ni nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ baanyɛ adamɔ nu afua naa jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ lɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ buɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe koni amɛkabote nu mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants curling up and turning yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to reduce water loss through their leaves when there is not enough moisture in the soil. Yellowing is a sign of water stress and nutrient shortage, meaning the plant needs irrigation or rainfall to recover.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu ni fiteɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ aba shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. Yellow ji nu he haomɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ he okadi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ehe miihia ni awo tsei lɛ nu loo nugbɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Does using clean stream water to irrigate my vegetable farm make a difference in how my crops grow?
ga: Te nu ni mli tse ni mikɛtsuɔ nii kɛshwieɔ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Yes, clean water free from harsh chemicals or high salt levels helps crops easily absorb nutrients from the soil. Dirty or polluted water can clog soil pores, introduce diseases, and stunt your vegetables' growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni mli tse ni tsofai ni mli wa loo ŋoo babaoo bɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mlɛo. Nu ni mli ewo muji loo nu ni mli ewo muji baanyɛ atsĩ sũ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ anaa, ekɛ helai aba ni ekɛtsi aduawai anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa plants have very tender leaves and cannot survive harsh, direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees to shelter them and keep the surrounding air humid during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Koni ekɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee shweshweeshwe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit mainly due to extreme heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii, titri lɛ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli babaoo Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than my planted crops after the rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally adapted to the local environment and have stronger root systems that absorb available moisture and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Amɛheɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is suitable for planting cassava this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmei dumɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Good soil for cassava should be loose, well-draining, and rich in organic matter so the tuber roots can expand easily. Hard, heavily compacted clay soil will restrict root growth and give you very small yields.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha ŋmei lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo Shikpɔji ni mli wa ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients like nitrogen and creates a permanent breeding ground for pests and diseases that attack that specific crop.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa sũ mli nibii komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ fiteɔ be fɛɛ be. ni efee he ko ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ afɔ yɛ daa.

english: What is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my crop field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mawo miŋmɔji lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Fertilizer is best applied when the soil is moist and the plants are actively growing, usually a few weeks after germination. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn plant roots and waste nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tso lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afite.

english: What is causing large holes in the leaves of my cabbage crops, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji wuji ni yɔɔ mi-cabbage tsei lɛ baai amli lɛ baa? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by caterpillars or pests like the diamondback moth eating the leaves. You can protect your crops by practicing field sanitation, using net coverings, or applying appropriate farm sprays.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tamɔ diamondback ŋmei ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabe baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ hetsemɔ ni ooofee yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Netting ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii

english: Why do my harvested yams begin to rot rapidly after I dig them out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ oya beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot quickly after harvest if they are bruised by farm tools during digging or if they are stored in damp, hot places where fungi and bacteria thrive.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ sɛɛ kɛji akɛ okwaayeli nibii fite amɛ yɛ be mli ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kɛji akɛ akɛto hei ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ shwereɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow tall. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure feed will help the leaves turn dark green and feed the plant again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni eha tso lɛ niyenii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with bushy leaves, but producing very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, they spend all their energy growing leaves above ground instead of storage roots below. To get bigger tubers, the plant needs soil rich in potassium and phosphorus, which encourage root development.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nitrogen babaoo fe nine kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe lɛ, Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shishi. koni ená yitso agbo Shikpɔŋ ni potassium kɛ phosphorus eyi mli obɔ lɛ he miihia tso lɛ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ

english: How do I tell if the fertilizer I put on my field is actually working on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: You will know fertilizer is working when you see visible changes within two weeks: leaves becoming broader and darker green, stems growing thicker, and the crop recovering quickly after rainfall. If there is no change, the soil might be too dry for the plant to drink in the nutrients.
ga: Obaale akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitsu nii kɛji ona tsakemɔi ni anaa yɛ otsii enyɔ mli. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli, amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji tsakemɔ ko bɛ lɛ Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni tsei lɛ nyɛŋ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off the stems before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani ebatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of phosphorus. Keeping the soil consistently moist and providing balanced plant nutrients helps the crop hold its flowers until tomatoes form.
ga: Tomato tsei baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tsei niyenii ni ja ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tomatoi lɛ feɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon is a crop's natural defense to slow down water loss in bright sunlight. If the leaves uncurl in the cool evening, the plant is normal, but if they remain curled overnight, it means the plant is dry or suffering from sap-sucking pests.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe koni ekɛha nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tee nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ hu? Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbi loo tsɛŋemɔ helai emɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop their small green pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Dani ebaada agbo?

english: Dropping young pods—known as cherelle wilt—happens when the cocoa tree doesn't have enough nutrients, water, or light to feed all its fruit at once. Pruning excessive shade leaves and enriching the soil gives the tree enough energy to carry its pods to harvest.
ga: Oblanyo fioo ni shwieɔ shi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ cherry wilt. Ebaa kɛ́ cacao tso lɛ bɛ niyenii, nu, loo la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii shikome. Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni yɔɔ hulutsoo fe nine lɛ amli ni afee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛfɛo lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛkpa eshishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin and fall over easily when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ adu amɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing stalks fight each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. The plants stretch quickly to reach sunlight, making them tall, weak, and easily blown down by strong rain or wind.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsoi ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe oya koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ, ni amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni nugbɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ akumɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why are my yam vines taking so long to sprout and climb after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ ni ekwɔɔ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines delay sprouting if the seed yam was planted in hard, dry soil or if the soil lacks moisture to trigger root growth. Planting in soft, raised mounds enriched with nutrients helps the seed yam wake up and send out strong climbing shoots.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei baaha amɛkwɛ̃mɔ aya hiɛ kɛji akɛ adu sweet potato dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni egbi nɔ. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ ni baaha shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nɔ kwɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛteɔ shi ni amɛtsuɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: Why do fall armyworms seem to destroy my maize leaves faster during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni fall flukes lɛ fiteɔ mi-corn baai lɛ oya yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Dry spells stress the maize plant, making its leaves softer and easier for caterpillars to chew. Warm, dry conditions also allow armyworm eggs to hatch much faster, causing rapid damage across the farm.
ga: Dry spell lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmãa tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛaaye. Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa helminth ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ oya kwraa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ fiteɔ nii oya.

english: Why do some of the seeds I plant sprout quickly while others in the same row fail to come up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ sɛɛkuu kome mli lɛ kwɛɛɛ oya lɛ?

english: Uneven sprouting happens if seeds are buried at different depths, if part of the soil is drier, or if insects eat the seeds underground. Planting all seeds at the same shallow depth in evenly moist soil ensures they sprout at the same time.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hei srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ lɛ, shweremɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee baa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko mli egbi Aloo kɛji kooloi yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi dumɔwui Dumɔ dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ be kome too mli.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct, intense sunlight. Leaving shade trees or intercropping with plantains creates a protective canopy that reduces heat stress and keeps moisture in the soil for the young roots.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛ́ ashi tsei yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo akɛ plantains du amɛ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo he haomɔ baa shi, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi kɛhaa shishifãi bibii lɛ.

english: When cassava plants are spaced too closely, their roots compete fiercely for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water. Proper spacing allows each plant enough room to develop large, healthy tubers instead of thin, weak ones.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, hulu la kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ bulbs agboi ni mli wa baa. Mohu ɔ, yi ɔ he tsɔ nɛ e he gbɔjɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize crop turn light green or yellow from the tip downward even during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which plants need to make food and grow strong. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer restores these essential nutrients to the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops yield less harvest when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts natural nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe sɛɛkuu lɛ mli

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, damp, and crowded farm conditions. Pruning excess branches lets sunshine and fresh air reach the pods, which keeps the farm dry and halts the disease.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa helai kpaa.

english: Why do small caterpillars appear and eat the leaves and shoots of my vegetable crop right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii jeɔ kpo ni amɛyeɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Warm, wet weather encourages pest eggs hidden in the soil or surrounding bush to hatch in large numbers. Inspecting crops early and using recommended botanical or chemical sprays controls them before they destroy the yield.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ woɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo tsei bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ. Amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo fɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ mra kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛkudɔ amɛ dani amɛfite nibii ni adu lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up and curl during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense mechanism plants use to protect themselves from intense heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun to prevent water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Tsei haa amɛhe ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ mli koni nu lɛ akaho oya tsɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does putting dead leaves or grass around the base of my tomato plants help them during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi ebɔle tomato tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around plants with dry plant matter is called mulching. It acts like a blanket, keeping the soil cool and stopping moisture from evaporating into the air so the plant stays hydrated longer.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ tsei ni egbi shwieɔ tsei ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I save from my previous harvest fail to sprout when I plant them again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can lose their vitality if stored in warm, damp places where invisible molds or small insects damage the seed embryos. Storing well-dried seeds in sealed containers or using certified seeds ensures high germination.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ afite hewalɛ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ, ni edɔ. he ni ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii ni anaaa lɛ fiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ Dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛtoɔ tsɛnsii ni atsĩ naa mli loo akɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli tsuɔ nii lɛ baaha amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested grains end up full of holes and dust after sitting in my store for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ sũ beni mita shwapo lɛ mli nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Small insects called weevils lay eggs inside stored grains that are not completely dry or properly sealed. Thoroughly sun-drying grains before storage and using proper storage bags or modern grain protection dust keeps weevils away.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmaa ni ato ni egbiko kwraa loo atsĩko naa jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Ha dumɔwui lɛ agbi yɛ hulu lɛ mli dani okɛto. Ni okɛ kotoku ni sa ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe loo ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmaa sũ ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛtsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: Young cocoa trees need partial shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out the topsoil before their roots grow deep enough to find groundwater.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ baahiɛ hulutsoo fioo koni amɛhi shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii ni egbiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛna shikpɔŋ shishi nu.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks next to my yam plants for them to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi koni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to spread their leaves high up to catch sunlight; lifting the leaves off the bare ground prevents leaf rot from ground heat and helps the plant produce larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ he ni agbele lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ la ni tsoɔ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the crop is starving for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil that plants need to build strong green leaves and make food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛfee niyenii.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt and curl during the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa mli be mli ni mifeee nakai lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During the hottest hours, crops lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it from the soil, so curling leaves is the plant's natural defense to trap moisture and protect itself from heat.
ga: yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars hiding inside the center funnel of my maize plants and eating the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the softest tender growth inside the center funnel of young corn plants, which slows down growth if not controlled early.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ hei ni dalɛ yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ni ehaa amɛdalɛ baa shi kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ amɛ mra.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off the stems without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperature extremes or water shortages stress the crop, preventing the flowers from completing pollination into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Etsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkafee pollination ni amɛfee aduawai.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same spot on my land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific crop pests and soil diseases to multiply in that spot.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool, stops moisture from evaporating quickly in the hot sun, prevents weeds from sprouting, and breaks down over time to feed the soil.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are mature enough to dig up and harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafo ni makpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off naturally, and the soil at the base of the main stem begins to crack as the tubers swell below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: How many suckers should I leave growing around one plantain stand to get big fruit bunches?
ga: Esa akɛ mashi tsei bibii enyiɛ ni mikɛdu he fɛɛ he? Dumɔwu kome koni ená aduawai wuji.

english: It is best to leave only three shoots (one main fruiting stem, one medium shoot, and one small sucker) per stand so the plants do not fight each other for nutrients, light, and water.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi ŋmeii 3 pɛ (tso titri ni woɔ yibii 1, tso ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ 1, kɛ tso bibioo 1) yɛ tso kome mli koni tsei lɛ akashi amɛhe yɛ niyenii, la, kɛ nu he.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow and drying up before the corn is fully formed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, it shows the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main food leaves need to stay green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or rotating your land with beans helps keep leaves green so they can feed the growing corn ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni efee V su ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni esa akɛ baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛ ŋmeii tsake shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli koni ekɛha ŋmãa toi ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of thick green leaves, but the tubers underground are small and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Baai eŋɔli lɛ mli tse waa. Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from soil or heavy shade, it spends all its energy making leaves and stems above ground. To get fat tubers, cassava needs balanced nutrients, proper sunlight, and potassium to push food down into the roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ naa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛma baai kɛ tsei ashishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. koni ená yitso ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ fɔ Cassava he miihia niyenii ni sa. hulu la ni sa kɛ potassium ni baaha niyenii aba shi kɛya shishifãi lɛ amli

english: Why do people say that planting cowpeas or beans makes the soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni adu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea roots have tiny nodules that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food. When the cowpea leaves and roots decay in the soil after harvest, that trapped food stays behind to feed your next crop of maize or vegetables.
ga: Cowpea shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. No mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ tsei aniyenii. Kɛji tsina ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Niyenii ni ekã shi lɛ hiɔ sɛɛ koni ekɛha onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii, tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai.

english: Why are many of the small young pods on my cocoa trees turning shriveled and black during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii ni fa babaoo yɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: While cocoa trees naturally shed extra young pods, fast-spreading black spots on pods during wet months indicate black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads through water droplets. Pruning excess canopy leaves lets sunlight in to dry out the pods and reduce fungus.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kookoo tsei shwieɔ amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa moŋ, Shi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ diŋ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyɔji amli lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii diji hela. Fuŋɔ ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nu bibii amli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la lɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni eha ŋmeii lɛ aba shi.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turning black and sunken before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ fãi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiibote mli dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, which happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium to the developing fruit. It usually occurs when watering is irregular—such as letting the soil dry out completely and then flooding it—which prevents smooth uptake of calcium.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha amɛyibii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ nu lɛ be fɛɛ be, tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ahaa egbiɔ kwraa, ni no sɛɛ lɛ, nu shwieɔ nɔ. ni tsiɔ calcium lɛ naa koni ekabote mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes curling upward and shrinking into tiny wrinkled clusters?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Wrinkled and curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites sucking sap from the young leaves. Controlling these insects early prevents them from spreading viral diseases that permanently stunt the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Etsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi daa lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over during strong winds, even when the fruit bunch is still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ aduawai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo moŋ

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches, especially if tiny root nematodes have weakened the roots underground. Propping the stems with sturdy wooden poles helps support the weight until harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ nematodes lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii. Ehaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ Kɛ akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaafi muji lɛ sɛɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them trail on the bush floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi lɛ? koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ nɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha enyiɛ jwɛi lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight on all their leaves to manufacture food for the tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves into full sunlight and away from damp ground diseases, allowing the plant to produce much bigger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni helai akashɛ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara kwraa.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce full shells with no peanuts inside when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ ni ŋmeii bɛ mli kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods, often called 'pops', happen when there is not enough calcium or moisture in the topsoil while the underground pods are filling. Groundnut pods absorb calcium directly from the surrounding soil to form healthy seeds.
ga: Peanut pods ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘pops’ lɛ baa beni calcium loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi pods lɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my rice plants turn yellow and stop growing when the water level in my field remains too deep?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ be mli ni nu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli kwɔ tsɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Although swamp rice needs plenty of moisture, deep standing water that stays stagnant prevents air from reaching the young roots. Without oxygen, the roots struggle to feed, causing leaves to turn yellow from root stress.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo he miihia peat moŋ, Shi nu ni damɔ shi, ni ekã shi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛna niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi ahe haomɔ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow from the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the center of maize leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Maize plants need nitrogen to stay green, build strong stems, and form full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Bɔɔ tso ni mli wa ni otswa cob ni eyi obɔ

english: Cowpeas and beans are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant decomposes, it releases this nitrogen back into the soil as free natural fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛ tsei lɛ fite Ejieɔ nitrogen nɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry conditions to reduce water loss. The plant goes dormant to protect its tubers underground until rains return to trigger new leaves.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Tso lɛ baawɔ koni ebu ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba ni ebaakwɛ baai heei.

english: Why do my tomato plant flowers dry up and fall off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot or water is inconsistent. High heat or water stress prevents proper pollination, so the plant sheds the blossom instead of producing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu mli haomɔ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when I clear away all the big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct harsh sunlight and high heat. They need temporary shade from taller trees or food crops like plantains to keep them cool and moist during early growth.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji loo niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛ dalɛ be mli mra.

english: Why do I get smaller plantain bunches when I leave many shoots growing around one mother plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ plantain tsei bibii anɔ beni mishiɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ fɔlɔ tso kome he lɛ?

english: Having too many shoots around the main plantain tree creates competition for water and soil nutrients, leaving less energy for the mother plant to grow a large, heavy bunch.
ga: having shoots around Shishijee dumɔwui babaoo tsɔ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha niyenii ni jɛɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli. Enɛ haa hewalɛ fioo pɛ eha tso nyɛ lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam leaves need sunlight to generate energy that feeds the tuber underground. Staking holds the leaves up towards the sun and spreads them out, leading to bigger yam roots.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la koni ekɛfee hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ. Kɛji oootswa tso lɛ, mɔmɔ baai lɛ kɛyashɛ hulu lɛ he ni ogbɛ amɛshwã. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ agbo.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is commonly caused by tiny pests like mites or thrips feeding on leaf sap, or viruses spread by insects, which weakens the plant and stunts new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni yeɔ stevia baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baai lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaaa ekwɛ ehee.

english: Why are there tiny holes appearing all over my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejie ehe kpo yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are caused by caterpillars or beetles eating the foliage, which reduces the plant's ability to gather sunlight and form a solid cabbage head.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ kaabeji baai amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛbuaa hulu la naa lɛ baa shi, ni etsɔɔ kaabe yitso ni wa.

english: Why are my sweet potato leaves getting eaten leaving behind webbing underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ayeɔ mi sweet potato baai lɛ aahu akɛ tsɔne ko pɛ yɔɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Webbing and leaf damage are signs of spider mites or caterpillars that reproduce quickly on leaves during warm, dry weather, feeding on plant juices.
ga: Webbing kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ ji ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni fɔɔ oya yɛ baai anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he okadi. Kɛtsɔ aduawai amli nu ni jɛ tsei amli lɛ ni ayeɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to intense heat and burn easily under full sun. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide necessary shade and shelter during the cocoa tree's first few years, while also giving you food and income while you wait for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo kɛ wɔɔhe ni he hiaa yɛ cacao tso lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Be nɛɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, ekɛ niyenii kɛ shika haa bo yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Can I continue growing food crops like maize on the same land once my cocoa trees grow big?
ga: Ani manyɛ maya nɔ madu niyenii, tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ? Beni mi-kookoo tso lɛ daa lɛ

english: Food crops can grow alongside cocoa only during the first two to three years. Once the mature cocoa branches form a thick cover overhead, sunlight cannot reach the ground, so crops like maize will no longer get enough light to grow.
ga: Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ kookoo masɛi pɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli. Beni kookoo niji ni eda lɛ feɔ tsɔne ni mli tse yɛ amɛyiteŋ lɛ Hulu la lɛ nyɛŋ akpɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa naaa la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa seedlings turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant is lacking essential nutrients in the soil or is being attacked by pests like mirids. Feeding the soil with compost or manure helps bring back healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pollen miitutua lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to turn black and rot right on the tree?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cold, overly wet, and shady conditions. Clearing weeds and trimming extra branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the trees and reduce infection.
