ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ Too wet and shady. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli kɛ tsei lɛ ahe ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa helai ni baa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do so many flowers fall off my cocoa tree without producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa bɛ mli lɛ?

english: A cocoa tree produces thousands of flowers, but only flowers visited by tiny beneficial insects get pollinated to become pods. Keeping the farm soil moist and shaded creates a good environment for these insects to do their work.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni abaawo lɛ pollin kɛyashi ebaatsɔ pod. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ hulutsoo lɛ, ebaaha shihilɛ kpakpa aba kɛha nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ koni amɛtsu nii yɛ mli.

english: Pruning removes crowded or weak branches so sunlight and fresh air can reach all parts of the tree. This prevents diseases and forces the tree to spend its energy producing bigger pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ niji ni mli ewo wu loo ni bɛ hewalɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ hei fɛɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ helai anaa ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai krokomɛi baafata he.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing much less fruit than they used to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei momo lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow older than 20 to 25 years, their internal systems slow down and soil nutrients run low. Pruning them heavily or replanting with newer, higher-yielding varieties helps restore farm production.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tsei eye fe afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, amɛmli gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ baa shi, ni niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa. Nibii heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ni aaafolɔ waa loo ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha ŋmɔ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: A ripe pod changes color from green to bright yellow, or from dark red to orange. Harvesting at this exact stage ensures the seeds inside have developed the full sugars needed for good chocolate flavor.
ga: Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ. aloo kɛjɛ tsuru ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛyashi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa nɛɛ mli lɛ haa sugar fɛɛ ni he hiaa kɛha tsokolate ŋmɔlɔ kpakpa lɛ yɔɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli.

english: Covering wet cocoa beans with plantain leaves allows them to ferment. This natural heating process kills the seed inside, removes bitter flavors, and turns the beans the rich brown color buyers look for.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ plantain baai ha kookoo yibii ni efɔ lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli latsaa gbɛ nɛɛ gbeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ehaa kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli kwɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ.

english: How can I protect my crop farm from drying out during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi tsei aŋmɔ lɛ he koni ekagbi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil around the base of your crops with dry leaves or straw traps soil moisture and protects roots from severe heat, helping the plants survive long periods without rain.
ga: Mulching around Okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi awo tso lɛ shishi koni ekɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ebu shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy, humid conditions. Removing infected pods regularly and pruning branches to let in sunlight helps keep the trees dry and stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ daa, ni afoɔ tso lɛ mli koni hulu la aje kpo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni egbiɔ ni ehaa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do I see small caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni miiye mi-ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the central growing tip of young maize plants. Catching them early by checking your farm regularly and applying recommended biological or chemical controls protects your crop from severe yield loss.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni miida yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ nɔ daa ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, obaaye obua ni obu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ yibiiwoo ni baafite waa lɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips transmitting a virus. Controlling these insects early with appropriate sprays or reflective mulches prevents the virus from stunting the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni sa loo ŋmɔtɔ ni haa hulu kpɛɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ atsĩ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to grow strong leaves, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-decomposed manure early in the season will restore healthy green growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni baai lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ wo mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow big leaves and bushy stalks but fail to produce plenty of fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ baai wuji kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ewooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes plants to focus all their energy on leaf growth instead of flowering and fruiting. Balancing your fertilizer with phosphorus and potassium encourages flowering and healthy fruit development.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai lɛ adalɛ he nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium woɔ mli lɛ haa fɔfɔi ni mli wa kɛ yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko bɛ po lɛ?

english: Plantain plants fall over when nematodes or banana weevils damage their underground root system, weakening their grip in the soil. Planting clean, pest-free suckers and applying proper pest management keeps the roots strong enough to hold heavy bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii kpata shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ. ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baa shi Nibii ni he tse ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli lɛ adumɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ ni sa tsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu panicles ni tsii ahe nii.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil around them for too long due to poor drainage. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so the roots remain healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause tomato plants stress, preventing flowers from pollinating successfully and causing them to drop off. Providing light shade and consistent watering helps plants hold onto their flowers until fruit sets.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi haoɔ tomato tsei. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee pollination yɛ omanyeyeli mli ni amɛgbee shi. Susumɔ ni mli tse kɛ nu ni afɔɔ lɛ daa yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my yam vines turning yellow and dying early before the tubers are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ oya dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Early yellowing of yam leaves is often caused by yam anthracnose, a fungal disease favored by warm, humid weather. Staking vines high off the ground improves airflow and keeps leaves dry, protecting them from early dieback.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni ji anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni baa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Wein tsei ni akɛma shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ oya, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ mli egbiɔ. Tsi tsei anaa koni amɛkagboi oya

english: Why do my cowpea plants lose all their flower buds before they open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ fɔfɔii fɛɛ miifite dani ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Flower bud drop in cowpeas is usually caused by tiny insects called flower thrips that feed on young buds. Planting on time and spraying recommended insecticides at the start of flowering protects the buds so they can turn into pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ji mɛi ni kɛ fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tsina ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ fɔfɔi thrips ni yeɔ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be naa kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ ashwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmeii lɛ ahe koni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant is short on nitrogen. When the soil lacks enough food, the maize plant pulls nitrogen out of its older bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with huge leaves but give me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or grows in extremely rich soil, it puts almost all its energy into building big stems and green leaves instead of storing energy in roots to form tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmei yɔɔ nɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ tsei agboi kɛ baai eŋɔlii. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, akɛ hewalɛ toɔ shishifãi lɛ amli koni ekɛfee bulbs.

english: Why are my cabbage heads staying soft and open instead of forming hard, tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe lɛ? Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ nɔ́ ko nɛ wa nɛ e mi mi wa.

english: Cabbage heads fail to form tightly when the weather is too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients during the period when inner leaves start packing together.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ etswaaa shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni mligbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛbuaa amɛhe naa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their young pods before the pods get mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ shi dani ŋmeii lɛ daraa kwraa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed young pods—a process called cherelle wilt—if the tree gets stressed by drought, lacks adequate shade, or does not have enough nutrients to support all the pods to full size.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbii bibii lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ cherel ni shwieɔ shi. Kɛji hɔmɔ miigba tso lɛ naa Shade ni sa ni bɛ Aloo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ adara kɛyashɛ elɛɛmɔ he lɛ bɛ.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up and become small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites, aphids, or thrips feeding on the tender shoots, or by viral diseases spread into the plant by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mites, aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei amli lɛ amli

english: How can I tell if my tomato plants are getting too much water in the rainy season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-tomato tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Overwatered tomato plants will have leaves that yellow and look soft or wilted despite wet soil, flowers that drop off without setting fruit, and roots that turn brown and soggy instead of bright white.
ga: Tomato tsei ni awo amɛ nu fe nine lɛ baaná baai ni baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔŋ loo amɛfee ŋmɔŋ, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ po. Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii kɛ shishifãi ni tsɔɔ blɔfo ni efɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse najiaŋ.

english: Why are the flowers on my eggplant dropping off without producing any garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-eggplant lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfɔɔɔ bii yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Eggplant flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out completely during flowering, or when there are not enough insects like bees visiting the field to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Eggplant fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni baa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ faaa koni amɛbawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that stay near the surface. As the heavy bunch matures, the weight pulls the whole plant down—especially during strong winds—unless you support the main stem with a sturdy wooden prop.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ da kwraa lɛ Muji lɛ baagbala tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛba shi. Titri lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli Ja okɛ nɔ ko ni wa fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means their roots work with helpful bacteria in the soil to pull nitrogen from the air and turn it into natural plant food that neighboring maize crops can draw on to grow stronger.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsake lɛ amɛfee adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii ni ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii koni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch maximum sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves dry, healthy, and exposed to sun, which allows the plant to produce more energy and grow larger underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Staking haa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ, amɛnáa hewalɛ ni hulu la shɛɔ amɛnɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa hewalɛ babaoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs wuji shwereɔ.

english: Why do my corn leaves roll up tightly into thin tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense to trap moisture and reduce water loss through evaporation during the heat of the day. Once the temperature drops in the evening, the leaves usually unroll.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni baaha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do the yellow flowers on my pepper plants drop off without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress, lack of soil moisture, or inadequate nutrients. When stressed, the plant saves energy by dropping flowers rather than producing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei buɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛjieɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start growing green sprouts inside my dark storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi tsũ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers have an internal biological clock. After a few months of rest (dormancy), the yam naturally awakes and uses its stored water and food to shoot leaves so it can find soil and sunlight to grow again.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ wala mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa. Yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni akɛjɔɔ amɛhe (wɔɔ) sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ teɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛhaa baai lɛ ahe ŋmeii bɔni afee ni amɛna shikpɔŋ kɛ hulu la ni amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow in patches and curling up like a twisted hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ? Ni ebɔle ehe tamɔ nine ni etsɔ mli?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies or by using infected stem cuttings. The virus distorts leaf growth and stops the plant from making large roots.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ Virus lɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ shishifãi wuji.

english: What causes small caterpillars to hide inside the leaves of my young corn plants and eat holes through them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ mli?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms. Moths lay eggs on the leaves, and when the caterpillars hatch, they crawl into the leaf funnel where it is dark and moist to eat the soft plant tissue.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Amɛshwereɔ kɛboteɔ baai ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ amli koni amɛye tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants have big, hard lumps on their roots when I pull out dead ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii wuji ni wa yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni egboi lɛ?

english: The lumps on tomato roots are caused by root-knot nematodes, which are tiny microscopic worms in the soil. They attack the roots, causing swollen knots that block water and nutrients from reaching the leaves.
ga: Nodules ni yɔɔ tomato shishifãi anɔ lɛ jɛɔ shishifãi nematodes, ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli. Amɛtutuaa shishifãi lɛ, ni amɛhaa ŋmeii ni efuu ni tsiɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: How do groundnuts help make my soil better for planting maize next season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen gas from the air and stores it in small nodules on their roots. When the roots rot after harvest, they release natural fertilizer into the soil.
ga: Peanuts ji legume weku lɛ mlinyo ni heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings dying off when I clear all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under full, direct sunlight. Shade trees or companion crops like plantains protect young cocoa trees from heat and conserve soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei ni fata he, tamɔ plantains lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why should I plant my maize in straight lines instead of broadcasting the seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil space without competing with its neighbors. It also makes weeding, fertilizer application, and harvesting much faster and easier.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso ni yaa hiɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, kɛ nikpamɔ hu yaa oya ni efeɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my cassava right after the first rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe mi-cassava lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and lie hidden in the soil for years waiting for rain. Because weeds are wild plants adapted to poor soil, they absorb water faster and sprout quicker than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo ni amɛmɛɔ nugbɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Amɛheɔ nu oya ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods falling off the trees to the ground before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo bibii lɛ miigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛmiiba shikpɔŋ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods often drop prematurely due to a natural condition called cherelle wilt, which is triggered when the tree is stressed by excessive sun heat, lack of water, or sudden loss of overhead tree shade.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherelle wilting lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ fe nine, nu ni bɛ, loo tsei ni yɔɔ amɛyiteŋ lɛ ahe hulutsoo trukaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn dark brown and fall off the tree during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, unpruned farms with high humidity. Proper farm sanitation and clearing low branches help prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ ni afolɔɔɔ mli ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Okwaafoi amli hetsemɔ ni sa kɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ajiemɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: How can I prevent my cocoa pods from dropping to the ground before harvest time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shikpɔŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ aba?

english: You can protect your pods by maintaining balanced shade to reduce heat stress, applying proper fertilizer to nourish the tree, and regularly clearing weeds and fallen pods from the farm floor.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu o-pods lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ hulutsoo ni ja ni ooona koni hulutsoo he haomɔ aba shi lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa awo tso lɛ mli koni eha tso lɛ aya hiɛ. ni ajie jwɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni egbee shi lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if I cut down all the large shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cocoa tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mifolɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Removing all shade trees exposes cocoa to intense direct sunlight and heat, causing leaves to scorch, soil moisture to dry up fast, and young pods to fall off from heat shock.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shade lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ baa kookoo nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. shã baai lɛ Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni baa trukaa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them on newly cleared land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ hee ni ajie nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings lack strong root systems and cannot survive direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains first creates a protective umbrella that keeps them cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli wa, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ ni afee hulutsoo ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: How do permanent shade trees help my cocoa farm during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ harmattan be ni hɔmɔ baa lɛ mli?

english: Permanent shade trees shield cocoa trees from dry harmattan winds, lower the air temperature, and pull water from deep underground to maintain moisture in the farm's air.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ he. ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dɔlɛ baa shi ni ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa leaves turning yellow and dropping after I heavily cut back the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi beni mifo amɛ waa lɛ?

english: Excessive pruning causes severe shock to the cocoa tree by suddenly exposing previously shaded inner branches to harsh sun while reducing the leaves available to feed the tree.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ mli fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha kookoo tso lɛ he afee shoo waa, ni tsutsu lɛ, tsei niji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ baashɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he trukaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai ni abaanyɛ akɛye tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: When is the best time of year to prune branches off my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tso niji?

english: It is best to prune cocoa trees light-to-moderately just before the main rainy season so the tree can easily heal and grow new leaves without suffering dry heat stress.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ fioo kɛyashi fioo dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ atsa oya ni ekwɛ baai heei ni ekɛ hulutsoo be ni mli egbi lɛ he haomɔ akaŋmɛ etsui shi.

english: Why does my cocoa farm's soil dry out so quickly after I clear away the surrounding bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing the surrounding bush removes the natural canopy and leaf mulch that traps ground moisture, allowing sunlight and wind to evaporate water directly from the soil.
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ajiemɔ Enɛ baajie adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ha hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers fall off without ever growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when cocoa trees suffer from drought stress, intense heat, or a lack of midges (tiny beneficial insects) that require damp, shaded soil to breed and pollinate the flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ cacao tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ hɔmɔ, latsaa ni naa wa, loo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni bɛ lɛ mli. (koolooi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ) ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo koni amɛfɔ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi amli

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves lose water faster than their small roots can drink. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby creates living shade umbrellas that keep the soil moist and protect young leaves from burning.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Akɛni baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ anu lɛ hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni haaa baai bibii lɛ ashã.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam vines need support to climb so their leaves can spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible. Getting good sunlight helps the plant make food, which allows the underground tubers to grow bigger and heavier.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia yelikɛbuamɔ ni amɛkɛkwɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la kpakpa ni anáa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant does not get enough water. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting plants from intense heat stress helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crop turning yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is a major food the plant needs from the soil. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its dark green color and produce strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei taoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛ su ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil each season and allows specific pests to build up in the field. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts refills nutrients in the soil and breaks insect cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli yɛ be fɛɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do people cover the soil around pepper plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket that traps soil moisture and stops water from evaporating quickly. It also keeps the roots cool, prevents weeds from growing, and slowly breaks down into food for the plant.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni tsiɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in the middle leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Nɛgbɛ ji mi ŋmãa gbekɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ?

english: These holes are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding deep inside the central growing shoot of the plant. Checking fields early and applying appropriate controls or neem-based sprays stops them before they destroy the crop's main growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ hei ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mra ni akɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa loo neem spray atsu nii. Ekpaa hei nɛɛ dani amɛfiteɔ hei titri ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa yɛ lɛ.

english: Continuous rain creates cold, damp conditions where a microscopic organism causing Black Pod disease thrives and splashes between pods. Pruning extra branches lets wind and sunlight dry the trees out, reducing pod rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ kɛ fɛ̃i baa. Nibii bibii ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ daa ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe yɛ pod lɛ ateŋ. Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ mli lɛ baaha egbi kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la mli. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ haa pod rot lɛ baa shi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on young leaves. Controlling these insects early prevents them from distorting the foliage and spreading plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkatsɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni amɛkagbɛ tsei amli helai lɛ amɛshwã.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are mature enough to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifã ko da bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, signaled when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and shed. Digging around one sample plant to examine tuber size helps confirm readiness before harvesting the entire farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, ni no ji be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Tsei lɛ ahe nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ni atsa koni ana tuber lɛ dalɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ama hesaamɔ nɔ mi dani akpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do tree crops like cocoa keep bearing fruit for many years while crops like maize die after just one harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo woɔ yibii afii babaoo yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa gboiɔ yɛ kpamɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize is an annual crop that puts all its energy into producing seeds once and then dies. Tree crops like cocoa are perennials; they build strong trunks and deep root systems that allow them to live for decades and bear fruit every season.
ga: Abɛi ji tso ko ni yeɔ daa afi ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ dumɔwui shikome ni no sɛɛ lɛ egboɔ. Tsei tamɔ kookoo ji tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo. Amɛfeɔ tsei ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni haa amɛhiɔ shi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii daa be mli.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to strong sunlight and can easily dry out. Plantain trees grow very quickly and provide broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa, ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop is starving for food, particularly nitrogen, or that heavy rain has logged the soil with water, preventing the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmɔshi nii lɛ. titri lɛ nitrogen Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewoɔ nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they feel stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or insect damage. Dropping flowers is the plant's natural way of saving energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni ehi wala mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but have tiny roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, ni eyɛ baai babaoo, shi shishifãi fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or too much shade, it sends all its energy upward to build big stems and leaves instead of sending energy underground to develop thick, food-storing tubers.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei ná nitrogen babaoo loo shade babaoo Etsuɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛfee ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji. Mohu ɔ, e ngɔɔ he wami kɛ yaa zugba a sisi konɛ e kɛ pee tubers nɛ mi wa nɛ e ngɔ niye ní kɛ to.

english: Why do my crops grow bigger and stronger when I leave space between seeds instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ mishi gbɛ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough resources to grow well and yield heavily.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even if they are growing on the side of the field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ masɛi po?

english: Weeds steal water, nutrients, and sunlight that your crops need to grow. They also act as hiding places for insects and crop diseases that can spread across your farm.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara. Amɛtsuɔ nii hu akɛ he ni kooloi bibii kɛ tsei ahelai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ teɔ shi yɛ.

english: Why does planting different crops on the same piece of land every season help the soil stay healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Different crops feed on different soil nutrients and attract different pests. Rotating crops prevents the soil from being drained of specific nutrients and stops pests from multiplying in the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yeɔ niyenii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛgbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai srɔtoi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii komɛi, ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What crops can I plant to earn quick money while waiting for my tree crops like oil palm to mature?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu koni maná shika oya yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ mu tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Short-term crops like maize, cassava, or vegetables take only a few months to harvest. Planting them in the spaces between young oil palms gives you regular food and income while your main trees grow.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo aduawai heɔ nyɔji fioo pɛ dani akpaa. Kɛ́ odu amɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mu tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaha oná niyenii kɛ shika ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni otsei titrii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield less food when I plant the exact same crop on the same land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naaa niyenii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil over and over. It also allows crop-specific diseases and pests to build up in the ground, causing lower harvests over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. Ehaa helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ tsei anɔ lɛ hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains around them protects their tender leaves from burning and keeps the soil moist while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa bibii lɛ akashã, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that stay close to the topsoil. When the heavy fruit bunch grows, the plant becomes top-heavy, so strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of wet soil unless you support the stem with a wooden prop.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu agbo ko da Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Ejeɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ mlɛo Ja okɛ tso ko tsu nii ni okɛfi tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants filled with small holes and powdery droppings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by fall armyworms or stem borers feeding on the soft leaf tissues inside the plant canopy. Applying appropriate treatments early prevents the caterpillars from destroying the growing point of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji fall armyworms loo stem borers ni yeɔ tso lɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Kɛ akɛ tsofafeemɔ gbɛi ni sa tsu nii mra Ebaatsi ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkafite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize turn yellow from the tips downward even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ kɛmiiba shi lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tips usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which plants need to make green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ afee amɛbaai lɛ eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ, ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the ground when the farm stays too wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Excess water fills all the soil spaces, causing waterlogging which starves the roots of air and promotes rotting fungal diseases.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baayi shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nu shwieɔ shi, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines onto tall stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up off the damp soil so they get maximum sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground, while also preventing fungal foliage diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ bulbs lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji fungal leaf lɛ hu naa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as very high daytime temperatures, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like boron and phosphorus needed for fruit set.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛhao, tamɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ boron kɛ phosphorus ni he hiaa kɛha yibiiwoo ni bɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and turning thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on sap and spreading leaf curl viruses, or by severe heat stress during dry periods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tomato mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ baa curl hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ mli.

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have friendly bacteria in their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for crops planted afterward.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helai ni haa mɔ he feɔ naanyo yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni adu sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and stay thin if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛhe feɔ mlɛo kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Because weeds grow quickly, they steal these vital resources before your main crops can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya. No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ baashɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil that plants need to stay green, photosynthesize, and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. fotosintɛsis ni edara waa

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tight during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing too much water when the sun is very hot and the soil is dry.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite fe nine kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso ni shikpɔŋ lɛ miigbi.

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting when the heat is too extreme or when the soil doesn't have enough balanced water and nutrients to support fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni ja ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their leaves when the Harmattan wind starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ahe baai babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛ́ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their leaves during the dry Harmattan season as a survival trick to preserve moisture when water in the soil becomes scarce.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛaatsɔ nɔ amɛhi shi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu faaa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when we get too much heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Excess rain makes the soil waterlogged, which prevents air from reaching the roots, causing the cassava tubers to drown and rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why does my maize crop grow much faster if I plant right after the first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ daa oya waa kɛji midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The season's first rain triggers a natural chemical reaction in dry soil that releases a surge of stored nitrogen, giving young seeds an extra boost of growth food.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa tsofai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ekome. Ebaajie nitrogen ni ato lɛ babaoo kpo. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii lɛ naa niyenii kroko ni haa amɛdaraa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun; plantains grow quickly and have big leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing necessary shade and soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines produce big green leaves but leave me with small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wain tso ni ji sweet potato lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen manure but lacks potassium, the yam plant uses all its energy to grow top leaves instead of storing food in the tuber below.
ga: Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ. Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eŋwɛi baai lɛ amli moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baatoɔ shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with deep root systems naturally adapted to compete aggressively for water and nutrients, unlike domesticated crops which need extra care.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛkɛ amɛhe awo nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Esoro amɛ yɛ shia tsei ni biɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my garden egg fruits get soft black spots on the bottom while still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplants ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lolo lɛ?

english: Soft black spots on garden eggs are usually caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil due to dry weather or irregular watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ shihilɛ ni mli egbi loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient that keeps plants green and helps them grow. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer to the soil helps restore their green color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly exhausts specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Alternating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility by adding nitrogen naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi kɛ tsei ahe helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa tamɔ tsina loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa cool and preserving soil moisture during their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with long wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji afi mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam plants rely on their leaves to capture sunlight and make food for the underground tuber. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes allows the leaves to get maximum sunlight and airflow, resulting in larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baafee wuji.

english: Why did my crop seeds fail to come up after I buried them deep in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibii dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds contain a limited amount of stored energy to push their early shoots above the ground. If planted too deep, the shoot runs out of energy and dies before reaching the surface sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko ni ato ni amɛkɛtsiɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ baaho ni amɛbaagboi dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, mites, or whiteflies that feed on the plant's sap and spread viruses. Spraying the leaves with organic neem oil or mild soap solution can keep these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids, mites loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem fɔ loo samla ni mli jɔ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akabote mli.

english: Why do weeds choke and destroy my young crops so quickly if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ oya kɛji mijieee amɛ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast-growing wild plants that aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before young crops can establish strong roots. Clearing weeds early gives young crops uninterrupted access to essential resources.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli dani tsei bibii baanyɛ ana shishifãi ni wa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ naa nibii ni he hiaa lɛ daa.

english: Why are the bottom tips of my tomatoes turning black and rotting before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist allows the roots to steadily absorb calcium and protect the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛŋɔɔ calcium, ni ebuɔ aduawai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot inside the soil during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in heavy soil without draining. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the roots safe from rotting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily before the bunches are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and become top-heavy when carrying full fruit bunches. Supporting the main stem with a strong, branched wooden prop helps hold the plant upright against heavy wind and rain.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛtsii kɛji aduawai lɛ eyi obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa kɛ tsei niji fiɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he.

english: When lower leaves turn yellow starting from the tip down the middle, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen. The maize plant pulls nitrogen from its older leaves to feed new growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure restores green growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛtee teŋgbɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller every year when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop loves from the soil while allowing crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts gives the soil a chance to rest and rebuild nutrients naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ebaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei sumɔɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kome mli. kɛ tsei amli tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa. Akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa hegbɛ ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ ehewalɛ nibii lɛ emaa shi ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves burn and dry up when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni tsei wuji bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, intense sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a protective umbrella that keeps the air humid and prevents solar burning.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa, ni ebaatsi hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why are my green tomato leaves curling up tightly and the plants stopping their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai eŋɔli lɛ ebɔle ehe shi shiŋŋ ni tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is typically caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies early with suitable sprays prevents the virus from taking over your tomato garden.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Early Whitefly Nɔkwɛmɔ Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ oye obua ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akaye o-tomato abɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the branch during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, wet conditions. Pruning low branches and removing infected pods helps sunshine and airflow reach the tree, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ ayashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. ni akpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ

english: Why is a weed with pink flowers making my maize dry up even when I give it water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli ni ji pinki lɛ haa mi-ŋmã lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo mli po lɛ?

english: That weed is likely Striga (witchweed). It is a parasite that attaches its roots to your maize underground, stealing nutrients and water directly from the crop before the maize can use them.
ga: Ekolɛ jwɛi lɛ ji Striga (abɛi jwɛi). Eji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpãa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmãa he. Ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ dani ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ ekɛtsu nii.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long without draining. Heavy, trapped water suffocates the roots, allowing fungal rots in the soil to break down the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ efooo Nu ni etsi ehe waa lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ fite yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and stake my yam vines high up on sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni madu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to capture maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to manufacture food, which is then sent downward to build large, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la haa baai lɛ woɔ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, atsuɔ lɛ kɛyaa shi koni efee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: Why are flowers dropping off my pepper plants without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Extreme heat during hot afternoons causes heat stress, forcing pepper plants to drop blossoms to save energy. Watering early in the morning or providing slight shade helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa shwane mli lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Enɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Nu ni oooha tso lɛ leebi loo ni oooha lɛ hulutsoo fioo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when strong winds blow during rainstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that lose their grip in soft, overly soaked soil. If tiny worms called nematodes damage their roots, the plant loses its anchor completely and falls in light wind.
ga: Plantain lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbala shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ tsɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ fite shishifãi lɛ, Tso lɛ baafite eshishifã lɛ kwraa ni ebaagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko ba.

english: How long after planting my cocoa trees can I expect them to start giving me pods?
ga: Beni adu kookoo sɛɛ lɛ Be enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ kookoo tso lɛ baaje ŋmɔtɔ shishi?

english: Most traditional cocoa trees start bearing pods around three to five years after planting, while improved hybrid varieties can start producing fruit in about two to three years if properly cared for.
ga: Cacao tsei ni afɔɔ feemɔ yɛ blema beaŋ lɛ ateŋ babaoo jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii aaafee afii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ sɛɛ beni adu amɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei sɔrɔtoi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ aaafee afii enyɔ loo etɛ mli kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn brown and dry up when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle full sunlight. Without shade from fast-growing companion crops like plantains, the sun scorches their leaves and slows down their overall growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko bɛ kɛjɛ nanemɛi tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ lɛ, Hulu lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa amɛdalɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know how far apart I should space my maize seeds when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ makɛ mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ato he kɛji midu?

english: Proper spacing, usually about 75 centimeters between rows and 25 to 30 centimeters between seeds, ensures that each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to grow strong and yield large cobs.
ga: jɛkɛmɔ ni sa Bei pii lɛ, enɛ feɔ sɛntimitai 75 yɛ ŋmeii ateŋ kɛ sɛntimitai 25 kɛyashi 30 yɛ dumɔwui ateŋ, ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods as a natural survival mechanism to reduce water loss. The roots stay healthy underground, and the plant will grow fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ shi. Shishifãi lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ni tsei lɛ baakwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Does a cocoa farm keep producing more cocoa every year as the trees grow older?
ga: Ani kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ baawo kookoo babaoo daa afi be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees increase their production as they mature over their first 10 to 15 years, reach a peak production period, and eventually slowly decline in yield as the trees get much older.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ haa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ beni amɛdaraa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 10 kɛyashi 15 lɛ mli lɛ, ni amɛshɛɔ yibiiwoo ni fe fɛɛ he. ni naagbee lɛ, nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi fiofio be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids, mites, or thrips, or by viral infections spread by these insects, which weaken the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites loo thrips, loo helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ

english: Pruning removes dead or diseased wood, improves airflow through the canopy, lets sunlight reach the branches, and prevents fungal diseases like black pod from spreading.
ga: Tsoi ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ Eha hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ahe. ni etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: How can I check if the soil on my farm is fertile enough for planting without expensive testing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa kɛha okwaayeli ni kaa ni jara wa akafee lɛ?

english: You can check soil fertility by looking at its color, texture, and natural life. Dark, crumbly soil that holds moisture well and has earthworms present is generally fertile and rich in organic matter.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii ahaa kɛtsɔ esu, bɔ ni eyɔɔ, kɛ adebɔɔ mli wala ni oookwɛ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli ewo muji ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɔɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, amɛwoɔ nii ni amɛmli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo.

english: How exactly do weeds harm my crops if they are just growing in the same soil?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Weeds steal vital nutrients, water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops. When weeds take over, your main crops become weak and produce much lower yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni he hiaa, nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni jwɛi lɛ ye nɔ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebaawo yibii ni baa shi kwraa.

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred for high yield, disease resistance, and uniform growth. Saved seeds from harvested hybrid crops lose those strong traits and usually result in a much smaller harvest.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛha yibii babaoo, helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ kɛ dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa. Dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui lɛ ni bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Young cocoa trees get burned easily under full sun. They need shade crops like plantains planted beside them to shield them from high heat and keep the soil moist until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa shɛ amɛnɔ. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Bɔni afee ni akafee dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop down in the afternoon heat even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: Plants fold or droop their leaves during hot afternoons to protect themselves from losing too much water through heat. Covering the soil with dried leaves or mulch helps keep the root zone cool.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo ni jɛɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ akafite amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my maize leaves have small ragged holes in them when they are just starting to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani eyɛ jɛmɛ beni amɛje shishi amɛmiikwɛ̃ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes are a sign of fall armyworm caterpillars feeding on tender young leaves. Spraying safe protective controls early in the morning before the pests hide deep in the plant saves the yield.
ga: Buji ni etse lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ yeɔ nii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni tsiɔ hela naa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ shwie nɔ leebi dani tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ kɛ amɛhe tee tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni yibiiwoo lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot during the rainy season before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, which spreads through water drops when the air around the tree stays too wet. Pruning extra branches lets air flow through to dry off the pods quickly.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nu mli nu mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Tso lɛ mli efɔ tsɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni egbi ŋmeii lɛ oya.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black spots at the bottom before commercial buyers come to pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔi diji yɔɔ dani jarayeli he nihɔɔlɔ ko baa koni ebajie lɛ?

english: Black spots at the bottom of tomatoes usually happen when the soil lacks calcium or water supply is uneven. Maintaining regular watering prevents this damage so the fruit stays attractive for market buyers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa kɛji calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Nu ni oooha lɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni akafite nɛkɛ nii nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, aduawai lɛ yaa nɔ ehaa mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ sumɔɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow while the top ones stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom mean the crop is lacking nitrogen food in the soil. The plant moves the remaining food from its old leaves up to keep the young green leaves alive.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with bushy leaves but give me tiny tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai bibii shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen, it puts all its energy into growing big stems and green leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji kɛ baai eŋɔlii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpea or beans in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This acts like natural food that feeds the maize crop growing next to it.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off the plant before making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani mifee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or sudden dry spells. Keeping the soil constantly moist helps the plant keep its flowers to form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɔ́ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and weak even when I planted good seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ kuku ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kpakpai moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the resources they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when exposed to direct sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the soil before their roots grow deep enough to absorb sufficient water.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani amɛshishifãi lɛ aya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I cut away the extra shoots growing at the base of my main plantain trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, take water and food away from the main plantain tree. Removing them leaves only one or two strong shoots, ensuring the main plant produces larger, healthier bunches.
ga: Tsoi loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishifã kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi, ni no baaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmei ni da ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I pick the right cassava stem to cut for planting my new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni sa ni esa akɛ mafo koni mikɛdu yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli?

english: Choose healthy, mature stems from the middle section of the plant that are firm and have clear buds, as soft top stems rot easily and very old bottom stems take too long to sprout.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni wa ni fɔfɔii ni mli tse yɔɔ mli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋwɛi tsei bibii lɛ fiteɔ oya, ni shishigbɛ tsei ni egbɔ waa lɛ heɔ be babaoo tsɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tuber growing under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground, preventing rot and maximizing sun exposure.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa ni ehaa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth, often washed away by heavy rains or exhausted soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ aya hiɛ waa Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛ.

english: What is causing tiny caterpillars to eat holes in the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai amli buji ni ayeɔ

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which feed inside the funnel of young maize. Catching them early and applying recommended treatments like neem extract helps save the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ niyenii yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra ni okɛ tsofafeemɔ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii tamɔ neem mli nu lɛ atsu nii. Ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures become extremely hot or when water levels jump suddenly from very dry to very wet, which causes stress to the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ mli shwie shi trukaa kɛjɛ he ni egbi waa kɛtee he ni edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. ni kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ lɛ

english: Why should I clear small weeds around my crops even when they don't look dangerous?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi bibii lɛ? ebɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe Kɛji akɛ jwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he po,.

english: Even small weeds absorb water and soil nutrients faster than young crops can, stealing the food your plants need to build strong stems and roots.
ga: Jwɛi bibii po gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni tsei bibii baanyɛ afee. Ejuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: When is the best time to spread fertilizer on my farm during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp but not during a heavy downpour, so the plant roots can absorb the food immediately rather than having the rain wash it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ niyenii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni nugbɔ baaho niyenii lɛ kɛya.

english: Planting maize continuously depletes the same nutrients year after year and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with legumes like groundnuts helps restore soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ baa shi daa afi. ni ebaanyɛ eha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and scorch easily in full, direct sunlight. Keeping taller shade crops like plantains or shade trees protects the young cocoa from heat and maintains soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu lɛ naa.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrients for growth. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its green color and yield healthy corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.
