english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting flowering herbs nearby to attract insects helps the fruit set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ tsofai ni woɔ fɔfɔi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Bɔni afee ni agbala kooloi bibii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewo yibii.

english: If I plant my cassava stems very close together, will I get a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he waa Ani mawo yibii babaoo?

english: Planting cassava too close causes the plants to fight for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and very small tubers. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to build large, healthy roots.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ yitsei bibii waa baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi wuji ni wa baa.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or viruses they transmit. Sprays made from neem oil or safe insecticides can control these insects before they damage the crop.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nibii ni akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofai krokomɛi ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fee lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Can I plant beans together with my maize on the same land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very helpful. Beans capture nitrogen from the air and naturally feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow better while maximizing your land's output.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ hu yaa hiɛ babaoo yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains even when there is no wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems. When heavy rains make the soil soft and waterlogged, the ground loses its grip on the roots, causing the heavy plantain tree to easily tip over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, sũ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu shwieɔ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbala amɛhe dɔŋŋ. Ehaa dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya.

english: How do I know when my underground yams are mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are ready to harvest when the leaves and vines above ground naturally turn yellow and dry up, showing that the plant has finished storing energy into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Should I cut off the extra shoots growing near the ground on my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ mi-koko tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, those side shoots (called chupons or water sprouts) steal water and food away from the main trunk and cocoa pods. Pruning them helps the tree focus its energy on producing healthy pods.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nakai sɛɛ ŋmeii (ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons loo nu mli dumɔwui) lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ amli. Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my stored maize seeds get tiny holes in them and fail to grow when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ekwɛɛɛ kɛji midu?

english: Tiny holes in stored seeds are caused by weevils that eat the seed from the inside out. Drying the seeds thoroughly and storing them in sealed, airtight containers or using safe seed treatment powders protects them from pest damage.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kpo lɛ amli. Gbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛto nɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli, ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli. Aloo okɛ powda ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsaa dumɔwui lɛ atsu nii ni okɛbu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: How do I know if my land is good enough for growing maize before I spend money on seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa dani mafite shika yɛ dumɔwui ahe?

english: Testing a small trial patch or getting extension officers to test your soil shows you whether the ground has enough nutrients and water retention, so you do not waste money planting a large farm in poor soil.
ga: Kaa tsɔnei bibii ni akaa Aloo ha extension nitsulɔ ko aka oshikpɔŋ lɛ ekwɛ. Ebaatsɔɔ bo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni ofite shika yɛ ŋmɔji wuji ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I plant my crops in straight rows instead of spreading seeds randomly across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli trukaa lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows gives every crop enough room to catch sunlight and draw nutrients from the soil without competing with neighboring plants, leading to healthier crops and a bigger harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa babaoo baa.

english: Why do my corn leaves turn yellow and look weak early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the corn plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key soil nutrient plants need to grow green and strong; applying fertilizer early fixes this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ okɛ fɔ wo mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ he.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves curl up and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants curl their leaves in extreme heat to protect themselves and save water from evaporating, which is a natural signal that they need shade or watering early in the morning.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo loo nu leebi.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller every year when I keep planting cassava on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot every year drains specific soil nutrients and attracts pests; rotating with legumes like groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsake shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Are packaged seeds from the agriculture office really better than the seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli kɛjɛɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Packaged modern seeds are specifically bred to resist local crop diseases, grow faster, and produce higher yields than seeds saved from previous harvests.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ kotokui amli lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsei ahe helai. amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni aŋmala ashwie shi kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off healthy-looking extra branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning extra branches helps the plant direct all its food and water into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes instead of wasting energy on excess leaves.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ eniyenii kɛ enu lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there is plenty of rain for all of them?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ babaoo nɛ kɛha amɛ fɛɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital soil nutrients, sunlight, and root space that your crops need, which reduces crop strength and overall yield even when rain is abundant.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ shishifãi ni he hiaa otsei lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa po.

english: Why are there small holes appearing on my cabbage leaves, and how does that hurt the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ anɔ Ni te enɛ fiteɔ tsei ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Holes mean insects are eating the leaves, which act as the plant's food factories; without full leaves, the plant cannot produce enough energy to form a big, firm cabbage head.
ga: Buji tsɔɔ kooloi ni yeɔ baai ni tsuɔ nii akɛ tso lɛ niyenii nitsumɔhe. Kɛji baa ni eyi obɔ bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ajie hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ cabbage yitsei wuji ni mli wa.

english: Yellow leaves on cassava usually mean the soil lacks nutrients like nitrogen or the plants are being attacked by sap-sucking pests like mealybugs. Adding compost or well-rotted manure to the soil helps keep leaves green and supports root development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ ŋmeii miitutua tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: How do I stop tiny worms from eating holes in my maize leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai amli bu lɛ anaa?

english: These worms are likely fall armyworms that hide in the central whorl of young maize plants. Inspecting fields early and applying recommended neem-based or approved chemical insecticides directly into the funnel of the plant can control them.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni afolɔ amɛhe ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛ neem fee loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ agbɛi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ enɛɛmɛi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewo pepper yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat, prolonged dry spells, or a shortage of plant nutrients. Mulching around the stem to keep soil cool and maintaining steady watering helps the plants hold flowers and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ tsei amli lɛ ni bɛ Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ Stems lɛ he koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni aná nu daa lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: What causes my garden eggs to stay small and taste bitter instead of big and sweet?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee agboi ni ŋɔɔ?

english: Bitter and small garden eggs usually result from water stress during fruiting or nutrient-poor soil. Ensuring the crop receives regular moisture and organic compost gives you larger, milder fruits for cooking.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, abɔɔ mli ŋmeii bibii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni jɛɔ nu mli haomɔ mli yɛ yibiiwoo be mli loo sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ mli baa. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni tsei lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛná aduawai wuji ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛhooɔ nii.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot or start sprouting quickly after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ loo ejeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ oya beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if bruised during harvest or stored in warm, poorly ventilated spaces. Storing undamaged yams in a cool, shaded, elevated barn with good air movement keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ sweet potatoes ni efiteee lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli. Ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I protect my tomato crop from dying during heavy rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Excess rain causes waterlogging and fungal diseases like blight on tomato leaves. Planting tomatoes on raised soil beds allows water to drain away while spacing plants apart improves airflow to dry leaves quickly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ kɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tomato baa mli tsɛŋemɔ baa. Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Be ni tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ lɛ, amɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni egbiɔ baai lɛ oya.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas in the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that capture nitrogen gas from the air and release it into the soil. This natural process fertilizes the surrounding soil, helping your maize grow stronger while naturally smothering weeds.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ehiɛ wa yɛ be mli ni ojieɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow tall and weak and fall over when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko tswa lɛ?

english: Maize grows tall and thin when seeds are planted too close together, forcing plants to stretch competing for sunlight. Planting seeds with proper spacing builds thicker, stronger stems and sturdy root systems.
ga: Abɛi lɛ daa ni efeɔ mlɛo kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ akpã amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛhe wa, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my tomatoes turning black and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot and happens when plants cannot absorb enough calcium, usually because soil moisture fluctuates too much. Consistent watering keeps the calcium moving smoothly into growing fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot ni ebaa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni calcium lɛ yaa tso lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant for next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their strength and produce lower yields in the next generation. It is best to purchase fresh certified hybrid seeds each planting season or use open-pollinated varieties if you want to save seed.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite hewalɛ ni amɛbaawo yibii ni baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Aloo okɛ ŋmeii ni agbele naa lɛ atsu nii kɛji oosumɔ ni okɛ odumɔwui lɛ ato.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and woody even after leaving them in the ground for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ po lɛ?

english: Cassava needs loose, well-draining soil and plenty of sunlight to build starch; if the soil is too hard or compacted, the roots cannot expand, causing the plant to use its energy on leaves instead of thick tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia Cassava. Ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛbaafee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Ehaa tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ bulbs ni mli tse najiaŋ.

english: How can I tell if my land is suitable for growing cassava without using expensive equipment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmãa ni akɛ nibii ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: You can test the soil by squeezing a damp handful; if it crumbles easily rather than sticking together like hard clay, water will drain well and allow cassava roots to grow large without rotting.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka shikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni okɛbaashɛje mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji efo mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ he tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Nu lɛ baaho jogbaŋŋ. ni oha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛfiteee

english: Why does cassava start turning dark blue or black inside just two days after I dig it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mifo lɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ bɔi bluu loo ediŋŋ feemɔ?

english: Once cassava is harvested, exposure to air triggers a natural chemical reaction inside the root that causes rapid discoloration and spoilage within 48 to 72 hours, which is why it must be consumed, processed, or sold quickly.
ga: Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei Kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni yɔɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ feɔ ekome. Enɛ haa ehiɛ su tsakeɔ oya ni efiteɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli, no hewɔ ni esa akɛ aye, atsu he nii, loo ahɔ̃ɔ oya lɛ.

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense mechanism where the plant reduces its leaf surface exposed to the hot sun to stop water from escaping and conserve moisture during heat stress.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei haa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baa shi koni nu akaje mli ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my plants start flowering early when the rains stop unexpectedly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa lɛ?

english: When crops experience drought stress, they sense survival danger and quickly produce flowers and seeds early to reproduce before the plant dies from lack of water.
ga: Kɛ tsei kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ kpe lɛ Amɛnuɔ oshara ko he yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui oya koni amɛkɛfɔ dani tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my crops turning yellow while the top leaves are still bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: When the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, the plant steals nutrients from its older bottom leaves and sends them up to nourish the younger, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ lɛ, tsei juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛtsuɔ koni amɛyaha baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava stems curling up and growing sticky during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like mealybugs that multiply in dry weather, draining energy from the shoot tips and causing leaf distortion.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ mealybugs, ni fɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Ejieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ naagbee. ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Is it better to plant cassava stem cuttings standing upright, at an angle, or buried flat in the ground?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ shi shiŋŋ, yɛ koŋ nɔ, loo afu lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting stems at a slant or upright encourages roots to grow deeper where moisture stays longer, while burying them flat produces shallow roots that spread out but can easily dry out during hot periods.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ tso lɛ yɛ koŋ loo he ko ni ja lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ. he ni hulutsoo be lɛ baahi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni afuɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaha shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shi ebaanyɛ egbi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Will planting cassava and maize together on the same piece of land cause them to fight for nutrients?
ga: Ani ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baatswa niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ?

english: Maize and cassava can share land well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within three to four months, leaving the field open just as the cassava begins its main growth stage to form large roots.
ga: Abele kɛ ŋmei baanyɛ aja shikpɔŋ jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmei daa oya ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ he ni ashiɔ lɛ ni agbeleɔ naa yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ jeɔ edalɛ fã titri lɛ shishi koni ekɛfee shishifãi wuji lɛ nɔ.

english: I bought an improved high-yielding seed variety, but the crops are weak and producing low yields. Why is this happening?
ga: Mihe tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ dumɔwui. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lolo ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Mɛni he je nɛ e baa jã a?

english: High-yielding crop varieties need more food and care than local seeds. If you plant improved seeds without giving them enough fertilizer, proper spacing, and good weed control, they cannot reach their high yield potential and may perform even worse than local seeds.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ biɔ niyenii kɛ kwɛmɔ babaoo fe maŋbii dumɔwui. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa haaa lɛ, Ha he ni sa ni okwɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ Nakai dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii babaoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ po fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two different parent plants to produce maximum yield in the first generation only. If you save and plant those seeds next season, the crop loses its power, resulting in uneven growth and very poor harvests.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ to ni odu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baafite hewalɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni ehiii kwraa baa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop all their young flowers before they turn into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miishwie amɛfɔfɔi bibii lɛ fɛɛ dani amɛbatsɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme sun heat, lack of shade, or dry soil. Dropping flowers is the tree's natural defense mechanism to conserve water and energy so it does not die.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hulu la ni fa babaoo, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbuɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ he ni ekɛtsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekagbo.

english: Why do my cowpea crops produce many lush green leaves but very few pods when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ waa lɛ?

english: When cowpea plants receive excess water and rich soil nitrogen, they put all their energy into growing foliage and stems. The plant assumes it is in an abundant environment and delays flowering until it feels threatened by drier weather.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsina tsei lɛ ná nu kɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsina hu kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ahe nii. Abuɔ tsei akɛ amɛyɛ he ko ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ ni amɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ miiwo amɛhe gbeyei.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling up and turning tiny during the warm season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ bibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips that attack plants in warm weather. As they feed on the leaves, they spread viruses that disrupt normal growth, making the leaves twist and stop fruit development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni tutuaa tsei yɛ hulutsoo be mli be mli ni eyeɔ baai Egbɛɔ helai ni tsiɔ amɛdalɛ ni sa lɛ naa lɛ eshwaa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ tsɔɔ ni ekpaa aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to make food and stay green. Heavy rains can also wash this nutrient deep into the soil where young roots cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ amɛ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow bent and short instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee kuku moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers expand downward through the path of least resistance. If the soil underground is hard, compact, or stony, the growing tuber bends around the obstacle instead of growing straight and deep.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã gbɛ ni shitee-kɛ-woo fioo pɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi yɔɔ mli lɛ, ŋmeii ni miida lɛ baabɔle gbɛtsii nii lɛ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛmli kwɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped around them in poorly drained soil. Cassava roots need oxygen to breathe, and waterlogged soil suffocates the roots while creating a perfect home for rot-causing fungi.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bote shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni amɛmu. Ni shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ feɔ shia ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does leaving weeds in my farm for a few extra weeks really reduce how much crop harvest I get at the end?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi krokomɛi lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ minitsumɔ lɛ naagbee lɛ nɔ aba shi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, because weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops during their most critical growing phase. Delaying weeding causes permanent damage to the crop's development that extra work later cannot fix.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ fiteɔ daa. ni sɛɛ mli lɛ, nitsumɔ kroko ni fata he lɛ nyɛŋ asaa.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow lots of bushy branches but yield small, poor-quality tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jwɛi babaoo shi ewoɔ tomato bibii ni ehiii kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants naturally produce extra side branches called suckers that steal food from the main stalk. If you do not prune these extra branches, the plant wastes its energy growing leaves instead of pumping nutrients into big fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei feɔ niji krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots koni amɛkɛju niyenii kɛjɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Kɛji ofolɔɔɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine nɛɛ ahe lɛ, Tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ebaai ni miida lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛya aduawai wuji lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. Large shade trees protect young cocoa leaves from scorching heat and retain soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to canopy themselves.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta.

english: When too many shoots (suckers) grow around the main plantain stem, they steal water and food from it. Removing extra shoots leaves only the strongest ones, ensuring the main plant produces big, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ plantain tso wulu lɛ he lɛ Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ nakai tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ashiɔ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava roots become soft and watery if I leave them in the ground after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu ni mli jɔ lɛ? Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ sɛɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When heavy rains begin, the cassava plant uses the starch stored in its roots to grow new leaves and branches. This process drains the food stored in the tuber, making the root watery and light.
ga: Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ato yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ niji heei. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ haa niyenii ni ato yɛ yitso lɛ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli nu ni amɛhe waaa

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to manufacture food for growing big tubers. Lifting the leaves off the ground on stakes catches more sunlight and prevents diseases that spread from damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ. Kɛ́ owó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná hulu la babaoo, ni ebaatsi helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ anaa.

english: Does it matter whether I insert my cassava stem cuttings slanted or straight into the soil?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni adu ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava stems at an angle (about 45 degrees) makes harvesting easier because the roots grow closer to the soil surface, whereas planting them straight down forces the tubers deep into the hard ground.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei yɛ koŋ nɔ (aaafee digrii 45) lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ feɔ mlɛo ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ daa ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. be mli ni aduɔ shi tɛ̃ɛ Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ abote shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate that your soil is running low on nitrogen. The maize plant naturally moves whatever nitrogen it has left from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the young leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does swamp rice grow well in flooded water, but my upland maize crop rots if water stays on the field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔŋ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu afua mli lɛ? Shi ani mi-ŋma lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo?

english: Swamp rice varieties have special hollow channels in their stems that carry oxygen down to their roots underwater, while maize roots do not have this feature and drown when covered by standing water.
ga: Swamp ŋmãa henɔi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Shi ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ bɛ su nɛɛ, ni kɛ́ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ ha amɛhe lɛ, amɛbaagboi.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into small tomatoes during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato bibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: High afternoon heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing pollination. When a flower fails to get pollinated, the plant sheds it to conserve energy.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Tsi pollination naa Kɛji fɔfɔii lɛ bɛ pollination Tsei jieɔ lɛ kpo koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually a sign of tiny pests like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from under the leaves, or a virus spread by whiteflies feeding on the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ he okadi. loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yeɔ tsei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell us to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ dani wɔdu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer, making the soil richer for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are seed yams so expensive to buy when it is time for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ jara wa waa kɛ́ be shɛ ni esa akɛ adu amɛ lɛ?

english: Seed yams are costly because farmers have to save part of their edible harvest to use as seeds instead of selling it, which reduces the supply available in the market right when everyone wants to plant.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ jara wa ejaakɛ esa akɛ okwaafoi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ayeɔ lɛ fã ko ato koni amɛkɛtsu nii akɛ dumɔwui moŋ fe ni amɛaahɔ̃ɔ. Enɛ baaha nibii ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ aba shi beni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ miisumɔ ni edu nii lɛ.

english: Can I cut up regular market yams that I buy for food and use them as seeds for planting?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni miheɔ daa kɛha niyenii lɛ ni mikɛtsu nii akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛduɔ nii?

english: Yes, you can cut clean, healthy eating yams into small pieces called setts to plant, but you must let the cut surfaces dry out in the shade or dust them with wood ash to prevent rot in the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli bibii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ Setts lɛ koni okɛdu, shi esa akɛ oha he ni ofo lɛ lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo okɛ tso sũ afɔ nɔ koni ekafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: How can I save my own seed yams from this year's harvest so I do not have to spend money buying them next season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ohere bo diɛŋtsɛ o-sweet potato kɛjɛ afi nɛɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli? Bɔni afee ni ehe ehiaaa ni mafite shika kɛhe sweet potatoes yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: You can save seed yams by setting aside healthy, disease-free small tubers at harvest, or by harvesting early (milking the yam) to allow the vine to produce smaller seed tubers before the plant dries up.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ sweet potatoes ni dumɔwui ewo mli lɛ ato he kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni oookpa lɛ nɔ. ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo kɛtsɔ kpamɔɔ mra nɔ (Milk the sweet potatoes) koni wain tsei lɛ awo dumɔwui ayitsei bibii dani tso lɛ agbi.

english: Why do yams need big soil mounds instead of being planted in flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ŋmeii akwɛ̃ yɛ gɔji wuji amli moŋ fe ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams grow downward into the earth, so loose and raised soil mounds allow the tuber to expand freely without pushing against hard ground, while also protecting the roots from waterlogging.
ga: Atomɔ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, gɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewó nɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ oya ni amɛtsiii amɛhe kɛyaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe hu koni nu akabote mli.

english: Why do yam vines need to climb up wooden stakes or trees to produce a good harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni sweet potato wain tsei akwɔ tsei loo tsei anɔ koni amɛwo ŋmaa kpakpa lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb to expose their leaves to direct sunlight, which allows the plant to produce food through photosynthesis and send that energy down into the ground to grow a large tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei feɔ niyenii kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. ni ekɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛfee tsɔnei wuji

english: Why do my planted seed yams sometimes rot in the ground before they even sprout leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui ni midu lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛwoɔ baai lɛ?

english: Seed yams usually rot when the soil is too wet and poorly drained, or when cut seed pieces are planted fresh without letting the cut sides heal and seal against soil bacteria.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fɔɔ fitemɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni nu shwieee mli jogbaŋŋ. Aloo kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni afo lɛ ehee ni ahaaa fãi ni afo lɛ lɛ atsa ni atsĩ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting and drying out around November?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ ni egbiɔ yɛ November aaafee lɛ?

english: Around November, the dry season begins and temperatures rise, which naturally signals the dormant yam tuber to break its sleep and use its stored water and nutrients to grow sprouts.
ga: Aaafee November mli lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eje shishi ni hulutsoo be lɛ miiya hiɛ. Enɛ feɔ sweet potato ni ewɔ lɛ okadi yɛ adebɔɔ naa akɛ etsui anyɔ emli ni ekɛ ehe ajɔɔ ehe. ni okɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni ebua naa lɛ atsu nii ni okɛdu dumɔwui.

english: When is the best time of the year in Ghana to start preparing my land for planting yams?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana ni esa akɛ aje shikpɔŋ he saamɔ shishi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Land preparation usually begins in the late dry season between November and February so that mounds are ready to catch the very first rains around March or April.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ jeɔ shishi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ naagbee gbɛ, yɛ November kɛ February teŋ. Koni afee ni gɔŋ lɛ afee klalo koni enine ashɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ March loo April aaafee.

english: How many big yams can I expect to harvest from just one seed yam planted?
ga: Sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii agboi enyiɛ manyɛ maná kɛtsɔ dumɔwu kome pɛ ni madu lɛ nɔ?

english: In most traditional yam varieties, one seed yam piece grows into one main large tuber per stand, though proper care and soil fertility can make that single tuber grow very heavy.
ga: Yɛ kusum mli ŋmeii srɔtoi babaoo mli lɛ, ŋmeii dumɔwu kome baakwɛ̃ ni etsɔ ŋmeii agbo kome yɛ shidaamɔ fɛɛ shidaamɔ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwereɔ lɛ baaha bulbs komekomei lɛ adara waa moŋ.

english: Why do weak or yellow leaves on my yam plant lead to small yams underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii loo ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ sweet potato bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Leaves act as the factory that makes food for the plant; if leaves turn yellow due to poor soil nutrients or disease, they cannot manufacture enough food to feed and expand the tuber beneath the ground.
ga: Baai tsuɔ nii akɛ nitsumɔhei ni feɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo hela hewɔ lɛ baai lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha niyenii ni amɛbaagbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How do I know if my crop has reached full maturity and is ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Each crop shows clear physical signs when mature, such as leaves turning yellow or drying up, stems hardening, or fruit reaching a specific color and firmness. Harvesting before these maturity stages are complete lowers the quality and yield of your crop.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko jieɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo beni edara lɛ, tamɔ baai ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo egbi, tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni wa, loo aduawai ni naa su pɔtɛɛ ko kɛ shiŋŋfeemɔ. Kɛ́ okpa nikpamɔ dani shweremɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ kɛ yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Why should I wait for the rains to fully settle before planting my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Planting right after the first rain can be risky because early rains are often followed by dry spells. Waiting for consistent rain ensures the soil maintains enough moisture for the seeds to germinate smoothly and build strong roots.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efee oshara. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do extension officers test a new seed variety on a small plot before giving it to us to farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ aka dumɔwui heei amɛkwɛ yɛ ŋmɔji bibii amli lɛ? Dani ekɛba wɔŋɔɔ koni wɔkwɛ nɔ?

english: Testing a new crop variety on a small patch allows officers to observe how it performs in local weather and soil conditions across a full growing cycle before recommending it for large-scale farm investment.
ga: Kaa tsei srɔtoi heei yɛ he bibioo ko Enɛ haa mɛi ni tsuɔ he nii lɛ naa bɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii ehaa yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ mli yɛ amɛdalɛ be lɛ fɛɛ mli. Dani ebaatsɔɔ akɛ akɛ shika awo ŋmɔji wuji amli

english: Why do some cassava varieties take over a year to mature while others are ready in six months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi heɔ nɔ ni fe afi yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi feɔ klalo yɛ nyɔji enumɔ mli lɛ?

english: Different cassava varieties have different genetic designs. Early-maturing varieties accumulate starch in their roots rapidly, while late-maturing varieties grow more slowly and take longer to develop full, high-yield tubers.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni afeɔ cassava henɔ fɛɛ henɔ. Henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ buaa starch naa oya yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ sɛɛ lɛ daraa blɛoo ni amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛnáa yitsei ni eyi obɔ ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and tender roots that easily scorch in direct sunlight. Providing temporary shade using crops like plantains protects them until their root systems grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei tamɔ plantains tsu nii ni akɛha hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ ahe baawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why is my maize growing very tall but producing small, weak ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa shi eyɛ toi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: When maize gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or plants are crowded too closely together, the crop uses all its energy to build tall stalks and leaves rather than putting energy into growing big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo ŋmãa kɛ baai ni kɛlɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or poor soil nutrients. The plant sheds flowers to conserve energy when growing conditions become unfavorable.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛji shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ ehiii.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants start curling and turning yellow during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are responses to drought stress and insect attacks, such as sap-sucking mealybugs or whiteflies, which multiply quickly during dry weather and weaken the plant.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji hetoo kɛha hɔmɔ he haomɔ kɛ kooloi bibii ni tutuaa mɛi tamɔ mealybugs loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu lɛ. Ni baafee babaoo oya yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ. ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: What will happen to my pepper crop if rainwater stays logged on the field for days?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo?

english: Standing water blocks air from reaching plant roots, causing them to suffocate and rot. Without healthy roots, the plant cannot take up nutrients, leading to yellowing leaves, wilting, and eventually plant death.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe. Enɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni efiteɔ. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa bɛ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbiɔ, ni naagbee lɛ tso lɛ gboɔ.

english: Seeds harvested from hybrid crops do not pass down the exact same strong traits to the next generation. Replanting saved hybrid seed usually results in uneven plant growth, smaller cobs, and a lower total yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ kɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ nɔŋŋ baaha yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aŋmala amɛhe saji awo mli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ ejaaa. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ ba shi

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure early in the season helps fix this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, or a virus they spread. Spraying your crop early with neem seed extract or appropriate organic soap solutions can protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ Ashwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ mra Kɛtsɔ neem dumɔwui amli nu loo samla ni sa ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ abu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the small pods on my cocoa tree turn black and shrivel up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is commonly caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads in wet, overly shady conditions. Pruning extra shade tree branches and removing infected pods quickly allows air and sunlight to keep the tree dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ babaoo lɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants, keeping the soil cool and moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my cassava stem cuttings when planting my field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo mi-cassava niji lɛ amli kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ miidu yɛ mi saatso lɛ nɔ?

english: Cassava stems should be planted about 1 meter apart from each other. Giving them enough space ensures the roots have room to swell into large tubers without competing for soil nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cassava tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome. Kɛ́ akɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ha shishifãi lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii wuji ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akaŋ.

english: Which suckers should I cut away from my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ mafo kɛjɛ midumɔwu titri lɛ mli?

english: You should remove small, thin 'water' suckers and leave only two or three strong 'sword' suckers with narrow leaves. This ensures the main plant gets enough food and water to yield a big, heavy bunch.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie ‘nu’ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni oshi ‘klante’ ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baai lɛ mli etse. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji ni amɛtsii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when water supply in the soil goes from very dry to suddenly wet. Keeping the soil consistently damp with mulch helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake kɛjɛ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛtee nɔ ni edɔ trukaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes beside my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso awo emasɛi lɛ? Sweet potato wain tsei beni amɛdaraa lɛ

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves up toward sunlight. When leaves catch full sunlight, they create the food necessary to nourish and grow large tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ nɔ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa lɛ Ebɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekɛha ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: What is causing ragged holes and sawdust-like dirt in the center of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni etse kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that feeds on young maize leaves. Catching them early and placing ash, sand, or recommended bio-pesticides inside the central leaf funnel helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ sũ, ŋã, loo tsofa ko ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo tso lɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my vegetable crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: The best times to water vegetables are early morning or late afternoon. Watering during these cooler hours prevents the sun from evaporating water quickly, allowing root systems to absorb it fully.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ aduawai anɔ nu ji leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ nu mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ oya. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmuɔ nu kwraa.

english: You should plant after the rain has soaked the soil deeply two or three times. This ensures the ground has enough steady moisture so your seeds can germinate and roots can grow without drying out.
ga: Esa akɛ adu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ, ni afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ shii enyɔ loo etɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why is planting crops around September or October good for some late-season plants in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni dumɔ yɛ September loo October mli lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Planting during the late rainy period allows crops to use the remaining moisture in the soil to establish strong root systems before the dry season starts, helping them survive and mature properly.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ nu ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛma shishifãi ni mli wa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which is the key food plants need to stay green and grow, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: What causes my crop leaves to curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing water in intense heat. It is a natural way for the plant to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun and conserve moisture.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Eji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbaa shikpɔŋ ni hulu lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and leafy but fail to produce good fruits or tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ waa ni ewoɔ baai shi ewooo yibii loo ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ?

english: When plants grow too tall without fruit, it usually means they were planted too close together and are fighting for sunlight, or the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough nutrients like phosphorus for fruit development.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ dara tsɔ ni amɛwooo yibii Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la. Aloo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni niyenii mli nibii tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aduawai akwɛ̃ lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops need proper spacing between them when I am planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mitsei lɛ abɔ he jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ?

english: Spacing gives each plant enough room to gather light, air, water, and soil nutrients without competing with its neighbors, which helps them grow stronger and yields more harvest.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbuaa la, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ akaŋ akaŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if they are just growing beside them?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ amɛmasɛi?

english: Weeds steal vital resources like water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. When weeds take those resources, your crops grow weak and produce smaller yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ jwɛi ye nakai nibii lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebaawo yibii fioo.

english: Why should I clear old dead plants from my farm before planting new seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei momoi ni egboi lɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu dumɔwui heei?

english: Clearing old crop remains removes hidden pests, insects, and fungal diseases that live in dead plants, preventing them from attacking your new seedlings as soon as they sprout.
ga: Tso momo ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ajie tsɛŋemɔ helai, kooloi bibii, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ tsei ni egboi amli lɛ. Enɛ ji koni amɛkatutua odumɔwui heei lɛ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ.

english: Is it better for my land if I plant different crops together or just one crop on the whole field?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ he kome loo midu tso henɔ kome pɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Planting different crops together, like cassava with beans, protects the soil because legumes fix natural nitrogen into the ground, feed neighboring plants, and reduce the spread of pests.
ga: Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome, tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ejaakɛ ŋmei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ saa nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ niyenii ni oha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ agbɛfaŋnɔ aba shi

english: How does heavy rain right after planting affect the seeds I put in the soil?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ saa dumɔwui ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy downpours can wash away light seeds, bury them too deep under mud, or trap excess water in the soil which causes the seeds to suffocate and rot before sprouting.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ, ni ekɛfu amɛ yɛ muji lɛ shishi tsɔ. loo ehiɛɔ nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong direct sun. They need shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or shade trees to protect their leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni aduɔ nii lɛ.

english: When too many shoots grow around one main plantain stem, they fight for the same water and soil nutrients. Removing extra shoots leaves more food for the main tree to produce bigger bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso wulu kome he lɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food corn plants need to stay healthy. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa tsei koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas before planting maize on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei dani madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas pull natural nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. This enriches the land naturally, providing free nutrients for the maize crop that follows.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Cassava is generally ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will see the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem will begin to crack as the tubers expand underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaje shishi egbɛ eshwa be mli ni tuber lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves in the sunlight. Sunlight helps the leaves manufacture food, which is then sent underground to feed and grow large yam tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu la lɛ mli. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. Akɛ enɛɛmɛi yaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛyaye yam ŋmeii wuji ni amɛkwɛ nɔ.

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the central leaf funnel. Applying neem extract or recommended pest control early helps protect the young plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ baa. Akɛ neem mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii mra lɛ he ŋaawoo haa. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before any peppers form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by intense heat, irregular watering, or excessive chemical fertilizer. Giving them consistent water and light shade during hot spells helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine Nu kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛwoɔ mli daa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a hot dry period. Planting immediately can cause seeds to sprout and then die from lack of water before the main rainy season fully sets in.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi sɛɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ ni aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi yɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my cleared land than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ nɔ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit hidden in the soil in large numbers, waiting for sunlight and water to germinate instantly. Crops grow slower at first, so weeding early gives your planted crop a fair chance to catch up.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli babaoo. Mɛɛ ni hulu la kɛ nu lɛ akwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Tsei baakwɛ̃ blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha otso lɛ aná hegbɛ ni ekɛ ehe awo mli.

english: Why do these new improved maize seeds from the program require so much fertilizer compared to my local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ kɛjɛ nitsumɔ lɛ mli lɛ biɔ ŋmãa babaoo fe mimaŋ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Improved or high-yielding crop varieties grow faster and produce larger yields, which means they consume nutrients much faster than traditional seeds, requiring added fertilizer to reach their full potential.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ loo ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii oya fe blema dumɔwui lɛ. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he koni enyɛ etsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the difference between saving seeds from my own harvest and buying new certified seeds every season?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ kɛ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni miheɔ daa afi lɛ teŋ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred for strength, disease resistance, and high yield, but their offspring lose these strong traits after one harvest, which is why planting saved seeds leads to smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛhe wa, helai akamɔ amɛ, ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi amɛshwiei lɛ laajeɔ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ kpamɔ kome sɛɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops turn pale yellow even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal that the crop is lacking essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that too much water is drowning the roots and preventing them from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu babaoo miiha shishifãi lɛ miiho ni ehaaa amɛmu.

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural survival trick to protect themselves from intense sunlight and reduce the amount of water escaping from their leaves.
ga: Abɛi baai ni oootsi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ko ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my crops start flowering early and stay short when rain stops falling for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi mra ni amɛbaa shi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: When plants experience water stress, they sense danger and rush to produce flowers and seeds quickly to reproduce before they dry up, instead of growing taller.
ga: Kɛ tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ kpe Amɛnuɔ oshara he ni amɛfeɔ oya koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui oya koni amɛfɔ dani amɛgbi. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeete shi

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers without producing any fruit during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Excessive heat damages the pollen inside the flowers, which stops pollination from taking place, causing the plant to drop the useless flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ baatsi pollination naa koni ekafee nɔ ko. Ha fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa lɛ agbee shi

english: Why do I get smaller yields when I plant my crops close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ kɛ́ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in weak, thin plants with small produce.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ baa, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi.

english: Why does fast-growing hybrid corn exhaust my farmland much quicker than my old crop varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ miifite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii momo lɛ?

english: Fast-growing crops pull food out of the soil aggressively in a short time frame, so they empty the soil's nutrient reserves faster and require compost or fertilizer to restore the soil.
ga: Tsei ni daa oya lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli waa yɛ be kukuoo mli, no hewɔ lɛ amɛfiteɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Ni esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii ni okɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers grow big in loose soil but stay tiny and twisted in hard clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miida waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ etse lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi eji bibioo ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots need soft, loose ground to expand easily; heavy clay soil acts like a wall that physically squeezes the roots and prevents them from swelling.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ he ko ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni tsii tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbogbo ni miimɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaaa amɛfu.

english: Why do crops planted on one side of my farm grow much better than the same crops on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fa kome lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni adu yɛ fa kroko lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Soil quality, depth, and moisture levels vary across different spots on the same field, meaning some areas naturally provide better support and food for roots than others.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su, emlibotemɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ he fɛɛ he. yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hei komɛi kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni hi kɛ niyenii haa shishifãi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe ekrokomɛi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient that gives plants healthy green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps the plants green up and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ náa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni mli wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and small even when the plant stems grow tall and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too tightly, cassava spends all its energy growing leaves and branches instead of swelling its roots. Loose soil and balanced nutrients encourage the energy to go into building large tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ, Cassava kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛduɔ baai kɛ tsei aniji lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ Shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji kɛ niyenii ni ja lɛ woɔ hewalɛ hewalɛ koni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from high heat or dry soil. Giving plants consistent water and shade during the hot afternoon helps flowers stay on the plant and develop into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ amɛna nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo ha tso lɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii.

english: When plants are crowded, they compete for sunlight and stretch upwards to reach the light. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to catch sunshine and pull nutrients from the soil to produce healthy fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛná la. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni ekɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ewo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper on the exact same spot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously allows specific soil pests and diseases to build up and drains the exact same nutrients every season. Rotating crops like pepper with beans or maize breaks disease cycles and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ daa lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa ni amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ mli daa be. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ, tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei. Ehaa helai lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo.

english: Why does applying my fertilizer right before a heavy rain ruin the crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ, efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes top-applied fertilizer away into drainage streams before the roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer when the ground is moist, but not during heavy downpours, ensures the nutrients stay near the roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛjɛɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ faa lɛ mli lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ abɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do young cocoa trees perform better when planted alongside plantain suckers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ plantain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense tropical heat. Plantains grow fast with big leaves that provide temporary shade and keep the soil moist, helping the young cocoa survive its first couple of dry seasons.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do armyworm caterpillars appear on my maize crops so quickly after the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-abele lɛ nɔ oya beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rainfall triggers new green leaves on young maize, which attracts adult moths to lay eggs on the tender shoots. The eggs hatch rapidly in warm, rainy weather, causing caterpillars to suddenly appear in large numbers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa bibii lɛ feɔ baai eŋɔlii heei. Enɛ gbalaa ŋmeii koni amɛwo amɛwui yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ anɔ. Wɔɔji fɔɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni haa ŋmeii babaoo jeɔ kpo amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why should I trim off the lower leaves and small shoots on my vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo baai ni yɔɔ shishi kɛ tsei bibii lɛ? Mi aduawai lɛ anɔ?

english: Trimming lower leaves stops the plant from wasting energy on old leaves and prevents soil diseases from splashing up onto the fruit. It forces the plant to send water and nutrients straight to growing fruits.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haaa tso lɛ afite hewalɛ yɛ baai momoi anɔ, ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ hu shwieɔ aduawai lɛ anɔ. Enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya aduawai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do improved crop seeds from agricultural research officers differ from the seeds I save from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli he niiamlitaomɔ nitsulɔi lɛ adɛŋ lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Improved research seeds are specially bred to resist local pests, tolerate dry spells, and produce bigger yields. Saved seeds often lose their strength and disease resistance over successive generations.
ga: Akwɛ niiamlitaomɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni ewoɔ babaoo Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, or the roots are trapped in waterlogged soil after heavy rains, preventing the plant from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo shishifãi ni ekpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ anine shɛɛɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce tiny tubers when I plant the cuttings close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii bibii be mli ni adu niji lɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava cuttings are planted too close to each other, their roots fight over the same water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leaving no extra energy for the roots to expand into big tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli pɛpɛɛpɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni eshwɛɛɛ hewalɛ ko kwraa ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds after the long dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the major rains have fully settled and the soil stays moist for several consecutive days, rather than planting right after the very first rain which can dry up quickly and burn the seeds.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba shi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ. Mohu ɔ, o duɔ amlɔ nɔuu ke hiɔmi nɛ ɔ kekleekle ɔ, ejakaa lɔ ɔ ma nyɛ maa gbi oya nɛ e ma ha nɛ duwu ɔmɛ nɛ sã.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and replant seeds from my last maize harvest instead of buying certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni mikɛduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo he dumɔwuhi nɛ a wo he odase ɔ.

english: Seeds saved from harvested crops lose their original strength and disease resistance over generations, while certified seeds are specifically bred to give higher yields and withstand common pests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛshishijee hewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli. Yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛná yibii babaoo kɛ amɛhe ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and small root systems that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need living shade plants like plantains to shield them and keep the soil moist while they establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni hiɛ ka ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛtoɔ shi lɛ.

english: What causes small caterpillars to hide inside the central leaves of my young corn plants and eat them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ?

english: These are pests like the Fall Armyworm, which target the soft, growing funnel of young maize plants where they can safely feed on tender leaves before the cob forms.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛdaraa lɛ anɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye baai bibii lɛ shweshweeshwe dani ŋmãa bibii lɛ afee lɛ.

english: Weeds are native, hardy wild plants adapted to survive on very few nutrients and water, allowing them to steal sunlight and soil food faster than domesticated crops can.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ ni amɛhe wa, ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ niyenii kɛ nu fioo ko pɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shia lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop without forming fruit when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or sudden changes in water supply, causing the plant to abort flower growth to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni ewooo yibii kɛji tso lɛ kɛ haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu jɛɛhe lɛ tsakemɔ trukaa kpe. Enɛ haa tsei kpaɔ fɔfɔi akwɛ̃mɔ bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does my farmland produce fewer crop yields now compared to five years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ miiwo ŋmɔshi nibii fioo fe bɔ ni eji afii enumɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Planting crops repeatedly on the same piece of land strips nutrients out of the soil every season without giving it time to recover, causing the soil to become exhausted unless organic manure or nitrogen-fixing crops are added.
ga: repetitive planting Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ja akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsei ni haa nitrogen lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ fata he.

english: Why do my vegetables rot faster when I don't clear the weeds and bush around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ miifite oya lɛ? Be mli ni minyɛɛɛ majie jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ?
