english: A crowded and bushy farm traps heat and moisture around your crops without letting fresh air pass through, creating an ideal damp environment for fungal diseases and rot to spread.
ga: Okwaafoi ni bɛ deka, ni eyi obɔ lɛ mɔɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. oŋmɔshi nibii ni oŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha fungal helai kɛ fitemɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a protective canopy that keeps the cocoa cool and retains soil moisture during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛitsu ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during strong winds and rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow shallowly, making heavy plants top-heavy once they develop fruit bunches. Propping the stems with sturdy bamboo or wooden stakes gives them extra support so wind storms do not blow them down.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ daaa fioo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ tsiimɔ ni ebaatsii babaoo kɛ́ eyɛ aduawai akui amli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha eye ebua babaoo. Koni ahum lɛ akatswa shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young corn plants turning yellow from the tip downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient corn needs to grow green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the corn regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishifãi ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi, ni haa niyenii ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei, ŋmei, loo ŋmei ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmei lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does the soil on my vegetable farm dry out and form hard cracks so quickly after watering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ́ awo nɔ nu lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture fast when exposed directly to hot sun and dry wind. Covering the ground around crops with dry grass or leaves—known as mulching—keeps the soil cool, preserves water, and prevents the ground from cracking.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shɛ enɔ. Ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle jɛmɛ lɛ ahe Mulching (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehaa nu hiɔ shi, ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli agbala.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in the central whorl of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ bu bibioo ni yɔɔ mi-abele tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that burrow into the tender center of young corn plants. Catching them early and applying approved pest treatments directly into the plant whorl stops them from destroying the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni aaamɔ amɛ mra ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or mites feeding on young leaves. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or targeted sprays allows new leaves to grow flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ kudɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akɛtoɔ hiɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai heei baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves look crumpled with patchy yellow patterns instead of smooth green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ekpɔtɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaafee ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by whitefly insects or infected stems. Planting improved, disease-resistant cassava stem varieties is the best way to prevent this disease on your farm.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava henɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela nɛɛ naa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my seed yams rot in the ground before they can sprout after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seed yams rot when planted in waterlogged soil or if the seed pieces have cuts that let fungal diseases in. Planting in raised mounds with well-drained soil and coating cut seed pieces with wood ash helps protect them.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ loo kɛji akɛ afo dumɔwui lɛ fãi komɛi ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni sũ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ, ni akɛ tso sũ ni afolɔ lɛ ha dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe.

english: No, planting seeds too close forces plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and small cob yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to produce large, full cobs.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa nitsumɔhe fɛɛ nitsumɔhe náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my harvested maize get moldy and infested with insects inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli ewo muji ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ewo mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize rots and attracts insects if it is put into storage while still holding water inside the grain. Drying the cobs thoroughly until the grains are hard before storing them in a clean, ventilated crib keeps mold and pests away.
ga: Abele fiteɔ ni egbalaa kooloi kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni nu yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli lolo. Agbiɔ ŋmeii lɛ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani akɛtoɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii akabote mli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with small cobs when I plant many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When you plant too many seeds close together, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Spacing them out allows each plant to get enough nutrients to build strong stems and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni kã tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha efee ŋmeii ni wa ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yam leaves need plenty of sunlight to make food that feeds the tuber growing under the ground. Staking lifts the vines off the dirt so the leaves get maximum sunlight and good airflow, which prevents diseases and makes the tubers grow much bigger.
ga: Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo ni amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa mɔ nɔ, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa babaoo.

english: The main plantain tree shares its food and water with all the small shoots (suckers) growing around it. By cutting away the extra suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones, the main tree gets all the power it needs to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Plantain titri lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ jaa niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso titri lɛ baaná hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfee plantains akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and weak roots that burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby acts like an umbrella, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist until its roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ adumɔ Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta Ha kookoo bibioo lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without producing any tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the sun is extremely hot and the ground is dry, the tomato plant gets stressed and drops its flowers to save energy for survival. Providing light shade and watering regularly during hot dry spells helps the flowers stay on and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he. Kɛ́ aha fɔfɔi lɛ hulutsoo kɛ nu daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very bushy green leaves above ground but produces tiny tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii akui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi bulbs bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much foliage growth usually means the soil has too much nitrogen or fertilizer at the wrong time. The plant spends all its energy making top leaves instead of storing starch down in the tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yaa hiɛ fe nine lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be ni esaaa mli. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋwɛi baai lɛ amli moŋ fe ni ekɛ starch baato ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is already moist and the plants are actively growing, but not right before a heavy downpour. Applying it when the soil is slightly damp allows the roots to absorb it before rain can wash it away.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Shi esaaa akɛ ofeɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Kɛ́ okɛwo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ afɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops weak and yellowish even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have very strong roots that steal the fertilizer and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Even with enough rain, your crops become hungry because the weeds are consuming their food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa waa ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po Hɔmɔ miiye onibii po ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ miiye amɛ niyenii.

english: What is causing small holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants with brown dirt left inside?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ, ni muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ eshwɛ yɛ mli lɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center funnel of the maize plant to eat the soft new leaves. Clearing weeds early and applying appropriate control methods into the plant funnel will stop them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ni akɛ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ lɛ baatsu nii yɛ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baatsi amɛnaa.

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the juices from under the fresh leaves. As they feed, they damage the leaf tissues, causing them to curl up and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai heei lɛ ashishi lɛ. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii Ebaafite baa lɛ mli fãji. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the bottom up before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: This usually happens when maize plants lack nitrogen, which is the main nutrient they need to stay green and grow strong. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the ground out of reach of the roots, causing the lower older leaves to turn yellow first as the plant moves remaining nutrients to newer leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tsei amli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ha baai bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ be mli ni tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei amli lɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans on my field make the soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and other leguminous plants work together with good bacteria in the soil to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant finishes growing and decomposes, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Ekɛ bacteria kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni emɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei dara ni amɛfite Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha sɛɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops wilt on hot afternoons even when it rained a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ moŋ?

english: On very hot and sunny days, water evaporates from plant leaves faster than their roots can pull moisture out of the ground. The leaves temporarily curl or droop to protect themselves from losing too much water, but they usually bounce back once the sun goes down and temperatures cool.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ Nu shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ baabɔle amɛhe loo amɛbaagbee shi be kukuoo ko koni nu akafite fe nine. Shi bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to full, direct sunlight and heat. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the air cool and soil moist so the young cocoa roots can establish without burning up.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ feɔ ni shãaa.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the small shoots keep growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii shwereɔ yɛ midumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: When too many young shoots grow around one main plantain stem, they compete for the same water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Trimming away extra shoots leaves only one or two strong suckers, ensuring the main plant has enough energy to grow big, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsei bibii babaoo dara yɛ tso titri kome he lɛ, no lɛ nakai tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi koni tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni etsɔ ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: The black pod disease is caused by tiny water molds that thrive in damp, humid conditions. When raindrops hit wet soil or infected leaves, they splash the mold spores onto nearby pods, causing the dark rot to spread quickly through the farm.
ga: Nu mli ŋmeii bibii kɛ black pod hela baa. No shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ loo baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ Ekɛ fungal spores lɛ shwieɔ pods ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hela ni ji dark rot lɛ gbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually a reaction to tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or a virus transmitted by these insects. The leaf shrinks and curls as it loses sap and vital juices to the pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛfiteɔ nu kɛ nu ni he hiaa waa kɛyaa kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: When day and night temperatures get too hot, the pollen inside tomato flowers dries up and dies before it can fertilize the blossom. Without successful pollination, the plant drops the unfertilized flower to save its energy.
ga: Beni shwane kɛ gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔɔ tsɔ Pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔ. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ yeee omanye lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows all the leaves to spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible to produce plant food. Keeping the leaves off the damp ground also prevents leaves from rotting and gives the root tubers plenty of energy to expand deep underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ fɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛfee tsei niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkafiteɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even when the plant above ground has giant stems and dark green leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ? Tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ po yɛ tsei wuji kɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa.

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium, the cassava plant spends all its food energy building large stems and leafy foliage above ground instead of storing starch in the roots below ground.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ eniyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ tsei wuji kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔ starch kɛ toɔ sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ a mi.

english: How do I know if my harvested corn is dry enough for buyers to accept it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ baakpɛlɛ nɔ?

english: You can check the dryness using a moisture meter or by pressing a kernel; buyers typically look for a moisture level around 11% to 13% so the grain will not rot or attract insects during storage and transport.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ mita loo kernel press akwɛ bɔ ni egbi ha. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo be ni miihe ashɛ 11% kɛyashi 13% bɔni afee ni ŋmaa lɛ akafite loo egbala kooloi kɛba be mli ni akɛtoɔ kɛ be mli ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do buyers test the moisture level of my maize before buying it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kaa bɔ ni mi-ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ amɛkwɛɔ dani amɛheɔ lɛ?

english: Buyers test moisture because high water content causes maize to heat up, grow dangerous molds, and spoil quickly during transport or in storage bags.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kaa bɔ ni nu lɛ mli edɔ ha lɛ amɛkwɛɔ ejaakɛ nu ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ mli dɔɔ. Fung ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baa ni efiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko loo yɛ kotokui ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ amli.

english: What is the ideal moisture percentage I should aim for when sun-drying my corn?
ga: Mɛni ji hulutsoo be ni sa jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ makwɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmãa miigbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Aiming for a moisture level of around 11% to 12% is ideal because at this low level, fungal growth stops, insects cannot breed easily, and the grain remains stable for months.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni miihe ashɛ 11% kɛyashi 12% ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ yɛ nɛkɛ hulutsoo be nɛɛ mli lɛ, Fungal dalɛ baakpa. Kplukai nyɛɛɛ afɔ́ mlɛo. ni dumɔwui lɛ baahi shi shiŋŋ nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why does wet corn spoil so quickly if I put it in bags right after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni efɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikɛwo kotoku mli beni akpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested corn contains trapped water; when sealed inside bags, this moisture releases heat and creates humidity, causing mold, fungi, and rot to destroy the whole bag within days.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa ehee lɛ nu ekpɛtɛ he. Kɛji akɛ atsĩ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ jieɔ dɔlɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fiteɔ kotoku muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: Why do maize kernels shrink and become hard as they dry in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: As maize dries, water evaporates out of the kernel cells, causing the inner starch to compact, tighten, and form a hard, protective outer layer that resists damage.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa lɛ egbi Nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli wala yibii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ehaa ŋmei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni ehaa kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa ni buɔ mɔ he ni nyɛɔ efiteɔ lɛ feɔ.

english: Why do commercial grain buyers bring moisture testing tools directly to my drying floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ ŋmaa ni akɛheɔ jarayeli lɛ kɛ tsɔnei ni akɛkaa ŋmɔtɔ baa mishikpɔŋ ni migbiɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Buyers test directly on your drying floor to confirm the moisture level has dropped to around 11% before loading, ensuring they do not pay to transport water weight or risk grain rotting in transit.
ga: Ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kaa shikpɔŋ ni okɛgbiɔ nii lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛma nɔ mi akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ eba shi kɛyashɛ aaafee 11% dani amɛjieɔ, ni amɛkwɛɔ koni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛwo nu lɛ tsiimɔ he nyɔmɔ loo amɛwo oshara mli akɛ ŋmaa lɛ baafite yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa lɛ.

english: Does selling heavy, wet corn bring in more money than selling dry corn?
ga: Abele ni mli efɔ ni tsii ni ahɔ̃ɔ Ani ehaa anáa shika babaoo fe abele ni egbi ni ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Although wet corn weighs more, buyers pay less or reject it entirely because extra water causes rapid spoilage, mold growth, and lower grain quality.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa ni efɔ lɛ tsiimɔ fe no moŋ, Shi mɛi ni heɔ lɛ woɔ nyɔmɔ fioo loo amɛkpooɔ kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa efiteɔ oya. Fungus daa ni dumɔwui lɛ ahilɛ baa shi

english: How does low moisture content protect my stored maize from mold?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni nu ni mli edɔ fioo lɛ abu ŋmãa ni ato lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmãa he?

english: Fungi and molds need water to survive and grow; keeping your grain moisture down near 11% starves the mold of water so it cannot grow or produce harmful toxins.
ga: Mold kɛ fungi he miihia nu koni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara. Kɛji akɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli nu lɛ ba shi aaafee 11% lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, edaaa loo ekɛ tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui baaa.

english: How can I tell if my corn is getting spoiled while it is still drying outside?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-abele lɛ efite be mli ni egbiɔ lolo yɛ kpo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Spoiling corn will feel unusually warm to the touch, may give off a sour or musty smell, and will show white, yellow, or dark powdery mold spotting on the kernels.
ga: Abɛi ni efite lɛ baanu he akɛ edɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ota he. Ekolɛ eŋɔɔɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ. ni ebaajie powder mildew yɛŋ, ŋmɔŋ loo ediŋŋ kpo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I bag my corn for sale while it is still warm from the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa yɛ kotokui amli be mli ni hulu lɛ mli edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Bagging warm corn causes moisture to evaporate inside the cool bag and turn into water droplets, which creates damp spots where mold quickly starts to grow.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa ni mli edɔ wo kotoku mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kotoku ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ nu ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ shishi edaa oya lɛ baa.

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantains on the same land with my new young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikɛ mi-cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ duɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct hot sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like umbrellas, providing shade and trapping soil moisture to help the young cocoa survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua kookoo bibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees falling off before turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers when they suffer from water stress during dry weather, or when insects damage the stem joint, causing the tree to drop flowers it cannot support.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ nu he haomɔ kpe amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. aloo beni kooloi bibii fiteɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni nyɛɛɛ akwɛ amɛnɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen nutrients, or the ground is too soaked with standing water, which prevents the roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ kɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aye nii.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close to each other, will I harvest more crop?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: No, planting seeds too close forces the crops to fight for light, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stalks and small or empty ears of corn.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which hatch from moth eggs. They hide in the center funnel of the plant because it is soft and damp, chewing up the tender leaves as they grow.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛmli edɔ. ni ekɛ baai bibii shwieɔ shi beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil during heavy rains because standing water stops air from reaching the roots, allowing harmful rot fungi in the soil to destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni yeɔ mɔ awui baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni baanyɛ akpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus, or by severe heat and dry weather stressing the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni haa tsei haoɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I avoid planting peppers on the exact same bed where I just harvested tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ dumɔ he yɛ saatso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikɛ mi-tomato lɛ shwie nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes and peppers belong to the same plant family and share the same soil diseases and pests. Planting them consecutively allows pests left in the soil to immediately attack the new crop.
ga: Tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, prevents moisture from evaporating under the hot sun, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is slightly moist after a light rain, and cover it with a little soil near the plant roots so heavy downpours do not wash it off the field.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ. ni okɛ sũ fioo aha he ni bɛŋkɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akajie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do some farmers choose to harvest fruits like mangoes late at night or early in the morning instead of during the sunny daytime?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi halaa akɛ amɛbaakpa aduawai tamɔ mango gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaakpa nii yɛ gbi ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ.

english: Harvesting in the cool hours of the night or early morning keeps the fruit cold and prevents it from losing water quickly in the afternoon sun. This helps the fruit stay fresh much longer during transport to the market.
ga: Nikpamɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli Gbi gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa yibii lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa nu lɛ afite oya yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my mango trees drop so many of their flowers before the small fruits even start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo dani bibii lɛ miiwo lɛ? Ani ebaaje shishi efee?

english: Mango trees naturally produce thousands more flowers than they can support, dropping many on purpose. However, excessive flower drop happens when the tree lacks water during flowering, suffers from insect damage, or experiences sudden high heat.
ga: Mango tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa mɛi babaoo tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔii amɛshwieɔ shi. Shi kɛlɛ, fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, kɛ́ kooloi bibii fite amɛ, loo amɛna hulutsoo ni naa wa trukaa.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and droop during the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ moŋ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves during the hottest part of the day as a defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and slow down water loss. They usually recover once the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛha hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ amɛhiɛ lɛ aba shi ni amɛha nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, elaajeɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: If I cut off some branches from my young fruit tree, won't that damage the plant and reduce my harvest?
ga: Kɛ mifo tso nine bibioo ko kɛjɛ mi tso bibioo lɛ mli lɛ Efiteee tsei lɛ ni ebaaha mi yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi, aloo jeee nakai?

english: Removing weak or crowded branches—known as pruning—actually helps the tree. It directs the plant's food and energy away from unnecessary leaves and into growing larger, healthier fruits on the main branches.
ga: Niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ pruning) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ waa. Etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ ahe kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji wuji lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: What happens to my maize plants if I plant the seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When maize is planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. As a result, the plants grow tall and thin with very small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawuu kɛha hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu fioo Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii bibii waa yɔɔ mli loo ŋmeii bɛ kwraa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my tomato plants turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a plant are usually the oldest leaves that are no longer getting enough sunlight, or it is a sign that the plant has used up the nitrogen nutrients in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ji baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ shɛɛɛ amɛhe dɔŋŋ. Aloo eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ efite nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to put chemical fertilizer on my crops when the ground is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve so the plant roots can safely drink them. Putting fertilizer on dry soil creates a strong concentration of chemicals that can burn and kill the roots.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tsofai babaoo baa. ni baanyɛ ashã ni efite shishifãi lɛ

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my young crops with dry grass or palm leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Mi dumɔwui ni jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei tsei yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, shields the ground from the hot sun so water doesn't evaporate quickly, keeping the roots cool and preventing weeds from growing.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. koni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃.

english: Why does planting cowpea or beans alongside my cassava make the cassava grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mi-cassava lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, they feed the soil with natural fertilizer that helps neighboring crops like cassava grow strong.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ koni amɛdara waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my young crops to look weak and turn pale green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi dumɔwui lɛ miifee tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal sunlight, water, and soil fertilizers away from your plants, leaving your crops starved of the food they need to stay green.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni ekɛ hiɛdɔɔ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli.

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantain trees alongside my young cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily in intense sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that shade the young cocoa from the hot sun while keeping moisture in the soil during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni buɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Does it matter which direction I point cassava stem cuttings when planting them in the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni afo lɛ baatsɔɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the growth buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes the sprouts to struggle to reach the surface, leading to weak plants and small harvests.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii wuji lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko baa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch full sunlight to make energy for growing tubers. If the vines lie flat on hot, damp soil, they produce much smaller yams and rot more easily.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la ni fa babaoo koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulbs ni miida lɛ. Kɛji wain tso lɛ kã shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ Ebaawo ŋmeii bibii waa ni baafite oya.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer early in the crop's growth helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ tso lɛ shishijee be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the dirt. Legumes like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which naturally enriches the soil for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ jara wa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli

english: Why do farmers put dry grass on top of the soil around their vegetable plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛbɔleɔ amɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops heat from drying out the ground too fast, keeps plant roots cool, blocks weeds from growing, and eventually breaks down into natural fertilizer.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi la ni tsoɔ lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛfiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Giving plants consistent water and light shade during hot spells helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo ha tso lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Curling and wrinkled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking the juice from the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by insects. Neem oil spray can help control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ kooloi bibii nɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my vegetable crops develop black spots and rot during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ diji ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains create damp conditions where fungal diseases easily spread through water splashes on wet leaves. Spacing plants further apart lets wind dry the leaves and prevents fungal spots from spreading.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nu ni shwieɔ baai ni efɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei lɛ to amɛhe shɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ akagbi, ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What will happen if I plant my seeds very close to each other to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mihe lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for water, soil food, and sunlight. This results in tall, thin, weak plants that yield much less produce overall than properly spaced plants.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo fe tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: What actually happens to my crops when I put fertilizer in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer acts like food for your plants, supplying extra nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium that your soil might lack. It helps young crops build strong roots, grow greener leaves, and produce larger yields.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛhaa tsei. Ehaa niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus kɛ potassium ni ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni wa. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ koni amɛfee eŋɔli. ni ekɛ nibii babaoo aba

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK gives the crops the food they need to turn green and produce big, healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛwo toi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Will putting a large amount of fertilizer on my crops at once make them produce fruit twice as fast?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo miŋmɔshi nibii amli shikome lɛ, ebaaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ oya shii enyɔ?

english: No, putting too much fertilizer at once can 'burn' the roots and destroy the plant. Crops need small, carefully measured amounts applied at key growing stages to absorb nutrients safely.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli shikome lɛ baanyɛ ‘ashã’ shishifãi lɛ ni egbe tso lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ nibii bibii ni asusuɔ he jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛdalɛ bei titrii amli koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land is fertile enough for me to clear and plant crops on?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafo mli ni madu nii?

english: Good, fertile land usually has dark, crumbly soil that retains moisture without standing in pools of water. If natural weeds and bushes grow thick and dark green on the plot, crops will usually thrive there too.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi ni baa nii lɛ fɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni edamɔɔɔ nubu mli. Kɛji akɛ adebɔɔ mli jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii lɛ dara ni amɛyɛ su ni tsuɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɛmɛ hu.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients. Leaving adequate space between plants lets every crop gather enough food to grow strong.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la fioo, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Shi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ abua niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa naa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with huge green leaves but leave me with tiny tubers at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi eshwɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akpa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too hard, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of expanding tubers below. Loosening the soil and avoiding excess nitrogen helps produce bigger tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ ebaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajie nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni afee bulbs wuji.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience heat stress, dry soil, or a sudden lack of plant food. Keeping the soil consistently moist and feeding the soil helps flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tso niyenii ni bɛ trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: How do wild weeds growing next to my crops actually hurt their growth?
ga: Koo mli jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigba edalɛ naa yɛ gbɛ fɔŋ nɔ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds act as thieving neighbors on your farm; they grow much faster than crops and steal the fertilizer, water, space, and sunlight intended for your plants, causing your crops to starve.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ akutsoŋbii julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, ŋwɛi, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ. Hɔmɔ ye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting cowpeas or groundnuts together with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ tsina ŋmei loo ŋmei afata ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds neighboring maize crops while preventing weed growth.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ebaatsi jwɛi ni shwereɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why does covering the bare soil around my crops with dry grass help them survive during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko woɔ nɔ lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, mikɛ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts like a shade cover that stops the hot sun from drying out the soil. It traps moisture near the roots and slowly decomposes into natural organic manure.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Emɔɔ nu ni ebɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and burn when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong, direct sunlight damages their delicate leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Leaving taller trees or planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains shields young cocoa from intense heat until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni aaashi loo adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the center shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ yɛ bu komɛi. Akɛtee teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which feed on the soft, growing tissue inside the central leaves of young maize plants. Catching them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or approved chemicals prevents them from destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite hei ni tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my field yield smaller cassava roots when I plant cassava on the exact same land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmei shishifãi bibii beni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows soil-borne pests to build up. Rotating cassava with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts gives the soil time to recover and naturally restores vital nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa A rotation of cassava kɛ legumes tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Leaf curling in strong afternoon heat is a plant's natural self-defense to lower its exposed surface area and reduce water loss. If the leaves uncurl and return to normal in the cool evening, it means the plant is simply managing extreme heat.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni edɔ lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hebuu. Koni ekɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni nu lɛ fiteɔ lɛ shi. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ efolɔɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ nɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ miikpe.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience environmental shock, such as sudden hot spells, prolonged dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Maintaining steady moisture and balanced fertilizer helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛ kpe shihilɛi ni bɛ shiŋŋ mli, tamɔ ahum ni naa wa trukaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ. loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni haa hulutsoo be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni enyɛ ewo yibii.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and skinny with tiny cobs when I put many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ daa ni ekwɛɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crowded plants compete against each other for sunshine, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets adequate food and light to develop thick stems and full-sized cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii ni fa babaoo aba.

english: Extra suckers act like extra mouths to feed, taking water and food away from the main mother plant. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the mother plant to focus its energy on growing a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krokomɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ krokomɛi kɛha niyenii. Kɛtsɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama plantains ŋmeii wuji ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: How does planting groundnuts help make my soil richer for the maize I want to plant next season?
ga: Te ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni efee ŋmɔshi nii babaoo kɛha ŋmeii ni misumɔɔ ni madu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots. When the groundnut plant leaves and roots decay in the soil, that stored nitrogen becomes natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔmɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Nitrogen ni ato lɛ bafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei kɛha sɛɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why did my maize seeds rot in the ground instead of sprouting after a heavy rain flooded my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds need both moisture and oxygen from the air inside the soil to sprout. When heavy rain causes long-standing water on the field, it blocks air from reaching the seeds, causing them to suffocate and rot before they can grow.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ehaa nu hiɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ tsiɔ dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafo ni amɛkafite dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my harvested yams turn soft and rot when I pile them inside a dark, warm room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egboɔ kɛ́ mikɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni duŋ ewo mli lɛ?

english: Harvested yams are still living tubers that breathe and release heat and moisture. When kept in a warm room without moving air, trapped humidity promotes fungal growth and rot; storing them on elevated, ventilated racks in a cool, shaded area keeps them healthy.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni akpa lɛ ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka lolo ni muɔ ni amɛjieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kpo. Kɛ akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ adara ni egbo. Okɛto adeka ni nɔ kwɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant yams in the space around my house compound, or do they only yield well on a far away farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu sweet potatoes yɛ mishia lɛ he, aloo amɛbaawo yibii kpakpai yɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ amli pɛ?

english: Yams can grow very well both in small household compound gardens and on large farm plots, provided the soil is deep, well-drained, fertile, and gets full sunlight.
ga: Sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shia abɔɔi bibii kɛ okwaayeli shikpɔji wuji fɛɛ amli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ, nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ, ewoɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni enáa hulutsoo be babaoo.

english: How do I choose the best type of yam variety to plant on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala sweet potato henɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Choosing a yam variety depends on your local rainfall, soil type, and market demand; speaking with local agricultural officers or successful neighboring farmers can help you select high-yielding varieties that suit your area.
ga: Bɔ ni ahalaa sweet potato henɔi lɛ damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ henɔ kɛ jara nɔ nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ loo okwaafoi ni yeɔ omanye ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ wie lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni sa kɛha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Where do farmers normally get healthy seed yams to start planting on a new farm?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni okwaafoi fɔɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛduɔ yɛ amɛŋmɔji heei lɛ amli lɛ namɔ yɛ?

english: Farmers obtain seed yams by saving small tubers from their previous harvest, cutting larger mature yams into smaller pieces, or buying clean, disease-free seed yams from certified agricultural suppliers.
ga: Okwaafoi naa sweet potato dumɔwui kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni amɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa tsutsu lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Kpãa ŋmɔtɔ ni edara lɛ mli bibii bibii. Aloo hemɔ ŋmeii ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nihɔɔlɔ ko ni aŋmɛ gbɛ lɛ dɛŋ.

english: Why do we need to heap soil into mounds before planting yams instead of planting directly into flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔbua muji naa wɔwo gɔji amli dani wɔdu ŋmeii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Making mounds creates loose, soft soil that lets underground yam tubers expand easily while also improving drainage so excess rainwater does not sit around the roots and cause them to rot.
ga: Gɔŋ ko ni afee lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ bɔni afee ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ akabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Why do yam plants need tall sticks to climb as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe hiaa ni amɛná niji kakadaji koni amɛkwɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbing vines, and using sticks keeps their leaves up off the ground where they can catch maximum sunlight to make food for growing large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni tsei niji ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛnáa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ.

english: Can I plant crops like maize or vegetables on the same soil mounds where my yams are growing?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping yams with quick-growing crops like maize or legumes is common because it maximizes land space and some crops like beans even help improve soil fertility for the yams.
ga: Hɛɛ, sweet potatoes ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ŋmãa duɔ. Enɛ hi ejaakɛ ehaa he lɛ yaa hiɛ babaoo. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi, tamɔ ŋmei hu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What causes my yam leaves to turn brown or develop spots during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Leaf spots are usually caused by fungal diseases that thrive in heavy humidity and rain, which damage the leaves and slow down the plant's ability to feed its growing tuber.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ he tsɔi baa. Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know that yams underground are mature and ready for harvesting when I cannot see them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa? He ni minaaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Yams are ready for main harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up, showing that the plant has completed its growth cycle and stored all its energy into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ebote edalɛ mli ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto bulb lɛ mli.

english: Is it possible to carefully harvest a yam tuber early without killing the plant?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akpa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ mra? Ni agbeee tso lɛ?

english: Yes, farmers use a practice called early harvesting or 'milking,' where the main tuber is removed carefully early in the season while leaving the roots intact so the vine can produce smaller seed yams afterward.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaafoi kɛ nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmaakpamɔ mra loo ‘ŋmɔlɔ’ tsuɔ nii ni ajieɔ ŋmeii titrii lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be lɛ mli mra, ni ashiɔ shishifãi lɛ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni wain tsei lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmeii bibii ni dumɔwui yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: What is the best way to store harvested yams so they do not rot quickly?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ toɔ koni amɛkafite oya?

english: Store harvested yams in a cool, well-ventilated, dry place like a shaded yam barn on raised wooden shelves, keeping them away from direct sunlight, moisture, and pests.
ga: Too sweet potato ni akpa lɛ he yɛ he ko ni egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ, tamɔ sweet potato ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ shade yɛ tso shɛlɛf ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛto he ko ni hulu la, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shɛɛɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to grow green and strong. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color and helps the plant grow big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ashishifãi, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmɔji wuji.

english: Why is extension officers telling me not to plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize in the same spot every year drains the soil of the specific nutrients maize needs and lets pests build up in the soil. Switching to crops like cowpeas or groundnuts rebuilds soil fertility naturally for your next crop.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abele lɛ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does planting my maize seeds too close together make the stalks tall and thin with tiny cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing gives each plant enough personal space to build thick stalks and large, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why does covering the dirt around my crops with dry grass help them survive when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around lɛ mikɛ jwɛi duɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass or leaves (mulching) acts like an umbrella for the soil. It blocks the hot sun from drying out the ground, keeping moisture near the roots so the crops don't wither.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shishifãi lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ akagbo.

english: What causes small caterpillars to hide inside the leaves of my young maize and eat holes in them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ bu yɛ mli?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, pests that prefer hiding in the soft, inner leaves of young maize where it is warm and safe. Catching them early with recommended organic or chemical sprays prevents them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii amli ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ mli. Kɛ́ mɔmɔmɔ amɛ mra kɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my tomatoes turning black and rotting before the fruit even gets ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes (blossom-end rot) happen when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil swings between very dry and soaked.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ Blossom tip rot (blossom end rot) baa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ miihoso yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa teŋ.

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they get stressed by prolonged hot dry weather or a lack of beneficial insects to pollinate them. Planting shade trees around cocoa keeps the air cool and moist so flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ loo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi lɛ bɛ lɛ haoɔ amɛ. Tsei ni aduɔ koni ekɛ hulutsoo aha yɛ Cocoa he lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Kɛkɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ bafeɔ pod.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their leaves and turn yellow when heavy rain floods my field for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Pepper roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the field for days, it drowns the roots, causing the plant to drop leaves because it can no longer draw water and food upward.
ga: Pepper shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu lɛ ehi ŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbala nu kɛ niyenii kɛya ŋwɛi dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot quickly under the ground if I leave them after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When rain saturates the soil completely, oxygen cannot reach the cassava tubers underground. The soggy, airless ground causes mature tubers to rot quickly if left unharvested.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyiɔ kwraa. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ haa bulbs ni eda lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpaaa.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous harvest yield less food than new certified seeds from the agriculture shop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni jɛ okwaayeli shwapo ko mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their strength and uniformity in the next generation, producing weaker offspring. Certified seeds are specially produced under strict conditions to give strong, high-yielding crops every time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ekomefeemɔ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji seshibii ni bɛ hewalɛ. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa shishi koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo aba be fɛɛ be.

english: Why does my freshly harvested cassava spoil so fast if I leave it in the house for just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni ajie ehee lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ yɛ shĩa mli gbii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots have high water content and begin a natural rotting process within 48 to 72 hours after being dug up. Processing cassava into gari removes this moisture, turning a fast-spoiling root into a dry product that can be stored safely for many months.
ga: Nu babaoo yɛ cassava shishifãi amli ni ejeɔ adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ shishi yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli beni atsa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ afee cassava ni afee lɛ gari lɛ, ejieɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni efite oya lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni egbi ni abaanyɛ akɛto shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do I need to press water out of crushed cassava before roasting it into gari?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ nu ni yɔɔ ŋmei ni atsɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi dani mikɛshãa koni mikɛfee Gari lɛ?

english: Raw cassava contains high levels of moisture and natural toxins (cyanide). Squeezing out the liquids during processing removes these dangerous compounds and reduces drying time, ensuring your gari turns out safe, dry, and crispy.
ga: Cassava ni ahoo lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ babaoo kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai fɔji (cyanide) yɔɔ mli. Nu lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ be mli ni atsuɔ he nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nɛkɛ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ. ni okɛ be ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ aba shi Ekwɛɔ koni o-condiments lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe, amɛgbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when I plant them in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate intense heat. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to young cocoa provides temporary shade and holds soil moisture to protect the seedlings.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi koni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the cocoa pods on my farm turning black and rotting while still hanging on the trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite lɛ? Ani okɛ ohe kpɛtɛ tso lɛ he lolo?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, overly shaded conditions with low airflow. Regular pruning of farm shade trees and frequent harvesting of ripe pods help keep humidity down and stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ. Shade babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni baa shi Shade tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni afoɔ daa kɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaa shii abɔ lɛ. Ehaa hulutsoo baa shi, ni ehaa helai gbɛfaŋnɔ kpaa.

english: Peppers drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or insect pests like thrips. Ensuring consistent soil moisture and using proper organic pest control helps the plant keep its flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Peppers baagbee shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa ha amɛ hao. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ thrips, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden egg plants turning yellow and curling upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing on garden eggs are usually caused by sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or aphids that transmit plant viruses. Removing weeds around your field and spraying with neem oil or insecticidal soap protects your crop from these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni hiɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa. Jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji amli kɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe.

english: Why are my pepper leaves turning pale green even though I water the farm every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ nu woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi?

english: Pale green leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Adding compost, well-rotted animal manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer will restore the green color and boost plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Koolooi ashishifã ni egbo lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli Loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains and storms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ ahum ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow, fibrous roots that do not anchor deeply into the soil. When soil becomes soft from heavy rain and the heavy fruit bunches weigh the plant down, strong winds can easily tip them over unless you stake them with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni tamɔ fiber ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ fee blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ aduawai ni fa babaoo lɛ hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha tsei akumɔ oya. Ja okɛ tso nibii ehi shi.

english: Why do small insects bore holes into my stored corn shortly after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize weevils often lay eggs in the corn while it is drying in the field. If the corn is not thoroughly dried below 13% moisture before storage, those eggs hatch inside sealed bags and destroy the grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ŋmeii woɔ ŋmãa mli be mli ni egbiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa ni ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shɛɛɛ 13% dani akɛtoɔ. Nakai ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ kotokui ni atsĩ naa mli ni amɛfiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why does processing surplus crops into products like gari protect my farm income when market prices are low?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ nibii tamɔ gari lɛ buɔ miŋmɔ mli shika ni mináa lɛ he be mli ni jara nɔ jara baa shi lɛ?

english: During bumper harvests, market prices for raw food drop significantly because everyone is selling fresh produce at once. Transforming raw crops into non-perishable goods allows you to hold your stock without spoilage and sell later when market demand and prices go back up.
ga: Yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli lɛ, niyenii ni ahoko lɛ jara eba shi waa. Ejaakɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ hɔ̃ɔ nibii heei yɛ be kome mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni akwɛɛɛ mli lɛ tsake nibii ni fiteee lɛ, ehaa okɛtoɔ nibii ahe ni efiteee. ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli kɛ́ jarayeli nibii kɛ jara tee hiɛ ekoŋŋ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, a vital nutrient in the soil, or that the roots are standing in too much water. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves regain their green color so the plant can make food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii.

english: Why does my corn cob have missing grains and gaps when I harvest it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmɔji lɛ amli dumɔwui kɛ ŋmeii bɛ mli beni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Missing grains happen when the plant does not get enough water during its flowering stage. If the corn silk dries out from heat before pollen touches it, those specific kernels fail to grow on the cob.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa siliki lɛ gĩ kɛjɛ la mli dani pollen lɛ kɛ lɛ kpe lɛ, ŋmãa dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my corn stalks grow thin and fall over easily when wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ?

english: Corn stalks become weak and thin when seeds are planted too close together or when the soil lacks potassium. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and sunlight to build strong, thick stalks.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe feɔ mlɛo kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo kɛ́ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hulu la ni baaha etsɔ tso ni mli wa ni mli wa.

english: Why do my maize plants die when rainwater sits on my farm for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gboiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When water covers the roots for too long, it suffocates them, causing the roots to rot and the plant to wilt and die.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ha shishifãi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ebaaha okɛ ohe awo mli Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni tso lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ.

english: Why does my land produce less corn when I plant corn on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo be mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Corn takes the same nutrients out of the soil every season. Planting corn in the same spot continuously exhausts the soil and builds up crop diseases; rotating with legumes like groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Abele jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni eyaa nɔ ekɛ helai baa tsei anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii atsake lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds make my corn plants look weak even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ewo amɛmli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your corn. Clearing weeds early ensures the fertilizer feeds your corn instead of the unwanted plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-ŋmãa lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ aha ŋmãa lɛ moŋ fe tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ.

english: Corn is fully mature when the outer leaves on the cob turn completely brown and dry, and the kernels are hard enough that your fingernail cannot easily press into them.
ga: Abɛi lɛ eda kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi kwraa. Ni dumɔwui lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa akɛ onine nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛmli mlɛo.

english: Why does my harvested corn turn black or moldy when I store it in my house or warehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mikɛto mishia loo nitoohe lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested corn contains invisible moisture inside the grains. If you store it before drying it thoroughly in the sun, trapped wetness creates heat and fungus (mold) that ruins the entire store.
ga: Abele ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni anaaa ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛto dani egbi yɛ hulu lɛ mli lɛ, Trapped wetness lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ (fungus) baa ni fiteɔ shwapo muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do small insects eat up my stored corn even when I stored clean grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni he tse toɔ?

english: Insects like weevils often lay tiny, hidden eggs inside the corn kernels while the crop is still in the field. Warm storage conditions cause these eggs to hatch into bugs that eat the grain from the inside out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ wɔji bibii. Akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ haa nɛkɛ wɔji nɛɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: Why do corn kernels become smaller and harder as I dry them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ mikɛ hulu lɛ fɔ̃ amɛmli lɛ?

english: Fresh corn is full of water weight. As the sun dries the crop, moisture evaporates from the grain, leaving behind solid starch that shrinks the kernel and makes it hard enough to store without spoiling.
ga: Abɛi ŋmɔŋ eyi kɛ nu shwiili. Kɛ hulu lɛ gĩ tsei lɛ Fɛ̃i baajɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Ashiɔ starch ko ni wa ni haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛwaa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto ni amɛfiteee.
