english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight when they are small. Planting taller crops like plantains or shade trees alongside them creates a canopy that protects delicate cocoa leaves from burning and helps keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Tsei kakadaji tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when rainwater sits in my field for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nugbɔ nu ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Maize roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water covers the field for too long, it drowns the roots, preventing them from taking up essential nutrients like nitrogen, which causes the leaves to lose their dark green color.
ga: Abɛi shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu ha ŋmɔ ko nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni no haaa amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni no haa baai lɛ ahe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why does my cassava plant have thick green leaves and big branches but produces very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ niji wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava receives too much rich nitrogen from the soil, it puts all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of sending food down to feed and expand the tubers below.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsu niyenii kɛya shi koni ekwɛ ni ewo bulbs yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why do the yellow flowers on my pepper plants drop off to the ground before turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani amɛfeɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from sudden heat or drought. The plant sheds its flowers to save water and energy so that the rest of the plant can survive the harsh weather.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na trukaa hulutsoo loo hɔmɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Bɔni afee ni tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa amli.

english: How can I tell if my yellowing crop leaves are caused by insects or by bad soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ jɛ kooloi loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii hewɔ?

english: Insect damage usually leaves visible holes, bites, or sticky patches on scattered leaves, while nutrient deficiency causes a clean, widespread yellow pattern across entire leaves or whole rows of plants without any insect marks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ kɛ bu, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii ni kpɛtɛɔ baai ni egbɛ eshwã lɛ baa. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ haa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni he tse lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei lɛ ahe baai loo tsei lɛ akutsei muu fɛɛ amli ni ŋmeii ko kwraa bɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves high into the air to catch maximum sunlight. Sunlit leaves produce the energy needed to send nutrients underground to swell the yam tuber.
ga: Shishitoo mla he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Baai ni hulu lɛ ewo mli lɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya shikpɔŋ shishi koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ amli alɛɛ.

english: Black pod rot is caused by a tiny fungus that travels through rain splashes. High humidity and trapped air around overcrowded branches create a moist environment where the fungus quickly grows and destroys the pods.
ga: Fungi bibii kɛ pods diji ni egbo baa. gbɛfaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi amli Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe Niji ni eyi obɔ tsɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ waa baa. Fuji lɛ daa oya ni ebaanyɛ efite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How does planting beans or cowpeas together with my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Te ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa ni mikɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ baadu lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen fertilizer straight out of the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, giving free plant food to the neighboring maize.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ naa tsei niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy winds right when the bunch is getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli kɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ aniji jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots near the surface of the soil rather than deep roots. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, the plant becomes top-heavy and needs wooden props to support the weight against strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ bafee tsii Tso lɛ baafee tsiimɔ ni ebaabi ni akɛ tsei awo mli koni ekɛfi tsiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up tightly and stop growing new branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa niji heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies that feed on leaf sap and spread plant diseases. The feeding damages the leaf veins, causing them to wrinkle and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies, ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei helai amɛshwãa lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Niyenii ni ayeɔ lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii baa ni etsĩɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops dry up fast when I plant them near certain big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ midu yɛ tsei wuji komɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Some tree species have deep and aggressive root systems that act like heavy water pumps, sucking up large amounts of soil water and leaving very little moisture for nearby crops.
ga: Tsei komɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ pɔmp ni tsiimɔ yɔɔ mli. Ejieɔ nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know if a wild tree growing near my farm boundary is harmful to my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji koo mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ he lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui?

english: A tree is harmful if it steals too much soil moisture, blocks essential sunlight, or acts as a breeding site that attracts and hides destructive crop pests.
ga: Tsei yɛ oshara kɛji amɛju shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo. hulu hebuu ni he hiaa lɛ loo etsu nii akɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ ni ekɛ amɛ teeɔ.

english: Why do my leafy vegetables wilt quickly when growing close to large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Large trees require huge quantities of water to survive, and their wide-spreading roots outcompete shallow-rooted vegetable crops for moisture in the topsoil.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia tsei ni edara lɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi. Ni amɛshishifãi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ feɔ aduawai ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do insects always attack my crops as soon as new leaves start sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji baai heei je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Young sprouting leaves are soft, tender, and rich in nutrients and moisture, making them much easier for insects to chew and feed on compared to tough, older leaves.
ga: Baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe yɛ mlɛo ni niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa kooloi bibii akɛ amɛaaye ni amɛye kɛ akɛto baai ni egbɔ ni wa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the leaves on my plants curl up with small insects hiding inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni kooloi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Ani okɛ ohe ewo mli?

english: Certain pests damage leaf tissue as they feed, causing the leaf to roll or fold around them to create a protected shelter against rain, strong sun, and predators.
ga: Kooloi komɛi fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe loo amɛbɔleɔ amɛhe. Koni afee abobaahe kɛjɛ nugbɔ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do tiny bugs suddenly show up in huge numbers when fresh shoots open on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii jeɔ kpo babaoo beni ŋmeii heei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Many insect pests lay eggs that are timed to hatch precisely when fresh plant shoots appear, giving the newborn pests immediate access to soft food.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo fɔɔ amɛwui kɛ be pɔtɛɛ ni amɛwoɔ amɛwui beni tsei ahe ŋmeii heei jeɔ kpo lɛ. Enɛ haa kooloi heei ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ naa niyenii ni mli jɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do I see thick lines of ants marching all over my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? Minyiɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Ants gather on crops to feed on a sugary liquid called honeydew, which is produced by sap-sucking insects like aphids and mealybugs feeding on your plants.
ga: Akpɔlɔi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛye nu ni mli ewo sugar ni atsɛɔ lɛ nectar. Kplukai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids kɛ mealybugs ni yeɔ otsei lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ amɛ.

english: Are ants on my crop leaves directly damaging the plant or are they attracted by something else?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ miifite tso lɛ tɛ̃ɛ loo nibii krokomɛi gbalaa amɛ?

english: Ants usually do not eat the plant itself; instead, their presence indicates that sap-sucking pests are on the plant, as ants actively protect these pests in exchange for sweet honeydew.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii yeee tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ enɛ lɛ, amɛhe ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii buɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkɛtsake ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ.

english: How do crawling caterpillars on my plant leaves turn into flying insects?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei ko ni shwieɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmei ni foɔ?

english: Insects go through a process called metamorphosis, where a crawling pest feeds on leaves, enters a resting pupa stage, and then changes into a flying adult moth, butterfly, or beetle.
ga: Kplukai tsɔɔ gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ metamorphosis lɛ mli. kɛtsɔ kooloi ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ anɔ Eboteɔ pupa hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ mli No sɛɛ lɛ etsakeɔ efeɔ ŋmei ni eda ni foɔ, ŋmei, loo ladybug.

english: Why do I find hard, tiny shells or webs stuck to the undersides of my leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni wa loo ŋmeii ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Those hard shells or webs are protective cocoons or egg sacs where insects stay safe while transforming from young larvae into full-grown adult pests.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni wa lɛ ji ŋmeii loo ŋmeii kotokui ni kooloi bibii lɛ hiɔ mli shweshweeshwe beni amɛtsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli kɛyaa ŋmeii bibii ni eda lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which acts like food for green foliage. Applying a balanced nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or adding well-rotted manure will help the plants green up and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛha tsei lɛ ahe baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ Kɛ akɛ nitrogen ni ja tamɔ urea tsu nii loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Is it better to spread fertilizer on top of the soil or bury it near my crop roots?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaashɛrɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo afu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ?

english: Burying fertilizer a few centimeters into the soil near the plant root zone is best. If left on top, heat and bright sunshine will evaporate the nutrients, and heavy rain can wash them away before the crop can drink them.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛntimitai fioo komɛi awo sũ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ nɔ lɛ Dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii anu amɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers say I should plant my cassava stems at an angle instead of straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni adu lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a 45-degree slant encourages the roots to grow deeper and spread out evenly, making the plant produce larger tubers that are much easier to pull up during harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ odu o-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ 45-degree angle mli lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ bulbs wuji ni ejiemɔ mlɛo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant again during the next major season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahere dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli ni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni he hiaa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to buy new hybrid seeds every season. Seeds saved from a hybrid harvest lose their vigor, resulting in weak plants, smaller cobs, and a much lower yield in the next crop.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid daa be. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ hybrid ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ Cob lɛ ji bibioo. kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before growing any small peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani eduɔ pepper bibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they feel stressed by extreme midday heat or lack of water. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulching around the roots helps the plants hold onto their flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo nu ni bɛ lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why does my cowpea crop grow mostly leaves but very few pods when planted during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ baai babaoo shi ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Too much water makes cowpeas focus all their energy on growing stems and leaves instead of flowers. Planting cowpeas toward the end of the rainy season encourages them to set flowers and fill pods properly.
ga: Nu babaoo haa tsina ŋmei kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii kɛ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔi. Kɛ́ adu tsina ŋmeii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I leave plantain trees or tall shade trees on my new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi dumɔwui loo tsei kakadaji yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch easily in strong sunlight. Plantain trees provide temporary shade and moisture, acting like natural umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow large enough to protect themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa oya. Dumɔwui haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli kɛ fɛ̃i. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kakao tso lɛ daa bɔ ni sa ni ebuɔ ehe he.

english: What is causing small holes in my cabbage leaves and how do I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ kaabeji baai anɔ Ni te ooofee tɛŋŋ otsi naa?

english: Holes are usually caused by tiny caterpillars eating the leaves. You can protect your cabbages by regularly picking caterpillars off by hand or spraying a natural remedy like crushed neem seed extract mixed with water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu baa. Obaanyɛ obu o-cabbage lɛ he kɛtsɔ oniji ni okɛbaajie ŋmeii lɛ daa lɛ nɔ. Aloo okɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛi tamɔ nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ neem dumɔwui ni atswa mli ni akɛ nu efutu mli lɛ afɔ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds cause my yam tubers to stay small even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi sweet potato tubers lɛ feɔ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds steal the plant food, water, and sunlight that your yams need to grow. Even with good rain, if weeds surround your crop, the yam roots will not get enough nutrients to expand into large tubers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ tsei aniyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa o-sweet potato lɛ koni ekwɛ̃. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ Shi kɛji jwɛi bɔle onibii ahe hu? Sweet potato shishifãi lɛ naaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: How can I tell if my soil has enough moisture before I plant my vegetable seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ fa bɔ ni sa dani madu aduawai dumɔwui?

english: Squeeze a handful of topsoil into a ball in your hand. If it holds its shape without dripping water and breaks apart gently when you poke it, your soil has ideal moisture for seeds to germinate.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ fioo ko ni okɛfee bɔɔlu yɛ onine mli. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni ekɛ nu shwieee shi ni egbɛɔ eshwaa blɛoo. Beni okɛwoɔ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni sa koni odumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under strong sunlight. Shade trees act like umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting young cocoa from harsh heat until their roots are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The virus stops the plant from making enough food, which shrinks the leaves and causes the tubers underground to stay small.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Virus lɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why are there holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hidden inside the tops of the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii Mine lɛ yɛ bu ni akɛtee tso lɛ yiteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Your maize is likely infested with Fall Armyworms. These caterpillars feed on the young, tender leaves of maize, and if they are not treated early, they can ruin the growing tip and destroy the whole harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ emɔ o-ŋmã lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Ni kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ mra lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the plant make food, which travels down to grow big, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni fã gbɛ kɛba shi koni eyadu sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii

english: If you leave too many suckers growing around one main plantain stem, they will all fight for the same water and nutrients in the ground, causing every plant to produce smaller and weaker bunches.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ, single main trunk Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei fɛɛ woɔ tsei niji bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts help improve my soil for maize next season?
ga: Te ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull natural nitrogen out of the air and store it in their roots. When the groundnut crop is harvested, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop, like maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei tsei Ni nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni akɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmei.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape from the tip down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛ naagbee kɛba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tip and moves down the center usually means your maize lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main nutrient that gives plants their deep green color and helps them grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaa ni eyaa shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely high temperatures, dry soil, or a sudden lack of water. Without stable moisture, the plant drops flowers to save its own life.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ nɔ ko tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni bɛ trukaa lɛ kpe. Kɛji hulutsoo be fɛɛ be bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why do my sweet pepper fruits develop dark, soft, rotten patches at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell peppers lɛ yɛ okadii ni tsuɔ, ni yɔɔ blɛoo, ni egbo yɛ shishi dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium inside the growing fruit. It usually happens when watering is uneven, preventing the plant roots from absorbing calcium consistently.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium daa.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard and woody if I leave them in the farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: As cassava plants get very old, they stop storing soft starch in their tubers and instead build tough woody fibers. Harvesting cassava at the right time ensures the roots stay soft and easy to cook.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ egbɔ waa lɛ Amɛbaakpa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛyitsei amli lɛ. ni afee tso mli tsɔi ni wa moŋ Kasava ni akpaa yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehoɔmɔ waaa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight and dry winds. They require temporary shade plants like plantains or shade trees to protect them and keep the soil moist until their leaves and branches grow large enough to shade themselves.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo, koni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni amɛha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi amɛbaai kɛ amɛniji lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha hulutsoo.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungal disease that spreads quickly in dark, wet, and cold conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to allow sunlight and airflow into the farm, clearing weeds, and removing infected pods helps protect healthy pods.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Niji ni fa fe nine ni aaafolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli, jwɛi ni ajieɔ, kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Yellowing leaves that start at the tip and form a yellow 'V' pattern usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Applying well-decomposed animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help the maize regain its green color and yield healthy cobs.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni feɔ ‘V’ ŋmɔŋ lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmei lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize stalks have small holes with powdery sawdust coming out of them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmei ni afee lɛ powder miije kpo?

english: Small holes with powdery waste indicate stem borer caterpillars are feeding inside the stalk. Planting early at the beginning of the rainy season and applying safe insect control early in the crop's growth prevents these pests from destroying the plant from the inside.
ga: Buji bibii ni ashikiŋsha bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ miiye nii yɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu nii mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli, ni akudɔ kooloi bibii lɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ mra mli lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite tso lɛ kɛjɛ emli.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and lacks potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing leaves instead of expanding its root tubers. Using balanced soil nutrients and avoiding excessive nitrogen encourages thicker tuber growth.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo ni potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shishifãi. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ nitrogen babaoo ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ baawo bulbs ni mli wa lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to catch light and convert it into food for the growing underground tubers. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and increasing overall yield.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛmɔ la lɛ ni amɛtsɔ niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni miida lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ baa helai anaa ni ehaa yibiiwoo fɛɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to compete with the main plant for water and soil nutrients, leading to small plantain bunches. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main mother plant to produce a big, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ abɔi nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni kɛ dumɔwui bibii baa Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri ni ji nyɛ lɛ awo dumɔwui wuji ni tsii.

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit, usually due to uneven watering. Keeping the soil steadily moist helps the plant transport calcium from the roots into the growing fruits.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni faaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these insects early with organic neem oil or recommended sprays prevents leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ. Nibii nɛɛ ahe nitsumɔ mra Kɛtsɔ organic neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akafite baa lɛ.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing wide leaves but refusing to form a hard, tight ball?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baai ni mli kwɔ shi efeŋ bɔɔlu ni wa ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbage requires cool root conditions, steady water, and space to form a tight head. If the plants are crowded or suffer from heat stress and dry soil, they will stay open and produce loose leaves instead of solid heads.
ga: Cabbage biɔ shishifãi ni mli ejɔ, nu ni damɔ shi, kɛ he ni ebaanyɛ efee yitsei ni mli ewo muji. Kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ amli eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi babaoo loo amɛmiina dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ, Tso lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni ebaana baai ni etse ehe yɛ yitsei ni wa najiaŋ.

english: How do I get plantain seeds to start planting on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná plantain dumɔwui ni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Plantains do not produce seeds. Instead of seeds, plantains are grown by using suckers, which are the small shoots that sprout from the base of an existing mother plant.
ga: Plantains lɛ wooo dumɔwui. yɛ dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii najiaŋ lɛ Akɛ suckers, ni ji ŋmeii bibii tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ Plantains. ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ nyɛ tso ni yɔɔ momo lɛ shishi

english: Do I need to buy new planting materials every year to keep my plantain farm going?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mahe nibii heei ni akɛduɔ nii daa afi koni mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ aya nɔ?

english: No, you do not need to buy new planting material every season. Because plantain plants continuously produce new shoots at their base, you can keep replanting using your existing crops.
ga: Dabi, ehe ehiaaa ni ohé nibii heei ni akɛduɔ nii daa be. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, plantains lɛ baawo ŋmeii heei be fɛɛ be. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ tsei ni yɔɔ momo lɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my plantain plant stay alive for so long even when I don't give it much attention?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ hi shi be kakadaŋŋ nɛkɛ be mli ni ehiɛɛɛ shi lɛ? Ni mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ emaaa nɔ tsɔ?

english: Plantain plants are naturally hardy and resilient. The old plant does not easily die out completely because its root system keeps producing fresh shoots to take its place.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ahe wa ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe. Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ gbooo oya. Ejaakɛ eshishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ ewoɔ ŋmeii heei ni baaye enajiaŋ.

english: How many bunches of fruit can I harvest from a single plantain stem?
ga: Yibii enyiɛ manyɛ makpa kɛjɛ plantain kome mli?

english: A single plantain stem produces just one bunch of plantains in its lifecycle. After it bears that bunch, the main stem finishes its work, and a new shoot takes over to produce the next bunch.
ga: Plantain tso kome pɛ baawo plantain kuu kome pɛ yɛ ewala be mli. Beni ewo nakai kuu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, agbe shaft titri lɛ naa. Ni ŋmeii heei baa koni amɛfee kuu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What happens to the plantain plant after I harvest the fruit bunch?
ga: Mɛni baa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ beni mikpa aduawai akui lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Once you harvest the bunch, the main stem's work is done, but the plant leaves behind young shoots at the base that will grow up to produce future harvests.
ga: Kɛji okpa ŋmei kome lɛ, agbe nitsumɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. Shi tso lɛ baashi ŋmeii bibii yɛ eshishigbɛ ni baakwɛ̃ koni ewo yibii wɔsɛɛ.

english: Does the way I cut down my plantain plant during harvest affect my future yields?
ga: Ani bɔ ni mifoɔ midumɔwui lɛ amli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ saa wɔsɛɛ be mli yibiiwoo lɛ he?

english: Yes, cutting plantains requires skill. If you cut the main plant carelessly, you can damage the young shoot growing beside it, which means you won't get a healthy new plant for the next harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains ŋmɔmɔ biɔ ŋaa. Kɛji ofo tso titri lɛ mli yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ Obaanyɛ ogbe tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ onine shɛɛɛ tsei heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ kɛha kpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why am I getting smaller plantain bunches on my farm after the first harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ plantain tsei bibii anɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If you do not manage and prune the new shoots growing around the base of the plant, they will crowd each other and compete for strength, leading to smaller bunches.
ga: Kɛji okwɛɛɛ ni ofolɔko ŋmeii heei ni bɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ, amɛbaabua amɛhe naa ni amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hewalɛ. ni kɛ tso bibioo ko baa

english: How much work do I need to put into my plantain farm to get good harvests?
ga: Mɔdɛŋbɔɔ enyiɛ esa akɛ mabɔ yɛ mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni maná yibii kpakpai?

english: Plantains reward basic care well. With just a little regular effort to manage the young shoots and clear the field, your plants will produce strong, healthy bunches.
ga: Plantains woɔ shishijee kwɛmɔ kpakpa he nyɔmɔ. Kɛtsɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ fioo nɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okwɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ anɔ ni ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Otso lɛ baawo niji ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is planting a large plantain farm a profitable business for a farmer in Ghana?
ga: Ani plantain ŋmɔji wuji ni aduɔ lɛ ji nitsumɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he kɛha okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ?

english: Yes, planting plantains in large quantities is very rewarding financially. Because it is a major food staple with constant market demand, expanding your crop yields good money.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ he yɛ shika gbɛfaŋ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Ejaakɛ eji niyenii ni jara wa ni mɛi biɔ daa. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii ni ooogbɛ oshwa lɛ woɔ sɛɛnamɔi.

english: Is plantain a difficult crop for a standard farmer to manage compared to other crops?
ga: Ani plantains ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa kɛha okwaafoi ni yɔɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ lɛ akɛ amɛaakwɛ nɔ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe?

english: Plantain is generally easy to maintain because of its natural toughness, but it requires basic skill in selecting and managing the right shoots to keep the farm producing well over time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains lɛ akwɛmɔ waaa yɛ bɔ ni amɛhe wa ha lɛ hewɔ. Shi eheɔ shishijee ŋaa koni anyɛ ahala ŋmeii ni sa ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ŋmɔ lɛ aya nɔ awo yibii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: If armyworms start eating my young maize leaves, does that mean my whole farm is ruined and I should clear it?
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bɔi mi-baby corn baai lɛ yeli Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ efite ni esa akɛ majie kɛjɛ mli?

english: Not necessarily. Maize plants are quite resilient; caterpillars usually eat the foliage, but if the growing center of the plant is unharmed, the crop can bounce back and still produce cobs for you to harvest.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Abɛi tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ baai. Shi kɛji akɛ eyeee tso lɛ dalɛ he lɛ awui pɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aku amɛsɛɛ ni amɛwo cob lolo ni obaakpa.

english: Can my maize crops really grow back after caterpillars eat most of their foliage early in the season?
ga: Ani mi-abele lɛ baanyɛ ada diɛŋtsɛ beni ŋmeii lɛ eye baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, as long as the central leaf shoot inside the stem isn't completely destroyed, the maize plant will continue to put out new green leaves and recover.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ efiteee kwraa. Abɛi tsei lɛ baaya nɔ akwɛ̃ baai heei ni eŋɔli ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ.

english: If insects attack my maize farm, will I still get anything to take home at harvest time?
ga: Kɛji kooloi bibii tutua mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ Ani maná nɔ ko lolo yɛ shia yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: In most cases, yes. Pest infestations usually lower your overall yield rather than wiping out the crop entirely, so you can still harvest a reasonable amount of grain.
ga: Yɛ bei babaoo mli lɛ, hɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ fɛɛ baa shi moŋ fe ni amɛaajie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ kɛya. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okpa dumɔwui abɔ ni sa lolo.

english: What should I do to help my maize plants recover after caterpillars have damaged the leaves?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni maye mabua mi-corn tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii efite baai lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Giving the plants good soil nutrients like fertilizer and ensuring they have enough water gives them the energy needed to sprout fresh leaves and form cobs.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpai ni haa tsei, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nɔmimaa akɛ tsei lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ baai heei ni efee ŋmeii.

english: Why do agricultural officers keep advising us to plant specific recommended maize varieties instead of my traditional saved seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔdu ŋmãa srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ ni ajieɔ yi akɛ wɔdu lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu shishijee ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ

english: Recommended varieties are specially tested and selected because they handle local pest attacks better, withstand dry spells, and produce higher yields than older saved seeds.
ga: Aka tsofai srɔtoi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ahala amɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛkpee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ atuatsemɔ naa jogbaŋŋ. Enyɛɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ anaa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui momo ni ato lɛ

english: How do I know if a new maize variety will do well against pests on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa henɔ hee ko tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ eshiɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Officers test these varieties in local soils to make sure they have strong stems and tough leaves that resist damage from pests like fall armyworms.
ga: Amralofoi lɛ kaa nɛkɛ tsoi srɔtoi nɛɛ amɛkwɛɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛyɛ tsei ni wa kɛ baai ni wa ni nyɛɔ amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ nibii ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ fall armyworm lɛ.

english: Does planting an improved maize variety mean pests will completely leave my farm alone?
ga: Ani ŋmãa henɔi ni atsake lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baatsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii baashi miŋmɔ lɛ mli pɛ?

english: No, pests may still feed on the crop, but improved varieties are tough enough to survive the feeding and still give you a harvest at the end of the season.
ga: Dabi, ekolɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ lolo. Shi henɔi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ niyenii mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii lolo yɛ be lɛ naagbee.

english: Why do armyworm caterpillars always tend to hide inside the leafy top part of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: They hide in the central funnel because it keeps them cool and safe from birds while providing tender, young leaf tissue for them to eat.
ga: Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋshɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli ejaakɛ ehaa amɛhe jɔɔ ni okpoi nyɛɛɛ amɛye amɛhe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛ baa bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛyeɔ.

english: When is the best time of day for me to walk through my farm to check if worms are attacking my maize?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana kɛji ŋmeii miitutua mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Check your farm early in the morning or late in the afternoon when caterpillars come out of hiding to feed on the leaves.
ga: Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi loo shwane mli beni ŋmeii jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛtee lɛ koni amɛbaye baai lɛ.

english: Does planting my maize early when the rains start help reduce pest damage on my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni aduɔ mra beni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, early planting allows your maize to grow strong before armyworm populations build up to large numbers later in the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔ mra Ye obua o-ŋmã lɛ ni edara waa dani cutworm lɛ ayibɔ aya hiɛ yɛ be lɛ naagbee.

english: What is the difference between buying improved seeds like Santein corn and just saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe tamɔ Santein ŋmãa ni miheɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Improved seed varieties are specially bred to produce higher yields, mature faster, and resist local pests or dry spells better than saved seeds, which gradually lose their strength and quality over seasons.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo, amɛshwere oya ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo hulutsoo be lɛ fe dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ, ni fiofio lɛ amɛhewalɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ baa shi yɛ bei lɛ amli.

english: Why do my corn yields get smaller every time I plant on the same piece of land without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be ni madu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Crops pull specific nutrients out of the earth every season. Without resting the land, rotating crops, or adding organic manure, the soil gets exhausted and cannot feed new plants properly.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛji shikpɔŋ hejɔɔmɔ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli tsakemɔ loo akɛ organic fertilizer fata he Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni enyɛɛɛ eye ebua tsei heei jogbaŋŋ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, acting like a natural food supply that helps neighboring maize plants grow stronger without extra fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa kroko afata he.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop is starving for nitrogen in the soil, or that waterlogged soil around the roots is suffocating the plant so it cannot take up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo shikpɔŋ ni nu ebɔle he lɛ Shishifãi lɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni enyɛŋ eŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to tall, weak stalks that produce very small ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmãa toi bibii waa lɛ baa.

english: How can I keep harvested corn in my barn without insects like weevils destroying it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato ŋmɔ mli ni kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii efiteee lɛ?

english: Drying the corn properly until the kernels are hard, and then storing them in special airtight (hermetic) bags suffocates insects and prevents moisture from causing destructive mold.
ga: Abɛi ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛtoɔ kotoku krɛdɛɛ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (vacuum) mli ni haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ afite.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds now that the rainy season changes every year?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui? Akɛni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ tsakeɔ daa afi hewɔ?

english: Rather than relying on fixed calendar months, plant only after the soil has received steady, soaking rainfall for a few days so the seeds have enough moisture to germinate and build strong early roots.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ohe afɔ̃ kalanda nyɔŋ pɔtɛɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Dumɔ pɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa ni edɔ gbii 2-3 bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why is it critical to clear weeds from my crop field within the first few weeks of planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛduɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and will steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight before the crop gets a chance to establish itself, permanently reducing your final yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛbaaju nu, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛma shi. Enɛ baaha onaagbee yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi kwraa.

english: Is it better to use animal manure or chemical fertilizer on my maize field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ kooloi aŋmeii loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ baatsu nii yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli?

english: Chemical fertilizer gives plants a quick, direct boost of food, while animal manure improves the soil's structure so it holds water longer. Combining both gives the best balance of fast growth and healthy soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ naa niyenii kpakpa tɛ̃ɛ ni yaa oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kooloi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni ehi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ fata he lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ yaa oya kɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ ekome ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up into tight tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism where the plant rolls its leaves to expose less surface area to the sun, preventing moisture from evaporating too quickly during extreme heat.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. He ni tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la akashɛ amɛhiɛ fioo lɛ. Enɛ ji koni ŋmɔtɔ akafo oya tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow and drying up before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: This usually happens when your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to stay green and strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the growing season helps prevent this yellowing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts on the same plot where I harvested maize last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ mli nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Maize takes away a lot of nutrients from the soil, while groundnuts put nitrogen back into the soil naturally through their roots. Rotating maize with groundnuts feeds your soil and helps reduce pest problems.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abɛi/ŋmei tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai baa shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt and die even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by a soil disease like bacterial wilt or root rot that damages the roots so they cannot take up water. Removing affected plants right away and avoiding planting peppers in that same spot for a few seasons stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ muawai loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ nu Jiemɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ooodu yɛ he kome lɛ he afii enyɔ loo etɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How can I tell if a chemical medicine will actually cure the disease on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofai ni akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ baatsa hela ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Different plant medicines target different problems—some only kill insects, while others treat fungal diseases or bacteria. Show a damaged leaf to an extension officer to identify the exact cause so you buy the right approved treatment.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tso mli lɛ eko fɛɛ eko kɛ ehiɛ fɔɔ naagba sɔrɔto ko nɔ. Henɔi komɛi gbeɔ kooloi bibii pɛ. yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi tsaa tsɛŋemɔ helai loo bacteria helai. Tsɔɔmɔ baai ni efite lɛ otsɔɔ extension official koni ena nɔ ni kɛba koni onyɛ ohe tsofa ni sa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in high moisture and deep shade. Pruning overhead branches to let in sunlight and clearing off infected pods regularly helps keep the disease away.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli kwɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Niji ni yɔɔ yiteŋ lɛ ni aaafolɔ koni hulu lɛ ashɛ nɔ, ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni hela aba.

english: Why are small worms eating my cowpea pods just when they start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-cowpea ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: These are pod borer caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid inside the flowers by small moths. Spraying approved biopesticides or neem seed extract right when flowers begin to open protects young pods before the worms get inside.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji pod borers ni ŋmeii bibii ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛwui amli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii loo neem dumɔwui amli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ beni fɔfɔi lɛ jeɔ shishi pɛ kɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe dani ŋmeii lɛ abote mli.

english: How do I select the best cassava stems to cut and plant for a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tso ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mafolɔ ni madu koni maná ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: Choose stems from healthy mature plants that are 8 to 18 months old. Cut your planting pieces from the middle section of the stem because those buds sprout much stronger than the soft top or the hard base.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 18 lɛ ashishifãi. Kpɔ̃ɔ fã ni miida lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ daraa waa fe ŋmeii bibii loo shishitoo ni wa lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need full sunlight to produce the food that grows big tubers underground. Lifting the vines on stakes helps leaves catch more sunlight and keeps them off damp soil where diseases spread.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ́ akwɛ bulb lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, ni no ji he ni helai shwereɔ yɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot or when the soil dries out completely. Keeping the soil evenly moist with regular watering and mulching around the plant base helps hold the flowers on the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ nɔ. Shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Which type of plantain sucker should I dig up to start a new farm?
ga: Mɛɛ dumɔwui sucker esa akɛ mafo koni maje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Look for 'sword suckers', which have narrow, blade-like leaves and a broad, heavy base underground. They grow much faster and produce larger bunches than 'water suckers' that have wide leaves but weak roots.
ga: Taomɔ ‘sword shoot’, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tseee ni tamɔ ŋmei kɛ shishitoo ni mli kwɔ ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Amɛdaraa oya kwraa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji fe ‘ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ shi amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants require me to tie them to sticks every week, while my cucumber plants can just grow on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ mi tomato tso lɛ akpɛtɛ tso nine he daa otsi lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mi-tomato tsei lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ pɛ nɔ.

english: Tomatoes have weak stems that can snap under the weight of heavy fruit, and keeping their leaves off the wet soil prevents fungal diseases. Cucumbers can spread on the ground, though trellising them can also improve air flow and fruit quality.
ga: Tomato yɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni baanyɛ akumɔ yɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ ashishi. Ni kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anaa. Abaanyɛ agbɛ kukumba ashwã shikpɔŋ. Shi kukumba ni akwɛɔ lɛ hu haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa aduawai lɛ hu feɔ fɛo.

english: Why do I have to inspect my tomato farm every single morning for insects, but my cassava farm doesn't need daily checking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ mi-tomato ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa leebi koni mana kɛji ŋmeii yɛ mli lɛ? Shi ani ehe miihia ni akwɛ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi?

english: Tomato plants have soft leaves and sweet fruits that attract pests like caterpillars and whiteflies daily. Cassava is a much hardier plant with natural defenses, storing its food underground where pests cannot easily reach it.
ga: Tomato tsei yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni ŋɔɔ ni gbalaa kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ daa gbi. Cassava ji tso ko ni he wa kwraa ni eyɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu. Amɛkɛ niyenii toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi he ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nyɛŋ ashɛ he mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do I need to spend time pinching off the small side branches of my tomato plants every week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be kɛfo tsei niji bibii lɛ amli lɛ? ni ji tomato tsei daa otsi

english: Removing those extra side branches, called suckers, forces the plant to send its water and nutrients into growing larger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on useless extra leaves.
ga: Nakai niji krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ lɛ shoo lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ Enɛ baaha tso lɛ atsu nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ koni ekwɛ̃ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai krokomɛi ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Is there a fast-growing vegetable I can farm in Ghana that doesn't require as much daily attention as tomatoes?
ga: Ani aduawai komɛi yɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni manyɛ madu yɛ Ghana ni biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ daa gbi tamɔ tomato?

english: Cucumbers are a great option because they grow very quickly, often ready to harvest in about 50 to 60 days, and generally require less hand-pruning and daily staking than tomatoes.
ga: Kukumba ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ edaa oya waa. Bei pii lɛ, amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa amɛ yɛ aaafee gbii 50 kɛyashi 60 mli ni bei pii lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ niji akpɛ amɛ ni akɛwo amɛ daa gbi fe tomato.

english: Why do some crops give me food in just two months while others like cocoa take years of work before I see any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi haa mi niyenii yɛ nyɔji enyɔ pɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi tamɔ kookoo heɔ afii babaoo dani minaa nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ?

english: Vegetables like cucumbers or leafy greens spend all their energy on quick leaves and fruit before dying off, whereas tree crops like cocoa must first build deep roots and strong trunks to yield harvests for decades.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ kukumba loo tsei ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai kɛ aduawai ni sɛɛ foɔ oya lɛ anɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ tsei ni tsei tamɔ kookoo lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni wa klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛwo yibii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Why do my cucumber plants seem to dry up and die so quickly after producing just a few harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mikukumba tso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ oya beni ewo yibii fioo pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cucumber plants have a short lifespan by nature. They put almost all their energy into one big push of fruit production and naturally end their lifecycle once that heavy fruiting phase is complete.
ga: Kukumba tsei lɛ hiɔ shi be kuku yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amɛkɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nitsumɔ wulu kome ni tsirɛɔ amɛ koni amɛwo aduawai lɛ ahe nii. Ni egbeɔ ebɔɔ su shihilɛ naa beni egbeɔ yibiiwoo ni tsii lɛ naa lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers say tomato farming requires more money for chemical sprays than growing maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ akɛ tomato dumɔ biɔ shika babaoo ni akɛbaafɔ tsofai anɔ fe ŋmãa dumɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes are delicate and very susceptible to blights, wilts, and heavy insect attacks in Ghana's humid climate, requiring regular protective spraying, whereas maize is hardier and faces fewer continuous disease threats.
ga: Tomatoi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni sɛɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ, tsɛŋemɔ hela kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ atutua amɛ yɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. ni biɔ ni afɔse tsofa ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ daa Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa wa waa ni ekɛ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ kpeee.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark, rotten spots at the bottom if I miss watering them for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato yibii lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɔɔ kɛji mikɛ nu shwieee nɔ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: That condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when uneven watering stops the plant from taking up calcium from the soil, causing the bottom of the developing fruit to break down.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai shihilɛ lɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli be fɛɛ be lɛ tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaná calcium ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ shishigbɛ fãa.

english: Can I plant tomatoes and cucumbers right next to each other in the same garden plot during the rainy season?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tomato kɛ kukumba yɛ abɔɔ kome mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: It is risky because both crops trap moisture around their leaves and are vulnerable to similar fungal diseases, which can easily spread between them in high humidity if spaced too closely.
ga: Oshara ko yɛ ejaakɛ tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ amɛbaai lɛ ahe lɛ, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei nɛɛ ateŋ mlɛo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo kɛji akɛ amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crop plants need to grow green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted animal manure helps restore their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su ni ji eŋɔli kɛ dalɛ kpakpa aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that catch nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When grown together or rotated with maize, they naturally feed the soil and boost your maize harvest without requiring extra expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛfata he loo akɛ ŋmã tsake lɛ Amɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛye amɛbua ni okɛ ŋmã ni okpa lɛ aya hiɛ ni tsofai ni jara wa babaoo he ehiaaa.

english: Why do I need to cut tall poles to stake my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni mikɛwo mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam leaves need full sunlight to make the energy required to grow big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines up into the light and improves air flow, which prevents leaf diseases and produces much larger yam roots.
ga: Hulu ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa la lɛ he ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ tsiɔ baa helai anaa ni ehaa sweet potato shishifãi lɛ daraa kwraa.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster and survive dry weather better than my planted crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that have adapted over centuries to survive harsh local soils and low water with deep root systems. Cultivated crops are bred to produce high food yields and need extra care, water, and protection to outgrow wild weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔji ni mli wa ni nu bɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ anɔ. Akwɛɔ tsei koni amɛwo niyenii babaoo. Ni ehe miihia ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ, aha amɛ nu, ni abu amɛhe koni jwɛi lɛ akakwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why are my cocoa trees shedding their flowers and small pods before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani ooogbee shi dani oshɛ dalɛ ni yeɔ emuu he?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers and young pods (often called cherelle wilt) due to water stress during dry spells, lack of nutrients, or attacks by pests like mirids (capsids). Managing tree shade and controlling insect pests helps the tree keep its pods until harvest.
ga: Cocoa tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Tso mli ŋmeii (ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ cherry bush hela) lɛ baa yɛ nu mli haomɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo ŋmeii tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ hewɔ. Tsoi ahe hulutsoo kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant as many maize seeds as possible close together so I can get a bigger harvest from my small land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ lɛ? Bɔni afee ni manyɛ makpa nibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak plants that produce tiny cobs or no cobs at all, whereas proper spacing gives fewer plants the space to yield larger, heavier cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ loo amɛwoɔ ŋmeii kwraa, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: How can I tell if the first rains of the season are enough for me to start sowing my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because the soil underneath is still dry, and a short dry spell afterward will kill germinating seeds. Wait until you get two or three steady, heavy rains that wet the soil deep down before planting your seeds.
ga: Kaadu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi lolo. Ni yɛ be fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gboiɔ. Mɛɛ ni oná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water collects and settles around the roots during heavy rains, or when fungal diseases attack wet soil. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away safely from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutua shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling tightly upward and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛtee ŋwɛi ni amɛfee bibii lɛ?

english: Curling leaves in tomatoes are usually caused by the Tomato Leaf Curl Virus, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects, or by extreme heat and drought stress. Controlling whiteflies early and keeping the soil evenly watered prevents severe leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Tomato Leaf Curl Virus, ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ mli. Whitefly Kudɔmɔ Mra Ni kɛji okwɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ nu awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite baai lɛ waa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers and tiny fruits before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii kɛ aduawai dani eda lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when the weather gets too hot, when watering is inconsistent (going from very dry to very wet), or when insect pests feed on the blossoms. Mulching the ground to keep roots cool and watering regularly helps keep flowers on the plant.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli (kɛjɛ be mli ni egbi waa kɛyashi be mli ni edɔ waa) loo be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli koni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i kɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if the liquid chemical spray or fertilizer I bought at the market is fake or genuine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mihe yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ji amale loo eji anɔkwale?

english: Genuine agro-chemicals in Ghana usually have clear labels with registration numbers from regulatory bodies like the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA), sealed caps, and expiry dates. Fake products often have blurry printing, no batch numbers, unsealed caps, or are sold in unbranded bottles, which can burn your crops or fail to control pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii diɛŋtsɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ yɛ nɔ ni aŋmala nɔ yibɔi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni jɛ nitsumɔhei ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ tamɔ Shihilɛ He Buumɔ Nitsumɔhe (EPA) kɛ Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe (MoFA) lɛ adɛŋ, ni akɛ tsitsii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ewo nɔ. kɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii lɛ Bei pii lɛ, amale nibii lɛ akalaa nɔ ni mli ka shi faŋŋ. Batch nɔmba ko bɛ Seal cap ko bɛ. loo ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ tɔi ni akadiko nɔ lɛ mli Enɛ baanyɛ ashã oŋmɔshi nibii loo enyɛŋ eye kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, or the roots are sitting in too much water after heavy rain. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the plant build green foliage again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo baai eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantain suckers on the same field where I am planting new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn under full sun. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil moist for the young cocoa trees during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from my last maize harvest yield less corn than the new seeds I buy from the agricultural extension store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo fe dumɔwui hee ni mihe kɛjɛ okwaayeli mlilɛɛmɔ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially bred to give strong growth and high yields in their first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special qualities in the next generation, producing smaller cobs and uneven plant growth.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛ dalɛ ni mli wa kɛ yibii babaoo aba yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii kɛ tsei adalɛ ni ejaaa baa.

english: How do I know if the soil is ready for planting immediately after the very first rain of the major season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be ni he hiaa lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: The first rain often wet only the top layer while the deep soil remains dry and hot. It is best to wait for two or three steady rains so the moisture penetrates deep enough, preventing your sown seeds from drying out and dying underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋwɛi fã lɛ pɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ kã he egbi ni edɔ. Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ ofee ji ni omɛ nugbɔshiimɔi fioo komɛi ni nyiɛɔ amɛsɛɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ abote mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui ni adu lɛ akagbi ni amɛkagbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why must I mix chemical concentrates with water before spraying them onto my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsofai ni mli wa futuɔ nu mli dani mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical concentrates are extremely strong in their raw form. Spraying them directly without diluting them in water will scorch and kill your crop leaves instantly instead of safely treating pests or weeds.
ga: Tsofai ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli ewo muji waa yɛ amɛhe ni amɛfee lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni akɛwooo mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashã ni amɛgboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaajie tsɛŋemɔ helai loo jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ shihilɛ mli shweshweeshwe

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot inside the soil before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ nɔ ni mikpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava rot is usually caused by waterlogged soil that does not drain well, combined with soil fungal diseases. Excess water prevents the tubers from breathing, allowing harmful fungi to break down the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni nu hoɔɔɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava fitemɔ baa. kɛ ŋmeii helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fata he Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa yitso lɛ amu. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants drying up and falling off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers stress from extreme weather heat, irregular watering, or a lack of essential nutrients like phosphorus. Without steady moisture and food, the plant sheds its flowers to preserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ha tsei lɛ hao. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ, kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii bɛ be fɛɛ be. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster and stronger than the crop seeds I deliberately planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe dumɔwui ni midu yɛ oshara mli lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are native plants naturally adapted to survive harsh soils and droughts with minimal water. Domesticated crops need special care, proper spacing, and balanced nutrients to outgrow tough local weeds.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔji ni mli wa kɛ hɔmɔ ni nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Shia tsei biɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko. sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni sa bɔni afee ni jwɛi lɛ adara oya fe jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ

english: Why does my farmland turn hard like stone just a few days after the rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ?

english: Soil becomes hard and compacted when it lacks organic matter like decayed leaves and compost. Adding organic material or manure loosens the soil structure, allowing it to hold water longer and letting roots breathe easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni ehaa ehe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔne lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Ehaa nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmuɔ mlɛo

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and dropping off during the hot sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct harsh sunlight on their own. Planting shade crops like plantain or cassava alongside them provides protective leaf shade and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa roots become strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ he kome. Enɛ baabu baai lɛ ahe ni eye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi kookoo shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and the stems staying very thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ hu egbɔjɔ waa lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves and thin stems are a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to build strong leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the maize turn dark green and grow sturdy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ tsei bibii ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni baai ni wa akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmei lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmei ni mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my tomato blossoms falling off the stem before any tomatoes appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani tomato lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or attacks from small insects like thrips. Ensuring consistent watering and mulching the soil helps hold moisture and protect the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvesting between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will know it is time when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Should I plant my maize right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is safer to wait until you get two or three steady rains so the soil holds enough deep moisture. Planting immediately after the first light rain can cause seeds to dry up and die if a dry spell follows.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa. Dumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my yam setts very close together on the same heap?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmeii kome nɔ?

english: When yam setts are planted too close, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients. This results in many small, thin tubers instead of large, healthy yams.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu sweet potatoes ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ kɛhaa nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why are there small holes in my pepper leaves and tiny worms inside the fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ aduawai lɛ amli?

english: These holes and worms are caused by fruit borer caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid by small moths. Plucking and destroying damaged peppers early stops the caterpillars from spreading to the rest of your farm.
ga: Fruit borers ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baa. Peppers ni efite lɛ ajiemɔ mra kɛ amɛhiɛkpatamɔ Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa hei krokomɛi. ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why is my plantain stand producing many small shoots but taking too long to yield fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miikwɛ̃ ŋmeii bibii babaoo shi amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Too many side shoots (suckers) steal water and food away from the main plant. Cutting away most of the extra shoots and leaving only one or two strong ones allows the main plant to focus its energy on producing heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Side shoots (shoots) babaoo tsɔ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni ajieɔ lɛ ni ashiɔ niji kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ haa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa yibii ni tsii ni ewoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I save seeds from my hybrid maize harvest to plant again next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni madu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Saving seeds from hybrid maize usually results in weak plants and a much smaller harvest the following season. It is best to buy fresh certified hybrid seeds every year or use traditional open-pollinated seeds if you plan to save your own.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa bibioo kwraa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi. Aloo kɛ dumɔwui ni agbele naa lɛ atsu nii kɛji oto gbɛjianɔ akɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ obaakwɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ.

english: Weeds steal the plant food, space, and sunlight that your crops need to grow. Clearing weeds while they are still small ensures your crops get all the soil nutrients and water available.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ tsei aniyenii, he ko, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and drying up under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains or cassava next to them acts like a sunshade, keeping the plant cool and preserving soil moisture until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la nyɛŋ ashɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛmasɛi. Etsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo be Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and slender with tiny cobs when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Planting maize with proper spacing ensures every plant receives enough light and food to produce thick stalks and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without setting fruit during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil place heavy stress on pepper plants. The plant drops its flowers to save water and energy so it can stay alive until it gets enough moisture to support fruit growth.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ babaoo baa pepper tsei anɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Enɛ ji koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi kɛyashi amɛbaaná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.
