english: Why do cassava plants shed all their leaves during the dry season, and does it mean the crop is dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbo?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods to reduce water loss. The crop is not dying; it is resting and storing energy inside the roots under the ground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Nibii ni adu lɛ gbooo, ejɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Continuous rain and high humidity create ideal conditions for fungal diseases like black pod to spread. Pruning excess branches lets air and sunlight flow through the farm, which dries out the pods and keeps fungal rot away.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: Why does mixing decomposed leaves or animal manure into my soil keep my crops green longer during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ baai ni egboi loo ŋmeii futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Organic materials like manure and decomposed leaves act like sponges in the dirt. They help the soil retain rainwater for a longer time while slowly feeding essential nutrients to your crop roots.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ kooloi afɔfɔi kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, fiofio lɛ Ehaa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa.

english: Maize feeds heavily on nitrogen in the soil, leaving the ground weak. Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally restoring soil food for your next crop.
ga: Abele haa nitrogen babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ egbɔjɔ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I avoid putting chemical fertilizer on dry soil when it hasn't rained?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔtsi wɔhe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can drink it up. Applying fertilizer on bone-dry soil can burn crop roots or blow away without benefiting the plant.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi tamɔ wu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi lɛ ashã loo amɛfo kɛya, ni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔ ko kwraa baaa tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and yellow even when rain is falling heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than domestic crops and steal nutrients, water, and root space out of the soil before your crop roots can reach them. Clearing weeds early ensures all soil food goes to your crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe shia tsei ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shɛɔ onibii ahe.

english: Why am I advised to pinch off small side shoots growing on my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ

english: Side shoots use up food and energy that the plant could use to make fruit. Removing extra shoots forces the tomato plant to channel its food into growing bigger and healthier tomatoes.
ga: Lateral shoots lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛwo yibii lɛ tsuɔ nii. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, enyɛɔ tomato tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii babaoo amaje koni ekwɛ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because full sunlight burns their sensitive leaves and dries out their small roots. Planting plantains alongside them provides natural shade and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa amɛbaai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa lɛ ni ehaa amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ gĩɔ. Ebaaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the plant's food for leaf growth. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores the healthy green color.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni haa tso lɛ niyenii kɛha baa lɛ dalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops before a heavy rain or after?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli dani nugbɔ nɛ waa loo no sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer after rain when the soil is already moist. Heavy rain right after applying fertilizer will wash it away before the plant roots can drink it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ, be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni awo ŋmɔshi nii lɛ sɛɛ Nu lɛ baaho dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: What makes my pepper fruits rot at the bottom while they are still growing on the plant?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pepper aduawai lɛ miifite yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni edaa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Rot at the bottom of pepper fruits usually happens when the soil lacks calcium or when the plant receives irregular water while the fruit is forming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni baa pepper aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ baa kɛ́ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛ nu ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee nɔ yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: How do fall armyworms cause damage to my maize farm?
ga: Te fall armyworms lɛ miifite mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Fall armyworm caterpillars hide in the central funnel of young maize plants and eat the leaves from the inside out, preventing the plant from growing healthy ears.
ga: Autumn mli ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná toi ni mli wa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant cassava cuttings too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava sticks too close causes their roots to compete for nutrients and water, which results in many small, thin tubers instead of large ones.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha eshishifãi lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa yɛ ŋmeii wuji najiaŋ.

english: Saving hybrid seeds for the next season gives a poor harvest because hybrid seeds lose their strength in the second generation, resulting in weaker plants.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ baaha kpamɔ ni ehiii aba. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso lɛ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Yams are ready to harvest when the leaves and vines stop growing, dry up, and turn brown, showing that all energy has moved into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ kpa dalɛ, amɛgbi, ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ efã kɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why is it important to trim off the extra side branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ tomato tsei aniji ni yɔɔ afã lɛ?

english: Trimming extra side branches helps the tomato plant send all its food and energy into producing bigger fruits rather than growing useless extra leaves.
ga: Niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tomato tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ eniyenii kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ baai ni fa fe nine ni he ehiaaa lɛ

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly right after I clear my farm land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds stay asleep in the dirt for long periods, and clearing the land lets sunlight and air reach them, causing them to sprout immediately.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How do I choose the best seed yams to buy in the market for planting on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala sweet potato dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mahe yɛ jara nɔ koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Select seed yams that are firm, healthy, and free from cuts, rot, or insect holes. Choosing seeds weighing around 200 to 300 grams with visible sprouts ensures they grow quickly into strong plants.
ga: Halamɔ sweet potato dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ, ni mli wa ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni efolɔ, egbo loo kooloi abu bɛ mli. Halamɔ dumɔwui ni tsiimɔ aaafee gram 200 kɛyashi 300 ni dumɔwui ni anaa lɛ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ adara oya ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do some of my planted seed yams take a very long time to sprout while others grow quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu daa oya lɛ?

english: Seed yams go through a natural resting phase called dormancy after harvest. If you plant a yam before its dormancy naturally breaks, or if the soil lacks moisture, it will delay sprouting.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu sweet potato dani dormancy lɛ fite yɛ adebɔɔ naa, loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ Ebaaha ekwɛ̃mɔ asɛɛ afo.

english: How can I stop my seed yams from rotting in the soil before they even grow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Ensure your soil is well-drained and treat any cut seed pieces with clean wood ash or recommended fungicides before planting to seal the cut surfaces against soil disease.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ tso sũ ni he tse loo tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu dumɔwui ni afo lɛ ahe nii dani odu koni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ ni afo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it better to grow yams in big soil mounds instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmeii yɛ gɔji wuji amli moŋ fe hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep, and soft soil so their tubers can easily expand downwards. Raised mounds also prevent water from pooling around the roots and causing rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia sweet potatoes bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛba shi mlɛo. Gɔŋ ni awo nɔ lɛ hu tsiɔ nu naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: What happens if I plant my crops too close to each other on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When planted too close, crops compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak plants and much smaller tubers or yields at harvest.
ga: Kɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo loo yibiiwoo baa kɛji akpa.

english: Yam vines are climbing plants that need to spread their leaves in full sunlight to produce energy for tuber growth. Staking also keeps leaves off wet ground, reducing diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulb lɛ dalɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai srɔtoi baa shi

english: Why does my neighbor get much bigger yam harvests than me even though we farm in the same area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe mi eyɛ mli akɛ wɔtsuɔ okwaa yɛ he kome moŋ lɛ?

english: Yield differences usually come from using healthier planting material, proper mound sizing, better soil nutrients, and clearing weeds early before they steal food from the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ yibiiwoo mli lɛ jɛɔ dumɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli. Gɔŋ lɛ dalɛ ni sa Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni hi kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra dani abaaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its power to grow good crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ dɔŋŋ?

english: If your crops show yellowing leaves, grow very slowly, or yield much smaller harvests than in previous years, your soil has lost essential nutrients.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ, edaa blɛoo waa, loo ewoɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ mli yibii lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ elaaje.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my crop seeds after buying them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni mihe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting should happen at the start of the steady rainy season when the soil has enough moisture to support root development without soaking the seed to the point of rot.
ga: Esa akɛ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa daa lɛ shishijee mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua shishifãi lɛ ni ehaaa dumɔwui lɛ agbo tsɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops even when the crop plants are already taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ fe jwɛi lɛ momo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital water and soil fertilizers directly from around the root zone, starving the main crop underneath the ground even if the crop looks bigger on top.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ shikpɔŋ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ ha hɔmɔ ye ŋmɔshi nibii titrii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni da kɛjɛ ŋwɛi po.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my crop so it yields well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ madu tsei koni maná yibii kpakpai?

english: Timing your planting with the start of the main rainy season ensures young roots get plenty of natural water to establish before dry spells hit, giving the crop enough growing time to develop strong fruit.
ga: Be ni akɛduɔ nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli koni shishifãi bibii lɛ ana adebɔɔ mli nu ni fa bɔ ni sa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa be ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my crops not producing good fruit even after I applied fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Fertilizer must be applied at specific times during the plant's growth cycle. If you apply it too late after the crop needed it, the plant cannot properly use those nutrients to support fruit development.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ be mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛwo mli sɛɛ tsɔ, yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ he miihia lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ekɛ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during dry spells are usually a sign of water stress and intense direct sunlight. Providing temporary or permanent shade crops helps keep moisture in the soil and protects leaves from scorching.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ ji nu he haomɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he okadi. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo loo daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi, ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ akashãa.

english: What does an extension officer mean when they talk about plant physiology on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni extension worker tsɔɔ kɛji eewie tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ agbɔmɔtso he?

english: Plant physiology simply refers to how a plant grows, breathes, and forms fruit. Understanding this helps you give the crop the right food, water, and shade at each growth stage to produce maximum yield.
ga: Plant physiology tsɔɔ bɔ ni tsei daa, amɛmuɔ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii kɛkɛ. Kɛ́ onu enɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulutsoo ni sa aha otsei lɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ be fɛɛ be mli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: What does 'bearing cocoa' mean and when should I expect my young trees to reach this stage?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘koo ni aaawo’ lɛ shishi? Ni mɛɛ be esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ midumɔwui lɛ baashɛ nɛkɛ shihilɛ nɛɛ he?

english: Bearing cocoa' refers to cocoa trees that have grown mature enough to start producing flowers and cocoa pods, which usually begins between three to five years after planting depending on the seed variety.
ga: Kokoo ni woɔ’ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni ebɔi kookoo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii feemɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ jeɔ shishi aaafee afii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ sɛɛ beni adu nii lɛ. Edamɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ anɔ

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce a heavy crop in one season but very little in the next?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be kome mli shi ewoɔ yibii fioo kwraa yɛ be kroko mli lɛ?

english: Producing a heavy harvest uses up a huge amount of energy from the tree. Proper pruning, weeding, and feeding the soil help the tree recover so it can maintain steady yields year after year.
ga: Nibii ni tsii ni akpaa lɛ biɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli. Tso lɛ he tsemɔ ni sa, jwɛi ni ajieɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ shi bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehiɛ yibiiwoo ni yaa nɔ daa afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do many of the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off before forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce many more flowers than they can support. Factors like drought, heat, or lack of tree energy cause the plant to drop surplus flowers so it can focus on developing healthy pods.
ga: Kookoo tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nibii tamɔ hɔmɔ, dɔlɛ, loo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama fɔfɔi ni mli wa lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: How should I examine my crop field to make sure nothing is disturbing the plants?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ koni mana nɔmimaa akɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko gbaaa tsei lɛ anaa?

english: Regularly walk through your farm looking closely at the leaves, stems, and fruits. Checking under leaves and along branches helps you spot pests or diseases early before they cause serious damage to your yield.
ga: Nyiɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa, ni okwɛ baai, ŋmeii, kɛ aduawai lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai kɛ tsei aniji ashishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai mra. dani ekɛ naagbai ni mli wa aba oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: How can I support heavy fruits on my young trees so the branches do not snap?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafi tso bibioo ko ni tsii sɛɛ? Koni tsei niji lɛ akakumɔ?

english: Pruning excess weak branches early and using physical supports like wooden Y-stakes under heavy stems keeps the tree balanced and stops fruiting branches from breaking under high yield.
ga: Niji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ mra. ni okɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa tamɔ tsei ni tsii ni tamɔ Y ni yɔɔ tsɔne lɛ shishi lɛ atsu nii. Ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaaa niji ni woɔ yibii lɛ akumɔ yɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo shishi.

english: What causes cocoa pods to turn black and dry up while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in cool, overly damp shade. Pruning overhead branches to let in sunlight and removing infected pods helps protect healthy fruits.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela kɛbaa Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni aaafolɔ koni hulu lɛ ashɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and moisture they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient plants need to stay green and healthy. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted manure early in the season helps feed the plant properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni sa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make energy for the tubers growing under the ground. Staking keeps the leaves high in the sun and off the damp soil where fungal diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ hulu lɛ mli ni amɛjeɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to sprout when the soil is packed hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ?

english: Seeds need soft soil, air, and water to push their young roots down and leaves up. Hard, compacted soil forms a physical barrier that stops seeds from breaking through to the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ nu koni amɛtsi shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ baai ni yaa ŋwɛi lɛ kɛya shi. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkabote shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rainwater sits in the ground without draining, the roots drown and soil fungi cause them to rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ efo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni nu bɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛgboi.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miikwɛ ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat or a lack of water. The plant sheds flowers to save energy and protect itself during harsh conditions.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ he. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites feeding on the undersides of leaves. Spraying early with neem water or pest treatments helps protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe

english: When rice receives too much nitrogen fertilizer or is planted too close together, the stems grow long, thin, and weak. Rain and wind can easily knock these weak stems over.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa. Nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ aha tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ nɛɛ agbo yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get full of small holes and powder in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni powda ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Insects called weevils eat the inside of stored grains if the maize is not dried properly or kept in airtight containers. Drying grains thoroughly in the sun before storage prevents infestation.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ baaye ŋmaa ni ato lɛ mli kɛji akɛ agbiko ŋmaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ loo akɛtooo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛto lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni dumɔwui lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do weeds make my young crops stay small even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔwui lɛ feɔ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and plant food directly from the soil surrounding your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to grow.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Ehaa oŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Officer, why do some crop varieties take up to three weeks to sprout while others take less than a week?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi heɔ otsii etɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi heɔ nɔ ni shɛɛɛ otsi kome dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties have different genetic traits. Improved or specialized seed varieties are bred to break dormancy and sprout within 7 days, while traditional or hard-coated seeds may naturally take 21 days or more to germinate.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ fɔmɔ sui srɔtoi. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ loo nɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto koni amɛha amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ gbii 7 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema dumɔwui loo ni akɛ nɔ ko ewo mli wa lɛ baanyɛ ahé gbii 21 loo nɔ ni fe nakai dani amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: How can I tell if an foreign seed variety, like an Israeli crop variety, will grow well in my soil in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui, tamɔ Israel tsei yɛ? Ani ebaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ nɔ?

english: Foreign seed varieties are tested for specific climate and soil conditions. Before planting them, you should check with an agricultural extension officer to confirm if that variety adapts well to Ghana's rainfall, sunlight, and local soil conditions.
ga: Akwɛɔ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ pɔtɛɛ. Dani obaadu lɛ, esa akɛ oyabi okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha Ghana maŋ lɛ mli nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ.

english: How long am I supposed to leave my seedlings in the nursery bed before moving them to the main field?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani mikɛ amɛ awo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: The time seedlings stay in the nursery depends on the crop variety. Fast-growing varieties may be strong enough to plant out in 7 days, whereas slower-growing varieties need about 21 days to build strong roots.
ga: Be ni dumɔwui lɛ baahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ damɔ tso lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ. Ekolɛ ŋmeii ni daa oya lɛ he wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu yɛ gbii 7 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni daa blɛoo lɛ he hiaa aaafee gbii 21 dani amɛshishifãi ni wa aba.

english: What simple things can I do to make my seeds sprout faster so I don't waste time waiting?
ga: Mafee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya koni amɛkafite be kɛmɛ?

english: Keeping the nursery soil consistently moist, providing gentle shade, and soaking hard seeds in clean water before sowing can trigger faster germination and shorten waiting time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ Ehaa ŋmɔlɔ ni mli jɔ Ni dumɔwui ni wa ni akɛwoɔ nu ni mli tse mli dani aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hewalɛ ni eha be ni akɛmɛɛɔ lɛ afee kuku.

english: Why are my neighbor's young plants ready for transplanting much earlier than mine when we planted around the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha dumɔwui mra fe minɔ̃ lɛ beni wɔduɔ amɛ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Your neighbor might be using a early-maturing seed variety engineered for quick sprouting, or their nursery bed had better moisture, soil warmth, and protection from harsh weather.
ga: Ekolɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni afee koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya lɛ miitsu nii. aloo gbekɛbii akwɛmɔ saatso lɛ ji hulutsoo ni mli edɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ hebuu ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi gbohii ahe.

english: What essential materials and tools do I need to prepare before I start planting a new crop variety?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii kɛ nitsumɔ dadei esa akɛ masaa mihe dani mabɔi tso hee ko dumɔ?

english: Before planting, you need fertile topsoil or compost, quality seeds, watering tools, nursery shade netting or palm leaves, and basic hand tools like a trowel or dibbler for safe transplanting.
ga: Dani obaadu lɛ, ehe miihia ni oná sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo. Dumɔwui ni hi, nu ni akɛhaa, shade ŋshɔŋloo loo tso baai. kɛ shishijee nibii ni akɛ niji tsuɔ tamɔ trowel loo tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii. kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe

english: Does applying fertilizer directly to seeds help them germinate faster in the soil?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya?

english: Fertilizer does not speed up initial germination, but adding well-rotted manure or starter phosphorus near the seed bed helps young roots grow strong immediately after the seed breaks open.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haaa ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ oya yɛ shishijee mli. Shi kɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo fɔsfɔs ni jeɔ shishi yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛdara waa kɛji dumɔwui lɛ tswa pɛ.

english: How do I know what type of starter nutrients or manure my specific crop variety needs at planting time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male shishijee niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa mi kɛha mi tso pɔtɛɛ lɛ yɛ dumɔ be mli?

english: Different varieties require different nutrient balances. You can check seed packaging guidelines or ask an extension agent to recommend the right mix of compost or fertilizer for your chosen variety.
ga: Henɔi srɔtoi biɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ srɔtoi ni sa. Obaanyɛ okwɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni kɔɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ he loo obi o-extension agent lɛ ni etsɔɔ bo ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha dumɔwui srɔtoi ni ohala lɛ.

english: Should I plant my crop seeds directly into the main farm field or start them in a nursery first?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo madu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Delicate seeds that take longer to sprout benefit from a protected nursery to survive pests and heavy rain, while hardy seeds like maize or cowpea do better when planted directly in the main field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ náa ŋmɔ ni abuɔ he lɛ he sɛɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni wa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How does choosing a crop variety with a shorter planting time benefit my farm harvest during the rainy season?
ga: Te tsei srɔtoi ni amɛdaraa be kukuoo lɛ ni mihalaa lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni akpaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Varieties that establish quickly allow you to make full use of short rainy seasons, reduce the risk of early drought damage, and free up your field sooner for a second cropping cycle.
ga: Srɔtoi ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa oshara ni yɔɔ hɔmɔ ni fiteɔ nii mra lɛ baa shi. ni oha he ko aya oya kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves in maize are often a sign of nutrient deficiency, like a lack of nitrogen, or insect pests like aphids feeding on the sap. Adding balanced fertilizer or treating early for pests helps the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen ni faaa, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ ŋmãa ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baawo mli loo ni atsa tsɛŋemɔ helai mra Ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium or phosphorus. High nitrogen forces the cassava plant to spend all its energy growing leaves instead of storing food in the root tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium loo phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ ebaa ni miida lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: How far apart should I plant my maize seeds so they grow big ears?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ tɛŋŋ koni maná toi wuji?

english: Planting maize about 75 centimeters between rows and 40 centimeters between seeds gives each plant enough space, sunlight, and soil nutrients to develop large, healthy cobs without competing with nearby stalks.
ga: Kɛ́ adu aaafee sɛntimita 75 yɛ ŋmeii ateŋ kɛ sɛntimita 40 yɛ dumɔwui ateŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ ŋmeii agbo ni mli wa aba ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akaŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without making any peppers when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔii ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, causing them to drop flowers to save water and energy. Providing light shade or watering early in the morning helps the plants keep their flowers and form fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ nyɛɔ pepper tsei anɔ koni amɛgbee shi koni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo loo nu ha tso lɛ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yibii ni ewoɔ lɛ mli.

english: Is it bad if I water my tomato crops in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ejaaa kɛji mikɛ nu wo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, watering during the hottest part of the day causes water to evaporate quickly before reaching the roots, and water droplets on the leaves can trap heat or encourage fungal leaf diseases. It is best to water early in the morning or late in the afternoon.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni oooha yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni nu ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ amɔmɔ dɔlɛ loo ewo fungal leaf hela he hewalɛ. Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo shwane.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants and keep the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa

english: Why are my plantain suckers taking a very long time to sprout after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers sprout slowly if they are planted too deep, if the soil lacks moisture, or if the planting material had root damage or weevil insects inside before being put in the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Kɛji adu mli tsɔ Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo kɛji akɛ dumɔ nii lɛ shishifãi efite loo ŋmeii yɛ mli dani adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by caterpillars such as the diamondback moth larva. Spraying neem leaf extract or appropriate organic pesticides on the leaves helps stop them from feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ diamondback ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ kaabe baa mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli lɛ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye amɛ.

english: How can I tell when my sweet potatoes are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-sweet potato lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Sweet potatoes are generally ready for harvest when the leaves begin to turn yellow and dry out, which usually happens around 3 to 4 months after planting depending on the variety.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ

english: Why are black spots spreading across my cocoa pods and turning them rotten?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji miigbɛ eshwa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ fɛɛ ahe ni eha amɛfite lɛ?

english: Black spots on cocoa pods are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads quickly during rainy, humid weather. Pruning extra tree branches to let air flow through and removing infected pods helps keep the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ cocoa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji krokomɛi koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crop seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which results in thin, weak crops that produce small yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo pɛ baa.

english: Staking exposes the leaves to maximum sunlight so the plant can make enough food to grow large tubers underground, while also keeping the leaves off the wet ground to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Staking haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ahe hulu la ni fe fɛɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ mli ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akashɛ ohe.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed to make leaves green and support strong plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni eye ebua tsei lɛ adalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when there is direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and sensitive to intense heat. They need shade crops like plantain to shield their leaves from severe sun exposure until their roots are deep enough to withstand the heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa, ni amɛnuɔ latsaa ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe jɔɔ, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo mli bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ naa.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small shoots growing around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi dumɔwui lɛ eje kpo.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and plant food from the main plantain tree. Removing most of them allows the main tree to focus all its energy on growing a larger, heavier bunch.
ga: Tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Tso lɛ fã ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso titri lɛ yeɔ ehe koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama tso ni da ni tsii fe no lɛ nɔ.

english: Curling pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by viral diseases spread by sap-sucking insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Cassava roots rot underground when soil stays overly wet due to poor drainage, creating an environment where destructive fungal diseases thrive and destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ko baa ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ yaa hiɛ ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil dries out completely, causing stress that makes the plant reject fruit production.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ shigbeemɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haa tsei kpooɔ yibiiwoo baa.

english: How do weeds growing near my crops hurt the size of my harvest?
ga: Te jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal vital nutrients, soil moisture, and sunlight away from your crops, leaving the main plants weak and drastically reducing the amount of crop you can harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni hulu la lɛ yaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaanyɛ okpa lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Fertilizer is best applied when the soil is moist and the crop is actively growing—usually a few weeks after germination—so the root system can easily absorb the nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tso lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii 2-3 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ oya.

english: Is it harmful to water my crops with very cold borehole water during hot afternoons?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ mikɛ nu ni mli ejɔ ni jɛɔ nubu mli lɛ baafɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, pouring very cold water on hot plant roots during a blazing afternoon shocks the crop and causes heat stress. It is always best to water your crops early in the morning or late in the evening when both the air and soil temperatures are cooler.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni mli ejɔ waa ni afɔɔ ashwieɔ tsei ni mli edɔ lɛ shishifãi anɔ yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe afee shoo ni ekɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baaba. Ehi jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be akɛ oooha oŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why do my plant leaves turn yellow even when I give them water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Overwatering can drown plant roots by pushing out the oxygen in the soil. When roots cannot breathe, they rot and fail to absorb nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow just as if the crop were suffering from drought.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ashishifãi atsɔ nu mli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu Ebaafite ni enyɛŋ eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ tamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiye hɔmɔ.

english: How often should I water my crops during the dry season to make sure they survive?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi?

english: Instead of light daily watering that evaporates quickly, give your crops a deep soaking two to three times a week. Deep watering encourages plant roots to grow farther down into the soil where moisture stays longer.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha nu blɛoo daa gbi, ni baaho oya lɛ, Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo nu mli jogbaŋŋ. shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ yɛ otsi mli Nu ni mli kwɔ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ daa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, he ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ.

english: Why do some fruits on my farm grow very big while others on the same crop stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ daa bibii lɛ?

english: Fruit size depends on how much water and nutrients reach each crop. If a plant carries too many fruits at once, it spreads its energy thin; trimming off excess weak leaves or smaller fruits allows the remaining ones to grow much larger.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni shɛɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ damɔ tso yibii lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ wo yibii babaoo shikome lɛ Ebaagbɛ hewalɛ fioo ko eshwa. Kɛ́ ofolɔ baai bibii ni fa fe nine loo aduawai bibii lɛ, ebaaha baai ni eshwɛ lɛ adara babaoo.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my crops so they do not spoil on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Crops give clear physical signals when mature, such as changes in skin color, firmness, or the drying up of leaves. Harvesting too early reduces crop weight and sweetness, while harvesting too late leaves them vulnerable to pests and rotting.
ga: Tsei haa gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ beni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ hewolo nɔ su tsakemɔi, shifimɔ, loo baai lɛ agbimɔ. Kɛ́ akpa tso lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ tsiimɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ aba shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akpa tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ fitemɔ baa tso lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Why are buyers in the market willing to pay higher prices for some farmers' crops than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛwo okwaafoi komɛi aŋmɔshi nibii ahe nyɔmɔ babaoo fe mɛi krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Market buyers pay premium prices for uniform size, clean appearance, and fresh quality. Sorting your harvested crops by size and removing damaged ones before going to market allows you to charge more for your top-grade produce.
ga: Jarayeli he jarayelɔi woɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kɛha dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa. He ni ehe tse kɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ ehee Kɛ́ ohala onibii ni okpa lɛ mli yɛ bɔ ni elɛɛmɔ ji lɛ naa, ni ojie tsei ni efite lɛ dani amɛba jara nɔ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ shika babaoo woɔ onibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ.

english: How can I keep my harvested crops fresh for longer if the market buyer does not arrive on time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ? Ni kɛji jara nɔ nihelɔ lɛ baaa yɛ be naa hu?

english: Store your harvested crops in a well-ventilated, cool, shaded area away from direct sunlight. Covering crops like root vegetables or fruits with clean, slightly damp jute sacks keeps them cool and prevents them from drying out quickly.
ga: Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulu la shɛɛɛ he. Jute kotokui ni he tse ni mli efɔ fioo ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ shishifãi loo aduawai ahe. Enɛ baaye abua ni kotoku lɛ mli ajɔ ni ebaaha egbi oya.

english: Why do my crops look weak and pale even after I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve so roots can absorb it. If applied to dry soil, or placed too close to the plant stems, fertilizer can actually burn the roots instead of feeding the crop.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tsɔ lɛ, Fɛ̃i baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my soil dry up quickly a few days after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil lacking organic matter cannot hold water efficiently. Adding well-rotted manure or compost acts like a sponge, holding rainwater in the soil around your crop roots for many days after a heavy downpour.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ ahi nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaatsu nii tamɔ sponji. Emɔ nugbɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli. Dumɔ shishifãi gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon is a plant's natural defense to reduce water loss and protect itself from strong direct sunlight. If the leaves uncurl by evening, the plant is managing well, but if they stay curled, your crops need water.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ tsei ahe koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛji baai lɛ shwieee shi gbɛkɛ Etsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle lɛ, nu he miihia otso lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to plant my crops before the main rains start in June?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei dani nugbɔ lɛ aje shishi yɛ June mli lɛ?

english: Planting just before the June rains begin ensures your seeds are safely in the ground ready to soak up the early rainfall, giving them a head start to germinate quickly before heavy downpours flood the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ odu dani nugbɔ lɛ nɛ yɛ June mli lɛ, ebaaha odumɔwui lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe, ni efee klalo akɛ ebaaŋɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ yiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens if I delay planting until well after the rainy season has already begun?
ga: Mɛni baaba kɛji akɛ ajie dumɔwui lɛ kɛtee sɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If you plant too late into the rainy season, heavy downpours can wash your seeds away or cause them to rot in waterlogged soil before they have a chance to grow strong roots.
ga: Kɛji odu sɛɛ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ agbe dumɔwui loo eha amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ dani amɛná hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I start clearing and preparing my field during the dry period before the rains come?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabɔi jɛmɛ shwiemɔ kɛ he saamɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli dani nugbɔ lɛ aba?

english: Yes, preparing your land during the dry period ensures your soil is loose and ready to absorb the first rains, allowing you to plant immediately without losing valuable growing time.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ooosaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee klalo akɛ ebaaŋɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ. Ehaa onyɛɔ oduɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni be ni he hiaa ni okɛduɔ nii lɛ fiteee.

english: How do seasonal rain patterns in Ghana affect when I should buy my planting seeds?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli yɛ Ghana lɛ saa be ni esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: You should secure your seeds early in the year so you are ready to plant right before the major rains arrive around May or June, avoiding last-minute shortages at the market.
ga: Eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ oookɛ odumɔwui lɛ ato yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli koni ofee klalo akɛ obaadu amɛ dani nugbɔ wulu lɛ aba yɛ May loo June aaafee. Bɔni afee ni akashɛ naagbee minitii lɛ amli nibii ni faaa yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: How can I water my crops if the nearby dam is located lower than my farm field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu kɛji akɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ baa shi fe miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: You can use small water pumps, channels, or buckets to fetch water from a downstream dam to irrigate your land, allowing you to grow crops even before the rainy season officially starts.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nu pɔmp, nu ŋshɔ, loo baagi bibioo ajie nu kɛjɛ faa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli ni okɛfɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ nu. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ tsei dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ po jeɔ shishi yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ.

english: Why should I bother with irrigation from a dam if the rainy season usually brings enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu nu ni jɛɔ faa mli lɛ he? Be ni bei pii lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Dam irrigation gives you full control over your water supply, protecting your crops from unexpected dry spells and allowing you to plant earlier than relying purely on rainfall.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ dam mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ oyeɔ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔ kwraa. Buu onibii ahe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ bei ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ ahe. ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni oduɔ nii oya fe ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ nugbɔshiimɔ pɛ nɔ.

english: Is it safe to plant my crops before June if I have access to a nearby water source?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu tsei dani June aba kɛji miyɛ nu jɛɛhe ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi?

english: Yes, having access to a water source like a dam allows you to start planting early without waiting for the rains, leading to an earlier harvest and better market prices.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu jɛɛhe ko ni oyɔɔ tamɔ faa lɛ haa onyɛɔ ojeɔ dumɔ shishi oya ni ehe ehiaaa ni omɛ nugbɔ. Enɛ haa akpaa nii oya, ni jarayeli jara hu hiɔ shi.

english: How much of my crop harvest should I save to use as seeds for the next planting season?
ga: Miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mlijaa enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛto koni mikɛtsu nii akɛ dumɔwui kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ?

english: It is best practice to set aside a portion of your healthiest crop harvest immediately after picking so you have reliable, high-quality seeds ready for the next season without extra cost.
ga: Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni okɛ ŋmaa lɛ fã ko aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ bɔni afee ni oná dumɔwui ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ, ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni asaa he kɛha be ni baa lɛ ni okɛ shika kroko fataaa he.

english: What should I do with my harvest if I want to both feed my family and plan for next season?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ mikpamɔ lɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni makwɛ miweku lɛ ni mato gbɛjianɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Divide your harvest into three portions: set aside healthy seeds for next season's planting, keep enough food for your family's daily needs, and sell the surplus at the market for cash.
ga: Jaa okpamɔ lɛ mli etɛ: Okɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ato kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli dumɔ. Too niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha weku lɛ daa gbi hiamɔ nii. ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ yɛ jara nɔ koni amɛná shika.

english: Can I use the exact same seeds harvested from my field to plant my next farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii ni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, as long as you select seeds from your strongest, healthiest plants and store them in a dry, cool place to keep them safe from pests until the next planting season.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ obaahala dumɔwui kɛjɛ tsei ni he wa fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli. Ni okɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite lɛ kɛyashi shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and scorching in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a protective canopy that shelters young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ehe wa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ enáa hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why does my plantain tree take so long to produce fruit when I leave all the small shoots growing around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani mi dumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: The small shoots (suckers) compete with the main plantain tree for water, food, and sunlight. Pruning away extra shoots and leaving only one or two healthy ones allows the mother plant to direct all its energy into growing a heavy fruit bunch.
ga: Tso bibii (tso) lɛ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni efoɔ ni eshiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, fɔlɔ tso lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛya aduawai akui ni tsii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Does it matter which direction the buds are pointing when I stick cassava stems into the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ midu ŋmei tso yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei lɛ baajɛ?

english: Yes, the small growth buds on the cassava stem must point upwards toward the sky. Planting stems upside down causes the plant to waste energy trying to grow roots upward before turning down, resulting in weak growth and smaller tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Tso lɛ yitso lɛ ni aaakwɛ shi lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni akɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni shishifãi lɛ adara dani egbee shi lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdalɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often moistens the topsoil temporarily, but it can be followed by several weeks of hot, dry weather. Waiting for the rains to become steady ensures the soil stays moist enough for your maize seeds to germinate and survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli fũuɔ be kukuoo ko. Shi otsii babaoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ anyiɛ sɛɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my yam plants grow better tubers when I put tall wooden sticks for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ha wain tso lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce the food that grows the underground tuber. Staking keeps the vines lifted off the hot soil, preventing leaf diseases and giving the plant maximum exposure to sunlight.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ́ akwɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa wain tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ehe nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi foliar helai anaa ni oha tsei lɛ aná hulu la babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I place chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my maize plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the plant stem can chemical-burn the stem and tender roots. Spreading fertilizer in a small ring a few inches away allows the root tips to safely absorb the nutrients without getting damaged.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ adara. Ebaanyɛ eshã kɛtsɔ tsofai anɔ Ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ kooyigbɛ bibii amli Inchi fioo komɛi ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni efiteee amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow starting from the middle vein down to the stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛteŋgbɛ kɛmiiya amɛshishifã lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves that start from the leaf tips and move inward usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps restore the dark green color necessary for the plant to form large corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni eyaa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ ni he hiaa koni tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii wuji lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants drying up and falling off without making fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off without setting fruit when the plant experiences extreme heat or sudden water stress. Regular watering and placing mulch around the base keeps the root zone cool and moist, helping the flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ loo nu he haomɔ trukaa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ tomatoi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly like tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips feeding on the undersides of the leaves. Spraying the plants with a mild neem-leaf extract or appropriate organic soap solution can help control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Ni akɛ neem baa mli nu ni mli ejɔ loo samla ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Weeds grow much faster than domestic crops and aggressively steal nutrients, water, and root space from the soil. Clearing weeds early in the season removes this competition so your crops can use all available nutrients to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe shia tsei ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ajie akaŋshii kɛya. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ atsu nii ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn soft and grow mould when I keep it inside my house?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mikɛto shia lɛ?

english: Maize naturally holds trapped moisture inside the grains even after harvest. If you put it in a dark room without drying it properly under the sun first, that trapped water creates heat and causes mould to grow, spoiling the crop.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ hiɛɔ nu ni emɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ mli yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ po. Kɛji akɛ okɛwo tsu ko ni mli ewo duŋ mli ni okɛ hulu lɛ egbiko lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Nu ni emɔ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ baa ni ehaa ŋmeii shwereɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ

english: Why do my fresh crops heat up and rot quickly when I pack them tightly into big sacks for transport?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni mikɛfee ehee lɛ mli woɔ la ni egboɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛwo kotokui wuji amli koni mikɛmaje lɛ?

english: Harvested crops are still living plant parts that continue to 'breathe' and release heat. Packing them tightly in sealed sacks traps this natural heat and moisture, which essentially cooks the crops and causes them to rot fast.
ga: Tsei ni akpa lɛ ji tsei ahe nibii ni hiɛ ka lolo ni yaa nɔ ‘amɛmuɔ’ ni amɛjieɔ dɔlɛ kpo. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotokui ni atsĩ naa mli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ ɔ ma ha nɛ ngmɔ ɔ nɛ e hwɔ, nɛ e ma puɛ mla.

english: Why shouldn't I dry my harvested grain directly on the bare ground outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ migbiɔ midumɔwui ni akpa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ yɛ kpo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Spreading grain directly on bare soil allows the crop to absorb moisture, dirt, and hidden insect eggs from the ground. This introduces fungi and pests that cause the grain to spoil much faster during storage.
ga: Dumɔwui ni agbɛɔ ashwãa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ, muji kɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ afɔfɔi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui baa ni haa ŋmaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kwraa yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots go bad and turn black just two days after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fite ni amɛtsɔ ediŋŋ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni akpa lɛ?

english: Once cassava is cut from the soil, its skin breaks easily during handling. Exposure to air causes a rapid natural chemical reaction inside the root that makes it spoil, darken, and go bitter within 48 hours.
ga: Kɛji afo ŋmei lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ehewolo lɛ fãa oya yɛ be mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tsofa ko ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ feɔ oya. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ, amɛfeɔ diŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli.

english: Why do buyers pay me very little money for my crops even when I put in a lot of hard work?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ mi nyɔmɔ fioo ko yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ nii waa moŋ

english: Market buyers look at crop quality rather than farmer labor. If crops show moisture, insect holes, or uneven sizes, their value drops heavily; properly dried, clean, and sorted crops attract much higher prices.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jarayelihe lɛ kwɛɔ nibii ni amɛduɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe okwaafoi anitsumɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ jie ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmeii, loo elɛɛmɔi ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ kpo Ejara baa shi waa, ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi, ni he tse ni ahala amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ gbalaa jara ni nɔ kwɔ babaoo.

english: Why do my crops lose weight and shrink a few days after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni mikpa nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops consist largely of water. After harvest, water naturally evaporates from the crop into the air over time, causing the produce to shrink and weigh less when sold.
ga: Nu ji nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli babaoo. kpamɔ sɛɛ Nu lɛ jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsiimɔ baa shi kɛ́ ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves turn brown and dry, and the kernels become hard enough that you cannot dent them with your fingernail. Leaving mature maize too long in the rain causes field rot and insect damage.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi, ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni onyɛŋ okɛ onineshi ŋmɔtɔ atsɔ mli. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔji lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaafite kooloi bibii.

english: How can I safely store my harvested grains at home so insects do not destroy them before I find a buyer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ato shia shweshweeshwe? Bɔni afee ni kooloi bibii lɛ akafite lɛ dani amɛna mɔ ko ni baahe.

english: Insects need air to survive. You can protect dried grains by storing them in airtight storage bags (like PICS bags) or sealed drums kept off the ground on wooden pallets, which suffocates any pests.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia koolooi koni amɛhi shi. Obaanyɛ obu dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ amɛ ni oookɛwo tsɔne ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ naa (tamɔ PICS kotokui) loo tsɔnei ni akɛwoɔ mli ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: If I cannot transport my harvested crops immediately due to bad roads, how can I protect them from rotting on the farm?
ga: Kɛji minyɛɛɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ aya amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ gbɛjegbɛi gbohii ahewɔ Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anaa?

english: To protect harvested crops temporarily on the farm, build a raised wooden platform off the wet ground (a crib) and cover it with a canopy to shield the crops from direct rain and harsh sunlight while allowing air to blow through.
ga: Bɔni afee ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe yɛ be kukuoo mli Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, maa tso ni awo nɔ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ (cradle) ni okɛ ŋwɛitsu aha nɔ koni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he yɛ be mli ni ohaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my crops produce small fruits and low yields even when I work on the farm every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops need specific nutrients from the soil to grow big fruits. Hard work alone cannot replace exhausted soil; crops need balanced fertilizers and weed-free fields so they don't have to fight for water and food.
ga: Niyenii pɔtɛɛ ko he miihia tsei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛwo yibii wuji. Nitsumɔ ni wa pɛ nyɛŋ aye sũ ni etɔ lɛ najiaŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja kɛ ŋmɔji ni jwɛi bɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ nu kɛ niyenii ashi akaŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build healthy green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives them the food they need to turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ baaha amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dry grass or palm leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Nibii ni akɛ jwɛi loo ŋmei baai ewo mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly in the sun. It also prevents weeds from taking over and turns into rich soil food as it rots.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu la mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi hu naa koni amɛkaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii beni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why is fresh animal manure bad to put directly onto my growing crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ehiii kɛji mikɛwo mitsei ni miida lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fresh animal manure releases strong gases and intense heat as it begins to break down, which can burn and kill soft plant roots. Letting the manure sit, dry, and rot completely over a few weeks makes it safe and highly nutritious for your crops.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa beni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi efiteɔ lɛ. ni baanyɛ ashã ni efite tso shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ Ha ŋmeii lɛ agbi. ni fitemɔ ni yeɔ emuu yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Rolling up leaves is a self-defense trick crops use to survive intense sun heat. By curling their leaves, they reduce the amount of surface area exposed to the sun, which stops water from escaping through the leaf pores.
ga: Baai ni akpɛɔ lɛ ji hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haaa nu akatsɔ baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. Instead of growing thick stems and big fruits, they stretch as fast as they can toward the sky to reach sunlight before their neighbors do.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ tsohi nɛ a he wa, nɛ e woɔ yiblii nguahi. Amɛkpãa amɛhe oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛyashɛ hulu la lɛ he dani amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ aná.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience sudden stress, such as extremely dry soil or intense heat. Keeping the soil moist continuously gives the plant the security it needs to hold onto its flowers and turn them into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe trukaa nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa loo latsaa ni naa wa waa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa shweshweeshwe shihilɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛmɔ fɔfɔii amli ni amɛtsake amɛ amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why are the young cocoa pods on my trees turning black and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, damp conditions. Pruning extra cocoa branches and clearing weeds allows sunlight and fresh air to dry out the farm, stopping the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ kɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. ni ekpa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Why are small green caterpillars hiding inside the center leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which prefer to hide in the soft, inner leaves of corn plants where they are safe while eating the young plant. Checking your corn early and applying approved treatments directly into the center leaf whorl can stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ tsei bibii lɛ. Abɛi mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛbaatsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha abɛi akpa dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava plant have plenty of big leaves above ground but very small tubers under the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen in the soil, it spends all its energy building lush leaves instead of underground roots. Giving the plants balanced nutrients and proper space helps them direct their food down into making large tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei ná nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii ni sa kɛ he ni sa ha tso lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ niyenii lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over before the heavy fruit bunches are fully ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ efee klalo kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain stems are filled with water rather than hard wood, making them soft and heavy. Supporting the stems with strong wooden poles or branched stakes helps hold up the heavy weight of the fruit until it is time to harvest.
ga: Akɛ nu woɔ plantain tsei lɛ amli yɛ tsei ni wa najiaŋ. Ha efee blɛoo ni etsii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei loo tsei niji ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso yibii lɛ tsiimɔ yaa hiɛ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a living umbrella that shields young cocoa plants and keeps the soil moist while their roots develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ Adumɔ tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant takes whatever nitrogen it has from its older bottom leaves and sends it to the growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen faaa Abɛi tsei lɛ ŋɔɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni amɛyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ, baai ni edara lɛ amli ni amɛkɛyaa baai ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Yes, cassava stems have growth buds that must point upwards toward the sky. If planted upside down, the shoots must bend underground to grow upward, wasting energy and leading to weak roots and poor yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei tsei yɛ hiŋmɛii ni esa akɛ amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Esa akɛ abɔle tso lɛ shishi bɔni afee ni eda. Wastes energy Enɛ haa shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi baa.

english: How does cutting into the bark of a rubber tree make liquid flow without killing the plant?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni rɔbɔt lɛ fã ni afo lɛ aha nu atsɔ mli ni egbeee tso lɛ?

english: Rubber trees store latex in tiny tubes located in the outer bark. Making a shallow cut opens these tubes so the liquid drains into a collection cup without cutting deep into the inner wood that feeds the roots.
ga: Rɔba tsei kɛ latɛs toɔ tsɔnei bibii amli. ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋshɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli efoɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ Enɛ gbeleɔ nɛkɛ tsɔnei nɛɛ amli koni nu lɛ atsɔ mli kɛbote nu ni abua naa lɛ mli ni efooo mligbɛ tso ni haa shishifãi lɛ niyenii lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: This damage is typically caused by fall armyworms. The caterpillars hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day, feeding on the soft leaf tissues before they unfurl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ amli fãji dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo.

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight to produce food for the plant. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get full sunlight and good airflow, which helps build bigger underground tubers and prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la ni fa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aba. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji feɔ, ni etsiɔ ŋmeii ahe helai anaa.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upward and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by heat stress or tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit viruses. The plant curls its leaves to conserve moisture or as a reaction to the virus, which slows down growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo loo kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ loo akɛ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ amɛhaa helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my field right before a heavy rain fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ anɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall causes water to wash over the topsoil, carrying away loose fertilizer before crop roots can absorb it. This wastes your money and deprives your plants of nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ojie ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse lɛ dani tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ shika ni ehaaa tsei lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruit bunch becomes big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantain trees do not have strong woody trunks or deep roots; their stems are made of packed leaf sheets. As the heavy bunch matures, top-heavy weight can easily uproot the plant unless supported with a wooden Y-prop.
ga: Plantains bɛ tsei ni wa loo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Akɛ baai ni akɛwo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ fee tso lɛ. Kɛji akɛ kuu lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Muji ni tsii ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie tsei lɛ kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi amli oya. ja akɛ tso ni tamɔ Y ni akɛ tso fee tsu nii

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my planted crops after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni adu yɛ nugbɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants naturally adapted to local soil and climate conditions. Their seeds lie dormant in the soil and can sprout and absorb water and nutrients much faster than domesticated crop plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Amɛdumɔwui lɛ ehi shi. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ̃ ni eŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya kwraa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ shia mli lɛ.
