english: Why do wild plants in the bush survive on their own, but my farm crops get sick and die easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi lɛ amli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ hiɔ shi lɛ? Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hela mɔɔ amɛ oya ni amɛgboiɔ?

english: Wild plants have adapted over hundreds of years to survive tough conditions, but farm crops are specially bred for high food yield. This high productivity makes farm crops softer, more delicate, and more sensitive to pests and climate changes.
ga: Ehe ebahia ni koo mli tsei atsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Shi akwɛɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii babaoo aba. Nɛkɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo nɛɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ blɛoo. eyɛ mlɛo fe tsutsu lɛ ni ehiɛ kã kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anɔ waa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves inward like a tube to reduce the leaf surface exposed to direct sunlight. This helps the plant conserve moisture and stop water from evaporating too quickly during the hottest parts of the day.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli tamɔ paipii koni ekɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and dry up during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Continuous rain creates high moisture and shade, which allows fungal spores (black pod disease) to spread quickly. The fungus attacks the pod tissue, causing it to rot and turn black.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ kɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo baa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai (black pod hela) lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Fung lɛ tutuaa pod fãji lɛ. Enɛ haa egboɔ ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ.

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients put stress on the plant. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival rather than producing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo sũ mli niyenii ni esaaa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Kɛ́ haomɔ ba Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei baawo yibii lɛ, amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and stop growing when I cannot see any insects on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa dalɛ be mli ni minaaa kooloi bibii komɛi lɛ?

english: Very tiny pests like mites or thrips, which are almost invisible to the naked eye, suck the juice from under young leaves and inject toxins that make the leaves curl and stunt growth.
ga: Nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui waa tamɔ mites loo thrips ni eshwɛ fioo ni hiŋmɛi enaaa lɛ Emuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi ni ekɛ tsofai fɔji ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛdaraa lɛ woɔ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick leaves but produce small tubers beneath the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are given excess fertilizer, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they shade each other and compete for sunlight. They stretch upward as fast as possible to reach light, leaving them with weak, thin stems.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Amɛkpãa amɛhe oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Shi amɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow twisted and short instead of smooth and long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee kuku moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Hard, compacted soil or heavy clay prevents young yam tubers from pushing downward easily. When the tuber hits hard ground or rocks, it bends and forms irregular shapes.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ tsiɔ sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anaa koni ekashɛ shi mlɛo. Kɛ yitso lɛ tswa nɔ ko ni wa loo tɛ ko Ebaaku ni efite.

english: Why do my plantain suckers wilt and struggle to grow right after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛdara beni mikɛ amɛ ewo he kroko pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Transplanting damages the fine feeder roots that absorb water. Until the plant grows new roots in the fresh soil, it experiences transplant shock and struggles to keep its broad leaves hydrated.
ga: Kɛ́ atsake lɛ, ebaafite niyenii kpakpai ni shwieɔ nu lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. kɛyashi tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ shishifãi heei yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ Tso lɛ baaná shoofeemɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ kroko nɔ lɛ mli ni ebaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ehiɛ ebaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli nu lɛ mli.

english: Why do insects attack my garden vegetables so much more than the weeds around my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa aduawai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo fe jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Farm crops are bred to be soft, juicy, and low in bitter natural chemicals, making them very tasty to insects. Weeds often have tough skins, bitter tastes, or natural toxins that keep insects away.
ga: Akwɛɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ koni efee bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ nu, ni tsofai ni mli edɔ ni adebɔɔ mli lɛ faaa yɛ mli. Ehaa efeɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛha kooloi bibii. Bei pii lɛ, jwɛi yɛ hewolo ni wa, ŋmɔlɔ, loo adebɔɔ mli tsofai fɔji ni shwieɔ kooloi bibii.

english: Why should I clear and tractor-plough my land before planting instead of just digging small holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni matsu nii dani madu nii? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofo bu bibioo ko

english: Ploughing breaks up hard, compacted soil so crop roots can easily push deep down to find food and stay strong during dry spells. It also buries weeds and allows rainwater to soak into the ground rather than running off the surface.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waɔ ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛre kɛya shɔŋŋ koni amɛna niyenii ni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Efuɔ jwɛi hu ni ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeejɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops dry out so quickly in the strong sun, and how can dry grass help them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aye abua tsei?

english: Bare soil loses moisture very quickly under intense heat. Covering the ground around your crops with dried grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks direct sunlight, keeps the soil cooler, and traps water near the roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni ehiɛɔ nu ni bɛŋkɛɔ shishifãi lɛ

english: Why do my crops grow weak and thin when I put many seeds close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni egbɔjɔ beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete against each other for the same limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant enough space allows its stem to grow thick and produce better yields.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaawo yibii kpakpai.

english: Is it helpful to plant cassava or beans alongside my maize crops on the same farm?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ aaadu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa masɛi yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting different crops together can protect your soil. Beans especially grab nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps heavy-feeding crops like maize grow bigger without burning out your land.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii srɔtoi ni ooodu yɛ he kome lɛ baanyɛ abu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he. Yɛ gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni yeɔ niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa, daa ni amɛshãaa he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and healthy. It can also happen when too much standing water suffocates the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ ha tsei shishifãi lɛ shwie shi.

english: Chemical fertilizer is very strong and can burn the stem and soft roots of young plants if applied directly. It is best to place it a short distance away from the stem in a small circle so the outer roots can safely feed on it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli wa waa, ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ amɛ awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ yɛ kooyigbɛ bibioo ko mli. Bɔni afee ni aye kponɔgbɛ shishifãi lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Weeds are wild native plants that have adapted to survive in harsh conditions with very little water and care. Because they grow so fast, they will steal water and food from your crops unless you clear them early in the season.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai ni nu fioo kɛ kwɛmɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdaraa oya waa. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Ja ojie amɛ yɛ be lɛ mli mra.

english: Why do caterpillars and bugs suddenly attack my young crops right after the first heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii trukaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The rain causes crops to put out fresh, tender green leaves, which attracts adult insects to lay their eggs. When the eggs hatch, the young insects feed on those soft leaves to grow.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ. ni gbalaa kooloi bibii ni eda lɛ koni amɛwo amɛwui Beni amɛwoɔ amɛwui lɛ Kooloi bibii yeɔ nakai baai bibii lɛ koni amɛdara.

english: How long will it take for a new mango tree seedling to start producing fruits on my farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mango dumɔwui heei jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A grafted mango seedling usually begins bearing fruit in about 3 to 4 years. If you plant a mango tree directly from an ordinary seed, it can take up to 7 to 10 years before giving you fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango dumɔwui ni akɛwo tso mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli kɛji akɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni afɔɔ daa lɛ tsu tso lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Ekolɛ ebaahe afii 7 kɛyashi 10 dani ewo yibii.

english: Why is it important for me to trim or prune some branches off my young fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ niji komɛi ni jɛ mitsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Trimming away dead or crowded branches allows light and fresh air to reach the center of the tree. This prevents fungal diseases from building up and directs the plant's energy into growing bigger, healthier fruit.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni mli edɔ lɛ koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii ahe helai abua amɛhe naa, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight and harsh winds. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains provides living umbrellas that keep the soil cool and protect tender young cocoa leaves from drying out.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why are the branches of my cocoa trees swelling up and stopping the trees from bearing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ niji lɛ efuu ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekawo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Swollen branch stems are a sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. Once a tree gets infected, it cannot be cured with medicine and must be cut down to stop the virus from spreading to healthy trees.
ga: Niji ni efuu lɛ ji cocoa shoot virus hela ni efuu lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Atsɛɔ lɛ mealybugs. Kɛji tso ko ná hela lɛ, anyɛɛɛ akɛ tsofa atsa lɛ ni esa akɛ afo lɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree when the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in wet, humid conditions. Regular weeding, pruning extra branches, and removing infected pods right away helps keep the air dry around the tree so the fungus cannot grow.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa Nibii krokomɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ oya. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ mli egbiɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii akakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods develop dark patches and dry up as if they were burned by fire?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ efee ediŋŋ ni amɛgbi tamɔ nɔ ni ashã amɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by small sucking insects called capsids or mirids. They bite into young pods and soft leaves to feed, injecting toxic saliva that kills the plant tissue, which requires targeted spraying during their peak breeding season.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni atsɛɔ amɛ capsids loo mirids lɛ. Amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ baai bibii kɛha niyenii. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni baafite tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ biɔ ni afɔse tsofa ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ yɛ fɔmɔ be ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How do small insects on the farm floor help my cocoa trees produce more pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Very tiny insects called midges carry pollen from flower to flower so cocoa pods can grow. Leaving fallen cocoa leaves on the soil creates a damp home where these beneficial midges can multiply and pollinate more flowers.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa fɔfɔi krokomɛi anɔ koni kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃. Kookoo baai ni egbee shi lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa shia lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nɛkɛ tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ baanyɛ ashwere ni amɛha fɔfɔi babaoo afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How does cutting away some of the healthy-looking branches on my cocoa tree help me get more yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kakao tso niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi koni mawo yibii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes crowded, shaded, or unproductive branches so sunlight and fresh air can reach the middle of the tree. This reduces fungal diseases and allows the tree to send its energy directly into developing big, healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni etsilɛ, ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, loo ni wooo yibii lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa kookoo ŋmɔji wuji ni mli wa lɛ amli.

english: Why does allowing tall weeds to grow under my cocoa trees make my farm more prone to sickness?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kakadaji ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ haa miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ hela he oshara mli waa lɛ?

english: Tall weeds trap damp air around the cocoa trunk, creating a wet greenhouse environment where fungal rot thrives. Weeds also compete with your cocoa trees for food and water in the soil, making the trees weaker against pests.
ga: Jwɛi kakadaji mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe, ni efeɔ hulutsoo shihilɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ hela baanyɛ ada. Jwɛi hu kɛ kookoo tsei yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tso lɛ oya.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce plenty of flowers, but most of them fall off before pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔlɔ babaoo lɛ? Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pods?

english: Flowers drop when trees are stressed by a lack of essential soil nutrients, prolonged dry spells, or pest attacks. Feeding the soil with recommended cocoa fertilizers helps the tree stay strong enough to hold onto its flowers until pods develop.
ga: Fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛmɔmɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛyashi be mli ni ŋmɔji lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why are my 30-year-old cocoa trees producing far fewer pods than when they were younger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso ni eye afii 30 lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo kwraa fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their natural productivity drops and their roots absorb nutrients less efficiently. Older trees need heavy pruning, soil rehabilitation, or gradual replanting with improved young seedlings to bring yields back up.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tso ko ye afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, nɔ ni ekɛbaa lɛ baa shi, ni eshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ. Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ biɔ ni afolɔ amɛ waa, asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ dumɔwui bibii ni asaa amɛhe lɛ adu fiofio koni amɛwo yibii ekoŋŋ.

english: What happens if I leave fully ripe cocoa pods on the tree for too long before harvesting them?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani mikpa?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree too long causes the beans inside to sprout and lose value. Overripe pods also attract pests and rot quickly, creating disease spots that easily infect surrounding healthy pods on the same branch.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ. Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ hu gbalaa kooloi ni fiteɔ oya. Enɛ haa helai ni fiteɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ baa. Ewaaa akɛ hela lɛ baa mɔ nine kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ.

english: When is the best time of the year for me to plant my new cocoa seedlings in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ Ghana?

english: The best time to plant cocoa seedlings in the field is at the start of the main rainy season, usually around May or June. Preparing or distributing seedlings late in the year, around November, helps ensure they are ready to go into the soil when the rains return.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ May loo June mli. Dumɔwui ahe saamɔ loo mlijaa yɛ afi lɛ naagbee November aaafee Enɛ baaye abua ni dumɔwui lɛ afee klalo ni amɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: How long will it take for my new cocoa trees to start bearing fruit after I plant them?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi-kookoo tso hee lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties in Ghana usually start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years if they receive adequate shade, water, and weed control, unlike older traditional varieties that took up to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cocoa hybrids ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ aha amɛ hulutsoo, nu kɛ jwɛi ni sa. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ kusum mli kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ ni heɔ afii 5 lɛ.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees during the dry Harmattan period around January, and how can I help them?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ Harmattan hulutsoo be lɛ mli aaafee January? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua cacao tso lɛ?

english: During the dry Harmattan season in January, cocoa trees often drop some leaves to conserve water. You can help young trees survive the dry heat by providing shade trees and spreading dry grass or leaves around the root base (mulching) to keep the soil moist.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan be mli ni hɔmɔ baa yɛ January mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ekomɛi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Obaanyɛ oye obua tsei bibii ni amɛdara. Ye ohe kɛjɛ latsaa ni mli egbi lɛ mli kɛtsɔ hulutsoo ni oooha kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni oookɛwo shishifãi lɛ ahe (mulch) koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How far apart should I plant my young cocoa seedlings on my farmland?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu kookoo tsei bibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Cocoa trees should be planted about 3 meters by 3 meters apart. Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and airflow to grow healthy and yield plenty of pods without competing with neighbouring trees.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cocoa tsei lɛ aaafee mitai 3 kɛ mitai 3 kɛjɛ amɛhe. Nɛkɛ jɛkɛmɔ nɛɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa ni tsɔɔ mli Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ adara waa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ akaŋ akaŋ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to prune or cut branches off my healthy-looking cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ bo akɛ ofolɔ loo ofolɔ kookoo niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes overgrown, diseased, or unnecessary branches so sunlight and fresh air can reach all parts of the tree. This prevents fungal diseases from forming and encourages the tree to produce more cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ niji ni edara fe nine, helai, loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ ji koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anaa, ni awo tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Do my young cocoa trees need shade from other trees, or should I clear the whole land?
ga: Ani mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ he miihia ni tsei krokomɛi aná hulutsoo? Aloo esa akɛ majie jɛmɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct, harsh sunlight can burn their leaves and dry out the soil. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides living shade that protects the young trees in their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: How do I harvest my cocoa pods without damaging the tree for future seasons?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa kookoo ŋmeii ni mifiteee tso lɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Always use a sharp harvesting hook or cutlass to cut the pod stalk cleanly off the trunk. Avoid pulling or twisting the pod off by hand, as this destroys the flower cushion where future cocoa pods must grow.
ga: Kɛ hoo loo kakla ni naa wa atsu nii. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ŋmɔ pod tso lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ pods lɛ ni okɛ oniji aaagbala loo oootsɔ mli lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, efiteɔ fɔfɔii ashishigbɛ he ni ehe baahia ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ wɔsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree during the rainy months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, humid conditions. You can prevent it by regularly pruning extra branches to let air flow through, clearing weeds, and removing infected pods immediately.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ tsei niji krokomɛi ni ooofolɔ amɛ daa koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli, jwɛi ni ooojie, kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie oya lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is my cocoa harvest heavier around November than during other months of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ni mikpaa yɛ November mli lɛ fa fe afi lɛ mli nyɔji krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Ghana has two cocoa harvest periods tied to rainfall patterns: the main crop season, which peaks between October and December/January, and a smaller mid-crop season mid-year. November falls right in the peak period when most pods ripen.
ga: Ghana yɛ kookoo kpamɔ bei enyɔ ni kɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔ he: be titri ni shwereɔ ni yaa hiɛ yɛ October kɛ December/January teŋ. ni afi teŋgbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ ni baa shi fe afi teŋgbɛ November lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ kpãa gbee beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ babaoo ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Since cocoa inputs and maintenance can be costly, how do I make sure I get the best profit from my farm?
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kookoo feemɔ kɛ ekwɛmɔ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni jara wa. Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can maximize your profit by keeping your farm properly pruned, weeding regularly, controlling pests at the right time of year, and properly drying your beans after harvest so buyers pay full price for high-quality cocoa.
ga: Obaanyɛ oná sɛɛnamɔi babaoo kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ ohe daa. Kwɛmɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni sa mli ni ogbala odumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ awo kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he nyɔmɔ fɛɛ.

english: Why do many farmers plant plantains together with young cocoa trees on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo kɛ plantains kɛ cocoa tsei bibii feɔ ekome yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that provide temporary shade, keeping the soil cool and moist so young cocoa trees can survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa, ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Will planting plantains next to my cocoa trees steal nutrients away from the cocoa?
ga: plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ani mi cacao tso lɛ baaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ cacao lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If planted with proper spacing, plantains act as friendly companion crops. They hold moisture in the soil and prevent weeds from taking over. Once the cocoa trees grow tall and strong, the plantains can be gradually thinned out.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa Dumɔwui hu tsuɔ nii akɛ naanyobɔɔ tsei. Amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ da ni ehiɛ wa lɛ, Plantains baanyɛ afee bibioo fiofio.

english: Does planting plantains on my farm help protect my soil during the dry season?
ga: Ani plantains ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ buɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Yes, plantain stems hold a lot of water inside them, and their wide leaves shield the ground from harsh sunlight. This reduces soil water evaporation and creates a cooler climate for nearby young cocoa plants.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, plantain tsei lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo. Ni amɛbaai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ haa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ baa kookoo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it important to cut down a plantain stalk after harvesting the bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stalk produces fruit only once in its lifetime and dies after harvest. Cutting it down frees up water, nutrients, and light for young sucker stems and nearby crops like cocoa.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ woɔ yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli, ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ afo lɛ ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ, ehaa tso bibioo lɛ kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ kookoo lɛ náa nu, niyenii, kɛ la.

english: If too many shoots grow from one plantain stem, they fight over soil food and water. This results in small bunches of fruit and weak stems. Leaving only one or two strong shoots ensures healthier growth.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo miikwɛ̃ kɛjɛ dumɔwu kome mli lɛ, Ebaatswa niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji aduawai bibii bibii. kɛ tso ni bɛ hewalɛ Kɛ́ ashi tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 1 loo 2 pɛ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ dalɛ ni mli wa he hewalɛ.

english: How many leaves should I keep on my plantain tree so it does not block too much sunlight from other plants?
ga: Plantain baai enyiɛ esa akɛ makɛwo midumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni amɛkatsi hulu la babaoo ni jɛɔ tsei krokomɛi amli lɛ naa?

english: Keeping 4 to 7 healthy green leaves is usually best. Trimming off yellow or dry lower leaves lets sufficient sunlight reach young cocoa trees underneath while keeping the plantain plant healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ baai eŋɔlii 4 kɛyashi 7 ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ, ni ofolɔ baai fɛɛ ni efee ŋmɔŋ loo egbi lɛ koni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ ashɛ cacao tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, plantains lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell when a cocoa pod is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A ripe cocoa pod changes color from green or deep red to a bright yellow or orange. Harvesting when yellow ensures the beans inside are fully mature and will ferment properly.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse. Kɛ́ akɛ safron tsu nii ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ, ehaa kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ kwraa ni amɛshwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my cocoa beans if I harvest the pods while they are still green?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-cocoa yibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikpa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ be mli ni amɛji ŋmɔtɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Green cocoa pods contain immature beans with low sugar content. Unripe beans will not ferment correctly, resulting in flat, bitter cocoa that buyers will reject or pay less for.
ga: Cocoa pods eŋɔli lɛ mli ŋmeii ni eshɛko, ni sugar fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Beans ni eshɛko lɛ shwieŋ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa anáa kookoo ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ baakpoo loo amɛbaawo he nyɔmɔ fioo.

english: Overripe pods begin to rot on the branch, inviting diseases like black pod disease to spread across your farm. The beans inside can also start germinating, making them unusable for sale.
ga: Pods ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ. Enɛ fɔ̃ɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ nine koni egbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hu baanyɛ aje shishi akwɛ̃. ni haaa anyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ

english: How far inside my boundary line should I plant food crops like plantain to avoid issues with neighbors?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains kɛyashɛ he ni koni mikɛ mikutsoŋbii akafee naagbai?

english: Planting crops at least two to three meters inside your official boundary keeps stems and roots strictly on your land. This prevents leaves from hanging into a neighbor's farm and avoids arguments over crop cutting or harvesting.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ mitai enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ husui lɛ amli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi baai ni shwieɔ okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋwanejeei ni kɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ loo nikpamɔ he lɛ he

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an important food plants need to stay green. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore the plant's health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ko ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I check if my farmland has the right nutrient levels before I plant my cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji niyenii ni sa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmei?

english: You can collect soil samples from different parts of your farm and take them to an extension officer or plant clinic, where they test the nutrient levels and recommend the right fertilizers.
ga: Obaanyɛ obua shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii kɛjɛ hei srɔtoi. ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni okɛya sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ he nitsulɔ loo tsei ahe helatsamɔhe lɛ. Koni aka niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa aha

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct heat and lose water quickly. Planting food crops like plantain beside them creates shade and traps moisture to protect the young trees.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ he waa, ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛbuɔ tsei bibii ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers drop off without growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Flowers often fall off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛwo baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: What is causing small holes in the leaves and center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Spraying safe pesticides or natural neem leaf extract into the plant leaves early in the morning helps get rid of them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo adebɔɔ mli neem baa ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ shwie tso lɛ baa lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems is the best way to keep your farm safe.
ga: Enɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi, ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha oŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my ripe tomato fruits developing black, rotten spots at the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit when watering is irregular. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the roots absorb calcium.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli kɛ́ afɔɔ amɛ nu be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium.

english: Why are my maize plants growing very tall and thin with small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the crops to compete for sunlight and soil food, resulting in weak stalks and smaller cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves wilt under the hot sun even after I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi beni mikɛ nu ewo amɛnɔ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wilting in wet soil usually means the roots are rotting from too much water or poor drainage, making them unable to draw up liquid to the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ miifite kɛjɛ nu babaoo loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nu lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbala kɛya baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Can I bring samples of my damaged crop leaves to the agriculture office for advice?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tso lɛ baai ni efite lɛ eko aya Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ koni amɛwo mi ŋaa?

english: Yes, extension offices run free plant clinics where officers inspect affected plant samples, identify the exact disease or pest, and advise you on how to treat your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, Extension Office lɛ kɛ helatsamɔhei ni akɛkwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ haa yaka. Amralofoi lɛ baakwɛ tsei ni ena naagbai lɛ ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii. Tsɔɔmɔ hela loo tsɛŋemɔ hela pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. ni amɛwo bo ŋaa yɛ bɔ ni ooofee okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ oha lɛ he.

english: Planting seeds too close forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with weak, thin stalks and smaller, fewer corn ears.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen in the soil or that water is sitting around the roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or clearing drainage paths helps them turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛfataa he loo nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I wait until after the rains start before putting fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ amɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ eho dani akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so the plant roots can drink it in. Putting fertilizer on dry soil can burn the plant roots, while light rain helps push the nutrients down to where roots can reach them.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã. Be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ miinɛ lɛ Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aba shi kɛya he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests build up in the ground, leading to poorer yields over time.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eha tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives and spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the pods and reduce rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ baa shi.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the juice out of the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Root rot happens when heavy rains soak the ground and water cannot drain away, suffocating the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater flow away from the tubers.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni nu nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajie kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why are flowers dropping off my tomato plants without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as severe heat, dry spells, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weather helps flowers stay on.
ga: Tomato baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ ekɛ haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, hɔmɔ ahum, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kpe. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Why do weeds seem to kill my young crops so much faster than older crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi gbeɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ oya fe tsei momo lɛ?

english: Young crops have small roots and short leaves, so fast-growing weeds easily steal all their sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Clearing weeds early gives young seedlings space to establish strong roots.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ baai kukuji. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ juɔ hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu fɛɛ mli mlɛo Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha tso bibioo lɛ aná hegbɛ ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young maize plants look completely healthy today, but overnight the inner leaves get destroyed with holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa ŋmɛnɛ lɛ? Shi nyɔɔŋ kome pɛ mli lɛ, baa lɛ mli bu ko kpata?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm feed actively during the night inside the central leaves of young maize. Daily field checks help you spot the tiny caterpillars early before they eat the growing tip and destroy the whole crop.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ yeɔ nii waa gbɛkɛ yɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli. Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ kwɛmɔ ni ooofee daa gbi lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni onaa ŋmeii bibii mra. Dani amɛbaaye ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to walk through my crop field every single morning to check under the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔ ŋmɔji amli daa leebi koni makwɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Diseases and pests usually start quietly on a few plants or under the leaves. Inspecting your field daily allows you to catch symptoms early and fix the problem before it spreads to the entire farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jeɔ shishi dioo. Yɛ tsei fioo komɛi anɔ loo baai ashishi Daa gbi nibii ni odu lɛ akwɛmɔ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona hela lɛ he okadii lɛ mra. ni amɛsaa naagbai dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn brown and dry up when I clear all the tall shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ? Mashi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade trees to act as living umbrellas that protect tender leaves from burning and keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni amɛtsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and collapse during the day even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli egbi moŋ? Ani ebaafee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that blocks the tubes carrying water up the stem. Even though the soil has water, the plant cannot transport it to the leaves, causing rapid wilting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ paipii ni kɛ nu yaa tso lɛ shishi lɛ anaa. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu moŋ Shi tso lɛ nyɛŋ ekɛya baai lɛ anɔ. ha amɛgbi oya

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their flowers instead of turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from high heat, water stress, or excess nitrogen. The plant drops flowers to save energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. nu mli haomɔ loo nitrogen ni fa fe nine Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning twisted and yellow-green even though the roots are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ shishifãi lɛ miida lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: Twisted and mottled leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, spread by tiny whiteflies. This sickness slows down food production in the leaves, resulting in smaller cassava harvests.
ga: Baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Hela nɛɛ haa niyenii ni baa yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei ni anáa lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize turn yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually show that the soil is running low on nitrogen. The maize plant naturally pulls nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the young growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛha tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my plantain stand produce very small bunches when I let all the young suckers grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ woɔ niji bibii waa beni mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ he lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow together, they steal water, light, and nutrients from the main stem. Removing extra suckers leaves energy focused on one main plant to produce a big, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Nibii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hewalɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tso titri kome nɔ koni ekɛfee tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Why does my maize field yield less grain every year when I keep planting it in the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi lɛ? Ani adu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific plant nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores soil fertility.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ mli niyenii komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start sprouting green shoots in the barn before the planting season even starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikɛto lɛ miije shishi amɛmiikwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ po jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally wake up from dormancy when warmth and humidity rise in storage. Keeping your barn cool, shady, and well-ventilated slows down early sprouting so tubers stay fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ baate shi kɛjɛ wɔɔhe be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i yaa hiɛ yɛ nitoohe lɛ. Ni oooha ŋmɔ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i, ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu abote mli jogbaŋŋ Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ fioo bɔni afee ni bulb lɛ ahi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn brown and drop off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan, dry winds strip moisture from the soil and air very quickly. Cocoa trees shed their leaves to save water, protecting the trunk and roots so the tree can survive until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya. Kookoo tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Buu tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi ahe koni tso lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra shoots growing at the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Those extra shoots, called chupons, steal water and nutrients away from the main stem. Removing them ensures all the plant's food goes into producing healthy flowers and large cocoa pods.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons nɛɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ yaa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ kookoo ŋmeii wuji ahe.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up into tight tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to hide their surface from the direct sun. This naturally reduces water loss through evaporation and keeps the plant from drying out heat during dry spells.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ akashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ baaha nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei akagbi yɛ latsaa be mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my farm make my maize grow better in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha mi ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen gas from the air and traps it in the soil. When you plant maize there afterward, it uses that trapped nitrogen as natural fertilizer to grow strong.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ jɛmɛ sɛɛ Ekɛ nitrogen ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become soft and watery if I harvest them right after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu kɛji mikpa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain forces cassava plants to suck up excessive water and start growing new stem leaves. This process drains starch out of the roots, making the tubers watery and quick to spoil.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmei tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo ni amɛjeɔ baai heei shishi. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ jieɔ starch kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛfiteɔ oya.

english: Yam leaves need as much sunlight as possible to produce energy for expanding the tuber underground. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes catches more sun and prevents ground rots.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha ŋmeii ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hulu la babaoo, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ akafite.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants turn yellow and fall off when I water them every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Too much water fills all the small air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots. When roots cannot breathe, they stop taking up food, causing the leaves to turn yellow and drop.
ga: Nu babaoo eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Be ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu Ebaakpa niyenii yeli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without making any fruits when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extremely high temperatures dry out and destroy the pollen inside tomato blossoms. If pollen dies before fertilizing the flower, the plant drops the unused flower to save energy.
ga: He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli gbɛ́ɔ ni efiteɔ. Kɛji pollen gbo dani ewo fɔfɔi lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni akɛtsuuu nii koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do black, rotten patches appear at the bottom of my tomatoes before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ tomato shishi dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the growing fruit. It usually happens when watering is uneven, preventing the plant from steadily carrying calcium up from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛwo calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do small green insects swarm my cabbage farm as soon as the rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shwieɔ mi-cabbage ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Insects like aphids reproduce much faster in dry, warm weather. Rain normally washes them off leaves, so when dry weather sets in, their numbers increase rapidly without rain to knock them down.
ga: Koolooi tamɔ aphids fɔɔ oya yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli egbi ni edɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ shwieɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ kɛ́ hulutsoo be ba lɛ Amɛyibɔ ​​baaya hiɛ oya ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ ni baatswa amɛ shi.

english: How do I know if my land is good for growing rice instead of maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi ŋmãa najiaŋ?

english: Rice grows best in low-lying flat areas or valley bottoms with clay soil that holds water well, whereas maize prefers higher, well-drained soil where water does not sit for long.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa loo jɔɔ lɛ shishi ni shikpɔŋ sũ ni ŋmɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɔɔ nɔ. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nu lɛ etsɛɛɛ tsɔ.

english: Why does my rice land need to be leveled flat before I start planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ dani adu lɛ?

english: Leveling your land ensures water spreads evenly across the field so every rice plant gets the same amount of water, which stops weeds from taking over high, dry spots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni afee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ haa nu lɛ mlijaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa baaná nu abɔ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni jwɛi akaye hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni egbi lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it better for me to scatter rice seeds directly on the farm or nurse them first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ magbɛ ŋmaa lɛ mashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo makwɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Raising seedlings in a nursery bed and transplanting them to the field gives your rice plants a strong head start over weeds and leads to a bigger harvest compared to scattering seeds directly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ooodu yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni okɛwo ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa o-rice tsei lɛ náa sɛɛnamɔ fe jwɛi. ni ekɛ ŋmaa babaoo baa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni agbɛɔ ashwaa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my rice plants need so much standing water in the field while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ he hiaa nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ mli beni eduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Water keeps the soil soft for roots to grow easily, regulates temperature, and acts as a natural barrier to prevent common weeds from suffocating the crop.
ga: Nu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ oya. hulutsoo be mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ jwɛi ni afɔɔ namɔ naa koni ekaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen nutrients or the soil water is stagnant and choking the roots, preventing them from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye onibii lɛ kɛha nitrogen niyenii. Aloo nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsĩɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haaa anyɛ aha amɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do improved seed varieties from government programs give me more rice bags than my old seeds?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ kɛjɛ nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoo ko mli lɛ aha mi ŋmãa kotokui babaoo fe dumɔwui momoi lɛ?

english: Modern improved seeds are bred to grow more stalks per plant and heavier grain heads, allowing you to harvest more food from the exact same size of land.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛná ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tso fɛɛ tso mli kɛ dumɔwui ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ he ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow faster than my crop after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal food faster than crops; clearing weeds before applying fertilizer ensures your plants get all the nutrients to boost production.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi dani akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni haa amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: What causes my rice stalks to fall over flat right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani akpaa?

english: Rice stalks fall over when they grow too tall and weak from using too much fertilizer or when planted too close together, making them unable to support heavy grain heads in strong wind.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ amɛkwɔ tsɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli loo kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ, ni no haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛfi dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do birds attack my rice farm mostly when the grains are young and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi tutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ babaoo lɛ? Ani dumɔwui lɛ dara lolo ni amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ?

english: When rice grains start forming, they contain a sweet, milky liquid that birds easily feed on before the grain hardens into rice.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa ŋmaa je shishi efee Nu ko ni tamɔ mliki ni okpoi baanyɛ aye mlɛo dani ŋmaa lɛ mli awa ni etsɔ ŋmãa lɛ baahi.

english: Harvest when about 80 percent of the grain heads turn golden yellow; waiting until the whole plant dries completely causes grains to shatter and fall to the ground, wasting your crop.
ga: Kpamɔ be mli ni aaafee dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ amli oha mlijaa 80 etsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ mɔ ko mɛ kɛyashi tso muu lɛ fɛɛ baagbi kwraa lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: If my land has been left unused for many years, will crops grow well on it right away?
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ tsuuu nii afii babaoo lɛ, ani dumɔ nii lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Land left untouched for many years usually recovers its natural nutrients and organic matter, making it fertile. However, you need to clear deep roots, test the soil, and break up hardened ground so crop roots can easily take root and absorb water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ashi ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ afii babaoo lɛ baaná adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ. Shi kɛlɛ, ha efee nɔ ni woɔ yibii, no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ otsi shishifãi lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ, oka shikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ, ni ogbala shikpɔŋ ni wa fɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli koni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ atswa shishifãi oya ni amɛŋɔ nu.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and hard even though the plant leaves look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe wa eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soft, loose soil to expand freely. If the soil beneath the surface is hard or compacted, the roots cannot swell properly to grow big, even if the leaves above ground look lush and tall.
ga: Kasava shishifãi taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã amɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli wa loo ebɔle ehe lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ koni amɛtsɔ agbo. Eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛlɛ moŋ, shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that your maize plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil or getting choked by too much water around its roots. Adding proper fertilizer or improving field drainage helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli loo oha nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers often fall off when the weather gets excessively hot or when the plant experiences drought stress. Extreme heat stops pollination from happening, causing the plant to drop its flowers to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ he haomɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baatsi pollination naa. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt and die during the sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have shallow roots that cannot reach deeper soil water, so strong afternoon sun dries them out faster than they can absorb moisture. Providing light shade and watering early in the morning helps them survive.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ nu he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, shwane hulu ni naa wa lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gĩɔ oya tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ aha amɛ hulutsoo kɛ nu leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Why do crop roots rot when heavy rain leaves standing water on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei shishifãi fiteɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air in the soil to breathe just like humans do. When excess water sits on the field for too long, it cuts off oxygen to the soil, causing the roots to drown, decay, and rot.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ebaafo kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛgboiɔ, ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops even when there is little rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to survive harsh conditions with very little water and nutrients. They aggressively steal sunlight, space, and moisture from your cultivated crops if they are not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli kɛtsɔ nu fioo kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ. Amɛjuɔ hulu la, ŋwɛi, kɛ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ amli lɛ kɛ ekãa. Kɛji akɛ ajieee mra

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete heavily with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and weak, resulting in smaller harvests overall.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afee lɛ fɛɛ fioo.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans alongside my main crops help the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special crops that naturally trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This feeds nearby crops like maize and improves soil fertility without needing extra chemicals.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ náa niyenii, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai krokomɛi fataaa he.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every season. It also allows specific pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the soil, reducing your total yield over time.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ fɛɛ baa shi yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin without producing big cobs when I plant many seeds together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛbɛ toi wuji beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo feɔ ekome lɛ?

english: When planted too close, maize plants compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of putting energy into growing thick stalks and heavy cobs, they stretch upwards to reach the sun.
ga: Kɛ adu Abele tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a haa tso ɔmɛ nɛ a mi wa kɛ tso ɔmɛ nɛ a tsiɔ nɛ a ngɛ wae ɔ he wami. Amɛbaashɛ hulu lɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to build green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Will planting beans alongside my maize help or harm my crop?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ baaye abua loo ebaaye mi ŋmãa lɛ awui?

english: Planting beans with maize helps your soil because beans take nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground, which feeds the maize and yields two crops from the same land.
ga: Beans ni akɛ ŋmãa baadu lɛ baanyɛ aye abua oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni ewoɔ ŋmãa henɔi 2 kɛjɛɔ he kome

english: If I save seeds from my harvested maize to plant next season, will they yield as well as certified seeds?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ to koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, Ani nakai dumɔwui lɛ baawo yibiiwoo ni awo he odaseyeli kɛ dumɔwui?

english: Seeds saved from old harvests lose their strength over time and produce lower yields. Certified seeds are specially bred to resist local pests and produce much bigger cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ momo mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli ni ebaawo yibii babaoo. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji babaoo.

english: Why is maize such a vital feed crop for farm animals like chickens?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔ mli kooloi tamɔ kooloi lɛ?

english: Maize kernels are packed with concentrated energy that chickens digest easily, helping them grow fast and produce strong eggshells better than most other local grains.
ga: Akɛ hewalɛ ni mli wa ni tsinabii nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ oya lɛ eyi ŋmãa mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa fe maŋ lɛ mli ŋmaa krokomɛi babaoo.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes in the leaves and cobs of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mibaai kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli?

english: These are usually Fall Armyworms that hatch on the plant and feed on the soft growing centers. Checking your field early and applying recommended treatments keeps them from destroying the cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms ni fɔɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛyeɔ hei ni shwereɔ yɛ blɛoo lɛ. Ohe ni oyɔɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni atsɔɔ lɛ ni oooye nɔ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmei lɛ.

english: Why does maize grain become so scarce in local Ghanaian markets right before the main harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaana ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ Ghana maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei dani kpamɔɔ titri lɛ?

english: Maize supply drops because old stock from the previous season runs out while the new crop is still drying in the fields, creating a temporary gap where demand is higher than supply.
ga: Abele nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ miiba shi yɛ be mli ni nibii momo ni yɔɔ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ miiho yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii heei miiho lolo yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Enɛ haa be kukuoo mli gbɛ ko baa he ni nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni akɛhaa lɛ.

english: How do I know when my maize is mature enough to harvest without spoiling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni efiteee?

english: Maize is ready when the outer husks dry completely brown and a small dark layer forms at the tip of the kernel, showing the grain has stopped growing and is safe to dry.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi kwraa ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko yɛ jɛmɛ. Ebaa yɛ dumɔwu lɛ naa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ekpa shweremɔ ni abaanyɛ agbi amɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do tiny insects turn my stored dry maize into powder after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tsakeɔ mi-abele ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ powda yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: These insects are maize weevils that bore into dry kernels to lay eggs. Properly drying your grain and storing it in airtight sacks or using approved storage dust prevents them from multiplying.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji ŋmãa ŋmeii ni tsɔɔ ŋmãa ni egbi mli koni amɛwo amɛwui. Dumɔwui ni agbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo akɛ sũ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtoɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ baatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafa babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea early in the season helps restore healthy green foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is my cowpea farm growing thick green leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi dumɔwui ŋmɔji fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cowpea plants to focus on growing leaves rather than producing flowers and pods. Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen from the air, so they need fertilizers rich in phosphorus instead to encourage pod development.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ awo mli moŋ koni ekɛha pod lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I choose the best plantain suckers to plant for a strong harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu koni maná ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: Look for maiden suckers, which have sharp, narrow sword-like leaves and a broad base, rather than water suckers with wide leaves. Maiden suckers grow faster, resist strong winds better, and produce larger bunches of fruit.
ga: Taomɔ tsei bibii ni baai lɛ mli tse ni tamɔ klante kɛ shishi ni mli kwɔ. Yɛ nu mli tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, Bamboo tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya. Ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo

english: The first rain is often followed by a heat wave or a short dry spell that can dry out and kill tiny newly sprouted seeds. It is safer to wait until the rainy season is fully established so the soil stays consistently wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No baanyɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baagbe naa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience water stress, extreme sun heat, or attack by tiny pests like mirids. Maintaining good shade trees and ensuring soil stays cool helps flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji nu mli haomɔ kpe amɛ. hulu la ni mli edɔ loo tutuamɔi ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen mli baa. Kɛ́ aha fɔfɔi lɛ hulutsoo kpakpa ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and stake my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo shi lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb up stakes to capture sunlight, which supplies energy to swell the tubers underground. Keeping leaves high off wet soil also prevents fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛná hulu la. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ baai helai ni ji fungal lɛ anaa.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are ready for harvest without digging them all up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni okɛ amɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower stem leaves turn yellow and drop, and the earth around the main stem begins to crack upwards.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso titri lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids, mites, or thrips sucking leaf juices, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. Spraying neem leaf oil can help control these small insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, mites, loo thrips ni nuɔ baa nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Neem baa mli fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ.

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is typically caused by bacterial wilt, a soil organism that blocks water movement inside the plant stems. Rotating crops each season stops this bacteria from building up in your farm soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Amɛji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni tsiɔ nu ni nyiɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli lɛ naa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni oootsake daa be lɛ haaa nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do farmers spread dry leaves and grass around the bases of their vegetable plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi shwieɔ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi amɛshwieɔ amɛ aduawai ni amɛduɔ lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Spreading dry leaves around plants, known as mulching, keeps the hot sun from evaporating soil moisture, cools the plant roots, and prevents unwanted weeds from taking over.
ga: Baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa Tsei lɛ ahe, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akafee ŋmɔtɔ. ehaa tsei ashishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ akaye nɔ.

english: How long will it take for my cashew trees to start producing nuts after I plant them?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mi-cashew tso lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii kɛji midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cashew trees usually take 3 to 5 years to start producing nuts if grown from seeds, but grafted varieties can start bearing fruit as early as 2 to 3 years after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cashew tsei lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ ŋmeii feemɔ shishi kɛji akɛ amɛdu kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli. Shi tsei srɔtoi ni akɛwo mli lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or maize between my young cashew trees?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Mi cashew tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, intercropping food crops between young cashew trees is recommended during the first 3 years because it helps keep weeds away and gives you food and income before the trees mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔɔ akɛ adu niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ cashew tsei bibii ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 3 lɛ mli ejaakɛ enɛ baaye abua ni agbe jwɛi ni eha niyenii kɛ shika aba dani tsei lɛ adara.

english: How far apart should I space my cashew trees when planting them on my land?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ mi-cashew tsei lɛ abɔ he beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cashew trees should be spaced about 10 meters by 10 meters apart because their branches spread out wide as they grow, and crowded trees produce far fewer nuts.
ga: Esa akɛ cashew tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 10 x mitai 10, ejaakɛ niji lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Ni tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cashew saplings turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young cashews usually mean the soil is holding too much water and choking the roots, or the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ cashews nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miihiɛ nu babaoo ni ekɛmiitsi shishifãi lɛ anaa. Aloo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Do my young cashew trees need to be watered during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni awo mi-cashew tso lɛ nu yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli?

english: While older cashew trees survive drought easily, young trees in their first two years need watering during severe dry spells so their root systems do not dry out.
ga: Cashew tsei ni edara po yeɔ hɔmɔ nɔ mlɛo. Shi ehe miihia ni awo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ amli lɛ nu yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli. koni shishifãi lɛ akagbi

english: Why are the flowers on my mango tree dropping off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mango tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Mango flowers often fall off due to fungal diseases like anthracnose during damp weather, insect attacks, or sudden dry spells that prevent the flowers from setting fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ anthracnose ni yɔɔ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli, kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ, loo trukaa ni amɛgbiɔ ni haaa fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii lɛ ahewɔ.

english: Is it better for me to plant mango seeds directly or buy grafted seedlings?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooodu mango tɛ̃ɛ loo ooohe ŋmeii ni akɛwo mli lɛ?

english: Grafted seedlings are much better because they produce fruit in just 2 to 3 years instead of 5 to 7 years, stay shorter for easier harvesting, and guarantee good fruit quality.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ mli moŋ fe afii 5 kɛyashi 7. Be kukuoo lɛ haa anyɛɔ akpaa yibii mlɛo. ni eha aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba

english: How can I protect my ripening mangoes from being ruined by fruit flies?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-mango ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ he koni aduawai amli ŋmeii akafite amɛ?

english: You can protect your mangoes by hanging fruit fly traps in the tree canopy, picking fruits early once they start changing color, and burying all fallen damaged fruits.
