ga: Obaanyɛ obu o-mango lɛ he kɛtsɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ nɔ. Gbalamɔ aduawai mra. Beni ejeɔ shishi etsakeɔ ehiɛ su ni efuɔ aduawai ni egbee shi lɛ fɛɛ

english: How deep and wide should I dig the hole before planting a new mango seedling?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo bu lɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ elɛɛmɔ mli eha tɛŋŋ dani madu mango heei?

english: Dig a hole about 60 centimeters wide and 60 centimeters deep, mix the topsoil with well-rotted manure or compost, and fill the hole back up to give the roots loose, fertile soil.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ bu ko ni elɛɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimita 60 ni elɛɛmɔ aaafee sɛntimita 60. Okɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ afutu ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ bu lɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why is it necessary for me to prune or trim the branches of my fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ loo mafolɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing light and air into the tree center, which reduces diseases and helps the tree produce larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ tso lɛ teŋ. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai srɔtoi baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does the crop medicine I sprayed on my cocoa trees take a few weeks before I see any visible improvement?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ cacao lɛ nɔ lɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi dani minaa hiɛyaa ni kadiɔ mɔ lɛ?

english: Systemic crop medicines work from the inside out. The plant absorbs the chemical through its leaves or roots and distributes it throughout its system, which takes time to stop diseases or kill pests completely.
ga: Tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ tsofai kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai loo amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛjaraa amɛ yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ heɔ be dani enyɛɔ ekpaa hela lɛ kwraa loo ejieɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ kɛyaa.

english: Will applying more chemical medicine than recommended make my crops grow faster and yield more?
ga: Ani tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe bɔ ni ajieɔ yi lɛ baaha mitsei lɛ adara oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: No, using more chemical than recommended can burn the plant's leaves, damage the soil, and leave harmful chemical residues on your harvest. Always stick to the exact dosage recommended by extension officers.
ga: Dabi, tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashã. ni kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ ni ebaanyɛ eshi tsofai ni eshwɛ yɛ okpamɔ lɛ mli. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ye tsofa pɔtɛɛ ni mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ wo he ŋaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Does rain wash away farm medicine if it falls right after I spray my crops?
ga: Ani nugbɔ lɛ baaho tsofa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, if heavy rain falls within 2 to 4 hours after spraying, contact chemicals can be washed off before the plant absorbs them. It is best to spray early in the morning on clear days.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 2 kɛyashi 4 mli yɛ be mli ni ashwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Abaanyɛ afɔ tsofai ni kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee lɛ ahe dani tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Esa akɛ afɔse nɔ leebi yɛ gbi ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: How many times in a season am I supposed to spray chemical medicine on my maize crop to protect it from armyworms?
ga: Shii enyiɛ yɛ be mli ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ koni ekɛtsi ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ anaa?

english: Most crops only need 2 to 3 well-timed applications per season depending on pest presence. Spraying too often wastes money and causes chemical resistance, while spraying too little allows pests to recover.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo he miihia ni atsa amɛ shii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Edamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ tsɔ lɛ heɔ shika ni ekɛ tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa fioo pɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Should I keep spraying my crops with protective medicine even after the pests seem to have disappeared?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maya nɔ mafɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe tsofa lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ etee moŋ?

english: No, continuous spraying after pests disappear is unnecessary and builds chemical resistance in insects. Only spray when you scout your field and notice fresh signs of pest re-infestation.
ga: Dabi, ehe ehiaaa ni aya nɔ ashwie tsofa lɛ nɔ beni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ elaaje lɛ sɛɛ. ni otswa tsofai ni yɔɔ kooloi amli lɛ ahe hewalɛ Oshwie nɔ kɛji okwɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni ona okadii heei ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi krokomɛi eba.

english: How long before harvesting my vegetables should I stop applying chemical medicines?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii dani akpa aduawai?

english: Every chemical has a safe pre-harvest interval, usually between 7 to 21 days. You must stop spraying during this period to allow the chemical to break down so your produce is safe for consumption.
ga: Tsofai fɛɛ yɛ be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe dani akpaa nii. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ yaa nɔ yɛ gbii 7 kɛyashi 21 teŋ. Esa akɛ okpa tsofa lɛ shwiemɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli koni tsofai lɛ akumɔ koni eha onibii lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ.

english: How can I tell if the pesticide medicine I applied to my tomato plants is actually working?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsu nii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You will notice new green leaves growing without spots or yellowing, flowers staying on the stem instead of falling, and a clear reduction in active insects under the leaves within a few days to two weeks.
ga: Obaana baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni miida ni ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli. Fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ shishi moŋ fe ni amɛaagbee shi. ni kooloi ni tsuɔ nii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ba shi kwraa yɛ gbii fioo komɛi kɛyashi otsii enyɔ mli.

english: If I apply crop medicine in October, will it keep my plants protected all the way until the December harvest?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii yɛ October mli Ani ebaabu mitsei lɛ ahe kɛyashi ŋmaakpamɔ yɛ December mli?

english: Most treatments only protect plants for 2 to 4 weeks depending on rainfall and chemical strength. A single treatment in October will not last until December, so you must monitor your field and re-apply if necessary.
ga: Tsofai babaoo baabu tsei ahe otsii 2 kɛyashi 4 pɛ, ni enɛ damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ tsofai lɛ ahewalɛ nɔ. Tsamɔ kome ni afeɔ yɛ October mli lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ kɛyashi December. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni okwɛ onitsumɔhe nine lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ ohe awo mli ekoŋŋ kɛ ehe miihia.

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed leaves during dry periods to reduce water loss and survive heat stress. Providing adequate shade trees and maintaining soil moisture helps them retain leaves until the rainy season.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be ni sa ha tsei lɛ, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ahi shi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do some cassava varieties take over a year to harvest while others are ready in just six months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi heɔ nɔ ni fe afi dani akpaa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni srɔtoi komɛi efee klalo yɛ nyɔji enumɔ pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different cassava varieties have distinct genetic growth timelines. Early-maturing varieties build up starch quickly for short rainy seasons, whereas traditional varieties grow larger roots over a longer period.
ga: Cassava henɔi srɔtoi Ayɛ be srɔtoi ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ buaa ŋmeii anaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni kusum mli henɔi lɛ yɛ shishifãi wuji yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa plants dying when there is too much rain and the soil stays completely soaked?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ gboiɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Too much standing water smothers plant roots because they cannot breathe. If the soil remains soaked without drying out, the roots rot, causing the cocoa crop to fail.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ fiteɔ tsei shishifãi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ tee nɔ efee ŋmɔtɔ ni egbiko lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baagboi, ni no baaha kookoo tso lɛ akatsu nii.

english: How can I tell if my farm ground is too wet for cocoa to grow properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni esaaa akɛ aduɔ kookoo jogbaŋŋ?

english: If rainwater pools on the surface and the ground stays muddy without drying out between heavy rains, the soil is too wet and can cause root rot in cocoa plants.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tee nɔ efee muji ni egbiko yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi ni yɔɔ cacao tso lɛ mli lɛ agbo.

english: What should I do if heavy rain keeps falling and soaking my farmlands every day?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa miiho miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa gbi?

english: You should create small drainage channels to help excess water flow away from your plants, preventing the roots from sitting in soaked soil and decaying.
ga: Esa akɛ ofee gbɛ bibioo ko ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ afu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu ewo mli lɛ mli ni amɛkagbo.

english: Is it bad for my cocoa trees if the ground never dries out between rainfalls?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tsei lɛ baaná he sɛɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ?

english: Yes, cocoa roots need the soil to dry out slightly between rains so air can reach the roots. Constant wetness starves the plant of oxygen.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kookoo shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi fioo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ. koni kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe Nu ni yaa nɔ ehaa tsei lɛ náa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa.

english: How many years does it usually take for newly planted cocoa trees to start bearing fruit?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ yibii?

english: It typically takes about four years after planting for cocoa trees to mature and begin producing a good harvest, provided they are properly cared for.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ adu kookoo sɛɛ lɛ, eheɔ aaafee afii ejwɛ dani kookoo tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛjeɔ yibii kpakpai feemɔ shishi. Kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ

english: Should I wait for my cocoa seeds to sprout before I plant them in the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ dani madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Allowing seeds to sprout slightly before planting gives them a head start in establishing roots, but you must plant them carefully so the tender shoots do not break.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ fioo dani adu lɛ, ehaa amɛjeɔ shishifãi lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ. Shi ehe miihia ni odu jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni okakumɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ.

english: Why does cocoa require so many years of waiting before you get any harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni kookoo amɛ afii babaoo dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a long-term tree crop that needs several years to build a strong trunk and deep root system before it has enough energy to produce cocoa pods.
ga: Kookoo ji tso ko ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni ekɛ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ baa dani enáa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Why do I need to clear the weeds and bush from under my cocoa trees for them to produce well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ koni maná ŋmaa kpakpa lɛ?

english: Clearing the undergrowth removes competition for soil nutrients and sunlight while improving air movement around the trees, helping them yield more pods.
ga: Nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la lɛ he lɛ kɛyaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔleɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: What usually causes young cocoa plants that I planted to fail?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo tsei bibii ni miduɔ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants often fail due to waterlogged soil that drowns the roots, poor weeding maintenance, or planting seeds that were not cared for properly during early germination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ fiteɔ ejaakɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni no haa amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. Jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ. loo adu dumɔwui ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ.

english: When is the right time to clean under my cocoa trees to help them yield fruit?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ atsumɔ cacao tso shishi koni ewo yibii?

english: Clearing under your trees should be done regularly as they mature, especially around the fourth year when the trees are ready to start bearing their first full harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie tsei ashishi daa be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ afi ni ji ejwɛ lɛ mli, beni tso lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaaje eklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn brown and drop off whenever muddy water overflows into my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni nu ni mli ewo muji baaho kɛba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When dirty or stagnant water sits on cocoa roots for too long, it cuts off the oxygen supply to the soil and damages root hairs, making it impossible for the tree to drink water or absorb nutrients.
ga: Beni nu lɛ mli ewo muji loo ehi shi yɛ kookoo shishifãi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni efiteɔ shishifãi ahe yitsɔi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ anu nu loo eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants rot at the stem base and die after heavy rain leaves water pooling in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛgboiɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shiɔ nu yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Pepper roots suffocate easily in waterlogged soil, allowing harmful fungal rot present in wet ground to invade and destroy the base of the stem.
ga: Pepper shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ oshara ni ji rot fungi lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ, ni amɛtutuaa tso lɛ shishi ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with big green leaves, but the tubers underneath remain tiny and woody?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi yitso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji bibioo lolo ni eyɛ tso?

english: When soil is heavily packed or lacks balanced nutrients like potassium, the cassava plant puts all its energy into leaf growth above ground instead of swelling its roots underground.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa, tamɔ potassium bɛ mli lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, e sisi ɔmɛ puɛɔ ngɛ zugba sisi.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers take so long to grow when planted on land that was previously cleared by heavy earth-moving equipment?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei bibii lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ akɛ nibii ni tsii ni akɛjieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy machinery packs the topsoil tightly together and strips away the rich top layer of soil, making it very hard for young plantain roots to push through and search for food.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii haa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ ekome ni ejieɔ ŋwɛi sũ ni baa nii lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa plantain shishifãi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaabote mli ni amɛna niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow starting from the middle tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛteŋgbɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips on young maize are a clear sign of nitrogen starvation, which happens when the soil lacks the basic food crops need to make dark green, healthy leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei lɛ yɔɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni eyɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turning black and rotting before they get a chance to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ naagbeei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, which occurs when tomato plants cannot get enough calcium from dry or unevenly watered soil while building their fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo ahaaa amɛ nu be fɛɛ be be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die during the dry season if I cut down all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli kɛji mifo tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and thin leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight, so they need shade trees like plantains or forest trees to keep them cool and hold moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni kookoo dumɔwui lɛ aná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cowpea plants drop all their flowers without forming bean pods during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baaa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants drop their flowers as a defense mechanism when they suffer from severe heat or water stress, saving energy to survive rather than producing seeds.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ miipiŋ amɛ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛhiɔ shi lɛ baa shi yɛ dumɔwui ni ajieɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very thin and fall over when I plant three or four seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛmiigbee shi beni mikɛ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When multiple seeds grow in the exact same spot, the plants compete fiercely for the same soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, resulting in weak, skinny stems that break easily in the wind.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni egbɔjɔ ni kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa amɛ lɛ, amɛkuɔ oya.

english: Why does my farm yield fewer bags of maize each year even though I plant on the exact same plot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be moŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the land time to recover, causing soil fatigue and letting crop-specific pests accumulate in the ground.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔ̃ɔ ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build healthy green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer to the soil helps restore this nutrient so the maize can grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops yield less harvest when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop feeds on from the soil and allows pests to build up. Rotating maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts puts vital nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ajɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ Haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive and burn easily under strong sun. They need shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to act as living umbrellas and keep the soil cool during their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ kã ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy storms when they start producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli beni ejeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots near the top of the soil, so when a heavy bunch grows, the top becomes unbalanced. Supporting the stems with strong wooden props or bamboo sticks prevents the wind from pushing them over.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ kuu lɛ da lɛ, ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei ni wa fĩ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ akatsɔ mli.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my crops even when there is plenty of rain for everything?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ waa kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal nutrients, space, and fertilizer directly from your crops' roots. Clearing weeds ensures your main crops get all the soil food they need to produce a full harvest.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni daa oya ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, he ko, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aná shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ kpakpa.

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to make food for the tuber underground. Lifting the vines off the ground onto stakes gives the leaves full access to sunlight, which results in larger, healthier yams.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are tiny ragged holes suddenly appearing in the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eje kpo trukaa yɛ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These holes are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the growing center of the maize stem and eat the soft leaves. Inspecting plants early and applying safe control methods stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Kɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baatsi amɛnaa dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curl is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or mites that suck the plant's juices and spread crop viruses. Controlling these insect pests early keeps the leaves flat and healthy so the plant can produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni nuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ awo yibii.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe, but waterlogged soil smothers the roots and encourages fungal diseases to rot them. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds helps water drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Shi shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ewoɔ fungal rot hela lɛ he hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the days are extremely hot or when the plant doesn't get enough water, which prevents proper pollination. Providing regular watering and light shade during hot spells helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa lɛ naa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Young cocoa plants have soft leaves and weak root systems that lose water quickly in direct sun. They need shade crops like plantains or bananas to shield them from high heat until their root systems grow deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ. ni nu fiteɔ oya kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo banana he miihia amɛ. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baaya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing on cassava is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties helps protect your crop from this problem.
ga: Kasava lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela kɛbaa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe kɛjɛ naagba nɛɛ he.

english: How do I know if my maize crop is hungry for fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mi-ŋma lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your maize leaves start turning pale green or yellowing near the bottom in a V-shape pattern, or if the stalks remain thin and short, the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen and needs fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-corn baa lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ni efee V su. Aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli etse lolo ni eyɛ kuku Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering and light shade during heatwaves help prevent this.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Planting corn seeds too close together forces the plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak stalks and very small corn cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant room to produce bigger ears.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ahe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni abele ŋmeii lɛ hu daraaa kwraa. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tsei atsu fɛɛ tsu náa toi wuji.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my planted crops right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ nɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to survive easily in local soil. They sprout quickly to steal water and fertilizer before your crops can establish strong roots, which is why clearing weeds early is necessary.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi mlɛo yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔji anɔ. Amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya koni amɛju nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia

english: Yam tubers rot underground when the soil holds too much water without proper drainage, creating a swampy environment where fungi thrive. Planting yams on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni nu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ewo muji ni ŋmeii baanyɛ ada yɛ mli lɛ baa. Sweet potato ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why is it bad to plant groundnuts on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting groundnuts in the exact same spot year after year allows soil-borne pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating groundnuts with crops like maize breaks the disease cycle and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ abua shikpɔŋ lɛ naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛduɔ nii tamɔ ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ehaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Removing weak or unnecessary branches allows sunlight and air to flow through the tree canopy. This prevents damp diseases like black pod and forces the tree to direct its energy into producing large, healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni he waaa loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ helai ni mli ewo fɔ tamɔ ŋmeii diji anaa, ni enyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ atsu nii koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Maize must be fully dried because moist grains attract mold and dangerous toxins like aflatoxins, as well as pests like weevils that will eat and destroy your stored crop inside the bags.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi kwraa ejaakɛ ŋmãa ni mli efɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmãa kɛ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ aflatoxin, kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ŋmãa ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmãa ni baaye ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛto kotokui amli lɛ.

english: What makes an improved crop variety like Abena perform better than the local seeds I usually plant?
ga: Mɛni haa tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ tamɔ Abina lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni miduɔ daa lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties like Abena are specially bred by agricultural researchers in Ghana to resist common local pests, tolerate heat, and yield significantly more harvest than traditional local seeds.
ga: Okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ji mɛi ni ekwɛ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ Abena lɛ anɔ krɛdɛɛ. Kɛha maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Heat resistant ni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ.

english: Can I take part of my harvest from this season and use it as seeds to plant my farm next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ maŋɔ mikpamɔ lɛ fã ko kɛjɛ be nɛɛ mli ni mikɛtsu nii akɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli afi ni baa lɛ?

english: While traditional seeds can be saved and replanted, high-yielding improved or hybrid seeds lose their vigor and high productivity when replanted. Buying fresh certified seeds each season guarantees the strong growth and yields you expect.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ abaanyɛ ahere shishijee dumɔwui lɛ ayiwala ni adu ekoŋŋ moŋ. Shi dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ loo ni akɛ amɛ ebɔ he ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ, amɛhewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo baa shi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ ekoŋŋ. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ni ooohe yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa anáa dalɛ ni mli wa kɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni okpaa gbɛ lɛ.

english: Why does a crop variety that yields very well in one region of Ghana struggle to grow in another region?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii waa yɛ Ghana kpokpaa ko nɔ lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ kpokpaa kroko nɔ lɛ?

english: Different regions in Ghana have distinct soil types, rainfall amounts, and temperatures. Crop varieties are bred for specific climatic conditions, so a variety tailored for forest regions will struggle in drier savanna zones.
ga: Ghana kpokpai srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi srɔtoi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ latsaa. Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi anaa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni etsake amɛhe amɛwo kooi amli hei lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ waa yɛ hei ni savannah ni mli egbi lɛ.

english: How do I determine the right amount of space to leave between my crops when planting them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni sa ni esa akɛ ashi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ kɛ́ midu nii?

english: Proper spacing prevents plants from competing against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Correctly spaced crops grow stronger, develop larger yield, and allow better airflow to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei ni akɛ amɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ baakwɛ̃ waa. Ha nitsumɔ babaoo aya hiɛ Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ni etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every time I plant on the same field without giving it a break?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Every crop pulls specific nutrients out of the earth during growth. Without adding fertilizer, compost, or letting the land rest, the soil becomes exhausted, leading to smaller yields with every new planting season.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite, ni no baaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi yɛ dumɔ be hee fɛɛ be mli.

english: Is it better for my farm to plant just one single crop across the whole land or mix different crops together?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ baadu ŋmɔshi nibii kome yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ loo ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni akɛfutu mli?

english: Mixing complementary crops, such as legumes alongside grain crops, improves soil fertility by trapping nitrogen, naturally reduces pest damage, and protects you from total loss if one crop fails.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni ehiɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ kwraa he kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kome fite.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my crops turning yellow before they even produce fruits or grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani amɛwo yibii loo dumɔwui po lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a cry for help indicating a lack of nitrogen in the soil or waterlogged roots from heavy rains. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps plants stay dark green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji yelikɛbuamɔ he bolɔmɔ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi ni edɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do insects seem to destroy some farms in my community while skipping other farms nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ ŋmɔji komɛi ni yɔɔ mikutso lɛ mli lɛ, yɛ be mli ni amɛhoɔ ekrokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Pests naturally target weak or nutrient-starved crops first. Farms with healthy soil, proper plant spacing, and clean weed management maintain strong defense systems that make them far less attractive to pest attacks.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai baatutua tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Okwaafoi ni shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɔɔ mli Gbɛ ni sa ni ka tsei ateŋ Kɛ jwɛi ni he tse nɔkwɛmɔ haa hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa hiɔ shi. Enɛ haaa amɛhe afee fɛo kwraa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why are the flowers on my crops falling off during long dry spells before they turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: When crops suffer from water stress during flowering, they drop their flowers as a survival mechanism to save energy. Mulching the soil retains moisture and helps plants hold onto their blossoms to produce fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii na nu he haomɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛto hewalɛ he. Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: How can I tell when my crop is completely ready for harvest so I do not pick it too early or too late?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ nikpamɔ? No hewɔ lɛ, mibuaaa naa oya tsɔ loo mikɛ mihe wooo mli blɛoo tsɔ?

english: Crops show clear physical signs of maturity: leaves turn yellow or brown, stalks dry out, and grains or tubers reach full firmness. Harvesting at full maturity ensures maximum weight, better taste, and a longer storage life.
ga: Nibii ni adu lɛ jieɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshwere lɛ kpo. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo asasu, tsei lɛ agbiɔ, ni dumɔwui loo bulbs lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ kwraa. Nikpamɔ beni ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ haa eshɛɔ shwiili ni fa fe fɛɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ shihilɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Yellowing and curling maize leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen or is being attacked by pests like fall armyworms. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or applying appropriate pest control early helps the leaves turn green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworm miitutua lɛ. Nitrogen babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli loo ni akɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baatsu nii mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe awa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my sweet potato leaves full of small holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ?

english: Small holes in sweet potato leaves are caused by leaf-chewing beetles or caterpillars eating the crop. Clearing weeds around the farm and using recommended sprays stops these insects from destroying the leaves before tubers grow fully.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ sweet potato baai amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ajiemɔ Okwaa ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite baai lɛ dani bulb lɛ adara kwraa.

english: Why is a white powder forming on the leaves of my garden eggs and vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powda yɛŋ ko yɔɔ ŋshɔŋloo kɛ aduawai ahe baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: That white powder is a common fungus called powdery mildew, which grows in warm, humid weather when plants are packed too closely together. Pruning crowded leaves to allow air flow prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Pauda yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛ́ tsei bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ahe tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my cassava stems grow tall and leafy, but the tubers underground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛyɛ baai lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or cassava is planted in deep shade, the plant puts all its energy into leaf growth instead of building root tubers. Plant cassava in full sunlight and avoid over-fertilizing with nitrogen-heavy manure.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo dumɔ ŋmei yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee shishifãi. Dumɔ cassava yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni okɛbaafata he lɛ he.

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when stressed by intense heat, drought, or insect attacks from pests like mirids. Providing light shade trees and controlling pests at the start of the season keeps flowers healthy enough to turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ afee tsei lɛ shade ni akudɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my yam sprouts when the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi sweet potato tsei lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds naturally have aggressive roots that soak up rainwater and soil nutrients faster than young yams can. Clearing weeds early in the season stops them from choking young yam vines before the crop canopy develops.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni boteɔ mli ni baanyɛ aŋɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii oya fe ŋmeii bibii. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkagbe sweet potato wein tsei bibii lɛ anaa dani tso lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant multiple maize seeds too close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and tiny cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough resources to grow big, healthy cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmei agbo ni mli wa.

english: When tomatoes get too much water, their lower leaves turn pale yellow, droop even when the soil is wet, and stems rot near the ground. Planting on raised soil beds allows excess water to drain away safely.
ga: Kɛji tomato ná nu babaoo lɛ Eshishigbɛ baai lɛ baafee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Amɛgbeeɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efɔ moŋ. ni tso lɛ baagbo yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: What causes the tips of my pepper leaves to look like they are burned after spraying medicine?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ashã yɛ be mli ni mikɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Burnt leaf tips usually happen when crop spray is mixed too strong or when chemical fertilizer touches the plant leaves directly. Always dilute chemicals strictly according to instructions and apply fertilizer in a ring around the plant stem, not directly on it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ yitso shãa baa kɛji akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ futu mli waa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, shwiemɔ tsofai lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ taakɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo ŋwɛi ŋta ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ he, shi jeee tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my groundnuts grow better on a field where I planted maize the year before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ ni midu ŋmãa yɛ mli nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rotating crops breaks the cycle of soil pests and diseases specific to one plant type. Groundnuts also naturally restore the soil balance by fixing nitrogen, making them thrive after heavy-feeding crops like maize are harvested.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ lɛ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii henɔ kome pɛ lɛ. Agbɛnɛ hu, ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ekome ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni esaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛshwereɔ beni amɛkpa niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do most farmers avoid planting major crops in January and February?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji adumɔ he yɛ January kɛ February mli lɛ?

english: January and February fall within the peak dry Harmattan season in Ghana, where low rainfall and dry soil prevent seeds from germinating properly, making it a better time for land clearing and planning rather than active planting.
ga: January kɛ February baagbee shi yɛ Harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haaa dumɔwui akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa efeɔ be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛbaajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ fe ni akɛ ekãa baadu ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I clear and prepare my farm land weeks before the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ ni masaa he otsii komɛi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Clearing early gives you enough time to clear weeds, remove debris, and loosen the soil so that when the first major rains fall, the ground is ready to soak up water and accept seeds immediately.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔji ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oná be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛjie jwɛi lɛ, ojie sũ ni efite lɛ, ni ojie sũ lɛ bɔni afee ni kɛ́ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ nɛ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ afee klalo amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni eŋɔ nu ni ená dumɔwui.

english: It is usually better to wait until the rains become regular, because the first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell that can scorch and kill newly sprouted seedlings.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ anɛ bɔ ni sa. No ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nyiɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baanyɛ ashã ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, their roots and leaves fight for the same sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leaving every plant weak and undernourished.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tse lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ nu ni falɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ Enɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ amɛmli.

english: Why is it harmful to plant cassava or maize in the exact same field year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How does growing beans or groundnuts alongside my maize help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and naturally fix it into the soil, providing free, natural fertilizer that helps companion crops like maize grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni fata he, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: What causes the leaves on my green crop plants to turn yellow during the growing period?
ga: Mɛni haa mi tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants lack essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that too much standing water around the roots is choking the plant's intake of oxygen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli, loo nu ni damɔ shi ebɔle ehe. Shishifãi babaoo haaa tso lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dry grass and leaves during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai yɔɔ mli yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the earth, shields young plant roots from intense sun heat, and helps prevent weed growth.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Buu tsei bibii ashishifãi ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi lɛ akakwɛ̃

english: Why do vegetable seeds like tomatoes need to start in a nursery bed before moving to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ aje aduawai dumɔwui, tamɔ tomato shishi yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani adu awo ŋmɔ titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato seeds are very delicate; growing them in a protected nursery bed allows you to easily shade, water, and defend them against pests until they become strong enough for the main field.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui lɛ waaa kwraa. Kɛ́ odu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji ni abuɔ he lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa onáa amɛhe hulutsoo, ohaa amɛ nu, ni obuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe mlɛo. Kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔ wulu lɛ

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil and grow mold inside my storage room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ miifite ni miifee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Grains spoil and develop mold if they are put into storage before being fully sun-dried, because residual moisture creates an ideal environment for fungi and pests to multiply.
ga: Ŋmaa baafite ni ebaaná ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni akɛtoɔ nii dani agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants scorching and turning brown in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to full, direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or leaving shade trees provides a canopy that protects young cocoa leaves from burning and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni ashiɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with small caterpillars hiding inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani okɛ ohe ewo gbɛjegbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm. They feed on the young, growing leaves inside the central whorl of the maize plant, and early intervention with recommended treatments into the funnel is necessary to prevent crop loss.
ga: Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ lɛ. Ni ehe miihia ni akɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ atsu nii mra koni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward, twisting, and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe, amɛmiibɔle amɛhe, ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is often caused by a virus spread by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or aphids. Controlling these insects early and removing heavily infected plants prevents the virus from spreading through the whole farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ni tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft, watery, and rot in the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, nu yɔɔ mli, ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and sits in the soil for too long during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away and prevents root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make food for the underground tuber to grow big. Lifting the vines on stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight and reduces moisture-related leaf diseases on the ground.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la babaoo shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe, ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients can cause tomato plants to drop their blossoms. Consistent watering and placing mulch around the root zone helps keep the soil cool and moist so flowers can form fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli Loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ. Nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ daa Shishifãi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why should I cut down most of the young shoot suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ ateŋ babaoo lɛ?

english: Too many suckers compete with the mother plant for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning to leave only one or two strong suckers allows the main plant to produce a bigger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli koni eshi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: The first rain often creates a false start where the soil becomes hot and moist, but no rain follows for weeks. Waiting until regular, consistent rains begin prevents seeds from germinating and then dying from drought.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shishijee ni ejaaa baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baadɔ ni edɔ hu. Shi nugbɔ enɛɛɛ otsii komɛi. Kɛ́ wɔmɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baatsi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkagboi yɛ hɔmɔ mli.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans together with my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ du ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi-ŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. This natural nitrogen feeds the surrounding soil, helping companion crops like maize grow greener and stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni fata he, tamɔ abele, ni amɛdaraa eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are my crops growing small and yellow even after I spread chemical fertilizer on the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ eshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: If fertilizer is applied too close to stems, it can burn the roots, or if the soil is too acidic, the roots cannot absorb the nutrients. Spreading fertilizer a few inches away from stems and adding organic compost improves nutrient absorption.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ he tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi inchi fioo ko pɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and build strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛma tsei ashishifãi ni wa.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly starves the soil of specific nutrients and allows pests and diseases that love that crop to multiply and stay hidden in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi akafee nɔ ko. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ tsei lɛ babaoo ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my young crops with dry bush grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Midumɔwui kɛ jwɛi?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass acts like a protective blanket that keeps rainwater from evaporating quickly in the sun, keeps the plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Mulch ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning dry even when the weather is not too dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni egbi eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ lɛ mli egbiko tsɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that transmit viruses into the plant, or by extreme heat stress that forces the plant to hide its leaves from the sun.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies, ni kɛ helai baa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛbaai lɛ ato hulu lɛ he lɛ mli.

english: Why do my sweet pepper plants suddenly droop and die in the middle of the day while still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell pepper tso lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting while leaves are still green is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a soil germ that gets inside the stem and blocks water from moving up from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ trukaa be mli ni baai lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bacteria wilt baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni boteɔ tso lɛ mli ni ehaaa nu lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are my yam vines turning black and dying off before it is time to harvest the tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigboi dani be ni akɛkpaa ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ lɛ?

english: Blackening yam leaves and stems are caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose, which spreads rapidly through farm fields during warm and rainy weather.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato baa kɛ eshishifãi ni etsɔ ediŋŋ lɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil holds too much water during heavy rains without proper drainage, causing fungal rot to attack the wet tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa rot fungus lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their flowers before any pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shi dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from water stress during dry spells, or when tiny pests like mirid bugs bite and damage the delicate stems holding the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna nu he haomɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ kooloi bibii ŋmɔ ni amɛfite tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmɛɔ fɔfɔii lɛ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees easily fall over when a small wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko pɛ tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when invisible microscopic worms or root borers eat away the underground roots, leaving the tall heavy plant with no firm grip in the soil.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shishifãi ni anaaa amɛ lɛ ye shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei kakadaji lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to plant cowpeas or beans inside the same farm with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmɔ mli ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, acting like a natural fertilizer that feeds nearby maize plants while giving you two crops on one land.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Officer, why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Officer Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellow and curling leaves usually mean your maize is either lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen, suffering from drought, or being attacked by pests like fall armyworms. Checking under the leaves can help identify if insects are damaging the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni hɔmɔ miipiŋ. loo ŋmeii tamɔ cutworms tutuaa lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli Baai lɛ ashishi kwɛmɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni ana kɛji ŋmeii miifite tso lɛ.

english: I see small white spots and fine webs under my cassava leaves, is my farm sick?
ga: Mina ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ kɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ ŋmeii baai lɛ ashishi. Ani hela mɔ miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, those spots and webs are caused by pests like spider mites or mealybugs, which suck the sap out of cassava leaves and weaken the plant. You can treat this by spraying an appropriate pest control product recommended for cassava.
ga: Hɛɛ, nakai ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni ji mealybugs lɛ kɛbaa. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmei baa lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Obaanyɛ otsa enɛ kɛtsɔ nibii ni sa ni akɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee kɛha ŋmei lɛ ni oookɛshwie nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my pepper fruits developing black spots and rotting before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni egboɔ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Black spots on pepper fruits are usually caused by a fungal sickness that thrives in high humidity and excessive moisture. Removing infected fruits early and improving space between plants for better air flow helps stop the sickness from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ pepper aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Ajieɔ aduawai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra ni ahaa gbɛ ni kã tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ebaaye ebua ni hela akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How do I know the right time of day to spray medicine on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: The best time to spray crop medicine is early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the sun is gentle and the wind is calm. Spraying in harsh afternoon heat causes the chemical to evaporate too quickly or burn the leaves.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ tsei anɔ tsofa ji leebi loo shwane mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ fioo ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu tswaa dioo. Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ shwane latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ loo ehaa baai lɛ shãa.

english: If my crops are very sick, can I mix two different plant medicines together to make it stronger?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hela mɔ amɛ waa Ani manyɛ mafutu tsei ahe tsofai enyɔ koni amɛhe awa?

english: No, mixing different plant medicines without professional guidance can damage your crops and pose health risks. Some chemicals react badly when combined, which can destroy the leaves or make the medicine completely useless.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ okɛ tsei ahe tsofai futu mli ni ŋaawolɔi komɛi bɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite oŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛ hewalɛnamɔ he osharai aba. Tsofai komɛi kɛ amɛhe wo mli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ, ni no baanyɛ afite baai lɛ loo eha tsofa lɛ afee nɔ ni he ehiaaa kwraa.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme weather heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Giving them consistent water and light shade during peak dry periods helps them hold flowers.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔ ko ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu kɛ hulutsoo ni anáa daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Why are my cocoa trees shedding many of their leaves during the dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ baai babaoo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry seasons to protect themselves from losing too much water. Plantaining shade trees alongside young cocoa and putting dry mulch around the base of the trees helps retain soil moisture during droughts.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ kɛfataa kookoo bibii ahe kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing huge green leaves but producing very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen in the soil, they focus all their energy on growing thick green leaves instead of building tubers underground. Balancing soil nutrition helps the plant direct energy into growing bigger roots.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shishifãi wuji lɛ anɔ.

english: How do weeds make my crops grow slow and remain weak?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ blɛoo ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm, competing directly with your crops for soil food, water, and sunlight. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crops get all the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Gbalamɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha tsei titrii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I stop a sickness on one side of my farm from spreading to the rest of the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi hela ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ fã kroko lɛ mli?

english: You can prevent sickness from spreading by promptly removing and burning infected plant parts, washing your farm tools after working in sick areas, and avoiding walking through healthy crops right after touching sick ones.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa kɛtsɔ efãi komɛi ni ooojie kɛjɛ ohe lɛ nɔ. ni ajieɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ashãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ahe kɛji otsu nii yɛ hei ni helatsɛmɛi yɔɔ lɛ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe nyiɛmɔ he kɛji ota tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why did my maize produce a good harvest in the first year, but now in the second year on the same land the harvest is very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ wo yibii jogbaŋŋ nɛkɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ? Shi amrɔ nɛɛ yɛ afi ni ji 2 lɛ nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ŋmaa lɛ faaa kwraa?

english: Crops pull up natural nutrients stored in the dirt during their first season. If you do not add manure or fertilizer back into the soil after harvesting, the ground becomes exhausted and cannot feed a second heavy crop.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee shoo ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ lɛ hu nyɛŋ aye abua.

english: I spent a lot of money buying expensive fertilizers, so why are my crops growing tall with lots of leaves but producing very few fruits?
ga: Mifite shika babaoo kɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Using too much of one type of fertilizer, like nitrogen, forces the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of putting energy into flowering and fruiting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome, tamɔ nitrogen tsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ɔ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ atsu nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfɔ̃ ni ewo yibii

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant beans together with my cassava instead of planting cassava alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei afee ekome kɛdu ŋmei lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmei kɛkɛ?

english: Beans take nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the dirt through their roots, which naturally feeds the cassava and keeps the soil fertile without extra costs.
ga: Beans gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Eji adebɔɔ mli ŋmei niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛ shika kroko fataaa he.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow even though I am giving them plenty of water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa lɛ nu babaoo daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much water drowns the roots so they cannot breathe or absorb food from the soil, which causes the leaves to turn yellow and starve.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ fe nine lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ ashwie shi kɛyashɛ he ko ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Why are my vegetable plants growing thin and tall without strong stems when I plant them under big shady trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Most crops need direct sunshine to manufacture their food; when grown under heavy shade, they stretch upwards toward the light, making them weak and fragile.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ pii biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii. Kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ dara yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, amɛbaagbala amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya la lɛ he, ni no baaha amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛhe afee shoo.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together in the field, won't I harvest more food from the farm?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli Ani minyɛŋ makpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food, resulting in stunted plants that yield very little crop.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just save seeds from my harvested maize to plant next season instead of buying new seed bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohe dumɔwui kotoku hee

english: Many modern commercial seeds are specially bred hybrids designed for a single powerful harvest; planting the seeds saved from that harvest produces weak crops with small yields.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ jarayeli dumɔwui babaoo ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni akɛkpaa nii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Dumɔwui ni yeɔ wala yɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yibiiwoo faaa lɛ aba.

english: Planting the same crop continuously builds up specific pests and diseases in that soil year after year while draining the exact same nutrients without giving the land time to recover.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli daa lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛ aba nakai sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ehaaa sũ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster and bigger than the crops I carefully plant and care for?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛdaraa fe tsei ni miduɔ ni mikwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that have adapted over centuries to survive harsh conditions, allowing them to steal soil food and water much faster than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ kooi amli ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Why are destructive insects attacking my farm much more this season than they did during my very first season of farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii babaoo miitutua miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli fe bɔ ni amɛfee yɛ miŋmɔshi nitsumɔ be klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When you farm the same spot continuously, local pests discover a reliable food supply and stay to breed, creating much larger insect populations with every new season.
ga: Kɛji oya nɔ otsu okwaayeli yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akutsoŋ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baaná niyenii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni hiɔ shi daa ni amɛkɛbaafɔ bii. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ayibɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ be hee fɛɛ be hee mli.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient it needs to grow. It can also happen when heavy rain causes water to sit around the roots for too long, preventing the plant from taking up food from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa lɛ koni eda Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I avoid burning the dry bushes on my land when preparing the soil for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni ashãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he beni misaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha dumɔ nii lɛ?

english: While burning clears the land quickly, the heat destroys important living organisms and organic material in the soil. Without this organic matter, the soil loses its ability to hold water and nutrients for your crops.
ga: Beni la ni tsoɔ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya lɛ Shi latsaa lɛ kpataa nibii ni he hiaa waa kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ. Kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa oŋmɔshi nii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it helpful to plant groundnuts or beans on the same plot where I harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpaa ŋmei yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of food from the soil as it grows. Groundnuts and beans are legumes, which means they have roots that actually pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the ground, restoring fertility to your soil for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni edaa lɛ. Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How does covering the soil around my young vegetable plants with dry grass help them grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, leaves, or crop waste is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, traps moisture so you water less, and stops weeds from taking over your crop field.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the plant suffers from environmental stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil from irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. When the plant is stressed, it cannot afford to feed developing fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni jɛɔ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli baa. loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni tsei lɛ miihao Anyɛŋ amɛha aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ niyenii

english: Why must I clear weeds from my crop field as early as possible after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ oya bɔ ni manyɛ beni midu nii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crops are small and weak, so they lose easily when competing with weeds. Weeds grow fast and steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight your young crops desperately need to establish strong roots.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛlaajeɔ oya kɛ́ amɛkɛ jwɛi miitswa akaŋ. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei bibii lɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites sucking the sap out of the young leaves. It can also be caused by viral diseases spread by whiteflies. Checking under the leaves early helps catch these pests before they ruin the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni haa chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ hu baanyɛ ekɛba. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni amɔmɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite tso lɛ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, cold, and humid conditions. Trimming excess shade branches and removing infected pods quickly helps airflow and stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo fe nine lɛ amli ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are mature and ready to harvest underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and dropping off naturally, and the ground around the base of the stem will begin to crack as the tubers grow bigger.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Obaayɔse akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baabɔi mligbalamɔ be mli ni bulb lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches. If pests like nematodes damage these roots underground, the plant loses its grip on the soil. Supporting the stem with a wooden prop helps hold it up during strong weather.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ kooloi tamɔ nematodes kpata nɛkɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi nɛɛ ahiɛ lɛ, Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ akpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he dɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni edamɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do my mango trees drop so many of their flowers before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo dani yibii lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?
