english: Mango trees naturally produce thousands of blossoms, but many drop due to dry Harmattan winds, extreme heat, or insect pests. The tree naturally sheds flowers it cannot support so it can focus energy on a smaller, healthy batch of fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi yɛ Harmattan, latsaa ni naa wa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahewɔ. Tso lɛ baawo fɔfɔi ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama aduawai akuu bibioo ko nɔ. ni hi kɛha gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ

english: Why do my pineapples get yellow burn marks on one side while they are still growing in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple lɛ yɛ shãa he okadi ni ji ŋmɔŋ yɛ efã kome be mli ni amɛdaraa lolo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Intense afternoon sunlight can scorch the side of the pineapple facing direct heat. Farmers often cover the growing fruits with dry palm leaves or straw to shade them and prevent sunburn damage.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã ŋmei lɛ fã ni kɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ kpeɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi kɛ ŋmei baai ni egbi loo jwɛi haa aduawai ni miida lɛ ahe koni ekɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni hulutsoo akafite amɛ.

english: Why are the fruit bunches on my young oil palm trees filled with tiny, empty nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ yibii ni yɔɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ nɔ lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: This usually happens because of poor pollination. Oil palms rely on small insects like palm weevils to carry pollen; if pollinator activity is low, flowers do not develop proper seeds inside the fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ pollination ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ. Mu tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ tsei amli ŋmeii anɔ koni amɛkɛ pollen awo mli. Kɛji akɛ pollinator nitsumɔ lɛ faaa lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baafee dumɔwui ni sa yɛ aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with huge leaves, but the roots under the ground stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or too much shade, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and stake my yam vines instead of letting them crawl on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mijieɔ jwɛi kakadaji ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ fĩɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahã amɛkpã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines onto stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight and air, which helps the plant make more energy to build big, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Maize leaves roll up as a survival trick to protect themselves from intense sun and conserve water by reducing the surface area exposed to dry air.
ga: Abɛi ni afolɔ mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni okɛbuɔ nu he kɛtsɔ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni ooofee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce plenty of flowers but fail to form any seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo dumɔwui ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Extreme heat during flowering or tiny insects called thrips eating the blooms can stop pollination, causing the flowers to fall off before pods can form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli loo kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ thrips ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ baanyɛ akpa pollination. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant lacks calcium while the fruit is forming, often caused by irregular watering that stops roots from taking up nutrients properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji calcium bɛ tso lɛ mli be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni haaa amɛná niyenii kpakpa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids hiding on the underside of leaves, or a virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Why is it recommended that I plant plantain suckers beside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛɔ akɛ adu plantain dumɔwui yɛ mimasɛi lɛ? kookoo dumɔwui heei

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have wide leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is short on nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to build green leaves. Adding compost or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ŋmãa babaoo koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in their roots. When the plants die, that nitrogen stays in the ground, acting as natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. They need shade from larger trees or temporary shade crops like plantains to keep them cool and retain moisture until their roots grow deep enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛha tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo mli bɔ ni sa.

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground allows their leaves to catch maximum sunlight, which the plant uses to make food. This extra food goes straight down into the tuber, giving you much bigger yams at harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa etso lɛ naa hulu la babaoo, ni tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛhoo nii. Niyenii krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ yaa yitso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa onáa sweet potatoes ni dara kwraa kɛji akpa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When soil stays flooded with water for too long, the roots cannot breathe and fungal diseases quickly take hold, causing the tubers to rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli baa lɛ baaye nɔ oya. ha yitso lɛ agbo

english: Covering the ground, also known as mulching, shields the soil from the hot sun so water doesn't evaporate as fast. It keeps the roots moist, prevents weeds from popping up, and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya tsɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaje kpo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ

english: If too many suckers grow at once, they all steal water and nutrients from the main plant. Removing most of them leaves only two or three strong shoots, ensuring the main stem produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo miida shikome lɛ, Amɛbaaju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii fioo komɛi pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha ŋmeii titri lɛ aná plantains wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce smaller yields when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are crowded, their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other and their roots fight for the same soil nutrients, causing weaker growth and fewer peppers.
ga: Beni pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ baa shi, ni ŋmeii hu faaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and dropping their blossoms without setting fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and flower drop are often caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit viruses, causing stress that forces the plant to abandon its flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ fɔfɔi ni laajeɔ lɛ baa. Nu ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwaa Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haa tsei lɛ shiɔ fɔfɔii lɛ baa.

english: Why does leaving weeds in my farm lower my crop yield even if I use good soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa tsuɔ nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and aggressively steal sunlight, root space, and nutrients from your crops, effectively starving your plants before they can reach full size.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ hulu la, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otso lɛ dani eda kɛyashɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen in the soil, which is their main food for growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK at the right time helps them turn green and produce strong ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa amɛdaraa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eha toi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around their crops with dry grass and fallen leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egboi kɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. Dry grass acts like a blanket over the ground, trapping moisture during dry spells, keeping the soil cool, and preventing weeds from growing and stealing nutrients from your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Jwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ boteɔ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ ni amɛju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows maize-specific pests to build up in the field. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. ni ehaa ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ehaa nitrogen lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to protect their soft leaves from harsh sunlight and to keep the soil moist. Leaving some large shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa provides the shelter young seedlings need to survive.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shi tsei wuji koni amɛha hulutsoo loo dumɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo masɛi koni amɛha dumɔwui bibii lɛ aná wɔɔhe. ni he hiaa koni anyɛ ahi shi

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food that feeds the growing tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground so they get maximum sunlight and stay safe from fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni miida lɛ niyenii. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni eha hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛ shweshweeshwe shihilɛ kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: If too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same soil food and water. Leaving only two or three strong shoots ensures the main plant produces big, heavy bunches of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ, Plantain kome Plantain muu lɛ fɛɛ baatswa niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo dumɔwui wuji ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop when the weather gets too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or if the plant lacks calcium. Regular watering early in the morning helps the plants retain their flowers and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ejaaa loo kɛji akɛ calcium bɛ tso lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii amli.

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide deep inside the leaf funnel of the maize plant. Spraying an recommended pesticide directly into the center funnel early in the morning destroys them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ baai amli shɔŋŋ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaakpata amɛhiɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot underground mainly when water collects in the soil and stays too wet for long periods. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away and protects the roots from rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehi shi ni edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites that feed on the leaf sap. Spraying the leaves with targeted organic or chemical remedies stops the insects and allows healthy new leaves to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ akpa ni eye ebua baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How do I know if the piece of land I bought is suitable for growing maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni miheɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Maize requires deep, loose soil that drains water easily and has plenty of organic matter. If your land is very rocky, heavy clay, or holds standing water for days after rain, maize roots will struggle to grow, leading to stunted plants and poor yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli edɔ ni nu hoɔ oya ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmãa. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ tɛi babaoo shikpɔŋ ni tsii Aloo nu ni ekã shi gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Abɛi shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ wa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: If my land is too dry or rocky for maize, what other crops can I plant on it?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo eyɛ tɛi ni akɛduɔ ŋmãa hu? Mɛɛ tsei srɔtoi manyɛ makwɛ?

english: Crops like cassava, cowpeas, and groundnuts are much hardier than maize. They can grow in poorer, drier, or tougher soil because their deep root systems can reach hidden moisture, and legumes like cowpeas even help feed nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, tsina ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa wa fe ŋmãa kwraa. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, ni egbi, loo ni wa nɔ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Ni ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Is burning the clearing residue after clearing my new plot good or bad for crop growth?
ga: Ani nibii ni eshwɛ ni ashãa beni ajie mi saatso hee lɛ sɛɛ lɛ hi loo ehiii kɛha tsei adalɛ?

english: While burning clears the field fast and releases a quick burst of ash nutrients, it ultimately damages your soil. It kills friendly soil organisms and burns away organic matter that keeps the soil cool and moist during hot spells.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ haa he ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli tseɔ oya ni ejieɔ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Shi yɛ naagbee lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Egbeɔ nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo lɛ, ni eshãa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni no haa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ waa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ.

english: Will applying chemical fertilizer fix soil that is hard and difficult to farm on?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ asaa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ewa akɛ aaakwɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer provides plant food, but it cannot fix hard or compacted soil on its own. You must first improve the soil structure by tilling or adding organic matter like poultry manure, which softens the soil so roots can absorb the fertilizer nutrients.
ga: Fertilizer ni akɛhaa tsei niyenii Shi enyɛŋ esaa shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Esa akɛ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo klɛŋklɛŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsu he nii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ kooloi afɔfɔi ni oookɛfata he lɛ nɔ, ni no baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ.

english: Why does my maize turn yellow and stay small even after I plant on fresh bush land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efee bibioo lolo eyɛ mli akɛ midu yɛ jwɛi shikpɔŋ hee nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves and stunted growth usually mean the plants lack nitrogen, which is essential for leaf development. Freshly cleared land may still lack active nutrients, so adding well-rotted manure or a nitrogen-based fertilizer early in the crop's life will turn the leaves green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ ashweremɔ Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ kpo ehee lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ lolo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: When is the right time to give fertilizer to my maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa awo ŋmãa mli?

english: Maize needs nutrients at specific growth stages. Give a small basal fertilizer application right at or shortly after planting to help root formation, followed by a second boost (top-dressing) when the stalks reach knee-high to support rapid growth and cob development.
ga: Abɛi biɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko mli yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ. Ha ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ afeemɔ. Nɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli shii enyɔ nɔ. (Top fertilizing) beni tso lɛ yitso lɛ shɛɔ etsitsi nɔ koni eye ebua ni eda oya kɛ cob lɛ shweremɔ.

english: What is the main difference between using animal manure and bag fertilizer for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Bag chemical fertilizers give your crops a fast, direct burst of nutrients, while animal manure releases nutrients slowly and improves the soil's structure so it holds water better. Using both together often yields the best results.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ haa otsei lɛ naa niyenii kpakpai ni yaa oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kooloi ashishifãi jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii fiofio. ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ aya hiɛ koni nu lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ tsu nii ekome lɛ, nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ baa.

english: Why do corn plants die when rainwater sits on my field for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei gboiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi nɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the air in the soil to breathe. When water covers the field without draining, oxygen cannot reach the roots, suffocating them and causing the plant to rot and die.
ga: Tsei shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ha ŋmɔ ko nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tso lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my young corn crops on a newly prepared field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe mi-baby corn tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ni misaa ehee lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit naturally in the soil and are adapted to sprout aggressively as soon as rain and sunlight hit them. Because they grow faster than young corn shoots, you must clear weeds early before they steal all the water and soil nutrients from your crop.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni atsake lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ni hulu la lɛ tswa lɛ pɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmãa bibii. Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra. Dani amɛbaaju nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: What happens to my maize if I plant the seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa koni ekɛ mihe lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the plants compete fiercely with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of getting more maize, you will end up with tall, thin, weak stalks that produce very small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona ŋmãa babaoo Ogbeɔ naa kɛ ŋmãa ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmãa bibii waa loo eko kwraa.

english: What are the early signs that my cocoa tree is infected with Cocoa Swollen Shoot disease?
ga: Mɛni ji klɛŋklɛŋ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ emɔ kookoo bloat hela?

english: A key sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot disease is when the leaves and the whole cocoa tree start turning pale instead of keeping their healthy green color.
ga: Okadi titri ni tsɔɔ akɛ cacao lɛ mli efu ji be mli ni baai lɛ kɛ cacao tso muu lɛ fɛɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahiɛ amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli.

english: I know insects like capsids damage cocoa trees, but how are diseases different from pest attacks?
ga: Mile akɛ kooloi tamɔ capsids fiteɔ cacao tsei. Shi mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe?

english: While pests like capsids directly attack and feed on the cocoa tree, severe diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot infect the tree internally, causing it to turn pale and eventually fail to respond to standard treatments.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids lɛ tutuaa cacao tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛyeɔ amɛ moŋ, shi helai ni mli wa tamɔ cacao ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ enyɛɛɛ etsu tsofafeemɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ he nii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees turn pale, and can I cure them by applying regular farm treatments?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Ni ani abaanyɛ atsa mi kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ nɔ?

english: When cocoa trees turn pale, it is often caused by Cocoa Swollen Shoot disease. Trying to fix or treat an infected tree does not work, and the tree usually needs to be removed.
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ shwieɔ shi Bei pii lɛ, kookoo mli fũu hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni akɛ tsofa awo tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli loo atsa amɛ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ. Ni bei pii lɛ, ehe bahiaa ni ajie tsei.

english: Can a cocoa tree recover on its own once it starts turning pale from sickness?
ga: Ani cacao tso lɛ baanyɛ atsa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛji hela mɔ lɛ pɛ?

english: No, if the paleness is caused by Cocoa Swollen Shoot disease, attempts to fix the tree will fail, and it will not recover on its own.
ga: Dabi, kɛji akɛ cocoa bloat hela lɛ hewɔ ni su lɛ tsakeɔ lɛ. Mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni asaa tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni bɛ sɛɛnamɔ. ni enyɛŋ ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ

english: Why would an agricultural officer tell me to cut down my sick cocoa tree instead of treating it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ moŋ fe ni matsa amɛ lɛ?

english: When a tree contracts Cocoa Swollen Shoot disease, chemical treatments and repair efforts no longer work, so cutting down the infected tree is the only effective way to handle the disease.
ga: Kɛji akɛ Cocoa Swollen Shoot hela lɛ ye tso ko nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛsaa tso lɛ tsuuu nii dɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ hela nɛɛ he nii.

english: What pests should I be watching out for on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui esa akɛ makwɛ mihe jogbaŋŋ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Capsids are common pests that attack cocoa trees and cause damage, which can lead to drops in farm production if left unchecked.
ga: Capsids ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tutuaa cacao tsei ni efiteɔ nii. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ aba shi kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: My cocoa farm yield has dropped lower than it has been in over eight years; what should I do?
ga: Yibii ni anáa yɛ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eba shi fe fɛɛ yɛ afii kpaanyɔ ni eho lɛ mli. Mɛni esa akɛ mafee?

english: When production drops significantly over a long period, you should monitor how the farm is doing and report the issue to agricultural extension leaders so they can assess the situation and assist you.
ga: Kɛji nibii ni anáa lɛ ba shi waa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ, Esa akɛ Okwɛ bɔ ni oŋmɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ehaa lɛ nɔ ni obɔ naagba fɛɛ naagba ni ba lɛ he amaniɛ otsɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ ahiɛnyiɛlɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni amɛkwɛ oshihilɛ lɛ mli ni amɛye amɛbua bo.

english: How can agricultural extension officers help me when my farm production drops?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ beni ŋmɔ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ miiba shi lɛ?

english: Agricultural leaders can visit your farm to help identify whether pests or diseases are causing the problem and offer assistance and plans to help revamp your farm's production.
ga: Okwaafoi ahiɛnyiɛlɔi baanyɛ ayasara oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛye amɛbua amɛ ni amɛna kɛji kooloi loo helai kɛ naagbai baa. ni okɛ yelikɛbuamɔ kɛ gbɛjianɔtoi ni baaye abua ni nibii ni anáa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ aha.

english: Why is it important for me to monitor my farm's harvest levels over several years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ makwɛ bɔ ni ŋmaa lɛ yaa hiɛ ehaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Tracking production year after year helps you notice major, unusual drops—such as declines not seen in eight years—so you can seek expert help early before problems spread.
ga: Nibii ni afeɔ lɛ asɛɛnyiɛmɔ afi fɛɛ afi baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona shigbeemɔi ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ, tamɔ shigbeemɔi ni ebako yɛ afii kpaanyɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ otao ŋaalɔi ayelikɛbuamɔ mra. Dani naagba lɛ baagbɛ eshwa

english: If I am forced to clear sick cocoa trees from my farm, how can I get help to rebuild my cocoa business?
ga: Kɛji akɛ anyɛ minɔ koni majie kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná yelikɛbuamɔ ni mikɛma mikookoo nitsumɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: You can reach out to agricultural leaders who can step in to provide support, guidance, and resources to help you revamp your farm work after removing diseased trees.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ okwaayeli he hiɛnyiɛlɔi ni baanyɛ abote mli ni amɛkɛ yelikɛbuamɔ, ŋaawoo, kɛ nibii ni baaye abua bo ni oha oŋmɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ abɔ beni ajie tsei ni helai emɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why should I plant plantains on the same land where I am starting my young cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mije mi-kookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ shishi yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow very fast with broad leaves, acting like living umbrellas to provide essential shade and moisture while the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela koni ekɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa aha be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings looking scorched and weak even though I keep the farm clear of weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛshã ni amɛgbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ jwɛi efo ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa needs protective shade from direct sunlight. Without nurse plants like plantains to block the harsh heat, direct sun exposure will cause the cocoa seedlings to suffer and dry out.
ga: Kookoo bibioo he miihia hulutsoo, hebuu kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei tamɔ plantains bɛ ni baatsi hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ naa lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do plantains help keep the soil safe and healthy for my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ plantains yeɔ ebuaa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Plantain plants trap moisture in the soil beneath their broad leaves and create a cooler climate, which protects young cocoa roots from heat damage.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ toɔ nu yɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ ashishi ni ehaa kɔɔyɔŋ mli jɔɔ. Enɛ buɔ kookoo shishifãi bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Is it normal for my plantain plants to grow big leaves within the first six months of planting?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni ja akɛ mi-plantain lɛ baaná baai wuji yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji enumɔ ni akɛdu lɛ mli?

english: Yes, plantains naturally grow rapidly in their first six months, shooting up large leaves quickly so they can establish shade and gather energy from sunlight.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains daa oya yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji enumɔ lɛ amli. Amɛ jieɔ amɛ baai agboi lɛ oya koni amɛ fee shade ni amɛ bua hewalɛ naa kɛjɛ hulu lɛ mli.

english: Why do plantain fruits stay attached to the stalk when ripe while other red fruits drop to the ground on their own?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains lɛ kpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛji ekwɛ̃ yɛ be mli ni aduawai tsuji krokomɛi feɔ nakai lɛ? Ani lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ebaagbee shikpɔŋ?

english: Plantain bunches are firmly anchored to the plant stalk and do not naturally fall off when ripe. If a plantain stem drops or falls, it is usually due to physical damage or pest disruption rather than natural fruit drop.
ga: Plantain ŋmeii lɛ kpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛgbeee shi kɛji amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji plantain lɛ tso lɛ gbee shi Bei pii lɛ, gbɔmɔtsoŋ nibii ni efite loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nɔ ni fe adebɔɔ mli yibii ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ

english: Why do young plantain plants uproot so easily when something pushes or pulls on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ shishifãi shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nɔ ko tsi amɛ loo egbala amɛ lɛ?

english: Young plantain suckers have shallow, soft root bases during their early months, making them easier to pull out of the ground compared to woody trees with deep taproots.
ga: Plantain bibii lɛ yɛ shishitoo ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ akɛto tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my plantain plant look like it wants to outgrow all the other crops on my farm so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi dumɔwui lɛ miisumɔ ni amɛdara oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ? yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya

english: Plantains are fast-growing herbaceous plants designed to take up surface space and light rapidly, which allows them to serve as quick ground cover for slow-growing crops like cocoa.
ga: Plantains ji jwɛi tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni afee koni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ atsu nii ni amɛha la aya oya. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akɛtsuɔ nii oya akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo tamɔ kookoo.

english: Why do monkeys in my farm pull up my whole young plantain plants instead of just eating the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbalaa midumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaye baai lɛ pɛ lɛ?

english: Monkeys target the sweet, juicy underground stem (corm) at the base of young plantain suckers, so they uproot the entire plant to eat the soft center inside.
ga: Akpɔlɔi lɛ kɛ amɛhiɛ fɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni ŋɔɔ ni mli ewo nu (corms) ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛtseɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛye emli hei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ.

english: What causes wild animals to attack my plantains within the first six months after planting?
ga: Mɛni haa koo mli kooloi tutuaa mi plantains lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji enumɔ ni akɛduɔ lɛ mli?

english: Young plantain plants in their first six months are tender, soft, and full of water, making them an easy and attractive food source for bush animals like monkeys.
ga: Plantains bibii ni yeɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji 6 lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe jɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋɔɔ kɛha koo mli kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii.

english: How can I prevent pests like monkeys from uprooting my plantains and destroying my cocoa shade?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkajie plantains lɛ ni amɛfite mi-kokoo lɛ su lɛ?

english: You can protect young plantains by using field border barriers, clearing nearby animal hiding spots, or using visual and sound deterrents to keep monkeys out of the farm boundaries.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ mli husu he gbɛtsii nii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ hei ni kooloi kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ. Aloo okɛ nibii ni anaa kɛ nibii ni anuɔ ni tsiɔ mɔ naa lɛ atsu nii koni ŋmeii akashɛ ŋmɔ husui lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct heat from the intense sun. They need living shade from plants like plantains or shade trees to protect their delicate leaves and keep the soil cool and moist while their roots develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli koni amɛbu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during heavy rains and high humidity. It moves from infected pods or soil onto healthy pods via splashing water, especially if the farm is too shady and unpruned.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ hela nɛɛ baa ji black pod disease, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ejɛɔ ŋmeii loo shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli kɛtsɔ nu ni ekɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni afolɔko tsei lɛ amli babaoo.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom of the plant usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil food. Adding fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure gives the maize the food it needs to stay green and form full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni efee ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do the leaves in the middle of my young corn plants have ragged holes and small brown dirt inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ yɛ bu ni mli egbala kɛ muji bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli lɛ?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides in the growing center (funnel) of the corn plant during the day, eating the leaves before they unfurl and leaving behind dark droppings that look like wet sawdust.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ dalɛ mli (cone) yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Ye baai lɛ dani amɛjie amɛhe kpo. ni eshiɔ ŋmeii diji ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cassava stem cuttings upside down in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ mi-cassava niji lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava stem buds point upward toward the sky. If you plant the stem upside down, the shoot has to bend all the way around to grow upward, which wastes the stem's energy and results in weak stems and very few tuberous roots.
ga: Kasava tsei ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu tso lɛ shishi lɛ Esa akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ abɔle ehe kwraa bɔni afee ni eda. ni fiteɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ shishifãi fioo ko pɛ baa.

english: Why do the leaves on some of my cassava bushes look twisted with yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness spread by tiny whiteflies or by using stems from already sick plants. The disease reduces the plant's ability to capture sunlight, leading to small, stunted stems and poor tuber yields.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Aloo okɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ momo lɛ ashishifãi atsu nii. Hela nɛɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛmɔɔ hulu la lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni egbɔjɔ kɛ tuber yibiiwoo ni ehiii baa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on wooden stakes so their leaves can catch direct sunlight to produce food for the underground tuber. Letting vines trail on the hot ground exposes leaves to soil diseases and reduces the size of your yield.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ anɔ koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ aya hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi wain tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baa helai aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayibɔ aba shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants curl their leaves up tight during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ shiŋŋ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the heat is a natural survival trick plants use to reduce water loss. By rolling its leaves inward, the pepper plant traps moisture and exposes less surface area to the burning sun until temperatures cool down.
ga: Baai ni afoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ shi. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni aaatsɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Pepper tsei lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛhaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ baa shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes suddenly from wet to dry. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, causing the plant to drop the useless flower instead of forming a fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ha fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa lɛ agbo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do people say planting cowpea or groundnuts makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni adu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have helpful bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and turn it into plant food in the soil. When the plant dies, that food stays in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Muawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa mli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa efeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ tsei gboi lɛ, nakai niyenii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with plenty of big leaves, but giving me tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from fertile soil or manure, it spends all its energy growing foliage above ground instead of storing starch in the roots. Balancing soil nutrients helps the plant send food down to fatten the tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei náa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mli. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso lɛ tsuɔ niyenii kɛyaa shi koni ekɛwo bulb lɛ mli fɔ.

english: Yam plants need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food. Staking lifts the vines above weeds and opens the leaves to sunlight, which allows the plant to produce and send more energy down to swell the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa jwɛi lɛ anɔ ni ehaa hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ yibii ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ amli alɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient needed for growth, or that heavy rains have soaked the soil so much that the roots cannot breathe and absorb plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Aloo nugbɔ nɛɔ waa, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛŋɔ tsei lɛ amli niyenii.

english: Why do small caterpillars hide deep inside the center whorl of my maize plants before the cobs even appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ dani ŋmeii lɛ po jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm target the tender central leaves because they are soft, moist, and easy to feed on, while the deep pocket of the plant protects the pest from hot sunlight and predators.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ kwɛɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ blɛoo, amɛmli edɔ ni amɛyeɔ oya, yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ fãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ buɔ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the tiny young pods on my cocoa tree shrivel up and turn black before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ yɛ mi koko tso lɛ nɔ lɛ egbo ni etsɔ ediŋŋ dani etsɔ agbo.

english: This is usually caused by black pod fungal disease, which spreads fast in wet weather and shade, or by natural pod wilt where the tree intentionally sheds surplus young pods it does not have enough food to feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod fungus ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. aloo kɛtsɔ tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli shwiemɔ nɔ yɛ he ni tso lɛ jwɛŋɔ ejieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua amɛ lɛ akafee nɔ ko lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves get large brown dry spots and die off early before the bunch is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni egbi ni amɛgboiɔ oya dani panicles lɛ daa lɛ?

english: This is caused by a airborne fungal disease called Black Sigatoka. It damages the leaf surface so the plant cannot process sunlight properly, resulting in smaller bunches and early ripening.
ga: Hela ko ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Sigatoka lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Efiteɔ baa lɛ hiɛ, ni ehaaa tso lɛ aná hulu la jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛshwereɔ oya.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that inject viruses into the leaves, damaging the leaf tissue and slowing down normal plant development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa baai lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni ehaa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme afternoon heat, poor watering, or lack of pollination. The plant sheds the flowers to conserve energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he. nu ni ehiii loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense mechanism crops use during hot weather. By curling their leaves, plants reduce the leaf area exposed to the sun and wind, helping them hold onto precious moisture.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsuɔ nii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ baa he ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ nu ni jara wa mli.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts make my soil richer for my next maize crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts work with beneficial soil bacteria in their root nodules to capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer that stays in the soil for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛtsake lɛ amɛfee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni hiɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Leaves usually turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or when there is too much standing water around the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea helps the maize regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ NPK loo urea fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall, slender, and weak when I plant the seeds close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa, amɛfeɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward trying to reach light, which makes the stems thin and weak, resulting in smaller corn ears.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi, ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛha la. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa toi lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees lose many of their small young pods before they can grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miifite amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? lots dani etsɔ agbo

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed extra young pods—a condition known as cherelle wilt—when they do not have enough water or nutrients to feed all the developing pods, especially during dry weather.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ ji shihilɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ Cherel hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Enɛ ji be mli ni amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua pod muu lɛ fɛɛ ni miiya hiɛ lɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for food and water in the soil. Removing excess suckers leaves more energy for the main plant to produce larger bunches of plantain.
ga: Tsobii loo tsei krokomɛi kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: What makes the leaves of my tomato plants curl up and wrinkle?
ga: Mɛni haa mi tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by the tomato leaf curl virus, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. It can also happen when the plant experiences extreme heat or sudden dry spells.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato baa curl hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whitefly lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hulutsoo be ni baa trukaa lɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the leaves at the center of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which like to hide inside the growing central leaves (the funnel) of maize plants. Catching them early and treating them stops them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhi amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ baai (funnels) ni miida lɛ amli. Kɛ́ omɔmɔ amɛ mra ni otsa amɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkafite tso lɛ yitsei lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the soil before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifoɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water after heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves toward the sun. Sunlight allows the leaves to produce food for the plant, which is then stored underground to form bigger, healthier yam tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baa lɛ ni ewoɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Akɛ enɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni akɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my hot pepper plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when the temperature gets too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, which encourages leaf growth instead of fruiting.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa loo kɛji akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa lɛ Enɛ woɔ baai hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a short dry period before the main rains begin. If seeds sprout right after the first rain, the scorching sun during the dry spell will dry out and kill the young seedlings.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ. Dani nugbɔ wulu lɛ baaje shishi Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ baagbi ni ekpata tsei bibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: How do I know the right time of year to apply fertilizer to my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afi lɛ mli be ni sa ni mikɛbaawo mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Apply fertilizer at the start of the rainy season when the soil is moist. This allows the tree roots to easily absorb the nutrients while the plant is actively growing new leaves and flowers.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miikwɛ̃ baai kɛ fɔfɔi heei.

english: Why are the young cocoa pods on my farm turning black and rotting before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, wet, and shady conditions. You can prevent it by pruning branches to let in sunlight and clearing heavy weeds from around the base of the trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni oookpa koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. ni ojie jwɛi ni tsii ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my crop turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your crop is missing key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the plant is getting too much direct sunlight without enough soil moisture.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, loo akɛ tso lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before the small pods start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani ebaaje shishi eshwere?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from stress caused by dry spells, intense heat, or lack of soil food. Giving proper shade and ensuring good soil nutrients helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ ni hɔmɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai haa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant shade trees inside my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Shade trees shield delicate cocoa trees from harsh direct sunlight, keep the soil cool and moist, and protect crops from strong winds, helping your farm stay productive for many years.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. ni obu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he Eyeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii afii babaoo.

english: Will cutting off branches from my crop hurt its growth or cause me to harvest less?
ga: Ani niji ni mifoɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaye edalɛ awui loo ebaaha maná ŋmɔshi nibii fioo?

english: Pruning actually helps your trees produce more. Removing dead or overcrowded branches allows air and sunlight to reach the main stem, which stops diseases and encourages big, healthy pods to grow.
ga: Kpojiemɔ yeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo diɛŋtsɛ. Niji ni egboi loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tso titri lɛ he. Enɛ haa helai kpaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa lɛ daa.

english: How can I easily tell when a cocoa pod is ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A fully ripe cocoa pod changes color completely, turning bright yellow or orange depending on the variety. Harvest them as soon as they change color so pests do not damage the beans inside.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kwraa. Amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ bɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ha lɛ naa. Kpãa kɛji amɛtsake amɛhe su pɛ. Enɛ ji koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Should I sweep away the fallen leaves under my crop or leave them on the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni egbee shi yɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ashishi loo mashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Leave the dry leaves on the ground. As they rot, they feed the soil with natural nutrients and act like a blanket that keeps moisture in the ground during dry months.
ga: Shi baai ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ. Kɛ amɛgboi lɛ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná adebɔɔ mli niyenii. Ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: What will happen if I plant my cocoa trees very close to each other to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting too close makes trees fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They will grow tall and skinny with very few pods, and diseases will easily jump from one tree to another.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛmli ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli, ni helai baanyɛ ajɛ tso kome mli kɛya tso kroko nɔ oya.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my main crops when the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants built to quickly grab available water and plant food from the soil. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing the fertilizer and water meant for your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni afee koni amɛjie nu ni yɔɔ lɛ oya ni amɛdu niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛha onibii titrii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow from the middle out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves, especially starting from the lower leaves along the main leaf vein, usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color and improves grain production.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, titri lɛ kɛjɛ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ yɛ baa lɛ fãji wuji lɛ ahe Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha dumɔwui lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce smaller fruits when many small shoots grow around the main trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ woɔ yibii bibii be mli ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso wulu lɛ he.

english: Those small shoots, called suckers, steal water and food from the main plant. Cutting away extra suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones allows the main stem to focus its energy on growing bigger plantain bunches.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi eko loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ agbala ejwɛŋmɔ kɛya dumɔwui wuji ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same plot where I grew maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them after heavy-feeding crops like maize naturally restores soil fertility for the next planting season.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full sun and hot winds. Planting plantains or shade trees alongside young cocoa creates living umbrellas that shelter them and retain soil moisture.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he ni ehiɔ shi lɛ baa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without forming fruit when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato pollen to dry up and fail to fertilize the blossoms. Mulching the soil with dry grass keeps the roots cool, and providing partial shade can help flowers stay on the plant.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato mli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaaa ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Ni kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo be ko ha lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground when heavy rains stay too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess water sits on the field without draining, it starves the roots of air and encourages fungal rot to spread.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eshwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ewo tsɛŋemɔ hela ni fiteɔ nii lɛ hewalɛ ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by viral diseases spread by whiteflies. Organic sprays like neem oil can help control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Organic spray tamɔ neem fɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves have small holes in them even when I do not see insects during the daytime?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kaabe baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, kooloi bibii komɛi bɛ ni abaanyɛ ana moŋ?

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves are often caused by caterpillars like the diamondback moth larva, which hide under the leaves or in the soil during the daytime heat and feed at night.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ diamondback moth larvae lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ kaabii baa lɛ amli lɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai ashishi loo sũ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛtaoɔ niyenii gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my crop stems early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Mi tso lɛ jeɔ shishi mra yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and compete with them for soil nutrients, fertilizer, and sunlight. Clearing them early gives your main crop the head start it needs to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Jiemɔ amɛ mra. Ebaaha otso titri lɛ aná yitso ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves upward to catch maximum sunlight for photosynthesis, which builds larger underground tubers. It also keeps leaves off damp soil, reducing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni enine ashɛ hulu la babaoo nɔ kɛha fotosintɛsis. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he. Ha fungal baa helai aba shi

english: I want to start growing wheat to make bread here in Ghana, so why does everyone tell me it will not yield well on my farm?
ga: Miisumɔ ni mabɔi ŋmaa dumɔ kɛha blodoo yɛ Ghana, no hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ miikɛɛ mi akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Wheat requires cool temperatures and dry conditions to set seeds properly. Ghana's warm, humid climate makes wheat plants weak and vulnerable to rot and diseases, resulting in very low yields.
ga: Ŋmaa he miihia he ko ni mli ejɔ ni mli egbi koni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ akwɛ shi jogbaŋŋ. Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa kɛhaa ŋmaa kɛ helai. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: If I buy high-yielding foreign seeds from the shop, why can't I just save seeds from my harvest to plant again next year?
ga: Kɛ mihe maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo kɛjɛ shwapo lɛ mli Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Many commercial foreign seeds are hybrids bred for a single generation. Seeds saved from hybrid plants lose their vigor, resulting in weak crops, small fruits, and uneven growth in the second season.
ga: Maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni afɔ yɛ yinɔ kome mli. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ yibii bibii kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: I have farmed my land for twenty years, but now my crops are small and weak. Why is my farm failing even though I work hard?
ga: Mikɛ afii nyɔŋmai enyɔ etsu nii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi amrɔ nɛɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni amɛhe waaa. Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ miifite yɛ minitsumɔ ni wa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous farming over many years removes essential food and nutrients from the soil. Without adding manure, fertilizer, or letting the land rest, the soil becomes tired and starved, leading to poor crop growth.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ yɛ afii babaoo mli lɛ jieɔ niyenii kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he loo ohaaa sũ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ baaye lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei lɛ adalɛ ni ehiii.

english: How do I know which crop will grow best when starting a fresh farm on a new plot of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mije ŋmɔ hee shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ?

english: Crops prefer different soil types; for instance, cassava tolerates poor or sandy soils, while maize needs rich, deep soil that holds water well. Observing how well water drains after rain helps determine what to plant.
ga: Tsei biɔ shikpɔŋ srɔtoi. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ŋã kpɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo ŋã nɔ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni nu baanyɛ ahi mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okwɛ bɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni okpɛɔ oyiŋ yɛ nɔ ni esa akɛ odu lɛ he.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes during dry spells, and does it mean the crop is dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigboi?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from hot sun and save water by reducing evaporation from their leaves. It is a natural self-defense mechanism during drought, not necessarily a sign that the plant is dead.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni akɛbu nu he kɛtsɔ baa lɛ mli la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Jeee akɛ eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbo.

english: How can I prevent my cassava leaves from curling up and turning yellow so my hard work does not go to waste?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi cassava baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ? Bɔni afee ni minitsumɔ ni wa lɛ akafee yaka?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. You can prevent it by planting clean, disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension officers.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ baa ni ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Abaanyɛ atsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmei srɔtoi ni he tse ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ nɔ taakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsulɔi lɛ wo ŋaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leads to thin, weak plants with very small yields instead of healthy plants with large fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ baa. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso nɛ he wa nɛ e woɔ yiblii nguahi.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa afata ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts add natural nitrogen fertilizer back into the soil through their roots. They feed the maize, cover the soil to prevent weeds, and give you two different food harvests from the same land.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Amɛhaa amɛ ŋmãa. Mulch shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akaje mli. kɛ niyenii srɔtoi enyɔ ni jɛ he kome lɛ ni akɛhaa

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that are naturally adapted to sprout quickly and steal water, light, and nutrients from the soil before young farm crops can establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛju nu, la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani okwaayeli mli ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ baanyɛ aná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why is it a mistake to spread fertilizer on my crop field right before a heavy rain storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji tɔmɔ akɛ magbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani ahum aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away expensive fertilizer from the topsoil into gutters before plant roots can drink it in, wasting your money and effort.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa nubui amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Enɛ baaha ofite oshika kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients away or when weeds are stealing the food from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo jwɛi ju niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I just save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially created in a laboratory to give a huge harvest in the first planting. If you plant the seeds harvested from that crop, the new plants will lose that special strength, growing unevenly and producing much smaller yields.
ga: Afeɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ krɛdɛɛ yɛ laboratori ko mli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ nakai tso lɛ mli lɛ Tsei heei lɛ laajeɔ nakai hewalɛ ni fa lɛ. Ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo kwraa.

english: Why is it helpful to plant cowpeas in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are naturally good at pulling nitrogen out of the air and feeding it into the ground. This acts like a natural fertilizer for your maize, while also covering the bare soil so weeds cannot grow easily.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ he esa waa yɛ nitrogen ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa o-corn lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃ oya.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits around the roots for too long without draining away, it chokes the roots and creates the right environment for water fungi to cause rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Nu lɛ gbeɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa nu mli ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa.

english: Why do I need to clear tall bushes and stake my yam vines with wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ amli ni mikɛ tsei adu sweet potato wain tsei lɛ?

english: Yam leaves are like tiny solar panels that need direct sunlight to make energy, which then sends food down to build big underground tubers. Staking keeps the leaves high in the sun and away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ tamɔ hulutsoo be mli tsɔnei bibii. ni biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba No sɛɛ lɛ, tsu niyenii kɛya shi koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ hulutsoo be mli ni helai kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: The color change is the plant's natural sign that the seeds inside are fully mature and the pod's sugar levels are at their peak. Harvesting when yellow ensures the cocoa beans ferment properly for good chocolate flavor.
ga: Su tsakemɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ edara ni sugar ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ eshɛ he ni fe fɛɛ. Kɛ́ akpa amɛ beni amɛji ŋmɔŋ lɛ, ehaa kookoo lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛ tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ aba.

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers, drink water and eat nutrients from the mother plant. Leaving too many suckers causes them all to fight each other, resulting in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ nuɔ nu ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ amɛhe awui. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like calcium in the soil. The plant drops flowers to save its own energy when conditions are tough.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji latsaa ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhewalɛ he kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli wa.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look burned during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etamɔ nɔ ni eshã yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the sun is very hot, pepper plants lose moisture from their leaves faster than the roots can drink water from the ground. The leaves curl up to hide from the sun and reduce water loss.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa Pepper tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛ amɛhe akawo hulu lɛ mli ni amɛha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: How can I tell if my farmland soil is getting weak and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Weak soil shows warning signs: your crops grow very slowly, leaves look pale green or purple, stems stay thin, and your final harvest gets smaller every year compared to when the land was fresh.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ tsɔɔ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii: Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daaa blɛoo waa. Baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo purple. Tso lɛ mli etse lolo. Ni onaagbee kpamɔ lɛ baafee bibioo daa afi. kɛ akɛto be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ehee lolo lɛ he

english: Why do my young cocoa trees burn and die when I plant them in a clear, open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse, ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle full, direct sunlight during their first two years. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a living umbrella that shields the fragile seedlings from harsh sun and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo be ni buɔ dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves on purpose when water is scarce to prevent moisture loss through leaf pores. This is a natural survival trick, and the plant will grow fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ yiŋtoo ko hewɔ beni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ni baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni baa kɛtsɔ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ naa lɛ. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaawoo. Ni tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛ baai heei kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: High mounds create deep, soft soil that allows yam tubers to expand downwards easily without resistance. Mounding also prevents water from sitting around the roots, which causes tubers to rot.
ga: Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shishi oya ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii amɛnaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aaabɔle he lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni nu akabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni baanyɛ aha yitso lɛ agbɔjɔ

english: Why am I seeing tiny holes on my young maize leaves and small caterpillars hidden in the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni Akɛtee yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ anɔ?

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, a very common cereal pest. They hide inside the central leaf whorl of young maize plants to feed, and early detection allows you to treat the crop before severe leaf damage occurs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fall armyworm tsɛŋemɔ hela, ni ji ŋmaa mli tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye niyenii. kɛ mra be mli ni anaa Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohereɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani baa lɛ fiteɔ waa.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to peel the outer skin and roots of plantain suckers before planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mafolɔ mi plantains lɛ kponɔgbɛ fãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ dani madu lɛ?

english: Peeling the base of a plantain sucker removes hidden pest eggs, root-knot nematodes, and fungal spores. Starting with clean, peeled suckers stops you from carrying pests into a fresh field.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie plantain suckers lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaajie tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ. Root knot nematodes kɛ fungal spores Je shishi kɛ ŋmeii ni he tse ni ajie amɛhe tsɔi Enɛ baaye abua ni okɛ kooloi ni ehao lɛ akawo ŋmɔji heei amli.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer to my corn farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-abele ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best practice is to apply fertilizer twice: first about 10 to 14 days after sprouting when young roots form, and a second time when plants are knee-high to support the fast growth spurt before flowering.
ga: Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni awo mli shii enyɔ. Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ ji aaafee gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 sɛɛ beni shishifãi bibii jeɔ shishi lɛ. kɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛnaji ahe koni amɛye amɛbua amɛdalɛ oya dani amɛwo fɔfɔi.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn dark brown and rot before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered by uneven soil moisture. Keeping watering steady helps the plant carry calcium to the growing fruit.
