ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ calcium baa tso lɛ yibii ni miida lɛ mli.

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nitrogen. Growing it repeatedly on the same plot strips that specific nutrient completely and allows maize-specific pests and soil diseases to build up in high numbers.
ga: Abele haa nitrogen babaoo yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni niyenii pɔtɛɛi fɛɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ji ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa babaoo.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help make my soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in tiny nodules on their roots. When the plant roots decay after harvest, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as free natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back so much faster after a heavy rain than my planted crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants with shallow, widespread root systems designed to instantly trap surface water and sunlight. Domesticated crops take more time to establish roots, giving weeds an early speed advantage.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ni afee koni emɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ hulu la amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shia tsei heɔ be babaoo dani amɛfeɔ shishifãi. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ náa sɛɛnamɔ oya.

english: Why should I cut off old leaves from my crops every few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai momoi kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ mli lɛ? otsii enyɔ komɛi

english: Cutting off old or damaged leaves every few weeks helps the plant focus its energy on producing healthy new shoots. It also opens up the plant so sunlight and air can reach all parts, reducing diseases.
ga: Baa ni egbɔ loo ni efite lɛ fɛɛ ni afoɔ. Otsii fioo komɛi baaha tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmeii heei ni mli wa ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ. Egbeleɔ tso lɛ hu koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ he fɛɛ he, ni no haa helai ni baa lɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know when it is time to remove old plant growth so new growth can come?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ majie tsei momo ni eda lɛ koni tso heei aba?

english: When leaves start to yellow, dry out, or look overgrown, usually every two to four weeks, it is time to cut them back. Removing the old growth triggers the plant to naturally generate fresh, strong leaves.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbi, loo amɛfee basabasa, bei pii lɛ daa otsii enyɔ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ, be eshɛɛ ni esa akɛ afolɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ ajie tso ni eda lɛ momo lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ awo baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I harvest or cut leaves from my plants repeatedly without killing the crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa loo mafolɔ baai kɛjɛ mitsei lɛ amli shii abɔ? Ani abaanyɛ afee ni akpataaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ?

english: Yes, as long as you only cut the mature leaves and leave the stem and young shoots intact, the plant will continuously grow new foliage to replace what was removed.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ obaafo baai ni eda lɛ pɛ ni oshi tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ pɛ. Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei be fɛɛ be koni ekɛye nɔ ni afo lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How does cutting away extra foliage help my farm perform better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Trimming leaves creates space for better air movement and prevents pests from breeding in dense foliage, leading to healthier plants and easier field management.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ baai lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee babaoo yɛ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ, ni ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ hu feɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do extension officers recommend using cord or string to tie up my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ tsɔne loo tsɔne ni akɛfiɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ atsu nii?

english: Using cord to tie crop stems keeps heavy plants upright and organized, preventing leaves and stems from trailing on the damp ground where they can rot or catch diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ kpãa fĩ tsei ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei ni tsii lɛ damɔɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ fɛo. Tsi baai kɛ tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkafo yɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ anɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi loo hela aba amɛnɔ lɛ.

english: Does the color or type of binding material I use to support my crops matter?
ga: Ani kɔla loo nɔ ni mikɛfiɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ he hia?

english: Using smooth, flexible cords—often green to match the plant—ensures you can tie stems securely without cutting into the living tissue as the plant grows.
ga: Kɛtsɔ kpãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nyɛɔ efoɔ lɛ nɔ Bei pii lɛ, amɛfeɔ eŋɔli koni amɛkɛ tsei lɛ akpã gbee. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe shweshweeshwe ni okɛ fãji ni hiɛ ka lɛ efoŋ mli beni tso lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why is it important to follow a strict schedule, like trimming every 2 to 4 weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa atsu nii, tamɔ hesaamɔ daa otsii 2 kɛyashi 4 lɛ?

english: Crops develop in predictable cycles, so sticking to a regular routine ensures you clear out old growth right before new growth needs space and resources to develop.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daa yɛ bei ni anyɛɔ atsɔɔ hiɛ atsɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ohe kpɛtɛ nifeemɔ ko ni afeɔ daa lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni ojie shweremɔ momo lɛ kɛjɛ ohe dani shweremɔ hee lɛ he ahia he ko kɛ nibii ni ekɛbaatsu nii.

english: Why do cut plant stems or leaves need to sit for about a week after being trimmed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ tsei loo baai ni afo lɛ ajɔɔ amɛhe aaafee otsi kome yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Allowing cut material to rest for about a week gives the cut ends time to dry and heal, which prevents rot or infection before the material is moved, planted, or processed.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ nibii ni afo lɛ gbɛ ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe aaafee otsi kome lɛ, ehaa nɔ ni afo lɛ naagbee lɛ naa be ni ekɛgbiɔ ni etsaa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa fitemɔ loo hela aba dani ajie nibii lɛ, adu loo atsu he nii.

english: Why do I need to carefully supervise my field workers during crop trimming and production?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ miŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni mikpaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nibii ni mifeɔ lɛ?

english: Proper supervision ensures that workers cut only the correct old leaves at the right time, preventing damage to sensitive young shoots and keeping production on schedule.
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa haa nitsulɔi lɛ shwieɔ baai ni eda ni sa lɛ pɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Tsi nibii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ afitemɔ naa ni oha nifeemɔ lɛ aya nɔ yɛ be ni ato lɛ naa.

english: How long can fresh crop cuttings remain kept in the field before they lose their quality?
ga: Be enyiɛ abaanyɛ akɛ tsei heei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ato ŋmɔ mli dani amɛhe afee fɛo?

english: Freshly cut plant material can usually stay safely in the field for about a week under proper conditions before it dries out completely or begins to decompose.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe nibii ni afo ehee lɛ baanyɛ ahi saatso lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe aaafee otsi kome yɛ shihilɛ ni sa mli dani egbi kwraa loo ebɔi fitemɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and sensitive leaves that burn in full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to act as living umbrellas that keep the soil moist and block harsh sun rays.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsĩɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa.

english: Why do people spread dry grass around the roots of their crops on hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbi amɛshwãa amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves around plants is called mulching. It traps moisture in the ground so the sun does not dry out the soil quickly, and it also stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa Tsei ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni jwɛi akakwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning light yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I avoid putting chemical fertilizer directly into dry soil during planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ he?

english: Chemical fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve safely. If applied to dry soil, the concentrated salts will draw water out of young roots and burn them, killing the seedling.
ga: Tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ amli ni eshãa dumɔwui lɛ.

english: How do I choose the right part of the cassava stem to cut and plant in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni sa ni mafolɔ ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The middle section of a mature cassava stem is best for planting because it has strong, healthy buds that sprout fast. The top tender part dries out quickly, while the bottom woody part sprouts too slowly.
ga: Cassava tso ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔ ejaakɛ eyɛ ŋmeii ni wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daraa blɛoo tsɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I leave all the small plantain shoots growing around one mother plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ plantain tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Nyɛ tso kome pɛ he

english: Leaving too many shoots causes them to fight with the main plant for soil nutrients and light, which leads to small bunches. Cutting away extra shoots and leaving only two or three gives you bigger plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ awuu koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ la. ni kɛ mɔ yaa tso nine bibioo ko nɔ Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oshi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha oná tso bibioo ko.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around my young crops every few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Mi tso bibioo fɛɛ tso Otsii fioo komɛi?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Keeping the farm clean gives your crops full access to food and water so they can grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oooha ehe atse lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa niyenii kɛ nu babaoo. koni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Why are small holes appearing in the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: Holes in the center leaves of young corn are usually caused by fall armyworms eating the leaves. Spraying an approved pest control product early in the morning when the worms are feeding will protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbee shi ni yeɔ baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ shwie nɔ leebi be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ yeɔ nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids sucking the sap from under the leaves. Spraying the leaves with soap water or recommended insecticides will stop them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni akɛ samla loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi amɛnaa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get enough water. Regular watering and keeping the root area cool with mulch helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ shishifã lɛ ni akɛ mulch haa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight in their first few years. They need partial shade from nurse crops like plantains to protect their leaves from burning and keep the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ fɔmɔ kotoku mli, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa

english: Why do other farmers tell me to plant cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi Ko ni amɛkɛɛ mi akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmãa yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans are special legumes that take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them alongside maize acts as a natural fertilizer, helping the maize grow stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans ji ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni ekɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Curling and yellowing leaves on cassava are usually caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stems stops this virus from ruining your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca mosaic hela lɛ kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. ni ji kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ ni hiɛɔ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baatsi nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ naa koni ekafite oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my maize fail to produce full cobs if it doesn't rain when the tassels appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ wooo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Flowering is the most critical time for maize because the plant is actively forming seeds. Drought during this short window dries up the silks before pollen can fertilize them, leaving you with empty or half-filled cobs.
ga: Fɔfɔii ji be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmãa ejaakɛ tso lɛ miiwo dumɔwui. Hɔmɔ ni baa be kukuoo mli Enɛ baaha siliki lɛ agbi dani pollen lɛ baanyɛ afee lɛ fɔmɔ nii. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli loo fã ni nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my yam setts very close together on the same mound?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa yɛ gɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need space underground to stretch and collect nutrients. When planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water and soil food, resulting in many tiny tubers instead of large, healthy ones.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ shishi he ko koni amɛgbala amɛhe ni amɛbua niyenii mli hewalɛ naa. Kɛji adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso bibioo yibɔi babaoo yɛ yitsei wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ

english: Why do my pepper plants keep falling sick when I plant them on the land where I just harvested tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hela mɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ beni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa tomato nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Peppers and tomatoes belong to the same crop family and suffer from the same soil diseases and pests. Rotating your field with a different crop family, like maize or cassava, starves those soil pests before you plant peppers again.
ga: Pepper kɛ tomato yɛ tsei akuu kome mli ni helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛbaa lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ tsakemɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Enɛ baaye abua ni hɔmɔ aye nakai shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi lɛ dani odu ŋmɔtɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my vegetable crops grow so small and weak if I don't clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that grow faster than domesticated vegetables. They drink up the water and eat the soil nutrients meant for your crops, effectively starving your plants during their early growth stage.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni daa oya fe shia tsei. Amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye otsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: Why should I pinch off some of the leafy side branches on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: When a tomato plant has too many leaves and shoots, it spends all its food growing foliage instead of fruit. Removing lower side branches directs the plant's energy into producing bigger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Kɛji tomato tso ko yɛ baai babaoo ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ Tomato tsei kɛ baai ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe aduawai lɛ fɛɛ. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ekɛwo tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do some of the maize grains I save from my previous harvest fail to sprout or grow poorly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ loo amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Saved grains often carry unseen seed-borne diseases or lose their vigor during storage. Certified seeds are specially selected, treated against diseases, and tested to ensure almost every seed sprouts into a strong plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa ni ato lɛ náa dumɔwui helai ni anaaa loo amɛhewalɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ, atsuɔ he nii, ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni ana akɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu baakwɛ̃ ni etsɔ tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do cassava roots become watery and tough if I leave them in the ground too long after they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛkpɛɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛdara sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava roots reach full maturity, the plant starts drawing starch back out of the tubers to survive dry weather or grow new leaves. Over-aged cassava loses its floury texture and turns woody and watery.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ baabɔi ŋmei jiemɔ kɛjɛ bulb lɛ mli koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo baai heei amli. Cassava ni egbɔ tsɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni etsɔɔ tso kɛ nu.

english: Why does my cocoa farm take so many years before I can start harvesting a full crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe afii babaoo dani mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ je ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo lɛ akpamɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees take time to establish deep roots and strong branches before they can support heavy pods. Although progress feels slow in the beginning, a well-cared-for cocoa farm will continue producing pods for decades, giving you long-term benefits for years to come.
ga: Cacao tsei he miihia be koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ niji ni mli wa dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfi ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, hiɛyaa nuɔ he akɛ eyaaa hiɛ fioo yɛ shishijee mli. Shi kookoo ŋmɔji ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaya nɔ afee pods afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Enɛ haa onáa sɛɛnamɔi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ afii babaoo ni baa lɛ.

english: How can I earn money while waiting several years for my oil palm trees to mature and bear fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná shika yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni mu tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛwo yibii afii babaoo lɛ?

english: You can plant quick-growing crops like cassava, maize, or legumes between the young palm trees. These short-term crops give you regular food and income step-by-step while your main cash crop grows.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ateŋ. Nɛkɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa bo niyenii kɛ shika ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni oshika ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: If I add organic compost to my soil today, why don't I see big results in my crops immediately?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ organic compost fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ŋmɛnɛ lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ minaaa yibii wuji yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Organic compost breaks down slowly in the soil, releasing nutrients little by little. While it takes time, this gradual process builds up healthy soil that keeps your crops producing well for many continuous seasons, unlike chemical fertilizers that wash away quickly.
ga: Organic compost lɛ fiteɔ fiofio yɛ sũ lɛ mli, ni ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii fiofio. Eyɛ mli akɛ eheɔ be moŋ Shi nɛkɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii fiofio nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ bei babaoo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ amli. Ejeee tamɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni shwieɔ oya lɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains the same specific nutrients from the soil year after year. Rotating your maize with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients naturally, ensuring your farm stays productive over a long period.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii atsake o-corn lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ Ehaa oŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: It is best to watch the weather and wait until the rains are steady for a week or two, rather than planting right after the very first shower. Planting too early can cause seeds to dry up if the rain stops unexpectedly.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ nɔ ni omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ ba shi otsi kome loo enyɔ. Mohu ɔ, mo du mɛ ngɛ kekleekle nu ɔ se amlɔ nɔuu. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ trukaa.

english: Why is it better to water my vegetable garden a little bit every day instead of flooding it once a week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ oooha o-vegetables abɔɔ lɛ mli nu fioo daa gbi moŋ fe shikome yɛ otsi mli lɛ?

english: Vegetables grow best with steady, continuous moisture. Flooding the soil all at once can drown the roots and wash away nutrients, whereas consistent daily watering keeps the plant growing steadily without stress.
ga: Aduawai daa jogbaŋŋ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa, ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ. Kɛ́ nu shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikome lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni ekɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ashwie shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni oooha tso lɛ daa gbi lɛ baaye abua ni eya nɔ eda ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Why should I cut off some healthy-looking branches from my fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ aniji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes excess branches so the tree can focus its strength on growing bigger, healthier fruit instead of just leaves. Doing this step-by-step allows sunlight and air to reach all parts of the tree, improving your yield over time.
ga: Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baa lɛ nɔ moŋ fe baai lɛ pɛ. Enɛ ni afeɔ lɛ fiofio lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do improved hybrid seeds give a better harvest than the seeds I save from my own farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred in laboratories to resist diseases and produce high yields consistently. Seeds saved from past harvests slowly lose these special qualities over time, leading to smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ laboratori ko mli krɛdɛɛ koni helai anyɛ amɛshi amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nikpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Sui krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ laajeɔ kɛ be shwieɔ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: Why do weeds keep growing back on my farm even after I clear the land completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miikwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mifo jɛmɛ moŋ?

english: Weed seeds hide under the soil for years and sprout whenever they get sunlight and rain. Clearing weeds regularly before they flower and drop new seeds will slowly reduce the weed population over time.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe ewo shikpɔŋ shishi afii babaoo ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ be fɛɛ be ni hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ amɛ. Ajieɔ jwɛi daa dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni aduɔ dumɔwui heei fiofio. Tsɔɔmɔ jwɛi lɛ ayibɔ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do I need to inspect my cassava farm for pests regularly even when the plants look fine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa kɛji ŋmeii yɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Pests and diseases start small and spread gradually before you notice major damage. Checking your farm continuously allows you to catch problems early and protect your harvest before serious losses occur.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai Jeɔ shishi bibioo ni egbɛɔ eshwaa dani oyɔseɔ nɔ ni efite waa. Kɛ́ oya nɔ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa onaa naagbai mra. ni obu onibii ahe dani nibii ni hiɛdɔɔ yɔɔ mli aba.

english: Why shouldn't I leave parts of my farmland unused during the farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ekomɛi ni mikɛtsuuu nii yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaving clear land unplanted allows weeds and pests to take over that area and spread to your active crops, while using all available space with proper crop planning maximizes your harvest and keeps the soil covered and healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni aduuu nii yɛ lɛ, ebaaha jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aŋɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã onibii amli. Yɛ be mli ni akɛ he fɛɛ he ni yɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aba ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ahi shi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, thin stems and very small cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni kɛlɛ Eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Why do I need to clear all the weeds before planting my crops instead of just planting through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ dani madu, shi jeee jwɛi lɛ pɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and will steal water, sunlight, and soil food away from your plants, weakening them before they can get established.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni ebaaju nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛ otsei lɛ amli. ni ehaa tsei gbɔjɔɔ dani amɛmaa shi.

english: Is it good to plant the exact same crop on the same piece of land every single year?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaadu ŋmɔshi nii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi?

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground, whereas changing crops keeps the soil rich and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni baafite tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting cassava together with beans or cowpeas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei?

english: Beans put natural nitrogen back into the soil to feed the cassava, while the cassava plants shade the ground to keep moisture in the soil and prevent weeds from taking over.
ga: Beans lɛ kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ koni ekɛye ŋmei. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmei tsei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: How do I know if my crops are hungry and need extra manure or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni ehe miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: If your plant leaves turn pale green or yellow, growth slows down, or the stems look thin and weak, the soil is running out of food and needs well-rotted manure or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ, edalɛ fiofio loo tso lɛ shishi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ awo mli.

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to shrink their surface area so they lose less water in extreme heat, which is a natural way for the plant to protect itself from drying out.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi bɔni afee ni nu fioo pɛ afite yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a heat spell that can dry out the ground and scorch newly sprouted seeds before the main rain pattern actually begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ dɔlɛ ni baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni eshã dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ dani nugbɔ wuji lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Bean plants drop their flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, severe dry spells, or too much nitrogen in the soil, causing the plant to focus on leaf survival instead of fruit.
ga: Bean tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ ashihilɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers rot quickly when I leave them under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Direct hot sun bakes the delicate skin of the yam, causing internal heat damage and moisture loss that allows fungi and bacteria to enter and rot the tuber.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa sweet potato lɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ekɛ fitemɔ baa kɛjɛɔ mligbɛ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni laajeɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ boteɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade and protect young cocoa from drying out during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo ni ebuɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he koni ekagbi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Cowpeas and beans gather nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which feeds the maize plants naturally and makes the soil richer for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa tsei ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale green and yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which maize needs to stay green and grow strong roots. Adding compost or fertilizer supplies this missing plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ shishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaatsu tso ni elaaje nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why shouldn't I burn the cleared bush and dried leaves on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa tsei bibii ni ajie kɛ baai ni egbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable natural food in the soil and kills beneficial living organisms. Leaving the cleared plants to rot returns rich nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni jara wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni efiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei lɛ koni amɛgboi lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa babaoo lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Removing excess branches lets sunlight reach all parts of the tree and improves air movement, which stops wet-weather diseases from spreading and helps the tree produce larger pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I need to push long wooden sticks into the ground for my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsi tso kakadaŋŋ? Muji kɛha sweet potato tsei?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves towards sunlight. Maximum sunlight on the leaves allows the plant to send more energy down into the ground to make big yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ ahe, ni ehaa tso lɛ tsɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: This is caused by a water-loving fungus called Black Pod disease, which thrives in cool, wet, and shady conditions. Clearing weeds and harvesting ripe pods quickly prevents it from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod hela. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi oya kɛ ŋmeii ni eda lɛ akpamɔ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my maize stems break easily and show small holes in the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ fãa oya ni bu bibii yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Stemborer caterpillars chew into the stems to feed, which weakens the stalk from the inside out. Inspecting plants early and applying proper controls stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Stemborer ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ tsei akutsei amli kɛtaoɔ niyenii. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛjɛ mli kɛya kponɔgbɛ. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Kɛ nibii ni sa ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa amɛkpaa dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves to save water when the weather becomes hot and dry. The plant goes to sleep temporarily to protect its roots underground until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi koni akɛbu nu he kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Tso lɛ baawɔ be kukuoo ko koni ebu eshishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing into fruit during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkwɛɛɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato flowers cannot fertilize properly, so the plant drops them to conserve energy. Shade nets or planting under light tree cover helps keep them cool.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ashiɔ tsei ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ koni amɛkafite hewalɛ. Shade net loo tso ni yɔɔ tso ni kpɛɔ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa edɔɔ.

english: Why should I spend money to buy fertilizer when my crops can already grow naturally in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafite shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ? Be ni miŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe?

english: Crops take food out of the ground as they grow. Fertilizer puts essential plant food back into the soil so your crops can grow bigger, stay healthy, and give you a much higher yield than unfertilized land.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Fertilizer kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara. Hiɛ shi jogbaŋŋ ni eha yibiiwoo babaoo fe hei ni anáaa ŋmɔshi nibii

english: What actually happens to my crop harvest if I farm my land without using any fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mifee okwaayeli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ko tsuuu nii?

english: Without fertilizer, your crops rely only on whatever nutrients are left in the soil, which usually leads to smaller plants, lower crop yields, and unpredictable harvests over time.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ, onibii lɛ baadamɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ pɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa tsei bibii baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ba shi ni kpamɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ ba shi yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops produce a smaller harvest every year even though I plant on the exact same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miikpa nii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Every time you harvest crops, they carry away nutrients from the earth. Without feeding the soil with fertilizer or manure, the soil becomes tired and weak, leading to lower yields each season.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ebaaŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ he feɔ shoo ni egbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: If commercial chemical fertilizer is hard to get in my area, what alternative options can I use to feed my crops?
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ wa yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ, Mɛɛ gbɛi krokomɛi manyɛ matsɔ nɔ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ?

english: You can use well-rotted animal manure, compost made from dry leaves and crop waste, or plant leguminous crops like beans, which naturally build up soil fertility at low cost.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ atsu nii. Kompost ni akɛ baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ. Aloo dumɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii, ni jɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shika fioo pɛ heɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crops on the field are suffering from a lack of nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ?

english: When crops are hungry for food, their leaves often turn pale green or yellow instead of dark green, their stalks remain thin, and they grow much slower than normal.
ga: Kɛ hɔmɔ ye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Etso lɛ mli etse lolo. ni edaa blɛoo kwraa fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ

english: When is the right time during the farming season to apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ mli ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied early in the plant's growth when roots are actively expanding, and when there is enough moisture in the soil from light rain to dissolve the nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo tsei lɛ amli mra. Beni shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. koni ekɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii

english: Can putting too much fertilizer or applying it incorrectly harm my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo ni ejaaa ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, putting fertilizer directly against crop stems or applying too much can burn the roots and leaves, which damages or kills the plant instead of helping it grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ loo okɛwo mli babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ashã. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ loo egbeɔ lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua lɛ ni eda.

english: Is using fertilizer actually profitable for a small-scale farmer like me?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛha okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi?

english: Yes, because the increase in yield from properly fertilized crops usually brings in significantly more income at harvest than the initial cost of purchasing the fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni yaa hiɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ kɛ shika ni anáa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ sɛɛ baa ni fe shishijee shika ni akɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwraa.

english: Why does fertilizer require rain or water in the soil to work properly for crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ loo nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni tsei lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crops cannot eat dry fertilizer. Water is needed to dissolve the fertilizer so the plant's roots can easily drink in the liquid nutrients from the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi. Nu he miihia koni akɛjie ŋmɔshi nibii koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu niyenii ni ji nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do crops grown with proper fertilizer mature faster than crops grown without it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa woɔ mli lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer provides concentrated doses of essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus, which give plants the quick energy they need to build leaves, stems, and fruits faster.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ oya koni ewo baai, tsei, kɛ aduawai oya.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient for leaf growth. Rain can wash nitrogen out of the soil, so applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plants turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nugbɔ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same plot of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be mli lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land drains specific nutrients and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen and breaks pest cycles naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ, ni ehaa sũ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaku adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap and transmitting viruses. Controlling these pests early with suitable sprays protects the plant so it can produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Emuɔ mliki ni ekɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ haa Eyeɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebuɔ tso lɛ he koni ewo yibii.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, dark conditions. Pruning excess branches to let air and sunlight into the farm and removing infected pods quickly stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and capture maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to produce energy, which feeds the underground tuber to grow large and heavy.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii koni amɛdara ni amɛfee tsiimɔ

english: Allowing too many shoots (suckers) to grow causes them to steal water and food from the main plant. Pruning away extra shoots leaves only one or two strong suckers, ensuring heavy, high-quality plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ suckers (tsobii) babaoo gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaha amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baashi, ni no baaha ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni tsii waa aba.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry Harmattan winds, or irregular watering. Keeping the soil moist and planting shade or windbreaks helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ dumɔwui loo kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔnei ni akɛduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Cassava roots rot in standing water because waterlogged soil suffocates the roots by cutting off air. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil can absorb water deeply before the sun gets too hot. Afternoon watering causes quick evaporation and can scorch warm leaves with droplets.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛya shɔŋŋ dani hulu lɛ adɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli shwane mli lɛ haa hulutsoo baa oya, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ashã baai ni mli edɔ lɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, prevents the sun from drying out the ground, stops weeds from growing, and eventually breaks down into rich soil matter.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and burning up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive. Without shade plants like plantains or shade trees to shield them, direct heat from the intense sun burns their soft leaves and stops them from making food.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ bɛ lɛ, Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ekpa amɛhoomɔ.

english: Why does my cassava plant grow so many big leaves but leaves me with tiny tubers when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei tsei lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi amɛhe ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akpa?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or lacks proper nutrients like potassium, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves above the ground instead of storing food in the tubers underneath.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo niyenii ni sa, tamɔ potassium bɛ mli lɛ, tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning light green or yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key food crops need to build strong stems and healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have beneficial roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a natural food supply for crops planted after them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds on my farm grow faster than my crops right after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong, aggressive roots that steal water and fertilizer faster than young crop plants. If you do not clear the weeds before applying fertilizer, the weeds will eat the plant food first.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ yeɔ tsei klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off instead of turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of water. The plant drops the flowers to save its own life until conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala kɛyashi shihilɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees start producing much smaller bunches after a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ panicles bibii babaoo yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: As a plantain tree grows, it produces many young shoots (suckers) around its base. If you do not prune these extra suckers, they fight with the main tree for soil food, resulting in smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ dara lɛ Ebaawo ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he kɛji ofolɔko ŋmeii ni fa fe nine nɛɛ. Ekɛ tsei ni ji gbɔi lɛ baawu koni amɛná niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa aduawai bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ baa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very thin and fall over easily when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya beni adu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they shade each other out and stretch tall to reach sunlight, making their stems thin, weak, and easy for wind to break.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, egbɔjɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ fiteɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up tightly like little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus, or by the plant trying to protect itself from extreme heat and dry soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the ground when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rain stays in the soil without draining away, it suffocates the yam roots by cutting off air, allowing fungi and bacteria in the wet mud to rot the tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efooo. Sweet potato shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ yɛ muji lɛ mli ni efɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my crops grow so dark green and tall when I plant on land that has been untouched for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ni amɛkwɔ waa beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etako he afii babaoo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Land left unfarmed for decades accumulates a deep bank of decomposed leaf litter and rich organic matter. When you clear and plant it, the soil releases a heavy supply of nitrogen and nutrients all at once, driving rapid stem and leaf growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atsuko nɔ nii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ nɛ lɛ ebua baai ni egboi babaoo kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo naa. Beni otsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa ni oduɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛ niyenii babaoo yɛ be kome mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ashishifãi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ daraa oya.

english: Why does my yam grow much bigger in high earth mounds than when I plant it in flat, unploughed soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ gɔji anɔ fe be mli ni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are soft underground stems that need loose, airy soil to stretch out and expand. Deep mounds give the root freedom to grow without hitting hard dirt while ensuring excess rainwater drains away so the tuber does not rot.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni he hiaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli koni ekɛgbala ni egbɛ eshwa. Gɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ heyeli ni amɛdaraa ni sũ ni wa etswaaa amɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekwɛɔ koni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni bulb lɛ akafite.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a signal that the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, its main leaf-building food. To keep growing, the plant robs nitrogen from its oldest bottom leaves and moves it up to feed the young top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmãa tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni akɛbɔɔ baai koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara Tso lɛ juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni ekɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Maize eats the same specific nutrients from the soil every time it grows. Repeated planting empties those nutrient stores completely and allows pests that feed specifically on maize to build up in the ground, lowering your yield each year.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ebaakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu shii abɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afite. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa titri lɛ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni ofeɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi.

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots compete fiercely underground for the same space, soil moisture, and food. Giving each stem proper distance lets the roots swell into thick, heavy tubers without fighting neighboring plants.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ atsɔ yitsei ni mli wa ni tsii ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ awuu.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop producing fruits when tall weeds grow around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ yibii beni jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔleɔ he lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves that steal sunlight, water, and ground nutrients from pepper plants. When shaded and starved by weeds, the pepper plant shuts down fruit production to direct its remaining energy just to survive.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi, ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni atswa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei amli. Beni jwɛi lɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ Pepper tso lɛ tsiɔ aduawai ni ewoɔ lɛ naa koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ atsu nii kɛha wala.

english: In strong afternoon heat, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can drink it up. The plant wilts on purpose to shrink leaf surface area and trap moisture, recovering once the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Tsei gboiɔ kɛ yiŋtoo akɛ ebaaba baa lɛ hiɛ dalɛ shi ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Ebaatsa ehe ekoŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and lose leaves when all the big shade trees are cut down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ shã ni ebaaji lɛ sɛɛ fo beni afo cacao tso agbo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees naturally develop under canopy shade, so direct sun burns their delicate leaves and bakes their shallow roots. Shade trees act like umbrellas that keep the cocoa cool and preserve soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ ni ebaashã eshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela koni eye ebua ni eha kookoo lɛ mli ajɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why didn't my maize seeds sprout up after I buried them very deep in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: A seed carries only a tiny package of stored food energy to push its shoot up through the soil. If planted too deep, the seed runs out of food before reaching the surface and dies in the dark.
ga: Niyenii hewalɛ paketii bibii pɛ yɔɔ dumɔwui amli. koni akɛtsi ŋmeii kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛji adu mli tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ niyenii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ dani amɛshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ duŋ mli.

english: Why are the flowers on my cowpea plants dropping off without making any bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛjieee pea ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers drop when tiny pests suck the sap from the buds or when extreme heat dries out the flower stems. Without protection from sap-sucking insects and severe drought, the blooms fail to set into pods.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii miinu nu ni jɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ loo kɛ́ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ ha fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbi. Kɛji akɛ abuuu he kɛjɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu kɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa he lɛ, Blossoms nyɛŋ afee ŋmeii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I clear all the big shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive and need shade from larger trees or plantains to protect their leaves from harsh sunlight and to keep the soil cool and moist while their roots develop.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛbiɔ hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains adɛŋ koni amɛkɛbu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. kɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch upward for light instead of developing thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ koni amɛmɔ kane lɛ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ tso nɛ mi wa kɛ tso agbo.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very bushy green leaves but produce small tubers in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii akui shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil or excessive leafy growth causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing leaves above ground rather than storing food in the tubers underground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo baai ni shwereɔ babaoo lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Extreme heat and lack of water cause tomato plants to undergo stress, making them drop their flowers to conserve water rather than spending energy setting fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ haoɔ tomato tsei. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato shiiɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he moŋ fe ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛdu aduawai.

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds nutrient-heavy crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tsei ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on to give me a big harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ koni eha mi ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Staking spreads out the leaves of the yam vine so they can catch maximum sunlight to make food, which is then sent down to grow larger and healthier tubers under the ground.
ga: Staking gbɛɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eshwaa koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. ni no sɛɛ lɛ atsuɔ kɛyaa shi koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I wait until the ground is moist after rain before applying fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ dani mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can safely drink it in; applying it to dry soil can burn the roots and waste the fertilizer.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: Why do elders recommend planting groundnuts together with cassava on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei afee ekome kɛdu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts grow low to cover the soil, keeping it cool and moist while adding nitrogen, while cassava grows tall, allowing both crops to share space and light without harming each other.
ga: Peanuts daa shi shiŋŋ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa mɔ he jɔɔ ni ekɛ nitrogen fataa he. be mli ni ŋmei daa lɛ Enɛ haa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ jaa he ko kɛ la ni amɛyeee amɛhe awui.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants suddenly covered in ragged holes with dirt inside the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni buji ni etse kɛ muji eyi mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the growing center of young maize to feed on soft leaves before they open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni boteɔ ŋmeii bibii ni miida lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl upward and turn wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding on the leaves, or viruses transmitted by these pests as they feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves shaped like a V at the leaf tip usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize plants need nitrogen to stay green and grow strong cobs, so when it runs out, the plant pulls nitrogen from the older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛyitsei tamɔ V yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ etee Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers and leaves during very hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi kɛ ebaa yɛ shwane latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, pepper plants drop their flowers to save water and energy. They focus on surviving the intense heat stress rather than growing new fruits until the weather cools down or moisture improves.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Amɛsusuɔ bɔ ni amɛaahi shi yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa mli lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ aduawai heei kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ loo hulutsoo be lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very small cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients, while their leaves block sunlight from neighboring plants. This stress prevents the crop from getting enough energy to form full, big cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni ebaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ amli lɛ naa. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ haaa tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up, twisting, and showing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled and distorted leaves on cassava are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The virus stops the leaves from making food properly, which leads to thin stems and small tuber yields underground.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe ni etsɔ yucca nɔ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Virus lɛ haaa baai lɛ ahoo jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ bulb bibii baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are small holes appearing in the tender leaves of my young maize, with dark dirt inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ anɔ. Muji ni tsuɔ waa yɛ funnel lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: This is typical damage caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the growing leaf funnel during the day and eat the soft inner leaves, leaving behind dark droppings that look like wet sawdust.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ fe fɛɛ. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ baai ni miida lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni oye mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ Muji diji ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ pɛ eshwɛ.

english: This condition is called blossom end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit. It usually happens when watering is irregular, making it difficult for the roots to pull calcium from the soil into the developing fruit.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines up on tall poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tso awo tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch direct sunlight to produce energy for bigger yam tubers. It also improves airflow around the leaves, preventing fungal diseases that spread easily on damp soil.
ga: Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha sweet potato ŋmeii wuji lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ yaa hiɛ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ oya lɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and weak root systems that get scorched under direct sunlight. Shade trees protect young cocoa from extreme heat and help keep moisture in the topsoil until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers dry up and fall off the branches without forming small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when trees are stressed by dry spells or insect attacks. Cocoa flowers also need tiny insects called midges to transfer pollen; if there are no pollinators around, the flower cannot form a pod and will drop off.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ majik ni egbi lɛ tswa tso lɛ loo kooloi bibii tutua lɛ. Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ hu he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni ekɛ pollen yaa. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ bɛ he lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmeii ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal vital soil food, root space, and sunlight away from your plants. Even with plenty of rain, your crops will starve because the weeds are taking up the soil nutrients first.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛ yiwalɛ juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ po baaye hɔmɔ ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ baaŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow instead of remaining deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant pulls nutrients from its older, lower leaves to feed new growth, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow at the tips and pale down the middle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ nitrogen faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any peppers start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they face extreme heat, very dry soil, or too much chemical nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist and providing light shade during extremely hot periods helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehiɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: If I spray strong agrochemicals on my vegetables to kill pests, can it cause health problems for the people who eat them?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ okwaayeli mli tsofai ni mli wa shwie aduawai anɔ koni mikɛgbe kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ, Ani ebaaha mɛi ni yeɔ nakai aduawai lɛ aná hewalɛnamɔ he naagbai?

english: Yes, if you use excess chemical pesticides or harvest your crops too soon after spraying, toxic residues remain on the crop. Consuming these residues over time can cause long-term stomach problems, liver issues, and other illnesses in humans.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi babaoo tsu nii loo okpa onibii oya tsɔ beni okɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ahe nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ baakã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ aye nɛkɛ nibii ni eshwɛ nɛɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ musu mli naagbai aba. mlɛbo mli naagbai kɛ helai krokomɛi ni baa adesai anɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli

english: How can I stop caterpillars from destroying the central funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛi lɛ?

english: Caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm hide inside the central growing whorl of maize. Spraying recommended biopesticides or applying a mixture of dry sand and neem seed extract directly into the funnel destroys the pest before it damages the growing point.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie nɔ loo okɛ ŋã ni egbi kɛ neem dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ futu mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaakpata kooloi lɛ ahiɛ dani ekpãtã he ni edara yɛ lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl tightly upward during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes during hot afternoons is a defense mechanism to conserve water. By rolling its leaves inward, the plant reduces the leaf surface exposed to direct heat and strong sunlight to protect itself from drying out.
ga: Tomato baai ni ajieɔ yɛ shwane mli ni edɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni akɛto nu he. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni aaatsɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Tsei haa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ hulutsoo tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baa shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and woody even after growing in the ground for over a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛji tsei eyɛ mli akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ ni fe afi moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain thin if planted in hard, compacted clay soil or soil lacking potassium. Cassava needs loose, well-drained soil and adequate potassium so its root branches can expand and accumulate starch effectively.
ga: Cassava shishifãi baanyɛ ahi shi bibioo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa loo shikpɔŋ ni potassium bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse he miihia cassava. Etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni eyɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa Bɔni afee ni eniji lɛ alɛɛ mli ni amɛbua starch naa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand intense direct sunlight and heat. Tall trees provide necessary shade and cool shade temperatures, acting as a canopy that protects young cocoa leaves from scorching until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cocoa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa.

english: Why do my okra plants grow very tall and slender with very few fruits when planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he lɛ?

english: When okra seeds are sown too close together, the plants compete fiercely for sunlight, air, and soil nutrients. They spend all their energy growing tall to reach light instead of producing sturdy branches and okra pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu okra dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa kɛha hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ okra niji kɛ tsohi nɛ a he wa.

english: Why does my cowpea crop grow lots of thick green leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo lɛ? Shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Cowpeas produce excessive leafy foliage and few bean pods when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. High nitrogen encourages green leafy growth rather than the flowering and fruiting necessary to produce bean pods.
ga: Cowpeas woɔ baai babaoo tsɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo kɛji nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ daa moŋ fe fɔfɔi kɛ yibii ni he hiaa koni akɛfee ŋmeii.

english: What causes my yam tubers to rot and turn soft inside the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground mainly when planted in soil with poor drainage that holds standing water, or when soil insects and nematodes create small wounds on the tuber that allow rot-causing fungi to enter.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi titri kɛji akɛ akwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nu ni damɔ shi yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛ nematodes lɛ feɔ pilamɔi bibii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni haa ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ boteɔ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside cocoa provides living umbrellas that shield the young plants from direct heat and keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ he ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tightly during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves in high heat to reduce leaf surface area exposed to the sun, which minimizes water loss through evaporation. It is a natural self-defense mechanism to conserve moisture until temperatures cool.
ga: Pepper tsei kɛ la ni mli wa shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ haa nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni haa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize plant usually indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The plant moves limited nitrogen upward to feed new growth, leaving older bottom leaves starved of nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ko kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛkɛha shweremɔ hee niyenii. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help keep my soil fertile?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii baa?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground through root nodules. This process naturally enriches the soil with nitrogen, which benefits neighboring heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ nii kɛ nitrogen yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha tsei ni haa kooloi aniyenii ni tsii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the soil after long periods of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?
