english: Cassava roots require well-aerated soil to stay healthy. Waterlogged soil starves the root system of oxygen and creates damp conditions where soil-borne fungal diseases quickly cause root rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. ni eha shihilɛ ni mli edɔ aba Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa nɛɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo oya.

english: What causes ragged holes and brown sawdust-like dirt inside the center leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni etse kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing center (whorl) of young maize plants, chewing tender leaves and leaving behind waste that looks like brown powder.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ hei (rings) lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Okɛ baai bibii lɛ atsu nii ni oshi jwɛi ni tamɔ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Excess suckers compete directly with the main plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Keeping only one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to channel its energy into producing large fruit bunches.
ga: Suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with small yields when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Overcrowded crops compete for limited sunlight, root space, and soil nutrients. Instead of building strong stems and heavy fruits, they stretch upward searching for light, leading to weak growth and poor harvests.
ga: Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la fioo, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ sũ mli niyenii. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ tsohi nɛ a he wa kɛ yiblii nɛ mi wa. Mohu ɔ, a kplɛɛ a he kɛ hla la a. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni waaa kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni ehiii baa.

english: Tomato plants shed blossoms when stressed by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or nutrient imbalances. The plant drops flowers to save energy when it senses conditions are unsafe to support fruit growth.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa ha amɛ hao yɛ shwane mli. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ejaaa Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he beni amɛnuɔ he akɛ shihilɛi lɛ bɛ shweshweeshwe ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to weed around my yam mounds early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi yɛ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ ahe yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow quickly and steal nutrients and moisture from the soil. Clearing them early ensures the young yam vine gets maximum nutrition to build strong foliage, which is required to swell the tubers underground later.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha sweet potato wain tsei bibii lɛ aná niyenii ni fa fe fɛɛ ni baaha amɛná baai ni wa. Esa akɛ enɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ alɛɛ mli yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot tolerate direct sunlight and will dry up easily. Plantain trees grow very quickly and produce large leaves that shield young cocoa plants from the hot sun while keeping the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ni amɛbaagbi oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient corn needs to grow strong and green. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers like Urea or NPK helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni enyɛ eda ni efee ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: What is causing small holes in my corn leaves and dark droppings inside the top of the stem?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmãa ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa lɛ yiteŋ lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, a pest common in Ghana that eats the growing center of maize plants. Catching them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem water sprays can protect your crop before major damage occurs.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi loo neem nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baanyɛ abu onibii ahe dani nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ aba.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 8 and 12 months after planting. You can tell it is ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack as the tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ efee klalo kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni yitso lɛ fũuɔ lɛ.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need plenty of sunlight to manufacture food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where they can catch maximum sunlight and avoids fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ lɛ, ni amɛbaatsi amɛhe kɛjɛ fungal leaf helai ahe.

english: Why should I avoid planting my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ dumɔwui adumɔ he yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry stretch that can scorch newly germinated seeds. It is safer to wait until the rains become frequent and steady so the soil stays moist enough for seedlings to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ shii abɔ ni ebaa daa bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm after harvesting corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and naturally fix it back into the soil through their roots. Rotating them with corn restores soil fertility so your next crop can grow better without needing as much commercial fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo he ehiaaa bo.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crops very close together to fit more plants on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni tsei babaoo akwɛ̃ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin stems and smaller overall yields compared to crops planted with proper spacing.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa, ni yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ hu baa shi kɛ akɛto tsei ni adu yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers fall off mostly due to extreme heat, insufficient soil moisture, or using too much nitrogen fertilizer which forces the plant to grow leaves instead of fruit. Consistent watering and balanced plant feeding help flowers set into tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo lɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa kɛ niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and puckering together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. Spraying the leaves with neem oil or soap solution helps manage these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo samla shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight because their root systems are still weak. They require shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect their leaves from scorching and to keep the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lolo. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei koni amɛbu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: When plants are overcrowded, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of putting energy into growing big fruits, they stretch upward to fight for light.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛdu aduawai wuji Moŋ lɛ, ekɛ ehe shwie shi koni ekɛ la lɛ abɔ he akaŋ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the top young leaves to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests and diseases specific to that crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ nakai tso lɛ he pɔtɛɛ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is extension officers asking me to cut off extra stems from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ bi mi akɛ mafolɔ tomato tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Removing extra side branches, or suckers, forces the plant to send its water and nutrients directly into making bigger, healthier tomatoes instead of wasting energy on useless leaves.
ga: Niji loo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and curl during the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Leaves curl in extreme afternoon heat as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and slow down water loss through evaporation.
ga: Ha oyitsɔi afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane latsaa be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Koni akɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. ni ehaa nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi

english: Why do pests attack my vegetables more during the dry season than during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa mi aduawai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Dry heat speeds up the life cycle of many destructive insects, making them reproduce faster. At the same time, drought-stressed plants are weaker and less able to fight off pest attacks.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli egbi lɛ haa kooloi bibii babaoo ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ashihilɛ yaa oya. Enɛ haa amɛfɔɔ oya. yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ Tsei ni hɔmɔ emɔ amɛ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops right after the early rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and lie dormant in the dry soil waiting for water. Once rain falls, they germinate instantly because they are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions better than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi waa ni amɛwɔɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni miimɛ nu Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ekwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ eji koo mli tso ko ni etsake ehe koni ehi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready for harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Mature cassava plants usually show signs like yellowing and falling lower leaves, cracking in the soil around the base of the stem, and reaching the recommended maturity month for that specific variety.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei ni eda lɛ jieɔ okadii tamɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ akpo. Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli egbɛ eshwa. Ni kɛ́ eba nyɔŋ ni ajieɔ yi akɛ adu nakai ŋmei srɔtoi lɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do seeds I saved from last year's hybrid maize harvest yield much less grain than the original pack I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii fioo kwraa fe shishijee ŋmãa ni mihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two unique parent lines for high yields, but their offspring (second-generation seeds) lose those special qualities and produce weaker plants with lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔi akui sɔrɔtoi enyɔ amli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo, shi seshibii (yinɔ ni ji enyɔ dumɔwui) lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my young tomato plants wither and dry up so quickly when the sun gets very hot during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ oya kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes water to evaporate rapidly from both the plant leaves and the topsoil. When the roots cannot draw water fast enough to replace what was lost, the plant wilts to protect itself.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ fɛɛ mli. Beni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ajie nu oya bɔ ni sa koni amɛkɛto nɔ ni elaaje lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, Tso lɛ gboɔ koni ebu ehe.

english: How does spreading dry grass or leaves around the roots of my crops help them grow better in hot weather?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa kɛbɔleɔ he Te mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground with organic materials, known as mulching, acts as a barrier against direct sun rays. It keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating, and gradually breaks down into food for your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii akɛ gãimlibi ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ ni efite fiofio ni etsɔ niyenii kɛha onibii.

english: Why is it important to plant plantains near my young cocoa seedlings when starting a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ ahe beni mijeɔ ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast with wide leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing necessary shade and keeping the micro-climate cool around the seedlings.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni oha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ afee dumɔwui ni mli ejɔ

english: Is it safe to mix two different liquid crop medicines together in the same sprayer tank to save time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ tso tsofai enyɔ ni ji nu baafutu mli yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ kome mli koni akɛ be akafite?

english: Mixing unapproved agricultural chemicals can cause a bad chemical reaction that ruins their effectiveness, hardens or scorches your crop leaves, and damages your soil over time.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ okwaayeli mli ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai lɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii ni efiteɔ tsofa lɛ nitsumɔ. Enɛ haa otso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ais loo amɛshãa. ni ekɛ fitemɔ aba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What will happen to my soil if I only use strong chemical fertilizers year after year without adding animal manure?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii afi fɛɛ afi ni mikɛ kooloi ashishifãi fataaa he?

english: Relying strictly on chemical fertilizers damages the natural structure of the soil over time, making it hard and acidic, which prevents plants from naturally absorbing nutrients.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii waa lɛ fiteɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ nii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why did my crops burn after I applied a heavy dose of fertilizer to make them grow faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya lɛ?

english: Applying too much fertilizer at once creates a high salt concentration in the soil that draws water out of the plant roots instead of feeding them, leading to root burn and plant death.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei babaoo ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shãa ni tsei lɛ gboiɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants producing tall, leafy tops but very small tubers underneath the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɛ baai kakadaji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground rather than storing nutrients in the roots to form large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye níhi kɛ woɔ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ a pee bulb nguahi.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off before any pepper fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper yibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress or irregular watering, as a survival mechanism to conserve energy when conditions are difficult.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo latsaa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Koni efee yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ hewalɛ toɔ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants turn yellow early in the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a warning sign that the soil lacks nitrogen or that excessive water in the soil is suffocating the roots and preventing proper food uptake.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa lɛ aná.

english: Why is clearing my land with fire worse for my soil in the long run than clearing it by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ la ni akɛjieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ehiii kwraa kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli fe ni akɛ niji atsuɔ he nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the living organisms, earthworms, and organic matter that keep the soil fertile and soft, leaving the land exposed, dry, and poor for future crop seasons.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni efeɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɔ ko nɔ ko, ni egbi, ni efee ohiafoi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be ni baakwɛ nii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves often mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or is being attacked by fall armyworms. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer and checking early for tiny caterpillars inside the leaf whorls helps the plant grow green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo fall armyworms lɛ miitutua lɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii afata he ni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii bibii yɛ mli. Yɛ baa lɛ mli kɛjɛ shishijee Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Cassava root rot usually happens when heavy rain leaves water sitting in the soil for too long, allowing fungi to grow. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shi nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii baanyɛ adara. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and covering the soil around the plant with dry leaves keeps the roots cool so flowers can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ nu daa. Ehe miihia ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant cowpeas between my maize rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which acts like a natural fertilizer for your maize. Their leaves also shade the ground, keeping moisture in the soil and preventing weeds from taking over.
ga: Cowpeas mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha o-corn lɛ. Amɛbaai lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper crops in the same spot where I harvested tomatoes last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ he ni mifo mi-tomato lɛ yɛ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Peppers and tomatoes belong to the same crop family and suffer from the same soil-borne diseases. Rotating them with crops like maize or groundnuts breaks the disease cycle and leaves the soil healthier.
ga: Pepper kɛ tomato yɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛyeɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsuɔ nii Enɛ haa helai lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi.

english: Yams naturally wake up from dormancy after a few months because warm air signals to the tuber that it is time to grow. Storing yams in a cool, well-ventilated barn on raised bamboo racks slows down this sprouting process.
ga: Sweet potatoes baate shi kɛjɛ wɔɔhe yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa bulb lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ eda. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato to ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli yɛ ŋmeii ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle strong direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain next to them provides cover from intense sun and keeps the surrounding air humid.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa, ni eye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Under intense heat, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can take it up, causing temporary wilting to conserve water. Adding dry grass mulch around the base holds water in the soil so the roots stay hydrated longer.
ga: yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi Tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Nɔ ni ejɛ mli eba ji akɛ, nu ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ egbɔjɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ he ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. koni shishifãi lɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why are the bottom ends of my watermelons turning dark and rotting before they fully ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ su feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, usually triggered by irregular watering. Water carries calcium through the plant, so maintaining a steady watering schedule stops the fruit bottoms from turning black.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu kɛ calcium tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni oooha aduawai lɛ daa lɛ baatsi aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ediŋŋ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back so much faster than my crop plants after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and can sit quietly in dry soil for years, ready to spring up instantly when rain hits. Clearing weeds while they are still very small stops them from stealing water and nutrients from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛta shi dioo. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ afii babaoo ni efee klalo akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii waa lolo lɛ haaa amɛju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade from taller canopy crops like plantains because direct sunlight stresses them and burns their tender leaves before they are fully established.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋwɛi tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ, ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ waa ni eshãa baai bibii lɛ dani amɛdaraa.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and tiny caterpillars hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli Mi nɔ lɛ akɛtee ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana that eats maize leaves and damages the growing tips if not managed early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai ni efiteɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upwards and turning light yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies, or it can be a reaction to excessive heat and erratic rainfall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Aloo ebaanyɛ efee nɔ ko ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ mli baa.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra shoots growing around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ eje kpo.

english: Leaving too many suckers forces them to compete for water and soil nutrients, which results in smaller bunches. Pruning extra suckers keeps the main mother plant strong.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ fe nine lɛ, ehaa amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii baa. Kɛ́ afo tsei krokomɛi amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso titri lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden sticks next to my yam plants as they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fɔ̃ɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ masɛi kɛ́ amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yams are climbing vines that need stakes to lift their foliage toward sunlight, which enables the plant to produce maximum energy for growing tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ amɛshishifãi anɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo kɛha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my farmland produce less maize after three years of planting the exact same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ miiwo ŋmãa fioo yɛ afii etɛ ni mikɛdu ŋmãa kome lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover, making the ground tired and less fertile.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ ni ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting beans or groundnuts on the field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani adu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly flooded, causing stress to the plant.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ kɛtee nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are mature enough to harvest underground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the stem starts to crack slightly, usually 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa fioo. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: How long should I wait after the first rainy days before sowing my maize seeds?
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ gbi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ ni okɛdu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: It is best to wait until the ground has received at least two or three heavy rains so the soil holds enough deep moisture to help the seeds germinate safely.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni kɛ hoo lɛ, nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my crop leaves get scorched and burned when I spray agrochemicals in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shãa kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ shwie nɔ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Applying chemicals during the hot afternoon sun causes the liquid spray to evaporate too quickly, leaving behind concentrated chemical residues that scorch leaf surfaces while high heat stresses the plant.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ. Eshiɔ tsofa ko ni mli eyi obɔ ni shãa baa lɛ hiɛ, yɛ be mli ni la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ.

english: Should I dilute my fertilizer or pesticide with extra water during hot, dry weather?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ nu kroko awo ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi amli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yes, during very hot weather, plants lose water rapidly and become highly sensitive. Adding extra water dilutes the mixture, preventing chemical shock and root burn while helping the plant stay hydrated.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya ni amɛhe feɔ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ nu kroko fata he lɛ, ebaaha nɔ ni akɛfutu lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe kɛ shishifãi ni shãa lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Will my pesticides and fertilizers spoil if I keep them inside a hot storage shed?
ga: Ani mi tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafite kɛji mikɛto tsũ ko ni mli edɔ mli?

english: Excessive heat in a closed room breaks down the chemical compounds in agrochemicals, reducing their strength or changing how they react when mixed with water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ tsũi ni agbele mli lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ agrochemicals lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa tsofa lɛ hewalɛ baa shi loo etsakeɔ bɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii ehaa kɛ́ akɛ nu futu mli.

english: Why does pest control spray seem to stop working faster during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ kpaɔ nitsumɔ mra yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Strong sunlight and high heat speed up the chemical breakdown of pesticides on crop leaves, causing the chemical to evaporate or break down before it can eliminate pests.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ tsei ahe lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsofai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛfiteɔ dani amɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ.

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense mechanism crops use during peak heat to shrink their surface area, reducing water loss through evaporation until the temperature cools down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsuɔ nii yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he lɛ shi. Ehaa nu ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off without forming fruit when the sun is too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulu la babaoo shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses plants, causing them to shed their flowers to conserve moisture and energy for survival rather than spending resources on developing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei ajie amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ koni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii baatsu nii koni akɛfee aduawai lɛ

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wither and die right after sprouting in the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Newly sprouted seeds have small, shallow roots and delicate foliage that cannot draw enough ground moisture to replace what intense sunlight quickly dries up.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ ajie nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛwo hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ni egbiɔ oya lɛ he nyɔmɔ.

english: Is it harmful to irrigate or water my vegetable crops during the hot afternoon heat?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ mawo mi tsei lɛ nu loo mawo amɛ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Watering in strong heat causes most water to evaporate before reaching root zones, and hot water droplets remaining on leaves can intensify heat damage on foliage.
ga: Nu ni akɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ la dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli nu ni eshwɛɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa afite baai lɛ.

english: Why does dry fertilizer turn my crop leaves yellow and dry them up during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ haa mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve correctly; without sufficient water, high salt levels around root zones draw moisture out of the plant roots instead of feeding them.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nu bɛ Nu ni fa babaoo ni ebɔle he lɛ Shishifãi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do crops grown under shade trees stay green longer than crops fully exposed to the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli be kakadaŋŋ fe tsei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Shade lowers leaf and soil temperatures, slowing moisture loss from transpiration and protecting plants from the heat stress that causes leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Shade haa baa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i baa shi. Ha nu ni faaa kɛjɛɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ he.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have natural microbes in their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, renewing its fertility naturally for the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni aha adebɔɔ mli nibii babaoo aya hiɛ kɛha be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually signals a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the newer top leaves to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. They need shade trees to protect them from scorching and to keep moisture in the soil while they are young.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni amɛkashã amɛ, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ.

english: How do I know which direction to stick a cassava stem cutting into the soil when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni esa akɛ madu ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look for the tiny nodes or leaf buds along the stem. These buds must point upward toward the sky so the shoots can easily grow up and the roots can go down.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Ehe miihia ni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ oya ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ atswa shishifãi.

english: Why do my maize yields decrease when I plant three or four seeds in one hole close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ bu kome mli ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting too many seeds in one spot causes the plants to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and very small cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni adu yɛ he kome lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs to lift its leaves off the ground to catch sunlight and avoid rot or diseases that spread easily in wet soil.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni shwereɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛtsi fitemɔ loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ oya lɛ naa.

english: Why do farmers spread dry grass and leaves around the base of pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo lɛ shwã jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai ebɔle he lɛ? Pepper tso shishi?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) keeps the ground cool under hot sun, traps moisture so you water less often, and blocks weeds from growing.
ga: Mulching (mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Locks yɛ moisture mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu fioo. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why is it important to weed my farm when the crops are still tiny instead of waiting for them to grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ moŋ fe ni mamɛ ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Young crops are weak and easily starved of water and fertilizer by fast-growing weeds. Clearing weeds early ensures the young crop gets all the nutrients it needs to build strong roots.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnáaa nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya yɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ ahewɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei bibii lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat, poor watering, or a lack of insects to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. nu ni ehiii loo kooloi ni baahã fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollin lɛ bɛ

english: What causes tiny caterpillars to hide inside the funnel of my maize leaves and eat holes in them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-corn leaf cones lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ bu yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest whose moths lay eggs in the soft inner leaves (whorl) of young maize plants where caterpillars hatch and feed.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni ŋmeii woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii amli baai bibii (rings) lɛ amli he ni ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I have to cut down my cocoa trees when only a few leaves look sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo cacao tso ko he be mli ni baai fioo ko pɛ haa hela mɔɔ lɛ lɛ?

english: Diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot spread through the roots and sap inside the tree long before the whole tree dies. Cutting down the infected tree removes the virus from your farm and stops it from spreading to your surrounding healthy trees.
ga: Helai tamɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ mli be saŋŋ dani tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gboɔ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baaye abua ni ejie hela lɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ebaatsi enaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ amli.

english: If my cocoa tree gets a disease, can't I just spray it with medicine instead of cutting it down?
ga: Kɛji hela mɔ kookoo tso lɛ Ani minyɛŋ mawo tsofa lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mafo lɛ?

english: Certain cocoa diseases, especially viruses like Swollen Shoot, have no chemical cure. Spraying chemicals only kills the insects carrying the disease, but the tree itself remains permanently infected and will keep spreading the virus until it is removed.
ga: Kookoo helai komɛi Titri lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ, anyɛɛɛ akɛ tsofa atsa amɛ. Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baagbe kooloi ni kɛ helai baa lɛ pɛ. Shi tso lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ hela lɛ mli daa ni ebaaya nɔ egbɛ hela lɛ eshwa kɛyashi abaajie lɛ.

english: Why are extension officers telling us to cut down sick trees immediately instead of waiting until after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ beni akpa kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The longer a sick tree stays standing, the more insects feed on it and carry the virus to nearby healthy trees. Acting quickly saves the rest of your farm and prevents you from losing your entire cocoa harvest in the future.
ga: Babaoo ni tso ni hela mɔ lɛ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ, Babaoo ni kooloi bibii baaye tso lɛ ni amɛkɛ hela lɛ baahã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ ofee nɔ ko oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu he ni eshwɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he. ni etsi bo gbɛ koni okafite o-cocoa nibii fɛɛ ni ofeɔ lɛ wɔsɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree is sick before it stops producing pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ dani amɛkpa ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ?

english: You can spot early signs of sickness by looking for swollen stems, yellow patterns along the leaf veins, or unusually small and misshapen cocoa pods long before the tree completely dries up.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona hela he okadii mra kɛtsɔ tsei ni efuu lɛ ataomɔ nɔ. Ayɛ mfonirii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ baa lɛ fãji lɛ ahe. Aloo kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bibioo yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ ni efite be kakadaŋŋ dani tso lɛ egbi kwraa.

english: Why does it matter if my neighbor doesn't cut down their sick cocoa trees if I cut down mine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ efooo cacao tso ni hela mɔ lɛ lɛ kɛji mifo cacao tso lɛ?

english: Diseases are carried by tiny insects like mealybugs, which crawl across branches or blow in the wind from farm to farm. If your neighbor keeps infected trees, those insects will easily travel over and infect your clean farm.
ga: Kooloi bibii, tamɔ mealybugs, ni shwereɔ yɛ tsei aniji anɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli lɛ gbɛɔ helai eshwaa. Kɛji okutsoŋnyo lɛ hiɛ tso ko ni hela emɔ Nakai kooloi lɛ baafo mli oya ni amɛbawo oŋmɔ ni he tse lɛ mli hela.

english: Can my harvesting cutlass or pruning tools spread disease from a sick cocoa tree to a healthy one?
ga: Ani mi-knife loo mi-fomɔ tso lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã kɛjɛ cacao tso ni hela mɔ lɛ nɔ kɛya tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, sap from a diseased tree left on your cutlass or shears can infect the next healthy tree you cut. Cleaning your tools with soap, water, or heat between trees helps stop disease transmission.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni jɛ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ ni ashi yɛ o-knife loo o-shears lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ofoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ samla, nu, loo la tsu nii yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Can other big trees on my farm pass diseases to my cocoa trees?
ga: tsei wuji krokomɛi Ani hela baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mi kokoo tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, certain wild forest trees like the Silk Cotton tree act as natural homes for the same viruses and insects that attack cocoa. An extension officer can help you identify which shade trees are safe to keep.
ga: Hɛɛ, koo mli tsei komɛi, tamɔ Silk Cotton tso lɛ, tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shia kɛha helai kɛ kooloi bibii ni tutuaa kookoo lɛ nɔŋŋ. Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ shĩa mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona shĩa tsei ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni esa akɛ okɛto.

english: Will the soil stay infected and ruin my new crops if I cut down diseased cocoa trees?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná hela ni ebaafite miŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ kɛji mifolɔ kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Most cocoa viruses live inside the living plant tissue and insects, not directly in the dirt. Once the old roots die completely, the soil is safe for planting new crops.
ga: Kookoo mli helai babaoo hiɔ tsei ni hiɛ ka kɛ kooloi amli. Jeee yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ Beni shishifãi momo lɛ egbo kwraa Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha tsei heei akwɛmɔ.

english: How long should I wait before planting new cocoa seedlings on land where sick trees were cut down?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni afo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: It is best to wait a few months after clearing all infected roots and removing host weeds. This gap ensures that all disease-carrying insects on the plot have died off before new seedlings arrive.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi beni ojie shishifãi fɛɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ni ojie jwɛi ni hiɛ ka lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ haa kooloi ni hiɛ helai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ gboiɔ dani dumɔwui heei baa.

english: Are there new cocoa types I can plant that won't get sick as easily?
ga: Ayɛ kookoo henɔi heei. Ani manyɛ makwɛ nɔ ni hela akamɔ mi oya?

english: Yes, institutions like the Cocoa Research Institute of Ghana produce improved hybrid varieties that grow faster, yield more pods, and are much stronger against common diseases than older trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, nitsumɔhei tamɔ Ghana Cocoa Research Institute lɛ feɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛdara oya. Ha pods babaoo ni ote shi owo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni edara

english: Why are there small holes appearing in my young maize leaves with tiny worms hidden inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ ni Akɛtee mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm. The young worms hide inside the central leaves and eat the plant tissue, which damages the growing point and prevents the maize from absorbing light efficiently to grow strong stalks and cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai bibii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ mli fãji. Enɛ fiteɔ he ni ŋmãa lɛ daa yɛ lɛ, ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ la jogbaŋŋ koni ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and turning thick and crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like mites or thrips, or viruses they spread. As these pests suck the fluid from the young leaves, the leaves grow unevenly, curl up, and reduce the plant's ability to produce flowers and fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips lɛ kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ Enɛ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nuɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai bibii amli lɛ. Baai lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, amɛkpãa shi ni amɛhaa tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with smaller fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they compete with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of putting energy into growing strong stems and large fruits, the plants stretch tall to fight for light, leaving them weak and low-yielding.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ he wami kɛ haa a tso ɔmɛ nɛ a he wa kɛ a yiblii nguanguahi ɔ. Mohu ɔ, tsei ɔmɛ ngɔɔ a he kɛ yaa hɛ mi konɛ a kɛ la nɛ ɔ nɛ su. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnáa yibiiwoo fioo.

english: Why does my cassava plant have big, bushy leaves but very small tubers underground when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛji akpa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen compared to other nutrients, the plant spends all its energy growing heavy leaves above ground. For big, thick cassava roots, the soil needs balanced nutrients with enough potassium to push food storage down into the tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo baai ni tsii. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛha ŋmei shishifãi wuji ni mli tse lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baatsi niyenii ni ato lɛ awo ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off without forming any tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes the pollen inside tomato flowers to dry out and become sterile. When pollen cannot fertilize the flower, the plant drops the bloom to save its energy and moisture until growing conditions improve.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Beni pollen lɛ nyɛɛɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ afee fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ. Tsei baajie fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow forces the main tree to share its food and water with all of them. Removing extra suckers leaves one or two strong followers, ensuring the main tree has enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei bibii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ amɛ fɛɛ aja niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha sɛɛnyiɛlɔ kome loo enyɔ ni he wa aba. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ plantain agboi babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains or shade plants next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly under intense direct sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide temporary living shade and retain soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to endure full sun.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hulutsoo be muu lɛ fɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tight like tubes during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the maize plant's natural defense against water loss. By curling its leaves inward, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun and dry air, trapping moisture inside so it does not dry out.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei amli lɛ naa. Tsei haa amɛhe ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ mli kɛyaa mli lɛ nɔ. Emɔɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni baai lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do my lowland rice leaves start turning yellow when floodwater sits too high in the field for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ fa tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When water covers the plant too deeply for weeks, oxygen cannot reach the submerged roots. Without oxygen, the roots stop breathing and cannot absorb nutrients like nitrogen from the soil, causing the leaves to turn yellow from hunger.
ga: Kɛ nu ha tsei ahe tsɔ otsii babaoo lɛ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ ahe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ mumɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ hewɔ.

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows leaves to catch maximum sunlight and improves air circulation around the plant. Leaves that get full light produce more food, which travels down to swell the yam tuber under the soil while keeping the leaves away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ yaa hiɛ. Baai ni naa la babaoo lɛ baawo niyenii babaoo. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ akashɛɔ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to wear thick overalls and rubber boots when spraying chemicals on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo atadei ni tsii kɛ rɔbɔt atadei kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai miifɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pest control chemicals protect crops from insects, but they can soak into your skin and cause serious health problems. Wearing protective gear keeps the chemicals off your body while allowing you to treat your crops safely.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe. Shi tsofai nɛɛ baanyɛ abote hewolo lɛ mli ni ekɛ helai ni mli wawai aba. Kɛ́ owo nibii ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni tsofai akabote ogbɔmɔtso lɛ mli, yɛ be mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa bo ni okwɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will spraying extra pest control chemical make my crops grow faster and yield more?
ga: Ani tsofai krokomɛi ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: No, pest chemicals are only meant to kill bugs, not feed the plant. Using too much chemical can actually burn the crop's leaves, stunt its growth, and reduce your final harvest.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi bibii pɛ. Jeee niyenii ni akɛhaa tsei. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ tsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashã. etsĩɔ dalɛ naa ni ehaa naagbee nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and wither even when I do not see any insects on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbo lɛ? Namɔ enaaa kooloi bibii komɛi?

english: Yellow leaves can be caused by tiny crop diseases, lack of nutrients in the soil, or damage from wrong chemical usage. Understanding what the crop needs helps you fix the issue before the whole plant dies.
ga: Tso helai bibii loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha baai ŋmɔŋ aba. loo nɔ ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli Kɛ́ onu nɔ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni osaa naagba lɛ dani tso muu lɛ fɛɛ agbo.

english: How does using a proper knapsack sprayer help my crops better than sprinkling chemicals with a leafy branch?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ fe tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: A knapsack sprayer turns the chemical into a fine mist that covers the leaves evenly. Sprinkling by hand leaves large drops and misses under the leaves where pests hide and eat the crop.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ baagi mli lɛ haa tsofai lɛ feɔ afua kpakpa ni haa baai lɛ ahe pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nine ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaha nu agboi aba ni ebaafo yɛ baai lɛ ashishi he ni kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What is the best time of day to spray my crops so the leaves do not get damaged?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ tsei anɔ koni akafite baai lɛ?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the evening. Spraying under the hot afternoon sun can cause the chemical to burn wet leaves and evaporate before it kills the pests.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai lɛ shwie shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsofai lɛ ashã baai ni efɔ lɛ ni etsɔ la dani egbe ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do buyers in the market prefer crops that do not have insect spots or chemical smells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ sumɔɔ tsei ni kooloi loo tsofai fɔji bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Market buyers want clean, healthy produce that looks fresh and is safe to eat. Insects damage crop quality, while heavy chemical smells suggest the food might be dangerous for human consumption.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ miitao nibii ni he tse, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni tamɔ nɔ ni ehe tse ni abaanyɛ aye. Kplukai fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofa ko ni mli wa waa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ he ŋmɔlɔ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara kɛha adesa niyenii.

english: Why must I wait a few days after spraying before I can harvest my crops to sell in the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ gbii fioo komɛi beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ dani manyɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical sprays take a few days to break down and disappear from the plant. Waiting the recommended time ensures the crop is completely safe for people to eat when it reaches the market.
ga: Tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baahe gbii fioo komɛi dani efite ni elaaje kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. Be ni awo he ŋaa lɛ ni akɛaamɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kwraa ni gbɔmɛi baanyɛ aye kɛji eshɛ jara nɔ.

english: How do I know if my harvested crops will meet the quality standards demanded by major food traders?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mikpamɔ lɛ baashɛ shishitoo mlai ni niyenii jarayelɔi wuji biɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Traders look for uniform crop size, clean skin without pest marks, and crops grown with safe inputs. Proper care during growth ensures your produce easily meets market standards.
ga: Jarayelɔi taoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdalɛ tamɔ amɛhe. Hewolo ni he tse ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ kɛtsɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe nɔ lɛ Hekwɛmɔ ni sa yɛ shweremɔ be mli lɛ haa onibii ni oduɔ lɛ yeɔ jarayeli he mlai lɛ anɔ oya.

english: Can my crops survive insect attacks using basic farming practices instead of buying expensive chemicals?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ kooloi ni baatutua amɛ lɛ amli kɛtsɔ okwaayeli gbɛi titrii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ moŋ fe tsofai ni jara wa ni aheɔ?

english: Yes, basic practices like clearing weeds early, rotating crops, and removing diseased plants reduce bugs naturally. Chemical inputs are just extra support tools, not the only solution for a good crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, shishijee nifeemɔi tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra, ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ, kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ baaha kooloi bibii aba shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji yelikɛbuamɔ dɛŋdade krɛdɛɛ ko kɛkɛ. Jeee no pɛ ji tsabaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why are there government rules on which chemicals I am allowed to use on my food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli mlai yɛ ni kɔɔ tsofai ni aŋmɛ mi gbɛ akɛ mikɛtsu nii yɛ miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Rules are in place to ensure you only buy genuine chemicals that protect crops without poisoning the soil, damaging the plants, or making the harvested food dangerous for buyers.
ga: Mlai yɛ ni baakwɛ koni ohe tsofai diɛŋtsɛ ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ pɛ ni ekɛ tsofai fɔji wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, efiteee tsei, loo efeee niyenii ni akpa lɛ oshara kɛhaa mɔ ni heɔ lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need plenty of sunlight to make food for the crop. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so leaves get maximum sunlight and stay clean from soil diseases, which helps grow larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. koni baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ he atse kɛjɛ helai ahe Enɛ baaye abua ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara.

english: How far apart should I plant my plantain suckers when setting up my field?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu plantain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔ ko miito?

english: Plantain suckers should usually be planted about 3 meters apart. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space, water, and soil nutrients to produce heavy fruit bunches without competing with neighboring plants.
ga: Esa akɛ adu plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai etɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ewo yibii ni tsii ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akaŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure will help bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ akwɛ̃ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my pepper plants before any peppers show up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Flowers often drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress, uneven watering, or nutrient shortages. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot periods helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ahaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and droop when the sun is very hot in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl and droop in high heat as a self-defense mechanism to stop water from evaporating too fast. As long as the soil has basic moisture, the leaves usually bounce back by evening.
ga: Cassava baakpã ni ebaagbee shi yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ehe koni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya tsɔ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa sɛɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains the specific nutrients maize needs and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abɛi lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei baaye abua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I use dry crop waste and fallen leaves to help feed my soil instead of buying chemical fertilizer?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsei ni egbi ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ atsu nii ni mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni mahe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, turning dry leaves and crop stems into compost adds rich organic matter to the soil. It improves how well the soil holds water and supplies natural nutrients to feed your future crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe tsei ni atsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa onibii ni obaadu wɔsɛɛ lɛ yeɔ nii.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have big leaves that shade the young cocoa plants like umbrellas while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa kookoo tso bibioo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack due to the tubers expanding underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow much slower even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo nɛkɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, light, and soil food away from your crops. Removing weeds early ensures all the goodness in the soil goes straight into growing your crops.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, la, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa nɔ ni hi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ náa onibii anɔ hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily burned by hot, direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide essential shade and retain soil moisture, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Buu kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and small worms inside the plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on young maize leaves and growing points. Spraying recommended organic or chemical treatments early in the morning or late evening when the worms are active helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with many leaves, but the tubers underground remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium or phosphorus. Excessive nitrogen encourages the cassava plant to spend its energy producing heavy foliage above ground instead of swelling its tubers below ground.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ fa babaoo ni potassium loo phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ woɔ yucca tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo baai ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e yi ɔ fĩɔ ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to expose maximum leaf surface to sunlight, which enables the plant to make food. Staking also keeps the leaves off damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and resulting in larger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei woɔ niyenii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji baa.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often triggered by irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist allows the tomato plant to absorb calcium properly from the ground.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have helpful bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop harvest is done, that extra nitrogen remains in the ground to feed high-demanding crops like maize.
ga: Muawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa mli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ agbe ŋmaa lɛ naa Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it better to raise pepper seeds in a seedbed before moving them to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani ajie kɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds are small and fragile, making them vulnerable to heavy rain, heat, and pests if planted directly in the field. A nursery allows you to protect and nurture the delicate seedlings until they grow strong roots for transplanting.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, dɔlɛ, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ afite amɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ. He ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni okwɛɔ amɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa ni akɛbaadu.

english: Why should I cut off extra sucker shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Too many suckers compete with the main plantain tree for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Pruning extra suckers to leave only one or two ensures the main plant gets full nourishment to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ afo tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ amli kɛyafee ekome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo tsei niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dry grass or cocoa husks during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ jwɛi loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry plant material, known as mulching, prevents soil moisture from evaporating quickly in the sun. It keeps roots cool and breaks down over time to enrich the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu la mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni efiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my young garden eggs turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate a shortage of nitrogen in the soil or poor drainage causing waterlogging around the roots. Adding well-rotted manure or compost and ensuring excess water drains away will restore the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he ni okwɛ koni ajie nu ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha efee ŋmɔŋ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and short roots that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa creates a canopy that protects them from harsh heat and retains moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli tamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo bibii ewo mli lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ baa, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: When crops are planted too closely together, their roots fight each other for water and nutrients in the soil, while their leaves block each other from sunlight. Spacing them correctly allows every plant enough room to grow strong and produce big yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni abuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la lɛ he Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra branches and chupons from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni jɛ cacao tso ni eda lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Removing unwanted branches and suckers (chupons) allows sunlight and fresh air to reach all parts of the tree. This reduces humidity inside the canopy, which helps prevent black pod disease and directs the tree's energy into producing large pods.
ga: Niji kɛ ŋmeii ni ataooo (chupons) ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ black pod hela lɛ naa, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning pale green and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food crops need to build green leaves; adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore their dark green color and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kɛ dalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I not plant maize on the exact same piece of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating with different crops keeps the soil balanced and healthy.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do groundnuts or cowpeas help make my farm soil richer for other crops?
ga: Te ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei baanyɛ aye abua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afee shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special nodules on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. When the leaves and roots decay, they leave behind free plant food for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite Amɛshiɔ tsei niyenii yɛ amɛsɛɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What is making small ragged holes in my maize leaves and leaving dark droppings inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing center (funnel) of the plant. Inspecting fields early and applying recommended biological treatments or approved chemicals into the funnel stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ dalɛ mli (cone) lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mra. ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ he nii loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ awo tsɔne lɛ mli. Kpa nibii nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: When water sits on flat soil without draining, it suffocates the roots and creates the right environment for soil fungi to attack the cassava tubers. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away safely.
