ga: Beni nu yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua ŋmei shishifãi lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around their plants with dry grass and plant leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ tsei ahe baai shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛtsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. Covering the soil acts like a blanket that stops the sun from evaporating water out of the ground, keeps root temperature cool, and breaks down over time to enrich the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Mulching tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli latsaa lɛ baa shi. ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops exclusive access to the water and plant food they need to flourish.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa nu kɛ tsei niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow strong, so adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist and providing proper nutrients helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji latsaa ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfataa he Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ niyenii ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the tall trees from the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ? kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle full sunlight and heat. They need shade crops like plantains or tall trees above them to shield their leaves from sunburn and keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu kɛ dɔlɛ ni fa babaoo lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Koni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it good practice to plant groundnuts or beans on the same land as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts and beans naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This enriches the soil naturally, helping feed nearby maize crops without extra fertilizer costs.
ga: Agbɛnɛ hu, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ahaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii ni ŋmãa he nyɔmɔwoo fataaa he.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes into the middle of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on the soft foliage inside the plant stem. Checking plants early and applying neem seed extract or approved pesticides will control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tsei akutsei amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akwɛ tsei lɛ amli mra ni akɛ neem dumɔwui amli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaakudɔ tso lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and stays around them in wet or poorly drained soils. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater flow away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa ni ebɔle amɛhe. Kasava shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ loo nu shwieee nɔ jogbaŋŋ Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: If I plant my seeds very close to each other, will I get a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani manyɛ makpa babaoo?

english: No, overcrowding causes crops to compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to develop strong roots and bigger yields.
ga: Dabi, nibii ni aduɔ fe nine lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa baakwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves to catch as much sunlight as possible to build large tubers. Staking lifts leaves off the ground, increasing food production and preventing soil diseases from attacking leaves.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee bulbs agboi. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Haa niyenii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ ni etsiɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ anaa koni amɛkatutua baai lɛ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out and crack so quickly during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture fast under direct sunlight. Covering the exposed soil around crops with dry grass or leaves retains soil moisture, keeps roots cool, and prevents soil cracking.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi baatsu nii ni akɛha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Tsei baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa sũ lɛ mli agbala

english: Why do weeds make my crops look stunted even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miikpa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal nutrients, water, and sunlight before your crops can get to them. Clearing weeds during the early stages of crop growth ensures the crops get all available nourishment.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow mainly due to a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow strong. Applying the right fertilizer early in the plant's life gives it the nourishment it needs to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ titri lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni sa wo tso lɛ mli mra yɛ tso lɛ wala be mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ewo ŋmeii wuji ni wa.

english: When is the best time to put fertilizer on my crops so the rain doesn't wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni nugbɔ akashwie amɛ?

english: Fertilizer is best applied when the soil is already moist after a light rain, and it should be covered slightly with soil near the plant's roots. Applying fertilizer during heavy downpours or on dry ground causes the water to carry the nutrients away before the crop can drink them.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Ni esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fioo yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ yaa dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nuɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops roll up tightly during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl or roll up as a natural defense to protect themselves from losing water in intense heat. It shows the plant is saving its moisture to survive, but if the leaves stay rolled up all day, the crop urgently needs water.
ga: Kɛ́ oha ebɔle ehe lɛ, eji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ nu ni faaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibu ŋmɔtɔ he koni ehi shi. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tee nɔ amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii hu oya.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the plant experiences sudden stress from extreme heat, dry weather, or lack of water and nutrients. To save its own life under stress, the plant drops its flowers instead of spending energy to produce fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔ trukaa kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ Bɔni afee ni ohere ohe kɛjɛ haomɔ shishi Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo yibii.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: Planting crops too close forces them to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak plants that produce very small yields, whereas proper spacing lets each plant grow fully and yield heavily.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ baaha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ada ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do people say I should plant beans or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it into the soil as natural plant food. Planting them alongside heavy-feeding crops like maize keeps the soil rich and helps both crops perform better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato stems are soft and fall over, putting the leaves and fruits in direct contact with damp soil where pests and diseases live. Staking lifts the plant into the air, keeping it dry and allowing air and sunlight to pass through to stop rotting.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Ha baai kɛ aduawai lɛ aba shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni kooloi bibii kɛ helai hiɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Staking woɔ tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli, ehaa egbiɔ, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ mli koni ekpa fitemɔ.

english: Why are dark spots appearing on my cassava leaves, and will it destroy the tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei baa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji lɛ? Ani ebaafite ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Leaf spots are usually caused by fungal or bacterial infections spread by wet weather or bad planting sticks. Mild spots only damage the leaves, but severe leaf damage stops the plant from making food, which shrinks the growth of the tubers underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal loo bacteria hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo niji ni ehiii lɛ nɔ kɛ baa lɛ he tsɔi baa. He ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ pɛ. Shi baa ni fiteɔ waa lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekawo niyenii. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ aba shi.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow so slowly and look pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi tsei titrii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm, stealing water, fertilizer, and sunlight directly away from your crops. When weeds surround your crops, your crops starve, leading to slow growth and pale leaves.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɔle oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Hɔmɔ baaye oŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa edaa blɛoo ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why did some of the maize seeds I bought from the open market fail to sprout after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui komɛi ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ kwɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds from local markets are often old, damaged by heat, or infested with tiny insects that kill the living embryo inside the seed. Certified seeds from agricultural officers are tested and treated so almost every seed sprouts into a strong crop.
ga: Dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei lɛ fɔɔ tsɛmɔ. hulutsoo efite loo kooloi bibii yɛ Infestation ni kpataaa fɔmɔ kotoku ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ hiɛ. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ amli ni atsu he nii. No hewɔ lɛ, nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu daa ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to press the soil down firmly around a newly planted plantain sucker?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli lɛ? dumɔwui heei ni adu

english: Pressing the soil firmly prevents rainwater from entering and pooling inside the hole around the stem, which can cause the sucker or the mother plant to rot.
ga: Kɛ́ onyɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ lɛ naa ni ekabote bu ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ mli, ni no baanyɛ aha tso ni nuɔ loo tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ afite.

english: What will happen to my crop if I do not cover the planting hole completely after putting in the sucker?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ sucker lɛ wo mli sɛɛ ni mikɛ dumɔ bu lɛ tsiii kwraa?

english: If the hole is left uncovered or loose, rainwater will collect inside it and cause the young sucker to decay before it can establish roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ loo ashi lɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ Nugbɔ nu lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ mli ni ehaa gbekɛbii lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛfeɔ shishifãi.

english: How firm should I pack the earth around the base of a new plantain shoot?
ga: Te esa akɛ makɛ sũ ni bɔle mitsei heei lɛ ashishi lɛ abɔ he lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: You should press the dirt down solidly enough so there are no loose gaps or open pockets where excess rainwater can sink in and settle near the stem base.
ga: Esa akɛ onyɛ muji lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni ŋmeii ni etse loo ŋmeii ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ mli yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: What is the correct way to cover a plantain sucker after placing it in the ground?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahaa plantains nɔ beni akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fill the hole completely with topsoil up to the surface level and press it down firmly so that rainwater runs off to the sides rather than sinking straight into the hole.
ga: Okɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ awo bu lɛ mli kɛyashi eshishigbɛ ni onyɛ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni nugbɔ nu lɛ ajɛ kpo kɛya sɛɛgbɛ moŋ fe ni eeebote bu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: People say plantain loves water, so why do my plantain plants rot when water sits around them?
ga: Mɛi komɛi kɛɔ akɛ plantains sumɔɔ nu. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ fiteɔ be mli ni nu ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: While plantains need steady soil moisture to grow well, standing water trapped directly around the base or inside the shoot starves the plant of air and leads to fungal rot.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ plantains he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ moŋ, shi nu ni damɔ shi ni ekpɛtɛ shishigbɛ tɛ̃ɛ loo eshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: How can I make sure my plantain crop gets enough water without causing the plants to spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana nɔmimaa akɛ midumɔwui lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mihaaa tsei lɛ agbo?

english: Provide good soil drainage and press the soil tightly around each plant base so moisture stays in the soil while excess rainwater drains away from the stem.
ga: Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ abɔle tso fɛɛ tso shishi shiŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do some of my plantains decay during the heavy rainy season if plantains need water all year round?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ banana tsei komɛi fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli kɛji akɛ nu he miihia plantains afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy downpours can fill poorly covered planting holes with trapped water, causing stem rot even though plantains naturally thrive on good water supply.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ayi nu ni damɔ shi yɛ dumɔ bui ni atsĩ naa jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ baanyɛ afite. Eyɛ mli akɛ plantains baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛ nu kpakpa jɛɛhei moŋ, shi.

english: Can water trapped around a young plantain sucker end up killing the main mother plant?
ga: Ani nu ni ebɔle dumɔwui bibii ahe lɛ baanyɛ agbe fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ?

english: Yes, if water collects and causes a sucker attached to the main plant to rot, that rot can easily spread directly into the connected mother plant and destroy it.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni efite suckers ni akɛkpɛtɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ. Nɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã fɔlɔ tso ni kɛ lɛ yɔɔ tsakpaa lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni efite lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why are my young plantain shoots rotting from the inside after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This happens when rainwater gets trapped inside the stem or planting hole because the soil around the shoot was not packed down tight enough during planting.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nu lɛ bote tso lɛ mli loo dumɔ bu lɛ mli. Ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle Shoots lɛ he lɛ ehiɛɛɛ shi bɔ ni sa yɛ dumɔ be mli.

english: How do I prevent rainwater from collecting inside the central stem of my young plantain shoots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekabua ehe naa yɛ plantain bibii lɛ ashishifã lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: Ensure you heap and firm the topsoil around the base of the shoot so that water naturally flows outward away from the center of the plant.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni okɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ato tso lɛ shishigbɛ he koni nu lɛ atsɔ ehe kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa leaves turning brown and drying up when there is plenty of sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct sunlight because their tender leaves burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them provides natural shelter until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli shihilɛhe aba kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baadara ni ená hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an important nutrient in the soil that helps plants stay green and grow strong. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores what the plant needs to develop normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nɔ ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when the rainy season is very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need soil that drains water easily. When heavy rain leaves standing water in the soil, the roots cannot breathe and harmful mold develops, causing the tubers to decay before harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ kpɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa.

english: Why do my crops yield less harvest when I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Alternating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally recharges the soil with nitrogen and keeps it fertile.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Akɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii tsakeɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Flowers often fall off due to stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of insect pollinators. Keeping the soil consistently moist and allowing natural bees to visit helps flowers convert into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo fɔfɔii ni haa fɔfɔi baa lɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni oha adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii abasara Enɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What happens to my yam crop if I leave the vines to grow on the ground instead of using wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji miha wain tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ tso ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the ground so they can catch direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers. Unstaked vines remain on damp soil, making them vulnerable to fungal diseases and resulting in much smaller tubers.
ga: Staking jieɔ ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tsei ni atswako amɛhe lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa amɛnɔ, ni no haa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ feɔ bibii kwraa.

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops compete against one another for sunshine, soil moisture, and food. Giving each plant proper space allows it to build thick stalks and grow large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and shrinking into tight clusters?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites feeding on the underside of young leaves. Treating these pests early stops them from stunting the plant's growth and reducing pepper yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsɔɔmɔ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ mra. Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ, ni amɛkaha ŋmɔtɔ ni anáa lɛ aba shi.

english: How do weeds growing in my farm reduce the size and weight of my crop harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ dalɛ kɛ egbɔjɔmɔ baa shi?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures that all the food in the soil goes directly into feeding your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ yaa otsei titrii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my vegetable plants with dry grass or leaves during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo he ni ebɔle he lɛ mli lɛ? Tsei ni jwɛi ni egbi loo baai yɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, blocks direct heat from the sun. This traps moisture in the ground, keeps the root area cool, and helps plants survive periods without rainfall.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ha shishifã lɛ he afee fɛ̃i ni eye ebua tsei ni amɛhi shi ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight in their early stages. Planting shade crops like plantains or cassava next to them shields the young leaves from sunburn and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ shishijee mli. Dumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛmasɛi. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the newer top growth, so you need to apply nitrogen fertilizer to feed the whole plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Tso lɛ baajie nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Does it matter which direction I point cassava stem cuttings when I push them into the soil?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ mihe wo shikpɔŋ lɛ Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ matsɔɔ yucca nine lɛ?

english: Yes, cassava cuttings must be planted with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the stems will struggle to grow properly, delaying your harvest and reducing tuber size.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baaná naagba yɛ edalɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ehaa tuber lɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. When it is too hot or dry, the flowers fail to pollinate and simply drop off to save the plant's energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛji edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ lɛ Anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi koni akɛbu tso lɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Leaving too many side shoots (suckers) forces them to steal nutrients and water from the main tree. Removing extra suckers ensures the main plantain tree gets all the food it needs to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi sɛɛ ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa dumɔwu titri lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry period of a few weeks. If you plant right away, the seeds will sprout and then dry up and die before the main rains arrive.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni heɔ otsii fioo sɛɛ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and becoming crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the underside of the leaves. Controlling these insects early stops the leaves from curling and keeps the plant growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baaha baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni eda.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and put wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ? Ni ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ tso ni ekɛkwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves in direct sun to make food for the underground tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot, wet ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping the tubers grow much larger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ aha amɛbaai lɛ ahi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking baaha baai akabote hei ni mli edɔ ni edɔ. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help my soil for the next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decay, they naturally leave that nitrogen behind in the soil to fertilize the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei fite Amɛshiɔ nakai nitrogen lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it better for me to water my garden early in the morning instead of in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ nu woɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli leebi moŋ fe shwane lɛ?

english: Watering in the afternoon causes most of the water to evaporate in the hot sun before the roots can absorb it. Morning watering lets the roots soak up moisture calmly before the heat of the day sets in.
ga: Nu ni oooha yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ la yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ fɛ̃i lɛ blɛoo dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green. The plant moves nitrogen from older leaves at the bottom to feed the new growth at the top, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of leafy branches but producing small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Eyɛ niji kɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ yitso bibioo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or water early in its growth, it spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of sending energy down to build big roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo nɔ yɛ shishijee be mli ni edara lɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni eeetsu lɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛfee shishifãi wuji.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown or black and rot while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ beni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, wet, and humid conditions. Trimming extra tree branches to let in sunlight and air helps keep the pods dry and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji krokomɛi ahe koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids hidden under the leaves sucking out the sap, or by a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these tiny bugs early protects the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ kooloi bibii akudɔmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Cowpea flowers are often attacked by small insects like pod-boring caterpillars or flower thrips that eat the flowers from the inside, causing them to drop before they can form pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ pod borers loo flower thrips ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ tutuaa cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ. Ha egbee shi dani efee pod.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or if the soil lacks key nutrients. The plant drops flowers to save water and protect itself from stress.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ haomɔ he.

english: Why do my yam leaves and vines dry up completely before the harvest season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes kɛ wain tsei lɛ egbi kwraa dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry up early if the soil runs out of moisture during the tuber-growing period, or if fungal leaf spot diseases destroy the leaves before the tubers are fully mature.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baagbi oya kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni aduɔ bulb lɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ fungal leaf spot hela lɛ kpata baai lɛ ahiɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ dara.

english: Why are my cabbage plants forming loose leaves instead of folding into a hard round head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeebɔle ehe ni efee yitso ni wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form hard heads when the weather is too hot or when watering is irregular. They need cool soil, constant moisture, and balanced nutrients to fold into a tight head.
ga: Kaabaji lɛ ewaŋ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ shwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ he miihia amɛ. hulutsoo ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ niyenii ni ja ni baaha yitso lɛ abɔle shi shiŋŋ

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to start growing after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛjeɔ dalɛ shishi beni mikɛ amɛ ewo he kroko lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Transplanted suckers lose water quickly through their large old leaves. Pruning back the leaves and planting during the early rains helps the sucker focus its energy on growing strong new roots first.
ga: Suckers ni adu lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ baai agboi ni egbɔ lɛ anɔ. Baai ni afolɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa mɛi ni nuɔ nu lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do my maize stalks bend over and fall flat whenever strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Maize falls over if the seeds were planted too shallow or if the root system is weak. Piling up extra soil around the base of the stalks (earthing up) gives the roots stronger anchor support against wind.
ga: Abele baagbee shi kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ krokomɛi ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ shishi (shikpɔŋ nɔ) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a crucial food plants need to grow strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure near the base helps the leaves regain their deep green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa ni tsei lɛ adara waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he ni bɛŋkɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa amɛdaramɔ yaa hiɛ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas out of the air and store it in their roots in the soil. When they grow alongside maize, they naturally feed the soil with nutrients, acting as a free, natural fertilizer for your maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi Amɛbaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa o-corn lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear huge trees away but leave a few standing when I prepare a farm for new cocoa seedling trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei wuji shi mashi tsei fioo komɛi beni miisaa ŋmɔ lɛ kɛha kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily in direct harsh sunlight, but mature trees need some sun to produce pods. Leaving a few shade trees protects young seedlings while letting enough light through for them to mature properly.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Shi kookoo tso ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ he miihia hulu la fioo koni ekɛwo ŋmeii. Kɛ́ ashi tsei fioo komɛi ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui bibii ahe yɛ be mli ni eha la ni fa bɔ ni sa baaha dumɔwui lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to place tall wooden poles in the ground for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants grow as long vines, and lifting them off the ground with poles allows their leaves to catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight gives the plant energy to send nutrition downward to grow bigger yam tubers under the soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daa tamɔ wain tsei kakadaji. ni okɛ tso awo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha ebaaji lɛ aje kpo yɛ hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ mli. Hulu la haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shi koni amɛkwɛ̃ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating small holes in the central funnel leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ cone baa lɛ mli

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that hides in the funnel of maize plants to feed on tender leaves. Spotting them early allows you to crush them by hand or apply recommended pest controls before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni teɔ shi yɛ ŋmãa tsei amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Amɛtaomɔ mra Enɛ baaha okɛ onine atswa amɛ loo okɛ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛyeɔ lɛ atsu nii dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap out of the leaves and spreading viruses. Controlling these small insects early prevents the leaf curl from spreading to the rest of your pepper crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. small insect control Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baatsi baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmei lɛ fãi krokomɛi amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot, when the plant receives inconsistent water, or when bees are not around to pollinate them. Keeping the soil evenly moist and planting flowering herbs nearby to attract bees helps fruits form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nu nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ jɛmɛ koni amɛfee pollination, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ fɔfɔi tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Kɛji oogbala ŋmeii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewo yibii.

english: How do I know which small shoots to cut away from my main plantain stem?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Kɛjɛ mi plantain tso titri lɛ mli?

english: You should leave only one or two strong shoots (called suckers) around the main mother plantain tree. Cutting away extra suckers prevents them from stealing food and water, ensuring the main tree produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. (ni atsɛɔ lɛ suckers) ni bɔleɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ awo plantains wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil around them for too long due to heavy rains or poor drainage. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my crops so the rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni nugbɔ akashwie amɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist right after a light rain, but avoid doing it right before a heavy downpour. Placing the fertilizer in a small ring around the plant and covering it lightly with soil keeps the rain from washing it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Shi kaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii awo tso lɛ he ni okɛ sũ aha he fioo. Koni nugbɔ akashwie shi

english: Maize leaves turn yellow mainly when the plant lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient it needs to grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rains flood the soil, preventing the roots from breathing and absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ amu jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii lɛ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that grab nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into soil food. This naturally fertilizes the soil, helping nearby crops like maize grow bigger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfeɔ lɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, ni amɛdaraa ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my pepper plants curl their leaves and droop during hot afternoons even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, pepper leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can drink it up from the ground. The plant intentionally wilts to protect itself from drying out, and it usually recovers naturally when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei tsɔɔ yiŋtoo ko nɔ amɛgbiɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava stems rot underground when I plant them during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil stays completely soaked with water for too long, oxygen cannot reach the buried cassava stem. Without air, the stem cannot sprout roots, allowing soil fungi to multiply and cause the stem to rot.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ ŋmei tsei ni afu lɛ ahe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faa babaoo ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: When plants are crowded together, their roots fight underground for water and nutrients while their leaves fight above ground for sunlight. This competition leaves all the plants weak and thin, resulting in smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Yam plants use climbing poles to spread their leaves high in the air where they can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make plant food, which travels down to build a large, healthy underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ ŋtayaai tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛgbɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ lɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ tsei niyenii. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: Why do armyworms seem to appear overnight and destroy my maize farm right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ je kpo nyɔɔŋ kome mli ni amɛfite mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Armyworm moths lay hundreds of hidden eggs on green leaves just before the rains start. Once it rains, all the caterpillars hatch at the same time and begin eating continuously, creating the appearance of a sudden invasion.
ga: Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ baai eŋɔli anɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ fɔɔ yɛ be kome mli ni amɛjeɔ niyenii yeli shishi yɛ amɛsɛɛ. Ekɛ trukaa tutuamɔ ko ni baa lɛ baa

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my crops after I clear and cultivate my farm land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mijie miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weed seeds can lie dormant in the dirt for years waiting for light. When you clear the land, you expose these buried seeds to sunlight and moisture, giving thousands of weed seeds the signal to sprout all at once.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ awɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo ni amɛmiimɛ la Kɛ́ ojie jɛmɛ Dumɔwui ni afu nɛkɛ lɛ, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa amɛnɔ. Enɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui akpei abɔ feɔ okadi akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ be kome mli.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when day temperatures become too high or when there is a drought spell. Under stress, the plant saves its energy to stay alive rather than spending energy to form new fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ loo kɛ́ hɔmɔ ba. yɛ haomɔ shishi Tsei buɔ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛfee aduawai heei

english: Why do the leaves on my plantain tree start dying off when the fruit bunch grows big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ beni aduawai akuu lɛ daa lɛ?

english: When a plantain tree produces a large bunch, it redirects almost all its energy and nutrients from its leaves straight into the growing fruit. The older leaves naturally dry up and die off because their food is being used to fill out the fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ plantain lɛ kwɛ̃ niji babaoo Etsɔɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Baai ni egbɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgboiɔ beni akɛ niyenii tsuɔ nii koni akɛwo aduawai lɛ amli ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen nutrients or are receiving too much water. Applying a balanced nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ ni nitrogen niyenii loo amɛná nu babaoo tsɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my cassava crop is sick with a plant disease or just suffering from hot weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ hela emɔ amɛ kɛ tsei ahela loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ pɛ?

english: Heat makes plants droop temporarily during the hottest part of the afternoon, but they bounce back by evening. A plant disease leaves permanent signs like twisted leaves, yellow spots, or stunted stems that do not go away at night.
ga: Dɔlɛ lɛ ha tsei lɛ gboi yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shi ebaaku esɛɛ eba gbɛkɛ. Tse helai kɛ okadii ni hiɔ shi daa tamɔ baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo tsei ni egbɔjɔ ni sɛɛ efooo gbɛkɛ baa.

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central funnel of the plant. Checking your field early and applying targeted controls into the funnel will protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli mra. Ni kɛ akɛ targeted control tsu nii yɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani aduawai kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat, uneven watering, or a lack of plant nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant hold onto its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo tso mli niyenii tamɔ calcium ni bɛ. Kɛ́ afee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔii ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I harvested corn last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Corn feeds heavily on nutrients and exhausts the soil. Groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the earth, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii mli nibii babaoo ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Peanuts kɛ cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha okwɛ̃mɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the tips of my pepper fruits turning black and rotting while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot and is caused by irregular watering, which prevents the plant from transporting calcium to the fruits. Regular, even watering prevents the fruit tips from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ kɛbaa. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ kɛ calcium aya aduawai lɛ amli. Nu ni oooha amɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: Yam vines need to climb up stakes to get maximum sunlight on their leaves. Sunlight allows the leaves to make energy, which travels down to swell and grow large, heavy tubers under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ koni amɛha baai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo he. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi ni efuɔ ni edaraa ni etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Weeds compete with your crops for water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients in the soil. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food and light they need to grow strong and yield heavily.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ ana niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: What happens if I plant my seeds too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants crowd each other out and fight for soil food and water. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to develop thick stems and full yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni adu lɛ buaa amɛhe naa ni amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tso ni mli tse ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants full of holes and looking chewed up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai eyi kɛ bu ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛye amɛhe lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which crawl into the growing tip of the plant to feed on fresh leaves. Early scouting and applying recommended biopesticides or neem extracts can protect your crop before the yield is ruined.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ ashishi koni amɛye baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ atao ni akɛtsu nii mra. Ebaanyɛ ebu onibii ahe dani efite.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow and curling up instead of growing big and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ agbo kɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves in cassava are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural officers is the best way to keep your plants healthy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi eto amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahaa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves get a white powdery coating on them and fall off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni akɛ powda yɛŋ ehà mi-pepper baai lɛ ahe ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: This white coating is a fungal disease called powdery mildew, which spreads in hot and humid weather when plants are crowded together. Giving your plants proper space so air can flow around them helps prevent the fungus from taking over.
ga: Nɛkɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Egbɛɔ eshwaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛ́ tsei ebua amɛhe naa babaoo. He ni sa ni ahaa tsei lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ abɔle amɛhe. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ akaye nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava planted alongside them to block the harsh heat and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Enɛ ji koni abu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall with many leaves, but produce small fruits and thin tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ waa ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ? Shi ehaa aduawai bibii kɛ yitsei bibii?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and lacks phosphorus and potassium. Nitrogen makes plants grow tall green leaves, but plants need balanced nutrients like phosphorus and potassium to build strong tubers and large fruits.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ sũ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ fa tsɔ, ni fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium bɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei lɛ baa eŋɔli ni nɔ kwɔ. Shi tsofai ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium he miihia tsei koni amɛfee bulbs ni mli wa kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why does the top layer of soil on my farm wash away every time a heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: When soil is left bare without roots or cover, heavy rain easily washes away the fertile topsoil. Covering your soil with dry grass (mulch) or planting cover crops helps protect the soil surface from heavy raindrops.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shishifãi loo nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ nɔ lɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ oya. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi (Mulching) loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize when the early rains keep starting and stopping?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛ be ni ekpaa lɛ?

english: Planting too early during false rains can cause your seeds to dry up in the soil. It is safest to wait until the ground has received two or three heavy, steady rains that soak deep into the soil before sowing your seeds.
ga: Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ amale be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii 2-3 ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ dani oduɔ dumɔwui.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and yellow even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa fiofio ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli po lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer away from your crops. Clearing weeds early in the growth season ensures that your crops get all the nutrients you put into the soil.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ miida lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my ripe tomatoes turn dark and soft at the bottom while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifee la yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant absorb calcium properly to build strong fruit walls.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛma aduawai gbogboi ni wa.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting or sprouting so quickly in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ loo shweremɔ oya yɛ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot or sprout quickly if they are kept in a hot, dark place without fresh air, or if they were cut during harvest. Storing undamaged yams in a cool, well-ventilated raised barn helps them stay fresh much longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. aloo kɛji akɛ afo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli Sweet potatoes ni efiteee lɛ ni akɛtoɔ shĩa ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni amɛhi shi ehee be babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the essential food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help them regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ nitrogen tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil seem to yield better crops after I harvest groundnuts or cowpeas from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai beni mikpa ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the ground, naturally enriching the soil for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that dry out easily under direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting plantains around them creates shade and preserves soil moisture so the seedlings can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. ejieɔ tsei kakadaji loo dumɔwui ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi koni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over so easily when strong winds blow during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that stay near the surface, making them top-heavy when carrying full fruit bunches. Propping up the stalks with strong wooden poles helps support the weight against wind.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa tsɔne lɛ tsiimɔ babaoo baa kɛ́ etere aduawai akuu ko. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni wa fĩ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ muji lɛ afi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with small caterpillars hidden in the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛtee baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a moth caterpillar that feeds on the soft growth inside the plant stem. Spraying early with appropriate organic or chemical controls kills them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni yeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni sa shwie amɛnɔ mra lɛ, ebaagbe amɛ dani amɛbaafite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or transmitting a virus. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaf twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, thrips, loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Why do my cassava roots start soft-rotting inside the soil before I can dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ mafo amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for long periods without proper drainage. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɛ Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their yellow flowers before any small tomatoes start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani tomato bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience severe stress, such as intense heat or irregular watering during flowering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa kpe, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall but only produce small, poorly filled ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ daa shi ewoɔ toi bibii ni yɔɔ kuku pɛ lɛ?

english: Maize plants put out tall growth first, but if they face drought or lack nutrients during pollination, the ears cannot develop full kernels, leading to small or empty cobs.
ga: Abele tsei daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ klɛŋklɛŋ. Shi kɛji akɛ ekɛ hɔmɔ kpe loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ yɛ pollination be mli lɛ Toi lɛ nyɛŋ afee nɔ ni dumɔwui eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Lifting yam vines on wooden stakes allows leaves to catch maximum sunlight for tuber growth while keeping leaves away from damp soil diseases that spread quickly on the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni tuber lɛ akwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I dig out tree stumps and old roots from my land before planting new crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei akutsei kɛ shishifãi momoi kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu tsei heei?

english: Old roots and tree stumps hidden in the soil act as homes for pests like termites and diseases like root rot. Removing them completely cleans the soil so your new crop roots can grow freely without getting infected.
ga: Shishifãi momoi kɛ tsei akutsei ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ko ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai tamɔ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atse. Enɛ baaha otso hee lɛ shishifãi lɛ ada ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko akabote mli.

english: The very first rain in Ghana is often followed by a heat spell before the rainy season fully sets in. Sowing too early causes seeds to sprout and then wither away in the dry, hot soil before the next rain comes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ nyiɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for leaf growth. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure restores green leaf health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baabii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: When maize is planted too close, the leaves block sunlight from each other and the roots fight for the same soil food and water. This competition results in tall, thin stalks with very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. ni shishifãi baatswa niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ tsei bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without forming into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree suffers from extreme sun heat, lack of soil moisture, or damage from insects like mirids. Maintaining shade trees and protecting the flowers from bugs allows them to develop into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ye tso lɛ nɔ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi tamɔ pollen efiteɔ Tsei lɛ ni akɛ amɛ woɔ hulutsoo mli ni abuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground if I leave them past harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Once cassava tubers fully mature, the plant stops protecting them from soil organisms. Leaving them in wet soil past maturity allows fungi and bacteria to enter the tubers and cause soft rot.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ kpaɔ ehebuu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ abote ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛha amɛgboi.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young corn plants right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid on leaves by moths during warm periods. The rain encourages fresh growth in the central leaf funnel, which attracts the worms to feed on the tender leaves.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii kɛwoɔ baai anɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ woɔ dalɛ hee he hewalɛ yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli. ni gbalaa ŋmeii koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ

english: This black soft spot is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit during growth, often triggered by uneven soil watering. Regular, consistent watering helps the plant carry calcium to the fruit tops.
ga: Nɛkɛ he diŋŋ nɛɛ miifite yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ naa. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa, daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ calcium baa tso lɛ yibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I dump fertilizer directly against the stem of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts that burn the tender plant stem and root crown on direct contact. Placing it in a small ring a few inches away from the stem allows roots to absorb it safely.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ shãa tsei bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛwo ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko mli lɛ, inchi fioo ko pɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does clearing weeds late in the season fail to bring my stunted crops back to full yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ haaa mi tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛba nitsumɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal most of the soil nutrients and water during the first few weeks when young crops establish their root systems. Removing weeds late cannot undo the early growth damage the crop already suffered.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli niyenii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli beni dumɔwui lɛ toɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ ni akɛbaagbe naa lɛ nyɛŋ ajie nɔ ni jɛ mra be mli dalɛ mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efite momo lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact time to start planting my maize when the rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Wait until the rains become steady—usually after two or three deep rains that wet the ground well—rather than planting after the very first light shower, so your seeds do not dry up in the hot soil.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be—bei pii lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũuɔ lɛ sɛɛ—shi moŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Afeɔ enɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi yɛ sũ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Is it better for me to plant pepper seeds directly in my main farm or start them in a nursery first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu pepper dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo mabɔi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Pepper seeds are very small and fragile. Starting them in a shaded nursery bed lets you water and protect them easily, so you can transplant only the strongest seedlings to your main farm.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ daraaa kwraa ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛ́ oje tsei shishi yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo akɛ oooha amɛ nu ni obu amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ aya oŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants are hungry for nitrogen (a vital soil nutrient) or that water is trapped in the soil. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. (nibii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli) loo nu ni ekã sũ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when the plant lacks nutrients. Covering the soil with dried grass (mulch) and watering regularly keeps the plants cool and protects the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (Mulch) shwieɔ nɔ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight because their tender leaves burn easily. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains beside them creates a cool shelter that keeps them alive during their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kookoo tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ ashi tsei yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo adu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa he ko ni mli ejɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: How far apart should I space my cassava sticks so I can harvest big tubers?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo mi-cassava tsei lɛ ateŋ bɔni afee ni manyɛ makpa ŋmeii wuji?

english: If cassava sticks are planted too close together, their roots fight for plant food and stay small. Leaving about one meter of space between each plant gives the tubers room to expand and grow thick.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni jɛ tsei amli lɛ he akaŋ ni amɛji bibii. Tsɔɔmɔ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ aaafee mita kome koni bulbs lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same piece of land every year give me a smaller harvest each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ haa yibiiwoo fioo baa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop diseases build up. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpea or groundnut puts goodness back into the land.
ga: Nibii komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ daa lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be mli, ni ehaa tsei ahe helai buaa amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake o-corn lɛ. lɛ kɛ ekpakpafeemɔ baaba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ

english: Cassava roots rot when heavy rainwater sits around them for too long without draining. Planting your cassava stems on raised mounds or ridges allows water to flow away easily, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔɔɔ Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains and winds just when the bunches are getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli beni jwɛi lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches along with broad leaves that catch the wind like a sail. Supporting the main stem with a strong bamboo fork or pole helps hold the weight through storms.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ tamɔ ŋshɔ hiɛ lɛlɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ fɔk loo ŋmei tso ni wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni etsɔ ahum lɛ mli.

english: Why does my harvested maize get destroyed by small insects while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii kpata mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ hiɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize gets eaten by insects in storage when it is put away before drying completely. Thoroughly drying your harvested maize under the sun until the grains are hard makes it difficult for insects and mold to survive.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ ŋmãa kɛji akɛ akɛto dani egbi kwraa. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu shishi kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa lɛ, ehaa ewaa ahaa kooloi kɛ ŋmeii akɛ amɛaahi shi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sun. They need shade crops like plantains or bananas to shield them and keep the soil moist during their early years.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantain loo banana he miihia amɛ. Koni abu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni eha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I pinch off the first set of flowers on my young pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ fɔfɔi klɛŋklɛŋ ni yɔɔ mi-baby pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Removing the earliest flowers encourages the plant to direct its energy into growing stronger roots and branches first, which leads to a bigger overall harvest later.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ fɔfɔi ni jeɔ shishi mra lɛ, ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛ shishifãi kɛ niji ni mli wa lɛ akwɛ̃ klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ fɛɛ ni da baa sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take a long time to sprout after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers require reliable soil moisture to break dormancy and sprout. Planting them right at the start of the rainy season triggers faster root growth.
ga: Plantain suckers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni amɛfo ŋmɛlɛtswaa kɛ shweremɔ mli. Kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ adara oya.

english: What causes my small maize leaves to turn purple or reddish?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Minɔ lɛ batsɔ purple loo etsuru.

english: Purple leaves usually mean the young maize plant is short on phosphorus in the soil, an essential nutrient needed to develop strong, deep roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni ji purple lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni shishifãi ni mli wa ni mli kwɔ lɛ aya hiɛ

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl inward tightly during the hottest time of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes curl their leaves in intense heat to reduce surface area and save water loss; they usually recover and uncurl once the afternoon cools down.
ga: Akɛ la ni naa wa shwieɔ tomato baai anɔ koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni nu akafite. Bei pii lɛ, etsaa ni egbɔjɔɔ be mli ni shwane lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow many green leaves but yield very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cowpeas focus all their growth on leaves instead of setting flowers and producing bean pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa edalɛ nɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii ni ekɛ bean pods baa lɛ
