english: Why do my crops get covered in a dusty white layer during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sũ yɛŋ haa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: That white powder is a fungal disease known as powdery mildew, which develops easily in warm weather when air cannot move freely around overcrowded plants.
ga: Pauda yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Enɛ baa mli mlɛo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ aya he fɛɛ he lɛ Tsei lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ mɛi tsɔ.

english: Why is it harmful if I plant my cassava too close to my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛji midu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for the same sunlight, ground nutrients, and water, causing both crops to grow weak and yield less.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaatswa amɛhe akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ nu ni falɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Yams are climbing plants that need stakes to lift their leaves up toward sunlight and keep them off damp soil, preventing leaf diseases from spreading.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ waa koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Koni baa helai akagbɛ ashwã

english: How do I know when my cassava is fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready when lower leaves begin turning yellow and dropping, the main stem turns woody, and the ground around the base begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Tso titri lɛ tsakeɔ efeɔ tso. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why are agricultural officers telling me not to let my harvested crops touch the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ mikaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ miishɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Ground contact exposes harvested crops to soil moisture, fungal spores, and bacteria, which cause rapid rotting and mold growth. Raising produce on clean tarpaulins or wooden racks keeps it dry, clean, and safe for market or consumption.
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko ta shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa tsei ni akpa lɛ naa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Fungal spores kɛ bacteria, ni kɛ fitemɔ oya kɛ fungal dalɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ tarpaulins ni he tse loo tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ anɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nibii ni aduɔ lɛ agbiɔ, ehe tseɔ ni ehiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛha jarayeli loo niyeli.

english: How can I stop my harvested yams and vegetables from spoiling quickly after harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potatoes kɛ aduawai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Vegetables and root crops spoil fast if they get bruised during harvest or are kept in hot, humid places. Handle your produce gently to avoid cuts, and store them off the ground in cool, shaded, well-ventilated areas.
ga: Aduawai kɛ ŋmeii fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo akɛto hei ni edɔɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Okɛ aduawai kɛ aduawai atsu nii blɛoo koni akafo bo. ni okɛto shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ.

english: Why do birds and rodents keep eating my crops when I spread them outside to dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi kɛ ŋmeii yaa nɔ amɛyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mikɛwoɔ kpo nɔ koni amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Grains and produce spread out openly in the sun are easy food sources for wild animals. Using raised drying racks covered with fine mesh netting allows sunshine and air to dry your crops while keeping pests out.
ga: Ŋmãa kɛ nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ mli ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hulu lɛ mli lɛ ji niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha koo mli kooloi. Kɛ́ okɛ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi ni akɛ ŋshɔŋlooi kpakpai ehà nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbiɔ yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why do tiny insects keep destroying the maize and beans I store inside my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛfiteɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni mikɛtoɔ mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Storage pests like weevils often come from eggs laid on crops before harvest, or they crawl into open bags. Storing thoroughly dried grains in airtight hermetic bags suffocates these insects without needing harmful chemicals.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe, tamɔ ŋmeii, jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani akpaa lɛ mli. Aloo okɛ ohe awo kotoku ko ni agbele mli mli. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ wo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ agbɔjɔ ni akɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui tsuuu nii.

english: Why do insects chew on the leaves of my crops before attacking the rest of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai dani amɛtutuaa tso lɛ fãi krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Leaves are soft, easy to chew, and full of nutrients that young insects need to grow quickly. Once the leaves are damaged or completely eaten, hungry pests move on to attack stems, stalks, and fruits.
ga: Baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe ŋmɔmɔ waaa, ni niyenii ni he hiaa kooloi bibii koni amɛdara oya lɛ eyi mli obɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ fite loo aye amɛ kwraa lɛ Hɔmɔ he kooloi lɛ boteɔ mli ni amɛtutuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi, tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ aduawai lɛ.

english: If insects eat all the leaves off my cassava or maize, will the crop still grow food under the ground or on the stalk?
ga: Kɛji kooloi bibii lɛ ye mi-cassava loo ŋmãa baai lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, Ani tsei baanyɛ akwɛ niyenii lolo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo yɛ tsei anɔ?

english: Leaves act like food factories that use sunlight to feed the plant. If insects destroy the leaves, the plant starves and cannot produce big cassava roots or healthy maize ears.
ga: Baai tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii afeemɔ he, ni amɛkɛ hulu la haa tso lɛ niyenii. Kɛji kooloi fite baai lɛ Tso lɛ hɔmɔ baaye lɛ ni enyɛŋ ekɛ ŋmei shishifãi wuji loo ŋmei toi ni wa aba.

english: What causes pests to bore holes and eat straight into the main body or stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tswaa bu ni amɛyeɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛboteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbɔmɔtso titri loo amɛshishifã lɛ mli?

english: Stem-boring pests hide inside the plant's body to protect themselves from heat, rain, and predators while feeding on internal sap. This cuts off water and nutrient flow, causing the plant to weaken or break.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ, nugbɔ, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe, yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ kɛjɛɔ emli lɛ. Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii lɛ hoɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ loo egbɔjɔɔ.

english: How can I tell if a strange new problem on my farm is caused by a disease rather than insects?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ naagba ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ yɛ? Ani helai yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe kooloi bibii?

english: Insects usually leave visible bite marks, holes, or bugs on the crop. Diseases often cause strange symptoms like leaf discoloration, spots, sudden wilting, or rotting without any visible insects present.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, bu loo kooloi ŋmɔji yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, helai kɛ okadii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ tamɔ baai ni tsakeɔ amɛhe su, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi trukaa baa. loo fitemɔ ni kooloi bibii ni anaaa bɛ mli

english: Why does a plant disease start on just one crop and then quickly spread across my whole farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso hela jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli ni no sɛɛ lɛ egbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya lɛ?

english: Plant diseases are caused by microscopic germs like fungi or bacteria. These tiny germs travel quickly through rain splashes, wind, crawling insects, or dirty farming tools from sick plants to healthy ones.
ga: Helai bibii tamɔ fungi loo muawai kɛ tsei helai baa. tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii Enɛɛmɛi tsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi, kɔɔyɔɔ, kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ shi loo okwaayeli nibii ni he tseee amli oya kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: If my crops get sick with a new disease, can I leave the rotten leaves on the farm to turn into manure?
ga: Kɛji hela hee ko mɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mashɛrɛ baai ni egboi lɛ mashwie. Ani abaanyɛ akɛto ŋmɔ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: No, leaves and crops affected by disease carry living germs that survive in the soil and will infect your next crop. You should carefully clear diseased plant parts away from the farm and burn or deeply bury them.
ga: Dabi, baai kɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ baawo hela lɛ mli wala yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛbaagbɛ hela lɛ amɛshwã oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli. Esa akɛ ojie fãi komɛi kɛjɛ mli. Kwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ akabɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he. No sɛɛ lɛ, shã loo ofu lɛ shɔŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense direct sunlight and heat. Leaving some big trees or planting shade crops like plantains gives them living umbrellas that protect their leaves from sun damage and keep the soil moist while their roots grow strong.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ oshi tsei wuji komɛi loo odu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi. Bɔni afee ni abu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli wa lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of the plant usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a major food crops need to grow green and strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore their health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Curled leaves with yellow patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that suck the plant's sap. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems is the best way to keep your harvest safe from this problem.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Whiteflies bibii ni nuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha onibii akafee shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ naagba nɛɛ he.

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which means they can pull free nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them with maize naturally feeds the soil and helps your maize grow bigger without relying only on bought fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli abele duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa o-abele lɛ ni edara ni okɛ ohe fɔ̃ɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ahe lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience too much stress, such as very high heat, lack of water, or poor nutrients in the soil. Keeping the soil moist around the root area and adding compost helps the flowers stay on the plant to produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛyɛ haomɔi babaoo mli, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha ebɔle Shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do I need to build mounds or ridges before planting yam instead of just putting them in flat soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ dani adu sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow underground and need soft, loose soil to expand into long, thick roots. Mounds and ridges break up hard ground, allowing the yams to grow easily while improving water drainage so the tubers do not rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehe miihia ni amɛná shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni shwieɔ shi koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ shishifãi kakadaji ni mli tse. Gɔji kɛ ŋshɔkei lɛ gbáa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli. Ha sweet potatoes lɛ akwɛmɔ afee mlɛo Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ koni tubers lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my vegetable crops dry up so fast when the Harmattan wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ bɔi tswaa lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind sucks moisture out of both plant leaves and the soil much faster than normal air. Covering the soil around your vegetables with dried grass or leaves helps trap moisture in the ground for much longer.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ shikpɔŋ fɛɛ mli oya fe kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ daa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi shwie shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle o-vegetables lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Planting seeds too close causes the crops to fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin plants with very small corn cobs. Giving each plant proper space ensures every single stalk gets enough nutrients to produce large, full cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei komɛi yɛ ŋmãa bibii waa. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why does leaving dry grass and plant leaves on top of my soil help my crops during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ tsei ahe baai ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves over your farmland acts like a blanket that blocks direct sunlight from drying out the earth. It keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni ooogbɛ ashwã he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and heavy tops, especially when carrying a heavy bunch of fruit. Heap extra soil around the base of the plant and support the main stem with strong wooden poles to keep them standing through storms.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ ootere aduawai ni tsii. Okɛ muji krokomɛi abɔle he. Akɛ tsei ni wa fĩɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ etso titri lɛ sɛɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ adamɔ ahum naa.

english: How do bright yellow and white sticky boards help protect my vegetable crops from small insects?
ga: Te ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ buɔ mi-aduawai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ahe amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Many flying pests, like whiteflies and aphids, are naturally attracted to bright colors like yellow and white. When you place sticky boards of these colors in your field, insects fly straight to them and get trapped, helping you monitor and control pests before they destroy your farm.
ga: Nɔ ni fata kooloi ni yɔɔ fɛ̃i babaoo ahe ji ŋmeii yɛŋ kɛ ŋmeii. Amɛsumɔɔ sui ni mli tse tamɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ eyɛŋ. Kɛ okɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kɔla ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ he nɛɛ wo oyale mli lɛ, ŋmeii baafo kɛba amɛŋɔɔ ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmeii. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni oyɔseɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ dani amɛfiteɔ oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why are insect pests attacking my crops more during the dry season than in the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Insects thrive in warm, dry weather because it speeds up their breeding cycle. Also, during dry periods, crops are under water stress and become weaker, making it easier for pests to feed on them.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli ejaakɛ ehaa amɛbotemɔ be lɛ yaa oya. Kɛfata he lɛ, yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Nibii ni Aduɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ nu he haomɔ shishi ni ebaagbɔjɔ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or when heavy rains wash nutrients away. It can also happen when weeds steal food away from your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fite. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji jwɛi ju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very big green leaves but produce tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves instead of tubers if the soil has too much nitrogen or if the soil is packed too tightly for the roots to expand.
ga: Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ebaa ni miida lɛ mli yɛ ŋmeii lɛ najiaŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily in full sun. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains nearby creates shade and traps moisture, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Pepper leaves curl during hot hours to reduce water loss from evaporation. It is the plant's natural defense against heat, but if leaves stay curled in the morning, it means the plant needs water or has insect damage.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ hebuu. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle ehe leebi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia tso lɛ loo kooloi bibii efite lɛ.

english: Why are my maize plants growing tall and thin with very small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving every plant proper spacing ensures stems grow thick enough to support large cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua tsei wuji lɛ.

english: Why do some of my planted seeds fail to pop out of the soil even after a good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are buried too deep, if the soil stays waterlogged and rots them, or if ants and soil insects consume them before they sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ tsɔ. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni egbo Aloo kɛji ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ye lɛ dani ekwɛ̃.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Consistent watering and mulching around the roots help keep the flowers on the plant.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe daa kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my watermelon fruits split open on the farm right before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miitswa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Watermelons crack open when sudden heavy rain follows a long dry period. The inside of the fruit absorbs water quickly and grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing it to burst.
ga: Watermelons tswaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amligbɛ lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni edaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ ehe. kɛ mligbalamɔ baa

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains nearby to act like natural umbrellas, keeping the air humid and protecting the tender leaves until the young trees grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i ni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi tsei bibii lɛ baadara waa.

english: During harmattan, the air becomes extremely dry. Cocoa trees drop their leaves naturally to reduce water loss through evaporation, which helps the tree conserve moisture and survive until the next rainy season.
ga: harmattan teŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baagbi waa. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects like midges to transfer pollen between them before pods can grow. If the weather is too dry or there are no pollinating insects around, the unpollinated flowers simply fall off.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, koni amɛkɛ pollen lɛ aya amɛteŋ dani ŋmeii lɛ afee. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kooloi ni feɔ pollin lɛ bɛ. Fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ pollen lɛ baagbee shi.

english: Why does cutting off excess branches from my cocoa trees help them produce more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe niji krokomɛi ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and air can reach all parts of the stem. It also prevents the tree from wasting energy on extra leaves, directing that energy into growing healthy pods instead.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Etsiɔ tso lɛ hu naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ jamɛ a he wami ɔ kɛ peeɔ pod nɛ he wa.

english: Why do green cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains and high humidity encourage a fungus that causes Black Pod disease. Rainwater splashes the fungus spores from the soil onto the low-hanging pods, causing them to rot rapidly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛ ŋmei ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa. Nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛfiteɔ oya.

english: Why do old cocoa trees produce far fewer pods than when they were young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo fe be mli ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow older, they exhaust the nutrients in the soil. Without added nutrients or organic compost, the soil can no longer supply the energy the trees need to continuously produce high pod yields.
ga: Kɛji kookoo tso lɛ da lɛ Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaho aya. Kɛji akɛ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛŋ aha hewalɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛwo yibii ni fa babaoo be fɛɛ be lɛ aha dɔŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with lots of leaves but yields only tiny underground tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii pɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is overly wet, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing big leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the roots underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are mature enough to dig up without ruining the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa ni mifiteee ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting, when the lower stem leaves begin to turn yellow and drop naturally, signaling that the plant has stopped feeding the tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji be mli ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii hamɔ.

english: Can I plant cassava right next to my young cocoa trees without harming them?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ kookoo tsei ahe ni miyeee amɛ awui?

english: Cassava can be planted on the same farm, but it shouldn't be placed too close to young cocoa trees. Cassava roots grow rapidly and aggressively, competing with young cocoa for soil nutrients and water.
ga: Abaanyɛ adu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli. Shi esaaa akɛ akɛtoɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe tsɔ. Cassava shishifãi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa. Ekɛ kookoo bibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ.

english: Why does cassava start to turn dark blue and spoil just two days after I harvest it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei lɛ jeɔ shishi etsɔɔ bluu ni mli edɔ ni egboɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ?

english: Once cassava is dug out of the soil, exposure to oxygen causes rapid chemical changes that ruin the root. Processing it quickly into gari or flour, or keeping it buried in moist soil, prevents rapid spoilage.
ga: Beni ajieɔ ŋmei kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Oxygen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛ tsofa tsakemɔi ni baa oya ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ baa. Akɛ oyaiyeli tsuɔ he nii ni akɛfeɔ gari loo ashikishaŋ. loo afu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ nibii ni efiteɔ oya lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot every year during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ daa afi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This rot is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, damp conditions. Raindrops bounce off infected soil or pods, spreading the fungus to healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. Egbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ eshwaa kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: If one of my cocoa trees gets sick, can the disease spread to healthy trees nearby?
ga: Kɛji hela mɔ kookoo tsei lɛ eko Ani hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, crop diseases spread easily through wind, rain splashes, shared harvesting tools, or insects. Leaving a sick tree untouched allows spores to travel and infect neighboring healthy cocoa trees.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, nibii ni akɛkpaa nii ni akɛhaa, loo kooloi bibii anɔ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etaaa he lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ fãa gbɛ ni amɛyeɔ cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why am I being advised to cut down cocoa trees that have swollen stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ awo mi ŋaa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tsei ni amɛshishifãi lɛ efu lɛ?

english: Swollen stems are a clear sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease. Because there is no chemical cure for this virus, cutting down the infected tree is the only way to stop it from spreading and destroying your entire farm.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni efuu lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo bud virus hela lɛ eba. Enɛ ji akɛ tsofa ko bɛ ni abaanyɛ atsa hela nɛɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ okpa amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛkafite oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are suffering from a pest attack or a fungal disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai emɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ amli?

english: Fungal diseases usually cause soft rots, black spots, or moldy growth on pods. Pest attacks, like capsids or bugs, usually leave visible bite marks, hard brown scars, or deformed pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ aduawai ni fiteɔ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsuɔ diŋ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ lɛ baa. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids loo kooloi bibii tutuaa mɔ. Bei pii lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmɔlɔ he okadii ni anaa. ŋmeii ni wa ni tsuɔ loo ŋmeii ni efite

english: Can I still harvest and use cocoa pods that show small spots of disease on the outside?
ga: Minyɛɔ mikpaa kookoo ŋmeii ni helai bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ hu ni mikɛtsu nii. Ani ebaanyɛ efee kponɔgbɛ?

english: If the rot is only on the outer husk and has not reached the beans inside, you can harvest and dry those beans. However, heavily rotted pods ruin bean quality and must be thrown away far from healthy trees.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ pɛ egbo ni jeee mligbɛ dumɔwui lɛ. Obaanyɛ okpa ŋmeii lɛ ni ogbi amɛ, bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni fee lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbo waa lɛ baafite ŋmeii lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ. ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe

english: Cocoa pods are ready when their color changes completely—usually turning bright yellow or orange depending on the variety. Harvesting pods while green yields small, low-quality beans, while leaving them too long causes beans to germinate inside.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ amɛhe su tsake kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, ebafeɔ ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ be mli ni amɛji ŋmɔji lɛ, no haa anáa kɔfi ŋmeii bibii ni ehiii kwraa. Kɛ́ oshi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mli.

english: Does leaving rotten cocoa pods hanging on the trees affect my next harvest?
ga: Ani kookoo ŋmeii ni egbo ni mashiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ saa mikpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ he?

english: Yes, leaving diseased pods on the tree allows the infection to dry into 'mummies' that hold disease spores. When the next rains come, those spores drop onto young pods and ruin your next harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ agbi ni etsɔ ‘mummy’ ni hela lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ yɔɔ mli. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ be kroko Nakai ŋmeii lɛ baagbee ŋmeii bibii anɔ ni amɛbaafite oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does leaving bushy weeds under my cocoa trees make disease worse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ kookoo tsei ashishi lɛ haa hela lɛ mli woɔ wu lɛ?

english: Tall weeds trap moisture and cool air under the crop canopy. This wet, humid environment makes it very easy for fungal diseases to multiply and attack lower cocoa pods.
ga: Jwɛi kakadaji lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi. Shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ haa efeɔ mlɛo waa akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli baa lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛtutua kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my old cocoa trees produce fewer pods now than when I first planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso momo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo fe beni midu lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Over many years, cocoa trees extract nutrients from the soil to grow pods. Without feeding the soil with fertilizer or organic manure, the ground becomes tired and cannot support high pod yields.
ga: Yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛfee ŋmeii. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo humus wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ eye ebua pod yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo.

english: Should I cut down a diseased cocoa tree immediately or wait to discuss it with the landowner first?
ga: Ani esa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo amɛ ni akɛ shikpɔŋtsɛ lɛ agba sane klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: It is best to inform the landowner right away about the disease so you both agree to cut the tree quickly. Waiting too long allows the disease to spread, reducing the overall harvest and crop value for both of you.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha shikpɔŋtsɛ lɛ ale hela lɛ he sane amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni nyɛyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ nyɛkpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ nyɛbaafo tso lɛ oya. Kɛ́ omɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi kɛhaa nyɛyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do so many cocoa farmers in Ghana plant plantains in their fields at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ duɔ plantains yɛ amɛŋmɔji amli yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that shade young cocoa seedlings from harsh sunlight, while also giving farmers food and income while waiting for cocoa to mature.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ahaa okwaafoi lɛ niyenii kɛ shika be mli ni amɛmiimɛ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Will planting too many plantains in my farm hurt the growth of my main crops?
ga: Ani plantains babaoo ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafite miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ adalɛ?

english: If plantains are planted too close together, they will compete with main crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, so proper spacing is essential.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dare ni okɛ tsei titrii lɛ abɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, he ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni sa lɛ he miihia.

english: Is it better for me to focus only on growing plantains instead of mixing them with other crops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ baama plantains pɛ dumɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ tsei krokomɛi baafutu?

english: Focusing solely on plantains gives fast returns, but mixing crops reduces market risks and allows plantains to serve as companion shade plants for long-term crops like cocoa.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ma plantains pɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaawo yibii oya. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ haa jarayeli he oshara baa shi. ni ehaa plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo tsei kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain plants turning yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during dry spells usually show that the plant is stressed from a lack of water and soil nutrients like nitrogen, which can be improved by mulching around the base.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao yɛ nu kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ, ni abaanyɛ aha eya hiɛ kɛtsɔ sũ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when there is heavy wind or rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and heavy fruit bunches, which makes them top-heavy and easy to blow over unless supported with wooden or bamboo props.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. ni haa efeɔ nɔ ni tsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ atswa oya, ja tso loo ŋmeii fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Why do I see so many small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe. Mi plantain shishitoo titri lɛ

english: Plantains produce natural offshoots called suckers to reproduce, but leaving too many will steal energy from the main stalk and reduce fruit size.
ga: Plantains lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii koni amɛfɔ bii. Shi ŋmeii babaoo ni ajieɔ lɛ juɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli ni ehaa aduawai lɛ ayibɔ baa shi.

english: Should I cut off the extra small plantain shoots growing near the main plant?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ banana tsei bibii krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Yes, pruning excess shoots (desuckering) and leaving only 2 or 3 healthy stems allows the main plant to direct its nutrients toward making large fruit bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi (ni atseɔ tsei lɛ amli) ni ashiɔ tsei 2 loo 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ haa tso titri lɛ heɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni efeɔ aduawai akui wuji.

english: How long does a plantain stalk take from planting until I can harvest the fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani akpaa plantain tsei lɛ?

english: A plantain plant usually takes between 11 to 15 months to produce a mature bunch ready for harvest, depending on rainfall and soil fertility.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ dumɔwui lɛ nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 15 dani amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni esa akɛ akpa. Edamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ falɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: What causes my plantain bunches to remain very small even when the tree looks green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni haa mi plantain tsei lɛ feɔ bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: Small bunches are usually caused by a lack of potassium in the soil or having too many suckers attached to the main stem drawing nutrients away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ baa ji potassium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo suckers babaoo ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he tsɔ ni nyɛŋ agbala niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ.

english: How can I stop diseases from spreading quickly through my plantain farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa oya yɛ mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can prevent disease spread by planting clean, healthy suckers, clearing away dead leaves regularly, and giving plants enough space so air can flow freely.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsi hela naa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ baai ni egboi lɛ daa. Ni oha tsei lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are dying from a disease or just suffering from lack of water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela miigbe miŋmɔshi nibii loo nu ni miiho kɛkɛ?

english: Diseases usually cause specific signs like dark spots, yellow patches, or rotting on leaves and stems, whereas dry crops will simply wilt evenly across the whole plant during the hot part of the day.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ kɛ okadii pɔtɛɛ komɛi tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ baa baai kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ. Beni tso lɛ miigbi lɛ, ebaagbo yɛ gbi lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops suddenly catch diseases even when I buy good seeds from the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe hela trukaa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mihe dumɔwui kpakpai kɛjɛ jara nɔ moŋ?

english: Even healthy seeds can contract diseases from the surrounding environment because fungal spores, bacteria, and viruses travel through wind, infected soil, shared tools, or insects from neighboring farms.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ po baanyɛ aná helai ni jɛɔ shihilɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, muawai, kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ mli Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo kooloi ni jɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ mlijaa

english: Is it safe for me to plant the same crop in my field right after a disease destroyed my previous harvest?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni hela kpata mitsutsu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ lɛ?

english: No, because disease organisms can survive in the soil for months. Planting a different type of crop starves the remaining germs and cleans the soil naturally.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ helai ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo. Tsei srɔtoi ni aduɔ Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye helatsɛmɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsuu yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do insects on my farm seem to make crop diseases spread much faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ?

english: Insects act like transportation for germs; when they feed on a sick plant and move to a healthy one, they carry bacteria and viruses directly into the healthy plant's sap.
ga: Kplukai tsuɔ nii akɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ. Enɛ ji be mli ni amɛyeɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ ni amɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Amɛwoɔ helatsɛmɛi kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli nu lɛ mli.

english: What usually causes a whole field of crops to fail all at once?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔ muu fɛɛ fiteɔ shikome?

english: Sudden total crop failure is typically caused by fast-spreading fungal or viral outbreaks, sudden dry spells right after planting, or severe pest invasions destroying root systems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei loo hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ trukaa baa. Hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni baa trukaa yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni naa wa ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: How can I protect my farm business from losing everything if a major crop disease strikes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ he koni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ akafite kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hela ni naa wa ba?

english: You can protect your investment by planting disease-resistant seed varieties, growing two or three different types of crops instead of just one, and practicing crop rotation.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oshika ni okɛwo mli lɛ he kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ tsei srɔtoi enyɔ loo etɛ moŋ fe ekome pɛ. ni akase ŋmɔshi nibii ahe tsakemɔ

english: What fast-growing crops can I plant to quickly get income if my main crop fails?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ madu koni maná shika oya kɛji miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ ehiii?

english: Short-duration crops like cowpeas, maize, or vegetables like okra and tomatoes mature within two to three months, allowing you to harvest quickly and recover lost funds.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ tsina ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo aduawai tamɔ okra kɛ tomatoi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okpaa shika ni elaaje lɛ oya ni oná ekoŋŋ.

english: If my young crops get damaged by disease in their first month, can they recover or must I clear the field?
ga: Kɛji hela fite mi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ani amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsa loo ehe baahia ni ajie ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: If the roots or main stems are rotten, the plants will not recover and should be removed. However, if only outer leaves are affected, proper treatment and fertilizers can help them bounce back.
ga: Kɛji shishifãi loo tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ egbo lɛ Tso lɛ he ejɔɔɔ lɛ ni esa akɛ ajie, shi kɛlɛ, kɛji akɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ pɛ efite. Tsamɔ ni sa kɛ fɔmɔ nii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛba bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ tsutsu lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Can poor soil quality cause my crops to catch diseases more easily?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ baaha helai aba miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ oya?

english: Yes, plants growing in weak soil lack essential nutrients, making their immune systems weak and leaving them far less able to fight off diseases and pests.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa. Ehaa amɛgbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nii ni gbeɔ muawai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hu.

english: Why do my crop plants stay green and leafy but fail to produce any food or seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji eŋɔli ni eyɛ baai shi ewooo niyenii loo dumɔwui lɛ?

english: This happens when plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces them to grow leaves instead of flowers, or when severe heat stress prevents flowers from turning into fruits.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. aloo be mli ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa tsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkatsɔ aduawai.

english: Yellow leaves usually show that your maize is missing nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build leaves and grow tall. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the soil or leaves the roots waterlogged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai ni amɛdara. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo eha shishifãi lɛ amli eyi kɛ nu.

english: You must dry your maize kernels completely until they are hard before storage. Storing them in airtight hermetic bags (like PICS bags) starves pests of oxygen so insects cannot survive or destroy your grain.
ga: Esa akɛ ogbi o-corn ŋmeii lɛ kwraa kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani okɛto. Kɛ́ akɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku) mli lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye tsɛŋemɔ hela ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kooloi bibii lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi loo amɛfite odumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why does my soil dry out so fast even after a good rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil loses water quickly when it lacks organic matter like compost or animal manure, or when it is left bare under direct sunlight. Adding dry leaves or straw as mulch over the soil helps hold moisture in the ground much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛji akɛ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii. aloo kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it better to plant my maize in straight rows instead of scattering seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni ja mli moŋ fe ni aaagbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in rows ensures every plant gets equal access to sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with its neighbors. It also makes weeding and applying fertilizer much easier for you.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hu feɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts on the same plot where I harvested maize last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ mli nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which naturally takes nitrogen from the air and puts it back into the soil. Planting them restores soil fertility for heavy-feeding crops like maize in the next season.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nibii nɛɛ adumɔ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on young maize leaves and cobs. Early scouting of your farm allows you to catch them early and control them using recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract sprays.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fɔɔ baa ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmãa bibii. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ omɔ amɛ mra. ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii loo neem mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ atsu nii kɛkudɔ amɛ.

english: What causes my cassava leaves to twist up and turn yellow in spots?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnáa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties is the best way to keep your farm healthy.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. ni ŋmei bibioo lɛ ji nɔ ni hiɛɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha oŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot, when the plant lacks sufficient water, or if there is not enough phosphorus in the soil to support fruit development.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ tsei bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aduawai akwɛ̃.

english: Yams need deep, soft, loose soil in tall mounds to expand freely. If the soil is hard, compacted, or full of stones, the expanding tubers cannot push through easily and become twisted.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni yɔɔ gɔji anɔ lɛ he miihia sweet potato koni egbɛ eshwa ehe. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ tɛi lɛ, anyɛɛɛ atsɔ Expanded heads lɛ mli mlɛo ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Plantain roots grow close to the soil surface, making the plants top-heavy as the bunch grows. Supporting heavy bearing trees with sturdy wooden poles prevents strong winds from uprooting them.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛji eniji lɛ dara. Tsei ni tsii ni akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekajie amɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants dry out and burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary shade with their broad leaves and keeps the soil cool while the young cocoa trees establish strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei ahe lɛ baaha baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ aná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i, yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ baafee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can spread out and catch direct sunlight to produce food. Staking also keeps the leaves off damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and allowing the main tuber underground to grow larger.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Tsi baa helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi tuber titri lɛ ni edaa.

english: Why am I finding small holes and ragged edges on my young maize leaves with tiny caterpillars inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe ŋmeii ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ.

english: This is a typical sign of a Fall Armyworm attack. These caterpillars hide inside the growing center of young maize plants to feed on fresh leaves, which weakens the crop early on if not managed quickly.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye baai heei. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbɔjɔ mra. Kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii oya

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper on the exact same patch of land where I just harvested tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa mi-tomato lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Peppers and tomatoes belong to the same plant family and share the same soil pests and diseases. Planting them back-to-back keeps those pests alive in the soil, whereas switching to a crop like maize or beans breaks the disease cycle.
ga: Pepper kɛ tomato yɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛyɔɔ sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai kome. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nakai ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. be mli ni etsakeɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa nɔ Ebaakpa helai asɛɛkuu lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when the soil stays wet for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need oxygen in the soil to stay healthy. Waterlogged soil fills up all the air gaps around the roots, suffocating them and causing bacteria and fungi in the damp earth to rot the crop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli obɔ, ni ehaa amɛmli shwieɔ shi ni ehaa sũ mli helai kɛ ŋmeii shwieɔ shi, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ.

english: Why should I wait until the ground is moist before applying chemical fertilizer to my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo miŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to break down into a liquid form that roots can actually drink up. Spreading fertilizer on dry soil leaves concentrated chemical salts near the roots, which can scorch and damage the plant.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛgbala ni amɛfee nu ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu diɛŋtsɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baaha tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ afee ekome yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ni efite amɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my main crop stay small and stunted even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mitso titri lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients from the soil before your main crop can reach them, effectively starving your crop of what it needs to grow big.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baashɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛdara.

english: When a plantain tree has too many young shoots growing around it, they all fight for the mother plant's nutrients and water. Removing extra shoots leaves enough energy for the main stem to produce larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ ná ŋmeii bibii babaoo Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yitso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ plantain tsei wuji.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of nutrients. The plant drops flowers to conserve its energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ he. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni shihilɛi ni amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable plot early in the morning or late in the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai aŋmɔ lɛ nɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Early morning is best because it gives roots time to drink water before the hot afternoon sun dries out the soil, while allowing the leaves to dry in the sun so plant fungus doesn't grow overnight.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ nu dani shwane hulu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ŋmeii akakwɛ̃ nyɔɔŋ kome.

english: Why is the top layer of soil on my farm better for crops than soil dug up from deep underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fe shikpɔŋ ni atsa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Topsoil contains decomposed leaves, plant matter, and living organisms that provide natural food for crops. Soil dug from deep underground, near rocks, lacks these nutrients and air, making it difficult for crop roots to feed and grow healthily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ fã lɛ ji baai ni egboi, tsei, kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Shikpɔŋ ni atsa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tɛi. Niyenii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaana niyenii ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when I plant them directly in deep soil dug out from a hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ mikɛdu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni atsa kɛjɛ bu lɛ mli lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Soil dug from deep underground has been isolated from air and organic materials for a long time. It lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, which crops need to make green leaves, so young plants will look weak and yellow until organic matter or compost is added.
ga: Atse shikpɔŋ ni atsa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ mli kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he.

english: How can I make the raw soil dug out from a deep pit good for growing vegetables?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha shikpɔŋ ni atsa kɛjɛ bu ni mli kwɔ mli lɛ afee nɔ ni sa kɛha aduawai akwɛmɔ?

english: You can make deep, nutrient-poor soil fertile again by mixing it with well-rotted animal manure, compost, or dark topsoil. This adds organic food and beneficial microbes that vegetables need to absorb nutrients and retain moisture.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ kooloi ashishifãi ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni mli edɔ ni okɛaafutu mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ kɛ niyenii ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni he hiaa aduawai koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ fataa he.

english: What happens to my tree crops if their roots hit solid rocks deep down in the ground?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitso lɛ nɔ kɛji eshishifãi lɛ tswa tɛ ni wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: When roots hit solid rock underground, they can no longer grow downward to search for deep water. Instead, they bend and grow sideways near the surface, making the tree less stable in high winds and more likely to suffer during long dry spells.
ga: Beni shishifãi lɛ tswa tɛ ni wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ ni amɛyatao nu ni mli kwɔ. Mohu ɔ, a gboɔ nɛ a wa kɛ yaa afã ngɛ nyu ɔ hɛ mi. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ ahi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli, ni ekolɛ amɛbaana amanehulu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do my crops dry up very quickly in areas where hard rock is close to the surface?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hei ni tɛi ni wa yɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ?

english: Shallow soil lying over rock layers cannot hold much rainwater. When the rain stops, the small amount of moisture in the thin soil evaporates rapidly, leaving crop roots dry with nowhere deeper to pull water from.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni yɔɔ tɛsaa lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ahiɛ nugbɔ nu babaoo. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, nu fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tseee lɛ mli lɛ baaho oya Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbala nu kɛya shɔŋŋ.

english: Does heavy rain harm my crops more if my land has rocks right under the soil layer?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui babaoo kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ tɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: Yes, because water cannot pass through solid rock. During heavy rains, water gets trapped above the underground rock layer, drowning crop roots in standing water, which causes root rot and prevents the plant from breathing.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ nu nyɛŋ atsɔ tɛ ni wa mli. yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Nu lɛ efo shikpɔŋ shishi tɛsaa lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei shishifãi lɛ boteɔ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaaa tso lɛ amu.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to dig deep holes before planting tree crops like citrus or cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔfo bu ni mli kwɔ dani wɔdu citrus loo cocoa tsei lɛ?

english: Digging deep planting holes breaks up compact subsoil so young roots can spread easily without struggling. Refilling the hole with loose, rich topsoil gives the young tree a soft, nutrient-dense home to establish strong roots.
ga: Dumɔ bu ni mli kwɔ ni atsa lɛ gbalaa sũ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ akafee nɔ ko. Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fata bu lɛ he lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ náa shia ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli koni shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃.

english: If I dig deep planting pits for root crops like cassava or yam, will the harvest be bigger?
ga: Kɛ mifo bu ko ni mli kwɔ koni mikɛdu tuber ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei lɛ, ani yibiiwoo lɛ baaya hiɛ?

english: Yes, digging and loosening deep soil allows root crops like yam and cassava to expand freely underground. Soft soil lets tubers swell big and straight, whereas hard soil restricts their growth and distorts their shape.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni atsa ni ajieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni shishifãi tamɔ sweet potato kɛ cassava yɔɔ lɛ. Gbalamɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nɔkwɛmɔnii lɛ amli yɛ heyeli mli Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa bulbs lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ tɛ̃ɛ. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni wa tsiɔ dalɛ naa ni efiteɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Can I use the deep subsoil dug out from a large hole to fill nursery bags for my seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mli kwɔ ni atsa kɛjɛ bu agbo ko mli lɛ awo grow kotokui amli kɛha midumɔwui lɛ?

english: Deep subsoil is good for nursery bags because it is usually free from weed seeds and diseases, but it lacks plant food. To use it successfully, you must mix it with fertile topsoil and decomposed manure before planting your seeds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kotokui ni akɛduɔ nii ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ helai bɛ mli. Shi tso niyenii ko bɛ. Kɛji oosumɔ ni okɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ Esa akɛ okɛ ŋwɛi sũ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo afutu mli dani odu dumɔwui lɛ.

english: How does digging large pits or trenches across my farmland help my crops during dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ bu agboi loo ŋmeii ni mifoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Deep pits act as rainwater harvesters during rainy periods. They trap runoff water and allow it to seep slowly into the surrounding underground soil, keeping the root zone of nearby crops moist long after the rains stop.
ga: Bu ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nugbɔ nu ni ajieɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Amɛmɔɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ ni amɛhaa etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi sũ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli fiofio. Ha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can stream water that looks clear to my eyes still harm my crop yields?
ga: Ani nu ni hoɔ ni tamɔ nɔ ni mli tse yɛ mihiɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui lolo?

english: Yes, water can carry hidden salts, acidic chemicals, or microscopic diseases that stunt plant growth and ruin yields, even if the water looks crystal clear.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu baanyɛ atere ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe loo helai bibii ni haaa tsei akwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu lɛ mli tse moŋ

english: Why are the leaves of my vegetables developing a salty white crust after I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛŋ beni mikɛ nu ewo amɛnɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A white crust usually means your water source has high mineral or salt content, which leaves deposits on the foliage and soil as it evaporates, potentially burning tender roots and leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋshɔŋloo yɛŋ tsɔɔ akɛ nu ni ojɛɔ mli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ minerals loo ŋoo. Enɛ haa nɔ ko eshwɛɔ yɛ baai lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni efoɔ lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi kɛ baai bibii lɛ ashã.

english: Why do my pepper plants develop stem rot when I irrigate them with pond water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fiteɔ kɛ mikɛ nubu mli nu shwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Stagnant water often carries fungal spores, and heavy watering chokes plant roots of oxygen, creating ideal conditions for root and stem rot to set in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai tsɛŋemɔ helai yɔɔ mli. Ni nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli babaoo lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni amɛdara. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ko baa ni shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbo.

english: Is borehole water safe for me to use directly on my young seedling nursery?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛbaatsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ akwɛmɔhe lɛ?

english: Borehole water is generally good, but some groundwater contains high levels of minerals or salts that can shock very young seedlings if the water quality is not tested first.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, nu ni jɛɔ nubu mli lɛ hi. Shi shikpɔŋ shishi nui komɛi yɛ mineral loo ŋmeii babaoo. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui bibii waa lɛ ahiɛ afee amɛ yaa kɛji akɛ akaaa nu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly like tubes in the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during hot afternoons as a defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, helping the plant save precious moisture.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he koni akɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ nu ni he hiaa.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before any fruit can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when they experience severe stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or bad irrigation water that prevents the roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Tomato baafɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi kɛ́ amɛmiifee nɔ ni haoɔ mɔ waa, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. aloo nu ni ashwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Cassava sheds its leaves during long dry spells as a survival trick to reduce water loss, staying dormant until water returns to grow fresh leaves.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛba nu ni fiteɔ lɛ shi. ni ejɔɔ ehe kɛyashi nu lɛ baaku esɛɛ eba ni ebaaná baai heei.

english: Early morning is best because the soil absorbs the moisture before the sun gets hot, allowing plant roots to drink fully with minimal water lost to evaporation.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ. Ehaa tso shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu jogbaŋŋ kɛ nu fioo ko pɛ ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my cabbage turning yellow and dying off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate that the plant's roots cannot absorb food properly, often caused by waterlogged soil, poor drainage, or dirty irrigation water damaging the root tips.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo nu ni mli ewo muji ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ

english: Why is my fertilizer not helping my crops even after I mix it with water from my dam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-fertilizer lɛ eyeee ebuaaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ faa lɛ mli lɛ futuɔ mli moŋ?

english: If your dam water is salty or dirty, the minerals in the water can react with the fertilizer and lock the nutrients away, preventing your crops from absorbing them.
ga: Kɛji nu ni yɔɔ o-dam lɛ mli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ muji Minerals ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee ekome kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the bottom up during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape pattern, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen fertilizer or the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to feed properly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmãa loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off the branches without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience sudden dry spells, lack enough shade overhead, or suffer from insect attacks that prevent pods from forming.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ ba. Shade ni bɛ yiteŋ loo kooloi ni tutuaa lɛ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ efeee

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry out and turn brown around the edges even when there is rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ egbi ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Brown and burnt edges on plantain leaves are a sign that the soil is low in potassium or that a leaf spot fungus is spreading across the farm.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ plantain baai lɛ anɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eshã lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ potassium faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛ leaf spot fungus lɛ miigbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cassava plants shed all their leaves as soon as the harmattan starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ fiteɔ kɛji harmattan je shishi pɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during hot dry spells to save water and protect itself; the plant will grow fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Yucca shwieɔ ebaai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe. Tsei lɛ baakwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why are my sweet potato vines growing lots of big leaves while the roots underground stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji babaoo yɛ be mli ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or animal manure, the sweet potato plant puts all its energy into growing green leaves on top instead of tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo kooloi aŋmei babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli yɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Why are my yam tubers cracking open while they are still growing in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miigba be mli ni amɛmiida lolo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams split open when heavy rains come suddenly after a long dry spell, causing the inside of the tuber to expand faster than the skin can stretch.
ga: Sweet potatoes tswaa kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa ba trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get dark, rotten patches at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli edɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shishigbɛ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This rot at the bottom of tomatoes happens when the soil lacks calcium or when the ground goes from very dry to very wet too quickly.
ga: Tomato shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Pepper leaves curl when tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies suck the sap from under the leaves or spread a virus into the plant.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ nu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ loo amɛgbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwã tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cabbage plants remain loose leaves instead of forming a hard round head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ yitsei ni wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head if the weather is too hot, if they are shaded from direct sunlight, or if planted too close together.
ga: Kaabe nyɛŋ akwɛ yitso kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ akɛwo he ko ni hulu la shɛɛɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my okra plants getting covered in a white powdery coating?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ powda yɛŋ ehà mi gumbo tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: That white powder is a fungal disease called powdery mildew, which spreads quickly when weather is humid and air cannot pass easily between plants.
ga: Pauda yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ. ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ tsei ateŋ mlɛo.

english: What makes these new improved maize varieties different from the traditional seeds I usually plant?
ga: Mɛni haa nɛkɛ ŋmãa henɔi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ nɛɛ feɔ srɔto yɛ blema dumɔwui ni miduɔ daa lɛ ahe?

english: Improved maize varieties are specifically bred to grow faster, resist dry spells better, and produce higher yields per acre compared to traditional seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ abele henɔi ni atsake amɛ koni amɛdara oya. Eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ahe gbɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ acre kome mli kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ahe.

english: What other crops are closely related to maize, and can I grow them on my farm in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei krokomɛi kɛ ŋmãa bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa? Ni ani manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Crops like sorghum and millet are close relatives of maize. They handle dry weather very well and grow successfully in drier regions, such as northern Ghana.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ji ŋmãa wekumɛi ni bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa. Amɛtsuɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ waa. ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nu bɛ tamɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant during the next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It is best not to replant seeds from hybrid maize. The second generation produces much smaller cobs and uneven yields, so buying fresh certified seeds each season gives the best harvest.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ mli. Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ woɔ cob fioo kwraa ni ewoɔ yibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa anáa yibiiwoo ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why should I use modern planting tools for my maize instead of planting manually with a hoe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nibii ni akɛduɔ ŋmãa lɛ atsu nii moŋ fe ni mikɛ mi nine baadu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Modern planting tools place seeds at a precise depth and spacing. This saves time, reduces seed waste, and helps every plant get an equal amount of sunlight and nutrients.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔ nibii kɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ mlibotemɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ. ni haa be baa shi Ehaa nibii ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli lɛ baa shi ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ.

english: How far apart should I plant my maize seeds to get the biggest harvest?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-ŋmã dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni maná yibiiwoo ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: Planting maize about 75 centimeters between rows and 40 centimeters between plants ensures the leaves do not crowd each other out for sunlight and soil nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa aaafee sɛntimitai 75 yɛ ŋtayaai ateŋ kɛ sɛntimitai 40 yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ekome koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How can using a tractor for land preparation help increase my maize harvest?
ga: Te trakta ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛtsuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Tractors loosen hard soil deeper and faster than hand hoes, allowing maize roots to spread deep into the earth for water and nutrients, leading to stronger plants.
ga: Trakta shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni etsuɔ ​​nii oya fe nine ni akɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa abɛi shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni he wa fe tsutsu lɛ

english: What should I prepare on my farm before hiring a machine to plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ masaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mahe tsɔnei ni akɛdu dumɔwui?

english: You should clear large tree stumps, rocks, and thick brush so the machinery can move smoothly through the field without breaking its parts.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie tsei agboi, tɛi, kɛ brɔshi ni mli tse. Enɛ haa tsɔne lɛ nyɛɔ etsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee ehe nibii.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my growing maize field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mawo mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Apply your first round of fertilizer about two weeks after planting when the leaves appear, and a second round when the plant reaches knee height to support cob formation.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ awo mli aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ beni baai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ. kɛ kpokpaa ni ji enyɔ lɛ, beni tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛnaji ahe koni amɛye amɛbua ŋmeii ni baa lɛ.

english: Growing maize on the same plot continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if pests are attacking my young maize leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ miitutua mi-baby corn baai lɛ?

english: Look for small holes or saw-dust-like material inside the central leaf funnels of young plants, which indicates pests like Fall Armyworm that need quick treatment.
ga: Taomɔ buji bibii loo nibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni ehe hiaa ni atsa lɛ oya.

english: Does it matter which way I stick my cassava stems into the ground when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ adu lɛ, ani ŋmei tso lɛ baakpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ gbɛ ko nɔ?

english: Yes, direction matters! The small buds on the cassava stem should point upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the stems will struggle to grow, taking longer to sprout and producing fewer tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, gbɛtsɔɔmɔ he miihia! Esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Ebaawa akɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ̃. Eheɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa.

english: No, planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and small ears. Giving each plant proper space ensures bigger, healthier crops and a better total harvest.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ toi bibii. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaha ená ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Na hewalɛ kpakpa ni oná ŋmaa kpakpa

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key food plants need to grow green and strong. It can also happen if heavy rains wash nutrients away or if water sits around the roots for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or if there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly moist and planting at the right time of the rainy season helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo kɛji akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli lɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ be fɛɛ be ni adu yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my young pepper seedlings dry up and die right after I move them into the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings suffer from transplant shock and intense sunlight. You should shade them with small leafy branches or palm fronds for the first few days and transplant them late in the afternoon when the sun is low.
