ga: Dumɔwui bibii naa amanehulu kɛjɛ shwiemɔ he shoofeemɔ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Esa akɛ okɛ tsei niji bibii kɛ baai awo mli. loo ŋmei tsei ahe tsei yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii 2-3 lɛ amli ni aduɔ yɛ shwane mli beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly during wet and humid weather. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight and air inside the canopy, removing rotten pods, and clearing weeds help stop the rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ahi ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ. ni ajie jwɛi lɛ koni eye ebua ni ekpa fitemɔ.

english: What is making small holes in my corn leaves and hiding caterpillars inside the stalks?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli lɛ baa? Ni okɛ ŋmei lɛ ato tso lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. Moths lay eggs on the leaves, and the caterpillars eat the young shoots and tunnel into the plant. Checking your farm early and using proper pest control stops them from destroying the field.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ŋmei ni woɔ wui yɛ baai anɔ. Ni ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ ni sa baaye abua ni akafite ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need plenty of sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves into the light and keeps them off damp ground, which protects the plant from soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ aje kpo yɛ la mli ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, usually right after a light rain or early in the growing season when plants are actively growing. Applying it during a drought can burn the roots, and applying it during heavy downpours washes it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ loo yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa waa lɛ shishijee mli. Kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashã. Ni kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ejieɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil uses up the same specific nutrients and allows maize pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores fertility and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔmɔ baa ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up into tight tubes when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize leaves roll up, the plant is trying to protect itself from losing water through evaporation in the hot sun. It acts like closing a window to keep moisture inside the plant so it doesn't dry out and die.
ga: Beni ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ Tsei lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hewɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni akɛhaa samflɛ nɔ koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, egbiɛɛ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during long dry spells to save water and energy. By dropping leaves, the plant stops losing moisture through transpiration and rests while keeping its food stored safely in the underground roots until rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni ekɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ kpaɔ nu ni efiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni etsɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa niyenii hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before turning into fruits when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: When tomato plants don't get enough water, they experience stress and abort their flowers to save energy. The plant chooses to keep its main stem and leaves alive rather than spending precious water on producing fruits.
ga: Beni Tomato Tsei lɛ Naaa Nu ni Fa Amɛnaa haomɔ ni amɛfoɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Tsei halaa akɛ amɛbaahã tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ baai lɛ ahi shi moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ nu ni jara wa baatsu nii koni amɛkɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves turn yellow when I give them too much water from my pump?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ mikɛ nu babaoo ni jɛ pɔmp lɛ mli lɛ ha amɛ lɛ?

english: Too much water drowns the crop's roots by filling up all the tiny air spaces in the soil. Without oxygen, the roots cannot breathe or absorb nutrients properly, which turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Nu babaoo haa tsei ashishifãi shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni ewoɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Will using groundwater from a well harm my crops compared to natural rainwater?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni jɛɔ nubu mli lɛ ni mikɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui kɛ akɛto adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ he?

english: Well water is safe and excellent for crops during dry periods because it provides the moisture plants need to keep growing. While rain contains extra atmospheric nitrogen that boosts leafy growth, clean well water satisfies the crop's basic water needs effectively.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Ejaakɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ jɛmɛ koni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ yɛ nitrogen kroko yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni haa baai lɛ daraa babaoo moŋ. Shi nu ni jɛɔ nubui ni mli tse mli lɛ tsuɔ nu he hiamɔ nii titrii ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it better for me to water my crops early in the morning instead of at midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi moŋ fe shwane?

english: Watering in the early morning allows the crop's roots to soak up moisture before the hot sun causes water to evaporate into the air. Watering at noon wastes water and can shock warm plants with cool water.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa efoɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ fiteɔ nu, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ nu ni mli ejɔ aha tso lɛ mli adɔ.

english: How do I know if my crops are thirsty before their leaves actually dry out?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kumai miiye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ dani baai lɛ agbi?

english: Before leaves dry completely, crops show early signs of thirst by losing their shiny green color, looking dull, or drooping slightly in the late afternoon. Catching these early signs allows you to water them before growth stops.
ga: dani baai lɛ agbi kwraa Nibii ni adu lɛ baajie kumai he okadii akpo mra kɛtsɔ amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ lɛ ni amɛbaafite lɛ nɔ, ni amɛbaafee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fioo kɛyashi shwane mli. Mra be mli okadii nɛɛ ni ooomɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nu woɔ mli dani dalɛ kpaa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods stay very small and flat when there is a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods need a steady supply of water to transport nutrients from the soil into the developing fruit. Without enough water, the plant cannot pump enough food into the pods, leaving them small and undersized.
ga: Nu ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ he miihia kookoo ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa awo pod lɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ bibioo tsɔ ni efeɔ bibioo tsɔ.

english: Why do pepper plant roots grow deeper into the soil during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the top soil dries out, crop roots naturally grow deeper into the ground searching for hidden underground moisture. Deep roots help the plant stay anchored and hydrated even when the surface soil is dry.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli egbi Tse lɛ shishifãi lɛ daa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ shi ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ egbi po.

english: If I provide my crops with regular water from a well, will they keep producing fruit throughout the dry season?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ nu jɛ nu bu mli miha midumɔ nii lɛ Ani amɛbaawo yibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Yes, many crops will continue to flower and fruit year-round if provided with consistent water. Regular watering tricks the plant into thinking it is still the rainy season, allowing for continuous growth and yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei babaoo baaya nɔ afɔlɔ ni amɛwo yibii yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli kɛji amɛná nu daa. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa lɛ baalaka tso lɛ ni esusu akɛ eyɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lolo. Ehaa tsei lɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ yibii daa.

english: Why do some of my pawpaw trees produce flowers but never bear any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi shi ewooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Pawpaw plants can be male, female, or hermaphrodite. Male pawpaw trees produce pollen to fertilize female flowers, but the male trees themselves will never grow any fruit.
ga: Pawpaw tsei baanyɛ afee nuu, yoo, loo nɔ ni kɛ hii feɔ yakayaka nii. Pawpaw tsei hii woɔ fɔfɔi ni haa fɔfɔi yei fɔɔ. Shi nuu paw tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ wooo yibii ko kwraa.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress, dry soil, or a lack of soil nutrients. Providing consistent water and balanced fertilizer helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Do I need bees or insects on my farm for my tomatoes to produce fruit?
ga: Ani ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii he miihia mi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mi-tomato lɛ awo yibii?

english: Tomatoes can self-pollinate through wind movement, but insects like bees shake the flowers better, resulting in more successful pollination and bigger, healthier fruits.
ga: Tomato baanyɛ ekɛ ehe awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ ehe lɛ nɔ, shi kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhosoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa pollination yeɔ omanye babaoo kɛ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know when my maize is fully mature and ready to harvest for dry grain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmã lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi?

english: Maize is ready for dry harvest when the leaves and outer husks turn completely brown and dry, and a small black layer appears at the base of the corn kernels when plucked.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni egbi beni baai kɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi kwraa lɛ. Ni kɛ́ ajie lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ bibioo ko ni ji ediŋŋ baaje kpo. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ashishi.

english: Yes, pruning lower leaves and side shoots allows the tomato plant to send its energy and water directly into developing larger, healthier fruits instead of growing useless leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ kɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ ni oookpa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa o-tomato tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaakwɛ̃ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my young crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Apply fertilizer about two to three weeks after planting or transplanting, when the young plant's roots have established enough to swallow the soil nutrients.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli aaafee otsii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ yɛ dumɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ tso bibioo lɛ shishifãi lɛ wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛmi niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ,.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide big leaves that shield young cocoa trees from the sun until the cocoa is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao lɛ mli waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and tiny tuber roots.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii baa.

english: Maize leaves roll inward as a natural protective response to reduce water loss from heat and sunlight, conserving moisture until the temperature cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hetoo ni haa nu ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la mli baa lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when weeds are present around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo be mli ni jwɛi ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from the soil, effectively starving your crops and slowing down their growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni ehaa amɛdalɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide living shade, keeping young cocoa seedlings cool and moist until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: What happens if I plant my crop seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow large and produce a bigger harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Adding manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps bring back the green color and supports healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer right before a very heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall will wash your fertilizer off the field or push it deep into the ground where plant roots cannot reach it. Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil during light rain or gentle weather.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baatswa o-fertilizer lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo ebaatsi kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli. loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni esaaa

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when water is inconsistent, or when there are no beneficial insects around for pollination. Keeping soil moist with mulch helps protect the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ mli ejɔɔɔ loo be mli ni kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha pollination bɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it good practice to plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Beans and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes your maize plants, improves the soil quality, and gives you two different crops from one farm.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha o-corn tsei lɛ afɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ aba kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch sunlight, which creates energy to grow big tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei wuji náa hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekafite.

english: Cassava root rot usually happens when water sits around the roots for too long during heavy rains, encouraging soil fungi. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Ekɛ ŋmeii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔŋ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli oya.

english: Why should I wait for two or three steady rains before planting instead of planting on the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ dani madu nii? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: The first rain after a dry season quickly evaporates in warm soil. Waiting for a few consistent rains ensures the ground holds enough deep moisture so your germinating seeds do not dry out and die.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be sɛɛ lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be be fioo komɛi ni abaamɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: How do weeds in my field hurt the growth of my pepper crops?
ga: Te jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa mi-pepper tsei lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds act like food thieves on your farm; they steal soil nutrients, sunlight, and water that your pepper plants need. Removing weeds early allows all the soil nutrients to go directly into growing your crops.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, hulu la, kɛ nu ni he hiaa o-pepper tsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛhaa tsei ni miida.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries up soil moisture quickly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa gives them the shelter and humidity they need to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa sũ mli nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ cocoa tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa amɛnáa wɔɔhe kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize crop turning pale yellow from the center instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost restores healthy green leaves and improves growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha amɛdaramɔ aya hiɛ.

english: How do groundnut plants help improve my soil for the next crop I want to plant?
ga: Te ŋmeii tsei baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni misumɔɔ ni makwɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested and roots decay, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni shishifãi lɛ egbo lɛ Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots soft rot in the soil when heavy rains fall for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water prevents oxygen from reaching them and encourages fungal disease. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi, ni no haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa lɛ ayashɛ he ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is it risky for me to sow my seeds right after the very first shower of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry spell that can scorch newly germinated seeds. Waiting until the major rains are steadily established ensures the soil stays wet enough for young plants to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaya nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni tsei bibii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores soil nutrients and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai shwereɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my seed crop very close together to fit more onto my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures stronger stems and bigger harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ehaa eshishifãi lɛ waa ni ekpaa nii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that develops big tubers underground. Staking keeps the vines off damp ground, maximizing sunlight exposure and preventing leaves from rotting.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ akwɛ̃. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni wain tso lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Ha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo ni otsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite

english: Pepper flowers fall off when plants experience stress from extreme heat or sudden dry spells. Regular watering and light shading during hot weather help flowers stay on the plant and form fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ loo nugbɔshiimɔ be trukaa. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even when I give them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal nutrients, water, and sunlight directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all available resources to grow tall and produce well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ náa nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kɛha dalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ yibii kpakpai.

english: What does cross-breeding mean when people talk about maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji crossbreeding shishi kɛji gbɔmɛi miiwie ŋmãa dumɔwui ahe?

english: Cross-breeding combines two different strong parent maize plants to produce hybrid seeds that grow stronger, yield more grain, and resist diseases better than local traditional seeds.
ga: Crossbreeding kɛ ŋmãa nyɛ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni he wa feɔ ekome ni ekɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni daa waa lɛ baa. Ehaa ŋmaa yibiiwoo babaoo ni helai nyɛɔ eshiɔ amɛ fe blema maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I save and plant seeds from my cross-bred maize harvest next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni maduɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid or cross-bred crops lose their vigor and high-yielding traits in the second generation, leading to smaller yields and uneven plant growth.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome loo tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛ sui ni haa yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu daaa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: Will using cross-bred crop varieties protect my plants from all diseases?
ga: Ani tsei ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ baabu mitsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ helai fɛɛ ahe?

english: While cross-bred seeds are bred to tolerate specific pests and diseases better than local seeds, they still require good field management, weed control, and proper nutrients to stay fully healthy.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ atsɔse dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛye kooloi kɛ helai komɛi anɔ fe dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ moŋ, Shi ehe miihia ni akwɛ he ko jogbaŋŋ lolo. jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ niyenii ni sa kɛha hewalɛ kpakpa ni yeɔ emuu

english: Is it more profitable for me to grow rice instead of maize this season?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ babaoo yɛ he akɛ abaadu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa najiaŋ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Both crops have strong market demand in Ghana, but rice currently offers very high market returns if you have well-watered land, while maize remains a reliable and steady food staple.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ jarayeli he nibii ni ataoɔ waa yɛ Ghana. Shi amrɔ nɛɛ Rice haa jarayeli mli nyɔmɔwoo ni nɔ kwɔ waa. Kɛji oyɛ he ko ni nu fa bɔ ni sa yɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa kã he eji niyenii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why are many farmers in my area switching over from maize to rice farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ miitsake kɛmiijɛ ŋmãa dumɔ mli kɛmiiya ŋmãa dumɔ mli lɛ?

english: High demand for locally produced rice has created ready buyers and good market prices, making rice a very attractive commercial crop for farmers looking to increase their income.
ga: Nibii ni ataoɔ babaoo yɛ ŋmãa ni afee yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ lɛ naa ŋmãa kpakpa kɛ jarayeli jara. Enɛ haa ŋmãa feɔ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋɔɔ waa kɛha okwaafoi ni miitao ni amɛha amɛshika aya hiɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my land is better suited for growing rice or maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Rice thrives in wet, low-lying areas or swampy soils that hold water, whereas maize prefers well-drained, fertile upland soil where water does not collect for long periods.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni nu yɔɔ nɔ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa sumɔɔ delta shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. ni nu buaaa ehe naa be kakadaŋŋ

english: Can I plant rice on the exact same plot where I just harvested my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ nɔ amrɔ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, but rotating crops or giving the soil time to rest helps break pest cycles and prevents the land from losing specific nutrients that one plant consumes heavily.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ahaa lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni efoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli, ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kome yeɔ waa lɛ afite.

english: Does rice take more nutrients out of the soil than maize does?
ga: Ani ŋmãa jieɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fe ŋmãa?

english: Both crops feed heavily on soil nutrients; rice uses high amounts of nitrogen and water, while maize demands phosphorus and nitrogen, so both need proper fertilization to keep soil rich.
ga: Tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Omɔ kɛ nitrogen kɛ nu babaoo tsuɔ nii. Abɛi he miihia phosphorus kɛ nitrogen, no hewɔ lɛ, amɛ fɛɛ amɛbiɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli jogbaŋŋ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya nɔ afee ŋmɔshi nii.

english: How do I know the right time of year to start planting rice?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale afi lɛ mli be ni sa ni akɛjeɔ ŋmãa dumɔ shishi?

english: Rice should be planted right at the onset of the major rainy season so that the seedlings receive constant moisture required for healthy germination and early root growth.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli koni dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni he hiaa be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃ waa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ mra.

english: Why does my maize grow much faster during certain times of the farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa oya waa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ fãi komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Maize responds strongly to a combination of warm sunlight and regular soil moisture; when heat and rains match perfectly, the plant processes nutrients faster and expands rapidly.
ga: Abɛi hereɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa lɛ nɔ waa. Kɛji hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ lɛ tee nɔ ehi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ Tsei tsuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ he nii oya ni amɛshwereɔ oya.

english: What is the difference between hybrid seeds and the regular seeds I save from my harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome kɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ daa ni mikɛkpaa lɛ ateŋ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred by crossing two different plant varieties to get the best traits of both, such as higher yields and disease resistance. Seeds saved from standard crops will not give you the same strong and uniform results if replanted.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ tsei srɔtoi enyɔ ni afɔɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ koni anyɛ ana sui ni hi fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli, tamɔ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ amli lɛ baahaaa yibii ni mli wa ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛji akɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: If I buy hybrid maize seeds this season, can I save some of the harvested grain to plant next year?
ga: Kɛji mihe hybrid ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ be nɛɛ mli Ani manyɛ makɛ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi ato koni madu afi ni baa lɛ?

english: It is not recommended to replant seeds from a hybrid harvest. The second-generation crops lose their special strength, leading to lower yields, uneven plant growth, and a higher risk of disease.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Tsei ayinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi. Tsei lɛ adalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni amɛyɔɔ helai ahe oshara babaoo mli

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants rolling up during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When leaves roll up, the plant is protecting itself from losing too much water in the heat. It is a natural defense mechanism to stay alive until the sun cools down or rain falls.
ga: Beni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ Tso lɛ baabu ehe koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni haa mɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ hulu lɛ mli jɔɔ loo nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant the seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the crops to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stems and small harvests instead of healthy, high-yielding plants.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛkpaaa nii jogbaŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, o ma ná tsohi nɛ a he wa nɛ a woɔ yiblii babauu.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing lots of green leaves but producing small roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When there is too much nitrogen in the soil, the plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of storing food and starch in the roots below ground.
ga: Kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní kɛ ngmlɛfia ngɛ tso ɔ sisi ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why do high-yielding crop varieties need extra fertilizer while local seeds grow without it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he yɛ be mli ni maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ daa ni akɛwooo mli lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are designed to grow faster and yield much more food, which consumes nutrients from the soil quickly. Fertilizer provides the heavy feeding these fast-growing crops need to perform well.
ga: Afee tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo niyenii babaoo. ni kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii oya Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa tsei ni daa oya nɛɛ babaoo koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why is it important to plant my improved seeds immediately after the first major rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu mi dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties follow strict growth schedules. Planting right when the rains start ensures the roots get steady moisture during their critical early growth stages.
ga: Tsei henɔi ni atsake amɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ dalɛ bei ni mli wa sɛɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ je shishi pɛ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ naa nu be fɛɛ be yɛ mra be mli dalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do pests attack my farm crops more aggressively during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In the dry season, wild bushes dry up, so insects move to farm crops to find food and moisture. Warm weather also causes insect populations to reproduce much faster.
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, koo lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ gbiɔ. Kɛkɛ lɛ koolooi fãa kɛyaa ŋmɔji amli koni amɛyatao niyenii kɛ nu. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ hu haa kooloi ayibɔ fɔɔ oya.

english: How does storing my planting seeds in a warm, damp room affect how they grow in the field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni adu lɛ ni akɛtoɔ tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ saa amɛdalɛ he yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Warm and damp air fools seeds into starting the germination process early or causes mold to grow on them, which damages or kills the seed before it ever reaches your soil.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, ni mli ejɔ lakaa dumɔwui koni amɛje amɛkwɛ̃mɔ shishi mra loo ehaa ŋmeii daa. Enɛ baafite loo ebaagbe dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds always grow faster and look stronger than my planted crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be ni etamɔ nɔ ni ehe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally built to survive tough weather and poor soil, whereas crops spend their energy producing grains or fruits and require human support to compete.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni adebɔɔ fee koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo ŋmaa loo aduawai, ni ehe miihia ni adesai aye abua amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛye akaŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over when strong winds and heavy rains hit my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa tswa miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over (a problem called lodging) when their roots are too shallow or weak to hold the tall stalk upright. Heaping soil around the base of the stems (earthing up) and planting at the right depth gives the roots strong anchorage to withstand heavy winds.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi Enáa dormancy (naagba ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy) kɛji eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo egbɔjɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ emɔ tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni aaabɔle tso lɛ shishi (shikpɔŋ nɔ) ni adu yɛ he ni sa lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ waa koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over right when the fruit bunch starts to grow heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi trukaa beni aduawai akui lɛ mli tsiimɔ wa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support the heavy weight of a maturing fruit bunch, especially in soft or wet soil. Propping up the trees with sturdy bamboo or wooden poles supports the heavy load and keeps the plant from uprooting.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ ni tsii lɛ anɔ. Titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tsei ni wa fee tso lɛ he fɛo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ muji lɛ atsu nii ni ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekaje shishi.

english: How does planting tall trees along the edge of my farm protect my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei kakadaji ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Tall trees planted along boundaries act as windbreaks, slowing down harsh storm winds before they hit your farm. This protects soft crops like plantains, maize, and cocoa from having their leaves torn or being completely uprooted.
ga: Tsei kakadaji ni adu yɛ husu lɛ he lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsiimɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ahum ni naa wa lɛ baa shi dani eba oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baabu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii tamɔ plantains, ŋmãa kɛ kookoo he koni amɛbaai lɛ akagbala loo akajie amɛ kɛjɛ amɛshishi kwraa.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings wither and die soon after I move them from the nursery to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings suffer from transplant shock when delicate roots break or dry out during moving. Watering the nursery bed before lifting plants, keeping root soil intact, and transplanting during late afternoons helps roots establish quickly without dying.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ fãa loo amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ yaa lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei akwɛmɔhe saatsoi anɔ dani akwɛɔ tsei anɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ koni shishifãi lɛ akafite ni aduɔ yɛ shwane mli Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmaa oya ni amɛgbooo.

english: Why should I put dry grass or straw around the base of my young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi abɔle mitsei bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the ground around plants (mulching) keeps the soil moist and cool, protecting young root systems from hot sunshine. It also prevents heavy raindrops from washing soil away from delicate roots.
ga: Mulching ni akɛwoɔ tsei ahe (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu shishifãi bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu naa koni ekafɔ sũ ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away topsoil on my farm and leave crop roots exposed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Rainwater flowing across bare or sloping land strips away loose topsoil, exposing plant roots and weakening their grip. Planting crops along hill curves (contour planting) and keeping cover crops stops soil erosion and keeps roots safely buried.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ baawó shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi jeɔ kpo ni ehaa nɔ ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baa shi. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji lɛ ashishigbɛ (Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji lɛ ashishi) kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ kpaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I need to build soil mounds or ridges before planting cassava and yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔma gɔŋ loo ŋshɔ dani wɔdu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei?

english: Building raised mounds loosens hard soil so crop roots can grow deep and tubers can expand easily. Deep root systems anchor the plant firmly into the ground and allow it to feed on nutrients stored below.
ga: Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni bulbs lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya. Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ fiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shi shiŋŋ ni ehaa tso lɛ nine shɛɔ niyenii ni ato yɛ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop roots stay short and weak when the soil is very hard and compact?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa waa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Hard, unworked soil acts like a brick wall that young roots cannot pierce, forcing them to remain shallow and weak. Deep tilling or ploughing loosens the soil so roots can push deep to anchor the plant and gather water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni asaaa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ brikii gbogbo ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ abote mli. ni nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛfee mɛi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ Shikpɔŋ nɔ nitsumɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛma tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛbua nu naa.

english: Planting too closely forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves them with thin, weak stems and small root systems that easily bend or uproot during bad weather.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ shishifãi bibii ni shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves turn yellow and rot when water sits on my farm for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Roots need air in the soil to breathe and stay healthy. When land stays flooded for days, roots drown, rot, and lose their ability to feed the plant, causing leaves to yellow and the entire plant to die.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua tso lɛ dɔŋŋ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gboɔ.

english: Young cocoa leaves drop during hot dry spells because the tree is trying to protect itself from losing water. Providing temporary shade crops like plantains keeps the soil moist and protects young cocoa from direct scorching sun.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ ejaakɛ tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni elaaje lɛ he. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily right before the fruits are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani aduawai lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow close to the surface and do not anchor deeply in the ground. When heavy wind blows while the plant is carrying a heavy heavy bunch, the plant easily topples unless it is propped up with sturdy wooden sticks.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ, ni afuuu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ miitswa waa be mli ni tsei lɛ miitere ŋmeii ni tsii Tsei lɛ baagbee shi mlɛo ja tso ni wa fiɔ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Yellowing of lower maize leaves is a natural warning sign that the soil lacks nitrogen. The plant is moving its limited nutrients from older bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Abɛi baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei miitsi niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo kɛmiijɛ baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do I see tiny worms hiding inside the middle of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mikɛ mihe ewo mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: Those worms are Fall Armyworms that lay eggs in the center whorl of young maize because the leaves there are soft and tender. Early identification and targeted treatment prevent them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmeii ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ ejaakɛ ŋmeii abifao lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ. Nibii ni ayɔseɔ mra kɛ tsamɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni miida lɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of dark leaves, but the roots underneath stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daraaa lolo.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or gets too much shade, cassava uses all its energy to build leaves and tall stems instead of storing food into big tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo lɛ, Kasava lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kakadaji kɛ ŋmeii. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ woɔ ngmɔkɔ nguahi a mi ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the ground before I even dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifolɔ amɛ po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water sits in the soil without draining, creating a wet environment that attracts soil rot fungi and nematodes that attack the tuber skin.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni gbalaa sũ mli ŋmeii ni fiteɔ kɛ nematodes ni tutuaa tuber hewolo lɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when water supply is irregular. Heat stress weakens the flower pollen, causing the plant to drop flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ haomɔ haa pollen ŋmaa lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Ha tsei agbo koni akɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do my crops look wilted and weak in the afternoon heat even when it rained two days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi ni amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ gbii enyɔ ni eho nɛ moŋ?

english: Plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck up from the soil during mid-day heat, causing them to temporarily wilt to conserve water until evening cool temperatures return.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛto nu he kɛyashi be mli ni hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow better and look greener when I plant beans or groundnuts in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji kɛ́ midu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally feeding and improving the surrounding soil for neighboring crops.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is healthy without paying for expensive chemical tests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni miwooo tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛkaa mɔ lɛ he nyɔmɔ?

english: Healthy farm soil is dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture without becoming waterlogged, and is full of living earthworms that loosen the ground for plant roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kpakpa mli lɛ yɛ diŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli ni nu shwieee mli. ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees start forming pods as soon as the rainy season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi pɛ?

english: Rainfall breaks the tree's dry-season resting period and provides the water needed for flowers to turn into cocoa pods, triggering the natural fruiting cycle.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fiteɔ tsei ni wɔɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ. ni eji nu ni he hiaa koni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ jɛɛhe. Ekanyaa adebɔɔ mli yibiiwoo shihilɛ lɛ

english: Why do cocoa pods mature slowly one after another instead of all at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ daa blɛoo, komekomei, shi jeee fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce flowers continuously over several weeks, which means the pods form at different times and ripen gradually throughout the rainy season.
ga: Kakao tso lɛ baaya nɔ awo fɔfɔi otsii babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli, ni amɛshwereɔ fiofio yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How does early rainfall affect the overall growth of my crops?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Early rains soften the soil and allow crop roots to easily absorb water and nutrients, which boosts plant energy and encourages new leaves and flowers to develop.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra be mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ yaa hiɛ ni ewoɔ baai kɛ fɔfɔi heei hewalɛ.

english: What kind of spray can I use to keep my cocoa trees strong and standing upright?
ga: Mɛɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ manyɛ mikɛtsu nii koni mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ?

english: Approved insecticides and fungicides protect the tree stem and leaves from pests and diseases like black pod, allowing the main stem to grow healthy, sturdy, and upright.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ buɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ ebaai ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi kɛ helai, tamɔ ŋmeii diji ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ shishi titri lɛ ni edaa waa, ehiɛɔ shi ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to spray my cocoa trees right at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afɔse kookoo tsei anɔ tsofa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: The warm, wet conditions of the rainy season create an ideal environment for fungal diseases and insects to spread, so early protective spraying stops them before they harm the crop.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ kooloi bibii gbɛfaŋnɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsofa ni tsiɔ hela naa kɛjɛɔ shishijee. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: Will heavy rain wash away the spray I put on my crop leaves?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, heavy rain right after spraying can wash away the chemicals; it is best to spray on clear mornings when the leaves are dry so the treatment has time to soak in.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ ajie tsofai lɛ. Esa akɛ afɔse nɔ yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso be mli ni baai lɛ egbi lɛ. Koni eha tsofafeemɔ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii.

english: Why are the stems of my young crops bending over instead of growing straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ebɔle amɛhe moŋ fe ni amɛaafee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young stems bend when plants do not get enough direct sunlight, lack sufficient soil nutrients, or are weakened by stem-boring insects.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei bibii lɛ baakɔ kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii ni woɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ egbɔjɔ

english: What causes cocoa pods to rot or fall off the tree before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Fungal infections like black pod disease thrive in excess moisture and high humidity, causing pods to darken, rot, and drop prematurely if left untreated.
ga: Fungal helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ duŋ, amɛgboɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ.

english: How can I help my cocoa farm yield more pods during the rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo aba yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Pruning excess branches to let air and sun reach the tree, clearing weeds around the base, and applying correct sprays will ensure the tree has energy for maximum pod output.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni akɛ tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ wo nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfee pod babaoo.

english: What should I do to protect delicate crop flowers when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mabu mitsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ fɔfɔi ahe kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa je shishi?

english: Maintain adequate shade trees around your main crops to break the force of heavy rain drops so flowers are not knocked off before they can form fruit.
ga: Ha tsei ni ebɔle ohe lɛ aná hulutsoo. Ha onibii titrii lɛ bɔ ni sa koni onyɛ otsɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewalɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi dani amɛwo yibii.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plants lack nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. This often happens after heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the soil or when the soil lacks organic matter.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa mli beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛtee sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ loo be mli ni sũ lɛ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller maize harvests if I plant maize in the exact same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the specific nutrients maize relies on and allows soil pests to build up. Alternating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas returns nitrogen to the soil and stops pests from multiplying.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi damɔ nɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafɔ.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves so quickly during warm weather?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: These holes are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which thrive in warm weather. They hide inside the central shoot of young maize plants during the day and feed heavily on the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ waa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits in the soil for too long, air cannot reach the roots, allowing water molds and bacteria to attack and rot the tubers underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that dry out and burn under full, direct sunlight. Leaving taller forest trees or planting plantains around them creates shade that keeps the soil moist and protects young cocoa roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni amɛshãa. Ni aaaha tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ adara loo adu dumɔwui yɛ he fɛɛ he Tsei lɛ feɔ hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Is it safe for me to work in my farm and weed early in the morning while dew is still on the leaves?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ matsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ leebi be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ kã baai lɛ anɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Working in the cool morning is good for you, but be careful moving through wet plants. Dew drops on leaves can carry fungal spores and bacteria from sick plants to healthy ones as you walk past them.
ga: Nitsumɔ yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ hi kɛha bo. Shi kwɛmɔ ohe jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ootsɔ tsei ni efɔ lɛ amli. Dew ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ fungal spores kɛ bacteria kɛjɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli beni onyiɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ.

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within three to four months, leaving plenty of space for the slower-growing cassava to expand and mature later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Enɛ haa gbɛ babaoo haa ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ koni egbɛ eshwa ni eda sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb up wooden stakes to produce big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ koni ekɛ bulbs agboi aba lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking lifts the vines high off the ground so leaves catch maximum sunlight, which sends energy down to grow large tubers below the soil.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing into tomatoes during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomato yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fruit from forming. When temperatures get too high or water is scarce, the plant drops its flowers to save water and survival energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa aduawai lɛ efeee Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu faaa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ wala nɔ lɛ he.

english: How do I choose the best shoot from an old plantain tree to plant in a new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmeii ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui momoi amli koni mikɛdu yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli?

english: Choose 'sword suckers,' which are young shoots with narrow, blade-like leaves and a broad base. They establish roots faster and grow into healthier, stronger plantain trees than shoots that already have wide leaves.
ga: Halamɔ ‘sword shoot’, ni ji tso bibioo ko ni baai lɛ mli tseee, tamɔ baa, ni eshishi lɛ mli kwɔ. Amɛfeɔ shishifãi oya ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ dumɔwui ni he wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ momo lɛ.

english: Why does my throat or mouth itch whenever I cook and eat certain fresh cocoyams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsitsi loo mi daaŋ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni mahoo nii ni maye kookoo hee lɛ?

english: Cocoyam tubers contain tiny needle-like chemical crystals called calcium oxalates. When the cocoyam is freshly harvested or cooked quickly without enough heat, these crystals survive and poke the soft lining of your mouth and throat, causing an itchy sensation.
ga: Tsofai bibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ji nɔ ni feɔ kookoo yitsei lɛ. Atsɛɔ nakai tsofa lɛ akɛ kalsium oksalate. Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmeii ehee loo ahoo amɛ oya ni akɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa tsuuu nii Nɛkɛ kristalo nɛɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛtswaa daaŋ kɛ tsitsi mli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa

english: How can I prevent cocoyam tubers from itching my hands and mouth when I prepare them for food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee miniji kɛ minaabu beni miisaa amɛ lɛ?

english: You can break down the itchy chemicals by letting freshly harvested cocoyams sit for a few days before cooking, peeling them under water, soaking them in salt water, and boiling them thoroughly until they are completely soft.
ga: Obaanyɛ ogbala tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ mli kɛtsɔ ŋmei ni akpa ehee lɛ ni oooha ehi shi gbii fioo komɛi dani ohoo lɛ nɔ. Peel under water Okɛwo nu ni mli edɔ mli No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛwo mli kɛyashi ebaafee blɛoo kwraa.

english: Why do raw cocoyams itch more when they are newly harvested compared to when they sit for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni ahoko lɛ shwieɔ shi waa kɛ́ akpa amɛ ehee lɛ? Kɛ akɛto gbii fioo komɛi ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ he

english: Freshly dug tubers have very high moisture and active defense chemicals. As the tuber rests after harvest, it loses excess moisture and the itchy compounds naturally break down and weaken over time.
ga: Bulb ni atsa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa waa ni tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli. be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miijɔɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Ebaafite ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ. Ni nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ fiteɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why does the juice from raw cocoyam skin irritate my hands when I peel it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni jɛɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ haa miniji mli fuɔ kɛ́ mijie amɛhe lɛ?

english: The plant produces a sap rich in natural compounds to defend itself against pests in the soil. Washing your hands with soap or rubbing a little palm oil on your skin before peeling creates a protective layer against this sap.
ga: Tsei jieɔ nu ni adebɔɔ mli nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ okɛ samla shwie oniji anɔ loo okɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma fioo ko shwie ohewolo lɛ nɔ dani ojie lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa-kɛ-ŋma nɛɛ he baa.

english: Why do the broad leaves of my cocoyam plant turn yellow and dry up during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoyam plants are sensitive to strong sunlight and heat. When exposed to direct, hot sun without shade, the plant loses water quickly through its large leaves, causing them to scorch and yellow to protect the underground tuber.
ga: Cocoyam tsei lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ baai wuji anɔ. Enɛ haa shãa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa koni ebu ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Why does planting cocoyam under tree shade like plantain help it grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu kookoo yɛ plantain tsei ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cocoyam naturally prefers cool temperatures and moist soil. Shade crops like plantains act as natural umbrellas, shielding the cocoyam leaves from harsh direct sunlight and keeping the soil cool and damp.
ga: Cocoyams sumɔɔ he ni hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ yɔɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: What causes my cocoyam tubers to rot directly inside the ground before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo yitsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ dani akpaa?

english: Tubers rot when water collects in the soil around the roots without draining properly during heavy rains. Excess water suffocates the tuber roots and allows harmful soil fungi to attack and soften the crop.
ga: Tuber rot baa kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tuber shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do my cocoyam plants grow huge leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen manure, the crop directs all its food and water to growing leafy foliage above ground instead of transferring energy down to expand the tuber.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ heɔ niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, ajieɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛgbala yitso lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell when my cocoyam is fully mature and ready to be dug out of the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-kookoo lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ atsa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cocoyam is ready for harvest when the lower outer leaves start turning yellow and naturally drying up. This signal means the plant has stopped growing new leaves and finished transferring its energy into the tuber.
ga: Cocoa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni shishigbɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Okadi nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa baai heei ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ, ni hewalɛ ni akɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ egbe naa.

english: Why shouldn't I leave freshly harvested cocoyams out in direct sunlight to dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishɛreɔ kookoo ni akpa ehee lɛ mishwieɔ lɛ? Egbi yɛ hulu lɛ mli

english: Direct hot sunlight cooks the outer skin of the harvested tuber, causing it to lose vital moisture quickly, turn hard, and spoil faster than tubers stored in a cool, shaded place.
ga: Hulu la ni mli edɔ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaho ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ahewolo lɛ kponɔgbɛ. Amɛlaajeɔ nu ni he hia oya, amɛwaa ni amɛfiteɔ oya fe kanei ni akɛto hei ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa shields the leaves from heat and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy plant growth. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the maize regain its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ ni mli wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays trapped around them due to poor soil drainage. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine ebɔle amɛhe. Enɛ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy fruit tops. Supporting them with sturdy wooden stakes or planting them in wind-protected areas stops them from falling over.
ga: Dumɔwu lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni mli tse. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni wa fi esɛɛ loo okɛdu yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ buɔ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekagbee shi.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and covered in tiny white insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ ehà amɛhe lɛ?

english: Whiteflies feed on tomato leaves and spread viruses that cause leaf curling. Spraying neem oil solution or soapy water on the underside of leaves helps control them.
ga: Whiteflies yeɔ tomato baai ni amɛgbɛɔ hela ko ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ amɛshwãa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ samla shwie baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye nɔ.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines to wooden sticks as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to build energy and produce big tubers underground. Staking holds the vines up high so they catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Okɛ wain tso lɛ awo ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni onine ashɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the middle of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, a common pest in maize. Applying recommended biological controls like neem extract or targeted insecticides early saves the growing tip.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall asraafoi. ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa mli Akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛyeɔ wala yibii tamɔ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akɛtoɔ hiɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ tip ni miida lɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers during sudden dry spells or extreme heat. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulching around the roots helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛ baai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi trukaa loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ muji wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains specific nutrients and lets soil pests build up. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores soil health.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes cowpeas to grow leaves instead of flowers. Cowpeas fix their own nitrogen, so avoiding extra nitrogen fertilizer helps them produce more pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea lɛ baa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Tsinai lɛ diɛŋtsɛ saa amɛ nitrogen lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okpa nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-peas lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aba.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants curling up when the afternoon sun becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant conserve water and protect itself from drying out during intense heat.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha hulu la ni shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkagbi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ.

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the soil can absorb the moisture before the sun heats up. Watering in the hot afternoon causes most of the water to evaporate quickly before plant roots can drink it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu dani hulu lɛ adɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa oya dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: What is the best time of the day for me to harvest my crops so they stay fresh for the market?
ga: Mɛɛ gbi mli be hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni ehi shi ehee kɛha jara nɔ?

english: Harvesting early in the morning or late in the evening when temperatures are cool keeps the crops full of moisture. This stops them from wilting or spoiling quickly during storage and transport.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baatsi amɛnaa koni amɛkagbo oya loo amɛkafite yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ kɛyaa he kroko lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without producing any tomatoes during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing proper pollination. When flowers cannot be pollinated due to high temperatures, the plant drops them to conserve energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Be mli ni fɔfɔii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa hewɔ lɛ Tsei baashi fɔfɔii ni amɛgbele koni amɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: How can I keep my harvested vegetables fresh if the vehicle coming to take them to the market is delayed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-aduawai ni mikpa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ? Kɛji tsɔne ni kɛ bo yaa jara lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ etsɛ?

english: Keeping harvested produce in a shaded, well-ventilated area—or covering them with damp jute sacks—cools the produce down and slows down water loss, keeping them fresh until transport arrives.
ga: Nibii ni akpa lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ. Aloo okɛ jute kotoku ni mli efɔ aha nɔ. Enɛ baaha nibii ni adu lɛ afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaaha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Enɛ haa efeɔ ehee kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nibii ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ baashɛ.

english: How can I prevent my fresh peppers from rotting while transporting them in hot weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-chili hee lɛ naa koni ekafite beni mikɛyaa he kroko yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pack peppers in ventilated wooden crates or woven baskets instead of airtight plastic bags, and transport them during cooler hours like early morning or night to keep air circulating and reduce heat buildup.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo tso adekai ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli loo tsɛnsii ni akpɛ́ mli yɛ plastic kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ najiaŋ. kɛ gbɛfaa yɛ bei ni mli ejɔ tamɔ leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ mli. Koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni ekɛba dɔlɛ ni buaa ehe naa lɛ shi

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves—known as mulching—covers the bare ground like a blanket. This keeps the soil cool and stops water in the ground from evaporating quickly in the heat.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa he ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ nɔ tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji akɛ edɔ.

english: Does very hot weather make my vegetables get ready for harvest faster or slower than usual?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha mi-aduawai lɛ afee klalo kɛha kpamɔ mra loo sɛɛ mli fe bɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ?

english: Moderate heat can speed up crop growth, but excessively hot weather stresses the plant. Without enough water, high heat stops growth altogether or causes fruits to ripen prematurely while still small.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni sa baanyɛ aha tsei ada oya. Shi kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa aduawai lɛ dalɛ kpaa kwraa loo ehaa aduawai lɛ shwereɔ mra be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ.

english: Which vegetables can I plant that will grow well even when the sun is very strong and hot?
ga: Mɛɛ aduawai manyɛ madu ni baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu kɛ latsaa mli?

english: Crops like okro, cowpea, cassava, and hot peppers are naturally hardy. Their deep root systems or thick leaves allow them to resist heat stress better than delicate leafy greens like lettuce.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ okra, tsina ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni mli edɔ lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo baai ni mli tse lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ lettuce.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings die after I move them from the nursery into the open field sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Young seedlings have weak, shallow roots that cannot take up water fast enough to replace what strong sunlight evaporates. Providing light shade for a few days after transplanting gives their roots time to establish.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛye hulu la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ najiaŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo be ha gbii fioo komɛi yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná be ni amɛkɛbaatswa shishifãi.

english: Do I always need to buy chemical fertilizer to get a good harvest from my crops?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mahe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ be fɛɛ be koni maná yibii kpakpai kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fertilizer is not always required for every crop; often, protecting your plants from pests and diseases through proper and timely spraying is much more critical to preventing total crop loss.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tsei fɛɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, ehe miihia waa akɛ ooobu otsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ahe kɛtsɔ tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ nɔ fe ni oootsi ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ kwraa lɛ anaa.

english: If I have limited money, should I prioritize buying fertilizer or buying protective sprays for my crops?
ga: Kɛji shika fioo pɛ miyɔɔ lɛ Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahemɔ loo tsofa ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ hemɔ afee nɔ ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ?

english: Protecting your growing crops from being destroyed by pests should be your primary focus, because even well-fertilized crops will fail to give a harvest if insects or diseases ruin them.
ga: Esa akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ni okwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ahe ni ooobu he koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite lɛ afee nɔ ni okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ maa nɔ titri. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, anyɛŋ akpa tsei ni awo amɛ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ po kɛji kooloi loo helai kpata amɛhiɛ.

english: How do I know if I am spraying my crops properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ tsofa miifɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Proper spraying is about even coverage and correct application technique rather than soaking the plants with chemical; doing it accurately ensures maximum protection without wasting product.
ga: Nɔ ni fata tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he ji ni akɛha he daa kɛ gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛtsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ tsofai baafɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa abuɔ he jogbaŋŋ ni afiteee nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: Is a small volume of chemical, like two gallons, really enough to protect my field?
ga: Ani tsofa fioo ko, tamɔ galɔn enyɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa diɛŋtsɛ ni baabu miŋmɔji lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, many crop protection sprays do not require large volumes to be effective; using just two gallons applied correctly can adequately shield your growing plants from damage.
