ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai babaoo ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe lɛ biɔ ni akɛ babaoo awo mli dani etsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Galɔn enyɔ pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ abu tsei ni miida lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ fitemɔ he.

english: Can applying too much spray liquid actually harm my crops instead of helping them?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ babaoo ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua amɛ?

english: Yes, crops do not need heavy or excessive chemical application; using only the required small quantity protects the plant while preventing chemical damage and saving you money.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii biɔ ni akɛ tsofai atsu nii babaoo loo akɛtsu nii fe nine. Kɛ́ okɛ fioo pɛ tsu nii taakɛ atsɔɔ lɛ lɛ, ebaabu otso lɛ he yɛ be mli ni ebaatsi tsofai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ anaa, ni ebaaha okɛ shika akafite.

english: Why is spraying necessary if my crops already appear to be growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsofa afɔ nɔ kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ momo lɛ?

english: Even healthy, growing crops can be suddenly destroyed by unseen pests and diseases; spraying acts as a safeguard to ensure the crops reach maturity safely.
ga: Kooloi kɛ helai ni anaaa amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ po. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela naa koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara shweshweeshwe.

english: What is the best way to prevent my growing crops from being completely destroyed before harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ atsĩ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ anaa koni ekafite kwraa dani akpa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: The most effective method is active crop protection through properly measured spraying, which keeps destructive pests away while the crops are actively growing.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni asusuɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ.

english: At what stage do my crops need protection the most?
ga: Mɛɛ be ehe hiaa ni abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe fe fɛɛ?

english: Crops need ongoing protection while they are actively growing, as young and developing plants are most vulnerable to attack and destruction.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe be fɛɛ be be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bibii kɛ tsei ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni tutuamɔ kɛ hiɛkpatamɔ baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ fe fɛɛ.

english: Can I grow crops like corn and beans together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, you can cultivate multiple crops such as corn and beans together, which helps maximize space and land productivity while both crops grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa afee ekome. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ kɛ yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ be mli ni tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ daraa lɛ.

english: How do I manage care and protection when I have multiple different crops growing together?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ mihe kɛ mihebuu nɔ? Beni mikɛ tsei srɔtoi babaoo feɔ ekome lɛ

english: When growing diverse crops like corn and beans together, monitor the health of each crop type and use protective spraying carefully so all plants remain safe from pests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ he kome, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni tso henɔ fɛɛ tso henɔ yɔɔ ha. ni okɛ tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ Bɔni afee ni tsei fɛɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under direct sunlight and high heat. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them to protect them from burning and to keep moisture in the soil until their roots grow deep.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ la ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb tall wooden stakes to produce big tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji aba lɛ?

english: Yam leaves make food for the plant using sunlight. Staking lifts the vines so the leaves get maximum sunlight, which allows the plant to produce and send energy down to swell the yam tuber beneath the ground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ nibii ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shi koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow at the bottom when the plants are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the maize is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow strong; adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure early will fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli mra lɛ baaye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why does planting beans alongside my maize make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This acts as a natural plant food that improves soil fertility for nearby plants like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they feel stressed, usually from extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer which forces the plant to grow leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛnu he akɛ amɛmiifee basaa. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ewo baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers grow very thin and produce tiny bunches when planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ amli tsei waa ni amɛmli etse amɛhe bibii lɛ? Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe

english: When plantain suckers are planted too close, their large leaves block sunlight from each other and their roots fight for nutrients and water, leaving them without enough energy to produce heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaai wuji lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii ni tsii lɛ bɛ.

english: Why are there small holes in the leaves and dirt like sawdust in the center of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni muji tamɔ ŋmei yɛ mibi lɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides and feeds inside the growing center of the maize plant. Checking crops early and applying appropriate control methods protects the growing shoot.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmei tso ni miida lɛ teŋgbɛ ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Kɛ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I spray my tomato plants with chemical pesticides while they are flowering in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi leebi lɛ?

english: Bees visit open flowers in the morning to pollinate them so that fruits can form. Spraying chemicals during this time kills the helpful bees, leading to fewer tomatoes on your harvest.
ga: Wuobii yasaraa fɔfɔi ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ leebi koni amɛyawo amɛmli koni amɛwo yibii. Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baagbe ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tomatoi fioo pɛ baa okpamɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if a cassava stem cutting is healthy enough to sprout properly when I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei tso ni afo lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu lɛ?

english: Healthy cassava cuttings should come from strong, mature plants that are 8 to 12 months old, free from insect holes or stem rot, and show a fresh green color beneath the bark when lightly scratched.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afolɔ lɛ ajɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni edara ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12, ni kooloi akutsei loo amɛshishifãi lɛ egboi bɛ mli lɛ amli. ni etsɔɔ su ni mli tse yɛ ŋshɔŋ lɛ shishi kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ fioo.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetable crops with dry grass keep them green during hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass (mulching) blocks direct heat from evaporation, keeps the soil moist and cool, and stops weeds from growing and stealing crop nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulching) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekaho. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkaju tsei amli niyenii.

english: If I see yellow or spotted leaves on a few of my cassava plants, should I cut them off or leave them?
ga: Kɛji mina baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmei tsei komɛi anɔ lɛ Ani esa akɛ mafo mli loo mashi mli?

english: Cutting off diseased leaves early stops the sickness from spreading to the rest of the plant or neighboring crops, preventing the disease from taking over your entire farm.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa hei krokomɛi. tsei ahe loo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Enɛ baatsi hela naa koni ekaye oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why is a plant disease from my neighbor's farm suddenly showing up on my crops this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso hela ko ni jɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli lɛ ba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ trukaa afi nɛɛ?

english: Crop diseases easily travel across neighboring farms through wind, splashing rain, insects, or shared farm tools, especially during wet seasons.
ga: Tsei ahe helai baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kooloi bibii, loo okwaayeli nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ amli kɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli oya. Titri lɛ, yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: Why is it dangerous to ignore a plant sickness when it first starts on a few leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaaku hiɛ ashwie tsei ahe helai anɔ beni klɛŋklɛŋ okadii lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ baai fioo komɛi anɔ lɛ?

english: Once a disease takes full hold of a plant, it gets into the plant's internal system, making it untreatable and causing the plant to die and infect surrounding crops.
ga: Kɛ hela lɛ ye tso lɛ nɔ kwraa lɛ Ebaabote tso lɛ mligbɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli. ni haaa anyɛ atsa ni ekɛ tsei gboiɔ kɛ helai baa tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli.

english: What should I do to the stem of my cocoa tree after cutting off a diseased branch?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishigbɛ beni mifolɔ niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: After cutting away diseased branches, you should apply wood ash or an approved fungicide to the cut area to seal the wound so new infections and insects cannot enter while it heals.
ga: Kɛji ofo tso niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Esa akɛ okɛ tso sũ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ awo he ni ofo lɛ koni ekɛtsi naa. Koni atsĩ helai kɛ kooloi heei anaa Obaanyɛ obote mli be mli ni etsaa lɛ.

english: What should I do with the infected branches and leaves after I prune them from my crops?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee tsei niji kɛ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should burn or deeply bury infected plant cuttings away from your farm so wind and rain do not carry the disease back onto your healthy plants.
ga: Esa akɛ oshã loo ofu tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ ji koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ akakɛ hela aba tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Can using my cutlass on a sick plant spread sickness to my healthy plants?
ga: Ani mi-dagger ni mikɛtsu nii yɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã mitsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, plant sap containing fungi or bacteria sticks to your cutlass blade, so you should clean your tools with soapy water or ash between plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni yɔɔ ŋmei loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ nu loo sũ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ atsumɔ dɛŋdade lɛ he.

english: Why do my maize crops keep performing poorly every year even though I plant them in the same place?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ he kome moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously in the same soil drains specific plant nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa tso lɛ mli hewalɛ nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How can I tell if my plant leaves are changing color because of disease rather than heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela hewɔ ni mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsake amɛhe moŋ fe dɔlɛ hewɔ?

english: Heat stress causes uniform wilting across the farm, while diseases usually create irregular spots, patches, mold, or yellow patterns on specific plants.
ga: Dɔlɛ he haomɔ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ shwieɔ shi. Yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto baa tsei komɛi anɔ lɛ.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to check on the health of my crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ha?

english: You should inspect your farm at least once or twice a week, checking under leaves and stems so you can catch early signs of disease before it spreads.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ baai kɛ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ nibii ni akwɛɔ lɛ nɔ koni onyɛ ona hela he okadii mra dani egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do crops near the edge of my farm usually get sick first before the ones in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ yeɔ hela dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ baa lɛ?

english: The edges of your farm are the first line of contact for pests, wind-borne spores, and diseases coming from surrounding bushes or neighboring farms.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ naagbeehei lɛ ji klɛŋklɛŋ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛbaa. Spores ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ helai ni jɛɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe loo ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli baa lɛ.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has from its old lower leaves up to nourish the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni amɛyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛkɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds once the rains begin in my area?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ madu dumɔwui kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Wait until the soil stays moist down to at least a hand's depth after two or three steady rains. Planting immediately after the very first light drizzle often causes seeds to germinate and then dry out and die.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashɛ he ko ni kɛ hoo lɛ, eshɛɔ tso nine kome yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Which way up should I put cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛji oodu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ mikɛ ŋmei niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Plant cassava cuttings with the leaf buds pointing upwards toward the sky, either straight or slanted. If you plant them upside down, the shoots struggle to grow upward and root production will be poor.
ga: Dumɔ ŋmei niji ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji edamɔ shi shiŋŋ loo etsɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Tsoi lɛ baaná naagba yɛ amɛdalɛ mli ni shishifãi lɛ afeemɔ baafee nɔ ni ehiii.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from heat stress, lack sufficient shade, or lack water during dry spells. It can also happen if tiny insects called midges are not present in the farm to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Shade ni sa ni bɛ loo nu ni bɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji kooloi bibii bɛ jɛmɛ. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge yɛ ŋmɔji amli koni ekɛwo fɔfɔi amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Sudden wilting is usually caused by soil-borne fungal diseases or viruses spread by tiny whiteflies. These block the veins inside the plant's stem, preventing water from traveling up to the leaves regardless of how much water you pour on the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tsɛŋemɔ hela bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa trukaa. Enɛɛmɛi tsiɔ lá fãji ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ anaa. Enɛ baaha nu akashɛ baai lɛ ahe bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni oooshwie nu babaoo oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: If I pack my crops closer together, will I harvest more food from my land?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani manyɛ makpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition results in thin stems, smaller fruits, higher disease risks, and a smaller total harvest overall.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa anáa tsei bibii. Yibii lɛ daraaa. Hela he oshara ni yɔɔ lɛ fa babaoo. ni kpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ falɛ faaa

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster on my farm than the crops I deliberately planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni mito he gbɛjianɔ akɛ makwɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to the local environment, with deep root systems built to grab water and soil nutrients instantly. Domestic crops need extra care because they are bred for fruit or grain production rather than wild survival.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Eyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni ama koni ekɛgbala nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shia tsei biɔ hiɛdɔɔ krɛdɛɛ ejaakɛ akwɛɔ amɛ koni amɛwo yibii loo ŋmaa moŋ fe ni amɛhi shi yɛ koo lɛ mli.

english: Why is my farm giving me far less crop yield today than it produced three years ago on the same soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ miiha mi ŋmɔshi nibii fioo kwraa fe nɔ ni ewo afii etɛ ni eho nɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing crops on the exact same plot every year drains specific food nutrients out of the earth without replacing them. Over time, the soil becomes tired and worn out unless you add manure, compost, or fertilizer, or rotate crops.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ amɛ tsakeee. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ni efite ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsake.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing big and leafy but not growing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai lɛ? Shi ani ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ?

english: Applying too much chemical nitrogen fertilizer makes pepper plants put all their energy into building large green leaves instead of flowers and fruit. Extreme heat during flowering can also cause the buds to drop before fruiting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni ji nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha pepper tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbo dani aduawai lɛ aba.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my main crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that extract nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil through small nodules on their roots. This naturally adds free plant food to the dirt that neighboring crops can feed on.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii fataa shikpɔŋ ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant them in straight rows with exact spacing instead of scattering the seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko yɔɔ amɛteŋ lɛ? Yɛ dumɔwui adumɔ najiaŋ?

english: Planting in straight lines gives each crop enough space to get sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without fighting its neighbors, making weeding and harvesting much easier.
ga: Tso ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ ená hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ awuu. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why does cassava planted in a neighboring village yield bigger tubers than the same cassava on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni adu yɛ akrowa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji fe ŋmei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different villages have different soil types, moisture levels, and local climates. Crops respond differently to local ecological conditions even if you use the exact same planting method.
ga: Akrowai srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi kɛ hulutsoo be srɔtoi. kɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ maŋ lɛ mli shihilɛi srɔtoi ahe nii. Kɛji akɛ okɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii po.

english: Why do agriculture technicians visit our village to collect data and soil samples before telling us what to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nilelɔi yaa wɔ akrowai lɛ amli koni amɛyabua saji kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii anaa dani amɛtsɔɔ wɔ nɔ ni esa akɛ wɔdu lɛ?

english: Technicians collect data to measure soil nutrients and local weather patterns, allowing science to give you farming recommendations tailored specifically to your village rather than relying on guesswork.
ga: Ŋaa he nilelɔi buaa saji anaa koni amɛkɛsusu shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe. Ehaa jeŋ nilee haa okwaayeli he ŋaawoo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ pɔtɛɛ aha okrowa lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ohe afɔ̃ susumɔi ni asusuɔ he lɛ anɔ

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and curl up when there is no rain for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko otsii fioo komɛi nɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are the plant's defense mechanism against drought, showing that it is conserving water and lacking the nitrogen it needs to stay green.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ji tso ko gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ he. Atsɔɔ akɛ tsei buɔ nu he, ni amɛbɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli.

english: Why are extension officers advising me to plant new certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ madu dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ dumɔwuhi nɛ je ngma kpami nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ kɛ to.

english: Certified seeds are scientifically bred to resist local pests, tolerate harsh weather, and produce higher yields compared to old seeds that lose their vigor over time.
ga: Akɛ jeŋ nilee ekwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa ni ekɛ yibiiwoo babaoo baa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui momo ni hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers during very hot dry weather without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa wooo mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes severe stress to the plant, making it drop its flowers to conserve energy and water for basic survival rather than spending resources on fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tsei anɔ. Ha tsei agbee shi koni akɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ato kɛha shishijee wala. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite nibii yɛ aduawai ahe lɛ

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my crops while the seedlings are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ darako kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are weak; removing weeds early stops them from stealing sunlight, water, and fertilizer away from your growing crops.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju hulu la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ otsei ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with tall wooden poles for them to give a good yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ awo tsei kakadaji anɔ koni maná ŋmaa kpakpa lɛ?

english: Lifting yam leaves off the ground with stakes allows them to capture maximum sunlight, which the plant converts into energy to expand the tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tso wo sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. ni tso lɛ tsakeɔ efeɔ hewalɛ koni ekɛgbala ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli

english: Why does my land produce a smaller harvest when I plant maize on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season; rotating crops restores soil health and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni ehaa helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ kpaa.

english: Why should I wait for the soil to be moist before applying fertilizer to my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so the plant roots can drink it in; applying it to dry soil can burn the crop roots or blow away in the wind.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso shishifãi lɛ ashã loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atswa amɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to grow strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea will help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops look dried and burnt after I apply chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi ni eshã beni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ewo mli lɛ?

english: Using too much fertilizer or placing it directly against the stem draws water out of the plant roots, causing leaf burn. Fertilizer should be applied in small, measured amounts a few centimeters away from the plant stem.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ shishi loo okɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbala nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai ni shãa Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli fioo fioo, ni ekɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimita fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when I clear all the tall trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ? Mashi miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh sunlight and drying winds. Leaving taller trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains creates a cool, moist environment that helps young cocoa survive.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni aaashi loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa kookoo bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch sunlight, which fuels the growth of the tubers underground. Staking also keeps the foliage off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe. ni ji tsofa ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ daraa lɛ Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ anaa koni ekashwɛ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: When seeds are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough space to build deep roots and produce bigger fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ baa ni ewoɔ yibii loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry stretch before the main rainy season settles in. Seeds planted too early may germinate and then dry up and die from lack of follow-up rain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: What is making ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown powder in the center whorl?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni amɛshiɔ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana. Inspecting your field early and spraying with recommended organic or chemical insecticides keeps them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ. Nibii ni odu lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra kɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni akafite tip ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and produce very small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital nutrients, water, and sunlight that your main crops need. Clearing weeds early in the growing season ensures your crops get all the soil resources.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa ni tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ taoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mra yɛ be mli ni okwɛ̃ɔ lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ amɛshikpɔŋ nɔ nibii fɛɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot, when the soil dries out suddenly, or when insects fail to pollinate the blooms. Consistent watering and light mulching help protect the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ trukaa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli fioo lɛ baaye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell that my cassava is mature and ready to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efoŋ?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 8 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and cracks appear in the soil around the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act like umbrellas, providing shade and cool moisture that cocoa trees need in their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo tsei yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Yellowing and curling cassava leaves are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stems for planting helps keep your farm safe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii kɛdu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oŋmɔ lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the ground. Leguminous crops like groundnuts and cowpeas put nitrogen back into the soil through their roots, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhaa nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha okwɛ̃mɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very thin and fall over when I put three or four seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛmiigbee shi beni mikɛ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. This competition makes the stalks grow weak and tall, causing them to fall over easily during heavy wind or rain.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ shwiili. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ebaagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔ nɛ waa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves droop during the afternoon heat even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ?

english: In the hot sun, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull water up from the soil. The leaves wilt temporarily to protect the plant from drying out, but they bounce back in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni tso lɛ akagbi. Shi efoɔ esɛɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing tall with dark green leaves but dropping all their flowers without giving me peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa kɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa shi efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Giving your crops too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant spend all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of fruit. A balanced fertilizer encourages the plant to hold flowers and form peppers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai kɛ ŋmeii amli yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why should I pinch off the small extra shoots growing in the leaf joints of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tsei ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers, waste the plant's food and water on growing extra branches. Removing them forces the plant to send its nutrients directly into growing larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii bibii. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ afite niyenii kɛ nu kɛ niji ni fata he lɛ. Tomato lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa tomato ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some cobs on my maize field have missing kernels instead of full rows of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi yɛ ŋmeii ni elaaje yɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Missing kernels happen when pollen from the top tassel fails to land on the soft silks of the cob during dry or windy spells. Every silk must receive dust-like pollen for a single corn kernel to develop.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji akɛ pollen ni jɛ ŋwɛi ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ ŋmeii lɛ a-silki ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi loo kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ. Esa akɛ siliki ŋmei fɛɛ ŋmei aná pollen ni tamɔ sũ koni enyɛ ekɛ ŋmei dumɔwu kome aba.

english: Why does leaving cut weeds on top of the soil help my crops survive the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaving dead leaves or cut grass on top of the earth creates a protective blanket called mulch. This blanket blocks the sun from drying out the dirt, traps soil moisture, and keeps crop roots cool.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi baai ni egboi loo jwɛi ni afo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Kuntu nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni ehaaa muji agbi. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Why do my yam tubers start sprouting shoots and shrinking after sitting in the barn for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ bɔi shweremɔ ni egbɔjɔ beni mita ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that wake up after a period of rest. They begin using up the water and nutrients stored inside themselves to grow new shoots, which causes the yam to shrink and lose weight.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi kɛ́ amɛjɔɔ amɛhe be ko sɛɛ. Amɛjeɔ shishi amɛkɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni ato yɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii heei. Enɛ haa sweet potato lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh sunshine while their roots develop. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or leaving larger trees provides the shelter and humidity cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains loo tsei wuji ni ashiɔ amɛma shi lɛ, ebaaha kookoo lɛ aná nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam plants are vines that need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to sun and preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni biɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Shi ni hulu la lɛ ashɛ nɔ ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why do my crops produce very small harvest when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water and nutrients in the soil, while their leaves block each other from getting sunlight, resulting in weak plants with smaller yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ tsiɔ enaa koni hulu la akashɛ enɔ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for green growth. It can also happen when weeds surround the crop and steal nutrients from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ jwɛi bɔle ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni amɛju niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When fields stay flooded with excess water, air is pushed out of the soil, causing the tubers to suffocate, decay, and rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine eyi ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ, anyɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi, egboɔ ni egboɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt during the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛgbi moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During intense afternoon heat, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can pull water from the soil. They temporarily wilt to conserve water and normally recover in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni amɛto nu he gbɛjianɔ be kukuoo ko, ni amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures become too high, or when they experience water stress or lack key nutrients. Without stable conditions, the plant cannot support fruit development.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ ekɛ nu he haomɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii titrii ni bɛ lɛ kpe. Kɛji shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Curled or twisted pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, which spread plant viruses and drain the plant's sap as they feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa ni ebɔle ehe loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tsei amli ni ehaa tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ hoɔ beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the earth. When the plant bears heavy fruit bunches and the soil gets wet and soft, wind can easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ bɔdɔɔ lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo

english: Planting the same crop continuously consumes the exact same nutrients from the soil season after season, leaving the soil exhausted. It also allows specific pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aaakwɛ nɔ aya nɔ lɛ biɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ. Ehaa kooloi kɛ helai komɛi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and die when I clear all the shade trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct harsh sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out soil moisture quickly. Keeping taller shade trees like plantains or timber trees protects the young cocoa plants while their roots grow strong.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo tsei bibii lɛ akwɛmɔ baaye abua ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava sticks too close to each other in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛɔ he tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting cassava too close causes the plants to fight with each other for space, sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leads to thin stems and small tubers instead of big, healthy roots.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu yɛ ŋwɛi, hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii he. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa yɛ shishifãi wuji ni mli wa najiaŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up tightly into tubes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni efeɔ tsɔne ko yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural defense to save water. By rolling its leaves, the maize reduces the surface area exposed to the sun and heat, preventing too much water from evaporating from the leaves.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ baashɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ nu babaoo naa koni ekajɛ baai lɛ amli.

english: Pepper flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there is too much rain. This stress stops the flower from turning into fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ shigbeemɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ baatsi fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkatsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my tomato plants rot at the bottom of the fruit before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miifite yɛ shishigbɛ dani etsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or irregular watering. When soil moisture fluctuates between very wet and very dry, the plant cannot move calcium to the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli be fɛɛ be. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli egbi waa teŋ lɛ Tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛya aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do people say it is good to plant groundnuts or cowpeas together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ehi akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baadu ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which can trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds the maize growing alongside it.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas fata legume weku lɛ he, ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eha ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. Nitrogen helps plants make food, and when there isn't enough in the soil, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has from old bottom leaves to feed new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni kɛ́ nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ jieɔ nitrogen fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops even when they both sprout at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛdaraa yɛ be kome mli?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that have naturally adapted over time to grow aggressively and grab water, light, and nutrients faster than farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli koni amɛdara oya ni amɛhe nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei.

english: Why did half of the maize seeds I bought from the local open market fail to grow after I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mihe yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe ni agbele naa lɛ mli lɛ fã edaaa beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds sold in open markets may be old, damaged by heat and humidity, or infested with tiny insects. Using certified seeds from registered agrodealers ensures high germination rates.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ etsɛ. Akɛni dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efite hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni jɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa shweremɔ yaa hiɛ waa.

english: How can I tell underground if my cassava tubers are mature enough for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava shows signs of maturity above ground when its lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the main stem starts to crack as the expanding tubers push against the earth.
ga: Cassava jieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ he okadii akpo kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii ni dara lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Is there a ready market in Ghana if I decide to grow oil palm on my land?
ga: Ani jarayeli ko ni yɔɔ klalo yɛ Ghana kɛji mikpɛ miyiŋ akɛ makwɛ mu tso yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, Ghana has many active processing refineries that require a constant supply of palm fruit to produce cooking oil and soaps, creating strong local demand for your harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, Ghana yɛ nitsumɔhei babaoo ni tsuɔ nii ni biɔ ŋmei yibii be fɛɛ be koni akɛfee niyenii ni akɛhooɔ fɔ kɛ samla. Enɛ haa mɛi biɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Which cash crops in Ghana have guaranteed local buyers so my produce doesn't go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ haa maŋ lɛ mli nihɔɔlɔ ko naa nɔmimaa koni minibii ni miduɔ lɛ akafee yaka?

english: Crops like oil palm and sugarcane have reliable local demand because domestic refineries and factories continuously buy them in bulk to turn into processed goods.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei fɔ kɛ ŋmei yɛ nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nitsumɔhei ni tsuɔ tsofai ahe nii kɛ nitsumɔhei ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ miihe nɛkɛ tsofai nɛɛ babaoo be fɛɛ be koni amɛkɛfee nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii.

english: Why is selling my harvest to a local factory better than selling at the open market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni minibii ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ ni mikɛbaahɔ̃ɔ maŋ lɛ mli nitsumɔhe ko lɛ hi fe ni mikɛbaahɔɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Factories and refineries buy produce in large quantities at steady rates year-round, whereas open village markets often experience seasonal price drops when everyone harvests at the same time.
ga: Nitsumɔhei kɛ dãatɔɔhei hɔɔ nibii babaoo yɛ nyɔmɔwoo pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ akrowai amli jarayeli hei ni agbele naa lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ be mli ni jara ni baa shi lɛ hewɔ beni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ kpaɔ nii yɛ be kome mli lɛ.

english: How long does it take for an oil palm tree to start producing fruits I can sell?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mu tso ko jeɔ yibii ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ shishi?

english: Modern high-yield oil palm varieties begin producing fruit bunches within 3 to 4 years after planting and can remain productive for over 25 years.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ mu tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ jeɔ yibii bibii ahe shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛwoɔ yibii fe afii 25.

english: Does sugarcane require a lot of water to grow thick enough for sugar processing?
ga: Ani nu babaoo he miihia ŋmei koni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛtsu sugar he nii?

english: Yes, sugarcane needs consistent moisture and plenty of water during its growing phase to build up the thick, juice-filled stalks that refineries buy.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ nu babaoo yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli tse ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni distilleries heɔ lɛ.

english: Can I grow cassava or maize between my young oil palm trees while waiting for them to mature?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ mu tsei ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yes, while young oil palm trees are small, you can intercrop food crops like maize or cassava between the rows to generate income and food during the first few years.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ mu tsei lɛ darako lolo moŋ. Obaanyɛ odu niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. linei lɛ ateŋ koni akɛná shika kɛ niyenii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli

english: What quality standard do processing factories look for in oil palm fruits?
ga: Mɛɛ shishitoo mlai ni hi jogbaŋŋ nitsumɔhei ni feɔ mu tso yibii lɛ taoɔ?

english: Refineries look for fully ripe, undamaged fruit bunches where a few loose fruits have naturally fallen off, as these contain the highest amount of oil.
ga: Nitsumɔhei ni feɔ wain lɛ taoɔ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee. kɛ aduawai komɛi ni shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa Ejaakɛ eyɛ fɔ babaoo fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do factory buyers want sugarcane delivered immediately after it is cut?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ nitsumɔhei lɛ miisumɔ ni akɛ sugar cane aba amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni afo lɛ?

english: Once sugarcane is cut, its internal sugar breaks down quickly, so delivering it rapidly ensures the highest sugar extraction yield and best price for your crop.
ga: Kɛ́ afo ŋmei lɛ Sugar ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, oyaiyeli ni akɛhaa lɛ haa anáa sugar ni fa fe fɛɛ kɛ jara ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Can I keep my harvested oil palm fruit bunches on the farm for a couple of weeks before selling?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ mu tsei ni akpa lɛ ato ŋmɔ lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: No, palm fruits begin to ferment and spoil within a few days of harvest, which lowers the oil quality, so they should be delivered to processors within 24 to 48 hours.
ga: Dabi, palm yibii lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ni efiteɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha mu lɛ mli kpakpa lɛ aba shi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛya tsɔne ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ ŋɔɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 mli.

english: How do I make sure I don't waste money transporting my harvested crops to buyers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mifiteee shika ni mikɛ mikpamɔ lɛ baaya mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Because processing factories operate in several regions across Ghana, you can arrange sales before harvest or sell directly to local collection agents who transport the produce for you.
ga: Enɛ ji akɛ, nitsumɔhei ni feɔ nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ kpokpai babaoo anɔ yɛ Ghana fɛɛ. Obaanyɛ oto jarayeli he gbɛjianɔ dani akpa ŋmɔshi nibii loo ohɔ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ oha maŋ lɛ mli nitoohe ni kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahã bo lɛ.

english: Why do mushrooms grow on my dead cassava stumps after it rains, and are they bad for my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmei tsei ni egboi anɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ? Ni ani ehiii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Mushrooms belong to a group called fungi. Unlike normal crops, they cannot make their own food from sunshine, so they feed on dead plant materials like old stumps, breaking them down into rich nutrients for your soil.
ga: Mushroom fata kuu ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ fungi lɛ he. Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ tsei krokomɛi lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii kɛjɛ hulu la mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ tsei ni egboi, tamɔ tsei akutsei ni egbɔ, koni amɛgbala mli ni amɛfee niyenii ni fa babaoo kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: What is the white powdery coating spreading on my pepper leaves, and where does it come from?
ga: Mɛni ji nakai powda yɛŋ ni akɛwo mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ni nɛgbɛ ejɛ?

english: That powdery coating is a fungal disease. Fungi travel as tiny, invisible seeds called spores through the wind or water drops, and they settle on damp leaves to grow, blocking sunlight and weakening your plants.
ga: Powda ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli baa. Fungi fãa gbɛ akɛ dumɔwui bibii. Spores ni anaaa, ni atsɛɔ amɛ spores lɛ tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nu mli nu mli. Ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ baai ni efɔ lɛ ahe koni amɛdara. Etsiɔ hulu la naa ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: I noticed white mold growing inside my compost heap, will it damage my farm if I mix it into the soil?
ga: Miyɔse akɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ miida yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ato lɛ mli. Kɛ́ mikɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ, ani ebaafite miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: No, that mold is actually helpful fungi hard at work breaking down dry leaves and manure into dark, rich plant food that will nourish your crops.
ga: Dabi, ŋmei ji ŋmei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ diɛŋtsɛ. koni etsu nii waa Efoɔ baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmeii amli ewoɔ tsei aniyenii ni yɔɔ ediŋ ni baaha onibii lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: When there is not enough food like nitrogen in the soil, the maize plant takes nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the young, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Beni niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Abɛi heɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves in intense heat to protect themselves from losing too much water through evaporation until the cool evening comes.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkafite nu babaoo kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni fɛ̃i be lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why do my okra plants keep dropping their flowers without producing any okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi ni ekɛ okra ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Okra drops flowers when the plant feels stressed by extreme heat or lack of water, or when insects like bees fail to visit and pollinate the flowers to form fruit.
ga: Rosella shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ emli lɛ mli. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ ayasara ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii kɛyashi amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do black spots appear and spread on my cocoa pods when the weather stays cold and wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo ni egbɛɔ eshwaa mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: Black spots are caused by black pod disease, a water-loving fungus that multiplies quickly during chilly, rainy weather and spreads from pod to pod through splashing water droplets.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni fɔɔ oya yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ pod kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli kɛtsɔɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot inside the ground when the rainy season gets too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Yam roots need air in the soil to survive. Excess rain fills up all air spaces in the soil, drowning the tubers and allowing harmful fungi in the dirt to attack and rot them.
ga: Sweet potato shishifãi hia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa bulb lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa amɛ ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why does witchweed attach itself to my maize roots and stop the maize from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ witchweed lɛ kpɛtɛɔ mi-abele shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaaa abele lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Witchweed, also known as striga, is a parasitic plant that cannot feed itself well. Its seeds wait in the soil until maize roots release chemical signals, then it attaches to steal water and nutrients directly from the maize.
ga: Witchweed, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ Striga lɛ ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli jogbaŋŋ. Edumɔwui lɛ mɛɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ shishifãi lɛ jieɔ tsofa okadi ko kpo. No sɛɛ lɛ, ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ he koni eju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: If I see strange organisms or spots growing on my crop leaves, does it always mean I must spray chemical medicine right away?
ga: Ni kɛji mina bɔɔ nii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ loo ŋmeii yɛ mitsei lɛ baai anɔ hu? Ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni mikɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Not always. Some organisms are harmless or even beneficial fungi that help your crop by attacking insect pests or breaking down dead leaf matter without harming the plant.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Nibii komɛi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni yeee mɔ awui loo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni amɛtutuaa amɛ loo baai ni egboi ni amɛgbeɔ ni amɛyeee tso lɛ awui lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do poultry feed factories in Ghana buy imported maize instead of buying from local farmers like me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi aniyenii ahe nitsumɔhei ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ heɔ ŋmãa ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ moŋ fe maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi tamɔ mi lɛ?

english: Poultry companies often buy imported maize because it arrives very dry, clean, and uniform in quality. Local maize can sometimes have high moisture or mold risks if not dried properly, which can make chickens sick. Improving your grain drying and cleaning helps meet their standards.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi akwɛmɔ nitsumɔhei lɛ heɔ ŋmãa ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ ejaakɛ ebaa ni egbi, ehe tse ni ehi jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be. Bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli loo eyɛ oshara akɛ ebaatsɔ ŋmãa kɛji agbiko lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha kooloi aná hela. Oŋmãa lɛ ni oooha egbi kɛ ehe saamɔ aya hiɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehiɔ shi yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ.

english: Is it profitable for me to clear a large land area like 10 acres just to plant maize for animal feed?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ baaba aha mi akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ wulu ko tamɔ acre 10 koni madu ŋmãa?

english: Planting a large acreage can increase your total profits because feed producers buy in large bulk quantities. However, it requires significant money upfront for seeds, fertilizer, and tractor services, so you should only scale up if you have enough capital and a reliable buyer lined up.
ga: Hei wuji ni oookwɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha sɛɛnamɔi fɛɛ ni onáa lɛ aya hiɛ ejaakɛ niyenii afeelɔi lɛ heɔ babaoo. Shi kɛlɛ, ebiɔ shika babaoo kɛtsɔ hiɛ kɛha dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ trakta nitsumɔi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ shika awo mli pɛ kɛji oyɛ shika ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ.

english: Which specific maize variety should I plant if I want to sell my crop to poultry farmers?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ esa akɛ makwɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni mahɔ̃ɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ maha mɛi ni kwɛɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ?

english: Poultry farmers generally prefer yellow maize varieties or high-protein hybrids because yellow maize gives egg yolks a rich color and provides good nutrition. Hybrid varieties like 'Obatanpa' or yellow feed maize yield well and attract commercial feed buyers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi alɛɛlɔi sumɔɔ ŋmãa henɔi ni ji yellow ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni protein babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Akɛni ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ haa ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ su ni mli wa kɛ niyenii kpakpa hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa tamɔ ‘Obatanpa’ loo ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ woɔ yibii kpakpai ni egbalaa jarayeli niyenii helɔi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crop plants need to grow green and bushy. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK at the right time will restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo NPK tsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with weak stems that fall over easily in high wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ, amɛgbeeɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight and grow thin and tall trying to stretch upwards. Giving plants proper spacing (around 75cm between rows and 25cm between plants) ensures strong stalks that withstand wind.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛbaatsɔ shwiili ni amɛkwɔ, ni amɛbaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgbala amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ he ko ni sa (aaafee 75 cm yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ kɛ 25 cm yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ amɛ.

english: Why do some of my harvested maize cobs have missing kernels or empty spaces at the tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi bɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ amɛnaagbee lɛ?

english: Empty cob tips happen when the crop lacks enough water or nutrients during the flowering stage when tassels release pollen. Dry spells or poor soil fertility during pollination prevent every silk on the cob from developing into a full grain.
ga: Cob naagbee ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ fɔfɔi be mli beni ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kwraa yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ siliki ŋmeii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ.

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil every season. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts the soil and allows pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ adu nii shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ fiteɔ, ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What is eating small holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants, and how will it affect my harvest?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ? Ni te ebaasa mikpamɔ lɛ he eha tɛŋŋ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms, small caterpillars that feed on tender young maize leaves. If not treated early with recommended pesticides or organic remedies, they can destroy the growing center of the plant and greatly reduce your grain yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ tsuuu he nii mra. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ ni amɛha ŋmaa yibiiwoo aba shi kwraa.

english: How can I tell if my harvested maize is dry enough to bag and sell without spoiling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mawo kotoku mli ni mahɔ̃ɔ ni efiteee?

english: You can test grain dryness by pressing a kernel hard with your thumbnail or using a moisture meter. If the kernel leaves a soft mark, it contains too much water. Grain must be dried until moisture is low (around 12-14%) so mold and fungi cannot grow during storage.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ egbi ha lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ amɛmɔmɔ waa nɔ. kɛ oshishifa loo okɛ moisture meter atsu nii Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ yɛ okadii ni yɔɔ blɛoo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu babaoo yɛ mli. Esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ mli kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi (aaafee 12-14%) bɔni afee ni ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa akakwɛ̃ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my stored maize turn white and powdery with tiny insects after a few months in the storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ futafuta ni eyɛ powder ni kooloi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Beni okɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ehi nitoohe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: This is caused by maize weevils that bore into kernels and lay eggs inside. If the storage room is warm, damp, or poorly ventilated, weevils hatch quickly and eat the grain from the inside out. Storing clean, dry grain in airtight bags or treating it with approved grain dust prevents this.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji akɛ, ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ nitoohe lɛ mli edɔ, edɔ, loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ oya ni amɛyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Dumɔwui ni he tse ni egbi ni akɛtoɔ vacuum kotokui amli loo akɛ dumɔwui amli sũ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ he nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: When maize lacks nitrogen in the soil, it moves available nutrients from older bottom leaves to feed new top leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps keep the whole plant green and healthy.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves, but the tubers underground remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium, the plant spends all its energy growing green leaves and stems instead of storing food in the underground roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when exposed to extreme heat, dry soil, or nutrient deficiencies, as the plant tries to save water and energy to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: If muddy, polluted water from a nearby galamsey site enters my farm, how will it affect my crops?
ga: Kɛji nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛ Galamsey ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ bote miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Te ebaaná miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Water contaminated by mining activity carries heavy mud and toxic chemicals that coat and damage plant roots. This prevents crops from absorbing clean water and nutrients, causing leaves to turn brown and plants to wither.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛɔ shika tsuru tsaa he nitsumɔi amli lɛ yɛ muji ni tsii kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni haa tsei shishifãi ahe ni efiteɔ amɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei akaŋɔ nu ni mli tse kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ asasu ni tso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in full sunlight without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sun. They need shade crops like plantains to shelter them, reduce heat stress, and keep moisture in the soil while their roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni amɛha amɛhe afee hulutsoo. Ha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli be mli ni shishifãi lɛ maa lɛ.

english: Why do I get smaller corn ears when I plant my maize seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyɛ ŋmãa toi bibii beni midu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Overcrowded maize plants compete heavily with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no individual plant with enough resources to produce large, healthy ears.
ga: Abɛi tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ waa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha efee toi wuji ni wa.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches even during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ nugbɔ be mli po lɛ?

english: Plantains need nutrient-rich soil and healthy roots to carry heavy fruit. Poor soil nutrients or root damage caused by pests in the soil prevent the tree from feeding a large bunch.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli kɛ shishifãi ni wa he miihia plantains koni ewo yibii ni tsii. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo shishifãi ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛbaa lɛ haaa tso lɛ aná niyenii babaoo.

english: Why do tiny young cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Koni amɛtsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods often shrivel due to a natural self-thinning process called cherelle wilt when the tree has too many pods, or from fungal infections like black pod disease during wet weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherry withering lɛ hewɔ, kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii babaoo. aloo kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling upward and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by a plant virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Affected leaves cannot produce enough food, causing the plant to stop growing well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Baai ni ena hela lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ehaa tsei kpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and die before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ miiho dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry up early when attacked by fungal diseases like leaf spot (anthracnose) or when roots lack water, which stops the tuber from growing to its full potential.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji ŋmeii helai tamɔ baa mli ŋmeii (anthracnose) tutua amɛ loo kɛji nu bɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ akadara kɛyashɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he.

english: Why do my newly planted cassava stems look completely dry and dead during the first few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ yucca tso ni midu ehee lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi kwraa ni egbo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings often shed leaves and look inactive after planting because they are focusing their energy underground to grow fresh roots before sending up green shoots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca ni afoɔ lɛ haa ebaai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni etsuuu nii beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkwɛ̃ shishifãi heei dani amɛtsuɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ.

english: Yellowing young maize leaves usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen or the roots are sitting in too much water, which stops the plant from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa bibii ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ nyɛŋ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves curl up and burn when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that dry out easily under intense heat; they need shade trees like plantains or shade nets to protect them while they establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo ŋshɔŋlooi ni buɔ amɛhe be mli ni amɛtoɔ shi lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when day or night temperatures get too high or when water is irregular, as the plant tries to save energy rather than make fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ shwane loo gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling into tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee bɔɔlu ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by small sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, or a virus spread by those insects, which stunts leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni haa baai lɛ kwɛɛɛ

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy rains and winds start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and heavy fruit heads, making them top-heavy; if soil becomes too soft from heavy rain, weak roots cannot hold the plant up.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ayitsei ni tsii. kɛ muji babaoo baa Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is my yam farm growing very bushy green leaves but small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes yam plants to put all their energy into leafy top growth above ground instead of sending nutrients down to swell the tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niyenii kpakpahi kɛ baa si konɛ e ha nɛ ngmlɛfia ɔmɛ a mi nɛ wa.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my maize for fresh eating compared to dry grain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa koni maye ehee? kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ ahe

english: Fresh maize is ready when the silk turns dark brown and kernels release milky juice when squeezed; dry grain maize requires the whole stalk and husk to dry completely on the field.
ga: Abɛi hee lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ siliki lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ jieɔ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛji akɛ amɔ mli. Abɛi ni egbi lɛ biɔ ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ agbi kwraa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow well even in poor soil where my maize fails?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii po nɔ ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen directly from the air and store it in their roots, allowing them to feed themselves even in nutrient-poor soil.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ amɛhe niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ nɔ lɛ po nɔ.

english: How can I use my smartphone and social media to show an extension officer what is eating my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mi-smartphone kɛ social media lɛ atsɔɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ nɔ ni yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Farmers can take clear photos of damaged leaves or pests and send them to WhatsApp groups or Facebook agriculture forums where officers can identify the problem remotely.
ga: Okwaafoi baanyɛ ajie baai loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe mfoniri ni mli ka shi faŋŋ. ni okɛmaje WhatsApp kui loo Facebook okwaayeli he kpeei, he ni onukpai lɛ baanyɛ ana naagbai kɛjɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my maize in straight lines instead of scattering the seeds everywhere on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã he fɛɛ he yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines helps you manage your farm row by row without getting overwhelmed. It allows you to give each plant enough space, weed easily, apply fertilizer directly where needed, and harvest efficiently without leaving any crops behind.
