ga: Dumɔ ni ooodu yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni onuuu he akɛ ogbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa onáa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tso fɛɛ tso. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ oya Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛ ehe miihia. ni amɛkpa nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛshiŋ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants start turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miije shishi amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen or that the farm has too much standing water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea in small, steady steps helps the leaves turn green and build strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii bibii tamɔ urea ni akɛfataa he. Daa lɛ ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni efee ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water stays trapped around them because the roots cannot breathe in soggy soil. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my pepper plants look stunted and stop growing after a big rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kpeteŋkpele ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away nutrients from the soil surface and hurt delicate roots, temporarily preventing pepper plants from feeding until the soil dries out and gentle fertilization is applied.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe ni eye shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ awui. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, anyɛɛɛ aha pepper tsei lɛ niyenii yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli blɛoo.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa trees dry up and drop during the dry Harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their leaves during Harmattan to protect themselves from losing water in the dry, hot wind. Providing temporary shade crops like plantain or shade trees keeps the air cool and moist around young cocoa.
ga: Kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ harmattan beaŋ. Koni obu ohe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ he. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni akɛhaa. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil lacks water during flowering, or if insects are not visiting to pollinate them. Regular watering keeps the plant steady during heat periods.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Be mli ni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii baaa ni amɛbafee pollination Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: What makes the tips of my yam vines turn brown and curl up during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato lɛ naji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔleɔ ehe yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Yam leaf curling and browning happen when intense sun heat drains moisture from the vine faster than the roots can drink, or when small pests like thrips attack the soft new leaves.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni jɛɔ mli lɛ jieɔ nu ni jɛɔ wain tso lɛ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips tutua baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of big leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi ŋmɔtɔi lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas produce excessive leaves instead of pods when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Beans make their own plant food from the air, so they do not need heavy nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas woɔ baai babaoo tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ kɛ́ nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Beans feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ tso niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii atsu nii.

english: Why should I clear weeds while my crops are still very small instead of waiting until they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo jwɛi be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ kɛyashi jwɛi lɛ aakwɛ̃?

english: Small crop plants are weak and cannot fight big weeds for sunlight, soil water, and manure. Removing weeds early gives your crops all the field resources so they can grow strong without stress.
ga: Nibii bibii ni aduɔ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi jwɛi wuji kɛha hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná ŋmɔ mli nibii fɛɛ. Enɛ baaha amɛdara ni amɛhe awa ni haomɔ ko bɛ amɛhe.

english: How does leaving old crop stems and leaves on the soil after harvest help my next planting?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tso shishifãi kɛ baai ni mashi yɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua mi yɛ midumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Leaving dry plant material on top of the soil acts like a cool blanket that stops sunlight from drying out the ground, stops rain from washing the soil away, and slowly rots into natural fertilizer.
ga: Tsei ahe nibii ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni haa hulu lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa nugbɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving the young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps them turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means they can pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. This naturally feeds the surrounding soil and provides free fertilizer for your maize crop.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa o-corn tsei lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: What causes small insects to gather under my pepper leaves and make them curl up?
ga: Mɛni haa kooloi bibii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ ashishi ni ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Those small insects are aphids that suck juices from the leaves. You can spray them with a mixture of mild soapy water or neem leaf extract to wash them off and protect your crop.
ga: Nakai kooloi bibii lɛ ji ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ ni mli ejɔ afɔ nɔ. loo Neem tso lɛ mli nu ni okɛbaatsu nii ni okɛbu onibii ahe.

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, their roots fight over water and food in the soil, which leaves you with many small, thin tubers instead of big, heavy cassava roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ efee ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmei bibii babaoo yɛ ŋmei shishifãi wuji ni tsii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning dark and rotten before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused when the plant cannot get enough calcium because the soil keeps drying out. Watering your tomatoes regularly and evenly helps stop this from happening.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato lɛ nɔ daa kɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni enɛ akafee.

english: How can I test if the maize seeds I saved from last harvest are still good for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ hi lolo kɛha dumɔ?

english: Wrap ten seeds in a wet cloth and keep it damp for four days. If at least eight of them sprout roots, then your batch of seeds is strong and ready to plant in the field.
ga: Okɛ mama ni mli efɔ abɔ dumɔwui 10 he ni oha ehi shi gbii ejwɛ. Kɛji kɛ hoo lɛ dumɔwui kpaanyɔ kwɛ̃ shishifãi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ odumɔwui akuu lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni efee klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Is it better to burn the dried grass on my field or leave it on top of the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ loo mashi yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Leaving dry grass on top of the soil keeps the ground cool, traps moisture during dry spells, and slowly breaks down into natural food for your crops, whereas burning destroys important soil nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi jwɛi ni egbi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni efiteɔ fiofio akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii. yɛ be mli ni shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my cucumber vines falling off without producing any cucumbers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ kukumba wain tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni kukumba ko kwraa wooo lɛ?

english: Cucumber plants produce male flowers first, which naturally drop off. If female flowers are dropping too, it usually means bees are not coming around to spread pollen, or the plants need more water.
ga: Kukumba tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii klɛŋklɛŋ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Kɛji fɔfɔi yei lɛ gbee shi Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii bɛ jɛmɛ koni amɛgbɛ pollen amɛshwã. loo tsei he miihia nu babaoo

english: How do I know the exact right time to dig up my yam tubers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafo sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: When the leaves and vines of your yam plant turn yellow and completely dry up, it means the plant has stopped growing and has stored all its energy into the tuber underground, making it ready for harvest.
ga: Beni sweet potato tso lɛ baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, sweet potato tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. koni amɛkɛsaa amɛhe kɛha nikpamɔ

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and showing holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee bu lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves with holes are often caused by pests like the fall armyworm feeding on the plant, or a lack of nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, plants cannot make green chlorophyll to photosynthesize.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms ni yeɔ tso lɛ loo nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ bu lɛ baa. Kɛji nitrogen faaa lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ afee klorofil eŋɔli kɛha fotosintɛsis.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. They need partial shade from larger trees like plantain or forest trees to keep the air humid and protect their leaves from burning until their roots mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei amli. koni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ baadara kwraa.

english: How do I know if my soil is ready for planting cassava after the dry season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaadu ŋmei yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Soil is ready when the rain has soaked deep enough so that a handful of soil forms a soft ball without sticking like heavy clay or crumbling like dry sand. Loose, moist soil allows cassava roots to penetrate easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni efee sũ ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo bɔɔlu. Ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo etseee tamɔ ŋã ni egbi. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni etse ehe lɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ boteɔ mli mlɛo.

english: Will planting cowpea together with my maize steal food from the maize plants?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmeii ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baadu lɛ baaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli?

english: No, leguminous crops like cowpea actually pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. This enriches the ground with natural food that helps the maize grow stronger.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ waa.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce a lot of flowers but no fruit comes out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting due to extreme heat, insufficient water, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil, which prevents proper pollination and fruit development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ tsiɔ pollination kɛ aduawai ni sa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves wilt in the afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon sun, pepper leaves lose water through evaporation faster than their roots can pull it from the soil. The plant droops to shrink its surface area and protect itself from drying out, usually recovering by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ koni ekɛha ehiɛ afee bibioo ni ebu ehe koni ekagbi. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: If I add a large amount of fertilizer at once, will my crops grow twice as fast?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he shikome Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya shii enyɔ?

english: No, applying too much fertilizer creates high salt levels in the soil, which can scorch plant roots, turn leaf tips brown, and actually stunt or kill the crop.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baanyɛ aha ŋmei aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi ashã. Baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ feɔ blɔfo. ni ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ loo amɛgboi.

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow so much faster than my planted crops after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ ni amɛdara oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are wild and adapted to survive long droughts in the soil. They are built to wake up instantly at the slightest moisture, while domestic crop seeds require more time and stable humidity to germinate.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Afee amɛ koni amɛte shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ ba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shia dumɔwui biɔ be babaoo kɛ nu ni mli edɔ daa dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly in my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot when cut or bruised during harvest, allowing microscopic fungi to enter. Storing them in warm, poorly ventilated spaces creates heat and moisture, which accelerates fungal decay.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ kɛji afo loo atswa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii boteɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛto he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo aba. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmei lɛ afite oya.

english: What causes white, dusty patches to form on the leaves of my garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni haa sũ yɛŋ shwieɔ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: White dusty spots are caused by a fungal disease called powdery mildew. It thrives in warm, humid air with poor air circulation and blocks the leaf from absorbing sunlight to make plant food.
ga: Fungi hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew kɛ sũ yɛŋ baa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ eyaaa jogbaŋŋ mli. ni etsĩɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ hulu la koni amɛkɛfee niyenii amɛha tsei

english: Should I plant seeds that look bent, small, or cracked if I do not have enough good seeds?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui ni ebɔle, bibii loo egbɛ eshwa kɛji amɛhiii jogbaŋŋ?

english: It is best to avoid planting deformed, cracked, or damaged seeds. These seeds often produce weak seedlings that die easily or yield very little food; choosing clean, whole, and plump seeds gives your crops the best start.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni efite, ni egbɛ eshwa, loo ni efite lɛ adumɔ he. Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ woɔ dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ ni gboiɔ oya loo amɛhaa niyenii fioo ko pɛ. Dumɔwui ni he tse ni ooohala Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ nɔ ni egbɔ lɛ fɛɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is there any real difference between planting brown cowpea seeds and black cowpea seeds?
ga: Ani srɔtofeemɔ ko diɛŋtsɛ yɛ tsina ŋmei dumɔwui ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsina ŋmei diŋ ni aduɔ lɛ teŋ?

english: Yes, seed color usually indicates different varieties. Brown and black cowpeas may have different maturity times, cooking qualities, and levels of resistance to local rain conditions or field pests.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ ahe su tsɔɔ henɔi srɔtoi. Ekolɛ tsina ŋmeii ni ji brown kɛ black lɛ baaná be ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃. kpakpa yɛ niyenii homɔ mli kɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai srɔtoi ni teɔ shi ewoɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ loo ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: How do I know if a new crop variety I have never planted before will grow well on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso hee ko ni miduko dã lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Before planting a new variety on your whole farm, test a small portion of your land first and consult an extension officer to confirm that the variety suits your local soil, rainfall, and market needs.
ga: Dani obaadu tsei srɔtoi heei yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ Kaa he bibioo ko okwɛ. onɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni okɛ extension official ko agba sane koni ema nɔ mi akɛ srɔtoi lɛ sa kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayeli he hiamɔ nii.

english: Why are my harvested maize grains turning black instead of staying bright yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize grains turn dark or black when fungal mold grows on them due to high moisture. Ensuring your maize dries fully in a clean, dry area before storage prevents this dark rot.
ga: Abele ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ loo ediŋŋ kɛji ŋmeii kwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo hewɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ koni o-abele lɛ agbi kwraa yɛ he ko ni he tse ni egbi dani okɛto lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ duŋ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do some of my green cocoa pods turn dark brown or black before they are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ dani amɛshwere kwraa lɛ?

english: When young cocoa pods turn dark brown or black and shrivel, it is usually caused by black pod disease or insect damage. Clearing heavy shade and pruning diseased pods helps stop the spread.
ga: Beni kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji black pod hela loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii. Kɛ́ ajie hulutsoo ni tsii kɛjɛ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Twisted and curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids or mites, or a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves growing flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etsɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaha baai lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my cassava roots grow crooked and bent instead of straight and long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ebɔle amɛhe shi jeee ni amɛfee tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛlɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers grow crooked when the soil is too hard, stony, or compacted for the roots to push through easily. Loosening the soil deeply before planting allows roots to stretch down straight.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, eyɛ tɛi, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ abote mli mlɛo. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani adu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams come out with strange, rough branches instead of smooth tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ yɛ niji ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ yitsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yams develop irregular, branched shapes when tiny soil worms called nematodes attack the growing tubers, or when the yam hits hard obstacles like rocks or compacted clay underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ niji ni bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli beni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ tutua ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. aloo kɛ́ yam lɛ tswa gbɛtsii nii ko ni wa, tamɔ tɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni akɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are some pods on my cocoa tree big and healthy while others remain tiny and dried up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ekomɛi dara ni amɛhe wa waa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni pods komɛi ji bibii lolo ni amɛgbi lɛ.

english: Trees shed or dry up extra pods when they lack enough water or soil nutrients to support all of them. Adding compost or fertilizer and managing shade helps more pods reach full size.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ loo amɛgbiɔ kɛji nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni baanyɛ aye abua amɛ fɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa.

english: How can I tell when a cassava variety I am not familiar with is ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei henɔ ko ni mileee lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Most cassava varieties are ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem, usually between 9 to 12 months after planting depending on the variety.
ga: Yucca henɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni ashiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ

english: When lower leaves turn yellow from the leaf tips inward, it usually means the maize plant is missing nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to feed the fresh, growing top leaves, leaving the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ baa lɛ naa kɛtee mli lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ koni eye baai heei ni miida lɛ. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni oooŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the afternoon heat becomes too intense or when water supply drops suddenly. The extreme heat damages the flower's pollen, preventing it from forming fruit, so the plant sheds the flower to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ba shi trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ fɔfɔi amli ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaaa enyɛ ewo yibii No hewɔ lɛ, tsei gbalaa amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally during dry periods to save water. Leaves lose moisture to the hot, dry air, so shedding them keeps the main stem and underground tubers alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛbu nu he. Baai lɛ laajeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi mli. No hewɔ lɛ, shi tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop during hot afternoons even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: In intense midday heat, leaves lose water through hot air faster than the roots can draw it from the ground. The leaves droop temporarily to protect themselves, but they usually bounce back once the afternoon cool sets in.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he. Shi efɔɔ sɛɛkuu kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ yɛ shwane mli.

english: Why do my crop roots turn soft and rot when heavy rain sits on my land for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen inside the soil to breathe. Standing water fills all the air gaps in the earth, suffocating the roots and causing them to rot.
ga: Tse shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni yɔɔ lolo lɛ eyi kɔɔyɔɔ hei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ je lɛŋ lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with wooden sticks to get big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato wain tsei anɔ koni maná ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Yam leaves produce food for the underground tuber using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground, ensuring they get maximum light and fresh air to make enough energy for a large harvest.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ awó amɛhe nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baa lɛ naa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa babaoo koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha kpamɔ agbo ko aba.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees growing thin and tall instead of strong and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miidara ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee hewalɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants stretch quickly upwards when there is too much shade covering them. They spend all their energy reaching for sunlight rather than building a thick stem and side branches.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shwereɔ oya kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛtaoɔ hulu la yɛ tsei akutsei ni mli tse kɛ niji ni yɔɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do new shoots grow around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei heei miikwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain shishitoo lɛ?

english: Plantains naturally produce side shoots called suckers from their root base to reproduce. These suckers feed off the main plant until they grow their own roots to form the next generation of fruit-bearing trees.
ga: Plantains woɔ sɛɛ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ koni amɛfɔ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yeɔ tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ niyenii kɛyashiɔ be mli ni lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshishifãi lɛ shwereɔ koni ekɛfee aduawai tsei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my okra seeds take longer to sprout out of the dirt than my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okra dumɔwui jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ fe ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Okra seeds have a tough outer shell that takes extra time to absorb water before waking up. Maize seeds have softer coats, allowing water to enter quickly for fast sprouting.
ga: Roselle dumɔwui yɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ko ni wa ni he hiaa be kroko koni ekɛjie nu dani ete shi. Abele ŋmeii yɛ nɔ ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe tsutsu lɛ. Ehaa nu boteɔ mli oya koni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Weeds are wild native plants that are adapted to thrive on local soil with very little water or care. They naturally grab soil food and sunlight faster than farm crops, which need extra care to stay competitive.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni atsake amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ jɛmɛ shikpɔji ni nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ nɔ loo akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ. Amɛheɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ mli oya fe okwaayeli mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ biɔ hiɛdɔɔ krɛdɛɛ ko bɔni afee ni akaŋ.

english: How can I tell if an oil palm tree has male or female flowers on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mu tsei yɛ fɔfɔi hii loo yei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Oil palm trees produce both male and female flowers on the same tree at different times. Male flowers look like long, thin, finger-like spikes grouped together, while female flowers look like compact, spiky rounded clusters where the fruit bunches will eventually grow.
ga: Mu tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei fɛɛ yɛ tso kome nɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Fɔfɔi hii lɛ yɛ kuu kakadaŋŋ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ niji ni akɛfee ekome. yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi yei lɛ ji kui ni yɔɔ kokroo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are some of my oil palm trees producing flowers but not bearing any fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ekomɛi yɛ fɔfɔi shi amɛwooo aduawai lɛ?

english: This usually happens when a tree is only producing male flowers at that time, or because there are no pollinating insects (like the oil palm weevil) to carry pollen from the male flowers to the female flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi hii pɛ yɛ nakai beaŋ. aloo akɛni kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi (tamɔ oil palm weevils) ni baanyɛ aŋɔ fɔfɔi ni jɛ fɔfɔi hii amli kɛya fɔfɔi yei amli lɛ bɛ hewɔ.

english: Is it true that an oil palm nut contains both a male and a female inside it?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ oil palm dumɔwui yɛ hii kɛ yei fɛɛ yɛ amɛmli?

english: A single palm nut does not have separate male and female nuts, but the seed grows into a tree that has the ability to produce both male and female flowers throughout its life depending on climate, age, and tree health.
ga: Palm nut kome bɛ nut nuu kɛ yoo ni yɔɔ srɔtoi. Shi dumɔwui lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni baanyɛ awo fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei fɛɛ yɛ amɛwala be fɛɛ mli. E da si ngɛ kɔɔhiɔ mi, tso ɔ jeha kɛ e he wami ɔ nɔ.

english: Why do some of my vegetable crops produce flowers that just drop off without giving me any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ ekomɛi yɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Plants often produce early male flowers that fall off after releasing pollen. If female flowers fall without making fruit, it means they were not pollinated by bees or insects, or the plant is stressed by heat or lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii mra ni shwieɔ shi beni amɛjie pollen lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji fɔfɔi yei lɛ gbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ jeee ŋmeii loo kooloi krokomɛi ji mɛi ni shwie nɔ. aloo tsei lɛ miihao yɛ dɔlɛ loo nu ni bɛ hewɔ.

english: Can I harvest nuts from my best oil palm tree and plant them directly to get high yield?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmeii kɛjɛ mi-oil palm tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ amli ni madu amɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni maná yibii babaoo?

english: It is not recommended because seeds taken from farm trees (second-generation hybrids) often produce trees with thick shells and very little oil. It is best to buy certified hybrid seeds (like Tenera) from recognized agricultural institutes.
ga: Akɛ enɛ haaa ejaakɛ ajieɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ amli. (Second generation hybrids) lɛ fɔɔ tsei ni amɛhe tsɔi lɛ mli tse ni fɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli (tamɔ Tenera) kɛjɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔhe ko ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ.

english: How do I choose the right seedling when buying oil palms for my new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui ni sa kɛ́ mihe ŋmei fɔ kɛha miŋmɔ hee lɛ?

english: Look for seedlings with dark green, broad leaves, a sturdy central stem (bulb), and healthy white roots without signs of yellowing, spotting, or stunted growth.
ga: Taomɔ dumɔwui ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni mli wa (bulb), kɛ shishifãi yɛŋ ni mli wa ni okadi ko bɛ he akɛ amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ, amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo amɛmiidamɔ egbɔjɔ.

english: How far apart should I plant my oil palm trees so they don't fight each other?
ga: Te esa akɛ adu oil palm tsei lɛ kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni béi akafee?

english: Oil palms should be planted in a triangular pattern about 9 meters (around 30 feet) apart. This spacing ensures their wide fronds get full sun and their roots have enough room to absorb nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ adu mu tsei lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni tamɔ koŋ etɛ nɔ, ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 9 (aaafee ninetalɔi 30). Nɛkɛ jɛkɛmɔ nɛɛ haa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ naa hulu la ni fa babaoo. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: How long will I have to wait after planting a young oil palm seedling before I can harvest fruit?
ga: Kɛ́ odu mu tsei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani anyɛ akpa yibii lɛ?

english: Improved hybrid oil palm varieties usually begin producing their first harvestable fruit bunches about 3 to 4 years after being transplanted into the main field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni ji hybrid oil palm henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ klɛŋklɛŋ aduawai akui ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ shishi aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ beni ajie amɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young oil palm turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-oil palm lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal a lack of essential nutrients in the soil—especially nitrogen or potassium—or poor soil drainage caused by waterlogging around the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Titri lɛ, nitrogen loo potasium. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ hewɔ

english: What can I do on my farm to help insects pollinate my oil palm flowers naturally?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ni mikɛ mi-palm fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollin yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Avoid spraying strong chemical insecticides directly on the open flowers, as this kills beneficial pollinators like weevils and bees that carry pollen to form heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mli wa ni oooshwie fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, egbeɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ aduawai akui babaoo lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects the tender cocoa leaves from sun scorch and keeps the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo baai ni mli tse lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and drying up in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: When the lower leaves of maize turn yellow starting from the leaf tips, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to stay green and grow leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ baai.

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with tiny beneficial bacteria in the soil to grab nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, leaving natural food for the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ helatsɛmɛi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ejie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ Adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni eshwɛɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the soil gets soaked with rain for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rainwater sits in the ground without draining, it starves the roots of air, causing them to rot underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu bɛ mli Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi nibii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do extension officers advise making high soil mounds before planting yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ awó shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu sweet potato lɛ?

english: Yams need deep, soft, and loose soil to push downward and expand. High mounds prevent water from drowning the seed yam and allow the tuber to grow large and smooth.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni shwieɔ shi koni ekɛtsi shi ni egbɛ eshwa. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ tsiɔ nu naa koni ekabote sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ amli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa yitso lɛ ni edara ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight with the main plantain tree for food, water, and sunlight, resulting in small plantain bunches and weak trees.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ awuu kɛha niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la, ni no baaha ŋmeii bibii aba. ni tsei lɛ hu bɛ hewalɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and shrinking into tight bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the sap out of the leaves and spread viruses that stunt plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haaa tso lɛ ada lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants have holes in them with what looks like sawdust inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn plants lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ nɔ ko ni tamɔ ŋmei yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the deep center funnel of the maize plant during the day and chew through the young leaves as they unpack.
ga: Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni okɛ baai bibii lɛ atsu nii yɛ be mli ni ojieɔ amɛ lɛ

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers but drop them off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi eshiɔ ni ebɛ tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures become too high during the day or when water is irregular, which prevents the flower from forming seeds and growing into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nu lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ awo dumɔwui ni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow lots of leaves for months but only produce pods late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo nyɔji babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ pɛ lɛ?

english: Certain traditional cowpea varieties rely on the changing length of daylight to know when to flower, so they will keep growing only leaves until the days grow shorter later in the year.
ga: Kusum mli tsina ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ hulutsoo be ni tsakeɔ lɛ nɔ koni amɛle be ni esa akɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi. No hewɔ lɛ, tsina ŋmei lɛ kwɛɔ baai pɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni gbii lɛ feɔ kuku yɛ afi lɛ naagbee.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves turn yellow when exposed to too much direct sun without enough shade cover, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ mli. aloo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed so many of their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shwieɔ baai babaoo yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop leaves during dry spells to conserve water and protect themselves from dying, though proper shade trees can help them retain more leaves.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hɔnɔ ni sa baanyɛ aye abua kookoo tso lɛ ni ehiɛ baai babaoo mli moŋ, shi.

english: It is normal for cocoa trees to drop many flowers, but severe flower loss happens when there are not enough pollinating insects (midges) or when the tree suffers from water stress.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi babaoo kpo. Shi fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ waa lɛ baa kɛji akɛ pollinators (teŋgbɛ nibii) ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ loo beni tso lɛ naa nu he haomɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in excessive shade and damp conditions during the heavy rainy season.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nine yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: How long does it take for a tiny cocoa pod to grow big enough for harvesting?
ga: cocoa pods bibii Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani edaa bɔ ni sa ni anyɛɔ akpaa?

english: It takes about 5 to 6 months for a cocoa flower to fully develop into a ripe, harvestable pod after successful pollination.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji enumɔ kɛyashi enumɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eda, ni abaanyɛ akpa amɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛye omanye yɛ pollination mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant cassava inside my new cocoa farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ ŋmei yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Cassava takes up too much water and nutrients from the soil, which competes with young cocoa; food crops like plantain or banana are better because they provide shade without smothering the cocoa.
ga: Cassava heɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni kɛ kookoo ni mli tse lɛ yeɔ akaŋ Niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains loo banana hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛhaa hulutsoo ni amɛfiteee kookoo lɛ.

english: Will cutting off extra branches from my cocoa tree reduce my harvest?
ga: Ani niji krokomɛi ni mifolɔ kɛjɛ mi cacao tso lɛ mli lɛ baaha mi yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi?

english: No, pruning extra branches helps sunlight and air flow through the tree, which lowers disease risk and directs energy into making bigger pods.
ga: Dabi, tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ baaye abua ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster around my young cocoa saplings during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi babaoo ebɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daa oya waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Weeds thrive on the heavy rains and full sunlight available around young trees, rapidly stealing moisture and nutrients meant for your crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ mli. Ejuɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ oya.

english: Mirids suck sap from young shoots and pods, leaving black sunken spots on the pods and causing young branches to dry up and die back.
ga: Mirids lɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Eshiɔ ŋmeii diji yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni ehaa tsei niji bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is healthy enough to support flourishing cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua cacao tsei ni shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Healthy soil for cocoa is dark, rich in decayed leaves, holds moisture well during dry periods, and feels soft and crumbly rather than hard like dry clay.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha kookoo lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Eyɛ baai ni fiteɔ babaoo Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. ni enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni egbɔjɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee nɔ ni wa tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain next to them creates a cool canopy that protects the young cocoa leaves and keeps moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ amɛdu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ Together masɛi lɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines on sticks instead of letting them crawl on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ sweet potato wain tsei yɛ miniji lɛ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need to climb high to get full sunlight so their leaves can make food for the plant. Lifting the leaves off the ground also prevents soil-borne diseases from attacking the leaves and leaves more room for the plant to send energy into growing big underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulutsoo be fɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni akɛ ebaai lɛ atsu nii akɛ niyenii aha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, no hu yeɔ ebuaa ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ baa lɛ baatutuaa baai lɛ. Ni ehaa gbɛ babaoo haa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the middle instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for leaf growth. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen out of the soil, so applying nitrogen fertilizer or compost helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ akwɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the same farm row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋtayaa kome mli?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant food. This competition makes the stalks grow tall, thin, and weak, resulting in small cobs with very few grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei aniyenii ahe akaŋshii mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii. Dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water around the roots for days, it cuts off oxygen and allows wet-soil fungus to grow, which makes the cassava tubers soft and rotten.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ he fɛɛ he. shishifãi gbii babaoo Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwereɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers before any tomatoes start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani tomatoi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by sudden heatwaves or dry spells. To save energy and survive heat stress, the plant drops its buds instead of spending moisture to form young fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be loo hulutsoo be lɛ hao amɛ. Bɔni afee ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato ni enyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa Tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small shoots growing around the stem of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Special ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Ajieɔ mi plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Small shoots (called suckers) share the root system with the main plantain tree and steal water and soil food from it. Leaving only one strong replacement sucker ensures that the main tree receives full nourishment to bear a large bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsobii bibii (ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers) kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ jaa shishifã gbɛjianɔtoo kome ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie sucker ni mli wa kome pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo plantains babaoo.

english: Why are my cabbage plants producing large outer leaves but failing to form a tight center head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage tso lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ baai wuji shi enyɛɛɛ efee yitso ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form a firm center head if the weather stays too hot or if they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer late in their growth. Balanced nutrients and steady watering encourage the inner leaves to curl tightly into a head.
ga: Cabbage nyɛŋ afee yitsei ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛji enine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ yɛ be mli ni edaa blɛoo lɛ. Niyenii ni ja kɛ nu ni akɛhaa daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛfeɔ bulbs ni mli wa.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids hiding under the leaves. As they suck the juice from young leaves, the leaf distorts and curls up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. be mli ni ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ Baai lɛ tsɔɔ sɛɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea farm mostly when the crop starts flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ mli babaoo beni tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers and young pods contain sweet nectar and soft tissues that attract pests like flower thrips and pod borers. Protecting the crop right before flowering prevents these pests from destroying the blooms before pods can form.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli nu kɛ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni gbalaa ŋmeii tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips kɛ pod borers. Nibii ni abuɔ he dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ haaa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akpata fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ dani ŋmeii aba.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight and need living umbrellas to survive. Plantains grow very fast and have wide leaves that provide the necessary shade and keep the soil moist for young cocoa plants during their early years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. ni esa akɛ ekɛ umbrella atsu nii koni ehi shi Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛhaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why are green caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides inside the growing tip of maize plants to feed on soft leaves. Early detection and applying recommended treatments into the center of the plant before damage spreads is crucial to saving the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ koni eye baai bibii lɛ. Nibii ni anaa mra Ni tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ dani nɔ ni efite lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he miihia waa koni eye ebua ni ahere ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: This leaf curling and yellowing is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by small whiteflies. The disease stops the plant from making food efficiently, leading to poor root development; using disease-resistant planting cuttings prevents this issue.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Hela nɛɛ haaa tsei afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni helai nyɛɔ emɔ amɛ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers without growing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi ni ewooo pepper yibii ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from high temperatures, lack of consistent watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Maintaining steady soil moisture during hot periods helps flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli baa lɛ he. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfataa he Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in an inverted V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the tips of lower leaves indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen gives plants their deep green color and growth energy; adding poultry manure or NPK fertilizer helps restore green growth.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛdaraa. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ashishifã loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ekoŋŋ.

english: What is this small plant with pinkish flowers that is making my maize turn yellow and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni ji tso bibioo ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni miiha mi-ŋmei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekpa dalɛ nɛɛ?

english: That plant is Striga, also known as witchweed, which attaches its roots to maize roots underground and steals the crop's water and nutrients. Uprooting Striga before it produces seeds and rotating crops with cowpeas helps reduce it over time.
ga: Nakai tso lɛ ji Striga, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ Witchweed, ni ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe, ni ejuɔ tso lɛ mli nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Striga ni ajieɔ dani eya dumɔwui amli ni akɛ cowpea tsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye abua ni ebɔi falɛ aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do I get very small cobs when I drop three or four maize seeds in one planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmeii bibii waa nɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ ŋmeii bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting too many seeds together causes the crops to fight one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and small cobs. Spacing seeds properly with one or two seeds per hole allows every plant to grow strong.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni ŋmeii lɛ hu yɛ bibii. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ ni dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ yɔɔ bu kome mli lɛ baaye abua ni tso fɛɛ tso adara waa.

english: Why did my maize seeds sprout normally after planting but then dry up and die a week later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ bɔ ni sa beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Shi egbiɔ ni egboɔ yɛ otsi kome sɛɛ?

english: Young seedlings dry up when early rains are followed by a sudden dry spell because their young roots haven't grown deep enough to reach subsoil moisture. Covering the ground with dried leaves or grass (mulching) helps retain moisture in the soil longer.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa trukaa lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi bibii lɛ edako jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛshɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is my farm producing lower yields every season even though I plant the exact same crop on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yibii lɛ baa shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ nibii ni miduɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year while allowing specific pests to build up in the field. Alternating your main crop with legumes like groundnuts or beans restores natural soil fertility.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so quickly after I place them in the storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ oya beni mikɛwo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot rapidly if they suffer minor cuts during harvest or if the storage barn lacks proper airflow and stays too hot. Handling tubers carefully during harvest and storing them in elevated, shaded, well-ventilated yam barns prevents rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ fioo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ, ni edɔ hu tsɔ. Kɛ́ akwɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli ni akɛto ŋmeii ŋmɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen in the soil, which is the key nutrient crops need to build healthy green foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly depletes specific soil nutrients and allows pests to build up; alternating with crops like beans restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha sũ mli niyenii komɛi afite ni eye ebua tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei tamɔ ŋmeii wo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are small worms eating holes inside the funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those are fall armyworms that feed on the growing point of the crop; catching and treating them early prevents them from destroying the entire plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall armyworms ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Mra ni ana kɛ tsamɔ Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of essential soil nutrients needed for fruit setting.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha yibiiwoo ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the plantain bunches on my farm much smaller than expected?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ faaa kwraa fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants produce extra shoots called suckers, and if you do not cut most of them back, they steal food and water away from the main fruiting stem.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ woɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii. Ni kɛji ofolɔɔɔ mli babaoo sɛɛ Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ yibiiwoo tso titri lɛ he.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my garden crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mawo mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Watering early in the morning or late in the evening prevents water from quickly evaporating in the afternoon heat, allowing roots to absorb maximum moisture.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ nu babaoo.

english: How can I easily tell when my cocoa pods are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color from green or deep red to bright yellow or orange, and make a hollow sound when you tap on them.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse. Ni efeɔ gbɛɛmɔ ko ni mli ewo muji kɛ́ ota kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water collects around them; planting your crop on raised soil ridges helps rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine bua amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry leaves help them grow?
ga: Mulching around Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ baai ni egbi koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves (mulching) keeps the ground cool, retains moisture during dry days, and suppresses weeds from stealing plant nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju tso lɛ mli niyenii.

english: When lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, it usually means the soil is running low on nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main fuel crops need to stay green, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant recover.
ga: Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji tsofa titri ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids hidden under the leaves, or by a virus they carry. Inspecting under the leaves early and applying neem oil or appropriate treatment keeps the foliage healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni amɛhiɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi mra Ni okɛ neem fɔ awo mli loo okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce tiny tubers when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, their roots fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and resources to expand and grow big tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshwa ni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when I clear away all the big trees on my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-koko tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight and extreme heat. Keeping large shade trees or planting temporary crops like plantains provides living umbrellas that shield tender cocoa leaves from sun damage.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ baanyɛ aha hulutsoo be ni buɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli nibii ni efiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when water supply is uneven. Extreme heat stresses the plant and prevents pollen from setting fruit, so watering regularly and providing light shade during heatwaves helps.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa pollen lɛ akawo yibii lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni oooha lɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines grow bushy with many leaves but yield very few tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes crops focus all their energy on growing tall stems and leafy foliage instead of tubers. Using balanced fertilizers rich in potassium encourages the plant to store energy underground instead.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni miida lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe bulbs. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaawo tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi moŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and wilt during hot afternoons even when the ground is still damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose water to the dry air faster than the roots can pump it up from the soil. This temporary wilting is a crop's natural defense to reduce water loss, and plants usually bounce back in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu koni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ be kukuoo mli shwiemɔ nɛɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛba nu ni efiteɔ lɛ shi. Ni tsei lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do powdery white spots cover my garden egg leaves when the weather is very humid?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni tamɔ powder haa eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Powdery spots are caused by fungal diseases that thrive in warm, damp air with poor airflow between plants. Spacing crops properly allows wind to dry the leaves quickly, preventing fungus from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i mli lɛ kɛ powder spots baa. kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ gĩɔ oya. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: Why do fall armyworms cause more damage to my maize during dry spells in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms lɛ fiteɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Dry spells slow down crop growth while speeding up the life cycle of pests, making it easier for caterpillars to multiply without rain washing them away. Monitoring fields closely during dry weeks helps catch infestations early.
ga: Be ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai wala shihilɛ yaa oya. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛaafɔ bii ni nugbɔ lɛ shwieee amɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ akwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni ana helai ni baa lɛ mra.

english: Why does my farmland yield less maize when I plant it on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets pest populations build up. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores soil nitrogen naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ sɛɛ foɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ayibɔ yaa hiɛ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: What is the benefit of buying certified seed varieties instead of using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ he yɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛaatsu nii lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to grow stronger, resist local diseases better, and produce higher yields, whereas saved seeds often lose their strength and produce smaller harvests over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛdara waa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli helai ahe ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ fɔɔ hewalɛ ni baa shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do I know which maize variety is best suited for my area's rainfall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmãa henɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Seed varieties are categorized by how long they take to mature. Fast-maturing varieties work best in areas with short rainy seasons, while longer-maturing varieties yield more where rainfall is steady and lasts longer.
ga: Ajara dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ amli yɛ be ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ naa. Henɔi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo yɔɔ lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tsei srɔtoi ni daa oya lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Can I plant two different varieties of the same crop in the same farm field?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tso kome lɛ henɔi srɔtoi enyɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, but it is best to plant them in separate rows or blocks so they do not shade each other out or mature at different times, which makes harvesting harder.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu amɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta loo blɔki sɔrɔtoi amli. Bɔni afee ni amɛkaha amɛhe loo amɛdara yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Enɛ baaha nikpamɔ afee nɔ ni wa waa.

english: Why is it important to measure the distance between my crops when planting instead of just scattering seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masusu gbɛ ni kã miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ he kɛ́ midu nii? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ dumɔwui kɛkɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures every plant gets its own share of sunlight, air, soil nutrients, and water without fighting neighboring plants for resources.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni nu lɛ ji lɛ diɛŋtsɛ enɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ nibii ni jɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ

english: What happens if I leave too many seedlings growing in one single spot?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome?

english: When too many seedlings grow in one spot, they compete with each other, leading to thin, weak stalks and very small harvests instead of a few strong, healthy plants.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui dara tsɔ yɛ he kome Amɛbaatswa akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ. Moŋ lɛ, tsei fioo komɛi ni he wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ni.

english: How can taking proper care of fewer plants give me more yield than having a crowded field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei fioo komɛi akwɛmɔ baanyɛ aha yibii babaoo aba fe ŋmɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: A well-fed, healthy plant with enough space and clean soil can produce its full potential in cobs or fruit, whereas many neglected plants will produce almost nothing.
ga: Tsei ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse baanyɛ awo cob loo aduawai bɔ ni sa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei babaoo ni akuɔ hiɛ ashwieɔ nɔ lɛ wooo nɔ ko kwraa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young crop plants start turning yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is lacking key nutrients like nitrogen, is struggling with weeds stealing its food, or is getting too much water around its roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli, ni ekɛ jwɛi ni juɔ niyenii lɛ miiwuu. aloo nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tsɔ

english: How soon after planting should I start clearing weeds from around my crops?
ga: Beni adu nii agbe naa lɛ, esa akɛ mabɔi he ni ebɔle he lɛ jwɛi lɛ shwiemɔ. Te ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya ha tɛŋŋ?

english: You should start clearing weeds within the first two to three weeks after germination because young crops are weak and easily choked by fast-growing weeds.
ga: Esa akɛ oje jwɛi lɛ ŋmɔmɔ shishi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 2-3 lɛ mli beni jwɛi lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ shwieɔ amɛ oya.

english: Fertilizer works like food for the plant, giving the soil essential elements like nitrogen and phosphorus that make plant roots grow deep and leaves stay strong and healthy.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei aniyenii. Ehaa nibii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Enɛ hãa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni ebaa lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know how much bag harvest to reasonably expect from my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kotokui enyiɛ ni esa akɛ makpa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Your final harvest depends on the seed variety's potential, how well you fertilize, and how effectively you protect the crop from pests, weeds, and water stress throughout the season.
ga: O naagbee kpamɔ lɛ damɔ bɔ ni dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii amɛha lɛ nɔ. Te okɛ fɔmɔ nii woɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ohaa tɛŋŋ? Ni te obuɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai, jwɛi, kɛ nu he haomɔi ahe yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ ohaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning light yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow leaves and stems. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients away or flood the roots, so adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii loo nu ewo shishifãi lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Cocoa flowers often drop off if the tree is stressed by excessive heat, lack of water, or attacks from tiny insects like mirids. Ensuring your cocoa trees have adequate shade trees during dry periods helps protect the flowers so they can turn into pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine, nu ni faaa yɛ emli, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen lɛ tutua tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni kookoo tso lɛ aná hulutsoo be ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves high up into the sunlight where they can manufacture food. When the leaves get enough sunlight, that food travels down to build a large, heavy yam tuber under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tsei ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli koni akɛtsu nii yɛ niyenii feemɔ mli. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Niyenii lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii agboi ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Cassava roots rot mainly when water sits in the soil for too long during heavy rainy seasons, suffocating the roots and causing fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised soil ridges or mounds helps extra rainwater drain away quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ babaoo kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa beaŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is commonly caused by a virus spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies, or by severe heat stress. Protecting seedlings with netting and controlling insects early prevents the virus from damaging your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly loo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli Obu dumɔwui ahe kɛtsɔ ŋshɔŋlooi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mra nɔ Ebaatsi helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do I see tiny caterpillars eating holes in the middle of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which love to hide and feed inside the central funnel of maize plants. Checking your farm early and spraying neem leaf extract or recommended organic treatments right into the funnel kills them before they destroy the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛye nii yɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni neem tso lɛ mli nu loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ lɛ baagbe amɛ dani amɛbaakpãtã tso lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or beans between my maize crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans are special plants that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This natural process fertilizes the soil for your maize crop without you needing to spend extra money on commercial chemical fertilizers.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehe ehiaaa ni afite shika babaoo yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ he.

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, called mulching, traps moisture in the ground so crops do not dry out during sunny days. It also stops weeds from growing and breaks down into rich organic food for your soil over time.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni jwɛi lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni amɛkafite ni amɛfee niyenii ni jara wa kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my crop seeds after the long dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground has received two or three heavy, soaking rains rather than planting right after the very first rain. Planting too early in dry, warm soil can scorch seeds before they can establish strong roots.
