ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa ni mli edɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why is it harmful to pour chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaafɔse tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is very strong and can burn the delicate skin and stems of your plants if touched directly. Fertilizer should always be placed in a small ring or shallow pocket a few inches away from the stem where the outer roots can safely drink it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli wa waa, ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei ahewolo kɛ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. loo yɛ kotoku ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli Inchi fioo pɛ kɛjɛ tsɔne lɛ mli. Kponɔgbɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni anuɔ.

english: Leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the plant build healthy green leaves again.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant groundnuts in the exact same spot on my farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that love that crop to build up in the ground. Rotating crops keeps the soil balanced and starves out crop-specific pests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baa shi.

english: Cassava grows best in loose, well-drained sandy or loamy soil because its edible roots grow underground. If the soil is too sticky with heavy clay or holds water for too long, the roots will rot instead of swelling into healthy cassava.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋã loo sũ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi ni ayeɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsii tsɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo ehiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafu ni amɛtsɔ ŋmei ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce smaller harvests if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli tseee ni ewooo yibii babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, their roots and leaves compete heavily with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows it to get enough food to produce a big harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ he akaŋ waa. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaha ená niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakpa nii babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and droop during the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu yɛ moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it up from the ground. They temporarily droop to conserve moisture, and they usually stand upright again in the evening as temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaakoto shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. ni bei pii lɛ, edamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress from extreme afternoon heat, uneven watering, or too much nitrogen. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy to survive rather than investing in new fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ yɛ shwane mli. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ mli Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha wala. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ shika awo aduawai hee ko mli lɛ

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout if I push them too deep into the soil when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ beni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need air, warmth, and moisture to sprout. If planted too deep, the tiny green shoot burns through all its stored food energy trying to push through the heavy soil and dies before it can reach sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, dɔlɛ, kɛ fɛ̃i dani amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmeii bibii ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ Eshãa eniyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛto lɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛtsiɔ ehe waa lɛ nɔ. ni egbo dani eshɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves off the ground and expose them to direct sunlight. Sunlight powers the leaves to create food, which then travels down the vine to build large, heavy underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ko ni baaha amɛwo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛha hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la haa baai lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Kɛkɛ lɛ, efãa kɛyaa wain tso lɛ shishi ni efeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight intended for your main crops. Because weeds grow very fast, they shade your plants and leave them starving for essential food.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei titrii lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehaa otsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ kɛha niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains get full of holes and spoil after a few months in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ eyi kɛ bu ni egbo yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils attack stored maize if the grains are not thoroughly dried before storage. Properly drying the grains makes them too hard for insects to feed on easily and prevents mould from growing.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii tutuaa ŋmãa ni ato. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛtoɔ Dumɔwui ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ewaa tsɔ akɛ kooloi yeɔ amɛ ni ehaaa ŋmeii akwɛ̃.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava stems so the roots can grow big?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-cassava tsei lɛ kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni shishifãi wuji akwɛ̃?

english: Spacing cassava about 1 meter apart gives each plant enough room and soil nutrients to expand its roots underground without competing with neighboring plants for sunlight and water.
ga: Aaafee mita kome ni kã ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛgbala eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔi hulu la kɛ nu he akaŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade, keeping the cocoa seedlings cool and moist while they establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules. When the plant dies, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil, naturally fertilizing the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tso henɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: What is eating small holes in the middle whorl of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the central leaves. Checking crops early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract stops them before they destroy the yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ mra kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he ŋaawoo. Ekpaa tsei nɛɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Curled and yellow-patterned leaves are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stems is the best way to prevent it.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ helai anaa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when plants face heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of potassium. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo potassium ni faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruit bunches start getting large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, so top-heavy trees easily get pulled down by heavy fruit and strong winds. Proping up the stem with a strong bamboo fork supports the weight until harvest.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi-tsii lɛ, yibii ni tsii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa amɛ kɛyaa shi oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei fɔk ni wa to tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛfiɔ muji lɛ sɛɛ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees lose their leaves and dry up during the Harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan beaŋ lɛ?

english: Dry Harmattan winds suck moisture out of cocoa leaves faster than roots can drink from dry soil. Mulching around the tree trunks keeps soil damp, and keeping shade trees reduces wind damage.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli. Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni tsei ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo mli lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ aba shi.

english: It is best to water early in the morning so plant roots can absorb water before the hot sun causes rapid evaporation, reducing stress on the plant during peak heat.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu lɛ leebi maŋkpa bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aha etsɔ la oya. Enɛ haa nɔnyɛɛ ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops perform better when I plant cassava and maize together on the same land instead of leaving empty spaces?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi he ko

english: Planting complementary crops together maximizes soil nutrients, creates ground cover to reduce weed growth, and helps retain soil moisture, allowing crops to support each other's growth.
ga: Tsei ni akɛfataa he lɛ ni aaakwɛ nɔ ekomefeemɔ mli lɛ baaha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ. Feemɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ ko ni baaha jwɛi lɛ adalɛ aba shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi Ehaa tsei yeɔ amɛbuaa amɛhe ni amɛdaraa.

english: What happens to my pepper plants if I sow the seeds too close to each other in one spot?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ he kome?

english: When seeds are planted too tightly together, the seedlings compete for the same water, light, and soil nutrients, causing them to grow thin, weak, and stunt each other.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ babaoo tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa amɛteŋ.

english: Why should I leave big mature trees on my farm when clearing land to plant young cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei wuji yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mijieɔ shikpɔŋ koni mikɛdu kookoo bibii lɛ?

english: Big mature trees act as a natural canopy shade, protecting delicate young cocoa plants from intense sunlight and harsh winds while keeping the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Why do the crops growing at the outer edge of my field near the road dry up faster than those in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ he lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe nɔ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Crops on the farm boundary are directly exposed to sweeping winds, hot dust, and uninterrupted sunlight without the protective shelter created by neighboring plants inside the farm.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji husui lɛ anɔ lɛ naa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, sũ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ daa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cowpea plants roll up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea leaves roll up to reduce the amount of surface area exposed to the sun, which is a natural survival trick that helps the plant conserve water during extreme heat.
ga: Akɛ cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni hulu la ni shɛɔ nɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young yam vines turn yellow and fail to grow when I do not stake them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni edaaa kɛji mikɛ shishifãi etswaaa lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need sunlight and air circulation to make food. When left on the ground, they come into direct contact with hot soil and damp conditions that foster disease instead of healthy growth.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ mli koni amɛhoo. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, amɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni kɛ helai baa lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaada jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does unkept bush bordering my farm affect my tomato crops?
ga: Te tsei bibii ni bɛ fɛo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ saa mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Overgrown weeds and wild bush around your field serve as breeding grounds for pests and plant diseases, which then easily cross over into your farm to attack your tomatoes.
ga: Jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine kɛ koo mli tsei bibii ni bɔle oŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ ji hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai fɔɔ yɛ. ni baanyɛ atsɔ mlɛo kɛbote oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eyatutua tomatoi

english: Why do insects attack one small patch of my maize field first before moving to the rest of the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ dani amɛyaa ŋmɔ lɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Pests usually gather where plants are most vulnerable or where shelter and moisture are highest, multiplying in that spot before migrating across the entire field.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ amɛhe buamɔ yɛ hei ni tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ loo hei ni shĩa kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa yɛ nakai be lɛ mli dani amɛfãa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my old coffee trees yield fewer fruits than when they were young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kɔfi tso momo lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe beni eji gbekɛ lɛ?

english: As crop plants age, their internal system becomes less efficient at drawing nutrients from roots to branches, requiring selective pruning to stimulate new, productive growth.
ga: Kɛ tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ dara lɛ Amɛmli gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ mligbalamɔ mli kɛjɛɔ shishifã kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli. Enɛ biɔ ni ahala tsei lɛ ashwie shi koni ewo dalɛ hee ni woɔ yibii lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why should I gather dry grass and place it around the base of my plantain suckers after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabua jwɛi anaa ni mikɛto he fɛɛ he lɛ? Dumɔwui ashishitoo yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ

english: Covering the soil around the plant base with dry grass acts as mulch, which seals in moisture, cools the roots, and stops competitive weeds from growing.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is rich enough to grow healthy food for my family?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛha miweku lɛ?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, holds water well after rain, breaks apart easily in your hand, and contains earthworms. You can also test your soil to see exactly which nutrients it has and what it needs added.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Ekɛ nu toɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ oniji amli. Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu yɛ. Obaanyɛ oka oshikpɔŋ lɛ hu okwɛ koni ona niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli kɛ nɔ ni esa akɛ akɛfata he.

english: Why should I mix organic manure into my field before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ afutu miŋmɔji amli dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Adding manure feeds tiny living organisms in the dirt that break down nutrients, helping the land hold onto water longer and giving your crop roots easy access to natural food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ adara. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fiteɔ lɛ mli Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaaná adebɔɔ mli niyenii.

english: Why is burning dry weeds on my land before planting harmful to my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni ashãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani aduɔ lɛ yeɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable nutrients on the surface, kills good insects and earthworms in the earth, and leaves the bare soil exposed to rain that washes away the top layer.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Egbeɔ kooloi bibii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kpakpai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni ehaa nugbɔ nɛɔ, ni no shwieɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient plant roots drink from the soil to grow strong leaves, or that heavy rainfall washed those nutrients away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Tse shishifãi nuɔ niyenii titrii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eha baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛyaa.

english: Beans pull nitrogen food out of the air and put it back into the earth through their roots, which naturally feeds neighboring crops like maize without exhausting the soil.
ga: Beans gbalaa nibii ni haa mɔ he waa ni ji nitrogen lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tamɔ ŋmãa niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteee

english: Why do my cassava plants lose their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry weather to reduce water loss and protect its roots underground; once the rains return, the plant quickly sprouts fresh leaves.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni egbiɔ koni nu ni elaaje lɛ aba shi ni ebu eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya.

english: How does covering the soil around my plants with dry leaves help them in hot weather?
ga: Bɔ ni tsei ni akɛ baai egbi ebɔle tsei ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves acts like a blanket that shades the soil, prevents sunshine from evaporating soil water, and keeps crop roots cool.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi haa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekafee nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when temperatures get extremely hot, when water is inconsistent, or when there are not enough insects nearby to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛŋkɛ lɛ Eshɛɛɛ ni ekɛbaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow bigger when I plant them in straight rows instead of scattering seeds randomly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã trukaa lɛ?

english: Row planting gives every plant equal space, sunlight, and airflow while making it much easier for you to weed, water, and add soil nutrients evenly.
ga: Row planting haa tsei fɛɛ náa he ko, hulu la, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ mli lɛ falɛ kome. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi, okɛ nu awo mli, ni okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: What can I do right after harvesting to keep my grains from spoiling quickly?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ nikpamɔ sɛɛ koni miŋmaa lɛ akafite oya?

english: Drying your harvested grains thoroughly under the sun to remove moisture and storing them in airtight bags in a cool, dry room prevents mold and insects from ruining your food.
ga: Kɛ́ ogbala odumɔwui ni okpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi koni ejie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ mli, ni okɛto vacuum kotokui amli yɛ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni mli egbi mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi bibii akafite oniyenii lɛ.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away my topsoil and young crops whenever there is a sudden downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ?

english: When heavy rain falls quickly on bare or unprotected land, the water creates fast-moving surface runoff that strips away rich topsoil and sweeps small seedlings along with it. Planting cover crops or making soil ridges across slopes helps slow down runoff and holds your soil in place.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni abuuu he lɛ nɔ. Nu feɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ hei ni nyiɛɔ oya lɛ anɔ. Enɛ jieɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa lɛ ni ekɛ dumɔwui bibii hu shwieɔ shi. Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aduɔ loo ŋmeii ni afee yɛ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: How can I protect my farmland from being swept away when floodwaters rush through my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni nu akaho kɛji nu afua miiho kɛmiitsɔ miŋmɔji amli?

english: You can protect your field by digging proper drainage channels around your farm to direct heavy water away safely, and by planting deep-rooted grasses like vetiver along field borders to hold the soil tightly together.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa ni oootsɔ mli kɛbɔle he lɛ nɔ. oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛjie muji lɛ shweshweeshwe. kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni shishifãi mli kwɔ tamɔ vetiver jwɛi ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa koni ekɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shiŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What should I do to rebuild my land after floodwaters sweep away the top layer of my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni matswa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ beni nu afua kpata miŋmɔ lɛ ŋwɛi fã lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You can restore washed-away soil by adding organic matter such as well-rotted manure, compost, or crop residues, which replaces lost nutrients and improves the soil's structure so plants can grow strong again.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni aho lɛ aku sɛɛ okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite lɛ baafata he, ni no yeɔ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ najiaŋ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nibii lɛ feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of my crops turn yellow and die after standing in heavy rainwater for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni amɛdamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the soil to survive. When excess rainwater stays on your field without draining, it suffocates the roots, causing them to rot and turning the leaves yellow because the plant cannot absorb nutrients.
ga: Tse shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eshwɛɔ yɛ oŋmɔji amli ni etsɔɔɔ mli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa egboɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Which crops are best for me to plant on dry ground that does not do well with too much water?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ makwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni esaaa nu babaoo nɔ?

english: Crops like cassava, millet, sorghum, and groundnuts grow well in dry or well-drained soils because their root systems are naturally built to survive with very little water and can suffer if roots stay wet for too long.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi kɛ nu fioo ko pɛ. Ni naagbai baanyɛ aba kɛji shishifãi lɛ hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: How can I tell if my field has too much water for my crops during the rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: If water forms stagnant pools on top of the soil, the ground stays muddy like paste for days after rain, or plant leaves start wilting despite wet ground, your land is waterlogged and needs drainage trenches.
ga: Kɛji nu fee ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi tamɔ shikpɔŋ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Aloo tsei ahe baai lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ, ni no tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni afee ŋshɔ ko ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli.

english: How do I know if a piece of land will collect too much water before I start planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ baahiɛ nu babaoo dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Check the slope and soil type before planting; low-lying valleys and heavy clay soils retain water for long periods, whereas slightly elevated or sandy-loam soils allow excess water to drain away freely.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋshɔ lɛ shishi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani odu. Jɔɔi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa lɛ haa nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ fioo loo ŋã ni yɔɔ ŋã nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: What harm does using river water polluted by galamsey do to my crops and soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ faa mli nu ni galamsey ewo mli lɛ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ awui?

english: Galamsey water contains heavy mud, dangerous chemicals, and toxic metals like mercury. This dirty water clogs soil pores, stops roots from breathing, poisons your crops, and can make harvested food unsafe to eat.
ga: Muji ni tsii yɛ Galamsey nu lɛ mli. tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ dade ni yɔɔ gbeyei tamɔ mercury. Nu ni mli ewo muji nɛɛ tsiɔ sũ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ anaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu Ehaa tsofai fɔji baa onibii amli. ni ebaanyɛ eha niyenii ni akpa lɛ afee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ.

english: Why do my crops stop growing after dirty, muddy runoff water covers my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpa shweremɔ beni nu ni mli ewo muji ni atatu yɔɔ mli lɛ ha miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Thick mud left behind by runoff coats the crop leaves and seals the soil surface like cement, which prevents light from reaching the leaves and blocks air from getting down to the roots.
ga: Muji ni mli tse ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei ahe baai ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ simenti. Enɛ haaa la ashɛ baai lɛ ahe, ni ehaaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my seeds as soon as the first light rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ ji oshara kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Early light rains can trick seeds into germinating, but if a dry period follows before the heavy rains start, the young sprouts will scorch and die in the soil from heat and lack of moisture.
ga: Nugbɔ fioo ni nɛɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ alaka dumɔwui ni amɛkwɛ̃. Shi kɛji akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ nɛ waa hu? Tsei bibii lɛ baashã ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How deep should I cut into my trees when tapping them for rubber or sap?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo mitso lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ni miitswa sap loo sap?

english: You should only cut into the outer bark where the liquid flows. If you cut too deep into the hard inner wood, you will damage the tree's health, stop the sap from flowing, and permanently scar the tree.
ga: Esa akɛ afo kponɔgbɛ fã ni nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ pɛ. Kɛji ofo mligbɛ tso ni wa lɛ mli tsɔ Obaafite tso lɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ. Ekpaa latɛs ni hoɔ lɛ. ni ehaa tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ daa.

english: What happens if I accidentally cut into the hard wood under the tree bark while harvesting?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ oshara shwie tso ni wa lɛ shishi yɛ tso lɛ shishi be mli ni mikpaa nii lɛ?

english: Cutting into the hard wood destroys the tree's internal channels that carry food and water. This weakens the tree, makes it vulnerable to diseases, and reduces your future harvests.
ga: Tsei ni wa ni afoɔ lɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ mli gbɛi ni kɛ niyenii kɛ nu yaa lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ, ni ebaaha helai aba enɔ oya, ni ebaaha onibii ni obaawo wɔsɛɛ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my harvesting cuts look broken and rough instead of smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ nibii ni mifo lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ekumɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Rough and broken cuts usually happen when tools are dull or when too much force is used. Gentle, careful slicing prevents the bark from tearing and keeps the underlying wood safe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa baa kɛji akɛ dɛŋdadei lɛ bɛ ŋmɔlɔ loo akɛ hewalɛ fe nine tsu nii. Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ blɛoo, ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ yibii lɛ amligbalamɔ naa, ni ebaaha tso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my rubber tree stop producing latex after a few harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi rɔba tso lɛ kpaɔ latɛs feemɔ yɛ ŋmaa fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Latex stops flowing if the tree is wounded too deeply into the wood, if the cuts are not done cleanly, or if the tree is being tapped too frequently without enough time to rest.
ga: Nu lɛ baakpa shwiemɔ kɛji akɛ afo tso lɛ mli tsɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ afeee tso lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ Aloo kɛji akɛ atswa tso lɛ shii abɔ tsɔ ni anáaa hejɔɔmɔ be ni sa.

english: Is it safe to lean a heavy ladder directly against a tall crop tree during harvesting?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oookɛ atswere ni tsii afɔ tsei kakadaji anɔ yɛ nikpamɔ be mli?

english: You must be very cautious when leaning ladders against trees. If the trunk is damaged or the wood is weak from past cuts, the branch or trunk can break, causing a dangerous fall and ruining the tree.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ ohe jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ okɛ atswele lɛ fĩ tso ko he. Kɛji tso lɛ shishi lɛ efite loo tso lɛ egbɔjɔ kɛjɛ tso ni afo tsutsu lɛ mli. Niji loo tsei akui baanyɛ akumɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ oshara nɔ, ni efiteɔ tso lɛ.

english: How do I safely harvest from very tall trees without damaging the trunk?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafo tsei ni kwɔlɔ waa lɛ amli shweshweeshwe ni mifiteee tsei lɛ ashishifã lɛ?

english: Use properly secured ladders tied to stable points, or use long pole pruners from the ground so you do not drag heavy tools against delicate trunk bark.
ga: Kɛ atswele ni akɛfi he ko ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni akɛfi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ atsu nii. Aloo okɛ sɛkɛs afo tsei niji kakadaji kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ. Bɔni afee ni ehe akahi ni okɛ nibii ni tsii agbala kɛbɔle ohe. Koni akumɔ tso lɛ yibii ni waaa lɛ

english: How can I tell if a tree trunk is strong enough to support my ladder and body weight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tso shishitso lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ atswele kɛ migbɔmɔtso lɛ mli tsiimɔ nɔ?

english: Inspect the base and trunk for deep cuts, hollow spots, or rotten wood from previous harvests. Trees with deep wounds into the wood are unstable and can snap under weight.
ga: Kwɛmɔ shishi kɛ eshishi lɛ mli kɛji ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ, okadii ni mli ewo muji, loo tsei ni egbo ni jɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa tsutsu lɛ amli. Tsei ni afolɔ awo tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkumɔ yɛ muji lɛ shishi.

english: Can tree bark heal itself if it gets broken or deeply gouged during work?
ga: Ani ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ atsa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe kɛji akɛ akumɔ loo afo mli yɛ nitsumɔ mli?

english: Tree bark can heal over small surface cuts, but deep gouges that reach the inner wood take a long time to heal and leave permanent scars that lower yields.
ga: Abaanyɛ atsa ŋmeii kɛjɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Shi ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ ni shɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani etsaa ni eshiɔ ŋmeii ni hiɔ shi daa ni wooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why does sap stop flowing even when my tree looks green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu lɛ ekpa shwiemɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mitso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Even if the leaves look healthy, damage to the wood right beneath the bark blocks the pathways liquid travels through, stopping sap from reaching your harvesting cut.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ Shi kɛ́ tso ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ fite lɛ, ebaatsi nu ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haaa latex lɛ ayashɛ ŋmeii ni okpaa lɛ ahe.

english: How often can I safely tap my trees without destroying them?
ga: Shii enyiɛ manyɛ matswa tso ko shweshweeshwe ni mifiteee lɛ?

english: Tapping should be done on a regular, rested schedule rather than every day. Giving the bark time to recover protects the wood and keeps the yield steady over many years.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nibii ni akɛtaa mɔ he lɛ yɛ be ni ato ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ mli daa gbi moŋ fe daa gbi. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ yibii lɛ be ni ekɛtsa amɛhe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he ni eha tso lɛ afee nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade because direct hot sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the topsoil. Keeping larger trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides shade and keeps the moisture near the seedlings so they can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Tsei wuji loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ akwɛmɔ haa hulutsoo ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and stop growing when the rain stops for a short time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ?

english: Maize plants have shallow roots and need steady water, especially when young. When the soil dries out, the roots cannot suck up nitrogen from the earth, which causes the leaves to lose their green color and stop growing.
ga: Abɛi shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni ehe hiaa nu daa. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ amɛji gbekɛbii, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ.

english: How do I know which direction to plant my cassava sticks in the ground so they produce big tubers?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ odu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni onine ashɛ ŋmei wuji anɔ?

english: Cassava cuttings should always be planted with the small buds pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the stems waste energy trying to turn around, resulting in weak plants and small tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Always pointing up at the sky If you plant it upside down The trunk wastes energy trying to rotate. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ bulb bibii baa.

english: Why do I need to place tall sticks for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on wooden stakes allows the leaves to catch more sunlight to make food for the underground tubers. It also keeps the leaves off the wet soil, protecting them from fungal diseases.
ga: Raising sweet potato vines on wooden stakes allows the foliage to get more sunlight to make food for the underground tubers. It also helps prevent leaves from remaining in wet soil. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and turning yellow during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny flying insects called whiteflies. These insects multiply quickly in warm weather and suck sap from the leaves, weakening the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni foɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ faa oya yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, ni amɛnuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or dry soil. When the plant is under stress, it drops its blossoms to save its own strength rather than trying to feed growing fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Kɛ tsei yɔɔ haomɔ shishi Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi koni ehiɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii

english: Why does my land yield fewer groundnuts if I plant them in the exact same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo kɛji midu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot repeatedly drains specific soil nutrients and allows pests that feed on that crop to build up in the soil. Rotating your crops helps the soil rest and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ. Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my plantain tree give me small bunches when many little shoots grow around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains haa tsei niji bibii lɛ? kɛha mi beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ ni miida yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ he lɛ?

english: The extra shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients and water. Removing most of the suckers leaves more energy for the main plant to produce a big, heavy bunch.
ga: Tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni shwieɔ nu lɛ ateŋ babaoo lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my crop roots burn or turn black when I pour fertilizer right against the stem of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shãa loo amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts that draw water out of the plant roots if placed too close. Fertilizer should be placed in a small ring a short distance away from the stem where feeder roots can safely reach it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni baajie nu kɛjɛ tsei ashishifãi amli kɛji akɛ akɛwo amɛhe tsɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. ni kɛ tso lɛ shishifãi ni niyenii haa lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ fioo.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops even when I clear the land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jɛmɛ dani midu nii moŋ.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to survive harsh local conditions and poor soil. They sprout quickly to capture sunlight and moisture before cultivated crop seeds can fully establish their roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii mli. Amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya koni amɛmɔ hulu la kɛ fɛ̃i dani dumɔwui ni adu lɛ anyɛ akwɛ shishifãi kwraa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow green and leafy. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure early in the crop's growth will restore the rich green color and help your corn produce full ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ená baai. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli mra yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ emuu lɛ aku sɛɛ aba, ni ebaaye ebua o-ŋmei lɛ ni ekɛ toi ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Why should I plant cowpea or beans on my field after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize drains a lot of nutrients from the land, leaving the soil tired. Legumes like cowpeas and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth, naturally restoring soil fertility for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ha shikpɔŋ lɛ he ajɔ Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot right on the tree when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp, and overly shaded conditions. Pruning low branches to let in sunlight and harvesting mature pods quickly will reduce moisture and stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, edɔ, kɛ shade fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ amli fioo koni hulu la aba mli, ni akpa tsei ni shwereɔ oya lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi, ni ebaatsi helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ anaa.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from young shoots, or by a virus carried by those pests. Spraying the foliage with neem oil solution or recommended crop protection products keeps these pests away and protects new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni ji mɛi ni kɛ nakai tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ baa lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe ni ebaatsi shweremɔ hee naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when water stays on my farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rainwater sits on flat land, it smothers the roots and allows fungal rots to take hold. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps surplus water drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ta shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ Ebaatswa shishifãi lɛ ni eha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ amɔ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they get stressed by sudden dry spells, extreme heat, or irregular watering. Providing steady water at the root zone during hot periods helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa, latsaa ni naa wa, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be ha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: Why are my plantain bunches getting smaller every year even though the plants look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii daa afi lɛ? Ni tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ?

english: When too many young suckers shoot up around a main plantain stem, they all fight for the same food and water in the soil. Cutting away excess suckers and leaving only one main stem and one young replacement ensures big, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo shwie shi yɛ main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ Amɛbaawuu kɛha niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi tso lɛ yitso titri kome kɛ ŋmeii kome pɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii agbo ni tsii baa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to make enough energy to grow big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves dry and off the wet ground, which also prevents fungal leaves diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha bulbs wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ agbi ni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ baa helai ni ŋmeii kɛbaa lɛ hu naa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only a few turn into actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can feed as full pods, so the tree drops extra flowers to preserve its energy. Ensuring friendly insects like tiny midges are present to pollinate the flowers helps maximize the number of pods that survive.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni abaanyɛ aye akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyi obɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi krokomɛi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he. Kwɛmɔ ni kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo, tamɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni pods ni hiɔ shi lɛ ayi afa babaoo.

english: Why do weeds harm my young crops so much faster than older, established plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi tutuaa mi tsei bibii lɛ oya fe tsei ni eda ni etswa shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have short roots and small leaves, making them weak competitors against tough weeds for soil food, water, and sunlight. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks gives young crops the space they need to establish strong roots.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji kɛ baai bibii. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ ekɛ jwɛi ni he wa lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni ená niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni agbeɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and leafy. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer feeds the soil so the maize can stay strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha sũ lɛ aná hewalɛ koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my farm soil dry out so fast even after it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ waa po lɛ?

english: Soil without organic matter like dried leaves or animal manure cannot hold onto water. Adding compost or putting dry grass around crop bases acts like a sponge, keeping moisture in the ground longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ baai ni egboi loo kooloi ashishifãi bɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ ahiɛ nu. Kompost loo jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ baatsu nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: These are likely fall armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the soft leaves of young maize. Checking your crops early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or ash mixtures saves your leaves and yields.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii ahe baai bibii lɛ. Okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii amli mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo sũ ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baahere oŋmɔshi nibii kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Why are my tomato leaves twisting up into curls and stopping the plant from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekadara lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Keeping your farm free of weeds where whiteflies hide and using insect soaps helps protect your tomato plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi akafee nɔ ni whiteflies kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli Ni okɛ kooloi ahe samla baatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu o-tomato tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper fruits get soft black spots at the bottom and fall off before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ amɛshishi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Black spots on pepper bottoms often happen when the plant cannot get enough calcium or when soil moisture jumps between very dry and very wet. Consistent watering helps stop this rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. aloo beni shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa teŋ lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akpa nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds when the rainy season begins?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: It is best to wait until the soil stays continuously damp after a few regular rains, rather than planting immediately after the very first short shower, so your seeds don't dry up underground.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ kuku lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ egbiŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Excess standing water suffocates the roots, causing rot. Planting cassava on high soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees falling off without turning into young pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when trees suffer from dry heat or when there aren't enough tiny pollinating insects around. Keeping shade trees on your farm cools the air and creates a good home for pollinators.
ga: Fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ latsaa ni mli egbi mli loo kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni haa fɔfɔii lɛ faaa lɛ faaa. Ni oooha tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ofee shia kpakpa kɛha ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my yam plants need long wooden stakes to climb up as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ he hiaa tsei kakadaji ni amɛkwɔ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines use stakes to spread their leaves high in the air where they catch maximum sunlight. The sunshine allows the leaves to make more food, which makes the tubers underground grow much larger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei kɛ tsei tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛgbɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ lɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ feɔ wuji babaoo.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and curl up when the sun gets very hot in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during hot afternoons to protect themselves and stop water from evaporating too fast. If they turn yellow, it usually means the crop is stressed from a lack of water or needs nitrogen fertilizer to handle the intense sunlight.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao yɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ loo ehe miihia ni akɛ nitrogen awo mli koni enyɛ etsu hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he nii.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very few leaves when I plant them under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ baai fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Plants need direct sunlight to make their food. When they are shaded by big trees, they spend all their energy stretching upwards to reach the sun, making them weak, thin, and unable to produce heavy yields.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ tso agbo ko ha amɛhe shade lɛ Amɛbaafite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ koni amɛshɛ hulu lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbɔjɔɔ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava plants shed almost all their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during the Harmattan to save water and stay alive in dry soil. While the top of the plant looks dead, the roots under the ground remain alive and continue storing starch until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ harmattan beaŋ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo moŋ Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛbaaya nɔ amɛto ŋmei kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why does my yam farm produce very big green leaves but tiny yam tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli baai lɛ dara waa lɛ? Shi ani sweet potato ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or chemical fertilizer, the yam plant uses all its energy to grow leaves and vines above ground instead of sending that energy down to build large tubers in the soil.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fa babaoo lɛ Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ baai kɛ wain tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsu nakai hewalɛ lɛ kɛya shi koni ekɛfee bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my groundnut roots have small round bumps on them, and are they bad for the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo ni ehiii kɛha tso lɛ?

english: Those bumps are called root nodules and are actually very good. They store helpful bacteria that trap air from the atmosphere and turn it into natural nitrogen food for the groundnut crop and the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ root nodules ni amɛhi jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ, amɛhiɛɔ helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfeɔ lɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen niyenii kɛhaa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off before growing into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they get too stressed, usually from extreme heat, sudden dry spells, or too much water in the soil. Without stable moisture, the plant cannot support new fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baagbee shi kɛji amɛhao tsɔ. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi trukaa loo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛji hulutsoo bɛ be fɛɛ be Tso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ yibii hee lɛ nɔ.

english: A plantain stem is designed by nature to flower and bear fruit only once. After harvesting the bunch, that main stem dies so that light and food can go to the young shoots growing around its base.
ga: Adebɔɔ ji nɔ ni fee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ. Beni akpa ŋmeii lɛ agbe naa lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã lɛ gboɔ koni la kɛ niyenii ashɛ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ ahe lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomatoes turn black and rot right when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium due to sudden changes in moisture—like a long dry period followed by heavy rainfall—causing the bottom tissue of the fruit to collapse.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo tsakemɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ hewɔ, tamɔ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa fãji ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli fãa.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my cocoa seedlings after I clear new land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-kokoo dumɔwui lɛ beni mijie he ko hee lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit hidden in the soil waiting for sunlight. When you clear the bush, direct sunlight wakes up these weed seeds, and because weeds naturally absorb nutrients faster than young tree seedlings, they grow quickly.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe tee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni amɛmiimɛ hulu la. Kɛji otsi jwɛi lɛ mli lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baate jwɛi dumɔwui nɛɛ ashi. Ni akɛni jwɛi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe dumɔwui bibii hewɔ lɛ, No hewɔ lɛ amɛdaraa oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my cowpea crop fold up and close every evening when the sun goes down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛŋmɛɔ amɛhe daa gbɛkɛ kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cowpea leaves fold up at night to trap warmth and prevent moisture loss from cool night winds. This natural behavior also keeps dew off the leaves, which helps protect the plant from fungal diseases.
ga: Cowpea baai lɛ fɔ̃ɔ amɛhe gbɛkɛ koni amɛhiɛ hulutsoo mli ni amɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ mli baa lɛ naa. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli subaŋ nɛɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ akagbee baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants turn yellow and drop off whenever heavy rain settles on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: When water stays around crop roots for too long, it suffocates them by cutting off oxygen. Without air, the roots cannot absorb food from the soil, causing the plant leaves to turn yellow and fall off.
ga: Kɛ nu hi tso shishifãi ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaafo kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baafo mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: What happens to my crop roots when floodwater collects in the low spots of my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nu afua lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pooled water starves root systems of air and leads to root rot. Once roots rot, the plant loses its anchor and cannot take up water or nutrients even after the floodwater dries up.
ga: Nu ni abua naa lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ gboi lɛ, tso lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni enyɛɛɛ eŋɔ nu loo niyenii mli hewalɛ beni nu afua lɛ mli nu lɛ egbi po lɛ.

english: How will digging small drainage channels across my farm help my crops grow better during the rainy season?
ga: Nu tsɔne bibioo ko ni afoɔ Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Drainage channels give heavy rain a path to flow away from your farm, preventing waterlogging so your crops' root zones remain loose, well-aerated, and healthy.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Tsi nu ni hoɔ lɛ naa No hewɔ lɛ, otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shi mlɛo. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ jɛmɛ. ni oná gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ kpakpa

english: Why do my crops grow better on raised mounds or ridges when the rains are heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ waa lɛ?

english: Mounds and ridges lift your crops' roots above standing water, keeping the root zone dry enough to breathe while allowing excess water to drain into the furrows between them.
ga: Gɔji kɛ ŋmeii woɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyaa nu ni damɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Ha shishifã lɛ he lɛ agbi bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ omu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ ŋshɔ ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very few fruits when I plant them close to my big orange trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni ewoɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ yɛ mi-orange tso agbo lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to produce food for fruiting. Under big trees, heavy shade forces crops to waste all their energy stretching upward searching for light, resulting in weak stems and poor fruit yield.
ga: Hulu la he miihia tsei tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha yibiiwoo. tso agbo lɛ shishi Shade ni mli wa haa ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛtaoɔ la. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cassava in the spaces around my mature orange trees, or will they starve each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ he ni ebɔle wɔhe lɛ? Ani abaanyɛ akwɛ tso ni ji akutu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ? Aloo hɔmɔ baaye amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe?

english: Mature orange trees have wide root systems that absorb most of the water and nutrients in the ground. Planting heavy-feeding crops like cassava too close will cause both crops to compete and yield poorly.
ga: Citrus tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo. Niyenii tso ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei enyɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe abɔ akaŋ ni amɛbaawo yibii kpakpai.

english: How can I safely use the empty open ground between my orange trees to get extra harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ he ni yɔɔ mi-citrus tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ atsu nii shweshweeshwe koni mikɛkpa nibii krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ?

english: You can plant low-growing or shade-tolerant crops outside the drip line of the orange trees where sunlight reaches, ensuring the new crops do not steal food directly from the tree roots.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ tsei ni shwereɔ fioo loo ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hulutsoo shi yɛ o-citrus tso lɛ drip line lɛ kponɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ haa tso hee lɛ juuu niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are crops on one side of my large field producing high yields while the crops right next to them stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ woɔ yibii waa lɛ? be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ Afee bibii lolo ni amɛhe waaa?

english: Soil quality and water movement vary across large lands. Areas with compacted soil or poor drainage hinder root growth, while well-prepared sections allow roots to spread deep and gather nutrients easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kɛ nu lɛ nyiɛmɔ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ hei wuji. Hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ loo nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, fã ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shɔŋŋ ni ebuaa niyenii mli hewalɛ naa mlɛo.

english: How do I know if my land needs to be properly leveled and cleared before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ehe miihia ni mafee mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ajie nɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ dani mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: If you notice water pooling in uneven hollows or rain washing away soil in sloped areas after a downpour, your land needs leveling and contouring so water distributes evenly to all plants.
ga: Kɛji ona nu ni miibua ehe naa yɛ bu ni ejaaa mli loo nugbɔ ni miiho shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Ehe miihia ni okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee ekome ni okɛ husu awo mli bɔni afee ni nu lɛ aja tsei lɛ fɛɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: What does clearing and loosening hard, unbroken soil do for the growth of new crops?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni etseee lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii heei akwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Loosening hard soil breaks up compacted layers so tender young roots can push down deeply to reach underground moisture and nutrients, helping the plant grow strong and resist dry weather.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ ashɛre kɛya shɔŋŋ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi.

english: How can I choose the right type of coconut seedlings that won't get attacked by diseases easily?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ahala ŋmei tso ni sa ni helai nyɛɛɛ aba lɛ?

english: Choosing disease-resistant varieties before planting protects your farm from common threats like Lethal Yellowing disease, ensuring long-term crop survival without heavy losses.
ga: Kɛ́ ohala tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ dani oduɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ gbeyeishemɔi ni afɔɔ namɔ, tamɔ helai ni yellow leaf hela kɛbaa lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko fiteee amɛ.

english: How do I know if the coconut seedlings I am buying are healthy and safe to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni ehi akɛ aduɔ?

english: Healthy seedlings have strong stems, vibrant green leaves without spots, and good root systems, and they should ideally be purchased from certified agricultural nurseries.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ tsei ni wa. Baai lɛ yɛ eŋɔli ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he. kɛ shishifãi kpakpai Ni esa akɛ ahe dumɔwui nɛɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli hei ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to ask agricultural experts questions before I start planting a new crop on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabi okwaayeli he nilelɔ ko saji dani mabɔi tsei heei dumɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Consulting extension officers before planting helps you pick the right variety for your soil type and climate, saving you money and preventing crop failure.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ extension staff ko gba sane dani odu lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ohala tso ni sa kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ. Kɛ shika ato ni otsi ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa.

english: How do I know if my farmland is suitable for growing coconuts before I waste money planting them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmeii adumɔ dani mafite shika kɛdu amɛ?

english: Coconuts require well-draining soil and plenty of sunlight; having an officer assess your land beforehand ensures your soil conditions match the requirements of the crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ hulu la babaoo he miihia ŋmeii. Kɛ́ mɔ ko kwɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, ebaaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ lɛ kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiamɔ nii aba mli.

english: What happens to my crops if I do not prepare my farm properly before planting?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji misaaa miŋmɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani miduɔ nii?

english: Poor land preparation leads to weak root growth, standing water, and high vulnerability to pests and soil diseases, whereas doing it properly gives your crops a strong foundation.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaaa he jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ, nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baanyɛ aba lɛ waa. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, hesaamɔ ni sa baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why does planting long-term tree crops require more careful planning than growing seasonal crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ adumɔ?

english: Tree crops remain in the ground for decades, so any mistake made during seedling selection or planting will negatively affect your yields and income for many years.
ga: Tsei ni ji jwɛi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tɔmɔ fɛɛ tɔmɔ ni baaba yɛ dumɔwui ahalamɔ loo dumɔ mli lɛ baaná onibii kɛ shika ni onáa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii afii babaoo.

english: Is it better to prevent crop diseases before planting or treat them after my crops get sick?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaatsi tso hela naa dani adu loo atsa lɛ beni tso lɛ hela mɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Preventing diseases by planting strong, resistant varieties and keeping clean land is far cheaper and more effective than trying to cure sick plants later.
ga: Helai ni abaatsi naa kɛtsɔ tsei srɔtoi ni wa, ni wa ni aduɔ kɛ he ni akwɛɔ koni he tse lɛ nɔ lɛ jara waaa kwraa ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni abɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni atsa tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do some coconut trees die suddenly or stop bearing fruit after a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akokoshi tsei komɛi gboiɔ trukaa loo amɛkpaa yibiiwoo yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Trees often die early due to soil-borne diseases, lack of proper nutrients, or planting weak seed varieties that cannot survive local environmental pressures.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa lɛ haa tsei gboiɔ oya. Niyenii kpakpa ni bɛ loo dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛŋ adamɔ shihilɛ mli nɔnyɛɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anaa.

english: I want to start growing coconuts for the first time, but I am afraid of losing my money. How should I begin safely?
ga: Miisumɔ ni makwɛ ŋmei klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa shi misheɔ gbeyei akɛ shika baafite. Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ maje shishi shweshweeshwe?

english: Reduce financial risk by getting advice on disease-resistant seeds, following correct planting spacing, and giving proper care to seedlings from day one.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ shika he osharai anɔ kɛtsɔ ŋaawoo ni ooona yɛ dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Ha dumɔ he jɛkɛmɔ ni sa lɛ ahi shi. ni okwɛ dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi lɛ nɔ

english: How does doing proper land work help my crops survive bad weather or pest outbreaks?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitsumɔ jogbaŋŋ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi gbohii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ amli?

english: Crops planted correctly in healthy soil develop deep roots and strong immunity, making them much more resilient to sudden drought, heavy rain, or pest attacks.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli hewalɛ ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ naa hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ.

english: If I clear a new farm plot by burning the bush, will it help my crops grow better?
ga: Kɛji mijie ŋmɔ hee ko kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni shãa lɛ nɔ Ani ebaaye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Burning provides a quick burst of ash that acts as short-term fertilizer, but it destroys essential organic matter and kills helpful living organisms in the soil. Over time, burning leaves the soil dry, hard, and poor at holding water for your crops.
ga: Shãa ni ashãa oya lɛ haa sũ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni efiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Beni be hoɔ lɛ Shãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbiɔ, ewaa ni enyɛɛɛ ehiɛ nu kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I know if the soil on my fresh land is good for planting vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha aduawai adumɔ?

english: Good soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hands, drains water well without leaving standing pools, and naturally supports thick, healthy green weeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Efoɔ nu jogbaŋŋ ni eshiuuu nubui. ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, efiɔ jwɛi ŋmɔji ni mli wa ni mli wa lɛ asɛɛ

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot dry spells as a survival trick to save water. The plant is not dead; once the rains return, it will quickly sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ koni akɛbu nu he. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Baai eŋɔli heei baakwɛ̃ oya ni amɛbaaya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up into tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi efeɔ tsɔne yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl to shield themselves from the harsh heat and reduce water loss through evaporation. It is the plant's natural way of protecting itself from drying out.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni amɛha nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ aba shi. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he koni ekagbi.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and weak when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the maize plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward to reach light instead of growing thick stalks and big ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Abele tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaná ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ toi wuji.

english: Extreme afternoon heat can dry out or damage the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fertilization. When a flower cannot be pollinated, the plant drops it to save energy.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ agbi loo efite. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Beni fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee pollin lɛ Tsei lɛ baashɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: How can I tell that my yams under the ground are mature and ready to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: When the yam leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up at the end of the rainy season, it signals that the plant has stopped growing and stored all its food energy into the tuber.
ga: Beni sweet potato baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ eniyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ miito bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant groundnuts or beans on the same land as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, this nitrogen acts as a free natural fertilizer for your maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ mli Nitrogen nɛɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa o-ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why do fall armyworms damage my maize mostly during the night and early morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworm fiteɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ fe fɛɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ kɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms dislike the hot daytime sun and hide deep inside the moist center funnel of the maize plant. They come out in the cool night to safely eat the leaves.
ga: Autumn cutworms lɛ sumɔɔɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ. ni ekɛ ehe tee ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni mli efɔ lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛye baai lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Saving and planting hybrid seeds usually yields poor results. Hybrid seeds are created through special breeding for one season only; seeds saved from that harvest will produce uneven, weak plants with much lower yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni abua naa ni aduɔ lɛ haaa yibii kpakpai aba. Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ feɔ dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi kɛha be kome pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei ni egbɔjɔ, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Does planting my maize seeds very close together give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ haa mináa ŋmãa babaoo?

english: No, planting too close causes the crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing allows each maize plant to grow strong stems and full cobs instead of many small, weak plants.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa tso mli lɛ haa ŋmãa tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ. Yɛ tso bibioo najiaŋ lɛ, mɛi babaoo ni bɛ hewalɛ

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them first enriches the soil with natural fertilizer, which makes heavy-feeding crops like maize grow better afterward.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa tsei ni akɛhaa kooloi babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to place long wooden stakes next to my yam plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to catch sunlight. Putting up stakes spreads the leaves out so they can catch maximum sun to make food, which the plant then sends underground to grow large, heavy tubers.
