ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. Staking gbɛɔ baai lɛ eshwaa koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ ni amɛkɛhoo nii. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛ tsei lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking the plant's sap and spreading viruses. Managing these insects early using organic or recommended sprays helps stop the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Nibii nɛɛ akwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown dirt in the growing tip?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛyitsei ni miida lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the whorl of the maize plant. Spraying approved insecticides or applying local remedies like fine sand in the center of the plant early in the morning can control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli lɛ. Abaanyɛ akudɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsofa ko ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋã kpakpa ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ leebi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my fruiting plantain trees easily fall over when a small wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko pɛ tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when microscopic worms called nematodes or stem borer insects destroy their root system underground. Without healthy roots to anchor the plant, the heavy weight of the plantain bunch causes the tree to topple.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ kpata amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahiɛ. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa ni baaha tso lɛ ahi shi lɛ bɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ baaha tso lɛ akumɔ shi.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight and high heat. Leaving tall trees or planting plantains provides shade and preserves soil moisture, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei kakadaji ni ashiɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ hiɔ shi. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil, or the ground is flooded with water, preventing the roots from breathing and taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu ni amɛkaná niyenii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant faces extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of beneficial insects like bees to pollinate the blossoms. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps prevent flower drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni baahã fɔfɔii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ mulch woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains cause standing water around the roots, the oxygen is cut off, causing fungal rot to set in and soften the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow and dropping off before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves turn yellow and drop early mainly because of nutrient shortages in the soil, water stress during dry spells, or damage from pests like cassava green mites. Healthy cassava needs balanced soil nutrients and moisture to keep its leaves green and feed the growing tubers underneath.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya. Nɔ titri ni kɛbaa ji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu mli haomɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli loo nɔ ni jɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ cassava green mite lɛ amli baa. Cassava ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ he miihia ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa koni eha baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni eha bulbs ni miida yɛ shishi lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak root systems that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or shade trees alongside them protects the seedlings from heat stress and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa matures.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo shade tsei ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Ebuɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants require a lot of water to develop thick stems and heavy fruit bunches. During the dry harmattan season, high winds and lack of rain cause the plant to lose moisture rapidly, which slows fruit growth and results in smaller yields unless extra water is supplied.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia plantains koni amɛná tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. Yɛ Harmattan be ni nugbɔ enyɔɔ lɛ mli Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ daraaa oya, ni ehaa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi, ja akɛ nu kroko fata he.

english: Why do my maize plants flower too early when the rains do not come on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ fɔ̃ɔ oya tsɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ be naa lɛ?

english: When maize faces heat and drought stress, its natural defense mechanism triggers early flowering to produce seeds quickly before the plant dies. This premature flowering leads to small cobs because the plant did not have enough time or water to build a strong frame.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa kɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ mli ba lɛ ŋmãa adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛi lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni baa mra kɛ dumɔwui ni baa oya lɛ he hewalɛ dani tso lɛ gboɔ. Fɔfɔi ni baa mra lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ be loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaafee tsɔne ni mli wa.

english: Why do my maize stalks become thin and fall over when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei babaoo amli lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition causes the stalks to grow tall and thin as they search for light, making them weak and easy for wind to blow down.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tso lɛ tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ beni etaoɔ la lɛ. Ehaa egbɔjɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ lɛ oya

english: Why do weeds make my pepper plants stay weak and produce small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi-pepper tsei lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛwo yibii bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds act as aggressive neighbors that steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your pepper plants. When weeds surround your crops, the pepper plants cannot get enough nutrients to build strong stems or develop plump fruits.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ akutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ basabasa ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ o-pepper tsei lɛ amli. Kɛ jwɛi bɔle oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, Chili tsei lɛ nyɛŋ ana niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmeii ni wa loo amɛwo yibii ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow huge green leaves but give me very few tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi amɛwoɔ tomato fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants produce mostly leaves instead of fruit when there is too much nitrogen in the soil relative to other nutrients like phosphorus and potassium. Excessive nitrogen encourages leafy growth, while phosphorus and potassium are needed to produce strong flowers and healthy tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ kɛ́ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium he. Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa baa lɛ daa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium he miihia koni fɔfɔi ni mli wa kɛ tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant beans or cowpeas on the farm before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has the special ability to take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛyɛ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okpa amɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi

english: What causes my yam tubers to rot inside the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa?

english: Yam tuber rot in the soil is usually caused by excessive water stagnation in poorly drained soil combined with fungal or bacterial infections. Pests like nematodes can also bite tiny holes into the tubers, allowing soil germs to enter and decay the yam.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato tuber fitemɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa. Kɛfata fungal loo bacteria helai ahe lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes hu baanyɛ akɔmɔ bu bibii ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ni eha helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ abote mli ni eha sweet potato lɛ fite.

english: Why do I need to prune and cut off some branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji komɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary and weak branches so sunlight and air can pass through the tree canopy. Good airflow reduces humidity inside the tree, which prevents pod diseases like black pod from spreading, and directs the tree's energy into growing bigger cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ atsɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ haa fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai ni jɛɔ pod mli kɛbaa tamɔ pod diji lɛ akagbɛ ashwã. ni okɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo kookoo ŋmeii wuji amli.

english: Officer, why are my crops dying even after I sprayed them with the crop medicine I bought from the market?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa shwie tsei ni mihe yɛ jara nɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ?

english: Spraying the wrong medicine or using incorrect dosages can burn and damage your crops instead of curing them. Always confirm with an extension officer that a chemical is approved for your specific crop and disease before applying it.
ga: Tsofa ni ejaaa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ ashã ni efite moŋ fe ni eeetsa lɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, bi o-extension official lɛ akɛ akpɛlɛ tsofai anɔ kɛha onibii pɔtɛɛ kɛ hela dani okɛtsu nii.

english: Can I let my goats feed around my farm right after I spray chemical medicine on my maize?
ga: Mibaanyɛ maha tooi lɛ aye nii yɛ he fɛɛ he. Ani manyɛ mafee okwaayeli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofai ewo ŋmãa mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: No, farm pesticides and crop medicines contain chemicals that are toxic to animals. Keep your livestock away from freshly sprayed fields for at least two weeks to prevent severe poisoning or death.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛ tsei ahe tsofai lɛ yɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi. Kɛ hoo lɛ, ha okooloi lɛ akabɔ ŋmɔji ni afɔ amɛ tsofa ehee lɛ ahe otsii enyɔ koni amɛkaye tsofai fɔji loo gbele ni naa wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plant turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are caused by viral diseases spread by tiny insects like whiteflies, not bad luck or spiritual forces. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties helps keep the crop healthy.
ga: Helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ, shi jeee shweremɔ loo mumɔŋ hewalɛi. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I know if the plant medicine I am buying in town is genuine and safe for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei ahe tsofai ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji anɔkwale ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Approved farm chemicals in Ghana are tested and registered by regulatory agencies like the EPA. Always look for official registration labels on the container and purchase from licensed agro-dealers.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ, nitsumɔhei ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ tamɔ EPA lɛ kaa amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛŋmalaa amɛgbɛi amɛwoɔ wolo nɔ. Taomɔ wolo ni aŋmala nɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be. kɛ nihɔɔmɔ kɛjɛ okwaayeli jalɔi ni aha amɛ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ

english: Why do my corn plants grow very tall with thick green leaves but produce tiny cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse shi amɛji ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: This happens when plants receive too much nitrogen but lack essential nutrients like phosphorus and potassium. Balanced fertilization ensures the plant directs its energy into forming large cobs rather than just leaves and stems.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo shi amɛbɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ni ja lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji. Jeee baai kɛ ŋmeii pɛ

english: Why do my tomato leaves wilt during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Under intense heat, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than roots can draw water from the soil, causing them to wilt to conserve water. As temperatures drop in the evening, the leaves naturally stand up again.
ga: yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi Tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ lɛ Baai lɛ baadamɔ shi ekoŋŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do armyworms keep eating my maize leaves even after heavy rain falls on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms yaa nɔ eyeɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ? Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli po?

english: Rainwater does not destroy pests like armyworms because they hide deep inside the central funnel of the maize plant. Targeted treatments applied directly into the plant funnel are needed to reach and control them.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ efiteee kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ cutworms. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ shɔŋŋ. Tsofai ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tsei akui ahe lɛ he miihia koni anyɛ ashɛ amɛhe ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to mix two different crop medicines together in the same spray knapsack to save time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe tsofai srɔtoi enyɔ atsake yɛ sɛɛgbɛ tsofa kome mli koni mikɛ be akafite?

english: Combining random crop chemicals can cause harmful reactions that damage your plants or render the treatments ineffective. Always ask an extension officer before mixing different products together.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli ni akɛfutuɔ he trukaa lɛ baanyɛ aha nibii ni yɔɔ oshara aba ni efite otsei lɛ loo eha tsofafeemɔ lɛ akatsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ obi mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ dani okɛ nibii srɔtoi afutu mli.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper yibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when plants face extreme heat stress, drought, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees. Regular watering and avoiding harsh chemical sprays while plants are flowering helps protect fruit formation.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ tamɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ lɛ mli. Nu ni oooha tso lɛ daa ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he be mli ni tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tso yibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do pests attack my neighbor's crops more heavily than mine when we planted at the exact same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fe mi nɔ lɛ kɛ́ wɔdu nii yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Crops grown in healthier soil build natural resilience that makes them stronger against insect attacks. Adding organic manure enriches soil quality, helping plants defend themselves against pests.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni haa amɛhe waa kɛshiɔ kooloi ni baatutua amɛ lɛ. Organic fertilizer ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to strong, direct sunlight and can easily dry out. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide essential shade and cool moisture, protecting the young cocoa plants during their early growth stage.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nuɔ hulu la he tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning pale yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or urea can help the maize turn deep green and grow stronger.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baa lɛ adalɛ ni mli wa Kɛ akɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ NPK loo urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ŋmãa ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help make the soil better for my next crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their root nodules. When the crop season ends and root parts decompose in the dirt, they leave behind rich natural plant food for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee ni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii babaoo yɛ amɛsɛɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: When planting cassava stems, check the small growth nodes or leaf scars on the stick and make sure they are pointing upward toward the sky. Planting stems upside down causes the plant to waste energy trying to sprout, leading to poor crop yield.
ga: Kɛji oodu ŋmei tsei Kwɛmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɛji ŋmeii bibii komɛi ekwɛ̃. loo ŋmeii ni jɛ baai ni yɔɔ tsei aniji anɔ lɛ amli Ni kwɛmɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kwɛ̃ shi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ be mli ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii

english: Why do my maize leaves look like small caterpillars are eating holes through them from the inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ŋmeii bibii miiye bu kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the central funnel of the maize leaves to feed. Checking your farm early and spraying targeted biological or chemical treatments directly into the plant whorls keeps the pest under control.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra ni okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies transmitting a virus. Sprays made from neem leaf extracts or recommended insecticides help clear these insects and stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ numɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ ni akɛ neem tso mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ feɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ ni ekpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without making any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when daytime temperature gets too hot or when soil moisture swings quickly between too dry and too wet. Watering your tomatoes evenly and giving them light shade during intense dry heat helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ teŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why is it important for me to lift my yam vines off the ground using tall stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko awo mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking yam vines keeps the leaves lifted into the air where they catch maximum sunlight to feed the underground tubers. It also keeps leaves off damp soil, which prevents leaf spot diseases from spreading across the farm.
ga: Wein tsei ni akɛwoɔ sweet potato mli lɛ haa anyɛɔ awoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni hulu la babaoo aná bɔ ni aaanyɛ koni akɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he. Enɛ baaye abua ni hela ni ji leaf spot lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow around one mother plantain tree forces them to compete for soil food and water. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures that the mother plant produces large, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baaha tso nyɛ lɛ awo ŋmeii babaoo ni tsii.

english: How does the dry Harmattan wind affect my vegetable garden, and how can I protect it?
ga: Te Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ saa mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he?

english: Dry Harmattan winds suck moisture out of topsoil and leaves quickly, causing tender plants to wilt. Covering the soil around crop stems with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps soil cool and retains moisture longer.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ baai lɛ amli oya. Ehaa tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when they are out in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch easily in direct heat. Planting shade crops like plantains next to them creates a protective umbrella that keeps the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni kookoo tso bibioo lɛ yaa nɔ edaa waa lɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or appropriate fertilizer helps the leaves turn green again and grow healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, spread out the leaves to catch sunlight, and prevents diseases from spreading from the soil to the leaves, leading to larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Gbalamɔ baai lɛ amli koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ nɔ. Ni otsi hela naa koni ekajɛ sũ mli kɛya baai amli. ni kɛ yitso ni da baa

english: Cassava is usually ready when the plant's lower leaves dry up and fall off, and the ground around the base of the stem starts to crack as the underground tubers swell up, typically 8 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. Ni he ni tso lɛ shishi yɔɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why does my land give me smaller harvests every time I plant maize on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land year after year uses up all the specific nutrients that crop needs. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts helps restore vital nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ kɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛi fɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ tsuɔ nii. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Early rains can be misleading and dry up quickly. Dig a small hole about hand-depth into the ground; if the soil is wet all the way down to that depth, there is enough moisture stored to help your seeds germinate safely.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ alaka mɔ ni egbi oya. Tsɔmɔmɔ bu bibioo ko kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛyashi nakai shishigbɛ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ Fɛ̃i ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe lɛ baahi.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce smaller fruits even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your main crop. Clearing weeds early ensures that all the plant food in the soil goes straight into making your crops grow big.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa onibii lɛ daraa.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that transmit viruses, or by severe heat stress. Protecting plants with shade nets or using insect-control methods stops the spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli Kɛ́ akɛ shade netting bu tsei ahe loo akɛ gbɛi ni akɛbuɔ kooloi ahe lɛ baakpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants drop off before producing any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ pepper ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as very high temperatures or sudden dry soil. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔi kpe, tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi trukaa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What is eating the inside of the young leaves in the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ yeli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows inside the growing center (funnel) of young corn plants. Checking your farm early and treating the funnels helps stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ adalɛ mli (cone) lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni ŋmeii lɛ ni oookwɛ amɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkpaa amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to grow green leaves and strong stems. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I leave dry grass on top of my soil after clearing instead of burning it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ beni mijie jwɛi lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mashã lɛ?

english: Leaving dry grass on top of the soil acts like a blanket that keeps the ground cool, traps moisture during hot days, and slowly decays into rich organic fertilizer instead of losing nutrients to smoke.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli, ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baafite lɛ

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough space allows its roots to spread and feed properly, resulting in bigger yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii babaoo ni afeɔ.

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for the growing tuber underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp soil, catching the sun while preventing rot and disease.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la naa, ni etsiɔ fitemɔ kɛ helai hu anaa.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in wet or poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ loo nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get dark, sunken spots at the bottom as they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi diji kɛ shishigbɛ ni eboteɔ mli kɛ́ ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by irregular watering or a lack of calcium in the plant while the fruit is forming. Mulching the soil and watering regularly helps the tomato take in calcium evenly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli be mli ni tso lɛ woɔ yibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli daa ni akɛ nu wo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tomato ni enáa calcium ni fa babaoo.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, very dry soil, or insect attacks. Giving the plants light shade and steady watering during hot spells helps them hold their blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa loo kooloi ni baatutua tso lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔlɔ wo tso lɛ nɔ ni okɛ nu wo mli daa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do experienced farmers tell me to plant groundnuts or beans together with my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ baakɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have tiny root sacs that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground. Planting them with corn naturally fertilizes the soil and helps the corn grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi bibii. koni ejie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Abele ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop many of their small pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? Mɛi enyiɛ dani etsɔ agbo?

english: Young cocoa trees drop excess pods, known as cherelle wilt, when they do not have enough water or nutrients to support all of them. The tree naturally sacrifices some young pods to save energy for the surviving ones.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine, ni ale lɛ akɛ Cherelle Wilt lɛ, kɛ́ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmeii muu lɛ fɛɛ bɛ. Tsei kɛ ŋmeii bibii shaa afɔle yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka lɛ ahe.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry heat wave that can scorch delicate young seeds before the main rains settle in. Waiting until the rainfall becomes regular ensures young plants do not dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ latsaa ni mli egbi ni baanyɛ agbe dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ, ebaatsi tsei bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do the seeds I buy from certified seed dealers grow better than the seeds I save from my own maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ahe jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred and tested to ensure high germination rates, strong plant growth, and disease resistance. Seeds saved from previous harvests gradually lose these strong traits over time, resulting in weaker plants and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni ana akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo. tsei ni yaa hiɛ waa kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Efiteɔ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: If I plant seeds harvested from last year's high-yielding hybrid crop, why do the new plants grow unevenly and yield less?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ tsei ni ji hybrid tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ tsei heei lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are created by crossing two specific parent plants to get maximum yield in the first generation. The seeds produced by that harvest lose those combined traits, leading to unpredictable plant growth and reduced harvests.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ feɔ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ ni akɛfoɔ mli koni anyɛ ana yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni akpaa lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba, ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do seeds bought from registered seed suppliers sprout almost all at the same time in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ahe nitsulɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ shikome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Registered seed supplies undergo strict quality control to ensure uniform seed age, size, and health. Because the seeds are equal in vigor, they all absorb water and break dormancy at the exact same pace.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ yaa nɔkwɛmɔ ni mli wa mli koni ana nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ wala, amɛdalɛ kɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ yaa nɔ daa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ kome. No hewɔ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu ni amɛfoɔ wɔɔhe lɛ mli yɛ oyaiyeli ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ mli.

english: What happens to my crop seeds if I plant them in the farm during the dry season without irrigation?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni nu shwieee nɔ?

english: Seeds require continuous soil moisture to awaken and stay alive. Without sufficient water, the seeds will either remain dormant, dry out right after starting to sprout, or get eaten by soil insects before the rains arrive.
ga: Dumɔwui hia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛhi shi ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi. Egbiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ŋmɔshi nibii je shishi lɛ. Aloo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ lɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ baa.

english: Does crop seed spoil or lose its power to sprout if I store it in my house for a full year before planting?
ga: Ani dumɔwui lɛ baafite loo amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo shĩa mli afi muu fɛɛ dani midu amɛ?

english: Yes, stored seeds naturally age and lose viability over time. Heat and humidity in normal room storage cause the living embryo inside the seed to weaken or die, leading to poor germination when eventually planted.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baagbɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhi shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ nitoohei lɛ haa fɔmɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ dumɔwui amli lɛ gbɔjɔɔ loo egbeɔ amɛ. Enɛ haaa ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu yɛ naagbee.

english: Why do my vegetable seeds take much longer to sprout when planted during cool rainy weather compared to warm weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ akɛto hulutsoo be he lɛ?

english: Seeds rely on soil warmth to trigger their chemical growth processes. Cooler temperatures slow down these internal processes, delaying sprouting and leaving the seeds vulnerable to rotting in damp soil.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ nɔ koni ekɛ tsofai awo dalɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli hewalɛ. Fɛ̃i ni mli ejɔ haa nɛkɛ mligbɛ nifeemɔi nɛɛ baa shi. Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ oshara mli akɛ amɛbaafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants start producing small flowers when the plants are still very short during a drought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miibɔi fɔfɔi bibii feemɔ lɛ? Akɛni tsei lɛ yɛ kuku waa lolo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli hewɔ lɛ?

english: When crops experience water stress, they feel threatened and switch from growing leaves to reproducing. Producing flowers early is the plant's survival trick to make seeds quickly before it potentially dies from lack of water.
ga: Kɛ tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ kpe lɛ Amɛnuɔ he akɛ awo amɛhe gbeyei ni amɛtsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ baai akwɛmɔ mli kɛyaa fɔmɔ mli. Fɔfɔi ni akɛhaa mra Eji tso lɛ teemɔŋ sane ni haa ehiɔ shi akɛ ebaawo dumɔwui oya dani egbo yɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize plants turn yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The maize plant copes by moving available nitrogen from its older, lower leaves up to feed the young, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abele tsei nyɛɔ amɛkpeɔ naa kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ baai bibii kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do some cassava varieties stay green and healthy while my local cassava leaves roll up and turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ? Beni mimaŋ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Improved cassava varieties have built-in genetic resistance to diseases like Cassava Mosaic Virus. Local varieties lack this defense, so viral attacks easily disrupt their leaf growth and food production.
ga: Kasava henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ fɔmɔ nii ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ helai tamɔ cassava mosaic virus. Kuu lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi lɛ bɛ hebuu nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbalaa baai adalɛ kɛ niyenii feemɔ mli oya.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with small ears when planted too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ toi bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When planted too close, maize stalks compete fiercely with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The plants stretch upward to reach light, spending energy on tall stems instead of developing full, heavy ears.
ga: Kɛ adu Abɛi tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Tso lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi koni eshɛ la lɛ he. kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ lɛ nɔ Yɛ toi ni tsii ni eyi obɔ lɛ najiaŋ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big shade trees away from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand direct sunlight and intense heat. They need taller shade trees or fast-growing plants like plantains to act as protective shields, preserving soil moisture and keeping the young cocoa plants safe from scorching until they are mature enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei kakadaji ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains koni amɛtsu nii akɛ gãimlibii. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oha cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ shãa he kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why is it better to raise pepper seeds under a temporary palm frond canopy before moving them into the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui yɛ ŋmei tso ko shishi be kukuoo ko dani ajie amɛ kɛya ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Tiny seeds and young sprouts are fragile and easily crushed by heavy rains or burnt by the midday sun. A temporary shade structure protects the delicate seedlings until their stems and roots are strong enough to survive full exposure.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii kɛ tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo gbɛjianɔtoi buɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my pawpaw trees produce flowers every season but never grow any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi daa be shi ewooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Pawpaw plants have distinct male and female trees. Male trees only produce pollen to fertilize the female flowers and will never carry fruits themselves, while the female trees rely on that pollen to develop healthy fruit.
ga: Pawpaw tsei yɛ tsei hii kɛ yei srɔtoi. Tsei ni ji hii lɛ woɔ pollen koni fɔfɔi yei lɛ pɛ awo amɛmli. ni ekɛ yibiiwoo ko baaa yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ emli. yɛ be mli ni tsei yei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nakai pollen lɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my maize cobs sometimes have missing grains with big empty gaps on the cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii ni elaaje kɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Maize relies on the wind to carry pollen from the top tassels down to the silks of nearby plants. If plants are spaced too far apart or exposed to heavy drying winds during flowering, proper pollination fails, leaving empty spaces on the cob.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ koni ekɛ pollen ajɛ ŋwɛi ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛba shi kɛya tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ asilki lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe teŋ jɛkɛ tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa tswa amɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, Proper pollination lɛ baafee nɔ ni bɛ sɛɛnamɔ. Enɛ haa he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ baa cob lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii kɛfata ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans act as natural fertilizer builders. They capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, feeding and strengthening the neighboring maize crops without needing extra chemical inputs.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii ni ewoɔ amɛ hewalɛ ni tsofai krokomɛi ahe ehiaaa.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my young crops with dry leaves and straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi aha he ni tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Mulching with dry grass or leaves creates a protective layer over the soil. This shield stops the sun from evaporating soil water, keeps root systems cool, and prevents weeds from sprouting and stealing nutrients from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Nɛkɛ tsɔne nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Why do I need to stick long wooden poles into the ground for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni mi sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam vines need vertical support to lift their leaves up toward the sunlight and keep them off the wet soil. Staking prevents leaf rot diseases and allows the plant to send maximum energy down into forming large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia nibii ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ koni amɛwo baai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ nɔ ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Staking tsiɔ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni ehaa tso lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ koni ekɛfee bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I trim off the lowest leaves of my tomato plants as they grow taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Removing the lowest leaves prevents soil-borne fungal diseases from splashing onto the plant during heavy rainfall and allows the plant to direct its strength into producing larger tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei kudɔɔ amɛhewalɛ koni amɛwo tomatoi wuji.

english: Why do some farmers plant bright flowers like marigolds around the edges of their vegetable beds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, tamɔ marigold, yɛ amɛ aduawai ŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Certain flowering plants act as natural guardians by releasing strong scents and root chemicals that repel damaging soil pests like nematodes and harmful insects, keeping nearby food crops safe.
ga: Tsei komɛi ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli bulɔi kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni naa wa kɛ tsofai ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi amli ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ. Ha niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: How does planting tall vetiver grass along the boundaries of my sloping farm protect my crops?
ga: Te vetiver jwɛi kakadaŋŋ adumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ naa lɛ baabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Tall, thick grasses planted in rows act as living walls that slow down running rainwater during heavy storms, preventing rich topsoil from washing away and protecting crop roots from being exposed.
ga: Jwɛi kakadaji ni mli tse ni adu yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbogbo ni hiɛ ka ni haa nugbɔ nu lɛ baa shi yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli. Ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ebuɔ tsei shishifãi ahe koni amɛkaje kpo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade to protect them from harsh sunlight and heat. Without taller shade trees like plantains or forest trees to filter the light, the tender cocoa leaves burn, turn yellow, and eventually wither.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui taoɔ hɔɔŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo ni nɔ kwɔ tamɔ dumɔwui loo kooi ni baatsi la lɛ naa lɛ bɛ lɛ, Soft cocoa leaves lɛ baashã. etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egboɔ

english: Why do my cashew trees drop their flowers without producing any fruit when heavy rains fall during flowering time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cashew tsei lɛ fɔfɔɔɔ ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away pollen and physically damage delicate blossoms, while high moisture creates ideal conditions for fungal diseases that rot the flowers before bees can pollinate them.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni efiteɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo be ni fa babaoo lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Yellowing that starts at the tips of lower leaves indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to build healthy green leaves and big ears, which can be restored using organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizers.
ga: Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ toi wuji aba. Abaanyɛ aku sɛɛ aku sɛɛ afee enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do other farmers tell me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in my field before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi Ko ni amɛkɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them enriches the soil with free nutrients that feed the maize crop during the next season.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni baaha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ aye nii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, or by viruses carried by these pests. Controlling insects early stops them from stunting leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni ji nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ nɔ Mra Be mli Kooloi Akwɛmɔ Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaha amɛbaai lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered by inconsistent soil moisture. Keeping soil moisture steady and adding calcium helps fix the problem.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium ni akɛfataa he lɛ saa naagba lɛ.

english: Why do my garden egg plants wilt and die within days after heavy rainwater collects on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ebua amɛhe naa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Standing water smothers the plant roots by cutting off oxygen, causing root rot. When the roots drown and die, the plant can no longer absorb water or nutrients, making it wilt and collapse.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ tsiɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ bote shi ni amɛgboi lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu loo niyenii mli hewalɛ dɔŋŋ. ni haa egbɔjɔɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa

english: Why does my cassava shed all its leaves during the dry season, and is the crop dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigboi?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells as a natural defense mechanism to conserve water. The plant is still alive underground and will quickly grow fresh foliage once the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ nu he. Tso lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo, ni ebaakwɛ baai heei oya kɛji nugbɔ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Allowing too many shoots, or suckers, to grow around one plantain stem creates competition for food and water, resulting in small bunches. Keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures maximum bunch size.
ga: Aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso kome he Enɛ haa akaŋshii baa niyenii kɛ nu he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji niji bibii. Kɛji akɛ okɛ suckers kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni mli wa to lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ona nɔmimaa akɛ kuu lɛ dalɛ fa fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do I have to train my yam vines onto tall stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking raises yam leaves toward the sun, allowing them to capture maximum light to manufacture food for growing big tubers, while also keeping leaves dry to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ akwɛ hulu lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛfee niyenii kɛha bulb agboi ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ agbi koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli.

english: When lower leaves turn yellow, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen if the roots are sitting in too much water.
ga: Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli.

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil. It also lets soil pests and diseases build up, making your harvests smaller each year.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ. Ebaaha nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ nɔŋŋ afite kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa okpamɔ lɛ feɔ bibioo daa afi.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and small roots that dry out very quickly in full sun. They need shade from fast-growing plants like plantains to protect them while they grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi bibii ni hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when they start carrying heavy fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ ebɔi yibii ni tsii womɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots in the soil. When heavy fruit grows at the top, strong winds or soft, wet soil can easily pull the roots up unless you support the trunk with a sturdy wooden prop.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ aduawai ni tsii kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋwɛi Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala shishifãi lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi oya. Ja okɛ tso ni wa fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yam plants are natural climbing vines. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground allows them to catch more sunlight to make food, and keeps the leaves dry so rot diseases don't spread.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛhooɔ nii. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ agbiɔ koni ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready to harvest without digging up the farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni akuuu mli?

english: As cassava reaches maturity, the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the main stem begins to swell and crack from the large tubers growing below.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbɛɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop without making fruit when the weather becomes too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no beneficial insects around to move pollen between flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he ni amɛbaajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi ateŋ lɛ.

english: Weeds are wild native plants that are naturally tough and well-adapted to the local soil and weather, allowing them to suck up water and nutrients much faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ko ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni eyɛ adebɔɔ mli ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the juices out of young leaves and transferring tiny viruses that stop normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ekɛ nu ni yɔɔ baai bibii amli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɛɔ helai bibii eshwaa. ni haa baai lɛ adalɛ bɔ ni sa lɛ kpaɔ

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is already moist after a light rain so the roots can drink it in, but never right before a heavy downpour that will wash it all away.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. koni shishifãi lɛ anu Shi kaaŋɔ ŋmɔshi nii dani nugbɔ ni naa wa ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ ashwie lɛ aba.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to grow strong and green. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help restore the green color and improve your crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which acts as free natural food for your maize. They also spread over the soil surface, keeping the ground cool, saving soil moisture, and blocking weeds from growing.
ga: Cowpeas mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa o-corn lɛ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu. ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up tightly during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl during the hottest part of the day as a natural defense to protect themselves from losing too much water. If the leaves uncurl when the evening weather cools down, your plant is healthy, but if they stay curled, the crop needs more watering.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Kɛji baai lɛ shwieee shi beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli woɔ la Tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ yɛ hewalɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle lɛ, no lɛ ehe miihia ni awo tso lɛ nɔ nu babaoo.

english: What makes the flowers on my pepper plants drop off before any pepper fruits grow?
ga: Mɛni miiha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper yibii lɛ baa?

english: Pepper flowers drop off mainly due to heat stress, sudden dry spells, or giving the plant too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during extremely hot afternoons helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Gbimɔ trukaa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛhaa tsei Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why am I seeing small caterpillars eating holes inside the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni miiye bu yɛ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely fall armyworms, which target the tender leaves in the center of young maize plants to feed. Checking your fields early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts early in the morning stops them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ fɔɔ feemɔ akɛ asraafoi ŋmeii ni kwɛɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ anɔ koni amɛye nii. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli mra. ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii leebi. Ebaatsi nibii nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and shrinking while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods turn black due to black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet and humid conditions. Pruning extra shade tree branches to let sun and air into your farm and removing affected pods quickly will stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ black pod hela lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Nibii ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ni kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How can I tell if my plantain bunch is ready for harvest while it is still fully green?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantain tso lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Plantains are mature and ready to harvest when the individual fruits change from having sharp, flat edges to becoming plump and rounded, even if the outer skin remains bright green.
ga: Plantains lɛ eda kwraa ni efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo moŋ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots turn out bitter and tough to chew?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ mli edɔ ni ewa akɛ abaaye lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become bitter and tough when left in the ground too long past maturity or when exposed to extended heat and drought, which causes the plant to build up natural defense chemicals.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛshwere fe nine loo kɛji akɛ amɛhi hulutsoo kɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ mli. Enɛ haa tsei feɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni buɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do my maize stalks keep falling over when strong winds blow through the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa kɛfo ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over when their roots are shallow or weak, often caused by planting seeds too shallowly, overcrowded spacing, or failing to heap extra soil around the base of the stems as they grow.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo amɛhe waaa. Bei pii lɛ nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Gbɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo enyɛɛɛ ekɛ sũ krokomɛi ato ehe Stem base kɛji eda

english: The best time to plant cassava stem cuttings is right after the first two or three steady rains, when the soil has soaked up enough moisture to help the stems sprout roots quickly before any dry spell returns.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ ji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi fioo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ, be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ eŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants turn yellow and drop during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves as a natural defense mechanism to conserve water during dry spells. Once the rains return, the plant sprouts fresh green leaves and resumes normal growth.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baai shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ nu he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaku esɛɛ eba bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do people spread dry grass around the base of young plantain suckers after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbi amɛshwãa tsei bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ beni amɛdu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective cover over the soil. It retains moisture, keeps the roots cool under hot sunshine, and prevents weeds from competing with the young plantain.
ga: Hay ni agbɛɔ ashwãa, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulutsoo be lɛ hiɔ shi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kɛ plantain bibii lɛ akaŋ lɛ naa

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same soil drains the specific nutrients maize needs and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the field. Rotating with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi he hiaa lɛ ajɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii atsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are there tiny holes in my young maize leaves with small dark dirt inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni muji bibii ni tsuɔ waa yɛ jɛmɛ. Yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm attack, a pest that feeds inside the whorl of young maize plants. Detecting this early allows you to manage the pest before it destroys the growing point of the maize.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm attack, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ he okadi. early detection Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ dani amɛfiteɔ hei ni o-corn lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees get dry leaves when the big shade trees around them are cut down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ ná baai ni egbi beni afo tsei ni eda ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because intense direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the topsoil. Keeping shade trees canopy protects young cocoa until they mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ tso lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds very close together to get more crops on my farm?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni maná yibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli hu?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete heavily for light, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow tall and thin, producing very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo. Enɛ haa ŋmei bibioo loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. Providing steady moisture and slight shade during extreme heat helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni ashwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo pollination ni bɛ Kɛ́ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be kɛ hulutsoo be fioo ko ba yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing huge green leaves but not producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni ji eŋɔli shi ewooo pepper ko lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen fertilizer causes pepper plants to spend all their energy growing stems and leaves instead of flowers and fruits. Balancing fertilizer with phosphorus and potassium promotes fruiting.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛdaraa amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium to he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially crossed for one generation of high performance. Saving and planting seeds from that harvest results in weaker plants, low yields, and uneven growth in the second season.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔ̃ɔ mli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛ yinɔ ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ aba. Dumɔwui ni jɛɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, yibiiwoo lɛ faaa, ni amɛdaraa yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crop right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie dormant in the soil and are naturally adapted to absorb moisture and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crop does not get choked out during its critical early growth stage.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛhe ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafee nɔ ko yɛ mra be mli dalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop roots rot when rainwater sits on my field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When water gathers and stays trapped on your field, it blocks air from reaching the soil, effectively drowning the roots and causing them to rot.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Beni nu shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he Nu tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ.

english: What kind of crops can I plant on lowland where water naturally flows and settles?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ makwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Lowland areas that collect water are ideal for crops like rice or sugarcane, which thrive in wet conditions, unlike crops such as cassava or maize that die if their roots stay under water.
ga: The marshy areas that store water are ideal for crops such as rice or sugarcane, which thrive in wet conditions. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni gboiɔ kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ nu shishi.

english: How can I prevent rainwater from washing away my topsoil on land that slopes downwards?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekafɔ mishikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting your crops in rows across the slope rather than up and down creates natural barriers that slow down flowing water and hold your rich topsoil in place.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ moŋ fe ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko baa ni haa nu lɛ hoɔ fioo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow even though there is rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for food, specifically nitrogen. When rain washes away soil nutrients or the soil becomes worn out, plants cannot get enough nourishment to stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ji niyenii bolɔmɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen Kɛ́ nugbɔ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ. Tsei nyɛŋ ana niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛhi shi akɛ eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my land better for future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots, naturally fertilizing the land for the next crops you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and leafy but fail to yield big fruits or tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni ewoɔ baai shi ewooo aduawai wuji loo tuberous lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil has plenty of nitrogen for leaf growth but lacks nutrients like phosphorus or potassium, which the plant needs to develop strong flowers, tubers, and fruits.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha baai lɛ akwɛ̃. Shi niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs loo potasium bɛ mli. Esa akɛ tsei lɛ aná fɔfɔi, bulb, kɛ aduawai ni mli wa.

english: Why is it important to make mounds or ridges before planting my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ama gɔŋ loo ŋshɔ dani adu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Making mounds creates loose, soft soil that lets cassava tubers grow big and long without pushing against hard ground, while also keeping the roots raised out of excess standing water.
ga: Gɔŋ ni afee lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ shishifãi lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ tsiii ehe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ shishifãi ni awó nɔ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nu ni ŋmɛɔ shi fe nine lɛ he.

english: What happens if I plant my seeds too close together in the same field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants that produce very small yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my planted crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to steal water and soil nutrients quickly, allowing them to shoot up faster than farm crops that need more gentle conditions.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Enɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei ni biɔ shihilɛ ni mli jɔ fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why do my young crops dry up when I plant them during strong sunny weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young plants have small, shallow roots that cannot reach deep underground moisture, so hot sun dries out the topsoil and causes the delicate leaves to lose water faster than the roots can drink.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni mli ekɔɔɔ. ni nyɛŋ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he No hewɔ lɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩɔ ni ehaa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow and drying up while the plant is still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants need to stay green and grow strong. It usually starts on the lower leaves because the plant moves its limited nutrients up to protect the newest growth.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ beni tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni fa fioo lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ebu nɔ ni eda fe fɛɛ lɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into small cups and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? ni ekpa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or aphids feeding on the underside of young leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies. The damaged leaves cannot make food for the plant, which stunts its growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Baai ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii aha tso lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ akpa dalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed all their flowers before any pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɛɛ woɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by drought, lack of soil nutrients, or severe heat. The tree drops its flowers to save energy so it can survive the tough conditions instead of trying to feed young pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo latsaa ni naa wa Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha ŋmeii bibii lɛ niyenii
