english: This is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium while the fruit is forming. It is usually caused by irregular watering—either too little water or long dry spells followed by heavy rain.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miiwo lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Eji akɛ nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ loo be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die if I clear all the big shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji mijie cacao tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are adapted to live under forest canopies and burn easily under full sunlight. Shade trees protect seedlings from harsh heat, keep the air humid, and shield soil from drying out while root systems develop.
ga: Atsake cacao tsei bibii lɛ koni amɛhi tsei ashishi ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kwɛmɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ ni otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi be mli ni shishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops dry up and die after I put fertilizer right next to their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is full of concentrated salts. Placing it directly against the stem or main roots creates a strong salt layer that sucks moisture out of the plant roots instead of feeding them, causing the plant to burn and wither.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛwo tso lɛ shishifãi titri lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋmei ni mli wa ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ baa moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to climb up tall wooden poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse sweet potato wain tso ko koni enyɛ ekwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants store energy in tubers below ground using sunshine captured by their leaves. Staking gets leaves off the hot ground into maximum sunlight and airflow, protecting leaves from soil diseases and helping tubers grow much bigger.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛbaai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking baaha tsei ahe tsei ni jɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ aná hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ babaoo. Ebuɔ baai ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa yitso lɛ ni edaa babaoo

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn watery and rot underground if I leave them in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ hoɔ nu ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rains waterlog the ground, oxygen is pushed out, causing the roots to suffocate and rots caused by soil fungi to spread rapidly through tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Akɛ oxygen lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops fail if I plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain after a long dry season is often a 'false start.' The ground remains extremely hot underneath, and if no rain falls for two weeks after, the seeds get baked in the soil or scorch immediately after germinating.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ ji ‘Apasa shishijee’ Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ waa lolo yɛ eshishi. Ni kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ otsii enyɔ yɛ no sɛɛ. Ashãa dumɔwui yɛ sũ mli loo ashãa amɛ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why don't the seeds I save from my hybrid maize harvest perform as well when I replant them the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛwo ekoŋŋ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two unique parent plants to give maximum yields only for the first planting. The seeds produced by that harvest lose those special traits, resulting in uneven growth, smaller cobs, and lower yields if planted again.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni fa fe fɛɛ aha klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ. Dumɔwui ni akpaa lɛ baafite nakai sui lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kɛji akɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops look very green and healthy in the first few weeks, but then suddenly turn yellow and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fee tamɔ eŋɔli waa ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, shi trukaa lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpa shweremɔ lɛ?

english: When plants turn yellow after early healthy growth, it usually means they have used up the initial nutrients in the soil and are now starving for nitrogen, or their roots are being damaged underground by waterlogging or pests.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ mra be mli dalɛ kpakpa sɛɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛye shishijee niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. Ni amrɔ nɛɛ nitrogen lɛ faaa. aloo nu afua loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Leaf curling is a crop's natural defense mechanism to save water; by rolling its leaves tight, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to heat to prevent moisture from evaporating too fast.
ga: Baai ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ mli shiŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ haa he ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni ŋmɔtɔ akafo oya tsɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without turning into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flower drop happens when plants experience extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of essential nutrients like potassium and calcium which the plant needs to form solid fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ calcium ni bɛ. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei awo yibii ni wa

english: Why do my crops wilt and die even after heavy rains fall on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Too much standing water without proper drainage starves plant roots of oxygen and causes root rot, preventing the plant from taking up food and causing it to collapse.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaye nii ni ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Is there a way I can protect my crops from harmful insects without spending so much money on expensive store chemicals?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe ni mikɛ shika babaoo efiteee tsofai ni jara wa ni aheɔ yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, you can use natural pest control methods like spraying mixtures of neem leaf extract or wood ash water, and intercropping your main crop with strong-smelling plants like pepper or onions to naturally drive pests away.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛi ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ neem tso mli nu ni akɛfutuɔ loo tso mli sũ mli nu ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ atsu nii. kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni okɛduɔ onibii titrii lɛ. Koni ekɛshwie tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: How can I stop weeds from taking over my farm if I cannot afford chemical weedicides this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi jwɛi ana koni ekaye miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ? Ni kɛji akɛ minyɛɛɛ mahe tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi yɛ be nɛɛ mli hu?

english: You can clear weeds early by mulching with dry leaves and grass around your plants to block sunlight from reaching weed seeds, or plant fast-growing cover crops like cowpeas to choke out weeds.
ga: Obaanyɛ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra. Kɛtsɔ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. otsei lɛ koni hulu lɛ akashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahe Aloo dumɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ tsina ŋmeii, koni ekɛha jwɛi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Should I harvest all my crops at the same time or clear them bit by bit as they grow?
ga: Ani esa akɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo mafo mli fiofio kɛ́ midu?

english: Grain crops like maize are best harvested all at once when fully dry, but vegetable crops like garden eggs and okra yield more total food when picked continuously as individual fruits mature.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaakpa ŋmaa nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa fɛɛ shikome kɛji egbi kwraa, shi aduawai, tamɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ okra, woɔ yibii babaoo kɛji akɛ akpa amɛ daa be mli ni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shwereɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if spending extra money on fertilizer and hybrid seeds will actually yield enough profit to cover my costs?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shika kroko ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baaha sɛɛnamɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛbaawo mihe nyɔmɔwoo lɛ he nyɔmɔ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds and proper fertilizer application increase crop yields significantly compared to saved seeds, but you must calculate your expected yield per acre against market prices before planting to ensure your sales cover the input costs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni awo he odaseyeli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ waa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ ahe. Shi esa akɛ obu yibiiwoo ni okpaa gbɛ akɛ obaaná yɛ acre kome mli lɛ he akɔntaa kɛ jarayeli jara dani odu koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ onihɔɔmɔ lɛ baaha onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo lɛ aba.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year even when I plant the exact same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land year after year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil; rotating your main crop with legumes like beans or groundnuts helps restore soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ sɛɛ foɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested grains get destroyed by insects so quickly inside the store room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ fiteɔ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Insects multiply inside stored grains if the crops are not dried properly to low moisture levels before storage, or if they are stored in ordinary bags instead of airtight hermetic bags (PICS bags) that suffocate pests.
ga: Kplukai babaoo yɛ ŋmaa ni ato lɛ mli kɛji akɛ agbiko ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi dani akɛto. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛwo kotoku ni afɔɔ mli nitsumɔ mli yɛ vacuum kotoku (PICS kotoku) ni haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the tall trees away from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot handle full direct sunlight. Leaving tall shade trees or planting plantains provides shade and retains soil moisture, protecting young seedlings from drying out and dying.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ lɛ Shade ni akɛhaa loo plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni aha shade ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Buu tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to spread their leaves upward to catch sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground to prevent rot and helps the plant produce more energy to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso ji wain tso ni esa akɛ egbɛ baai lɛ eshwã ŋwɛi koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ koni akafite, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo baa koni ekɛ bulbs agboi akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small shoots growing around my main plantain stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: When too many shoots (suckers) grow around one plantain stem, they steal water and nutrients from the main plant. Leaving only two or three strong suckers allows the mother plant to produce a larger bunch of plantains.
ga: Beni ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo ni miida yɛ plantain tso kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ awo dumɔwui babaoo.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my green maize plants turning yellow and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. Nitrogen is the plant food responsible for deep green leaves and strong vegetative growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni haa tsei lɛ daa waa.

english: Why is it better for my soil if I leave dead crop leaves to rot on the farm instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji mishi tsei ahe baai ni egboi lɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ lɛ?

english: Burning crop leftovers destroys organic matter and kills beneficial soil organisms. Leaving the plant material to rot slowly feeds nutrients back into the dirt and helps the soil hold moisture during dry periods.
ga: Nibii ni eshwɛ ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Ehaa tsei amli nibii fiteɔ fiofio Ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Is it helpful to plant groundnuts together with my maize on the same field?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and naturally feed it into the soil through their roots. This helps enrich the soil for nearby maize plants without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ kɛhaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my crop seeds after the long dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ eho lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safest to wait until two or three heavy rains have soaked deep into the ground rather than planting after the very first light rain, which can leave seeds to dry up if the rain pauses.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, du ngɛ kekleekle hiɔmi nɛ ɔ se, nɛ lɔ ɔ ma nyɛ ma ha nɛ duwu ɔmɛ nɛ a gbi ke hiɔmi ɔ kpa nɛ be bɔɔ ko.

english: What is making small holes in the leaves of my young maize and hiding inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn baai lɛ miifee bu bibii? Ni akɛtee teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaf funnel (whorl) of maize plants during the day and feed on new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baa gbɛi (rings) lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni amɛye baai heei ni eda lɛ

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused when plants do not get enough calcium from the soil or when watering is irregular, preventing the fruit from forming properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni nu lɛ bɛ be fɛɛ mli Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava roots are mature enough to dig up without pulling out the plant early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafo ni mijieee tsei lɛ mra?

english: Cassava is usually ready to harvest when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving bare stems, and when the earth around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Bare trunk left kɛ beni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle trunk lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Is watering my farm by hand as good for my crops as natural rainfall?
ga: Ani nine ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ mli nu lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Rainwater is naturally better because it contains dissolved nitrogen from the atmosphere that feeds crops, and it washes the entire plant. Manual watering keeps crops alive, but it usually only wets the topsoil without providing that extra nitrogen boost.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ hi fe no yɛ adebɔɔ naa ejaakɛ nitrogen ni mli ewo muji ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii niyenii lɛ mli lɛ yɛ mli. ni ofɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ he Nu ni okɛwoɔ ehe lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii hiɔ shi. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ mli fɔ̃ɔ ni ekɛ nitrogen fataaa he.

english: Why do my crops look greener after rain compared to when I water them with a bucket?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ eŋɔli kɛji nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Ani akɛto nu ni akɛ baagi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ he?

english: Raindrops clean dust off the leaves so the plant can breathe better, and rain carries natural air nutrients straight into the ground, which gives plants an instant green boost that borehole or tap water cannot match.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ sũ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli koni tsei lɛ anyɛ amu jogbaŋŋ. Ni nugbɔ lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ naa su eŋɔli amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni nu ni jɛɔ nubu mli loo nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi mli lɛ nyɛŋ afee ekome.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly during the dry season even if I give them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu moŋ?

english: During the dry season, the intense heat and hot winds make water evaporate quickly from the leaves. The crops spend most of their energy trying to cool down and survive the heat stress rather than growing tall.
ga: Yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛha amɛhe ajɔɔ ni amɛhi shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ̃.

english: How can I keep the soil on my farm from drying out too fast during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akagbi oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: You can cover the ground around your crops with dried grass or leaves, which is called mulching. This acts like a blanket that shades the soil from the sun and traps moisture in the earth for longer.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ he ni ebɔle he lɛ atsu nii. Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi akpɛ onibii lɛ. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young plants wither in the heat even when I water them daily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ miiho yɛ latsaa be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Young plants have small, shallow roots near the surface where the sun bakes the soil. If you only give them a little water, the heat evaporates it before the roots can drink it, so deep watering is needed to push moisture deeper.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ he ni hulu la shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ nu fioo pɛ ha lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ baaho dani shishifãi lɛ anu nu. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni awo nu mli jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Early morning is the best time to water your crops because the soil is cool, allowing the plants to drink deeply before the hot sun causes the water to evaporate into the air.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ okɛ nu awo onibii amli ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nuɔ nu waa dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Is it better to water my crops a little bit every day or give them a lot of water a few times a week?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahã miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu fioo daa gbi loo mahã amɛ nu babaoo? Shii fioo komɛi yɛ otsi mli?

english: Giving a lot of water a few times a week is better because it forces the roots to grow deep into the ground looking for moisture, making the crops stronger against dry weather.
ga: Nu babaoo ni akɛhaa Shii fioo yɛ otsi mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ enyɛɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni amɛdara kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛtao ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi.

english: How can I tell if the water I applied reached deep enough into the soil for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ fa kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Push a dry stick or your finger about three inches deep into the soil near the plant. If the tip comes out dry, you need to apply more water so it reaches down to where the roots feed.
ga: Tsɔ tso ni egbi lɛ loo onine lɛ mli aaafee inchi etɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ he lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ egbi lɛ, ehe baahia ni okɛ nu babaoo afata he koni eba shi kɛya he ni shishifãi lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from a lack of water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni faaa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ miipiŋ?

english: Crops show they are thirsty when their leaves start curling, drooping down, or turning yellow at the edges during the hottest part of the afternoon.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye amɛ kɛ́ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛgbee shi, loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Can applying too much bucket or well water damage my crops?
ga: Ani baagi loo nu bu mli nu babaoo ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, putting too much water can drown the roots by driving away the air in the soil, which rots the roots and makes the leaves turn yellow just like a drought would.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu babaoo ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ tamɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up when I plant them out in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade to protect them from direct sunlight and harsh heat. Planting nurse crops like plantains or shade trees alongside them creates a cooler environment and retains soil moisture until the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui taoɔ hɔɔŋ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Nurse tsei tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ adumɔ Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ baa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer at the right growth stage helps restore healthy green leaves and improves grain yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dalɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha tso lɛ yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha dumɔwui ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Is it better to plant my cassava stem cuttings slanting or flat in the ground?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei niji ni etse ehe loo etse ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava stem cuttings at a slanting angle helps the plant root deeper and sprout faster, while also making it easier to harvest the tubers later compared to planting them completely flat.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛdaraa oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaakpa bulb lɛ sɛɛ mli kɛ akɛto amɛ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ he.

english: Flower drop in tomatoes is often caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of essential soil nutrients. Consistent watering and protecting plants from excessive heat help fruits set properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ tomato nɔ lɛ baa. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etswaa shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny dark droppings inside the stem funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ jɛmɛ. Yɛ tsɔne lɛ mli

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the central leaf funnel of the maize plant. Early detection and applying recommended sprays are necessary to protect the leaves and yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ ana mra ni akɛshwie nɔ Ehe miihia ni abu baai lɛ ahe ni awo yibii.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to capture enough sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, which prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ eshwɛɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baaa.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains specific soil nutrients and allows pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, which can also carry viruses to the plant. Controlling these insects early prevents leaf damage and stunted growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ni baanyɛ aŋɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛya tsei amli lɛ hu Mra be mli ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ baai lɛ afitemɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ naa.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because plants absorb moisture before the sun gets hot, and leaves dry quickly during the day, preventing fungal diseases that thrive on wet leaves overnight.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ. Ni baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baai ni efɔ nɔ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ anaa.

english: Why should I cut off some of the young shoots sprouting around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Leaving too many shoots causes them to fight with the main tree for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning extra shoots ensures the main plant gets enough energy to produce large bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la he. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ plantains babaoo.

english: Why am I seeing small dark spots on my plantain leaves, and should I be worried about them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii diji bibii yɛ plantain baai anɔ lɛ, ni ani esa akɛ enɛ ahao mi?

english: Small spots on plantain leaves are often early signs of leaf spot diseases like Sigatoka. If left unchecked, these spots grow larger, destroy the leaves early, and prevent the plantain bunch from growing full and heavy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni yɔɔ plantain baai lɛ anɔ lɛ ji mra be mli okadi ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ helai tamɔ sigatoka. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, nɛkɛ hei nɛɛ baafee wuji. Kpata baai lɛ ahiɛ mra. ni etsĩ plantain tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkadara kwraa ni amɛdara waa

english: If one of my plantain trees gets heavily diseased with leaf spots, why is it recommended to cut it all the way down?
ga: Kɛji mi plantains lɛ eko yɛ leaf spot hela ni naa wa waa lɛ Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ afo dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cutting down a severely infected plantain tree stops the disease spores from spreading through the wind or soil to your healthy crops. Completely removing diseased plants keeps the rest of your farm safe.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni oookpa lɛ haaa helai amli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ akatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛya onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kwraa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I prevent crop diseases from spreading from one plant to another when trimming my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tsei ahelai anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya tso kroko nɔ beni mifoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Diseases often travel on cutlasses and farm tools. Cleaning your cutlass with soap, water, or a simple disinfectant between plants prevents you from carrying unseen germs from sick crops to healthy ones.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dade kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii gbɛɔ helai. Kɛ́ okɛ samla, nu, loo tsofa ni gbeɔ helai ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ tsumɔ o-daggers lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ helai ni anaaa lɛ akajɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How do I know whether to spray a diseased plantain tree or completely remove it from my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ loo majie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kwraa?

english: If only a few outer leaves have spots, you can cut off those leaves and treat the plant. However, if the center leaves or main stem are rotting and weak, full removal is best to protect neighboring plants.
ga: Kɛji kponɔgbɛ baai fioo pɛ yɔɔ Obaanyɛ ofolɔ nakai baai lɛ ni ohere tso lɛ yiwala, shi kɛlɛ, kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ loo tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ egbo ni ebɛ hewalɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojie kwraa koni obu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Can applying too much fertilizer to my crops actually cause spots or make them sick?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo eha hela aba amɛnɔ?

english: Yes, putting too much fertilizer—especially chemical types—can burn plant roots and stem tissues. This chemical burn weakens the crop, making it much easier for diseases and pests to attack and cause leaf spots or rot.
ga: Hɛɛ, fɔmɔ nii ni fe nine. titri lɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ ashã. Tsofa nɛɛ ni ashãa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baatutua ni amɛkɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ aba.

english: What is the proper way for me to apply fertilizer around my plantains so I do not burn them?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ plantains mli koni amɛkashã?

english: Always apply fertilizer in a wide circle about 30 to 50 centimeters away from the base of the plantain trunk. Never dump fertilizer directly against the stem, as the strong chemicals can burn the skin of the plant.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ kooyigbɛ ni mli kwɔ aaafee sɛntimita 30 kɛyashi 50 kɛjɛ plantain lɛ shishi. Kaashi ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsofai ni mli wa lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ hewolo.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain plants turning brown and dying before the fruit matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Lower leaves dying early is usually caused by leaf spot diseases or a lack of proper soil nutrients. Removing dead leaves regularly helps the plant focus its energy on building strong fruits rather than feeding dying leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ gboiɔ oya, bei pii lɛ, baa lɛ he hela loo niyenii ni sa ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ baai ni egboi lɛ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ebaakwɛ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeeha baai ni miigboi lɛ niyenii.

english: How can I tell if the plantain suckers I want to plant on my land are healthy and free from disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ plantain tsei ni misumɔɔ ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni helai bɛ amɛhe?

english: Choose suckers with bright green leaves and clean, white bases. If you peel back the outer root layer and see dark brown or black spots and tunnels, the sucker is infected with pests or disease and should not be planted.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni baai lɛ yɛ eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ kɛ shishigbɛ yɛŋ ni he tse. Kɛji ojie shishifã lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ ni ona ŋmeii ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ kɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela loo hela ko emɔ sucker lɛ. ni esaaa akɛ aduɔ

english: Does poor soil quality make my crops more likely to get leaf spots and rot?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ baa baa nɔ tsɔi ni amɛfiteɔ?

english: Yes, when soil lacks essential nutrients or holds too much stagnant water, crops become weak and stressed. Stressed plants have weak defenses, making them easy targets for fungi and diseases that cause spots.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu ni ekã shi babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛhaoɔ. Tsei ni haoɔ amɛhe lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbuɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ nɔ ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ oya.

english: Can I use wood ash on my crops to protect them from spots and small farm pests?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tso sũ awo miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni mikɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii ahe?

english: Wood ash provides helpful nutrients like potassium and can deter some fungal spots and insects when lightly sprinkled around the base of plants, but it should be used in moderate amounts so it does not harm the soil balance.
ga: Tso mli sũ haa niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ potassium ni ebaanyɛ etsi ŋmeii kɛ kooloi komɛi anaa kɛji akɛ ashwie nɔ fioo yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ he, shi akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ bɔni afee ni ekafite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Can I actually get a good harvest from that small piece of land behind my house?
ga: Manyɛ makpa ŋmaa kpakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Ani manyɛ mikɛtsu nii yɛ mishia lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, even small backyard plots can produce high yields if you plant fast-growing crops like peppers, tomatoes, or leafy vegetables. Managing a small piece of land closely allows you to give it better water, manure, and care, giving you steady food and extra income.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔji bibii po Shia lɛ sɛɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo kɛji odu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, tomato, loo aduawai ni yɔɔ baai. Shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔkwɛmɔ He ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ haa onáa nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ kwɛmɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, obaaná niyenii kɛ shika kroko ni obaaná.

english: Why are my backyard crops growing tall and thin instead of producing heavy fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mishia lɛ sɛɛ lɛ miida ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops are planted close to buildings or under big shade trees, they don't get enough direct sunlight. The plants stretch upward searching for light, using all their energy on stems rather than producing strong flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛji oodu tsei yɛ tsũi ahe loo tsei wuji ashishi Tso lɛ naaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ. Tso lɛ tsɔ ehe nɔ koni etao la. kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii Moŋ lɛ, ewoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni mli wa.

english: Why does my cocoa farm take so many years before I see any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ naa pods lɛ?

english: Perennial crops like cocoa focus their early years on developing strong root systems and thick branches so they can absorb water during dry seasons. Once established, that patient wait pays off with decades of regular pod production.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ kookoo lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi ni wa kɛ niji ni mli wa lɛ anɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛjie nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Beni okpɛ oyiŋ lɛ Helatsɛ lɛ mɛmɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni sa afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni akɛfeɔ pod daa lɛ.

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival defense for cassava during drought. By shedding leaves, the plant reduces water loss through evaporation and protects the energy stored in its underground tubers until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ buɔ ŋmei lɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Tsei haa nu ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ, ni amɛbuɔ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ ŋmeii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why should I plant beans or cowpeas on a plot where my maize grew poorly last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Legume crops like beans and cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. Planting them restores nutrients naturally so future crops like maize can grow healthy without relying entirely on expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ anyɛ adara waa ni ekɛ ehe efɔɔɔ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ anɔ kwraa.

english: How do I know if my crops are just thirsty from the sun or actually infected with a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hulu la he kumai miiye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛkɛ loo hela ko yɛ enɔ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Thirsty crops wilt during the heat of the afternoon sun but perk back up by early morning. Disease-infected plants stay wilted, develop yellow spots, or show unusual growth even after heavy rain or early morning moisture.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shi ebaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ leebi. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baagbi. Ayɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Aloo dalɛ ni ejaaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo leebi hulutsoo be sɛɛ po.

english: Planting plantains too close forces them to compete underground for soil nutrients and above ground for sunlight. Giving each sucker enough space ensures strong trunks that can carry big, heavy bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa sucker fɛɛ sucker lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe wa ni baanyɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of key nutrients. When the plant gets stressed, it sheds flowers to preserve its own life until conditions get better.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa bɛ mli. Kɛ tsei miihao Ebaajie fɔfɔii koni ekɛbu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala he kɛyashi shihilɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow crooked and irregular instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfeee ekome moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers twist when they hit hard, compacted soil or rocks under the ground. Raising deep, loose mounds or ridges breaks up hard soil, giving the tubers room to expand smoothly.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa loo tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ tswa amɛ. Gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ni ooowo nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli agbala. Ehaa yitso he lɛ mli lɛɛɔ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why does my maize crop have yellow leaves even after I weeded the entire plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ baa ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni mijie ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli jwɛi lɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeding removes weeds that steal water, but yellow leaves mean the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the leaves their rich green color so cobs can fill out properly.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ jwɛi ni juɔ nu lɛ. Shi baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli bɔni afee ni ŋmei lɛ anyɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out soil moisture before their roots are strong enough to reach water deep underground.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ dani shishifãi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛshɛɔ nu lɛ he yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ.

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and air can reach the trunk, which prevents damp fungal diseases and helps the tree direct its strength into making large cocoa pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni haa mɔ mli fũuɔ lɛ naa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii wuji yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ baai krokomɛi baafata he.

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly during damp weather when rain drops splash fungal spores from the soil onto low-hanging pods.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa seedlings very close to each other to get more trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: If cocoa trees are planted too close together, their roots fight over water and food in the soil, and their upper branches block light from one another, resulting in thin trees that produce very few pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tsiɔ la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food maize needs to grow green leaves; adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving the land time to rebuild, and it allows pests that feed on maize to multiply in the ground.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaaa jɛmɛ be ni ekɛma ekoŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ ayiɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it better to apply fertilizer right after it rains instead of during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ moŋ fe be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so that plant roots can drink it in; applying it to dry ground can burn the roots or cause the fertilizer to blow away without helping your crops.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni tso shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛ́ okɛwo hei ni egbi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ loo eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afo kɛya ni eyeee ebuaaa onibii lɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the plant reaches 9 to 12 months of age, its lower leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off naturally, and the soil around the base starts to crack as the roots swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛji tso lɛ eye nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers cover the soil around their plantain suckers with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛdumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, traps moisture during dry weeks, stops weeds from growing, and feeds the soil as the leaves decompose.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Eŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ mli Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii be mli ni baai lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow so much faster and stronger than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that have adapted to quickly steal water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil, allowing them to outgrow cultivated crops if they are not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa fe tso lɛ kɛji ajieee amɛ mra.

english: Why did my maize crop fail even though I planted right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ shwere eyɛ mli akɛ midu yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ moŋ?

english: The very first rain of the season is often followed by a hot, dry period. If you plant too early, seeds sprout but quickly die from heat and lack of moisture before the main rains actually settle in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ latsaa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ shi amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ latsaa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa baa.

english: Why do some farmers in my community plant maize twice a year while others only plant once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi ni yɔɔ mikutso lɛ mli lɛ duɔ abele shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni mɛi krokomɛi Adu shikome pɛ?

english: In southern Ghana, there are two distinct rainy seasons (major and minor), allowing farmers to plant twice. In drier northern areas with only one rainy season, crops can only be planted once a year without artificial irrigation.
ga: southern ghana Nugbɔshiimɔ bei srɔtoi enyɔ yɔɔ. (Nugbɔshiimɔ be titri kɛ nɔ ni ji enyɔ) haa okwaafoi duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii shii enyɔ. Yɛ kooyigbɛ kpokpaa ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kome pɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Abaanyɛ adu tsei shikome pɛ yɛ afi mli. ni nu ni akɛfee lɛ bɛ mli

english: How can I tell if there is enough moisture in the soil before I start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ fa bɔ ni sa dani mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: Dig a small hole about hand-deep and squeeze a handful of soil. If it holds together in a ball without crumbling, the soil has enough moisture for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ bu bibioo ko ni miihe ashɛ onine mlibotemɔ he. No sɛɛ lɛ, shwiemɔ sũ fioo ko kɛjɛ mli. Kɛji amɛbua amɛhe naa ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbalaaa shi lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: What is late-season or 'finishing corn', and when should I plant it?
ga: Mɛni ji be lɛ naagbee? ‘Abɛi ni agbe naa’ ni mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu?

english: Finishing corn' refers to maize planted during the minor rainy season later in the year. It relies on the final rains of the season to mature right before the long dry season begins.
ga: Abɛi ni akɛwulaa’ lɛ tsɔɔ abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni naagbee nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ aje shishi.

english: How do I know when my maize has reached the final stage and is ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ enaagbee gbɛhe ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Maize is fully mature when the outer leaves surrounding the cob turn brown and dry, the silk turns black, and the grains become hard when pressed with your fingernail.
ga: Abele lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa. Kooloi lɛ feɔ blɔfo ni amɛgbiɔ. Silk lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛ nineshi tsɔne miimɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young corn plants curling up during hot sunny afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miihoso yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: When sunlight is intense and water is limited, corn plants curl their leaves to reduce exposed surface area, which helps them save moisture and protect themselves from burning.
ga: Kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli wa ni nu lɛ faaa lɛ, Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ shãa he.

english: What can I do to protect my crop if the rain stops for two weeks after I have already planted?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mabu miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ otsii enyɔ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You can cover the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching). This traps moisture in the ground for longer and shields the plant roots from harsh sun heat.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Enɛ baaha nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni ebu tsei shishifãi ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni naa wa lɛ mli dɔlɛ he.

english: Why do my neighbor's crops survive long sunny days better than mine during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli jogbaŋŋ fe minɔ̃ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli lɛ?

english: Your neighbor may be using certified drought-tolerant seed varieties, which are specifically bred to endure strong sun and survive on minimal rainfall compared to traditional seeds.
ga: Okutsoŋnyo lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ atsu nii. Atsɔse amɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo ko mli kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ahe.

english: Why do extension officers advise against planting all my maize seeds on the exact same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting your farm in batches a week or two apart reduces risk. If a sudden dry spell hits, it will only harm one stage of crops instead of destroying your entire harvest.
ga: Planting your farm in batches A week or two reduces the risk. If there is dry magic It will only cause damage to the crops for a short period of time. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite onitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ

english: What happens to my maize if it gets strong sun but does not get enough rain during the flowering stage?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ kɛji hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ shi nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Flowering is the most sensitive stage for maize. Strong heat without rain prevents the plant from producing proper grains, leading to empty cobs and crop failure.
ga: Fɔfɔi fɔmɔ ji be ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmãa. The intense heat without rain prevents plants from producing seeds properly. Ekɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ baa.

english: How do I know if my land is good enough to start growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cocoa needs deep, well-drained soil rich in organic matter that holds moisture without getting waterlogged. Testing if your soil stays moist but drains well after rain gives you a good foundation before planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ he miihia kokoo. Rich in organic matter that helps retain moisture without waterlogging. Testing to see if your soil is still moist but drains well after rain. This will give you a good foundation before planting.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings need shade trees planted above them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo dumɔwui lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants sunburn easily and dry out quickly under harsh, direct sunlight. Shade trees act like living umbrellas that cool the air, keep moisture in the soil, and protect the young plants while their roots grow.
ga: Hulu shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, overly shaded conditions. Clearing weeds, pruning dead branches to let air flow through, and harvesting ripe pods early helps prevent the rot from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. weeding Niji ni egboi lɛ afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli kɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni akpaa mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How does participating in government spraying programs protect my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nɔyeli lɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma shwiemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli ni mikɛ mihe aaawo lɛ baabu miŋmɔ lɛ he?

english: Programs organized by bodies like Cocobod spray across entire communities at once. This stops destructive pests like mirids from simply flying from an unsprayed farm to your sprayed farm, protecting crops across the whole region.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoi ni gbɛjianɔtoi tamɔ Cocobod to he gbɛjianɔ lɛ shwieɔ akutseiaŋ fɛɛ shikome. Enɛ haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ mirids lɛ akafo kɛjɛ oŋmɔ ni okɛ tsofa efɔko nɔ lɛ mli kɛya oŋmɔ ni okɛ tsofa efɔ nɔ lɛ mli. koni akɛbu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ fɛɛ

english: Why is it necessary to trim or prune my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afo loo afolɔ kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak or diseased branches so the tree doesn't waste energy on them. It allows sunlight and fresh air into the canopy, reducing fungal dampness and encouraging the tree to produce more healthy pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. koni tsei akafite hewalɛ Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shi ni oha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa

english: Can I grow cassava or maize in the same field as my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting food crops alongside cocoa is beneficial during the first two to three years because it gives you food and income while providing temporary shade to the cocoa, before the cocoa canopy closes.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika kɛ agbɛnɛ hu, be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛha kookoo lɛ. Dani kookoo ŋwɛitsu lɛ baakpa

english: How can having a water dam nearby benefit my crop farm during the dry season?
ga: Ni aaana faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua mi tsei ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: A water dam stores rainfall so you can irrigate your crops during dry months. This prevents crop stress, stops leaves from wilting, and allows you to farm and harvest food throughout the entire year.
ga: Dams buaa nugbɔ nu naa koni onyɛ okɛ nu afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ tsei ahe haomɔ naa. Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa otsuɔ okwaayeli ni okpaa niyenii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting too much water from heavy rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: If soil stays waterlogged for too long, crop leaves may turn yellow and roots will begin to rot because they cannot breathe. Building proper drainage channels helps excess water flow away from plant roots.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu eshwɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Tso lɛ baai baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shishifãi lɛ baabɔi fitemɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ mli. Nu ni hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ ni afee lɛ baaye abua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ akashɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe.

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant lacks nitrogen or other essential soil nutrients. Adding organic compost or the right fertilizer restores nutrients so the plant can make green chlorophyll and food again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen loo niyenii krokomɛi ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni tso lɛ anyɛ afee klorofil eŋɔli kɛ niyenii ekoŋŋ.

english: Where exactly around the cocoa tree should I apply fertilizer?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ awo mli?

english: Fertilizer should be spread in a circle beneath the outer edge of the tree's branch canopy (the drip line), because that is where the tree's active feeding roots are located to absorb nutrients efficiently.
ga: Esa akɛ aja ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ kooyigbɛ yɛ tso lɛ niji lɛ asɛɛgbɛ (drip line lɛ), ejaakɛ jɛmɛ ji he ni tso lɛ shishifãi ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛjie niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so fast when they get wet during rain while being transported?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ gbɛfaa mli lɛ shwie shi lɛ?

english: Harvested yams absorb excess moisture through their skin. When rain hits them during transit, it creates a warm, damp environment that allows rot-causing fungi and bacteria to multiply rapidly.
ga: Atomɔ ni akpa lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛhewolo nɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ gbɛfaa be mli Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ ayi fa oya.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes turn soft and spoil before I can get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi ni mikpa lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egboi dani mikɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes continue to ripen and release heat and natural gases after being picked. Packing them tightly together in hot conditions speeds up this ripening process, causing them to crush each other and spoil quickly.
ga: Tomato yaa nɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ ni ejieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli la ni ji gas lɛ kpo beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo he kome jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛshwere oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛfiteɔ oya.

english: Which staple crops can I plant in Ghana that can survive dry spells when food is getting scarce?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titrii manyɛ madu yɛ Ghana ni baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni niyenii baa shi lɛ?

english: Cassava and cowpeas are very reliable during dry spells because cassava stores water in its underground roots, while cowpeas have deep taproots that reach moisture buried far below the dry surface soil.
ga: Anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei nɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei toɔ nu yɛ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsina ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ shishi lɛ he.

english: Why does planting groundnuts alongside my maize help prevent total food loss during bad weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni fiteɔ kwraa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Different crops react differently to harsh weather. While hot, dry conditions might scorch tall maize, groundnuts grow low to the ground, shade the soil to keep moisture in, and still yield food even if the maize crop fails.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa waa amli. Shi kɛlɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmãa ni kɛlɛ lɛ ashã. Peanuts kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ akahi nɔ. Ni eyaa nɔ ewoɔ yibii kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ fite po.

english: What happens to my harvested maize if I leave it stored in high humidity or damp air?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa?

english: Dry maize grains attract moisture from humid air like a sponge. Once damp, microscopic mold grows on the grains, which destroys the crop and produces harmful toxins that make the food unsafe to eat.
ga: Abɛi ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli tamɔ sponji. Kɛji edɔ Microscopic fungi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛ tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ oshara ni haa niyenii feɔ nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why does stored grain get warm and moldy even inside a dark, closed storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ mli dɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsũ ko ni mli ewo duŋ ni aŋã po mli lɛ?

english: If grain is not completely dried under the sun before storage, the living seeds give off moisture and heat inside the room. This trapped warm, humid air creates the ideal environment for mold and insects to spread.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto Dumɔwui ni hiɛ ka lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ kɛyaa tsu lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa.

english: Why do my leafy vegetables wilt almost immediately if I harvest them in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi aaafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mikpa amɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: During the hot afternoon sun, plants lose water rapidly through their leaves. Cutting the plant at this time stops its roots from supplying water while heat is high, causing the leaves to dry out and wilt instantly.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ afo tsei yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaha nu yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa lɛ. Amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why does cassava spoil within just two or three days after digging it up from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii 2-3 mli beni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Once cassava is separated from its root system, a natural chemical reaction occurs as the tuber reacts to oxygen in the air. This process, called deterioration, turns the flesh dark and spoils the flavor within 72 hours.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ mli gbala kɛjɛ shishifã lɛ mli Adebɔɔ mli tsofafeemɔ ko baa kɛji ŋmei shishifã lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ ekome. Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ dalɛ. Enɛ baaha loo lɛ afee ediŋŋ ni eŋɔɔɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 72 mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants turn yellow and lose their leaves when heavy rains cover the farm with standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ nu ni damɔ shi ha ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from tiny air pockets in the soil to breathe. When standing water covers the farm, it suffocates the roots, causing the plant to turn yellow and drop its leaves to conserve energy.
ga: Tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii amli lɛ. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛmu Kɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ ha ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛlaajeɔ baai koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do green plantains turn yellow and soft much faster when kept together in a tight, closed container?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains eŋɔlii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto tsɛnsii ni akɛwo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: As plantains mature, they naturally release an invisible gas called ethylene that triggers ripening. Keeping them tightly sealed traps this gas, causing all the plantains inside to ripen at the same time very quickly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ plantains lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Amɛjieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni anaaa ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene ni woɔ amɛshweremɔ he hewalɛ lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɔ ni akɛfiɔ nii ahe waa lɛ baamɔmɔ gas nɛɛ. Oya ni okɛ plantain fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahoo yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why does my rice crop need standing water in the field while my maize crops rot in it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ he hiaa nu ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels that allow air to reach their roots even under water, whereas maize roots drown and rot when trapped in standing water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmli ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ́ amɛyɔɔ nu shishi po. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ he.

english: Why does my field soil dry out and crack so quickly just a few days after a good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy clay soils shrink as water evaporates, creating deep cracks. Adding organic material like crop leaves or compost helps the soil act like a sponge and hold water longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ sũ fee lɛ shwieɔ shi beni nu lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. ni kɛ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ baa Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ tsei ahe baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ spunji ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop seeds rot underground instead of sprouting when I plant right before heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ beni midu amɛ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: When heavy rain completely floods dry soil, it displaces the air, causing the buried seeds to suffocate and rot from lack of oxygen before they can germinate.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu yiɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baaye najiaŋ Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni afu lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to produce green leaves and convert sunlight into energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa baai feɔ eŋɔli ni tsakeɔ hulu la lɛ ewoɔ hewalɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but produce tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni ebaa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to put all their energy into growing stems and leaves above ground rather than storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato tuber ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why is it bad if I plant my seeds very close together to try to fit more crops in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni mabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni makwɛ tsei babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete with one another for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, resulting in weak plants and a lower overall harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sun and require shade trees or food crops like plantains to shelter them while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. and need shade trees or food plants such as plantains to provide cover while their root systems develop.

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow so much faster in my farm than the actual crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants adapted to soak up moisture and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops, which is why early weeding is necessary.
ga: Weeds are wild and hardy plants that have adapted to absorb moisture and nutrients in the soil much faster than cultivated plants. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off before turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when stressed by sudden high temperatures, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii lɛ faaa

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly appear in huge numbers on my crops during certain months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii babaoo eba trukaa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ nyɔji komɛi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Moths lay their eggs based on rainy season patterns, timing the hatching of caterpillars to match the period when young, tender crop leaves are available.
ga: Kplukai fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ bɔ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ yaa nɔ ehaa lɛ naa. Kɛtsɔ be ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ be ni baai lɛ ji gbekɛbii ni amɛfee klalo lɛ akpã gbee lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen or getting too much water. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost helps the leaves regain their deep green color and produce better yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni eha yibii kpakpai aba.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops immediately on the day I plant the seeds or wait a few weeks?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ dumɔwui adumɔ gbi lɛ nɔ loo mamɛ otsii fioo komɛi?

english: It is generally best to wait about 2 to 3 weeks after seeds sprout before applying the first round of fertilizer. This gives the young plants time to grow roots capable of absorbing nutrients without getting burned.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ omɛ otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ awo mli. Enɛ haa tso bibioo lɛ be ni ekɛ shishifãi ni baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni shãaa lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts refills nitrogen into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa Rotate ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ebaakɛ nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and how can I protect my crop from them?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmã baa lɛ nɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ amɛhe?

english: Holes in maize leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworms feeding on the central shoots. You can manage them by inspecting crops early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem leaf extracts directly into the plant whorls.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ni oookwɛ mli mra lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii loo neem baa mli nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids that transmit viruses. Spraying soapy water or suitable insecticidal oil controls the insects and stops the virus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni akɛ samla loo mu ni gbeɔ kooloi shwie nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi lɛ ni ebaatsi helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: If I notice a strange disease spreading on a few crop leaves, how should I take a sample to show an extension officer without infecting the rest of my farm?
ga: Kɛji ona hela ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ Gbalamɔ tso baai fioo komɛi anɔ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabua nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ko naa ni mikɛtsɔɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ hiɛyaa nɔ lɛ? ni ekɛ hela lɛ egbɛ eshwaaa ŋmɔ lɛ hei krokomɛi

english: Cut a stem segment containing both diseased and healthy leaf parts using clean shears, place it in a clear plastic or paper bag, and wash your hands and tools immediately before touching any healthy plants.
ga: Kɛ sɛkɛs ni he tse afo tso lɛ fã ni baa lɛ fãi ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Okɛwo plastic loo wolo kotoku ko ni mli tse mli. ni ofɔ oniji kɛ nitsumɔ dadei ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani ota tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and die when I cut down all the surrounding big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings require shade during their first two years to protect their delicate leaves from severe heat and soil moisture loss. Keeping plantains or shade trees alongside cocoa provides natural cover until the canopy closes.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui biɔ hulutsoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli koni ebu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni yɔɔ kookoo masɛi lɛ akwɛmɔ baaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba kɛyashi be mli ni ŋwɛitsu lɛ baakpa.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot in the ground before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil holds excessive water that cannot drain away properly during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to run off, preventing fungal root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni anyɛɛɛ ajie jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ ajo foi. Etsiɔ fungal shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are extremely hot, when plants lack consistent water, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. Ensuring regular watering and balanced feeding keeps the flowers on the plant so fruit can set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ nu daa loo be mli ni nitrogen fertilizer fa babaoo Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ niyenii ni ja baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni yibii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ shi.

english: Plantain trees fall over because their root systems are shallow and can be damaged by underground pests like root nematodes or stem borers. Staking heavy fruiting bunches with sturdy wooden poles helps hold the tree upright.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo stem borers lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ. Staking ji yibiiwoo kuu ko ni tsii ni akɛ tsei ni wa ni haa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Leaving large shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains alongside cocoa creates a canopy that keeps the young plants cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning light green and yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting at the tips usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers like urea or well-decomposed animal manure helps restore green growth and supports healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when heavy rains flood my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe in saturated ground. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away from the tuber roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily right when the fruit bunches grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and become top-heavy when bearing fruit, making them vulnerable to wind. Supporting the main stem with a sturdy wooden or bamboo prop counteracts the fruit weight and keeps the tree standing.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni amɛhe wa kɛji amɛwo yibii. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ nyɛɔ etswaa bo Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa fi tso lɛ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha tso lɛ adamɔ shi.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant beans alongside my tall maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmei kakadaŋŋ lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Beans cover the ground to prevent weeds from spreading, and their roots naturally capture nitrogen from the air to enrich the soil. This extra soil food nourishes the nearby maize without requiring extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Mulch beans koni jwɛi lɛ akagbɛ ashwã. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ŋmɛɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ haa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ hewalɛ ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.
