english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes through the inner leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These pests are likely Fall Armyworms, which feed inside the soft central leaves of young maize where they are safe from heat and predators. Checking your crops early and applying safe control measures into the central funnel stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ. Eji he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe. Okwɛmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli mra ni okɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii yɛ gbɛjegbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ Etsiɔ nakai tsei lɛ anaa dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Yam vines climb naturally to expose maximum leaf area to sunlight, which powers the growth of the tuber below. Staking lifts leaves off the wet ground, reducing leaf diseases and boosting overall yield.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛha hulu la lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ateŋ babaoo he. ni tsirɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ adalɛ Staking haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa baa helai shi ni ehaa yibiiwoo lɛ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly during the hottest time of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during severe heat to reduce surface area and limit water loss. Watering plants early in the morning and spreading dry grass mulch around the base keeps the soil cool and root zones hydrated.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni eha nu ni laajeɔ lɛ aba shi. Okɛ nu awo tso lɛ mli leebi ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi awo shishigbɛ lɛ he koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Pruning removes overgrown or dead branches to allow sunlight and fresh air to flow through the tree canopy. Good airflow reduces humidity that causes fungal diseases like black pod, allowing the tree to direct energy into healthy pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine loo egboi lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ diji aba lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ ehewalɛ lɛ gbɛ kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my last maize harvest produce weaker yields than newly bought certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ?

english: Commercial certified seeds are specifically bred hybrids designed for high performance in their first generation. Saving seeds from that harvest causes the offspring to lose those special hybrid traits, leading to smaller plants and lower yield.
ga: Commercially certified seeds are the first generation of hybrid seeds designed for high performance. Preserving seeds from harvest will cause the offspring to lose those special hybrid characteristics. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: Why does a bright weed growing next to my maize make my crops turn yellow and stop growing even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-ŋmãa lɛ ha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpa shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli moŋ.

english: That weed is likely Striga, commonly called witchweed. It acts like a parasite, attaching directly to the roots of your maize underground to steal water and food, which causes your crop to starve and turn yellow before the weed even appears above ground.
ga: The weed is likely Striga, more commonly known as Witchweed. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko. They attach directly to underground corn roots to steal water and food. This causes your crops to starve and turn yellow before the weeds even appear above the ground.

english: Why are my maize plants staying very short and dried up while the weeds standing beside them look healthy and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ miida kuku ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ? Etamɔ nɔ ni ehe wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ

english: Certain parasitic weeds attach to your crop's root system beneath the soil and draw out all the plant's nourishment. The weed thrives because it is feeding directly on your crop, leaving the crop stunted and dry.
ga: Jwɛi komɛi ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe ni amɛmuɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii fɛɛ. Jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ ejaakɛ amɛyeɔ onibii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: How can I tell if an underground parasite is attacking my farm before I even see weeds sprouting out of the dirt?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ helai miitutua miŋmɔ lɛ? Dani wɔbaana jwɛi po ni miikwɛ̃ kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: If your crops begin wilting, curling their leaves, or turning yellow during the early growing season despite getting enough rainfall and nutrients, underground parasites like witchweed are likely already attached to the roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ, ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ shishijee mli eyɛ mli akɛ He ni nugbɔ nɛɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ abɛi baanyɛ ahi shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: What does it mean when an officer tells me to buy a crop variety that is 'resistant' to weeds?
ga: Kɛ́ onukpai lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mahe tsei ni ‘ŋmɛɔ’ jwɛi ahe gbɛ’ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: A resistant variety is a crop bred with natural defenses that stop parasitic weeds from successfully attaching to its roots, allowing the crop to grow strong and yield well even in infested fields.
ga: Henɔi ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ helai lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ amɛhe ni yeɔ omanye ni tsiɔ jwɛi ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkakpɛtɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ ŋmɔji ni efite lɛ po amli.

english: What kind of seeds should I request at the agriculture office if witchweed keeps destroying my grain harvest every year?
ga: Mɛɛ dumɔwui esa akɛ mabi yɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔhe lɛ kɛji akɛ abɛi fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii daa afi?

english: You should ask for certified 'Striga-resistant' maize or sorghum seeds. These special varieties prevent the weed from feeding on their roots and help reduce the weed population in your field over time.
ga: Esa akɛ obi ŋmãa loo ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aŋmala nɔ akɛ 'Striga resistant'. Nɛkɛ tsei srɔtoi krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ baatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye shishifãi lɛ, ni ebaaye ebua ni jwɛi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: If I pull out witchweed with my hands when I see it, will that save my crops from damage?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ minine gbala witch hazel lɛ beni mina lɛ Ani ebaahere miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala kɛjɛ fitemɔ mli?

english: Hand-pulling stops the weed from spreading thousands of new seeds for next season, but it won't save your current crop because most of the damage was already done underground before the weed emerged.
ga: Nine ni akɛgbalaa jwɛi lɛ haaa gbɛ dumɔwui heei akpei abɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ. Shi ebaahereŋ onibii ni okwɛɔ amrɔ nɛɛ yiwala. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa shikpɔŋ shishi dani jwɛi jeɔ kpo.

english: Can planting crops like groundnuts or cowpeas help clean dangerous weeds out of my grain field?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ejie jwɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli?

english: Yes, legumes like cowpeas act as trap crops. They trick the witchweed seeds into germinating underground, but because the weed cannot feed on legume roots, it starves and dies before it can reproduce.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsuɔ nii akɛ amale ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛlakaa witchweed dumɔwui koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shi akɛni jwɛi nyɛɛɛ aye ŋmeii ashishifãi hewɔ lɛ, No sɛɛ lɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ ni egboɔ dani enyɛɔ efɔɔ bii.

english: Why does witchweed seem to attack my crops more on fields where the soil is old and tired?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni abɛi tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔji ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Witchweed thrives in soil with low nitrogen and low organic matter because weak crops cannot defend themselves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer strengthens the crop so it can better resist the weed.
ga: Witchweed lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nitrogen faaa yɛ nɔ, ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ abu amɛhe. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi a-nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye jwɛi anɔ.

english: How many years can seeds from destructive farm weeds remain alive in my soil if I leave the field fallow?
ga: Afii enyiɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi ni kpataaa nibii ahiɛ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ahi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni ŋmɔ mli nibii bɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: Seeds from parasitic weeds like witchweed can stay dormant in the soil for over 10 to 15 years, waiting until you plant crops like maize or sorghum again before waking up to attack.
ga: Dumɔwui ni jɛɔ jwɛi ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ tamɔ witchweed mli lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛhiɛ aka shi nɔ ni fe afii 10 kɛyashi 15. Mɛɛ ni odu tsei tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ekoŋŋ dani ote shi ni otutua bo

english: Why do my young cocoa trees struggle and dry up when there are no taller plants grown next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei komɛi bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct hot sun. Taller companion plants like plantains provide living shade and shelter, keeping the soil moist and protecting the young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Hefatalɔi tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ plantains lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ wɔɔhe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak when I plant many seeds close together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing them out gives every plant enough room for its roots to absorb food and leaves to catch sunlight, resulting in strong stalks and bigger cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baatswa akaŋ kɛha hulu la. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni kã tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, ni ebaa lɛ hu aná hulu la. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe wa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it better to plant my cassava sticks slanted in the ground rather than laying them flat or standing them straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ koŋ nɔ fe ni akɛaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ loo akɛma shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a 45-degree angle helps the plant sprout leaves quickly above ground while allowing root tubers to develop evenly in the soil, making them easier to harvest later.
ga: Kɛ́ odu o-yucca tsei lɛ yɛ 45 degree ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaakpa yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The worms hide inside the growing funnel of the maize plant during the day, eating the tender leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ gbɛi ni miida lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ baai bibii ni ayeɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, usually from extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or a lack of specific soil nutrients like calcium. Without steady moisture and moderate temperature, the flower cannot set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ kpe. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa shwane mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium, kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo ni sa bɛ mli. Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo yibii.

english: Why did my crops burn and dry up after I put fresh chicken manure directly around their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ hee ebɔle tsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fresh animal manure releases high amounts of heat and ammonia gas as it decomposes, which burns plant roots. Manure must be dried or left to rot into compost for a few weeks before applying it to crops.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ jieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ammonia gas babaoo kpo beni efiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi ashã. Esa akɛ agbi ŋmɔshi nibii loo aŋmɛ gbɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii otsii fioo komɛi dani akɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: Why does my farmland produce good yields for the first two years but starts producing small crops by the third year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli shi ebɔi ŋmɔshi nibii bibii awomɔ yɛ afi ni ji etɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the soil every harvest season. If you do not put nutrients back through compost, manure, fertilizers, or leguminous crops like beans, the soil becomes tired and depleted.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa kpamɔɔ be mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ efataaa o-compost, ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ekoŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ni ebaafee nɔ ni shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do extension officers tell me not to plant pepper on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkadu pepper yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously allows soil-borne diseases and pests that feed on that specific crop to build up in the ground. Rotating pepper with crops like maize or cassava breaks the life cycle of these pests.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Peppers ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa shwieɔ nɔ lɛ Ebaafite nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ashihilɛ gbɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and getting scorched?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or gliricidia trees planted near them to provide living cover while their roots mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo glicidia tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛha amɛhe nɔ ko yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my yam leaves droop and roll up during the hot afternoon even when the ground is slightly moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebɔleɔ ehe yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo moŋ lɛ?

english: Leaves curl or droop on very hot days as a defense mechanism to reduce water loss through evaporation. As long as the soil has moisture, the leaves usually bounce back by evening when temperatures drop.
ga: Ha amɛku amɛsɛɛ loo amɛgbee shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa gbɛkɛ mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when there is heavy rainfall for many weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa otsii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rain saturates the soil for too long without proper drainage, water displaces the air, causing fungal rots to attack and destroy the underground tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewoɔ nu be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nu baaye kɔɔyɔɔ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why should I take my farm's soil to a laboratory for testing before I start planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ aya laboratori ko mli koni aka lɛ akwɛ dani mibɔi dumɔwui?

english: Soil testing tells you what nutrients your land already has and what it lacks. It helps you choose the right crops for your ground and saves you money on buying fertilizers you might not need.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa baatsɔɔ bo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ nɔ ni bɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni ohalaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ, ni ehaa shika ni okɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekolɛ ehe ehiaaa bo lɛ baa shi.

english: Can cocoa trees grow well and produce good yields in drier regions like Accra?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei baanyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ hei ni nu bɛ tamɔ Accra?

english: Cocoa naturally thrives in warm, humid forest regions with regular rainfall. While it can grow in drier places like Accra, it requires extra effort like planting heavy shade crops, rich soil conditioning, and regular watering during dry spells.
ga: Kookoo daa yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ koo mli hei ni edɔ, fɛ̃i ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa. Eyɛ mli akɛ ebaanyɛ eda yɛ hei ni mli egbi tamɔ Accra moŋ. Shi ebiɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kroko, tamɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni aduɔ. Tsakemɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni efee nɔ ni baa nii. kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli

english: Why do farmers recommend planting plantain on the same land with young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ kookoo tsei bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct heat. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the cocoa seedlings with essential shade and soil moisture during their first few years.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Can I plant cocoyam together with cocoa and plantain on one field without them harming each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ kookoo kɛ kookoo kɛ plantain yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni miyeee mihe awui?

english: Yes, planting them together works well because they occupy different heights and soil depths. Cocoyam spreads close to the ground to shade the soil and suppress weeds, while plantain grows tall to protect the young cocoa above.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ bɔ ni ŋwɛi ŋsɔɔdo kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ ha lɛ hewɔ. Cocoa gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha jwɛi akabote shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni plantain lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni ebu kookoo bibii ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Is it good to grow pawpaw on the same plot where I am planting other food crops?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu paw paws yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ niyenii krokomɛi yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, pawpaw can be mixed with crops like plantain and cocoyam because it grows straight up and does not take up too much ground space, allowing you to harvest early fruit while other crops mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ Paw Paw afutu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantain kɛ cocoa. Ejaakɛ edaa jaŋŋ ni ehiɛɛɛ he ko tsɔ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa aduawai lɛ mra yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi daraa lɛ.

english: Tender young cocoa leaves cannot tolerate full, harsh sunlight. If there are no shade plants nearby to filter the heat, the seedlings lose moisture too fast, causing the leaves to scorch and dry up.
ga: Kookoo baai ni bɔdɔ nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa nɔ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ni baajie dɔlɛ Dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: How do I know if my farmland has enough nutrients for heavy crops like plantain and pawpaw?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ plantains kɛ pawpaws?

english: Healthy, nutrient-rich soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily, and retains moisture. If your crops display deep green leaves and strong stems, the soil is fertile; otherwise, yellowing leaves often signal a lack of nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ fɔɔ su ni tsuɔ, ni efiteɔ oya, ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛji otso lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa Tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli.

english: Can I filter dirty river or pond water through sand before pouring it on my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋã atsɔ nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛ faa loo ŋshɔ mli lɛ nɔ dani mafɔse miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, pouring water through layers of clean sand helps filter out large dirt particles, debris, and parasites. This gives you cleaner water that flows better into the root zone without clogging the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ ŋã ni mli tse nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ muji wuji, jwɛi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Enɛ haa onáa nu ni mli tse ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsiii.

english: How does feeding my crops with nutrient-enriched water help them grow faster?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli ni mikɛhaa mitsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya?

english: Plants absorb food through their roots in liquid form. When you add organic nutrients directly to irrigation water, the roots take in food instantly, encouraging faster root development and bigger leaf growth.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ niyenii kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ nu mli. Beni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fataa nu ni akɛshwieɔ nu lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ boteɔ niyenii lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya ni baai lɛ feɔ wuji.

english: If I plant multiple crops like cocoa, plantain, and cocoyam in the same hole, how do I keep them all fed?
ga: Kɛji midu tsei babaoo tamɔ kookoo, plantain, kɛ kookoo yɛ bu kome mli. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha amɛ fɛɛ niyenii?

english: Mixing multiple crops in close space means high demand for food. You must regularly supply rich organic compost or liquid manure so all plants get enough nutrients without competing and slowing down each other's growth.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni akɛfutuɔ he ko ni afo he lɛ haa niyenii he miihia babaoo. Esa akɛ okɛ organic compost loo organic fertilizer ni mli ewo muji aha daa. Bɔni afee ni tso fɛɛ tso aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ehe akatswa akaŋ ni ekɛ ehe akawo mli fioo.

english: How do I know if my soil lacks food before I plant my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmãa?

english: If your previous crop leaves turned yellow instead of dark green, or if the stalks grew thin and short, your soil is low on nutrients like nitrogen and needs manure or fertilizer before planting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsutsu lɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ Aloo kɛji tso lɛ shishifã lɛ bafee ŋmɔŋ ni efee kuku Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli dani odu.

english: Why do weeds always grow so much faster than the seeds I plant in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally stronger and better at pulling water and nutrients from the soil quickly. They must be cleared early so they do not steal food away from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni wa waa yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛhe esa waa yɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli oya. Esa akɛ ajie amɛ mra. Bɔni afee ni akaju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a living umbrella, giving the tender cocoa trees the shade they need to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Enɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa shade ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning yellow under the midday sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up during hot weather to save water from evaporating. If they also turn yellow, the plant is stressed from high heat, lack of moisture, or poor nutrients in the root area.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni nu akatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji etsɔ ŋmɔŋ Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa, ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli.

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stalks and smaller cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do I need to make big, soft soil mounds before planting my yam sets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee shikpɔŋ agbo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ dani madu ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth to expand downwards easily. Hard or rocky soil blocks the tuber from growing, resulting in short, thin, or crooked yams.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse bɔni afee ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shi mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi tsiɔ bulbs naa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji sweet potato kukuji, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, loo ni ekpɔtɔ.

english: What is causing the white powder on my cassava stems and making the leaves fall off?
ga: Mɛni haa powda yɛŋ feɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ anɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi?

english: That white powder is made of tiny pests called mealybugs. They suck the juice out of the stems, which starves the plant and stops the cassava roots underground from growing big.
ga: Akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii feɔ powda yɛŋ lɛ. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Amɛmuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ adara.

english: Flowers fall off when the soil gets too dry, temperatures drop or rise too suddenly, or insects fail to visit the flowers to help them form fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Temperature lɛ baa shi loo eyaa ŋwɛi trukaa tsɔ. Aloo kooloi bibii nyɛŋ ayasara fɔfɔi koni amɛye amɛbua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Is it better for my crop yield if I water my vegetable garden early in the morning or in the afternoon heat?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji mikɛ nu wo mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the cool soil absorbs the moisture deeply before the afternoon sun can evaporate the water or burn wet leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani shwane hulu lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi loo eshãa baai ni efɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know that my groundnuts under the ground are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the outer leaves turn yellow and dry up. You can pull up one test plant; if the inside of the pods has dark veins and firm nuts, the crop is mature.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Obaanyɛ ogbala kaa nitsumɔhe kome kɛya ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni wa Tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ.

english: Why does my farmland seem less fertile after using chemical fertilizers for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kwraa yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni mikɛtsu nii afii babaoo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Continuous reliance on synthetic chemicals without adding organic matter can destroy beneficial soil microbes and reduce the soil's natural ability to retain water and nutrients.
ga: Tsofai ni afee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ daa ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he lɛ baanyɛ akpata sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: Can applying too much chemical spray or fertilizer actually damage my crops?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ babaoo baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, excessive chemicals can burn plant roots and leaves, weaken the crop's natural defenses, and make the soil too acidic for healthy plant growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai. Ehaa tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu nibii lɛ baa shi. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ acid tsɔ ni tsei nyɛŋ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I bring life back to my land if chemicals have made the soil dry and weak?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aba wala mli ekoŋŋ kɛji tsofai haa egbiɔ ni egbɔjɔ?

english: You can restore soil health by adding organic materials like poultry manure, compost, and leaving clear cut leaf litter to decay on the farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ kooloi ashishifãi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ baai ni afolɔ ni oooshi koni amɛgboi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do officers ask us to cut off branches from cocoa trees if we want them to produce more yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ biɔ ni wɔfolɔ kookoo niji kɛji wɔmiisumɔ ni wɔwo babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing sunlight and air to reach the tree trunk where flowers form, while also reducing shade that breeds black pod disease.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ shishi he ni fɔfɔi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do I need to keep spraying my farm regularly instead of applying chemicals just once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ tsofa daa moŋ fe shikome pɛ lɛ?

english: Rain washes away chemical sprays, and pests or fungal spores continually return from nearby bushes, so regular applications are needed during vulnerable growth cycles.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ ahe. Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛjɛ tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli be fɛɛ be. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛtsu nii daa yɛ be mli ni shweremɔ ni waaa lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: When is the right time to cut tree branches so I don't ruin upcoming cocoa flowers?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ ofo tso ko he koni ekafite kookoo fɔfɔi ni baa lɛ?

english: Pruning is best done immediately after the main harvest season during the dry period, before the tree begins its new flowering cycle.
ga: Esa akɛ akpɛ tsei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ sɛɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Dani tsei lɛ baabɔi fɔmɔ ekoŋŋ

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing far fewer pods now than they did ten years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiwo ŋmeii babaoo fioo fe afii nyɔŋma ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, their production naturally drops due to worn-out roots, nutrient-depleted soil, or lingering diseases that weaken the plant over time.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ da lɛ, nibii ni ejieɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ shishifãi ni miifite lɛ hewɔ. shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli loo hela ko ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Is it better to cut down my old, tired cocoa farm and start fresh, or try to keep saving the old trees?
ga: Ani ebafeŋ nɔ ni hi akɛ aaafolɔ kookoo ŋmɔji momo ni etɔ lɛ amli ni aje shishi ekoŋŋ? Aloo oya nɔ obɔ mɔdɛŋ ni okwɛ tso momo lɛ nɔ?

english: If trees are very old or infected with incurable diseases like swollen shoot virus, clearing and replanting with modern, fast-yielding hybrid seedlings gives better profits long term.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ egbɔ waa loo hela ko ni anyɛɛɛ atsa tamɔ bud swollen virus lɛ emɔ lɛ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni woɔ yibii mra lɛ du ekoŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha sɛɛnamɔ kpakpa aba yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant new seedling cocoa right next to an old, sick cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo tsei heei yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ momo ko ni hela mɔ lɛ masɛi?

english: Insects and fungal diseases living on the old, sick trees will quickly cross over and destroy the weak young seedlings before they have a chance to mature.
ga: Kplukai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hiɔ tsei ni egbɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ baafo mli oya ni amɛbaakpãtã tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛná hegbɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why do cocoa trees drop their leaves and stop flowering during intense hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai ni amɛkpaa fɔfɔi yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves to conserve water during extreme heat, but without adequate moisture or shade canopy, the heat stress prevents flowers from turning into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Heat stress tsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee pods.

english: Which part of the cassava stem should I cut and plant to get a strong yield?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã esa akɛ afo ni adu koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba?

english: You should cut the mature middle part of a healthy stem, about 20 to 30 centimeters long. Avoid using the very woody base or the soft green top, as they do not sprout as strongly.
ga: Esa akɛ ofo tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ mli kɛyashɛ aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 30. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tso shishitoo loo shishitoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he. Ejaakɛ ekwɛɛɛ shi waa

english: How do I pick the best plantain shoots from my old farm to start a new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantains ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Look for 'sword suckers', which are young shoots with narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad base. These grow much faster and produce heavier bunches than shoots with broad, flat leaves.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante ŋmeii’, ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni baai lɛ mli tseee, tamɔ akpɔlɔi, ni amɛshishi lɛ mli kwɔ. Enɛɛmɛi daa oya ni amɛwoɔ niji ni tsii fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make energy to grow big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up to catch sunlight and keeps them off the damp soil where diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ yaa ŋwɛi koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, ni no ji he ni helai shwereɔ yɛ.

english: Yellowing starting from the leaf tips usually means your soil is low on nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK early in the plant's growth will help it regain its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK fata he yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the weather gets too hot and dry, or if you use too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant grow extra leaves instead of holding onto its fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii Enɛ baaha tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ babaoo moŋ fe ni eeekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ aduawai ahe.

english: Why are my green tomatoes turning black and soft on the bottom end?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo yɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit. It usually happens when the soil dries out completely between waterings, preventing the plant from taking up minerals.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni shɛɛɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ ni faaa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ kwraa yɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ teŋ. Koni tsei akaŋɔ minerals

english: What is eating small ragged holes in the leaves and center whorl of my corn?
ga: Mɛni ji buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-ŋma lɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Spraying approved insecticides or applying neem extracts early in the morning or late in the evening helps control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ loo okɛ neem mli nu lɛ wo nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Is it good for me to plant cowpeas between my rows of cassava?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas or beans between rows feeds nitrogen back into the soil naturally while covering the bare ground to prevent weeds from taking over.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ateŋ lɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Agbɛnɛ hu, ha hei ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ ahe koni jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why does my rice crop grow so poorly when the ground dries out completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Lowland rice roots need consistent moisture or shallow water to take up nutrients effectively. Dry soil stresses the plants and allows weeds to outcompete the rice.
ga: Omɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ biɔ nu ni mli edɔ daa loo nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ koni enyɛ eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kunim.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. They need shade trees to protect their leaves from sun damage and to keep the soil moist during their first few years of growth.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛbu amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni amɛdaraa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam vines produce much bigger tubers when I give them tall sticks to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ shwereɔ bulbs wuji babaoo beni mihaa amɛ niji ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants store energy in their tubers through photosynthesis, which happens in their leaves. Staking spreads the leaves out so they can catch maximum sunlight instead of shading each other on the ground.
ga: Atomɔ tsei toɔ hewalɛ yɛ amɛ tsei amli kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis, ni baa yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Staking gbɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ amli bɔni afee ni enyɛ ená hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha amɛhe nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yellowing starting from the tip and moving down the center leaf vein is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency. The maize plant is taking nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the younger top leaves.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni eyaa shi yɛ baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Abɛi tsei miiye nitrogen kɛmiijɛ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is my cowpea plant growing plenty of dark green leaves but hardly making any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa shi eshwɛ fioo ni ebɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes leguminous plants like cowpeas focus all their energy on leaf growth instead of flowering and setting fruit. Beans naturally make some of their own nitrogen, so they need less added nitrogen.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo haa ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii lɛ, Beans jieɔ nitrogen yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe ehiaaa nitrogen babaoo.

english: Excess water in heavy or poorly drained soil pushes oxygen out of the dirt, causing roots to suffocate and allowing waterlogging fungi to infect and rot the cassava tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ ni mli wa loo sũ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ tsɛŋeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni efiteɔ amɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or water is inconsistent. Extreme heat causes pollen to become sterile, so the plant drops unpollinated flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ haa pollen lɛ feɔ nɔ ni bɛ fɔmɔ kotoku. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in pepper is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips, mites, or aphids feeding under the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni haa ŋmeii baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my garden egg plants look healthy in the morning but completely wilt during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ leebi lɛ? Shi ani ebaagbi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Midday wilting happens when root damage from nematodes or bacterial wilt prevents the roots from absorbing water as fast as the hot sun evaporates it from the leaves.
ga: Gbi mli la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji akɛ nematodes loo bacteria wilt fite shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya tamɔ bɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over at the root when the fruit bunches grow large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛyaa shishigbɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Plantains fall easily if their root system is weakened by microscopic root pests called nematodes or plantain root weevils, which eat away the anchor roots supporting the heavy stem.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ shishifãi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo plantain root moths lɛ ha amɛshifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni baaye ŋwɛi shishifãi ni fiɔ tso lɛ shishi ni tsii waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why does a weed with purple flowers cause my maize plants near it to stay small and turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli lɛ gbaa abele tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anaa lɛ? Amɛji bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: This is Striga (witchweed), a parasitic plant that attaches its roots directly to maize roots under the soil, stealing water and vital nutrients before the maize can use them.
ga: Enɛ ji Striga (witchweed), tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpãa ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa dani akɛ ŋmãa lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing very small pods instead of growing to full size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaada kɛyashɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Tiny cocoa pods, often called cherelle wilt or stunted pods, can happen when the tree lacks sufficient soil nutrients, water, or when too many pods compete for energy on the same tree. Proper pruning and balanced fertilizer help the tree focus energy on producing full-sized pods.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii bibii, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ cherelle wilt loo dwarf pods lɛ baanyɛ aba kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu mli, loo kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo miitswa amɛhe shi koni amɛná hewalɛ yɛ tso kome nɔ. Tso lɛ ni afolɔ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni dalɛ fa babaoo.

english: How long does a newly planted cocoa tree usually take before it starts bearing pods?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties usually take about 3 to 5 years to start fruiting, while improved hybrid varieties can begin producing pods in about 2 to 3 years when given good soil, shade, and field care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hybrid cocoa henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aje ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ aha amɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa, hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ.

english: Why do flowers keep dropping off my crop plants before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Flower dropping happens when a crop experiences stress from dry weather, extreme heat, pest damage, or poor soil fertility. Maintaining soil moisture and keeping pests away helps flowers develop successfully into healthy fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na nɔnyɛɛ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ amli. loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ ajiemɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛyeɔ omanye ni amɛfeɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do fruits on my farm grow into strange, misshapen forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee nɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni efite lɛ?

english: Misshapen or deformed fruits are usually caused by incomplete insect pollination or damage from sap-sucking pests when the fruit is still very small and developing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ aduawai ni efite loo efite lɛ mli baa ji kooloi ni shwieɔ shi ni eshɛɛɛ he loo nibii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu lɛ fiteɔ beni aduawai lɛ ji bibii lolo ni amɛmiiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn yellow and wither when there are no shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo be bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle intense direct sunlight without losing water rapidly. Shade trees shield them from harsh heat, keep the ground cool, and help the foliage stay green and healthy.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ni nu lɛ sɛɛ efooo oya. Tsei haa hulutsoo, ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni eye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: During the dry harmattan, cold winds and low air moisture cause crops to lose water quickly. Plants naturally drop leaves and slow growth to protect themselves until rainfall returns.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ fioo lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaafee amɛdalɛ fioo koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil lacks the right nutrients for a good crop yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai aba?

english: Poor soil fertility shows up through slow growth, yellowish leaves, weak stems, and small or sparse yields. Adding organic compost or appropriate fertilizers restores essential nutrients to the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ jieɔ ehe kpo akɛ dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, kɛ nibii ni baa shi loo ni baa shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it necessary to cut away extra water shoots and unwanted branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo nu mli ŋmeii ni fa fe nine kɛ niji ni ataooo kɛjɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, often called chupons, consume water and nutrients that the main tree needs to make pods. Pruning them allows sunlight and airflow into the canopy, leading to better fruiting.
ga: Tsobii ni fa fe nine, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ chupon. Ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Nibii ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibiiwoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes cocoa pods to turn black and rot while still attached to the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ he lolo lɛ?

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungal infection that thrives in wet, overly shaded conditions. Regular harvesting, clearing farm weeds, and pruning heavy branches reduce humidity and slow down disease spread.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji fungal hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo fe nine mli. regular harvest Jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Ni niji ni tsii ni afoɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi ni ebaaha helai agbɛ ashwa.

english: Can I plant coconut trees on the same piece of land alongside my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ ŋmei tsei ahe?

english: Yes, coconut trees can be intercropped with cocoa because tall coconut palms provide gentle canopy shade while allowing sunlight to reach the cocoa below, helping maximize farm space and yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmei tsei awo kookoo mli. Akɛni akokoo tsei kakadaji lɛ haa hulutsoo hewɔ lɛ, amɛhaa hulutsoo blɛoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ kookoo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ mli he kɛ nibii babaoo ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Can I plant food crops on land where oil palm trees were previously growing?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ aduɔ mu tsei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, but oil palm trees pull a lot of nutrients out of the soil over their lifetime. Before planting food crops, you should add compost or manure to restore the soil's strength so your new crops can thrive.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi mu tsei jieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ amɛwala beaŋ. Dani obaadu niyenii Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ koni tsei heei anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Is land that stays wet or holds water good for farming?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efɔ loo eyɛ nu ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: It depends on the crop. Swampy land is excellent for water-loving crops like rice, sugarcane, or leafy vegetables, but roots of crops like cassava, cocoa, and maize will rot if they sit in standing water for too long.
ga: Edamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. He ni ŋmɔji yɔɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei ni sumɔɔ nu tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo aduawai ni yɔɔ baai, shi tsei tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa shishifãi baanyɛ afite kɛji amɛtara nu ni damɔ shi mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Is freshly cleared bush land always better for crops than land that has been farmed before?
ga: Ani koo mli shikpɔŋ hee ni ajie lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fe shikpɔŋ ni atsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Freshly cleared land usually has rich topsoil filled with decomposed leaves, giving crops a great boost. However, clearing all trees exposes the bare soil to sun and heavy rain, which can wash away those nutrients if you do not cover or protect the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hei ni ajie sũ lɛ ehee lɛ yɛ sũ ni nɔ kwɔ ni baai ni egboi eyi mli obɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ waa. Shi kɛlɛ, tso fɛɛ tso ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ ajie nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛji okɛhaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo obuuu he.

english: Why do crops grow very well on one section of my family land but poorly on another section?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miweku lɛ fã ko mli shi ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he kroko lɛ?

english: Soil quality changes across even a small piece of land. Differences in underground rock, soil depth, moisture retention, and how heavily that specific patch was farmed in past years all affect crop growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su tsakeɔ yɛ shikpɔji bibii po anɔ. Srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tɛi amli shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ mli Fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ ni adu yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ saa tsei lɛ adalɛ he.

english: Why is it important to test small patches of land before planting my main crops on all of it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ aka he bibioo ko akwɛ? Ehe miihia dani adu mi tso titri lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ fɛɛ.

english: Testing small patches lets you see how well the soil holds water and nutrients without risking all your money. It shows you which section of your land yields the best harvests before you commit your full effort.
ga: small piece test Ehaa onaa bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ oshika fɛɛ wooo oshara mli. Ebaatsɔɔ bo oshikpɔŋ lɛ fãi ni woɔ yibii fe fɛɛ lɛ dani okɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ aha lɛ.

english: How long does it usually take to know if a piece of land is good for long-term tree crops?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani anyɛɔ aleɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ko hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ adumɔ?

english: For long-term crops like palm trees or cocoa, it can take several years to see their true performance. While young trees show basic health in 2 to 3 years, knowing the full yield quality of the land requires observing them over 10 to 15 years.
ga: Kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ ŋmei tsei loo kookoo Ekolɛ ehe afii babaoo dani ana bɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei bibii jieɔ shishijee hewalɛnamɔ lɛ kpo yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli moŋ, shi bɔni afee ni ale bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akwɛ tsei nɛɛ amli yɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 15 mli.

english: What happens to the soil when I clear heavy trees and bush off my farmland?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kɛ tsei bibii ni tsii kɛjɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ?

english: Removing trees removes shade and organic matter. Sun dries out the soil faster, and heavy rain can wash away topsoil. Leaving crop residue or planting cover crops helps protect the newly cleared ground.
ga: Tsei ni ajieɔ lɛ baajie hulutsoo kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Hulu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Tsoi ni afolɔ ashwie shi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ he ni ajie lɛ ehee lɛ he.

english: What kind of crops should I plant on low land near streams that gets flooded during rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ adu yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ faai ni nu hoɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Low, flood-prone land is ideal for crops that thrive in damp soil, such as rice, taro (cocoyam), and certain vegetables. Avoid planting deep-rooted cash crops or tubers that decay easily in soggy earth.
ga: Hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu afua fɔɔ baa lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ, tamɔ omɔ, taro (kookoo), kɛ aduawai komɛi. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ shika ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmeii ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni fiteɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ dumɔ he.

english: How can I farm land that has water sitting in it so my crops do not drown?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsu okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ koni miŋmɔshi nibii akagbo?

english: You can dig drainage channels to move standing water off the land, or build high ridges and mounds. Raising the soil lifts the crop roots above the water level so they can breathe while still drinking moisture from below.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ koni okɛjie nu ni damɔ shi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. aloo ama ŋmeii kɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni awoɔ lɛ woɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyaa nu lɛ nɔ koni amɛmu yɛ be mli ni amɛnuɔ nu ni jɛɔ shishi lɛ lolo.

english: How does oil palm affect the ground compared to other crops?
ga: Te oil palm lɛ saa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe?

english: Oil palm trees create dense shade and develop deep, thick root networks that stay in the soil for decades. This keeps the ground under them shaded and cooler, but it changes how water moves through the earth after the palms are removed.
ga: Mu tsei feɔ hulutsoo ni mli kwɔ ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ hulutsoo shishi ni ehaa edɔɔ. Mohu ɔ, e tsakeɔ bɔ nɛ nyu ɔ guɔ kɛ guɔ zugba a nɔ ke a je tso ɔ kɛ je ɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen or the roots are sitting in too much water. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea when the soil is moist helps the leaves turn green and produce good corn heads.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why does my okro plant keep growing very tall with big leaves but produces almost no pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eshwɛ fioo ni ebɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: When okro receives too much nitrogen fertilizer, it spends all its energy growing stems and leaves instead of flowering. Switching to fertilizers higher in phosphorus encourages the plant to stop growing leaves and start fruiting.
ga: Kɛji okra nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ Ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ moŋ fe ni eeewo fɔfɔi. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee fɔsfɔs ni fa babaoo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekpa baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ ni ebɔi yibiiwoo.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme hot weather, lack of water, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and watering at the base helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli fũu pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ nu ni awoɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees shed their small pods during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop small pods—a process called cherelle wilt—to save water and survive when soil moisture is low. Providing shade and keeping organic mulch around the root area helps retain water and reduces pod loss.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii, ni ji nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ cherel wilting. Koni ekɛ nu akafite ni ehi shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa. Ni akɛ jwɛi ni wala yɔɔ mli baaha he ni ebɔle he lɛ he hulutsoo kɛ mulching. He ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehaa pod ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cassava cuttings very close together on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need enough underground space to swell into large tubers. Planting them too close forces the plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, woody roots with little harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ŋmaa lɛ faaa.

english: Yam tubers struggle to grow straight when the soil in your mounds or ridges is too hard and compact, or full of large stones. Loosening the soil deeply when building mounds allows the tubers to expand freely.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. loo tɛi wuji eyi mli obɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ama gɔŋ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ oya.

english: Why do my pepper plants dry up and wilt suddenly even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This usually happens because of root rot disease caused by excessive water around the roots. When water stays too long without draining, fungi attack the roots, preventing the plant from taking up water and causing it to wilt.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ ni nu babaoo ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ, kɛ́ nu ta shi be kakadaŋŋ ni efooo. Fuji lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ nu ni ehaa amɛgboɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my plantain suckers turning brown and burning at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiishã yɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Brown, burnt edges on plantain leaves are often a sign of water stress or potassium deficiency in the soil. Giving the plants enough water and applying wood ash or potassium fertilizer helps keep the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain baai lɛ ahe ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eshã lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nu mli haomɔ loo potassium ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛ tso sũ loo potassium ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛbaa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tiny holes are usually caused by small caterpillars like the diamondback moth larvae eating the leaves. Inspecting under the leaves regularly and applying recommended organic or chemical sprays will protect the cabbage heads.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii, tamɔ diamondback moth lɛ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi daa, ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsofa mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kaabe yitsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I dry fertilizer directly on dry soil around my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the plant roots can drink it in. Placing dry fertilizer on dry soil can burn the crop's roots and waste the fertilizer because it sits uselessly on top of the ground.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya fitemɔ ejaakɛ eta shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Why do my delicate young nursery seedlings wilt and die right after I transplant them into my main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings experience 'transplant shock' because their roots get disturbed and cannot pull up water fast enough in full sunlight. Watering them well before moving and transplanting late in the afternoon helps them adjust smoothly.
ga: Tsei bibii baaná piŋmɔ kɛjɛ Amɛnaa ‘transplant shock’ he piŋmɔ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ haoɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie nu oya bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ dani aduɔ lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I handle young crop seedlings without breaking or destroying them when moving them to the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsu dumɔwui bibii ahe nii ni mifiteee amɛ loo mifiteee amɛ beni mikɛ amɛ yaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Always lift seedlings by holding the soil ball around the roots or by the leaves, never by the main stem. Grabbing the main stem crushes the inner tubes that carry water and nutrients, which kills the plant.
ga: Wo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ sũ ni okɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe loo yɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Kaata tsɔne wulu lɛ he. Kɛ́ mɔmɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ, efoɔ mligbɛ tsɔne ni kɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbo.

english: Why do young cocoa plants need to be planted under plantain trees when setting up a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu kookoo tsei bibii yɛ plantain tsei ashishi kɛ́ ato ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide canopy shade and keep the soil moist, giving delicate cocoa seedlings time to mature before they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ haa hɔɔŋ ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ be ni amɛkɛdara dani amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: How can I protect my young vegetable crops from being scorched by the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui lɛ ahe koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ akashã amɛ?

english: You can build temporary shade structures using palm fronds or tall grasses over the young plants. This reduces heat stress while the crops build strong root systems.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei tsei loo jwɛi kakadaŋŋ atsu nii ni okɛfee hulutsoo be kukuoo ko yɛ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ, ni no baaha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ maa shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ.

english: Why do my newly sprouted crops look tall, thin, and weak instead of bushy and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛkwɔ, amɛhe ejɔ, ni amɛhe waaa, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Sprouts stretch out and grow thin when they do not receive enough sunlight. The plant spends all its energy reaching upward looking for light instead of developing a thick, sturdy stem.
ga: Tsobii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ baagbala amɛhe ni amɛbaafee bibii kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ taoɔ la. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tso nɛ mi wa nɛ e hiɔ si daa.

english: Curling yellow leaves on young crops usually mean the plant is stressed by heat or attacked by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies. Keeping the soil cool with mulch helps reduce this growth stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe yɛ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulutsoo eba tso lɛ nɔ loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii yɛji etutua lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ dalɛ nɛɛ he haomɔ aba shi.

english: How do I know when my fragile seedlings have settled in and no longer need special shade or protection?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni midumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ewo shishifãi? ni ebiii hulutsoo loo hebuu krɛdɛɛ ko dɔŋŋ.

english: Once your seedlings start producing dark green new leaves and firm stems, their roots have established. At this stage, they are strong enough to withstand direct sunlight and regular field conditions.
ga: Beni odumɔwui lɛ jeɔ baai heei kɛ tsei ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shishi lɛ. Eshishifãi lɛ ema shi momo yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli, ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ anaa.

english: How can I keep the soil moist around my young crops during dry periods?
ga: Mibaafee shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi yɛ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the dirt around your crops with dry grass, straw, or fallen leaves (mulching) traps moisture in the ground and prevents the sun from drying out fragile roots.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi, jwɛi loo baai ni egbee shi (mulch) shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaaa hulu la akagbi shishifãi ni waaa lɛ.

english: How deep should I dig the holes when transplanting my young crop seedlings?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo bu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ midumɔwui bibii lɛ miidu shi?

english: Dig holes just deep enough so the seedling's root ball sits level with the ground surface. Planting too deep causes the stem to rot, while planting too shallow leaves roots exposed to drying heat.
ga: Tsɔmɔmɔ bu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwu lɛ shishifã bɔɔlu lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ekome. Kɛ́ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbo. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu nii yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná la ni mli egbi.

english: Why are insects attacking the leaves of my young plants much more than my older crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii lɛ tutuaa mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ babaoo fe mi tsei momo lɛ?

english: Young leaves are soft, tender, and full of water and sugars, making them easy for insects to chew. Older crops develop tougher, fibrous leaves that are harder for pests to destroy.
ga: Baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛyɛ velvet ni nu kɛ sugar eyi mli obɔ. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ ŋmɔmɔ feɔ mlɛo Tsei ni edara lɛ feɔ baai ni wa, ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni ewa akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ baafite.

english: Why do many flowers on my cocoa trees dry up and fall off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers require pollination to turn into pods. Naturally, very tiny insects called midges carry pollen between flowers, but there are often not enough midges on the farm, causing many unpollinated flowers to simply drop off.
ga: Esa akɛ afee kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ŋmɔtɔ. Shi bei pii lɛ, yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ, kooloi bibii ni haaa ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmeii bɔ ni sa lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi babaoo ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Hand pollination is a technique where a person manually transfers pollen from one cocoa flower to another using small tools like tweezers. This ensures that almost every flower gets pollinated, significantly increasing the number of cocoa pods your tree produces.
ga: Nine nɔ fɔfɔi ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ ji gbɛ ko ni mɔ ko tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ enine shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni jɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ dɛŋdade bibioo ko, tamɔ tweezers nɔ. Enɛ haa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi nɔ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baaha kookoo ŋmeii ni otso lɛ woɔ lɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: What is the best time of day for cocoa flowers to be pollinated on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afee kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Early morning is the best time for pollination because cocoa flowers open during the night and early morning hours when pollen is most fertile and the flowers are fresh.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha pollination. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ kɛ leebi maŋkpa be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ fa babaoo ni fɔfɔi lɛ hu yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo lɛ.

english: How can I tell if a cocoa flower on my tree was successfully pollinated?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ eye omanye yɛ ŋmɔlɔ mli?

english: Within two to three days after pollination, a successful flower will remain firmly attached to the stem and its base will start swelling into a tiny green pod, whereas an unpollinated flower will turn brown and drop off.
ga: Yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli yɛ pollination sɛɛ Fɔfɔi ni yeɔ omanye lɛ baakã he akpɛtɛ tso lɛ shishi shiŋŋ. ni eshishigbɛ lɛ baaje shishi etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibioo ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi ni bɛ pollen lɛ feɔ blɔfo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Can I do hand pollination on my cocoa farm by myself, or do I need extra labor?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ awo mli? Aloo ehe miihia ni mikɛ nitsumɔ kroko atsu nii?

english: You can hand-pollinate your own trees after basic training, but because the process requires careful attention flower by flower, many farmers choose to recruit and train extra workers to cover large farms quickly during peak flowering season.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ pollen awo bo diɛŋtsɛ otsei lɛ amli yɛ shishijee tsɔsemɔ sɛɛ. Shi akɛni gbɛ nɛɛ biɔ ni akwɛ fɔfɔi komekomei jogbaŋŋ hewɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ okwaafoi babaoo halaa akɛ amɛbaahe nitsulɔi krokomɛi ni amɛtsɔse amɛ koni amɛtsu ŋmɔji wuji ahe nii oya yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii babaoo yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: How long does it take from the time a cocoa flower is pollinated until I can harvest the ripe pod?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo fɔfɔi ni awo mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekwɛ̃?

english: It typically takes between five to six months from the day a cocoa flower is successfully pollinated for the pod to fully grow, mature, and turn yellow or orange for harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee nyɔji enumɔ kɛyashi enumɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ ji koni eha ŋmeii lɛ adara, amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ.

english: Why do some of the tiny young pods on my cocoa tree turn black and shrink before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji No hewɔ lɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbɔjɔ dani etsɔ agbo.

english: This is often caused by 'cherelle wilt,' a natural process where the tree discards excess pods it cannot feed, but it can also be caused by diseases like black pod or sap-sucking insects attacking young pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ‘Cherelle wilt’, ni ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni tsei shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aye lɛ Shi helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni tutuaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ hu baanyɛ aha enɛ aba.

english: Why are there fewer midges to pollinate my cocoa flowers during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieee ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Midges need damp leaf litter and shade to breed and survive. During dry periods, the soil and leaves dry out, reducing the midge population and leading to lower natural pollination.
ga: Dwarfs he hiaa baa jwɛi kɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ koni amɛfɔ ni amɛhi shi. yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ baai lɛ baagbi. Nɔ ni ejɛ mli eba ji akɛ, kooloi ni ji midge lɛ ayibɔ eba shi. ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Will hand pollination weaken or damage my cocoa trees over time?
ga: Ani nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baaha mi-cacao tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ loo ebaafite yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Hand pollination does not harm the tree itself, but because it causes trees to yield many more pods than usual, you must provide extra fertilizer and water to keep the trees strong and nourished.
ga: Nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ yeee tso lɛ awui. Shi akɛni enɛ baaha tso lɛ awo ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe baahia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu krokomɛi aha koni eha otsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná niyenii kpakpa.

english: How do I observe and measure if a new practice like hand pollination is actually increasing my farm yields?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ ni masusu bɔ ni nifeemɔ hee ko tamɔ nine nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsuɔ nii eha lɛ he? Ani ehaa nibii ni anáa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You can test the practice on a specific section of your farm, count the number of healthy pods growing on those trees compared to untreated trees, and track the final harvest weight from that section.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka nifeemɔi okwɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ fãi pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli. Kanemɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nakai tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ayibɔ. Okɛto tsei ni atsako amɛ lɛ ahe. ni okwɛ naagbee ŋmaa lɛ mli tsiimɔ kɛjɛ nakai fã lɛ mli.

english: Why should I clear all the weeds and bushes from my field before I start planting seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with young crops for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Clearing them completely before planting gives your new seeds a strong, clean start without having to fight for survival.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ dani adu lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui heei lɛ aje shishi yɛ gbɛ ni he tse ni mli wa nɔ, ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛwuu koni amɛhi shi.

english: How do I know if my land has been worked enough to be ready for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsu nii yɛ nɔ?

english: Your land is ready when the soil is cleared of deep roots, broken down into soft, loose crumbs, and holds enough moisture so that young roots can easily push through and feed.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ ajie sũ lɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli. Efoɔ mli bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ehiɛɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli oya ni amɛye nii.

english: Why does rice need so much wet land compared to crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔkpɔ babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants are specially built to survive and thrive in very wet or flooded soils where other crops would drown. The standing water also acts as a natural shield to stop common weeds from growing.
ga: Atswa ŋmãa tsei krɛdɛɛ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛshwere yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ, he ni tsei krokomɛi baanyɛ agbo yɛ nu mli lɛ. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ hu tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ jwɛi ni afɔɔ namɔ naa koni ekakwɛ̃.

english: How long does it usually take from the day I plant rice until it is ready for harvesting?
ga: Be enyiɛ bei pii lɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Most standard rice varieties in Ghana take between 3 to 4 months (90 to 120 days) from planting to reach full maturity and be ready for harvesting.
ga: Omɔ henɔi ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 (gbii 90 kɛyashi 120) kɛjɛɔ dumɔ mli dani eshɛɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni esaa ehe kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Can I plant rice on high dry land, or must it always be in a valley or swamp?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ gɔŋ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ? Aloo esa akɛ adu yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli loo ŋshɔkei amli be fɛɛ be?

english: You can plant special 'upland rice' varieties on dry land if there is steady rainfall, but 'lowland rice' varieties must be planted in marshy valleys or flooded fields to produce a good harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ‘Khao Don’ tso krɛdɛɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ daa. Shi esa akɛ adu ‘ŋmãa folo’ henɔi lɛ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli loo ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli koni aná yibii kpakpai.

english: Why are the leaves of my young crops turning yellow instead of staying bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants are starving for essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or they are getting too much or too little water, preventing them from making food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ yɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ loo fioo tsɔ. Ehaa anyɛɛɛ ahoo nii

english: What makes crops grow very tall and healthy on one part of my farm, but remain short on another part?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔshi nibii daa ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome mli? Shi fã kroko hu yɛ ni elaaje lolo.

english: Soil quality changes across the land. Areas with deeper topsoil, higher organic matter, and better water holding capacity will feed plants much faster than dry, rocky, or washed-out patches.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su tsakeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. Hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ Eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ Enɛ baaha tsei aye niyenii oya fe hei ni egbi. tɛ loo nu ni miiho kɛmiijɛ mli yɛ jɛmɛ

english: Why does my land produce smaller crop yields each year even though I plant the same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Ni midu yɛ nakai gbɛ nɔ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Planting the exact same crop on the same soil every season drains specific nutrients from the earth without giving it time to recover. Rotating crops or adding compost helps restore the soil's strength.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.
