english: How do I choose the right time of the year to start planting my food crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala afi lɛ mli be ni sa koni mabɔi niyenii ŋmɔ?

english: Planting should be timed right at the start of the steady rainy season so that young seeds receive continuous moisture to germinate and grow without drying up in early droughts.
ga: Esa akɛ adu be ni sa kɛjɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli daa. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui bibii lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara ni amɛgbiŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: How do improved seed varieties differ from the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake lɛ yɔɔ srɔto yɛ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Improved seeds are carefully selected and bred to grow faster, resist local pests and diseases, and yield significantly more food than seeds saved repeatedly from old harvests.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛɔ amɛ koni amɛdara oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ maŋ lɛ mli helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ewoɔ niyenii babaoo kwraa fe dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I know if my crop branches are starting at the right height?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miniji lɛ miije shishi yɛ he ni sa?

english: A practical way to check is by using your arm's reach. If the branches start where your hand comfortably reaches, it means the tree will be easy and affordable to care for and harvest without needing expensive ladders.
ga: Gbɛ ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ ji ni akɛ nine ni akɛshɛɔ he lɛ atsu nii. Kɛji akɛ nine lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ he ko ni obaanyɛ okɛ onine ashɛ he oya lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ amɛkpamɔ waaa ni amɛhe ehiaaa ni atswerei ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: What happens if my crop branches split off very low to the ground?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji miniji lɛ kwɛ̃ shi kɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: When branches split low, the plant divides its energy early, which can keep the tree short and make weeding around it difficult. Managing low branches helps the main trunk grow strong before it spreads out.
ga: Kɛji niji lɛ dara shi lɛ Tsei lɛ jaa hewalɛ oya. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ kuku, ni ehaa ewaa akɛ abaajie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei niji lɛ ba shi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ tso titri lɛ dani egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my young trees split into multiple branches instead of growing straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ mli gbalaa ewoɔ niji babaoo mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ?

english: Trees naturally split their stems to spread their leaves and catch more sunlight. While branching is good for crop yield, guiding where it happens ensures the plant stays sturdy and easy to work with.
ga: Tsei gbalaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Eyɛ mli akɛ niji ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ, shi kɛ́ oyɔse he ni ejɛɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ mli awa ni ekɛ nitsumɔ afee mlɛo.

english: How tall should I allow my crop stems to grow before letting them spread out?
ga: Te esa akɛ maha tsei ashishifãi lɛ adara dani mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã?

english: It is best to let the main trunk grow until the branching point is within your physical reach. This keeps the fruit-bearing canopy low enough for easy maintenance and spraying.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ada kɛyashi niji lɛ ahe hei lɛ baashɛ he ni ashɛɔ he. Enɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni woɔ yibii lɛ baa shi bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ tsofa afɔ nɔ.

english: Why do extension officers suggest using my hand to measure branch height instead of buying a measuring tape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nitsumɔhe nine lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ niji asusu nitsumɔhe nine lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta moŋ fe ni ooohe tsɔne ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe lɛ?

english: Using your hand span costs no money and automatically customizes the tree height to your personal physical reach, making field management simple and affordable.
ga: Odɛŋ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ he ehiaaa ni ekɛ tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni obaanyɛ oshɛ he lɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ feɔ mlɛo ni ejara hu waaa

english: Why should I use stretchy material like rubber instead of hard rope to tie my plant stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ nɔ ko ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tamɔ rɔba atsu nii yɛ kpãa ni wa najiaŋ kɛfi tso shishifãi lɛ?

english: Stretchy rubber expands as the plant grows thick. Hard rope will strangle the stem and cut into the bark, while rubber allows the trunk to swell safely without blocking water and nutrients.
ga: Nu ni anyɛɔ agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ mli lɛɛɔ be mli ni tso lɛ mli shwieɔ shi lɛ. Kpãai ni wa lɛ fiɔ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛfoɔ lɛ ni efeɔ tso lɛ yibii. yɛ be mli ni rɔbɔt lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni etsĩii nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii anaa.

english: When is the right time to cut off the rubber ties I used to guide my plant branches?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafo hoso ni mikɛtsuɔ nii kɛkudɔɔ tso lɛ niji lɛ?

english: You can safely cut and remove the rubber ties once the branch has grown strong enough to hold its position on its own, ensuring it won't choke the mature stem later.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofo hoso lɛ ni ojie lɛ shweshweeshwe kɛji tso lɛ nine lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni enyɛ ehiɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛhe lɛ. Enɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ rɔbɔt tso lɛ efiteee tso ni eda sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: What happens to a branch if I trim the tip after it reaches my height limit?
ga: Mɛni baa tso nine ko nɔ kɛji mifo eshishigbɛ beni eshɛ he ni ekɛlɛ ji lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Trimming the top tip stops the branch from growing higher and encourages the plant to put energy into thickening the stem and producing flowers and fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ofo tso lɛ yitso lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ nine lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃. ni ekanyaa tsei koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛha amɛshishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwo fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai

english: Why does a branch that splits low remain short compared to other branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ kuku lolo kɛ akɛto niji krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: A low-splitting branch shares nutrients with the main stem and often gets shaded by upper leaves, which stops it from climbing high into the sunlight.
ga: Niji ni niji bɛ amɛhe lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ jaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bei pii lɛ amɛyɛ ŋwɛi baai ni haa hulu tsoɔ. ni haaa anyɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulu la lɛ mli

english: Will supporting young stems with elastic ties prevent them from becoming strong trunks?
ga: Ani tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni akɛ elastic tsɔnei fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafee hewalɛ?

english: No, flexible ties give the stem room to sway slightly in the wind while growing, which actually helps the plant build thick, strong wood while staying in the right shape.
ga: Dabi, wekukpaa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli ni tsakeɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ shishi tsu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli beni edaa lɛ, ni no yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni ewoɔ tsei ni mli tse ni mli wa yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ mli.

english: Why should I pick off black and rotten cocoa pods from my trees instead of leaving them there?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie kookoo ŋmeii diji ni miifite lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashi amɛ yɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Leaving infected or rotten pods on the tree allows fungal spores and insects to spread the sickness to healthy cocoa pods nearby every time it rains.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ loo ni egboi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii gbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: What should I do with infected cocoa pods after cutting them off the tree?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kookoo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: You should gather and throw infected pods far away from healthy trees or bury them, preventing insects and rain from carrying the disease back to your good crops.
ga: Esa akɛ obua ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anaa ni okɛshwie tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe loo ofu amɛ. Enɛ ji koni kooloi bibii kɛ nugbɔ akakɛ hela aba onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Does leaving old cocoa husks on the farm ground after harvesting hurt my healthy trees?
ga: Ani kookoo ŋmeii momo ni mashi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ baaye mi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ awui?

english: Yes, leaving piles of diseased husks on the ground creates a breeding site for pests and fungi, which can splash back up onto lower pods during heavy rains.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ. ni baanyɛ aku esɛɛ kɛya shishigbɛ pod lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: How does keeping my cocoa farm clear of dead pods help protect my harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ bɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Clearing out bad pods removes the main hiding places for diseases, keeping the air around your trees clean and reducing the chances of healthy pods catching sickness.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii gbohii lɛ, ejieɔ he titri ni helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ Otsei lɛ ahe atse. ni ehaa hegbɛ ni yɔɔ akɛ pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baaná hela lɛ baa shi.

english: Is there any spray or chemical I can use to cure a cocoa tree once it gets a severe disease?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsofai komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ mikɛtsa mi-kookoo tsei lɛ kɛ́ hela ko ni naa wa mɔ amɛ?

english: Some serious cocoa diseases have no cure once they infect the tree, so removing infected pods or destroying sick trees is the only way to save the rest of your farm.
ga: Kookoo helai komɛi ni naa wa lɛ bɛ tsabaa kɛji amɛbote tso lɛ mli pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie loo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ akpãtãmɔ ji gbɛ pɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oye obua oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn soft, watery, and useless before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, nu yɔɔ mli, ni sɛɛnamɔ ko bɛ he dani amɛshwereɔ po lɛ?

english: Diseases like black pod attack the flesh of the cocoa, destroying the pulp and seeds inside until the pod turns into a watery, rotten shell.
ga: Helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ tutuaa kookoo lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ. Kpata loo kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahiɛ kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baatsɔ nu ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baafite.

english: Can a single sick cocoa tree spread disease to all the other trees on my farm?
ga: Kakao tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala hela kɛya tsei krokomɛi anɔ. Fɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, insects, wind, and rain droplets easily carry disease particles from one sick tree to nearby healthy ones if left untreated.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kooloi bibii, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ nu mli ŋmeii baanyɛ ajie helai bibii kɛjɛ tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ nɔ kɛya tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ nɔ oya kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: How can I tell if a swollen or sick cocoa tree can be saved or needs to be cut down?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji abaanyɛ atsa kookoo tso ni efuu loo hela mɔ lɛ loo ehe miihia ni afo lɛ?

english: If the disease is only on the pods, removing them works, but if the tree trunk or shoots are swollen and dying, there is no cure and the whole tree must be cut down.
ga: Kɛji hela lɛ ba yɛ pod lɛ mli pɛ lɛ, ejiemɔ lɛ tsu nii. Shi kɛji tso lɛ shishi loo eyiteŋ fũu ni egbo Tsamɔ ko bɛ. ni esa akɛ afo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ afɔ shi

english: Why is my harvested cocoa pile turning into bad waste instead of good dried beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ni akpa lɛ ni mikɛto lɛ baafite yɛ ŋmeii ni egbi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Mixing infected pods with healthy ones during harvest allows rot to ruin the good beans, turning your hard work into a wasted, low-quality pile.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ futu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afite. ni otsɔ onitsumɔ ni wa lɛ nɔ otsɔ ŋtayaa ni efite, ni sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he.

english: Why am I seeing fewer healthy cocoa pods on my trees during harvest time than before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaaa kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ kpamɔ be mli fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: Unmanaged diseases slowly weaken your trees over time, causing pods to rot early or stop forming properly, which steadily reduces your total harvest yield.
ga: Helai ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha otso lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya loo amɛkpaa amɛhe feemɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha nɔ ni ojieɔ lɛ fɛɛ aba shi be fɛɛ be.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a canopy that shields the young cocoa from heat and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: When cocoa trees are too close, their roots compete for soil nutrients and their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other. Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough food, air, and light to grow strong and produce plenty of pods.
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why should I leave fallen cocoa leaves on the ground instead of clearing my farm clean?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi kookoo baai ni egbee shi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni majie ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni he tse lɛ?

english: Fallen leaves form a natural carpet that keeps the soil cool and moist during dry periods. As the leaves rot, they turn into rich organic fertilizer that feeds the cocoa tree's roots.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli kapɛti ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Beni baai lɛ miifite lɛ Amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli yɛ cacao tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: What causes the pods on my cocoa trees to turn black and rot before they are ready to pick?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, damp conditions. Clearing weeds and trimming overgrown branches lets fresh air and sunlight into the farm, which dries out the trees and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ afolɔ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do the stems of some of my cocoa trees look swollen and the leaves turn red or yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei komɛi ashishifãi lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfuu ni amɛbaai lɛ feɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Swollen stems and discolored leaves are signs of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. Because there is no cure, infected trees must be removed so the disease does not spread through the roots to healthy trees.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni efuu kɛ baai ni etsake amɛhe lɛ ji cocoa bud virus hela, ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Ejaakɛ tsamɔ ko bɛ. Esa akɛ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ koni hela lɛ akatsɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow even when it is raining heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during heavy rain usually mean the ground is waterlogged, making it hard for the roots to breathe. Heavy rain can also wash away essential nutrients from the topsoil, leaving the tree hungry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Ehaa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. hɔmɔ yeɔ tso lɛ

english: Why do I need to cut healthy-looking branches off my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary or weak branches that waste the tree's energy. By trimming them, you direct nutrients straight to the main branches that bear fruit, resulting in bigger and healthier pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa loo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni haa tso lɛ he waaa lɛ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa niji titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do so many small flowers drop off my cocoa tree without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Amɛteŋ mɛi enyiɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to transfer pollen from flower to flower. If there are few insects, or if the tree is stressed by drought or poor soil, the unpollinated flowers simply drop off.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ midges koni amɛkɛ pollen ajɛ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli. Kɛji kooloi bibii fioo pɛ yɔɔ loo tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ hɔmɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii mli lɛ Fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ baagbee shi.

english: How do I know when a cocoa pod is fully ripe and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A ripe pod changes color completely, usually turning from green to bright yellow, or from red to orange. Harvesting pods when fully yellow ensures the beans inside have reached peak size and sugar content.
ga: Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ baatsake ehiɛ su kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. aloo kɛjɛ etsuru nɔ kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ mli Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ beni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ kwraa lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ ni fe fɛɛ he ni sugar ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ emuu.

english: Covering the fresh beans causes them to ferment, which kills the germ inside the bean and develops the rich chocolate flavor and dark brown color buyers look for. Drying unfermented beans leaves them bitter and low quality.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii heei ha nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni gbeɔ helai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ Enɛ haa enáa tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ waa kɛ su ni mli kwɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa ni afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmei lɛ mli ŋɔɔ ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and shriveling up on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and shady conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning extra branches lets sunshine and air into the farm to stop the moisture that allows the fungus to grow.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei krokomɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ daa lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key nutrient for leaf growth. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient deep into the soil where roots cannot reach, showing that the crop needs fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii nɛɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do small caterpillars hide inside the funnel of my maize plants and eat the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei amli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ?

english: Those are Fall Armyworms. They lay their eggs on young maize leaves because the center of the plant provides shelter and fresh food. Catching them early with recommended sprays or neem mixture prevents them from destroying the crop's growing point.
ga: Amɛji Fall Asraafoi. Amɛwoɔ amɛwui lɛ yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ ejaakɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ haa amɛnáa wɔɔhe kɛ niyenii hee. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Kɛ akɛ neem tsofa loo tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkafite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess water sits in the ground without proper drainage, it drowns the roots and encourages mold, causing the cassava to soften and rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ efo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni nu lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni ewo ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egboɔ.

english: What makes my yam leaves develop dark brown spots and dry up early before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya dani akpaa?

english: This is a disease called leaf spot or anthracnose, which spreads during warm, rainy weather. It weakens the leaves so they cannot feed the yam tuber underground, resulting in smaller yams at harvest.
ga: Atsɛɔ hela nɛɛ akɛ baa mli ŋmɔtɔ loo anthracnose. Egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii baa kɛji akpa.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. If the plant gets too hot or dries out completely, it protects itself by shedding flowers instead of making fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛji tso lɛ mli edɔ fe nine loo egbi kwraa Tso lɛ buɔ ehe he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yɛ yibiiwoo najiaŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Giving pepper plants proper spacing allows each plant to get enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Good spacing also keeps air moving between plants so wet leaf diseases do not build up.
ga: Pepper tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ hu haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ. Koni baa ni efɔ lɛ he hela akabua ehe naa

english: How do I know it is safe to start planting after the first rain of the year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mabɔi dumɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until you get steady rains for about two weeks rather than planting after the very first rain. The first rain often tricks seeds into sprouting, but if dry weather returns, the young seedlings will wither and die.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be aaafee otsii enyɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ lakaa dumɔwui koni amɛkwɛ̃. Shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso bibioo lɛ baagbo ni ebaagbo.

english: Why does my farm soil get extremely hard and crack open during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbɛ eshwa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Soil cracks and turns hard when it lacks organic matter like dead leaves or decomposed manure. Adding manure or leaving crop leaves on top of the soil keeps the ground cool, retains moisture, and stops it from baking under the sun.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbalaa ni ewaa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ baai ni egboi loo ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo ashi tsei ahe baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni otsi hulutsoo naa

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen nutrients or getting too much water in flooded soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or improving soil drainage helps the leaves turn green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ nitrogen niyenii loo enine eshɛ nu babaoo nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I use dried animal manure on my farm instead of buying chemical fertilizer?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi atsu nii yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahemɔ najiaŋ?

english: Yes, well-rotted animal manure improves the soil structure and slowly feeds your crops essential nutrients. Mixing composted manure into the soil before planting keeps crops healthy and reduces fertilizer costs.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ni fiofio lɛ Ehaa otsei lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani odu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nyɔmɔwoo baa shi.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that shade the cocoa seedlings and keep the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak plants and a smaller harvest compared to properly spaced crops.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii baa kɛ akɛto tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know the best time to sow my seeds after the major rainy season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee sɛɛ?

english: Wait until rain has soaked deep into the soil at least two or three times consistently. This ensures the ground retains enough moisture for seeds to germinate without drying out in a short dry spell.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛ hoo lɛ shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Why do my tomato plant flowers fall off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high, when the plant lacks enough water, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Regular watering during hot weather helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ tsei ahe loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks or stakes for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso loo tso ama shi koni mi-sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in the sunlight to produce energy for the tubers under the ground. Staking holds the leaves up off the wet soil, preventing rot and disease.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni amɛná hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ amɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ akabote shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ kɛ helai anaa

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to steal water and food from the soil faster than cultivated crops can. Clearing weeds early stops them from overpowering your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye onibii titrii lɛ anɔ kunim.

english: Cassava tubers rot when water sits in the soil without draining away, creating excessive moisture that encourages fungal decay. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water run off.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ejeee kpo. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni woɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why are there small holes in my crop leaves and caterpillars eating the center of the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii komɛi yɛ ni yeɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Small holes and eaten plant centers indicate pest caterpillars, such as the fall armyworm. Checking crops early and applying recommended neem-based sprays or bio-pesticides protects your yield.
ga: Bu bibii kɛ hei ni tsei ni ayeɔ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworm. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Kɛ neem sprays loo bio-insecticides ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller when I plant them on top of a hill compared to the valley below?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kɛ́ midu yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ kɛ akɛto jɔɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: When it rains, water washes the rich topsoil and fertilizers down from the hill to the bottom land. Crops on hills suffer because the soil loses water quickly and lacks nutrients, so adding compost or building soil ridges across the slope helps retain soil moisture and plant food.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, nu lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fiteɔ oya ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo afee shikpɔŋ ŋmeii yɛ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsei aniyenii akahi shi.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away my seeds whenever I plant on sloped ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ dumɔwui kɛyaa be fɛɛ be ni abaadu amɛ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Rainwater flows faster down sloped land, creating small streams that carry away seeds and topsoil. Planting your rows across the slope rather than up and down creates natural barriers that slow the water down and hold seeds in place.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya yɛ hei ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ. ni ekɛ faa bibioo ko ni shwieɔ dumɔwui kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ lɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ moŋ fe ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni haa nu lɛ hoɔ fioo ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi lɛ baa.

english: Can I safely grow food crops on land that was previously used for small-scale mining?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ shika tsuru bibii amli lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe?

english: Mining turns up deep, infertile subsoil and can leave behind rocks or chemical residues that stunt plant growth. Before planting food, the land needs heavy organic matter like manure and compost mixed in, or deep-rooted cover crops to rebuild healthy soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ mli kwɔ ni ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. ni ebaanyɛ eshi tɛi loo tsofai ni tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. dani aduɔ niyenii Shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nibii babaoo ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutu mli loo tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ koni ekɛma shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ ni ewo lɛ hewalɛ.

english: I noticed my land doesn't produce as much maize as it used to years ago. Why is the soil behaving differently now?
ga: Miyɔse akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo ŋmãa babaoo tamɔ afii komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ. Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ enii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ amrɔ nɛɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same land every season drains the soil of specific nutrients without giving them time to recover. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas helps put nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: If I completely clear and burn all the trees and grass off my land before planting, will my crops grow better?
ga: Kɛji mijie tsei kɛ jwɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mishã amɛ dani midu Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaya hiɛ?

english: Clearing and burning leaves soil exposed to intense sun and heavy rain, which bakes the ground hard and destroys natural plant food. Leaving some organic matter or shade protects moisture and keeps the soil fertile for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛ la ni ashãa lɛ haa hulu la ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ais ni efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii. Kɛ́ oshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo hulutsoo be lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔtɔ he, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Will covering the soil around my plant roots with dried grass or leaves help or hurt my crops?
ga: Ani jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua loo ebaaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Covering the soil with dried leaves or straw, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool and traps moisture during hot days. It also stops weeds from growing and turns into rich plant food as it decays.
ga: Atsɛɔ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi hu anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ebafeɔ tsei aniyenii ni jara wa beni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves burn and turn brown when I remove the tall trees around my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji ni bɔle miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to strong, direct sunlight and hot winds. Tall shade trees act as natural umbrellas that cool the air and protect young cocoa leaves from scorching while they are developing.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe koni amɛkashã be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and woody instead of swelling big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei moŋ fe ni amɛaafee wuji ni amɛfuu lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, uncompacted soil to expand. If the ground is too hard, packed down, or heavily shaded, the plant puts its energy into growing tall stems and leaves instead of filling out tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni ehiɛɛɛ shi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛmaa tsei kɛ baai ni kɛlɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ yitso lɛ baafata he lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my vegetable plants curling up during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Vegetable leaves curl during intense heat to reduce the amount of surface area exposed to the sun, which stops them from losing water too fast. It is a natural protection response, but frequent curling means the plants need shade or more water.
ga: Aduawai baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu lɛ akafite oya tsɔ. Eji adebɔɔ mli hetoo ni buɔ mɔ he. Shi ŋmɔlɔ ni afeɔ shii abɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔlɔ loo nu babaoo.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts alongside my main crops make the soil better?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts have friendly bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This provides free fertilizer for neighboring plants and improves future crop yields.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ helai ni haa mɔ he feɔ naanyo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aná ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko, ni ebaaha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ.

english: If I have a piece of land that is completely clear with no trees, what is the best crop for me to plant there first?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ shikpɔŋ ni agbele naa ni tsei bɛ lɛ Mɛɛ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ madu yɛ jɛmɛ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Clear land with direct sunlight is ideal for light-loving crops like maize, cassava, or cowpeas. These crops thrive without shade and help you quickly establish a productive farm on open land.
ga: Hulu la ni agbele, ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei ni sumɔɔ la tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji hulutsoo bɛ. ni ehaa onyɛɔ ofeɔ ŋmɔ ni woɔ yibii oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is good enough for planting groundnuts without sending it to a laboratory?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii adumɔ ni mikɛmajeee laboratori?

english: Groundnuts need soft, loose, sandy soil that crumbles easily in your hand. If the soil is too hard or clay-heavy, the flower pegs cannot push into the ground to form pods.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli edɔ, ni ŋã yɔɔ mli ni fãa oya yɛ nine mli lɛ he miihia ŋmei. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ Flower pegs lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni efee pods.

english: What is the difference between the local seeds I save from my harvest and the improved seed varieties sold in agricultural shops?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni asaa amɛhe ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ okwaayeli shwapoi amli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Local seeds are saved from past crops and are well-known to you, but improved seeds are specially bred by scientists to yield more food, resist local diseases, and mature faster.
ga: Ahereɔ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ tsutsu ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni ole amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, je mi si kpali maa wo dumɔwui nɛ a pee lɛ saminya konɛ a ná niye ní fuu. helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya

english: How do I know which cassava variety I should plant if I want to make good quality fufu?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmãa henɔ ni esa akɛ madu kɛji miitao ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cassava varieties differ in their starch and water content. Soft, high-starch varieties like 'Amankwa' or 'Bankye Hemaa' yield smooth, poundable fufu, whereas drier varieties are better suited for processing into gari.
ga: Cassava henɔi lɛ yɛ starch kɛ nu falɛ srɔtoi. Starch henɔi ni fa babaoo tamɔ ‘Amankwa’ loo ‘Bankye Hemaa’ woɔ yibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ be mli ni srɔtoi ni egbi lɛ sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha nitsumɔ kɛyaa Gari mli lɛ.

english: How do I know it is the right time to start planting my crops after the early rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ?

english: Do not plant after the very first rain because the soil may dry out again. Wait until you get two or three heavy rains and the soil stays moist a few inches below the surface.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ agbi ekoŋŋ. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo inchi fioo komɛi yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Which fast-growing garden crops can I plant if I need quick harvests to make soup for my family?
ga: Mɛɛ abɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ madu kɛji akɛ ehe miihia ni akpa oya koni mikɛfee shwiili maha miweku lɛ?

english: Leafy green vegetables like Gboma, Kontomire (cocoyam leaves), and Okra grow very fast and can be harvested within a few weeks to two months after planting.
ga: Tsofai ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ Gboma, Kontomire (koko baa) kɛ okra daa oya waa ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ otsii fioo kɛyashi nyɔji enyɔ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is lacking key nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are drowning because there is too much standing water in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ miiho yɛ nu ni damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli babaoo lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very big with plenty of leaves but fail to produce any flowers or fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi enyɛɛɛ ewo fɔfɔi loo aduawai lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they put all their energy into growing leaves instead of flowering. They need balanced nutrients, including phosphorus, to produce flowers and fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Niyenii ni ja he miihia amɛ. ni fɔsfɔs fata he koni akɛfee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai

english: Why does my sweet corn taste tasteless or tough when I harvest and cook it early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet corn lɛ mli ŋɔɔ loo ewaa kɛji mikpa ni mihoo oya lɛ?

english: Crops need time to build up sugars and starches as they ripen. If harvested too early, the grains contain mostly water and have not developed their sweet flavor and soft texture.
ga: Tsei he miihia be koni amɛkɛfee sugar kɛ starch kɛji amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akpa mra tsɔ Nu yɛ ŋmaa mli babaoo. ni ebɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo.

english: How do I know that my yam tubers are mature and fully ready to be dug up from the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up, showing that the plant has stopped growing and transferred all its stored food into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni ekɛto lɛ fɛɛ etee ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: If water is too dirty or salty for me to drink, is it still safe to give to my vegetable crops?
ga: Kɛji nu lɛ mli ewo muji loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli tsɔ ni minuuu Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe lolo akɛ maha mi-vegetable tsei lɛ?

english: No, water that is unsafe for humans to drink can also harm your crops. Dirty or highly salty water can carry diseases that infect plants, ruin the soil, and cause crops to stunt or die.
ga: Dabi, nu ni esaaa akɛ adesai baanu lɛ baanyɛ aye oŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui. Nu ni mli ewo muji loo nu ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmei babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ helai ni tsɛŋeɔ tsei, ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ, ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo egbeɔ amɛ.

english: Will using wastewater from gutters or drains harm my cabbage farm?
ga: Ani nu fɔŋ ni jɛɔ nu tsɔji loo nu tsɔji amli lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaye mi-cabbage ŋmɔ lɛ awui?

english: Yes, gutter water often contains harsh chemicals, oils, and harmful bacteria. This can destroy beneficial soil life, damage crop roots, and make your produce dangerous for people to eat.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni mli wa, fɔ, kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ nubu mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ akpata shikpɔŋ nɔ wala ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ hiɛ, efite tsei ashishifãi, ni eha onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara kɛha gbɔmɛi ni baaye.

english: Can watering my crops with standing, stagnant pond water cause them to rot?
ga: Ani nu ni damɔ shi, nubu mli nu ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ agbo?

english: Yes, stagnant water often breeds harmful fungi and bacteria. Watering your crops with it can introduce diseases like root rot, causing the plants to wilt and die from the bottom up.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, bei pii lɛ, nu ni damɔ shi lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ helai tamɔ shishifãi ni fiteɔ aba, ni eha tsei lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi kɛjɛ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: Can I use water directly from a underground borehole to irrigate my tomato plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi bu ko mli lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛfɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ nu?

english: Yes, underground water is generally good for crops, but if it has a high salt or mineral content, those salts can build up in the soil over time and slow down your tomatoes' growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi nu hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi kɛji akɛ ŋmei loo minerals babaoo yɛ Nakai ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ abua shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli ni eha tomato lɛ akwɛ̃ blɛoo.

english: Does tap water treated with chlorine cause any problems for my young seedlings?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛ chlorine ewo mli lɛ kɛ naagbai baaba mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ?

english: Treated tap water is safe, but high levels of fresh chlorine can sometimes stress delicate young seedlings. Letting the water sit in an open container for a day before watering allows the chlorine gas to escape.
ga: Nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ pɔmpi mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe. Shi bei komɛi lɛ, klorin hee ni fa babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ aná haomɔ. Kɛ́ oha nu lɛ hi tsɛnsi ko ni agbele naa mli gbi kome dani okɛ nu awo mli lɛ, ebaaha chlorine gas lɛ ajie.

english: Is rainwater better for my maize plants than water pumped from a shallow well?
ga: Ani nugbɔ nu ni mikɛhaa mi-abele tsei lɛ hi fe nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ nu bu ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli lɛ mli?

english: Rainwater is usually better because it is naturally free of heavy minerals and salts, and it contains dissolved nitrogen from the air that helps maize leaves turn dark green and grow quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ nu hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, shika tsuru kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii bɛ mli. Ni nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ hu yɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Why does the surface of my soil form a hard white layer after I water my cassava regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ yɛŋ ni wa beni mikɛ ŋmei shwieɔ nɔ daa lɛ?

english: A white crust on top of the soil usually means your water source contains dissolved salts. When the water evaporates in the sun, the salt stays behind, which can harden the soil and prevent roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ onu jɛɛhe lɛ eyɛ ŋmeii ni egbɛ eshwa. Kɛ́ nu tsɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ, Nu lɛ baahi shi. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awa ni eha shishifãi lɛ akamu.

english: Why do my pepper leaves turn yellow and drop off after I water them from the local stream?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi beni mikɛ nu shwieɔ amɛnɔ kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli faa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Streams near farming areas can carry chemical runoff or fungal spores from fields further up. When you apply this polluted water, it can attack root systems and cause leaves to turn yellow and drop.
ga: Faji ni bɛŋkɛ okwaayeli hei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ tsofai ni hoɔ loo ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Kɛ okɛ nu ni mli ewo muji nɛɛ tsu nii Ebaanyɛ etutua shishifãi lɛ. ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: How can I tell if the water I am using is making my crops sick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miihe hela?

english: If your plants show burnt leaf edges, stunted growth, sudden wilting despite wet soil, or dark rotted roots, bad water quality or waterborne fungi are likely the cause.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ baai lɛ ashã lɛ, ehiɛ edɔ waa Trukaa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ loo edɔ, shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, nu lɛ ehiii Loo ŋmei ni nu kɛbaa lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: Why do my crops droop in the hot afternoon sun even when I gave them water in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu leebi moŋ?

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink it up. Temporary drooping is a normal protective behavior to reduce water loss, and plants usually recover by evening.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Be kukuoo mli ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji subaŋ ni yaa nɔ daa, ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛba nu ni fiteɔ lɛ shi. Ni bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ he baajɔ amɛ kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why should I plant shade trees among my main cocoa crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kookoo tso titri lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Shade trees protect your young crops from harsh sunlight, cool down the farm during hot seasons, and retain soil moisture so the crops do not dry out.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ onibii bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i yɛ hulutsoo be mli nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni ŋmɔshi nibii akagbi

english: What happens if I harvest my cocoa pods too early before they mature?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ mra tsɔ, dani amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Harvesting immature pods results in small, flat beans that do not ferment properly, leading to low crop quality and lower prices from buyers.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii ni edako lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nyɛɛɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baa shi, ni jara hu baa shi kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ adɛŋ.

english: How do changing rain and sun patterns affect when I should pick my crops?
ga: Te tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaná be ni esa akɛ mahala ŋmɔshinii lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Unpredictable weather changes how fast crops ripen and dry. Adjusting your harvest time to match dry spells prevents your harvested beans from rotting or getting moldy.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii shwereɔ oya ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ atsake ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ koni ekɛ hulutsoo be lɛ akpã gbee lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmaa ni akpa lɛ naa koni ekafite loo ekafee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How do extra trees on my land help keep the soil healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei babaoo ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Trees drop leaves that turn into rich natural manure as they decay, and their roots hold the soil together so heavy rains do not wash away nutrients.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ, ni amɛbafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa beni amɛfiteɔ lɛ. ni amɛshishifãi lɛ fiɔ sũ lɛ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieee niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know when my cocoa pods are truly ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-kokoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ he diɛŋtsɛ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Ready pods completely change color—usually turning bright yellow or orange—and make a hollow sound when you tap them gently.
ga: Pods ni asaa he lɛ tsakeɔ ehiɛ su kwraa—bei pii lɛ, eji ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse—ni efeɔ gbee ni mli ewo ŋmɔlɔ kɛji otswa nɔ fioo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young plants turning brown and drying up in the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Direct heat and sunshine burn young leaves faster than their roots can draw water from the soil, causing heat stress that weakens the plant.
ga: Dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ baa.

english: Does leaving big trees on my farm take away food and water from my cocoa crops?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ni mashi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baajie niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli?

english: While big trees use some water, they protect your crops from heat and draw deep nutrients up to the topsoil, helping your main crop live longer.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei wuji kɛ nu fioo tsuɔ nii moŋ Shi ebuɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni egbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa otsei titrii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do some cocoa farms produce good yields for many years while others die quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji komɛi woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai afii babaoo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi gboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Farms protected by shade trees and well-timed harvests suffer less environmental stress, keeping the soil and crops healthy over many decades.
ga: Okwaafoi ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo buɔ he kɛ ŋmaa ni akpaa yɛ be naa lɛ kɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔ fioo pɛ kpeɔ. Shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ

english: Why should I avoid drying my harvested cocoa beans during sudden wet weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ mi-kokoo yibii ni mikpa lɛ ni mikɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be baa trukaa lɛ he?

english: Drying beans in wet or humid conditions creates mold and black spots, which ruins the beans and makes them unmarketable.
ga: Beans ni agbiɔ yɛ shihilɛ ni mli efɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji aba. Enɛ fiteɔ kɔfe yibii lɛ ni ehaa anyɛɛɛ ahɔ̃ɔ amɛ.

english: Can planting trees on my farm help prevent crop diseases?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai anaa?

english: Yes, shade trees create a cooler environment that reduces heat stress on crops, making them stronger and better able to fight off diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni haa dɔlɛ ni baa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ he waa ni enyɛɔ ewuɔ eshiɔ helai jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing starting from the tip and moving down the center of lower maize leaves is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen is a plant food that helps leaves stay green and make food; when the soil lacks it, the plant moves what little it has to the upper new leaves.
ga: Abɛi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ashishigbɛ kɛyashi amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwie shi lɛ, tsei lɛ kɛ nɔ fioo ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ yaa baai heei anɔ.

english: Why do people say that planting groundnuts or beans on my field makes the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen directly from the air and store it in the soil. When the groundnuts are harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth to feed the next crop, acting like natural fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why do my crops grow slow and weak when weeds are nearby, even if I put fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni ebɛ hewalɛ beni jwɛi bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ fɔmɔ woɔ mli moŋ

english: Weeds are stronger competitors than young crops. They quickly steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer you give to the field before your crop's roots can reach them, starving your plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni he wa fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛhaa oŋmɔji lɛ oya dani tsei shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otsei lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh, direct sunlight and hot winds. High shade trees act like umbrellas and windshields, keeping the air cool and moist around the young cocoa while their roots establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli glasei. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Kookoo tso lɛ ji gbekɛ yɛ be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ ema shi lɛ.

english: Why does putting dry grass or dry leaves around the base of my pepper plants help them stay alive in the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ebɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that blocks the hot sun from evaporating soil water. It keeps the ground moist longer and keeps the roots cool so the plant doesn't wilt.
ga: Mulching ni egbi (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni buɔ hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akagbo.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground if rain falls heavily right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa dani akpa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Excess water in heavy rain fills all the air spaces in the soil. Cassava roots need air to breathe, and when they are soaked in waterlogged soil for too long, fungi and bacteria quickly multiply and rot the tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. ni kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Mold kɛ bacteria babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ oya.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming any tomatoes during very hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ shwie fɔfɔi ni ewooo tomato yɛ otsi kome ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato pollen becomes dry and sterile, preventing the flowers from being fertilized. The plant senses it cannot make healthy seeds, so it sheds the flowers to save energy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato pollen lɛ mli egbi ni ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. Etsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkawo fɔ Tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ enyɛɛɛ ewo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, afoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni akɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce smaller bunches when many young shoots grow around the main trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ feɔ kui bibii bibii beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: All the young suckers attached to the main plantain trunk share the same food and water source. When too many suckers grow at once, they draw energy away from the mother plant, leaving less food to build a big fruit bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ tso titri lɛ he lɛ yɛ niyenii kɛ nu jɛɛhe kome. Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ shikome lɛ Ebaajie hewalɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa niyenii fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ koni ekɛfee aduawai akui wuji.

english: This pest is likely the Fall Armyworm, which prefers hiding inside the central leaf funnel (the whorl) where the tissue is softest and newest. They stay hidden inside where rain and direct sun cannot reach them.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworm, ni sumɔɔ ni ekɛ ehe awo baai lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii (rings) amli yɛ he ni fãji lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ hei ni nugbɔ kɛ hulu la nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up, shrinking, and turning rough?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso, amɛmiigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck the sap out of leaves and spread plant viruses. The damaged leaves fold up because their growth cells are disrupted by the feeding insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni shwieɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli Baai ni efite lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe ejaakɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ tsiɔ wala yibii lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dropping off when the sun gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight yet. Without shade crops like plantain or shade trees to protect them, high heat burns their leaves and dries out the soil quickly.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni buɔ amɛhe lɛ bɛ lɛ, Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baashã baai lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya.

english: Why do my maize stalks stay short and yellow instead of growing tall and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ kukuji ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves and short stalks usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for green leaf growth. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps them green up and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ tsei kukuji tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ adara. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: In extreme heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up. As long as the soil stays moist, the leaves will usually bounce back once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Be abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛshwieɔ shi kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is often caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant varieties is the best way to prevent this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa ji tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off the plant before any peppers start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi edaa lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is stressed, which happens if the soil is too dry, too wet, or if the weather is extremely hot during the flowering stage.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Enɛ baa mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ, edɔ tsɔ, loo kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: Why should I wait for the main rains to settle before planting my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ?

english: If you plant after just one early rain, the soil might dry out completely before the next rain comes, causing the young seeds to dry up and die before establishing strong roots.
ga: Kɛji odu yɛ leebi nugbɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi kwraa dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce smaller harvests if they are just growing next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water, effectively stealing the food and space your main crops need to grow big fruits or grains.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ nu mli, ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ he ni oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ he hiaa koni ekɛdu aduawai loo ŋmaa wuji lɛ.

english: Why does my yield get smaller every year when I plant maize on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every year drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground over time.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are fully ready to be harvested under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-peanuts lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the lower leaves of the plant start turning yellow and dry, and the inside of a freshly pulled pod shell turns dark brown with visible vein lines.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii efee klalo beni tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Ni ŋmɔtɔ ni ajie ehee lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ fãji ni anaa.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they crowd each other out, fighting for sunlight and soil nutrients, which results in thin, weak plants and smaller overall yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa koni amɛye hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ fɛɛ mli baa.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crop turn yellow when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive rainfall washes away vital nutrients like nitrogen from the topsoil and floods the roots, preventing the maize plant from breathing and absorbing food properly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni eŋɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with bushy leaves but gives me small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai bibii shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has high nitrogen content, cassava puts most of its energy into growing upper branches and leaves instead of storing energy in its underground roots.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa babaoo lɛ, Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ babaoo woɔ ŋwɛi niji kɛ baai lɛ anɔ shweremɔ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Why do my crops yield better when I plant cowpeas on the farm land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani midu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that trap natural nitrogen from the air into the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants look like small holes were shot through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ tamɔ buji bibii lɛ? Atswa nakai tu kɛtsɔ mli?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by fall armyworm caterpillars feeding on the inner leaf funnel, which can stunt crop growth if left untreated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbee shi ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli tsũi lɛ amli buji baa. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei adalɛ naa kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up into small wrinkled shapes instead of expanding flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmeii bibii lɛ? yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa flat

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaf underside, or by a virus carried by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ hiɛɔ lɛ anɔ

english: Why do my cashew trees drop so many flowers before any nuts start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Cashew flowers drop prematurely when attacked by sap-sucking insects like thrips, or when dry weather and low soil moisture stress the tree during flowering.
ga: Cashew fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips lɛ tutua amɛ, loo kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ fioo lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and wither when I clear away all the big trees on the plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that lose water rapidly in direct heat; shade trees shield them from sunburn and keep the air around them humid.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nu fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Tsei haa hulutsoo, amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli fũuɔ.

english: Black spots on tomato bottoms, called blossom-end rot, happen when soil water levels fluctuate unevenly, preventing the plant from taking up calcium.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ diŋ yɛ tomato tsei anɔ Atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Ehaa tsei lɛ náaa calcium

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over in light winds once the fruit bunch grows large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ? Be ni aduawai akuu lɛ daa?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and tiny soil pests called nematodes often eat away the root base, weakening the plant's grip in the soil under heavy fruit loads.
ga: Plantain lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii Bei pii lɛ Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes lɛ yeɔ shishifãi lɛ. Ehaa tsei ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baa shi kɛ́ aduawai babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my yam mounds early in the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Atomɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni ato kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Early weeding prevents wild weeds from stealing the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients that young yam sprouts need to establish strong vines and large tubers.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Etsiɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni sweet potato tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ wain tsei ni wa kɛ bulbs wuji lɛ.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for starting a new crop field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmɔ hee shishijee?

english: Good land generally has dark, loose topsoil that holds moisture well without becoming swampy, receives plenty of sunlight, and is reasonably flat so topsoil does not wash away easily during heavy rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni hiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ ni efeee nubu. Na hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieee shi mlɛo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to clear bushes and loosen hard soil before I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ amli ni mafolɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Clearing removes weeds that steal nutrients and sunlight, while loosening hard soil makes it easier for young plant roots to spread, absorb water, and breathe.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ, ebaajie jwɛi lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa, amɛmɔɔ nu, ni amɛmuɔ mlɛo.

english: Why is it better to raise delicate seeds in a nursery bed before moving them to my big farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui ni waaa yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani mikɛ amɛ aya miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A nursery allows you to protect fragile young seedlings from harsh weather, pests, and heavy rains until they grow strong enough to survive transplanting into the main field.
ga: He ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ dumɔwui bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu amɛ kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crops very close to one another in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for space, soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, leading to weak plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná he ko. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ kɛ amɛhe feɔ ekome. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko baa.

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting too much sun during the hot season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiye hulu babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: When crops suffer from excessive heat stress, their leaves will curl up, look wilted or limpy during the afternoon, and start turning brown or dry at the edges.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii na dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni fe nine lɛ, baai lɛ baabɔle amɛhe. Etamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ loo egbɔjɔ yɛ shwane mli. ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ yɛ eshishigbɛ

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my young crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mawo tsei bibii lɛ nu?

english: Watering early in the morning or late in the evening is best because the cooler air allows water to sink deep into the roots rather than evaporating quickly under the hot midday sun.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, e pueɔ oya ngɛ hulu nɛ mi tsoɔ ɔ sisi.

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal the groundwater, fertilizer, and sunlight intended for your crops, effectively starving your main plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii titri lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my soil has lost its nutrients and needs fertilizer or manure?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ miiho ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Weak soil usually causes crop leaves to turn pale yellow instead of dark green, makes plants stay small and stunted, and leads to smaller harvests than previous years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ haa tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa. ni ekɛ kpamɔ bibioo ko ba fe afii ni eho lɛ.

english: Why should I change the type of crop I plant on the same land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ daa afi lɛ?

english: Alternating different crops keeps the soil rich because different plants use and return different nutrients, and it breaks the cycle of pests and diseases that target a specific crop.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni aduɔ Gbɛjianɔtoo yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, esoro bɔ ni tso henɔ fɛɛ tso tsuɔ nii ehaa kɛ bɔ ni ekɛ niyenii haa lɛ. Ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ lɛ amli.

english: What causes small holes to appear on my crop leaves, and how does it affect the plant?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ mi tso lɛ baai anɔ Ni te enaa tsei anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Holes are usually caused by insects or caterpillars eating the leaves, which weakens the plant because leaves act as factories that catch sunlight to create food for growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ejaakɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nitsumɔhe ko ni heɔ hulu la koni ekɛfee niyenii kɛha dalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil. They temporarily wilt to protect themselves from heat, but usually recover by evening once the sun cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaasumɔ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ he be kukuoo ko. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ beni hulu lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow much faster after natural rain falls compared to when I water them by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya yɛ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto nu ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ lɛ he

english: Rainwater naturally contains dissolved nitrogen from the atmosphere, which acts like a natural booster for leaf growth. Rain also washes dust off leaves, allowing crops to absorb sunlight better.
ga: Nitrogen ni egbɛ eshwa kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ nugbɔ nu mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni haa baai lɛ daraa Nugbɔ lɛ hu hoɔ sũ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛheɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or lack of pollination. Keeping adequate shade and soil moisture helps flowers stay attached and form pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo pollination ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni sa kɛ sũ mli nu ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Yellow lower leaves mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen. The plant naturally steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves and sends it up to nourish the new growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛtsuɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots growing small and crooked instead of thick and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe shi moŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soft, loose soil to expand easily. When the soil is hard or compacted, the roots struggle to push through the dirt, resulting in small and misshapen tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa oya. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo ebɔle ehe lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa yitso bibioo ni ehiii lɛ baa.

english: Can pouring too much water on my vegetable bed cause the plants to die?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛwoɔ aduawai aŋmɔ lɛ mli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ agbe tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, too much water fills up all the tiny air pockets in the soil, preventing the roots from breathing. Drowned roots begin to rot, causing the plant leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu babaoo yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Shishifãi ni ebote nu shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ, ni no haa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce plenty of green leaves but no peppers when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi pepper bɛ mli be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Excessive heat damages pepper pollen, causing the flowers to fall off before fruit can form. The plant focuses on surviving the heat by growing leaves until cooler conditions return.
ga: Dɔlɛ babaoo baafite ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo. Tsei kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa bɔ ni amɛbaafee amɛhi shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil food. They stretch upward to fight for light, leaving very little energy to produce big fruits or seeds.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpã amɛhe koni amɛye la lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ fioo pɛ ahi shi koni akɛwo aduawai loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: Why does removing side shoots from my tomato plant make the remaining tomatoes bigger?
