ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mijie sɛɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa tomato ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ agbo lɛ?

english: Side shoots steal energy and nutrients from the main stem. By cutting them off, you force the plant to direct all its food straight into growing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ juɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ efomɔ nɔ lɛ, onyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekwɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ lɛ nɔ kwraa koni ekwɛ yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does using an overhead sprinkler pipe system help my leafy vegetables stay healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni mi-aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Overhead watering acts like gentle rain, washing dirt off the leaves without splashing mud from the soil onto the plant. Mud on leaves often carries fungal diseases that ruin crops.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ yiteŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ. Efɔ muji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni ekɛ muji ni jɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieee tso lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, muji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii baa.

english: Why do I need to uproot my tomato plants after a few months instead of leaving them in the soil to keep growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie mi-tomato tsei lɛ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, moo ngmɛɛ lɛ ngɛ zugba a mi konɛ e ya nɔ nɛ e wa.

english: Vegetable crops like tomatoes have a limited productive lifecycle. After about three months, the plants become weak, produce smaller or fewer fruits, and become easy targets for pests and diseases. Uprooting them clears space for a fresh, healthy start.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ aduawai amli, tamɔ tomato lɛ, yɛ shihilɛ be ni fa fioo. Yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ, ni ebaawo yibii fioo loo ebaawo yibii fioo. ni ebatsɔ nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ ashɛ he oya. Shishifãi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa gbɛ kɛhaa shishijee hee ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know when it is time to pull out my old crops and prepare the field for a new batch?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii momoi lɛ kɛjɛ mli ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei?

english: When you notice your crops are no longer growing vigorously, their leaves are yellowing, or fruit production slows down significantly after two to three months, it means the crop cycle is finishing and it is time to uproot and replant.
ga: Beni oyɔse akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ hewalɛ dɔŋŋ Ebaai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Aloo aduawai ni anáa lɛ baa shi kwraa yɛ nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. No tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔ be lɛ efo ni be eshɛɛ ni abaajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Will uprooting my crops after just three months waste my money and effort?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni mafo yɛ nyɔji etɛ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baafee shika kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ fitemɔ?

english: No, it actually saves money in the long run. Keeping old plants in the field yields very little food while wasting water and soil nutrients, whereas planting a fresh crop restores high harvest yields and keeps your income steady.
ga: Dabi, ekɛ shika toɔ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Tsei momoi ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaha niyenii fioo ko pɛ aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, efiteɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni ooodu lɛ baaha oná yibii babaoo ni ebaaha shika ni onáa lɛ aya nɔ ahi shi.

english: Why is it harmful to leave old, dying crop stalks standing in my farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashi tsei ahe tsei ni egbɔ ni egboi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Old and dying crop stalks act as hiding spots and breeding grounds for insects, fungi, and diseases. Removing them completely prevents these pests from attacking your next batch of young plants.
ga: Tsoi ashishifãi ni egbɔ ni miigboi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni kooloi bibii, ŋmeii, kɛ helai fɔɔ amɛhe yɛ kɛ he ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ kwraa lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkatutua tsei bibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I switch to planting tomatoes after clearing my farm instead of planting the exact same crop again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake kɛya tomato dumɔ nɔ beni mijie miŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ekoŋŋ lɛ

english: Switching to a different crop, known as crop rotation, starves out soil pests that feed on the previous crop. Different crops also feed on different nutrients, giving the soil a chance to rest and balance itself.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni atsakeɔ lɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsakemɔ. Ebaaha hɔmɔ aye kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ ni tsutsu lɛ amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahenɔi srɔtoi hu yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ srɔtoi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa hegbɛ ni ekɛ ehe jɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ ehe woɔ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: What does it mean to plant 'clean seeds,' and why are they better than seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni ‘dumɔwui ni he tse’ ni aduɔ lɛ tsɔɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehi fe dumɔwui ni mikpa kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Clean seeds are certified seeds that are free from seed-borne diseases, weeds, and damage. Using clean seeds gives your crops a strong start with uniform growth and much higher disease resistance compared to saved seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni he tse ji dumɔwui ni ana he odaseyeli akɛ helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa, jwɛi, kɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni he tse ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa po ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe babaoo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahe.

english: How does planting a new crop type after clearing the land keep my soil healthy?
ga: Te tsei heei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee tɛŋŋ?

english: Different crops draw different nutrients from the soil. Rotating crops prevents the soil from being completely drained of specific plant nutrients and helps maintain overall soil fertility without over-relying on synthetic chemical fertilizers.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ srɔtoi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekafite tsei amli niyenii komɛi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ehe afɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ tsɔ.

english: Why is my farm taking longer than two or three months to fully fill up with healthy, leafy plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ heɔ be fe nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ dani eyi kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Slow growth and patchy fields usually happen due to poor seed quality, low soil nutrients, improper seed spacing, or dry weather. Ensuring good spacing, quality seeds, and proper watering helps the field fill out evenly and quickly.
ga: Dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo kɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa yɛ dumɔwui ni ehiii lɛ ahewɔ. Niyenii ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni esaaa loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ akwɛmɔ Kɛ nu ni sa baaye abua ni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi daa ni efee oya.

english: If my crops look weak and stunted after three months, should I try to fertilize them or start over?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ sɛɛ Ani esa akɛ maka ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli loo mabɔi ekoŋŋ?

english: If crops are weak and stunted after three months, their growing phase has passed, and fertilizing will not rescue them. It is best to uproot them, fix the soil, and start fresh with healthy new seeds.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ sɛɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ eho. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua tsei. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ obaajie shishifãi lɛ, otsake shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni okɛ dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aje shishi ekoŋŋ.

english: How does completely turning over the soil before planting new seeds help my next harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni matsɔ mli kwraa dani madu dumɔwui heei lɛ baaye abua mikpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Turning over the soil loosens it so young roots can spread easily to find food and water. It also buries weeds and exposes hidden soil pests to the heat of the sun, killing them before you plant.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa shishifãi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛna niyenii kɛ nu. Efuɔ jwɛi hu ni ekɛ sũ mli kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ nɔ. Ni ogbe amɛ dani odu.

english: Why do extension officers always tell me to plant plantains on the same land as my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi be fɛɛ be akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as a living umbrella, providing essential shade and keeping the soil moist so the cocoa seedlings can survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on growing corn usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the primary plant food responsible for healthy green leaves. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore their green color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni jɛɔ tsei amli ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛná amɛhe su kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Does cutting off the green leaves of my cassava plants help the tubers underground grow bigger?
ga: Ani mi yucca tso lɛ baai eŋɔli ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: No, removing healthy leaves actually reduces tuber size. A plant uses its leaves to trap sunlight and turn it into food, which is then stored in the tubers underground to make them grow.
ga: Dabi, baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tuber lɛ dalɛ aba shi diɛŋtsɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛ baai lɛ mɔmɔɔ hulu la ni amɛ tsakeɔ lɛ niyenii. Kɛkɛ lɛ, akɛ amɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why should I leave dead leaves and clear weeds on top of the soil around my crops instead of burning them away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi ni ajie yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ?

english: Leaving organic materials on top of the dirt, called mulching, keeps the ground cool, retains moisture during dry weeks, and eventually rots down into natural fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli Ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaafite ni ebatsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii.

english: Why are small worms destroying the middle leaves of my young corn plants during the early season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii fiteɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides in the center funnel of young maize plants to feed on tender leaves. If left untreated, they destroy the plant's ability to grow and produce healthy cobs.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Ebaakpata tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa lɛ hiɛ.

english: Is it helpful to burn my entire field to clear it before planting season begins?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ baaba akɛ mashã he ni miyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ koni mikɛjie jɛmɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ aje shishi?

english: While burning clears land quickly, it kills beneficial soil organisms, destroys natural organic matter, and leaves the topsoil exposed and damaged, leading to lower crop yields over time.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ haa jɛmɛ tseɔ oya. Shi ekpãtãa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ. ekpãtãa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahiɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ jeɔ kpo ni efiteɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which naturally grabs nitrogen from the air and feeds it back into the ground, restoring soil fertility for your next grain crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ Koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread chemical fertilizer on my farm right before a big rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ wulu ko baanɛ?

english: Heavy rainwater will wash the fertilizer away off the farm or push it too deep into the dirt where your plant roots cannot reach it, effectively wasting your input investment.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji amli loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. ni haa shika ni akɛwo mli lɛ fiteɔ yaka

english: Why do my crops yield less food when I squeeze seeds close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naaa niyenii babaoo beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ miibɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni amɛhi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too tightly together, their roots and leaves compete fiercely with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants with smaller yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei waa tsɔ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to spend time put tall wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be kɛma tsei kakadaji anɔ lɛ? yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Yam vines need to spread out in full sunlight high above the ground to generate energy for tuber growth. Lifting the leaves off the moist soil also prevents destructive fungal diseases from attacking the plant.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulb lɛ dalɛ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ hu tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ anaa koni amɛkatutua tso lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and brown when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Fast-growing shade plants like plantains act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young trees need to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa tsei bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Can I plant cassava or plantain inside my young cocoa farm without hurting the cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei loo plantain yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni miyeee kokoo tsei lɛ awui?

english: Yes, planting plantains with young cocoa helps by providing necessary shade. However, plant cassava slightly farther away so its roots do not compete with cocoa roots for soil water and food.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei dumɔwui bibii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɛtsɔ hɔɔŋ ni he hiaa ni ehaa lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, dumɔ ŋmei yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ fioo bɔni afee ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ kookoo shishifãi lɛ akashi akaŋ kɛha sũ mli nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the small flowers on my cocoa trees falling off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by dry weather, lacks nutrients, or lacks small insects like midges that pollinate them. Proper shade and soil moisture help flowers stay attached and form pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ. Shade ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Dropping leaves is a self-defense mechanism trees use to conserve water during dry weather. Placing dry bush mulch around the roots helps hold water in the soil so the tree loses fewer leaves.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni egbi wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ baai fioo pɛ fiteɔ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet and humid weather. Pruning thick leaves to let light in and clearing out infected pods stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ fɛ̃i, fɛ̃i shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Kpãa tsei ahe tsei lɛ ahe koni la abote mli ni ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to cut off the small extra shoots growing at the base of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: These extra shoots, called suckers or chupons, waste the tree's energy. Removing them forces the plant to send water and nutrients to the main trunk and flowering branches instead.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii loo chupons. Ebaaha tso lɛ hewalɛ afite. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ atsɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛya tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ niji ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ moŋ.

english: Why does trimming off heavy branches help my crop produce more fruit later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei niji ni tsii ni afoɔ lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii babaoo sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Trimming removes old or shaded branches, allowing sunlight and air to reach all parts of the tree. This reduces humidity, stops disease, and encourages fresh flower buds to grow.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwieɔ shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egbɔ loo ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i baa shi, etsiɔ helai anaa ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi heei hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How do I know if the soil in my farm is running low on nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa?

english: If your plant leaves turn pale green or yellow instead of dark green, or if the stem stays thin and weak, the soil usually lacks key plant nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ baai lɛ batsɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ loo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ egbɔjɔ lolo ni ebɛ hewalɛ Bei pii lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen.

english: Why do weeds stop my cocoa seedlings from growing even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi tsiɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal water, fertilizer, and light away from young crops. Keeping the base of your seedlings clear gives them full access to nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli. Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How many years after planting should I expect my cocoa trees to start giving me pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ kookoo tso lɛ baaje shishi ewo ŋmeii?

english: Modern improved cocoa varieties start producing pods within 2 to 3 years if cared for well, whereas older traditional cocoa varieties take around 4 to 5 years.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni kusum mli kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily in direct sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and preserves moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to endure direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe. Ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni eha hulutsoo be lɛ aya nɔ aahu kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why should I wait for the steady rainy season before sowing my maize seeds in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yaa nɔ daa dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds need continuous moisture to germinate and establish roots. Planting in dry or unpredictable soil can cause seeds to dry out and die before sprouting, while waiting for steady rains ensures consistent growth.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛkwɛ̃. Yɛ be mli ni amɛmɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main plantain tree. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to concentrate its energy on growing larger, healthier fruit bunches.
ga: Tsoi loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for leaf growth. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha sũ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts in the same farm help my maize crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, which naturally pull nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil. This enriches the soil with free nutrients that neighboring crops like maize can use to grow strong.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ niyenii ni he ehiaaa ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii kɛha dalɛ kpakpa.

english: Why do weeds in my farm make my crops stay small and produce poor yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, water, space, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to grow tall and produce big harvests.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la, nu, ŋwɛi, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: These worms are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on tender corn leaves. Inspecting plants early and applying neem leaf extract or targeted pest controls can stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni kɛ akɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa tso lɛ dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap out of young leaves, or by viral infections spread by these pests. Managing insects early prevents leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Mra be mli kooloi ahe nitsumɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ baai lɛ ahe fitemɔ naa.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water builds up around them because the soil cannot drain. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater flow away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu ni ekã shi ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they suffer from high heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like phosphorus. Maintaining steady soil moisture and soil nutrients prevents flower drop.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe baai lɛ anaa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen or getting too much water in the roots. Feeding the soil with manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant turn green and grow strong leaves again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛnáa baai ni wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop all their leaves during the dry season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves to save water when the weather gets dry. The plant goes to sleep above ground while keeping its roots safe underneath, and it will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi koni akɛbu nu he kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ. Tso lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaaha eshishifãi lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe yɛ eshishi. Ni ebaajie baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing into any fruits when the sun is too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When the day gets extremely hot, tomato plants get stressed and cannot process pollen properly. The flowers dry up and drop off to save energy until temperatures cool down slightly.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsu pollen lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ. Fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ fioo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stems very close to each other to get more yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots fight underground for water and food, while their leaves block sunlight from each other. Spacing them out gives each cassava plant enough space to build big tubers.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe lɛ. Gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ haa ŋmei tso fɛɛ ŋmei naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant beans or cowpeas together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have tiny root bags that trap good air from the soil and turn it into plant food. They share this natural food with neighboring crops like maize, making the soil richer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi bibii. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa efeɔ tsei aniyenii Amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ jaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and wrinkle like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny, invisible insects sucking juice from the underside of the leaf. Spraying mild soapy water or recommended neem oil helps clear these insects so new leaves grow flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni anaaa amɛ ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ loo neem fɔ ni ajieɔ yi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, baai heei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do fall armyworms attack my maize field mostly during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ babaoo yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ?

english: Armyworm moths prefer laying eggs during hot, dry weather because heavy rains usually wash their eggs off leaves. Dry periods allow young worms to hatch safely and feed on the green growing points of maize.
ga: Caterpillar ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛwo amɛwui lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe fɔ̃ɔ baa lɛ nɔ. Be ni nu hɔmɔ yɔɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How do I know if the soil is warm and wet enough for planting after the first rain?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: First rains are often 'false rains' that dry out fast. Squeeze a handful of soil from a palm-depth down; if it holds together into a soft ball without squeezing out water, the ground is ready for seed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji ‘amale nugbɔ’ ni gbɛ́ɔ oya, ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ fioo ko shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛyaa shishi. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ he ni efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ekɛ nu lɛ shwieee mli lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔwui adumɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot so quickly inside my barn after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akpa lɛ?

english: Yams rot fast if they get wounded during digging or if the barn is too hot and trapped with stale air. Storing them on open racks with good airflow keeps them cool and prevents decay.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛpila yɛ be mli ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni efite emɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛwo shĩai ni agbele mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa amɛhe jɔɔ ni ehaaa amɛfite.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and curling up under the direct sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. They need shade from fast-growing plants like plantains during their first few years to protect them from heat and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains amli yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli. Koni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make my land better for maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa he ni miyɔɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leguminous crops like groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on that natural fertilizer left in the ground.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot quickly depletes specific soil nutrients and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground, leading to weaker harvests over time.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi baa shi oya. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why is my maize growing tall stems but producing very small or weak corncobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii loo amɛhe waaa kwraa lɛ?

english: Maize requires strong soil nutrients early in its lifecycle. If the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen when the stalk is growing, the plant spends all its energy on leaves and height instead of filling out the cob.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ he miihia ŋmãa yɛ ewala shishijee bei amli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen, beni tso lɛ shishi lɛ miida lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and plant food from the main plantain stem. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem gets enough energy to grow big bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ plantain tso titri lɛ mli. Ajieɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ panicle agbo ko nɔ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight. Lifting the leaves up helps the plant create energy, which swells the yam tuber underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Baai lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baa. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the farm and water stays pooled around the roots for too long, the roots suffocate and rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ ni nu damɔ shi ebɔle he lɛ. shishifãi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ baafo ni amɛbaagboi.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme afternoon heat or when there is an irregular supply of water, as the plant tries to conserve energy to survive the heat stress.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he yɛ shwane mli loo kɛ́ nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ yɛ jɛmɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛye dɔlɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl inward during the sunniest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up during peak sunlight to reduce leaf surface area and prevent water loss. As the sun goes down and temperatures drop, the leaves usually unroll and flatten back out.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ebaa baa lɛ hiɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu ni elaaje lɛ naa. Kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to absorb water and nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. If left unchecked, they quickly outgrow crops and steal the sunlight and soil food meant for your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Amɛshwereɔ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ kɛha okpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to grow green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the topsoil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbaai eŋɔli lɛ akwɛ̃. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies that suck plant sap. It stops the plant from growing properly and reduces fruit yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. plant sap sucker Ebaatsi tsei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ebaaha yibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When the ground remains waterlogged for too long, oxygen gets trapped out, causing fungal rot to attack the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni eshwɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Oxygen lɛ mɔ̃ɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Groundnuts are unique because their pods mature underground. Once the flower is pollinated above ground, the stem bends downward to push the developing pod into the soil so it can grow into a nut.
ga: Peanuts yɛ srɔto kwraa ejaakɛ amɛpods lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ ni miiya hiɛ lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni eda ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: If too many shoots (suckers) grow together, they fight with the main plantain tree for food and water. Removing excess suckers ensures the main tree produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ Amɛkɛ ŋmeii titrii lɛ baawu kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why am I seeing small holes and yellowish dust inside my maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli lɛ

english: That dust is caused by stem borer caterpillars. They hatch from eggs laid on the leaves and tunnel into the stem to feed, which weakens the stalk and makes the corn break easily.
ga: Kplukai ni woɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ lɛ baa. Amɛfoɔ kɛjɛɔ wɔji ni akɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli ni amɛboteɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛye nii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ fãa oya.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees falling off without turning into small cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ cacao ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off if tiny insects called midges do not pollinate them, or if the tree experiences water stress during dry spells, causing it to drop flowers to save energy.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kooloi bibii ba amɛnɔ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ efɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. aloo kɛji tso lɛ naa nu he haomɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Ha fɔfɔi lɛ agbee shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why is it necessary to provide tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb up high to catch as much sunlight as possible. Exposure to sunlight helps the leaves make food, which is then sent down to expand the yam tuber under the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsu lɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛgbala sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I avoid spreading fertilizer on my field right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔji amli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ shi dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ he?

english: Heavy rainwater carries loose fertilizer off the surface of the soil into nearby gutters and streams before the plant roots get a chance to drink it up, wasting your money.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli tseee lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa nubui kɛ faai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. Dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baaná hegbɛ amɛnu shika lɛ fɛɛ

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to stay green and grow big. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni yɔɔ nitrogen tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper fruits get black rotten spots at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni fiteɔ yɛ shishi dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Black spots at the bottom of peppers happen when the soil lacks calcium or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet too quickly. Keeping the soil evenly moist and adding wood ash or agricultural lime helps prevent this condition.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi lɛ baa kɛji akɛ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli oya tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũu daa ni okɛ tso sũ loo okwaayeli mli sũ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ shihilɛ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are my cocoa flowers dropping off the tree without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off if they are not pollinated by tiny insects, or if the tree is stressed by intense heat and dry soil. Keeping good shade trees on your farm protects the blossoms and provides a home for beneficial insects that pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. aloo kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe, ni ehaa kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anáa shia.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves get covered in small holes soon after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ehà mi-cowpea baai lɛ anɔ lɛ? Beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Small holes in cowpea leaves are caused by insect pests like beetles chewing on the green leaves for food. Spraying organic neem leaf extract or appropriate insecticides early in the morning can stop these insects from damaging your crop.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ cowpea baai lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmɔɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ koni amɛye niyenii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem tso lɛ mli tsofa loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa kooloi nɛɛ ni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and feel dry during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up during extreme heat to protect themselves from losing too much water, but it can also be a sign of virus diseases spread by tiny insects like whiteflies. Giving the plants light shade and controlling sucking insects keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Shi ebaanyɛ efee hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi hu. Tso lɛ he hulutsoo kɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ni akudɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess rainwater sits around them for too long and drowns the roots. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges of soil allows surplus water to drain away easily so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi jɛmɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Groundnuts are legumes, which means their roots can pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the groundnut plant dies, that stored nitrogen remains in the dirt to feed nearby crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ŋmei tso lɛ gbo Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛye tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmei.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers take so long to shoot up after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei bibii lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ shi beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers grow slowly if they are planted in hard, compact soil or if the old leaves and roots were not cleaned before planting. Digging a deep, loose hole enriched with compost gives the sucker's roots space to spread quickly.
ga: Dumɔwui baakwɛ̃ blɛoo kɛji adu yɛ sũ ni wa ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ atsumɔko baai kɛ shishifãi momo lɛ ahe dani adu. Bu ni mli kwɔ ni etse ehe ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii eyi mli obɔ lɛ ni aaaku lɛ baaha sucker lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: How do I know when my yams underground are fully mature and ready to dig up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Yams are ready to harvest when the green leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up naturally. This color change shows that the plant has finished sending all its energy down into the root tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Nɛkɛ su tsakemɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ etsu ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛtee shishifã lɛ shishi.

english: Why do small insects attack my harvested maize even when it is stored inside sealed bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ akɛwo kotokui ni atsĩ naa mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Insects called weevils often lay tiny eggs on maize grains while they are still in the field, which hatch inside the bag later. Thoroughly drying your maize under the sun until it crackles and using airtight storage bags (PICS bags) suffocates the pests without chemicals.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ wɔji bibii. yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo ni baafo sɛɛ mli yɛ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ. Okɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi kɛyashi ebaagbala. Ni kɛ akɛ vacuum storage bags (PICS bags) tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii.

english: Why does my corn crop dry up and die during dry spells while farmers near the river keep harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ faa lɛ yaa nɔ amɛkpaa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Corn plants require a steady supply of moisture to grow and form kernels. When rainfall stops, dry soil starves the roots of moisture, whereas fields near water sources or those using irrigation can supply steady water year-round.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ taoɔ nu be fɛɛ be koni amɛdara ni amɛwo dumɔwui. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ kpa Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ akafee ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhei loo hei ni nu shwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha nu aba daa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Can I use water from a hand-dug well or pond to grow maize during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ nu bu loo nubu ni akɛ niji atsa lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛdu ŋmãa yɛ harmattan be ni nu lɛ mli egbi lɛ mli?

english: Yes, using well or pond water for simple hand-watering or drip irrigation allows maize to grow successfully even during the dry season when there is no rain.
ga: Hɛɛ, nubu mli nu loo ŋshɔnaa nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa nine nɔ nu loo nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli po ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: Why do farmers from drier neighboring countries like Burkina Faso seem to manage dry season farming so well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni okwaafoi ni jɛ maji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ, ni hulu enyɔ shi waa tamɔ Burkina Faso lɛ kwɛɔ hulutsoo be mli okwaayeli nɔ jogbaŋŋ nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Farmers in drier regions rely heavily on water conservation methods and small-scale irrigation systems like digging water retention ponds, allowing them to keep crops watered and healthy despite low rainfall.
ga: Esa akɛ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ hei ni nu bɛ lɛ kɛ amɛhe afɔ̃ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he kɛ nu shwiemɔ gbɛjianɔtoi bibii, tamɔ nubui ni atsaa koni akɛto nu lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa nu ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ po.

english: How can I harvest corn more than once a year if rain only falls in one major season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa ŋmãa fe shikome yɛ afi mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ be kome pɛ?

english: To get a second harvest outside the rainy season, you need a reliable source of water, such as a river, shallow well, or water pump, to irrigate the field during the dry months.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni okpa nii shii enyɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ. Nu jɛɛhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ, tamɔ faa, nubu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, loo nu pɔmp, he baahia bo kɛha nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: If I only have two acres of land, can I still make a good living compared to someone with a huge farm?
ga: Kɛ́ miyɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ani manyɛ maná shihilɛ ni sa lolo kɛ akɛto mɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ agbo ko he?

english: Yes, farm size does not determine success on its own. Focusing good farming practices, proper watering, and soil care on a small two-acre plot often produces higher yields per acre than a large farm that is neglected.
ga: Hɛɛ, jeee ŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsɔɔɔ omanyeyeli. Okwaayeli nifeemɔi kpakpai anɔ ni akɛjwɛŋmɔ maa Nu ni sa Kɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ni dalɛ ji acre enyɔ nɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ bei pii lɛ ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo baa acre kome mli fe ŋmɔ agbo ko ni aku hiɛ ashwie nɔ.

english: Is it safe for me to expand my farm to ten acres if I rely only on rainfall?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ matsake miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyashɛ acre 10 kɛji akɛ mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ pɛ nɔ?

english: Expanding to a large area like ten acres is risky if you rely only on rainfall. If the rains fail or stop early, you risk losing a much larger investment than if you had a secure water supply.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni da, tamɔ acre 10 nɔ lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ ji oshara kɛji akɛ okɛ ohe fɔ̃ nugbɔshiimɔ pɛ nɔ. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ enɛɛɛ loo ekpaaa mra Okɛ ohe woɔ oshara mli akɛ obaafite shika babaoo ni okɛwo mli lɛ fe kɛji oyɛ nu jɛɛhe ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do crops planted far away from a water stream grow much slower than crops planted close to it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni kɛ nu jɛɛhei lɛ yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ daraa blɛoo kwraa fe tsei ni akwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhei lɛ?

english: Crops close to water streams benefit from higher natural soil moisture and underground water levels, allowing their roots to absorb nutrients constantly without suffering drought stress.
ga: Tsei ni bɛŋkɛ faai lɛ náa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni fa babaoo lɛ he sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛŋmɛɛɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ naa.

english: Why do my corn leaves roll up into tight tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a corn plant's natural defense against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun to conserve its internal water.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Tsei haa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ mli koni nu akafite yɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: At what stage of growth does my maize plant need the most water to produce big ears?
ga: Mɛɛ be mi ŋmãa tso lɛ he hiaa nu fe fɛɛ koni ekwɛ toi wuji?

english: Maize needs water most during the flowering and silk-forming stage. If the plant lacks water at this critical time, the cob will end up missing kernels or growing very small seeds.
ga: Nu he hiaa ŋmãa fe fɛɛ yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ siliki feemɔ be mli. Kɛji tsei bɛ nu yɛ nɛkɛ be ni he hiaa waa nɛɛ mli lɛ Cob lɛ bɛ dumɔwui loo ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ afee bibii waa.

english: What happens to maize seeds if the ground stays completely dry for two weeks after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmãa dumɔwui anɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa otsii enyɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize seeds need moisture to swell and germinate. If the soil remains dry for too long, the seeds will either fail to sprout or sprout and quickly wither before their roots can reach deep soil.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ nu koni amɛfuu ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ loo amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaagboi oya dani shishifãi lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the big shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect them from intense heat and direct sunlight. Without canopy trees or plantains providing shade, the leaves scorch, soil moisture evaporates rapidly, and the young plants suffer severe heat stress.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo be koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛji tsei bibii loo dumɔwui ni haa hulutsoo bɛ lɛ, Ashã baai lɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. ni tsei bibii lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa.

english: Yam vines naturally spread out to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for their underground tubers. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground where air can circulate, preventing fungal diseases and allowing maximum sunlight to fuel tuber growth.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ abɔle he lɛ. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni oha hulu la babaoo aba bɔ ni ooonyɛ ni eha bulb lɛ ada.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize crop turning light yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves that start at the tip and move down the middle indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for leafy growth and green color; applying compost, manure, or a nitrogen-based fertilizer will help the plant recover.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni eyaa shishi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baa lɛ dalɛ kɛ eŋɔli su. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with thick foliage, but giving me small, thin tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ? Shi ani yitsei bibii komɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excess wet organic matter, the cassava plant directs all its energy into leaf and stem growth instead of root development. Balanced soil nutrients ensure the plant balances top growth with tuber development.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni efɔ babaoo lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe shishifãi lɛ adalɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ dalɛ ni fe fɛɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to rotate my crop field with cowpeas or groundnuts before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ mikɛ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake midumɔi lɛ dani midu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. When you harvest them, the stored nitrogen stays in the ground and naturally feeds the next hungry crop like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa amɛ Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their blossoms during the hot dry season without producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and low humidity dry out the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fertilization. When temperatures rise too high, the plant drops its blossoms to save energy and water until growing conditions improve.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo be ni baa shi lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves look like they have holes chewed into them overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛye bu nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: This destruction is typically caused by pests such as the Fall Armyworm, which feed inside the central funnel of young maize plants during the night. Early detection and applying organic or recommended treatments into the funnel saves the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela nɛɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ anɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ amli. Nibii ni anaa mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ baaye abua ni akwɛ he ni shweremɔ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my vegetable plants grow weak and small even during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-aduawai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and aggressively steal nutrients, water, and root space from your soil. Even with plenty of rain, your vegetables will starve if weeds consume the plant food first.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. ni ekɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa moŋ O-vegetables lɛ po baaye hɔmɔ kɛji jwɛi lɛ ye tso lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: If I plant my pepper crops very close together, will I get a larger harvest from my farm plot?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close causes crops to compete against each other for sunlight, soil space, and water, leading to thin stems and small yield. Proper spacing gives each plant room to branch out and bear more large fruits.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la, shikpɔŋ kɛ nu akaŋ, ni no haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni ekɛ niji baaje kpo ni ewo yibii wuji.

english: Why does my harvested maize rot or turn moldy inside the sack when I store it immediately after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ loo ehiɛɔ kotokui lɛ amli beni mikɛtoɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain contains high internal moisture. Storing moist corn traps humidity, allowing fungi and mold to grow rapidly; grains must be sun-dried until dry and hard before bagging for safe storage.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa babaoo. Abele ni mli efɔ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwereɔ oya. Esa akɛ agbi ŋmaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaagbi ni ewa dani akɛwo kotoku mli koni akɛto he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes when the sun is very hot around noon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ shwane mli yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during intense heat to reduce their surface area, which cuts down on water loss through evaporation and protects the plant from drying out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi. Enɛ haa nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. ni ebu tsei ahe koni amɛkagbi

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during long dry spells to conserve water and energy, storing its strength in the roots underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baanɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Staking gets the leaves up off the hot ground and opens them to sunlight, allowing the vine to make more food, which results in larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Staking haa baai lɛ jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ. Ehaa wain tsei lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the shade trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight; without shade, intense sun burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil before their roots can establish.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Tomato plants often drop their blossoms when daytime temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates wildly, which stresses the plant and stops fruit formation.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ekpaa yibiiwoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden eggs curling upwards and looking wrinkled like a net?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often a sign of tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or a virus transmitted by these insects damaging leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to spray water directly onto my cabbage leaves during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ nu baashwie kaabeji baai anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watering leaf surfaces in hot sun creates warm, humid micro-environments that encourage fungal diseases to spread, and much of the water evaporates before reaching the roots.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ bibioo ko ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. ni woɔ ŋmeii helai ahe hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã Ni nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ shi dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Removing excess shoots—called suckers—ensures that all the soil nutrients, water, and sunlight go directly to the main plant so it can produce a larger bunch of fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la fɛɛ yaa tso titri lɛ nɔ koni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in my field make the soil richer for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules, naturally enriching the soil with essential nutrients for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my young watermelons turning black and soft at the bottom ends before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon gbekɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo yɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ dani eda lɛ?

english: This rot at the tip of the fruit is caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, which often happens when soil moisture goes up and down unevenly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ aduawai tip rot fiteɔ ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: How do I know if my maize crops are not getting enough water during the dry period?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Maize leaves will roll up tightly into tubes during the hottest part of the day to save water. If you notice the leaves remain rolled up early in the morning, it means the soil is too dry and the plant is suffering from severe water stress.
ga: Abele baa lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyaa tsɔnei amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛji oyɔse akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lolo leebi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ ni tso lɛ miina nu he haomɔ ni naa wa.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt and die even when I water them in the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ amɛnɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Watering under the blazing afternoon sun causes water to evaporate rapidly before reaching the roots, and the droplets left on leaves can scald them under hot sunlight. It is best to water early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the air is cooler.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni nu ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã amɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Esa akɛ afɔse nu lɛ leebi loo shwane mli. ni ji be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ

english: Why do my pepper plants rot when water sits around their stems after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fiteɔ beni nu ebɔle tso lɛ he yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen to breathe just as much as they need water. When water stays trapped around the roots for too long, it smothers them, causing root rot and fungal diseases that kill the plant.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa tsei shishifãi taoɔ lɛ koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni tsei shishifãi hu taoɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. kɛ nu he hiamɔ Kɛ́ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, eyeɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ akpata tsei lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade protection because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out their roots. Plantains or temporary shade trees are needed to act as umbrellas for young cocoa until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ agbi. Plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko he miihia koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo kɛha kookoo bibii kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: High daytime temperatures combined with dry air can cause tomato plants to drop their blossoms to survive heat stress, as the plant decides it does not have enough moisture to support fruit growth.
ga: Gbi mli latsaa ni naa wa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi fata he lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛbaai koni amɛye amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he haomɔ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ kpɛɔ eyiŋ akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants losing their leaves during the harmattan dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves naturally during dry or dusty weather to stop water from escaping through leaf pores. The plant is not dead; it is conserving energy and water in its underground tubers until rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi loo sũ yɔɔ lɛ koni nu akatsɔ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Akɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu miito shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How can I tell if my soil lacks food for my crops without going to a laboratory?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa miduɔ nii lɛ bɛ mli ni miyaaa laboratori?

english: Check the lower leaves of your crops: if they turn pale light green or yellow while the rest of the plant stays stunted, your soil is usually missing nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build leaves and stems.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ: Kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ lolo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛmaa baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ

english: Why is it better to plant my crops in straight rows instead of scattering the seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni aaadu dumɔwui yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows ensures each plant gets equal space, light, and water without competing with neighbors, while making weeding, watering, and harvesting much faster and easier for you.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko, la, kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ yaa oya ni efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce small, weak harvests even if I fertilize the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ?

english: Weeds are stronger and grow faster than most farm crops, so they steal the food, sunlight, and soil moisture meant for your crops before your crops get a chance to absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ahe wa ni amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ niyenii, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my bean plants grow long vines with many leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei kakadaji ni baai kakadaji babaoo yɔɔ mli shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes bean plants to spend all their energy building tall vines and big leaves instead of flowering and setting fruit pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ wain tsei kakadaji kɛ baai wuji. Yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai ashishifãi ni fɔ̃ɔ lɛ najiaŋ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-decomposed manure helps the leaves turn green so the plant can produce healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tso lɛ dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli koni tso lɛ anyɛ awo toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does planting beans or cowpeas help improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants die, that nitrogen remains in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies, or by a plant virus they carry. Using neem oil spray or safe insecticides helps keep these pests away so fresh leaves can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni amɛhiɛ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ he. Bɔni afee ni baai heei lɛ anyɛ ada bɔ ni sa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is too hot, when plants don't get enough water, or when insects fail to pollinate them. Keeping soil moist and spacing plants properly helps flowers stay on and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni okɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ tomato.

english: Is it better to plant my cassava on flat ground or on raised mounds?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ loo yɛ gɔŋ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges makes the soil loose, allowing the roots to expand easily into large tubers. It also stops water from logging around the roots and causing rot during heavy rains.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bulbs agboi Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni nu akabɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why should I clear weeds from my farm while my young crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients your plants need. Removing weeds early ensures your crop gets all the food it needs to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm produce many flowers but very few cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi kookoo ŋmeii fioo pɛ woɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny beneficial insects called midges to transfer pollen between flowers. If the farm is too dry or sprayed heavily with harsh chemicals, midges disappear and flowers drop without producing pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Atsɛɔ amɛ midges koni amɛkɛ pollen aya fɔfɔi ateŋ. Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo akɛ tsofai ni mli wa efɔ nɔ Midge lɛ laajeɔ ni fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains before the fruit is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli dani aduawai lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that cannot easily hold heavy bunches, especially in soft, wet soil. Supporting the main stem with a strong wooden prop or bamboo pole prevents wind and weight from knocking the tree over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni efeee ŋmeii ni tsii oya, titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ muji naa koni ekagbee tso lɛ shi.

english: How do I know the exact time my cassava is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when lower leaves turn yellow and drop off. You can carefully dig around one plant to check if the tubers have reached a good size before harvesting the whole field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli. Kwɛmɔ tso kome jogbaŋŋ koni ona kɛji ŋmeii lɛ dalɛ sa dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What causes my harvested yam tubers to rot quickly inside the storage barn?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are cut or bruised during harvest, or if stored in a hot, crowded space. Keeping unbruised yams in a well-ventilated, shaded barn off the ground prevents moisture buildup and keeps tubers fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ loo atswa yɛ kpamɔ be mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni mɛi eyi mli obɔ Too sweet potatoes ni etseee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni baa lɛ naa, ni ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What is the best way to prepare my land before I start planting a new crop of plantains?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ajeɔ plantains heei adumɔ shishi?

english: Proper land preparation involves clearing weeds and bushes, removing large roots, and loosening the topsoil so that young plantain roots can easily penetrate the earth and absorb water and nutrients.
ga: Nɔ ni fata shikpɔŋ he saamɔ kpakpa he ji jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. shishifãi wuji ni ajieɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ koni plantain shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo ni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Spacing plantains about 2 to 3 meters apart ensures that each plant gets enough sunlight, air circulation, and soil space to grow large bunches without competing with neighboring plants.
ga: Ha dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 2 kɛyashi 3, ni oha tso fɛɛ tso aná hulu la. kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tsei wuji ni aduɔ ni akɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ akaŋ akaŋ.

english: How often do I need to visit and inspect my farm after planting to ensure my crops grow well?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe hiaa ni mayasara miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni makwɛ mli beni midu nii sɛɛ koni mana nɔmimaa akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lo?

english: Visiting your farm at least once or twice a week helps you spot early signs of weed competition, pest attacks, or dry soil conditions so you can address them before they damage your crop yield.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛ́ oya oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ jwɛi kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mra. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ atsu nii dani amɛfite onibii.

english: How does placing cassava or plantain peels at the base of my plantain trees help them?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmei loo plantain ŋmei wo midumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi?

english: Crop peels act as natural mulch and food for the soil. As they break down, they release essential nutrients back into the dirt, retain soil moisture, and protect the soil from direct heat.
ga: Tso lɛ he tsɔi tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ egbo lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he

english: Why is it important to keep the soil around my plantain stems moist throughout the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle plantain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ afee fɛ̃i yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?
