english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry a high percentage of water in their trunks. Moist soil helps the plant absorb nutrients continuously, resulting in thicker trunks and heavier fruit bunches.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni nu babaoo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii.

english: Should I place organic waste directly against the stem of the plantain tree or a little distance away?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ashishi yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi loo mafo mli fioo?

english: It is best to place organic waste a few inches away from the stem base to prevent excessive moisture build-up and rot against the stalk, allowing the spreading roots to safely draw in the nutrients.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ awo tso lɛ shishi inchii fioo komɛi koni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine akabua ehe naa ni efite tso lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nyɛɔ amɛgbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I tell if my plantain crop is getting enough nourishment from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantains lɛ miiná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: A well-nourished plantain tree displays dark green, broad leaves and a thick trunk. Pale or yellowing leaves usually indicate that the plant lacks nutrients or water in the soil.
ga: Plantains ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ baai ni mli edɔ, ni mli kwɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii loo nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why is regular weeding necessary on a plantain farm even after the trees have grown tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi daa yɛ plantain ŋmɔ mli eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ kɛlɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your plantains. Regular weeding ensures all the goodness in the ground goes directly into growing your plantains rather than wild plants.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ o-plantains lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ haa nibii kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa oplantain tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe koo mli tso lɛ.

english: Can I leave the weeds I cut down on the farm floor after weeding?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi jwɛi ni mifo lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mifo jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, leaving cleared weeds on the ground creates a dry cover that shades the soil, prevents new weeds from sprouting quickly, and decomposes into rich organic matter over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni ajie lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi heei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ oya ni amɛfiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: When is the most critical time to clear weeds from my crop field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔji amli?

english: It is best to weed early in the growing season when young plants are establishing themselves, and before weeds grow tall enough to drop seeds and spread further across your farm.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaajie jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ miida waa lɛ. Ni no ji dani jwɛi lɛ baashɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛdu dumɔwui ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up and droop during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the afternoon sun gets very hot, maize leaves roll up to trap moisture inside and protect themselves from burning. This is a natural defense, and the leaves will usually open back up when the temperature cools down in the evening.
ga: Kɛ́ shwane hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ, Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu. Ni baai lɛ fɔɔ gbelemɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young pepper plants turning dry and white under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi ni eyɛ futafuta yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Delicate young pepper plants can get leaf sunscald when exposed to severe heat without shade. The harsh sun destroys the green tissue, causing leaves to turn dry, pale, and paper-thin.
ga: Pepper tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baanyɛ aná hulutsoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ latsaa ni naa wa ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ he. Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ fãji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ, efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ wolo.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting shade trees inside cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees get stressed and scorched easily under direct sunlight. Planting shade trees protects young cocoa from severe heat, keeps the soil cool, and helps retain water around the root zone.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ feɔ mɛi ni haoɔ amɛ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe

english: How do I know if my tomato plants are needing more water during the hot dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu babaoo he miihia mi-tomato tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Tomatoes show water shortage when their bottom leaves turn yellow, flowers fall off before fruiting, and the plant stops growing. Checking if the top two inches of soil are dry tells you it is time to water deeply.
ga: Tomato baajie nu ni faaa lɛ he okadi kpo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii. ni tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ Kwɛmɔ koni ana kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi inchi enyɔ lɛ mli egbi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ awo nu mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does covering the soil around my yam mounds with dry grass help my crops stay hydrated?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi shwie mi-sweet potato pile lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that blocks the hot sun from evaporating soil moisture, keeping the roots cool and wet for much longer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛtsiɔ hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Is it harmful to my cassava plants if their leaves get covered in heavy dust or mud?
ga: Ani ebaaye mi yucca tso lɛ awui kɛji akɛ sũ loo sũ ni mli edɔ ehà ebaa lɛ nɔ?

english: A thick layer of dust or mud blocks sunlight from hitting the leaf surface, which prevents the plant from producing its own food and slows down crop growth.
ga: Muji loo muji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekatswa baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ afee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eniyenii, ni ehaaa tso lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: My groundnut leaves have dark spots that look like dirt—is this dirt or a crop sickness?
ga: Mi ŋmei baa lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni tamɔ muji. Ani enɛ ji shikpɔŋ loo tso hela?

english: Dark brown patches on groundnut leaves are usually caused by fungal leaf spot disease rather than ordinary dirt. This condition weakens the plant's leaves and reduces groundnut yield if left untreated.
ga: Ekolɛ fungal leaf spot hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei baa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa fe muji folo. Shihilɛ nɛɛ haa tso lɛ baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni baa lɛ baa shi kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: What causes my tall maize stalks to fall over flat after heavy rains and wind?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele tsei kakadaji lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over (known as lodging) when their root systems are weak or shallow. Heap up extra soil around the base of the stalks during early growth to help anchor them firmly in the ground.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ baagbee shi. (ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy) beni shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo amɛmli ekɔɔɔ Pile muji krokomɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ. Stem bases yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee bei amli koni eye ebua ni amɛfi shikpɔŋ lɛ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Can my cowpea crop survive a long period of severe heat without dying?
ga: Ani mi-cowpea tso lɛ baanyɛ adamɔ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli ni egbooo?

english: Cowpeas are naturally drought-tolerant. During extreme sun and dry spells, they temporarily slow down their growth to save water, but they will recover quickly once rain returns.
ga: Cowpeas ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. Yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ Amɛbaafee amɛdalɛ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Shi ebaatsa oya kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: If my vegetable plants droop completely during a dry period, will watering them make them bounce back?
ga: Kɛji mi-aduawai lɛ gboi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli Ani nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ baaha tso lɛ aku esɛɛ?

english: If a wilted plant's roots are still alive, watering it will help it pull up moisture and stand back up within a few hours. However, if it stays wilted overnight, root damage or disease may have set in.
ga: Kɛ́ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ egbi lɛ, wala yɛ lolo. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba mli ni tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi amli. Shi, kɛji akɛ egbo nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ, Roots baanyɛ afite loo hela aba enɔ.

english: When is the best time for me to start preparing my land for the major rainy season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabɔi shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: In Ghana, the major rainy season typically begins around February or March. Preparing your land just before these months—by clearing weeds and tilling the soil—ensures your seedbed is ready to catch the very first rains for strong root growth.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ February loo March. Saamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ dani nyɔji nɛɛ aba kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ooojie kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitsumɔ nɔ. Enɛ baasaa odumɔwui ashishi kɛha klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ adara waa.

english: What is the difference between the major season and the minor season for planting crops?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ shishijee kɛ sɛɛ mli be ni akɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: The major season (usually starting around February/March) brings longer and heavier rainfall, making it best for long-term crops. The minor season (around September) has shorter rains, so it is safer to plant fast-growing crops that mature quickly before the dry season starts.
ga: Be titri lɛ (bei pii lɛ ejeɔ shishi yɛ February/March aaafee) lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni naa wa baa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be kakadaŋŋ mli ŋmɔshi nibii, be ni ji enyɔ (aaafee September mli) lɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo. No hewɔ lɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, ni shwereɔ oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why did my crops produce flowers in September even though the rains stopped very early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ September mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ mra tsɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Plants respond to changes in weather and water. A brief rain in September can trigger plants to flower, but if the rains end too quickly, the plant drops those flowers to save water and stay alive, resulting in little or no harvest.
ga: Tsei tsuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ nu shihilɛi ahe nii. Nugbɔ nɛ be kukuoo ko. Yɛ September mli lɛ ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ afee fɔfɔi. Shi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra tsɔ Tsei baashwie nakai fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛhere nu ni amɛhi wala mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmaa fioo loo nɔ ko kwraa.

english: Why are my plants growing big green leaves but failing to show any flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi enyɛɛɛ ejie fɔfɔii akpo lɛ?

english: Plants often produce mostly leaves when the soil has too much nitrogen or when they aren't getting enough sunlight. To get flowers, plants need balanced soil nutrients—especially phosphorus—and steady water as they mature.
ga: Tsei fɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwiemɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Niyenii ni ja ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei. titri lɛ fɔsfɔs Kɛ nu daa kɛji eda kwraa koni ená fɔfɔi.

english: What kind of farm work can I do to make sure my crops flower reliably?
ga: Mɛɛ nitsumɔi manyɛ matsu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Adding compost or phosphorus-rich fertilizer, clearing weeds that steal nutrients, and watering regularly during dry weeks signals to the plant that it has enough strength and food to produce healthy flowers.
ga: Kompost loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus eyi mli obɔ lɛ ni akɛaawo mli Ajieɔ jwɛi ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa daa yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ eyɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo fɔfɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my crops drop off before turned into actual fruit or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off mainly due to stress from hot dry spells, severe pest attacks, or lack of water. When a plant gets too dry, it sheds its flowers to conserve energy for survival.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa yɛ hɔmɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa lɛ hewɔ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ tso lɛ mli Kɛ́ tso lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato koni ehi shi.

english: How do I know if my crop flowers will successfully develop into a full yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ baatsɔ yibiiwoo ni yeɔ emuu?

english: If your flowers stay attached to the stem, look bright, and the weather stays warm with steady moisture, insects or wind will pollinate them, causing the base of the flower to swell into fruit within a few weeks.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ofɔfɔi lɛ ekpɛtɛ tso lɛ shishi, ni amɛmiikpɛ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Kplukai loo kɔɔyɔɔ haa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Fɔfɔi lɛ ashishi lɛ fũuɔ ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baa yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: How does unexpected hot weather affect when my crops produce flowers?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Extreme heat and sudden dry weather shock the plant's internal clock. Some plants panic and flower early while they are still small, while others delay flowering until cooler, wetter weather returns.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni ba trukaa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ha ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni yɔɔ nitsumɔhe lɛ mli lɛ hoso. Tsei komɛi feɔ gbeyei ni amɛwoɔ mra be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ. yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu sɛɛ tsɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I guarantee a good harvest if I miss planting during the February and March rains?
ga: Kɛji mikpa dumɔ yɛ February kɛyashi March nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ani abaaha yibiiwoo kpakpa aba?

english: Missing the early February/March rains makes farming riskier because your crops won't get the full duration of heavy rainfall. You can still plant, but you may need extra irrigation to help the crops finish flowering and fruiting.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ yɛ February/March shishijee gbɛ lɛ baaha okwaayeli afee nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eshɛɛɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe. Obaanyɛ odu lolo. Shi kɛlɛ, ekolɛ nu kroko he baahia bo koni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: How does keeping my farm free of weeds help my crops bloom on time?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi yɛ be naa?

english: Weeds compete with your crops for underground water and nutrients. Clearing them ensures your crops get all the soil food they need to build the energy required to bloom flowers on schedule.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ fɔfɔi yɛ be naa.

english: I want to farm on someone else's land and they asked for a 'one-third' share of the harvest. How does this land agreement work?
ga: Miisumɔ ni matsu okwaa yɛ mɔ kroko shikpɔŋ nɔ. Ni amɛbi koni aha amɛ nikpamɔ lɛ mli ‘jai etɛ mli ekome’. Te shikpɔŋ he nitsumɔ nɛɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: This traditional agreement is known as 'Abusa' in Ghana. Under Abusa, the farm yield or land is divided into three equal parts: the landowner receives one-third, while you keep two-thirds to reward your labor, seeds, and farm investment.
ga: Atsɛɔ kusum gbɛjianɔtoo nɛɛ akɛ ‘Abusa’ yɛ Ghana. Yɛ Abusa shishi lɛ, ajaa okwaayeli mli nibii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awoɔ fãi etɛ ni yeɔ egbɔ mli. Shikpɔŋtsɛ lɛ nine shɛɔ mlijaa etɛ mli ekome nɔ. yɛ be mli ni okɛ mlijaa etɛ mli enyɔ toɔ akɛ nyɔmɔwoo kɛha onitsumɔ lɛ. dumɔ dumɔwui ni okɛ shika awo oŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Before I start clearing land given to me by a local landowner, how can I protect myself from future land disputes?
ga: Dani mabɔi shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋtsɛ ko ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kɛha mi lɛ mli tsemɔ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mihe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ he béi ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ he?

english: Always establish clear boundaries with the owner in the presence of local community witnesses. It is best to write down a simple signed agreement stating whether it is an Abusa or Abunu arrangement, how long you can farm the land, and what crops you are allowed to grow.
ga: Too husui ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kɛ nuŋtsɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ odasefoi ni yɔɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ ni ooona be fɛɛ be lɛ nɔ. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni oŋma kpaŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Akɛ nine wo nakai kpaŋmɔ lɛ shishi ni tsɔɔ akɛ eji Abusa loo Abunu kpaŋmɔ kɛha be enyiɛ obaanyɛ otsu okwaayeli he nii? Ni mɛɛ tsei aŋmɛ bo gbɛ ni okwɛ?

english: Is it better to plant my maize in straight rows or in circles across my land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni ja loo ŋmãa mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ?

english: Planting in straight, well-spaced rows is better than planting in circles. Straight rows ensure every plant gets equal sunlight, water, and nutrients, while making weeding, fertilizer application, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ehi fe ni ooodu yɛ kooyigbɛ. Nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni ja lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ewaaa kwraa akɛ abaajie jwɛi, abaawo ŋmɔshi nibii, ni akpa.

english: Can I plant maize on the same land where I am starting a new cocoa farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mijeɔ kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishi yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize with young cocoa is a good practice. The maize gives you food and income during the first season while providing helpful shade to protect young cocoa seedlings from the hot sun.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ kookoo bibii duɔ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Abele haa onáa niyenii kɛ shika yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: How often should I walk through my cocoa farm to inspect my trees, and what should I look out for?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ kookoo ŋmɔ ko mli koni mayakwɛ tsei lɛ? Ni mɛni esa akɛ makwɛ mihe nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he?

english: Inspect your cocoa farm at least once a week. Look out for early signs of black pod disease, insect damage on young leaves, and swollen branches so you can treat them before they spread to the whole farm.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, kwɛmɔ o-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome yɛ otsi mli. Taomɔ black pod hela lɛ he okadii mra. Kplukai fiteɔ baai bibii kɛ tsei niji ni efuu, no hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ otsa amɛ dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: My young cocoa trees have not produced any pods after two years. Is something wrong with them?
ga: Mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ bɛ ŋmeii yɛ afii enyɔ sɛɛ. Ani naagba ko yɛ amɛhe?

english: Not necessarily. While modern hybrid cocoa can start bearing pods in 2 to 3 years, older or traditional varieties often take 4 to 5 years. As long as the trees look green and healthy, give them time and proper maintenance.
ga: Dabi, yɛ be mli ni ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ baaje shishi amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ loo blema kookoo lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5, kɛji tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛji ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa. Ha lɛ be kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to prune branches from our cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔfo wɔ kokoo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the canopy so sunlight and fresh air can reach all parts of the tree. This reduces dampness that causes black pod disease and encourages the tree to produce more healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the best way to prepare my land for maize without damaging the soil fertility?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ ni afiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Clear the bush without burning it if possible. Burning destroys good soil organic matter and beneficial organisms. Leaving cleared vegetation to decompose enriches the soil with nutrients for your maize.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ jwɛi ni okɛshãaa amɛ kɛji ebaahi. Shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tsei lɛ gbɛ ni amɛfite lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ náa niyenii babaoo.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer to my maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-abele lɛ mli?

english: Apply the first round of NPK fertilizer about 2 weeks after the seeds sprout. Apply the second round (top-dressing with Urea or SOA) when the corn reaches knee height, just before it starts flowering.
ga: Okɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ awo mli aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Okɛ fã ni ji enyɔ lɛ awo mli (ni akɛ urea loo SOA woɔ nɔ) beni ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ enaneshi dani fɔfɔi lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ.

english: How do I know that my maize is fully ripe and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize is ready for grain harvest when the leaves and outer husks turn completely brown and dry, and the corn kernels become hard enough that you cannot easily dent them with your fingernail.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ kɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi kwraa lɛ. Ni ŋmãa mli ŋmeii lɛ wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aha otsitsii lɛ atsɔ mlɛo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help your plants become dark green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni mli wa lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo otsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting inside the soil before I even dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifolɔ amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in heavy or poorly drained soil during rainy seasons. Planting your cassava stems on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shikpɔŋ ni mli wa loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Groundnuts and beans naturally trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds your maize crop, improves long-term soil fertility, and gives you an extra harvest.
ga: Peanuts kɛ nuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa o-corn lɛ niyenii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ aya hiɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni eye ebua bo ni okpa babaoo.

english: What is eating ragged hole marks into the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni elaaje yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central growing tip of maize plants. Checking your farm early and applying recommended pesticides or neem leaf extract will protect your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Curling leaves are often caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking sap from the plant and spreading viruses. Spraying neem oil or recommended insecticidal soaps helps control these pests before they ruin your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi shwieɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off without growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil runs out of water. Covering the soil around the plants with dry grass keeps the roots cool and moist, helping the flowers turn into big tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i. Ye obua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomatoi wuji.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their tiny young pods before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? Dani ebaada kwraa?

english: Young cocoa pods drop off when the tree lacks sufficient water and soil nutrients, or when targeted by pests like capsids. Providing moderate tree shade and applying proper cocoa fertilizer helps the tree retain its pods.
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids miitswa tso lɛ, kɛ́ aha tso lɛ hulutsoo ni sa kɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ etsitsii lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to use long wooden stakes to lift my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni mikɛwo mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight to grow large tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases and rot.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni ená hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ bulbs agboi akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa.

english: Too many extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main tree for food and water. Pruning them so only one or two strong shoots remain ensures the main plantain tree produces a thick, heavy bunch.
ga: Tsoi loo tsei babaoo ni kɛ tso titri lɛ miitswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ashwɛ lɛ, ebaaha plantain titri lɛ afee tso ni mli edɔ ni tsii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that create a living umbrella, giving the cocoa trees the shade and moisture they need during their first years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni feɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Can I apply fertilizer on my cocoa farm when it is raining?
ga: Ani manyɛ mawo mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji nugbɔ nɛ?

english: Yes, light or moderate rain helps soil absorb fertilizer so roots can take it in. However, you should avoid applying inputs during heavy downpours that wash chemicals away, or during severe dry spells when the soil is completely dry.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo loo ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ awo mli Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ tsofai lɛ amli lɛ mli. aloo yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I feed my cocoa trees with inputs during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa mi-cacao tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: During the dry season, the soil lacks the moisture required for cocoa roots to absorb nutrients. Applying fertilizers in dry conditions can burn the plant roots and waste your money.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nu ni he hiaa koni kookoo shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii yɛ hei ni nu bɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi ni efite shika.

english: What happens to chemicals or fertilizer if heavy rain falls right after I put them on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba tsofai loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away the fertilizer or chemical treatments off the leaves and topsoil before the cocoa plant has a chance to absorb them, reducing their effectiveness.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni yɔɔ baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe dani kookoo tsei lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ amɛ. Enɛ baaha nitsumɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Will my cocoa trees suffer if I apply fertilizers when the ground is very dry?
ga: Ani mi-kokoo tsei lɛ baaná he sɛɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ?

english: Yes, dry ground prevents the tree from absorbing nutrients. Concentrated chemicals sitting near dry roots can burn the roots and cause the leaves to turn brown or drop.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Tsofai ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni egbi lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ loo amɛgbee shi.

english: How do I know the best week to spray or fertilize my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male otsi ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ cacao tsei anɔ loo akɛwo amɛmli?

english: Watch your local weather patterns. The best time is during periods when your area receives regular weekly rainfall, ensuring moist soil without heavy floods.
ga: Kwɛmɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ daa otsi. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu afua ni naa wa akafee.

english: Does cocoa need fertilizer all year round, or only in specific seasons?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia kookoo afi muu lɛ fɛɛ loo yɛ bei komɛi amli pɛ?

english: Cocoa only needs fertilizer during wet growing periods when soil moisture allows roots to draw in nutrients. You should avoid applying inputs during dry months.
ga: Cocoa he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ haa shishifãi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ pɛ. Esa akɛ okpa nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do cocoa trees seem to slow down their growth during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry months, cocoa trees naturally conserve water and reduce their growth to survive heat and drought, which makes it an ineffective time to force growth with fertilizers.
ga: yɛ nyɔji ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ amli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ buɔ nu he yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛhaa amɛdalɛ baa shi koni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hɔmɔ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ be ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛɔ dalɛ nɔ.

english: When my young cocoa trees reach about eight months old, what main care do they need?
ga: Beni mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ eye aaafee nyɔji kpaanyɔ lɛ. Mɛɛ yelikɛbuamɔ titri he hiaa amɛ?

english: At around eight months, young cocoa trees are actively growing and need routine weed control, shade management, and proper timing for soil nutrients during rain periods to build strong stems.
ga: Aaafee nyɔji kpaanyɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ miida waa. Ni ehe miihia ni akudɔ jwɛi lɛ daa. Shade nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ be ni sa ni akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni afee tsei akui ni wa.

english: How does constant rain affect the health of cocoa pods on my farm?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ saa kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahewalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Continuous rain creates high humidity, which can promote fungal diseases like black pod disease. You need to monitor your farm closely during rainy months to keep pods healthy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela aba. Esa akɛ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyɔji lɛ amli koni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How old must my young cocoa plants be before I start regular field maintenance?
ga: Esa akɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ aye afii enyiɛ dani manyɛ mabɔi ŋmɔ lɛ mli saamɔ daa?

english: Maintenance starts from the day of planting, but intensive upkeep—like structured fertilizer feeding and pruning—becomes crucial as the plants establish themselves over their first year.
ga: Ajeɔ ekwɛmɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ gbi ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi helatsamɔ ni mli wa—nɔkwɛmɔnɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso mli kɛ tso ni afoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ nɔ—ni he hiaa waa yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ toɔ ehe shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How long does it usually take for my maize crop to grow and be ready for harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mi-ŋma lɛ daa ni efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Most maize varieties take between 2 to 4 months to reach full maturity and be ready for harvest, depending on whether you plant quick-maturing seeds or late-maturing varieties.
ga: Abele babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 4 dani ekwɛɔ ni efeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ. Edamɔ dumɔwui ni shwereɔ mra loo dumɔwui ni shwereɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I choose the right crop seeds if the rains in my area only last for two months?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tso dumɔwui ni sa? Kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ nyɔji enyɔ pɛ

english: You should ask for early-maturing or short-duration seed varieties, which are bred to grow fast and complete their harvest cycle within 60 days before the rain stops.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooobi dumɔwui srɔtoi ni daa oya loo ni hiɔ shi be kukuoo. Koni afɔ tsei ni amɛdara oya ni amɛgbe kpamɔ lɛ naa yɛ gbii 60 mli dani nugbɔ lɛ akpa.

english: How many times in a year can I plant and harvest crops on the same piece of land?
ga: Shii enyiɛ manyɛ madu ni makpa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ afi kome mli?

english: If you depend only on rainfall, you can usually plant once or twice a year during the major and minor rainy seasons. However, if you have a reliable water source like a well or river, you can plant year-round.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ ohe fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔshiimɔ pɛ nɔ Obaanyɛ odu lɛ shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri kɛ nɔ ni baa shi fioo lɛ mli, shi kɛlɛ, kɛji oyɛ nu jɛɛhe ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ, tamɔ nubu loo faa. Abaanyɛ adu afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why is it difficult for me to plant maize during the dry season without an irrigation setup?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaa kɛhaa mi akɛ makwɛ ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ?

english: Maize requires steady soil moisture to sprout and build strong roots; without rain or supplemental irrigation, the seeds will dry up in the hot soil and die.
ga: Abɛi he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ koni ekwɛ̃ ni efee shishifãi ni wa. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ loo nu kroko fataaa he lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛbaagboi.

english: Is it safe for me to plant my crops at any time of the year as long as I have seeds ready?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ tsei yɛ afi lɛ mli be fɛɛ be, kɛji akɛ miyɛ dumɔwui ni mifee klalo?

english: No, crops rely heavily on specific weather conditions. Planting outside the natural rainy season without extra water will result in poor germination and crop failure.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii damɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ waa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ ni nu fataaa he lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hu baafee nɔ ni ehiii.

english: Why do some of my crops yield better during the major rainy season compared to the minor rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ be titri lɛ mli kɛ akɛto nugbɔ fioo be lɛ he lɛ?

english: The major rainy season brings longer and more reliable rainfall, which gives crops continuous moisture and time to produce maximum yield compared to the shorter minor season.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ baa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ kɛ be ni amɛkɛbaawo yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto be kuku ni ji enyɔ lɛ he.

english: What can I do to keep my crops alive when the dry spell lasts longer than expected?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya nɔ ahi nu lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: You can conserve soil moisture by spreading dry grass or leaves around the roots of your crops (mulching), or set up simple bucket watering systems to keep the root zones moist.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni oookɛshwie oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ (mulching) loo okɛ baagi mli nu ni akɛwoɔ mli ni yɔɔ mlɛo awo mli koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ.

english: How does covering my crop fields with dry leaves help protect plants during hot dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ baai ni egbi baaha miŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei ahe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Dry leaves act as a protective blanket (mulch) over the soil, shading it from direct sunlight, reducing water evaporation, and keeping the soil cool for the roots.
ga: Baai ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he (mulch) yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha shishifãi lɛ

english: What steps should I take to plan my farming activities when rainfall becomes unpredictable?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mato okwaayeli nitsumɔi ahe gbɛjianɔ beni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nugbɔ ni baa lɛ?

english: You should check weather forecasts, prepare your field early to capture the very first rains, choose drought-tolerant crop varieties, and plan for simple water storage methods on your farm.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he adafitswaa lɛ mli. Saamɔ he lɛ kɛjɛ shishijee. Bɔni afee ni onyɛ okpee klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ naa Halamɔ tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. ni oto gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni oootsɔ nɔ okɛ nu ato oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he gbɛjianɔ

english: Which crops are best for me to plant if I am worried about sudden dry spells during the season?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ madu kɛji hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa yɛ be mli ni mihaoɔ lɛ he miihao?

english: Crops like cassava, sorghum, millet, and cowpea have deep roots or low water needs, making them much better at surviving sudden dry spells than moisture-heavy crops like young maize.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo nu ni he ehiaaa tsɔ. Enɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni biɔ hulutsoo babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa bibii.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when the heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is waterlogged or lacks nitrogen because heavy rains wash nutrients away. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea after severe rains helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nitrogen bɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii laajeɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why are my cassava roots growing very small even though the branches and leaves are tall and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ? He ni tsei niji kɛ baai lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or shade, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tuberous roots below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off the tree before forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they do not get enough water, lack key soil nutrients like potassium, or suffer from insect attacks that disturb pod development.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium, loo kooloi ni tsiɔ pod lɛ shweremɔ naa lɛ tutuaa lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips that suck the sap out of leaves and spread viruses that stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni shwieɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni tsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my young maize plants have holes in the leaves and dark dirt inside the center stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn plant lɛ yɛ bu yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the leafy center of young maize to feed on tender new growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye ŋmeii heei ni ekwɛ̃ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark black rotten patches at the bottom before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni mli edɔ dani etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering during dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Cowpea plants fold their leaves toward the sun during intense heat to protect themselves from losing too much moisture through evaporation.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be destroyed by banana root nematodes or weevils underground, leaving the heavy plant without a strong anchor against strong winds.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni banana shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii baanyɛ afite amɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni tsii lɛ náaa osɛɛ ni amɛkɛdamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ naa.

english: Early morning is best because the soil absorbs water before the sun gets hot, allowing roots to take in moisture without losing it quickly to evaporation.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu dani hulu lɛ shɛɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ naa nu ni amɛfiteee kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ oya lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and turn black early before harvest time arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ egbi ni amɛmiifee ediŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Early drying of yam vines is often caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose, which spreads quickly during periods of high humidity and rainfall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbiɔ mra. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to grow healthy and green. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer to the soil helps the leaves regain their green color and strength.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛfee eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that get scorched easily under direct sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside cocoa creates a canopy that protects the young cocoa from heat and keeps moisture in the ground.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my pepper plants before any peppers start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi yɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or sudden lack of water. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots using mulch helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Roots lɛ he lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni okɛ mulch tsu nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller cassava yields now compared to three years ago on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmei fioo fe afii etɛ ni eho nɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil gets tired and drained of nutrients when the same crop is planted on it year after year. Rotating your crops with leguminous plants like cowpeas or letting the land rest allows the soil to rebuild its natural nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa tsake oŋmɔshi nibii loo oha shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ehe adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops wilt and turn yellow even during the rainy season when there is plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ po mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rain floods the field and water stays trapped around the roots, the roots cannot breathe and begin to rot. Creating simple drainage furrows allows excess water to flow away so the plant roots stay healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ha ŋmɔ ko mli nu ni nu tsɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli lɛ he tsɔne ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni afee Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. No hewɔ lɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ mli wa.

english: Why are the stems of my young maize seedlings getting cut off at night near the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ afoɔ mi-baby corn dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɛkɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Underground insects called cutworms hide in the soil during the day and chew through weak plant stems at night. Keeping your field clean of weeds and tilling the land before planting exposes cutworms to sunlight and birds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni atsɛɔ amɛ cutworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ shwane mli, ni amɛyeɔ tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ gbɛkɛ. Kɛ́ oha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he tse ni jwɛi bɛ jɛmɛ, ni otsu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii dani odu nii lɛ, ebaaha cutworms lɛ aná hulu la kɛ okpoi.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and small when I plant many stems very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ midu tsei babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots compete heavily with each other for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Proper spacing gives each cassava plant enough room to expand and produce thick tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmei tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa ŋmei tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshwa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse aba.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even when the weather is good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ lɛ mli hi moŋ?

english: Weeds act like food thieves because their roots grow faster and steal water and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Weeding early prevents weeds from starving your crops of essential nourishment.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ niyenii julɔi ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye niyenii ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why should I remove the extra suckers growing at the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too many young shoots growing from the base pull food and water away from the main stem. Removing all except one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree gets full energy to produce big, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ tsɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baagbala niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do seeds I saved from last year's maize harvest produce lower yields than certified seeds bought from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii ni baa shi fe dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically carefully bred to fight off local diseases and produce high yields. Seeds saved from previous harvests naturally lose this vigor, leading to weaker plants and smaller harvests over time.
ga: Akɛ hiɛdɔɔ kwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ maŋ lɛ mli helai awuu ni ewo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ amɛhewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ hu baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: This usually happens when your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the plant's main food for green growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the soil, so applying urea or well-rotted manure gives the crops their strength back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei yeɔ kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ urea loo ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my maize help my soil?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the field, they release this natural food into the ground, fertilizing neighboring crops like maize for free.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛwoɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yaka.

english: Cassava roots rot when water pools around them without draining. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the roots dry enough to stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. ni nu shwieee shi Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. ni oha shishifãi lɛ agbi bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my lowland rice grow much better when standing water is kept in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-flat rice lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ akɛ nu to ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Lowland rice thrives in standing water because the water smothers weeds that compete for food, while helping the rice roots absorb nutrients easily from the muddy soil.
ga: Omɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli ejaakɛ nu lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii he akaŋ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa shishifãi ni amɛnáa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛjɛɔ sũ ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli lɛ mlɛo.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with dirty powder inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ powda muji yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the plant's central leaves. Spraying an approved pesticide or neem extract solution directly into the plant's funnel early in the morning destroys these worms.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaakpata nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahiɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking sap from the leaves and spreading viruses. Spraying neem oil or soapy water deters these insects and protects new shoots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa ni ebu ŋmeii heei ahe.

english: Why do my fruiting plantain trees keep falling over during strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow shallowly, and heavy bunches make the tree top-heavy. Supporting the fruiting stems with sturdy bamboo props and planting suckers deeper in rich soil prevents wind damage.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ daaa fioo. Ni niji ni tsii haa tso lɛ yiteŋ feɔ tsii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni wa fiɔ yibiiwoo tsei lɛ asɛɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ akafite amɛ.

english: Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground to catch maximum sunlight, which gives the plant energy to build larger tubers underground while protecting the foliage from soil-borne rot.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping all their small flowers without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Ni efeee pods kwraa?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when exposed to intense direct heat or prolonged drought. Maintaining tall shade trees in your farm creates a cool microclimate that helps the flowers stay on the tree and turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo loo hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ he. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ni oookwɛ nɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni haa fɔfɔii hiɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning dark black and sunken before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efoɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by irregular watering and a lack of calcium in the plant. Water your tomato plants consistently and add wood ash or agricultural lime to the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ lɛ daa kɛ calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli. Okɛ nu awo tomato tsei lɛ amli daa ni okɛ tso sũ loo okwaayeli mli sũ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young maize seedlings need different fertilizer than when they start producing cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi dumɔwui bibii lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ srɔto fe beni amɛbɔi ŋmɔshi nibii feemɔ lɛ?

english: Young maize seedlings need nitrogen-heavy food to build strong stems and leafy green leaves early on, but once they start producing cobs, they require more phosphorus and potassium to grow full, healthy grains.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui bibii lɛ he miihia niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nitrogen koni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli mra. Shi kɛ́ amɛbɔi cob feemɔ Amɛmiitao phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo koni amɛdumɔwui lɛ ayi obɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How do I know when my nursery cocoa plants are old enough to be transplanted to the main farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu amɛ awo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Cocoa seedlings are ready to leave the nursery after 3 to 6 months when their green stems turn brown and woody and they have developed at least two full sets of mature, dark green leaves.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaashi ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 6 sɛɛ, beni amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsei lɛ. ni kɛ hoo lɛ, eyɛ baai ni edara ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa lɛ akui enyɔ.

english: Can I feed my young pepper transplants the same amount of fertilizer as my full-grown pepper plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha ŋmeii bibii ni adu amɛ awo mli lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii tsei ni eda lɛ amli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, young transplants have weak, delicate roots that can easily burn from full doses of fertilizer. They need a lighter, milder food mix until they grow bigger and stronger roots.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni atsake amɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo wo mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã oya. Niyenii ni mli tse ni mli wa waa he miihia amɛ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why should I mix dried manure into the dirt instead of just dumping it straight onto the plant roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mikɛbaafɔse tsei lɛ ashishifãi anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Mixing manure into topsoil allows the nutrients to spread evenly and break down slowly, preventing raw manure from generating heat that can burn young plant roots.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa pɛpɛɛpɛ ni efiteɔ fiofio. Enɛ ji koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ akafee dɔlɛ ni baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi.

english: Is it better to put fertilizer right next to the stem or spread it in a circle around the plant?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo tso lɛ masɛi loo akɛshwie nɔ yɛ kooyigbɛ kɛbɔle tso lɛ he?

english: Placing fertilizer in a circle a few inches away from the stem allows the feeding roots—which spread outwards underground—to drink up the nutrients safely without touching the main stem.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ kooyigbɛ ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi ni yeɔ niyenii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ nuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni etaaa tso lɛ titri lɛ he shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big foliage above ground but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil forces the cassava plant to spend all its energy growing leaves instead of roots. Cassava needs balanced soil with adequate potassium to build thick tubers underground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ ebaa lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe eshishifãi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni ja kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia cassava koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli edɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves turn yellow and drop off during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away nutrients from the soil and drown roots, making it hard for plants to breathe and absorb food, which causes leaves to turn yellow and fall.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaamu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my land help the next crop of maize grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, leaving behind natural soil food that feeds the maize crop planted in the next season.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmãa tsei ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Black pod disease is caused by excess moisture and shade. Pruning overhead branches lets sunlight and air dry out the farm, preventing fungal germs from damaging the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine. Nibii ni afoɔ yɛ yiteŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Tsi fungal helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite pods lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers and stop growing during the dry harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ekpaa dalɛ yɛ harmatta hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry harmattan winds strip moisture from leaves faster than roots can draw water, forcing the plant to drop flowers and pause growth to conserve energy and survive.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ ajie fɔfɔii ni amɛkpa amɛdalɛ be kukuoo ko bɔni afee ni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Fertilizer adds essential nutrients back into tired soil. If your crops have yellowish leaves, weak stems, or grow very slowly, adding the right fertilizer restores soil strength and helps the plants grow strong.
ga: Fertilizer kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ baai ŋmɔŋ, shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ loo eedara blɛoo waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara waa.

english: What actually happens to my cocoa trees when I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer provides food that cocoa trees absorb through their roots. This strengthens the trunk, makes the leaves green and healthy, and gives the tree enough energy to produce many flowers and pods.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni cacao tso lɛ tsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ eshɛɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli waa. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ni ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How does clearing weeds from my cocoa farm help the fertilizer work better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer food from the soil before your cocoa trees can reach it. Clearing weeds around the base of the trees ensures your cocoa roots get all the nutrients to grow well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani cacao tsei lɛ shɛɔ he. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa kookoo shishifãi lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is hand pollination, and why are farmers calling it cocoa paneɛ?
ga: Mɛni ji nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi tsɛɔ lɛ kookoo paneɛ?

english: Hand pollination, locally called cocoa paneɛ, is manually taking pollen from one cocoa flower and placing it onto another using a small brush or tool. It ensures flowers successfully turn into pods instead of falling off.
ga: hand pollination of flowers Loo ale lɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli akɛ Cocoa paneɛ Ekɔɔ pollen ni jɛ kookoo fɔfɔi kome mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ brɔsh loo dɛŋdade bibioo ko nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ omanyeyeli mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbee shi.

english: Why do so many flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop because natural insects do not transfer enough pollen between them. Hand pollination solves this by making sure pollen reaches the flower, turning almost every flower into a pod.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi nyɛɛɛ ajie pollen ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛteŋ. Nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ naagba nɛɛ he nii kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ni ekwɛɔ koni fɔfɔi lɛ ayashɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi ni etsɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to do hand pollination on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ mihe baawo fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli?

english: The best time for hand pollination is early in the morning, between 6:00 AM and 10:00 AM, when cocoa flowers are fresh, open, and full of active pollen.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛ niji feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji leebi, yɛ ŋmɛji 6:00 AM kɛ 10:00 AM teŋ, be mli ni kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ efee ehee, amɛgbele amɛhe, ni ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ nii eyi mli obɔ lɛ.

english: Can hand pollination work on old cocoa trees, or is it only for young farms?
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ atsu nii yɛ kookoo tsei momo anɔ. Aloo yɛ ŋmɔji bibii pɛ amli?

english: Hand pollination works on any mature cocoa tree that produces flowers, regardless of age, as long as the tree is healthy and well-fed with soil nutrients.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ nine nɔ ŋmɔtɔ awo cacao tsei ni eda ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ekɔɔɔ afii ni amɛye lɛ he. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ hewalɛ ni enáa niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ,.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow even during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during rainy weather often mean the soil is missing key nutrients like nitrogen. Rain gives water, but the trees still need nutrients from fertilizer to maintain healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ haa nu, shi tsei hu he miihia niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛbaa eŋɔli lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I apply fertilizer, do I still need to do hand pollination to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ miniji afee pollinate lolo koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Yes. Fertilizer gives the tree the strength to produce many flowers, but hand pollination guarantees those flowers actually set into pods, giving you the highest yield possible.
ga: Hɛɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ baafee ŋmɔtɔ diɛŋtsɛ. Enɛ baaha oná yibii babaoo fe fɛɛ.

english: How many months does it take a cocoa flower to become a ripe pod ready for harvest?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Once a flower is successfully pollinated, it takes about 5 to 6 months to grow into a fully mature, ripe cocoa pod ready to be harvested.
ga: Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ye omanye yɛ pollination mli lɛ Eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 5 kɛyashi 6 dani kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni asaa he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and drop off when the Harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ harmattan be lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan, the air becomes very dry and cold. Cocoa trees drop their leaves on purpose to reduce water loss through evaporation so they can survive the dry season until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu ni amɛlaaje kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ ji koni cacao tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense mechanism. By curling its leaves, the crop reduces the amount of leaf surface exposed to the sun and heat, which stops water from escaping too quickly.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni baa lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haaa nu lɛ ho oya tsɔ.

english: Why does adding too much nitrogen fertilizer cause my crops to grow big green leaves but very small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli fe nine lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii waa lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen signals the plant to focus all its energy on vegetative leaf growth instead of reproductive growth, delaying flowering and reducing fruit development.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ tsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baawo baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔmɔ dalɛ. ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ehaa aduawai lɛ ayibɔ baa shi

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize plants turn yellow in an upside-down 'V' shape before the rest of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ‘V’ ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ mli dani tso lɛ fãi krokomɛi lɛ?

english: This pattern shows a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves stored nitrogen from its older, lower leaves up to feed the new, growing top leaves, causing the bottom leaves to starve and turn yellow first.
ga: Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni ato lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛye ŋwɛi baai heei ni miida lɛ. Ha baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when I plant them in fields that retain a lot of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. In waterlogged soil, water fills all the air spaces, suffocating the roots and allowing fungal diseases to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ mli. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed all their blossoms without forming any tomatoes during very hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the tomato flowers, preventing fertilization. When a flower is not fertilized, the plant drops it to avoid wasting energy on a blossom that cannot produce fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa enyɛŋ ekɛ fɔfɔi awo fɔfɔi mli Kɛ́ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi ko fɔfɔi lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛ koni akafite hewalɛ yɛ fɔfɔi ni nyɛɛɛ awo yibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is my maize producing tall stalks with big leaves, but the cobs are missing seeds or are mostly empty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ baai wuji shi ŋmãa lɛ bɛ ŋmeii loo bei pii lɛ ehiɛ efolo lɛ?

english: Empty cobs usually mean poor pollination. If heat or drought hits when the maize tassels shed pollen, the silks dry up before catching pollen, leaving gaps where seeds should have formed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ pollination lɛ ehiii. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo latsaa loo hɔmɔ mli beni ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ Siliki lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani eŋɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii baa he ni esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ afee lɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield less harvest when I plant many seeds very close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa ŋmaa bibioo beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kome mli lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots and leaves compete fiercely with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving every individual plant too weak to produce a heavy yield.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkpa nii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds stunting my crops so heavily during the first four weeks after planting compared to later in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ ni mikɛduɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto be lɛ naagbee fã lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings grow slowly and have small roots. During the first month, aggressive weeds easily steal the water and nutrients the young crops desperately need to establish themselves.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ daraa blɛoo ni amɛyɛ shishifãi bibii. yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli Jwɛi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ aná lɛ oya.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field make my next maize crop grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi-ŋmei srɔtoi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa waa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special bacteria in their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a free natural fertilizer for the following maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa tsei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ nɛɛ.

english: Is it really necessary to dig out old tree stumps before planting my crops, or can I just plant around them?
ga: Ehe miihia ni atsa tsei akutsei momoi. Ojie lɛ kpo dani odu loo okɛwooo mli? Aloo manyɛ madu nii yɛ he fɛɛ he.

english: Removing tree stumps prevents underground roots from blocking your crop roots, stops termites and root diseases from breeding, and makes it much easier to plow and weed your farm evenly.
ga: Stump ni ajieɔ lɛ baatsi shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anaa. Ekpaa termites kɛ shishifãi helai ni baa lɛ naa. Ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ oootsu oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okɛ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do my crops struggle to grow properly if I leave big shade trees standing in the middle of my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji mishi tso agbo ko ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Big trees block the direct sunlight your crops need to manufacture food, and their large root systems suck up most of the water and soil nutrients before your small crops can reach them.
ga: Tsei wuji tsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii lɛ naa. Ni amɛshishifãi wuji lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo dani ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe.

english: How does loosening hard ground with a plow or hoe help my seeds grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Breaking up hard soil creates soft space for delicate roots to spread easily, while allowing rainwater and air to sink deep into the ground where the crop roots can absorb them.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni akuɔ mli lɛ haa he ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo baa koni shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting plantains alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi kookoo tsei bibii lɛ adu kookoo tsei lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that burn under full direct sun. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, sheltering the young cocoa until it grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ambrela. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara waa.

english: Leaves curl up to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps the plant conserve water during extreme heat until the cool evening air arrives.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛtoɔ nu yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ lɛ baashɛɔ.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant seeds very close together to fit more on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ miŋmɔ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: When crops are packed too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stems and very small or poorly formed fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛfeɔ bibii waa loo amɛhiɛ bɛ amɛhe nɔ.

english: Why do weeds manage to grow so much faster than the food crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants naturally adapted to steal water, light, and nutrients rapidly, which is why they will easily overcrowd and starve your crops if you do not clear them early.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Enɛ hewɔ ni amɛyiɔ obɔ kɛ hɔmɔ ni gbeɔ onibii lɛ kɛji okɛ jwɛi shwieee nɔ mra lɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale yellow even though we have been receiving good rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ? Nɛgbɛ nugbɔ miinɛ yɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, which crops need to stay dark green and healthy, indicating that your soil needs manure or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, ni he hiaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee eŋɔli ni mli edɔ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does cassava stay green through the dry season while my maize wilts and dies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei hiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ? Beni mi ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep, thick tuber roots that store water and nutrients deep underground, whereas maize has shallow roots that dry out quickly when rain stops for a long time.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni mli tse ni kɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, egbiɔ oya.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows specific pests to build up; rotating different crops allows the soil to recover.
