ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ehe feɔ fɛo.

english: I cleared a huge piece of land to plant maize this season, so why am I getting fewer bags of harvest than my neighbor who has a much smaller farm?
ga: Mijie he ko ni da koni madu ŋmãa yɛ be nɛɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ ŋmaakpamɔ kotokui fioo nɔ fe mikutsoŋnyo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ bibioo kwraa lɛ?

english: A large harvest depends on how well you care for your crops—such as proper plant spacing, weeding, and soil feeding—rather than just having a big piece of land. A smaller, well-managed farm often produces far more grain than a large farm that doesn't get enough attention.
ga: Nikpamɔ babaoo damɔ bɔ ni okwɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ ohaa, tamɔ bɔ ni okɛ tsei lɛ toɔ he ni sa lɛ nɔ. jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ niyenii ni ayeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaaná shikpɔŋ wulu Okwaafoi bibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛwo ŋmaa babaoo fe okwaafoi wuji ni akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: If I plant many maize seeds very close together in one hole, won't that give me more crops and a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa ŋmeii babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ, Ani no haŋ maná yibii babaoo kɛ ŋmaa babaoo?

english: When seeds are crowded together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak stalks and empty cobs. Giving each seed its own space allows it to grow strong and yield full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua dumɔwui lɛ anaa lɛ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛhe lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ená hewalɛ ni ekɛ dumɔwui akui ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crops turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop is hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, or that too much water is trapped around the roots. Feeding the soil with manure or the right fertilizer will help the leaves turn green again so the plant can grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye oŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ nitrogen. aloo nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better to scatter fertilizer across the whole farm or put it right next to each crop?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaagbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashwã ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ loo akɛto he ko? Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko?

english: Placing fertilizer directly near the base of each crop ensures the roots absorb the food immediately, rather than feeding the weeds in between rows or getting washed away by heavy rain.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso fɛɛ tso shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ niyenii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha jwɛi lɛ aye niyenii yɛ ŋmeii ateŋ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ baaho amɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and produce very little food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo ni niyenii fioo pɛ woɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm by stealing the water, fertilizer, and sunlight that your crops need. Clearing weeds early gives your crops all the food they need to produce a good yield.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: What is eating the leaves and center of my young maize plants, leaving small green droppings behind?
ga: Mɛni ji mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai kɛ amɛteŋgbɛ ni ayeɔ, ni eshiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: That is likely the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that destroys the growing center of young maize. Finding them early and using the right pest control methods will protect your crop before the farm is ruined.
ga: No baafee Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni fiteɔ ŋmei bibii lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ. Amɛtaomɔ mra Ni gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akuɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe lɛ baaye abua ni abu onibii ahe dani akpata amɛhiɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just buy cheap maize from the local market to use as seeds for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miheɔ ŋmãa ni jara waaa kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ koni mikɛtsu nii akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Market grain is meant for eating and may carry diseases or come from varieties that don't yield well. Certified seeds bought from approved dealers are specially bred to fight off local diseases and yield much more food.
ga: Afee jarayeli ŋmaa lɛ koni aye ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela aba loo ejɛ ŋmaa srɔtoi ni wooo yibii kpakpai amli. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni jaa ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛwu eshi helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii babaoo aba.

english: I have planted maize on the exact same piece of land for three years, but now the plants refuse to grow tall. What is happening?
ga: Mikɛ afii etɛ edu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Shi amrɔ nɛɛ tso lɛ kpooɔ akɛ ebaada kwraa. meni ba?

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot every season drains the soil of its nutrients and builds up pests. Rotating your land with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas helps restore the soil's strength.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai aba. Oshikpɔŋ lɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei baatsake lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops dry up so quickly whenever the rain stops for just one week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ lɛ baakpa otsi kome pɛ lɛ?

english: Soil without organic matter cannot hold onto water. Adding compost or leaving old crop stalks on the field helps lock moisture in the ground so your plants can survive short dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ ahiɛ nu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli loo ashi tsei momoi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ otsei lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell the exact time my maize is ready for harvest so it doesn't spoil in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni ŋmãa lɛ esa akɛ akpa koni ekafite yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Maize is ready when the outer husks turn dry and brown, and the grains become hard with a small dark spot at their base. Harvesting at this stage prevents mold, decay, and insect damage in the field.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaaná ŋmɔlɔ bibii diji yɛ amɛshishi. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ ŋmeii anaa. ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli

english: Why do some of my pawpaw trees flower heavily but never bear any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Pawpaw plants have different sexes; male trees produce flowers with pollen but will never grow fruit themselves because only female or bisexual trees can develop fruits after being pollinated.
ga: Pawpaw tsei lɛ yɛ bɔlɛnamɔi srɔtoi. Tsei hii fɔ̃ɔ kɛ pollen. Shi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewoŋ yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni ji yei loo tsei ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ yakayaka nii lɛ pɛ baanyɛ awo yibii yɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do I need insects like bees around my farm for my watermelons to form proper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maná kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni bɔle miŋmɔ lɛ he koni watermelon lɛ awo yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Watermelons have separate male and female flowers on the same vine, so bees are needed to carry pollen from the male flower to the female flower so the fruit can develop.
ga: Watermelon yɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi yɛ wain tso kome nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni wuobii aŋɔ pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi hii amli kɛya fɔfɔi yei anɔ koni aduawai anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: What will happen if I keep planting cassava on the same piece of land year after year without giving the soil a break?
ga: Mɛni baaba kɛji akɛ midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ efooo?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the ground and causes pests to build up in the soil, leading to smaller roots and poorer harvests over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii kɛ kpamɔ ni ehiii kwraa baa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do extension officers advise that I let part of my farmland rest and bush over for a season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ maha miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ekomɛi ajɔɔ amɛhe ni mafolɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be kome lɛ?

english: Letting land lie fallow gives the soil time to naturally rebuild its organic matter, restore lost nutrients, and break pest cycles so future crops can yield more.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ashiɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatswa ehe nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Tsɔɔmɔ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ ekoŋŋ ni ofo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli bɔni afee ni wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and bent when I plant them in hard, unplowed soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuko nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are underground stems that need soft, loose earth mounds to expand smoothly; hard soil restricts their expansion and causes misshapen roots.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsiɔ shweremɔ naa ni efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants take so long to produce a bunch if I leave all the small shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ ŋmeii kɛji mishi ŋmeii bibii ni bɔle tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Multiple suckers compete with the main plant for water and nutrients, so removing extra shoots allows the primary stem to grow faster and produce larger bunches.
ga: Suckers babaoo kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ ada oya ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants turn light yellow after they produce their first batch of peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse beni amɛjie amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ pepper kuu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fruit production consumes large amounts of plant food, so yellow leaves indicate the plant has exhausted its soil nutrients and needs compost or fertilizer to keep producing.
ga: Yibii ni anáa lɛ biɔ tsofa niyenii babaoo. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ eye niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. ni ehe miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛya nɔ amɛfee nii

english: Why is it important to prune old, dry branches off my tomato plants after a heavy harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ tomato tsei aniji ni egbi ni egbɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni mli wa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Removing dead or old stems stops the plant from wasting energy on dying parts and directs food toward generating fresh leaves and new flower buds.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni egboi loo ni egbɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ yɛ tsei ni miigboi lɛ anɔ. ni ekɛ niyenii baa koni ekɛfee baai heei kɛ fɔfɔi heei

english: How can I tell that my maize is completely ready for harvest just by looking at the plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ kɛha kpamɔ kɛtsɔ tso lɛ kwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: Maize is mature when the silk at the top of the cob turns dark brown and dry, and the outer husks turn yellow-brown instead of green.
ga: Abɛi eda kɛji siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ yiteŋ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi. ni kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown and soft before they are fully grown during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo dani amɛdaraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in cold, overly shaded, and damp conditions where moisture stays on the pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ. Shade babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is missing nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to build strong, green leaves. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure around the plant base will help bring the dark green color and healthy growth back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛbaabɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsuɔ nii waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Weeds steal vital plant food, water, and sunlight away from your main crop. Even when rain is abundant, your crops will starve if weeds are allowed to drink up the soil nutrients first.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ tsei aniyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ waa moŋ Oŋmɔshi nibii hu baaye hɔmɔ kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ jwɛi gbɛ ni amɛnu niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Which way should I face cassava stem cuttings when pushing them into the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ ootsi lɛ kɛmiiya shikpɔŋ lɛ, te esa akɛ otsu ŋmei niji ni oookpa lɛ he nii oha tɛŋŋ?

english: Look closely at the small buds or 'eyes' along the cassava stick; those buds must point upward toward the sky. If you plant the stick upside down, the roots will struggle to form and your yield will be very small.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘hiŋmɛii’ ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ he lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ nakai ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu nine lɛ hiɛ shi lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baaná naagba yɛ amɛfeemɔ he ni oyibiiwoo lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to generate energy that builds large underground tubers. Elevating the vines on stakes keeps the leaves away from damp ground diseases and gives them maximum sunlight to produce bigger yams.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa lɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ buɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ, ni ehaa hulu la ni fa babaoo baa koni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die during the bright dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn under direct sunshine. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to your cocoa gives them a living umbrella that keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ Cocoa masɛi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ naa hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: If too many shoots grow around one main plantain stem, they all fight for the same water and soil nutrients, resulting in small fruit bunches. Keeping only one or two strong shoots ensures the main stem gets enough food to grow large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ, single main trunk Tsofai fɛɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa anáa aduawai bibii. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni etsɔ panicle agbo ni tsii.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by hot weather, irregular watering, or insect attacks. Covering the soil with dried leaves as mulch to retain water and spraying with natural neem extract helps save the flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ Akɛ mulching ni akɛ baai ni egbi tsuɔ nii akɛ mulching ni akɛtoɔ nu he. Ni kɛ́ akɛ neem ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: What is eating hole patterns into the central leaves of my maize, and how do I stop it?
ga: Mɛni ji bɔ ni ayeɔ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, caterpillars that hide inside the central funnel of maize plants. You can suppress them by applying crushed neem seed powder or approved organic insecticides directly into the center funnel early in the morning.
ga: Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Obaanyɛ otsi amɛnaa kɛtsɔ neem dumɔwui ni atswa lɛ powda loo tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni okɛbaawo ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects called whiteflies that spread crop viruses. Spraying the undersides of the leaves early with soapy water or neem oil helps clear the insects before the whole field gets infected.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli Ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra Nu ni akɛ saamɔ loo neem fɔ tsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni ejie helai lɛ dani jɛmɛ fɛɛ aba.

english: How do I know if the soil is wet enough to plant my seeds after the first rainfall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often tricks farmers because only the top layer of dirt gets wet while deep soil remains dry. Dig down about the depth of your hand; if the soil at that depth forms a wet ball when squeezed, it is safe to plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ lakaa okwaafoi ejaakɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ mli shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni sũ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi. Tsɔɔmɔ shi kɛyashi onine mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nakai mli lɛ feɔ bɔɔlu ni efɔ kɛji akɛ ashɛre lɛ. Abaanyɛ adu lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen fertilizer or isn't getting enough water to pull nutrients out of the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmãa loo enáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are there small holes and caterpillar droppings inside the leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii afɔfɔi?

english: This is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, a common pest in Ghana that eats the growing center of maize plants and must be controlled early to prevent severe leaf damage.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm caterpillar, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ. ni esa akɛ akudɔ mra Koni akafite baai lɛ waa

english: How do I tell which end of a cassava stem should face up when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole ŋmei tso lɛ naagbee ni esa akɛ okwɛ nɔ kɛ́ oodu lɛ?

english: Look closely at the tiny raised leaf buds along the stem; they should point upwards toward the sky so the leaves can sprout in the right direction.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. ni teɔ shi ebɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni baai lɛ adara yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight with their leaves, which gives the plant the energy it needs to form large tubers under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfee bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Cocoa flowers fall off if they are not pollinated by tiny insects like midges, or if the tree experiences water stress during dry weather.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii shwieee amɛ nɔ, loo kɛji tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Leaving too many suckers creates competition for water and soil nutrients, which makes the main tree produce smaller bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ekɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ plantains bibii bibii.

english: Pepper leaves curl when the weather is extremely hot to save water, or when tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites are attacking the underside of the leaves.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛbu nu he. aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tutua baai lɛ ashishi.

english: This is called blossom end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium, usually caused by irregular watering during fruiting.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: How does planting groundnuts on my farm help my next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen gas from the air and traps it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the land for future crops.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even if I add fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that steal the applied fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your crops, effectively starving them if not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni akɛfataa he kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aye hɔmɔ kɛji ajieee amɛ mra.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them provides the living shade and moist microclimate they need to survive until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Enɛ baaha amɛná shade kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, a major nutrient needed for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the plants regain their deep green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ adara Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Why does my crop harvest get smaller every year when I plant cassava on the exact same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ faaa daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows plant diseases to build up. Rotating your cassava with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil and keeps it healthy.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsei ahe helai aba Ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake ŋmeii Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eye ebua ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with small caterpillars hiding inside the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛtee tso lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They feed inside the growing tip of the plant, which weakens the maize stalk and reduces yield if not treated early with recommended organic or chemical pest controls.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ tsei amli ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ. ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra. kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Waterlogged soil starves the roots of oxygen and promotes fungal root rot, so planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ náa lɛ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii fiteɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences stress from hot dry winds, irregular watering, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the flowers set healthy fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees bend and fall over when the fruit bunches start getting large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbee shi beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have woody trunks or deep taproots, so heavy fruit bunches pull the plant off balance. Supporting the main stem with strong wooden Y-props prevents wind and weight from snapping the plant before harvest.
ga: Plantains bɛ tso shishifã loo shishifã ni mli kwɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ baaha tso lɛ akafee nɔ ni ja. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni tamɔ Y ni akɛ tso ni wa fee lɛ fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ muji naa koni ekakumɔ tso lɛ dani akpa.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants compete for sunlight, ground moisture, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak stalks that produce very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa onáa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ tsei bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why should I clear weeds early while my crops are still small seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ mra? Be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji dumɔwu bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have small roots and struggle to compete with aggressive weeds for water and soil food. Clearing weeds early ensures your young crops get all the nutrients they need during their critical early growth phase.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkɛ jwɛi ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ abɔi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei bibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ mra be mli dalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow when I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain after a long dry spell is often followed by several hot, dry days that dry out the soil. Planting too early causes seeds to sprout and then wither; it is safer to wait until the rains become consistent.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ, gbii babaoo ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagboi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and leaves that dry out easily under intense heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a living umbrella that protects the tender cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ he kroko. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ebaada.

english: When seeds are crowded together, the plants end up fighting each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong stems and produce larger yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua dumɔwui lɛ anaa lɛ Tsei lɛ baawu koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ hewalɛ, ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Does the size of the seed yam I plant affect the size of the tubers I harvest?
ga: Ani bɔ ni sweet potato dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ dara ha lɛ saa bɔ ni ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ dara ha lɛ he?

english: Yes, larger and healthier seed yam pieces contain more stored food energy. This extra energy helps the plant build a strong leaf and root system early on, leading to larger harvested tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, sweet potato fãi ni dara, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baaná niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo ni ato. Hewalɛ ni fa nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmaa baai kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa mra. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ baafee wuji.

english: Yellow lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green foliage. Applying manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the growing stage helps restore the plant's health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I alternate planting maize with cowpeas on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil. Legumes like cowpeas naturally pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, enriching the soil for future crops.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Legumes, tamɔ cowpeas, jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni akɛ sɛɛnamɔ afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why is it wrong to apply fertilizer when my farmland is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli be mli ni he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mli egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Plant roots can only absorb nutrients when they are dissolved in moisture. Applying fertilizer to bone-dry soil can scorch the roots and leave nutrients trapped where the plant cannot use them.
ga: Tso shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛji akɛ amɛshwie ŋmɔtɔ mli pɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wui yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ ni eha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahi hei ni tsei nyɛŋ amɛkɛtsu nii yɛ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when stressed by irregular watering, extreme heat, or a shortage of soil nutrients. Maintaining steady soil moisture helps flowers stay attached and form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants twisting and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is commonly caused by tiny pests like whiteflies or thrips transmitting plant viruses. Using natural sprays like neem oil early helps manage these insects before they damage the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem fɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ atsu nii dani amɛfite onibii.

english: Cassava roots suffocate and rot when water collects around them for too long because excess water blocks oxygen. Planting cassava on raised mounds or soil ridges allows extra rain to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni nu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Etsɛ tsɔ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa naa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha nugbɔshiimɔ aya hiɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to sprout quickly and steal moisture, sunlight, and fertilizer from young crops. Clearing them within the first three weeks gives your crops a fair chance to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛju ŋmɔtɔ, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why can't I just plant my maize seeds in hard, uncleared soil without ploughing first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieee nɔ ko nɔ ko nɔ ni mikɛtsuuu nii klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Ploughing breaks up hard soil so seeds can easily push roots deep into the ground to find water and nutrients. Planting in hard, unworked soil starves the young roots and causes weak, stunted plants.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ashɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ oya koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ, ni ebaaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why is it important to make raised mounds or ridges before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni awo gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow underground and need soft, loose earth to expand smoothly. Mounds also keep water from settling around the roots, which prevents the tubers from rotting.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Gɔŋ lɛ hu tsiɔ nu naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa bulb lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why should I measure proper spacing between my cassava stems instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu gbɛ ni sa ni kã ŋmei tsei ateŋ lɛ he moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close, their leaves block sunlight from each other and their roots compete for soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food to build large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛfee bulbs agboi ni tsii.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and turn yellow when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and lose water rapidly under intense sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains beside them creates a cool environment that protects young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnuɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa.

english: Why do my tomato plants need to be tied to wooden stakes as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ akpɛtɛ tsei ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Tomato stems are weak and bend under the weight of heavy fruit. Staking lifts the branches off the damp ground, preventing soil-borne diseases, fruit rot, and pest attacks.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkotoɔ yɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ ashishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsei niji kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ, aduawai ni fiteɔ, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa.

english: Why does water standing around the base of my pepper plants make them wilt and drop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni bɔleɔ pepper tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Excess water drowns the roots by cutting off oxygen in the soil. Without air, roots rot and can no longer pump water and nutrients to the leaves, causing the plant to wither.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛpomp nu kɛ niyenii kɛya baai lɛ amli dɔŋŋ. haa tsei gboiɔ

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants turn pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abele tso baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. Adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant build healthy green leaves needed to form big maize ears.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni he hiaa koni amɛwo ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up tightly during hot afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi waa yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl inward to reduce surface area and minimize water loss during intense heat. It is a natural protection mechanism showing the crop is experiencing heat and water stress.
ga: Akɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni nu ni fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ aba shi. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii jieɔ lɛ kpo kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ kɛ nu mli haomɔ mli.

english: Why do my cowpea plants drop their flowers before producing pods during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ shi dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water is scarce, cowpea plants drop their flowers to save energy and water for survival instead of spending resources on producing seeds.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa lɛ Cowpea tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii baatsu nii ni akɛwo dumɔwui

english: Why do my cassava leaves develop sticky spots and turn twisted when small white flies gather under them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛshishi lɛ?

english: Whiteflies suck plant sap and spread viral diseases that alter leaf growth. Consulting an extension specialist early helps identify the pest and protect your crop yield.
ga: Whiteflies lɛ nuɔ tso mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ muawai amli ni tsakeɔ baai lɛ adalɛ amɛshwãa. Kɛ mɔ ko ni le ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nii lɛ agba sane mra Ebaaye ebua ni ana tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa onibii amli lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if a farm chemical I bought at the market is safe to spray on my food crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛshwieɔ miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Always check the bottle label for an official regulatory approval mark and clear instructions for food crops. If the label is missing, in a language you cannot read, or recommended by an uncertified seller, consult an extension officer before spraying, as improper chemicals can ruin crops or poison harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tɔ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛha mla lɛ hegbɛ okadi kɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni mli ka shi faŋŋ kɛha niyenii tso lɛ. Kɛji akɛ nɔ ni aŋmala nɔ nii lɛ bɛ lɛ, no lɛ eyɛ wiemɔ ko ni onyɛɛɛ okane. loo mɛi ni hɔ̃ɔ nibii ni bɛ odaseyeli lɛ jieɔ yi lɛ Bi mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ dani okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofai ni esaaa baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii loo akpa tsofai fɔji.

english: Why should I avoid mixing two different farm chemicals together in the same sprayer tank?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai enyɔ ni akɛfutuɔ he yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Mixing random farm chemicals can cause dangerous reactions that render the products ineffective, lock sprayer nozzles, or create toxic combinations that burn crop leaves instantly.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmɔ mli trukaa lɛ baanyɛ aha nibii ni yɔɔ oshara aba ni haa nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ. lock spray nozzle loo afee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shãa tso lɛ baai amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How long do I need to wait after spraying my crops with pest chemicals before I can safely harvest and sell them?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani manyɛ makpa ni mahɔ̃ɔ shweshweeshwe?

english: Every agricultural chemical has a required waiting period, called a pre-harvest interval, usually printed on the bottle. Waiting for the full duration—often between 7 to 14 days—allows the chemical to break down so the food is safe for human consumption.
ga: Okwaayeli mli tsofai fɛɛ yɛ be ni akɛmɛɛɔ ni ale lɛ akɛ dani kpamɔ be lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, akalaa enɛ yɛ tɔ lɛ nɔ. Be muu lɛ fɛɛ ni mɛɔ Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ (bei pii lɛ, gbii 7 kɛyashi 14 teŋ) haa tsofai lɛ fiteɔ koni niyenii lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha adesa niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or the ground is overly waterlogged, which prevents the roots from taking up nutrients needed to grow strong green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli tsɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ.

english: What causes my pepper flowers to fall off before they can turn into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper aduawai?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience extreme heat, lack of water, or when tiny pests like thrips attack the flowers, causing the plant to protect itself by dropping the blooms.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa, nu bɛ, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips tutua fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ buɔ ehe kɛtsɔ shigbeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why are my bean plants growing plenty of large leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing thick green stems and leaves rather than producing flowers and crop seed pods.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ baama ŋmeii kɛ baai ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwuhi.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die suddenly even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is often caused by bacterial wilt or soil fungus, which attacks the roots and blocks the plant's internal tubes from moving water up into the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Enɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ mli tsɔnei lɛ anaa koni nu akaya ŋwɛi kɛya baai lɛ amli.

english: Is it safe to spray chemical weedkillers directly near my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe?

english: No, young cocoa seedlings have soft green leaves and stems that easily absorb weedkiller drift, which will stunt their growth or kill them completely. It is best to weed around young seedlings by hand.
ga: Dabi, Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ amɛshishifãi ni nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni hoɔ nu lɛ nɔ lɛ oya. Enɛ baaha dalɛ akpa loo egbo kwraa. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ afeɔ enɛ ji ni ajie jwɛi fɛɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. dumɔwui kɛtsɔ nine nɔ

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground after heavy rain falls on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water sits in the soil for too long, cutting off oxygen to the roots and creating ideal conditions for fungal rot. Planting on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. ni ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaa shihilɛ ni sa kɛha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: How does spraying my crops in the middle of a hot, sunny afternoon affect the plants?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ saa tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Spraying during peak heat causes liquid chemical drops to evaporate rapidly before doing their job, and the intense sun combined with chemical residue can scorch and damage the crop leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tsofai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaaha tsofai ni ji nu lɛ atsɔ oya dani amɛtsu nii. Ni hulu la ni naa wa ni kpɛɔ waa ni akɛ tsofai ni eshwɛ lɛ fata he lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai ni efite nii.

english: How can I tell if the crop seeds I saved from last harvest will actually grow before I spend time planting them in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ dani maŋɔ be kɛdu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can test your seeds before planting by wrapping a small sample of 10 seeds in a damp cloth for a few days; counting how many sprout shows you their strength and helps you know if the whole batch is good to plant.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka dumɔwui lɛ okwɛ dani odu kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni ji nɔkwɛmɔnɔ bibioo ko ni oookɛwo mama ni mli efɔ mli lɛ nɔ. gbii fioo komɛi Tsei lɛ akanemɔ baatsɔɔ bo bɔ ni amɛhe wa ha, ni ebaaye ebua bo ni ole kɛji esa akɛ odu fã muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What does an extension officer mean when they tell me a seed is 'strong' or 'weak'?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ tsɔɔ kɛ amɛkɛɛ mi akɛ dumɔwu ko ‘he wa’ loo ‘ebɛ hewalɛ’?

english: A strong seed has enough stored energy to sprout quickly and push through hard soil, while a weak seed grows slowly, struggles to break out of the soil, or dies easily after sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ato koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui bibii lɛ daraa fiofio lɛ. Ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni efo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo egbo mlɛo yɛ shweremɔ sɛɛ

english: How do I perform a simple germination test at home using wet paper or cloth?
ga: Miiya ni miyafee kwɛ̃mɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Te aaafee tɛŋŋ afee yɛ shia kɛtsɔ wolo loo mama ni efɔ nɔ?

english: Place ten seeds on a damp cloth or paper, roll it up loosely, and keep it in a cool spot while keeping it moist. After several days, unroll it to count how many seeds sprouted shoots—if eight sprout, you have an 80% germination rate.
ga: Okɛ dumɔwui 10 awo mama loo wolo ni mli efɔ nɔ. Roll up loosely. Ni okɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ yɛ be mli ni okwɛɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Gbii komɛi asɛɛ lɛ Gbelemɔ mli koni okane dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ayibɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui 8 kwɛ̃ lɛ, oyɛ 80% ni kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why are my planted seeds taking so long to come out of the ground compared to my neighbor's crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋnyo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Seeds take a specific number of days to sprout depending on soil moisture, planting depth, and seed vigor; dry soil or weak seeds will delay sprouting compared to healthy seeds planted in moist ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baa he gbii babaoo dani amɛ kwɛ̃. Edamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aduɔ lɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ dumɔwui ahewalɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ baaha shweremɔ asɛɛ afo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ he.

english: How many days should I wait after planting before I know my seeds failed and I need to replant?
ga: Kɛ́ midu nii lɛ, gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ koni male kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbo ni ehe miihia ni adu ekoŋŋ?

english: Most common crops like maize or beans sprout within 4 to 10 days in warm, moist soil; if nothing comes up after two weeks, the seeds have likely failed to germinate and you should replant.
ga: Tsei ni afɔɔ namɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa, kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii 4 kɛyashi 10 mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Kɛji otsii enyɔ eho ni nɔ ko bako. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ ni esa akɛ odu amɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for my soil to stay wet right after I sow my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ beni midu midumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Water acts as a signal that wakes up the living part inside the seed and softens the outer shell so the young shoot can easily burst out and grow into the soil.
ga: Nu lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ okadi ni haa wala yibii ni yɔɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ teɔ shi ni ehaa kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ anyɛ ajɛ mli oya ni amɛdara kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: I planted my crops last week but none of them sprouted, what could have killed the seeds under the soil?
ga: Midu tsei lɛ otsi ni eho lɛ shi dumɔwui lɛ eko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ. Mɛni baanyɛ agbe dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Seeds can fail to sprout if they were old, stored in hot conditions, buried too deep in the soil, or ruined by soil pests and rot due to overly dry or flooded ground.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji amɛgbɔ. Kɛto he ko ni mli edɔ. Afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ Aloo shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ amɛ ni amɛgboiɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ.

english: Does keeping my seed bags in a hot kitchen or shed ruin their ability to sprout when the rainy season starts?
ga: Ani dumɔwui kotoku ni akɛtoɔ ŋtayaa ni mli edɔ loo dumɔwui atoohe lɛ fiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yes, storing seeds in hot or damp places drains their strength and reduces their lifespan, causing them to rot or fail when you plant them in the field.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ hei ni edɔɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ aba shi ni ebaaha wala be aba shi. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ loo efiteɔ kɛ́ odu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Does how deep I bury my seeds in the dirt affect how well they come up?
ga: Ani bɔ ni afu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ aha lɛ baaná amɛkwɛ̃mɔ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, burying seeds too deep wastes all their energy before the shoot reaches the sunlight, while planting too shallow causes seeds to dry out or be eaten by birds.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni aaafu tsɔ lɛ baafite amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi loo okpoi aye amɛ.

english: Is it fine to plant tiny or wrinkled seeds, or should I only pick the big, smooth ones?
ga: baadu dumɔwui bibii loo dumɔwui ni ekpɔtɔ Aloo esa akɛ ohala dumɔwui wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛ?

english: It is best to pick full, undamaged seeds because tiny or wrinkled seeds often lack enough energy to sprout strongly and will produce small, weak crop plants.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohala dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ ni efiteee yɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahewɔ. Aloo, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni egbɔjɔ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ waa. ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ aba.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to grow green and healthy. It can also happen when heavy rains flood the field and drown the roots, preventing them from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha ŋmɔ ko nɔ nu ni eha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi. Tsi niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ naa

english: Can I put fresh chicken manure directly onto my vegetable crops as soon as I clean the coop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ hee awo mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛji mitsumɔ tsina tsina lɛ mli pɛ?

english: No, fresh chicken manure is too strong or 'hot' and will burn your crop roots and stems. You need to mix it with dry plant material and let it decompose (compost) for a few weeks until it cools down before putting it near your plants.
ga: Dabi, tsina ŋmei hee mli wa tsɔ loo ‘edɔ’ ni ebaashã tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi. Esa akɛ okɛ tso mli nibii ni egbi afutu mli ni oha egbo (compost) otsii fioo komɛi kɛyashi ebaajɔ dani okɛma otsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly and the plants stop growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni tso lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by a plant virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies, or by extreme heat and drought. The plant curls its leaves to conserve water or as a reaction to the insect damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni haa tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ mli Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he loo akɛ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ kɛji kooloi fiteɔ amɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot in the ground when water gets trapped around them for too long, causing fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps heavy rain drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nu ta shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Kasava ni aaadu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aya. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Peppers drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot and dry, or when the plant doesn't get enough water. High heat prevents the flowers from forming seeds, so the plant drops them to save its energy.
ga: Peppers shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni tso lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo dumɔwui. No hewɔ lɛ tsei shwieɔ dumɔwui koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many flowers, but most of them drop off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔii babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed extra flowers they cannot support, but losing almost all flowers happens during dry spells or when there are no tiny midges (beneficial insects) around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Kakao tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi krokomɛi ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kpo. Shi nɔ ni miihe ashɛ fɔfɔii ni laajeɔ lɛ fɛɛ baa yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛ. (Kplukai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ) lɛ ebɔle amɛhe koni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when the plantain bunch gets big, even without strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ jwɛi lɛ miida kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko bɛ po lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over when tiny pests called nematodes or stem borers eat and weaken the underground roots. Without deep, healthy roots anchored in the ground, the tree cannot support the weight of the heavy plantain bunch.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji kooloi bibii ni ale amɛ akɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ yeɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa bɛ ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Tso lɛ nyɛŋ atere plantains akuu ni tsii lɛ muji.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves get full of tiny holes just a few weeks after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani otsii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Tiny holes in cowpea leaves are caused by small chewing pests like beetles and caterpillars that eat young leaves. Protecting the leaves early allows the plant to catch sunlight and produce a good yield.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ cowpea baai lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ niyenii tamɔ ladybugs kɛ caterpillars ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ. Baai lɛ ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛgbekɛbiiashi lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do weeds on my land grow much faster and greener than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miida oya ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔji fe tsei ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to survive poor soil and harsh weather. They greedily steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight faster than cultivated crops, which is why clearing them early is essential.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛkɛ hiɛjoomɔ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie tsei lɛ amli mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia.

english: Why are my harvested yams starting to sprout shoots inside the barn before the next planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miije shishi ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yams sprout when the air inside the storage barn becomes warm and humid, signaling to the yam tuber that rainy season is near. Keeping your yam barn well-ventilated and cool keeps the yams dormant longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ okadi kɛya sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anɔ akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ebɛŋkɛ. Kɛ́ oha o-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-sweet potato lɛ ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in an open field without any big trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to strong direct sunlight, which dries out their leaves faster than their tender roots can absorb water. Planting them alongside taller crops like plantains or shade trees shields them from the harsh sun and keeps the surrounding air moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and drying up from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to build green leaves. When nitrogen is low, the plant steals it from older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni eha baai eŋɔli aba. Kɛ nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ juɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting groundnuts or beans in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni mi ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans have tiny beneficial bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps the nearby maize grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei bɛ bacteria fioo ko ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when there is too much rain for several weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛ babaoo otsii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to stay alive and healthy. When soil stays flooded for a long time, water fills all the air spaces, suffocating the tubers and causing rot-causing fungi to multiply rapidly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu be kakadaŋŋ Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ he lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ babaoo oya.

english: Yam plants make food for growing tubers underground through their leaves catching sunlight. Staking lifts the vines high off the wet ground so the leaves get maximum sunshine and stay safe from ground-based leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ feɔ niyenii amɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaa ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ koni eha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ baa helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into tomatoes when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomatoi beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Very high temperatures damage the pollen inside tomato blossoms, making it dry and unable to fertilize the flower. When fertilization fails, the plant sheds the flower to conserve water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Ehaa egbiɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ awo mli. Kɛji fɔmɔ nii lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small shapes and stopping new growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe bibii bibii lɛ? ni ekpaa dalɛ hee

english: Leaf curl is caused by tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap out of young leaves, or passing a virus to the plant. The damage causes the leaf tissues to grow unevenly and twist up.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baa bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ baa. loo ekɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ yaa tsei anɔ Nɔ ni efite lɛ haa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ daraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do people cover the ground around crops with dry leaves and grass during the Harmattan dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ baai kɛ jwɛi ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic matter, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops the harsh wind and hot sun from evaporating soil water, keeping the roots cool and moist for longer.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akafee nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it a bad idea to throw dry chemical fertilizer on my farm when the ground is dry and rain hasn't fallen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mashɛrɛ tsofai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ashwie miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni mibɛ eko lɛ? He ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Fertilizers must dissolve in water before plant roots can drink them. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn crop roots and waste the nutrients, as heat causes them to evaporate into the air before rain comes.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afite. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ haa tsei ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I leave too many small shoot suckers growing around one main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ tso wulu kome he lɛ?

english: Every extra sucker competes with the main mother stem for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Cutting away extra suckers leaves enough food for the main stem to produce a single, large plantain bunch.
ga: Sucker krɛdɛɛ fɛɛ sucker kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli kɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tso lɛ yitso lɛ ni efee plantains akui wuji.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight and high heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and preserves soil moisture so the seedlings can establish healthy roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ aná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why should I make mounds or ridges for cassava and yams instead of planting them on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afee gɔji loo ŋshɔkei kɛha ŋmei kɛ ŋmei? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mounds and ridges loosen the soil, giving root crops the room they need to expand and produce big tubers. Raising the soil also prevents water from settling around the roots and causing them to rot during heavy rains.
ga: Gɔji kɛ ŋshɔkei lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni aduɔ lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni nu akabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eha amɛgboi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: What will happen if I plant my crops very close together to fit more on my piece of land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: When plants are crowded, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in weak, thin plants with very low crop yields instead of a bigger harvest.
ga: Kɛ tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa yɛ yibii babaoo ni amɛwoɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow strong, so adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost will restore healthy growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Will planting cowpeas between my maize crops steal nutrients away from the maize?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ teŋ lɛ baaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, leguminous crops like cowpeas actually take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which feeds the neighboring maize plant and keeps weeds down by covering the bare soil.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, ni ejieɔ jwɛi kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni ehaa nɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Is it best to apply fertilizer at the exact same time I place seeds in the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be kome too mli?

english: Seeds already contain enough stored energy to sprout on their own. Placing strong chemical fertilizer directly on seeds can burn them, so it is better to wait until the plant sprouts its first true leaves.
ga: Dumɔwu lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛto momo koni lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ekwɛ̃. Tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛshã, no hewɔ lɛ mɛ kɛyashi tso lɛ baaná eklɛŋklɛŋ baai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ.

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on young foliage. Applying targeted treatments early in the morning or late evening directly into the leaf funnels destroys the pests before they kill the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ wo baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaakpata tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ hiɛ dani egbe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I grow tomatoes on the exact same spot of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously allows soil-borne pests and diseases that target tomatoes to build up in the ground. Rotating tomatoes with crops like maize or cassava breaks disease cycles and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tsɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tomato ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni efo helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ amli, ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed their blossoms and drop flowers when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni egbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers as a survival tactic to conserve water during heat and drought. Spreading dry grass around the plant base as mulch keeps the soil cool and moist, helping the flowers stay on and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi akɛ wala gbɛtsɔɔmɔ koni akɛto nu he yɛ dɔlɛ be mli, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi. Mulch kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni oooha tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How do I choose the best stem cuttings from a harvested cassava plant for my next planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala niji ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ mi-cassava tso ni mikpa lɛ mli kɛha mi-dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Select mature, healthy stems from the middle section of a harvested plant, cutting pieces about 20 to 30 centimeters long with clear raised buds. The middle portion contains enough stored energy to sprout roots and shoots quickly.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni eda, ni he wa kɛjɛ tso ni akpa lɛ teŋgbɛ. Afolɔ mli bibii aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 30, ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni etee ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ. Teŋgbɛ fã lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni ato ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do some of my seeds float when I soak them in a bucket of water before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi shwieɔ nu nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo nu baagi mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Seeds that float in water are usually hollow, light, or damaged by pests, meaning they will not sprout well. The heavy seeds that sink to the bottom are healthy and filled with nutrients, so planting only the sunken seeds gives you strong, healthy sprouts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni hoɔ yɛ nu mli lɛ mli ewo bu, amɛ kpɛɔ, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui efite amɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni tsii ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishi lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni efo lɛ pɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha oná dumɔwui ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I test if the maize seeds I saved from my last harvest are still good to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ hi lolo kɛha dumɔ?

english: Take ten seeds from your batch and place them on a wet paper or cloth in a warm area for three to five days. If at least eight of them grow roots and green sprouts, your seed batch is strong enough to plant in your field.
ga: Okɛ dumɔwui nyɔŋma kɛjɛ o-batch lɛ mli ni okɛwo wolo loo mama ni efɔ nɔ yɛ he ko ni mli edɔ gbii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ. Kɛji kɛ hoo lɛ tsei kpaanyɔ yɛ shishifãi kɛ ŋmɔji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ odumɔwui akuu lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells to protect themselves and save water. It is a natural self-defense habit, and the plant will grow fresh green leaves as soon as the rains start again.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛbu nu he. Eji adebɔɔ su ni haa mɔ he fãa. Ni tsei lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Maize leaves curl inward during the heat of the day to hide their surface area from the sun and cut down on water loss. Once the temperature drops in the late afternoon or evening, the leaves uncurl and spread back out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be mli koni amɛkɛha hulu lɛ akashɛ amɛhe ni amɛha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi yɛ shwane loo gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã sɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper and tomato plants drop their flowers without forming any fruits when it gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ yibii ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High daytime temperatures dry out the pollen inside the flowers, preventing them from forming fruit. Adding mulch around the base of the plants keeps the roots cool and helps the flowers stay attached.
ga: Gbi mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ gĩɔ. tsiɔ yibiiwoo naa Mulching around Shishitoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my yams on high mounds of soil instead of flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu sweet potatoes yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mounding loosens the dirt so the yam tuber can grow long and thick without pushing against hard soil. It also protects the roots from rotting when heavy rains flood the field.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oootswa lɛ baaha egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ waa. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eyi ŋmɔji lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the tall trees around my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji ni bɔle miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn quickly in direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving taller trees like plantains or shade trees protects the young cocoa plants from heat until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya kɛji hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Ashiɔ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, koni ebu kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he kɛjɛ latsaa he kɛyashi ebaada ni ená hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo nɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpea in my maize field make the soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Cowpea belongs to the legume family, which absorbs nitrogen gas from the air and transfers it into the soil through its roots. This naturally enriches the land with free fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmei tso ko ni shwieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops dry up and burn if I plant them right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshãa kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season often moistens only the top layer of dry, hot soil without soaking deep down. If a hot week follows without rain, the delicate new seeds burn in the warm dirt, so waiting for steady rains keeps the seedlings alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni ekɛwooo mli. Kɛji otsi ni mli edɔ lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ Dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shãa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi wala mli.

english: Why do armyworms prefer to attack my young maize plants instead of my mature ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms sumɔɔ ni amɛtutua mi ŋmã tsei bibii lɛ moŋ fe mi ŋmã tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young maize plants produce tender, soft leaves at the center of the stem that are easy for young caterpillars to chew and digest. Checking the central shoots early lets you spot pests before they ruin the growing point of the plant.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaaye ni amɛye nii. Kwɛmɔ middle balance lɛ mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai dani amɛfite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: How do I know if my harvested crop is good enough to be sold for export to other countries?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mikpamɔ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ koni mikɛya maji krokomɛi anɔ?

english: Export markets require crops to meet strict standards regarding size, cleanliness, and freedom from disease or chemical residue. Buyers and extension officers inspect these standard qualities before approving crops for international export.
ga: Jarayeli hei ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ biɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashɛ shishitoo mlai ni mli wa ni kɔɔ amɛdalɛ, amɛhe tsemɔ kɛ helai loo tsofai ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe lɛ he. Mɛi ni heɔ nibii kɛ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ kwɛɔ nɛkɛ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɛɛ amli dani amɛkpɛlɛɔ nibii ni aduɔ lɛ anɔ koni akɛya maŋsɛɛ.

english: Why are crop buyers offering me low prices or rejecting my harvest at the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ jara ni baa shi haa mi loo amɛkpooɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Low prices or rejections usually happen when crops have insect damage, mold, or were harvested at the wrong time. Proper drying, careful handling, and good pest control preserve crop quality so buyers pay higher prices.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, jara ni baa shi loo nɔ ni baa shi lɛ baa kɛji kooloi bibii, ŋmeii, loo akpa tsei yɛ be ni esaaa mli. Egbimɔ ni sa ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, mɔ ni heɔ lɛ woɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe no.

english: Why should I change my old traditional way of farming to adopt these new recommended practices?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake mi blema okwaayeli gbɛi lɛ koni mikɛ nifeemɔi heei ni ajieɔ yi nɛɛ atsu nii?

english: Traditional methods often drain soil nutrients over time, leading to lower yields. Modern recommended practices help protect the soil, control pests better, and produce larger harvests on the same size of land.
