ga: Kusum gbɛi lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii mli nibii lɛ hoɔ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi. Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nifeemɔi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛbaatsu nii ni afee nibii ni afee lɛ agbo yɛ he ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How long will it take for a new crop variety to give me good harvest yields after I plant it?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani tso henɔ hee ko baawo yibii kpakpai beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are bred to grow faster and resist local diseases, with many seasonal crops maturing in 3 to 4 months so you can harvest and sell sooner than traditional varieties.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai. Nibii babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ be mli lɛ shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, no hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okpa ni ohɔ̃ɔ oya fe blema nibii srɔtoi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow and wilting before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, is getting too much or too little water, or has root damage from soil insects. Adding the right fertilizer or improving soil drainage usually fixes this.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nu babaoo loo fioo ni ooona? loo shishifãi ni kooloi bibii efite yɛ sũ lɛ mli Bei pii lɛ, sũ lɛ mli nu ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ loo sũ lɛ mli nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why is my crop growing tall green leaves but failing to produce heavy yield or leaves worth selling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kakadaji shi enyɛɛɛ ewo yibii babaoo loo baai lɛ jara wa akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer makes them spend all their energy growing leaves instead of developing strong foliage or fruit. A balanced fertilizer containing phosphorus and potassium helps the crop produce valuable yields.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee baai loo aduawai ni mli wa lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni phosphorus kɛ potassium yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ yibii ni jara wa.

english: How does heavy rainfall affect the leaves and quality of my cash crops during the growing season?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa mi shika ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rain can wash nutrients out of the soil and create damp conditions where fungal diseases spread quickly on crop leaves. Creating drainage channels helps excess water flow away from plant roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ aba ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei lɛ ahe oya. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ he gbɛi ni afee lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli.

english: What can I do if my farmland no longer produces high yields like it used to years ago?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo tamɔ afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ dɔŋŋ?

english: Continuous farming empties the soil of essential food for plants. Rotating your crops with beans or groundnuts and adding manure or compost restores vital nutrients to tired soil.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ ni efite lɛ mli.

english: What happens to my crop if I use chemical fertilizer instead of animal manure?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii najiaŋ?

english: Chemical fertilizer releases nutrients quickly to boost plant growth right away, while animal manure improves the soil's ability to hold water over a long time. Using both together gives fast growth and healthy soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii oya koni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kooloi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ daa oya, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops dry up and wither even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ egbi ni egbi eyɛ mli akɛ mishwieɔ amɛ nu daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops wither if the soil cannot hold moisture, if the roots are damaged by underground pests, or if watering is done during the hottest part of the day when water evaporates before reaching the roots.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baagbi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efite shishifãi lɛ Aloo kɛji akɛ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, nu lɛ shwieɔ shi dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct sunshine. Tall trees provide necessary shade and maintain soil moisture, protecting fragile cocoa leaves from burning during their first few years of growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Buu kookoo baai ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛ la he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni amɛdaraa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily before the fruit is even ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani aduawai lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have very shallow roots and carry heavy bunches at the top. When strong winds come, the weak root system cannot hold the weight, so you need to support the stem with wooden stakes or bamboo poles.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa kɛ fɔfɔi ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ba lɛ, shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ tsɔne ni tsii lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ tsei loo ŋmei afĩ tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off instead of turning into fruits during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of moisture cause stress to tomato plants, leading them to drop their blossoms to save energy rather than producing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ aba amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: What is causing small worms to chew holes inside the leaves and stems of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmei gbekɛ lɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the growing funnels of corn plants and feed on young leaves, requiring early targeted spraying or hand-picking to manage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Esa akɛ ashɛre nɔ loo akɛ nine aŋɔ klɛŋklɛŋ dani anyɛ atsu he nii.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from under the leaves and spreading plant viruses, which slows down fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛgbɛɔ tso lɛ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ baaha tso yibii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why are black spots spreading across my cassava leaves and causing them to drop early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji miigbɛ eshwa mi-cassava baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ ni eha amɛmiigbee shi oya lɛ?

english: Black leaf spots are caused by fungal diseases that spread during warm, humid weather, especially when leaves remain wet for long periods due to poor air circulation between closely planted crops.
ga: Fungal hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ dɔlɛ, fɛ̃i be mli lɛ kɛ baa ediŋŋ baa. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ baai lɛ shwie shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni hoɔ yɛ tsei ni adu amɛ bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa lɛ ateŋ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn turning pale yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient corn needs to grow strong green leaves and produce healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni yɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the field for too long without draining, roots suffocate, leading to fungal rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Ebaanyɛ eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Planting the same crop continuously removes the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting and turning soft while stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo kɛ́ akɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams react to heat and humidity as a sign that it is time to grow again. Warm air and poor ventilation inside the storage barn trigger the tuber to break dormancy and use its stored energy to sprout.
ga: Sweet potatoes tsuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i he nii akɛ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni yɔɔ shĩa lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ akumɔ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃.

english: How do I know when my oil palm fruits are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-oil palm yibii lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Oil palm fruits are ready for harvesting when you notice some of the ripe reddish-orange palm nuts naturally loosening and dropping to the ground from the fresh fruit bunch.
ga: Mu tso yibii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni oyɔseɔ tso yibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ekomɛi ni miijɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe amɛmiijɛ tsei akui heei lɛ amli ni amɛmiigbee shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my oil palm trees produce flowers but never grow any actual fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ekomɛi fɔɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛwooo yibii diɛŋtsɛ kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Oil palms need balanced water and nutrients to develop female flowers; under stress or poor nutrient conditions, the tree produces mostly male flowers which do not bear fruit.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ he miihia mu tsei lɛ koni amɛná fɔfɔi yei. yɛ shihilɛi ni haa mɔ haoɔ loo niyenii ni esaaa mli Tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii babaoo ni wooo yibii.

english: If I do not trim or prune my tree crops, will they produce more fruit?
ga: Kɛ mifolɔɔɔ tso lɛ loo mifolɔɔɔ lɛ Ani tso lɛ baawo yibii babaoo?

english: Unpruned trees actually produce less quality fruit because overgrown branches block sunshine from the rest of the tree and consume nutrients that should go into fruit production.
ga: Tsei ni ashi amɛ ni afolɔko amɛhe lɛ baawo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ tsei niji ni eda fe nine lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ hei krokomɛi lɛ naa. tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni esa akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ aduawai afeemɔ mli

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, which can happen when heavy rains wash nutrients away from the root zone.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aba mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even when the top leaves look healthy and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ waa eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ moŋ?

english: When soil has excessive nitrogen or is too hard and compact, the plant puts all its energy into growing tall leaves and stems above ground instead of expanding tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black while still hanging on the trees?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal infection that thrives when humidity is high and there is poor airflow around the trees during rainy periods.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni daa kɛji hulutsoo be babaoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Tsei ehiii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees dropping their tiny pods before they can grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? dani eda

english: Cocoa plants naturally shed young pods when they experience stress from heat, drought, or poor soil nutrients to save energy for the plant's overall survival.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbii bibii lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ mli baa lɛ he. Koni akɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha tsei fɛɛ ashihilɛ.

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can absorb it, so they temporarily droop to conserve internal moisture.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ be kukuoo ko bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi emli.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over so easily once the fruit bunch starts growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and heavy upper stems, making them prone to tipping over when wet soil weakens root anchorage under heavy fruit weight.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ ŋwɛi tso ni tsii. Enɛ haa su ko baa shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he ni ekɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baa shi kɛ́ aduawai lɛ tsii.

english: How does constant heavy rain affect the fruiting of my palm trees?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ saa ŋmei tsei awomɔ he?

english: Continuous rain washes away pollen and keeps pollinating insects inactive, leading to poor flower fertilization and smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ hoɔ pollen lɛ he ni ehaa pollenbii lɛ tsuuu nii. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ ni aduawai lɛ baafee kui bibii.

english: Why are my maize crops dying on one side of my land while growing fine on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fã kome shi eshwereɔ yɛ fã kroko lɛ?

english: Different parts of your land can have different soil types, depth, and drainage levels. Soil in lower or rocky areas may hold too much water or lack key nutrients, causing crops on the same field to behave differently.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ hei srɔtoi baanyɛ aná shikpɔŋ henɔi, emlibotemɔ, kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ srɔtoi. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi loo hei ni tɛi yɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahiɛ nu babaoo mli loo niyenii titrii ni he hiaa bɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ.

english: How do I know if my piece of land is suitable for growing cassava profitably?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he?

english: Cassava needs loose, well-drained soil so its root tubers can expand easily. Land that gets waterlogged easily will cause the cassava roots to rot, leading to poor yields and financial losses.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia Cassava. koni eshishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agbo. Enɛ haaa nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni shika hu afite.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies are sucking nutrients from the leaves, or that the soil is low in nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies miinu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli. aloo etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during light rain and wind before the fruits mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ be mli fioo dani yibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow close to the soil surface and are naturally shallow. When heavy bunches grow, the plant becomes top-heavy, so supporting the stem with bamboo sticks helps hold it up.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ daa ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ, ni amɛmli ekɔɔɔ he eko. Beni tso lɛ da lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei fĩ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: Why am I getting very few tomatoes even though my plants have plenty of leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ tomato fioo ko pɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mitsei lɛ yɛ baai babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes tomato plants spend all their energy growing tall stems and leafy green leaves instead of producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: Why am I making less money from my yam harvest than my neighbor who has the exact same farm size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mináaa shika fioo kɛkpaa ŋmeii fe mikutsoŋnyo ni ŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ tamɔ nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ?

english: Profitability depends on seed quality, proper planting distance, and timely weeding rather than land size alone. Healthy seed yams and weed-free fields yield larger tubers that sell for higher prices.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ ni anáa lɛ damɔ bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ hi ha lɛ nɔ. He ni sa ni akɛduɔ nii kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be ni sa mli Fe shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ kɛkɛ Sweet potato dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔji ni jwɛi bɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni ahɔ̃ɔ kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: Why do fall armyworms keep destroying my young maize leaves every farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms lɛ fiteɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ daa be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Armyworm moths lay their eggs on young maize leaves, and the warm weather allows caterpillars to hatch quickly and eat the tender growing center of the plant.
ga: Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii baa bibii anɔ. Ni kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ oya ni amɛyeɔ tsei lɛ ahe hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea flowers drop off before turning into bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ pea ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers drop mainly due to insect pests like flower thrips attacking the buds, or because the crop is experiencing heat and water stress during flowering.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ cowpea fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips ni tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ. aloo akɛni tso lɛ miina dɔlɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ hewɔ.

english: It is safer to wait for two or three steady rains because the ground beneath the surface stays dry after the first rain, which can scorch and dry out young seeds.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ fioo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ baagbi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui bibii lɛ ni amɛgbi.

english: Why does leaving weeds near my crops reduce the size of my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, stealing resources the crops need to grow big and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, ni juɔ nibii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe awa

english: Why do people tell me to plant plantains alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ madu plantains yɛ mimasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow very fast and have large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil moist, giving young cocoa trees the protection they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Enɛ haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ buɔ amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I loosen and clear my farm land before the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔjie he ni wɔduɔ nii yɛ lɛ ni wɔjie wɔhe kɛjɛ mli dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Clearing and loosening the soil before the rains start allows rainwater to soak deep into the ground rather than washing away topsoil. This makes it easier for crop roots to spread out and absorb water quickly once seeds are planted.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ajieɔ lɛ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ moŋ fe ni eeefɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tso shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛmu nu oya kɛji amɛdu dumɔwui.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant groundnuts or beans on my field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pulls natural nitrogen out of the air and puts it back into the earth. Planting them first naturally enriches the soil, providing free nutrients for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amɛhaa niyenii kpakpai ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa tsei ni akɛyeɔ kooloi babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young corn plants turning pale yellow from the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize crop is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Adding well-rotted manure or the right nitrogen fertilizer gives the plants the strength they need to stay green and produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahi shi akɛ ŋmɔji ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight to produce energy for tuber growth. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground, which prevents leaf diseases and ensures the plant directs its energy into growing larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant is stressed by severe heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the root area helps the plant hold its flowers so they can turn into healthy fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni etsɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ

english: Why do experienced farmers spread dry grass or leaves around the base of pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ shwieɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi amɛshwieɔ he lɛ? Pepper tso shishi?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that shields the soil from hot sun, holds in water so you water less, stops weeds from growing, and eventually turns into fertilizer.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi haa lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehiɛɔ nu hewɔ lɛ okɛ nu fioo pɛ haa. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why do tiny caterpillars leave ragged holes in my maize leaves and hide inside the central stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ shĩɔ bu ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ mi-abele baa lɛ mli ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. They feed on young shoots, but detecting them early and applying organic treatments like neem leaf extract or recommended control sprays saves your corn plants.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ. Amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii. Shi kɛji akɛ ayɔse amɛ mra ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ nii tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ atsu nii. Ebaaye ebua ni o-corn tsei lɛ akafite.

english: How can I tell that my cassava crop is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Cassava is usually mature around 9 to 12 months after planting. You will know it is ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and shed, and the ground around the base of the main stem begins to swell and crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shɛɔ shweremɔ he aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso titri lɛ shishi jeɔ shishi efuɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why does leaving weeds in my crop field make my harvest so small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ?

english: Weeds act as aggressive neighbors that steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Removing weeds early ensures all the food and moisture in the soil goes straight to your crops.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ akutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ basabasa ni juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants get scorched easily when exposed to direct heat. They need shade crops like plantain or cassava planted nearby to shield them from excessive sunlight and help the soil retain moisture during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ fe nine lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Do I really need to put wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni makɛ tsei afata he koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yes, staking yam vines lifts the leaves toward the sunlight so the plant can capture light efficiently. This helps the plant produce more food, which directly results in larger underground tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he koni tso lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ la jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is my maize growing thin and pale green instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize requires nitrogen to develop strong, dark green leaves. Pale or yellowish leaves usually mean the soil is low in nutrients, which can be fixed by applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or compost.
ga: Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ená baai ni mli wa, ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do people tell me that planting cowpeas or beans will make my soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni midu lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have tiny organisms on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the dirt. When the plant dies, that natural fertilizer stays in the ground to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi anɔ ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso lɛ gbo Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the small shoots growing around my main plantain stem to stay?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi plantain tso titri lɛ ji nɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Too many extra shoots compete with the main plantain stem for food, water, and sunlight. Keeping only one or two strong shoots (suckers) ensures the main plant gets enough energy to produce a large bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo ni fata he lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ shishifã kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ (ŋmeii) lɛ to lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ niji wuji.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes often drop flowers when they suffer from sudden dry spells or intense heat. Watering them regularly at the root level without splashing the leaves helps keep the flowers healthy so they can turn into fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni baa trukaa loo latsaa ni naa wa miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni akɛshwieee baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhe waaa aahu akɛ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny pests like mites or thrips sucking the juice from young leaves. Spraying the plants with neem oil or organic pest controls gets rid of these insects and allows new leaves to expand normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebaaha baai heei lɛ agbɛ ashwã bɔ ni sa.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center of the plant and feeds on young leaves. Applying targeted treatments or wood ash into the whorl early on helps protect the growing crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni akɛtsaa hela loo tso sũ ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are ready to be harvested under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the main stem begins to crack open as the tubers swell underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso titri lɛ shishi jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb ko daa yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why does rice need so much water standing in the field compared to my other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa yɛ miŋmɔ mli kɛ akɛto miŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Rice plants can grow in wet soil, and keeping standing water in the field prevents weeds from growing and competing with the rice for light and soil nutrients.
ga: Omɔ tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Ni nu ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ haaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ akaŋ koni amɛná la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to make food and grow green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛfeɔ niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do older farmers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my field before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them first naturally enriches your soil with free fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔ mra baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and root diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating crops gives the soil time to recover and breaks the lifecycle of diseases.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shishifãi ahe helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe ni efoɔ helai ashihilɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot handle strong direct sunlight or harsh winds. Planting plantains or shade trees alongside them creates a canopy umbrella that protects the young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow tall and thin with very small cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛmli ŋmeii bibii waa yɔɔ mli lɛ beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow strong stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it important for me to remove the side shoots growing out of my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie sɛɛ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing side shoots prevents the plant from wasting energy on extra leaves. This allows the tomato plant to direct its food and water into growing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ, no tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu nɔ koni amɛwo aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting under the ground during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rain fills the soil with excess water, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing them to drown and rot. Planting on raised soil mounds or ridges helps drain excess water away from the roots.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni haa efoɔ nu mli ni egboɔ Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔnaa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass acts like a blanket that keeps the hot sun from evaporating water out of the dirt, helping your plants stay hydrated longer between waterings.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ teŋ.

english: Holes in the center leaves of young corn are typically caused by caterpillars, like the Fall Armyworm, eating the soft green tissue. Checking your field early allows you to control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. He lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ lɛ dani efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants fall off without producing any peppers when the weather gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, pepper plants drop their flowers as a natural defense mechanism to save water and energy. Providing light shade or adequate water can help reduce flower loss.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni amɛkɛbuɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni sa ha lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Can too much rain actually hurt or kill my crops?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui loo efite amɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, excessive water fills the air spaces in the soil, suffocating crop roots so they cannot breathe or absorb nutrients, which leads to root rot and plant death.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni tsei lɛ gboiɔ.

english: How can I protect my cassava farm from getting destroyed when heavy rains flood the land?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ abu ŋmɔji ahe kɛjɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛ waa nɛ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges and digging small drainage channels allows excess rainwater to flow away safely, keeping root tubers out of stagnant water.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ loo gɔŋji lɛ anɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ he gbɛ bibioo ko ni afoɔ Enɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa kɛjɛɔ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plant leaves start turning yellow after several days of non-stop heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii babaoo ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni ekpaaa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes away essential plant food like nitrogen deep into the ground where roots cannot reach it, causing the leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Besides plenty of rain, what else do my crops need to give me a good harvest?
ga: Kɛfata nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he lɛ Mɛni hu he hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii aná ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Rain alone is not enough; crops also require good sunlight to make food, healthy soil nutrients, proper weeding, and protection from destructive insects and diseases.
ga: Nugbɔ pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Tsei hu hia hulu la kpakpa koni amɛfee niyenii. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpai Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi kɛ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly during the rainy season when there are many cloudy days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ daa blɛoo waa yɛ nugbɔ be mli ni atatu gbii babaoo yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Plants use sunlight like fuel to make their food; when heavy clouds block the sun during long rainy periods, plants cannot produce enough energy to grow fast.
ga: Tsei kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii tamɔ fuɛl kɛhooɔ nii. Beni atatui ni mli tse tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Tsei nyɛŋ afee hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛdara oya.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my maize crop right before a big rainstorm comes?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmãa mli dani nugbɔ wulu ko aba?

english: No, strong rainstorms will wash the fertilizer off the farm into streams before the soil absorbs it, wasting your money and effort.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔji amli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa faai amli dani shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Eheɔ bo shika kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ.

english: Why does the dark top layer of my farm soil wash away whenever it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil left exposed to heavy raindrops easily breaks apart and washes away; leaving crop residues or planting cover crops keeps the soil tied down and protected.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni ashiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ oya ni nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Tsoi ni afolɔ ashwie shi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi ni ebuɔ he.

english: Why do white or dark spots suddenly spread on my pepper leaves during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ loo ediŋŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High moisture and constant humidity create perfect conditions for fungal diseases to multiply and spread quickly across wet crop leaves.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ haa ŋmeii helai babaoo ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya yɛ tsei ahe baai ni efɔ lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops wither so quickly when a sudden dry spell hits right after weeks of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji hɔmɔ ba trukaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa otsii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When water is always available at the surface during heavy rains, plant roots stay short and lazy; when the ground suddenly dries, those short roots cannot reach deeper moisture.
ga: Beni nu yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Tso shishifãi lɛ yɛ kuku ni amɛhe waaa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ trukaa lɛ Nakai shishifãi kukuji lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why is building ridges and mounds better for tuber crops like yam than planting on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaafee ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii beni aduɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mounds loosen the soil so roots expand easily into big tubers, while also lifting the crop higher so water drains off instead of pooling around the roots.
ga: Gɔji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ bulb agboi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, wo tso lɛ nɔ koni nu lɛ ajɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and intense heat. Without shade crops like plantain or taller canopy trees to shield them, strong sun burns their leaves and dries out the soil, causing the leaves to turn brown and drop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ plantains loo tsei bibii ni kɛlɛ bɛ lɛ, hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ asasu ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale yellow starting from the bottom of the stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen gives plants their healthy green color and helps them grow tall, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-decomposed manure will fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli, amɛnáa hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: How can I tell when my cassava is ready to harvest underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the ground around the base of the main stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baa ko edara kɛ́ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso wulu lɛ shishi miije shishi egbɛ eshwa.

english: Yams need loose, uncompacted soil to expand and grow large tubers easily. Making mounds softens the earth, prevents standing water from rotting the seed yam, and makes it much easier to harvest later.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa oya ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji. Gɔji ni afeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Etsiɔ nu ni ekã shi lɛ naa koni ekaha sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ agbo. Ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts in the same field alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ ŋmei masɛi?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them with maize feeds the soil naturally, helping your maize grow stronger without relying entirely on purchased chemical fertilizers.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ehiɛ wa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni aheɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are tiny insects causing my pepper leaves to curl up, and how do I fix it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids or thrips feeding on the underside of the leaves. Spraying the plants with a mild soapy water solution or soapy neem oil mixture helps clear these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ Neem fɔ loo samla ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Why do the bottom tips of my tomatoes turn black and rot before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, often brought on by irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and adding wood ash or lime to the soil helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ mli baa Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli ni ejaaa lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni okɛ tso sũ loo lime fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil can absorb moisture before the sun gets too hot, reducing water loss from evaporation and keeping leaf surfaces dry enough to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ adɔ tsɔ. Ha nu ni laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi ni oha baa lɛ hiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ hela naa.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoots growing at the bottom of my plantain stand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: If too many sucker shoots grow at once, they compete with the main plant for food and water, leading to smaller plantain bunches. Pruning back excess suckers leaves more energy for the main stem to produce a big, heavy cluster.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ shikome lɛ Nakai ŋmeii lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yitso lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and lie waiting in the dry soil. They germinate immediately with the first rain to steal light, water, and soil nutrients, which is why clearing weeds early is crucial to give young crops a head start.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛmɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ pɛ koni amɛju la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛná sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and moisture until the young cocoa trees are strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa kɛyashi kookoo tsei bibii lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build strong green leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore their dark green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the field. Rotating maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei tsakeɔ Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efo adebɔɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli.

english: Why do groundnut stems bend downward and push into the soil after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts flower above the ground, but the actual nuts mature underground. After pollination, the stems naturally elongate and push into the soil so the pods can develop in a safe, moist environment away from heat and pests.
ga: Peanuts fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ, shi anɔkwa nuts daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. yɛ pollination sɛɛ Tso lɛ yitsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Ekɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akabɔ he.

english: Why do I need to clear the ground around my yam mounds and give the vines tall wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe bahia ni majie he ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ he lɛ yɔɔ lɛ, ni mawo wain tsei lɛ anɔ mafee tsei kakadaji koni makwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to manufacture the food required to swell their underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves into the sun and off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and encouraging bigger yam tubers.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ baa helai anaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ahe hewalɛ.

english: If too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they compete for nutrients and water, resulting in thin plants and small bunches. Removing extra suckers leaves enough food for the main plant to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso kome he lɛ, Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ kui bibii. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop mainly when the plant is stressed by extreme dry heat or lack of water in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the blossoms stay on the plant and turn into peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my ripe tomatoes crack open on the skin while still attached to the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ miitswa yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ be mli ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ tso lɛ he lolo lɛ?

english: Tomatoes crack when they take in a lot of water suddenly after a dry spell. The flesh inside grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing it to split. Watering plants evenly prevents sudden swelling and cracking.
ga: Tomato baatswa kɛji akɛ aha lɛ nu babaoo trukaa yɛ be ni nu egbi lɛ sɛɛ. Mligbɛ fãji lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. cause disintegration Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekafu trukaa ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack due to the expanding tubers beneath the surface.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops immediately after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely hardy and rest in the soil waiting for moisture. When the rains start, they absorb water rapidly and sprout faster than crop seeds because they are adapted to wild soil conditions.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ lɛ Eŋɔɔ nu oya ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya fe dumɔwui ejaakɛ ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ kpãa gbee.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn red or pink before turning green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ etsuru loo pinki dani amɛfeɔ eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves produce red pigments as natural sunscreen to protect their soft tissues from intense sunlight and insect damage. As the leaf hardens and matures, it develops chlorophyll and turns green to start making food for the tree.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe. Kɛji baai lɛ mli wa ni amɛdara Ebaafee klorofil ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ebɔi niyenii feemɔ kɛha tso lɛ.

english: Why do some of my small cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ tsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo yɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in excess moisture and shade. The fungus attacks the pod, turning it black, drying it out, and stopping it from growing into a healthy mature cocoa pod.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Fungus tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ. Ehaa efeɔ ediŋŋ, egbiɔ ni ehaaa eda ni etsɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni eda kwraa.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are getting too much shade from the bigger trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo tso lɛ miiná hulutsoo babaoo kɛmiijɛ tsei wuji amli?

english: When cocoa trees get too much shade, they grow tall, thin, and stretched out searching for light. Their leaves will be dark green, but the tree will produce very few flowers and pods compared to trees receiving balanced light.
ga: Kɛji kookoo tsei ná hulutsoo babaoo tsɔ Kookoo tso lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, efeɔ mlɛo ni ekpãa ehe kɛtaoɔ la. Ebaai lɛ yɛ eŋɔli diŋŋ. Shi tso lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ. Kɛ akɛto tsei ni naa la ni ja lɛ ahe

english: Why does my cassava grow many bushy leaves but leaves me with small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is heavily watered, the cassava plant puts most of its energy into growing upper branches and leaves instead of storing starch underground. Balanced nutrients encourage root growth over foliage.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo awo mli nu babaoo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ŋmei baato shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eniji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Niyenii ni ja lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa yɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why must I put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much direct sunlight as possible to produce the food needed to swell the tuber underground. Staking also keeps the foliage off the hot ground, preventing rot and leaf diseases.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he miihia sweet potato baai babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ aba. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ baa helai anaa.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that can be weakened by soil pests like nematodes or rot. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, the root base cannot support the top weight without wooden stakes for extra balance.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo ŋmeii baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Ejaakɛ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsii. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni akɛtswaa ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni haa ŋwɛi ŋtayaa lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ bɛ lɛ, shishitoo lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ ŋtayaa ni tsii fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tip and moves down the middle stem is a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen. The plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaa ni eyaa shi kɛyaa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why are my maize stalks breaking easily near the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ fãa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ masɛi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Stalk breakage is usually caused by stem borer caterpillars that eat into the main stem from the inside, making the plant hollow and weak so that wind easily knocks it over.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ titri lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tso lɛ fãa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ bu ni egbɔjɔ bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ atsɔ mli oya.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely high daytime temperatures, dry soil, or lack of insect pollinators. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant hold onto its blooms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛna haomɔi, tamɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo fɔfɔi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ baa lɛ bɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotten while still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni edara lolo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit. It usually happens when watering is irregular, preventing the plant roots from continuously absorbing calcium from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ tso yibii ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be.

english: What should I do when my farmland becomes worn out and crops stop growing well?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ efite ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekpa shweremɔ?

english: When land gets tired, it lacks essential nutrients. You can restore it by letting the land rest (fallowing), planting nitrogen-fixing crops like beans or groundnuts, or adding organic manure and compost to rebuild soil fertility.
ga: Kɛ́ sũ lɛ etɔ lɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ mli. Obaanyɛ okɛku sɛɛ okɛtsu nii kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha ejɔɔ ehe (ni egbee shi lɛ nɔ), ni ooodu nibii ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. Aloo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my maize yield get smaller every year if I keep planting it in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating your maize with crops like cassava or cowpeas helps keep the soil balanced and healthy.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. They need shade from larger forest trees or food crops like plantains to protect them from heat and retain soil moisture during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ koo mli tsei wuji loo niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains amli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to cut off some branches from mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfolɔ kookoo niji ni edara lɛ ekomɛi lɛ?

english: Pruning removes excess or diseased branches so sunlight and air can reach the inner parts of the tree. This reduces dampness that causes black pod disease and encourages the tree to direct its energy into producing more pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni fa fe nine loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ayashɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛ black pods babaoo aba.

english: Why is it bad to plant my crop seeds very close together to fit more on my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ madu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow strong and produce large yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know the exact right time to sow my seeds at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: It is best to plant after the soil has received two or three heavy, steady rains. Sowing too early during unreliable light showers can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up if the rain stops.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni naa wa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli Tsei ni anyɛɛɛ ahe aye lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Yellow, twisted leaves are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. You can prevent this by planting disease-resistant cassava stems provided by agricultural agencies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli nitsumɔhei kɛhaa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: How do weeds harm my crops even if I give the plants enough water and manure?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui kɛji miha amɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa po?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and aggressively steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight from your plants. They also serve as hiding spots for insects and diseases that attack your farm.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli kɛ hiɛdɔɔ. Amɛji hei hu ni kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni tutuaa oŋmɔ lɛ teɔ shi yɛ.

english: Why should I buy seed maize from agro-dealers instead of using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Certified seeds from dealers are specially bred to resist diseases, tolerate dry spells, and produce much higher yields than saved seeds, which lose their strength and vigor over generations.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni jɛ mɛi ni jaa lɛ adɛŋ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni ato ni baafite hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli

english: When is the right time to put fertilizer on my farm so the rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not during heavy rainfall. Placing the fertilizer in a small ring around the plant base and covering it lightly with soil stops rain from washing it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli Kɛbɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ, okɛ sũ aha nɔ fioo. Enɛ baaye abua ni nugbɔ akashwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantain plants grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key nutrient maize needs to stay green and build strong stalks. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps solve this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli ni etswa ŋmãa ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when they suffer from high heat or irregular watering. When stressed by extreme heat or drought, the plant drops flowers to conserve energy rather than growing fruit.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ kpe Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: How do I know if my farm land is suitable for planting yams?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ?

english: Yams need deep, loose, and well-drained soil free of large rocks so the tubers can grow long and smooth. Soils that trap water will cause the yam roots to rot underground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ he miihia sweet potato. Ehe kɛjɛ tɛi wuji ahe Bɔni afee ni yitso lɛ atsɔ kakadaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni hiɛɔ nu lɛ haa eshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Curling and pale leaves are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The virus prevents the plant from producing enough food, leading to smaller tubers.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Virus tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings fall over and die right after sprouting in the seedbed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called damping-off, which attacks tender stems when nursery soil is kept too wet and overcrowded. Keeping the seedbed moist but not waterlogged prevents it.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dampening off, ni tutuaa tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ oha dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ mli edɔ shi nu ehiɛɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my cowpea pods have tiny holes in them before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea pods lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? dani akpa kpamɔ

english: Tiny insects called pod borers lay eggs inside the flowers. When the eggs hatch, the young worms eat their way into the developing pods to feed on the growing seeds.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ pod borers lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Beni ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ lɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ niyenii kɛyaa ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli koni amɛye dumɔwui ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested plantains ripen and turn soft so quickly before I can sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ shwereɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo oya dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Harvested plantains produce a natural gas that speeds up ripening. Heat accelerates this process, so storing harvested bunches in a cool, shaded, and well-ventilated area helps keep them fresh longer.
ga: Plantains ni akpaa lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli la ni haa amɛshwereɔ oya. Dɔlɛ haa nifeemɔ nɛɛ yaa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ to he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu yɔɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my sweet peppers turning black and rotting on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell peppers lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, usually caused by inconsistent soil moisture during dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni bɛ shiŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Can I save seeds from the corn I bought at the market to plant for my next crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Market corn is often hybrid grain, meaning seeds saved from it will grow into weaker plants with much smaller yields. Buying certified seeds ensures strong plants and a high harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baatsɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni wooo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ baaha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo aba.

english: Why do my seeds take so long to sprout when the soil feels cold and wet after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ ni edɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cold or waterlogged soil slows down seed germination because seeds need warmth and air in the soil to wake up and start growing roots properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ fioo ejaakɛ dumɔwui lɛ he miihia hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛte shi ni amɛje shishifãi lɛ akwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ shishi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant three or four maize seeds together in the exact same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii etɛ loo ejwɛ feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the young plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and tiny cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa.

english: How does covering the bare soil around my crops with dry leaves help them grow?
ga: Mulching bare soil around Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ baai ni egbi koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil cool and moist under hot sun while stopping weeds from growing quickly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ oya.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen food in the soil, or the soil has too much water preventing the roots from feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen niyenii bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli bɔ ni no hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛye nii.

english: Why are my plantain leaves rolling up tightly during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees roll their leaves in intense heat to trap moisture and protect themselves from losing too much water.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni amɛfiteɔ fe nine lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Extreme sun heat, sudden heavy rain, or lack of soil food stresses tomato plants, causing them to drop flowers to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa mli nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa Aloo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ ashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ashwie koni akɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or whiteflies sucking the plant sap and spreading viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Amɛmuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: Cassava tubers rot under the ground when heavy rain leaves excess standing water in the soil, allowing harmful microscopic fungi to attack the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha nu babaoo tsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do I see ragged holes in my maize leaves and small dirt-like waste inside the plant leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu ni etse ehe yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli kɛ jwɛi bibii ni tamɔ muji lɛ? Yɛ baa lɛ mli

english: This leaf damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a pest that burrows into the center of the young maize plant to eat fresh leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm caterpillars, ni ji ŋmeii ni boteɔ ŋmeii bibii amli koni amɛye baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds from around my crops even if the weeds are not touching the crop stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ, kɛji jwɛi lɛ etaaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe po lɛ?

english: Tall weeds block sunlight and fresh breeze from reaching your crops, while also attracting plant pests and diseases to your farm.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsiɔ hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa naa koni ekashɛ onibii ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai kɛbaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and burn when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that lose water very quickly in direct sun, so they need shade crops like plantains to protect them from heat during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni kookoo dumɔwui lɛ aná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Staking lifts yam vines off the ground so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight for food production, while also keeping the foliage dry to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni eshishifãi lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ kɛha niyenii feemɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ agbi koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli.

english: How do I know the right position to plant my cassava stem cuttings in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings should be planted with the tiny buds on the stem pointing upward toward the sky, ensuring the stems grow leaves easily and roots form properly underneath.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akwɛ baai oya ni shishifãi lɛ hu ahi shishigbɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering soil with dried grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground, keeps crop roots cool during hot days, and stops weeds from taking over your field.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni otsĩ jwɛi ni yeɔ oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the center outward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ kɛmiiya kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is a major nutrient plants need to produce healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts help improve the soil for my next farming season?
