ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, leaving natural plant food in the soil for the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Shi adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Water pooling on the surface means the soil is heavily compacted or high in clay, which blocks water drainage and can rot crop roots if ridges or drainage paths are not created.
ga: Nu ni ebɔle ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ loo eyɛ shikpɔŋ sũ babaoo. ni tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ naa ni ebaanyɛ eha tsei shishifãi lɛ afite kɛji akɛ afeee ŋmeii loo gbɛi ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap out of young leaves or spreading a virus that stunts normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. loo helai ni haa mɔ daa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of essential nutrients needed to hold and mature the fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni ashwieɔ shi daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai lɛ atomɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ ni bɛ

english: Why do weeds growing near my main crops cause them to stay small and yield less?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ haa amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, effectively starving your main crop while it tries to build fruits or tubers.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii titri lɛ yɛ be mli ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ewo yibii loo ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How can I know if my land is strong enough to give me a good harvest before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai dani madu nii?

english: You can check your land's strength by observing the soil's color, its texture, and the types of weeds growing naturally on it. Dark soil with lush green weeds usually indicates strong, fertile land.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ wa ha kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ su, bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha kɛ jwɛi srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ waa ni jwɛi eŋɔli yɔɔ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ he ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni baa nii.

english: How do I check if my soil has nutrients without taking it to a laboratory?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni mikɛyaaa laboratori?

english: You can inspect the soil's top layer for organic matter like decayed leaves and earthworms, dark soil color, and good moisture retention, or ask surrounding farmers about the history and performance of crops grown on that land.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ fã lɛ nɔ kɛji nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, kɛ bɔ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ ehaa. Aloo bi okwaafoi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. ni kɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe yinɔsane kɛ bɔ ni amɛtsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ he

english: Why should I inspect my land before buying seeds and planting crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mahe dumɔwui ni madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Inspecting your land helps you understand what nutrients the soil already has so you can choose crops that will naturally thrive there, saving you from wasting money on crops that will fail.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni onu niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni bakwɛ̃ yɛ jɛmɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Enɛ haaa ofite shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baafite lɛ ahe.

english: What signs show that the soil on my farm lacks the nutrients my crops need?
ga: Mɛni ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ?

english: Common signs of low nutrients include crops that grow slowly, plants with yellowish or stunted leaves, thin stems, and very low produce yields during harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ he ji tsei ni daa blɛoo. Tsei ni baai lɛ efee ŋmɔŋ loo egbɔjɔ, amɛshishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Can the wild weeds growing on my land tell me if the soil is good for farming?
ga: Ani koo mli jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ mi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha okwaayeli loo ehiii?

english: Yes, heavy growth of broad-leafed, deep green weeds usually signals fertile soil, while thin, dry, yellowish grass or spiky weeds often grow on soil that lacks nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa hiɛ waa lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ jwɛi ni mli tseee ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Does the color of my farm's soil tell me anything about its strength?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ su tsɔɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ shiŋŋ ha lɛ he nɔ ko?

english: Yes, darker brown or black soils generally contain more organic matter and nutrients, whereas light red or sandy soils often have lower fertility and require organic manure to perform well.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ lɛ fɔɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shikpɔji ni tsuɔ loo ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi ni ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What can I do to make weak soil fertile again for my crops?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: You can strengthen weak soil by adding decomposed animal manure or compost, planting nitrogen-fixing crops like beans and groundnuts, or letting the land rest for a season.
ga: Obaanyɛ owo shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo kooloi aŋmɔji ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen-fixing nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni aduɔ loo ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe be kome.

english: How do I choose the right crop to plant on my specific field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni makwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ pɔtɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Match your crop choice to your soil type and local rainfall. For example, crops that need lots of water do best in clay-like soils, while root crops like cassava prefer loose, well-draining soil.
ga: Kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ni ohala lɛ ato he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, tsei ni he hiaa nu babaoo lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow well on one part of my land but fail on another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko nɔ, shi ehiɛɛɛ fã kroko lɛ?

english: Different parts of a single field can have varying soil depth, moisture levels, and nutrient content. Low spots may hold more nutrients washed down by rain, making them richer than higher, drier spots.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmɔ kome mli hei srɔtoi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ srɔtoi. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni falɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ srɔtoi He ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahiɛ niyenii ni nugbɔ shwieɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo baa fe hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni egbi lɛ.

english: How does leaving my land unplanted for a season help rebuild soil nutrients?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mishi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aduko nɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ama shi?

english: Leaving land unplanted, or fallow, allows natural plant cover to return organic material to the earth, giving the soil time to rest and naturally restore lost nutrients for future planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ashiɔ ni atsuuu nii yɛ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and die if I do not plant plantains around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji miduuu plantains yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under full, direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and provide wide leafy shade, creating a cool, moist microclimate that protects the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛhaa shade kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ baa ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has from its older lower leaves to feed the new top leaves, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow and wither.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my field make my maize grow better in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa miŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts have natural microscopic organisms on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei Nibii bibii waa yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni okpaa Nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot inside the soil when there is continuous heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ ni naa wa miinɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need oxygen in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain stays trapped in the soil without draining, it starves the roots of air, allowing rot-causing fungi to attack and soften the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, efoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efooo. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ. Ha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ atutua bulbs lɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Why should I wait for the rains to settle before planting my corn seeds instead of sowing in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ moŋ?

english: Seeds need a steady supply of moisture to wake up and sprout. If planted in dry soil with only one light rain, the seed might start sprouting and then immediately dry up and die before the next rain falls.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa nu be fɛɛ be koni amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo shikome pɛ nɔ Dumɔwui lɛ hu baanyɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete fiercely with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The plants waste energy stretching upwards to reach light instead of using that energy to form thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Tsei fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkpãa kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛná la. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ jamɛ a he wami ɔ peeɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ tsohi agbohi.

english: Why do I need to cut away extra suckers from my plantain mat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-plantain lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extra suckers share the same root system with the main plantain tree. If you leave too many suckers, they steal water and food from the mother plant, causing the main plant to produce small, weak bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi lɛ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ plantain wulu lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso nyɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ niji bibii kɛ bibii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops weak and stunted even after I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that swallow up fertilizer and water faster than your crops can. Leaving weeds in your field means you are feeding the weeds instead of your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni miɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛ́ oshi jwɛi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ ooha jwɛi lɛ niyenii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: These are pests like Fall Armyworm that seek shelter in the central funnel (whorl) of the maize plant where the tender young leaves grow, feeding on them before the leaves expand.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni naa abobaahe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi (rings) ni baai bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ dani baai lɛ mli lɛɛɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant without producing any tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, dry soil, or lack of nutrients. The plant drops flowers to save its own life when conditions are too harsh to support fruit growth.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ mli. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhere amɛhe kɛji shihilɛi lɛ bafee nɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which plants need to make food. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the soil the boost it needs to make the leaves green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tsei ni he hiaa koni akɛfee niyenii Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ he hiaa koni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that easily scorch in hot sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them acts like a living umbrella, keeping the soil moist and protecting the cocoa until it grows stronger.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ shade ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ehaa ehe waa.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even when the leafy branches on top look big and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ lolo lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi niji lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛji eŋɔli moŋ, shi.

english: When soil is too hard or lacks nutrients like potassium, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of pushing outward to swell the roots below.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ potassium bɛ mli lɛ, Yucca tsei lɛ kudɔɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaatsi amɛ kɛya kponɔgbɛ koni amɛha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly flooded. Keeping soil moisture steady with mulch helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ kɛtee nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akɛ mulch haa be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my yam leaves curl up and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Curling leaves is a crop's natural way of protecting itself from losing too much water during high heat. As the sun lowers and temperatures cool down, the leaves usually flatten back out.
ga: Leaf curling ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu babaoo ni elaajeɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa lɛ he. Kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa sɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with small cobs when I put many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures every single plant gets enough food to grow a thick stalk and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field help the maize crop I plant there next season grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ŋmãa ni midu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to a plant family that pulls natural nitrogen from the air and stores it in the soil through small root nodules. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays behind to feed your next crop.
ga: Peanuts fata tsei aweku ko ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ he. Kɛji okpa amɛ Nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ sɛɛ koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small suckers growing around my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ Ajieɔ.

english: If too many suckers grow around one main plantain stem, they steal nutrients and water from each other. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, which results in bigger and heavier bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ, single main trunk Amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ, ni no baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmeii ni da ni tsii.

english: Why do white, powdery spots appear on my pepper plant leaves after rainy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: White spots are typically caused by fungal growth that thrives in warm, damp, and crowded conditions. Leaving enough space between plants allows wind to dry the leaves quickly and stops fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ yɛ hulutsoo, fɛ̃i, shihilɛi ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ hetsemɔ baa. Shi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aha baai lɛ agbi oya ni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ hela ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that drink up water and steal soil nutrients much faster than young crops can. Clearing weeds early ensures that all the food and water in the ground goes directly to your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni nuɔ nu ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ baa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need for healthy green growth. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant moves what little it has to the top leaves to survive, leaving the bottom leaves to starve.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa amɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Ha shishigbɛ baai lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why is my cassava growing tall with lots of big leaves, but producing very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or water, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing thick leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the roots. Balanced soil nutrients encourage the plant to direct its energy into expanding the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkudɔ amɛ hewalɛ koni amɛgbala amɛ bulbs ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants drying up and falling off before any fruits form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, prolonged dry spells, or irregular watering. Protecting soil moisture with mulch around the base of the plant helps keep the root zone cool and hydrated so flowers can set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be Sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ he buu kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ ehe lɛ nɔ. Shishitoo lɛ haa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. koni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii

english: Why do my small green oranges keep dropping off the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, minɔ lɛ gbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani eda?

english: Young citrus fruits drop early when the tree faces sudden water stress or when fruit flies puncture the skin to lay eggs inside. Consistent watering during dry weeks and hanging simple fruit fly traps in the tree help keep the fruit attached until harvest.
ga: Citrus yibii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ trukaa. Aloo kɛ́ aduawai amli ŋmeii tsɔɔ hewolo lɛ mli koni amɛwo ŋmeii yɛ mli. Nu ni oooha bo daa yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli kɛ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ baaye abua bo. yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be mli.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark brown and rotting right on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cool, damp, and shady conditions. Clearing weeds, pruning excess cocoa branches to let in sunlight and breeze, and removing infected pods quickly will stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, hulutsoo be, kɛ hulutsoo. Jwɛi ahe nitsumɔ Afolɔ kookoo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Ni kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking juice from under the leaves, or by a virus carried by these insects. Controlling these pests early with neem oil spray helps prevent the leaves from twisting and stunting the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Kudɔmɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa egbɔjɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my pineapples so they are sweet enough for juice makers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Enɛ baaha pineapple lɛ afee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ bɔ ni sa kɛha nu.

english: A pineapple is ready for picking when the base of the shell changes color from dark green to golden-yellow and gives off a sweet aroma. Pineapples do not get any sweeter after being cut from the bush, so harvesting too early results in sour fruit.
ga: Afee klalo akɛ abaakpa pineapple kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ tsake su kɛjɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛtee shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ baa. Pineapple lɛ sɛɛ efooo kɛjɛ jwɛi lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ efooo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, yibii ni mli edɔ baa.

english: Why does my mango tree produce a huge harvest one year and almost no fruits the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tso woɔ yibii babaoo afi kome shi afi ni baa lɛ eshwɛ fioo ni ebaawo yibii ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Mango trees often experience 'alternate bearing' because producing a massive crop drains almost all the energy and reserves from the tree. Feeding the tree with organic manure and pruning old branches right after a big harvest helps it recover energy to bear fruit every year.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, anaa mango tsei akɛ ‘gbɛ kroko’ ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ nibii ni ato lɛ fɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ha tso lɛ, ni afolɔ niji momoi lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ wulu ko sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ewo yibii afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees fall over during rainstorms even when the stem is strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ? Ani tsɔne lɛ mli wa lolo?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that hold onto the topsoil loosely while carrying heavy bunches of fruit at the top. Supporting the main stalk with sturdy wooden Y-props before the fruit gets too heavy prevents wind from uprooting the whole plant.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he mlɛo. be mli ni ehiɛɔ aduawai babaoo yɛ nɔ lɛ Tso titri lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛ tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tamɔ Y fiɔ sɛɛ. Dani aduawai lɛ baafee tsiimɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekajie tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why should I let my seed yam sprout before planting it in the soil mound?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ dani mikɛ amɛ awo muji lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting a seed yam that has already sprouted ensures that the plant immediately sends roots down to feed. If you plant unsprouted yam pieces into hot or overly wet soil, they can rot before they ever wake up to grow.
ga: Kɛ́ odu sweet potato dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ atsu eshishifãi lɛ kɛya shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni eyatao niyenii. Kɛji odu sweet potatoes ni ekwɛko yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo edɔ tsɔ nɔ lɛ, Ebaanyɛ egbo dani ete shi ni eda.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dying after I cleared all the tall trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie cacao tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. They need shade from tall trees or plantains to shield their leaf canopy from strong heat and preserve soil moisture while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji loo plantains amli koni amɛbu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves fall off during the dry season, and does this mean the crop is dead?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbo?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells as a survival mechanism to reduce water loss. The plant is not dead; its roots under the ground remain alive and will sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baa shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my field make the next batch of maize grow greener and stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ shwereɔ ni ehaa ehe waa lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When maize is planted afterwards, it uses this natural nitrogen to produce healthy green leaves and bigger stalks.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Be ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ sɛɛ mli Ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: My tomato plants have plenty of flowers, so why are the flowers falling off without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi shi amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when daytime temperatures get too high or when there is sudden water stress, which prevents the flowers from successfully pollinating and forming fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu he haomɔ ba trukaa. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee nɔ ni yeɔ omanye ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my farm land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani mana yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak stalks that produce very small or empty cobs.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii mli nibii ahe. Enɛ haa onáa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ tsei bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Upward leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking nutrients from the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: Why is it necessary to mound soft soil around the base of my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ato shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo abɔle mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ shishi be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Mounding creates loose, uncompacted soil that allows the subterranean yam tuber to expand easily while protecting it from scorching sun heat and surface pests.
ga: Gɔji lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ mlɛo yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop down during the hot afternoon sun but stand upright again by morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi shidaamɔ tɛ̃ɛ ekoŋŋ leebi?

english: Plantain leaves fold or droop during the hottest part of the day to lower the leaf area exposed to direct heat and conserve moisture, recovering overnight as temperatures drop.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Koni ajie he ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo tɛ̃ɛ baa lɛ shi ni aha hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi. Ebaatsa ehe nyɔɔŋ kome mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi.

english: What is causing this white powdery layer to cover the leaves of my garden eggs during damp weather?
ga: Mɛni haa powder yɛŋ ko haa eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: That white substance is a fungal growth called powdery mildew, which thrives in warm, humid conditions when there is limited air movement between closely spaced plants.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ futafuta lɛ ji ŋmei ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew lɛ dalɛ. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ fioo pɛ nyiɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ ateŋ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops right after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants native to the local soil that can absorb water and nutrients immediately, whereas domesticated crops take longer to settle roots and establish growth.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ shia lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛshishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi ni amɛdaraa.

english: Can I use chicken manure to grow my maize instead of buying chemical fertilizers from the shop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei atsu nii kɛdu ŋmãa moŋ fe ni mahe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli kɛjɛ shwapo mli?

english: Yes, chicken manure is rich in nitrogen and phosphorus, which maize needs to grow strong. It feeds the soil and crops naturally, often saving you money compared to store-bought chemical fertilizers.
ga: Hɛɛ, nitrogen kɛ phosphorus babaoo yɛ tsina ŋmɔ mli. ni ŋmãa he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ waa Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa okɛ shika toɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ ahe.

english: How long should I wait after putting fresh chicken droppings on my farm before planting corn?
ga: Beni mikɛ tsina ŋmei hee fata ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu ŋmãa?

english: Fresh chicken manure can burn young corn roots because it generates heat and has high ammonia levels. It is best to let the droppings dry out and compost for a few weeks before mixing them into your soil.
ga: Kooloo ŋmei hee baanyɛ ashã ŋmei bibii shishifãi ejaakɛ ekɛ dɔlɛ baa ni eyɛ ammonia babaoo. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi ni edɔ otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛfutu sũ lɛ mli.

english: Will using animal manure improve my soil quality better over time than buying outside fertilizer?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be ni sa mli fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaahe kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, animal manure adds organic matter that improves soil structure, helps the ground hold water longer, and keeps the soil healthy for future seasons, whereas chemical fertilizers only feed the plants for a short time.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ fataa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii yɛ be kukuoo mli pɛ.

english: Can I mix chicken droppings with chemical fertilizers for my corn crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ afutu tsina ŋmei kɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ?

english: Yes, combining manure with a small amount of commercial fertilizer can give your corn a quick boost while maintaining good long-term soil health.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei futu jarayeli ŋmei fioo ko lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ aya hiɛ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why is it important for me to till my land before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani madu ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Tilling loosens hard soil, making it easier for young crop roots to spread out and absorb water. It also helps break up weeds and mixes manure evenly into the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaajara nu ni amɛŋɔ nu. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni egbɛɔ jwɛi lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: What is a soil test, and how does it help my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa? ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: A soil test checks what nutrients your land already has and what it lacks. It prevents you from wasting money on the wrong fertilizers and tells you exactly what your crops need to yield well.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa baatsɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ nɔ ni bɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okɛ shika akafiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa lɛ ahe. ni ekɛɛ bo nɔ pɔtɛɛ ni ehe hiaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo.

english: When is the best time for me to till my land for the maize season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ makwɛ ŋmãa be lɛ mli?

english: Till your land shortly before the rains start. Doing it too far in advance can dry out the exposed soil, while tilling wet soil can create hard clods that make planting difficult.
ga: Kɛyashi ebaashɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ. Kɛ́ afee babaoo kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ agbi. Yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmeii ni wa ni haa dumɔ waaa lɛ.

english: People say agriculture is a science, but what does that mean for a small maize farmer like me?
ga: Mɛi kɛɔ akɛ okwaayeli ji jeŋ nilee. Shi mɛni ji nɔ ni no tsɔɔ kɛha okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi?

english: It means observing how your plants react to soil, water, and nutrients, and using proven techniques—like proper plant spacing and soil testing—to get a reliable harvest rather than relying on guess work.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ okwɛ bɔ ni otsei lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ niyenii mli nibii ahe, ni okɛ ŋaai ni ana he odaseyeli tamɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kaa atsu nii. bɔni afee ni anyɛ ana nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ he aaafɔ̃ susumɔi ni asusuɔ he lɛ anɔ

english: How can I tell if my corn leaves are showing that the plant needs fertilizer or manure?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-abele baa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If the lower leaves of your corn start turning pale yellow from the tip down the center of the leaf, your crop is lacking nitrogen and needs manure or nitrogen fertilizer applied.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishi baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛ amɛnaagbee kɛtee baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli ni ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen awo mli.

english: My family suggested a new way to plant maize, but how can I safely try it without risking my entire harvest?
ga: Miweku lɛ kɛ gbɛ hee ko ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ ba. Shi te mafee tɛŋŋ maka enɛ mafee shweshweeshwe ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ wooo oshara mli?

english: You can set up a small control plot on one corner of your field to try the new method. Compare how the maize grows there against your traditional plot before changing how you farm your entire land.
ga: Obaanyɛ oto gbɛjianɔtoo bibioo ko ni okɛbaakwɛ nɔ. Yaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni oka gbɛi heei okwɛ. Okɛ ŋmãa ni yaa hiɛ yɛ nakai he lɛ ato oshishijee shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Dani obaatsake gbɛ ni otsɔɔ nɔ otsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ fɛɛ

english: How can I earn money from my farm while waiting for long-term trees like cocoa to start producing yield after a few years?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná shika yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ tsei ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo lɛ ni amɛje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: You can intercrop fast-growing short-term crops like cassava, plantain, or maize between your young tree rows. These provide immediate food and harvest income during the first two to three years before your cash crop matures.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kuku, ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, loo ŋmei yɛ otsei bibii lɛ ateŋ. Enɛɛmɛi haa niyenii kɛ kpamɔ shika amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli dani oshika ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do my young seedlings wither and die under the strong heat soon after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ la ni naa wa lɛ shishi beni mikɛ amɛ wo he kroko amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have delicate roots and burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain leaves or fast-growing cover crops act as living shade umbrellas to protect tender young plants while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi. Plantain baai, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ ko ni shwereɔ oya lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ni buɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my farmland produce less yield every year even when I keep planting the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the exact same crop on the same piece of land continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your primary crops with legumes like beans or cowpeas restores nutrients naturally and keeps the soil healthy long-term.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsake oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: How can I keep my farm soil moist when the rains stop for a few weeks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa nɛmɔ otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Covering the exposed soil around your crops with dry grass, leaves, or straw—a practice called mulching—blocks direct sunlight, slows down evaporation, and keeps moisture trapped in the ground longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ nɔ ni oookɛwo mli Okɛ jwɛi, baai loo jwɛi aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe - nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching - baaye abua ni etsĩ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ebaaha la ni hoɔ oya lɛ aya hiɛ ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the seedlings compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong stems and large roots.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛ amɛhe feɔ ekome. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi wuji baakwɛ̃.

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that your plants lack nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leaf growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-based fertilizer will help restore their green color and health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist, typically right after a light rain or early in the rainy season. Applying fertilizer on dry soil causes it to evaporate, while heavy downpours will wash it away before plants can absorb it.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo ko sɛɛ loo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ atsɔ la. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ sũ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my main crops and overtake the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that quickly steal sunlight, water, and food from your crops. Clearing weeds early within the first month after planting gives your crop a strong advantage to outgrow and shade out the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli oya. Jwɛi ni agbeɔ yɛ nyɔji ni jeɔ shishi yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa onibii lɛ náa sɛɛnamɔ kpele akɛ jwɛi lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni amɛhaa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my crop leaves, and how can I stop it without expensive chemicals?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi tso lɛ baai amli Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa ni mikɛ tsofai ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: Holes in leaves are usually caused by insects like beetles or caterpillars eating your plants. Spraying a natural mixture made from boiled neem leaves and water can repel pests without harming your soil or crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ otsei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni akɛ neem baai ni ahoo kɛ nu fee lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshwie tsɛŋemɔ helai ni efiteee oshikpɔŋ loo oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant seeds from my current maize harvest for next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa amrɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni maduɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from harvested hybrid crops lose their strength and disease resistance in the next generation, producing smaller yields. Using fresh, certified seeds ensures high germination, pest resistance, and better harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmaa kpakpa

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow and drying up before the corn is ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: This usually happens when your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or planting beans in that soil before maize helps keep the leaves green and increases your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo aduɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani aduɔ ŋmei lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves develop brown spots and turn yellow quickly during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ anɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by a leaf fungal disease that thrives in warm, wet weather. Removing infected leaves and cutting down overcrowded plants helps air move through the farm, which stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni egbɔ fe nine lɛ afolɔmɔ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What causes the leaves of my young corn plants to look like someone shot tiny holes through them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ mɔ ko efo bu bibii etsɔ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the central leaf shoot of young maize plants. Treating the crop early with recommended control methods before the pest multiplies saves your farm from major leaf damage.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ teŋgbɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ mra Kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ nibii dani tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ayi fa lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaajie oŋmɔ lɛ kɛjɛ baai wuji ni baafite lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When water sits in the field without draining, it suffocates the roots and allows tiny organisms in the wet soil to attack and decay the cassava tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu ŋmɛ ŋmɔ ko mli ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ Nu lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni ha bɔɔ nii bibii lɛ Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etutuaa ni ehaa ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do I need to put up stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight gives the leaves energy to send food down underground, which makes the yam tubers grow big and heavy.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la haa baai lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ niyenii yaa shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by too much heat, lack of water, or when there are no tiny insects around to transfer pollen between flowers. Proper shade and keeping moisture in the soil helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine, nu ni faaa, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni baanyɛ ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ lɛ bɛ haomɔ mli. Kɛ́ aha fɔfɔi lɛ hulutsoo ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot when the rains become very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by water droplets spreading tiny fungi in overly shady, damp conditions. Pruning excess branches to let sunlight and wind into your cocoa farm keeps the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nu mli nu ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ, Fɔlɔmɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote okokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas take food from the air and store it in their roots in the ground. When planted with maize, they naturally feed the soil with nitrogen, acting like a free natural fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa lɛ Amɛbaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nitrogen lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko

english: Is it better for me to water my pepper plants early in the morning or late in the evening?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs the water before the sun gets hot, and wet leaves dry quickly in the daytime sun, preventing plant diseases from taking hold.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ dani hulu lɛ shɛɔ. Ni baai ni efɔ lɛ baagbi oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Koni akɛtsi tsei ahe helai anaa

english: Why do my tomato seedlings wilt and die right after I move them from the nursery to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This happens because moving delicate plants causes transplant shock when roots are damaged or exposed to strong sun too quickly. Moving seedlings late in the afternoon and watering them immediately helps them survive the move.
ga: Enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ tsei ni waaa ni atsiɔ amɛhe lɛ kɛ shoofeemɔ baa kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ fite loo hulu la ni fa babaoo shɛ amɛnɔ oya tsɔ. Kɛ́ ajie dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ he kroko yɛ shwane mli ni awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ mli.

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetable crops late in the evening instead of during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo mitsei lɛ nu gbɛkɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha nu yɛ shwane mli?

english: Watering in the late afternoon or evening gives the plant roots plenty of time to soak up moisture continuously throughout the cool night without losing water to heat evaporation, keeping them well-hydrated.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ shwane loo gbɛkɛ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ náa be ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛya nɔ amɛŋɔ nu yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ fɛɛ mli. ni nu ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ mli la ni hoɔ lɛ mli baaa lɛ Kwɛmɔ ni tsei lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my pepper plants look limp and tired in the afternoon heat but perk up by morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni etɔ lɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi enáa hejɔɔmɔ leebi lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water quickly through their leaves, causing them to wilt slightly. At night, when the heat drops, they rest and draw up moisture from the soil to regain their strength by morning.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ebaagbi fioo. Gbi gbɛkɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi lɛ Amɛjɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛgbala ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ leebi.

english: When is the best time of day for me to apply liquid fertilizer to my maize crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ baawo mi ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: Applying liquid fertilizer late in the afternoon or early evening prevents the strong sun from drying out the liquid quickly, allowing the crop roots to steadily absorb the nutrients overnight.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo mli yɛ shwane mli loo gbɛkɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaatsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekaha nu lɛ agbi oya. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nyɔɔŋ kome.

english: How do I know if I am giving my crops enough manure or if they are still hungry?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli bɔ ni sa loo hɔmɔ miiye lɛ lolo?

english: If crop leaves are deep green and growing steady, they are well-fed. If the leaves turn pale yellow or stems remain thin, the plants need an extra portion of manure around their root zone to satisfy their hunger.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛdaraa. Etsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ yeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo Tsei lɛ hu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni ebɔle amɛhe. shishifã he lɛ koni akɛtsu hɔmɔ he nii

english: Can I give my cassava crops extra compost right before the dry season starts?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha mi-cassava lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi dani hulutsoo be lɛ aje shishi?

english: Yes, giving an extra portion of rich compost around the base before dry weather helps store moisture and slowly feeds the roots, ensuring the plant stays satisfied through tough periods.
ga: Hɛɛ, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ babaoo fataa he. Shishifãi lɛ dani kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ niyenii fiofio. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ jaramɔ bei amli.

english: Do my crops keep growing at night when there is no sunlight?
ga: Ani midumɔ nii lɛ baakwɛ̃ gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulu la bɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, crops make their food using sunlight during the day, but at night they use that stored energy along with soil water to build stems, roots, and fruits while resting from the daytime heat.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii hoɔ nii kɛ hulu la yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Shi gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hewalɛ ni ato kɛfataa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi, shishifãi, kɛ aduawai yɛ be mli ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn to face the sun throughout the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop leaves turn toward the light to capture maximum sunshine, which acts as the main energy source plants use to prepare their daily food.
ga: Atsɔɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ amli kɛyaa la lɛ he koni abua hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ naa. Etsuɔ nii akɛ hewalɛ jɛɛhe titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛsaa amɛ daa gbi niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow much faster after a night of soft rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daa oya waa beni nugbɔ enɛɔ gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rainfall provides a deep soak to the root area during cool hours, giving the plants all the moisture they need to feed heavily and stretch rapidly overnight.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛboteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Ha tsei lɛ nu fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni tsii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ oya mli nyɔɔŋ kome mli.

english: Should I leave dry grass mulch over my crop roots through the night?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ sũ ni egbi aha mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: Yes, keeping mulch over the soil traps moisture overnight so the roots can continuously drink water without the soil drying out.
ga: Hɛɛ, mulching baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ nyɔɔŋ kome. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anu nu be fɛɛ be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do my garden plants drop some of their leaves when I do not water them enough?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ekomɛi anɔ beni mikɛ nu haaa amɛ bɔ ni sa lɛ?

english: When crops do not get enough water and food, they shed older leaves to save energy and protect their stem and main roots from starving.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Eshwieɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he ni ebu tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their leaves dry out quickly under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to young cocoa creates a canopy that provides shade, retains soil moisture, and protects the cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ hulutsoo baa. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni obu kookoo lɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the bottom leaves upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-corn tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves from the bottom up usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to stay green and grow healthy. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted manure will help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe in waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to put tall wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ hiɛyaa nɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ aba lɛ? Koni okwɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Yam plants make underground tubers by catching sunlight through their leaves. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground so all leaves get full sunlight and air circulation, resulting in larger yam tubers and fewer leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛnaa kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛná hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa, ni helai ni baa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ hu faaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of soil nutrients. Giving plants consistent water at the base and applying mulch keeps the soil cool and helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei ashishigbɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: What benefit do I get by covering the soil with dry grass around my vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔi maná kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mi-vegetables lɛ ahe lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops sunlight from drying out the earth, reduces weed growth, and keeps the soil cool. As the dry grass decays, it turns into rich manure for your crops.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu la lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ha jwɛi ni shwereɔ lɛ aba shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Be mli ni jwɛi ni egbi lɛ fiteɔ Ebaatsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii.

english: Why is it bad for my farm if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why are tiny green and brown worms eating the center whorl of my young maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye mibi lɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ?

english: These worms are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that burrows into maize stalks to feed on soft new leaves. Checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem leaf extract in the plant whorl destroys them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmei tsei amli koni eye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii loo neem baa ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baafite amɛ dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields when I put seeds very close to each other in a single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops grow too closely together, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited water, sunlight, and soil food. Spacing crops correctly gives every single plant enough room to feed and grow thick, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer when the ground is completely dry during a drought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil water to dissolve so crop roots can drink it in. Applying chemical fertilizer to dry soil can burn plant roots and kill the crop, so it is best applied when the soil is damp after a rain.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛtsu nii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why are my maize plants turning yellow and weak even though we are receiving heavy rain this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooloi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbɔjɔ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ yɔɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Excessive rainfall can wash away essential soil nutrients like nitrogen through leaching, and waterlogged soil prevents roots from breathing. Creating proper drainage furrows and applying nitrogen fertilizer after heavy rains help crops recover.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli lɛ he gbɛjegbɛi ni sa ni afee kɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and die when I clear all the big trees from my farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Leaving shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby creates a cooler canopy that protects young cocoa seedlings until they are mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ehaa ŋwɛi ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: If I plant my cassava stems very close together, will I harvest more cassava from my land?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa Ani makpa ŋmei babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to small roots. Giving cassava recommended spacing allows each plant enough root room to produce thick, healthy tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akɛto ŋmei lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso shishifãi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni mli wa.

english: Why are holes appearing in the leaves of my young corn plants with small brown powder inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe ni powda bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is a sign of the Fall Armyworm, a destructive caterpillar that feeds on maize leaves and growing points. Inspecting crops early and applying appropriate control measures early in the morning or late evening keeps them under control.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ he okadi. Nibii ni adu lɛ akwɛmɔ mra ni akɛ gbɛi ni sa ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: My tomato plants have many flowers, but why do the flowers fall off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomatoi lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when plants face stress like extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of specific nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and maintaining balanced soil health helps flowers set into healthy fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ kpe. loo niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ ni bɛ Sũ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be ni oha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ofɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my land become hard like stone when the dry season begins, making my yams small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ tɛsaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ? Ha mi sweet potato lɛ afee bibioo?

english: Hard soil prevents yam tubers from expanding underwater. Adding organic matter like compost, animal manure, or crop leaves softens the soil texture and helps it retain moisture so roots can grow large.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ tsiɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã nu shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsei ahe baai fata he lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ afee blɛoo ni eye ebua ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ adara.

english: How do I know the best time to sow my seeds when the rain starts unexpectedly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔ jeɔ shishi trukaa lɛ?

english: Sowing immediately after the very first light shower can cause seeds to dry up if the rain stops for days. It is safer to wait until the soil is deeply moist from steady rains before planting your main crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii babaoo. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ waa kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli dani okɛ otso titri lɛ adu.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly and overwhelm my pepper plants after a rain storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛhaa mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that absorb water and fertilizer much faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early while they are small prevents them from stealing food and light from your crop plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Amɛ bibioo po baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ la kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies or infected planting stems. Using disease-free stems and planting resistant varieties protects your field from leaf curling and crop loss.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Virus ko ni whiteflies bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. loo tso shishifãi ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni helai bɛ mli lɛ tsu nii kɛ tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛduɔ nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do small insects turn my harvested maize into white dust after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni mikpa lɛ tsɔ sũ yɛŋ beni mikɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Storage insects like weevils thrive when grain is stored with moisture still inside. Thoroughly drying your maize until it is hard and using airtight storage bags starves pests of oxygen and preserves your harvest.
ga: Kplukai ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmaa to ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lolo. Kɛ́ oogbi ŋmãa waa ni okɛ vacuum storage bags tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ, ni ebaaye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and powdery dirt inside the central shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ kɛ muji ni tamɔ powda ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the maize funnel. Applying neem oil extract or recommended insecticides into the central leaf funnel early in the morning or late evening kills the caterpillars effectively.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ mli nu loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom parts of my growing tomatoes turning black and soft before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni miida lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani tomato lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the plant combined with uneven soil moisture. Watering your farm regularly and adding organic compost or agricultural lime helps the plants absorb calcium and prevents fruit rot.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shiŋŋ lɛ mli. Nu ni oooha oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni okɛ organic compost loo lime afata he lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ aŋɔ calcium ni amɛtsi aduawai lɛ anaa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning light green and yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop leaves need to stay healthy and dark green. Applying animal manure, well-rotted compost, or a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea will feed the plants and restore their green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei ahe koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ. Koolooi amli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ Loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea baaye abua ni eha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni eha amɛ su lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to a family of crops that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small bumps on their roots. When the plants die and decay, this stored nitrogen stays in the soil as natural food for your next maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts fata tsei ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe kɛji tso lɛ gbo ni egbo. Nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or lacks potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing big leaves and stems above ground instead of roots. Using fertilizers higher in potassium encourages the plant to store food in large tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo potassium bɛ mli Yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ato e-bulbs agboi lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make the energy required to produce big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to full sunlight while preventing fungal diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ hulu la ni eŋmɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hu he lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide immediate shade to protect young cocoa plants and keep the surrounding soil cool and moist while the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ebu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give high yields only in their first planting generation. Seeds saved from a hybrid harvest lose their vigor, resulting in uneven plant growth, smaller cobs, and lower yields in the second season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ hybrid ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ daraaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni yibiiwoo lɛ ba shi yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my soil become hard like rock after it rains and dries under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ tɛsaa yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ, ni egbi yɛ hulu shishi lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses its moisture and structure quickly when exposed to direct heat from the sun. Covering the soil with dried grass, leaves, or crop residues (mulching) keeps the soil cool, soft, and moist for plant roots to spread.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛ enɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, efeɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why shouldn't I spray liquid pest sprays on my crop leaves in the middle of the afternoon when the sun is bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ji nu lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baa lɛ nɔ shwane mli beni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Spraying in hot sunlight causes the spray drops to evaporate into the air before they can work, and water droplets on hot leaves can act like tiny magnifiers that burn the leaves. Spraying early in the morning or late afternoon ensures maximum effectiveness and safety.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli nui lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani amɛtsu nii. Ni nu ni hoɔ yɛ baai ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee tamɔ glase bibii ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo. ni baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi loo shwane lɛ haa etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Officer, why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of green?
ga: Officer Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are starving for nitrogen nutrients in the soil, or the ground has too much water which is choking the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their blossoms before any peppers start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat, lack of regular watering, or when they get too much nitrogen fertilizer which makes leaves grow instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa ko miipiŋ amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa loo be mli ni anáa nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni haa baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ lɛ.

english: Why do plantain leaves dry up and turn brown during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have huge leaves that lose water very quickly in dry winds. Without enough soil moisture, the plant drops its outer leaves to protect its main stem and survive.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni nu fiteɔ oya waa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ gĩ. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baashɛ esɛɛ baai lɛ ashwie shi koni ebu tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he ni ehi shi.

english: Since my land is very small, can I plant beans and maize together on the same plot?
ga: Ejaakɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ faaa kwraa. Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting maize and beans together is great for small farms. Beans trap nitrogen from the air and feed the soil, which helps the maize grow stronger while saving field space.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔji bibii. Beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa yɛ be mli ni ehaa he ko sɛɛ foɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do the crops planted near the edge of my small field grow bigger than the ones in the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ ŋmɔji bibii lɛ anaa lɛ No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ daa fe nɔ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?
