english: Crops at the edges get more direct sunlight and fresh air flow, and their roots face less competition for water and soil nutrients than plants crowded together in the middle.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ naa hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa babaoo ni amɛtsɔɔ mli. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ akaŋshii fioo ko pɛ kpeɔ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he fe tsei ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cocoa pods so buyers won't reject them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ? koni mɔ ni heɔ lɛ akakpoo.

english: Cocoa pods are ready to harvest when the pod color turns completely yellow or orange. Gathering them green means flat, bitter beans that buyers will reject or buy for a cheap price.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ kwraa. Green gathering tsɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni jarayelɔi baakpoo loo amɛhe jara waaa.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot so fast before I can transport them to the market to sell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes rot quickly if they are picked while wet from dew, stacked too deep in wooden crates which bruises them, or left sitting directly in hot sunlight after harvest.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ajie lɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ ewo mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛtoɔ adekai amli ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Aloo shi ni eta shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ beni okpa kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What makes grain buyers pay a higher price for another farmer's dried maize than mine?
ga: Mɛni haa mɛi ni heɔ ŋmaa lɛ woɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi aŋmaa ni egbi lɛ jara babaoo fe mi nɔ lɛ?

english: Buyers pay top price for maize that is thoroughly dried to low moisture, free from mold, stripped clean of cob dirt, and shows no holes from weevil insects.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ ŋmãa ni egbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ he nyɔmɔ ni fe fɛɛ. Ebɛ ŋmɔtɔ Gbalamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ni otsumɔ he. Ni bu ko bɛ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin like sticks even after standing in the ground for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo tamɔ tsei beni midamɔ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot expand into big tubers if the soil is packed too hard and clayey, or if the plants were planted too close together and fought over soil food.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtsɔ bulbs agboi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ. Aloo kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni amɛmiitswa niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he akaŋ.

english: What causes my yam tubers to split open underground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ?

english: Yam tubers crack when heavy rains suddenly follow a long dry period, causing the inside of the tuber to grow faster than its outer skin can stretch.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baatswa trukaa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ mligbɛ lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Maize plants yellow at the bottom when they are short on nitrogen food or water. The plant prioritizes growing young top leaves and draws nutrients away from the older lower leaves to survive.
ga: Abɛi baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ kɛji akɛ nitrogen niyenii loo nu bɛ mli. Tsei kɛ ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ adalɛ yeɔ hiɛ ni amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi.

english: Leaf curling is a tomato plant's natural way of protecting itself. It reduces leaf surface area exposed to the sun to save water and stop moisture from escaping during peak heat.
ga: Leaf curling ji tomato tso adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he. Ehaa baa lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaje kpo yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do pests attack my weak and dry crops more than the healthy green ones in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni egbi lɛ fe tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Stressed crops emit scents and produce softer tissues that signal to insects that the plant is weak, making them an easy food source compared to strong, healthy plants.
ga: Tsei ni haoɔ lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔlɔ ko ni amɛfeɔ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni haa kooloi bibii leɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ niyenii jɛɛhe ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ akɛto tsei ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and delicate root systems that burn under direct sunlight. They need plantains or shade trees above them to filter heat until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ amɛyiteŋ koni amɛjie la ni tsoɔ lɛ kɛjɛ mli kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very tall and thin with almost no peppers when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni eshwɛ fioo ni pepper ko bɛ mli beni miduɔ amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are crowded, they compete for light and spend all their energy stretching upward toward the sun rather than developing branches and producing fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ni amɛkpãa kɛyaa hulu lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee niji ni ewo yibii

english: Why does my cowpea crop produce mostly big green leaves and very few pods after I add a lot of fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai agboi babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ewo mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer signals the plant to keep growing branches and leaves instead of flowering. Cowpeas naturally fix their own nitrogen and need less fertilizer to produce pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ okadi akɛ ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ eniji kɛ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi. Cowpeas kɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen lɛ toɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehe ehiaaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo koni ekɛfee pods.

english: How do I know if my soil has enough moisture for cassava planting without using expensive farm tools?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmei dumɔ ni okɛ okwaayeli nibii ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: You can dig hand-deep, take a fistful of soil, and squeeze it into a ball. If it holds together without dripping water, the soil is retaining enough moisture for cassava roots to take hold.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa shi kɛya shɔŋŋ. Okɛ sũ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nine awo mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛmimɔ mli ni efee bɔɔlu. Kɛji amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni nu shwieee shi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my yam vines turn yellow and dry up completely toward the end of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: The yam plant naturally ends its above-ground growth cycle as rains reduce, sending all remaining energy down into the underground tuber to complete its development.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ gbeɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ be lɛ naa kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ ba shi. Ekɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛgbe shweremɔ naa.

english: Why is it better for my cassava crop if I water early in the morning instead of late in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mi yucca tsei lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛmli leebi moŋ fe gbɛkɛ?

english: Morning watering lets plant roots drink before heat sets in, while evening watering leaves damp soil overnight that can cause fungal diseases to attack root tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu leebi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu dani hulutsoo be lɛ jeɔ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ, ni no baanyɛ aha ŋmeii ahe helai atutua shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees easily fall over during strong rains and winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and heavy fruit stems. Removing extra sucker shoots and using wooden prop stakes helps support the main stem against wind balance issues.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni aduawai ahe tsei lɛ hu tsii. Suction cup krɛdɛɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ tso ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni efiɔ tso titri lɛ sɛɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ŋmɛɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ he naagbai amli.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape, it usually means the soil is running low on nitrogen. Nitrogen is essential for green growth, and when the plant lacks it, it pulls remaining nitrogen from older leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ. Ni kɛ́ tsei lɛ etee lɛ Egbalaa nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas helps restore soil nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ayaa nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry chemical fertilizer to my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve into a liquid form that plant roots can actually drink. Applying dry fertilizer to dry soil can concentrate chemical salts around the roots and burn or kill the crop.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ nu ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ anu diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi fata shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ afee ekome ni eshã loo efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sunlight and dry winds. Keeping taller shade trees or planting plantains provides necessary shade and retains humidity until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin when I plant the cuttings too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo beni adu tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava cuttings are planted too close, their root systems compete heavily for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough underground space to swell and grow large tuberous roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛgbɛ eshwa ni ekwɛ shishifãi wuji.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a hot, dry spell that dries out the topsoil. Planting too early causes seeds to absorb moisture, start germinating, and then die from heat and lack of follow-up rain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli gbiɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aŋɔ nu, amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃, ni amɛgboi yɛ latsaa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: What is causing sawdust-like dirt and holes in the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ muji kɛ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the growing funnel of the maize plant. The sawdust-like dirt is the pest's waste matter as it eats the soft green leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ ji ŋmeii ni ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ beni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on leaf sap and spreading a virus. The attack damages leaf tissues, preventing the plant from growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Tutuamɔ lɛ kpataa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ ahiɛ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. Keeping soil consistently moist and planting at the right temperature window helps fruit set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa. loo pollination ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ dumɔ yɛ samflɛ mli latsaa ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ akwɛ.

english: Why is it better to remove weeds while they are still tiny instead of waiting for them to grow large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaajie jwɛi lɛ be mli ni amɛdara lolo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with young crops for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Removing weeds early stops them from starving your crops during their critical early growth stages when yield is determined.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli, ni jieɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baatsi otsei lɛ anaa koni hɔmɔ akaye amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli beni osusuɔ yibiiwoo he lɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava in the same field where my yams are already growing?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, you can plant cassava between your yam plants around the fourth month of yam growth. This allows the cassava to establish itself without interfering with yam tuber formation, giving you two harvests from the same piece of land.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmei tsei ateŋ yɛ aaafee nyɔji ejwɛ ni ŋmei lɛ daa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ ŋmei shishifã lɛ feemɔ kpaaa gbee. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii shii enyɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: When is the best time to introduce cassava into an existing yam field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ momo mli?

english: It is best to wait about four months after planting your yams. By this time, the yam vines are well-established, so adding cassava won't compete heavily with the yams while they mature.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ aaafee nyɔji ejwɛ beni odu sweet potato lɛ sɛɛ. Amrɔ nɛɛ, sweet potato wain tso lɛ etswa shi jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ kɛ ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ lɛ akaŋ tsɔ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: If I plant cassava in my yam field, won't the cassava crowd out my yams?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔ mli Ani amɛbaaŋɔ mi ŋmei lɛ mli obɔ?

english: If you plant the cassava later in the yam's growth cycle (around month four), the yam is already mature enough. The cassava will grow slowly at first and take over fully only after you dig up the yams.
ga: Kɛji akɛ odu ŋmei yɛ ŋmei lɛ dalɛ be mli (aaafee nyɔŋ ni ji ejwɛ lɛ) lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei lɛ edara kwraa. Yucca lɛ daa fiofio yɛ shishijee mli, ni kɛ́ okɛ yucca lɛ shwie shi pɛ kɛkɛ ni edaa.

english: How long will cassava remain on my field compared to yams?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmãa baahi miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto ŋmãa he?

english: Yam matures faster and is harvested earlier, while cassava stays in the ground longer, usually maturing between 9 to 12 months. This allows cassava to occupy the land into the following year after yam is gone.
ga: Sweet potatoes daa oya ni akpaa mra. Yɛ ŋmei gbɛfaŋ lɛ, ebaahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be babaoo. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ yeɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12, ni no haa ŋmei lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli beni ŋmei lɛ etee lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Do different cassava varieties serve different purposes, or are they all the same?
ga: Kasava henɔi srɔtoi Ani amɛyɛ yiŋtoi srɔtoi? Aloo fɛɛ yɛ ekome?

english: Different cassava varieties are bred for specific uses. Some varieties have high dry-matter ideal for making gari, others are rich in starch for industrial use, and some are best suited for boiling and eating.
ga: Cassava henɔi srɔtoi Akwɛ amɛ kɛha nitsumɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Nibii ni egbi babaoo yɛ henɔi komɛi amli, ni amɛhi kɛha kri feemɔ. Yɛ henɔi krokomɛi ahe lɛ, Eyɛ starch babaoo kɛha nitsumɔhei ni akɛtsuɔ nii Ni henɔi komɛi hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shãa kɛ niyenii.

english: Which cassava variety should I plant if I want to process my harvest into gari?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei srɔtoi esa akɛ makwɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni mafee lɛ gari?

english: Look for high-yield cassava varieties with high dry-matter content. These produce a higher amount of flour and gari per bag of roots harvested compared to sweet cooking varieties.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmei henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ nibii ni egbi babaoo. Enɛɛmɛi haa ŋmeii kɛ gari babaoo baa shishifã kotoku kome mli kɛ akɛto ŋmeii ni akɛsaa he lɛ ahe.

english: What kind of cassava should I grow if I want to sell to a starch processing factory?
ga: Miisumɔ ni mahɔ̃ɔ ŋmei maha nitsumɔhe ko ni feɔ ashikishaŋ. Mɛɛ tso esa akɛ madu?

english: You should seek out specific industrial cassava varieties that are high in starch content. Factories pay based on starch extractable from the roots, so ordinary cooking varieties will yield less profit.
ga: Esa akɛ otao nitsumɔhei pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmãa. Tso lɛ kɛ starch ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ haa, no hewɔ lɛ, sɛɛnamɔ fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ nihoomɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo he.

english: Can I use any cassava variety from my local market to produce starch?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ mimaŋ jarayelihe lɛ eko fɛɛ eko afee ashikishaŋ?

english: While all cassava contains starch, specialized starch varieties give much higher extractions. Using the wrong variety can lead to low starch yields and reduced profit for your effort.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ starch yɛ cassava fɛɛ mli moŋ, shi ashikiŋshai krɛdɛɛi haa anáa nɔ ni fa babaoo fe tsutsu lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ni ejaaa tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmeii ni anáa lɛ aba shi, ni ebaaha sɛɛnamɔi ni jɛɔ mɔdɛŋ ni obɔɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ aba shi.

english: How can I make sure my land stays productive immediately after harvesting my yams?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ baaya nɔ awo yibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: By planting cassava in the farm a few months before harvesting your yams, the cassava continues to grow seamlessly. When the yams are harvested, your land instantly becomes a cassava farm for the next season without needing to clear new land.
ga: Kɛtsɔ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔji fioo komɛi dani akpaa ŋmei lɛ nɔ. Cassava baaya nɔ akwɛ̃. Be ni esa akɛ akpa sweet potatoes Oshikpɔŋ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ajie shikpɔŋ hee nɔ.

english: Why do many farmers combine yam and cassava production instead of planting them on separate plots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo kɛ sweet potato kɛ cassava ŋmɔshi nibii miifee ekome yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadu yɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi anɔ lɛ?

english: Combining them saves time, land, and labor. You clear and weed the farm once, harvest the yam first for quick food or income, and leave the cassava to grow into the next year as a backup food source.
ga: Amɛfeɔ ekome kɛbuɔ be, shikpɔŋ kɛ nitsumɔ he. Okɛ jwɛi shwieɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli be kome. Kpaa sweet potatoes klɛŋklɛŋ kɛha niyenii loo shika oya. ni oha ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential food for leaf growth, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do different varieties of sweet potato have orange or white flesh inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ yɛ loo ni ji ŋmeii loo yɛŋ yɛ mli lɛ?

english: The colors come from natural plant pigments; orange sweet potatoes contain high levels of beta-carotene, a natural pigment that gives them color and provides Vitamin A.
ga: Su lɛ jɛɔ tsei adebɔɔ mli sui amli. Beta-carotene babaoo yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ mli. ni ji adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni haa mɔ he feɔ fɛo kɛ vitamin A

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants developing dark spots and yellow edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: This is typically a sign of leaf blight, a fungal disease that thrives in warm, humid weather when moisture stays on plant leaves for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji sɛɛkuu-kɛsaramɔ he okadi. Enɛ ji fungal hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Beni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ tso lɛ baai anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ

english: Why does my neighbor harvest much larger yams than I do, even though our farms are side by side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa babaoo fe mi be mli ni wɔŋmɔji lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Soil richness can vary even on neighboring plots depending on organic matter content, crop rotation history, soil depth, and mound preparation.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ afee srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ateŋ po. Edamɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ayibɔ nɔ Yinɔsane ni kɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tsakemɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ gɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ he

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or having too much nitrogen fertilizer which pushes leaf growth instead of fruit production.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa Aloo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ ni haa baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in root nodules, naturally fertilizing the soil for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ wɔsɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees getting too much direct sun will develop pale yellow or scorched brown leaves, showing they need shade trees to protect them from intense light.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii ni hulu la kpɛɔ amɛ babaoo tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaná baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eshã. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: When planted too tightly, plantain roots and leaves compete with each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients, leaving less energy for big bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ babaoo tsɔ lɛ, Plantain shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Enɛ haa hewalɛ fioo pɛ baa jwɛi wuji anɔ.

english: Dropping leaves is a cassava plant's natural defense mechanism to conserve water during dry spells so the root tuber can stay alive in the ground.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ŋmei tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my maize stalks falling over in the wind before harvesting time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa ŋmãa tsei dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Maize falls over when its roots are shallow, when planted in overly wet soil, or when stem borer pests bore into the stalk and weaken it from the inside.
ga: Abɛi baagbee shi kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ nɔ loo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui bote tso lɛ mli, ni amɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli ni amɛhaa egbɔjɔɔ kɛjɛɔ emli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and scorching?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to strong sunlight. Without shade trees or plantain plants growing next to them to block the harsh sun, the young leaves burn and dry out.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi bɛ lɛ, Koni ekɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa Baai bibii lɛ baashã ni amɛbaagbi.

english: Why do my maize plant leaves have small ragged holes and look like something is eating them from the inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni etamɔ nɔ ni nɔ ko miiye lɛ kɛmiijɛ emli?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which burrow into the central leaves of young maize plants and eat the foliage before it unfolds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai amli ni eyeɔ baai lɛ dani egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and turning yellow before the fruits grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects, or by extreme heat and irregular watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa mli

english: Cassava plants naturally shed their leaves during dry periods to conserve water and survive drought. The plant stays alive underground and grows new leaves when the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛwoɔ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from excessive heat, dry soil, or heavy rains that wash away the pollen before insects can pollinate the plant.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli baa, ni no hoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ dani kooloi bibii baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tip and moves down the middle indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is an essential nutrient maize needs to stay green and grow well.
ga: Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naagbee ni eyaa shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa ni he hiaa koni ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli ni eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I spread dry grass around the base of my crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass around crops acts as mulch, which shades the soil, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and keeps the plant roots cool.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛbaabɔle Crops lɛ he lɛ baatsu nii akɛ mulch. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks next to my yam plants as they start to sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato tso ko masɛi beni ejeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need stakes to support them so their leaves can spread out in the sun, which helps the plant build large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa tso ni fiɔ amɛsɛɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often leaves the soil underneath still hot and dry. Planting too early can cause seeds to dry out and die if a dry spell follows before the regular rains start.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli dɔɔ lolo ni egbiɔ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi kɛji akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does leaving weeds near my crops reduce my harvest at the end of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and plant food in the soil, effectively starving your crops and reducing the size of your yield.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ ni ebaaha onibii lɛ anɔ aba shi.

english: Why do some of the new cocoa seedlings I bring to my farm die within the first month of planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei ni mikɛbaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi gboiɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni akɛduɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings often suffer from transplant shock if their roots get damaged during planting, or if they are exposed to harsh sunlight and dry soil before their root system is established.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ naa transplant shock kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ fite yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ enɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ dani shishifãi lɛ je shishi.

english: What is the best time of the year for me to plant new crop seedlings on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli be hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ madu dumɔwui heei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting at the start of the major rainy season ensures that young crops get continuous water to grow deep roots before the dry Harmattan period begins.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ náa nu ni yaa nɔ koni amɛwo shishifãi dani harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and drying up in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tender cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct, intense sunlight; they need temporary shade from larger plants like plantains to protect their delicate leaves and keep the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni ebu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in damp, dark, and crowded farm conditions during the rainy season.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela kɛbaa Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔ mli hei ni hulutsoo be, duŋ, kɛ gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: What is causing the stems and branches on my cocoa trees to swell up and stop bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa tso lɛ shishi kɛ eniji ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa yibiiwoo?

english: Swollen branches are a symptom of cocoa swollen shoot virus, which is transmitted by tiny insects called mealybugs and weakens the tree's ability to carry food and water.
ga: Niji ni efuu lɛ ji kookoo bud virus ni efuu lɛ he okadi. ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ mealybugs. ni ehaa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛ niyenii kɛ nu yaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why am I seeing small dark spots and burn marks on my young cocoa shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ? Ni shãa he okadii ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: These burn spots are usually caused by insects called mirids or capsids that bite into the tender parts of the plant to suck sap, causing the tissue to die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids loo capsids ni ŋmɔɔ tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ koni amɛnu nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shãa hei nɛɛ baa. kɛ fãji gbele baa

english: How do crop diseases spread from one tree to another on my farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Diseases spread through wind, rain splashes, dirty pruning tools, or insects moving from infected plants to healthy ones.
ga: Helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ nibii ni akɛfoɔ tsei ni he tseee lɛ anɔ. loo kooloi ni fãa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why does my cocoa tree grow plenty of heavy green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When a tree has too many bushy branches, it wastes its energy on leaf growth instead of flowering, and the lack of sunlight inside the canopy stops pods from forming.
ga: Kɛ tso ko yɛ niji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ Efiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai lɛ moŋ fe ni eeewo fɔfɔi. Ni hulu la ni bɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli lɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ ada.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or maize between my newly planted cocoa trees?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ani abaanyɛ afee yɛ kookoo tsei ni adu ehee lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, intercropping works well during the early years to provide shade and income, but crops must be spaced properly so they do not compete with young cocoa for water and soil nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli. koni ekɛ hulutsoo kɛ shika aha Shi esa akɛ tsei lɛ abɔ he jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo bibii lɛ akatswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds regularly around the base of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni bɔle mitso lɛ he lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ashishitoo lɛ ji daa.

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from your crops, and they also provide hiding places for pests and diseases that can attack your plants.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baanyɛ atutua otsei lɛ hu náa he ko ni amɛhiɔ amɛhe.

english: How can I tell if my farm land is losing its power to grow good cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ adu kookoo kpakpa dɔŋŋ?

english: Soil loses its power when leaves turn yellow unexpectedly, young trees grow very slowly, or pod yields drop year after year. Adding organic compost or the right fertilizers helps feed the soil so it can nourish your trees again.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ baa shi kɛ́ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ trukaa. Tsei bibii lɛ daraa blɛoo waa. Aloo pod ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi afi fɛɛ afi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni eha otso lɛ niyenii ekoŋŋ.

english: What happens to my farmland if I plant crops on it every year without letting it rest?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nɔ daa afi ni mihaaa ejɔɔ ehe?

english: Planting every season without resting the land or adding manure drains all the natural plant food out of the soil. Over time, the land becomes weak, leading to smaller harvests and crops that catch diseases easily.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni aŋmɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii fɛɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni be hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ baa shi fioo, ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni helai baanyɛ aba lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do cocoa buyers reject some of my beans even when the pods looked healthy on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ kookoo lɛ kpooɔ mi kookoo lɛ ekomɛi eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Buyers check for proper fermentation and moisture content. Beans that are not dried well, became moldy during storage, or were harvested too early are rejected because they cannot produce good chocolate flavor.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kwɛɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli edɔ ha kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa. Beans ni egbi jogbaŋŋ Mold baa yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Aloo abaakpoo nibii ni akpaa mra tsɔ lɛ ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛha tsokolate kpakpa aba.

english: How do I know when my harvested cocoa beans are dry enough to take to the buying clerk?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cocoa yibii ni mikpa lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛya mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ aŋɔɔ?

english: Well-dried cocoa beans make a crackling sound when you squeeze a handful together. When you peel one open, the inside should be dark brown and brittle, not soft, purple, or slate-grey.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ gbee ni tswaa kɛji akɛ akɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni akɛ nine ebɔ he lɛ ebɔ he. Kɛji otsi ohe lɛ Esa akɛ emli lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ, shi jeee ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ loo slate gray.

english: Why do I need to cover my fresh cocoa beans with plantain leaves for a few days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ plantain baai aha kookoo yibii heei ahe gbii 2-3 dani mikɛgbi lɛ?

english: Covering the fresh beans creates heat, which starts a process called fermentation. This crucial step destroys the bean sprout, removes bitterness, and creates the chocolate flavor that buyers require.
ga: Beans heei ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ haa dɔlɛ baa. Enɛ jeɔ nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmɔtɔ shishi. Nɛkɛ gbɛ ni he hiaa nɛɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ehaa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why should I clear away bad or damaged cocoa pods left behind on the farm after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashɛrɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni ekumɔ loo efite ni eshwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashwie beni akpa kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving damaged or diseased pods on the trees or on the ground allows sicknesses like black pod disease to spread to your healthy trees. Removing and burying them keeps the farm clean and safe.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni efite loo hela emɔ amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ ni ofu amɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse ni ehi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches so air and sunlight can reach all parts of the tree. This keeps the farm dry enough to prevent black pod disease and encourages the tree to produce more pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbiɔ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛtsiɔ podi lɛ anaa ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo podi babaoo.

english: What can I do to keep weeds down on my farm if I do not have enough money to hire farm labor?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Ni kɛji akɛ mibɛ shika ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛbaahe ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi hu?

english: You can plant cover crops like shade plants or food crops in empty spaces to block sunlight from reaching weeds. Working in small, manageable sections each week also helps keep the farm clean without overwhelming you.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa nɔ ko nɔ tamɔ shade tsei loo niyenii tsei yɛ hei ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ koni hulu la akashɛ jwɛi lɛ ahe. Nitsumɔ yɛ fãi bibii amli Nɛkɛ shika ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii daa otsi nɛɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli tseɔ ni ehaaa onu he akɛ ogbɔjɔ.

english: Is it safe for me to grow food crops like cassava or plantain on the same land as my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting food crops alongside cocoa provides shade for young cocoa trees and gives your family food and quick cash while you wait for the cocoa trees to mature and yield pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ baaha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo. ni okɛ niyenii aha oweku lɛ kɛ shika oya be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni cacao tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛwo ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do many flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛhe diɛŋtsɛ amɛfeee kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers but can only support a small fraction as pods. Flowers drop if the tree lacks water, nutrients, or shade, or if there are not enough tiny insects around to pollinate them.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi ebaanyɛ eye ebua fã bibioo ko pɛ. No pɛ ji pod lɛ. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji nu, niyenii, loo hulutsoo bɛ tso lɛ he, loo kɛji kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ ehe.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, damp conditions. When bushes around the trees grow too wild or cocoa trees are too crowded, air cannot circulate, allowing dampness to stay on the pods and spoil them.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Beni jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Tsei lɛ daraa tsɔ loo kookoo tsei lɛ shwereɔ tsɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abɔle he. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmɔtɔ hi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite.

english: How do I know if the first rainy day of the season means it is time to plant my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa?

english: The very first rainfall after a dry season is usually not enough because the ground underneath is still very hot and dry. It is best to wait until there are two or three heavy rains so the soil becomes deeply moist before putting seeds into the earth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be sɛɛ lɛ faaa. Ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli edɔ waa lolo ni egbi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ aba koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i waa dani odu dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops dry up so quickly even when it rained a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩ oya eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Soil without organic cover acts like a open hot pan under the sun, letting water evaporate rapidly. Covering the soil around plants with dried grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool and locks in moisture longer after rain.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ pan ni mli edɔ ni agbele yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yam vines naturally want to climb toward the sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. If the vines stay on the ground, the leaves get shaded, wet, and diseased, resulting in very small tubers.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛkwɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ niyenii. Kɛji wain tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Baai lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛbaafee ŋmɔtɔ ni hela baamɔ amɛ, ni no baaha amɛyitsei bibii waa aba.

english: Plantain roots do not go deep into the earth; they spread wide near the topsoil. When the soil becomes soaked with water and heavy fruit bunches grow on top, strong winds easily pull the shallow roots out of the soft ground.
ga: Plantain shishifãi eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Amɛgbɛ amɛshwã he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewo nu ni aduawai babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Eshiɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: Yes, planting them together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in about three to four months, leaving plenty of room and soil nutrients for the slower-growing cassava to expand afterward.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji 3-4 mli, ni ehaa gbɛ kɛ niyenii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sun, soil food, and water. This results in thin, weak stalks with small ears of maize instead of strong plants with big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ, ni no haa anáa ŋmãa ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ji bibii kɛ toi bibii. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso nɛ wa nɛ e ngɛ tso agbo nɛ e he wa.

english: Why are there small holes in the leaves of my young maize plants with green waste inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni jwɛi eŋɔli yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the center whorl of the maize plant during the day and eats the tender leaves, which weakens the plant's growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tsei ateŋ yɛ gbi mli ni eyeɔ baai bibii, ni no haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, lack of regular water, or insufficient nutrients in the soil. Without a steady balance of moisture and nutrients, the plant cannot afford the energy to turn flowers into fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni faaa daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛtsake fɔfɔi amɛwo yibii kɛkɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers check the green leaves of my crops so closely when they visit my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kwɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai eŋɔli lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ amɛbasara miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves show the early signs of plant health. Inspecting leaves helps spot plant diseases, insect pests, or nutrient shortages early before your whole field gets damaged.
ga: Baai tsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ mra. Kɛ́ akwɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni anaa tsei lɛ amli helai, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ mra. Dani okpokpaa muu lɛ fɛɛ baafite

english: Pale leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to make food from sunlight and keep their leaves dark green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni mli tse lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ hulu la mli ni ehaa baa lɛ su eŋɔli ni mli edɔ.

english: Why are tiny insects gathering on the underside of my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii Buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Insects like aphids hide under leaves to shelter from rain and direct sun while sucking sap from the plant, which starves the crop of nutrients.
ga: Kplukai, tamɔ aphids, kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai ashishi koni amɛná hebuu kɛjɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. yɛ be mli ni enuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni haa tsei lɛ náaa niyenii kpakpai lɛ

english: What causes the leaves on my rubber trees to get spots and drop off early?
ga: Mɛni miiha baai ni yɔɔ mi rɔba tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbee shi oya?

english: Early leaf drop in rubber trees is usually caused by fungal leaf spot diseases that spread in damp weather, which weakens the tree and reduces latex yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal leaf spot hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni fiteɔ mra yɛ rɔbɔt tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa latɛs ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does rainwater sit on top of my farmland without soaking into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehe wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When farm soil is packed too tightly or has poor drainage, water cannot flow through it. Standing water starves plant roots of air and causes root rot.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo ebɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Nu nyɛŋ atsɔ mli. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ aye tsei shishifãi lɛ ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings die when I pour too much water on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛmli babaoo lɛ?

english: Overwatering fills up all the tiny air spaces in the soil, which drowns the young roots and causes soil fungi to attack and rot the delicate stems.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ ayi obɔ, ni ebaaha shishifãi bibii lɛ atsɔ nu mli. ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why is it useful for an extension officer to inspect my field every single week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eyeɔ ebuaa akɛ extension officer ko baakwɛ mi nitsumɔhe nine lɛ daa otsi lɛ?

english: Weekly farm checks allow you to catch pest outbreaks or mold early while they are small, saving you from losing your entire crop harvest later.
ga: Otsi fɛɛ otsi ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ haa onyɛɔ onaa tsɛŋemɔ helai loo ŋmeii mra. Be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ Enɛ haa ohereɔ onibii fɛɛ ni okɛfiteɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: What will happen to my plants if I crowd too many of them in a small space?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsei babaoo fata he bibioo ko?

english: Plants crowded together fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems, weak crops, and poor yields.
ga: Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: How do buyers or extension officers decide the grade or quality of my harvested crops?
ga: Te mɛi ni heɔ nii loo mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ amɛkpɛɔ amɛyiŋ yɛ bɔ ni mikpamɔ lɛ ji loo bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ he?

english: Harvested crops are graded based on their size, color, moisture level, and lack of insect holes or disease spots. Clean and damage-free produce gets a higher grade and better price.
ga: Akɛ tsei ni akpaa lɛ toɔ amɛdalɛ, amɛhe su, kɛ bɔ ni amɛmli nu yɔɔ ha lɛ he. kɛ kooloi akutsei loo helai ahe hei ni bɛ Nibii ni he tse ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee lɛ baafã nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does keeping my rubber tree leaves healthy help the tree yield more liquid latex?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mi-latex baai lɛ ni mikɛhaa amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitso lɛ ni ekɛ latɛs babaoo baa?

english: Healthy green leaves act like small solar panels that make food energy for the tree. The more energy the tree makes, the more latex it produces when tapped.
ga: Baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulu hewalɛ ni haa tso lɛ niyenii. Babaoo ni tso ko baanyɛ afee hewalɛ, Babaoo ni ofeɔ latɛs lɛ, babaoo ni otaa he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen. The maize plant moves available nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to support new leaves at the top, showing that your crop needs fertilizer or well-rotted manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahi shi. Etsɔɔ akɛ otsei lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ.

english: Growing maize in the same spot repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. It also allows soil-borne pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply in that area, leading to weaker plants and lower yields.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. Ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ hu feɔ babaoo yɛ nakai he lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the roots of my crops help them survive during the hot season?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛyeɔ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, which acts like a blanket over the soil. It blocks harsh sunlight to keep the soil cool, prevents moisture from evaporating into the air, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch, ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsĩɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut away small suckers growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ

english: Small suckers compete with the main plantain tree for food, light, and water. By removing most of them and leaving only one or two, all the nutrients go into making the main stem grow big, heavy bunches.
ga: Suckers bibii lɛ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, la, kɛ nu. Kɛtsɔ amɛteŋ babaoo ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashiɔ eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ yaa mli ni ehaa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to produce energy for growing underground tubers. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground so the leaves get maximum light and reduces the risk of leaf fungal diseases from damp soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ la babaoo aba ni ebaa oshara ni baa baa lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ hela ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ shi.

english: Why do young cocoa trees die when I plant them in a clear open field without larger trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very sensitive leaves that easily burn and dry out under intense direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants nearby gives them the shelter and humidity they need to survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni shwereɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ haa amɛnáa wɔɔhe kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil when the rainy season becomes too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave standing water in the farm, the roots get suffocated from lack of oxygen, allowing waterlogging fungi to break down and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ ŋmɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ baafite ni amɛbaafite.

english: Why do my cowpea bean plants attract so many tiny insects as soon as they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii babaoo kɛ amɛjeɔ fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi pɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar and tender buds that serve as prime food for insects like thrips and aphids. This flowering stage naturally draws pests, making it the most vital time to inspect and protect your crop.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni ji niyenii titri kɛha kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips kɛ aphids. Nɛkɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be nɛɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa efeɔ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ni okɛbaakwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii amli ni obu he.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and stopping the crop from growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni ehaa tsei lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips feeding on the sap under tender new leaves, or by severe heat stress causing the leaves to fold up to conserve water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ashishi lɛ nu ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into fruits during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing successful pollination. When flowers fail to pollinate, the plant drops them off to save energy rather than trying to feed infertile flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. ni ehaa pollination lɛ yeee omanye. Beni fɔfɔii lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee pollin lɛ Tso lɛ baashi lɛ koni ekɛto hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni eeebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eha fɔfɔii ni nyɛɛɛ afɔ bii lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist, helping the young cocoa survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off before forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani ŋmeii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree lacks water, faces extreme heat, or is attacked by tiny pests like mirids. Maintaining shade trees and protecting the farm from insects helps flowers turn into full cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu bɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Ni ekɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kpeɔ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen ni tutuaa lɛ. Tsei lɛ ni oooha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni abu ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches during storms. Supporting the stems with strong bamboo poles and piling up soil around the base helps anchor the plant.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni eye ebua aduawai ni tsii lɛ yɛ ahum be mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ, ni okɛ sũ ni ato shishi lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ tso lɛ ama shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your maize is starving for nitrogen. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea when the corn is young keeps leaves green and feeds the growing cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii beni ŋmãa lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa ŋmei ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the centers of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which hide in the growing center of maize to feed on soft leaves. Applying recommended insecticides or sprinkling clean wood ash into the leaf funnel early helps kill them before they destroy the plant.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii loo tso sũ ni he tse ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ amli mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni agbe amɛ dani amɛkpãtã tso lɛ hiɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because they suffocate when buried under standing water. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ kɛ́ afu amɛ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo shishi lɛ, amɛmuɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines onto tall stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines must climb high to catch enough sunlight to produce food for big tubers underground. Staking also lifts leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaaha niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji lɛ. Staking hu woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni ekɛtsi fungal baa helai anaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and stopping growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Curled tomato leaves are usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies, or by extreme heat. Using neem oil sprays to control whiteflies and watering regularly keeps the plants healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly loo kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akɛkudɔɔ whiteflies kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem causes chemical burns to the plant's skin and roots. Fertilizer should be placed in a small ring a few inches away where roots can safely absorb the nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa tsofai lɛ shãa tso lɛ hewolo kɛ shishifãi lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. No mli lɛ, jɛmɛ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: How does planting cowpeas between my corn rows improve my farm soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas gather nitrogen gas from the air and put it back into the soil, which naturally feeds the corn. Their spreading leaves also cover the ground, keeping weeds down and conserving soil moisture.
ga: Cowpeas buaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, he ni ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: How can I prepare my land properly so my crops produce strong, healthy flowers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo fɔfɔi ni wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Clearing the land properly, adding compost or rich manure, and making sure the soil holds water well gives plant roots the nutrients they need to produce strong flowers that eventually turn into heavy fruits.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he. kɛ nɔmimaa ni akwɛɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahiɛ nu jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha tsei shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛbaafee nɔ ni tsii.

english: What is the benefit of spraying liquid fertilizer on my crop leaves and flowers instead of applying solid fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baa kɛ fɔfɔi anɔ yɛ nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Liquid fertilizer sprayed directly on the foliage works much faster because plants absorb nutrients quickly through their leaves, giving them an immediate boost right when flowers are starting to form.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii oya kwraa ejaakɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii oya kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Okɛ amɛ awo mli kɛji fɔfɔii je shishi amɛfee pɛ.

english: When is the best time of day for me to spray liquid fertilizer on my blooming crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ afɔ tsei ni miifɔ lɛ anɔ?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the sun is cool, so the liquid does not evaporate quickly or burn the delicate flowers under hot sunlight.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔse nɔ lɛ leebi loo shwane mli. Kɛ hulu la lɛ mli ejɔ Enɛ ji koni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya loo eha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ashã yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Will spraying fertilizer directly onto open flowers cause them to burn or drop off?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi ni agbele nɔ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha amɛshã loo amɛgbee shi?

english: If mixed at the right strength and applied during cool hours, mild liquid fertilizers strengthen flowers. However, using strong chemicals or spraying during hot sun can cause delicate flower petals to burn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛfutu bɔ ni sa mli ni akɛwo mli gbɛkɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni bɛ hewalɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ aná hewalɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ adara waa. Aloo kɛ́ akɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã fɔfɔi lɛ ahe tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why are bees and other insects visiting the flowers on my farm important for my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii krokomɛi No hewɔ lɛ, saralɔi ni baa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe hiaa yɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli.

english: Insects transfer tiny yellow grains called pollen from flower to flower. This process, called pollination, fertilizes the crop so that flowers actually turn into fruits, pods, or seeds instead of drying up.
ga: Kplukai kɛ dumɔwui bibii ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ yaa. Atsɛɔ nakai akɛ pollen ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli. Atsɛɔ gbɛ nɛɛ akɛ pollination. Ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tso lɛ mli bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo dumɔwui yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbi.

english: Why do the flowers on my vegetables keep falling off without making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Flowers usually drop without forming fruit because of extreme heat, lack of water, poor soil nutrients, or a lack of insects like bees to carry pollen between flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni hiɛɔ pollen yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ lɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do some farmers plant other types of flowering plants alongside their main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ fɔfɔii srɔtoi krokomɛi yɛ amɛŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Planting attractive flowering crops nearby lures useful pollinators like bees to your farm, ensuring continuous pollination for your main crops throughout the growing season.
ga: Fɔfɔi tsei fɛfɛji ni ooodu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ baagbala ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii, kɛba oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha otsei titrii lɛ aya nɔ aná ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Is there anything I can do by hand to help my crop flowers make fruit if there are no bees around?
ga: Ani nɔ ko yɛ ni manyɛ mikɛ miniji afee koni eye ebua mitsei lɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛji ŋmeii bɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, you can practice hand pollination by gently shaking the plants or using a soft brush to transfer pollen from one flower to another to help fertilization happen manually.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ nine afee pollination kɛtsɔ tso lɛ ni oootsi lɛ blɛoo lɛ nɔ. Aloo okɛ brɔsh ni yɔɔ blɛoo atsu nii ni okɛjie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli koni ekɛha fɔfɔi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ fɔmɔ aya hiɛ.

english: How can I keep my crops flowering for a longer period so I can harvest over many weeks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee fɔfɔi be kakadaŋŋ bɔni afee ni akpa amɛ otsii babaoo?

english: Providing steady watering, feeding the plants liquid nutrients periodically, and picking ripe fruits quickly encourages the plant to keep producing fresh new flowers.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa daa Ha tsei niyenii ni ji nu yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Ni aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpɛɔ oya lɛ woɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni eya nɔ ewo fɔfɔi heei heei.

english: What kind of quick farm tasks require extra young workers during the flowering stage?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ ni he hiaa waa biɔ oblahii kɛ oblayei nitsulɔi yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli?

english: During flowering, young workers are helpful for delicate tasks like applying liquid sprays, carefully removing weeds without shaking off flowers, and monitoring for pests that attack blooms.
ga: yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Obalahii kɛ oblayei nitsulɔi baaye abua yɛ nitsumɔi ni mli wa tamɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ fɔfɔi lɛ akashwie shi. ni okwɛ koni ana kooloi ni tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need plantain trees planted right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni adu plantain yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing young cocoa with essential shade and soil moisture until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eshɛɔ shweremɔ he.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and dry up so quickly during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and broad leaves that lose water fast. During dry weather, the plant drops its leaves to conserve internal moisture and protect its main root system from dying.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli ni amɛbu shishifãi titri lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbo.

english: Why are my yam tubers coming out so small even though I planted a lot of seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ bibii waa beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When yams are planted too close, their roots fight each other for limited water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough spacing allows the roots to expand fully into large tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu sweet potatoes ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baawu koni amɛná nu fioo, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when stressed by severe heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, causing the plant to focus on leaf growth rather than fruit production.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baa lɛ dalɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai ni ebaawo lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning small and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a clear sign of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that suck plant sap and prevent the leaves from making food for the root.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ. Agbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee niyenii amɛha shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do fall armyworms attack my maize farm when the crop is still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms miitutua mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ? He ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms prefer young maize plants because tender green shoots are easy to eat and full of nutrients that help the pests feed and multiply rapidly.
ga: Fall cutworms lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ejaakɛ ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ yeli waaa, ni niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni yeɔ nii ni efɔɔ oya lɛ eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why is my maize growing very tall but with weak stems that fall over in strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abele lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ shi eshishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ fãa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa hewɔ lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer makes maize grow tall too fast without building strong, thick stalks or strong root anchor systems.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ ada oya tsɔ ni ekɛ ŋmãa ni mli wa, ni mli wa loo shishifãi ni mli wa baaa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow at the tips even after I applied fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛnaagbɛ beni awo amɛ ŋmãa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can soak it up. If the ground is too dry or lacks balanced nutrients, the plant cannot feed properly and turns yellow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo niyenii ni sa bɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aye niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni ebaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do fast-growing hybrid tomato seeds need much more water and care than my local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hybrid tomato dumɔwui ni shwereɔ oya lɛ biɔ nu kɛ saamɔ babaoo fe mimaŋ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Hybrid tomato varieties are bred to grow very fast and produce heavy fruit yields, which means they consume water and nutrients at a much higher rate than hardy local varieties.
ga: Akwɛ tomato ni ji hybrid lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ oya waa ni ewo yibii babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, tomato kɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii babaoo fe maŋ lɛ mli tsei ni wa lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava turn hard and woody if I leave it in the ground too long waiting for high market prices?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni efeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni miimɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are temporary energy stores. Once fully mature, the plant begins converting its soft starch into tough woody fiber to survive, lowering the cooking quality of the root.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji hewalɛ jɛɛhe ni yɔɔ be kukuoo mli. Kɛji Tsei lɛ dara kwraa lɛ, amɛbaabɔi ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ tsakemɔ amɛwo tso mli tsɔi ni wa mli koni amɛhi shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ hoɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does rice grow so well in flooded water when other crops die if there is too much water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu afua mli lɛ? Akɛni tsei krokomɛi gboiɔ kɛji nu fa babaoo hewɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special hollow spaces in their stems and roots that act like tiny breathing tubes, allowing air to reach the roots even when submerged in water, unlike crops like maize whose roots rot without dry soil air.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ mumɔ tsɔnei bibii. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛji akɛ amɛbote nu mli po. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ tsei tamɔ ŋmãa ni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the plant is short on soil nutrients like nitrogen, so it starves its older leaves to send whatever food it has left to keep the new top leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, no hewɔ lɛ hɔmɔ miiye lɛ baa momoi lɛ koni ekɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje baa heei yɛ nɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water, resulting in tall, thin, weak plants that produce very small or empty food heads.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei ni eda lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ niyenii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow slower when the weather stays cloudy and dark for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ewo atatu ni atatu ewo mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crops use sunlight as their main source of energy to make their own food. When there is heavy cloud cover for long periods, the plants produce less energy and their growth slows down.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii akɛ amɛ hewalɛ jɛɛhe titri ni amɛkɛfeɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii. Kɛ atatu ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ Tsei lɛ baajie hewalɛ fioo ni amɛdalɛ baafee mlɛo.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant rice on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests that feed on that specific crop to build up in large numbers in the ground.
ga: Nibii komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be, ni eyeɔ ebuaa nibii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛbuaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster on my land than the actual seeds I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants naturally built to survive under tough conditions, so they quickly suck up the water and soil nutrients meant for your crops before your crop roots get established.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni adebɔɔ fee koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛmuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ okɛbaatsu nii lɛ mli lɛ oya dani tso lɛ shishifãi baa.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to clear and break up hard soil before planting our seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔjie shikpɔŋ ni wa dani wɔdu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Loosening hard soil allows young plant roots to push deep into the ground easily to find water, while also letting air into the soil so seeds can breathe and sprout.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛna nu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, aŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛ ni eboteɔ sũ lɛ mli koni eha dumɔwui lɛ amu ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do so many insects show up on my farm right when the crops start to flower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo jeɔ kpo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ je fɔfɔi shishi pɛ?

english: Flowers and developing grains contain soft tissues and natural sugars, which act as a rich food source that attracts hungry insects looking for energy to feed and lay eggs.
ga: Fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui ni miida lɛ yɛ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ adebɔɔ mli sugars. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni fa babaoo ni gbalaa kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni miitao hewalɛ ni amɛkɛyeɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ amɛwui lɛ.

english: Seeds usually fail to sprout if they were buried too deep for the shoot to reach the surface, if the soil was too dry for the seed to wake up, or if soil insects ate the seed underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃, Aloo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How can I tell if my rice crop is fully mature and ready for harvest instead of just drying up from disease?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa? Yɛ hɔmɔ ni jɛɔ hela mli baa lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Healthy mature rice turns a golden yellow color across the whole head while the stem stays firm, and the grains feel hard when pressed or bitten, whereas diseased crops dry up prematurely with soft or empty grains.
ga: Omɔ ni eda lɛ tsɔɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ yɛ bulb lɛ mli fɛɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ mli waɔ lɛ. ni dumɔwui lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ anyɛ amɛnɔ loo akɔmɔ amɛ. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baagbi mra kɛ dumɔwui ni edako loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do fall armyworms suddenly appear on my farm even when I did not see them last week?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni fall flukes lɛ je kpo trukaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Eyɛ mli akɛ minaaa amɛ yɛ otsi ni eho lɛ mli moŋ?
