english: Adult armyworm moths can fly long distances at night or travel on wind currents across wide areas to lay hundreds of eggs on healthy green crops before you even notice them.
ga: Kplukai ni eda lɛ baanyɛ afã kɛya he ko shɔŋŋ gbɛkɛ loo amɛfã gbɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ hei wuji koni amɛyawo ŋmeii ohai abɔ yɛ tsei eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ dani oyɔse amɛ po.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during prolonged dry weather as a natural defense to save water and protect their roots from drying out. They will sprout fresh green leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu nɔ ko ni akɛbuɔ nu he ni ebuɔ eshishifãi lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi. Amɛbaakwɛ̃ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa plants turn yellow and burn when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and tender roots that dry out easily under direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains during their early years to shield them until their roots grow deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ mli baawo shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Can wild birds or roaming animals carry diseases to my farm crops?
ga: Ani koo mli okpoi loo kooloi ni nyiɛɔ kɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛ hela aba ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, wild birds and animals can pick up fungal spores, bacteria, or insects on their feet, feathers, or fur from distant areas and drop them onto your healthy crops while searching for food.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, okpoi kɛ koo mli kooloi baanyɛ aŋɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai, bacteria, loo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ amɛnaji, amɛtsitsii, loo amɛtsitsii anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmɛɛ he yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ beni otaoɔ niyenii lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing very tall with many green leaves but producing no flowers or tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Baai eŋɔlii babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Shi fɔfɔi loo tomato ko bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen manure relative to other nutrients, the tomato plant puts all its energy into growing tall stem and foliage instead of producing flowers and fruit.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Tomato tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii kɛ baai ni kɛlɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into tubes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl inward during hot afternoons to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the sun, which helps the plant conserve water and survive the day's heat.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba baa lɛ nɔ ni hulu lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛjoɔ dɔlɛ naa foi nakai gbi lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants stay thin and produce small cobs when I plant many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds are planted in a single spot, the young plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, causing all of them to grow weak and thin.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ Tsei bibii baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ daa ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why do my crops stop growing well when weeds surround their roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekpaa shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ jwɛi bɔle amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal essential soil nutrients, moisture, and sunlight away from your crops, effectively starving the crop plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli oya. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do birds attack my cereal crops right when the grain starts forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi tutuaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛji dumɔwui je shishi amɛfee pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Birds target young grains during the milk stage because the seeds are soft, sweet, and easy to digest, providing high energy for them.
ga: Okpoi kwɛɔ dumɔwui bibii anɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa amɛ nu lɛ ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛmli ŋɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ oya, ni amɛhaa hewalɛ babaoo.

english: Why do white powdery spots appear on my plant leaves after a long period of rain and damp weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: High moisture and damp air allow fungal spores to multiply rapidly on wet leaf surfaces, leading to fungal diseases like powdery mildew.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ haa fungal spores lɛ shwereɔ oya yɛ baa ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ powdery mildew baa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizers like urea or well-decomposed animal manure helps restore green leaves and improves crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What causes small holes in my cabbage leaves, and how can I stop insects from eating them?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ kaabeji baai anɔ Ni te abaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye lɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by caterpillars like the diamondback moth larvae. You can protect your crop by inspecting plants early, removing weeds where pests hide, and applying approved crop protection sprays when needed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ diamondback ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ onibii ni oookwɛ mli mra lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe ewo mli lɛ. ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii kɛ ehe miihia.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stems too close to each other on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives the roots enough space to expand into large, healthy tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are ready to be harvested?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions. Pruning extra shade tree branches to let sunlight reach the cocoa trees and removing infected pods helps control the spread.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ amli koni hulu la ashɛ kookoo tso lɛ he, ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Is it better to plant saved seeds from my last harvest or buy certified seeds from the agro-dealer?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli loo mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred to resist local pests, survive drought better, and produce higher yields. Seeds saved from past harvests often lose these protective traits, leading to lower yields.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ mli ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ nibii ni buɔ mɔ he nɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi.

english: How does a delay in rainfall affect my seeds right after I plant them?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ saa midumɔwui lɛ ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Seeds need moisture to sprout and build early roots. If the rains delay after planting, seeds can dry up in the hot soil, fail to germinate, or produce weak seedlings that struggle to grow.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa nu koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi mra. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui baanyɛ agbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ loo eha dumɔwui lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ewa akɛ amɛakwɛ̃

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn to dust and show tiny holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ mli eyi kɛ sũ ni bu bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: This damage is caused by storage pests like maize weevils that feed on the inside of the grain. Drying your maize thoroughly before storage and keeping it in airtight bags stops these pests from multiplying.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa dani okɛto ni okɛwo kotoku ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafa babaoo.

english: Can I plant groundnuts together on the same land with my maize crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Yes, planting groundnuts with maize is beneficial because groundnuts naturally capture nitrogen from the air and add it to the soil, which helps feed the maize and improves soil fertility.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmei duɔ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Enɛ baaye abua ni akwɛ ŋmãa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing food and water from your young plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my soil is losing its power to grow healthy crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Soil is losing fertility if your crops grow very slowly, look pale or stunted, and produce lower yields than in previous years despite good rainfall. Adding organic compost or rotated leguminous crops helps restore its strength.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ miifite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ onibii lɛ miida blɛoo waa. Etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo egbɔjɔ Ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi fe nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ yɛ nugbɔ kpakpa ni nɛ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ organic compost loo legume rotation fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leaf growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea during early growth helps keep leaves green and improves your grain yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha dumɔwui lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my farmland produce less corn when I plant corn on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Is it better for me to apply fertilizer immediately after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: Heavy rains wash away fertilizer before your crops' roots can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not overflowing with heavy running water.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu ni hoɔ waa lɛ ehiɛɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my young cocoa plants dying when they are exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that dry out easily under harsh sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a protective canopy until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ feɔ ŋtayaa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my crops very close together so more seeds fit on my land?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná dumɔwui babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and poor yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to produce larger fruits.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii wuji.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Providing steady water at the soil level during flowering helps the blooms stay on and develop into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and small worms eating inside the plant tops?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ amli

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on maize leaves and stalks. Checking your farm early and using recommended biopesticides or neem leaf extracts when crops are young protects them from heavy damage.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem baa mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baabu ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ fitemɔ ni mli wa he.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids spreading viruses. Controlling these insects early with soapy water sprays or safe insecticides prevents leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ numɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Nu ni akɛ samla loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akafite baa lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in clay heavy or poorly drained soil during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I stop tiny black beetles from destroying my harvested maize while it is stored in bags?
ga: Matsi ŋmei diŋ bibioo lɛ naa. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ akafite be mli ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ?

english: These beetles are grain weevils that thrive in moist grains. Drying your harvested maize thoroughly in the sun until it is completely hard and storing it in airtight, hermetic bags suffocates pests without needing harsh chemicals.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji dumɔwui amli ŋmeii ni shwereɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni mli ewo fɔ mli. Okɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛwo vacuum bag mli ni okɛwo mli. Ebaaha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ekɛ tsofai ni mli wa tsuuu nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need shade from bigger trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni tso ni da fe no lɛ aná hulutsoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Shade trees act as protective cover, cooling the air and retaining soil moisture so the young cocoa can establish strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Bɔni afee ni kookoo bibioo lɛ anyɛ afee shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: What will happen to my cocoa farm if I clear all the big trees off the land?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Removing all big trees leaves your cocoa exposed to harsh sun and wind, which can dry out the soil quickly and cause the cocoa leaves to scorch or the plants to die early.
ga: Tsei wuji fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa aba kookoo lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya ni eha kookoo baai lɛ ashã loo tso lɛ agbo oya.

english: How do I know if my cocoa farm has too much shade?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be babaoo?

english: If the tree canopy is too thick and blocks almost all sunlight, your cocoa trees will grow tall and thin without producing many pods, and fungal diseases can spread more easily in the damp dark conditions.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli tse tsɔ ni etsĩ hulu la lɛ babaoo naa lɛ, O-cacao tso lɛ baakwɛ ni efee bibioo ni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo baaa. Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli baa lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli.

english: Should I cut down all the old trees on my plot before I start planting standard crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo tsei momo fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani mabɔi tsei ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ adumɔ?

english: You do not need to cut down every old tree. Leaving select shade trees helps protect your farm's ecosystem, while removing only diseased, weak, or overly dense trees makes room for your crops.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni ofolɔ tso momo fɛɛ tso momo. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni oooshi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ, ni bɛ hewalɛ, loo tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ pɛ. Enɛ baaha gbɛ aha oŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Why do some trees keep growing so well even after I clear the land around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mijie he ni amɛbɔle amɛhe lɛ po lɛ?

english: Certain deep-rooted forest trees are very resilient and naturally adapted to the soil. When surrounding vegetation is cleared, they gain access to more sunlight and continue to thrive alongside your new crops.
ga: Koo mli tsei komɛi ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi waa, ni amɛfeɔ amɛhe amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ, tsei lɛ náa hulu la babaoo. ni oya nɔ oda yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ ahe.

english: How do I choose which old trees to keep on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei momoi ni mikɛbaato miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Keep trees that provide light, filtered shade and do not harbor cocoa pests or diseases. Avoid keeping trees that have massive shallow roots that aggressively steal water and nutrients from your crops.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsei ni haa la, hulutsoo ni amɛhiɛɛɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo kookoo helai. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni shishifãi wuji ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni baaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ waa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli lɛ ahe.

english: Can I grow food crops under the shade of bigger trees on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi?

english: Yes, shade-tolerant food crops or short-term crops like plantains and root vegetables can be grown under trees while your main crop is young, providing food and extra shade.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ adu tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hulutsoo shi loo niyenii ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ plantains kɛ shishifãi aduawai yɛ tsei ashishi be mli ni otsei titrii lɛ darako lolo lɛ. Kɛtsɔ niyenii kɛ hulutsoo kroko ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔ.

english: If I care for and weed my food crops underneath the trees, will the shade trees benefit too?
ga: Kɛ mikwɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ anɔ ni mijie amɛ Ani tsei ni haa shade lɛ hu baaná he sɛɛ?

english: Yes, when you weed, water, or add nutrients to the food crops beneath, the surrounding shade trees also absorb those extra nutrients and water, helping them stay healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni okɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shi, okɛ nu woɔ mli, loo okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ woɔ niyenii tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ shade ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ hu shwieɔ nakai niyenii kɛ nu ni fa lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Won't large shade trees steal all the water and nutrients from my food crops?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ejuŋ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Large shade trees usually have deeper root systems that pull nutrients from lower soil layers, while food crops feed near the surface. Managed properly, they can coexist without starving your food crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei wuji ni yɔɔ shade lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. be mli ni niyenii tsei yeɔ nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ Kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi ni hɔmɔ egbeee oniyenii tsei lɛ.

english: Do temporary food crops help young cocoa trees survive their first year?
ga: Ani niyenii ni akɛhaa yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli?

english: Yes, fast-growing food crops like plantain provide immediate side-shade to shield young cocoa seedlings from direct sun while the long-term shade trees grow taller.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa sɛɛgbɛ hulutsoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ebu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when exposed to direct sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate full sunlight. Planting shade trees or plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects seedlings from solar heat and helps soil retain moisture.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which plants need to produce chlorophyll. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or waterlog the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛfee chlorophyll Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ehaa shishifãi lɛ ebɔle nu he.

english: Why should I plant cassava stem cuttings at a slant instead of pushing them straight down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi yucca tsei lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni madu shi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a 45-degree angle buries multiple nodes under the soil, giving the plant more points to grow strong roots, which leads to a larger crop of tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tso yɛ 45 degree angle mli lɛ, ebaafu nodes babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ehaa tso lɛ náa shishifãi ni mli wa waa. Enɛ haa akwɛɔ bulbs wuji.

english: What causes small worms to eat holes in the leaves inside the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which target the tender central leaves (whorl) of young maize. Controlling them early prevents them from destroying the growing point of the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo (rings) lɛ anɔ. Amɛ nɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my piece of land produce smaller yields every year even though I plant at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Nɛgbɛ miduɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Crops remove nutrients from the soil every season. Without adding compost, manure, or fertilizer, or rotating with crops like beans, the soil loses its fertility over time.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ tamɔ ŋmeii fataaa he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Removing excess shoots (suckers) prevents them from stealing water and nutrients from the main plant, allowing the main stem to produce larger and healthier bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii (ŋmeii) ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ woɔ plantains wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops wilt so quickly during short dry spells even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gboɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mikɛ nu wo mli po

english: Bare soil loses moisture rapidly through sun evaporation. Placing dry grass or leaves (mulch) around the base of plants shades the dirt, keeping the root area moist for much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ hulu la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (Mulch) wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi muji naa. ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting when air temperatures get too high or when watering is irregular, which causes heat stress that stops pollination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ shwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni haa pollination kpaɔ baa.

english: Staking raises yam vines off the ground so their leaves get full sunlight to make food for the growing tuber under the ground, while keeping leaves safe from soil diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ koni ekɛ ehe baai lɛ aje kpo yɛ hulu la ni yeɔ emuu lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baa lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout if I plant immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain often only wet the surface while deep soil stays hot and dry. If rain stops for days after, the seeds get scorched by the trapped ground heat before they can root properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ pɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ ni egbi. Kɛji nugbɔ kpa nɛmɔ yɛ gbii komɛi asɛɛ lɛ, la ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shãa Dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo shishifãi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How should I handle weeds on my farmland before I plant my crops?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mafee jwɛi ni yɔɔ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ dani madu?

english: Clearing weeds before planting gives your young crops a strong start. Removing weeds prevents them from stealing sunlight, water, and soil food from your seeds while they are trying to sprout.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi dani odu lɛ, ehaa odumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ. Jwɛi ni ogbeɔ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ odumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ be mli ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Is it better to burn the cut weeds on my farm or leave them on the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni afo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ loo mashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Leaving cut weeds on the soil to dry and rot into mulch is better than burning them. Mulch keeps the soil cool, holds rainwater, and turns into natural organic matter that feeds your crops.
ga: Ehi akɛ oooshi jwɛi ni afo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni egbi ni egbo tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fe ni oooshã amɛ. Mulches yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ebuaa nugbɔ nu naa, ni ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do weeds grow back so fast and choke my young plants after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni ehaa mitsei lɛ shwereɔ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds produce many seeds that stay buried in the soil and sprout quickly when exposed to rain and sunlight. Clearing weeds regularly during the first few weeks gives your crops enough time to grow tall and shade out the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ woɔ dumɔwui babaoo ni afuɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ kɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi lɛ shwie shi daa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛdara ni amɛha jwɛi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are weeds dangerous to the growth of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ awui lɛ?

english: Weeds act as aggressive neighbors to your crops by competing directly for food in the soil, space, and water. If left unattended, weeds will make your crops weak, thin, and unable to produce good yields.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ akutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ basabasa kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ akaŋshii ni amɛfeɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ, ŋwɛi kɛ nu mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi baaha onibii lɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ, amɛhe afee mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: How can I turn farm waste and household scraps into food for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsɔ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi kɛ shia nibii ni efite lɛ mafee niyenii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: You can pile up plant stalks, dead leaves, vegetable peels, and animal dung in a shaded area to rot over time into compost. Spreading this dark, rich compost around your crops acts as natural organic fertilizer.
ga: Obaanyɛ oto tsei ahe tsei ahe. Shi baai ni egboi, aduawai ahe tsɔi, kɛ kooloi afɔfɔi yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ koni amɛgbo yɛ be ni sa mli ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli ewo duŋ, ni jara wa nɛɛ ni akɛaabɔle he. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does natural organic fertilizer help my soil stay soft and rich?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii baa lɛ?

english: Natural organic matter binds soil particles together while leaving tiny air spaces, making hard soil soft and crumbly. This allows crop roots to grow easily, breathe well, and absorb water.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fiɔ sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ ahe, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii shwieɔ shi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egbɛɔ eshwaa Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni amɛdaraa mlɛo, amɛmuɔ mlɛo, ni amɛmuɔ nu.

english: Can using natural compost keep my crops green during dry periods?
ga: Ani adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni mitsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, natural compost acts like a sponge in the ground that holds onto soil moisture for a long time. During brief dry spells, crops growing in compost-treated soil can still draw water to stay healthy.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii hiɔ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ hulutsoo be kuku lɛ mli lɛ Tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ewo mli lɛ hu baanyɛ agbala nu koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves are often a sign that your crop is hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is trapped around the roots. Adding rotted organic manure provides steady nutrients to make leaves green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye onibii tamɔ nitrogen loo nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ be fɛɛ be ni baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is healthy enough to support good crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Healthy farm soil is usually dark in color, feels moist and soft when squeezed, smells fresh, and contains earthworms. If your soil is pale, hard, or sandy, adding natural organic waste will build back its strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kpakpai amli lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ blɛoo kɛji akɛ ashɛre lɛ. Eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ hee. ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli tse, ewa, loo ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ, adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ewaje lɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant the same crop on the same land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and lets pests settle in the field. Mixing or rotating different crops keeps the soil balanced and naturally prevents pests from taking over.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ayaa nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni oha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ loo atsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baaye nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh, direct sunlight. Planting them in direct sun without shade trees or plantains causes the leaves to scorch, turn yellow, and dry out due to heat stress and excessive moisture loss.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛ́ adu yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo loo dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ ashã. tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni fiteɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning light green and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen helps plants produce green leaves and grow strong, so adding nitrogen fertilizer or manure helps restore their dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha tso lɛ su ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts together with my maize makes the soil richer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, which means their roots have tiny bacteria that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally feeding and fertilizing nearby crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ muawai bibii yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. No yeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when the rains become too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot survive in waterlogged soil. Excess water fills all the air gaps in the dirt, suffocating the roots and allowing fungal diseases to rot the tubers under the ground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii helai fiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my crops wilt in the hot sun even if it rained heavily two days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii enyɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Without leaf cover or mulch on the ground, intense tropical sun bakes the topsoil and evaporates water quickly. If roots are shallow, they cannot reach deeper soil moisture once the top layer dries out.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛshɛ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ he kɛyashɛ sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ be mli ni ŋwɛi fã lɛ gĩɔ lɛ.

english: Extreme daytime heat, dry afternoon winds, or irregular watering stress the tomato plant. As a defense mechanism, the plant drops its flowers to save energy rather than spending effort to grow fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa yɛ gbi lɛ mli Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi yɛ shwane mli Loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei lɛ anɔ. akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do cocoa pods grow straight out of the thick trunk of the tree instead of small branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni mli wa lɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ niji bibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally flower and fruit on their main trunk and thick branches—a trait called cauliflory—so the tree can support the heavy weight of full cocoa pods without breaking thin outer branches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ eniji ni mli tse lɛ anɔ. ni atsɛɔ lɛ cauliflower No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ anɔ ni efoŋ kponɔgbɛ niji bibii lɛ.

english: Too many young shoots (suckers) steal food and water from the main mother plant. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the main stem to produce larger plantain bunches.
ga: Tso bibii (tso) bibii babaoo tsɔ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha ŋmeii titri lɛ afee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam vines need maximum exposure to light to make energy for their underground tubers. Lifting the vines off the wet ground on wooden stakes keeps leaves healthy, prevents fungal diseases, and grows bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia la babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛjɛ amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ amli. Wein tsei lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ feɔ fɛo. Tsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa ni oha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee wuji

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than the corn I planted in the same dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe ŋmãa ni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, local plants that are naturally tough and well-adapted to the local climate. They grab available soil nutrients, water, and sunlight much faster and more aggressively than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni ekɛ ehe kpãa gbee jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ lɛ mli oya kɛ hewalɛ fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct heat from the sun. Plantain trees grow very quickly and provide broad, leafy umbrellas that give young cocoa plants the shade and moisture they need during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crop full of holes with tiny caterpillars inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on maize leaves and stems. Applying recommended insecticides early in the morning or late evening when caterpillars are active helps protect your plants and recover your yields.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmãa shishifãi. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu otsei lɛ ahe ni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava start rotting within two or three days after I dig it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ bɔi fitemɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli beni mifo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots lose moisture very quickly and naturally break down once exposed to oxygen after harvest. Leaving cassava tubers in the soil until you are ready to process or sell them keeps them fresh for a much longer time.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ amɛbote kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ mli lɛ mli yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Ni oooshi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaatsu he nii loo ohɔ̃ɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ehi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build strong leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers like NPK or well-rotted animal manure around the crop roots restores their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛfee baai ni mli wa Kɛji akɛ nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmei ni fiteɔ ni bɔle Tsei lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Will I get more food if I plant my seeds very close to each other in the row?
ga: Ani maná niyenii babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: No, planting seeds too close together forces crops to compete for sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing helps them grow larger leaves, bigger roots, and higher yields.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii he. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ baai wuji, shishifãi wuji, ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my pepper plants dry up so quickly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture fast because hot sunlight turns ground water into steam. Covering the soil around your crop stems with dry grass or fallen leaves keeps the ground cool and traps water in the soil longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya beni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ tsɔɔ lasu lɛ. Mulching around Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ ha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is too hot, water is irregular, or the soil lacks nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil evenly moist and feeding plants properly encourages flowers to set healthy fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu lɛ ejaaa. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ calcium. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni oha otsei lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaawo fɔfɔi lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my cut seed yams rot in the mound before sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mifo lɛ miifite yɛ gɔji amli dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Fresh cut surfaces on seed yams easily attract rot-causing fungi when buried in wet soil. Rubbing clean wood ash onto the cut surfaces and letting them dry before planting creates a protective shield against soil disease.
ga: Nɔ ni afo ehee yɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ oya. Tso mli sũ ni he tse ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni afo lɛ nɔ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni egbiɔ dani aduɔ lɛ haa helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he.

english: Why is my maize crop producing smaller yields every year on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same spot every season drains the specific nutrients that crop relies on. Rotating your maize plot with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts refills nitrogen naturally in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo. Abɛi ŋmɔji ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii baatsake Ebaaye ebua ni akɛ nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I trim off extra side shoots from my tomato vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tomato wain tso ko mli tsei ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ?

english: Trimming unnecessary side branches forces the tomato plant to direct its energy into developing bigger, healthier tomatoes instead of wasting food on excess leaves and stems.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ sɛɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baaha tomato tso lɛ afite hewalɛ babaoo koni ekɛwo tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite niyenii yɛ baai kɛ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when there is too much direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that quickly lose moisture under full sun. Providing shade using temporary crops like plantains protects the seedlings until they grow strong enough to endure harsh sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shwieɔ nu oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the leaves regain their green color and produce better grain.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli, ni ji niyenii ni he hia kɛha tsei adalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛwo dumɔwui kpakpai.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil around them for too long, suffocating the roots. Planting on mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Beans and cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This naturally enriches the land and helps your maize grow better without needing as much expensive store-bought fertilizer.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ tsinabii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa o-ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inside leaves of my young maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which target tender new leaves inside the plant funnel. Treating them early with recommended pest controls keeps them from destroying the plant before it matures.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ anɔ. Amɛtsamɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ nɔ lɛ, obaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tso lɛ dani eshɛ shweremɔ he.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to capture maximum sunlight. Elevating the leaves off the ground prevents leaf rot and allows the plant to send more food down to build large yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni hulu la lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ fiteɔ, ni ehaa tso lɛ tsuɔ niyenii babaoo kɛyaa shi koni efee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts under the soil are ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni atsaaa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the outer leaves turn yellow and dry up. You can pull up one or two plants to check—if the insides of the shells have dark brown markings and firm nuts, it is time to harvest.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. You can pull up one or two plants to inspect. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ okadii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa Be eshɛɛ ni abaakpa.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow fast and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya, ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra small shoots growing around the bottom of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Mɛi krɛdɛɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi.

english: Multiple shoots steal food and water from the main mother plant. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoot, allowing the plant to produce a much bigger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ashiɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ plantains ni dara ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get stressed easily under direct sun and dry winds. Yellowing leaves mean the plant is losing moisture faster than its roots can drink, which is why young cocoa needs shade trees or plantains nearby to protect it.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ haoɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shishi. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ miifite oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni abu amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars feeding inside the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baa nɔ ni ŋmeii naa niyenii yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. The moths lay eggs on the leaves, and the caterpillars eat into the center of the maize plant, which can stop it from growing if not treated early.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ. ni ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ akpa dalɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the juice from the leaves, or by a virus carried by those insects. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ mli waa.

english: Why is it better for me to clear my farm without burning the weeds and dry bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ majie ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikɛ jwɛi lɛ kɛ brɔshi ni egbi lɛ shãaa lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the rich organic matter in the soil that holds water and nutrients. Allowing cleared weeds to decay naturally turns them into compost, which feeds the soil and keeps it moist.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ ni kɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ toɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni he tse lɛ fite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa sũ lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep, and well-drained soil to expand downward. High mounds make it easy for the tubers to grow long and thick while preventing water from settling and rotting the seed.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shi. Pile ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ bulb lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the plants grow very tall with many leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ? He ni sweet potato tsei lɛ daa waa ni amɛyɛ baai babaoo lɛ?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing tall stems and green leaves instead of expanding its underground roots.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe lɛ, Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ baai eŋɔlii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ shishifãi lɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over when the fruit bunches start getting large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, so top-heavy bunches can pull the weak stems down, especially during heavy rains or wind. You need to support the heavy fruit stems with bamboo or wooden props.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei niji ni tsii lɛ baanyɛ agbala tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ kɛba shi. Titri lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei loo tsei ni akɛfiɔ tso yibii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Extreme heat, lack of regular water, or uneven soil moisture can cause tomato plants to drop their blossoms. When stressed by heat or drought, the plant drops flowers to save its own life.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ be fɛɛ be Loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ejaaa lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ agbo. Kɛ ekɛ latsaa loo hɔmɔ kpe lɛ Tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why does leaving weeds on my field lower my harvest even if I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and will steal the fertilizer, soil moisture, and sunlight intended for your plants, leaving your crops weak and reducing your total yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. ni ebaaju fertilizer sũ mli nu kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ kɛha otsei lɛ Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi ni ehaa onibii fɛɛ ni onáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Beans and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which helps feed the maize naturally while covering the ground to prevent weeds from taking over.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ tsinabii amɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why do I see bees and tiny insects crawling on my crop flowers, and are they destroying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii krokomɛi lɛ? ni shwieɔ mi tso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ Ni ani amɛmiikpãtã amɛhiɛ?

english: Those insects are actually helping your farm through a process called pollination. They move pollen from one flower to another, which allows the plant to form healthy fruits, pods, and seeds.
ga: Nakai kooloi bibii lɛ miiye amɛmiibua oŋmɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ pollination lɛ nɔ. Amɛjieɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ aduawai, ŋmeii, kɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What actually causes my crop flowers to turn into healthy fruits and seeds?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔi ni miduɔ lɛ tsɔɔ aduawai kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Flowers need to be pollinated before they can make fruit. Pollination happens when wind, bees, or other small insects carry pollen between flowers, allowing the plant to successfully produce a harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli muji dani amɛwo yibii. Pollination baa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ, wuobii, loo kooloi bibii krokomɛi wo pollen yɛ fɔfɔi ateŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkpaa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do many of my crop flowers fall off without ever turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ aduawai kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers often drop off when they fail to get pollinated. If there are not enough insects like bees visiting your farm to spread pollen, the flowers die without producing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ anyɛɛɛ afee pollination. Kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni baasara oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ pollen lɛ amɛshwã. Fɔfɔ lɛ baagbo ni ewooo yibii.

english: How does keeping big forest trees around my farm help my crops produce more?
ga: Koo mli tsei wuji ni ebɔle mihe lɛ akwɛmɔ Te miŋmɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Big trees and natural forests provide homes and breeding grounds for bees and wild insects. When these trees are present, more insects come out to pollinate your crop flowers and boost your yield.
ga: Tsei wuji kɛ adebɔɔ mli kooi ji shihilɛhei kɛ hei ni ŋmeii kɛ koo mli kooloi fɔɔ yɛ. Kɛ tsei nɛɛ yɛ lɛ, kooloi baaje kpo koni amɛbawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen ni amɛha nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I avoid cutting down all the wild bushes and trees surrounding my crop fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ jwɛi kɛ koo mli tsei ni bɔle miŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ ahe?

english: Clearing all natural trees and bush destroys the natural shelter for helpful insects. Without a place to live, pollinating insects disappear, leading to poor pollination and smaller harvests.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli tsei kɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛhe ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛji he ko bɛ ni abaahi lɛ, Pollinators lɛ laaje. Enɛ haa pollination lɛ ehiii ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Will leaving some wild trees standing inside my farmland reduce or help my harvest?
ga: Ani koo mli tsei ni mashi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ aba shi loo ebaaye ebua?

english: Leaving some wild trees intact actually helps your harvest because it preserves natural habitats for bees and birds that visit your farm to pollinate your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi koo mli tsei komɛi ni amɛhiɛɛɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo diɛŋtsɛ yɛ okpamɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli shihilɛhe lɛ hiɔ shi kɛhaa ŋmeii kɛ okpoi ni baa oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛbawo onibii amli ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why did our elders get higher crop yields in the past compared to what we harvest today?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔ onukpai lɛ náa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli kɛ akɛto nɔ ni wɔkpaa ŋmɛnɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: In the past, intact forests provided natural habitats for abundant pollinators and rich natural systems, which naturally boosted crop fruit setting without heavy chemical intervention.
ga: Yɛ yinɔsane mli lɛ, kooi ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ eha adebɔɔ mli shihilɛhei eha ŋmeii babaoo ni shwieɔ ŋmeii kɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛjianɔtoi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛ tsofai babaoo tsuuu nii.

english: Does cutting down trees in nearby forest areas affect my farm even if the trees are not on my land?
ga: Ani tsei ni afoɔ yɛ kooi ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli lɛ baaná miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po?

english: Yes, because destroying nearby forests destroys the natural homes of wild pollinators. Fewer insects in the general area means fewer visits to your crop flowers, reducing your overall yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ kooi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni akpataa lɛ fiteɔ koo mli ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ adebɔɔ mli shia lɛ. Kplukai fioo ni yɔɔ he fɛɛ he lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ saramɔi fioo pɛ baa otso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa onitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why did my crop yields drop after the forest patch near my farm was completely cleared?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ ba shi beni ajie koo ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The nearby forest was housing wild bees and insects that naturally pollinated your crops. Destroying that forest removed those beneficial insects, leaving your flowers unpollinated.
ga: Koo ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ji he ni koo mli ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni jɛ adebɔɔ naa amɛwoɔ onibii amli ŋmeii lɛ yɔɔ. Tsoi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ nakai kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa ofɔfɔi lɛ shwieee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How do wild insects in the environment affect the weight and quality of my harvested crops?
ga: Te koo mli kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shihilɛ mli lɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ tsiimɔ kɛ bɔ ni ehi ha lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Insects ensure thorough pollination, which leads to properly developed, larger, and healthier fruits and seeds, resulting in a heavier and better harvest.
ga: Kplukai haa pollination lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa aduawai kɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ. amɛfeɔ agboi ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kpakpa Enɛ haa yibiiwoo ni tsii ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct sunlight and high temperatures. Shade trees protect them from sunburn, keep the surrounding soil cool and moist, and reduce water stress while their root systems are establishing.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. Ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. ni amɛha nu he haomɔ aba shi yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ miitswa amɛhe lɛ.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in high humidity and wet conditions. Raindrops splash the fungal spores from the soil or infected leaves onto healthy pods, causing them to blacken.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ diji.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow; when it runs out, the plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the younger top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda. Kɛ́ efo lɛ, tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over easily when strong winds blow through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over (a condition called lodging) when their brace roots are weak, shallow, or damaged, often due to poor soil structure, planting too shallowly, or lacking nutrients like potassium that strengthen stalks.
ga: Abɛi tso lɛ gbee shi (Shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy.) Kɛ́ shishifãi ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, amɛmli ekɔɔɔ, loo amɛfite lɛ, bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ. Dumɔ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tsɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium ni haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ waa lɛ bɛ mli

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee tsei kakadaji lɛ? koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up into the sunlight and air. This allows the plant to capture maximum light for leaf growth while keeping the leaves away from damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and encouraging larger underground tubers.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ la babaoo kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni owo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ahe hewalɛ

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The disease stops leaves from making food efficiently, resulting in stunted growth and smaller cassava tubers.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Hela nɛɛ haaa baai lɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dalɛ baa shi ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Allowing too many shoots (suckers) to grow creates intense competition for soil nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring the main plant yields big, heavy bunches.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo shwereɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ aba ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ afee agbo ni etsii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot or when soil moisture fluctuates sharply. These stress factors prevent proper pollination inside the flower, causing the plant to shed the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya. Nɛkɛ haomɔi nɛɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa ni baa fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni fɔɔ fɔfɔi

english: Why do my pepper leaves look wilted in the hot sun during midday even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ egbo lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: On very hot afternoons, pepper plants lose water vapor through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to close leaf pores and conserve water until temperatures cool in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu mli la kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛŋa eshishifãi lɛ be kukuoo ko ni ehiɛ nu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans on my farm make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have beneficial bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and convert it into a form stored in the soil. When the crop harvested, this natural nitrogen stays behind to nourish future crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa efeɔ nɔ ko ni buaa ehe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Beni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ baakã he ahi sɛɛ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaba wɔsɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: What will happen to my crops if the rains stop falling for a long period?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kakadaŋŋ?

english: When rain stops, crops lose the water they need to make food and absorb nutrients from the soil. This causes leaves to wilt, growth to stall, and can lead to total crop failure if the soil dries out completely.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛgbala niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. shweremɔ lɛ kpaa Ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akafite kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa.

english: Crops lacking water will look limp, their leaves will roll or curl inwards during the hottest part of the day, and the lower leaves may turn yellow and dry up as the plant tries to save water.
ga: Tsei ni nu efo mli lɛ baafee tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe loo amɛshwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Ni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi be mli ni tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ nu ato he lɛ.

english: Why do my crops dry up so quickly when the sun becomes very bright and hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso ni edɔ lɛ?

english: Hot sun makes water evaporate quickly from the soil and causes plants to lose water rapidly through their leaves. If the roots cannot pull up water fast enough from dry soil, the crop wilts and dries out.
ga: Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ Kɛji shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ oya bɔ ni sa lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbi.

english: How can I keep moisture in the soil for longer when the rain is delayed?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ?

english: You can cover the bare soil around your crops with dry grass, straw, or leaves. This layer blocks direct sunlight, keeps the ground cool, and stops water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ sũ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko awo ehe. Abaanyɛ akɛ jwɛi, jwɛi, loo baai adu ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ baatsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni otsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya.

english: Can I still grow crops during the dry season in Ghana if there is no rain?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii lolo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli yɛ Ghana kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Yes, you can farm in the dry season if you have access to a water source like a river, stream, or borehole and use a system to deliver water to your crops regularly.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ otsu okwaayeli yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛji oyɛ nu jɛɛhe ko tamɔ faa, faa loo nubu ni okɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni okɛ nu baaha onibii lɛ daa lɛ tsu nii.

english: How does using a water pump near a river help my crops survive?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu pɔmp ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ faa ko he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi?

english: A water pump draws water directly from a river or water source through pipes to your field, giving your crops a reliable supply of water whenever rainfall is not enough.
ga: Nu pɔmp lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ faa loo nu jɛɛhe mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ paipii amli kɛyaa oŋmɔji amli. Kwɛmɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nu jɛɛhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: Is it good practice to plant my crops right next to a river bank?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ yɛ faa lɛ naa lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa?

english: Planting near a river provides moist soil and easy access to water, but you must be careful because heavy water flow or sudden flooding can wash away your soil and drown crop roots.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ faa ko he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaaha nu aba mlɛo. Shi esa akɛ okwɛ ohe jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ nu afua ni naa wa loo nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ awo nu mli.

english: What is the best time of day for me to pump water onto my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mikɛ nu baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Early morning or late evening is best because temperatures are cooler, allowing the water to soak deep into the root zone before the hot sun can evaporate it.
ga: Leebi loo gbɛkɛ ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ boteɔ shishifã lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nyɛɔ efoɔ.

english: Why should I spend money to hire help for my farm work instead of doing it all alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika koni mahe mɔ ko ni eye ebua mi ni matsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mikome too matsu he nii?

english: Hiring extra help ensures critical tasks like land preparation, planting, and irrigation are completed on time, preventing crop damage and helping you produce a larger, more profitable harvest.
ga: Yelikɛbuamɔ krokomɛi ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ haa anyɛɔ agbeɔ nitsumɔi ni he hiaa tamɔ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ, dumɔwui, kɛ nu shwiemɔ naa yɛ be naa. Tsi ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni eye ebua bo ni oná nibii babaoo kɛ sɛɛnamɔ babaoo.

english: Can giving my crops too much water from a river or pump actually harm them?
ga: Ani nu babaoo ni jɛɔ faa loo pɔmp mli ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aye amɛ awui?

english: Yes, overwatering fills all the air spaces in the soil with water, which suffocates the plant roots, causes root rot, and prevents the crop from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yiɔ kɛ nu. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ehaa amɛgboɔ, ni ehaaa tso lɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does using a tractor to prepare my land help my crops grow better than manual clearing?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ trakta ni mikɛtsuɔ nii kɛsaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe ni mikɛ mi nine baatsu he nii?

english: A tractor plows deep into the ground, loosening hard soil so crop roots can easily grow deep, find hidden water, and absorb nutrients. This makes the crop stronger and helps it survive dry periods much better than crops planted in hard, hand-cleared ground.
ga: Trakta lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Gbalamɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ koni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ. Taomɔ nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni okɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ awo mli Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ waa ni eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: How does using a machine for shelling corn benefit me compared to stripping the grains by hand?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa mi lɛ he kɛ akɛto ŋmãa ni akɛ niji shwieɔ lɛ he?

english: A shelling machine quickly removes grains from hundreds of cobs in minutes without cracking the seeds. Doing it by hand takes days and can damage grains, making them more vulnerable to insect attacks during storage.
ga: Mɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ amli oya yɛ minitii fioo komɛi amli ni ekuuu ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ ni akɛ niji feɔ lɛ heɔ gbii babaoo ni ebaanyɛ efite dumɔwui lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii baanyɛ atutua lɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: What is the best way to tell if my harvested corn is dry enough to safely store in sacks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto kotokui amli?

english: You can test dry corn by biting a grain or pressing it with your thumbnail. If it makes a sharp cracking sound and feels rock-hard without leaving a mark, it is dry enough. If it feels soft, moisture is still inside and will cause rot.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwu lɛ ni ooomɔ nɔ loo okɛ okadi bibioo lɛ anyɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji efee gbee ni naa wa ni enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ hewalɛ ni eshiii okadi ko. Etsɔɔ akɛ egbi bɔ ni sa. Kɛji enu he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo lɛ Moisture hiɔ emli ni ebaaha egbo.

english: Should I sun-dry my harvested corn on the open ground or dry it using a mechanical dryer?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ agbi yɛ he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ nɔ loo mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛgbiɔ ŋmãa lɛ atsu nii?

english: Sun-drying on clean tarpaulins works very well when the weather is hot and bright. However, if harvest happens during a rainy period, using a drying machine protects your grains from rain, dampness, and harmful mold growth.
ga: Hulu ni akɛgbiɔ yɛ tarp ni he tse nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ miitso. Shi, kɛji akɛ kpamɔ lɛ ba yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, Kɛ́ okɛ tsɔne ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebuɔ oŋmaa lɛ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ he.

english: Why does my harvested corn turn moldy and hot when I pack it into bags immediately after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ mli ewo muji ni edɔ beni mikɛwoɔ kotoku mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa lɛ?

english: Freshly picked corn still contains a lot of water and heat inside the grains. When tightly packed into bags without drying first, this trapped moisture creates a humid environment where fungi and heat build up quickly, causing the corn to spoil.
ga: Abele ni ajie ehee lɛ yɛ nu kɛ dɔlɛ babaoo lolo yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛwo kotokui amli jogbaŋŋ ni egbiko klɛŋklɛŋ Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ baa. he ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ baabua amɛhe naa oya Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Is it better to strip the husks off my corn cobs right after harvest or leave them on while drying?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaajie ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ loo abaashi amɛ koni amɛgbi?

english: Removing the outer husks immediately allows warm air and sunlight to dry the grains much faster. Leaving husks on traps moisture underneath, which can cause mold to grow right on the cob.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulu la haa ŋmaa lɛ gĩɔ oya kwraa. Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii lɛ agbele lɛ, ebaamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmei akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ.

english: What will happen to my corn if rain falls on it while it is spread out to dry outside?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ be mli ni egbiɔ yɛ kpo lɛ nɔ?

english: If rain hits drying corn, the grains quickly absorb water, which causes them to swell, crack, or start germinating. Wet grain also attracts fungi that produce toxins, making the corn unsafe for humans and animals to eat.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ gbalaa nu oya. Enɛ haa abele lɛ fuuɔ, egbɛɔ, loo ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ. Nibii ni efɔ lɛ hu gbalaa ŋmeii ni feɔ tsofai fɔji lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha adesai kɛ kooloi ni amɛyeɔ.

english: What is the difference between harvesting corn fresh for boiling versus harvesting it for dry grain?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa hee ni akpaa koni akɛshã kɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa kɛha ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ teŋ?
