english: Fresh corn for boiling is picked early while the plant is still green and kernels are soft and sweet. Corn grown for dry grain is left in the field until the leaves turn brown and dry so the grains harden enough to be ground into flour or stored for months.
ga: Afoɔ ŋmãa hee ni akɛhooɔ nii lɛ mra. Yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo ni dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛmli ŋɔɔ lɛ, ashiɔ Abele ni adu kɛha dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ afee nɔ ni wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsɔ mli afee ashikishaŋ loo akɛto nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves of my corn plants roll up tightly during hot dry afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni edɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism to save water. By curling, the plant reduces the leaf surface exposed to the hot sun, preventing water from evaporating too quickly during the heat of the day.
ga: Abɛi baai shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛtoɔ nu he. kɛtsɔ yitsɔi ni afolɔ mli lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ baaha amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashɛ amɛhe lɛ nɔ aba shi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young corn plants turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is starving for nutrients like nitrogen, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away and waterlogged the roots. Adding appropriate fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni eha shishifãi lɛ amli eyi kɛ nu. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right food to give my cassava plants so the roots grow very big and heavy?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male niyenii ni sa ni mikɛha mi-cassava tso lɛ? bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ afee wuji waa ni amɛhe wa

english: Cassava needs balanced soil nutrients to grow strong tubers. Nitrogen helps the plant grow leaves, but too much nitrogen makes big leaves and very small tubers. Potassium is the key food that makes the cassava roots swell up fat and heavy.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni sa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia Cassava koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ baai. Shi nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha baai wuji kɛ bulbs bibii waa aba. Potassium ji niyenii titri ni haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fũuɔ, amɛfeɔ fɔ ni amɛfeɔ shwiili.

english: Is animal manure better for feeding my maize crop than store-bought chemical fertilizer?
ga: Ani kooloi aŋmei hi fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Animal manure improves the soil long-term by helping it hold water and build organic matter, but it releases nutrients slowly. Chemical fertilizers work quickly to feed crops when they are growing fast. Using dry, well-rotted manure early and supplementing with standard fertilizer gives the best yield.
ga: Manure haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli kɛtsɔ yelikɛbuamɔ ni ekɛhaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ emaa shi lɛ nɔ. Shi ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii fiofio. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii oya koni ekɛha tsei niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiida oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii mra, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ aba.

english: Why do some of my crops yield fruit twice in a year while others yield only once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ ekomɛi woɔ yibii shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome pɛ lɛ?

english: Fast-maturing crops like maize and beans grow quickly enough to match Ghana's major and minor rainy seasons, allowing two harvests a year. Long-term tree crops like cocoa follow seasonal flowering cycles that depend on cooler months and rain patterns, giving one main harvest and one smaller mid-crop harvest.
ga: Nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ abele kɛ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ Ghana nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ji shishijee kɛ nɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ kpãa gbee. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akpaa nii shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli. Tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ, tamɔ kookoo, nyiɛɔ be mli fɔfɔi ni damɔ nyɔji ni mli ejɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akpaa kpamɔ titri kome kɛ nyɔŋ teŋ kpamɔ bibioo ko.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crops every year when I plant maize on the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the exact same crop on the same piece of land continuously sucks out specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Switching your land between maize and legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas puts vital nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa lɛ haa nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Can I plant pepper and garden eggs in between my young cassava plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ mi yucca tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, planting short-term vegetables alongside young cassava allows you to harvest food quickly while the cassava takes its time to grow. It also covers the ground, keeping weeds away and preventing the hot sun from drying out the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, be kukuoo mli aduawai ni ooodu yɛ ŋmei bibii ahe lɛ haa onáa ŋmãa oya yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ heɔ be dani ekwɛɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu nɔ. Tsi jwɛi lɛ anaa ni otsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi

english: Will planting my seeds very close together give me a bigger harvest from my small land?
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ni madu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. mi nɔ loo daabi

english: No, planting crops too close together forces them to fight for sunlight, water, and soil food. This makes the plants tall and weak, producing very small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to feed and yield healthy fruit.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛwu amɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kwɔlɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What can I do to protect my crops if the rain stops unexpectedly after planting?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mikɛbu midumɔ nii ahe kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa beni midu nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You can place dry grass, maize stalks, or leaves around the roots of your crops (mulching). This acts as a blanket that traps moisture in the dirt and shields the roots from direct heat until the rains return.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi, ŋmãa tsei, loo baai abɔle oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe (mulch), ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ muji lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ he kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant juice and spreading viruses. Spraying early with neem leaf extract solution or recommended bio-pesticides keeps these insects away before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Aloo, tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akabote mli dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How often do I need to clear weeds so they don't steal food from my young plants?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ amli?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and take away water and soil nutrients. You should clear your farm within the first 3 to 6 weeks after planting, because that is when young crops are too small to defend themselves against aggressive weeds.
ga: Jwɛi daa oya fe tsei ni amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ojie oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 6 mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bibii lɛ daraaa tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ jwɛi ni baa amɛŋɔɔ lɛ ahe.

english: How can I prevent insects from destroying my harvested maize while it is stored in the barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Insects thrive in damp grain. Make sure your maize is completely dried in the sun until the kernels are hard before storing them in airtight bags (like PICS bags) or treated storage bins to suffocate weevils without chemicals.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye yɛ ŋmãa ni mli efɔ mli. Kwɛmɔ ni o-ŋmã lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ amli tsɔi lɛ mli wa dani okɛwo vacuum kotokui amli (tamɔ PICS kotokui) loo nibii ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe ni atsa mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ agbɔjɔ ni tsofai bɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to protect them from direct sunlight and harsh winds, especially during the dry season. Keeping larger shade trees helps retain soil moisture and keeps the young plants cool.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo be fioo koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Titri lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tsei ni eda lɛ ahe shading yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen fertilizer, or the ground is flooded with too much water, which prevents the roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ashishi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii.

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves and wet waste inside the top funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ jwɛi ni efɔ yɛ tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing center (funnel) of the maize plant to eat the fresh green leaves before they open up.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei (cones) lɛ amli koni amɛye baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ.

english: Why is a strange purple-flowered weed making my maize look stunted and withered even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli nɛɛ haa mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: That weed is likely Striga (witchweed), a parasitic plant that attaches its roots directly to your maize roots underground, stealing water and nutrients meant for your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ jwɛi lɛ ji Striga (witchweed), ni ji tso ko ni yɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli ni ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpãa o-corn shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛhaa onibii lɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots remain thin and woody even after the plants have grown for over a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛfee tsei lolo eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ ekwɛ nɔ ni fe afi moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava needs loose, well-drained soil to expand its roots into large tubers. If planted in hard clay soil or affected by diseased planting stems, the plant uses all its energy for leaves instead of tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni mli tse he miihia cassava koni eshishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ bulbs agboi. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ emɔ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear the ground and build high mounds or ridges before planting my yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie he ko ni mafee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko dani madu sweet potatoes lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow straight down deep into the earth. Loose, tall soil mounds make it easy for the tubers to expand smoothly and protect them from rotting in standing water.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ mlɛo, ni ehaaa amɛgboi yɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain stems snap and fall over easily right before the fruits get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ fãa ni egbeeɔ shi oya dani aduawai lɛ feɔ agbo lɛ?

english: Plantain stems usually collapse because root-boring insects (weevils) or underground worms (nematodes) have eaten away the root foundation, leaving the heavy plant without support.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ shishifãi (ŋmeii) loo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ahewɔ. (Nematodes) lɛ eye shishifãi lɛ. Feemɔ tsei ni tsii ni nɔ ko bɛ ni fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Why do my tomato plants produce a lot of flowers, but the flowers just fall off without growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the daytime temperatures are too hot, when the soil dries out suddenly, or when there are no bees around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ trukaa loo be mli ni ŋmeii ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ bɛ

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts together with my main crops improve my farm soil?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow, they release this natural fertilizer into the soil to feed neighboring crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ eda lɛ, ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ ewoɔ sũ lɛ mli koni ekɛ niyenii aha tsei lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry stretch of sun. If seeds sprout during this false start, the young seedlings will quickly dry out and die before the real rainy season begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui kwɛ̃ yɛ amale shishijee mli Tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baa.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough for crops, or if I need to get it tested first?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔ? Aloo esa akɛ maka shikpɔŋ lɛ makwɛ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Soil holds the nutrients plants need to grow. If your soil lacks key minerals or is too acidic, crops will stay stunted no matter how much water you give them. Getting your soil tested tells you exactly what nutrients or fertilizers your specific land needs before you spend money on seeds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ toɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ. Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ minerals titrii loo eyɛ acid tsɔ lɛ, Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni nu ni okɛhaa amɛ lɛ fa ha lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa baatsɔɔ bo niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ dani ofite shika yɛ dumɔwui ahe.

english: Why is it important to clear and loosen the topsoil properly before planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ajie lɛ dani adu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Loosening the topsoil makes it easier for delicate young crop roots to spread out, breathe, and drink water. Hard, packed ground prevents roots from growing deep, making the plants weak and easily knocked over by strong winds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo ahaa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akɛ amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã, amɛmu ni amɛnu nu. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ akumɔ amɛ oya.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that feeds the underground tuber. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so all the leaves catch light and stay away from damp soil where diseases like to spread.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ fɛɛ aje kpo yɛ la mli. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni ji he ni helai tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it uses to build green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rains wash food too deep into the soil for young roots to reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmãa tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do my crops wilt and rot when water sits on my farm for too many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like people do. When water gathers and sits on top of the soil without draining away, it suffocates the roots, causing them to rot and preventing the plant from feeding.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Beni nu buaa ehe naa ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaaa tso lɛ aná niyenii.

english: Tomato flowers drop off without making fruit if the weather gets too hot, if the soil dries out completely, or if there is no gentle wind or insects to shake pollen inside the blossom to fertilize it.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa, loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli jɔ bɛ. Aloo kooloi bibii baa ni amɛhosoɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ koni ekɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping the plant from growing new peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ pepper heei lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips hiding underneath and sucking out the plant's juices. As they feed, they distort the leaves and prevent the plant from flowering and fruiting properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii Ebaatsɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekawo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava plants show they are mature when their lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to swell and crack open from the thick tubers expanding beneath.
ga: Cassava tso tsɔɔ akɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ je shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbɛɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni shwereɔ yɛ shishi lɛ amli.

english: The first rain often dries up quickly, leaving the soil hot and dry for weeks. If seeds germinate after one rain and then face a sudden dry spell, the young shoots will burn and die before the steady rainy season begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ gbiɔ oya. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adɔ ni egbi otsii babaoo. If the seeds germinate after one rain and suddenly face dryness. Young shoots burn and die before the stable rainy season begins.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away my topsoil and young crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rain hits bare or sloped ground, the soil cannot absorb all the water quickly. The excess water flows over the surface, creating a strong stream that carries away fertile topsoil, fertilizers, and young plants with weak roots.
ga: When heavy rain hits open areas or slopes The soil cannot absorb all the water quickly. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ nu lɛ hiɛ. This causes strong water currents to wash away fertile topsoil, fertilizer, and young plants with weak roots.

english: How can I stop heavy floodwater from flowing straight across my field during the rainy season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ akpa nu afua ni naa wa ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: You can dig simple drainage channels along the borders of your farm and build soil ridges across sloped land. These structures slow down water, trap topsoil, and safely direct excess rainwater away from your crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ gbɛ yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa ni ebaanyɛ efee shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni tsɔɔ hei ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni ojie nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛ onibii amli shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and die when water sits on my farm for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like people do. When rainwater collects and overflows your field without draining, it smothers the roots, preventing them from taking up nutrients and causing the leaves to turn yellow and rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Beni nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa ni ehoɔ oŋmɔji amli ni etsɔɔɔ mli lɛ. ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my crops wilt suddenly when the hot sun comes out immediately after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ je kpo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The hot sun forces water to evaporate quickly from leaf surfaces. Because the flooded ground has temporarily weakened the roots' ability to drink water, the plant loses moisture faster than roots can replace it, causing wilting.
ga: Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛnu nu yɛ be kukuoo mli. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ atsake lɛ. kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa

english: Why do my crop leaves develop dark spots and mold after many continuous days of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous rain creates high moisture and trapped air around plant leaves, which are perfect conditions for fungal diseases to sprout and spread across damp crops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ ahe, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã tsei ni mli edɔ lɛ fɛɛ amli.

english: Will heavy rainfall carry away the fertilizer I just spread on my farm?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɛɛ?

english: Yes, water flowing across the ground surface easily washes away loose fertilizer. To protect your fertilizer, cover it lightly with soil near the crop stems rather than leaving it exposed on the surface.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ oya. koni obu o-fertilizer lɛ he Ha shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ fioo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ

english: Why does my farmland become hard and cracked after heavy rain is followed by strong sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mli wa ni egbɛ eshwa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulu la ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy raindrops break down the loose soil into fine dust that packs tightly together. When the intense sun dries out this packed layer, it bakes into a hard crust that makes it difficult for roots to spread.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ feɔ sũ bibioo ni kpɛtɛɔ he waa. Kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ ha nɛkɛ ŋtayaa ni ebɔle ehe nɛɛ gĩ lɛ, Ebaashã hu ni etsɔ ŋtayaa ni wa, ni baaha ewa aha shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do some farmers plant crops like cassava or maize on raised soil mounds or ridges instead of flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi anɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Raised mounds and ridges lift crop roots above floodwater, preventing root rot during heavy rains while making it easier for surplus water to run off safely between the rows.
ga: Gɔji kɛ ŋshɔkei ni awó nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsei shishifãi anɔ kɛyaa nu afua nu lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ewaaa akɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaho kɛje kpo shweshweeshwe yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋ.

english: How does spreading dry grass or leaves on my farm soil help protect my crops from heavy rain and hot sun?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi loo baai ni mikɛshwãa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ buɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he?

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a shield. It softens the impact of heavy falling raindrops so topsoil isn't washed away, and keeps the soil cool and moist under the hot sun.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛ ashwã, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he. Ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he hewalɛ baa shi. Koni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ akaho. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: How can I prevent my crops from falling over when strong winds and rain hit my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni amɛkagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds at the correct depth and pulling dirt up around the base of the plant stem (hilling) gives the roots a firm anchor in the ground to support the crop against rain and wind.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni sa ni agbalaa sũ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛbɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi (ŋwɛi) lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atswa shikpɔŋ lɛ shi shiŋŋ koni ekɛfi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ asɛɛ kɛjɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my okra plants keep dropping their flowers before forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi be fɛɛ be dani efeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Okra plants drop their flowers when they experience heat or water stress. When the plant senses there is not enough moisture in the soil, it sheds its flowers to conserve energy and survive, rather than using resources to grow pods.
ga: Rosella tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo nu he haomɔ kpe amɛ. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii baatsu nii kɛdu pods

english: Why are my okra plants growing very tall with large leaves, but yielding very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni ebaai wuji yɔɔ mli shi ewoɔ aduawai fioo lɛ?

english: This usually happens when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen makes the plant spend all its energy growing leaves and stems (vegetative growth) instead of producing flowers and pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi. (tso lɛ dalɛ) Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii

english: Why should I leave part of my farm land to rest for a season instead of planting on it every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ eko koni mahe ajɔɔ mi be kome moŋ fe ni madu daa afi lɛ?

english: Leaving land fallow allows nature to rebuild the soil's nutrients naturally. During this rest period, plants die and decompose, turning into organic matter that refreshes the soil so future crops can grow strong without needing expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ashiɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ lɛ nyɛɔ etswaa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ emaa shi ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yɛ hejɔɔmɔ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, tsei gboiɔ ni amɛfiteɔ. Ebafeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ wɔsɛɛ tsei baanyɛ ada waa ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why does my crop yield get smaller every year when I plant okra on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛ́ midu okra yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same spot every season sucks out the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows pests and soil diseases that love that crop to build up in the dirt. Changing crops or resting the land breaks this cycle.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ. ni ehaa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hejɔɔmɔ fiteɔ sɛɛkuu lɛ.

english: Why do weeds sprout much faster than my crops right after I clear fresh bush land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mijie jwɛi heei ni yɔɔ he ko lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can sleep underground for years. When you clear the land and expose the soil to direct sunlight, it wakes up these wild seeds, and because they are native to the area, they grow faster than introduced crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi afii babaoo. Kɛji ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, Nɛkɛ koo mli dumɔwui nɛɛ baate shi. Ni akɛni amɛji jɛmɛ bii No hewɔ lɛ amɛdaraa oya fe tsei ni ajieɔ yi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops wither and die when water stands around their roots for too long after irrigation?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni nu hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nu ni afɔ amɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen to breathe just like humans do. When water fills all the air spaces in the soil and stays there, the roots suffocate and start to rot, preventing the plant from taking up food and water.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ taoɔ amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ nu eyi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ ni ehi jɛmɛ Shishifãi lɛ baafo ni amɛbɔi fitemɔ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii kɛ nu.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetables early in the morning or during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil can absorb the moisture before the sun gets too hot. Afternoon watering causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before reaching the plant roots.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ adɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli shwane mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani eshɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why does the soil on my vegetable plot dry up so fast even after I water it heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji mikɛ nu babaoo wo nɔ po lɛ?

english: Bare soil left exposed to the blazing sun loses moisture rapidly through evaporation. Covering the dirt around your crops with dried grass or leaves keeps the ground cool and traps the water in the soil longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baafite ŋmɔtɔ oya kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Mulching around Nibii ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How does using heavy machines like tractors to clear my land affect how my crop roots grow?
ga: Te tsɔnei ni tsii tamɔ traktɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛjie mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ saa tsei shishifãi lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy machinery can press the lower soil layers down so hard that it creates an invisible barrier called a 'hardpan.' This hard layer prevents plant roots from pushing deep to reach underground water and nutrients.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii baanyɛ anyɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo aahu akɛ ekɛ gbɛtsii nii ko ni anaaa ni ale lɛ akɛ 'pan ni wa' baa. Nɛkɛ fã ni wa nɛɛ tsiɔ tsei ashishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni amɛyashɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he.

english: Why do improved crop seeds from government projects require more water and care than our local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ kɛjɛ nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoi amli lɛ biɔ nu kɛ saamɔ babaoo fe wɔ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are bred to produce very heavy harvests quickly, which means they eat and drink much faster. Local seeds grow slower and yield less, but they have naturally adapted over time to survive tough dry spells.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii waa oya. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyeɔ nii ni amɛnuɔ nii oya kwraa. Kuu lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ daaa blɛoo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo. Shi maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ daaa blɛoo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo. Shi esa akɛ nɛkɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ hu atsake amɛhe yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be kɛ bei amli koni amɛye amɛhe yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Leaf yellowing usually means your soil is low on nitrogen, which is essential food for maize growth, or that the plant is getting too much water. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps restore green growth and boosts harvest size.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmãa dalɛ loo tso lɛ nine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off mainly due to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Consistent watering early in the morning and providing light shade during the hottest parts of the day can prevent flower drop.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Nu ni afɔɔɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni afɔɔ daa leebi ni ahaa hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ anaa.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot under the soil before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa?

english: Cassava roots rot when planted in waterlogged soil that lacks good drainage, encouraging fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ ni nu kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. cause fungal disease Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: What makes my pepper plant leaves curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck plant sap and spread diseases. Spraying the leaves with a mild neem oil mixture can clear the insects and protect new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Akɛ neem fɔ ni mli ejɔ ni akɛfutuɔ baai lɛ baashwie nɔ. Ebaanyɛ ejie kooloi bibii kɛya ni etsĩ baai heei adalɛ naa.

english: Why is planting my crops in straight rows better than scattering seeds randomly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mitsei lɛ adumɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ trukaa lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows gives each plant equal access to sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. It also makes weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting much faster and easier compared to random seed scattering.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu yaa oya ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ trukaa lɛ.

english: Why do seeds I buy from the agricultural officer yield more than seeds I save from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli he onukpai adɛŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved certified seeds are specifically bred to resist local pests, tolerate dry spells, and produce bigger yields. Saved seeds naturally lose their strength over generations and often carry over diseases from past seasons.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni aha amɛ he odaseyeli ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Ehiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni ewoɔ babaoo Dumɔwui ni ato yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli ni bei pii lɛ amɛkɛ helai ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when I leave too many big trees shading my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni mishiɔ tsei wuji babaoo ni tsiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: While young cocoa trees need heavy shade, mature cocoa trees need direct sunlight to produce abundant flowers and pods. Excessive shade keeps the farm too damp, which triggers black pod disease and reduces overall yield.
ga: Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ni mli wa. Cacao tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo. Shade babaoo baaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i tsɔ. Enɛ baaha black pod hela aba ni ebaaha yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aba shi.

english: How does clearing my land without burning the dry grass help my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛbaatsu nii ni mikɛshãaa jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter and beneficial insects in the soil. Clearing land manually and leaving cut weeds to rot creates natural mulch, which keeps the soil cool, retains moisture, and feeds your crops naturally.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ bo diɛŋtsɛ ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oha jwɛi ni afo lɛ agbo lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo ahi shi ni oha onibii lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do insects attack my field more when I plant maize on the same plot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every year allows specific crop pests to multiply because their favorite food never runs out. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts starves those pests and restores nutrients to your soil.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ haa kooloi komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ bii. Ejaakɛ niyenii ni amɛsumɔɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ efooo kɔkɔɔkɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ebaaha nakai kooloi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I show my children modern farming methods so they want to continue farming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsɔɔ mibii lɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛi? Bɔni afee ni amɛsumɔ ni amɛtsa okwaayeli nɔ?

english: Giving young people small demonstration plots where they can test row planting, improved seeds, and safe fertilizers shows them that modern farming brings faster profits with less manual labor, turning farming into an attractive business.
ga: Ni akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko baaha oblahii kɛ oblayei koni amɛka row planting amɛkwɛ. ha tsei amli dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ aya hiɛ Atsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli haa sɛɛnamɔ baa oya ni akɛ niji tsuuu nii babaoo. Nɔ ni ejɛ mli eba ji akɛ, okwaayeli ebatsɔ jarayeli nitsumɔ ko ni ŋɔɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn brown and drop off during the Harmattan dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed leaves during severe dry periods to prevent water loss and survive the heat. Planting permanent shade trees alongside your cocoa keeps the soil cool and moist, reducing leaf drop.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli koni nu akafite amɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa baa shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning pale yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for maize. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure near the plant base restores healthy green foliage.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmãa Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmãa loo kooloo ŋmãa ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaawo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that shade the young cocoa and keep the soil moist while the cocoa grows strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni haa kookoo bibioo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enine shɛɔ hulu la ni fa nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow tall. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How do I know when my cassava in the ground is ripe and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack from the growing tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me not to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ mikadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains all the same nutrients from the soil and allows corn pests and diseases to build up in the dirt. Changing crops every season gives the soil time to recover.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ baaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ daa be lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛwoɔ ehe hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars chewing holes in the inner leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that hides inside the central funnel of the plant to eat soft leaves. Controlling them early prevents them from destroying the plant before it can grow corn ears.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Amɛ nɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tso lɛ dani ebaanyɛ ekwɛ ŋmãa toi.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my fertilizer right before a very heavy rain comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer off your land before the plant roots can drink it in, wasting your money. It is best to apply fertilizer when the ground is damp after rain or to cover it lightly with soil.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Enɛ baaha ofite oshika. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ loo oooha nɔ fioo.

english: Tomato flowers drop off without making fruit when the weather becomes too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer in the soil. Regular watering helps fix this.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb up so their leaves can catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the leaves produce food, which is sent underground to grow large, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. ni akɛmajeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛyadu sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny nodules on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. When the plants die, that left-behind nitrogen feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Eyɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ haa niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does allowing weeds to grow in my field result in smaller crops during harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ yɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii baa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. When weeds steal these resources, your crops do not have enough energy to produce full, healthy yields.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ jwɛi ju nibii nɛɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen or getting choked by waterlogged soil. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or urea when the soil is moist helps the plants turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen loo eefo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛfataa he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts together with my maize will help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ du ŋmei lɛ, ebaaye ebua mi-ŋmã lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through small nodules on their roots. This natural fertilizer stays in the ground and feeds the maize growing alongside it.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmei ko ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out the plant's juice. Spraying early with recommended insecticides or soapy water mixtures helps clear them off.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Recommended early spraying of insecticide or soapy water. Ebaaye ebua ni ajie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛya.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and sits in heavy soil for too long, suffocating the roots and attracting fungal diseases. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ekɛ ehe wo shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves and small worms inside the center of the stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii Mine lɛ yɛ bu ni etse. Yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: Those chewed holes and worms are caused by Fall Armyworms feeding on the tender leaves inside the funnel. Catching them early and applying approved pest control treatments directly into the funnel stops them before they ruin the cob.
ga: The holes and chewed worms are caused by Fall Armyworms eating the young leaves in the cones. Catching them early and apply approved pest control directly into the channel. Tsĩ amɛnaa dani amɛkpãtã ŋmei lɛ hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that scorch under direct sunlight. Retaining tall shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains provides a canopy shield that protects the seedlings from heat and retains soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ adumɔ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to expose their leaves to sunlight, which allows them to make food for the growing tuber below. Staking also lifts the leaves off wet soil, preventing diseases from spreading.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ aje kpo yɛ hulu la mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii haa bulb ni miida yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ koni helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra small shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajie nɔ ni fa fe nine ni miida yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ

english: If too many sucker shoots grow around one main plantain stem, they steal food, water, and sunlight from each other, resulting in tiny bunches. Leaving only two or three healthy shoots lets the main plant produce large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ, single main trunk Nɛkɛ plantains nɛɛ juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. ni kɛ tso bibioo ko baa Kɛ́ ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when water supply drops suddenly. Watering your plants consistently at the root zone helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ba shi trukaa. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa yɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop in the middle of the day even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can draw it from the ground. The leaves droop naturally to reduce their surface area in the hot sun and will bounce back once the evening cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Ni ebaaku esɛɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ edɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under strong heat and sunlight. They need partial shade from plantains or shade trees to retain soil moisture and protect their leaves until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaashɛ amɛhe.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my young maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii anɔ lɛ, Mi-mi lɛ etee tso lɛ mli.

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which feed on the leaves and growing point of young maize plants. Treating the crop early with approved extension-recommended sprays helps protect the growing whorl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai kɛ hei ni amɛdaraa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ baabu ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my tomato leaves getting dark black spots and dying when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Excess rain and dampness encourage fungal diseases like tomato blight to spread. Lifting the plants off the ground with wooden stakes and trimming low leaves allows sunlight and airflow to dry the plant faster.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tomato blight he hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ tsei ni atswaa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni afoɔ Enɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abɔle he koni tsei lɛ agbi oya.

english: Why do I need to clear the leaves and place tall sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie baai lɛ ni mikɛ niji kakadaji ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that require sunlight to produce food for underground tuber growth. Staking gets leaves off the damp ground to reach sun light and prevents leaves from rotting.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni amɛná niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. Staking jieɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ ni eha baai lɛ akafite.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves yellow and drop off, leaving a tall bare stem, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack open from expanding tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Tso lɛ kakadaŋŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ eshwɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ yitso ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ mli.

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen and keeps soil healthy.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ayaa nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil still need fertilizer if it already looks dark?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii lolo kɛji akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni edɔ momo lɛ?

english: Dark soil contains organic material, but every harvest removes key nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. Fertilizer replaces these essential plant foods so the next harvest stays high.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɔɔ mli. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ tsei niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ najiaŋ. Bɔni afee ni kpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ahi shi yɛ gbɛ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and stop growing when rainwater collects on my land for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air in the soil to breathe and gather nutrients. Standing water suffocates the roots, preventing them from feeding the plant and causing leaves to turn yellow from lack of food.
ga: Tse shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu ni amɛbua niyenii mli hewalɛ naa. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Etsiɔ tsei ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ anaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni bɛ hewɔ

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small, thin bunches when many young shoots grow around the base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain nine lɛ tsɔɔ jwɛi bibioo mli beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Multiple suckers growing around one stem compete for the same soil water and nutrients. Pruning extra suckers to keep only one or two strong shoots ensures the main plant gets full nourishment for larger bunches.
ga: Suckers babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso kome he lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he koni tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ kɛha tsei niji wuji lɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when stressed by severe heat, irregular watering, or a shortage of plant nutrients like phosphorus. Maintaining steady soil moisture helps flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo tso mli niyenii tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Is it bad for my farm if I grow different varieties of crops on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani ebaaye miŋmɔ lɛ awui kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Growing different crop varieties protects your farm from total crop loss. If a pest or sudden drought affects one variety, the other varieties may survive, ensuring you still harvest something and can attract different buyers with various products.
ga: Nibii srɔtoi ni ooodu lɛ buɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baafite kwraa lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo hɔmɔ ni ba trukaa lɛ ye tso lɛ henɔ kome nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ henɔi krokomɛi baanyɛ ahi shi. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nɔ ko lolo ni ebaanyɛ egbala jarayelɔi srɔtoi kɛ nibii srɔtoi babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without any plantains or shade trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni kookoo tsei loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like human babies—they burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantain produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ woɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava sticks very close together so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛɔ he koni maná gbɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving cassava enough space allows each plant to build strong roots and grow larger tubers, giving you a bigger total yield.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ oha o-cassava lɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná shishifãi ni wa ni ekwɛ̃ bulbs wuji. Ehaa onine shɛɔ nibii babaoo ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil food needed for growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its rich green color and build full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba su ni mli kwɔ mli ni amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why is it good to plant beans or cowpeas on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil naturally. Planting them after maize restores soil nutrients so your next crop grows stronger without relying as heavily on expensive fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ abɛi sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the plant's sap, or by a virus spread by those insects. Controlling pests early with organic sprays keeps the plant healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. or by viruses that those insects spread Early Pest Control With organic spray helps plants stay strong.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if they are just growing on the side of the field?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ masɛi?

english: Weeds steal vital groundwater, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your main crops. They also act as hiding places for insects and diseases that quickly spread to your healthy plants.
ga: Weeds steal important groundwater, sunlight and fertilizer for your main crops. Amɛji hei ni kooloi bibii kɛ helai hu teɔ shi amɛwoɔ amɛhe. No gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛyaa otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I pinch off extra side shoots from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Removing extra branches, called suckers, forces the tomato plant to direct all its energy and nutrients into producing bigger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on unnecessary stems and leaves.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ suckers lɛ nyɛɔ tomato tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Instead of wasting energy on unnecessary stems and leaves

english: Why is it risky to sow my corn seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell. If seeds sprout and then face weeks without rain, the delicate young seedlings will dry up and die before the reliable rainy season officially settles in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa otsii babaoo lɛ, Tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ aba yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ.

english: Saving and replanting hybrid seeds usually results in weaker plants with much smaller cobs in the second generation. It is best to buy fresh certified hybrid seeds each season or use open-pollinated seed varieties if you prefer to save seed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ ni akɛtoɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo baa yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi. Aloo okɛ dumɔwui ni agbele naa lɛ atsu nii kɛji oosumɔ ni ohere dumɔwui lɛ ayiwala.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight for long periods. Without shade trees or plantain plants nearby to block the intense heat, the leaves get scorched, lose moisture quickly, turn yellow, and fall off to keep the plant alive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ Koni hulutsoo ni naa wa waa akafee lɛ Abaashã baai lɛ. Loes moisture oya ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbee shi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ahi shi

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips that suck the sap from tender leaves and spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or natural sprays stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips kɛ chili baa baa. which sucks the sap from young leaves and spreads viruses in plants Early control of these insects With neem oil or a natural spray, the leaves will not curl.

english: Why are my young maize plants developing small holes in the leaves and dying from the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni gboi yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing heart of the maize plant. Inspecting your farm early and putting a bit of dry sand or recommended botanical spray into the center funnel can stop them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni ŋã ni egbi fioo loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tsofa mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwieɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped around them for too long because the soil does not drain well. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows rainwater to flow away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu tsɔ amɛhe. Etsɛ tsɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔnaa lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ joɔ foi kɛyaa koni eha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry period that can dry out the soil and scorch new sprouts. It is safer to wait until the rains become steady so the soil stays moist long enough for the roots to establish.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni eha ŋmeii heei lɛ ashã. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ atswa shi.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is weak and needs fertilizer before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani adu nii?

english: If your previous crops grew slowly, had light yellow leaves instead of rich green ones, or produced very small fruits, your soil lacks essential plant nutrients. Adding compost, animal manure, or fertilizer restores the soil power.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ dara blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ. loo ha aduawai bibii waa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Will planting cowpeas together with my maize reduce the yield of my maize?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmãa ni mikɛduɔ lɛ baaha miŋmãa yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi?

english: No, cowpeas actually help maize grow better. Cowpeas pull natural plant food from the air into the soil, which feeds the maize while ground cover from cowpea leaves keeps the soil moist and cool.
ga: Dabi, tsina ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni edaa jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ. Cowpeas gbalaa tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni haa ŋmãa niyenii Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ tsina ŋmãa baa shwieɔ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Too many shoots steal water, sunlight, and food from the main plantain stalk. Leaving only one or two strong shoots allows the main stalk to produce much larger, heavier bunches of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ plantain tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii 1 loo 2 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛhiɛɛɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii titri lɛ awo ŋmeii ni dara ni tsii babaoo.

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight so their leaves can make food for the growing tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground, preventing rot diseases and helping you get much larger yams.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ aha niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni miida lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa ŋmɔtɔ ni da babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly fall over and wilt even when the ground is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a disease living in the soil that blocks water from moving up the stem. Rotating tomatoes with crops like maize or cassava prevents this disease from staying in your soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, bacteria wilt ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni haaa nu aya ŋwɛi tso lɛ nɔ. Tomato ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ. Ye obua ni hela nɛɛ akahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I always find tiny bugs inside my mango seeds when I cut them open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be fɛɛ be lɛ, yɛ mango dumɔwu lɛ mli kɛ́ afo mli?

english: This is caused by the mango seed weevil. An adult insect lays its egg on the tiny young mango, and the young bug eats its way inside the seed to grow, remaining hidden until you split the seed open.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa lɛ ji mango dumɔwu mli ŋmei lɛ. Kplukai ni eda lɛ fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ mango bibii anɔ. Ni kooloi bibii yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Akɛ amɛ tee kɛyashi obaagbala dumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: How do small insects manage to get inside my fruit before it even turns ripe?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii abote mi yibii lɛ amli dani ekwɛ̃?

english: Insects like fruit flies and seed weevils pierce the soft skin of very small, young fruits while they are still growing on the tree and lay their eggs directly inside.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii tsɔɔ aduawai bibii bibii waa lɛ ahewolo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mli. Beni amɛyaa nɔ amɛdaraa yɛ tsei anɔ ni amɛwoɔ amɛwui yɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ.

english: Is it safe for my family to eat a mango if there is a bug inside the seed?
ga: Ani miweku lɛ baanyɛ aye mango kɛji kooloi yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli?

english: Yes, as long as the flesh of the mango is clean and not rotten, it is safe to eat. The mango seed weevil usually stays inside the hard seed shell and does not make the fruit flesh poisonous.
ga: Hɛɛ, be fɛɛ be ni mango lɛ mli tse ni efiteee lɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ayeɔ. Bei pii lɛ, mango dumɔwu lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ hiɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli ŋmei ni wa lɛ mli, ni ekɛ poison wooo aduawai lɛ amli ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: What should I do with old mango seeds after eating so pests don't spread on my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ afee kɛ́ aye mango dumɔwui momoi lɛ sɛɛ? Koni kooloi bibii akagbala ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should gather and burn or deeply bury the seeds instead of throwing them on the ground. This kills any pests sleeping inside the seeds and stops them from attacking your next crop.
ga: Esa akɛ obua dumɔwui lɛ anaa ni oshã loo ofu amɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ fe ni oooshɛrɛ amɛ ashwie shikpɔŋ. Enɛ baagbe kooloi ni ewɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ, ni ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkatutua oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my fruit trees seem to have more pest problems every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ naa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo daa afi lɛ?

english: Pests often survive the dry season inside old fallen fruits and seeds left on the ground. If the farm is not cleaned up after harvest, those hidden pests hatch and attack the new fruits next season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli yɛ aduawai kɛ dumɔwui ni egbee shikpɔŋ lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ asaaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Nakai tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ baafɔ ni amɛbaatutua aduawai heei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: How can I protect my young mango fruits while they are still very small on the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-mango lɛ he be mli ni amɛji bibii waa lolo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: You can protect young fruits by spraying recommended organic or chemical controls early in the flowering season, or by physically wrapping the young fruits to block insects from laying eggs on them.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu aduawai bibii ahe kɛtsɔ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofa ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ ni oookɛshwie nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ aduawai bibii ni akɛwoɔ mli koni kooloi akawo amɛmli lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if a small green fruit on my tree already has insect eggs inside it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tso yibii bibioo ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha mi? Mi tso lɛ yɛ kooloi awui yɛ emli momo?

english: Check the skin of the small fruit closely for tiny dark spots, sticky sap drops, or small scars, which are signs that an insect pierced the skin to lay eggs.
ga: Kwɛmɔ aduawai bibii ahewolo lɛ mli. Kwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ona hei bibii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ, ni ji latɛs ni shwieɔ shi. loo ŋmeii bibii Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloo ko ebote hewolo lɛ mli koni ekɛwo ŋmeii.

english: When is the best time for me to start protecting my fruit trees from insects?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabɔi mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ahebuu kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe?

english: The best time is right after the tree flowers and the tiny green fruits begin to form, because that is when insects search for young fruits to lay their eggs.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji beni tsei lɛ ewo fɔfɔi ni aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ebɔi feemɔ sɛɛ, ejaakɛ be nɛɛ mli ji be ni kooloi bibii taoɔ aduawai bibii ni amɛkɛwoɔ amɛwui lɛ.

english: Why do my small green mangoes drop off the tree before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Young fruits often fall off early if insects have laid eggs inside them, or if the tree does not have enough water and nutrients to support all the growing fruit.
ga: Yibii bibii lɛ fɔɔ gbee oya kɛji kooloi wo amɛwui lɛ amli. aloo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aduawai fɛɛ ni miida lɛ aye abua lɛ.

english: Can I cover my growing fruits with paper or cloth bags to keep insects away?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ wolo loo mama kotokui aha aduawai ni miida lɛ ahe koni kooloi akabote mli?

english: Yes, covering small growing fruits with protective bags prevents insects from reaching the skin to lay eggs, helping you harvest clean fruit without heavy chemical spraying.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ kotoku ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ ha aduawai bibii ni miida lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkashɛ hewolo lɛ he koni amɛwo amɛwui. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okpaa aduawai ni he tse ni tsofai ni tsii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ fataaa he.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build healthy green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps them regain their deep green color and grow faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and shriveling up on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, heavily shaded farms. Pruning excess canopy branches to let in light and removing infected pods immediately helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ekɛ la aba, ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How can I protect my tomato plants from drying out quickly during the Harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi oya yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil around the base of your plants with dry grass or leaves—a practice called mulching—keeps the soil cool and traps moisture so your tomatoes do not dry out quickly in hot, dry winds.
ga: Ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Enɛ baaha tomatoi lɛ akagbi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ mli.

english: What causes small worms to eat holes through the leaves inside my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ye bu kɛtsɔ baa ko nɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ mli?

english: These are fall armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the tender center leaves of maize. Applying recommended biopesticides or a mixture of clean neem leaf extract directly into the plant funnel early in the morning can control them.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Abaanyɛ akudɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii loo neem baa ni he tse ni akɛfutu mli lɛ ni akɛwo dumɔwui lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting in the ground before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ nɔ ni mikpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe in waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, lack of water, or a shortage of nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and ensuring good soil fertility encourages the flowers to stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okwɛ koni efee nɔ ni baa lɛ, ebaawo fɔfɔi lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly and look weak even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?
