english: Weeds steal light, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early in the season ensures your crops get all the food and moisture they need to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava cuttings very close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei niji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots fight each other for limited water and soil food, resulting in small, thin tubers. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to expand and produce large tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ shikpɔŋ fioo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, yitso lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ mlɛo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshwa ni ekɛ bulbs agboi aba.

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that can easily weaken if underground pests attack them or if the fruit bundle gets too heavy. Supporting heavy stems with bamboo or wooden props prevents them from snapping or uprooting in strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni baanyɛ agbɔjɔ oya kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua amɛ loo kɛji akɛ akpɛtɛ aduawai lɛ ahe tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ni akɛfiɔ tsei ahe lɛ fiɔ tsei ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkakumɔ loo amɛkaje shishi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Young cocoa saplings burn easily under harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that shade the young cocoa plants and keep the surrounding soil cool until the cocoa is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni shwereɔ oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao lɛ mli waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flowers before they can turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often fall off when the weather becomes too hot and dry, or when there are not enough tiny insects in the farm to transfer pollen from flower to flower.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ shigbeemɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli lɛ.

english: How does changing weather and unpredictable rain affect the way my crops produce fruit?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ saa bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ woɔ yibii lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Changes in weather disrupt the crop's natural flowering cycle. High heat dries out the delicate flower parts, which means fewer flowers get fertilized naturally to produce high yields.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ gbalaa adebɔɔ mli fɔfɔii ni yaa nɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha fɔfɔi lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, fɔfɔi fioo ko pɛ ji nɔ ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees flower heavily in some seasons but produce very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ bei komɛi amli shi amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: A tree can produce many flowers, but if pollination does not happen, those flowers simply wither away. Heavy flowering only leads to high yield if the pollen gets moved to fertilize the flowers.
ga: Tso lɛ baanyɛ awo fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi kɛji akɛ afeee pollination lɛ Nakai fɔfɔi lɛ baagboi. Fɔfɔi ni tsii lɛ haa yibiiwoo babaoo baa pɛ kɛji akɛ ajie pollen lɛ koni ekɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What is crop pollination, and why is it important for my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni ji tsei amli ŋmɔtɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Pollination is the process of moving pollen inside a flower so it can grow into a fruit or pod. For cocoa, proper pollination is essential because without it, the tree cannot form any cocoa pods at all.
ga: Pollination ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ pollen yɛ fɔfɔi mli koni etsɔ aduawai loo pod. Kɛha kookoo lɛ, pollination ni sa he miihia. Ejaakɛ kɛji ebɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa.

english: What kind of small insects help pollinate cocoa flowers, and where do they live?
ga: Mɛɛ kooloo bibioo yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ kookoo fɔfɔi amli? Ni nɛgbɛ amɛyɔɔ?

english: Tiny insects called midges pollinate cocoa flowers. They live and breed in dark, damp environments on the farm floor, such as under decaying leaf litter or decomposing banana stalks.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ shwieɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ, tamɔ yɛ baai ni egboi loo banana tsei ni egboi lɛ ashishi.

english: If a flower is successfully pollinated, its stem remains green and attached to the trunk, and within a week or two, you will see a tiny green pod beginning to swell where the flower was.
ga: Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ye omanye yɛ pollination mli lɛ Eshishifã lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. ni yɛ otsi kome loo enyɔ mli lɛ Obaana ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. Ebaaje shishi efuu yɛ he ni fɔfɔi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: How can I manually assist my cocoa flowers to make sure they turn into pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii?

english: You can perform hand pollination by using a tiny brush or forceps to pick pollen from a fresh cocoa flower and gently touch it to the center part of another flower on the tree.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ onine afee pollination kɛtsɔ brɔsh bibioo loo pliers nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ pollen ko kɛjɛ cacao fɔfɔi hee ko mli ni okɛta fɔfɔi kroko ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ blɛoo.

english: What is the best time of day for me to work on pollinating my cocoa flowers by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ minine adu kookoo fɔfɔi?

english: Early morning is the best time because the flowers are newly opened, fresh, and moist, making it easier for the pollen to stick and fertilize successfully before the midday sun dries them out.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ fɔfɔi ni etse ehee, ni yɔɔ ehee, ni mli ewo fɔfɔi lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ baakpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ dani hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa amɛgbiɔ.

english: What simple steps can I take on my farm to get a higher yield of cocoa pods this season?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Mɛni afeɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni anyɛ ana kookoo ŋmeii ni kwɔlɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: To increase your yield, you can manually assist flower pollination, maintain moderate shade trees to protect crops from harsh heat, and keep wet plant debris on the soil to attract natural pollinating insects.
ga: Bɔni afee ni nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ Obaanyɛ oye obua ni okɛ fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination bo diɛŋtsɛ. Ha tsei lɛ ahi hulutsoo be ni sa mli koni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni okɛ tsei ni afolɔ ni efɔ lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛgbala ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How long does it take for a cocoa flower to grow into a fully mature pod once it gets pollinated?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ kɛji akɛ amɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli pɛ?

english: Once a flower is successfully pollinated, it takes about five to six months for the tiny pod to grow, mature, and turn yellow or red for harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ fɔfɔi lɛ ye omanye yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ, eheɔ aaafee nyɔji enumɔ kɛyashi enumɔ dani fɔfɔi bibii lɛ daraa, amɛdaraa, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ loo etsuru kɛha kpamɔɔ.

english: How do I know which crop will give me good money before I start planting my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni baaha mi shika kpakpa dani mabɔi amɛdumɔ?

english: Before planting, check local market demand and what feed mills or processors are buying. Crops like soybeans or oil palm often have steady buyers because they are constantly needed for animal feed and cooking oil.
ga: Dani obaadu lɛ, kwɛmɔ nibii ni jarayelihe lɛ taoɔ kɛ niyenii afeemɔ hei loo nitsulɔi ni miihe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ soybeans loo ŋmei fɔ lɛ. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ fa babaoo be fɛɛ be. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛmiitao kooloi aniyenii kɛ fɔ ni akɛhooɔ nii be fɛɛ be.

english: Is it better for me to grow crops for animal feed or food crops for the local market?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ niyenii ni akɛbaatsu nii kɛha kooloi aniyenii loo niyenii ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Feed crops like maize and soybeans often have large, predictable demand from livestock and poultry farmers, whereas fresh food crops can suffer from market gluts where prices drop suddenly during peak harvest.
ga: Koolooi aniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ soybeans Bei pii lɛ, nibii babaoo ni abaanyɛ atsɔɔ hiɛ atsɔɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi kɛ kooloi akwɛlɔi adɛŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, niyenii heei ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ ana amanehulu yɛ niyenii ni fa fe nine lɛ hewɔ, he ni jara baa shi trukaa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my soybean plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ soybean tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves often mean the plant lacks nitrogen or root nodules are not working properly. Soybeans require specific soil bacteria to fix nitrogen and build healthy seed pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo shishifãi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ. Soybeans he miihia sũ mli helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi koni amɛsaa nitrogen ni amɛfee dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce empty shells underground even though the leaves look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts need calcium in the topsoil while the pods are developing underground. Without enough calcium or soil moisture during pegging, the plant grows healthy leaves but fails to fill the pods with nuts.
ga: Calcium he miihia ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miiya hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ calcium loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛfiɔ shi lɛ, Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni mli wa shi enyɛŋ ekɛ ŋmeii awo ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Oil palms need continuous water to form female flowers and fill fruit bunches with oil. During dry periods, the tree conserves energy by reducing flower and fruit production.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ biɔ nu ni yaa nɔ koni amɛfee fɔfɔi yei ni amɛkɛ mu afata aduawai lɛ ahe. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tsei buɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni amɛbaa shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Planting too close forces crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leads to thin, weak plants with smaller yields rather than a larger total harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii ni fa fe ŋmaa fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ baa.

english: Why does my neighbor get over three tons of maize per acre while I only get two from the same land size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ naa ŋmãa ni fe tɔn etɛ yɛ acre kome mli lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, minine shɛ ŋmãa tɔn enyɔ pɛ ni dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ.

english: Yield differences depend heavily on seed variety, plant spacing, fertilizer timing, and weed control. Using improved seeds and proper spacing helps maximize output per acre.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ yibiiwoo mli lɛ damɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ anɔ. tsei ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ Be ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛ jwɛi akudɔmɔ Dumɔwui ni atsake kɛ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni yibii babaoo aba yɛ acre kome mli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall but produce small, unfilled cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ daa shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni eyiko mli lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen early in the season or crowded planting can cause maize to put energy into leaf growth instead of cob development, especially if water is lacking during flowering.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli loo dumɔ ni fa babaoo baanyɛ aha ŋmãa kɛ hewalɛ babaoo awo baai lɛ adalɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaaya hiɛ Titri lɛ kɛji nu faaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: Why does my cassava become hard and woody if I leave it in the ground past harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni efeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: As cassava roots age past maturity, the plant converts tender starch into tough woody fibers, making the roots hard, fibrous, and difficult to sell or process.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fe afii pɔtɛɛ ko Tso lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ewoɔ tso mli ŋmei ni mli wa mli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, ni ewa akɛ abaahɔ̃ɔ loo atsu he nii.

english: Why do young sunflower plants face the sun and follow it across the sky during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulutsoo tsei lɛ kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ ni amɛnyiɛɔ esɛɛ kɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young sunflowers track the sun to capture maximum sunlight for growth. Once the flower fully opens, it stays facing east to warm up quickly and attract pollinating bees.
ga: Hulu fɔfɔi bibii nyiɛɔ hulu lɛ sɛɛ koni amɛmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛdara. Kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ebɔi fɔfɔii lɛ Ebaakwɛ bokagbɛ koni edɔ oya ni egbala ŋmeii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: High temperatures and dry air stress tomato plants. When it gets too hot, the plant drops its flowers to conserve water and energy rather than spending resources on developing fruit.
ga: Nibii ni mli edɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi haoɔ tomato tsei. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii baatsu nii koni akɛfee aduawai lɛ

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize start turning yellow before the crop matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to build green leaves and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why should I rotate my farm with groundnuts or beans after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsake miŋmɔ lɛ beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen from the air and puts it back into the soil. Planting them improves soil fertility naturally for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yams need loose, deep, and well-mounded soil to expand smoothly. If the soil is too hard, stony, or poorly prepared, the tubers struggle to penetrate downwards and become misshapen.
ga: Sweet potatoes hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ, eyɛ tɛi, loo asaaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Tubers baanyɛ abote mli kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efite.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl upward and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking juice from under the leaves, or by viruses carried by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni ji nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ anɔ

english: Why do insects swarm my cowpea field as soon as the plants start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔji lɛ amli kɛji tsei lɛ bɔi fɔmɔ pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers and young pods produce sweet scents and soft tissue that naturally attract pests like pod borers looking for food and places to lay eggs.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni taoɔ niyenii kɛ hei ni amɛbaawo amɛ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do weed seeds grow much faster than my crop seeds after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ daa oya fe mi nɔ lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive hard conditions. Their seeds wake up instantly with tiny amounts of water, while crop seeds require specific soil warmth and moisture balance to germinate.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛdumɔwui lɛ teɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ nu fioo ko. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, aduawai dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when the rains are heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When land remains flooded for too long, water fills all the air spaces, causing the roots to suffocate and decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Nu lɛ baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ fɛɛ amli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: When is the best time for me to clear my land before the major rainy season begins?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ matsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ aje shishi?

english: Land should be cleared towards the end of the dry season so the cut weeds dry out completely. This allows easy land preparation and lets organic material start breaking down as soon as the first rains arrive.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ naagbee. Bɔni afee ni jwɛi ni afo lɛ agbi kwraa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni esaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mlɛo. ni ehaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfiteɔ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ba pɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen fertilizer or when excess water around the roots prevents them from taking up plant food from the soil.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen loo kɛ́ nu babaoo ebɔle ehe. Shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekaye niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava and pepper plants wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil is not completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca kɛ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbiko kwraa moŋ?

english: Crops lose water faster through their leaves under intense heat than their roots can draw up from the ground. They temporarily droop to shield themselves from drying out.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaatsi amɛhe be kukuoo ko koni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunshine. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act like natural shade umbrellas to protect cocoa seedlings in their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Planting seeds too close forces plants to fight one another for sunlight, water, and soil food, which results in tall, thin stalks with small or missing cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni dumɔwui bibii loo nɔ ni bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do armyworms and caterpillars suddenly attack my farm right after the early rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ trukaa beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Early rains trigger crops to grow tender green shoots, which attract adult moths to lay eggs. These hatch into hungry caterpillars that feed heavily on new foliage.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shwie shi. ni gbalaa ŋmeii koni amɛwo amɛ ŋmeii Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni yeɔ baai heei lɛ waa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot in the ground when heavy rains flood my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to stay alive. Flooded land cuts off air supply to the roots, causing waterlogging and fungal diseases that decay the tubers underground.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ naa. Enɛ haa nu shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmeii helai ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers before developing into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛbatsɔ anɔkwa yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or absence of pollinating insects causes tomato plants to drop flowers to preserve energy for their survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: How do I know if my cassava crop is fully mature and ready for harvesting underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Mature cassava plants show signs such as yellowing lower leaves that naturally fall off, cracking in the ground around the stem base, and a firm, starch-filled root core when sample tubers are checked.
ga: Cassava tsei ni eda lɛ baajie okadii tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ kpo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ starch beni akwɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why does growing cowpea or groundnut on my farm help my maize grow better in the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in soil root nodules, naturally enriching the ground with fertilizer for future crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster during the rainy season than during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Abundant rainfall combined with sunlight speeds up weed seed germination and growth, causing them to rapidly outcompete your cultivated crops for light and nutrition.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo kɛ hulu la baaha jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛdara oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ aye otso lɛ nɔ oya kɛha la kɛ niyenii kpakpai.

english: Why do the roots of my crops rot when there is continuous heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni naa wa miinɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Excessive rain fills up air spaces in the soil, effectively suffocating plant roots. Waterlogged soil also creates an ideal environment for harmful fungi to multiply and attack the root system.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ hu feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ koni amɛshwere ni amɛtutua shishifãi lɛ.

english: Can heavy downpours wash away the fertilizer I just applied around my crops?
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwo he fɛɛ he kɛkɛ lɛ. Ani manyɛ maná miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, heavy rain causes surface runoff that carries away topsoil and fertilizer before plants can absorb it. It is best to bury fertilizer slightly in the soil or apply it when light rain is expected rather than a heavy storm.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofu ŋmɔshi nibii fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo okɛtsu nii kɛ́ akpaa gbɛ akɛ nugbɔ baanɛ fioo. Yɛ ahum ni naa wa najiaŋ

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds and bushes before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii dani madu lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds removes direct competition for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. It also destroys hiding places and breeding grounds for insects and rodents that attack young seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii ni yaa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Efiteɔ hei ni kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni tutuaa tsei bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli kɛ hei ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ lɛ hu.

english: Does burning cleared bush make my soil better for growing crops?
ga: Ani tsei bibii ni ajie lɛ ni ashãa lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ?

english: While ash provides a temporary nutrient boost, burning destroys valuable organic matter, kills beneficial soil organisms, and leaves the soil exposed to drying out faster in the heat.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ sũ lɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fataa he yɛ be kukuoo mli moŋ, shi shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Efiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya kɛji akɛ edɔ

english: Why do leaves on my cassava plants turn yellow and curl up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are typical symptoms of viral plant diseases spread by tiny insects like whiteflies, or a signal that the plant lacks important nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ji okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ tsei ahe helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ahe. Aloo eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen.

english: How does plant sickness travel from a diseased crop field to my clean farm?
ga: Te tsei ahe helai tsɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni helai yɔɔ mli lɛ amli kɛyaa miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Diseases travel through rain splashes, wind, sap carried on dirty cutlasses and tools, or insects moving from infected fields to feed on healthy plants.
ga: Helai tsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ latɛs ni kpɛtɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ nitsumɔ dadei ni he tseee lɛ amli. loo kooloi bibii ni fãa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli koni amɛyaye tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it good to leave rotting farm waste on top of my field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashi ŋmɔ mli jwɛi ni egbo lɛ yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli?

english: Leaving healthy plant waste on soil acts as mulch, which protects the ground from excessive heat, traps moisture, and decomposes into rich organic matter. However, waste from diseased plants should be removed so it does not infect new crops.
ga: Tsei ahe jwɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine he. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ ajie jwɛi ni jɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ koni hela akamɔ tsei heei.

english: Why does my soil stay hard and dry even after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni egbi yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ po lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic material like compost or animal manure, forming a hard top crust that causes rainwater to run off the surface instead of soaking deep to the roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. Efeɔ ŋshɔŋloo ko ni wa yɛ nɔ ni haa nugbɔ nu lɛ joɔ foi kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni eeebote shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why should I leave proper distance between my plants instead of putting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ ni sa yɛ tsei ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni makɛ amɛ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each crop gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nourishment without competing with its neighbors, leading to healthier plants and larger harvest yields.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa. ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ akutsoŋbii akaŋ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do pests attack my crops more when nearby farms are overgrown and unmaintained?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be mli ni ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ efee ŋmɔji ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Overgrown farms act as nurseries for pests and diseases. Once their population increases or food runs out on the abandoned land, they migrate to attack neighboring healthy crops.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ji hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai fɔɔ yɛ. Kɛ gbɔmɛi ayibɔ tee hiɛ loo niyenii ba naagbee yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ewo muji nɔ lɛ Amɛfãa kɛyaa hei krokomɛi koni amɛyatutua ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops stop producing yield if I do not feed the soil regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ yibii kɛji mikɛ niyenii haaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Just like animals need continuous food to produce, crops rely on soil nutrients to make leaves, flowers, and fruits. If the soil becomes empty of nutrients, the plant stops growing and producing food to survive.
ga: Nakai eji yɛ kooloi ni biɔ niyenii ni fa daa koni amɛfɔ lɛ hu ahe. Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ koni ewo baai, fɔfɔii, kɛ aduawai. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ, Tsei lɛ kpaɔ amɛdalɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer to my maize in small stages instead of putting it all at once at planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-abele lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ bei bibii amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ awo mli shikome beni oduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Applying fertilizer bit by bit gives the maize plant nutrients right when it is growing fastest. If you put everything at once, heavy rains can wash the extra fertilizer away before the roots can absorb it.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he fiofio lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha niyenii ni he hiaa o-ŋmei tsei lɛ koni amɛdara oya bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Kɛ okɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ wo mli shikome Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ aya dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to walk through my crop field every few days instead of visiting once a month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔ ŋmɔji amli daa gbii fioo moŋ fe ni mayasara shikome yɛ nyɔŋ fɛɛ nyɔŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Regularly checking your farm allows you to spot pests, leaf diseases, or dry soil early. Catching issues early prevents small problems from spreading and destroying your entire harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai, tsei ahe helai, loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mra. Saji ni ooomɔ mli mra Ebaatsi naagbai bibii anaa. Gbalamɔ ni okpãtã onibii fɛɛ ahiɛ.

english: How does keeping my cassava field clean of weeds during the first few months help the plants grow bigger roots?
ga: Bɔ ni kɛ́ oha o-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse ni jwɛi bɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi wuji.

english: Young cassava plants grow slowly at first. If weeds grow around them, they steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that the cassava needs to build strong underground tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei bibii lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli. Kɛji jwɛi komɛi yɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ Ejuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa ŋmei lɛ koni ekɛkwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up into tight tubes during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves to protect themselves from hot sun and reduce the amount of water lost through their leaves when the soil is dry.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni ehaa nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my tomato plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When a plant lacks nutrients like nitrogen or gets too much water around its roots, it steals food from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Kɛ́ tso ko bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu babaoo ebɔle eshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ejuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does picking my pepper fruits continuously make the plant produce more peppers over time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mitee nɔ mikpa mi-peppers lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ woɔ peppers babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: When you harvest mature peppers, the plant shifts its energy from holding old fruit back into making new flowers and setting fresh fruits over many weeks.
ga: Kɛji okpa ŋmeii ni eda lɛ Tsei tsakeɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ aduawai momo ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa fɔfɔi heei afeemɔ kɛ aduawai heei ni atoɔ otsii babaoo lɛ mli.

english: Why do some improved crop varieties mature faster than the traditional seeds I usually plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi komɛi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ shwereɔ oya fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ daa lɛ?

english: Improved crop seeds are bred to complete their growth cycle quicker so they can produce full grains or fruits before dry seasons begin or rains stop early.
ga: Akɛ tsei dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe lɛ fɔɔ koni amɛgbe amɛdalɛ be lɛ naa oya. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni dumɔwui loo aduawai aba jogbaŋŋ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi loo nugbɔ lɛ akpa mra.

english: Why do my plantain stems take longer to bear fruit when I allow many young suckers to grow around one mother plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ? Akɛni miha tsei bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso ni ji nyɛ kome lɛ he hewɔ lɛ

english: Multiple suckers attached to one mother plant share the same root water and soil food. Pruning extra suckers leaves more energy for one stem to produce a big bunch quickly.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi babaoo ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ fɔlɔ kome he lɛ yeɔ shishifã nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kome lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ehaa tso kome náa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛfeɔ kuu agbo oya.

english: Why do cowpea plants drop their flowers when insects attack them during flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua amɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants drop damaged flowers as a stress response when insects feed on the buds, which prevents the plant from forming healthy pods.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni efite lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nɔnyɛɛ hetoohamɔ mli beni kooloi yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ afee ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: Is it good practice for me to burn my bush after clearing the land before planting?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooshã tsei bibii beni ajie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani adu?

english: Burning clears the field quickly, but it destroys important organic matter and beneficial micro-organisms in the topsoil. Over time, burning weakens the soil, makes it lose moisture fast, and lowers your crop yields.
ga: Shãa lɛ jieɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ oya. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Shãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa shi oya ni ehaa onibii ni oduɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle harsh direct sunlight. Large shade trees protect seedlings from intense heat and keep the soil moist, giving the young cocoa time to grow strong enough to survive on its own.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ be ni ekɛdara ni ehe wa bɔ ni sa koni lɛ diɛŋtsɛ enyɛ ehi shi.

english: If I plant my cassava stalks very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for sun, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each cassava plant enough room to build large, healthy tubers, resulting in a heavier total harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmei tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmei agbo ni mli wa. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow before the ears are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize relies on for green leafy growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or rotating your maize with beans can help restore leaf health and crop strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa lɛ damɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo mli loo ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni baa lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I put chemical fertilizer in the same hole as my seed when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ midu lɛ, ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo bu ni dumɔwui lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against a seed can burn the seed and stop it from sprouting. It is better to place fertilizer a few centimeters away from the seed or wait until the seedling has already emerged.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛshã ni amɛkpa kwɛ̃mɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli aaafee sɛntimitai 2-3 kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe loo amɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ momo.

english: What is making ragged holes in the leaves of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmeii?

english: Ragged holes in young corn are often caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the central leaves. Checking your field early in the morning and treating affected plants early prevents major leaf loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ niyenii yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli leebi ni otsa tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni akafite baai wuji.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these tiny pests with early spraying keeps the foliage healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ Akɛ tsofa shwieɔ enɛɛmɛi anɔ mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ mli waa.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting inside the soil when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and sits around them for too long. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots do not suffocate.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni shishifãi lɛ akagbɔjɔ

english: Why do my crops perform poorly if I wait until the weeds are tall before I clear them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji mimɛ kɛyashi jwɛi lɛ shwere dani mijie amɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital nutrients, soil moisture, and sunlight away from young crops when they need them most. Weeding early prevents weeds from choking your crop during its most critical growth period.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu Ni hulu la yaa kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa amɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekafite onibii yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or drought. Keeping the soil consistently moist and using mulch around the stems helps the flowers stay on the plant and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are some farmers building plastic shade houses to grow vegetables instead of planting directly in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi maa plastic tsũi ni akɛduɔ aduawai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadu yɛ ŋmɔji amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Growing crops inside plastic or net structures (greenhouses) protects delicate plants from heavy rains, harsh sunlight, pests, and diseases. It allows farmers to control water and heat, leading to healthier vegetables like tomatoes and peppers all year round.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ plastic loo ŋshɔŋlooi amli (greenhouses) lɛ buɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ahe, ni ehaa okwaafoi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ nu kɛ dɔlɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa anáa aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build strong green leaves. It can also happen if the soil is too waterlogged, which prevents the plant roots from breathing and absorbing food.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa tso shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛmu niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop and look dead during the hot afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛ Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the ground. They wilt to protect themselves from losing more moisture, and they usually stand back up when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi babaoo lɛ he, ni amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛte shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when the plant doesn't get enough water, or when there is a lack of nutrients like potassium in the soil. Without the right temperature and food, the flower dies before it can grow into a fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo be mli ni niyenii tamɔ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji hulutsoo kɛ niyenii ni sa bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagboi dani amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cassava sticks very close to each other on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are too close together, their leaves shade each other from the sun, and their roots fight for the same water and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin stems with very small tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ baaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bulbs bibii waa yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baa.

english: Tomatoes and garden eggs belong to the same plant family and attract the same pests and soil diseases. If you plant them back-to-back in the same spot, the diseases left in the soil from the previous harvest will easily attack the new plants.
ga: Tomato kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ fata tsei akuu kome he, ni amɛgbalaa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛji odu amɛ yɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ Helai ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ tutuaa tsei heei oya.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around their crops with dry grass or cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmeii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or organic materials (called mulching) keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly in the heat, stops weeds from growing, and adds rich food to the soil as it rots.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (Atsɛɔ enɛ mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji akɛ edɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ Ni ekɛ niyenii ni jara wa fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he beni egboɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I snap off the small extra shoots growing in the stem joints of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Those extra shoots (called suckers) steal food and water from the main plant. Removing them forces the plant to send all its energy and nutrients into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes instead of extra useless branches.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii krokomɛi (ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers) lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli Tomato ni ajieɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo tomato ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli moŋ fe niji ni he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings wilt and die shortly after I move them from the nursery bed to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seedlings go into shock if their roots are broken or if they are moved under strong afternoon sunshine. It is best to move seedlings late in the afternoon or on a cloudy day and water them immediately so they can adjust smoothly.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakpokpo kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ fã loo amɛtsi amɛhe yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui yɛ shwane mli loo yɛ gbi ni atatu yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ nu awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni enyɛ ekɛ ehe awo mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there is plenty of space for all plants to grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Kɛji akɛ he ko yɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akwɛ tsei lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively drink up the soil's water and fertilizer. They also block sunlight from reaching your crops and can hide harmful insects that will later jump onto your plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛnuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo. Ehaa hulu la hu shɛɔ onibii ahe. Ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni sɛɛ mli lɛ amɛbaatu kɛya otsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ato.

english: Why should I bring a sample of my farm soil to you for lab analysis before I start planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ aba bo koni akwɛ mli yɛ laboratori mli dani mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: Testing your soil in a lab tells us exactly which nutrients your land is missing, so you don't waste money buying the wrong fertilizers and can give your crops the right food to produce a high yield.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa ni afeɔ yɛ laboratori mli lɛ baatsɔɔ wɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ ni bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni ofite shika kɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa ni obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii ni sa aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: What basic steps should I take to clear and prepare my field before sowing my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titri esa akɛ mafee koni mikɛjie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ ni masaa he dani madu dumɔwui?

english: You need to clear weeds, remove plant debris, and gently loosen the topsoil so that seed roots can easily penetrate the ground, hold moisture, and absorb nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi kɛjɛ ohe. Jiemɔ tsei amli sũ ni efite lɛ ni okɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ afee blɛoo koni dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ abote sũ lɛ mli. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ shwieɔ mli oya

english: Is there any chemical or soil treatment I should apply to my land before planting to prevent pests and diseases?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai atsu nii loo mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii dani madu nii koni kooloi kɛ helai akabote mli?

english: Treating the soil or seeds with safe, recommended chemicals before planting creates a protective shield against soil insects and fungal infections that destroy young seeds before they sprout.
ga: Tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii kɛtsa shikpɔŋ loo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ dani adu lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ baa.

english: How do I know the exact right day or week to start planting my maize during the rainy season in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbi loo otsi pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli yɛ Ghana?

english: You should start planting right after the first two or three steady rains when the soil is deeply moist, ensuring the seeds have continuous moisture to germinate and grow strong roots.
ga: Esa akɛ oje dumɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi 2-3 ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ náa nu ni yaa nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my tomato seeds need to start in a nursery bed before I move them into my main farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mije mi tomato dumɔwui lɛ ashishi yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani ajie kɛya miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tiny seeds are very delicate; starting them in a protected nursery keeps them safe from harsh sun, heavy rain, and insects until they grow strong enough to survive in the open field.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ waaa kwraa. Kɛ́ oje amɛ shishi yɛ he ko ni abuɔ he lɛ, ebaaha amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ hulu ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: How should I pour water on my vegetable crops so that I do not wash away the roots or drown them?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mafɔse nu yɛ mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ koni amɛkafɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe loo amɛkafo amɛ?

english: You should water gently at the base of the plant early in the morning so the roots absorb the moisture deep underground before the heat of the sun evaporates it.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ nu awo shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ fioo leebi koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ dani hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: If crops receive too little water, their leaves wilt and curl up to save moisture; if they receive too much water, their leaves turn yellow and the plant stops growing because the roots cannot breathe.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛɔ nu fioo nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpãa koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why are the leaves on my corn plants turning yellow instead of staying healthy and dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for help showing that the crop is starving for nitrogen nutrients or that too much standing water is choking the plant's roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji yelikɛbuamɔ he bolɔmɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen niyenii bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli loo nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ miitsi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and small when I let weeds grow close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ miha jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal light, water, and fertilizer away from your crops, leaving your crops weak and malnourished.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ, ni amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnáaa niyenii kpakpa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant cassava or maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the field, while rotating crops keeps the soil fertile and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like umbrellas, providing necessary shade and preserving soil moisture for young cocoa trees during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ aha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Look closely at the small leaf buds along the cassava stem—they must always point upwards toward the sky. Planting stems upside down causes the buds to struggle to reach light, resulting in weak plants and low yield.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Nyiɛmɔ ŋmei lɛ tso lɛ sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ dara kɛtee shishi lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná la. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Yam plants are natural climbing vines that produce tubers based on how much light their leaves receive. Staking keeps the leaves spread out off the wet ground so they can catch maximum sunlight and prevent leaf rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni feɔ bulbs ni damɔ la ni baai lɛ náa lɛ nɔ. Staking haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛtsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build green leaves. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like urea quickly helps the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛwoɔ mli oya lɛ baaye abua baa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good practice to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina loo ŋmãa?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have natural abilities to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them with maize feeds the soil naturally, reducing your need to buy expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I avoid putting granular fertilizer on dry soil during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve safely into the soil so roots can drink it. When applied to dry soil in heat, concentrated fertilizer stays dry and severely burns the roots, which can stunt or kill your crops.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe koni shishifãi lɛ anu nu. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, egbiɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shãa waa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ loo egbo.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before producing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or sudden shifts between drought and heavy rain. The plant drops its flowers to protect itself and conserve energy until weather conditions stabilize.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa yɛ hɔmɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa teŋ lɛ he. Tsei baajie fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop and wilt in the afternoon heat even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni mi lɛ shwieee lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, vegetable leaves lose water through evaporation faster than their roots can drink from the soil. As long as the soil stays damp, the leaves will bounce back once the evening cool arrives.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, tsei ahe tsei ahe tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji gbɛkɛ mli fɛ̃i lɛ bashɛ shi pɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turning black and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni midu lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo lɛ?

english: Black, sunken bottoms on tomatoes are caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often brought on by irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture constant allows the plant to smoothly transport calcium to growing fruits.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato shishi diŋ ni ebote mli lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɛɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium lɛ yaa aduawai ni miida lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are small ragged holes suddenly appearing in the leaf funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eba trukaa yɛ mi-ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize foliage are classic signs of fall armyworms feeding inside the plant's growing center. Spotting these holes early allows you to target insecticides directly into the plant heart before crop loss occurs.
ga: Buji ni ekumɔ yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ fall cutworms ni yeɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ mli. Buji nɛɛ akwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaha okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛya tso lɛ teŋgbɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. Giving them proper space helps each plant grow strong and yield a bigger harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni jɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ he ni sa ha tso lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do some farmers plant cassava on raised soil mounds instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ moŋ fe hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Raised mounds soften the earth so cassava roots can grow easily into large tubers. Mounds also prevent rainwater from staying around the roots, which stops them from rotting.
ga: Gɔŋ ni awo nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, cassava shishifãi baanyɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji oya. Gɔŋ lɛ hu tsiɔ nugbɔ nu naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekafite.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth, or that the soil is holding too much water. Adding the right fertilizer can bring back their green color and help them grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ baaha amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt during the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can soak it up. They wilt to protect themselves from losing moisture, and they usually recover once the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Amɛmiisumɔ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open field with no trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tso ko bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides them with a cool, moist environment until they are old enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha amɛná he ko ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Fertilizer works best when the soil is moist right after a soft rain and when the plant is actively growing. Putting fertilizer on dry soil can burn the plant's roots and waste your money.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛ fioo sɛɛ. kɛ be mli ni tsei miida Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ shishifãi ni efite shika.

english: What will happen to my crops if I put too much chemical spray on them to kill weeds?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai babaoo shwie shi koni mikɛgbe jwɛi?

english: Using too much chemical spray can burn and stunt your crops, or even kill them along with the weeds. Always follow the exact measurement given for clean water to keep your plants safe.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii anɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ashã ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbɔjɔ. Aloo gbemɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ jwɛi lɛ po. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, nyiɛmɔ susumɔi ni ja kɛha nu ni mli tse koni otsei lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do weeds cause my crop yields to drop so much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ miiba shi waa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Removing weeds early ensures your crops get all the energy they need to produce a good yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: How can I tell if insects are damaging my crops inside the stem where I cannot see them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii miifite miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ tsei lɛ amli ni minyɛɛɛ mana amɛ?

english: Look out for small holes in the leaves, yellowish dust around the center leaves, or stems that break easily. These are signs of pests like stalk borers or armyworms that require specific crop treatments to protect the harvest.
ga: Taomɔ bu bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli, sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔle baa lɛ teŋgbɛ, loo tsei ni fãa oya. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ stem borers loo cutworms ni biɔ ni akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ koni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ he okadii.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil year after year and causes pests to build up in the ground. Switching your field to groundnuts or beans restores good food to the soil and stops pests from multiplying.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. ni ehaa ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni atsakeɔ awoɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii amli lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii kpakpai aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaatsi ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkafɔ.

english: Can I mix multiple farm chemicals together in one spray tank to save time on my cocoa farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai babaoo afutu mli yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kome mli koni mikɛ be akafite yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Combining different chemicals without professional guidance can cause a bad chemical reaction, neutralizing their active ingredients and rendering the mixture completely useless against pests.
ga: Tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛaafata he ni ŋaalɔi akudɔɔɔ amɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofa lɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii. ehaa nibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ehaa nɔ ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ he ehiaaa kwraa yɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why did my spray mixture separate into oil and water after I stirred it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-spray mixture lɛ mli gbalaa kɛfeɔ fɔ kɛ nu beni mikɛwo mli lɛ?

english: Certain oil-based farm medicines are incompatible with specific liquids or other chemicals. When mixed incorrectly, the solution breaks down and loses its ability to stick to or protect plants.
ga: Tsofai komɛi ni akɛ mu tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kɛ nu komɛi loo tsofai krokomɛi kpaaa gbee. Kɛji akɛ akɛfutu mli yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ, tsofa lɛ fiteɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ tsei ahe loo ebu amɛhe dɔŋŋ.

english: What is the proper way to mix liquid farm medicines with water?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofa ni ji nu futuɔ nu mli?

english: Always follow the specific instructions on the label. Mixing oil-based formulas incorrectly with water can cause the active ingredients to clump or separate, preventing them from working on your crops.
ga: Nyiɛmɔ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ wolo lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ akɛ fɔ kɛ nu ni akɛfutuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha nibii ni tsuɔ nii lɛ afee ekome loo amɛgbala amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ onibii lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why are insects still destroying my cocoa pods even after I sprayed the farm with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Spraying may fail if you mixed incompatible chemicals together, used the wrong proportions, or accidentally ruined the active ingredients during preparation.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee futu mli. Kɛ akɛ nibii ni ejaaa tsu nii loo akɛfite nibii ni tsuɔ nii lɛ yɛ oshara mli yɛ be mli ni asaa he lɛ.

english: How can I tell if a chemical mixture I prepared on the farm has gone bad before spraying?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofa ni mikɛfutu ni mifee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite dani mikɛshwie nɔ?

english: If the liquid separates into distinct layers, forms thick sludge, or leaves floating oil on top after adding water, the chemical balance is ruined and it will not protect your crops.
ga: Kɛji nu lɛ mli gbala mli ewo fãi amli lɛ Efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ Aloo ehaa mu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi beni akɛ nu efata he sɛɛ. Tsofai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baafite ni anyɛɛɛ abu onibii ahe.

english: Why did my crop medicine stop working after I combined it with another spray?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmɔshi tsofa lɛ kpaɔ nitsumɔ beni mikɛ tsofa kroko ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ efutu lɛ?

english: Different farm chemicals contain ingredients that can clash and cancel each other out when mixed together, leaving your crop completely unprotected.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ nibii ni baanyɛ atswa amɛhe ni amɛfo amɛhe kɛji akɛ akɛfutu mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, abuuu onibii ahe kwraa.

english: Why shouldn't I mix five different crop medicines together to fight farm diseases faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai srɔtoi 5 ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ futuɔ koni mikɛ helai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ awuu oya?

english: Mixing too many chemicals creates an untested compound that can scorch plant leaves, fail to cure diseases, and waste your money.
ga: Tsofai babaoo ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ haa anáa nibii ni akako amɛ akwɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso baai ashã. Enyɛŋ etsa helai kɛ shika ni afiteɔ

english: How do I know which farm medicines are safe to combine before applying them to my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni mikɛbaafutu dani mikɛwo mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: You should read the product label or consult an agricultural extension officer who understands chemical compatibility and knows which ingredients work safely together.
ga: Esa akɛ okane nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe saji loo oyabi okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko ni nuɔ tsofai ni kɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee kɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ shishi.

english: Is it safer to buy ready-made chemical formulas or mix individual treatments myself?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooohe tsofa ko ni afee momo loo bo diɛŋtsɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ afutu mli?

english: Ready-made formulas produced by experts are correctly balanced to protect crops, whereas self-mixing at home often ruins the oils and active ingredients required for pest control.
ga: Fomulai ni afee klalo ni ŋaalɔi feɔ lɛ ja pɛpɛɛpɛ koni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, shia nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ fiteɔ fɔ kɛ nibii ni tsuɔ nii ni he hiaa kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ.

english: Why is it important to ask an agricultural expert before trying a new chemical mix on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni obi okwaayeli he nilelɔ ko dani oka tsofa hee ni akɛfutuɔ nii yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ okwɛ?

english: Extension officers provide accurate knowledge on safe chemical combinations and proper usage, preventing costly mistakes that ruin farm inputs and harm crop yields.
ga: Nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ nilee ni sa ni kɔɔ tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛ bɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ he lɛ he hewalɛ. Tsi tɔmɔi ni jara wa ni fiteɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni yeɔ ŋmɔ mli yibiiwoo lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very big leaves but produce very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava plants produce small tubers when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or when planted too close together. High nitrogen makes the plant put all its energy into growing green leaves on top instead of storing food in the roots underground.
ga: Cassava tsei woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ́ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai eŋɔli ni miida yɛ nɔ lɛ he nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Why are the tips of my lower maize leaves turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ ashishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the tips of lower leaves and moves down the central leaf rib usually means the plant lacks nitrogen. The maize plant automatically moves its remaining nitrogen up to feed the young, growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni eyaa shishi kɛyaa shishigbɛ tsitsii lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Abɛi tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: What causes my maize leaves to get holes in them with brown sawdust-like dust inside the middle fold?
ga: Mɛni haa mi ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ bu kɛ sũ ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The caterpillar hides inside the central shoot fold of the maize plant to feed on young leaves, leaving behind sawdust-like droppings called frass.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Amɛshiɔ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ frass lɛ yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Leaf drop in cocoa trees during dry periods is usually caused by water stress from the Harmattan wind or damage from sap-sucking pests like capsids. The tree drops leaves to protect itself from losing too much moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu mli haomɔ ni jɛɔ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ mli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ kookoo tsei amli yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ baa. loo nibii ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ capsids lɛ adɛŋ lɛ, tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni hoɔ fe nine lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my cowpea plants curling up and feeling sticky to touch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji ota he lɛ?

english: Curling and sticky leaves on cowpeas are caused by aphids—tiny insects that cluster under leaves to suck plant sap. As they feed, they excrete a sweet, sticky waste called honeydew that attracts mold.
ga: Aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ekpɛtɛɔ he yɛ tsina ŋmei nɔ lɛ baa. Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi bibii ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ baai ashishi koni amɛnu tso mli nu. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii Amɛjieɔ muji ni shwieɔ shi. Atsɛɔ no akɛ honeydew, ni gbalaa ŋmeii.

english: Why do people recommend planting groundnuts or cowpeas inside my maize farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmei ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. This natural fertilizer feeds the soil and helps your maize grow greener and stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: What will happen to my plantain farm if I plant the suckers too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmeii lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting suckers too close forces the plantains to fight for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in weak, thin stems that easily break in heavy winds and produce much smaller banana bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ ahe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei akui ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa ni kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa amɛ lɛ, amɛkuɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ banana tsei bibii waa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into tomato fruits when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when day and night temperatures get too high. Extreme heat damages the flower pollen, preventing it from fertilizing the bloom to form a tomato fruit.
ga: Tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ shwane kɛ gbɛkɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ fɔfɔi amli ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haaa anyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi kɛyashi amɛbaatsɔ tomato aduawai.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly inside the storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miifite oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly when bruised during digging or stored in hot, unventilated barns. Fungi and bacteria enter through cut skin and multiply fast if hot air and moisture stay trapped around the tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ be mli ni atsaa loo akɛto ŋmɔ ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ mli. Fungi kɛ bacteria boteɔ hewolo ni afo lɛ mli ni amɛshwereɔ oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ebɔle tuber lɛ he.

english: Why do my fresh hot peppers turn soft and spoil within two days of picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers heei lɛ fee blɛoo ni egbo yɛ gbii enyɔ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni ajie lɛ lɛ?

english: Peppers spoil quickly if harvested during the hot afternoon heat or kept inside sealed plastic bags. Trapped heat and sweat moisture cause fungal decay to spread rapidly through the fruit.
ga: Chili shitoi fiteɔ oya kɛji akpa yɛ shwane ni edɔ loo akɛto plastic kotoku mli. Dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni jɛɔ latsaa mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the large trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gĩ ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive, tender leaves that burn under full, direct sunlight. Keeping mature shade trees or planting fast-growing plants like plantains creates a humid canopy that shields young cocoa from heat until its roots are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni nuɔ he waa, ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nuɔ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to make green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea restores healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni aná baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ni yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, providing free natural food for crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni nine shɛɔ nitrogen gas nɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa efeɔ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko, ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Does it matter which way up I push cassava stem cuttings into the ground when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ adu lɛ, ani abaatsi ŋmei niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbɛ ko nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cassava stems upside down forces the shoots to grow downward before turning upward, which weakens the plant and reduces the number and size of tubers you harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ nyɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ nɔ koni ekwɛ shi kɛya shishi dani ekɛ ehiɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni okɛ bulbs ni okpaa lɛ ayibɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ aba shi.

english: Why do I need to put tall bamboo stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ ŋmei tsei kakadaji ama shi lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high into the open sunlight so they can produce maximum food energy, which is then sent underground to swell the tuber.
