ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛná niyenii hewalɛ babaoo. ni abaamaje yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni eha yitso lɛ ada

english: Why shouldn't I let all the tiny suckers keep growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii shwereɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow creates competition for water and soil nutrients, leading to small bunches; leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaha akaŋshii aba kɛha niyenii ni jɛɔ nu lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii baa. Ashiɔ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni ekwɛ akɛ tso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers drop off without setting fruit when the air gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no beneficial insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why does my mango tree bear heavy fruit one year and almost nothing the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tso woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi kome mli shi afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ewooo yibii kwraa lɛ?

english: This is called alternate bearing; producing a massive fruit harvest uses up almost all of the tree's stored food energy, requiring the tree to spend the following year recovering before it can fruit heavily again.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ bearing ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ. Yibii babaoo ni akpaa lɛ kɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni tso lɛ eto lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ he hiaa be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli dani enyɛ ewo yibii ni tsii ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap from soft leaves and spreading plant viruses that stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ baai bibii amli nu lɛ kɛ tso mli helai ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable garden in the afternoon sun or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu shwane loo leebi?

english: Watering early in the morning gives roots time to soak up moisture before the heat of the day causes evaporation, preventing plant heat stress and leaf disease.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛjieɔ nu dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa amɛshwieɔ shi. Etsiɔ tsei amli dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛ tsei ahe helai anaa.

english: The bottles of spray brought to us have writing in foreign languages that I cannot read, so how can I know what chemical is inside?
ga: Akɛ maŋsɛɛ wiemɔ ko ni anyɛɛɛ akane lɛ wo spray tɔ ni akɛba wɔŋɔɔ lɛ mli. Te wɔfeɔ tɛŋŋ wɔleɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Agrochemical bottles use color-coded bands at the bottom of the label to show toxicity levels, and symbols to show if it is for insects or diseases. You can also ask your extension officer to translate the active ingredient name so you know exactly what crop medicine you are putting on your farm.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ kɛ tsɔne ko ni yɔɔ kɔla ni yɔɔ wolo lɛ shishi lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ bɔ ni tsofai fɔji lɛ yɔɔ ha. kɛ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ eji kooloo loo hela nɔ ko. Obaanyɛ obi o-promotions najiaŋdamɔlɔ lɛ hu ni etsɔɔ nibii ni tsuɔ nii lɛ agbɛi shishi. Bɔni afee ni ole tsei ni okɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What is the difference between an insecticide spray and a fungicide spray for my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akɛshwieɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ teŋ?

english: Insecticides are designed specifically to destroy insect pests like capsids that bite crop leaves and pods, while fungicides are designed to prevent and kill fungal diseases like black pod that cause the crop to rot.
ga: Afee tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛkɛfite kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids ni ŋmɔɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, afee tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii koni akɛtsi ŋmeii ni gbeɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii diji ni haa tsei fiteɔ lɛ anaa ni egbe amɛ.

english: How do I know the right amount of chemical liquid to mix into my knapsack sprayer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛfutu mi-baagi mli tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ mli?

english: Using too much chemical can burn crop leaves, while using too little will not kill the pests. Always use the standard measuring cup provided with the chemical container or ask an extension officer to help you measure the exact dose based on your sprayer size.
ga: Tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ baai lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni akɛ nɔ ko fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ egbeŋ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ susumɔ kɔɔpoo ni akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baa lɛ atsu nii be fɛɛ be. Aloo bi o-extension nitsulɔi lɛ ni amɛye amɛbua bo ni osusu bɔ ni o-sprayer lɛ da ha lɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do I need to spray my cocoa farm repeatedly every two weeks instead of just once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ ekoŋŋ daa otsii enyɔ moŋ fe shikome pɛ lɛ?

english: A single spray only protects crops for a short period. Cocoa pods grow continuously and rain washes off the protection, so spraying every two weeks creates an ongoing shield that stops pests and black pod disease from attacking while the pods develop.
ga: Spray kome pɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe be kukuoo ko pɛ. Kookoo ŋmeii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛdaraa ni nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ hebuu lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa Otsii Enyɔ lɛ haa gbɛtsii nii ko ni yaa nɔ ni tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ black pod hela lɛ naa koni amɛkatutua amɛ be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: This black rot is caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which thrives in cool, wet weather. Regular fungicide spraying protects the developing pods from fungal spores so they can grow healthy until harvest.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod disease lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black rot hela nɛɛ baa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ mli. Tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe. Bɔni afee ni amɛdara ni amɛhe awa kɛyashi nikpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: If heavy rain falls right after I spray my cocoa trees, do I need to spray them again?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni afɔ kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ tsofa lɛ Ani ehe baahia ni afɔse nɔ ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, heavy rain that falls within a few hours of spraying washes the chemical off the crop surfaces before it can protect them, leaving the cocoa pods exposed to pests and diseases again.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni nɛɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni ashwieɔ tsofai lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ tsofai ahe nii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani anyɛɔ abuɔ he. Enɛ haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need extra protection while the pods are developing compared to when there are no pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe hiaa ni abu amɛhe babaoo yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miida lɛ? Kɛ akɛto be mli ni pod bɛ lɛ he?

english: Developing cocoa pods are soft, sweet, and full of water, making them the main food target for insects like capsids and fungal spores. When there are no pods, the tree requires less frequent protection.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni miiya hiɛ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, ŋɔɔ, ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ niyenii titri ni kooloi bibii, tamɔ capsids kɛ fungal spores lɛ yeɔ. Beni pod bɛ Tsei hu biɔ hebuu fioo.

english: Mature cocoa pods change color on the tree—green pods turn bright yellow, and dark red or purple pods turn orange-yellow. This color change indicates that the seeds inside are fully grown and ready for harvesting.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni eda lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmei. Nɛkɛ su tsakemɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Should I stop spraying my cocoa crops when the pods are almost ready to harvest?
ga: Ani esa akɛ makpa cacao tsei lɛ anɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ beni ŋmeii lɛ ebɛŋkɛ kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Yes, you must stop spraying a few weeks before harvesting—known as the pre-harvest interval—so that chemical residues wash off naturally, ensuring the harvested beans are safe to sell and process.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ okpa tsofa lɛ shwiemɔ otsii fioo komɛi dani kpamɔ lɛ aba. Ale lɛ hu akɛ be ni tsɔ ŋmaakpamɔ hiɛ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsofai ni eshwɛ lɛ ajɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha jarayeli kɛ nitsumɔ.

english: Why do some of my young cocoa pods shrivel up and turn black when they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ ekomɛi miigbo ni amɛmiitsɔ ediŋŋ lɛ? Ni eji nɔ bibioo kwraa lolo?

english: Small pods can shrivel due to cherelle wilt, which happens when the cocoa tree naturally thins out pods it cannot feed, or because insect pests bit the young pod and drained its nutrients before it could mature.
ga: Pods bibii baanyɛ agbo yɛ cherel ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ baa mli beni cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye nii. aloo akɛni tsɛŋemɔ helai ŋmɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ dani amɛdaraa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is a major food source in the soil. Heavy rains can wash this food away, so adding manure or fertilizer helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo niyenii nɛɛ kɛya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits around the roots without draining away, it chokes them and causes decay. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps extra water flow off safely.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ taraa shishifãi lɛ ahe ni efooo kɛyaaa lɛ. Ebaaha ŋmɔlɔ aba ni ekɛ fitemɔ aba. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Is it better for me to plant my pepper crop during the major rainy season or the dry season?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ mli loo nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Peppers grow easily in the rainy season because of natural water, but heavy rain can cause leaf diseases. If you have access to water for irrigation, planting in the dry season can produce good yields when market prices are higher.
ga: Chili peppers lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ nu ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ baa helai aba. Kɛji oyɛ nu kɛha nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ Dumɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaha yibiiwoo kpakpa aba beni jara nɔ jara wa lɛ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they suffer from stress caused by extreme heat, dry soil, or uneven watering. When temperatures get too high, the plant drops flowers to save its energy until conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli baa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the ground, leaving the soil weak. Beans and groundnuts put natural food back into the soil through their roots, which restores fertility for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. gbɔjɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Beans kɛ peanuts kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers dry up and die when I plant them under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young plantain suckers have soft tissues and fresh roots that cannot absorb water fast enough to survive harsh sunlight. Providing temporary shade or planting them beside fast-growing shade plants protects them until their roots grow strong.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi heei ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa koni amɛdamɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo loo dumɔ yɛ tsei ni daa oya lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, dark, and overly shaded farms during rainy periods. Pruning thick tree branches to let in sunlight and removing infected pods keeps the sickness from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ amli. Niji ni mli tse lɛ ni afoɔ Enɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ ni ejieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller and produce less when weeds are left around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni jwɛi eshwɛ yɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. When weeds grow close, they steal the food meant for your crops, causing your plants to stay small and weak.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ jwɛi kwɛ̃ ni ebɛŋkɛ bo Ebaaju niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why do some crop seeds take a very long time to sprout after I put them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds require continuous moisture and warm soil to wake up and germinate. If the soil is too dry, packed too hard, or the seeds are buried too deep, they will struggle to sprout or fail to come up.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa nu kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni eyi tsɔ loo afu dumɔwui lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baaná naagba akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ loo amɛkwɛɛɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams spoil quickly if I leave them lying under the sun on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ hulu shishi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that lose water and generate heat after being dug up. Direct sunlight burns their outer skin and speeds up decay, so harvested yams should always be kept in a cool, well-ventilated shade.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni nu fiteɔ ni ehaa dɔlɛ baa kɛji atsa amɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã hewolo lɛ kponɔgbɛ ni eha egbo oya. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ sweet potatoes ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient crops need to stay green and build food. When soil nitrogen is low, the plant moves food from older bottom leaves to nourish new growth, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛfee niyenii lɛ yɔɔ mli. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛha shweremɔ hee lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: How does fertilizer actually help my crops grow bigger and produce better yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: Fertilizer works like vitamins for the soil. Continuous farming depletes natural soil nutrients; fertilizer replaces vital elements like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium so crop roots grow strong and produce larger fruits or grains.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ vitamini kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasium najiaŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ daa waa ni amɛwoɔ aduawai loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and short roots that lose moisture quickly in direct sun. Temporary shade crops like plantains protect them by blocking harsh sunlight and maintaining soil moisture while the cocoa gets established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛtsɔ hulu la ni naa wa ni amɛtsiɔ naa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbuɔ he yɛ be mli ni kookoo jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni miŋmɔ lɛ mli nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water on undrained land, the roots suffocate and soil fungi quickly attack them, causing tubers to decay.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ hei ni nu hoɔ yɛ lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni sũ mli ŋmeii tutuaa amɛ oya. ha yitso lɛ agbo

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches when I allow many shoots to grow around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miifee bibii lɛ? Akɛni miha ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ hewɔ lɛ. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ

english: All young shoots growing around the main plantain trunk share the same underground root system. Leaving too many shoots forces them to compete for water and food, leaving less energy for the main stem to develop large bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso wulu lɛ he lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi kome. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii he. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ bɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaawo niji wuji.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and tall with small cobs when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ hewɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crops compete fiercely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The plants stretch upward to search for light instead of developing thick stalks and big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Tso lɛ shwieɔ ehe nɔ koni etao la lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɛ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ tso agbohi nɛ a he wa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the crop is stressed by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or lack of key nutrients like calcium. The plant sheds flowers to save energy for basic survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium ni bɛ. Tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ toɔ hewalɛ kɛha shishijee wala.

english: Why are small ragged holes appearing inside the whorl leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Holes inside the inner leaves of young corn are usually caused by pests like the fall armyworm caterpillar, which crawls into the center funnel of the plant to feed on fresh leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei.

english: Why do weeds slow down crop growth even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa tsei lɛ daraaa fioo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa po lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with aggressive roots. Even during good rains, weeds consume the applied fertilizer and topsoil nutrients faster than your crops, starving the crops of food.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ basabasa. Yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po mli lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ hu yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. ni haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ

english: Why do crops grow very well on one side of my field but remain small on another side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ? Shi eji bibioo lolo yɛ fa kroko lɛ nɔ?

english: Soil quality varies across the same land due to differences in topsoil depth, water drainage, shade, or past land clearing practices. Areas with richer soil organic matter naturally grow stronger plants.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su srɔtoi yɛ he kome mli. Nɔ ni ha ebalɛ nakai ji srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mlibotemɔ, nu ni hoɔ, hulutsoo, loo bɔ ni afeɔ atsuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ahe nii yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Hei ni sũ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Is it good for me to leave a big Onyina tree standing in the middle of my farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashi Onina tso agbo ko yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ teŋ?

english: It depends on what you are growing. While an Onyina tree provides shade and leaf litter that enriches soil, its huge trunk and wide root system can take up too much space and block sunlight from crops like maize or young cocoa.
ga: Edamɔ nɔ ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ, eyɛ mli akɛ Onyina tsei lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ baai ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ. Shi tso lɛ shishifã agbo lɛ kɛ eshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ he babaoo tsɔ ni etsĩ hulu la ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo kookoo bibii amli lɛ naa.

english: Why should I keep certain wild trees on my farm instead of cutting them all down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ koo mli tsei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mafo tsei lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Certain trees serve as natural protectors for your farm. They prevent soil erosion, keep the land cool, provide shade for sensitive crops, and can be harvested later for timber, medicine, or firewood.
ga: Tsei komɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli bulɔi kɛha oŋmɔ lɛ. Amɛtsiɔ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anáa hulutsoo. ni abaanyɛ akpa koni akɛtsu nii sɛɛ mli akɛ tso, tsofa loo la tso.

english: Do all trees on my land help my crops grow, or do some harm them?
ga: Ani tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa loo amɛteŋ ekomɛi yeɔ mɔ awui?

english: Not all trees are helpful to crops. Some trees have aggressive shallow roots and dense leaves that rob nearby crops of water and light, while others fix nitrogen into the soil and provide good overhead shade.
ga: Jeee tsei fɛɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Tsei komɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu kɛ la ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ. yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi saa nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛhaa ŋwɛi ŋmɔlɔ kpakpa.

english: Can I put kitchen salt on my farm soil to make my crops grow better?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmei ni akɛhooɔ nii afata shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: No, common kitchen salt can ruin your farm soil by pulling moisture away from roots and burning your plants. To make your soil productive, use compost, animal manure, or recommended fertilizers instead.
ga: Dabi, ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ okpɔlɔ nɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ afite shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni ekɛshãa otsei lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ awo yibii Moŋ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ atsu nii.

english: Is tree ash good for my farm soil, and how does it help my crops?
ga: Ani tso mli sũ lɛ hi kɛha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Ni te eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Tree ash acts like a natural soil sweetener and fertilizer. Spreading small amounts of cool wood ash adds potassium to the soil, which helps crops resist diseases and produce stronger fruits.
ga: Tso mli sũ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ ŋɔɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ okɛ tso mli sũ ni mli ejɔ fioo ko shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha potassium afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Enɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni amɛwo yibii ni mli wa.

english: How can I use the trees and crop waste on my farm to make local soap?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ tsei kɛ jwɛi tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii koni mikɛfee maŋ lɛ mli samla?

english: You can burn waste from trees and crops, such as plantain peels or cocoa pods, into ash. Mixing this wood ash with water and vegetable oils like palm oil produces traditional black soap.
ga: Obaanyɛ oshã jwɛi ni jɛ tsei kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli, tamɔ plantain ŋmɔji loo kookoo ŋmɔji amli. Abaanyɛ atsɔ sũ Kɛ́ akɛ tso sũ futu nu kɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma mli fɔ, tamɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma mli fɔ lɛ, ehaa anáa kusum mli jatropha.

english: Can the trees growing naturally on my farm give me extra income besides my main crop?
ga: Ani tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha maná shika kroko yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, keeping useful trees allows you to harvest extra materials like medicinal bark, fruits, firewood, or wood ash for soap-making, which you can sell in the local market.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nibii krɛdɛɛi tamɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma, aduawai, tso loo tso sũ ni akɛfeɔ samla. ni obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ

english: Why do older farmers consider trees like the Nyame Dua to be beneficial on a farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni edara lɛ buɔ tsei tamɔ Nyame Dua akɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha amɛŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Trees like Nyame Dua are valued because they have deep roots that pull up valuable nutrients to the topsoil, while their leaves and bark offer natural remedies and shade for delicate crops.
ga: Tsei tamɔ Nyame Dua lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ ejaakɛ amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni gbalaa niyenii ni jara wa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni baai kɛ eshishifãi yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ he ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo.

english: How do large trees shield my crops during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Te tsei wuji buɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Large trees act as windbreaks to block dry Harmattan winds from snapping your crops. Their high leaves also shield crops from the scorching heat while trapping humidity near the ground.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ naa koni ekafite oŋmɔshi nibii. Baai ni kwɔlɔ lɛ hu buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: How do I know if a tree overhead is giving too much shade to my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ hulutsoo babaoo tsɔ?

english: If your crops are growing tall and thin, turning pale green or yellow, or failing to produce good fruit, the tree above them is blocking too much sunlight and needs its lower branches pruned.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dara ni amɛfee mlɛo Amɛji ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. loo ekɛ yibii kpakpai baaa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ miitsi hulu la babaoo naa. Ni ehe miihia ni afo niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the key food crops need to grow green and leafy. Giving the soil nitrogen fertilizer or manure helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii tso titri ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ baai. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen loo ŋmeii wo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off the extra shoots growing around my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: If too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same food and water in the soil, resulting in small bunches. Keeping only one or two strong shoots allows the main stem to produce bigger, heavier fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miikwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ, Plantain kome Plantain muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii bibii baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ awo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam plants use their leaves like solar panels to make food that grows the big tuber underground. Staking the vines lifts the leaves off the ground so they get full sunlight and stay safe from heat rot on the soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo be mli nibii ni akɛfeɔ niyenii ni haa bulb agboi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni enyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo. ni ehi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ fitemɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the sap. Treating the plants with organic or recommended pest spray removes the insects and lets new leaves grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tsu tso lɛ he nii lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi bibii lɛ ni ebaaha baai heei akwɛ̃ bɔ ni sa.

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop flowers if they lack enough water or if there are no tiny insects like midges around to pollinate them. Ensuring good shade to hold moisture and avoiding harsh sprays that kill beneficial insects helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji nu loo kooloi bibii tamɔ midges ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo amɛmli. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo kpakpa ha koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli, ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my ripening tomatoes splitting open while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ miijara be mli ni miyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they get a sudden rush of water after a long dry period. The inside of the fruit expands faster than the skin can stretch, so keeping watering consistent prevents the fruit skin from cracking.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo nu mli trukaa beni egbi be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaha aduawai lɛ ahe tsɔi lɛ akagbala.

english: Which direction should the small buds face when I push a cassava stem cutting into the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ ootsi ŋmei tso ni afo lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ oyitso lɛ atsɔ?

english: The small buds on the cassava stem must point upwards toward the sky. Planting them pointing down forces the new stems to grow upside down before reaching light, which weakens the plant and reduces root yield.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔ ni akɛtsɔɔ shi lɛ baaha tsei heei akwɛ̃ dani amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni shishifãi ni baa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die if I plant them in an open field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily dry out and burn in direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain or shade trees nearby protects the young cocoa until it is old enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantain loo shia tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Legume plants like cowpeas have a special natural ability to trap nitrogen food from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that stored food stays in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛmɔɔ nitrogen nibii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: How can I tell if the soil has enough moisture to safely sow my maize seeds after a dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa shweshweeshwe yɛ hɔmɔ sɛɛ?

english: Scoop up a handful of soil from a few inches deep and squeeze it in your hand. If it forms a ball that stays together without dripping water, the soil has enough moisture for seeds to sprout safely.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ sũ ni mli kwɔ fioo ko kɛjɛ mli ni okɛmimɔ oniji amli. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni nu shwieee shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sũ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves regain their deep green color and grow strong.
ga: Abɛi baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but produce small stems underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ tso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much shade or too much nitrogen from the soil, it puts all its energy into growing tall leaves instead of building large tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ naa hulutsoo babaoo loo nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kakadaji moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How can I tell if my farm land is healthy enough to support my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Healthy farm soil is usually dark in color, holds water well without staying flooded, feels crumbly when squeezed in your hand, and contains living earthworms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kpakpai amli lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ekɛ nu toɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nu shwieee nɔ. E nuɔ he kaa e ngɛ hɛ mi nyami ke o ngɔ o nine ɔ. ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka yɛ jɛmɛ

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt during the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In intense afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil. Adding dry leaves or straw as mulch around the stem keeps the ground cool and moist.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ Tso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather, especially if trees are too bushy and shade prevents air from drying the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji tso lɛ mli tse tsɔ ni hulutsoo tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa koni ekaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juice, which transfers viruses into the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni baaha hela lɛ aya tso lɛ mli

english: Yam leaves need to reach up into direct sunlight to generate food for the roots. Lifting the vines off the damp soil also prevents ground rots and leaf diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shishifãi lɛ. Wein tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ fitemɔ kɛ tsei ahe helai anaa.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress caused by sudden heat, dry soil, or a lack of calcium in the ground.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo trukaa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli baa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do bean plants make the ground better for other crops planted later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha tsei krokomɛi ni adu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and peanuts have special root nodules that pull natural nitrogen gas out of the air and store it in the soil, leaving rich natural fertilizer behind for future crops.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ ahaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to weed around my young crops early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ mra?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal their water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, effectively starving your crop before it can establish itself.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ dani amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why should I spend money buying certified seeds from an official dealer instead of just saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika yɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ maŋ onukpa ko ni jaa lɛ dɛŋ lɛ he? Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ dumɔwuhi nɛ je ngma kpami nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ kɛ to.

english: Certified seeds are specifically tested and bred to resist local diseases, tolerate dry spells, and yield more produce. Saved seeds lose their strength over generations, leading to smaller harvests and higher risk of crop failure.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni akwɛ amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni ewoɔ babaoo Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi, ni oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafite lɛ hu yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do some varieties of maize grow much faster and produce bigger cobs than the local seeds I normally use?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi daa oya kwraa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa wuji fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni mikɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ?

english: Improved maize varieties are bred to use soil nutrients and sunlight more efficiently. They mature quicker to beat unpredictable rains and are designed to concentrate their energy into forming large cobs.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmãa henɔi ni atsake amɛ koni amɛkɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Amɛdaraa oya koni amɛye nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ nɔ kunim. ni afee lɛ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ afee ekome ni ekɛfee ŋmei agbo ko.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep wilting and dying when I plant them in an open field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh direct sunlight because their roots are not deep enough to draw sufficient water. Planting plantains or shade trees alongside cocoa creates a cooler environment that protects the young seedlings until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni buɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why is it better to plant my crops in straight rows with proper spacing rather than scattering the seeds across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Proper spacing prevents plants from competing with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Planting in rows also makes it much easier for you to weed, apply fertilizer, and harvest.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tsei akaye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ odu nii yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni obaakpa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the tips downward during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishi kɛyaa shishi yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the key nutrient crops need to stay green and grow strong. Applying the right fertilizer early in the season fixes this deficiency.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa nɛkɛ naagba nɛɛ.

english: Why do experts advise me to plant beans or cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nilelɔi kɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ duɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans take nitrogen from the air and naturally store it in the soil through their roots. This feeds the neighboring maize crop, enriches your soil for future seasons, and gives you an extra crop to harvest.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aye niyenii. Ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ bei. ni eha nyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛi ni nyɛkpaa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up, shrink, and get yellow patches during warm weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties stops the virus from taking over your field.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ baa ŋmei baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baatsi helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa koni ekaye he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do small worms suddenly appear and eat up the middle leaves of my young maize plants after early rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii jeɔ kpo trukaa ni amɛyeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which hatch quickly after rains and feed on young crop leaves. Inspecting your fields early and applying recommended control methods when plants are small keeps them from destroying your yield.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni fɔɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli mra ni okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔɔ lɛ atsu nii kɛ́ tsei lɛ darako. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ akafite onibii.

english: Why does my soil dry out and crack so quickly just a few days after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni egbɛɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water rapidly due to sun heat and wind. Covering the soil around your crops with dried grass or leaves traps moisture in the ground, keeps the soil cool, and reduces how often you need to rely on rainfall.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Mulching around Nibii ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi eduɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shii abɔ ni esa akɛ okɛ ohe afɔ̃ nugbɔshiimɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting in the storage barn even when they looked healthy when I dug them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ sweet potato lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ beni mifo mli lɛ moŋ.

english: Yams rot quickly if they are kept in hot, damp, or poorly ventilated spaces, or if they suffered tiny cuts during harvest. Storing them off the ground on raised racks in a shaded, airy barn stops moisture build-up and keeps them fresh.
ga: Atomo fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni edɔ, edɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ. Aloo kɛji amɛyɛ fãi bibii ni afo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli Okɛ amɛ ato shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ shɛlɛf ni awo nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni buaa ehe naa lɛ kpaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi.

english: Why are small insects eating the leaves of my maize plants, and will it destroy my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye mi ŋmãa baai lɛ? Ni ani ebaafite miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Insects like armyworms chew on tender leaves to feed themselves. If caught early, using recommended natural or chemical sprays protects the growing shoots so the plant can still recover and produce healthy corn ears.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yeɔ baai bibii koni amɛye amɛhe niyenii. Kɛji akɛ amɔ lɛ mra lɛ Adebɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmãa toi ni mli wa.

english: If I see worm damage on a few crop plants, should I cut the whole plant down or just leave it?
ga: Kɛ mina ŋmeii ni miifite ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi Ani esa akɛ mafo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ loo mashi lɛ?

english: You do not need to cut down the entire plant immediately. Removing only the heavily damaged leaves and applying targeted pest treatments allows the rest of the plant to keep growing safely.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni ofo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni efite waa lɛ pɛ ni akɛ tsofa ko ni akɛtaoɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ daa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow and curling up instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow, curled leaves are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant stem cuttings prevents this sickness from taking over your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Niji ni nyɛɔ helai ahe lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni hela nɛɛ akaye he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it safe to sell cocoa pods or crops that show brown rotten spots on the tree?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaahɔ̃ɔ kookoo ŋmeii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋmeii ni egbo yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: No, crops with rot or black spots carry fungal diseases that ruin bean quality and easily spread to healthy trees. Sick pods should be harvested separately and destroyed rather than sold or mixed with good produce.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni egboi loo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ hiɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe nibii, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli oya. Esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ srɔtoi ni akpata amɛhiɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaahɔ̃ɔ loo akɛ nibii kpakpai afutu mli

english: How often should I use my cutlass to clear weeds around my crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ dagger ajie jwɛi ni bɔle ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ?

english: Clear weeds when they are young and small, especially during the first few weeks after planting. Weeds compete with your crops for water and soil nutrients, so keeping the area around plant stems clean helps them grow faster.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛji amɛji bibii ni amɛji bibii. Titri lɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 2-3 ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ahe tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why is it helpful to leave cleared weeds on top of the soil around my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ashi jwɛi ni ajie lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ? No hewɔ lɛ mitsei lɛ ahe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Leaving dead weed vegetation on top of the soil creates a protective blanket called mulch. This keeps the ground moist during dry days, cools the roots, and slowly turns into natural fertilizer as it breaks down.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni fiofio lɛ etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii beni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crop plants are getting too much water during the rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: When plants receive too much standing water around their roots, their leaves will start turning yellow and stems will become soft or mushy because the roots cannot breathe underwater.
ga: Kɛ́ tso ko ná nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaai lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ baafee bɔdɔɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu yɛ nu shishi.

english: Why do my young vegetable crops wilt in the middle of the afternoon even when the soil is slightly damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo moŋ lɛ?

english: Strong afternoon sunshine causes young plants to lose moisture through leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the soil. Providing light temporary shade or watering early in the morning prevents this stress.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo loo nu ha lɛ be kukuoo ko lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ekɛtsi nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why is it a good choice to leave a portion of my farmland without planting anything on it for a season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji halamɔ kpakpa akɛ mashi miŋmɔshi shikpɔji lɛ ekomɛi ni miduuu tsei komɛi lɛ? kɛha be kome

english: Leaving land to rest, known as fallowing, allows the soil to naturally rebuild its organic nutrients and moisture so future crops grow much stronger and give higher yields.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ defoliation lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Bɔni afee ni wɔsɛɛ tsei lɛ adara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Can I plant cassava and pepper together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ he kome?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava with lower-growing crops like pepper works well because pepper matures quickly before the cassava tall canopy grows large enough to block light and space.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni shwereɔ fioo, tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni akɛaawo mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ daa oya dani ŋmei ŋmei kakadaŋŋ lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni baatsi la kɛ he ko naa.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow at the bottom when the plant is still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer like urea gives the plant the nutrient boost it needs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ yɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ babaoo.

english: Why do my cowpea plants make the soil better for the maize I plant in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and other beans pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small bumps on their roots. When the cowpea plant dies after harvest, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil, serving as natural food for your next maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli beni cowpea tsei lɛ gboi yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Okɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha o-cornmeal ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: The best planting material comes from the middle part of a mature, healthy cassava stem that is about as thick as your thumb. Avoid the soft green top section and the hard bottom section because the middle sprouts fastest and produces stronger roots.
ga: Nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ jɛɔ ŋmei tso ko ni mli wa ni eda ni elɛɛmɔ tamɔ ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ. kɛ oshishifa lɛ Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ shishigbɛ ni wa lɛ he ejaakɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ daa oya fe fɛɛ ni ehaa shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Excess water sitting in the soil drowns the roots by cutting off oxygen, which allows fungal decay to set in. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps heavy rainfall drain away quickly so the roots can breathe.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni buaa ehe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ abote mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ oya bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Why should I cut off the extra shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main plantain tree. Removing most of them and leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to grow big and produce heavy bunches.
ga: Tsoi ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni edara ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food. The more sunlight the leaves receive, the larger the yam tubers grow under the ground.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. Babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, Babaoo ni sweet potato ŋmeii baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What is creating small ragged holes inside the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: Ragged holes in the center whorl of young maize are caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Spraying an organic neem seed solution or a recommended pesticide early in the morning directly into the center funnel kills the worms before they ruin the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii abifao lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem dumɔwui ahe tsofa loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ shwie ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋta lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling tightly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during hot weather to reduce water loss through their surfaces, but it can also be caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading leaf curl virus. Mulching the soil and controlling sap-sucking insects helps keep the leaves healthy.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Shi kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ leaf curl hela lɛ hu baanyɛ ekɛba. Kplukai ni nuɔ nu lɛ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akudɔɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ haa baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering soil with dry plant matter, known as mulching, shields the ground from hot direct sunlight. This keeps moisture in the soil longer, keeps roots cool, and prevents weeds from springing up around your peppers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akakwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: When is the best time during the day for me to put fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli?

english: Apply fertilizer early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the weather is cool and the ground is slightly damp. Applying fertilizer under hot midday sun can burn the tender roots and leaves of your plants.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo shwane mli. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure will help them regain their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, intense sunlight because their delicate leaves scorch and dry out. They need shade crops like plantains or temporary shade trees planted nearby to protect them during their first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni ebu amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know the best time to plant cassava so the stem cuttings do not dry up in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei? Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbi yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should be planted right at the start of the rainy season when the soil is consistently moist. This moisture encourages the stem to sprout roots quickly before the hot sun can dry it out.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Fɛ̃i nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Extreme heat, inconsistent watering, or using too much nitrogen fertilizer can stress tomato plants, causing their flowers to fall off. Keeping the soil evenly moist and using balanced fertilizer helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli Loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ baanyɛ agbee shi. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ baajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɔɔ ŋmãa he pɔtɛɛ aba. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: What causes holes in my maize leaves with dark powdery waste left inside the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli kɛ powder ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaves of the plant to feed. Applying targeted biopesticides or neem extract early in the morning when the pest is active helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ateŋ baai amli koni amɛye nii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu lɛ wo mli leebi be mli ni kooloi lɛ miitsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them very close together to fit more on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ miŋmɔ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin, weak plants that produce much smaller fruits or grains overall.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii loo dumɔwui bibii kwraa yɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks for my yam vines to climb as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ niji ni kwɔlɔ afata he koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to make food for the plant. If the leaves stay on the ground, they receive less light and are more likely to rot, leading to smaller tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Kɛji baai lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lolo lɛ Ebaaná la fioo ni ebaanyɛ egbo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso bibioo.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and shrinking in size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee bibioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. Spraying with neem oil or insecticidal soap kills these pests and prevents further damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi nɛɛ ni ebaatsi nibii krokomɛi ni baafite lɛ anaa.

english: Why is it helpful to cover the soil around my vegetables with dry grass during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground, keeps the plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing, allowing your vegetables to stay healthy during dry spells.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni o-vegetables lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize crops turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to build strong, green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes small ragged holes in the leaves of my maize plants, making them look like insects chewed them from the inside?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii miiye amɛ kɛmiijɛ amɛmli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central funnel of the maize plant and feeds on the soft young leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining, suffocating the roots and allowing destructive soil fungi to attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them lie on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ekã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight and air, which helps the plant produce more food to grow bigger underground tubers while keeping leaves safe from ground diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up tightly into balls and stopping the plants from bearing big fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bɔɔlu ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekawo yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck plant sap and spread viruses, which prevents leaves from expanding and flowers from forming fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛ baa lɛ baa. Enɛ haaa baai lɛ alɛɛ ni fɔfɔi lɛ hu awo yibii.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small suckers growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: If too many small suckers grow around one plantain stem, they steal water, nutrients, and sunlight from the main mother plant, resulting in smaller, weaker bunches of plantains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii kwɛ̃ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso titri ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant before turning into actual tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ tomato diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, causing the plant to focus on growing leaves rather than setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa hao tso lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry leaves or grass help them stay alive during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi shwie miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves (mulching) acts like a blanket that shades the earth, keeps the roots cool, and prevents groundwater from evaporating quickly into the hot air.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baai ni egbi (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpeas or beans in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and beans have roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, providing free natural food for the maize growing alongside them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. koni akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko aha ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have wide leaves that create living umbrellas, giving the young cocoa trees the shade and moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Which direction should I point cassava stem cuttings when inserting them into the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ŋmei niji lɛ atsɔɔ?

english: The small buds or nodes on the cassava stem should always point upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down makes it difficult for the roots to develop and sprout leaves properly.
ga: fɔfɔi bibii loo nodes Esa akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifã lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Dumɔ ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ haa ewaa akɛ shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden poles next to my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama emasɛi lɛ? Sweet potato wain tso be mli ni edaa?

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs to lift its leaves toward the sun to produce food. Using stakes to elevate the vines ensures maximum sunlight exposure, which helps the plant grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛná niyenii. Kɛ akɛ tsei tsu nii kɛwo wain tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ he babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my main crop help improve my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo?

english: Cowpeas and other beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown near other crops, they naturally share this nitrogen with the soil, working like a natural fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ adu yɛ tsei krokomɛi ahe lɛ Amɛbaajara nitrogen nɛɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on the soft center of young maize plants. Catching them early and applying recommended natural or chemical controls protects the plant's growing point.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ bibii lɛ. Amɛ ni ooomɔ mra Ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and puckering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, or a virus spread by them. Spraying the plants with soap water or organic pesticides helps control these pests and stops the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni akɛ samla loo tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ ni ekpaa ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of insect pollination. Regular watering and light shade during severe hot spells help the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ falɛ faaa Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa ni ehaa hulutsoo fioo Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell before the main rains settle in. Planting too soon can cause seeds to sprout and then die from a sudden lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ baa. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi yɛ nu ni bɛ trukaa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Weeds grow much faster than young maize and compete directly for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing them early gives your young crop the space and nutrients it needs to establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmãa bibii ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ni oootsi ohe mra Enɛ baaha otsei bibii lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Can I use fertilizer to cure my cocoa trees if they start showing signs of sickness?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsa mi-cacao tsei lɛ kɛji hela bɔi amɛ?

english: No, fertilizer provides nutrients for plant growth but cannot cure viral diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot. Applying fertilizer to a sick tree will not stop the disease from killing it or spreading to your healthy trees.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛdara. Shi enyɛŋ etsa helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli tamɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ. Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni oookɛ amɛ awo mli lɛ haaa hela lɛ agbe loo egbɛ eshwa otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut down my cocoa trees when only a few leaves look sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛfolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ? Ni kookoo baai fioo komɛi hela mɔ amɛ?

english: Certain cocoa diseases spread deep inside the tree and travel to neighboring trees through tiny insects like mealybugs. Cutting down infected trees is the only proven way to stop the disease from destroying your entire farm.
ga: Kookoo helai komɛi gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni amɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs lɛ anɔ amɛyaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni ana he odaseyeli ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekafite oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Is there any chemical spray or medicine I can buy to save a cocoa tree that is already infected with disease?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ cacao tsei anɔ loo tsofai komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ mahe koni mikɛtsa cacao tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ momo lɛ?

english: Currently, there is no chemical spray or medicine that can cure Cocoa Swollen Shoot disease once a tree is infected. Chemical sprays can kill the insects that carry the disease, but infected trees must be cut down to clear the virus.
ga: Amrɔ nɛɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ loo tsofai ni baanyɛ atsa kookoo ni efuu kɛji tso lɛ he hela lɛ bɛ. Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi ni kɛ helai baa lɛ. Shi esa akɛ afo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ koni ajie hela lɛ kɛjɛ mli.

english: How does a cocoa disease move from one farm to another so quickly?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kookoo helai lɛ yaa oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli?

english: Diseases travel mainly through small insects like mealybugs that carry the virus from tree to tree, as well as on infected farm tools, clothing, or plant materials moved between farms.
ga: Helai babaoo tsɔɔ kooloi bibii, tamɔ mealybugs, ni kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nakai eji yɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii, atadei loo tsei ahe nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ateŋ lɛ hu he.

english: If my neighbor has sick cocoa trees on their farm, will my healthy trees catch the sickness too?
ga: Kɛji mikutsoŋnyo lɛ yɛ kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ eŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ani mi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ hu baaná hela?

english: Yes, insects carrying the disease can easily crawl or be carried by wind from your neighbor's farm to yours. It is important for community farmers to work together to identify and cut down sick trees to protect everyone's crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi bibii ni kɛ helai baa lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ mlɛo loo kɔɔyɔɔ aŋɔ amɛ kɛjɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛba onɔ̃ lɛ mli oya. Ehe miihia ni akutsoŋ okwaafoi afee ekome kɛyoo ni amɛfolɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ koni amɛkɛbu mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: What should I do to my land after my diseased cocoa trees are cut down?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mifo kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: After cutting down diseased trees, you should clear the infected roots, let the land rest while planting plantains for shade, and then replant with new, disease-resistant cocoa hybrid seedlings.
ga: Beni ofo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Esa akɛ ojie shishifãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe be mli ni oduɔ dumɔwui koni eha hulutsoo. Kɛkɛ ni adu kookoo dumɔwui heei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ.

english: How can I tell the difference between a cocoa tree that is sick with disease and one that just needs water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ cacao tso ni hela miipiŋ lɛ kɛ cacao tso ni he hiaa nu lɛ teŋ?

english: A thirsty tree usually has dry, drooping leaves all over, while a tree sick with swollen shoot disease will show swollen stems, red leaf veins, or yellow patchy patterns on the leaves before dying.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ baa ni egbi ni shwieɔ shi yɛ he fɛɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ yeɔ he amanehulu lɛ baajie ŋmeii ni efuu, baai lɛ ahe fãji tsuru, loo nɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kpo. Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ yɛ baai anɔ dani gbele

english: Can I spread sickness to my healthy cocoa trees using my cutlass?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsɔ dade nɔ magbɛ hela ashwã cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli?

english: Yes, sap or tiny insects on your cutlass can transfer infections from sick trees to healthy ones. Cleaning your farm tools after working on sick plants helps prevent spreading the disease.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu loo kooloi bibii Yɛ o-knife lɛ nɔ lɛ, hela lɛ baanyɛ ajɛ tso ni hela mɔ lɛ mli kɛya tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli. Kɛ́ otsumɔ oŋmɔ mli nibii amli beni okɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ etsu nii sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: If I apply extra fertilizer to my healthy cocoa farm, will it make my trees immune to getting sick?
