ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ etsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods shrivel and turn black due to a natural process called cherelle wilt when the tree has too many pods to support, or due to black pod fungal disease during wet seasons.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherel wilting lɛ hewɔ beni tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni baanyɛ aye abua lɛ lɛ. aloo yɛ fungal hela ni yɔɔ pods diji amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ hewɔ

english: Why do my yam vines start drying up early before the harvest season even arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miije shishi amɛgbi dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry up prematurely when underground pests like root nematodes or beetles attack the tuber, blocking water and nutrients from reaching the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baagbi oya kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo lady beetles tutua ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: I noticed fresh holes in my cabbage leaves overnight, what is happening to my crop?
ga: Miyɔse buji heei ni yɔɔ kaabe baai anɔ nyɔɔŋ kome. Mɛni ba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Holes appearing overnight mean night-feeding pests like armyworms or diamondback moth caterpillars are eating your plants while it is dark. Checking under leaves at dawn helps catch them.
ga: Buu ni jeɔ kpo nyɔɔŋ kome mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ gbɛkɛ mli kooloi tamɔ cutworms loo diamondback ŋmeii miiye otsei lɛ yɛ be mli ni duŋ ewo lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi yɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni amɔmɔ baai lɛ.

english: What causes a white powdery film to spread across the leaves of my garden egg plants?
ga: Mɛni haa sini yɛŋ ni tamɔ powda gbɛɔ eshwaa eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: That white powder is a fungal infection called powdery mildew, which spreads quickly when humidity is high and crops are planted too closely together without good airflow.
ga: Nakai powda yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo. kɛ tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli.

english: Will planting cowpeas alongside my maize affect how my maize grows?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ baaná mi ŋmãa lɛ dalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Planting cowpeas with maize actually helps the maize grow better because leguminous plants like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, acting as a natural food source for maize.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa wo tsina ŋmãa mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha ŋmãa.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow even after I apply fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Namɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo ŋmɔ mli?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen. This happens if heavy rain washes the fertilizer away before the plants can use it, or if fertilizer is applied when the soil is too dry for roots to absorb it.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ baa mli kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani tsei lɛ kɛtsu nii. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: How do I know which chemical spray will actually protect my crops from pest destruction?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni baabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe?

english: Different chemicals target specific pests. Identifying the exact insect damaging your crop allows you to buy the correct approved insecticide and apply it safely according to instructions for full protection.
ga: Tsofai srɔtoi kɛ amɛhiɛ fɔɔ kooloi pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ. Kɛ́ oyɔse kooloi bibii ni miifite onibii lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ oheɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni akɛtsu nii shweshweeshwe taakɛ atsɔɔ lɛ koni abu he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with broad leaves but producing tiny tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ waa ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cassava puts its growth energy into leaves instead of tubers when the soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are placed too close together, blocking sunlight from reaching lower branches.
ga: Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ ni haa edalɛ woɔ baai lɛ amli yɛ ŋmeii lɛ najiaŋ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsĩ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when weather becomes extremely hot, when water supply is irregular, or when the soil lacks key nutrients like calcium during the flowering stage.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ calcium yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: Why do some of my young cocoa pods shrivel and turn black before reaching full size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ ekomɛi gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛshɛɔ shweremɔ he lɛ?

english: This can happen due to cherelle wilt, where the tree discards extra pods it cannot nourish, or from fungal infections like black pod disease during cool, wet weather.
ga: Enɛ baanyɛ aba mli yɛ cherelle lɛ ni egbo lɛ hewɔ. Tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aye niyenii lɛ eshwieɔ. aloo kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper seeds take so long to sprout after I sow them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds need warmth and constant soil moisture to germinate. Planting seeds too deep in the soil or letting the nursery bed dry out delays sprouting.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui taoɔ dɔlɛ kɛ sũ mli nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ loo ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ agbi lɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why are my crop yields smaller this year even though I spent more money and effort on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ faaa afi nɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mifite shika kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Yields can drop despite hard work if soil fertility has declined over time, if seeds are of low quality, or if unpredictable rainfall patterns disrupt critical plant growth stages.
ga: Nibii ni anáa lɛ baanyɛ aba shi yɛ nitsumɔ ni wa fɛɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ehiii loo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ gbala tsei lɛ adalɛ mli nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli.

english: How does planting shade trees help my young cocoa seedlings survive the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in full sun. Shade trees block intense heat, reduce water loss from the soil, and create a cooler mini-climate so the young cocoa can survive.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa shɛ amɛnɔ. Tsei tsiɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ naa. Nu ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi ni ehaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ni mli ejɔ ni kookoo bibii baanyɛ ahi mli lɛ aba.

english: Why do my cowpea plants suddenly wither and die just as they begin flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ kɛji ebɔi fɔmɔ pɛ?

english: Sudden wilting during flowering is usually caused by soil-borne fungal diseases or root rot that attack and block the plant's water-transport vessels when the crop comes under reproductive stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ sũ mli loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ ni tutuaa ni etsĩɔ tso ko nu gbɛfaa gbɛi lɛ anaa kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ fɔmɔ he haomɔ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni baa trukaa yɛ fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ be mli lɛ baa.

english: Yam rot underground is caused by water pooling in fields with poor drainage, which lets fungal spores and nematodes invade injured or waterlogged roots.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji nematodes lɛ boteɔ shishifãi ni epila loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli.

english: Leaf yellowing that starts at the lower leaves usually means your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves grow green and strong again.
ga: Yellowing okadii ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing and get tiny, curled leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni eyɛ baai bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curled, stunted leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or mites. Applying appropriate neem oil or recommended organic treatments clears the insects so healthy leaves can emerge.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni egbɔjɔ yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ ni sa loo tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ he nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi bibii lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water around the roots, oxygen is cut off, allowing soil fungi to multiply and decay the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ tsɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ babaoo ni amɛgbalaa ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that stay near the surface rather than digging deep. Propping up trees carrying heavy fruit bunches with strong bamboo stakes helps keep them standing during storms.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafo kɛya shɔŋŋ. Tsei ni woɔ yibii ni tsii lɛ adumɔ Bamboo tsei ni he wa yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔɔ shi yɛ ahum be mli.

english: Why do tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruit during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: High temperatures dry out tomato pollen, preventing the flowers from getting fertilized. When pollination fails, the plant naturally drops the flower to save energy.
ga: He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa tomato pollen lɛ gĩɔ. Etsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo fɔmɔ Beni pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my yam vines twist and turn brown during the dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam leaves curl and brown to conserve internal moisture when soil water is low. It is the plant's natural survival mechanism to stop water from evaporating too fast.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ asarasu koni amɛha emli fɛ̃i ahi shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa. Eji tso ko adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nu naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my young crops regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ ji daa.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Keeping the field clear ensures your crops get all available nourishment and reduces insect breeding grounds.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ oha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ, ni ehaa he ni kooloi fɔɔ yɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field where I planted maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, restoring fertility that heavy feeder crops like maize drain out.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni aku sɛɛ aha fɔmɔ ni tsei ni yeɔ kooloi wuji, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ baatsɔ mli lɛ aba.

english: Blackened pods are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that thrives in excessive shade and damp conditions. Pruning overhead branches to let in sunlight and airflow prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pods hela ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nine kɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do crop seeds sprout faster if I soak them in water before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo nu mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Soaking seeds softens their hard outer shell and signals to the plant embryo inside that it is time to wake up, shortening the days needed for germination.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ haa kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa lɛ feɔ blɛoo. ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ mli fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ ete shi. Enɛ baaha be ni akɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ afee kuku.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning light green and yellow starting from the bottom, even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ?

english: Your maize plants are hungry for a nutrient called nitrogen. When the soil lacks nitrogen, the plant pulls food from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top, which causes the lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen. Beni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: If I plant groundnuts between my rows of maize, won't the groundnuts steal all the food from the soil?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ ateŋ Ani ŋmeii ejuŋ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts actually add food to the soil rather than taking it away. They take nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the dirt, which feeds the soil and helps your maize grow better.
ga: Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ niyenii fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he moŋ fe ni eeejie. Amɛheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ekɛ niyenii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa o-ŋmã lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha efo kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make the energy required to build big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get full sun and protects them from rotting on damp soil.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my corn seeds very close together so I can get more corn from my small piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni maná abele babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ?

english: When corn seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients, while their leaves block sunlight from one another. This produces weak plants with very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why does covering the soil around my pepper plants with dry grass keep the ground moist for longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: The layer of dry grass acts like a blanket over the dirt. It blocks the direct heat of the sun, which prevents water in the soil from evaporating quickly into the air and keeps the plant roots cool.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ la ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa Enɛ haaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Why do my cassava plants drop almost all their leaves during the dry season, and does it mean they are dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ eegbo?

english: Your cassava is not dying; it is protecting itself. Cassava plants intentionally drop their leaves when water is scarce to stop moisture from evaporating, while keeping their food safely stored in the roots until the rains return.
ga: O cassava ɔ gbo we lolo. Emiibu ehe he. Yucca tsei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ni baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ naa koni ekaho. Kɛ agbɛnɛ hu niyenii ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees burn and dry up during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate strong, direct sunlight. Without shade from companion plants like plantains or canopy trees, the hot afternoon sun burns their soft leaves faster than the roots can supply water.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko bɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei bibii amli lɛ, Gbi gbɛkɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa ebaai bibii lɛ oya fe bɔ ni eshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aha nu jɛɛhe.

english: My pepper plants produce many flowers, but why do the flowers keep falling off without turning into peppers?
ga: Mi pepper tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from heat stress or lack of water. The plant discards the flowers to save its remaining energy so that the main plant can survive the harsh weather.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ latsaa loo nu ni bɛ hewɔ. Tso lɛ baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni tso titri lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa amli.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have small ragged holes and green dirt inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Mɔ ni etse ni eyɛ muji eŋɔli yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by a caterpillar called the Fall Armyworm. It crawls inside the dark, moist center whorl of the maize plant to eat the young leaves before they unfold, leaving behind holes and droppings.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ. Ekɛ ehe shwieɔ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ mli koni eye baai bibii lɛ dani amɛjie amɛhe kpo. Kɛtsɔ bu kɛ ŋmeii ni ashiɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaf stems on my plantain trees turning soft and snapping off easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efoɔ oya lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by banana weevil pests or fungal infections attacking the bulb underground. When insects burrow into the base of the plant, they destroy the inner structure, making the stems weak and unable to hold their own weight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, banana ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni tutuaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ kooloi bibii bote tso lɛ mli lɛ, amɛfiteɔ nibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ, ni no haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ehiɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsitsi nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen or getting too much water. When maize doesn't get enough nutrients from the soil, it cannot make food properly, which causes the lower leaves to turn yellow first.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ nitrogen loo enine eshɛ nu babaoo nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa nine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enyɛɛɛ ehoo niyenii jogbaŋŋ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer to my crops so it doesn't spoil them?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛkafite?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is when the soil is moist and the plant is actively growing, usually two to three weeks after planting. Applying fertilizer on dry soil or directly against the stem can burn the roots and kill the plant.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tso lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ, bei pii lɛ otsii 2-3 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni egbe tso lɛ.

english: If maize is planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. This struggle causes them to grow thin, weak, and produce very small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ nɔmɔ nɛɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo, amɛgbɔjɔɔ, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii kwraa loo amɛwooo ŋmeii ko kwraa.

english: Yam vines need stakes so their leaves can climb high to catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight gives the leaves energy to make food, which then flows down into the ground to build big, heavy tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe miihia akutsei koni baai lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Hulu la haa baai lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Kɛkɛ lɛ, efoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni efeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in the soil for too long without draining, which breeds rot-causing germs. Planting your cassava on raised mounds helps extra rainwater drain away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Enɛ haa helai ni baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ helai aba lɛ baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up tightly and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny pests like whiteflies feeding on the plant and spreading diseases, or by excessive heat. The plant curls its leaves to try to protect itself and reduce water loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yeɔ tso lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine mli Tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛha nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping all their flowers without growing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from dry weather stress, lack of soil nutrients, or when tiny insects called midges are not available to pollinate the flowers to turn them into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli egbi lɛ hewɔ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii amli ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers and small fruits when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai bibii kɛji hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers and young fruits to survive extreme heat and drought. Dropping extra load allows the plant to save its water and energy just to keep the main stem and roots alive.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi kɛ amɛ aduawai bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ mli. Jatsu kroko ni fata he lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛkɛ.

english: Why do weeds always grow much faster than the crops I planted after the rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are better adapted to steal water and food from the soil than farmed crops. They sprout rapidly after rain to crowd out your crops, which is why clearing them early is essential.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu kɛ niyenii ni amɛjuɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ koni amɛkɛwo onibii amli. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie amɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my crops with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass or leaves—called mulching—acts like a blanket. It stops the hot sun from drying out the water in the soil, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ (Atsɛɔ enɛ mulching.) Etsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava underground is fully ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava lets you know it is mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, the main stem turns dark brown, and small cracks appear in the soil right around the base of the plant where tubers are expanding.
ga: Yucca haa oleɔ akɛ eshɛ kwraa kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ tsɔɔ blɔfo. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ Ejeɔ kpo yɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ tso lɛ shishi he ni ŋmeii lɛ egbɛ eshwã lɛ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to stake my yam vines with wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso tswaa sweet potato wain tso lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce the energy required to grow large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing rot and maximizing sun exposure.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa ni ehaa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear signal that your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the key food maize needs to build healthy green leaves. Applying manure or nitrogen fertilizer early restores their green color and growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii mra Ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help make my farmland better for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha miŋmɔ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen directly from the air and fix it into the ground. When the crop dies, that extra nitrogen stays in the earth to naturally feed whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ helai krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees dropping off before any pods start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they face environmental stress, such as severe heat, lack of moisture, or attacks from sap-sucking insects like mirids. Maintaining moderate shade and keeping moisture in the soil helps trees hold their flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ kpe. loo tutuamɔi ni jɛɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ pollen lɛ adɛŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be ni sa ha tso lɛ, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant plantains right next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and get scorched under direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly with broad leaves that create a living canopy, offering essential shade and keeping the soil moist during the cocoa plant's vulnerable early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni hulu lɛ baanyɛ ashã amɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishijee afii ni egbɔjɔ lɛ amli.

english: Wrinkled or curled pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant juices, or by a virus carried by those same insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe tee baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni egbɔjɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi bibii lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and dry up even when there is water in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgbiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: This sudden wilting is usually caused by soil bacteria that enter the roots and block the tubes that carry water inside the plant. Even if the ground is wet, the water cannot reach the leaves, causing the plant to dry out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛtsiɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ baa. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efɔ moŋ, shi Nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe. gĩ tso lɛ

english: Why do extension officers tell us to wait for two or three good rains before planting maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nitsumɔ nɔ lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔmɛ nugbɔ kpakpa lɛ? Tsei enyɔ loo etɛ dani adu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: The very first rain can be a trick. If you plant immediately and a dry spell follows, the soil gets extremely hot and dries out, scorching the new seed sprouts before the main rainy season settles in.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ baanyɛ atsu nii. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni hɔmɔ ba lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baadɔ waa ni ebaagbi. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui heei akwɛ̃ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba.

english: Covering the earth with dry plant material acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation from the sun, prevents weeds from growing, and adds nutrients to the soil as it rots.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ tsei ni egbi woɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ afee mlɛo. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he beni egboɔ lɛ.

english: How many years do I need to wait after planting cocoa before I get my first harvest?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko du kookoo sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ emɛ dani akpa klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need time to establish strong root systems and sturdy branches. Traditional cocoa varieties take about 3 to 5 years to bear fruit, while modern hybrid seedlings can start producing pods in about 2 to 3 years with proper weeding and fertilizer application.
ga: Cocoa tsei he miihia be dani amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ amɛniji ni mli wa. Kusum kookoo heɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani ewoɔ yibii, yɛ be mli ni ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he lɛ baanyɛ aje ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ ajie jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches and side shoots from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji kɛ esɛɛ tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mi-koko tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-productive shoots (chupons) that steal food from the main tree. Cutting these off channels nutrients directly into pod development while opening up the branches to allow sunlight and fresh air to pass through, reducing fungal diseases.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei ni wooo yibii (chupons) ni juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli lɛ. Niyenii nibii nɛɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa pod lɛ yaa hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ. kɛfata tsei lɛ aniji ni agbeleɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi.

english: Why am I advised to cut down an entire cocoa tree when only a few leaves look sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo cacao tso muu lɛ fɛɛ be mli ni baai fioo komɛi pɛ tamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Diseases such as Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus spread rapidly through roots and mealybug insects. Cutting down and removing infected trees creates a barrier that stops the virus from spreading and killing the rest of your healthy cocoa farm.
ga: Helai tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii amli. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo ni ojie lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ni egbe o-cocoa ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots that dry out quickly under direct sun. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains keeps the soil cool and moist, protecting the young cocoa until it develops a strong root system.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli waa.

english: Is it better to plant seeds from my own harvest or get approved hybrid seedlings from a nursery?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ dumɔwui kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli loo maná dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid ni akpɛlɛ nɔ kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe ko?

english: Seeds taken directly from older farm trees may carry diseases or give low pod yields. Approved nursery seedlings are specifically bred to grow faster, resist common cocoa pests, and yield many more pods per tree.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni etsɛ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aná hela loo pod yibiiwoo ni baa shi. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ koni amɛdara oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kookoo mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. ni eha tso fɛɛ tso mli ŋmeii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ

english: How does mistletoe growing on my cocoa branches hurt my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mistletoe ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi kokoo niji lɛ anɔ lɛ miiye miŋmɔ lɛ awui?

english: Mistletoe is a parasitic plant that taps directly into the cocoa tree's branches to steal water and food. If you do not cut mistletoe off cleanly, it will weaken the tree, reduce your pod output, and eventually kill the branch.
ga: Mistletoe ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni tswaa kookoo niji tɛ̃ɛ koni eju nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛji ofolɔɔɔ mistletoe lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Ebaaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ ayibɔ aba shi, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aniji lɛ agboi.

english: Why do the small pods on my cocoa tree turn black and shrivel before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Pods often turn black due to fungal infections like Black Pod disease during wet seasons, or from severe dry weather when the tree cannot find enough water. Regular weed clearing, proper spacing, and timely spraying protect young pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii ni baa tamɔ black pod hela lɛ hewɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. aloo kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa beni tsei nyɛɛɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ mli. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ jwɛi amli daa lɛ he jɛkɛmɔ ni sa Ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baabu jwɛi bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Will planting cassava next to my young cocoa trees slow down their growth?
ga: Ani yucca ni miduɔ yɛ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ masɛi lɛ baaha edalɛ aya hiɛ fioo?

english: Yes, cassava is a heavy feeder that aggressive absorbs nutrients and water from the topsoil, competing directly with cocoa. It is better to use plantains or cocoyams, which provide gentle shade without aggressive root competition.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ji niyenii ni tsii ni shwieɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli waa. Ekɛ kookoo yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ plantain loo cocoa, ni haa hulutsoo blɛoo ni shishifãi akaŋshii ni mli wa bɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii.

english: Should I burn all the bush clearings and cut logs on my land before planting new cocoa?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi amli hei ni agbele naa lɛ ni mafo tsei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu kookoo hee?

english: Burning destroys beneficial nutrients and good soil microbes that help cocoa trees feed. Allowing cut plant matter to rot naturally forms rich topsoil, retains moisture during dry spells, and keeps the cocoa healthy.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii kpakpai ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa cacao tso lɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tsei ni afolɔ amɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni jara wa. Kwɛmɔ fɛ̃i yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni eye ebua ni eha kookoo ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without forming pods during the Harmattan dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping flowers is a defense mechanism. When water is scarce during severe dry weather, the tree drops flowers to conserve moisture and energy so it can survive until the rainy season returns.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he. Beni nu faaa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa plants are very tender and burn easily under full sun. Big trees provide natural canopy shade and keep the soil cool and moist, protecting young cocoa plants from drying out and dying during hot months.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni eda lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi ni amɛgboi yɛ nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the soil for too long without draining away, it suffocates the roots and creates wet conditions where soil fungus can easily destroy the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Nu lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ baa Fuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ akpata shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ oya.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is essential plant food. When soil food runs low, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛ niyenii fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do people tell me to plant cowpeas together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko miikɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen out of the air and put it back into the ground. Planting them with maize naturally feeds the soil, helping your maize grow strong without relying entirely on costly fertilizers.
ga: Cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and weak even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your crops. Even with enough rain, your crops will starve because the weeds are taking the best nutrients from the soil.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ Hɔmɔ baaye onibii po ejaakɛ jwɛi jieɔ niyenii ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling is a tomato plant's defense trick to protect itself from losing moisture. By rolling its leaves inward, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun so it holds onto its water.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji ŋaa ni buɔ tomato tsei ahe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ he. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni aaatsɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Tsei haa amɛhe ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni amɛnyɛ amɛhiɛ nu mli.

english: Why do flowers drop off my pepper plants without producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ni amɛwooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat, drought, or bad soil conditions. The plant drops its flowers to save energy so it can survive until weather conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout if I plant them right after a heavy rainstorm when the soil is soaked?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need oxygen in the soil alongside moisture to wake up and grow. Soil that is completely flooded leaves no room for air, causing the seeds to drown and rot underground before sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛfata ŋmɔtɔ he koni amɛte shi ni amɛdara. Nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa, ni eshwɛɛɛ gbɛ ko kwraa kɛha kɔɔyɔɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground where diseases spread easily and exposes them to the light they need to produce large yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la babaoo koni ekɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni mli edɔ yɛ ni helai fɔɔ baa lɛ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni ehaa enine shɛɔ la ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni afeɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Extra suckers act like extra mouths to feed, taking water and nutrients away from the main stem. Removing the surplus suckers ensures all the soil energy goes into producing a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krokomɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ krokomɛi kɛha niyenii. Kɛtsɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my maize when the rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ?

english: You should wait until the rains become steady for about two to three consecutive days so the soil stays moist enough to help seeds germinate without drying out.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be gbii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa ni eye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant them very close together on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low on essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the plant is suffering from water stress or root damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo tso lɛ miina nu he haomɔ loo shishifãi ni efite.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, damp, and overly shaded farm conditions during the rainy season.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why does my soil become hard and dry very fast even after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni egbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Hard soil lacks organic matter such as decayed leaves or manure, which helps hold water like a sponge and keeps the ground soft for plant roots to breathe.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ nu mli tamɔ sponji ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Does the size of my farm determine the exact amount of fertilizer I should buy and apply?
ga: Ani bɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ da ha lɛ ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni esa akɛ mahe ni mikɛwo mli lɛ abɔ?

english: Yes, fertilizer amounts are calculated based on land size and crop spacing so that every plant gets enough nutrients without burning the crop or wasting money.
ga: Hɛɛ, abuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayibɔ he akɔntaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ nɔ bɔni afee ni tso fɛɛ tso aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni eshãaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo efiteee shika.

english: Plantain suckers need continuous soil moisture, rich compost, and weed-free ground to build strong roots before they can support heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Plantain suckers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa. Kompost ni jara wa kɛ he ko ni jwɛi bɛ koni shishifãi ni wa aba dani enyɛ eye ebua aduawai akui ni tsii.

english: Can I grow vegetables directly underneath my mature oil palm trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai yɛ mu tso ko ni eda lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Most vegetables need full direct sunlight to grow, so they will struggle and produce very little under the heavy shade of mature tree crops.
ga: Hulu la he hiaa aduawai babaoo koni amɛdara. No hewɔ lɛ, aduawai bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ tsei ni eda ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ ashishi.

english: How do weeds cause my crops to grow slowly and look weak?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal the water, sunlight, and soil food that your main crops need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ koni amɛdara waa lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested grains get damaged by insects while sitting in my storage room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fiteɔ dumɔwui ni mikpaa lɛ beni mita nitoohe lɛ?

english: Insects attack stored grain if the crops were not dried completely to a low moisture level before storage or if the storage space is not properly cleaned and sealed.
ga: Kplukai tutuaa ŋmaa ni ato lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbiko kwraa kɛyashɛɛɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be baa shi dani akɛtoɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ atsumɔko he ni akɛ nibii lɛ toɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni atsĩii naa.

english: How do I know if the pest medicine I sprayed on my crops is actually working?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsu nii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You can tell a pest medicine is working if you see dead insects around the plant base within 24 to 48 hours, fewer active pests on the leaves, and fresh, healthy green leaves growing without new feeding marks.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ miitsu nii kɛji ona kooloi ni egboi ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 mli. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni tsuɔ nii waa lɛ faaa yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Ni baai eŋɔli heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni niyenii he okadi hee ko bɛ he.

english: Why do my crop leaves look weak or burnt right after I spray them with chemical medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ loo amɛshã amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofai ewo mli lɛ?

english: Crops can suffer leaf burn or chemical shock if you apply chemicals during the hot afternoon sun or if the mixture is too strong. Spraying early in the morning or late in the evening helps plants absorb the treatment safely.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai loo tsofai ni tswaa kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai tsu nii yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛfutu lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsɔne. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa tsofa lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: What is the best time of day for me to apply liquid fertilizer or pesticides to my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time to spray is early morning (6:00 AM to 9:00 AM) or late afternoon (4:00 PM to 6:00 PM). During these cooler times, plant pores are open to absorb treatment, and the heat won't evaporate the medicine or burn the leaves.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ ji leebi maŋkpa (6:00 AM kɛyashi 9:00 AM) loo shwane mli (4:00 PM kɛyashi 6:00 PM) yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ gbeleɔ koni amɛŋɔ tsofa lɛ. Ni latsaa lɛ haŋ tsofa lɛ atsɔ la loo ebaaha baai lɛ ashã.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat, insufficient water, or a lack of soil nutrients like calcium and boron. When the plant gets too stressed by dry weather, it drops its blossoms to save its own life.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium kɛ boron Kɛji tsei miihao tsɔ kɛjɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ Ebaawo fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing very tall with plenty of dark leaves but no peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa shi pepper bɛ mli lɛ?

english: This usually happens when you use too much nitrogen fertilizer. Nitrogen makes plants produce strong stems and leafy growth, but too much of it prevents the plant from flowering and fruiting. You need phosphorus and potassium for good fruit yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii. Nitrogen haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ daa. Shi nitrogen lɛ baatsi tsei anaa koni amɛkawo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii babaoo tsɔ. Fosfɔs kɛ potasium he miihia bo koni oná yibii kpakpai.

english: Young cocoa leaves will look yellowish, thin, and scorched around the edges if they get too much sun. Planting shade crops like plantains near them protects the young cocoa leaves from burning.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ baafee ŋmɔŋ, amɛbaafee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaashã yɛ amɛnaa kɛji hulu la babaoo shɛ amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he.

english: Maize leaves can turn yellow if heavy rains wash nitrogen out of the reach of roots, if the soil stays waterlogged and suffocates roots, or if fertilizer was placed too close to the stalk and burnt the root system.
ga: Abɛi baai baanyɛ afee ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho nitrogen lɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu, Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi tsɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ shã.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and turning light green or yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is typically caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Affected leaves shrink and distort, reducing the plant's ability to build big tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whitefly lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Baai ni ena hela lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛfeɔ bulb agbo lɛ baa shi.

english: What causes black spots to spread across my cabbage leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa kaabe baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Black spots on cabbage during rainy periods are usually caused by fungal or bacterial leaf spot diseases. High humidity and water sitting on the leaves create the perfect condition for these germs to grow and spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo bacteria leaf spot hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ kaabɛji nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ baa. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛgbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines suddenly turn brown and dry up long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi be kakadaŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Early drying of yam vines is often caused by yam anthracnose disease or subterranean pests like nematodes damaging the roots. When roots are damaged, the vine cannot draw up water and dries out prematurely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii anthracnose loo shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya. Kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ fite Wein tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ nu mli ni egbiɔ oya.

english: Why do my crops get sick and rot more often during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hela mɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛfiteɔ shii abɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High air moisture and wet leaves create the ideal environment for fungi and bacteria to grow and spread rapidly across your crops, causing rot and leaf spots.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya yɛ onibii fɛɛ amli. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ baa mli ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do the leaves of my plants turn yellow after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive rain fills up air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots. Without air, roots cannot absorb essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, causing leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does rainwater spread plant diseases from one side of my farm to another?
ga: Te nugbɔ lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ egbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome kɛyaa fã kroko lɛ nɔ?

english: Raindrops hitting the ground splash fungal spores and bacteria from infected soil or plants onto nearby healthy crops, while flowing rainwater carries disease germs across your field.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Beni nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ lɛ, ekɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yaa oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crop seeds rot in the soil before sprouting when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil deprives seeds of the oxygen they need to breathe and germinate, allowing fungi in the cold, wet soil to attack and decay the seeds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ haaa dumɔwui aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛmu ni amɛkwɛ̃. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atutua ni eha dumɔwui lɛ agbo.

english: Why do insects and pests multiply so quickly on my crops when the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ faa oya yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Rain causes crops to produce soft, tender young leaves, which provide abundant food for pests, while the humid weather helps insect eggs hatch more successfully.
ga: Nugbɔ haa tsei woɔ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ bibii. ni haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ niyenii babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛfɔɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops wither and die when water stays standing around their stems for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni nu hiɔ tsei lɛ ahe gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Standing water drowns the root system, preventing roots from taking up oxygen and food. Dead roots can no longer send water up to the rest of the plant, causing it to wilt.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii. Shishifãi ni egboi lɛ nyɛŋ aha tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ nu dɔŋŋ. ha egbi

english: No, heavy rain will wash away the fertilizer before your crops can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after the rain has stopped.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baajie ŋmɔshi nibii dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How does clearing weeds from my farm help protect my crops during wet weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ buɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Weeds trap extra moisture around your crops and hold plant diseases and insects. Clearing them lets air flow freely through your field so leaves dry faster after rain.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ mɔɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. oŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsei ni akɛto he lɛ helai kɛ kooloi bibii He ni ooojie lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ oyale mli oya. Baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow fast during the rains but easily break or fall over?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei daa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli shi amɛkuɔ loo amɛgbeeɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Abundant water makes plants expand rapidly with soft, watery tissues rather than strong woody stems, making them top-heavy and vulnerable to strong winds.
ga: Nu babaoo haa tso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya kɛ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu yɔɔ mli. Yɛ tso shishi ni mli wa najiaŋ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa nyɛɔ amɛtswaa amɛ.

english: What simple step can I take to reduce disease spread among my crops when it rains continuously?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo mafee koni helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ aba shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ tee nɔ nɛ?

english: Spacing your plants further apart gives each crop enough room to dry off quickly in the sun and wind, making it harder for mold and rot to survive.
ga: Tsei ni ajara mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbi oya yɛ hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baahi shi.

english: If someone did galamsey mining on a piece of land, can I plant my cassava there right away?
ga: Kɛji mɔ ko baajie galamsey yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, land that has been used for galamsey usually loses its fertile topsoil and may contain harmful chemicals like mercury. You need to clear the land of toxic mud, add organic manure, and test the soil first, otherwise crops will fail to grow or absorb harmful chemicals.
ga: Dabi, shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ akɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ galamsey lɛ fɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ yɔɔ nɔ ni jara wa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mercury baanyɛ ahi mli. Esa akɛ ojie muji ni yɔɔ gbeyei kɛjɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. kɛ organic fertilizer afata he ni oka shikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ klɛŋklɛŋ Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ adara loo amɛŋɔ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Why are crops struggling to grow on the farm plot I cleared next to an old mining pit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii miitao ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mifo mli yɛ shika tsuru bu momo ko masɛi lɛ?

english: Mining strips away the rich topsoil layer where plants get their natural food. Without that fertile upper soil, crops cannot form strong root systems or gather enough nutrients to grow properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ ni tsei lɛ naa amɛ niyenii yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ mli ni aaafo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná shishifãi ni mli wa loo ebua niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ naa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow after I water them with water from the nearby river?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ amɛnɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If the river water is polluted with heavy mud or chemicals from upstream mining activities, it can block the roots from breathing and taking up nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow and wilt.
ga: Kɛji akɛ muji ni tsii loo tsofai ni jɛɔ ŋshɔ hiɛ shika tsuru tsaa nitsumɔi amli lɛ ewo faa lɛ mli nu lɛ mli lɛ, Enɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ akamu ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and cannot handle direct sunlight. They need temporary shade plants, such as plantains, grown beside them to act as living umbrellas that trap moisture and shade the young trees.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni mɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants stay small and weak when wild weeds are growing close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe waaa nɛkɛ be mli ni koo mli jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crop. When weeds grow too close, your maize cannot get enough food and remains stunted.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Oŋmãa lɛ nyɛŋ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ebaaya nɔ ehi shi ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Yam tubers become misshapen when the soil is too hard or compacted. Yams need soft, deep, well-mounded soil so the tuber can easily push downward and expand evenly.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ yitso lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ shi kɛya shi ni egbɛ eshwa pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long without draining. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds helps excess rainwater drain off so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ efooo Shika ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the heat is too intense or when the plant gets too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji la lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ tsei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: If I add extra fertilizer to my pepper plants, will it make them produce pepper faster?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fata mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ani ebaaha amɛwo yibii oya?

english: No, adding too much fertilizer can burn the roots and damage the plant. Excess fertilizer often causes excessive leaf growth while delaying or ruining your pepper yield.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni efite tso lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo haa baa lɛ daa fe nine. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni afeɔ lɛ hu sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo efiteɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily whenever heavy winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not grow deep into the soil. When the bunch grows heavy, the plant becomes top-heavy, so you need to prop the stem with a strong wooden stick to keep it upright.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ da lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ tso ni wa afi sɛɛ koni ehi shi jaŋŋ.

english: How long does protective spray usually stay active on my cocoa trees after I apply it?
ga: Be enyiɛ tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ fɔɔ hiɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ beni mikɛshwie nɔ sɛɛ?

english: Most protective sprays for cocoa remain effective on the leaves and pods for about 3 months, after which rain, sun, and plant growth wear it away and you need to spray again to protect against pests.
ga: Cocoa hebuu tsofai babaoo tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii anɔ aaafee nyɔji etɛ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ nugbɔ, hulu la kɛ tsei adalɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Ni ehe miihia ni okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ ekoŋŋ koni obu ohe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Will rain wash away the protective chemical if I spray my cocoa pods during the wet season?
ga: Ani nugbɔ baajie tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ kɛji mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii shwie nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: If it rains immediately after spraying, the chemical can wash off. However, once the spray dries completely on the cocoa pods, it bonds well and will continue protecting the crop for up to 3 months even with rain.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni okɛ tsofai lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, tsofai lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ mli. Shi, kɛ́ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kookoo lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ, tsofai lɛ baaho. Ebaahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ebaaya nɔ ebu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛyashi nyɔji 3, kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po.

english: How can I tell that it is time to spray my cocoa trees again for insects?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni esa akɛ okɛ tsofa afɔ o-cocoa tsei lɛ anɔ koni akɛgbe kooloi bibii lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: You can tell it is time to spray when 3 months have passed since your last treatment, or when you notice early signs of fresh insect bite marks on young pods and leaves.
ga: Obaanyɛ ole be ni esa akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ beni nyɔji 3 eho kɛjɛ be mli ni okɛ tsofa lɛ tsu nii naagbee lɛ. Aloo kɛ́ ona mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi emɔ bo yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot during the wet months of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Excess moisture and high humidity encourage black pod disease to spread fast during rainy months, which is why protective spraying and pruning branches to let in sunlight are necessary before wet weather arrives.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo woɔ black pod hela lɛ hewalɛ ni egbɛ eshwa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyɔji lɛ amli. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsofa ni tsiɔ hela naa kɛ tsofa ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni hulu la aba dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba lɛ.

english: Why does the main cocoa harvest season happen around the time school fees are due in September?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo kpamɔ be titri lɛ baa yɛ be mli ni esa akɛ awo skul nyɔmɔ yɛ September mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally complete their main pod production cycle around September to December after the major rains, which nicely aligns with the start of the school year when farm families need income.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ boteɔ amɛ pod feemɔ be titri lɛ mli kɛjɛɔ September kɛyashi December yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ. Enɛ kɛ nikasemɔ afi lɛ shishijee be mli ni okwaafoi awekui lɛ taoɔ shika lɛ kpãa gbee.

english: How many months before harvest should I start preparing my cocoa trees so I get a good yield?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ dani kpamɔ baa lɛ esa akɛ oje kooloo tsei lɛ ahe saamɔ shishi koni onine ashɛ yibiiwoo kpakpa nɔ?

english: You should start preparing your trees about 3 to 4 months before the main harvest by weeding, pruning, and applying pest protection so the pods can mature fully without damage.
ga: Esa akɛ oje otsei lɛ ahe saamɔ shishi aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 dani kpamɔ titri lɛ aba kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ooojie lɛ nɔ. ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbuɔ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe Koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara kwraa ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akafite.

english: What months of the year are best for carrying out main maintenance work on a cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔŋ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni abaanyɛ atsu saamɔ nitsumɔi wuji yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli?

english: In Ghana, major maintenance like pruning and weeding is usually done around April to June before the heavy rains, while spraying for pests continues through August and September ahead of the main harvest.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, ehe miihia ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ tamɔ tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ. Bei pii lɛ, afeɔ kɛjɛɔ April kɛyashi June dani nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ baaya nɔ yɛ August kɛ September fɛɛ mli dani ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ aba.

english: How do I know for sure that my cocoa pods are fully mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Mature cocoa pods change color from green or dark red to a bright golden-yellow or orange, and when tapped gently with your knuckle, they sound slightly hollow inside.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ tsakeɔ su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse. Ni kɛ́ okɛ onine tswa lɛ fioo lɛ, obaatswa gbee fioo ko yɛ mli.

english: What steps am I supposed to take to properly ferment my cocoa beans after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni manyɛ mafee kookoo ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: After opening the mature pods, you pile the wet beans on fresh plantain leaves, cover them tightly with more leaves, and let them ferment for about 6 days while turning them every two days.
ga: Kɛji ogbele ŋmeii ni edara kwraa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Okɛ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ ato plantain baai heei lɛ anɔ. Okɛ baai babaoo aha nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ni ha edɔ aaafee gbii 6, ni otsake lɛ daa gbii enyɔ.

english: What happens to cocoa pods if the tree receives too much direct sunlight without shade?
ga: Mɛni baa cocoa ŋmeii anɔ kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛ hulu la babaoo nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo bɛ nɔ?

english: Too much direct sunlight can scorch young cocoa pods and leaves, causing them to dry up early and reducing the total amount of healthy cocoa you harvest.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ashã kookoo bibii lɛ kɛ baai lɛ. Enɛ haa egbiɔ oya, ni ehaa kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni okpaa lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together in the same farm with my maize crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is very helpful because cowpeas trap nitrogen food from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow stronger while giving you two different harvests from the same plot.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen nibii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmãa lɛ adara waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ajieɔ nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: How long will my young cocoa trees take before they start giving me pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ baahe dani amɛje shishi amɛwo ŋmeii?

english: If you plant improved hybrid cocoa varieties, they usually take about three years to mature and start producing pods, provided they receive proper shade, water, and protection from pests.
ga: Kɛji okwɛ cocoa hybrids ni atsake lɛ Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee afii 3 dani edara ni ebɔi pods feemɔ. Esa akɛ aha amɛ hulutsoo ni sa, nu kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot or the plant doesn't get enough water. When the plant feels heat stress, it drops its flowers to save energy to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ tsei nu dɔlɛ he haomɔ he lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛto hewalɛ ni ekɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my seeds too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in tall, weak plants that produce small yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure restores their bright green color and gives them energy to grow big ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha efee ŋmɔŋ ni eha lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ toi wuji.

english: Why do my crop leaves fold or droop during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ

english: Leaves droop on hot afternoons to protect themselves from losing water too quickly in the heat. It is a natural way for the crop to rest until the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu lɛ akafite oya tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛjɔɔ amɛhe kɛyashiɔ hulu lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing and look sickly after heavy flood water covers the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ekpa kwɛ̃mɔ ni amɛfeee nɔ ni ehiii yɛ be mli ni nu afua ni naa wa ha ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Crop roots need to breathe air in the soil just as we breathe air. Standing flood water drowns the roots, stopping them from taking up plant food until the water drains away.
ga: Ehe miihia ni tsei ashishifãi amu kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ bɔ ni wɔ hu wɔmuɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ. Nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aye tso lɛ niyenii kɛyashi nu lɛ hoɔ.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stems for planting keeps your crop healthy.
ga: Curling of leaves in cassava Ekɛ cassava mosaic hela ni ŋmei bibioo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ Kɛkɛ Cassava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛduɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them grow?
ga: Mulching around Te jwɛi ni mikɛyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out the earth, keeps moisture around the roots longer, and eventually decays to fertilize the soil.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, efiteɔ koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ

english: Officer, I keep hearing other farmers talk about cocoa swollen shoot. What exactly is this disease?
ga: Ofisa, minu okwaafoi krokomɛi lɛ ahe. Wɔwieɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ ahe be fɛɛ be. Mɛni tuuntu ji hela nɛɛ?

english: Cocoa swollen shoot is a serious disease caused by a virus that makes the stems and roots of cocoa trees swell up, discolors their leaves, reduces pod yields, and eventually kills the trees.
ga: Cocoa shishifãi ni fuuɔ lɛ ji hela ni naa wa ni hela ko ni haa cocoa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ fuuɔ, etsakeɔ baai lɛ ahe su, ehaa pod yibiiwoo baa shi, ni naagbee lɛ egbeɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why are the stems and branches of some of my cocoa trees swelling up and becoming unusually thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei komɛi ashishifãi kɛ amɛniji lɛ efuu ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Unusual swelling on stems and branches is a major symptom of the cocoa swollen shoot virus, which disrupts the tree's normal growth and prevents nutrients from flowing properly.
ga: Fuumɔ ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yitso kɛ eniji anɔ lɛ ji okadi titri ni tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli fuumɔ hela lɛ yɛ. Enɛ gbalaa tso lɛ dalɛ ni sa lɛ naa, ni ehaaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ atsɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: I noticed that the leaves on some of my cocoa trees have strange red patterns and yellow spots. What is happening to them?
ga: Miyɔse akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Mɛni ba a nɔ?

english: Leaves turning red or yellow along the veins are often the earliest warning signs that a cocoa tree has been infected with the swollen shoot virus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ etsuru loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ fãji lɛ ahe lɛ ji kɔkɔbɔɔ mra fe fɛɛ ni tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko ni efuu lɛ emɔ cacao tso lɛ mli.

english: What actually causes a healthy cocoa tree to get swollen shoot disease?
ga: Mɛni baanyɛ aha kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ apiŋ kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ ahe?

english: The disease is caused by a virus that gets transmitted into the cocoa tree when tiny sap-sucking insects, called mealybugs, feed on the plant.
ga: Virus ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa cacao tsei lɛ amli kɛji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ tswa amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ hela nɛɛ baa. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ mealybugs lɛ yeɔ tsei.

english: Can bad weather or poor soil cause my cocoa trees to get swollen shoot disease?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ baanyɛ aha mi-kokoo tsei lɛ aná ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ ahe amanehulu?

english: Poor soil and harsh weather do not directly cause the disease, but they act as predisposing factors by weakening the tree, making it much easier for the swollen shoot virus to take over.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ helai baaa tɛ̃ɛ. Mohu ɔ, a tsuɔ ní kaa níhi nɛ haa nɛ nɔ ko peeɔ lɛ kɛ gu tso ɔ nɛ a haa nɛ e gbɔjɔɔ ɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ helai ni efu lɛ baaye nɔ.

english: If my neighbor's farm has cocoa swollen shoot, can it spread to my farm?
ga: Kɛji akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli kookoo yitsei ni efuu lɛ, ani ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, insects like mealybugs can carry the virus from infected trees on your neighbor's farm to healthy trees on your farm, especially if ants help transport the insects between farms.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs baanyɛ ajie helai ni baa mɔ mli kɛjɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkɛ kooloi bibii yaa ŋmɔji ateŋ.

english: Is there any chemical spray I can buy at the agro-chemical store to cure swollen shoot once my cocoa trees get it?
ga: Ani tsofai komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ mahe yɛ agrochemical shwapo lɛ mli koni mikɛtsa ŋmeii ni efuu kɛji mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ná eko?
